genes: JmLFY (flowering regulation, Juglans mandshurica)
phenotype: Overexpression of JmLFY promotes early flowering (6-8 days earlier than wild type), reduces rosette leaves by ~40%, increases plant height and secondary branches, and restores normal flower morphology in lfy mutants
mechanism: JmLFY activates flowering-related genes AtAP1, AtSOC1, AtFT, and AtPI, promoting transition from vegetative to reproductive growth and floral meristem formation

genes: WAK1 (WALL-ASSOCIATED KINASE 1, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), WAK2 (WALL-ASSOCIATED KINASE 2, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), WAK3 (WALL-ASSOCIATED KINASE 3, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), WAK4 (WALL-ASSOCIATED KINASE 4, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), WAK5 (WALL-ASSOCIATED KINASE 5, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Generation of wak1/2 double mutant and wak1/2/3/4/5 quintuple mutant Arabidopsis thaliana plants with loss of function in all five WAK genes
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing using sgRNA targeting third exons of WAK1-WAK5 genes

genes: OsABCG43 (Oryza sativa, Cd importer gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsABCG43 causes Cd accumulation which inhibits photosynthesis and development, alters the antioxidant system, resulting in phytotoxicity. Overexpression also results in retarded plant growth and enhanced rice sensitivity to Cd stress.
mechanism: OsABCG43 functions as a Cd importer, leading to Cd accumulation in rice plants, which disrupts photosynthesis, plant growth, and antioxidant systems.

genes: OsABCG43 (Oryza sativa, Cd importer gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: osabcg43 mutants have unaltered Cd levels in leaves and roots compared to wild type. The mutants show similar plant growth to wild type under Cd stress.
mechanism: OsABCG43 knockout does not alter Cd accumulation in rice plants, indicating functional redundancy in the ABCG family.

genes: OsABCG43 (Oryza sativa, promoter region, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsABCG43pro:GUS transgenic plants show GUS activity specifically in the vasculature of roots, stems, leaves, and panicles.
mechanism: OsABCG43 promoter drives GUS expression in vascular tissues, confirming its tissue-specific expression pattern.

genes: OsABCG43 (Oryza sativa, Cd importer gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsABCG43-YFP fusion protein localizes to the plasma membrane in rice protoplasts, confirming OsABCG43's plasma membrane localization.
mechanism: OsABCG43-YFP colocalizes with SCAMP1-RFP, a plasma membrane marker, indicating plasma membrane localization.

genes: MtEF1A1 (salt stress resistance, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Overexpression of MtEF1A1 increases salt stress resistance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with higher germination rate, longer roots, and more lateral roots compared to wild type plants.
mechanism: MtEF1A1 may realize its function by binding to calmodulin (CaM) or by participating in Ca2+-dependent signaling pathway.

genes: NahG (NahG, salicylate hydroxylase, Pseudomonas putida)
phenotype: Overexpression of NahG increases adventitious root formation in leaf explants by reducing endogenous salicylic acid (SA) levels.
mechanism: NahG converts SA to catechol, lowering SA levels which removes SA-mediated suppression of adventitious root formation.

genes: GhWRKY70 (GhWRKY70, transcriptional activator, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhWRKY70 in Arabidopsis thaliana results in better growth performance, higher lignin content, antioxidant enzyme activities, and jasmonic acid (JA) levels after V. dahliae infection.
mechanism: GhWRKY70 enhances JA production by upregulating GhAOS1 expression.

genes: GhWRKY70 (GhWRKY70, transcriptional activator, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Knockdown of GhWRKY70 in Gossypium hirsutum via VIGS results in higher disease index (DI) values, lower chlorophyll and lignin contents, and decreased GhAOS1 expression and JA abundance.
mechanism: GhWRKY70 is a positive regulator of Verticillium wilt tolerance by promoting JA production via regulation of GhAOS1.

genes: IbCCD4 (IbCCD4, carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 4, Ipomoea batatas)
phenotype: Total carotenoid content decreased in tuberous roots of transgenic sweetpotato
mechanism: IbCCD4 cleaves carotenoids, reducing their accumulation in sweetpotato tuberous roots

genes: VPT1 (VPT1, vacuolar phosphate transporter 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of VPT1 in leaves reduces phosphorus content in seeds by ~20% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: VPT1 enhances vacuolar phosphate influx, reducing Pi allocation to reproductive organs, thereby decreasing seed phosphorus content.

genes: VPT1 (VPT1, vacuolar phosphate transporter 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), VPT3 (VPT3, vacuolar phosphate transporter 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: native promoter of VPT1-GUS-NA---native promoter of VPT3-GUS-NA
phenotype: Expression of GUS under native promoters of VPT1 and VPT3 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: RAPTOR1B (RAPTOR1B, RAPTOR1B subunit of TOR complex, Arabidopsis thaliana), RAPTOR1BS916A (RAPTOR1B with S916A mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complemented the raptor1b mutant phenotypes in germination, root elongation, and plant growth under normal conditions. RAPTOR1BS916A partially suppressed autophagy induction upon BRZ or sucrose starvation.
mechanism: BIN2 phosphorylation of RAPTOR1B modulates autophagy by affecting TOR activity. Loss of phosphorylation at RAPTOR1B Ser916 increases ATG13a phosphorylation, repressing autophagy.

genes: ATG13a (ATG13a, autophagy initiation complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Used for immunoblotting to analyze phosphorylation. Enhanced BL signaling increased ATG13a phosphorylation, repressing autophagy.
mechanism: ATG13a phosphorylation by TOR represses autophagy. Loss of RAPTOR1B Ser916 phosphorylation increases ATG13a phosphorylation.

genes: BIN2 (Brassinosteroid Insensitive 2, kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), TurboID (synthetic), YFP (Yellow Fluorescent Protein, Aequorea victoria)
phenotype: Overexpression of BIN2-YFP-TurboID in transgenic Arabidopsis results in dwarf phenotypes similar to BIN2-overexpressing or bin2-1 mutant plants.
mechanism: BIN2-YFP-TurboID biotinylates BZR1 and other substrates in vivo, allowing identification of BIN2-proximal proteins through proximity-dependent biotinylation.

genes: YFP (Yellow Fluorescent Protein, Aequorea victoria), TurboID (synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of YFP-YFP-TurboID in transgenic Arabidopsis does not induce visible phenotypic changes compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: SlMYB72 (transcription factor, tomato, tomato), GUS (reporter gene, Escherichia coli, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS staining showed expression in stamen, especially pollen and tapetum in tomato.
mechanism: NA

genes: SlMYB72 (transcription factor, tomato, tomato)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlMYB72 caused abnormal pollen development, reduced pollen viability (50–60%), and premature tapetum degradation in tomato anthers.
mechanism: SlMYB72 promotes autophagy-related gene expression (e.g., SlATG7), leading to tapetum degradation and pollen abortion.

genes: SlATG7 (autophagy-related gene, tomato, tomato)
phenotype: RNAi-SlATG7 plants exhibited reduced pollen viability (60–70%), abnormal pollen morphology, and delayed tapetum degradation in tomato anthers.
mechanism: SlATG7 is essential for autophagy in tapetum cells; its downregulation inhibits autophagy, leading to impaired pollen development.

genes: SlATG7 (autophagy-related gene, tomato, tomato)
phenotype: Dual-luciferase assays showed SlMYB72 activates SlATG7 promoter-driven luciferase expression in transient assays.
mechanism: SlMYB72 directly binds to the AC-rich motif in the SlATG7 promoter, transcriptionally activating its expression.

genes: MUTE (MUTE, MUTE gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of MUTE-GFP under MUTE promoter in stomatal lineage cells for live imaging
mechanism: NA

genes: MUTE (MUTE, MUTE gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Nuclear-localized YFP expression under MUTE promoter in embryonic stomatal lineage cells
mechanism: NA

genes: FAMA (FAMA, FAMA gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of FAMA-GFP under FAMA promoter in stomatal lineage cells for live imaging
mechanism: NA

genes: PlaCCI (CDT1a-eCPF, HTR13-mCherry, N-CYCB1;1-YFP, cell cycle markers, synthetic)
phenotype: Multicolor cell cycle phase markers for live imaging in stomatal lineage cells
mechanism: NA

genes: OsMO25A1 (OsMO25A1, scaffold for kinase signaling, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Recovery of homozygous mutant seeds with normal embryo morphology; germination and growth until maturity
mechanism: OsMO25A1 acts as a scaffold for kinase signaling, necessary for normal embryogenesis after 3 DAP

genes: PpCDKA1 (CDKA1, cyclin-dependent kinase A1, Physcomitrium patens)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpCDKA1 promotes protonema cell growth with 10% shorter gametophores and 15% smaller gametophore cells in Physcomitrium patens.
mechanism: PpCDKA1 overexpression downregulates PpPIN (auxin efflux carrier) by >80%, reducing auxin transport and gametophore differentiation. Transcript levels of G2/M phase markers (CYCB1, CYCB2) increase by 80-121%, suggesting involvement in G2/M transition.

genes: PpCDKA2 (CDKA2, cyclin-dependent kinase A2, Physcomitrium patens)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpCDKA2 results in protonema-dominant growth with small gametophores (6% shorter, 12% larger cells) in Physcomitrium patens.
mechanism: PpCDKA2 upregulates PpCDKA1, PpCYCD1, PpCYCD2 and downregulates PpKRP, promoting G1 phase progression. PpPIN expression is suppressed but less severely than in PpCDKA1, allowing partial gametophore development.

genes: PpCYCD1 (CYCD1, cyclin D1, Physcomitrium patens)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpCYCD1 promotes gametophore development (1.6-1.7× taller) with larger cell area (35% increase) in Physcomitrium patens.
mechanism: PpCYCD1 upregulates PpPINA and PpRSL2, enhancing gametophore differentiation. Downregulation of G2/M markers (CYCB1, CYCB2) and KRP suggests involvement in G1/S transition. Gametophore cells arrest in late S phase, supporting increased cell size.

genes: PpCYCD2 (CYCD2, cyclin D2, Physcomitrium patens)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpCYCD2 results in reduced gametophore height (38% shorter) and cell size (38% smaller) in Physcomitrium patens.
mechanism: PpCYCD2 upregulates early S phase marker HFO (92-70%) and induces G2/M transition. No significant PIN downregulation but RSL2 upregulation on BCD suggests auxin-related differentiation inhibition.

genes: AhGLK1 (AhGLK1, chlorophyll synthesis and photosynthesis, Arachis hypogaea)
phenotype: AhGLK1 overexpression increases relative water content during drought stress in Arachis hypogaea
mechanism: AhGLK1 enhances chlorophyll synthesis and photosynthesis, improving post-drought recovery growth

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Histochemical staining indicates OsERF106MZ is mainly expressed in root exodermis, sclerenchyma layer, and vascular system in transgenic rice seedlings.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsERF106MZ (ethylene response factor, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsERF106MZ overexpression in rice seedlings leads to an increase in primary root (PR) length.
mechanism: OsERF106MZ represses ABA biosynthetic gene OsAO3 and reduces ABA sensitivity gene OsNPC3 expression, lowering ABA levels and reducing ABA-mediated root growth inhibition.

genes: SYMRK (SYMRK, receptor-like kinase, Phaseolus vulgaris)
phenotype: T589A mutation in SYMRK reduces intracellular puncta formation by 54% in nonhair-epidermal cells, indicating impaired endocytosis.
mechanism: Phosphorylation at T589 regulates SYMRK kinase activity and endocytosis; mutation disrupts this process.

genes: SYMRK (SYMRK, receptor-like kinase, Phaseolus vulgaris)
phenotype: K618E mutation in SYMRK reduces intracellular puncta formation to <25% of wild-type levels, indicating kinase activity is required for endocytosis.
mechanism: K618 is part of the kinase active site; its mutation (K618E) inactivates SYMRK, blocking endocytosis.

genes: VfMYB36 (VfMYB36, involved in oil biosynthesis, Euphorbiaceae)
phenotype: Overexpression of VfMYB36 significantly increases linolenic acid (C18:3) content and oil content in Euphorbiaceae species.
mechanism: VfMYB36 is involved in oil biosynthesis.

genes: NPTII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, maize ubiquitin1, synthetic), DsRed (red fluorescent protein, maize ubiquitin1, synthetic)
phenotype: NPTII confers resistance to geneticin (G418) selection; DsRed produces red fluorescence in transgenic sorghum roots
mechanism: NPTII detoxifies G418 by phosphorylation; DsRed acts as a visual marker for transgene expression

genes: StTGA2.1 (transcription factor involved in immune response, potato)
phenotype: Overexpression of StTGA2.1 in SA-deficient potato reduces PVY replication by ~15% at 10 days post infection.
mechanism: StTGA2.1 activates class III peroxidase StPRX07, enhancing apoplastic ROS production in immune signaling.

genes: ThsB (ThsB, Bacillus cereus MSX D-12), BdTIR (BdTIR, Brachypodium distachyon), SARM1-TIR (SARM1-TIR, Homo sapiens), AbTIR (AbTIR, Acinetobacter baumannii)
phenotype: Expression of ThsB, BdTIR, SARM1-TIR, and AbTIR in Nicotiana benthamiana triggers chlorotic cell death or HR (hypersensitive response) depending on EDS1 presence. SARM1-TIR and AbTIR cause EDS1-independent cell death via NAD+ depletion.
mechanism: ThsB and AbTIR produce cADPR isomers that activate ThsA, leading to NAD+ depletion and cell death. SARM1-TIR depletes NAD+ directly, causing cell death.

genes: ThsB-Auto (ThsB variant, Bacillus cereus MSX D-12)
phenotype: ThsB-Auto coexpression with ThsA in Nicotiana benthamiana triggers chlorotic cell death and NAD+ depletion, indicating ThsA activation.
mechanism: ThsB-Auto produces 3′cADPR isomers that activate ThsA, leading to NAD+ depletion and cell death.

genes: ThsB2-TIR (ThsB2-TIR, Bacillus cereus MSX D-12)
phenotype: ThsB2-TIR expression in Nicotiana benthamiana triggers ThsA-mediated cell death and NAD+ depletion, producing 3′cADPR but not the undefined isomer from ThsB-Auto.
mechanism: ThsB2-TIR generates 3′cADPR isomers that activate ThsA, leading to NAD+ depletion and cell death.

genes: FaPG1 (endopolygalacturonase, Fragaria x ananassa)
phenotype: Increased fruit firmness (up to 70% firmer than wild type), reduced susceptibility to Botrytis cinerea infection, and reduced transpirational water loss in Fragaria x ananassa cv. Chandler strawberries
mechanism: FaPG1 knockout reduces pectin degradation in cell walls, maintaining higher pectin content (35% more than wild type) and preserving cell wall integrity, which correlates with increased firmness and reduced water loss

genes: IbNAC29 (NAC transcription factor, sweet potato, Ipomoea batatas)
phenotype: Overexpression of IbNAC29 increases carotenoid levels in storage roots of sweet potato by ~1.71-fold compared to wild type, with increased accumulation of α-carotene, lutein, β-carotene, zeaxanthin, and capsanthin
mechanism: IbNAC29 forms a regulatory module with IbMYB1R1 and IbAITR5, which represses IbSGR1 transcription. This reduces inhibition of IbPSY gene expression, leading to enhanced carotenoid biosynthesis

genes: CsTRM5 (Cucumis sativus TRM5, responsible for fruit shape, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: Knockout of CsTRM5 results in decreased fruit length (2.3–2.9 FSI) and increased diameter compared to control (4.9–5.6 FSI), with shorter and wider seeds (17-19% reduction in length/width ratio).
mechanism: CsTRM5 regulates fruit shape by controlling cell division direction (enhanced cross-direction, repressed longitudinal) and cell expansion in cucumber. ABA pathway is involved in fruit elongation via cell expansion but not cell division direction.

genes: TIP1 (TIP GROWTH DEFECTIVE 1, S-acyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of grm1 mutant phenotypes (reversion of dwarf stature and humidity-dependent dysbiotic phenotypes to wild-type levels)
mechanism: Restoration of TIP1 function via native promoter-driven expression in grm1 mutant background

genes: AgMYB5 (AgMYB5, transcription factor, celery cv. 'Jinnanshiqin')
phenotype: Ectopic expression of AgMYB5 increases β-carotene content and promotes drought tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AgMYB5 promotes β-carotene biosynthesis by triggering the expression of AtCRTISO and AtLCYB, which increases antioxidant enzyme activities, decreases H2O2 and MDA contents, inhibits O2− generation, and promotes endogenous ABA biosynthesis leading to stomatal closing and delayed water loss.

genes: ZmBBM2 (Zea mays BABY BOOM 2, maize, ZmBBM2), sgRNA2.0 (synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: Activation of ZmBBM2 in egg cells leads to parthenogenesis phenotypes, including double embryo sacs and maternal haploid generation with 0.4–3.55% haploid kernels.
mechanism: CRISPRa5BBM targets ZmBBM2 transcription in egg cells, inducing parthenogenesis by bypassing fertilization and enabling maternal haploid development.

genes: OsMADS27 (OsMADS27, MADS-box transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsMADS27 increases salt tolerance and grain yield in rice.
mechanism: OsMADS27 activates stress-related genes, maintains ion homeostasis, and enhances ROS scavenging.

genes: OsMADS27 (OsMADS27, MADS-box transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsMADS27 promoter drives GUS expression in roots, leaves, and sheaths of transgenic rice.
mechanism: The OsMADS27 promoter activity is specific to root stele and other tissues.

genes: OsMADS27 (OsMADS27, MADS-box transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsMADS27-GFP localizes to the nucleus in the presence of nitrate in rice.
mechanism: Nuclear accumulation of OsMADS27-GFP is nitrate-dependent and correlates with transcript levels.

genes: FYVE domain (phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate-binding domain, mouse EEA1), soybean PR1a signal peptide (secretory signal, Glycine max)
phenotype: SP-eGFP-FYVE accumulates in the apoplast and detects PI3P levels around Phytophthora infestans hyphae in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: SP-eGFP-FYVE binds PI3P to visualize its localization and quantify its reduction by SP-PIP5K1 in the apoplast.

genes: SR45 (SR45, splicing factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of SR45-eGFP reduces ABA sensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings, with OX2 lines showing strongest hyposensitivity.
mechanism: SR45 acts as a negative regulator of ABA signaling by stabilizing protein levels through ABA-induced dephosphorylation and reduced ubiquitination.

genes: SR45 (SR45, splicing factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of SR45-eGFP under UBQ10 promoter reduces ABA sensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings, with OX2 lines showing strongest hyposensitivity.
mechanism: SR45 acts as a negative regulator of ABA signaling by stabilizing protein levels through ABA-induced dephosphorylation and reduced ubiquitination.

genes: SR45 (SR45, splicing factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Phosphomutant SR45_T264A-eGFP overexpression lines show reduced ABA sensitivity compared to wild type.
mechanism: T264 phosphorylation promotes SR45 ubiquitination and degradation; mutation to alanine stabilizes SR45 protein.

genes: SR45 (SR45, splicing factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Phosphomimetic SR45_T264D-eGFP overexpression lines show increased ABA sensitivity despite higher SR45 protein levels.
mechanism: T264 phosphorylation promotes SR45 ubiquitination and degradation; aspartic acid mimic enhances degradation.

genes: SlDCD2 (SlDCD2, D-cysteine desulfhydrase 2, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Transient silencing of SlDCD2 accelerates tomato fruit ripening, with fruits turning red 8 days earlier than wild-type and showing increased carotenoid accumulation and decreased chlorophyll content.
mechanism: SlDCD2 silencing increases expression of ripening-associated genes (NYC1, PAO, SGR1, PSY1, PDS, ACO1, ACS2, E4, CEL2) and reduces endogenous H2S levels, which antagonizes ethylene's effect on ripening.

genes: miR156 (microRNA 156, regulatory RNA, Arabidopsis thaliana), SPL9 (SQUAMOSA PROMOTER-BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE 9, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of miR156 target mimicry (MIM156) blocks miR156 activity, resulting in a 50% reduction in warm temperature-induced hypocotyl elongation compared to wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MIM156 inhibits miR156 function, leading to increased SPL9 expression which antagonizes thermoresponsive hypocotyl elongation by repressing auxin sensitivity.

genes: SPL9 (SQUAMOSA PROMOTER-BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE 9, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of miR156-resistant SPL9 (rSPL9) causes a >2-fold decrease in warm temperature-induced hypocotyl elongation compared to miR156-sensitive SPL9 (sSPL9) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: rSPL9 overexpression antagonizes thermoresponsive hypocotyl elongation by repressing auxin sensitivity through miR156-resistant SPL9 accumulation.

genes: MtABCG46 (Medicago truncatula ABCG transporter, Medicago truncatula, synthetic), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MtABCG46 in Nicotiana tabacum BY2 cells enables ATP-dependent transport of phenolic compounds like liquiritigenin and 4-coumarate, with mutant variants showing altered transport capabilities (e.g., F562L retains liquiritigenin transport but loses 4-coumarate transport).
mechanism: MtABCG46 functions as a plasma membrane transporter for phenolic compounds, with residue F562 influencing substrate specificity through structural rearrangements of transmembrane helices and access path availability.

genes: CASP1 (CASP1, Casparian Strip Membrane Domain Protein 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), CASP2 (CASP2, Casparian Strip Membrane Domain Protein 2, Arabidopsis thaliana), CASP3 (CASP3, Casparian Strip Membrane Domain Protein 3, Arabidopsis thaliana), CASP4 (CASP4, Casparian Strip Membrane Domain Protein 4, Arabidopsis thaliana), CASP5 (CASP5, Casparian Strip Membrane Domain Protein 5, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: caspQ mutants display abnormal lignin foci, delayed barrier formation, and disrupted plasma membrane attachment to the cell wall in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CASPs are required for forming a protein exclusion zone and plasma membrane-wall attachment, and for evicting EXO70A1 from CS initiation sites.

genes: CASP3 (CASP3, Casparian Strip Membrane Domain Protein 3, Arabidopsis thaliana), CASP5 (CASP5, Casparian Strip Membrane Domain Protein 5, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Triple CASP1-CASP3-CASP5 complementation efficiently rescues caspQ mutant phenotype, restoring CS formation and plasma membrane attachment.
mechanism: A minimum of three CASPs is required for complementation, with CASP1, CASP3, and CASP5 being the most effective combination.

genes: CASP1 (CASP1, Casparian Strip Membrane Domain Protein 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CASP1-proximity labeling identifies novel CS-associated Rab GTPases, including RabA6a, which are enriched in the CASP1-tID sample.
mechanism: CASPs interact with Rab GTPases to regulate vesicle trafficking and exocyst complex activation during CS formation.

genes: ERD2 (AtERD2, Arabidopsis thaliana), YFP (synthetic)
phenotype: Co-expression of YFP-TM-AtERD2 resulted in high-frequency callus formation and fertile plants with bright punctate Golgi structures, while AtERD2-YFP and ST-YFP-HDEL constructs failed to form roots and were lost.
mechanism: YFP-TM-AtERD2 compensates for antisense-mediated ERD2 knockdown by localizing to Golgi bodies, whereas AtERD2-YFP and ST-YFP-HDEL fail to rescue the phenotype due to ER localization or low expression.

genes: ERD2B-1 (PpERD2B-1, Physcomitrium patens), YFP (synthetic)
phenotype: YFP-TM-PpERD2B-1 expression under native promoter in P. patens rescued the ERD2 knockdown phenotype, showing normal growth with YFP-TM fluorescence in growing tips and cell plates.
mechanism: YFP-TM-PpERD2B-1 localizes exclusively to punctate Golgi structures, replacing both endogenous ERD2 genes in P. patens.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS expression in vascular cells of cotyledons and roots under sucrose and ABA treatment
mechanism: Regulation by sucrose and ABA through the promoters of MED12 and MED13

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS expression in vascular cells of cotyledons and roots under sucrose and ABA treatment
mechanism: Regulation by sucrose and ABA through the promoters of MED12 and MED13

genes: BrLSH2 (BrLSH2, nuclear protein, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Inhibition of growth and development in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NA

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, marker gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP confers fluorescence on seed tissue and most other plant tissues in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: GFP expression allows visual tracking of pollen transfer between plants.

genes: CYS-C1 (CYS-C1, cyanide synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CYS-C1 increases salt stress resistance, with higher germination speed and faster cyanide detoxification under 50-200 mM NaCl conditions.
mechanism: CYS-C1 reduces cyanide and H2S toxicity, maintaining antioxidant enzyme activity to mitigate oxidative damage.

genes: CYS-D1 (CYS-D1, cyanide synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CYS-D1 increases salt stress resistance, with higher germination speed and moderate cyanide detoxification under 50-200 mM NaCl conditions.
mechanism: CYS-D1 reduces cyanide and H2S toxicity, maintaining antioxidant enzyme activity to mitigate oxidative damage.

genes: GRF4-GIF1 (GRF4-GIF1, chimeric fusion of GRF and GIF genes, synthetic), rGRF4-GIF1 (GRF4-GIF1 with miR396-resistant mutations, synthetic)
phenotype: Increased regeneration efficiency (up to 75.1% in Cobham Green, 53.0% in Armenian 999) and shooting frequency (up to 2.32 shoots/explant in Cobham Green, 1.68 shoots/explant in Armenian 999) compared to controls.
mechanism: GRF–GIF fusions enhance shoot regeneration by promoting cell proliferation and organogenesis; miR396-resistant versions avoid post-transcriptional regulation, increasing protein stability and activity.

genes: GRF4-GIF1 (GRF4-GIF1, chimeric fusion of GRF and GIF genes, synthetic)
phenotype: Increased regeneration efficiency (48.75% in Cobham Green, 46.92% in Armenian 999) and shooting frequency (1.33 shoots/explant in Cobham Green, 0.82 shoots/explant in Armenian 999) compared to controls.
mechanism: GRF–GIF fusions enhance shoot regeneration by promoting cell proliferation and organogenesis.

genes: dsRED (dsRED, fluorescent reporter protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of dsRED in transgenic shoots confirmed by fluorescence microscopy, with frequencies up to 100% in co-transformations with GRF–GIF.
mechanism: The L. sativa ubiquitin promoter drives constitutive expression of dsRED in plant cells.

genes: TRB (TRB, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TRB-FLAG leads to interaction with JMJ14 and NAC050/052, contributing to gene silencing via H3K4me3 demethylation.
mechanism: TRBs recruit JMJ14 to remove H3K4me3, thus contributing to gene silencing.

genes: JMJ14 (JMJ14, histone H3K4me3 demethylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of JMJ14-FLAG interacts with TRBs and contributes to gene silencing via H3K4me3 demethylation.
mechanism: JMJ14 is recruited by TRBs to remove H3K4me3, thus contributing to gene silencing.

genes: JMJ14 (JMJ14, histone H3K4me3 demethylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of JMJ14-Myc interacts with TRBs and contributes to gene silencing via H3K4me3 demethylation.
mechanism: JMJ14 is recruited by TRBs to remove H3K4me3, thus contributing to gene silencing.

genes: TRB-ZF108 (TRB fused with artificial zinc finger 108, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TRB-ZF108-FLAG fusions causes early flowering in fwa epiallele by silencing FWA expression through H3K27me3 deposition and H3K4me3 demethylation.
mechanism: TRB-ZF fusions trigger gene silencing via H3K27me3 deposition and H3K4me3 demethylation, independent of DNA methylation.

genes: TRB3-ZF108 (TRB3 fused with artificial zinc finger 108, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZF108-FLAG-TRB3 causes early flowering in fwa epiallele by silencing FWA expression through H3K27me3 deposition and H3K4me3 demethylation.
mechanism: TRB-ZF fusions trigger gene silencing via H3K27me3 deposition and H3K4me3 demethylation, independent of DNA methylation.

genes: GaZnF (Zinc finger homeodomain transcription factor, Gossypium arboreum, GQ169757.1)
phenotype: Overexpression of GaZnF in Gossypium hirsutum increases drought tolerance, as evidenced by 27.18% higher plant height, 0.59 root-to-shoot length ratio, and 33% leaf relative water content under drought stress compared to non-transgenic controls.

mechanism: Transient expression using Agrobacterium-mediated gene transfer into Nicotiana benthamiana leaves.

genes: PGT121 (human HIV envelope glycoprotein-directed bNAb, synthetic codon-optimized variable domains)
phenotype: Expression of PGT121-YTE in Nicotiana benthamiana plants produces plant-derived antibodies with enhanced FcRn binding affinity.
mechanism: Transient expression using Agrobacterium-mediated gene transfer into Nicotiana benthamiana leaves with YTE (Y100F, T329N, E330A) mutations in the Fc domain.

genes: VRC07-523 (human HIV envelope glycoprotein-directed bNAb, synthetic codon-optimized variable domains)
phenotype: Expression of VRC07-523-LS in Nicotiana benthamiana plants produces plant-derived antibodies with enhanced FcRn binding affinity.
mechanism: Transient expression using Agrobacterium-mediated gene transfer into Nicotiana benthamiana leaves with LS (M428L, N434S) mutations in the Fc domain.

genes: OsbHLH069 (OsbHLH069, bHLH transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsbHLH069 results in sparse panicles with reduced spikelets in rice.
mechanism: OsbHLH069 physically interacts with LAX1 and regulates inflorescence axillary meristem (AM) development through starch and sucrose metabolism pathways.

genes: cbbL (Form-1A Rubisco large subunit, H. neapolitanus), cbbS (Form-1A Rubisco small subunit, H. neapolitanus), CsoS2 (linker protein, H. neapolitanus), csoS4A (shell pentamer, H. neapolitanus), csoS4B (shell pentamer, H. neapolitanus), csoSCA (carbonic anhydrase, H. neapolitanus), csoS1A (shell hexamer, H. neapolitanus), csoS1B (shell hexamer, H. neapolitanus), csoS1C (shell hexamer, H. neapolitanus)
phenotype: Expression of α-carboxysome proteins in tobacco chloroplasts results in formation of polyhedral carboxysome-like structures and enables autotrophic growth in 1% CO2-supplemented air but not in ambient CO2.
mechanism: Engineered α-carboxysomes contain functional Rubisco and carbonic anhydrase, with structural similarity to native carboxysomes from H. neapolitanus and E. coli. The protein shell creates an acidic microenvironment for CO2 fixation and restricts CO2 leakage.

genes: OsMIR393a (OsMicroRNA393a, targets OsTIR1 and OsAFB2, Oryza sativa), OsMIR393b (OsMicroRNA393b, targets OsTIR1 and OsAFB2, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsMIR393a and OsMIR393b results in loss of scutellum-derived callus formation on CIM in rice.
mechanism: OsMIR393a and OsMIR393b target and degrade mRNA of auxin receptor genes OsTIR1 and OsAFB2, disrupting auxin signaling required for callus formation.

genes: OsMIR393b (OsMicroRNA393b, targets OsTIR1 and OsAFB2, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsMIR393b results in loss of scutellum-derived callus formation on CIM in rice.
mechanism: OsMIR393b targets and degrades mRNA of auxin receptor genes OsTIR1 and OsAFB2, disrupting auxin signaling required for callus formation.

genes: HaTCP1 (HaTCP1, negatively regulates sunflower branching, Helianthus annuus)
phenotype: significant decrease in branch number in Arabidopsis
mechanism: HaTCP1 played a key role in negatively regulating sunflower branching

genes: SvSCR1 (Setaria viridis SCR1, source), SvSCR2 (Setaria viridis SCR2, source), SvNKD (Setaria viridis NKD, source)
gene_construct: rice U3 promoter-SvSCR guides---rice U3 promoter-SvNKD guides
phenotype: Generation of Svscr1;Svscr2;Svnkd mutants with no stomata, fused veins, and severe growth perturbations in Setaria viridis.
mechanism: CRISPR-induced loss-of-function mutations in SvSCR1, SvSCR2, and SvNKD genes disrupt stomatal and inner leaf patterning.

genes: SvSCR1 (Setaria viridis SCR1, source), SvSCR2 (Setaria viridis SCR2, source)
phenotype: Generation of Svscr1;Svscr2 mutants with no stomata and reduced mesophyll cells between veins in Setaria viridis.
mechanism: CRISPR-induced loss-of-function mutations in SvSCR1 and SvSCR2 genes disrupt stomatal and inner leaf patterning.

genes: SvNKD (Setaria viridis NKD, source)
phenotype: Generation of Svnkd mutants with no obvious leaf phenotypes but enhanced scr mutant phenotypes when combined with scr mutations in Setaria viridis.
mechanism: CRISPR-induced loss-of-function mutations in SvNKD gene synergize with scr mutations to exacerbate leaf patterning defects.

genes: DefH9-iaaM (iaaM, tryptophan monoxygenase, Pseudomonas syringae pv. savastanoi)
gene_construct: DefH9-iaaM (iaaM, tryptophan monoxygenase, Pseudomonas syringae pv. savastanoi)-NA
phenotype: Increased fruit productivity by 30–35% under greenhouse and open field cultivation; seedless fruits with improved quality; faster fruit development under optimal conditions
mechanism: DefH9-iaaM produces indole-3-acetic acid (auxin) in placenta/ovules, enabling parthenocarpic fruit development without fertilization

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP-TurboID-HF serves as a specificity control for the APEAL approach.
mechanism: NA

genes: PfFAD3-1 (Physaria fendleri fatty acid desaturase 3-1, Physaria fendleri)
phenotype: Overexpression of PfFAD3-1 increases 18:3 (ALA) content by ~12-14% and decreases 18:2 content by ~7-13% in Camelina sativa seeds
mechanism: PfFAD3-1 converts 18:2 fatty acid to 18:3 fatty acid (ALA) in seed-specific expression

genes: gpk1 (Glyoxysomal protein kinase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knockout of gpk1 impairs priming of defense response to pathogen infection in Arabidopsis
mechanism: DDM1-mediated gene body methylation regulates inducibility of immune response

genes: DWF5 (DWF5, brassinosteroid biosynthesis enzyme, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of DWF5 rescues the delayed vegetative phase change phenotype of del2/dwf5 mutant, restoring abaxial trichome production to wild-type levels.
mechanism: DWF5 is required for brassinosteroid (BR) biosynthesis. BRs stabilize SPL9 protein and maintain its function in activating MIR172B, which promotes vegetative phase change.

genes: SPL9 (SPL9, SBP domain transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR156-insensitive SPL9 in dwf5 partially rescues the delayed vegetative phase change phenotype, with 75.7% of plants producing abaxial trichomes on leaf 1.
mechanism: SPL9 is destabilized in dwf5 due to BIN2-mediated phosphorylation. Overexpression of SPL9 compensates for this instability, partially restoring MIR172B activation and trichome production.

genes: SPL9 (SPL9, SBP domain transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Inducible overexpression of SPL9 in dwf5 partially activates MIR172B expression (2.6-fold vs 1.5-fold in dwf5), demonstrating impaired SPL9 function in dwf5.
mechanism: SPL9 function is partially impaired in dwf5, as evidenced by reduced MIR172B induction upon DEX treatment. DWF5 stabilizes SPL9 and maintains its function.

genes: MIR172B (MIR172B, microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MIR172B in dwf5 rescues the delayed vegetative phase change phenotype, with abaxial trichomes appearing on leaf 4.5 vs 11.3 in dwf5.
mechanism: MIR172B represses AP2-like genes (TOE1/TOE2) that delay vegetative phase change. Reduced MIR172B in dwf5 contributes to its delayed phenotype.

genes: BIN2 (BIN2, GSK3-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BIN2 in dwf5 leads to elevated BIN2 protein levels and delayed vegetative phase change (abaxial trichomes on leaf 11.7 vs 9.4 with LiCl treatment).
mechanism: BIN2 physically interacts with and phosphorylates SPL9 and TOE1, leading to their destabilization. Elevated BIN2 in dwf5 exacerbates the delayed phenotype.

genes: TOE1 (TOE1, AP2-like transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR172-insensitive TOE1 in dwf5 leads to delayed vegetative phase change (abaxial trichomes on leaf 7.7 vs 9.1 in wild-type TOE1).
mechanism: BIN2 phosphorylates TOE1 at threonine 124, destabilizing it. Constitutive phosphorylation (T-D) impairs TOE1 function, delaying phase change.

genes: ZmPMP3g (ZmPMP3g, drought tolerance gene, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmPMP3g enhances drought tolerance in maize, with increased leaf relative water content, reduced leaf wilting index, and improved root growth under drought conditions.
mechanism: ZmPMP3g overexpression increases osmoprotectant accumulation (betaine, soluble sugars), enhances antioxidant enzyme activity (SOD, CAT), and modulates ABA-GA homeostasis to improve drought tolerance.

genes: ACTIN2 (ACTIN2, actin gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Inhibition of ACTIN2 gene expression in Arabidopsis thaliana using LDH-dsRNA delivery method.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing via LDH-dsRNA bioconjugates.

genes: PDS (phytoene desaturase, carotenoid biosynthesis enzyme, Arabidopsis thaliana), WUS (WUSCHEL, stem cell regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana), WOX5 (WUSCHEL-related homeobox 5, stem cell regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana), RHD6 (ROOT HAIR DEFECTIVE 6, root hair development, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: High-efficiency knockdown of PDS, WUS, WOX5, and RHD6 genes in Arabidopsis thaliana using LDH-dsRNA system.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing via LDH-dsRNA bioconjugates.

genes: NBS-LRR (nucleotide-binding site and leucine-rich repeat, disease resistance, Manihot esculenta)
phenotype: Significant reduction in NBS-LRR gene expression in cassava, weakening resistance to pathogens.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing via LDH-dsRNA bioconjugates.

genes: PpWRKY44 (WRKY transcription factor involved in anthocyanin biosynthesis regulation, Pyrus pyrifolia)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpWRKY44 in Pyrus communis calli and leaves increases anthocyanin accumulation by ~6-fold compared to empty vector controls.
mechanism: PpWRKY44 activates the PpMYB10 promoter, which upregulates anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway genes (PcCHI, PcCHS, PcF3H, PcUFGT, PcANS, PcDFR).

genes: PpWRKY44 (WRKY transcription factor involved in anthocyanin biosynthesis regulation, Pyrus pyrifolia)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of PpWRKY44 in Pyrus pyrifolia fruit and leaves increases anthocyanin accumulation by ~6-fold compared to empty vector controls.
mechanism: PpWRKY44 activates the PpMYB10 promoter, which upregulates anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway genes (PpCHS, PpF3H, PpDFR, PpUFGT).

genes: PpWRKY44 (WRKY transcription factor involved in anthocyanin biosynthesis regulation, Pyrus pyrifolia)
phenotype: Transient silencing of PpWRKY44 in Pyrus pyrifolia fruit reduces anthocyanin accumulation by ~60% compared to empty vector controls.
mechanism: PpWRKY44 silencing suppresses PpMYB10 expression, leading to downregulation of anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway genes (PpCHS, PpF3H, PpDFR, PpUFGT).

genes: RFO1 (RFO1, plasma membrane-localized receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), RFO1Ty-0 (RFO1Ty-0, plasma membrane-localized receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), RFO1chim (RFO1chim, chimeric RFO1 protein with Col-0 ectodomain and Ty-0 cytosolic domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of rfo1-1 mutant restored resistance to F. oxysporum to wild-type levels (Figure 1D), restored EGCG-induced root growth inhibition (Figure 2B), and restored PMEIox-induced phenotypes (Figure 2D). The chimera construct (RFO1chim-GFP) also restored resistance to F. oxysporum (Figure 3A) and EGCG sensitivity (Figure 3C).
mechanism: RFO1 binds demethylated pectin (dmPectin) in vitro, senses pectin methylation changes at the cell wall, and activates MAPK3/6 signaling to regulate defense gene expression (Figure 5B). The extracellular domain of RFO1Col-0 is sufficient for these functions (Figure 3).

genes: RFO1 (RFO1, plasma membrane-localized receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RFP-N7 expression was observed in root epidermal cells, with enhanced nuclear-localized RFP signal in roots exposed to F. oxysporum5176 pSIX1::GFP (Supplemental Figure 1C and 1D).
mechanism: NA

genes: CaOMP24 (Capsicum annuum OMP24, outer membrane protein 24, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Silencing of CaOMP24 in pepper facilitates PMMoV infection, with increased viral symptoms and higher PMMoV CP accumulation.
mechanism: CaOMP24 interacts with PMMoV CP and its silencing reduces antiviral defense, allowing enhanced viral replication and spread.

genes: NbOMP24.1 (Nicotiana benthamiana OMP24.1, outer membrane protein 24.1, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbOMP24.2 (Nicotiana benthamiana OMP24.2, outer membrane protein 24.2, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Silencing of NbOMP24s in N. benthamiana facilitates PMMoV infection, with increased viral foci, faster systemic infection, and higher PMMoV CP accumulation.
mechanism: NbOMP24s interact with PMMoV CP and their silencing reduces antiviral defense, allowing enhanced viral replication and spread.

genes: NbOMP24 (Nicotiana benthamiana OMP24, outer membrane protein 24, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Silencing of NbOMP24 via hairpin RNA in N. benthamiana facilitates PMMoV infection, with increased viral foci and higher PMMoV CP accumulation.
mechanism: NbOMP24 interacts with PMMoV CP and its silencing reduces antiviral defense, allowing enhanced viral replication and spread.

genes: NbOMP24.1 (Nicotiana benthamiana OMP24.1, outer membrane protein 24.1, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of NbOMP24.1 in transgenic N. benthamiana enhances resistance to PMMoV, with reduced viral foci and lower PMMoV CP accumulation.
mechanism: NbOMP24.1 induces perinuclear chloroplast clustering (PCC), stromules, and ROS accumulation, which activate antiviral defense pathways.

genes: ELF3 (ELF3, EARLY FLOWERING 3, Brachypodium distachyon)
phenotype: Overexpression of ELF3 in the elf3 mutant background results in delayed flowering and lower PPD1, FT1, and VRN1 expression levels in Brachypodium distachyon.
mechanism: ELF3 acts as a broad repressor of CCT domain-containing genes, reducing FT1 and VRN1 expression which are key flowering activators.

genes: ELF3 (EARLY FLOWERING 3, Triticum monococcum, synthetic)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of ELF3 under the maize UBIQUITIN promoter (UBI::ELF3-HA) in wheat leads to downregulation of PPD1 and FT1 and delayed heading, including in plants carrying the elf3 mutation.
mechanism: ELF3 acts as a transcriptional repressor of PPD1 by direct binding to its promoter. The UBI::ELF3-HA transgene can complement the elf3 mutant phenotype.

genes: HsSNARE1 (HsSNARE1, t-SNARE domain-containing effector in beet cyst nematode, Heterodera schachtii), HgSNARE1 (HgSNARE1, t-SNARE domain-containing effector in soybean cyst nematode, Heterodera glycines), HsSNARE1-M1 (HsSNARE1-M1, mutant of HsSNARE1 with E141D, A143T, and -148S mutations, Heterodera schachtii)
phenotype: Expression of HsSNARE1 significantly enhanced BCN susceptibility of Arabidopsis, while expression of HgSNARE1 and HsSNARE1-M1 remarkably suppressed BCN susceptibility.
mechanism: HsSNARE1 interacts with AtSNAP2 and AtPR1 via its t-SNARE domain and N-terminal, respectively, and suppresses AtSHMT4 and AtPR1 expression. HgSNARE1/HsSNARE1-M1 cannot interact with AtPR1 but bind AtSNAP2, inducing AtSHMT4 and AtPR1.

genes: AtPR1 (AtPR1, pathogenesis-related protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtPR1 significantly suppressed BCN susceptibility of Arabidopsis.
mechanism: AtPR1 stimulates expression of AtSHMT4 and AtNPR1, enhancing resistance to BCN.

genes: MSL (male-specific gene, Populus deltoides)
phenotype: Overexpression of the forward strand of MSL in Arabidopsis promotes maleness, leading to stamen abnormalities such as six to nine stamens, branched stamens, or stamens with multiple anthers.
mechanism: MSL functions as a maleness promoter by modulating androecium development.

genes: MSL (male-specific gene, Populus deltoides)
phenotype: Overexpression of the reverse strand of MSL in Arabidopsis exhibits the same phenotypic changes in the flower sexual organs as the forward strand, including stamen abnormalities.
mechanism: MSL functions as a maleness promoter by modulating androecium development.

genes: MSL-1 (partial sequence of MSL, Populus deltoides)
phenotype: Overexpression of MSL-1 in Arabidopsis leads to stamen abnormalities such as seven to nine stamens, branched stamens, or stamens with multiple anthers.
mechanism: MSL-1 functions as a maleness promoter by modulating androecium development.

genes: MSL-2 (partial sequence of MSL, Populus deltoides)
phenotype: Overexpression of MSL-2 in Arabidopsis leads to stamen abnormalities such as seven to nine stamens, branched stamens, or stamens with multiple anthers.
mechanism: MSL-2 functions as a maleness promoter by modulating androecium development.

genes: MSL-3 (partial sequence of MSL, Populus deltoides)
phenotype: Overexpression of MSL-3 in Arabidopsis leads to stamen abnormalities such as seven to nine stamens, branched stamens, or stamens with multiple anthers.
mechanism: MSL-3 functions as a maleness promoter by modulating androecium development.

genes: MSL (male-specific gene, Populus deltoides)
phenotype: Overexpression of MSL in Arabidopsis using internal cis-acting elements leads to stamen abnormalities similar to those observed with the CaMV35S promoter.
mechanism: Transcription of MSL is activated by internal cis-acting elements, promoting maleness.

genes: AGO2a (AGO2a, AGO2 gene, Solanum lycopersicum), AGO2b (AGO2b, AGO2 gene, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: ago2a, ago2b, and ago2ab knockout mutants show increased viral accumulation (CMV-Fny and CMV-Δ2b) by ~56-115% compared to wild-type tomato.
mechanism: AGO2a and AGO2b are involved in antiviral RNAi; AGO2a restricts viral accumulation, while AGO2b does not function in antiviral immunity.

genes: AGO2a (AGO2a, AGO2 gene, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: ago2a knockout mutants show increased viral accumulation (CMV-Fny and CMV-Δ2b) by ~56-75% compared to wild-type tomato.
mechanism: AGO2a restricts viral accumulation through antiviral RNAi.

genes: AGO2b (AGO2b, AGO2 gene, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: ago2b knockout mutants do not show significant changes in viral accumulation (CMV-Fny and CMV-Δ2b) compared to wild-type tomato.
mechanism: AGO2b does not function in antiviral immunity in tomato.

genes: PelncRNA1 (PelncRNA1, long intergenic non-coding RNA, Phyllostachys edulis)
phenotype: Overexpression of PelncRNA1 increases UV-B stress tolerance in Phyllostachys edulis protoplasts
mechanism: PelncRNA1 regulates the expression of homologous target genes involved in UV-B stress response

genes: PelncRNA1 (PelncRNA1, long intergenic non-coding RNA, Phyllostachys edulis)
phenotype: Overexpression of PelncRNA1 increases UV-B stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: PelncRNA1 regulates the expression of homologous target genes involved in UV-B stress response

genes: TOR (amiRNA targeting TOR gene, synthetic)
phenotype: TOR knockdown reduces lateral root formation and promotes adventitious root formation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: TOR regulates translation of auxin-responsive transcription factors (ARF19, LBD16) and inhibits WOX11 expression, which is required for lateral root initiation.

genes: RAPTOR1B (RAPTOR1B, regulatory-associated protein of TOR, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: RAPTOR1B promoter-driven GUS::eGFP expression marks TOR complex activity in the stele, pericycle, and lateral root primordia of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: RAPTOR1B is a subunit of the TOR complex, which is activated during lateral root initiation.

genes: COMT (Caffeic acid O-methyl transferase, SORBI_3007G047300, Sorghum bicolor)
phenotype: Downregulation of COMT reduces lignin content and improves forage quality in sudangrass with 10% editing efficiency
mechanism: COMT is a key enzyme in lignin biosynthesis; its downregulation reduces lignin content, enhancing biomass digestibility and saccharification efficiency

genes: MeChlD (magnesium chelatase subunit D, cassava)
phenotype: VIGS-induced silencing of MeChlD results in significantly decreased chlorophyll content, reduced expression of photosynthesis-related nuclear genes, and reduced storage root numbers, fresh weight, and total starch content in cassava storage roots
mechanism: MeChlD located at the chloroplast is required for chlorophyll biosynthesis and affects starch accumulation in cassava

genes: GNAT1 (acetyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana), GNAT2 (acetyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana), GNAT4 (acetyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana), GNAT7 (acetyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana), GNAT10 (acetyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knockout of GNAT1, GNAT2, GNAT4, GNAT7, and GNAT10 leads to significant changes in metabolome (111 compounds altered), including reduced ascorbate, oxylipins, and altered lipid profiles. gnat2 shows light-dependent growth retardation and altered photosynthetic parameters (Y(NO), NPQ). gnat7 exhibits reduced N-acetylproline and increased sinapine/sulforaphane. gnat10 shows increased amino acids, peptides, and nucleosides.
mechanism: GNAT enzymes regulate acetylation of proteins and metabolites, affecting photosynthesis, lipid metabolism, and stress responses. Altered acetylation impacts thylakoid protein organization (e.g., PSI–LHCII complex in gnat2), Rubisco/RCA recruitment to thylakoids, and phosphorylation of LHCII/PSII proteins.

genes: CsBPC2 (BPC transcription factor, cucumber gene, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: Csbpc2 mutants exhibit hypersensitivity to salt stress with reduced biomass, increased membrane damage (MDA and EL), impaired osmolyte accumulation, reduced antioxidant enzyme activity, and disrupted ion homeostasis compared to wild-type cucumber plants.
mechanism: CsBPC2 regulates ABA synthesis and signaling, osmolyte biosynthesis, ROS scavenging, and ion homeostasis (Na+/K+ balance and H+-ATPase activity) under salt stress conditions.

genes: LTP1 (LTP1, LTP gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), LTP2 (LTP2, LTP gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ltp1 ltp2 double knock-down seedlings show hypocotyl lengths, hypocotyl/root ratios, and cuticle integrity similar to wild-type Col-0 seedlings
mechanism: Upregulation of LTP1 in dark-grown ltp2 seedlings contributes to phenotypic variation; simultaneous knockdown of LTP1 and LTP2 restores wild-type-like hypocotyl development

genes: PcWRI1 (PcWRI1, transcription factor, P. chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of PcWRI1 increases seed oil content and monounsaturated FA level in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PcWRI1 upregulates genes relevant for carbon flux allocation (plastidic glycolysis and acetyl-CoA generation), FA synthesis, TAG assembly and oil storage.

genes: PcLEC1 (PcLEC1, transcription factor, P. chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of PcLEC1 increases seed oil content and monounsaturated FA level in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PcLEC1 upregulates genes relevant for carbon flux allocation (plastidic glycolysis and acetyl-CoA generation), FA synthesis, TAG assembly and oil storage.

genes: LsRGL1 (LsRGL1, negative regulator of bolting, Lactuca sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of LsRGL1 reduces plant weight, height, leaf length, and stem length in Lactuca sativa compared to wild-type and RNAi plants.
mechanism: LsRGL1 acts as a negative regulator of bolting by inhibiting stem elongation and growth.

genes: LsRGL1 (LsRGL1, negative regulator of bolting, Lactuca sativa)
phenotype: RNAi-LsRGL1 plants exhibit increased plant weight, height, leaf length, and stem length compared to wild-type and overexpression plants.
mechanism: LsRGL1 inhibition promotes bolting by enhancing stem elongation and growth.

genes: LsWRKY70 (LsWRKY70, regulator of bolting and nutritional quality, Lactuca sativa)
phenotype: TRV2-LsWRKY70 silencing delays bolting and improves nutritional quality in Lactuca sativa by reducing soluble sugar, vitamin C, and malondialdehyde content while increasing cellulose content.
mechanism: LsWRKY70 silencing modulates ABA and GA pathways, enhancing stress tolerance and altering phytohormone levels to delay bolting.

genes: Wox3a (Wox3a, homeodomain gene, Zea mays), Wox3b (Wox3b, homeodomain gene, Zea mays)
phenotype: wox3a;wox3b double mutants showed no phenotypic differences from their WT siblings; triple mutant ns1;ns2;wox3a plants had narrower leaves, reduced plant height, and increased leaf curling/twisting
mechanism: Wox3a/b function in the lateral rim domain, and their loss leads to deletion of the lateral leaf domain, affecting mediolateral outgrowth

genes: KNL2 (KNL2, centromere licensing factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Haploid induction when used as female parent
mechanism: The point mutation abolishes centromeric localization of KNL2, leading to haploid induction

genes: KNL2 (KNL2 (W-R mutation), centromere licensing factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Haploid induction when used as female parent
mechanism: The point mutation abolishes centromeric localization of KNL2, leading to haploid induction

genes: StSP3D (FLOWERING LOCUS T-Like 3, potato, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Overexpression of StSP3D induces tuber formation under non-inductive long-day (LD) conditions in potato E109 plants, with 1-4 mature tubers formed after 10 weeks under LDs.
mechanism: StSP3D acts as a graft-transmissible tuber-inducing signal, promoting stolon-to-tuber transition by upregulating StMADS1 and secondary activation of StSP5G and StSP6A in swelling stolons.

genes: StFTL1 (FLOWERING LOCUS T-Like 1, potato, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Overexpression of StFTL1 promotes tuber formation under non-inductive LD conditions in potato E109 plants, with tuberization observed in graft combinations regardless of scion/rootstock position.
mechanism: StFTL1 functions as a graft-transmissible tuber-inducing signal, upregulating StSP5G and StSP6A in swelling stolons and inducing StMADS1 expression in leaves.

genes: SNE (SNE, GA-related F-box protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SNE rescues the delayed germination and hypocotyl elongation defects in the hop1 hop2 hop3 mutant.
mechanism: SNE accumulation is essential for GA signaling, leading to reduced RGA protein levels.

genes: RGA (RGA, DELLA protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of GFP-RGA leads to increased RGA protein levels in the hop2-1 mutant.
mechanism: RGA accumulation is regulated by SNE, and reduced SNE levels in hop mutants lead to increased RGA.

genes: SmNPR4 (Salvianolic acid receptor, Salvia miltiorrhiza)
phenotype: Overexpression of SmNPR4 reduces salvianolic acid B content to 46-56% of control levels and decreases total phenolic acid content in Salvia miltiorrhiza.
mechanism: SmNPR4 negatively regulates phenolic acid biosynthesis by repressing key enzyme gene expression (SmPAL1, SmTAT1, etc.) and inhibiting SA-induced accumulation.

genes: SmTGA5 (bZIP transcription factor, Salvia miltiorrhiza)
phenotype: Overexpression of SmTGA5 increases salvianolic acid B content to 33.36-35.98 mg/g dry weight and elevates total phenolic acid content in Salvia miltiorrhiza.
mechanism: SmTGA5 directly activates SmTAT1 gene expression via binding to as-1 elements in its promoter, enhancing phenolic acid biosynthesis.

genes: AtCBBYA (AtCBBYA, AtCBBYA gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the atcbbyab mutation restores wild-type growth and photosynthetic parameters.
mechanism: AtCbbYA and AtCbbYB are required for efficient photosynthetic electron transport and CO2 assimilation.

genes: AtCBBYB (AtCBBYB, AtCBBYB gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the atcbbyab mutation restores wild-type growth and photosynthetic parameters.
mechanism: AtCbbYA and AtCbbYB are required for efficient photosynthetic electron transport and CO2 assimilation.

genes: RscbbY (RscbbY, XuBP phosphatase, Rhodobacter sphaeroides)
phenotype: Complementation of the mutant photosynthetic phenotype, restoring wild-type-like Y(II) and Y(NPQ).
mechanism: RsCbbY can substitute for AtCbbYA and AtCbbYB in dephosphorylating XuBP.

genes: OsNPR1 (non-specific pathogen resistance 1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of OsNPR1 increases susceptibility to RSV infection in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsNPR1 is essential for SA-mediated activation of JA signaling and antiviral immunity.

genes: AtWRI1 (full-length, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased fatty acid and TAG levels in vegetative and reproductive tissues of Indica rice, with 20% higher bio-methane production from rice straw compared to wild type.
mechanism: NA

mechanism: PsERF1B interacts with PsMYB10.1 to form a PsERF1B-PsMYB10.1-PsbHLH3 module that synergistically activates the PsUFGT promoter, accelerating anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: PYL1 (PYL1 H87P A190V E141D), ABI1aid (ABI1 49 aa truncation), edCitrineT9, T7edCerulean

mechanism: PYL1 E141D mutation increases ABA affinity and enhances FRET signal by altering PYL1-ABI1aid interaction dynamics. Shortened and rigidified linkers between sensory domain and FRET pair contribute to improved affinity and ratio change.

genes: PYL1 (PYL1 H87P A190V R143S), ABI1aid (ABI1 49 aa truncation), edCitrineT9, T7edCerulean

genes: HOS15 (HOS15, histone deacetylase complex subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RNAi line (hos15-i) of HOS15 is insensitive to low ambient temperature–mediated repression of flowering with a flowering time ratio (16°C/23°C) of ~1.2–1.3 compared to wild-type.
mechanism: HOS15 repression of flowering is mediated through post-translational regulation of GI protein abundance via 26S proteasome activity.

genes: GI (GI, photoperiodic flowering activator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of gi-2 and hos15-2 mutants with 35S:GI-HA restores GI protein levels and flowering time regulation under low ambient temperature.
mechanism: HOS15-mediated 26S proteasome activity degrades GI protein at low ambient temperature, and GI stabilization in hos15-2 mutants is insensitive to proteasome inhibitors.

genes: COP1 (COP1, E3 ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of COP1-GFP in cop1-4 mutants restores COP1 protein levels and interacts with HOS15 at 23°C but not at 16°C.
mechanism: HOS15 and COP1 form a complex in the nucleus to regulate GI degradation, with HOS15 acting independently of COP1 at low ambient temperature.

genes: SiAT1 (salidroside hydroxycinnamoyltransferase, S. indicum), RgUGT79G15 (osmanthuside B 1,4-rhamnosyltransferase, Rehmannia glutinosa), SiCYP98A20 (osmanthuside B hydroxylase, S. indicum)

genes: B1 (TraesCS5A02G542800, C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factor, wheat)
phenotype: Overexpression of B1-Hap1 significantly reduces awn length in wheat, while overexpression of B1-Hap7 (with amino acid substitutions) does not affect awn length.
mechanism: B1 inhibits awn elongation by repressing downstream genes TaRAE2 and TaLks2. Loss of EAR motif in B1-Hap7 weakens its repression activity.

genes: B1 (TraesCS5A02G542800, C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factor, wheat)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated knockout of B1 in awnletted wheat accessions (CAU157 and CAU183) results in significantly longer awn lengths compared to control lines.
mechanism: B1 knockout removes its repression on TaRAE2 and TaLks2, leading to increased cell division and awn elongation.

genes: B1 (TraesCS5A02G542800, C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factor, wheat)
phenotype: B1-GFP fusion protein localizes exclusively to the nuclei of Nicotiana benthamiana leaf epidermal cells and wheat protoplasts.
mechanism: B1 is a nuclear-localized transcription factor with two EAR repression domains.

genes: B1 (TraesCS5A02G542800, C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factor, wheat)
phenotype: B1 haplotypes repress firefly luciferase (LUC) activity in transient assays, with B1-Hap1 showing stronger repression than B1-Hap7.
mechanism: B1 acts as a transcriptional repressor via its EAR motifs. Loss of the second EAR motif in B1-Hap7 weakens repression.

genes: TaRAE2 (TraesCS5A02G542800 downstream target, wheat)---TaLks2 (TraesCS5A02G542800 downstream target, wheat)
phenotype: B1 represses TaRAE2 and TaLks2 expression, which are positive regulators of awn elongation. EMSA confirms B1 binds to their promoters.
mechanism: B1 directly represses TaRAE2 and TaLks2 by binding to their promoters, inhibiting cell division and awn elongation.

genes: TaTCP4 (bHLH transcription factor, wheat)---TaTCP10 (bHLH transcription factor, wheat)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated knockout of TaTCP4 leads to shorter awn lengths in wheat, indicating TaTCP4 positively regulates awn elongation.
mechanism: TaTCP4 and TaTCP10 synergistically repress B1 expression by binding to its promoter. Knockout of TaTCP4 reduces B1 repression, indirectly affecting awn elongation.

mechanism: NA

genes: CqFTL2-1 (CqFTL2-1, floral activator, Chenopodium quinoa)

mechanism: MdMAPK3 silencing prevents phosphorylation of MdNAC72, reducing its ubiquitination and degradation by MdPUB24, which maintains repression of MdPG1 transcription.

genes: MdPUB24 (ubiquitin-protein ligase PUB24, Malus domestica, synthetic)

mechanism: MdPUB24 silencing prevents ubiquitination and degradation of MdNAC72, maintaining its repression of MdPG1 transcription.

genes: MdNAC72 (NAC domain-containing protein 72, Malus domestica, synthetic)

mechanism: MdNAC72 silencing derepresses MdPG1 transcription, promoting cell wall degradation.
