genes: OsAAI1 (Amino Acid Sequence, Oryza sativa L., NCBI), GFP (Green Fluorescent Protein, synthetic)
phenotype: OsAAI1-GFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus in rice protoplasts, unlike free GFP which is distributed throughout the cell.
mechanism: OsAAI1 subcellular localization in the nucleus suggests potential nuclear functions in rice.

genes: CCaMK (calcium- and calmodulin-dependent protein kinase, Nicotiana attenuata)
phenotype: The irCCaMK line does not show any internal colonization structures by AM fungal, but exhibits a highly similar vegetative growth when compared to WT plants in absence of AM fungi.
mechanism: NA

genes: pSOL3NC (selectable marker)
phenotype: The EV line has been shown to be equivalent to the WT in growth and other traits over several years of field studies.
mechanism: NA

genes: FvePL1 (FvePL1, RNAi target gene, Fragaria vesca)
phenotype: Reduced leaf size, altered petal architectures, disrupted normal pollen development, and rendered partial male sterility
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing

genes: AS2 (ASYMMETRIC LEAVES 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of AS2 on both inner and outer epidermis of the WT leads to lumps and outgrowths on the sepal outer epidermis, similar to as2–7D.
mechanism: Ectopic AS2 expression disrupts growth patterns and tissue properties, leading to buckling.

genes: REV (REVOLUTA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of REV in WT sepals is insufficient to generate buckles or outgrowths.
mechanism: REV overexpression does not disrupt growth patterns or tissue properties to cause buckling.

genes: AS2 (ASYMMETRIC LEAVES 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The mutant AS2 promoter drives GFP on both the inner and outer epidermal layers, confirming ectopic AS2 expression in as2–7D.
mechanism: The mutation in the AS2 promoter disrupts the binding site of the repressor KANADI, leading to ectopic AS2 expression on the abaxial side.

genes: REV (REVOLUTA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic REV expression in as2–7D does not enhance the phenotype.
mechanism: REV expression does not disrupt growth patterns or tissue properties to cause buckling in as2–7D.

genes: FIL (FILAMENTOUS FLOWER, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: No ectopic juxtaposition between inner and outer gene expression was formed in the as2–7D sepal surface.
mechanism: FIL expression patterns are not disrupted in as2–7D, indicating no inner-outer polarity disruption.

genes: KRP1 (Kip-related protein 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpressing KRP1 in as2–7D results in a striking smoothing of the outer sepal epidermis.
mechanism: Increased giant cell formation restores directional growth and increases outer epidermal stiffness, preventing buckling.

genes: CHE (CCA1 HIKING EXPEDITION, circadian clock transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of che-2 mutant rescues systemic acquired resistance (SAR) deficiency, restoring SA and Pip production in systemic tissues.
mechanism: CHE binds to ICS1 promoter via sulfenylation at cysteine 51, enhancing systemic SA synthesis independent of circadian clock function.

genes: cheCS (cysteine 51→serine mutant of CHE, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: cheCS mutant fails to rescue SAR deficiency in che-2 mutant, showing compromised systemic ICS1, PR1, ALD1, and FMO1 induction and reduced SA/Pip production.
mechanism: Cysteine-to-serine mutation prevents sulfenylation, impairing CHE binding to ICS1 promoter and systemic SA synthesis.

genes: cheCW (cysteine 51→tryptophan mutant of CHE, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: cheCW mutant fails to rescue SAR deficiency in che-2 mutant, showing compromised systemic ICS1, PR1, ALD1, and FMO1 induction and reduced SA/Pip production.
mechanism: Cysteine-to-tryptophan mutation prevents sulfenylation, impairing CHE binding to ICS1 promoter and systemic SA synthesis.

genes: GbHY5 (GbHY5, Ginkgo biloba), GFP (GFP)
phenotype: Overexpression of GbHY5 increases total flavonoid content by 1.5–1.75 times in ginkgo calli and Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GbHY5 promotes flavonoid accumulation by activating genes in the flavonoid biosynthesis pathway.

genes: GbMYB1 (GbMYB1, Ginkgo biloba), GFP (GFP)
phenotype: Overexpression of GbMYB1 increases total flavonoid content by 1.42–1.51 times in ginkgo calli and Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GbMYB1 promotes flavonoid accumulation by activating genes in the flavonoid biosynthesis pathway.

genes: BraPDS (BraPDS, key enzyme in carotenoid production, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Knockout of BraPDS leads to albino phenotype with 72.72% efficiency.
mechanism: Disruption of BraPDS causes frameshift mutations leading to non-functional protein.

genes: BraRGL1 (BraRGL1, crucial for bolting and flowering, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Knockout of BraRGL1 accelerates flower bud differentiation and bolting.
mechanism: Mutation in BraRGL1 leads to increased sensitivity to GA signaling.

genes: BraRGL1 (BraRGL1, crucial for bolting and flowering, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Overexpression of BraRGL1 delays bolting and flowering.
mechanism: BraRGL1 negatively regulates bolting and flowering-related genes.

genes: LDC (Lupin dihydropiperideine synthase, from white lupin), CAO (Cycloartenol synthase, from white lupin)
phenotype: Accumulation of pauper metabolites (QA pathway intermediates) in transiently transformed leaves.
mechanism: Blockage of QA biosynthesis at a step downstream of CAO, leading to accumulation of intermediates.

genes: LDC (Lupin dihydropiperideine synthase, from white lupin), CAO (Cycloartenol synthase, from white lupin), AT (Acetyltransferase, from white lupin accession P27174)
phenotype: Accumulation of ammodendrine (6) and pauper metabolites in transiently transformed leaves.
mechanism: AT catalyzes acetylation of tetrahydroanabasine (5), leading to ammodendrine (6) formation and pathway blockage.

genes: PR1 (pathogenesis-related protein 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, native), eYFP (enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PR1-eYFP leads to cleavage into AtCAPE9-eYFP (~27.0 kDa) and intact PR1-eYFP (~44.7 kDa) in Arabidopsis, with cleavage dependent on aspartate residues in the CNYD motif.
mechanism: PR1 is cleaved by aspartate-specific protease (CNYDase) to release AtCAPE9, which enhances systemic immunity and resistance to Pst DC3000 by regulating SA levels.

genes: PR1 (pathogenesis-related protein 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, D150A mutant), eYFP (enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PR1D150A-eYFP results in reduced cleavage into AtCAPE9-eYFP compared to native PR1-eYFP, indicating the aspartate at position 150 is critical for proteolysis.
mechanism: Mutation of D150 in PR1 disrupts CNYD motif recognition by CNYDase, preventing AtCAPE9 release and impairing systemic immunity.

genes: PR1 (pathogenesis-related protein 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, P151A mutant), eYFP (enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PR1P151A-eYFP results in reduced cleavage into AtCAPE9-eYFP compared to native PR1-eYFP, indicating the aspartate at position 151 is critical for proteolysis.
mechanism: Mutation of P151 in PR1 disrupts CNYD motif recognition by CNYDase, preventing AtCAPE9 release and impairing systemic immunity.

genes: XCP1 (xylem cysteine peptidase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), HisTag (histidine tag, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of XCP1-His in xcp1 mutant restores CNYDase activity and systemic immunity to Pst DC3000, confirming XCP1 as the enzyme responsible for AtCAPE9 production.
mechanism: XCP1 cleaves PR1 at the CNYD motif to release AtCAPE9, which activates SA-mediated systemic immunity through a positive feedback loop.

genes: GT1 (GT1, homeodomain leucine zipper gene, rice)
phenotype: Overexpression of GT1 increases susceptibility to sheath blight (ShB) in rice.
mechanism: GT1 activates SWEET2a and SWEET3a, leading to increased sugar efflux to the apoplast, enhancing R. solani virulence.

genes: GT1 (GT1, homeodomain leucine zipper gene, rice)
phenotype: RNAi of GT1 reduces susceptibility to sheath blight (ShB) in rice.
mechanism: GT1 activates SWEET2a and SWEET3a, leading to increased sugar efflux to the apoplast, enhancing R. solani virulence.

genes: GT1 (GT1, homeodomain leucine zipper gene, rice)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gt1 mutants show reduced susceptibility to sheath blight (ShB) in rice.
mechanism: GT1 activates SWEET2a and SWEET3a, leading to increased sugar efflux to the apoplast, enhancing R. solani virulence.

genes: mIBV-S2P-NDV-FTM/CT (synthetic construct, modified IBV S protein with stabilizing proline residues, synthetic), NDV-Matrix (NDV matrix protein, NDV)
phenotype: Production of IB virus-like particles (VLPs) with 67 ng/µL S protein concentration in PBS-extracted samples
mechanism: Co-expression of modified IBV S protein and NDV matrix protein enables VLP assembly

genes: JAM1 (jasmonate-associated MYC2-like 1, tomato)
phenotype: Overexpression of JAM1
mechanism: NA

genes: ATG8f (autophagy-related 8f, tomato)
phenotype: Expression of GFP-ATG8f for autophagosome detection
mechanism: NA

genes: JAM3 (jasmonate-associated MYC2-like 3, tomato)
phenotype: Silencing of JAM3
mechanism: NA

genes: TfBOP2 (TfBOP2, gene involved in corolla differentiation, Torenia fournieri)
phenotype: TfBOP2 loss-of-function mutants exhibit developmental defects in the proximal corolla region, including ectopic tissues, altered pigmentation, and disrupted corolla tube fusion. Epidermal cell morphologies in the proximal corolla are affected, with ectopic trichomes and altered cell sizes.
mechanism: TfBOP2 controls proximal corolla differentiation by acting on cell expansion and boundary formation. It genetically interacts with TfALOG3 to regulate proximal cell differentiation, with TfALOG3 antagonizing TfBOP2's activity in corolla boundary formation.

genes: PnMYB4 (PnMYB4, R2R3-MYB transcription regulator, Panax notoginseng)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated suppression of PnMYB4 in P. notoginseng calli significantly increased the expression of PnSS, PnDS, and PnSE and the content of Rg1.
mechanism: PnMYB4 negatively regulates saponin biosynthesis by repressing PnSS, PnSE, and PnDS expression.

genes: PnMYB4 (PnMYB4, R2R3-MYB transcription regulator, Panax notoginseng)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis of PnMYB4 in P. notoginseng calli significantly increased the expression of PnSS, PnDS, and PnSE and the contents of Rg1 and Rb1.
mechanism: PnMYB4 negatively regulates saponin biosynthesis by repressing PnSS, PnSE, and PnDS expression.

genes: PnMYB4 (PnMYB4, R2R3-MYB transcription regulator, Panax notoginseng)
phenotype: PnMYB4-GFP fusion protein exclusively accumulated in the nucleus and strictly colocalized with Osghd7:RFP.
mechanism: PnMYB4 is a nuclear-localized protein.

genes: AtFT (FLOWERING LOCUS T, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Heat-inducible overexpression of AtFT induces flowering in male clone 353 (22.4% flowering rate) and female clone 717 (34.1% flowering rate) under controlled heat conditions.
mechanism: Overexpression of AtFT (FLOWERING LOCUS T) promotes early floral induction by activating flowering pathways.

genes: AtFT (FLOWERING LOCUS T, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Constitutive overexpression of AtFT induces flowering in male clone 353 (52.2-83.3% flowering rate in selected LFY events) but not in female clone 717.
mechanism: Overexpression of AtFT (FLOWERING LOCUS T) promotes early floral induction by constitutively activating flowering pathways.

genes: BoNA1 (dihydroflavonol-4-reductase-like protein, structural gene for anthocyanin biosynthesis, Brassica oleracea)
phenotype: Knockout of BoNA1 results in no anthocyanin accumulation in cabbage (Brassica oleracea) plants, with green hypocotyls and leaves instead of purple
mechanism: BoNA1 encodes a dihydroflavonol-4-reductase-like protein essential for anthocyanin biosynthesis; its disruption prevents anthocyanin production

genes: MAC3A (MAC3A, core subunit of MAC complex, Arabidopsis thaliana), MAC3B (MAC3B, core subunit of MAC complex, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MAC3A-GFP in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to co-condensation with CRY2 in light-responsive liquid condensates, promoting hypocotyl elongation under blue light.
mechanism: MAC3A co-condenses with photoexcited CRYs in liquid condensates, competing with HY5 for DNA binding at promoters of target genes like YUC8 and IAA19, thereby attenuating HY5's transcriptional repression and promoting hypocotyl elongation.

genes: MAC3A (MAC3A, core subunit of MAC complex, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MAC3AMut1-GFP in Arabidopsis thaliana rescues the short-hypocotyl phenotype of mac3a3b mutants under blue light.
mechanism: MAC3AMut1, a U-box domain mutant lacking ubiquitin ligase activity, still promotes hypocotyl elongation, indicating that DNA binding activity of MAC3A, not ubiquitin ligase activity, is responsible for the phenotype.

genes: MAC3A (MAC3A, core subunit of MAC complex, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MAC3AMut2-GFP in Arabidopsis thaliana rescues the short-hypocotyl phenotype of mac3a3b mutants under blue light.
mechanism: MAC3AMut2, a U-box domain mutant lacking ubiquitin ligase activity, still promotes hypocotyl elongation, indicating that DNA binding activity of MAC3A, not ubiquitin ligase activity, is responsible for the phenotype.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Detection of 20-nt foreign DNA fragments in genome-edited potatoes using k-mer analysis
mechanism: Agrobacterium-mediated T-DNA integration into potato genome

genes: SSR2 (target gene, synthetic), NPTII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, selectable marker, synthetic)
phenotype: Detection of T-DNA fragments in genome-edited potato line #84 using k-mer analysis
mechanism: Agrobacterium-mediated T-DNA integration into potato genome

genes: NPTII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, selectable marker, synthetic)
phenotype: Detection of 150-bp T-DNA fragment in genome-edited potato line #79 using PCR validation
mechanism: Agrobacterium-mediated partial T-DNA integration into potato genome

genes: unknown (triterpenoid biosynthesis gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Contaminant plasmid DNA detected in genome-edited potato line #117 during NGS analysis
mechanism: Plasmid DNA contamination during genomic DNA extraction

genes: H2B (H2B, histone H2B, Arabidopsis thaliana), sfGFP (sfGFP, superfolder green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: CLE3 (CLE3, CLE gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CLE3 increases gall numbers in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: CLE3 positively regulates gall formation by promoting systemic signaling through CLV1 receptor in shoots

genes: NtCCD4 (carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 4, Nicotiana tabacum), NtCCD4-S (carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 4, Nicotiana sylvestris), NtCCD4-T1 (carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 4, Nicotiana tomentosiformis), NtCCD4-T2 (carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 4, Nicotiana tomentosiformis)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated silencing of NtCCD4 genes results in yellow mature leaves due to accumulation of carotenoids (lutein 1.9–2.4 fold, β-carotene 1.3–1.9 fold, violaxanthin 2.4–3.5 fold, zeaxanthin 1.5–1.6 fold higher than non-transformed plants)
mechanism: Silencing of NtCCD4 genes blocks carotenoid cleavage, leading to accumulation of carotenoids in mature leaves

genes: HIPP27 (HIPP27, nematode-responsive S gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: HIPP27 (HIPP27, nematode-responsive S gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Phenotypic analysis of homozygous, 'transgene-free' T2 plants revealed reduced nematode infection compared to wild-type plants
mechanism: loss of function of HIPP27 by CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutagenesis

genes: FvWRKY50 (FvWRKY50, transcription factor, Fragaria vesca)
phenotype: Mutation of FvWRKY50 leads to dwarf phenotype in diploid strawberry, delayed anthocyanin accumulation in fruit, and early flowering.
mechanism: FvWRKY50 regulates auxin biosynthesis and signaling, leaf senescence by targeting SAUR36, flowering by regulating FT and CO genes, and fruit ripening by regulating anthocyanin accumulation. Under low temperature, FvWRKY50 is phosphorylated by FvMAPK3 and degraded.

genes: FvWRKY50 (FvWRKY50, transcription factor, Fragaria vesca)
phenotype: Overexpression of FvWRKY50 accelerates anthocyanin accumulation in strawberry fruit.
mechanism: FvWRKY50 regulates anthocyanin accumulation by directly targeting FvCHI and FvDFR gene expression.

genes: FvWRKY50 (FvWRKY50, transcription factor, Fragaria vesca)
phenotype: RNAi of FvWRKY50 delays anthocyanin accumulation in strawberry fruit.
mechanism: FvWRKY50 regulates anthocyanin accumulation by directly targeting FvCHI and FvDFR gene expression.

genes: CitFNSII-1 (Citrus flavone synthase II-1, CYP93B26, Citrus clementina), CitFNSII-2 (Citrus flavone synthase II-2, CYP93B27, Citrus clementina)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of CitFNSII-1 in Ponkan fruit peel increased total PMF content by 32% and individual PMF contents.
mechanism: CitFNSII-1 catalyzes flavanone hydroxylation to produce flavones, promoting PMF biosynthesis in citrus.

genes: CitFNSII-1 (Citrus flavone synthase II-1, CYP93B26, Citrus clementina), CitFNSII-2 (Citrus flavone synthase II-2, CYP93B27, Citrus clementina)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of CitFNSII-2 in Ponkan fruit peel increased total PMF content by 53% and individual PMF contents.
mechanism: CitFNSII-2 catalyzes flavanone hydroxylation to produce flavones, promoting PMF biosynthesis in citrus.

genes: CmWRKY6-1 (CmWRKY6-1, WRKY transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmWRKY6–1 increases susceptibility to Fusarium oxysporum in Chrysanthemum morifolium, with higher disease severity index (DSI) compared to wild-type.
mechanism: CmWRKY6–1 negatively regulates resistance to F. oxysporum by inhibiting ROS scavenging and endogenous salicylic acid (SA) synthesis, and directly inhibiting CmWRKY15-like expression.

genes: CmWRKY6-1 (CmWRKY6-1, WRKY transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Expression of CmWRKY6–1 fused with VP64 (FVuv-R4-CmWRKY6–1) in Chrysanthemum morifolium reduces susceptibility to Fusarium oxysporum, with lower disease severity index (DSI) compared to wild-type.
mechanism: CmWRKY6–1 fused with VP64 acts as a transcriptional activator, enhancing resistance by promoting ROS scavenging and SA synthesis, and indirectly upregulating CmWRKY15-like expression.

genes: CmWRKY15-like (CmWRKY15-like, WRKY transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of CmWRKY15-like in Chrysanthemum morifolium increases susceptibility to Fusarium oxysporum, with higher disease severity index (DSI) compared to wild-type.
mechanism: CmWRKY15-like silencing reduces endogenous salicylic acid (SA) levels and impairs ROS scavenging, leading to increased susceptibility to F. oxysporum.

genes: CsBZIP40 (CsBZIP40, transcription factor, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsBZIP40 enhances resistance to citrus bacterial canker (CBC) in sweet orange plants, with CBC lesion sizes reduced to 39.3–40.7% of wild-type (WT) lesions and disease indices reduced by 41.1–52.6%.
mechanism: CsBZIP40 represses antioxidant enzymes (CsPrx52, CsPrx53, CsPrx55, CsSOD13), leading to increased ROS levels and enhanced CBC resistance.

genes: CsWRKY43 (CsWRKY43, WRKY transcription factor, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsWRKY43 increases CBC susceptibility in sweet orange plants, with CBC lesion sizes 1.27–1.50 times larger than WT lesions and disease indices increased by 15.5–25.5%.
mechanism: CsWRKY43 activates antioxidant enzymes (CsPrx53, CsSOD13), reducing ROS levels and CBC resistance.

genes: CsWRKY43 (CsWRKY43, WRKY transcription factor, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: CsWRKY43 silencing enhances CBC resistance in sweet orange plants, with CBC lesion sizes reduced to 64.1–80.1% of WT lesions and disease indices reduced by 22.6–39.4%.
mechanism: CsWRKY43 silencing reduces antioxidant enzyme activity (CsPrx53, CsSOD13), increasing ROS levels and CBC resistance.

genes: CsPrx53 (CsPrx53, peroxidase, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of CsPrx53 increases peroxidase (POD) activity by 1.37-fold and reduces H2O2 levels in Wanjincheng plants.
mechanism: CsPrx53 enhances ROS scavenging, reducing H2O2 levels and CBC susceptibility.

genes: CsSOD13 (CsSOD13, superoxide dismutase, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of CsSOD13 increases superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity by 1.34-fold and reduces O–2 levels in Wanjincheng plants.
mechanism: CsSOD13 enhances ROS scavenging, reducing O–2 levels and CBC susceptibility.

genes: CsPrx53 (CsPrx53, peroxidase, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Silencing of CsPrx53 enhances CBC resistance in Wanjincheng plants, with lesion sizes reduced to 41.1% of control lesions and disease indices reduced by 44.1%.
mechanism: CsPrx53 silencing reduces POD activity and increases H2O2 levels, enhancing CBC resistance.

genes: CsSOD13 (CsSOD13, superoxide dismutase, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Silencing of CsSOD13 enhances CBC resistance in Wanjincheng plants, with lesion sizes reduced to 50.1% of control lesions and disease indices reduced by 56.3%.
mechanism: CsSOD13 silencing reduces SOD activity and increases O–2 levels, enhancing CBC resistance.

genes: PpbZIP44 (EVM0042575, PpbZIP44, Pyrus)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpbZIP44 increases fructose and sorbitol metabolism, leading to higher sugar:acid ratio in pear fruits.
mechanism: PpbZIP44 activates PpSDH9, enhancing SDH activity and fructose accumulation while reducing sorbitol. It also upregulates glycolytic genes (SUS, FRK2, PFP, PFK, FBA) and affects TCA cycle intermediates.

genes: PpbZIP44 (EVM0042575, PpbZIP44, Pyrus)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of PpbZIP44 reduces fructose and increases sorbitol, lowering sugar:acid ratio in pear fruits.
mechanism: PpbZIP44 silencing inhibits PpSDH9, reducing SDH activity and fructose accumulation while increasing sorbitol. It downregulates glycolytic genes and affects TCA cycle intermediates.

genes: PpbZIP44 (EVM0042575, PpbZIP44, Pyrus)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpbZIP44 in tomato fruits increases soluble sugars, amino acids, and flavonoids while decreasing organic acids and proline.
mechanism: PpbZIP44 activates PpSDH9, PpProDH1, PpADT, and PpF3H, enhancing fructose and phenylalanine accumulation. It upregulates glycolytic and TCA cycle genes and affects secondary metabolism pathways.

genes: SlHAKAI (SlHAKAI, full-length, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlHAKAI increases resistance to PepMV by reducing viral RNA and coat protein accumulation in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: SlHAKAI enhances antiviral defense through m6A modification of viral RNA, which reduces viral accumulation.

genes: SlHAKAI (SlHAKAI, full-length, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of SlHAKAI increases susceptibility to PepMV by increasing viral RNA and coat protein accumulation in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: SlHAKAI knockout reduces m6A modification of viral RNA, which increases viral accumulation.

genes: NbATG7 (ATG7, autophagy-related, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbBeclin1 (Beclin1, autophagy-related, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Knockdown of NbATG7 and NbBeclin1 inhibits autophagy-mediated degradation of SlHAKAI, reducing PepMV accumulation in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: Autophagy inhibition via NbATG7 and NbBeclin1 knockdown prevents SlHAKAI degradation, enhancing antiviral defense.

genes: SlHAKAI (SlHAKAI, full-length, Solanum lycopersicum), RdRP (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, PepMV)
phenotype: Co-expression of SlHAKAI-YFP and RdRP in Nicotiana benthamiana leads to autophagic degradation of SlHAKAI, reducing its protein accumulation.
mechanism: RdRP interacts with SlHAKAI and promotes its degradation via autophagy, mediated by SlBeclin1.

genes: NLE (nucleolar localization gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AtNLE-GFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus in Arabidopsis root cells
mechanism: NLE contains a bipartite nuclear localization signal and interacts with AtMDN1 via its UBL domain to participate in ribosome biogenesis

genes: Chit1 (endochitinase, Trichoderma longibrachiatum)
phenotype: Transgenic cotton plants expressing Chit1 show increased chitinase activity (5.64 U/mL) and higher mortality of A. gossypii nymphs (38.75% after 144h) and adults (21.67% after 144h).
mechanism: Chitinase activity targets the insect's chitin, leading to increased mortality.

genes: Exo84c (Exo84c, exocyst complex subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of exo84c mutant phenotype by Exo84cp::Exo84c:GFP construct restores wild-type stigmatic papilla cell senescence and seed set.
mechanism: Exo84c promotes the formation of ER-membrane-derived punctae and regulates stigmatic senescence through autophagy.

genes: Exo84c (Exo84c, exocyst complex subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of Exo84c in Arabidopsis thaliana reduces the ratio of live papilla cells by ~40% at 72 HAE compared to wild type.
mechanism: Exo84c overexpression accelerates stigmatic senescence and reduces seed set by promoting autophagy-mediated degradation of exocyst complexes.

genes: Exo84a (Exo84a, exocyst complex subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana), Exo84b (Exo84b, exocyst complex subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of Exo84a or Exo84b in exo84c mutant background does not complement the delayed stigmatic senescence phenotype.
mechanism: Exo84a and Exo84b cannot replace Exo84c in regulating stigmatic senescence, indicating isoform-specific function.

genes: Sec6 (Sec6, exocyst complex subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of Sec6 in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to increased vacuole accumulation of Sec6:GFP puncta during stigma senescence.
mechanism: Sec6 overexpression enhances autophagy-mediated degradation of exocyst complexes, regulated by Exo84c and VAP27.

mechanism: Cox2 promoter directs mitochondrial-specific expression of GFP

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)

genes: Renilla luciferase (RLuc, reporter gene, synthetic)

genes: Renilla luciferase (RLuc, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: RLuc expression in plant nucleus as a quantitative measure of transfection efficiency
mechanism: 35S promoter directs nuclear expression of RLuc

genes: Fib2 (Fibrillarin 2, redox sensor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of Fib2-roGFP2 allows monitoring of nucleolar/nuclear redox state in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Fib2-roGFP2 is a redox sensor where GRX1-roGFP2 is targeted to the nucleolus via the Fib2 GAR domain, enabling redox state measurement through 405/488 nm fluorescence ratio

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity detected in seed coat, endosperm, micropylar endosperm, young embryo, ovules, developing roots, leaf petioles and leaf tips at 4-7 DAP
mechanism: PMEI14 promoter drives expression of GUS and GFP fusion protein in seed coat and other tissues

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Strongest GUS expression in seed coat palisade cell layer of wild-type seeds, reduced in gl2 mutant seeds and absent in ttg2 mutant seeds
mechanism: PAE1 promoter drives GUS expression in seed coat palisade cells regulated by GL2 and TTG2

genes: Cas13d (CRISPR/Cas13d system, Ruminococcus flavefaciens XPD3002), gRNA1 (targeting CP gene of PVS), gRNA2 (targeting CP gene of PVX), gRNA3 (targeting CP gene of PLRV), gRNA4 (targeting CP gene of PVY)
phenotype: Transgenic potato plants expressing Cas13d/PTG exhibit resistance to four RNA viruses (PLRV, PVY, PVS, PVX) individually and in mixed infections, with reduced viral accumulation and no disease symptoms.
mechanism: The Cas13d/PTG system produces four gRNAs targeting viral CP genes, enabling CRISPR/Cas13d to cleave viral RNA and confer resistance.

genes: DMC1 (DMC1, DNA repair protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: DMC1-FLAG transgenic plants show ubiquitination of DMC1 in vivo, with smeared bands indicating poly-ubiquitination
mechanism: DMC1 is ubiquitinated by SCFRMF1/2 complex and degraded via 26S proteasome

genes: PtoWRKY68 (PtoWRKY68hap1, Populus tomentosa, synthetic), PtoWRKY68 (PtoWRKY68hap2, Populus tomentosa, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtoWRKY68hap1 in Arabidopsis increases drought tolerance by reducing stomatal conductance (Gs) by 43.87%, transpiration rate (Tr) by 15.16%, and enhancing water-use efficiency (WUE) by 26.62%, ABA levels by 42.7%, and proline (PRO) by 18.33% under drought stress. PtoWRKY68hap2 overexpression also increases drought tolerance but with less pronounced effects compared to PtoWRKY68hap1.
mechanism: PtoWRKY68hap1 enhances drought tolerance by activating PtoABF2.1 and PtoRD26.1 while repressing PtoDTX49.1, modulating ABA signaling and efflux. PtoWRKY68hap2 has lower binding affinity to these targets, resulting in reduced drought tolerance. ABA signaling and stomatal closure are amplified in PtoWRKY68hap1 overexpressors.

genes: PtoWRKY68 (PtoWRKY68hap2, Populus tomentosa, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtoWRKY68hap2 in Arabidopsis increases drought tolerance compared to wild-type but shows enhanced wilting compared to PtoWRKY68hap1 overexpressors. Transgenic plants have lower WUE, ABA, and PRO values than PtoWRKY68hap1 overexpressors under drought stress.
mechanism: PtoWRKY68hap2 has reduced binding affinity to PtoABF2.1, PtoRD26.1, and PtoDTX49.1 compared to PtoWRKY68hap1, leading to less effective activation of ABA signaling and efflux regulation. This results in lower drought tolerance than PtoWRKY68hap1 overexpressors.

mechanism: Virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) mediated by CGMMV-based vector pV190 reduces PDS and TEN expression levels.

genes: CmoNCED6 (9-cis-epoxycarotenoid dioxygenase, ABA biosynthesis, pumpkin rootstock)

mechanism: CmoNCED6 regulates ABA synthesis and stomatal closure, and K+/Na+ homeostasis by binding to promoters of CmoRBOHD1 and CmoNCED6, and K+/Na+ transporters CmoAKT1;2 and CmoHKT1;1.

genes: CmoNCED6 (9-cis-epoxycarotenoid dioxygenase, ABA biosynthesis, pumpkin rootstock)
phenotype: CmoNCED6 overexpression in pumpkin rootstocks increased salt tolerance of grafted cucumbers, with 22.8% and 23.8% increases in shoot and root dry weight, respectively, under salt stress.
mechanism: CmoNCED6 regulates ABA synthesis and stomatal closure, and K+/Na+ homeostasis by binding to promoters of CmoRBOHD1 and CmoNCED6, and K+/Na+ transporters CmoAKT1;2 and CmoHKT1;1.

genes: NnbZIP36 (NnbZIP36, transcription factor, Nelumbo nucifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of NnbZIP36 promotes anthocyanin accumulation by upregulating 4CL, CHI, CHS, F3H, F3'H, DFR, ANS and UF3GT in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NnbZIP36 upregulates genes related to anthocyanin synthesis (4CL, CHI, CHS, F3H, F3'H, DFR, ANS and UF3GT)

genes: E-Luc (E-Luc, green-emitting luciferase, synthetic), Red-F (Red-F, red-emitting luciferase, synthetic)
phenotype: Ratiometric normalization using E-Luc and Red-F reduces luminescence variability in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves to a coefficient of variability (CV) of 9.85%.
mechanism: Ratiometric normalization using two luciferases with distinct emission peaks allows correction of technical variability in transcriptional activity measurements.

genes: Red-F (Red-F, red-emitting luciferase, synthetic)
phenotype: Red-F is used as a normalizer reporter in the ratiometric system to account for signal overlap with E-Luc.
mechanism: Red-F's stable luminescence under low-expression conditions allows reliable normalization of E-Luc activity.

genes: Nitrate-Regulated Promoter (Nitrate-Regulated Promoter, nitrate-responsive promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana), E-Luc (E-Luc, green-emitting luciferase, synthetic)
phenotype: The Arabidopsis Nitrate-Regulated Promoter drives E-Luc expression in root protoplasts, showing significant induction of green/red luminescence proportional to nitrate concentration.
mechanism: Nitrate-responsive promoter activity increases E-Luc expression in response to nitrate, enabling quantification of transcriptional regulation.

genes: β-estradiol inducible promoter (β-estradiol inducible promoter, synthetic), E-Luc (E-Luc, green-emitting luciferase, synthetic)
phenotype: The β-estradiol inducible promoter drives E-Luc expression in Nicotiana benthamiana, showing a 40-fold induction of green/red luminescence 24 h after 20 μM β-estradiol treatment.
mechanism: β-estradiol activates the inducible promoter, leading to increased E-Luc expression and luminescence.

genes: D14L (rice strigolactone receptor, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: D14L-defective mutant (d14l-c1) shows inability to interact with arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) and insensitivity to (−)-GR5-induced strigolactone (SL) biosynthesis in rice.
mechanism: D14L is essential for D14L-mediated activation of SL biosynthesis via transcriptional upregulation of biosynthetic genes in rice roots.

genes: MpaSMXL (KAI2 pathway component, Marchantia paleacea, synthetic)
phenotype: Mpasmxl-2 mutant shows reduced bryosymbiol (BSB) levels and inability to establish symbiosis with arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) in Marchantia paleacea.
mechanism: Excessive activation of the KAI2 pathway via MpaSMXL knockout negatively regulates BSB biosynthesis in M. paleacea.

genes: Pi23226 (pathogen effector, P. infestans, synthetic), Pi23015 (pathogen effector, P. infestans, synthetic), Pi07550 (pathogen effector, P. infestans, synthetic), Pi04089 (pathogen effector, P. infestans, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient expression of N-terminally GFP-tagged effectors colocalized with RFP-Fib2 in nucleoli, with Pi23226 causing nucleolar inflation and cell death in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: Pi23226 binds 25S rRNA, disrupts pre-rRNA processing, and inhibits global translation, leading to nucleolar stress and cell death.

genes: Fibrillarin (nucleolar marker, N. benthamiana, native)

mechanism: NA

mechanism: Pi23226 binds 25S rRNA, disrupts pre-rRNA processing, and inhibits global translation, leading to nucleolar stress and cell death.

genes: Pi23226 (pathogen effector, P. infestans, synthetic)
phenotype: Pi23226-NES localized in the nucleus but not nucleolus, failed to cause nucleolar inflation or cell death, and did not enhance P. infestans virulence.
mechanism: Nuclear export signal (NES) prevents nucleolar localization, disrupting Pi23226's interaction with 25S rRNA and ribosome biogenesis.

genes: Pi23226 (pathogen effector, P. infestans, synthetic)
phenotype: Pi23226ΔC retained nucleolar localization but failed to enhance P. infestans virulence or cause nucleolar inflation compared to full-length Pi23226.
mechanism: C-terminal deletion removes variable region but retains nucleolar localization; Pi23226ΔC still binds 25S rRNA but fails to disrupt ribosome biogenesis as effectively as full-length Pi23226.

mechanism: CsLH encodes a PHYB protein that regulates light-dependent hypocotyl elongation; the 7-bp deletion in lh disrupts the open reading frame, leading to a premature stop codon

genes: CcaSHL (CcaS with NLS and TMD removed, codon-optimized for plants), CcaRHL (CcaR with NLS and VP64 TAD, codon-optimized for plants)
phenotype: Optogenetic control of target gene expression with light-dependent YFP/RFP fluorescence ratios in N. benthamiana leaves, showing lower YFP/RFP in blue light and higher in red/darkness.
mechanism: CcaSHL and CcaRHL form a light-inducible transcription system where CcaSHL phosphorylates CcaRHL, which binds to PHL to activate gene expression. Blue light inactivates CcaSHL, reducing target gene expression.

genes: nlsedAFPt9 (nuclear targeted yellow fluorescent protein)
phenotype: YFP expression under PHL control shows light-dependent regulation, with lower YFP/RFP ratios in blue light and higher in red/darkness.
mechanism: PHL is a synthetic promoter with CcaR binding motifs that activates gene expression when bound by CcaRHL, which is phosphorylated by CcaSHL in response to light.

genes: NRC4D478V (auto-active immune regulatory protein)
phenotype: Optogenetic control of hypersensitive response (HR) in N. benthamiana leaves, with HR-associated fluorescence reduced in blue light and increased in red/green light.
mechanism: NRC4D478V activates HR when expressed under PHL control, which is regulated by CcaSHL/CcaRHL light-dependent activation.

genes: RUBY (tricistronic betalain biosynthesis enzymes: 2A-linked)
phenotype: Red pigment (betalain) accumulation in N. benthamiana leaves under Highlighter control, with higher redness in red/green light and lower in blue light.
mechanism: RUBY encodes three enzymes for betalain synthesis from tyrosine, expressed under PHL control to produce a chromogenic reporter.

genes: CIPK1 (CIPK1T179D, constitutively active variant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CIPK1CA leads to lower water retention capacity and higher water dissipation compared to wild type in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CIPK1 negatively regulates ABA responses during drought by phosphorylating PYLs, which inactivates ABA receptors and prevents inhibition of ABI1 phosphatase activities.

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression pattern of CIPK1 is comparable to CBL1/9, with guard cell expression similar to CBL1, CBL9, and CIPK23.
mechanism: NA

phenotype: Transgenic plants with PYL4 and PYL4S129A restore ABA sensitivity and drought resilience in quintuple-mutant 12458, while PYL4S129D exhibits ABA insensitivity and drought hypersensitivity.
mechanism: Phosphorylation at PYL4 Ser129 by CIPK1 inactivates ABA receptors, preventing inhibition of ABI1 phosphatase activities and downstream ABA signaling.

genes: SlRUP (negative regulator of UVR8-mediated UV-B photomorphogenesis, tomato), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: SlRUP overexpression leads to hyposensitivity to UV-B (hypocotyl length under UV-B is ~56% of white light control), reduced anthocyanin accumulation (~1.5–2-fold vs 3-fold in wildtype), and slower SlUVR8 redimerization post UV-B.
mechanism: SlRUP accelerates redimerization of UV-B-activated SlUVR8 monomer, inhibiting UV-B signaling by promoting reversion to inactive homodimer.

genes: SlRUP (negative regulator of UVR8-mediated UV-B photomorphogenesis, tomato)
phenotype: Slrup mutants show hypersensitivity to UV-B (hypocotyl length under UV-B is ~56% of white light control), increased anthocyanin accumulation (~6–7-fold vs 3-fold in wildtype), and slower SlUVR8 redimerization post UV-B.
mechanism: SlRUP accelerates redimerization of UV-B-activated SlUVR8 monomer, inhibiting UV-B signaling by promoting reversion to inactive homodimer.

genes: mSDE460 (mature secretory protein CaLasSDE460, Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus)
phenotype: Overexpression of mSDE460 increases CaLas bacterial population by ~30-70% in citrus and accelerates HLB symptom development (53.62-69.62% symptomatic leaves vs 31.43% in WT at 16 MAI). High temperature (32°C) reduces CaLas proliferation in transgenic plants compared to WT.
mechanism: mSDE460 disrupts MAPK signaling pathway, plant hormone signal transduction, and protein processing in endoplasmic reticulum. Specifically suppresses SA biosynthesis (CsSAMT1) and JA pathway (LOX2), and alters HSP70b expression affecting photosynthesis at 32°C.

genes: CaSLP (capsicum annuum 40S ribosomal protein SA-like, synthetic), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: 35S:CaSLP:GFP fusion protein localized in cell nucleus and membrane of tobacco epidermal cells
mechanism: NA

genes: CaSLP (capsicum annuum 40S ribosomal protein SA-like, synthetic)
phenotype: CaSLP-silenced pepper plants showed reduced drought tolerance with higher ROS levels and lower chlorophyll content
mechanism: CaSLP acts as a positive regulator of drought signaling by modulating stomatal development genes

genes: CaSLP (capsicum annuum 40S ribosomal protein SA-like, synthetic), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient CaSLP overexpression improved drought tolerance with lower ROS levels and higher chlorophyll content
mechanism: CaSLP enhances drought tolerance by regulating stomatal development genes and ROS homeostasis

genes: CaSLP (capsicum annuum 40S ribosomal protein SA-like, synthetic), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: CaSLP overexpression in Arabidopsis increased drought tolerance with lower REL/MDA and higher chlorophyll content
mechanism: CaSLP enhances drought tolerance by interacting with CaNAC035 to regulate stomatal development and ROS clearance

genes: CaNAC035 (NAC domain-containing protein 035, synthetic), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: CaNAC035 overexpression in pepper enhanced drought tolerance when CaSLP was silenced
mechanism: CaSLP interacts with CaNAC035 to enhance binding to CaPR1 promoter and modulate drought response

genes: SlDof1 (SlDof1, transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Knockdown of SlDof1 delays fruit ripening, with reduced lycopene accumulation and ethylene production.
mechanism: SlDof1 affects the expression of ripening-related genes.

genes: SlDof1 (SlDof1, transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: SlDof1 is specifically located in the nucleus.
mechanism: NA

genes: PymiR156a (microRNA, PIR156 family, Pyrus spp.), PySPL9 (Squamosa promoter binding protein-like, Pyrus spp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of PymiR156a promotes anthocyanin accumulation in apple calli, pear skin, and Arabidopsis seedlings, resulting in red pigmentation. Suppression of PymiR156a prevents anthocyanin accumulation.
mechanism: PymiR156a cleaves PySPL9 mRNA, reducing PySPL9 protein levels. PySPL9 forms heterodimers with PyMYB114/PyMYB10 to block anthocyanin biosynthesis. PymiR156a overexpression disrupts this complex, allowing anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: PymiR156a (microRNA, PIR156 family, Pyrus spp.)
phenotype: Histochemical GUS staining confirmed PymiR156a promoter activity in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: The PymiR156a promoter contains light-responsive elements including G-box motifs, which are bound by PyPIF5 to suppress miRNA expression.

genes: PymiR156a (microRNA, PIR156 family, Pyrus spp.), PySPL9 (Squamosa promoter binding protein-like, Pyrus spp.)
phenotype: Dual-luciferase assays confirmed PymiR156a cleavage of PySPL9 mRNA in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: PymiR156a binds to and cleaves PySPL9 mRNA, reducing PySPL9 protein levels which form inhibitory complexes with PyMYB114/PyMYB10.

genes: GhPRGL (GASA protein, promoter region 1732 bp upstream of ORF, contains hormone and floral organ development elements), GhBPE (bHLH transcription factor, represses GhPRGL expression)
phenotype: GhPRGL overexpression promotes ray petal elongation by 3.36-fold and increases cell elongation; GhBPE overexpression inhibits petal elongation by 0.72-fold and reduces cell elongation. GhPRGL silencing reduces petal length by 0.42-fold, while GhBPE silencing increases it by 1.38-fold.
mechanism: GhPRGL promotes petal elongation through cell elongation regulation. GhBPE represses GhPRGL expression by binding to its promoter (containing JA-responsive elements), inhibiting petal elongation. JA and GA crosstalk modulates this module: GA upregulates GhPRGL, while JA upregulates GhBPE to repress GhPRGL.

genes: GhIMP10D (GhIMP10D, alkaline stress response gene, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Increased MDA content and decreased POD, SOD, chlorophyll, and AsA content in pYL156:GhIMP10D plants compared to 156 control plants under alkaline stress
mechanism: GhIMP10D regulates antioxidant enzyme activity and AsA content to modulate alkaline stress tolerance

genes: NtMYB12 (NtMYB12, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Narcissus tazetta)
phenotype: Knockdown of NtMYB12 reduces flavonol and anthocyanin biosynthesis gene expression (NtFLS, NtLAR, NtDFR, NtANS) and decreases flavonol content by ~6-fold while increasing anthocyanin content by ~2.5-fold in transformed Arabidopsis.
mechanism: NtMYB12 directly targets and regulates NtFLS, NtLAR, and NtDFR gene expression in flavonoid biosynthesis. NtMYB12 forms an MBW complex with NtbHLH1 and NtWD40-1 to specifically activate NtDFR expression in (pro)anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: NtMYB12 (NtMYB12, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Narcissus tazetta)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtMYB12 increases flavonol content by ~15% and activates NtFLS and NtLAR gene expression while repressing NtDFR expression in Narcissus tazetta. In Arabidopsis, overexpression of NtMYB12-NtbHLH1-NtWD40-1 complex results in 15-fold higher anthocyanin accumulation in leaves and 2-fold in seeds.
mechanism: NtMYB12 directly activates NtFLS and NtLAR promoters and represses NtDFR promoter. When forming an MBW complex with NtbHLH1 and NtWD40-1, it specifically activates NtDFR expression in (pro)anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: SlPZF1 (Solanum lycopersicum PERICARP-associated ZINC FINGER PROTEIN 1, Solyc07g063970, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlPZF1 reduces pericarp cell size and fruit size in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: SlPZF1 regulates fruit size through its action on cell size by attenuating endoreduplication and modulating cell cycle regulators.

genes: SlPZF1 (Solanum lycopersicum PERICARP-associated ZINC FINGER PROTEIN 1, Solyc07g063970, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: RNAi repression of SlPZF1 reduces pericarp cell size and fruit size in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: SlPZF1 regulates fruit size through its action on cell size by attenuating endoreduplication and modulating cell cycle regulators.

genes: TaNRAMP3 (TaNRAMP3, plasma membrane Mn transporter, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaNRAMP3 increases fresh weight and chlorophyll content by ~2-fold in Triticum aestivum under Mn deficiency.
mechanism: TaNRAMP3 mediates Mn transport in the plasma membrane, enhancing Mn uptake and maintaining photosynthesis under Mn deficiency.

genes: TaNRAMP3 (TaNRAMP3, plasma membrane Mn transporter, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: RNAi of TaNRAMP3 decreases fresh weight and chlorophyll content by ~5-fold in Triticum aestivum under Mn deficiency.
mechanism: TaNRAMP3 knockdown reduces Mn transport capacity, leading to Mn deficiency symptoms and impaired photosynthesis.

genes: TaNRAMP3 (TaNRAMP3, plasma membrane Mn transporter, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: TaNRAMP3 complements the nramp1 mutant phenotype in Arabidopsis, restoring root length and fresh weight under Mn deficiency.
mechanism: TaNRAMP3 functions as an ortholog of AtNRAMP1, mediating Mn transport in the plasma membrane to maintain Mn homeostasis.

genes: TaNRAMP3 (TaNRAMP3, plasma membrane Mn transporter, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaNRAMP3 in Arabidopsis increases root length and fresh weight under Mn deficiency.
mechanism: TaNRAMP3 enhances Mn uptake in the plasma membrane, improving Mn homeostasis and growth under deficiency.

genes: GSE9 (grain shape regulator, Oryza sativa, synthetic)

genes: GSE9 (grain shape regulator, Oryza sativa, synthetic)

mechanism: GSE9 regulates grain shape by controlling both cell expansion and cell proliferation.

genes: GSE9 (grain shape regulator, Oryza sativa, synthetic)

mechanism: GSE9 regulates grain shape by controlling both cell expansion and cell proliferation.

genes: GSE9 (grain shape regulator, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: GSE9pro::GUS transgenic plants show no obvious phenotypic differences in grain shape compared to wild-type ZH11.
mechanism: GSE9 is expressed in various tissues including spikelet hulls and panicles, with strong activity in younger tissues.

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of eGFP in transgenic hairy roots of Fragaria vesca, with a transgenic efficiency of up to 71.43%.
mechanism: The CaMV35S promoter drives constitutive expression of eGFP in all tissues of the transgenic hairy roots.

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)

mechanism: PPD3 knockdown perturbs sensory plastid function, leading to epigenetic reprogramming and transgenerational memory.

genes: TaHsfA1-A (heat shock factor A1, Triticum aestivum), TaHsfA1-B (heat shock factor A1, Triticum aestivum), TaHsfA1-D (heat shock factor A1, Triticum aestivum)

genes: TaHsfA1-D (heat shock factor A1, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: NA

phenotype: Overexpression of RUBY-S in carrot callus results in variable coloration (yellow-orange, red, red-violet) due to differing betacyanin/betaxanthin ratios, with 246.9 μg·g−1 DW betacyanin and 269.48 μg·g−1 DW betaxanthin in taproots.
mechanism: Heterologous expression of BvCYP76AD1 and BvDODA1 (without MjcDOPA5GT) leads to betalain biosynthesis with altered betacyanin/betaxanthin ratios.

genes: RUBY (BvCYP76AD1, cytochrome P450, Beta vulgaris; BvDODA1, DOPA 4,5-dioxygenase, Beta vulgaris; MjcDOPA5GT, cyclo-DOPA-5-O-glucosyltransferase, Mirabilis jalapa)
phenotype: Root-specific overexpression of RUBY in carrot taproots results in red-violet coloration and betalain production (313.1 μg·g−1 DW total betalains in taproots vs. 36.2 μg·g−1 in leaves), with minimal betalain accumulation in aerial parts.
mechanism: Root-specific expression of BvCYP76AD1, BvDODA1, and MjcDOPA5GT via the pDJ3S promoter restricts betalain biosynthesis to taproots.

genes: RUBY (BvCYP76AD1, cytochrome P450, Beta vulgaris; BvDODA1, DOPA 4,5-dioxygenase, Beta vulgaris; MjcDOPA5GT, cyclo-DOPA-5-O-glucosyltransferase, Mirabilis jalapa)
phenotype: Vascular cambium-specific overexpression of RUBY in carrot taproots creates a 'volcano-like' red ring in cross-sections (92.7 μg·g−1 DW betalains in xylem vs. 25.8 μg·g−1 in phloem), with no betalain accumulation in flowers or seeds.
mechanism: Vascular cambium-specific expression of BvCYP76AD1, BvDODA1, and MjcDOPA5GT via the p15 promoter localizes betalain biosynthesis to the vascular cambium.

genes: PhOBF1 (PhOBF1, bZIP transcription factor involved in flower senescence, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of PhOBF1 accelerates petunia flower senescence, shortening flower longevity by 1.0 to 1.2 days.
mechanism: PhOBF1 negatively regulates ethylene-mediated corolla senescence by modulating GA production.

genes: PhOBF1 (PhOBF1, bZIP transcription factor involved in flower senescence, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of PhOBF1 delays petunia flower senescence, extending flower longevity by 1.4 to 2.2 days.
mechanism: PhOBF1 negatively regulates ethylene-mediated corolla senescence by modulating GA production.

genes: PhGA20ox3 (PhGA20ox3, GA biosynthetic gene, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: VIGS silencing of PhGA20ox3 accelerates petunia flower senescence, decreasing flower longevity by 1.6 days.
mechanism: PhGA20ox3 is a downstream target of PhOBF1 and is involved in GA biosynthesis, which inhibits flower senescence.

genes: GFP (GFP protein CDS, synthetic)
phenotype: Intermediate GFP fluorescence in shoot apex, hypocotyl, and root of Arabidopsis thaliana, correlating with moderate S-PTGS (RNA silencing) of the transgene.
mechanism: The construct's pararetrovirus enhancer and minimal 35S promoter drive GFP expression, but alternative splicing of the transcribed RNA generates non-translatable splice variants that produce siRNAs, triggering RNA silencing (S-PTGS). The translatable AU-AC splice variant escapes silencing and determines the observed fluorescence level.

genes: StTST1 (tonoplast sugar transporter, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Suppression of StTST1 dramatically inhibits reducing sugar (RS) accumulation in tubers during cold storage, improves potato chip quality, and decreases acrylamide levels by ~80% in cold-stored tubers.
mechanism: StTST1 functions as a tonoplast sucrose transporter, transporting sucrose into vacuoles where it is hydrolyzed by invertase to produce reducing sugars (RS) during cold-induced sweetening (CIS). Silencing StTST1 reduces RS accumulation by preventing sucrose import into vacuoles, leading to cytosolic sucrose retention that promotes starch synthesis and inhibits starch degradation. High cytosolic sucrose also suppresses ABA signaling, downregulating β-amylase StBAM1 expression.

genes: MpPAH (phosphatidate phosphatase, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Loss-of-function mutation in MpPAH perturbs growth even under Pi-replete conditions, with shorter rhizoids and reduced fresh weight under Pi and N starvation
mechanism: MpPAH is involved in PC degradation and plastid glycolipid synthesis through the ER pathway, affecting lipid remodeling and membrane composition

genes: MIM156 (MIM156, target mimicry of miR156 and miR157, synthetic)
phenotype: Accelerates the transition to the adult phase by reducing miR156 and miR157 levels.
mechanism: MIM156 acts as a target mimicry to reduce miR156 and miR157 levels, leading to accelerated transition to the adult phase.

genes: MIR156a (MIR156a, microRNA 156a, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Delays the transition to the adult phase by increasing miR156 levels.
mechanism: Overexpression of MIR156a increases miR156 levels, leading to delayed transition to the adult phase.

genes: MIR156A (MIR156A, microRNA 156A, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Delays the transition to the adult phase by increasing miR156 levels.
mechanism: Genomic insertion of MIR156A increases miR156 levels, leading to delayed transition to the adult phase.

genes: OsP0A (OsP0A, predominant P0 gene essential for embryo development, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Genomic DNA of OsP0A complements the lethal phenotypes of osp0a mutant in rice
mechanism: NA

genes: sgRNA-LCYe (LCYe1, LCYe2, targeting, synthetic)
phenotype: Zeaxanthin accumulation in leaves of Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9 mediated knockout of LCYe and ZEP genes.

genes: sgRNA-ZEP (ZEP1, ZEP2, targeting, synthetic)
phenotype: Zeaxanthin accumulation in leaves of Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9 mediated knockout of LCYe and ZEP genes.

genes: AtCAS9 (Arabidopsis thaliana, codon-optimized)
phenotype: Zeaxanthin accumulation in leaves of Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9 mediated knockout of LCYe and ZEP genes.

genes: Zm305 (allele-specific imprinting gene, Zea mays)
phenotype: mutation and overexpression of Zm305 affects kernel length and width
mechanism: NA

genes: DARPin G3 (DARPin G3, antibody mimetic for HER2 targeting, synthetic)
phenotype: Chloroplast-made DARPin G3 accumulates at ~3.4 mg/g fresh leaf weight and remains stable for >9 months at room temperature in lyophilized leaves and chloroplasts with 16- and 32-fold increased concentrations, respectively
mechanism: Chloroplasts enable proper protein folding and disulfide bond formation, maintaining HER2-binding affinity (91 pmol/L) and functionality in lyophilized materials

genes: TAT (taxadien-5α-ol acetyltransferase, Taxus), T10βH (taxadien-5α-acetoxy-10β-hydroxylase, Taxus), DBAT (10-deacetylbaccatin III:10-O-acetyltransferase, Taxus), T13αH (taxadien-5α,13α-diol synthase, Taxus)
phenotype: Successful reconstitution of early paclitaxel biosynthetic pathway producing 5α,10β-diacetoxy-taxadiene-13α-ol (14) in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: Sequential enzymatic oxidation and acetylation of taxadiene intermediates by TAT, T10βH, DBAT, and T13αH.

genes: ZmHSP90 (heat shock protein 90, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmHSP90 increases antioxidant enzyme activity (SOD, POD, CAT) and maintains Na+/K+ homeostasis in tobacco under salt stress, enhancing salt tolerance.
mechanism: ZmHSP90 enhances expression of NtSOS1, NtHKT1, and NtNHX1 to regulate Na+ transporters and maintain K+/Na+ balance. It also increases antioxidant enzyme activity to scavenge ROS.

genes: GmILPA1 (Glycine max Increased Leaf Petiole Angle1, Glycine max), GFP (green fluorescent protein, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmILPA1-GFP in the Gmilpa1-2 mutant background restores the mutant phenotype to the wild type, as evidenced by plant height.
mechanism: GmILPA1 promotes plant height by ubiquitinating and degrading GmGA2ox-like in a UV-B-dependent manner, thereby repressing the UV-B-induced reduction of active gibberellin (GA) levels.

genes: GmGA2ox-like (2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase, Glycine max)
phenotype: RNA interference (RNAi) silencing of GmGA2ox-like in the Gmilpa1-2 mutant significantly rescues the dwarf phenotype under UV-B irradiation.
mechanism: GmGA2ox-like is a GA 2β-hydroxylase that converts bioactive GAs to non-bioactive forms. Its knockdown reduces GA catabolism, thereby increasing active GA levels and promoting plant height.

genes: GmILPA1 (Glycine max Increased Leaf Petiole Angle1, Glycine max), GUS (β-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Transient expression of GUS under the control of GmILPA1 haplotype promoters in N. benthamiana leaves showed differential GUS activity under UV-B irradiation, with haplotypes Hap1, Hap3, Hap5/indel, and Hap6 exhibiting higher activity than Hap5.
mechanism: The deletion of a light-responsive cis-regulatory element (CRE) in the GmILPA1 promoter of Hap5 reduces transcriptional activity under UV-B, leading to lower GmILPA1 expression and increased susceptibility to UV-B-induced dwarfism.

genes: GmGA2ox-like (2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmGA2ox-like in soybean results in a dwarf phenotype compared to non-transgenic wild-type plants.
mechanism: GmGA2ox-like catalyzes the conversion of bioactive GAs (GA1 and GA4) to non-bioactive forms (GA8 and GA34), reducing active GA levels and inhibiting plant growth.

genes: miR156b (miR156b, microRNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Constitutively expressing miR156b (OX156b) plants strengthened Arabidopsis resistance against S. sclerotiorum accompanied by smaller necrotic lesions.
mechanism: miR156 positively modulates the resistance to S. sclerotiorum infection by restricting colonization of S. sclerotiorum mycelia.

genes: miR156 (miR156, microRNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Blocking miR156 expression in Arabidopsis (MIM156) led to greater susceptibility to S. sclerotiorum disease, associated with extensive cell death of necrotic lesions.
mechanism: miR156 positively modulates the resistance to S. sclerotiorum infection by restricting colonization of S. sclerotiorum mycelia.

genes: Sr50 (NLR, wheat)
phenotype: Double mutant Sr50_M844V_V868E exhibits autoactivity similar to wild-type Sr50 but retains AvrSr50 recognition
mechanism: Residues M844 and V868 modulate autoactivity through NB-ARC/LRR latch interactions

genes: OsGA3ox1 (gibberellin 3-oxidase 1, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: Mutation of OsGA3ox1 reduces seed-setting rate by ~97% and pollen viability by ~50% in Oryza sativa, with homozygous knockout mutants producing ~2.8-3.4% fertile seeds compared to wild type.
mechanism: OsGA3ox1 regulates pollen starch granule accumulation and pollen wall development through GA biosynthesis. Mutation causes thinner exine (81-89% of wild type thickness), reduced starch granules in pollen, and downregulation of OsGAMYB, OsTDR, and OsbHLH142 expression.

genes: BntWG10016451 (MYB gene, NA, ramie)
phenotype: Overexpression of BntWG10016451 increases xylem fiber number and secondary wall thickness in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: MIR319C (MIR319C promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic, source)
phenotype: MIR319C promoter activity is detected throughout incipient leaf primordia and excluded from the shoot meristem in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MIR319C promoter activity is restricted to the leaf base by JAW-TCP proteins, which repress its transcription via direct binding to cis-elements and chromatin modification.

genes: miR319c (miR319c microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic, source)
phenotype: miR319c activity is detected throughout the primordia in young leaves, with GUS signal appearing in the distal half as leaves grow.
mechanism: miR319c activity is ubiquitously expressed under the UBIQUITIN10 promoter, and its activity is inferred from the absence of GUS signal in the pUBQ10::miR319c-GUS transgenic line.

genes: TCP4 (TCP4 transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic, source)
phenotype: TCP4 promoter activity appears in the distal half of leaf primordia, with protein localization spreading toward the basal region as leaves grow.
mechanism: TCP4 promoter activity and protein localization are spatially restricted by miR319c activity, with JAW-TCP proteins repressing MIR319C to establish a feedback loop.

genes: TCP4 (miR319-resistant TCP4-GR fusion protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: Ectopic TCP4 expression almost completely clears the leaf primordia of GUS expression, with only speckles remaining at the junction of leaf and shoot meristem.
mechanism: TCP4-GR fusion proteins, inducible by dexamethasone, repress MIR319C promoter activity by binding to cis-elements and recruiting chromatin silencing complexes.

genes: MIR319C (MIR319C promoter with mutated TCP-binding sites, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), MIR319C (pre-MIR319C transcript, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: Mutated TCP-binding sites in the MIR319C promoter lead to increased cotyledon epinasty in transgenic lines compared to wild-type.
mechanism: JAW-TCP binding to cis-elements in the MIR319C promoter reduces its phenotypic effects, as evidenced by lower epinasty in wild-type compared to mutant lines.

genes: Vr2-C (Vr2-C, scab resistance gene, Malus x domestica)
phenotype: Transgenic lines show resistance to scab isolate 104 (race 1) but are susceptible to isolate 1634 (race 4).
mechanism: Vr2-C confers resistance to scab by recognizing specific isolates, with resistance to race 1 but susceptibility to race 4.

genes: VvWRKY5 (VvWRKY5, WRKY transcription factor, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvWRKY5 enhances resistance to Coniella diplodiella (Cd) in grape by increasing hydrogen peroxide content, superoxide dismutase activity, and peroxidase activity.
mechanism: VvWRKY5 binds to the promoters of VvJAZ2 and VvMYC2, repressing VvJAZ2 transcription and activating VvMYC2 transcription. VvWRKY5 physically interacts with VvJAZ2 to enhance its transcriptional regulatory activity, thereby strengthening jasmonic acid (JA)-mediated defense responses.

genes: VvWRKY5 (VvWRKY5, WRKY transcription factor, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvWRKY5 in grape and Arabidopsis significantly enhances resistance to Coniella diplodiella (Cd) and Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 (Pst DC3000), respectively, by upregulating jasmonic acid (JA) and salicylic acid (SA) signaling pathways.
mechanism: VvWRKY5 activates the jasmonic acid (JA) signaling pathway by repressing VvJAZ2 and activating VvMYC2. It also interacts with VvJAZ2 to form a protein complex, enhancing JA-mediated defense responses. Additionally, VvWRKY5 promotes crosstalk between JA and SA pathways, increasing salicylic acid (SA) content in infected grape calli.

genes: VvWRKY5 (VvWRKY5, WRKY transcription factor, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Knockdown of VvWRKY5 in grape reduces resistance to Coniella diplodiella (Cd), as evidenced by increased fungal plaque areas and decreased hydrogen peroxide content, superoxide dismutase activity, and peroxidase activity.
mechanism: VvWRKY5 knockdown suppresses the activation of jasmonic acid (JA) signaling pathways, leading to reduced ROS accumulation and antioxidant enzyme activity, which compromises defense responses against Cd.

genes: WRI1 (WRI1, WRINKLED1 transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), Di (DGAT1, diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 with intron, Thermoanaerobacterium), OLE1 (OLE1, oleosin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-expression of WDiO resulted in leaf TAG accumulation up to 3.85% of dry weight (192-fold increase over wildtype) and TFA up to 8.4% of dry weight (6.1-fold increase over wildtype), with stem TAG up to 1.14% of dry weight and TFA up to 2.08% of dry weight
mechanism: Constitutive expression of lipogenic 'push pull and protect' factors (WRI1, DGAT1, OLE1) enhances lipid accumulation by increasing TAG synthesis and protection

genes: GauERF105 (GauERF105, ethylene-responsive factor, Gossypium australe)
phenotype: Overexpression of GauERF105 enhances resistance to Verticillium dahliae in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GauERF105 activates defense genes and reduces oxidative stress, enhancing resistance to Verticillium dahliae.

genes: GauERF105 (GauERF105, ethylene-responsive factor, Gossypium australe)
phenotype: Silencing of GauERF105 decreases resistance to Verticillium dahliae in cotton.
mechanism: GauERF105 is involved in defense mechanisms, including lignin deposition and activation of defense genes.

genes: VvBBX44 (VvBBX44, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: VvBBX44-eGFP fusion localizes to both nucleus and cytoplasm in tobacco leaves.
mechanism: NA

genes: VvBBX44 (VvBBX44, Vitis vinifera), VvMYBA1 (VvMYBA1, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: VvBBX44 suppresses the activity of the VvMYBA1 promoter by ~70% in tobacco leaves.
mechanism: VvBBX44 directly binds to the VvMYBA1 promoter containing the T/G-box element and inhibits its transcriptional activity.

genes: VvBBX44 (VvBBX44, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: VvBBX44 binds to the T/G-box element in the VvMYBA1 promoter in yeast.
mechanism: NA

genes: VvBBX44 (VvBBX44, Vitis vinifera), VvMYBA1 (VvMYBA1, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Co-expression of VvBBX44 and VvMYBA1 reduces the activation of VvBBX44 and VvUFGT promoters by ~50% compared to VvMYBA1 alone.
mechanism: VvBBX44 interferes with the transcriptional activation of VvMYBA1 on VvBBX44 and VvUFGT promoters without direct physical interaction.

genes: VvBBX44 (VvBBX44, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Exogenous anthocyanin (cyanidin-3-glucoside) increases VvBBX44 promoter activity by ~1.5-fold in tobacco leaves.
mechanism: Anthocyanin induces VvBBX44 expression, which in turn represses VvMYBA1 to regulate anthocyanin biosynthesis in a feedback loop.

genes: SIET4 (SIET4, Silicon Efflux Transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of SIET4 leads to death of rice when grown in soil with Si. Growth inhibition in hydroponic solution with Si, reduced shoot and root dry weight (<10% of WT), leaf symptoms (white spots, yellowing, twisting), and failure to set seed.
mechanism: SIET4 functions as an efflux transporter for Si, exporting Si from leaf cells to apoplastic space for proper deposition. Knockout causes abnormal Si accumulation in mesophyll cells, leading to metabolic disturbances and plant death. Transcriptome analysis shows stress-related gene expression changes in mutants.

genes: GuApiGT (Glycyrrhiza uralensis apiosyltransferase, Glycyrrhiza uralensis), UAXS (UDP-apiose/UDP-xylose synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtPAL (phenylalanine ammonia-lyase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtC4H (cinnamate 4-hydroxylase, Arabidopsis thaliana), At4CL (4-coumarate:CoA ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtCHS (chalcone synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana), GuCHR (chalcone reductase, Glycyrrhiza uralensis), Pgm (phosphoglucomutase), GalU (UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase), CalS8 (UDP-glucose:flavonoid 7-O-glucosyltransferase), GuGT53 (glycosyltransferase, Glycyrrhiza uralensis)
phenotype: De novo biosynthesis of liquiritin apioside (1a) and isoliquiritin apioside (2a) in tobacco leaves with yields of 5.46 and 4.73 mg/g (dry weight), respectively
mechanism: GuApiGT catalyzes 2″-O-apiosylation of flavonoid glycosides using UDP-Api produced by UAXS. The engineered pathway includes biosynthesis of flavonoid aglycones (module 1), UDP-donor production (module 2), and glycosylation (module 3)

genes: bZIP16 (bZIP16, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of bZIP16WT in the bzip triple mutant background delays de-etiolation and reduces LHCB1.1/LHCB2.4 expression compared to wild type
mechanism: bZIP16 acts as a repressor of photosynthesis-related gene expression during de-etiolation through redox-regulated DNA binding

genes: bZIP16 (bZIP16, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of bZIP16C1 in the bzip triple mutant background delays de-etiolation and reduces LHCB1.1/LHCB2.4 expression compared to wild type
mechanism: bZIP16 acts as a repressor of photosynthesis-related gene expression during de-etiolation through redox-regulated DNA binding

genes: bZIP16 (bZIP16, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of bZIP16C2 in the bzip triple mutant background delays de-etiolation and reduces LHCB1.1/LHCB2.4 expression compared to wild type
mechanism: bZIP16 acts as a repressor of photosynthesis-related gene expression during de-etiolation through redox-regulated DNA binding

genes: RHM1 (RHM1, UDP-l-rhamnose synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: rescued cellulose organization defects, with non-helical wild-type petal morphology
mechanism: RHM1 prevents cellulose bundling by supplying rhamnose for RG-I, which maintains dispersed microfibrils

genes: AIL5 (Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic copy with 3' UTR)
phenotype: Increased AIL5 expression complements ant-4 phenotype, rescuing petal size, anther locule number, floral organ number, and seed production in some lines.
mechanism: ANT promoter drives AIL5 expression, which compensates for the ant-4 mutation by promoting growth in floral tissues.

genes: AIL7 (Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic copy with 3' UTR)
phenotype: Increased AIL7 expression partially complements ant-4 phenotype, rescuing anther locule number and fertility in some lines, but not floral organ number.
mechanism: ANT promoter drives AIL7 expression, which partially compensates for the ant-4 mutation by promoting growth in anther locule development.

genes: AlcR (Arabidopsis thaliana, LEAFY promoter), AIL7 (Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic copy with 3' UTR)
phenotype: Ethanol-inducible AIL7 expression results in mosaic floral organs, altered floral organ number, and secondary flowers in some lines.
mechanism: Ethanol-inducible AlcA promoter drives AIL7 expression under the control of AlcR, which is expressed under the LEAFY promoter, leading to overexpression of AIL7 during flower development.

genes: ZIP4 (ZIP4, exon 1 targeted, synthetic)
phenotype: Inactivation of ZIP4 leads to a complete blockage of the ZMM pathway responsible for Class I crossovers and a strong reduction of plant fertility due to crossover scarcity.
mechanism: Knockout of ZIP4 blocks the ZMM pathway, leading to reduced crossovers and fertility.

genes: HEI10 (HEI10, overexpression, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of HEI10 preserves the hetero-/homozygosity juxtaposition effect and increases crossover frequency.
mechanism: Overexpression of HEI10 stimulates Class I crossovers.

genes: AT4G32060 (AtMICU, gene involved in calcium transport, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knockout of AtMICU increases intracellular calcium uptake in leaf mesophyll protoplasts by ~2-fold compared to wild-type Col-0
mechanism: AtMICU regulates MCU-dependent calcium transport by modulating mitochondrial calcium uniporter activity

genes: GhACTIN1 (actin gene, cotton fiber development, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhACTIN1 increases cotton fiber strength by ~24.2%, fiber length by ~5.3%, and cellulose content by ~4.7% in Gossypium hirsutum.
mechanism: GhACTIN1 enhances F-actin filament accumulation during fiber elongation, promoting cellulose deposition and fiber strength. Increased F-actin reorients to oblique positions, enhancing fiber strength and maturity.

genes: PH13 (homologue of SUPPRESSOR OF PHYA, soybean, Glycine max)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of PH13 partially rescues the dwarf phenotype of the spa134 mutant at both seedling and adult vegetative stages.
mechanism: PH13 is homologous to the SPA family proteins, supporting its role in the same pathway.

genes: PH13H1 (plant height regulator, soybean, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of PH13H1 in TL1H3 background increases plant height.
mechanism: PH13 functions as a plant height enhancer by promoting stem elongation and increasing node number.

genes: PH13 (plant height regulator, soybean, Glycine max)
phenotype: Loss-of-function mutants (ph13-1, ph13-2, etc.) show significant dwarf phenotype with >30% reduction in plant height.
mechanism: PH13 functions as a plant height enhancer by promoting stem elongation and increasing node number.

genes: AcbHLH144 (AcbHLH144, transcription factor, Ananas comosus)
phenotype: Overexpression of AcbHLH144 in pineapple fruit reduces total phenolic compounds (TPC) by ~30% and suppresses phenolic biosynthesis pathway genes (AcC4H, Ac4CL5, AcHCT4, AcC3′H, AcCSE).
mechanism: AcbHLH144 directly binds to the promoter of Ac4CL5 via N-box motifs (CACGAG) and suppresses its transcription, inhibiting phenolic biosynthesis.

genes: AcbHLH144 (AcbHLH144, transcription factor, Ananas comosus)
phenotype: Overexpression of AcbHLH144 in Arabidopsis seedlings reduces total phenolic compounds (TPC) by ~40% and suppresses phenolic biosynthesis pathway genes (AtC4H, At4CL, AtHCT, AtC3H, AtCSE).
mechanism: AcbHLH144 negatively regulates phenolic biosynthesis by suppressing key pathway genes in Arabidopsis, consistent with its role in pineapple.

genes: Ac4CL5 (Ac4CL5, 4-coumarate:CoA ligase, Ananas comosus)
phenotype: Overexpression of Ac4CL5 in pineapple fruit increases browning area by ~50% and elevates total phenolic compounds (TPC) by ~40%.
mechanism: Ac4CL5 is a key enzyme in phenolic biosynthesis; its overexpression enhances phenolic compound accumulation and tissue browning in pineapple.

genes: CePP2C19 (putative group A PP2C-encoding gene, highly induced by drought stress, Cyperus esculentus)
phenotype: Overexpression of CePP2C19 in transgenic Arabidopsis results in extreme tolerance to ABA and mannitol stresses during seed germination and root growth, and higher drought tolerance at the mature stage confirmed by visible phenotype and physiological parameters.
mechanism: CePP2C19 is involved in the ABA signaling pathway, reducing ABA sensitivity and enhancing drought tolerance in Cyperus esculentus.

genes: RTFL18 (RTFL18, plasma membrane-localized peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RTFL18 reduces cotyledon petiole, first and second leaf petiole, and hypocotyl elongation under low R:FR conditions in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: RTFL18 interacts with BSK3/6 to repress BR signaling, reducing low R:FR-stabilized PIF4 levels and suppressing petiole elongation.

genes: BSK3 (BSK3, RLCK-VII subfamily kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), BSK6 (BSK6, RLCK-VII subfamily kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BSK3 and BSK6 increases cotyledon petiole and leaf petiole elongation under low R:FR conditions in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: BSK3/6 positively regulate low R:FR-induced petiole elongation by promoting BR signaling, which is antagonized by RTFL18.

genes: RTFL18 (RTFL18, plasma membrane-localized peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RTFL18-GFP confirms plasma membrane localization in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: RTFL18 localizes to the plasma membrane, where it interacts with BSK3/6 to repress BR signaling.

genes: BSK3 (BSK3, RLCK-VII subfamily kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), BSK6 (BSK6, RLCK-VII subfamily kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BSK3-GFP and BSK6-GFP confirms plasma membrane localization and interaction with RTFL18 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: BSK3/6-GFP localize to the plasma membrane and interact with RTFL18, mediating BR signaling repression under low R:FR.

genes: RTFL18 (RTFL18, plasma membrane-localized peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana), BSK3 (BSK3, RLCK-VII subfamily kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), BSK6 (BSK6, RLCK-VII subfamily kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Dual overexpression of RTFL18 and BSK3/6 in dvl1-1D background rescues the RTFL18-mediated repression of BR signaling, restoring petiole elongation under low R:FR in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: RTFL18 antagonizes BSK3/6-mediated BR signaling, and BSK3/6 overexpression counteracts RTFL18's inhibitory effect on petiole elongation.

genes: AtBAG4 (AtBAG4, cytoprotective co-chaperone, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtBAG4 increases seed number per plant and 100 seed weight under water-deficit stress in Cicer arietinum. Transgenic lines show higher nodulation, nitrogen fixation, and seed protein content compared to non-transgenic controls under well-watered conditions.
mechanism: AtBAG4 enhances stress tolerance by suppressing cell death and regulating autophagy pathways, leading to improved water use efficiency and nitrogen fixation. It also modulates potassium homeostasis via interaction with KAT1 to optimize stomatal movement and photosynthesis.

genes: SAG114 (promoter of SAG114, senescence-specific promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter gene, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS staining reveals senescence-specific expression in senescent leaf parts, veins, and guard cells of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: SAG114 (serine/threonine protein kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: SAG114-GFP fusion protein localizes to the Golgi apparatus in guard cells of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SAG114-GFP co-localizes with the cis-Golgi marker ERH1-DsRED, confirming Golgi apparatus localization.

genes: Ehd5 (Early heading date 5, flowering regulator, Oryza sativa ssp. japonica)
phenotype: Complementation of ehd5 mutant restores wild-type flowering time and agronomic traits in Oryza sativa ssp. japonica.

mechanism: AsRCOM may be the crucial gene that could significantly enhance the resistance to purple curl leaf disease in agave, with obvious ROS accumulations

mechanism: Golgi apparatus localized-NtUXS16 plays an important role in hypocotyl and root growth in the dark

genes: PPD1 (regulator of flowering, Brachypodium distachyon)
