mechanism: PPD1 overexpression accelerates flowering in short days and is necessary for rapid flowering in response to long days

genes: GAUT9 (GAUT9, galacturonosyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GAUT9-GFP fusion protein is localized in the Golgi apparatus of Arabidopsis thaliana protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: ELMO1 (ELMO1, unknown function, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ELMO1-GFP fusion protein complements the elmo1-/- mutant phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana hypocotyls.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsJRL45 (OsJRL45, salt stress-responsive jacalin-related lectin, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsJRL45 increases salt tolerance at all growth stages, with significantly higher seed setting rate and 1,000-grain weight in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsJRL45 enhances antioxidant capacity and maintains Na+-K+ homeostasis under salt stress conditions by mediating ion transport-, salt stress response-, and hormone response-related genes.

genes: HBF1 (HBF1, hybrid transcription factor with VP64, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of HBF1-VP64 delays flowering time in rice by ~15% under natural day, long-day, and short-day conditions.
mechanism: HBF1 enhances transcriptional activation of flowering repressor genes (Ehd1, Hd3a, RFT1) and directly activates OsWRKY64, which inhibits flowering.

genes: HBF1 (HBF1, hybrid transcription factor with MYC, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of HBF1-MYC delays flowering time in rice, though less significantly than HBF1-VP64 under natural day, long-day, and short-day conditions.
mechanism: HBF1 enhances transcriptional activation of flowering repressor genes (Ehd1, Hd3a, RFT1) but with lower activity compared to HBF1-VP64.

genes: Ehd1 (Ehd1, flowering gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of Ehd1 delays flowering time in rice under long-day conditions compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: Ehd1 promotes flowering by inducing Hd3a and RFT1 expression; its overexpression partially counteracts HBF1's repressive effects.

genes: OsWRKY64 (OsWRKY64, WRKY transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsWRKY64 delays flowering time in rice under natural day, long-day, and short-day conditions.
mechanism: OsWRKY64 is a direct target of HBF1 and inhibits flowering by repressing flowering genes.

genes: OsWRKY64 (OsWRKY64, WRKY transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi knockdown of OsWRKY64 promotes flowering time in rice under natural day, long-day, and short-day conditions.
mechanism: OsWRKY64 inhibits flowering by repressing flowering genes; its knockdown removes this repression.

genes: OsHARBI1-1 (OsHARBI1-1, Cd-responsive gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Enhanced tolerance to Cd stress in Arabidopsis thaliana with increased root Cd accumulation and altered antioxidant enzyme activities
mechanism: Affects antioxidant enzyme activities, Cd chelation, absorption and transport, and phytohormone homeostasis and signaling

genes: HTTexon1 (human mutant HTT exon 1 with 28 glutamine repeats, Q28, human), HTTexon1 (human mutant HTT exon 1 with 69 glutamine repeats, Q69, human)
phenotype: Overexpression of Q28 and Q69 in Arabidopsis thaliana does not cause deleterious effects; plants exhibit similar development, lifespan, flowering time, and photosynthetic activity compared to wild-type controls.
mechanism: Arabidopsis sp. prevents Q69 aggregation under normal conditions through mechanisms involving chloroplast proteostasis components.

genes: HTTexon1 (human mutant HTT exon 1 with 28 glutamine repeats, Q28, human), HTTexon1 (human mutant HTT exon 1 with 69 glutamine repeats, Q69, human)
phenotype: Overexpression of Q28 and Q69 in Arabidopsis thaliana does not cause deleterious effects; plants exhibit similar development, lifespan, flowering time, and photosynthetic activity compared to wild-type controls.
mechanism: Arabidopsis sp. prevents Q69 aggregation under normal conditions through mechanisms involving chloroplast proteostasis components.

genes: TALEN arm (targeting nad9, synthetic)
phenotype: TALEN-induced deletion of the mitochondrial nad9 gene results in cytoplasmic male sterility, reduced male fertility, altered leaf anatomy, and impaired photosynthetic assimilation under high-light conditions.
mechanism: TALEN-induced double-strand breaks in the mitochondrial nad9 locus trigger microhomology-mediated end-joining, leading to deletions and genomic rearrangements. The resulting loss of functional Nad9 protein disrupts complex I assembly in mitochondria.

genes: OsFIE1 (OsFIE1, FIE gene, rice), OsFIE2 (OsFIE2, FIE gene, rice)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations at OsFIE1 and OsFIE2 cause seed abortion and asexual embryo formation in rice
mechanism: Loss of FIE function de-represses pluripotency factors (e.g., BBM and WUS homologues) in the egg apparatus, triggering asexual embryo formation. Autonomous endosperm development provides signals/nutrients to support asexual embryo growth.

genes: ZmRL6 (ZmRL6, drought-responsive MYB TF, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmRL6 increases drought tolerance in maize by enhancing antioxidant activities and reducing membrane damage.
mechanism: ZmRL6 enhances drought tolerance by upregulating antioxidant enzymes and repressing lignin synthesis genes.

genes: ZmRL6 (ZmRL6, drought-responsive MYB TF, Zea mays)
phenotype: Knockout of ZmRL6 reduces drought tolerance in maize, leading to increased membrane damage and lower survival rates.
mechanism: ZmRL6 knockout leads to downregulation of antioxidant enzymes and upregulation of lignin synthesis genes.

genes: ZmRL6 (ZmRL6, drought-responsive MYB TF, Zea mays)
phenotype: ZmRL6 activates or represses the expression of target gene promoters in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: ZmRL6 regulates target genes through binding to specific motifs.

genes: PRX102 (peroxidase, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: PRX102 knockout mutants exhibit root hair defective phenotype with 80-79% reduced root hair length and 2.9-fold increased root hair thickness compared to wild type.
mechanism: PRX102 is localized to the endoplasmic reticulum and participates in root hair tip growth by maintaining dense cytoplasmic streaming, which facilitates material delivery to growing tips.

genes: PRX102 (peroxidase, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: PRX102-GFP accumulates at root hair tips and trichoblast bulges, confirming its polarized localization during root hair growth.
mechanism: PRX102 is localized to the endoplasmic reticulum and participates in root hair tip growth by maintaining dense cytoplasmic streaming, which facilitates material delivery to growing tips.

genes: PRX102 (peroxidase, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RFP-PRX102 co-localizes with ER markers in Nicotiana benthamiana leaf epidermal cells, confirming its ER localization.
mechanism: PRX102 is localized to the endoplasmic reticulum and participates in root hair tip growth by maintaining dense cytoplasmic streaming, which facilitates material delivery to growing tips.

genes: STL2 (STL2, protein involved in SmaCCs/MASCs localization, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complements the stl1 stl2 phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: STL2 localizes to SmaCCs/MASCs derived from Golgi, facilitating CSC transfer to the plasma membrane.

genes: fABD2 (fABD2, actin filament visualization, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: NA

phenotype: Knockout of HPT in DJY1/NIL-qHMS1 F1 rescues pollen fertility, with segregation fitting 1:2:1 ratio.
mechanism: HPT truncation in DJY1 removes C-terminal domains (HELICc and CC), destroying its toxicity.

genes: HPA (Hybrid Pollen Antidote, F-box protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Introduction of Mer HPA into DJY1/NIL-qHMS1 F1 restores male fertility to ~75%.
mechanism: HPA detoxifies HPT via SCF-mediated protein degradation, protecting pollen from abortion.

genes: HPA (Hybrid Pollen Antidote, F-box protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Introduction of DJY1 HPA into NIL-qHMS1 does not restore fertility due to transposon insertion.
mechanism: Transposon insertion in HPA promoter inactivates its transcription, preventing detoxification of HPT.

genes: MdNup62 (MdNup62, nucleoporin involved in stress response, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdNup62 reduces salt-stress and osmotic-stress tolerance in Arabidopsis and tomato, as evidenced by significantly shorter root lengths and lower fresh weights under salt and mannitol treatments.
mechanism: Overexpression of MdNup62 reduces the expression levels of four AtHSPs (AtHSP101, AtHSP70T-2, AtHSP22.0-ER, and AtHSP21) under salt- and osmotic-stress conditions, thereby negatively regulating stress tolerance.

genes: MdHSFA1d (MdHSFA1d, heat shock factor A1d, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdHSFA1d promotes salt-stress and osmotic-stress tolerance in Arabidopsis, as evidenced by significantly longer root lengths and higher fresh weights under salt and mannitol treatments.
mechanism: Overexpression of MdHSFA1d increases the expression levels of four AtHSPs (AtHSP101, AtHSP70T-2, AtHSP22.0-ER, and AtHSP21) under salt- and osmotic-stress conditions, thereby positively regulating stress tolerance.

genes: RAD51 (AT5G20850, DNA repair factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), CYCB1 (AT4G37490, cell cycle regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana), Rep (viral replication protein, CaLCuV), HOP2 (AT1G13330, DNA repair factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Cloning of RAD51, CYCB1, Rep, and HOP2 into pENTER/D-TOPO vectors for yeast two-hybrid and transient expression studies
mechanism: NA

phenotype: Transient expression of RAD51, BRCA1, RPA1A, HOP2, and CYCB1;1 in Nicotiana benthamiana for protein interaction studies

mechanism: NA

mechanism: NA

genes: PpMADS2 (transcription factor, Prunus persica)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpMADS2 increases ester and lactone content in peach leaves by 2.3- to 3.5-fold.
mechanism: PpMADS2 activates PpAAT1 expression, which catalyzes ester and lactone biosynthesis in peach fruit.

genes: MaNAC029 (MaNAC029, ripening-induced NAC transcription factor, Musa acuminata), MaXB3 (MaXB3, E3 ligase, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: Overexpression of MaNAC029 in banana fruits accelerates ethylene biosynthesis and quality formation during ripening, including faster yellowing, increased ethylene production, and reduced fruit firmness, starch, and chlorophyll content. MaXB3 overexpression attenuates these effects by ubiquitinating and degrading MaNAC029.
mechanism: MaNAC029 transcriptionally activates genes involved in ethylene biosynthesis (MaACS1, MaACO1, MaACO13) and fruit quality formation (cell wall degradation, starch degradation, aroma compound synthesis, chlorophyll catabolism). MaXB3 ubiquitinates and degrades MaNAC029, reducing its trans-activation activity.

genes: MaNAC029 (MaNAC029, ripening-induced NAC transcription factor, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: MaNAC029 promoter activity is significantly activated by ethylene treatment in banana fruits.
mechanism: MaNAC029 promoter contains ethylene-responsive elements that are activated during ripening.

genes: MaNAC029 (MaNAC029, ripening-induced NAC transcription factor, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: MaNAC029 exhibits transcriptional activation activity in yeast and tobacco leaves, particularly in its C-terminal region.
mechanism: The C-terminal domain of MaNAC029 contains a transcriptional activation domain that enhances promoter activity of target genes.

genes: MaNAC029 (MaNAC029, ripening-induced NAC transcription factor, Musa acuminata), MaXB3 (MaXB3, E3 ligase, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: MaNAC029 and MaXB3 interact in yeast two-hybrid and bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) assays, confirming their physical interaction.
mechanism: MaXB3 ubiquitinates MaNAC029, leading to its proteasomal degradation and reduced transcriptional activation.

genes: MaNAC029 (MaNAC029, ripening-induced NAC transcription factor, Musa acuminata), MaXB3 (MaXB3, E3 ligase, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: BiFC assays in tobacco BY-2 protoplasts show YFP fluorescence in the nucleus when MaNAC029 and MaXB3 are co-expressed, confirming their interaction.
mechanism: MaXB3 interacts with MaNAC029 in the nucleus, facilitating its ubiquitination and degradation.

genes: MaNAC029 (MaNAC029, ripening-induced NAC transcription factor, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: MaNAC029 is localized in the nucleus of tobacco BY-2 protoplasts, as shown by GFP tagging and co-expression with nuclear marker NLS-mCherry.
mechanism: The N-terminal domain of MaNAC029 contains a nuclear localization signal (NLS) that directs its nuclear import.

mechanism: LHP1-mediated H3K27me3 repression of subgenome-diversified defense genes is eliminated in mutants, leading to increased expression of defense-related genes and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-stimulated defenses

genes: H2A.X (Green Fluorescent Protein (GFP) fusion, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: H2A.X could function in preventing access of the DME demethylase to non-canonical sites

genes: PoWRKY71 (Paeonia ostii WRKY transcription factor 71, Paeonia ostii), PoCAB151 (Paeonia ostii CAB151, Paeonia ostii)
phenotype: Overexpression of PoWRKY71 increases drought tolerance in Nicotiana tabacum by 20.32% survival rate, reduces H2O2 and O2·− accumulation, maintains higher leaf water content, chlorophyll content, and photosynthetic efficiency. Overexpression of PoCAB151 increases drought tolerance by 18.06% survival rate, stabilizes photosynthesis, and promotes drought-resistant substance accumulation.
mechanism: PoWRKY71 activates PoCAB151 transcription via binding to W-box element in PoCAB151 promoter. PoCAB151 stabilizes photosynthesis by regulating chloroplast homeostasis and chlorophyll content, reducing ROS accumulation.

genes: PoWRKY71 (Paeonia ostii WRKY transcription factor 71, Paeonia ostii)
phenotype: Silencing of PoWRKY71 in Paeonia ostii increases sensitivity to drought stress, with 37.38% decrease in leaf water content and accelerated chlorophyll degradation compared to wild-type.
mechanism: PoWRKY71 positively regulates drought resistance by stabilizing photosynthesis and chlorophyll content. Silencing PoWRKY71 leads to increased ROS accumulation and reduced drought tolerance.

genes: PoCAB151 (Paeonia ostii CAB151, Paeonia ostii)
phenotype: Silencing of PoCAB151 in Paeonia ostii reduces resistance to drought stress, with increased H2O2 and O2·− accumulation, chloroplast disintegration, and reduced leaf water content, chlorophyll content, and photosynthetic efficiency.
mechanism: PoCAB151 stabilizes photosynthesis by regulating chloroplast homeostasis and chlorophyll content. Silencing PoCAB151 leads to increased ROS accumulation and reduced drought tolerance.

genes: PoCAB151 (Paeonia ostii CAB151 promoter, Paeonia ostii)
phenotype: PoCAB151 promoter activity increases by 48.63% in Paeonia ostii callus under drought treatment, indicating drought responsiveness.
mechanism: PoCAB151 promoter contains light-responsive elements (GT1-motif, G-box, LAMP) that activate GUS reporter gene under drought stress.

mechanism: CsTT8 activates carotenoid metabolism-related genes (CsDXR, CsHDS, CsHDR, CsPDS, CsLCYE, CsZEP, CsNCED2) in the MEP and carotenoid biosynthesis pathways, increasing carotenoid accumulation.

genes: CsTT8 (CsTT8, transcriptional activator, Citrus sinensis)

mechanism: CsTT8 upregulates carotenoid biosynthesis genes (CsDXR, CsHDS, CsHDR, CsPDS, CsLCYE, CsZEP, CsNCED2), promoting carotenoid accumulation and fruit coloration.

mechanism: GhGAPDH9 positively regulates drought resistance by affecting antioxidant capacity and osmoregulation in cotton.

genes: AtRNH1A (AtRNH1A, RNA:DNA hybrid cleavage activity, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: AtRNH1A cleaves RNA:DNA hybrids, reducing topoR-loop accumulation and subsequent DNA damage, thereby alleviating topological stress.

mechanism: Mutated AtRNH1AD160N fails to cleave RNA:DNA hybrids, leading to increased topoR-loop accumulation and DNA damage, worsening topological stress.

phenotype: Overexpression of HpMYB1 in tobacco significantly increases anthocyanin levels in various tissues
mechanism: Overexpression activates anthocyanin-related genes

genes: UBP1B (SG marker, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: mCherry-UBP1B tagging confirms SG localization and interaction with AtALKBH9B.

mechanism: OsAOS1 limits As accumulation through altered gene expression of phosphate transporters (OsPT1, OsPT4) and ROS homeostasis, increasing As translocation from root to shoot.

genes: OsAOS1 (allene oxide synthase 1, rice, Oryza sativa), OsAOS2 (allene oxide synthase 2, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Mutation of OsAOS2 increases arsenic (As) sensitivity in Oryza sativa under As(V) treatment, with reduced root and shoot biomass and altered As distribution.
mechanism: OsAOS2 contributes to As tolerance through altered expression of phosphate transporters (OsPT8, OsNIP3;2) and vacuolar sequestration (OsABCC1), but does not affect As translocation.

genes: BpMAX1 (BpMAX1, ortholog of AtMAX1, Betula pendula)

mechanism: BpMAX1 is an ortholog of AtMAX1 involved in shoot branching regulation.

mechanism: BpMAX1 expression is associated with xylem tissue and SL biosynthesis.

mechanism: BpMAX1 is involved in SL biosynthesis, and its downregulation reduces SL levels, affecting branching.

phenotype: rin1CR1 and rin1CR2 mutants exhibit pronounced dwarfism with fewer nodes and shorter internode lengths under long-day photoperiods.
mechanism: RIN1 functions as a positive regulator of node number and internode length by interacting with STF1 and STF2 to promote their degradation, thereby suppressing GA2ox7a and GA2ox7b expression and balancing gibberellin levels.

genes: STF2 (STF2, soybean HY5 homolog, Glycine max)
phenotype: STF2 over-expression lines exhibit a dwarf phenotype with shorter internode lengths.
mechanism: STF2 promotes gibberellin catabolism by up-regulating GA2ox7a and GA2ox7b expression, leading to reduced internode elongation.

genes: PbPAL1 (phenylalanine ammonia-lyase 1, involved in lignin biosynthesis, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbPAL1 resulted in significant changes in stone cell and lignin contents in pear fruits.
mechanism: NA

genes: PbPAL1 (phenylalanine ammonia-lyase 1, involved in lignin biosynthesis, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: PbPAL1-RNAi resulted in significant changes in stone cell and lignin contents in pear fruits.
mechanism: NA

mechanism: Formation of MBW regulatory complexes (MYB-bHLH-WDR) that transactivate ANR and LAR1 promoters, with TT2b and MYBPA2 showing stronger activation than MYB5.

genes: amiRNA-NOA1 (NOA1, artificial microRNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient reduction of endogenous NO levels via amiRNA-NOA1 expression increases WUS and CLV3 expression.
mechanism: NO signaling represses WUS expression and stem cell fate.

mechanism: NO acts indirectly via WUS to promote PZ identity and cell proliferation.

genes: mCherry-AGO4 (AGO4, argonaute, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: mCherry-AGO4 reporter expression is reduced by NO donor SNP treatment.
mechanism: NO signaling represses AGO4 expression and activity in the SAM.

genes: AlcR (AlcR, alcohol dehydrogenase repressor, synthetic), GUS (GUS, β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: p35S::AlcR; pAlcA::GUS control plants show unchanged endogenous NO levels.
mechanism: AlcR and GUS serve as controls for ethanol-inducible amiRNA experiments.

genes: WUS (WUS, WUSCHEL, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: WUS overexpression from CLV3 promoter creates a positive feedback loop expanding stem cell pools.
mechanism: WUS activity is suppressed in RdDM pathway mutants, indicating DNA methylation dependency.

genes: WUS (WUS, WUSCHEL, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: mCherry-GR-WUS expression is used for ChIP experiments to study WUS-AGO4 interaction.
mechanism: WUS physically interacts with AGO4, and this interaction is disrupted by NO signaling.

genes: AtTT10 (promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: High promoter activity in seed coat with low or no expression in other tissues in Thlaspi arvense and Camelina sativa
mechanism: Promoter drives gene expression specifically in the outer integument of the seed coat

genes: AtDP1 (promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: High promoter activity in seed coat with low or no expression in other tissues in Thlaspi arvense and Camelina sativa
mechanism: Promoter drives gene expression specifically in the outer integument of the seed coat

genes: BnOPR3 (jasmonate biosynthesis gene, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Complete male sterility in Brassica napus that can be restored by exogenous MeJA treatment, with anther indehiscence and no pollen grains observed in mutants
mechanism: BnOPR3 is involved in jasmonate (JA) biosynthesis; its disruption causes anther indehiscence and defective pollen maturation

genes: MIR2111-3 (miR2111, microRNA, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR2111 reduces lateral root numbers in Lotus japonicus.
mechanism: miR2111 targets TML for posttranscriptional regulation, reducing lateral root initiation.

genes: MIR2111b (miR2111, microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR2111 reduces lateral root initiation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: miR2111 represses HOLT, a positive regulator of lateral root initiation.

genes: MIR2111a/b (promoter, regulatory element, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS activity in phloem of leaf veins in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: MIR2111b (miR2111, microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Shoot-derived miR2111 reduces lateral root initiations in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: miR2111 systemically represses HOLT, a positive regulator of lateral root initiation.

genes: Brapa05T000840 (RRM1 gene family member, cold stress response, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Transgenic BrRBP (Brapa05T000840) Arabidopsis thaliana plants show notably higher survival rate under low temperature treatment compared to wild-type plants
mechanism: Enhanced cold tolerance via elevated reactive oxygen species-scavenging enzyme activity

genes: SiWAKL6 (SiWAKL6, involved in the salicylic acid signaling pathway and reactive oxygen species homeostasis, Sesamum indicum)
phenotype: Enhanced resistance to M. phaseolina by inducing the expression of genes involved in the salicylic acid signaling pathway and reconstructing reactive oxygen species homeostasis
mechanism: Inducing the expression of genes involved in the salicylic acid signaling pathway and reconstructing reactive oxygen species homeostasis

genes: AhUGT75A (flavonoid 7-O-UGT, Arachis hypogaea)
phenotype: Overexpression of AhUGT75A reduces malondialdehyde (MDA) and superoxide accumulation, enhancing drought and salt stress tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis.
mechanism: AhUGT75A confers abiotic stress tolerance through reactive oxygen species scavenging.

genes: Ugp1 (UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase 1, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of Ugp1 increases Pi uptake rate by 1.4-fold and total P concentration by 23-31% in shoots and roots under high Pi supply in rice.
mechanism: Ugp1 enhances Pi uptake by up-regulating PHT1;1 and PHT1;8 genes involved in Pi transport and homeostasis, increasing sucrose accumulation which acts as a systemic signal for Pi uptake regulation.

genes: miR159a (microRNA 159a, drought-responsive microRNA, Populus alba × Populus glandulosa)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR159a increases drought tolerance in poplar by reducing stomatal aperture (3.6–33.1% smaller), lowering water loss rate (48.51–49.02% fresh weight loss vs 66.63% in WT), and enhancing ROS scavenging (higher SOD and POD activity).
mechanism: miR159a reduces stomatal aperture and enhances ROS scavenging via upregulation of antioxidant enzymes (SOD, POD) and cleavage of MYB transcription factor targets (Pop_A03G020024, Pop_A09G059498), improving water use efficiency (WUE) and membrane stability (lower MDA and REC).

genes: miR159a-STTM (short tandem target mimic, miR159a suppressor, synthetic)
phenotype: miR159a suppression reduces drought tolerance in poplar, with increased stomatal aperture (3.6–33.1% larger), higher water loss rate (66.63% fresh weight loss vs 48.51–49.02% in OX159a), and reduced ROS scavenging (lower SOD and POD activity).
mechanism: miR159a-STTM increases stomatal aperture and reduces ROS scavenging capacity, leading to higher membrane damage (elevated MDA and REC) and reduced water use efficiency (WUE).

genes: HCC1 (LOC_Os01g19170, polygalacturonase, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: Knockout of HCC1 results in deep-green leaf phenotype with increased chlorophyll a and b contents (~15% higher than wild type) and reduced plant height, tillers, kernels per spike, 1000-grains weight, and seed setting rate in Oryza sativa L.
mechanism: HCC1 encodes a polygalacturonase (PG) that alters cell wall composition and represses PG activity. Mutation in HCC1 leads to decreased ethylene (ETH) content, reduced pectin hydrolysis, and disrupted ETH signaling pathway, which inhibits chlorophyll degradation.

genes: HCC1 (LOC_Os01g19170, polygalacturonase, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: Complementation of hcc1 with HCC1 rescues the deep-green leaf phenotype, restoring chlorophyll a and b contents to wild-type levels and normal agronomic traits (plant height, tillers, kernels per spike, 1000-grains weight, seed setting rate) in Oryza sativa L.
mechanism: Complementation restores HCC1 function, which encodes a polygalacturonase (PG) involved in cell wall remodeling and ethylene (ETH) pathway regulation. This rescues pectin metabolism, ETH signaling, and chlorophyll degradation.

genes: SsSMAX1 (Sapium sebiferum SMAX1, Sapium sebiferum)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of SsSMAX1 in Arabidopsis reduces seed germination frequency, increases hypocotyl length, and alters leaf morphology (longer petioles, increased leaf length, reduced leaf width) compared to wild-type and Atsmax1 mutants.
mechanism: SsSMAX1 regulates seed germination, hypocotyl elongation, and leaf development through karrikin signaling and auxin homeostasis pathways, similar to AtSMAX1 function in Arabidopsis.

genes: OsbHLH079 (OsbHLH079, basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsbHLH079 delays dark-induced and natural leaf senescence in rice, maintaining higher chlorophyll levels and delaying yellowing by 30-50 days after heading.
mechanism: OsbHLH079 suppresses ABA signaling by down-regulating ABA signaling genes (OsABF2, OsABF4, OsABI5, OsNAP) and repressing senescence-associated genes (SAGs) and chlorophyll degradation genes (CDGs).

genes: nisin (antibacterial peptide, Lactococcus lactis, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of nisin in carrot leaves produces antibacterial protein with activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli
mechanism: Nisin accumulates in endoplasmic reticulum (ER) via KDEL signal sequence, forming pores in bacterial membranes and inhibiting cell wall biosynthesis

genes: OsGLO1 (OsGLO1, rice glycolate oxidase 1, Oryza sativa), CmMS (CmMS, Cucurbita maxima malate synthase, Cucurbita maxima), OsAPX7 (OsAPX7, Oryza sativa ascorbate peroxidase 7, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: GMA rice shows increased photosynthetic rate (14%-21% higher net photosynthetic rate), enhanced light-saturated photosynthetic rate (14%-21% higher Amax), and increased grain yield (18%-26% higher under greenhouse conditions, 11%-19% higher under field conditions) compared to wild-type rice.
mechanism: The GMA bypass in chloroplasts increases CO2/O2 ratio by metabolizing glycolate to CO2, promoting Rubisco carboxylation and suppressing photorespiration. OsAPX7 detoxifies H2O2 more efficiently than OsCAT, and light-inducible pRbcS promoter regulates OsGLO1 expression to avoid photosynthate overaccumulation.

genes: At5g54370 (late embryogenesis abundant protein-like, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP-GUS (enhanced green fluorescent protein-beta-glucuronidase fusion, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP expression was restricted to the root-cap cells of homozygous 5-day-old At5g54370 promoter:eGFP-GUS plants
mechanism: The At5g54370 promoter drives eGFP-GUS expression specifically in root-cap cells

genes: JAL10 (jacalin-related lectin 10, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP-GUS (enhanced green fluorescent protein-beta-glucuronidase fusion, synthetic)
phenotype: JAL10 reporter gene expression was confined to the root-cap cells from imbibition to germination and after germination
mechanism: The JAL10 promoter drives eGFP-GUS expression specifically in root-cap cells

genes: JAL20 (jacalin-related lectin 20, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP-GUS (enhanced green fluorescent protein-beta-glucuronidase fusion, synthetic)
phenotype: JAL20 reporter gene expression was apparent from imbibition onward but visible throughout the entire root apical meristem, not only the root cap
mechanism: The JAL20 promoter drives eGFP-GUS expression in root apical meristem and root-cap cells

genes: CBF3 (C-REPEAT BINDING FACTOR 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CBF3 expression is enriched in the root endodermis and lateral root meristem, with higher expression levels in lateral root apical meristems than in primary root apical meristems.
mechanism: CBF3 is regulated by SHORT-ROOT (SHR) and functions downstream in the SHR network to regulate root development.

genes: CBF3 (C-REPEAT BINDING FACTOR 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of cbf3-1 mutant with mobile CBF3-YFP restores wild-type root growth and quiescent center (QC) organization.
mechanism: CBF3 movement from the endodermis to other meristematic tissues is required for regulation of root development and QC maintenance.

genes: CBF3 (C-REPEAT BINDING FACTOR 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of cbf3-1 mutant with CBF3-3X-mCherry fusion results in longer roots and abnormal QC organization.
mechanism: Reduced mobility of CBF3-3X-mCherry prevents proper regulation of root development and QC patterning.

genes: CBF3 (C-REPEAT BINDING FACTOR 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CBF3-YFP expression in ground tissue of RAM reveals protein movement to multiple meristematic tissues.
mechanism: CBF3 protein or transcript movement from the endodermis to other root tissues is required for developmental regulation.

genes: AtMYBS1 (AtMYBS1, negative regulator of heat tolerance, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtMYBS1 increases hypersensitivity to heat stress in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtMYBS1 negatively regulates MAX1 expression, which is part of the SL pathway involved in heat tolerance.

genes: MAX1 (MAX1, positive regulator of heat tolerance, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MAX1 increases heat tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MAX1 activates the SL pathway, enhancing heat-resistance mechanisms.

genes: MAX1 (MAX1, positive regulator of heat tolerance, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtMYBS1 (AtMYBS1, negative regulator of heat tolerance, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: MAX1 overexpression counteracts AtMYBS1-mediated repression of the SL pathway.

genes: AtMYBS1 (AtMYBS1, negative regulator of heat tolerance, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HA-tagged AtMYBS1 increases hypersensitivity to heat stress in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HA-tagged AtMYBS1 directly represses MAX1 expression via the MYB binding site.

genes: MAX1 (MAX1, positive regulator of heat tolerance, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: MAX1 activates the SL pathway, enhancing heat-resistance mechanisms.

mechanism: MAX1 overexpression counteracts AtMYBS1-mediated repression of the SL pathway.

genes: MAX3 (MAX3, positive regulator of heat tolerance, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: MAX3 activates the SL pathway, enhancing heat-resistance mechanisms.

genes: MAX4 (MAX4, positive regulator of heat tolerance, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: MAX4 activates the SL pathway, enhancing heat-resistance mechanisms.

mechanism: miR165a represses HD-ZIP gene expression by cleaving target transcripts or inhibiting translation.

phenotype: Overexpression of GR-LhG4 up-regulates a small number of genes in Arabidopsis thaliana ap1cal mutants.
mechanism: LhG4 acts as a transcriptional activator, up-regulating gene expression.

genes: gat (glyphosate acetyltransferase, bacterial, synthetic), gr79-epsps (5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase, bacterial, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic maize event GG2 exhibits high resistance to glyphosate (up to 14,400 g a.e. ha–1) with no negative effects on agronomic traits or yield
mechanism: GAT acetylates glyphosate to N-acetyl-glyphosate, while GR79-EPSPS confers resistance by shunting shikimate pathway

genes: Me3GT (flavone metabolism, Manihot esculenta)
phenotype: Gene silencing of Me3GT reduces flavone content in cassava storage roots.
mechanism: Me3GT is involved in flavone metabolism, affecting the levels of flavone metabolites in cassava.

mechanism: MeMYB4 regulates anthocyanin metabolism, controlling the coloration of cassava storage roots.

mechanism: UGT85K4 is involved in cyanogenic glucoside metabolism, affecting the levels of these compounds in cassava.

genes: UGT85K5 (cyanogenic glucoside metabolism, Manihot esculenta)
phenotype: Gene silencing of UGT85K5 reduces cyanogenic glucoside content in cassava storage roots.
mechanism: UGT85K5 is involved in cyanogenic glucoside metabolism, affecting the levels of these compounds in cassava.

phenotype: Overexpression of TRINITY_DN2608 gene elevated the susceptibility to drought stress possibly by suppressing the glucose level
mechanism: Suppressing glucose level

genes: FvePhyB (photoreceptor gene, Fragaria vesca)

mechanism: NA

genes: FvePhyB (photoreceptor gene, Fragaria vesca)

mechanism: NA

phenotype: Disruption of GuCSyGT leads to complete absence of soyasaponin I and its biosynthetic intermediates (soyasaponin III and SBMG) in hairy roots
mechanism: GuCSyGT catalyzes 3-O-glucuronosylation of soyasapogenol B in soyasaponin biosynthesis

genes: StSN2 (Soltu.DM.01G050660.1, full-length coding sequence, Solanum tuberosum), StBIN2 (Soltu.DM.03G001350.2, full-length coding sequence, Solanum tuberosum)

mechanism: StSN2 enhances StBIN2 expression and enzyme activity, which modulates ABA/BR signaling to maintain dormancy by suppressing BR signaling and promoting ABA signaling.

genes: StSN2 (Soltu.DM.01G050660.1, antisense sequence, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: RNAi of StSN2 accelerates tuber sprouting, with sprout length increased compared to wild type after 60 days of storage.
mechanism: Reduced StSN2 leads to lower StBIN2 expression and activity, disrupting ABA/BR signaling and promoting sprouting.

genes: GaTFL1 (terminal flower 1a, Gossypium hirsutum, Gossypium arboreum)
phenotype: Silencing of GaTFL1 results in terminal flowers and determinate growth architecture in Gossypium arboreum line DQJ, similar to dt1 mutant phenotype
mechanism: VIGS-mediated gene silencing of GaTFL1 disrupts indeterminate growth by altering shoot apical meristem (SAM) development

genes: NIP1 (NIP1, boron transporter, Dimocarpus longan), NIP19 (NIP19, boron transporter, Dimocarpus longan)

mechanism: NIP1 overexpression overcomes unilateral cross incompatibility between YD♀ × SX♂

mechanism: StPUB25 overexpression reduces oxidative damage by increasing POD activity and decreasing ROS/MDA accumulation, thereby enhancing drought tolerance.

genes: BpWOX11 (BpWOX11, homolog of AtWOX11 from Arabidopsis thaliana, Betula pendula)
phenotype: Overexpression of BpWOX11 increases rooting rate of cuttings by ~30-72% in Betula pendula compared to wild-type (33.33%)
mechanism: BpWOX11 promotes adventitious root (AR) formation by upregulating cell division genes (SCR, SHR) and expansin genes for cell wall loosening, and stress-related genes

phenotype: TaWRKY74s-RNAi transgenic plants displayed significantly fewer tillers compared to wild-type plants under normal conditions. mechanism: TaWRKY74s might regulate wheat tiller number through abscisic acid (ABA) and auxin signal transduction pathways

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)

mechanism: vv-miR156b represses VvSBP8/13, which compete with the MBW complex for anthocyanin biosynthesis regulation.

genes: RtNAC055 (NAC transcription factor, drought-responsive, R. trigyna)
phenotype: Overexpression of RtNAC055 in R. trigyna callus increases JA and H2O2 synthesis, enhances mannitol tolerance, and improves growth rate under drought stress.
mechanism: RtNAC055 promotes ROS accumulation in stomata via RtRbohE, accelerates stomatal closure, and upregulates proline synthesis (PtP5CS2) and antioxidant activity (SOD/POD).

genes: RtNAC055 (NAC transcription factor, drought-responsive, R. trigyna)
phenotype: Complementation of atnac055 mutant Arabidopsis with RtNAC055 rescues drought-sensitive phenotype, increases root length, and improves survival rate under drought stress.
mechanism: RtNAC055 reduces stomatal aperture, increases leaf surface temperature, and enhances stomatal closure via ROS accumulation in guard cells.

genes: RtNAC055 (NAC transcription factor, drought-responsive, R. trigyna)
phenotype: GUS staining of proRtNAC055 transgenic Arabidopsis shows expression in roots and stomatal guard cells, indicating roles in root development and stomatal movement.
mechanism: RtNAC055 promoter contains stress-response cis-elements (LTRs, ABREs, MYB-binding sites) and drives GUS expression in root and guard cells.

genes: LuxRAM (Vibrio fischeri, synthetic), CinRAM2 (Rhizobium leguminosarum, synthetic), LasRAM (Pseudomonas aeruginosa, synthetic), RpaRAM (Rhodopseudomonas palustris, synthetic), phosphinothricin acetyltransferase (synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of HSL receptor constructs in Arabidopsis thaliana results in 180-fold, 40-fold, and 7-fold induction of GFP expression in response to pC-HSL, OC12-HSL, and OHC14-HSL respectively, with no significant phenotypic differences compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: HSL-induced dimerization of regulators binds to the output promoter, activating GFP expression. The cassette includes a phosphinothricin acetyltransferase gene for herbicide resistance.

genes: LuxRAM (Vibrio fischeri, synthetic), CinRAM2 (Rhizobium leguminosarum, synthetic), LasRAM (Pseudomonas aeruginosa, synthetic), RpaRAM (Rhodopseudomonas palustris, synthetic), hygromycin resistance (synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of the pC-HSL receiver in potato (S. tuberosum) results in a small decrease in fresh and dry stem weight, a small increase in chlorophyll content index, and 10-fold upregulation of gfp transcripts upon 100 µM pC-HSL induction.
mechanism: HSL-induced dimerization of regulators binds to the output promoter, activating GFP expression. The cassette includes a hygromycin resistance gene for selection.

genes: trpE8 (anthranilate synthase alpha subunit, feedback-resistant, Escherichia coli), trpD (anthranilate synthase beta subunit, feedback-resistant, Escherichia coli), aroG4 (3-deoxy-D-arabino-heptulosonate-7-phosphate synthase, feedback-resistant mutant, Escherichia coli), Nt-JAT2 (vinca alkaloid transporter, Nicotiana tabacum)
gene_construct: CaMV35S-trpE8-aldolase signal sequence-HSP-T---CaMV35S-aroG4-aldolase signal sequence-HSP-T---CaMV35S-trpD-aldolase signal sequence-HSP-T---CaMV35S-Nt-JAT2-HSP-T
phenotype: Overexpression of feedback-resistant tryptophan pathway genes increases free tryptophan content by 3-7x (0.23-0.44 µmol/g F.W.) and elevates catharanthine (1.88-3.33 µmol/g F.W.), ajmalicine, and vindoline levels in Catharanthus roseus leaves.
mechanism: Feedback-resistant microbial enzymes (trpE8, trpD, aroG4) bypass endogenous regulatory checkpoints in tryptophan biosynthesis, increasing precursor availability for alkaloid pathways. Nt-JAT2 may facilitate alkaloid transport but showed no significant effect in this study.

genes: aadA (aadA gene, spectinomycin/streptomycin resistance, Nicotiana tabacum), GFP (GFP reporter gene, reporter, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Integration of aadA and GFP into plastid DNA via homologous recombination, with GFP expression in plastids of N. benthamiana meristems.
mechanism: Homologous recombination between homology arms (trnV-rps12/7 region) and plastid DNA, followed by expression of aadA and GFP under N. tabacum chloroplast regulatory sequences.

genes: LATE (LATE, C2H2 zinc finger protein with EAR motif, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Genome-edited plants did not show early flowering phenotype under long-day and short-day conditions.
mechanism: LATE may function redundantly with unknown proteins in flowering regulation.

genes: LATE (LATE, C2H2 zinc finger protein with EAR motif, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: LATE:VP16 fusion increased transactivation activity by 1.75-fold in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts.
mechanism: VP16 activation domain fused to LATE enhances transactivation activity.

genes: LATE (LATE, C2H2 zinc finger protein with EAR motif, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: LATE:SRDX fusion showed comparable repression activity to LATE in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts.
mechanism: SRDX repression domain fused to LATE does not enhance repression activity.

genes: smGFP (soluble modified GFP, derived from plasmids pEGFP-1 and pBICGFP), eGFP (enhanced GFP, derived from plasmid pEGFP-1)
phenotype: Overexpression of smGFP in N. benthamiana 16c line leads to green fluorescence, which is silenced by agroinfiltration with pAT-smGFP or pAT006 vectors.
mechanism: Transcriptional gene silencing (TGS) via siRNAs derived from the CaMV 35S promoter; post-transcriptional gene silencing (PTGS) via siRNAs derived from the GFP coding sequence.

genes: NA
phenotype: Agroinfiltration with pAT006 (empty vector) induces transcriptional gene silencing (TGS) of the CaMV 35S promoter in N. benthamiana 16c line, leading to reduced green fluorescence.
mechanism: TGS via siRNAs derived from the CaMV 35S promoter, likely due to homology between the T-DNA promoter and the host nuclear DNA.

genes: smGFP (soluble modified GFP, derived from plasmid pBICGFP)
phenotype: Overexpression of smGFP in N. benthamiana 16c line leads to green fluorescence, which is silenced by agroinfiltration with pRI-smGFP, but TGS is suppressed compared to pAT-smGFP.
mechanism: Post-transcriptional gene silencing (PTGS) via siRNAs derived from the smGFP coding sequence; suppression of TGS due to the Arabidopsis HSP terminator.

genes: eGFP (enhanced GFP, derived from plasmid pEGFP-1)
phenotype: Overexpression of eGFP in N. benthamiana 16c line leads to green fluorescence, which is silenced by agroinfiltration with pRI-eGFP, with delayed TGS induction compared to smGFP.
mechanism: Post-transcriptional gene silencing (PTGS) via siRNAs derived from the eGFP coding sequence; delayed TGS due to lower sequence homology with host nuclear DNA.

genes: NA
phenotype: Agroinfiltration with pRI-SA (shortened T-DNA with CaMV 35S promoter and NOS terminator) induces TGS in N. benthamiana 16c line, leading to reduced green fluorescence at 7 dpi.
mechanism: TGS via siRNAs derived from the CaMV 35S promoter, with faster induction compared to pRI201-AN due to shorter T-DNA.

genes: NA
phenotype: Agroinfiltration with pRI-EH (NOS promoter and NOS terminator) does not induce TGS in N. benthamiana 16c line, with no reduction in green fluorescence.
mechanism: Absence of CaMV 35S promoter homology with host DNA prevents TGS induction.

phenotype: Higher levels of cell division were observed in both the stomatal lineage and epidermal cells of the OsCYCD2;2-overexpressing plants.
mechanism: NA

phenotype: Higher levels of cell division were observed in both the stomatal lineage and epidermal cells of the OsCYCD6;1-overexpressing plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsCYCD7;1 (OsCYCD7;1, cyclin D, rice)
phenotype: Lower levels of cell division were observed in the OsCYCD7;1-overexpressing plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: SiABI5.12 (SiABI5.12, ABI5 gene from foxtail millet, foxtail millet)
phenotype: Overexpression of SiABI5.12 confers tolerance to osmotic stress in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NA

genes: FaLEA167 (FaLEA167, LEA1 group member, strawberry)
phenotype: Overexpression of FaLEA167 increases green fruit percentage while reducing full red fruit proportion, decreases anthocyanins content and a* value (color redness indicator), and increases citric acid, soluble protein and malondialdehyde content
mechanism: FaLEA167 negatively regulates strawberry fruit ripening

genes: OsGP1 (vegetative cell wall protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsGP1 increases soda saline-alkali stress tolerance in rice, with higher fresh weight and plant height, lower MDA content, and higher SOD and POD activities compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: OsGP1 enhances cell wall strength and ROS scavenging to maintain cellular homeostasis under stress.

genes: LcSPL2 (SPL transcription factor, Liriodendron chinense, Liriodendron chinense)
phenotype: Overexpression of LcSPL2 accelerates flowering and reduces the number of rosette leaves in A. thaliana under long-day conditions
mechanism: Ectopic expression of LcSPL2 increases the expression of AtSOC1, AtFT, AtFUL, and AtAP1, promoting flowering

genes: OsNOMT (sakuranetin biosynthetase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNOMT increases sakuranetin accumulation in rice seedlings and reduces its presence in roots and seeds.
mechanism: OsNOMT catalyzes the conversion of naringenin to sakuranetin, leading to its accumulation in tissues where the gene is expressed.

genes: OsNOMT (sakuranetin biosynthetase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Constitutive overexpression of OsNOMT increases sakuranetin in rice shoots but not in seeds.
mechanism: OsNOMT overexpression under the CaMV35S promoter enhances sakuranetin biosynthesis in vegetative tissues.

genes: OsNOMT (sakuranetin biosynthetase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Endosperm-specific overexpression of OsNOMT increases sakuranetin in rice seeds and enhances blast resistance.
mechanism: OsNOMT overexpression under the OsGluD-1 promoter drives sakuranetin accumulation in endosperm, acting as a phytoalexin against rice blast.

genes: RcFAH12 (RcFAH12, fatty acid hydroxylase, castor)
phenotype: Overexpression of RcFAH12 in a fae1 mutant of Arabidopsis led to the accumulation of HFA content up to 17% in the seed oil (called the 'CL37 line')
mechanism: RcFAH12 converts 18:1 of the sn-2 position of PC to 18:1-OH, but without DGAT or PDAT to transfer HFA into TAG

genes: RcPDAT1-2 (RcPDAT1-2, phospholipid:diacylglycerol acyltransferase, castor)
phenotype: Introduction of RcPDAT1-2 into CL37 increased HFA content up to 25% due to efficient transfer of HFAs from PC to TAG (called the 'P327 line')
mechanism: RcPDAT1-2 synthesizes TAG by transferring HFA at the sn-2 position of PC to DAG

genes: OsERF1 (ethylene-responsive transcription factor, rice, synthetic)
phenotype: ERF1-hdr line shows increased pre-harvest sprouting (PHS) resistance with <10% germination at 11 DAI compared to 30% in Dongjin control
mechanism: HDR-induced structural changes in ERF1 protein alter ABA signaling pathway, increasing endogenous ABA levels and upregulating ABA-related genes (PYL, SnRK2, ABI3, ABI5, Sdr4)

genes: RGA1 (rice, splice site mutation causing premature stop codon, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Introduction of the RGA1 mutant allele into two indica rice varieties resulted in small and round rice grains with less chalkiness.
mechanism: The SNP at the splice site of the first intron disrupted the normal splicing of the RGA1 transcript precursor, resulting in a premature stop codon. This mutation is associated with regulation of ABA metabolism and suppression of rice seed germination and shoot growth.

genes: PbrGA2ox1 (PbrGA2ox1, GA 2-oxidase, Pyrus sp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbrGA2ox1 increases Chl accumulation in chlorotic pear leaves.
mechanism: PbrGA2ox1 facilitates chloroplast development by increasing chloroplast number per cell and compacting the thylakoid granum stacks.

genes: PbrGA2ox1 (PbrGA2ox1, GA 2-oxidase, Pyrus sp.)
phenotype: Silencing of PbrGA2ox1 leads to Chl degradation in normal pear leaves.
mechanism: PbrGA2ox1 silencing leads to chloroplast degradation as evidenced by the chlorosis phenomenon.

genes: PbrGA2ox1 (PbrGA2ox1, GA 2-oxidase, Pyrus sp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbrGA2ox1 increases Chl accumulation in tobacco plants, evidenced by significantly higher Pn and Fv/Fm.
mechanism: PbrGA2ox1 overexpression increases abscisic acid (ABA), methyl jasmonate (MeJA), and salicylic acid (SA) concentrations and signaling pathways; elevates reducing and soluble sugar contents; and reduces starch and sucrose levels.

genes: AtCLV3 (CLV3, signaling peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Deletions in the 5' region of AtCLV3 produced weak phenotypes, with AtCLV3Reg5'-11 showing ~3-4 locules per fruit compared to ~2 in wild type and >5 in Atclv3 null mutants.
mechanism: Redundant cis-regulatory elements (CREs) upstream and downstream of AtCLV3 interact synergistically to maintain function.

genes: AtCLV3 (CLV3, signaling peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Deletions in the 3' region of AtCLV3 (e.g., AtCLV3Reg3'-1 and AtCLV3Reg3'-3) showed weak phenotypes, resembling AtCLV3Reg5'-11.
mechanism: Redundant cis-regulatory elements (CREs) upstream and downstream of AtCLV3 interact synergistically to maintain function.

genes: SlCLV3 (CLV3, signaling peptide, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Complete deletion of the 5' region of SlCLV3 (SlCLV3pro-28) produced a null-like phenotype on locule number, while smaller deletions showed weaker effects.
mechanism: Upstream cis-regulatory elements (CREs) dominate SlCLV3 regulation, with minimal contribution from downstream CREs.

genes: SlCLV3 (CLV3, signaling peptide, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Deletions in the 3' region of SlCLV3 showed weak or no effects on locule number, with some alleles exhibiting minor phenotypic changes.
mechanism: Upstream cis-regulatory elements (CREs) dominate SlCLV3 regulation, with minimal contribution from downstream CREs.

genes: DEK1 (Linker-Calpain domains of DEK1, Physcomitrium patens)
phenotype: Overexpression of DEK1 Linker-Calpain domains enhances secondary filament extension, increases percentage of filaments forming buds, and increases gametophore bud initiation rate per filament in Physcomitrium patens.
mechanism: DEK1 cleavage of activating/repressing TFs can inhibit/activate the expression of all downstream target genes, indirectly regulating gene expression.

genes: ADARcd (catalytic domain of ADAR from Drosophila melanogaster, source), MS2 (MS2 coat protein from bacteriophage MS2, source), NLS (nuclear localisation signal, source)
phenotype: ADARcd and MS2-ADARcd cause editing of MS2-containing reporter RNAs, with MS2-ADARcd showing significant A-to-G editing at multiple sites in the reporter RNA.
mechanism: ADARcd, when fused to MS2, edits RNA at sites bound by the MS2 protein/RNA interaction, leading to A-to-G conversions in the reporter RNA.

genes: PcOMT10 (PcOMT10, O-methyltransferase, Polygonatum cyrtonema), PcOMT11 (PcOMT11, O-methyltransferase, Polygonatum cyrtonema), PcOMT12 (PcOMT12, O-methyltransferase, Polygonatum cyrtonema), PcOMT13 (PcOMT13, O-methyltransferase, Polygonatum cyrtonema)
phenotype: Overexpression of PcOMT12 increases chrysoeriol-6,8-di-C-glucoside content in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves by ~significant amount.

phenotype: Overexpression of PcOMT12 increases chrysoeriol-6,8-di-C-glucoside content in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves by ~significant amount.

genes: PheSnRK2.9 (Phyllostachys edulis, PheSnRK2.9, Phyllostachys edulis)
phenotype: Overexpression of PheSnRK2.9 inhibits root growth and increases leaf starch accumulation in Arabidopsis thaliana under salt stress.
mechanism: PheSnRK2.9 binds to phosphatidic acid (PA), inhibiting starch degradation under starvation conditions and enhancing salt tolerance.

genes: SMB (SMB, NAC transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of smb-3 rescued halotropic root bending in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SMB regulates asymmetric auxin distribution in the root cap to promote halotropism by transcriptionally activating AUX1.

genes: SMB-GR (SMB fused with rat glucocorticoid receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Inducible overexpression of SMB-GR under DEX treatment enhanced halotropic root bending in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SMB-GR promotes auxin redistribution in the root cap, leading to increased halotropic sensitivity.

genes: nls-3xVENUS (nuclear localization signal fused with 3xVENUS, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of nls-3xVENUS under the SMB promoter in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: iaaH (indole-3-acetamide hydrolase, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of iaaH under the SMB promoter in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: SMB-GFP (SMB fused with GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of smb-3 with SMB-GFP under native promoter rescued halotropic root bending in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SMB-GFP restores auxin redistribution in the root cap, enabling halotropic response.

genes: KAKU4 (KAKU4, KAKU4 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation rescued accelerated leaf senescence in kaku4 mutant; overexpression caused delayed leaf senescence with higher chlorophyll content compared to wild type
mechanism: KAKU4 regulates H3K27me3 deposition on genes involved in SA, JA, ABA signaling, H2O2 metabolism, and leaf senescence pathways

genes: BrrFT1 (BrrFT1, FT homologue from turnip, turnip), BrrFT2 (BrrFT2, FT homologue from turnip, turnip), BrrFT3 (BrrFT3, FT homologue from turnip, turnip), BrrFT4 (BrrFT4, FT homologue from turnip, turnip)
phenotype: All four BrrFT proteins localized to both nucleus and cytoplasm in N. benthamiana leaf cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: rolB (root locus B, T-DNA gene from Agrobacterium rhizogenes, Agrobacterium rhizogenes)
phenotype: Induction of hairy roots with transformation efficiency up to 80.55% in V. erianthum using A13 strain
mechanism: T-DNA transfer from Agrobacterium rhizogenes plasmid integrates into plant genome, altering auxin/cytokinin balance to induce hairy root formation

genes: TaPIF4 (TraesCS5B02G380200, transcription factor, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Impaired heat tolerance compared to controls (72.9% vs. 25.0% vs. 27.08% of SSRH in Fielder vs. Tapif4-2 vs. Tapif4-7).
mechanism: TaPIF4 regulates heat-responsive genes including TaMBF1c, which is down-regulated in knockout lines.

genes: TaPIF4D (TraesCS5B02G380200, transcription factor, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Higher seedling survival rate under heat stress (29.17% vs. 79.17% vs. 81.25% of SSRH in WT [Fielder] vs. TaPIF4D-OE-3 vs. TaPIF4D-OE-9).
mechanism: Enhanced protein stability and phosphorylation of TaPIF4D, leading to increased activation of heat response genes like TaMBF1c.

phenotype: Sustained autonomous bioluminescence with signal strengths suitable for bioluminescence imaging in transgenic Nicotiana benthamiana plants
mechanism: Hispidin biosynthesis via PpASCL enables the bioluminescence pathway, with nnLuz catalyzing the light-emitting reaction

plant_species: Ziziphus jujuba, Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa

genes: ZjACO3 (aconitase 3, Ziziphus jujuba, Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa)

genes: ZjbHLH113 (bHLH transcription factor 113, Ziziphus jujuba)

mechanism: ZjbHLH113 binds to the ZjACO3 promoter, activating its expression to enhance citric acid degradation.

genes: CsGGT4 (CsGGT4, γ-glutamyl transpeptidase, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsGGT4 in tobacco leaves significantly increases theanine levels compared to empty vector controls.
mechanism: CsGGT4 synthesizes and degrades theanine in tobacco cells, demonstrating functional differences from theanine hydrolase CsGGT2.

genes: CsGGT4 (CsGGT4, γ-glutamyl transpeptidase, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Silencing CsGGT4 in tea leaves significantly reduces theanine levels and slightly increases ethylamine levels.
mechanism: CsGGT4 silencing inhibits theanine synthetase activity in tea leaves, indicating its role in theanine synthesis.

genes: CsGGT4 (CsGGT4, γ-glutamyl transpeptidase, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of CsGGT4 in N. benthamiana confirms its role in theanine synthesis and degradation.
mechanism: CsGGT4 exhibits dual enzymatic activity for theanine synthesis and degradation in heterologous expression systems.

genes: ZmBON1 (ZmBON1, loss-of-function, Zea mays), ZmBON3 (ZmBON3, loss-of-function, Zea mays)
phenotype: Knockout of ZmBON1 leads to dwarfism in maize, with enhanced dwarfism in Zmbon1 Zmbon3 double mutants.
mechanism: ZmBON1 is involved in brassinosteroid (BR) signaling, and its loss reduces BR sensitivity, leading to growth defects.

genes: SERK4 (SERK4, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SERK4-FLAG transgenic plants were generated in pad4-1 and bon1-1 bon2-2 bon3-3 pad4-1 backgrounds for studying BRI1-SERK complex formation.
mechanism: SERK4 interacts with BON1 and BRI1 to form the BR receptor complex, which is critical for BR signaling.

genes: SBEIIa (starch branching enzyme, Hordeum vulgare, Hordeum vulgare), SBEIIb (starch branching enzyme, Hordeum vulgare, Hordeum vulgare), SBEI (starch branching enzyme, Hordeum vulgare, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Increased amylose content to >99% of starch fraction in barley
mechanism: Simultaneous reduction of SBEIIa, SBEIIb, and SBEI expression by >90% blocks amylopectin formation

genes: ZmMADS42 (transcription factor involved in reproductive development, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmMADS42 promotes meristem tissue growth and enables plants to enter reproductive growth earlier.
mechanism: ZmMADS42 enhances reproductive growth by promoting meristem development and accelerating the transition to reproductive stages.

genes: ZmMADS42-GFP (fusion with GFP for subcellular localization, Zea mays)
phenotype: ZmMADS42 is localized in the nucleus of tobacco mesophyll cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: CKX5 (CKX5, cytokinin oxidase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: CKX5 enhances resistance by increasing cytokinin degradation, thereby counteracting the benefits Botrytis cinerea gains from cytokinins

genes: DA2 (DA2, negative regulator of seed size, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: DA1-UBI2 constitutively activates DA1 protease activity, restricting growth.

genes: DA1 (DA1, peptidase, Arabidopsis thaliana), Ubiquitin (synthetic, synthetic)

genes: DA2 (DA2, negative regulator of seed size, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, foreign)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under DA2 promoter in da2-1 mutants.

genes: DA2C59S (DA2 mutant, RING domain mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, foreign)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under DA2 promoter in da2-1 mutants with RING domain mutation.
mechanism: NA

genes: HvAGO4a (HvAGO4a, barley AGO4 homolog, Hordeum vulgare), HvAGO4b (HvAGO4b, barley AGO4 homolog, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Complementation of ago4-3 mutant restores AGO4 function, including regulation of AtSN1 retrotransposon methylation and expression, and suppression of heat stress-induced transposon activation.
mechanism: Barley HvAGO4 proteins bind 24-nt sRNAs and mediate DNA methylation at target loci, restoring RdDM pathway functionality in Arabidopsis ago4-3 mutants.

genes: OsUBC12 (Oryza sativa, Oryza sativa), OsUBC12C92A (synthetic, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsUBC12 accelerates seed germination at low temperature (15 °C) and reduces ABA sensitivity, while OsUBC12C92A overexpression shows reduced germination promotion and ABA sensitivity compared to wild type.
mechanism: OsUBC12 negatively regulates ABA signaling by promoting the degradation of OsSnRK1.1 via K48-linked polyubiquitination, thereby enhancing low-temperature germination.

genes: OsUBC12 (Oryza sativa, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of OsUBC12 (osubc12 mutants) results in delayed low-temperature germination (15 °C) and increased ABA sensitivity compared to wild type.
mechanism: OsUBC12 knockout leads to elevated ABA signaling via increased OsABI5 and OsRAB21 expression, inhibiting germination at low temperatures.

genes: OsUBC12 (Oryza sativa, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: The transposon insertion in the OsUBC12 promoter (Koshihikari) increases promoter activity and OsUBC12 expression compared to the IR64 promoter, enhancing low-temperature germination.
mechanism: The transposon insertion in the OsUBC12 promoter up-regulates OsUBC12 expression, which in turn promotes low-temperature germination by modulating ABA signaling.

genes: GhN/AINV23 (GhN/AINV23, alpha-amylase inhibitor 23, Gossypium hirsutum)

mechanism: CspB promotes drought tolerance by preserving normal plant functions under water stress, including better grain set under drought conditions and maintaining ear length, kernel number, and grain weight.

genes: RBE (RBE, repressor of cell expansion, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: RBE recruits TPL-HDA19 complex to repress TCP5 transcription, inhibiting cell expansion during petal development.

genes: RBE (RBE, repressor of cell expansion, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: The EAR motif is necessary for RBE function; mRBE lacks this motif and cannot recruit TPL-HDA19 to repress TCP5.

genes: RBE (RBE, repressor of cell expansion, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of deleted RBE (dRBE) does not alter petal blade size or cell expansion in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: The EAR motif is necessary for RBE function; dRBE lacks this motif and cannot recruit TPL-HDA19 to repress TCP5.

genes: RBE (RBE, repressor of cell expansion, Arabidopsis thaliana), TPL (TPL, transcriptional corepressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of mRBE-TPL fusion protein recapitulates the small petal phenotype of RBE-OX in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Fusing TPL to mRBE compensates for the loss of EAR motif function, restoring TPL recruitment to repress TCP5.

genes: RBE (RBE, repressor of cell expansion, Arabidopsis thaliana), TPL (TPL, transcriptional corepressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of dRBE-TPL fusion protein recapitulates the small petal phenotype of RBE-OX in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Fusing TPL to dRBE compensates for the loss of EAR motif function, restoring TPL recruitment to repress TCP5.

genes: HDA19 (HDA19, histone deacetylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: HDA19 requires RBE recruitment to repress TCP5; overexpression alone is insufficient for repression.

genes: RBE (RBE, repressor of cell expansion, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of GR-RBE induces epigenetic repression of TCP5, delaying its transcription for several days in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GR-RBE recruits TPL-HDA19 to repress TCP5 via chromatin remodeling, creating an epigenetic memory that persists until cell division dilutes the repression.

genes: GCR1 (Gland Cell Repressor 1, transcription factor with MYB-like domain, tomato), GCR2 (Gland Cell Repressor 2, transcription factor with MYB-like domain, tomato)
phenotype: Knockout of GCR1/2 dramatically promotes gland formation in tomato trichomes, with 96% of trichomes producing glandular structures in the double mutant. Trichomes become significantly elongated with increased cell numbers.
mechanism: GCR1/2 act as repressors of gland formation by inhibiting LFS expression and maintaining non-glandular trichome fate through self-inhibition and interaction with SlTOE1B/TPL2 complexes.

genes: GCR1 (Gland Cell Repressor 1, transcription factor with MYB-like domain, tomato), GCR2 (Gland Cell Repressor 2, transcription factor with MYB-like domain, tomato)
phenotype: Forced expression of GCR1/2 in trichome apical cells by the MTR1 promoter entirely inhibits gland formation, resulting in defective trichomes with only 1–2 cells.
mechanism: GCR1/2 repress gland formation by maintaining non-glandular trichome fate through self-inhibition and interaction with SlTOE1B/TPL2 complexes.

genes: SlTOE1B (Solanum lycopersicum TOE1B, AP2/ERF transcription factor, tomato), rSlTOE1B (miR172-resistant form of SlTOE1B, tomato)
phenotype: Forced expression of miR172-resistant SlTOE1B (rSlTOE1B) under the MTR1 promoter promotes gland formation, with all non-glandular trichomes replaced by digital glandular trichomes at 2-fold expression and increased glandular cells in both DGT and PGT at 10-fold expression.
mechanism: SlTOE1B antagonizes GCR1/2 by enhancing their self-inhibition and recruiting TPL2 to form a repressive complex, promoting gland formation.

genes: SlTOE1B (Solanum lycopersicum TOE1B, AP2/ERF transcription factor, tomato)
phenotype: cr-sltoe1b mutants show reduced digital glandular trichomes (DGT) and increased non-glandular trichomes (NGT), indicating that SlTOE1B promotes gland formation.
mechanism: SlTOE1B antagonizes GCR1/2 by enhancing their self-inhibition and recruiting TPL2 to form a repressive complex, promoting gland formation.

genes: LFS (Leafless, AP2 transcription factor, tomato)
phenotype: cr-lfs mutants lose glands of digital glandular trichomes (DGT) and show reduced glands in peltate glandular trichomes (PGT) in homozygous lines.
mechanism: LFS promotes peltate trichome formation; its knockout disrupts gland formation, indicating it is downstream of GCR1/2.

genes: TPL2 (Topless 2, transcriptional co-repressor, tomato)
phenotype: tpl2 mutants display increased glands (mostly in peltate trichomes) and branched trichomes (mostly in digital trichomes).
mechanism: TPL2 forms a repressive complex with GCR1/2 and SlTOE1B to maintain non-glandular trichome fate by inhibiting LFS expression.

genes: miR156B (microRNA 156B, regulatory RNA, tomato)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of miR156B by either the 35S or MTR1 promoter promotes gland formation, with increased SlTOE1B expression and repressed GCR1/2 expression.
mechanism: miR156B promotes gland formation by upregulating SlTOE1B and downregulating GCR1/2, acting downstream of GCR1/2 in gland regulation.

phenotype: Overexpression of HSFA7b in Arabidopsis thaliana shoot apical meristem (SAM) during thermomemory, leading to altered ethylene response and enhanced thermotolerance.
mechanism: HSFA7b overexpression activates ethylene biosynthesis and signaling pathways by directly regulating genes like ETO1, EOL1, and EIN3, modulating ethylene homeostasis at the SAM during thermopriming.

genes: TLR3 (Trichomeless Regulator 3, transcription factor, Artemisia annua)
phenotype: Overexpression of TLR3 in Arabidopsis suppresses trichome formation, reducing trichome density by ~40% and altering trichome branching (1-2 branches instead of 3). Root hair density is also reduced.
mechanism: TLR3 upregulates negative regulators of trichome development (CPC, TRY) and root hair development (WER, ZHD8, SCN1), acting as a negative regulator of trichome and root hair formation.

genes: TLR3 (Trichomeless Regulator 3, transcription factor, Artemisia annua)
phenotype: TLR3 RNAi in A. annua increases trichome density by 45-69% and artemisinin content by 60-80%, with normal trichome morphology and cuticle structure.
mechanism: TLR3 RNAi upregulates trichome development genes and artemisinin biosynthesis genes, counteracting the negative regulatory effects of TLR3 overexpression.

genes: TLR3 (Trichomeless Regulator 3, transcription factor, Artemisia annua)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated TLR3 editing in A. annua increases trichome density by 75-100% and artemisinin content by 60-90%, with normal trichome morphology and cuticle structure.
mechanism: TLR3 gene editing upregulates trichome development genes and artemisinin biosynthesis genes, reversing the negative regulatory effects of TLR3 overexpression.

genes: TLR3 (Trichomeless Regulator 3, transcription factor, Artemisia annua)
phenotype: Overexpression of TLR3-intron in Arabidopsis results in a more pronounced trichome suppression phenotype compared to TLR3-OE lines, with significantly lower trichome density.
mechanism: The intron-containing TLR3 variant enhances the negative regulatory effect on trichome development, possibly through altered gene expression or splicing.

genes: TLR3 (Trichomeless Regulator 3, transcription factor, Artemisia annua)
phenotype: TLR3 promoter-GUS reporter in A. annua shows strong GUS staining in callus stage S3 and stoma regions of mature plants, indicating TLR3 expression during trichome development.
mechanism: The TLR3 promoter drives GUS expression in trichome-rich tissues, confirming TLR3's role in trichome development.

genes: AelMLKL (Pm13a, powdery mildew resistance gene, Aegilops longissima)
phenotype: Transgenic wheat cultivar Fielder overexpressing AelMLKL shows complete resistance to powdery mildew (infection type IT 0) compared to susceptible control (IT 4).
mechanism: AelMLKL mediates resistance through MLKL_NTD domain-induced cell death and STK domain kinase activity, triggering immune responses against Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici (Bgt).

genes: SPP (Signal Peptide Peptidase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of SPP in 79–1 and 171–1 suppressor mutants restores pi4kβ1,2-like size, autoimmunity, and root length defects.
mechanism: SPP is localized to the ER and functions in ER stress response, which is dysregulated in pi4kβ1,2.

genes: SPP171-1 (Signal Peptide Peptidase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: SPP171−1 is a dominant-negative allele that reduces ER stress sensitivity in pi4kβ1,2.

mechanism: SPP is an ER-localized protease involved in ER stress response and protein processing.

genes: HsSPP (Signal Peptide Peptidase, Homo sapiens)
phenotype: Human SPP complements the phenotype of the suppressor 79–1, partially restoring pi4kβ1,2-like dwarfism and root defects.
mechanism: HsSPP functions similarly to Arabidopsis SPP in ER stress response and immune regulation.

genes: HC (heavy chain of 5C4, codon-optimized murine variable region fused to human IgG1 constant region (GenBank AAX09634.1), synthetic), LC (light chain of 5C4, codon-optimized murine variable region fused to human IgG1 kappa constant region (GenBank AAD29610.1), synthetic)
phenotype: Production of anti-RSV monoclonal antibodies 5C4 and CR9501 in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves with yields up to 33.5 mg/kg (5C4) and 12.0 mg/kg (CR9501) of fresh leaf weight.
mechanism: Transient expression via Agrobacterium-mediated infiltration using geminiviral vector pBYR2eK2Md with CaMV 35S promoter, SP2 signal peptide, and SEKDEL ER retention signal. Co-expression of HC and LC leads to antibody assembly and purification via protein A chromatography.

genes: DlLFY (LEAFY gene involved in flowering control, Dimocarpus longan)
phenotype: Overexpression of DlLFY in Arabidopsis promoted early flowering and restrained growth, resulting in reduced plant height and rosette leaf number and area in transgenic plants.
mechanism: DlLFY interacts with TFL1 (terminal flower 1) to inhibit its function, as AtTFL1 was strongly inhibited in transgenic lines.

genes: SD1 (LOC_Os01g66100, gibberellin 20-oxidase (GA20ox2), Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of SD1 reduces shoot length by ~18.5% in Nipponbare rice seedlings compared to wild type.
mechanism: SD1 encodes gibberellin 20-oxidase (GA20ox2), a key enzyme in gibberellic acid biosynthesis. Knockout disrupts GA biosynthesis, reducing shoot elongation.

genes: OsRibA1 (OsRibA1, rate-limiting enzyme in riboflavin pathway, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsRibA1 in rice callus increases riboflavin content by 28%
mechanism: OsRibA1 is the rate-limiting step in the riboflavin biosynthesis pathway

mechanism: Enhances enzymatic antioxidant activities (superoxide dismutase, peroxidase, catalase, phenylalanine ammonia-lyase) and facilitates Na+ transport in salt stress

mechanism: GFP-ATG8 is driven by the tapetum-specific promoter NtTPE8, allowing visualization of autophagosomes in the integumentary tapetum.

genes: PeGIF3 (PeGIF3, gene involved in leaf development, Populus euphratica)
phenotype: Overexpression of PeGIF3 in Arabidopsis thaliana results in leaf expansion along the medial-lateral axis and increased leaf cell count.
mechanism: PeGIF3 enhances leaf cell proliferation, thereby resulting in the expansion of the central-lateral region of the leaf.

genes: ALR1 (Arabidopsis thaliana receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), ALR1CD (cytoplasmic domain of ALR1, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: ALR1 (Arabidopsis thaliana receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: ALR1 (Arabidopsis thaliana receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Cys939/944/985/987 in ALR1 are essential for Al binding and kinase activity. Kinase-dead mutation (K762R) abolished PSK response.

genes: ALR1 (Arabidopsis thaliana receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
