phenotype: Overexpression of PsMYB65 increases PsCYCD3;1 expression, promoting cell cycle progression and budbreak.
mechanism: PsMYB65 directly binds to the promoter of PsCYCD3;1 to activate its expression.

genes: FKF1 (FKF1, blue-light photoreceptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FKF1 complements the late-flowering phenotype of the fkf1 mutant, reducing the average leaf number at bolting from 44.0 to 23.2.
mechanism: FKF1 induces FT mRNA expression in the evening through multiple feedforward mechanisms, promoting flowering.

genes: FKF1 (FKF1 I160R, blue-light photoreceptor with I160R mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The FKF1 I160R variant promotes earlier flowering, with transgenic lines flowering significantly earlier than wild-type plants under long-day conditions.
mechanism: The I160R mutation enhances FKF1's function in regulating flowering time by increasing FT mRNA levels while reducing homodimerization and increasing interaction with GI and COP1.

genes: FKF1 (FKF1, blue-light photoreceptor, Arabidopsis thaliana), ZTL (ZTL, FKF1 homolog, Arabidopsis thaliana), CO (CO, FT activator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transient expression in tobacco leaves was used to study FKF1 homodimerization, interactions with ZTL, and interactions with CO in planta.
mechanism: The constructs enabled co-immunoprecipitation assays to analyze protein-protein interactions, revealing reduced homodimerization of FKF1 I160R and increased interaction with GI.

genes: EcCYP87A126 (sterol side chain cleaving enzyme, Erysimum cheiranthoides), Ec3βHSD (3β-hydroxy-Δ5-steroid dehydrogenase, Erysimum cheiranthoides), Ec3KSI (3-ketosteroid isomerase, Erysimum cheiranthoides), EcP5βR2 (progesterone-5β-reductase, Erysimum cheiranthoides)
phenotype: Coexpression of EcCYP87A126, Ec3βHSD, Ec3KSI, and EcP5βR2 in N. benthamiana leads to production of a compound with m/z and retention time matching epipregnanolone 6.
mechanism: The enzymes work together in planta to produce intermediates in cardenolide biosynthesis, including epipregnanolone.

genes: AlSRKb (receptor domain, Arabidopsis thaliana), AlSCRb (s, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transformants show SI, wSI, or SC phenotypes depending on AlSRKb mutations; 105/299 showed strong SI, 3 weak SI, 191 SC
mechanism: Mutations in AlSRKb disrupt plasma membrane localization, with SC phenotype occurring when plasma membrane localization rate <10%

genes: SFTSV Gn (SFTSV glycoprotein, SFTSV, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of SFTSV Gn in N. benthamiana leads to high yield of recombinant Gn protein (~7 mg/kg of leaves) with enhanced solubility and secretion.
mechanism: The use of BaMV subgenomic promoters (SGP1 and cpSGP) drives expression of P19 and Gn. The inclusion of signal peptide (SSExt) and (SP)10 repeats in the pKB19-Gn-Dual construct enhances soluble expression and secretion of Gn.

genes: SFTSV Gn (SFTSV glycoprotein, SFTSV, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of SFTSV Gn in N. benthamiana with dual signal peptides (SSExt and (SP)10) results in significantly higher rGn expression (detectable at 3 dpi) compared to the pKB19-Gn construct, with a yield of ~7 mg/kg of leaves.
mechanism: The fusion of SSExt and (SP)10 to the N-terminus of Gn enhances soluble expression and secretion, reducing endogenous protein contamination (e.g., RuBisCO) during purification. The BaMV subgenomic promoters (SGP1 and cpSGP) drive expression of P19 and Gn.

genes: PtDGAT2b (acyl-CoA:diacylglycerol acyltransferase2b, Phaeodactylum tricornutum)
phenotype: Transient expression in tobacco leaves increased triacylglycerol (TAG) production to 8% of total lipids
mechanism: NA

genes: SlNAP1 (SlNAP1, NAC transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: VIGS-mediated silencing of SlNAP1 in tomato fruits results in mottled green and orange patches with delayed color transition during ripening, reduced lycopene content, and impaired chlorophyll degradation and carotenoid biosynthesis.
mechanism: SlNAP1 suppresses GA degradation genes (SlGA2ox1/5) and activates ethylene biosynthesis genes, promoting fruit ripening through GA-ethylene crosstalk.

genes: SlNAP1 (SlNAP1, NAC transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of SlNAP1 in tomato fruits delays ripening by 8 days compared to wild-type, reduces ethylene production by 1.4-fold, and decreases lycopene content by ~50% at Br stage.
mechanism: SlNAP1 directly binds and activates promoters of GA degradation genes (SlGA2ox1/5), reducing endogenous GA3 levels and promoting ethylene-dependent ripening.

genes: GhDMT6 (GhDMT6, DNA methyltransferase, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Cotton seedlings silencing GhDMT6 show significant stress resistance compared to non-silenced seedlings under different stress treatments
mechanism: GhDMT6 is involved in methylation modification and stress response in cotton

genes: LYK8 (Medicago truncatula, LYK8), CERK1 (Medicago truncatula, CERK1)
phenotype: Complete restoration of fungal infection and colonization in lyk8/cerk1 mutant roots
mechanism: LYK8 and CERK1 are functionally redundant in arbuscular mycorrhiza symbiosis (AMS)

genes: SlSCaBP8 (Solanum lycopersicum SCaBP8/CBL10, Solanum lycopersicum, synthetic)
phenotype: slscabp8-cr mutants exhibit compromised saline-alkaline tolerance with reduced survival rates, lower chlorophyll content, and increased oxidative damage markers (MDA, H2O2, O2−) compared to wild-type M82 tomato plants.
mechanism: SlSCaBP8 functions as a positive regulator against saline-alkaline stress by maintaining Na+/K+ homeostasis and interacting with SlSOS2 to mitigate oxidative damage.

genes: OsNAR2.1 (OsNAR2.1, drought tolerance and nitrogen use efficiency, Oryza sativus)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNAR2.1 increases survival rate under drought stress, raises photosynthesis by 39.2%, water use efficiency by 28.8%, grain yield by 25.5% under full watering and 66.4% under limited water, and nitrogen use efficiency by 25.5% and 66.4% under respective conditions in Oryza sativus.
mechanism: OsNAR2.1 improves drought resistance by increasing nitrogen uptake and regulating OsPLDα1 expression.

genes: CrPINMa (CrPINMa, PIN family protein, ferns)
phenotype: retarded leaf emergence and reduced leaf size though they could survive and reproduce
mechanism: PINs can play a role in fern leaf development

genes: NtWRKY65 (transcription factor, upregulated by NaCl treatment, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtWRKY65 increases root length, leaf area, fresh weight, and chlorophyll content in transgenic tobacco under salinity stress. Transgenic lines show elevated antioxidant enzyme activity, reduced malondialdehyde content, lower Na+ content, and higher K+/Na+ ratio compared to wild type.
mechanism: NtWRKY65 regulates genes involved in salt stress response including cell wall component metabolism, osmotic stress response, cellular oxidant detoxification, protein phosphorylation, and auxin signaling pathway.

genes: BoGSTF12 (BoGSTF12, anthocyanin transporter, Brassica oleracea)
phenotype: Rescued anthocyanin-loss phenotype in the stem and rosette leaves of Arabidopsis thaliana tt19
mechanism: BoGSTF12 encodes an anthocyanin transporter that affects the accumulation of anthocyanins

genes: RsDES6 (Δ6 lipid-linked desaturase, Rhizopus stolonifer, AY795076.1)
phenotype: Expression of RsDES6 leads to production of GLA and SDA in N. benthamiana leaves, with GLA and SDA accounting for 0.4% and 0.7% (RsDES6) and 2.8% and 4.7% (OtDES6) in total lipid extract.
mechanism: RsDES6 converts linoleic acid to GLA and linolenic acid to SDA, but its activity is less efficient compared to OtDES6.

genes: PtLPCAT (acyl-CoA:lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase, Phaeodactylum tricornutum, EEC48011.1)
phenotype: PtLPCAT expression modifies the TAG pool by increasing 18:3∆9,12,15 content from 36% to 43% and increases PC and TAG pool sizes by 5.9% and 2.2%, respectively.
mechanism: PtLPCAT transfers acyl groups between cytosol and PC pools, favoring omega-3 substrates and potentially alleviating substrate dichotomy.

genes: RsDES6 (Δ6 lipid-linked desaturase, Rhizopus stolonifer, AY795076.1), PtLPCAT (acyl-CoA:lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase, Phaeodactylum tricornutum, EEC48011.1)
phenotype: Co-expression of RsDES6 and PtLPCAT reduces SDA levels below detection in the PC pool but increases GLA by 1.8-fold in the TAG pool.
mechanism: PtLPCAT's reverse activity may reduce SDA availability for TAG synthesis, while enhancing GLA accumulation.

genes: OtDES6 (Δ6 acyl-CoA desaturase, Osterococcus tauri, XM_003082530.1), PtLPCAT (acyl-CoA:lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase, Phaeodactylum tricornutum, EEC48011.1)
phenotype: Co-expression of OtDES6 and PtLPCAT increases GLA and SDA to 13.1% and 19.1% in the TAG pool, with a 1.8- and 1.5-fold increase compared to OtDES6 alone.
mechanism: PtLPCAT enhances acyl-CoA desaturase activity by transferring substrates to the cytosol, boosting GLA and SDA production.

genes: OtDES6 (Δ6 acyl-CoA desaturase, Osterococcus tauri, XM_003082530.1), PSE (Δ6 elongase, Physcomitrium patens, AF428243.1), TcDES5 (Δ5 lipid-linked desaturase, Thraustochytrium sp., AF489588), PtLPCAT (acyl-CoA:lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase, Phaeodactylum tricornutum, EEC48011.1)
phenotype: This combination produces EPA at 1.4% of total fatty acids in the TAG pool, with 17.5% of 'Other' fatty acids being EPA.
mechanism: The pathway converts GLA and SDA to EPA via elongation and desaturation, with PtLPCAT enhancing substrate availability for omega-3 synthesis.

genes: OtDES6 (Δ6 acyl-CoA desaturase, Osterococcus tauri, XM_003082530.1), PSE (Δ6 elongase, Physcomitrium patens, AF428243.1), PtDES5 (Δ5 lipid-linked desaturase, Phaeodactylum tricornutum, GQ352540.1), PtLPCAT (acyl-CoA:lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase, Phaeodactylum tricornutum, EEC48011.1)
phenotype: This combination results in 4.5% EPA in the TAG pool (20.1% of newly synthesized fatty acids), with increased PC and TAG pool sizes.
mechanism: PtLPCAT's substrate preference for omega-3 intermediates enhances EPA production by channeling substrates through the omega-3 pathway.

genes: phyB (photoreceptor phytochrome B, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHYB-CFP increases PB size and alters hypocotyl length in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PHYB-CFP forms phase-separated condensates (LLPS) that regulate PIF5 stability and signaling.

genes: phyB (photoreceptor phytochrome B, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Intermediate overexpression of PHYB-CFP rescues the long-hypocotyl phenotype of phyB-9 and increases PB size.
mechanism: PHYB-CFP phase separation (LLPS) enhances PB size and alters PIF5 dynamics.

genes: PIF5 (phytochrome-interacting factor 5, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of mCherry-PIF5 rescues the hypocotyl-growth defect of pif5-3 and localizes to PHYB condensates.
mechanism: mCherry-PIF5 colocalizes with PHYB in PBs and is stabilized by PHYB-mediated phase separation.

genes: PIF5 (phytochrome-interacting factor 5, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HA-mCherry-PIF5 in PBC enhances PIF5 stabilization and alters hypocotyl elongation.
mechanism: Constitutive expression under UBQ10 promoter increases PIF5 retention in PHYB condensates.

genes: PsNAC1 (PsNAC1, transcription factor, Picea sylvestris var. mongolica)
phenotype: Enhanced drought resistance in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NA

genes: PfeDGAT1 (diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1, Physaria fendleri), PfeDGAT2 (diacylglycerol acyltransferase 2, Physaria fendleri), PfeTAGL1 (triacylglycerol lipase-like 1, Physaria fendleri)
phenotype: Expression of PfeDGAT1-GFP and PfeDGAT2-GFP localized to the ER in N. benthamiana leaf cells. PfeTAGL1-GFP also localized to the ER and co-localized with ER markers.
mechanism: ER localization of PfeDGAT1, PfeDGAT2, and PfeTAGL1 facilitates TAG remodeling by enabling substrate channeling and interaction between enzymes.

genes: PfeDGAT1 (diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1, Physaria fendleri), PfeDGAT2 (diacylglycerol acyltransferase 2, Physaria fendleri), PfeTAGL1 (triacylglycerol lipase-like 1, Physaria fendleri)
gene_construct: 2S albumin promoter-PfeDGAT1-RNAi, 2S albumin promoter-PfeDGAT2-RNAi, 2S albumin promoter-PfeTAGL1-RNAi
phenotype: RNAi knockdown of PfeDGAT1, PfeDGAT2, and PfeTAGL1 reduced total seed oil accumulation and HFA content in P. fendleri, confirming their roles in HFA-containing TAG biosynthesis.
mechanism: RNAi suppression of TAG remodeling genes disrupts the enzymatic steps required for HFA incorporation into TAG, leading to reduced oil and HFA accumulation.

genes: PfeDGAT1 (diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1, Physaria fendleri), PfeDGAT2 (diacylglycerol acyltransferase 2, Physaria fendleri), PfeTAGL1 (triacylglycerol lipase-like 1, Physaria fendleri)
gene_construct: 2S albumin promoter-PfeDGAT1-glycinin terminator, 2S albumin promoter-PfeDGAT2-glycinin terminator, beta-conglycinin promoter-PfeTAGL1-soy oleosin terminator
phenotype: Overexpression of PfeDGAT1, PfeDGAT2, and PfeTAGL1 in Arabidopsis RcFAH lines increased total seed oil and HFA content compared to controls.
mechanism: Enhanced TAG remodeling via PfeDGAT1, PfeDGAT2, and PfeTAGL1 activity increases HFA incorporation into TAG, alleviating feedback inhibition of fatty acid synthesis.

genes: GUS (reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: trichome-specific expression in Ler ecotype reporter lines
mechanism: NA

genes: AtPLC1 (phospholipase C gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: suppression of trichome development in Ler, rescue of trichome and seed coat phenotypes in ttg2-1
mechanism: AtPLC1 positively mediates TTG2 control of epidermal traits

genes: ZmLARP6c1 (ZmLARP6c1, pollen-specific gene, Zea mays)

mechanism: NA

mechanism: TALE-DdCBE-mediated base editing using evolved DddA variants (DddA6/DddA11) with optimized spacer lengths between TALE binding sites

genes: NA
phenotype: C•G-to-T•A conversions in the chloroplast genome of rice
mechanism: TALE-DdCBE-mediated base editing using DddA11 variant with broader sequence compatibility for non-TC target editing

genes: PHYB-CFP (PHYB-CFP, photoactivated phytochrome B fused with CFP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHYB-CFP increases photobody (PB) condensation and number in Arabidopsis thaliana under cool temperatures (16 °C).
mechanism: PHYB condensation is driven by liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), with higher PHYB concentration in PBC line promoting nonrandom PB formation at chromocenter-associated sites.

genes: TS (3β-tigloyloxytropane synthase, A. belladonna, A. belladonna)
phenotype: Overexpression of TS increases the content of 3β-tigloyloxytropane in hairy roots of A. belladonna by ~3.00-fold for Kcat/Km values compared to wild-type.
mechanism: TS catalyzes the esterification of 3β-tropanol with tigloyl-CoA to generate 3β-tigloyloxytropane via esterification reactions. The TSS40T mutant enhances catalytic efficiency by forming a hydrogen bond with Asn135, stabilizing the active site.

genes: TS (3β-tigloyloxytropane synthase, A. belladonna, A. belladonna)
phenotype: Silencing of TS disrupts the biosynthesis of calystegine A3 in A. belladonna, reducing 3β-tigloyloxytropane content by ~90% in TS-silenced lines.
mechanism: TS catalyzes the esterification of 3β-tropanol with tigloyl-CoA to generate 3β-tigloyloxytropane. Silencing TS leads to accumulation of 3β-tropanol and reduced downstream metabolites.

genes: TS (3β-tigloyloxytropane synthase, A. belladonna, A. belladonna), EnODC (ornithine decarboxylase, Erythroxylum novogranatense, E. novogranatense), AbPMT (putrescine N-methyltransferase, A. belladonna, A. belladonna), AbMPO (N-methylputrescine oxidase, A. belladonna, A. belladonna), AbPYKS (type III polyketide synthase, A. belladonna, A. belladonna), AbCYP82M3 (tropinone synthase, A. belladonna, A. belladonna), DsTRII (tropinone reductase II, Datura stramonium, D. stramonium)
phenotype: De novo synthesis of 3β-tigloyloxytropane in N. benthamiana leaves, with TSS40T mutant increasing 3β-tigloyloxytropane content by 1.33-fold and 3β-acetoxytropane by 5.02-fold compared to wild-type TS.
mechanism: The six upstream genes provide intermediates for 3β-tropanol biosynthesis, while TS catalyzes the final esterification step. TSS40T enhances catalytic efficiency via hydrogen bonding, improving 3β-tigloyloxytropane production.

genes: BcDFR (BcDFR, dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, Brassica sp.)
phenotype: BcDFR promotes the synthesis and accumulation of anthocyanin in tobacco.
mechanism: BcDFR is involved in the anthocyanin biosynthesis pathway.

genes: RhMED15a-like (RhMED15a-like, drought-responsive Mediator subunit, Rosa hybrid)
phenotype: Overexpression of RhMED15a-like increases osmotic stress tolerance in Arabidopsis, evidenced by increased germination rate, root length, and fresh weight.
mechanism: RhMED15a-like controls transcript levels of drought-responsive genes and stress-related hormone signaling pathways.

genes: RhMED15a-like (RhMED15a-like, drought-responsive Mediator subunit, Rosa hybrid)
phenotype: Silencing RhMED15a-like in rose results in elevated malondialdehyde accumulation, exacerbated leaf wilting, reduced survival rate, and downregulated expression of drought-responsive genes during drought stress.
mechanism: RhMED15a-like downregulation reduces drought tolerance by impairing oxidative stress response and hormone signaling pathways.

genes: Ta1SST (Ta1SST, sucrose: sucrose 1-fructosyltransferase, wheat), Ta6SFT (Ta6SFT, sucrose: fructan 6-fructosyltransferase, wheat)
phenotype: Transgenic wheat plants accumulated more fructan polymers in leaf, stem and grain compared to transgene null lines, with increased accumulation of high DP fructans under water-deficit conditions and specific DP4 fructan deposition in grain
mechanism: Tissue-regulated expression of the gene fusion between Ta1SST and Ta6SFT modified fructan accumulation influenced by water-deficit stress conditions

genes: VviERF003 (ethylene-responsive transcription factor, Vitis vinifera, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of VviERF003 in grape calli significantly increases VviGT14 expression and glycosylated monoterpenoid accumulation (e.g., β-citronellol, menthol).
mechanism: VviERF003 activates VviGT14 transcription, leading to enhanced glycosylation of monoterpenoids.

plant_species: Vitis vinifera L. × Vitis labrusca L. Summer Black
genes: VviERF003 (ethylene-responsive transcription factor, Vitis vinifera, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of VviERF003 in grape skins increases VviGT14 expression and glycosylated/free-form monoterpenoid concentrations (e.g., linalool, geraniol).
mechanism: VviERF003 activates VviGT14 transcription, enhancing glycosylation and free-form monoterpenoid biosynthesis.

genes: VviERF003 (ethylene-responsive transcription factor, Vitis vinifera, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of VviERF003 in tomato fruits increases glycosylated and free-form monoterpenoid concentrations (e.g., linalool, α-terpineol).
mechanism: VviERF003 activates VviGT14 transcription, promoting monoterpenoid glycosylation and accumulation.

genes: VviERF003 (ethylene-responsive transcription factor, Vitis vinifera, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of VviERF003 in grape leaves increases glycosylated monoterpenoid concentrations (e.g., linalool, α-terpineol) and free-form monoterpenoids.
mechanism: VviERF003 activates VviGT14 transcription, enhancing glycosylation and free-form monoterpenoid biosynthesis.

plant_species: Vitis vinifera L. × Vitis labrusca L. Summer Black
genes: VviERF003 (ethylene-responsive transcription factor, Vitis vinifera, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient silencing of VviERF003 in grape skins reduces VviGT14 expression and glycosylated/free-form monoterpenoid concentrations.
mechanism: VviERF003 knockdown suppresses VviGT14 transcription, decreasing monoterpenoid glycosylation and accumulation.

genes: CsMYB36 (promoter, promoter of CsMYB36, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: Overexpression of GUS under CsMYB36 promoter in cucumber roots.
mechanism: NA

genes: CaMV35S (promoter, CaMV35S promoter, Cauliflower mosaic virus)
phenotype: GFP expression in cucumber roots for transformation screening.
mechanism: NA

genes: CsMYB36 (gene, CsMYB36, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: Knockout of CsMYB36 in cucumber roots.
mechanism: NA

genes: PINNA2 (Medtr1g096030, GRAS transcription factor, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Complementation of pinna2-2 mutant leaf phenotype with no pleiotropic effects in six of 15 transgenic lines, and semi-dwarfism in others.
mechanism: PINNA2 represses SGL1 expression through direct promoter binding, controlling leaflet morphogenesis.

genes: PINNA2 (Medtr1g096030, GRAS transcription factor, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Complementation of pinna2-2 mutant leaf phenotype with semi-dwarfism.
mechanism: PINNA2 represses SGL1 expression through direct promoter binding, controlling leaflet morphogenesis.

genes: kaiA (cce_0424, part of the KaiABC clock, Cyanothece 51142), kaiB1 (cce_0423, part of the KaiABC clock, Cyanothece 51142)
phenotype: Deletion of kaiA and kaiB1 in Cyanothece 51142 results in more stringent reduction in endogenous rhythms compared to the ∆kaiA mutant alone.
mechanism: The combined knockout of kaiA and kaiB1 disrupts the KaiABC clock's ability to regulate cellular oxygen dynamics, leading to impaired segregation of photosynthesis and nitrogen fixation.

genes: AGO10 (Arabidopsis thaliana, AGO10 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AGO10 in Arabidopsis thaliana roots leads to shorter meristems and increased cell division in the stele, phenocopying the shortroot (shr) mutant phenotype.
mechanism: AGO10 competes with AGO1 for miR165/166 binding, modulating HD-ZIP III silencing and influencing root meristem activity.

genes: TCSn (TCSn, cytokinin response reporter, synthetic), UBQ10 (UBQ10, constitutive promoter, synthetic)
phenotype: Enlarged expression domain of pTCSn:2xVenus-NLS and increased reporter fluorescence in the stele of sgo1 mutants compared to wild type.
mechanism: AGO10 buffers cytokinin responses by controlling formative cell divisions in the root vasculature.

genes: STTM165/6 (STTM165/6, miR165/6 target mimic, synthetic)
phenotype: Alleviation of the sgo1 phenotype by sequestration of miR165/6.
mechanism: Sequestration of miR165/6 by the target mimic reduces its availability, thereby restoring HD-ZIP III expression and normal vascular patterning.

genes: MaERFVII3 (MaERFVII3, transcription factor involved in waterlogging stress tolerance, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: MaERFVII3-expressing Arabidopsis showed increased survival and biomass under waterlogging stress compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: MaERFVII3 enhances waterlogging tolerance by upregulating transcripts related to waterlogging and hypoxia response.

genes: MaERFVII3 (MaERFVII3, transcription factor involved in waterlogging stress tolerance, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: MaERFVII3 was localized in the nucleus of onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: MaERFVII3 localizes in the cell nucleus, suggesting it functions as a transcription factor.

genes: MdARF3 (ARF3, auxin response factor 3, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdARF3 in transgenic tobacco increases root length by ~30% and promotes aboveground growth (plant height and internode length) compared to wild type.
mechanism: MdARF3 enhances root elongation by increasing hemicellulose content in root cell walls and promoting cell elongation in the root elongation zone.

genes: MdARF3 (ARF3, auxin response factor 3, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdARF3 in transgenic apple increases root length by ~30% and promotes aboveground growth (plant height and internode length) compared to wild type.
mechanism: MdARF3 enhances root elongation by increasing hemicellulose content in root cell walls and promoting cell elongation in the root elongation zone.

genes: MdWOX4-1 (WOX4-1, WUS element binding protein, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdWOX4–1 in apple callus increases MdARF3 expression and promotes root elongation.
mechanism: MdWOX4–1 binds the WUSATAg element in the MdARF3 promoter, enhancing its transcriptional activity and promoting root elongation.

genes: Smi-miR858a (artificial microRNA, Salvia miltiorrhiza)
gene_construct: Ptc-MIR408 backbone with Smi-miR858a and Smi-miR858a* sequences
phenotype: Overexpression of Smi-miR858a in S. miltiorrhiza plants repressed SmMYB targets and caused growth retardation characterized by smaller leaves and roots and fewer leaves and roots. Fresh weight was decreased from 15.50 g in the wild type to 8.08 g in transgenic lines.
mechanism: Smi-miR858a negatively regulates phenolic acid and tanshinone biosynthesis by targeting SmMYB genes, leading to downregulation of SmMYB6, SmMYB97, SmMYB111, and SmMYB112.

genes: IAA17 (Aux/IAA transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of IAA17-FLAG stabilizes the protein and inhibits auxin-induced degradation, leading to reduced auxin responsiveness and altered root elongation and lateral root density.
mechanism: IAA17 overexpression inhibits TIR1–IAA17 co-receptor formation by S-nitrosylation at Cys-70, reducing proteasomal degradation and attenuating auxin signaling.

genes: IAA17 (Aux/IAA transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Native promoter-driven IAA17-FLAG expression stabilizes the protein via S-nitrosylation at Cys-70, disrupting TIR1–IAA17 interaction and attenuating auxin signaling.

genes: IAA17 (Aux/IAA transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants with IAA17::IAA17C70W-FLAG show defective growth and development, with resistance to 2,4-D and reduced lateral root density.
mechanism: Cys-70 to tryptophan mutation in IAA17 mimics S-nitrosylation, stabilizing the protein and inhibiting TIR1–IAA17 interaction, thereby attenuating auxin signaling.

genes: TobaccoRBCS (plastid localized YFP, Tobacco)
phenotype: Expression of plastid-localized YFP in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NA

genes: AUR1 (Aurora-A kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana, native promoter)

mechanism: AUR1 localizes to phragmoplast midzone during cytokinesis and interacts with MAP65-3 to regulate microtubule dynamics

genes: TUB6 (tubulin, Arabidopsis thaliana, native promoter)

mechanism: Phragmoplast expansion velocity reduced by 38% in aur1 aur2 cells compared to wild-type

genes: MAP65-3 (microtubule-associated protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, native promoter)

mechanism: MAP65-3 turnover delayed in aur1 aur2 cells, leading to persistent microtubule decoration and impaired phragmoplast expansion

genes: MAP65-3AA (phospho-defective mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana, native promoter)

mechanism: Phospho-defective mutation disrupts α-Aurora-mediated regulation of MAP65-3 microtubule binding and turnover

genes: MAP65-3DD (phospho-mimetic mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana, native promoter)

mechanism: Phospho-mimetic mutation compensates for α-Aurora deficiency by promoting MAP65-3 turnover and proper microtubule association

genes: MeHKT1 (plasma membrane-bound protein transporter, cassava)
phenotype: Under low K+ stress, transgenic Arabidopsis with MeHKT1 exhibits improved growth due to increasing shoot K+ content. In contrast, transgenic Arabidopsis accumulates more Na+ under salt stress than wild-type (WT) plants.

phenotype: Silenced plants show significantly greater sensitivity to salt stress compared to negative control plants

mechanism: MeFtsZ2-1 modulates pigment biosynthesis and hormone pathways, altering chloroplast structure and storage capacity for pigments.

phenotype: SLRL2 overexpression increases rice amylose content (AC) by ~15%, while knockout decreases AC. bHLH144 and NF-YB1 knockout also decreases AC.

genes: GmDR1 (GmDR1, disease resistance gene, Glycine max)

mechanism: Syn-tasiRNAs target the PVY and PVX CP genes via RNA silencing, inducing PTGS to suppress replication of both viruses.

genes: FTRB (FTR catalytic subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FTRB increases FTR protein levels to ~700-900% of wild-type levels in Arabidopsis thaliana. Growth phenotypes show impaired growth under fluctuating light conditions compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: FTR acts as a central hub in the Fd/Trx pathway linking electron transport chain and redox-sensitive proteins in chloroplasts. Overexpression disrupts chloroplast redox balance, affecting photosynthetic electron transport efficiency and protein redox states.

genes: PhPIF4/5 (Phytochrome Interacting Factor 4/5, floral scent regulation, Petunia × hybrida)

genes: PhPIF4/5 (Phytochrome Interacting Factor 4/5, floral scent regulation, Petunia × hybrida)

mechanism: PhPIF4/5 overexpression upregulates expression of scent-related genes (EOBI, EOBII, ODO1, PAAS, PAL2, BSMT, IGS, EPSPS, ADT1) and activates the EOBII promoter via G-box motif binding.

genes: EOBII (Emission of Benzenoids II, floral scent regulation, Petunia × hybrida)
phenotype: PhPIF4/5 overexpression increases DsRED fluorescence and mRNA levels in petals expressing DsRED under the EOBII promoter by 2-fold compared to controls without PhPIF4/5.
mechanism: PhPIF4/5 binds to G-box motif in EOBII promoter to activate its transcription. Mutation of G-box motif abolishes this activation.

genes: RTL1 (suppresses siRNA biogenesis in pollen, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Overexpression of qE and downregulation of PSII and PSI allow for increased LHCII clustering and qE activation.

mechanism: Simultaneous modification in xylan and lignin loosens cell wall complexity, enhancing xylose and xylobiose release without compromising growth or defense against Pseudomonas syringae

genes: EPMEI (Pectin MethylEsterase Inhibitor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

phenotype: Knock-out of PhTFL1 reduces plant height by ~49.74%, enhances early flowering by 18.5 days, increases branching (11 branches vs 5.5 in wild-type), and alters inflorescence architecture (3.5 flowers per inflorescence vs 7.3 in wild-type).
mechanism: PhTFL1 regulates gibberellic acid pathway genes (PhGAI) and flowering regulators (PhSOC, PhCO). Knock-out leads to downregulation of PhGAI and upregulation of PhSOC/PhCO, promoting early flowering and compact growth.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Escherichia coli)

mechanism: CaMV35S is a constitutive viral promoter providing basal gene expression independent of stress conditions.

genes: Nitab4.5_0011760g0030.1 (R2R3-MYB transcription factor)
phenotype: Overexpression of R2R3-MYB transcription factor Nitab4.5_0011760g0030.1 increases the number of branched glandular trichomes in tobacco.
mechanism: NA

genes: PHYB (phytochrome B with G767R mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHYB-G767R rescues the phyB-5 mutant under red light in a dosage-dependent manner, promoting photomorphogenesis and reducing PIF3 levels.
mechanism: PHYB-G767R triggers PIF3 turnover and/or inhibits PIF3 translation under red light, leading to photomorphogenesis.

genes: YHB (phytochrome B with Y276H and G767R mutations, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of YHB-G767R promotes light-independent seed germination and inhibits negative gravitropism in darkness and under red light.
mechanism: YHB-G767R induces PIF3 loss in the cytosol, leading to de-etiolation and germination.

genes: PHYB (phytochrome B with C357S mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complements the phyB-1 mutant under red light, promoting photomorphogenesis and reducing PIF3 levels.
mechanism: PHYB-C357S mediates PIF3 turnover under red light, leading to photomorphogenesis.

genes: YHB (phytochrome B with Y276H mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of YHB promotes light-independent seed germination and inhibits negative gravitropism in darkness and under red light.
mechanism: YHB induces PIF3 loss in the cytosol, leading to de-etiolation and germination.

genes: PtWRKY2 (WRKY transcription factor, Paeonia ternata)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtWRKY2 in Arabidopsis increases heat tolerance, with transgenic lines showing 76.9-81.9% survival under 42°C stress vs 31.8% in wild type, and enhanced ROS scavenging capacity
mechanism: PtWRKY2 upregulates heat shock-associated genes (HSFA1A, DREB2A, HSP70) and antioxidant enzymes (CAT, SOD, POD), reducing ROS accumulation and enhancing thermotolerance

genes: TadCBEa (TadA-8e-derived cytosine base editor, synthetic), TadCBEd (TadA-8e-derived cytosine base editor, synthetic), TadCBEd_V106W (TadA-8e-derived cytosine base editor, synthetic), TadDE (TadA-8e-derived dual base editor, synthetic)

mechanism: TadA-8e-derived deaminases fused to nCas9 enable precise C-to-T and A-to-G base editing with narrow editing windows and low indel rates.

genes: OsALS (acetolactate synthase, Oryza sativa), sgR17 (guide RNA, synthetic), sgR18 (guide RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: TadDE-mediated C-to-T mutations in OsALS (R190H, G628E, G629S) conferred herbicide resistance to bispyribac-sodium in rice.
mechanism: C-to-T mutations in OsALS alter the catalytic core, preventing herbicide inhibition.

genes: PmDAM6 (PmDAM6, dormancy-associated MADS-box transcription factor, Prunus mume)
phenotype: Overexpression of PmDAM6 increases bud set rate (percentage of apices with a terminal bud: WT: 55.9 ± 8.3%, 35S-2: 97.6 ± 3.3%, and 35S-4: 100%) and delays bud break under forcing conditions (23°C and 18-h day/6-h night), with chilling requirement increased by ~140–180 chill hours.
mechanism: PmDAM6 promotes lipid body accumulation by down-regulating lipid catabolism-related genes (GDSL ESTERASE/LIPASE, SFAR, OBL1) and up-regulating lipid biosynthesis-related genes (LDAP), while repressing cell division via down-regulation of cell cycle genes (CYCD6-1, CYCS13-6) and modulating phytohormone metabolism (ABA, GA, CTK).

genes: PmDAM6 (PmDAM6, dormancy-associated MADS-box transcription factor, Prunus mume)
phenotype: DEX-inducible overexpression of PmDAM6 in transgenic apple plants (35S:PmDAM6-GR) leads to similar phenotypic effects as constitutive overexpression, including increased lipid body accumulation and delayed bud break, with gene expression modulated by DEX treatment.
mechanism: PmDAM6-GR expression is repressed by DEX treatment, leading to down-regulation of lipid catabolism-related genes (GDSL ESTERASE/LIPASE, SFAR, OBL1) and cell cycle genes (CYCD6-1, CYCS13-6), while up-regulating phytohormone metabolism genes (ABA, GA, CTK).

genes: WOX2 (WUSCHEL-related homeobox 2, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic overexpression of WOX2-YFP-GR in roots induces shoot meristem-like structures, increases root width, root hair production, and upregulates CLV3 and PHB expression by ~2-fold in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: WOX2-YFP-GR reprograms root cells toward shoot meristem formation by activating CLV3 and PHB, which are markers of shoot stem cell identity and regulators of shoot meristem initiation.

genes: WOX2 (WUSCHEL-related homeobox 2, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP-WOX2 rescues protoderm defects in cdc48a-1/+ embryos but fails to rescue shoot meristem defects in cdc48a-1/+ seedlings in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GFP-WOX2 compensates for CDC48A loss in protoderm formation by enhancing WOX2 activity, but CDC48A is required for additional processes in shoot meristem initiation.

genes: CDC48A (AAA+ ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CDC48A-FLAG rescues protoderm defects in cdc48a-1/+ embryos but does not rescue shoot meristem defects in cdc48a-1/+ seedlings in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CDC48A-FLAG complements protoderm formation by interacting with WOX2, but additional CDC48A functions are required for shoot meristem initiation.

genes: CDC48A (AAA+ ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of YFP-CDC48A under its native promoter rescues protoderm and shoot apical meristem defects in cdc48a-1/+ embryos and seedlings in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: YFP-CDC48A complements CDC48A function by co-localizing with WOX2 in the nucleus during embryogenesis, supporting their interaction in protoderm and shoot meristem formation.

genes: CDC48A (AAA+ ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of GFP-CDC48A in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts co-localizes with tdTomato-WOX2 in the nucleus, confirming their interaction.
mechanism: GFP-CDC48A and tdTomato-WOX2 co-localize in the nucleus, supporting their physical interaction during embryogenesis.

genes: AtqFT1 (AtqFT1, activator type FT gene, Agave tequilana), AtqFT2 (AtqFT2, activator type FT gene, Agave tequilana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtqFT1 and AtqFT2 in Arabidopsis thaliana significantly reduces flowering time (13.8 days after germination) compared to wild type (38 days), with transgenic lines producing 2-4 small rosette leaves (1.3 cm diameter) and dying within 25 days.
mechanism: AtqFT1 and AtqFT2 act as activator type FT proteins that promote flowering by interacting with endogenous components of the Arabidopsis FT regulatory system.

genes: AtqFT4 (AtqFT4, repressor type FT gene, Agave tequilana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtqFT4 in Arabidopsis thaliana significantly delays flowering time (55.2 days after germination) compared to wild type (38 days), with transgenic lines producing 30-32 rosette leaves (3.5-4.5 cm diameter) and showing phenotypes similar to the ft-10 mutant.
mechanism: AtqFT4 acts as a repressor type FT protein that interferes with the activity of the Arabidopsis FT gene (AtFT) by preventing correct interactions between AtFT and the FD and 14–3–3 proteins in the SAM.

genes: ABA3 (ABA3, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ABA3 promotes hypocotyl growth in white light.
mechanism: NA

genes: DCS1 (DCS1, spliceosomal component, Arabidopsis thaliana), DCS2 (DCS2, DEAD-box helicase, Arabidopsis thaliana), DCS5 (DCS5, Slu7 homolog, Arabidopsis thaliana), DCS6 (DCS6, CACTIN homolog, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: DCS3 (DCS3, Prp8 homolog, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: DCS3 interacts with other spliceosomal components; its overexpression stabilizes the spliceosome complex.

genes: DCS4 (DCS4, DEAD-box helicase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of DCS4 (DEAD-box helicase) in the spliceosome restores interactions with DCS3, indicating its role in spliceosome dynamics.
mechanism: DCS4 interacts with DCS3; its overexpression stabilizes the spliceosome complex.

genes: EXPA15 (cell expansion regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)

mechanism: Enhancer trap construct with Ds transposon carrying GUS reporter gene under EXPA15 regulatory elements allows visualization of gene expression patterns

mechanism: PbrMYB114 interacts with PbrbHLH3 to activate anthocyanin biosynthesis genes, and further interacts with PbrMT2/3 to regulate copper homeostasis, stabilizing anthocyanin accumulation.

genes: PbrbHLH3 (bHLH transcription factor, anthocyanin biosynthesis regulator, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Co-expression with PbrMYB114 significantly enhances anthocyanin biosynthesis in 'Yuluxiang' pear fruits, increasing pigmentation and anthocyanin levels by ~3.5-fold compared to controls.
mechanism: PbrbHLH3 interacts with PbrMYB114 to activate anthocyanin biosynthesis genes, and further interacts with PbrMT2/3 to regulate copper homeostasis, stabilizing anthocyanin accumulation.

genes: PbrMT2 (Metallothionein-like protein type 2, copper homeostasis regulator, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Co-expression with PbrMYB114 and PbrbHLH3 in 'Duli' seedlings increases anthocyanin content by ~2.8-fold compared to controls, with more pronounced pigmentation than PbrMT3 co-expression.
mechanism: PbrMT2 interacts with PbrMYB114 to regulate copper homeostasis, stabilizing anthocyanin accumulation by enhancing vacuolar anthocyanin stability.

genes: PbrMT3 (Metallothionein-like protein type 3, copper homeostasis regulator, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Co-expression with PbrMYB114 and PbrbHLH3 in 'Duli' seedlings increases anthocyanin content by ~2.2-fold compared to controls, with less pronounced pigmentation than PbrMT2 co-expression.
mechanism: PbrMT3 interacts with PbrMYB114 to regulate copper homeostasis, stabilizing anthocyanin accumulation by enhancing vacuolar anthocyanin stability.

genes: RABE1C (RABE1C, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the suppressor line M20 rescues the spi-4 mutant trichome phenotype
mechanism: RABE1C rescues the spi-4 mutant by redirecting vesicle transport pathways

phenotype: Expression of RABE1CS29N rescues the spi-4 mutant trichome phenotype
mechanism: RABE1CS29N mimics the suppressor phenotype by creating an inactive RABE1C variant

genes: CLC2 (CLC2, clathrin light chain 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: CLC2-mCherry co-localization analysis reveals altered vesicle trafficking patterns

genes: MYB36 (MYB36, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: MYB36Loop creates a positive feedback loop where MYB36 induces itself and downstream targets in endodermal cells already committed to Casparian strip (CS) formation, uncoupling CS formation from SGN3 dependency and creating earlier functional barriers

genes: Cas9 (codon-optimized S. pyogenes, hCas9, expression), nptII (kanamycin resistance), DsRed (red fluorescent protein)

mechanism: NA

genes: sgPDS (single-guide RNA targeting PHYTOENE DESATURASE, PDS)

mechanism: Loss-of-function PDS mutations disrupt carotenoid biosynthesis, causing photobleaching.

genes: sgSGR (single-guide RNA targeting STAYGREEN 1, SGR1)
phenotype: Indels in SGR1 gene produce green-flesh phenotype in tomato fruits.
mechanism: SGR1 inactivation prevents chlorophyll degradation, leading to chlorophyll accumulation in fruits.

mechanism: CsCLV3 peptide transmits the signal during flower development, interacting with CsCLV1 to regulate meristem size and floral organ number.

genes: CsCLV1 (receptor CLV1 homolog, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: Functional disruption of CsCLV1 led to increased floral organ numbers (sepals, petals, stamens, carpels) and stumpy fruits with significantly reduced fruit shape index compared with wild type.
mechanism: CsCLV1 negatively regulates floral organ number but positively controls fruit shape index by interacting with CsGPA1 and modulating CsWUS expression.

genes: CsGPA1 (Gα-subunit (GPA1) homolog, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: Functional disruption of CsGPA1 produced similar phenotypes to Csclv1 mutants: increased floral organ numbers and stumpy fruits with significantly reduced fruit shape index.
mechanism: CsGPA1 physically interacts with CsCLV1 at the protein level, modulating CsWUS expression and CsCRC transcription to regulate floral organ number and fruit elongation.

genes: LinA (γ-HCH dehydrochlorinase, Sphingobium japonicum strain UT26)

mechanism: LinA expression relieves γ-HCH toxicity by degrading γ-HCH into metabolites

genes: EuLEGA (legumin A gene, seed storage protein, Eucommia ulmoides)

mechanism: EuLEGA is associated with legumin synthesis in seeds and indirectly with rhamnose synthesis.

mechanism: The promoter fragment (−1 to −1395 bp) contains drought-responsive MYB elements and photoresponse elements.

mechanism: Parakletos negatively regulates ROS and Ca2+ bursts, suppressing plant immune signaling.

genes: Parakletos (M1CUF4, thylakoid protein, potato)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-generated parakletos-KO potato lines exhibit enhanced ROS bursts and increased resistance to Phytophthora infestans.
mechanism: Parakletos knockout disrupts its negative regulation of ROS and Ca2+ signaling, enhancing immune responses.

genes: bZIP17 (bZIP17, salt stress-responsive gene)
phenotype: AGB1 depletion decreases nuclei-localization of transgenic mRFP-bZIP17 under salt stress
mechanism: AGB1 functions in S1P and/or S2P-mediated proteolytic processing of bZIP17 under salt stress to regulate the induction of salinity-responsive gene expression

genes: OfYABBY12 (OfYABBY12, transcription factor, Osmanthus fragrans)

mechanism: OfYABBY12 negatively regulates NtCCD1/4 and OfCCD4 expression, decreasing β-ionone biosynthesis.

genes: PsMDL2 (PsMDL2, mandelonitrile catabolism enzyme, P. sibirica)

mechanism: PsMDL2 upregulates transcript of mandelonitrile metabolic enzymes and oil synthesis enzymes (involving FA biosynthesis and TAG assembly), revealing a role in seed amygdalin and oil biosynthesis.

genes: P2K1t (C-terminal truncated P2K1, overexpressed, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of P2K1t-GFP in dorn1–3 mutant plants results in exaggerated extracellular ATP (eATP) responses compared to wild type.
mechanism: P2K1t-GFP overexpression enhances eATP signaling, leading to increased calcium influx and altered gene expression patterns.

genes: AEQ (aequorin, overexpressed, synthetic)

mechanism: Aequorin binds calcium ions and emits luminescence, allowing quantification of eATP-induced calcium mobilization.

mechanism: The absence of ER retention (HDEL) likely reduced protein stability and accumulation in N. benthamiana.

genes: Dup-scFv (synthetic antibody fragment, codon-optimized for plant expression, synthetic)

mechanism: ER retention via HDEL increased protein stability and accumulation in N. benthamiana.

genes: AcCENH3 (AcCENH3, centromeric histone H3, Allium cepa)

mechanism: RNAi-mediated knockdown of AcCENH3 disrupts centromere function, leading to biased segregation distortion, reduced seed set, and haploid induction through genome elimination

genes: VvIDI (isopentenyl diphosphate isomerase, grape, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvIDI inhibits biosynthesis of grape linalool and α-terpineol
mechanism: The 64-amino acid N-terminal extension guides VvIDI protein to target the chloroplast

phenotype: Overexpression of TaTDF1 in Arabidopsis thaliana results in normal anther coloration (red) by Alexander staining and an average bolting time of 33 days.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaTDF1 (Triticum aestivum, DEFECTIVE IN TAPETAL DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTION 1, wheat)
phenotype: Dominant mosaic suppression of TaTDF1 in Arabidopsis thaliana results in blue-green coloration, shrimpy and thin anthers.
mechanism: NA

genes: BGLU28 (AtBGLU28, myrosinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtBGLU28 reduces glucosinolate (GSL) accumulation in qs-2 mutant plants while maintaining the small plant phenotype.
mechanism: AtBGLU28 hydrolyzes GSLs, reducing their levels and insect resistance in qs-2.

genes: LOX2 (LOX2, 13-lipoxygenase, Arabidopsis thaliana), MYB28 (MYB28, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), MYB29 (MYB29, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), MYB34 (MYB34, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), MYB51 (MYB51, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRISPR knockout of LOX2, MYB28, MYB29, MYB34, or MYB51 in qs-2 rescues jasmonate (JA) and glucosinolate (GSL) hyperaccumulation, restoring plant growth and insect resistance.
mechanism: LOX2 catalyzes α-linolenic acid hydroperoxidation to initiate JA biosynthesis, while MYB28/29 and MYB34/51 regulate aliphatic and indolic GSL biosynthesis, respectively.

genes: HsSARM1-TIR (TIR domain of human SARM1, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient expression of HsSARM1-TIR in N. benthamiana leaves reduces NAD+ content, increases 1O2, JA, and JA-Ile levels, mimicking the defense response observed in NAD+ deficiency.
mechanism: HsSARM1-TIR hydrolyzes NAD+ to trigger 1O2 production and JA biosynthesis, linking NAD homeostasis to plant defense.

genes: SlSYTA (SlSYTA, negative regulator of plant immunity, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlSYTA increases susceptibility to TMV, P. capsici, B. cinerea, and P. syringae pv. tomato DC3000 infections in N. benthamiana and S. lycopersicum.
mechanism: SlSYTA suppresses ROS signaling, callose accumulation, and stomatal defense, promoting pathogen invasion via negative regulation of plant immunity.

genes: SlSYTA (SlSYTA, negative regulator of plant immunity, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of SlSYTA confers broad-spectrum resistance to TMV, P. capsici, B. cinerea, and P. syringae pv. tomato DC3000 in S. lycopersicum.
mechanism: SlSYTA silencing enhances ROS accumulation, callose deposition, and stomatal closure, activating plant immunity via SA and ABA signaling pathways.

genes: OsCKq1 (OsCKq1, a gene regulating rice yield and photoperiod sensitivity, Oryza sativa spp. japonica)
phenotype: Earlier heading by 3-5 days, increased grain length, grain width, 1,000-grain weight, and yield compared to Ilmi (Oryza sativa spp. japonica).
mechanism: Reduced OsCKq1 mRNA levels alongside increased mRNA levels of Hd3a, Ehd1, and RFT1 (flowering-promoting genes) under long-day conditions.

genes: MCA-II-a (metacaspase II-a, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), MCA-II-b (metacaspase II-b, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), MCA-II-f (metacaspase II-f, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MCA-II-a, -b, and -f under native promoters leads to partial colocalization with ER sheets and associated structures in embryonic root cells.
mechanism: MCA-II-a partially co-fractionates with the ER-associated luminal protein BiP2, suggesting transient association with ER-related structures but not direct luminal protein access.

genes: MCA-II-a (metacaspase II-a, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MCA-II-a under RPS5a promoter leads to colocalization with CDC48 on lipid droplets in embryonic root cells.
mechanism: MCA-II-a and CDC48 colocalize on lipid droplets, suggesting transient association with structures derived from or associated with the ER.

genes: PUX10 (Ubiquitin regulatory X domain-containing 10, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PUX10 under native promoter leads to increased stability and levels in mca-II-KOc mutants.
mechanism: PUX10 stability depends on active MCA-II-a, as confirmed by degradation rate experiments with cycloheximide and MG132.

genes: CDC48a (CELL DIVISION CYCLE 48a, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of CDC48a under CaMV35S promoter leads to altered localization in mca-II-KOc mutants, with increased association with lipid droplets.
mechanism: In mca-II-KOc, CDC48 accumulates on lipid droplets and shows reduced ER association, suggesting retention due to lack of MCA-II-mediated PUX10 cleavage.

genes: BRI1 (BRASSINOSTEROID INSENSITIVE 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of mutant BRI1 (Bri1-9) under RPS5a promoter leads to increased plasma membrane localization in mca-II-KOc roots.
mechanism: ERAD malfunction in mca-II-KOc allows Bri1-9 to escape ER lumen to plasma membrane, suggesting reduced ERAD activity.

genes: TMM (stomatal lineage marker, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased stomatal lineage cells marked by TMMpro::GUS-GFP in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: MUTE (stomatal lineage marker, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased stomatal lineage cells marked by MUTEpro::nucYFP in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: SCRM (SPCH/MUTE/FAMA partner, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SCRM protein expression in stomatal-lineage cells of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: SCRM (SPCH/MUTE/FAMA partner, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Stabilized SCRM protein expression in stomatal-lineage cells of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: EPF1 (EPF-ERECTA-family signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana), EPF2 (EPF-ERECTA-family signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Induced overexpression of EPF1/2 severely inhibits stomatal development in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: EPF1/2 overexpression activates the EPF-ERECTA-family signaling pathway, counteracting kC9 effects.

genes: MPK6 (mitogen-activated protein kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), SCRM (SPCH/MUTE/FAMA partner, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: MPK6-SCRM interaction detected via ratiometric bimolecular fluorescence complementation (rBiFC) in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: kC9 treatment disrupts MPK6-SCRM association in planta.

genes: SlPIRE1 (negative regulator of immune responses, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Increased apoplastic ROS production upon flg22 treatment and enhanced resistance to foliar bacterial pathogens (18-12-fold reduction in bacterial titers).
mechanism: SlPIRE1 negatively regulates immune responses by ubiquitinating and degrading RBOHB, reducing ROS production. Gene editing removes this negative regulation, leading to higher ROS and disease resistance.

genes: SlPIRE2 (negative regulator of immune responses, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: No significant changes in ROS production or disease resistance compared to wild-type. Slpire2–1 exhibited low germination and delayed growth.
mechanism: SlPIRE2 does not appear to regulate RBOHB or ROS production in the same way as SlPIRE1, based on observed phenotypes.

genes: SlPIRE1 (negative regulator of immune responses, Solanum lycopersicum), SlPIRE2 (negative regulator of immune responses, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Unsuccessful in generating a viable double mutant (likely lethal).
mechanism: NA

genes: NRL5 (N-terminal BTB domain, NPH3 domain, C-terminal region), NRL5P335L (N-terminal BTB domain, NPH3 domain with P335L substitution, C-terminal region), RABE1c (RAB small GTPase), VAMP721 (R-soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptor)
phenotype: NRL5 overexpression complements nrl5-1 and nrl5-2 mutants by restoring low ψw stress resistance and normal proline metabolism. NRL5P335L fails to complement these mutants. RABE1c and VAMP721 overexpression aids in studying NRL5 interactions and trafficking.
mechanism: NRL5 interacts with RABE1c, RABH1b, and VAMP721/722 to regulate vesicle trafficking and GTPase activity. NRL5P335L mutation disrupts these interactions, leading to aberrant proline metabolism and low ψw hypersensitivity.

genes: sgRNA10 (GAAGCAAGCGCGTGCAGAGA, guide RNA for SlDND1, synthetic), sgRNA5 (ATGTGTTTGGATGTCAATGG, guide RNA for SlDND1, synthetic), sgRNA6 (GTCAATGGACCATTTCCATA, guide RNA for SlDND1, synthetic), sgRNA8 (GCCACAAGCATACTTGAGCC, guide RNA for SlDND1, synthetic), NPTII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, resistance marker, synthetic), Cas9 (CRISPR-associated protein 9, nuclease, synthetic)
phenotype: Homozygous mutants (aa) show increased resistance to powdery mildew (Oidium neolycopersici) with reduced fitness costs (less dwarfism and auto-necrotic spots in E3 mutants) in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: CRISPR-induced mutations in SlDND1 (encoding a cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel) alter Ca2+ signaling, leading to constitutive defense responses against powdery mildew. E3 mutants retain partial functionality with conformational changes in the pore-loop domain affecting ion selectivity.

genes: PvMYB60 (promoting stomata aperture, Phaseolus vulgaris)
phenotype: Promoting stomata aperture in Arabidopsis thaliana by complementing the myb60-1 mutant
mechanism: PvMYB60 promotes stomata aperture, restoring the defective phenotype in Arabidopsis myb60-1 mutant

genes: CaSLR1 (CaSLR1, MYB61 transcription factor, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Silencing of CaSLR1 in pepper results in stem twisting and lodging, reduced cellulose (36.39%), hemicellulose, and lignin contents, and decreased stem strength (501.47 mg puncture strength vs. 1222.97 mg in controls).
mechanism: CaSLR1 regulates secondary cell wall (SCW) biosynthesis by modulating cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin accumulation. SCW thinning in xylem fiber cells reduces mechanical support.

genes: SlMYB61 (SlMYB61, MYB61 homolog, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Knockout of SlMYB61 in tomato (Micro-Tom) leads to stem lodging, reduced root branching, shorter inflorescence branches, and thinner secondary cell walls (SCWs) in xylem fiber cells.
mechanism: SlMYB61 knockout disrupts SCW biosynthesis, reducing cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin accumulation. Thinner SCWs in xylem fiber cells compromise stem mechanical strength.

genes: CaSLR1 (CaSLR1, MYB61 transcription factor, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Subcellular localization of CaSLR1 in Arabidopsis protoplasts shows GFP fluorescence in the cell membrane and nucleus, confirming nuclear localization.
mechanism: CaSLR1 is localized in the nucleus, suggesting its role in gene regulation. Co-localization with nuclear marker Ghd-RFP confirms nuclear presence.

genes: AtRaptor1B (Raptor homologue involved in TOR signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of AtRaptor1B-/- phenotype restores wild-type transition to bolting, shoot branching and root growth in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtRaptor1B is essential for maintaining shoot apical meristem activity and post-embryonic growth regulation via TOR signaling.

genes: NtERF10 (NtERF10, AP2/ERF family transcription factor, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: NtERF10 knockout causes significant reduction in plant height (~30% decrease) in Nicotiana tabacum during maturation stages
mechanism: NA

genes: Cas9 (Cas9, nuclease, Zea mays), gRNA (gRNA, guide RNA, arrayed), gRNA (gRNA, guide RNA, arrayed)
phenotype: 100% of T0 barley plants and >90% of T0 wheat plants were edited in all three target genes simultaneously
mechanism: Codon-optimised Cas9 with 13 introns and arrayed guides driven by U6/U3 promoters enhance mutagenesis efficiency

genes: Cas12a (Cas12a, nuclease, Arabidopsis thaliana), gRNA (gRNA, guide RNA, tRNA-based array), gRNA (gRNA, guide RNA, tRNA-based array)
phenotype: 90% mutant alleles in three barley genes and 86%-93% mutation in two wheat genes simultaneously
mechanism: Codon-optimised Cas12a with 8 introns and tRNA-based multiguide arrays enhance mutagenesis efficiency

genes: OsPRX83 (Oryza sativa japonica cv. Nipponbare cDNA, full-length coding region, Oryza sativa japonica cv. Nipponbare)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsPRX83 increases osmotic stress tolerance in rice, with a survival rate of 87% compared to 60% in wild type after 120 mM mannitol treatment.
mechanism: OsPRX83 enhances ROS scavenging by increasing peroxidase (POD) and ascorbate peroxidase (APX) activities.

genes: OsPRX83 (Oryza sativa japonica cv. Nipponbare cDNA, sgRNA target site, Oryza sativa japonica cv. Nipponbare)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of OsPRX83 reduces osmotic stress tolerance in rice, with a survival rate of 30% compared to 87% in overexpression lines after 120 mM mannitol treatment.
mechanism: OsPRX83 knockout decreases ROS scavenging capacity, leading to reduced peroxidase (POD) and ascorbate peroxidase (APX) activities.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, pCXGUS-P vector, synthetic)
phenotype: OsPRX83 promoter-driven GUS expression shows high activity in roots and low activity in leaves, stems, and spikelets of transgenic rice.
mechanism: The OsPRX83 promoter is tissue-specific, with strong activity in roots and weak activity in aerial tissues.

genes: MlBOP (MlBOP, BOP homolog, Mimulus lewisii)
phenotype: Overexpression of MlBOP rescues the bop-1 mutant phenotype, confirming BOP as the causal gene.
mechanism: MlBOP interacts with MlCYC2A to modulate self-activation of MlCYC2A, influencing flower symmetry.

genes: MlCYC2A (MlCYC2A, CYC-like gene, Mimulus lewisii)
phenotype: Overexpression of MlCYC2A leads to completely dorsalized flowers in Mimulus lewisii.
mechanism: MlCYC2A self-activates its own transcription by binding to the P1 element in its promoter, regulated by MlBOP.

genes: MlBOP (MlBOP, BOP homolog, Mimulus lewisii)
phenotype: Rescues the bop-3 mutant phenotypes.
mechanism: MlBOP interacts with MlCYC2A to modulate self-activation of MlCYC2A, influencing flower symmetry.

genes: Cry1Ac (Cry1Ac endotoxin, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of Cry1Ac in cotton provides insect resistance by producing a toxic endotoxin effective against lepidopteran pests like cotton bollworm
mechanism: Cry1Ac endotoxin is toxic to lepidopteran pests, inhibiting their growth and reducing damage to cotton

genes: OsNADP-ME2 (NADP-malic enzyme, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNADP-ME2 with N-terminal GFP tag localizes the protein to the cytosol in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: OsNADP-ME2 is a cytosolic protein involved in NADP-malic enzyme activity.

genes: OsNADP-ME2 (NADP-malic enzyme, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of OsNADP-ME2 decreases plant height in rice by reducing panicle and internode lengths.
mechanism: Down-regulation of GA biosynthesis and signaling genes (OsCPS1, OsKS1, OsKAO, OsGA3ox1, OsGA3ox2, OsGA20ox1-4) and up-regulation of GA signaling suppressor SLR1.

genes: OsNADP-ME2 (NADP-malic enzyme, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of OsNADP-ME2 in rice results in reduced plant height due to decreased panicle and internode lengths.
mechanism: Frame shift mutation in OsNADP-ME2 leads to reduced GA1 and GA4 levels, altered GA signaling, and up-regulation of SLR1.

genes: TgLBD40 (LOB domain-containing protein 40, Torreya grandis, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of TgLBD40 significantly increases seed oil content in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: TgLBD40 enhances oil accumulation by affecting oil biosynthesis pathway genes such as TgDGAT1.

genes: TgLBD40 (LOB domain-containing protein 40, Torreya grandis, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient expression of TgLBD40-GFP in N. benthamiana leaves increases oil content.
mechanism: TgLBD40-GFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus and promotes oil accumulation.

genes: AhAftr1 (Arachis hypogaea Aflatoxin resistance 1, disease resistance protein, Arachis hypogaea)
phenotype: Transgenic plants with overexpression of AhAftr1(ZH6) exhibited 57.3% aflatoxin reduction compared to that of AhAftr1(XH13)
mechanism: AhAftr1 might be involved in disease resistance via the effector-triggered immunity (ETI) pathway

genes: SmWRKY40 (SmWRKY40, WRKY transcription factor involved in salt stress response, Solanum melongena)
phenotype: Overexpression of SmWRKY40 in Arabidopsis thaliana increases salt stress tolerance, with 95.4% germination rate under 75 mM NaCl (vs 79.3% in WT) and 56.8% germination under 150 mM NaCl (vs 18.7% in WT). Root lengths are significantly longer under salt stress (28.2-3.6 mm vs 27.6-1.6 mm in WT).
mechanism: SmWRKY40 enhances salt tolerance by upregulating antioxidant enzymes (SOD, POD, CAT, APX), increasing soluble protein and proline content, and modulating stress-related genes (AtKIN1, AtCOR15A, AtABI1). It also downregulates ABA signaling positive regulators (AtPYR1, AtPYL2, AtSnRK2.2/3) while upregulating negative regulators (AtABI1, AtABI2).

genes: EAT1 (promoter, reporter gene)
phenotype: EAT1p had a weak expression, similar to mini35Sp in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsiWAK1 (full-length, receptor-like kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsiWAK1 vector had an activating effect on EAT1p in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsiWAK1 (extracellular domain deleted, receptor-like kinase, Oryza sativa)

mechanism: NA

mechanism: NA

mechanism: NA

phenotype: OsiWAK1_TDR_TIP2 combination increased EAT1p activation 33.40 times compared to EAT1p alone in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

phenotype: OsiWAK1_TDRi reduced EAT1p activation to 0.61 times that of OsiWAK1_GUSi in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: PbPRR59a (PbPRR59a, PRR gene homologous to AtPRR5/9, Pyrus bretschneideri), PbPRR59b (PbPRR59b, PRR gene homologous to AtPRR5/9, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Ectopic overexpression of PbPRR59a and PbPRR59b significantly delayed flowering in Arabidopsis transgenic plants under long-day conditions
mechanism: Repression of AtGI, AtCO and AtFT expression

genes: ALD1 (AGD2-LIKE DEFENSE RESPONSE PROTEIN 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), SARD4 (SAR DEFICIENT 4, Arabidopsis thaliana), FMO1 (FLAVIN MONOOXYGENASE 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ALD1, SARD4, and FMO1 leads to severe phenotypes including smaller rosette size, early senescence in Arabidopsis, and failure to set fruit in tomato. NHP and NHPG accumulate significantly in transgenic plants.
mechanism: Constitutive activation of immune responses via NHP biosynthesis, leading to enhanced SA production and upregulation of defense-related genes.

genes: NAC90 (NAC DOMAIN CONTAINING PROTEIN 90, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NAC90 overexpression leads to enlarged rosette size and suppressed defense responses compared to wild-type plants. NAC90 overexpression lines show reduced NHP and SA accumulation and enhanced susceptibility to Psm ES4326.
mechanism: NAC90 negatively regulates NHP and SA biosynthesis by directly repressing the expression of ALD1, SARD4, FMO1, and ICS1. This repression suppresses immune responses and allows for plant growth.

genes: NAC61 (NAC DOMAIN CONTAINING PROTEIN 61, Arabidopsis thaliana), NAC36 (NAC DOMAIN CONTAINING PROTEIN 36, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NAC61 and NAC36 knockout mutants display enhanced resistance to Psm ES4326, reduced growth, and early senescence. These mutants show elevated levels of NHP, SA, and defense-related metabolites.
mechanism: NAC61 and NAC36 function as negative regulators of NHP and SA biosynthesis. Their knockout leads to constitutive activation of immune responses and increased defense gene expression.

genes: MDMV coat protein gene (viral gene, MDMV, synthetic)
phenotype: Exogenous siRNA treatment reduces MDMV viral RNA and coat protein levels by ~60% in sweet corn, delaying infection peak by one week.
mechanism: siRNA triggers RNAi-mediated antiviral defense by activating DCL, RDR, and AGO genes, leading to viral RNA degradation and translational inhibition.

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic), NIa-Pro (non-structural protein, SCMV), VPg (viral protein genome-linked, SCMV)
phenotype: Expression of eGFP-NIa-Pro or SCMV-GFP significantly increased the splicing ratio of RLPK.1 to RLPK.2 reporters in transgenic N. benthamiana plants.
mechanism: NIa-Pro regulates pre-mRNA splicing by associating with splicing factors, particularly U2AF65B.

genes: ZmU2AF65B (pre-mRNA splicing-associated protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmU2AF65B in N. benthamiana plants showed altered splicing ratios when coexpressed with NIa-Pro.
mechanism: ZmU2AF65B interacts with NIa-Pro to regulate pre-mRNA splicing, as demonstrated by LCI and co-IP assays.

genes: OsDes1 (OsDes1, transcriptional activator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsDes1 leads to stay-green in rice, with delayed senescence and increased grain yield.
mechanism: OsDes1 interacts with and stabilizes OsPetC, activates its expression, and is involved in ABA- and JA-mediated signaling pathways.

genes: OsDes1 (OsDes1, transcriptional activator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of OsDes1 does not show stay-green phenotype or delayed senescence.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsPetC (OsPetC, Rieske Fe/S protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsPetC leads to delayed dark-induced senescence and increased greenness under ABA or MeJA treatment.
mechanism: OsPetC accumulation contributes to delayed senescence and enhanced photosynthesis.

genes: GF14h (GENERAL REGULATORY FACTOR14h, Arroz da Terra)
phenotype: Overexpression of GF14h in Hitomebore increased germination by ~40% at 15°C compared to wild-type Hitomebore.
mechanism: GF14h enhances low-temperature germination by modulating phytohormone signaling pathways.

genes: GrxS5 (Glyoxalase family protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GFP-GrxS5 signals in the nucleus of root endodermal, cortical, and epidermal cell layers
mechanism: GrxS5 functions as a phloem-mobile shoot-to-root signal that suppresses nitrate transporter gene expression

genes: GFP (Green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP expression in root epidermis, cortex and vasculature overlapping with CEPDL2 localization
mechanism: NRT2.1 promoter drives GFP expression for co-immunoprecipitation control

genes: TGA1 (Transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: TGA1-GFP binds to promoters of nitrate transporter genes NRT2.1 and CEPH

genes: CEPDL2 (C-terminally encoded peptide-like 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CEPDL2 upregulates NRT2.1 and CEPH in wild-type but not in tga1,4 mutant
mechanism: CEPDL2 acts as coactivator for TGA1/4-mediated transcription of nitrate transporter genes

genes: GrxS5 (Glutathione reductase family protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GrxS5 overexpression suppresses NRT2.1 and CEPH expression in wild-type plants
mechanism: GrxS5 forms corepressor complex with TPL/TPR1/4 to repress TGA1/4-mediated transcription

genes: GrxS5 (Glutathione reductase family protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Estradiol-inducible GrxS5 expression reduces CEPDL2-TGA1/4 interaction in roots
mechanism: GrxS5 competes with CEPDL2 for TGA1/4 binding, forming corepressor complex with TPL

genes: DoSPX1 (DoSPX1, reduces phosphate accumulation and promotes PSIs gene expression, Dendrobium officinale), DoMYB37 (DoMYB37, binds promoter of DoCSLA6, Dendrobium officinale)
phenotype: Decreased Pi content and increased expression of DoCSLA6 in D. officinale protocorm-like bodies
mechanism: DoSPX1-DoMYB37-DoCSLA6 signaling pathway enhances polysaccharide accumulation under phosphorus starvation

genes: lncRNA1 (unknown, unknown, unknown), lncRNA2 (unknown, unknown, unknown)
phenotype: Altered phenotypes under low R/FR light in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: lncRNA1 (unknown, unknown, unknown), lncRNA2 (unknown, unknown, unknown)
phenotype: Altered phenotypes under low R/FR light in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, pCAMBIA1305)

mechanism: NA

genes: OsRH52A (rice RH52A DEAD-box RNA helicase, Oryza sativa), EGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP fluorescence observed in the nucleus and cytoplasm of Nicotiana benthamiana leaf epidermal cells, indicating OsRH52A subcellular localization
mechanism: Fusion of OsRH52A with EGFP allows visualization of protein localization in plant cells

genes: TaWAK2 (wall-associated kinase, Triticum aestivum), TaNAL1 (trypsin-like protease, Triticum aestivum)

mechanism: TaWAK2-A phosphorylates TaNAL1, which interacts with and degrades TaDST, leading to reduced cytokinin (CK) degradation and increased CK levels, promoting leaf expansion.

genes: TaWAK2-A (wall-associated kinase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaWAK2-A in wheat results in wider flag leaves at the mature plant stage, with a 12.7–14.2% increase in grain weight per spike.
mechanism: TaWAK2-A phosphorylates TaNAL1, which degrades TaDST, reducing TaCKX gene expression and increasing cytokinin (CK) levels, promoting leaf expansion and grain weight.

genes: TaWAK2-A (wall-associated kinase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Expression of TaWAK2-A–GFP in Nicotiana benthamiana confirms plasma membrane localization and phosphorylation activity of TaWAK2-A.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaWAK2-AA525V (mutant wall-associated kinase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Expression of TaWAK2-AA525V–GFP in Nicotiana benthamiana shows reduced protein accumulation compared to TaWAK2-A–GFP, indicating destabilization due to the A525V mutation.
mechanism: The A525V mutation reduces TaWAK2-A protein stability via the 26S proteasome pathway.

genes: TaCKX9 (cytokinin oxidase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Transient expression of the TaCKX9 promoter-LUC reporter in Nicotiana benthamiana confirms TaDST-mediated activation of TaCKX9 transcription.
mechanism: TaDST binds to the TaCKX9 promoter and activates its expression, while TaNAL1 inhibits this activation.

genes: OsERF52 (Oryza sativa, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Rescued cold-sensitive phenotype in homozygous oserf52-1 progenies at T2 generation
mechanism: OsERF52 acts as a positive regulator of chilling tolerance by stabilizing its protein under cold stress

genes: OsERF52 (Oryza sativa, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression lines of OsERF52 displayed obviously enhanced chilling tolerance (fig. S2)
mechanism: OsERF52 enhances chilling tolerance by stabilizing its protein under cold stress

genes: OsSAPK9 (Oryza sativa, protein kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Rescued chilling-sensitive phenotype in homozygous ossapk9-1 progenies at T2 generation

genes: OsbZIP01 (VIG1, gene for bZIP transcription factor, Oryza sativa), OsbZIP18 (gene for bZIP transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of vig1a and vig1b mutants with wild-type OsbZIP01 and OsbZIP18 fully rescues the mutant phenotypes including seedling vigor (SV), chilling tolerance (CT), heading date, and grain number per panicle (GNP).
mechanism: VIG1 and OsbZIP18 synergistically repress downstream genes involved in cell expansion, cell division, cold tolerance, and grain yield. The R121H substitution in vig1a disrupts VIG1 function, which is rescued by complementation with wild-type OsbZIP01 and OsbZIP18.

genes: VIG1 (OsbZIP01, gene for bZIP transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of VIG1 reduces shoot length and increases seminal root length compared to wild-type KY131. However, CT is significantly reduced in overexpressing lines. VIG1 overexpression also delays flowering by 13–15 days and increases plant height and GNP.
mechanism: VIG1 overexpression represses downstream genes like EXPB4, OsPID, and Ehd1, which are involved in cell expansion, grain yield, and heading date regulation. This leads to reduced shoot elongation but increased grain production.

genes: OsbZIP18 (gene for bZIP transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsbZIP18 in the vig1a background partially rescues the vig1a mutant phenotype, including SV, CT, and GNP. This indicates functional overlap between OsbZIP18 and VIG1.
mechanism: OsbZIP18 interacts with VIG1 to repress downstream genes like EXLA2, CYCD1-2, OsDREB1A, OsDREB1B, and OsPID. This interaction is disrupted in vig1a, leading to enhanced SV, CT, and GNP.

genes: VIG1 (OsbZIP01, gene for bZIP transcription factor, Oryza sativa), OsbZIP18 (gene for bZIP transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CRISPR-mediated knockout of VIG1 and OsbZIP18 in KY131 results in increased SV and CT but decreased GNP. This mimics the vig1b phenotype, indicating that VIG1 and OsbZIP18 function redundantly in regulating these traits.
mechanism: Disruption of VIG1 and OsbZIP18 leads to upregulation of genes like Ehd1 and downregulation of OsPID, which are involved in heading date and grain yield regulation. This results in increased SV and CT but reduced GNP.

genes: PvTOC1 (circadian rhythm gene, switchgrass, Panicum virgatum)
phenotype: Overexpression of PvTOC1 in Arabidopsis leads to delayed flowering (~3 days later than wild-type), increased rosette leaf number, shorter root length (7 days on ½ × MS medium), and longer root apical meristem. Transgenic plants show increased sensitivity to oxidative stress (reduced photosynthetic efficiency after H2O2 treatment) and altered hormone responses (reduced sensitivity to TIBA, 6-BA, lovastatin, and PAC; GR24 promotes root growth).
mechanism: PvTOC1 overexpression disrupts circadian rhythm by repressing AtLHY expression while upregulating endogenous AtTOC1. It alters hormone pathways by upregulating ABA biosynthesis gene NCED, GA-related genes (GA20ox, GAI), and auxin-related genes (YUCCA8, TIC). This leads to delayed flowering, root growth inhibition, and altered stress responses.

genes: PvLHY (circadian rhythm gene, switchgrass, Panicum virgatum)
phenotype: Overexpression of PvLHY in Arabidopsis results in delayed flowering (slightly later than wild-type), shorter root length (7 days on ½ × MS medium), and altered root apical meristem morphology. Transgenic plants show reduced sensitivity to ABA (longer roots at 60 μM ABA), increased salt tolerance (higher survival at 150 mM NaCl), and heightened sensitivity to oxidative stress (reduced photosynthetic efficiency after H2O2 treatment). Hormone treatments show reduced sensitivity to NAA, 6-BA, and lovastatin, with GR24 promoting root growth.
mechanism: PvLHY overexpression suppresses both AtTOC1 and AtLHY expression, disrupting circadian rhythm. It downregulates ABA biosynthesis gene NCED and GA-related genes (GA20ox), while upregulating strigolactone biosynthetic genes (MAX1, D27). This leads to altered hormone homeostasis, delayed flowering, and modified stress responses. Oxidative stress tolerance is reduced due to impaired photoprotective mechanisms.
