genes: PabGLK5 (PabGLK5, gene involved in chloroplast development, Populus alba × P. berolinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of PabGLK5 leads to 18.23% reduced plant height and 28.5%–65.9% increased chlorophyll and carotenoid content in Populus alba × P. berolinensis.
mechanism: Overexpression of PabGLK5 upregulates photosynthesis-related genes (PabLhcb1, PabLhcb2, PabLhcb4, PabLhca3, PabCHLD1, PabCHLD2), increasing pigment content but reducing photosynthetic efficiency (Pn) by 20.83%.

genes: NtCBL1-1 (NtCBL1-1, calcium sensor involved in abiotic stress response, Nitraria tangutorum)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtCBL1-1 increases germination rate by ~30% under 150 mM NaCl and 300 mM mannitol stress in Arabidopsis thaliana. Transgenic plants show delayed wilting, higher chlorophyll content, and lower MDA levels under salt/drought stress.
mechanism: NtCBL1-1 encodes a calcium sensor that activates stress response pathways, enhancing chlorophyll retention, soluble protein accumulation, and reducing oxidative damage (MDA) under abiotic stress.

genes: MpGGGT1 (Mapoly0094s0053, glycerol-1-phosphate acyltransferase, Marchantia polymorpha), MpGGGT2 (Mapoly0082s0065, glycerol-1-phosphate acyltransferase, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Transient expression of MpGGGT1-GFP in N. benthamiana leaves results in TGDG production, while MpGGGT2-GFP does not.
mechanism: MpGGGT1 catalyzes TGDG synthesis in chloroplast membranes, whereas MpGGGT2 lacks this activity.

genes: MpGGGT1 (Mapoly0094s0053, glycerol-1-phosphate acyltransferase, Marchantia polymorpha), MpGGGT2 (Mapoly0082s0065, glycerol-1-phosphate acyltransferase, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Knockout of MpGGGT1 or MpGGGT2 does not affect Marchantia growth under control conditions but reduces acetic acid tolerance and induces chlorosis in gggt1 mutants.
mechanism: MpGGGT1 is required for TGDG synthesis and TAG accumulation during acetic acid stress, which protects chloroplast membranes and prevents cell death.

genes: AkCSLA11 (AkCSLA11, drought response gene, Amorphophallus konjac)
phenotype: Overexpression of AkCSLA11 reduces drought tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Overexpression inhibits drought response genes and alters cell wall sugar components

genes: SMAX1 (SMAX1, SMAX1 repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana), eYFP (enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, fluorescent marker, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of eYFP-SMAX1 in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to constitutive germination in the dark and nuclear-localized eYFP signal in root cells.
mechanism: SMAX1 accumulation in the dark represses germination by inhibiting light signaling pathways and modulating phytochrome responses. Light exposure or rac-GR24 treatment degrades SMAX1, allowing germination.

genes: AtKAI2 (AtKAI2, karrikin receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtKAI2 in Arabidopsis thaliana enables germination in the dark at low nanomolar KAR2 concentrations and activates genes like DLK2, KUF1, and BBX20.
mechanism: AtKAI2 signaling promotes germination by degrading SMAX1 and SMXL2, which otherwise repress germination in the dark. This pathway interacts with PIF1 to modulate hormone (ABA/GA) balance and light signaling.

genes: ShHTL7 (ShHTL7, karrikin receptor homolog, Striga)
phenotype: Overexpression of ShHTL7 in Arabidopsis thaliana complements htl-3 (kai2) phenotypes and enables germination in the dark when combined with KAR2 treatment.
mechanism: ShHTL7 functions similarly to AtKAI2 in activating the KL signaling pathway, leading to SMAX1 degradation and germination in the dark. This pathway interacts with PIF1 and modulates hormone signaling.

genes: gRNA1 (targeting BnaFAH exon 4), gRNA2 (targeting BnaFAH exon 4), gRNA3 (targeting BnaFAH exon 6)
phenotype: Simultaneous knockout of both BnaFAH alleles (BnaC05FAH and BnaA06FAH) under short-day (SD) conditions induces programmed cell death (PCD) in Brassica napus L., characterized by H2O2 accumulation and cell death confirmed by Trypan blue staining.
mechanism: Knockout of BnaFAH alleles leads to H2O2 accumulation under SD conditions, triggering ER stress, oxidative stress, and PCD. Upregulated ER stress genes (BnaBIP1/BIP2, BnaCNX1, etc.), suppressed autophagy-related genes (BnaATG8c/e/f, etc.), and increased ROS production via mitochondrial/chloroplast communication contribute to PCD.

genes: GSNOR (GSNOR, GSNOR, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GSNOR overexpression in shoots reduces Cd tolerance, increases H2O2 accumulation and oxidative damage under Cd stress
mechanism: GSNOR inhibits CAT activity under Cd stress by down-regulating CAT1 and CAT2 expression, leading to H2O2 over-accumulation

genes: ZjCRC (ZjCRC, key to nectary development, Ziziphus jujuba 'Dongzao')
phenotype: Ectopic expression of ZjCRC in Arabidopsis crc-1 mutant rescues lost nectary, carpel, and silique defects
mechanism: ZjCRC is required for nectary development and directly activated by ZjAGAMOUS1 (ZjAG1)

genes: SlHDA7 (SlHDA7, histone deacetylase, Solyc01g009110)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlHDA7 delays tomato fruit maturation.
mechanism: SlHDA7 deacetylates H4ac to inhibit transcription of ripening-related genes.

genes: SlHDA7 (SlHDA7, histone deacetylase, Solyc01g009110)
phenotype: Knockout of SlHDA7 accelerates tomato fruit maturation.
mechanism: SlHDA7 deacetylates H4ac to inhibit transcription of ripening-related genes.

genes: OsPIPK-FAB (phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinase, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsPIPK-FAB reduces rice resistance to M. oryzae, increasing lesion numbers and area compared to wild-type ZH11.
mechanism: OsPIPK-FAB suppresses the transcription of multiple genes with potential functions in various immune-related signaling pathways during the invasion by the blast fungus.

genes: OsPIPK-FAB (phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinase, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: Knockout of OsPIPK-FAB significantly enhances rice resistance to M. oryzae, reducing lesion numbers and area compared to wild-type ZH11.
mechanism: OsPIPK-FAB suppresses the transcription of multiple genes with potential functions in various immune-related signaling pathways during the invasion by the blast fungus.

genes: OsMBL1 (mannose-binding lectin, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: Knockout of OsMBL1 reduces rice resistance to M. oryzae, increasing lesion area and fungal biomass compared to wild-type Nipponbare.
mechanism: OsMBL1 activates defense genes and reactive oxygen species upon chitin binding, enhancing photoprotection by accelerating NPQ relaxation.

genes: OsMBL1 (mannose-binding lectin, Oryza sativa, synthetic), OsPIPK-FAB (phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinase, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: Double knockout of OsMBL1 and OsPIPK-FAB increases susceptibility to M. oryzae, with more lesions compared to wild-type.
mechanism: OsMBL1 acts upstream of OsPIPK-FAB, inhibiting its function to enhance disease resistance.

genes: OsMBL1 (mannose-binding lectin, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: OsMBL1-RFP localizes to the cytoplasm and nucleus in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsPIPK-FAB (phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinase, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: OsPIPK-FAB-GFP localizes to the cytoplasm in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsNCED4 (ABA biosynthetic enzyme, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Disruption of OsNCED4 significantly reduces NaCl stress tolerance in rice, with reduced survival rate, shoot and root length, and fresh weight under salt stress.
mechanism: Reduced ABA levels and increased ROS accumulation in osnced4 mutants lead to salt sensitivity.

genes: OsNCED4 (chloroplast-localized ABA biosynthetic enzyme, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsNCED4-GFP fusion localizes to chloroplasts in rice protoplasts, confirming its chloroplast localization.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsNCED4 (promoter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: ProOsNCED4-GUS transgenic plants show deeper GUS staining in leaves under NaCl and cold stress, indicating induced OsNCED4 expression.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaPT2 (phosphate transporter, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaPT2 increases shoot and root dry weight by ~15% in Arabidopsis thaliana under normal and low-Pi conditions.
mechanism: TaPT2 enhances phosphate transport, leading to increased Pi uptake and storage in roots and shoots.

genes: TaPT2 (phosphate transporter, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaPT2 increases shoot and root dry weight by ~15% in Arabidopsis thaliana under normal and low-Pi conditions.
mechanism: TaPT2 enhances phosphate transport, leading to increased Pi uptake and storage in roots and shoots.

genes: WAKL4 (WAKL4, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of wakl4 mutants restores Cd tolerance to wild-type levels, including root length, biomass, and chlorophyll content.
mechanism: WAKL4 regulates Cd tolerance by limiting Cd accumulation.

genes: WAKL4 (WAKL4, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of WAKL4-FLAG leads to rapid protein accumulation within 1 hour of Cd treatment, peaking at 2-4 hours.
mechanism: WAKL4 protein accumulation is specific and rapid in response to Cd stress.

genes: WAKL4 (WAKL4, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: WAKL4-GFP localizes to the plasma membrane and intracellular punctate structures in root apical meristem under Cd treatment.
mechanism: Cd treatment enhances BFA-induced foci of WAKL4-GFP, indicating reduced endocytosis.

genes: NRAMP1 (NRAMP1, metal transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Phospho-dead NRAMP1Y488F variant reduces Cd tolerance compared to wild-type and NRAMP1-expressing plants.
mechanism: Phosphorylation at Tyr488 is essential for NRAMP1 function in Cd tolerance.

genes: NRAMP1 (NRAMP1, metal transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Phospho-mimetic NRAMP1Y488E variant shows Cd tolerance similar to nramp1 mutant.
mechanism: Phosphorylation at Tyr488 is essential for NRAMP1 function in Cd tolerance.

genes: ARF10 (ARF10, auxin response factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (GFP, green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: ARF10-GFP expression is detected in a few cells surrounding the MMC (L1 and L2 layers) at pre-meiosis, becoming restricted to meiotic cells and integuments during gametogenesis.
mechanism: ARF10 is transcribed throughout the ovule but silenced by miR160 in most cells except those surrounding the MMC and outer integuments.

genes: mARF10 (mutated ARF10, auxin response factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (GFP, green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: mARF10-GFP lines exhibit supernumerary enlarged cells around the MMC, with 22.5% (mARF10a) and 21.6% (mARF10b) of ovules showing multiple enlarged cells compared to 7% in wild type.
mechanism: miR160 insensitivity in mARF10 leads to ubiquitous ARF10 expression in the ovule, causing ectopic FM identity in nucellar cells and apospory-like phenotypes.

genes: KNU (KNU, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), nlsYFP (nlsYFP, nuclear-localized yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: pKNU:nlsYFP marker identifies MMC identity in wild type (central signal) but only one cell expresses YFP in mARF10 lines, with extra enlarged cells lacking YFP signal.
mechanism: KNU promoter drives YFP expression specifically in the MMC, revealing that only one enlarged cell in mARF10 lines retains MMC identity.

genes: ASY3 (ASY3, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), RFP (RFP, red fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: ASY3:RFP marker detects meiotic precursor accumulation in the MMC in wild type, but only one enlarged cell in mARF10 lines accumulates the meiotic precursor.
mechanism: ASY3 promoter drives RFP expression in the MMC, indicating meiotic entry. In mARF10 lines, only one enlarged cell accumulates the meiotic precursor.

genes: LC2 (LC2, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), nlsYFP (nlsYFP, nuclear-localized yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: pLC2:nlsYFP marker detects FM identity in wild type (49% ovules with one FM) but 19% of mARF10 ovules show multiple FMs and 32% lack signal, indicating apospory-like phenotypes.
mechanism: LC2 promoter drives YFP expression in the FM, revealing ectopic FM formation in mARF10 lines with non-reduced cells.

genes: WOX2 (WOX2, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), CENH3_GFP (CENH3_GFP, centromere histone H3 fused with GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: pWOX2:CENH3_GFP marker reveals non-reduced cells in mARF10 lines with more than five chromosomes, indicating apospory-like gametophyte formation.
mechanism: WOX2 promoter drives CENH3_GFP expression in the FM, allowing chromosome counting and identification of non-reduced cells.

genes: EC1 (EC1, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), NLS_3xdsRed (NLS_3xdsRed, nuclear-localized red fluorescent protein, synthetic), DD22 (DD22, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), NLS_YFP (NLS_YFP, nuclear-localized yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic), DD2 (DD2, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), NLS_3xGFP (NLS_3xGFP, nuclear-localized green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: FGR7.0 marker line labels synergid cells (GFP), egg cell (RFP), and central cell (YFP) in wild type, but mARF10 lines show supernumerary egg cells, synergid/central cell identity mix-ups, and multiple embryo sacs.
mechanism: FGR7.0 combines markers for synergid, egg, and central cells, revealing cell identity misspecification in mARF10 gametophytes.

genes: GLP (glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, N. yezoensis, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GLP increases lipid accumulation by ~22.63% under nitrogen starvation and enhances survival rates under abiotic stress (NaCl, H2O2, heat) in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
mechanism: GLP upregulates starch phosphorylase (SP), glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GPDH), and pyruvate ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR) to redirect carbon partitioning from starch to lipid synthesis. It also enhances expression of stress-response genes including HSF1, CAT, APX, and AOX for ROS scavenging and heat tolerance.

genes: StGPT1 (glucose 6-phosphate transporter, Solanum tuberosum, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of StGPT1 reduces P. infestans colonization, with significantly smaller disease lesion diameters in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: StGPT1 localizes to chloroplasts and ER, enhances ROS production, and upregulates JA and SA levels to activate immune responses.

genes: StGPT1 (glucose 6-phosphate transporter, Solanum tuberosum, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of StGPT1 in potato reduces P. infestans colonization, with significantly smaller disease lesion diameters in transgenic lines.
mechanism: StGPT1 localizes to chloroplasts, enhances ROS production, and upregulates JA and SA levels to activate immune responses.

genes: StGPT1 (glucose 6-phosphate transporter, Solanum tuberosum, synthetic)
phenotype: RNAi lines of StGPT1 in N. benthamiana exhibit increased susceptibility to P. infestans and stunted growth.
mechanism: Reduced StGPT1 expression leads to lower ROS production and downregulation of immune-related genes.

genes: StGPT1 (glucose 6-phosphate transporter, Solanum tuberosum, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP-StGPT1 (with interfered cTP) increases susceptibility to P. infestans, while StGPT1ΔcTP-GFP retains partial resistance.
mechanism: Chloroplast localization is necessary for StGPT1's resistance function; disruption of cTP reduces resistance.

genes: StGPT1 (glucose 6-phosphate transporter, Solanum tuberosum, synthetic), StRFP1 (E3 ligase, Solanum tuberosum, synthetic)
phenotype: Co-expression of StGPT1 and StRFP1 in N. benthamiana synergistically enhances resistance to P. infestans, with significantly smaller disease lesions.
mechanism: StRFP1 ubiquitinates StGPT1, promoting its accumulation in chloroplasts and enhancing immune responses.

genes: SlATG8f (SlATG8f, autophagy-related gene 8f, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlATG8f decreases heat tolerance in tomato plants but increases chlorophyll content and protects chloroplasts under heat stress.
mechanism: SlATG8f overexpression enhances autophagy activity, which stabilizes SlHSP21 expression and mitigates chloroplast damage during heat stress.

genes: VvGA2ox7 (VvGA2ox7, hydrophilic protein with DIOX_N and 2OG-FeII_Oxy domains, grape)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvGA2ox7 in Arabidopsis thaliana enhanced antioxidant enzymatic activities and proline, chlorophyll, and ABA contents, and decreased relative electrical conductivity, malondialdehyde, and GA3 contents
mechanism: VvGA2ox7 positively regulated the expression of salt stress response genes (KAT1, APX1, LEA, P5CS1, AVP1, CBF1), indicating improved salt stress tolerance

genes: HcOSC6 (HcOSC6, gene catalyzing cucurbitadienol formation, Cucurbita chinensis)
phenotype: OE-HcOSC6 lines exhibit significantly higher cucurbitadienol levels than genome-edited lines
mechanism: Transcriptomic analysis revealed up-regulation of downstream genes HcCYP87D20, HcCYP81Q58, and HcSDR34 in OE lines

genes: ATHB8 (homeobox protein ATHB8, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli, source)
phenotype: ProATHB8::GUS expression increases at the periphery of the developing syncytium during BCN infection in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ATHB8 promoter activity is upregulated at the infection site, suggesting a role in syncytium formation.

genes: ATHB8 (homeobox protein ATHB8, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic, source)
phenotype: ProATHB8::4xYFP expression is elevated at the periphery of the syncytium during BCN infection in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ATHB8 promoter activity shifts to the periphery of the syncytium, indicating a role in syncytium expansion.

genes: MIR165a (microRNA 165a, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic, source)
phenotype: ProMIR165a::GFP expression is down-regulated at the BCN infection site in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Reduced MIR165a activity at the infection site may contribute to syncytium formation by suppressing HD-ZIP III gene expression.

genes: MIR165a (microRNA 165a, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), XVE (synthetic, source)
phenotype: Inducible expression of MIR165a suppresses BCN female development and syncytium size in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MIR165a knockdown of HD-ZIP III genes disrupts syncytium establishment.

genes: ATHB8 (homeobox protein ATHB8, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic, source)
phenotype: Overexpression of ATHB8d-YFP does not increase susceptibility of Arabidopsis to BCN.
mechanism: Overexpression of ATHB8d-YFP does not affect nematode penetration or syncytium size, suggesting ATHB8 alone is not sufficient for hyper-susceptibility.

genes: p3a (p3a, viral protein, Barley yellow dwarf virus)
phenotype: Overexpression of p3a in wheat promotes BYDV infection, intensifying leaf tip yellowing symptoms and increasing viral accumulation.
mechanism: p3a interacts with the zinc finger domain of TaDOF, inhibiting its repression of TaHSP70 promoter activity, thereby promoting TaHSP70 expression and BYDV infection.

genes: p3a (p3a, viral protein, Barley yellow dwarf virus)
phenotype: Overexpression of p3a in N. benthamiana inhibited BAX- and INF1-induced cell necrosis and suppressed immune-related gene expression.
mechanism: p3a inhibits the expression of immune-related genes stimulated by BAX, such as NbHSP90, NbSGT1, and NbMYB30.

genes: TaDOF (TaDOF, transcription factor, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaDOF in wheat inhibited BYDV infection, reducing yellowing symptoms and viral accumulation.
mechanism: TaDOF interacts with the TaHSP70 promoter, repressing its activity, thereby suppressing BYDV infection.

genes: TaHSP70 (TaHSP70, heat shock protein 70, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaHSP70 in wheat promoted BYDV infection, increasing yellowing symptoms and viral accumulation.
mechanism: TaHSP70 expression is upregulated by p3a-mediated inhibition of TaDOF repression, promoting BYDV infection.

genes: TaHSP70 (TaHSP70, heat shock protein 70, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Knockdown of TaHSP70 in wheat inhibited BYDV infection, reducing yellowing symptoms and viral accumulation.
mechanism: TaHSP70 is required for BYDV infection; its knockdown suppresses viral accumulation.

genes: LhWUS (LhWUS, WUSCHEL transcription factor, Liriodendron chinense × Liriodendron tulipifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of p35S:LhWUS-GFP-GR increases callus weight by ~3–6 fold and promotes somatic embryogenesis in Liriodendron hybrid callus.
mechanism: DEX/GR system regulates LhWUS nuclear localization, enhancing cell proliferation and embryo formation.

genes: LhWUS (LhWUS, WUSCHEL transcription factor, Liriodendron chinense × Liriodendron tulipifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of p35S:LhWUS-GR increases callus weight by ~4–8 fold and promotes somatic embryogenesis in Liriodendron hybrid callus.
mechanism: DEX/GR system regulates LhWUS nuclear localization, enhancing cell proliferation and embryo formation.

genes: JrPP2A07 (JrPP2A07, osmotic stress response gene, Juglans regia)
phenotype: Overexpression of JrPP2A07 reduces ROS accumulation and cell damage, improving osmotic stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: JrPP2A07 is involved in Ca and ABA signaling pathways, enhancing osmotic stress tolerance.

genes: JrPP2A09 (JrPP2A09, osmotic stress response gene, Juglans regia)
phenotype: Overexpression of JrPP2A09 reduces ROS accumulation and cell damage, improving osmotic stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: JrPP2A09 is involved in Ca and ABA signaling pathways, enhancing osmotic stress tolerance.

genes: JrPP2A14 (JrPP2A14, osmotic stress response gene, Juglans regia)
phenotype: Overexpression of JrPP2A14 reduces ROS accumulation and cell damage, improving osmotic stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: JrPP2A14 is involved in Ca and ABA signaling pathways, enhancing osmotic stress tolerance.

genes: OsYABBY6 (YABBY transcription factor, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsYABBY6 increases cold tolerance in rice by enhancing ROS scavenging and osmoregulatory systems, reducing cellular damage under cold stress.
mechanism: OsYABBY6 overexpression upregulates cold-responsive genes (OsDREB1A, OsDREB1B, etc.) and reduces ROS accumulation (H2O2, superoxide anion), while increasing antioxidant enzyme activities (CAT, SOD) and proline content.

genes: OsYABBY6 (YABBY transcription factor, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockdown of OsYABBY6 increases drought tolerance in rice by reducing water loss rate, ROS accumulation, and increasing osmolyte content (soluble sugar, proline).
mechanism: OsYABBY6 knockdown downregulates NADPH oxidase genes (OsRbohA, OsRbohG, OsRbohH) and upregulates OsSIK1, enhancing antioxidant systems. It also reduces endogenous ABA synthesis and promotes ABA signaling, increasing drought tolerance.

genes: OsYABBY6 (YABBY transcription factor, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: GUS activity is detected in palea, lemma, leaf blade, leaf sheath, culm, stem node, and embryo, with weaker signals in root, anther, and pistil.
mechanism: NA

genes: AHA2 (plasma membrane H+-ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of plasma membrane H+-ATPase accelerates stomatal opening and closing kinetics, increases stomatal aperture by ~15% during daylight, and improves water use efficiency (WUE) under fluctuating light conditions while reducing WUE under constant light.
mechanism: H+-ATPase overexpression enhances H+ efflux and plasma membrane hyperpolarization, increasing [Ca2+]i levels which suppress K+ influx and activate anion channels, accelerating stomatal responses to light transitions.

plant_species: Oryza sativa L. subsp. japonica cv. Nipponbare
genes: SLR1 (OsSLR1, rice DELLA protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SLR1 increases salt tolerance in rice.
mechanism: SUMOylation disrupts SLR1 interaction with stress-associated transcription factors, modulating gene expression related to GA biosynthesis and stress response.

plant_species: Oryza sativa L. subsp. japonica cv. Nipponbare
genes: SUMO1SLR1 (fusion of SUMO1 and SLR1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SUMO1SLR1 increases salt tolerance and improves recovery in rice.
mechanism: SUMOylation disrupts SLR1 interaction with stress-associated transcription factors, modulating gene expression related to GA biosynthesis and stress response.

genes: apoaequorin (apoaequorin, calcium sensor protein, Aequorea victoria)
phenotype: Expression of apoaequorin enables in vivo measurement of cytosolic calcium transients in potato leaves without visible growth effects.
mechanism: Apoaequorin binds Ca2+ and emits luminescence upon Ca2+ binding, allowing quantification of [Ca2+]cyt changes.

genes: AsHSFB1 (AsHSFB1, heat shock transcription factor B1, Allium sativum)
phenotype: Overexpression of AsHSFB1 in Arabidopsis thaliana reduces heat tolerance, as evidenced by lower germination rates and increased wilting under heat stress.
mechanism: AsHSFB1 negatively regulates heat resistance by suppressing the expression of downstream heat shock protein (HSP) genes.

genes: AtDEG2ΔPDZ1 (AtDEG2ΔPDZ1, mutant proteolytically active version of AtDEG2 lacking holdase and disaggregase activities, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtDEG2ΔPDZ1-GFP in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to increased homodimerization of γ1 subunit of ATP synthase via disulphide bridges under long-term high irradiance stress.
mechanism: AtDeg2ΔPDZ1-GFP lacks holdase activity, allowing γ1 subunit homodimerization via disulphide bridges under high irradiance stress. Native AtDeg2 normally inhibits this homodimerization through holdase activity.

genes: phyD-YFP (phyD-YFP, fusion of phyD and YFP, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of phyD-YFP increases photomorphogenesis efficiency in the presence of phyC at low temperatures (17°C) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: phyD-YFP forms photobodies in the nucleus and binds chromophore, leading to light signaling. The presence of phyC and low temperature enhances phyD-YFP accumulation and photomorphogenic response.

genes: phyD-GFP (phyD-GFP, fusion of phyD and GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of phyD-GFP leads to temperature-dependent accumulation and photomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: phyD-GFP accumulates to higher levels at low temperatures and functions in a temperature-dependent manner, similar to phyD-YFP.

genes: phyB-CFP (phyB-CFP, fusion of phyB and CFP, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of phyB-CFP mediates photomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis thaliana under red light at both low and high temperatures.
mechanism: phyB-CFP binds chromophore and activates light signaling, leading to photomorphogenic responses. It functions efficiently at both 17°C and 27°C.

genes: SlSTOP1 (Solanum lycopersicum STOP1, transcription factor), GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS activity observed in roots, flowers, and fruits but absent in stems and leaves; Al treatment did not affect root GUS activity, indicating constitutive expression.
mechanism: SlSTOP1 is a master regulator of Al tolerance, with GUS reporter activity reflecting its constitutive expression and Al-induced nuclear accumulation.

genes: SlSTOP1 (Solanum lycopersicum STOP1, transcription factor), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: SlSTOP1-GFP accumulation observed under Al treatment, with intensified GFP fluorescence in root tips, consistent with Al-induced nuclear accumulation in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: SlSTOP1 overexpression leads to nuclear accumulation under Al stress, enhancing Al tolerance through transcriptional regulation of downstream genes.

genes: SlHAK5 (Solanum lycopersicum HAK5, high-affinity K+ transporter), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: SlHAK5-GFP localized to the plasma membrane in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves, confirming its role in K+ uptake and Al-induced citrate secretion for Al tolerance.
mechanism: SlHAK5, a high-affinity K+ transporter, is directly regulated by SlSTOP1 and mediates Al-induced citrate secretion, reducing Al accumulation in root tips.

genes: LOC_Os05g11120 (An7 candidate gene, cytochrome P450 CYP90D3, Oryza glumaepatula), LOC_Os05g11130 (An7 candidate gene, cytochrome P450 CYP90D3, Oryza glumaepatula), LOC_Os05g11160 (An7 candidate gene, cytochrome P450 CYP90D3, Oryza glumaepatula)
phenotype: Complementation of awn phenotype with average awn length of 5.8 mm in transgenic T65 plants.
mechanism: An7 encodes cytochrome P450 CYP90D3 involved in brassinosteroid (BR) biosynthesis, which cooperates with RAE3 for awn elongation.

genes: LOC_Os05g11140 (An7 candidate gene, cytochrome P450 CYP90D3, Oryza glumaepatula)
phenotype: Complementation of awn phenotype with average awn length of 5.8 mm in transgenic T65 plants.
mechanism: An7 encodes cytochrome P450 CYP90D3 involved in brassinosteroid (BR) biosynthesis, which cooperates with RAE3 for awn elongation.

genes: Ghd7 (promoter region, promoter fragment, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Mutations in the f3 region of Ghd7 promoter delay heading by ~2 days under LD conditions and upregulate Ghd7 expression.
mechanism: Ghd7 upregulation in f3 mutants leads to later heading, indicating f3 is a repressive cis element for Ghd7.

genes: OsIAA23 (full-length protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsIAA23-YFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: OsIAA23 is a nuclear protein, as demonstrated by YFP fluorescence co-localizing with nuclear marker Ghd7-RFP.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of GUS reporter gene in embryogenic callus and regenerated plants, confirmed by histochemical staining showing blue spots.
mechanism: The CaMV35S promoter drives constitutive expression of the GUS reporter gene, enabling visualization of gene activity through GUS staining.

genes: LkPDS (phytoene desaturase, target gene, Larix kaempferi)
phenotype: Albino and mosaic phenotypes in somatic embryos due to disruption of LkPDS gene function, with albino plants showing severe stunted growth and eventual death.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated editing of the LkPDS gene disrupts phytoene desaturation in carotenoid biosynthesis, leading to albinism and impaired chlorophyll synthesis.

genes: MPK12 (MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASE 12, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Guard cell-specific MPK12 complementation in gad2-1* restores CO2 sensitivity, with transpiration rates adjusting to altered CO2 concentrations (100 ppm and 800 ppm) and stomatal responses returning to near-normal levels.
mechanism: MPK12 suppresses the activity of HT1, a negative regulator of high CO2 signaling, thereby enabling stomatal closure in response to elevated CO2.

genes: Yr87/Lr85 (leaf and stripe rust resistance gene, Aegilops longissima)
gene_construct: native promoter-Yr87/Lr85 cDNA-native terminator---native promoter-Yr87/Lr85 gDNA (four exons separated by shortened introns)-native terminator
phenotype: Transgenic wheat lines expressing Yr87/Lr85 show resistance to Puccinia triticina (leaf rust) and Puccinia striiformis (stripe rust) isolates, with gDNA constructs showing variable resistance and cDNA constructs showing susceptibility.
mechanism: Yr87/Lr85 slows pathogen development without completely blocking infection, preventing disease progression in seedlings and adult plants.

genes: BcGRP20 (BraA02g002400.3 C, membrane-localized protein, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: BcGRP20-GFP fusion protein localizes to the cell membrane in transiently expressed tobacco
mechanism: Subcellular localization of BcGRP20 to the cell membrane

genes: BcGRP20 (BraA02g002400.3 C, membrane-localized protein, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of BcGRP20 in Arabidopsis grp20 mutant restores pollen fertility to wild-type levels
mechanism: Complementation of grp20 mutant defects in pollen wall formation and tapetum development

genes: GhATL68b-A (GhATL68b-A, E3 ubiquitin ligase with RING-H2 domain, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of GhATL68b-A results in significantly shorter cotton fiber cells (mean fiber length reduced compared to wild-type) and reduced fiber elongation at break, uniformity, and total fiber weight from 100 seeds.
mechanism: GhATL68b-A ubiquitinates GhDECR (2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase) for 26S proteasome-mediated degradation, modulating polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) metabolism and membrane fluidity in developing fiber cells.

genes: GhATL68b-D (GhATL68b-D, E3 ubiquitin ligase with RING-H2 domain, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of GhATL68b-D results in significantly shorter cotton fiber cells (mean fiber length reduced compared to wild-type) and reduced fiber elongation at break, uniformity, and total fiber weight from 100 seeds.
mechanism: GhATL68b-D ubiquitinates GhDECR (2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase) for 26S proteasome-mediated degradation, modulating polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) metabolism and membrane fluidity in developing fiber cells.

genes: BRG8 (Blast Resistance Gene 8, blast resistance gene, TTP)
phenotype: Cytosol-localized BRG8 (BRG8Hap3-EGFP-NES) enhances resistance to M. oryzae and Xoo but induces dwarfism and cell death.
mechanism: Cytosol-localized BRG8 activates immune signaling but causes autoimmunity, leading to growth penalties.

genes: LA4 (LOC_Os05g33830, tiller angle regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of la4 mutant rescued the large tiller angle phenotype in rice.
mechanism: LA4 positively regulates shoot gravitropism, which controls tiller angle by mediating asymmetric auxin distribution.

genes: LA4 (LOC_Os05g33830, tiller angle regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CRISPR-engineered la4 mutants exhibited significantly enlarged tiller angles in rice.
mechanism: LA4 functions in a novel pathway independent of LA2–LA3-mediated gravity sensing to regulate asymmetric auxin distribution and shoot gravitropism.

genes: OsNLP3 (OsNLP3, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNLP3 increases grain weight by ~3.23% and grain dimensions in rice.
mechanism: OsNLP3 enhances grain weight by stimulating cell division and expansion during grain development.

genes: OsNLP3 (OsNLP3, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNLP3 increases grain weight by ~3.23% and grain dimensions in rice.
mechanism: OsNLP3 enhances grain weight by stimulating cell division and expansion during grain development.

genes: CsWRKY29 (cold- and ABA-inducible WRKY transcription factor, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: CsWRKY29-GFP fusion protein localized in the nucleus of N. benthamiana leaves
mechanism: CsWRKY29 contains a WRKY heptapeptide domain and C2H2 zinc finger motif, enabling nuclear localization

genes: CsWRKY29 (cold- and ABA-inducible WRKY transcription factor, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsWRKY29 increased freezing tolerance (survival rate 85% vs. 55-32% in WT under ABA) and enhanced ABA sensitivity during germination
mechanism: CsWRKY29 upregulates cold-responsive genes (AtCBF1-3, AtCOR47, AtZAT12) and ABA-associated genes (AtABI5), increases SOD activity, and accumulates ROS under cold stress

genes: SlCDPK27 (calcium-dependent protein kinase 27, tomato), SlCDPK26 (calcium-dependent protein kinase 26, tomato)
phenotype: Increased soluble solids content (SSC) in large-fruited tomato cultivars without reduction in fruit weight or yield
mechanism: SlCDPK27 and SlCDPK26 act as sugar brakes by phosphorylating and degrading SlSUS3, a sucrose synthase. Genome editing removes this brake, allowing higher sugar accumulation

genes: SlCDPK27 (calcium-dependent protein kinase 27, tomato)
phenotype: Expression pattern analysis of SlCDPK27 in tomato tissues
mechanism: NA

genes: SlCDPK27 (calcium-dependent protein kinase 27, tomato), SlCDPK27-CR1 (mutant allele of SlCDPK27)
phenotype: Subcellular localization analysis of SlCDPK27 and its CR1 mutant variant
mechanism: NA

genes: SlCDPK27 (calcium-dependent protein kinase 27, tomato), SlCDPK27-CR1 (mutant allele of SlCDPK27), SlCDPK27-CR2 (another mutant allele of SlCDPK27), SlCDPK26 (calcium-dependent protein kinase 26, tomato), SlSUS3 (sucrose synthase 3, tomato)
phenotype: Analysis of protein-protein interactions between SlCDPK variants and SlSUS3 in Nicotiana benthamiana
mechanism: NA

genes: SuTPS1 (SuTPS1, terpene synthase, Sanionia uncinata)
phenotype: Overexpression of SuTPS1 in Arabidopsis thaliana does not significantly alter terpene volatile profiles.
mechanism: NA

genes: SuMTPSL2 (SuMTPSL2, microbial terpene synthase-like, Sanionia uncinata)
phenotype: Overexpression of SuMTPSL2 in Arabidopsis thaliana recapitulates amorpha-4,11-diene production and generates germacrene B.
mechanism: SuMTPSL2 catalyzes farnesyl pyrophosphate to amorpha-4,11-diene and germacrene B via promiscuous enzymatic activity.

genes: GFP-ADF7 (ADF7, actin depolymerization factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP-Profilin2 (Profilin2, actin depolymerization factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), GCaMP5 (calcium sensor, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP-ADF7 and GFP-Profilin2 in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to ~15% reduction in seed setting rate and aberrant pollen tube growth.
mechanism: ADF7 and Profilin2 mediate actin spatial organization essential for sperm cell biogenesis and male fertility.

genes: GFP-ATG5 (ATG5, autophagy-related protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP-ATG7 (ATG7, autophagy-related protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of ATG5 and ATG7 under their respective native promoters rescues the phenotypes observed in atg5-1 and atg7-2 mutants, restoring seed setting rate to levels comparable to those in the WT.
mechanism: ATG5 and ATG7-mediated autophagy modulates pollen germination and tube growth.

genes: ADF-RNAi (ADF, actin depolymerization factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), Profilin-RNAi (Profilin, actin depolymerization factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Down-regulation of ADF and/or Profilin partially restores the defective phenotypes of atg5 and/or atg7 mutants, including seed setting rate and actin filament organization.
mechanism: ADF7 and Profilin2 mediated actin spatial organization is functionally essential for the sperm cell biogenesis and male fertility in Arabidopsis.

genes: ADF-RNAi (ADF, actin depolymerization factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), Profilin-RNAi (Profilin, actin depolymerization factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Dual down-regulation of ADF and Profilin in atg5-1/atg7-2 mutants partially restores seed setting rate and actin filament organization.
mechanism: ADF7 and Profilin2 mediated actin spatial organization is functionally essential for the sperm cell biogenesis and male fertility in Arabidopsis.

genes: SlRbohB (RbohB, NADPH oxidase, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Knockout of SlRbohB causes a 1 bp insertion in the first exon, resulting in a loss-of-function mutation in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) cultivar Rio Grande PtoR.
mechanism: The 1 bp insertion in SlRbohB leads to a frameshift mutation, disrupting the gene's function in NADPH oxidase activity.

genes: SlSERK3A (SERK3A, co-receptor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of SlSERK3A in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) reduces flg22Pst-induced ROS burst compared to empty control (EC1).
mechanism: VIGS-mediated knockdown of SlSERK3A disrupts its role as a co-receptor in FLS2-mediated ROS production.

genes: SlSERK3B (SERK3B, co-receptor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of SlSERK3B in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) does not significantly reduce flgII-28Pst-induced ROS burst compared to empty control (EC1).
mechanism: VIGS-mediated knockdown of SlSERK3B does not affect its role in FLS3-mediated ROS production, suggesting differential interaction with PRRs.

genes: SlSERK3A (SERK3A, co-receptor, Solanum lycopersicum), SlSERK3B (SERK3B, co-receptor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of both SlSERK3A and SlSERK3B in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) reduces flgII-28Pst-induced ROS burst compared to empty control (EC1).
mechanism: VIGS-mediated knockdown of both SlSERK3A and SlSERK3B disrupts their combined role in FLS3-mediated ROS production.

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic, eGFP)
phenotype: pRC-eGFP produces 7.2-fold higher eGFP signal than pJL-TRBO-eGFP in leaf lamina, with high per-cell expression but reduced vascular expression
mechanism: Combination of CaMV 35S promoter, synthetic 5' UTR, CPMV 3' UTR, double terminators, and MAR enhances translation and transcript stability

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic, eGFP)
phenotype: pR5-eGFP produces 5.6-fold higher eGFP signal than pJL-TRBO-eGFP with high expression in both leaf lamina and vasculature
mechanism: Synthetic 5' UTR enhances translation and transcript stability

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic, eGFP)
phenotype: pRU-eGFP shows reduced eGFP expression compared to pR5-eGFP
mechanism: Combination of 5' and 3' UTRs does not enhance expression as effectively as 5' UTR alone

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic, eGFP)
phenotype: pJL-TRBO-eGFP shows high vascular expression but low lamina expression compared to pRC/pR5
mechanism: Native TMV UTRs drive vascular-specific expression

genes: miR394a (microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana), miR394b (microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knockout of miR394a and miR394b results in axillary meristem (AM) defects in Arabidopsis thaliana, with reduced AM formation in rosette leaf axils.
mechanism: miR394a and miR394b redundantly regulate AM formation by downregulating LCR mRNA, which inhibits AM initiation.

genes: miR394a (microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana), miR394b (microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR394a and miR394b did not result in a change in the number of axillary meristems (AMs) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: miR394 overexpression does not alter AM formation, suggesting that miR394's role is primarily through downregulation of LCR.

genes: LCR (F-box protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), LCR4m (miR394-resistant LCR variant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of LCR4m under the LCR promoter or CaMV 35S promoter leads to strong axillary meristem (AM) deficiency in Arabidopsis thaliana, with 97.7% of rosette leaves presenting bare axils.
mechanism: LCR inhibits AM formation through its F-box domain, likely by ubiquitinating TPL and promoting its degradation.

genes: LCR (F-box protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), LCR4mΔF-box (F-box domain-deleted LCR variant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of LCR4mΔF-box (F-box domain removed) results in normal axillary meristem (AM) formation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: The F-box domain of LCR is necessary for its function in inhibiting AM initiation.

genes: LCR5m (miR394-resistant LCR variant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of LCR5m under the REV promoter causes severe axillary meristem (AM) defects in Arabidopsis thaliana, while expression under the KAN1 promoter does not.
mechanism: LCR5m expression in the adaxial domain (REV promoter) inhibits AM formation, whereas expression in the abaxial domain (KAN1 promoter) does not.

genes: miR394a (microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana), miR394b (microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of GFPer under the MIR394A and MIR394B promoters reveals miR394 expression in the boundary region between leaf primordia and the shoot apical meristem (SAM) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: miR394 is expressed in the adaxial domain of leaves and AMs, indicating its role in AM initiation.

genes: TPL (TOPLESS, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TPL rescues the axillary meristem (AM) deficiency caused by LCR4m overexpression in Arabidopsis thaliana, restoring normal AM formation.
mechanism: TPL promotes AM initiation by activating the REV and STM pathways, counteracting LCR-mediated inhibition.

genes: TaZFP8-5B (TaZFP8-5B, negative regulator of plant immunity, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Knocking down TaZFP8 increased wheat resistance to Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Pst).
mechanism: TaZFP8-5B plays a negative role in the modulation of plant immunity.

genes: TaZFP8-5B (TaZFP8-5B, negative regulator of plant immunity, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaZFP8-5B reduced wheat resistance to stripe rust and rice resistance to Magnaporthe oryzae.
mechanism: TaZFP8-5B plays a negative role in the modulation of plant immunity.

genes: CHE (Circadian Clock Transcription Factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CHE-HA/che-2 complements the che-2 mutant in inducing systemic ICS1, FMO1, and PR1 expression, restoring SA and NHP production.
mechanism: CHE-sulfenylation enhances binding to the ICS1 promoter, activating systemic SA synthesis.

genes: CHE (Circadian Clock Transcription Factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: cheCS-HA/che-2 fails to complement che-2 in inducing systemic ICS1, FMO1, and PR1 expression, leading to compromised SA and NHP production.
mechanism: CHE-sulfenylation is disrupted in cheCS-HA, preventing binding to the ICS1 promoter and systemic SA synthesis.

genes: CHE (Circadian Clock Transcription Factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: cheCW-HA/che-2 fails to complement che-2 in inducing systemic ICS1, FMO1, and PR1 expression, leading to compromised SA and NHP production.
mechanism: CHE-sulfenylation is disrupted in cheCW-HA, preventing binding to the ICS1 promoter and systemic SA synthesis.

genes: PSBO (photosystem II oxygen-evolving complex protein, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii)
phenotype: Downregulation of PSBO leads to severe decrease in Fv/Fm values (photosynthetic activity) with halftime of 5-53 hours depending on light intensity and carbon availability in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
mechanism: PSBO is essential for OEC activity; its loss causes donor-side photoinhibition leading to rapid Fv/Fm diminishment

genes: PbELF4a (PbELF4a, homologous to AtELF4, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbELF4a significantly delayed flowering and suppressed the expression of flowering-related genes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: PbELF4b (PbELF4b, homologous to AtELF4, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbELF4b significantly delayed flowering and suppressed the expression of flowering-related genes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: PbELF4b (PbELF4b, homologous to AtELF4, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbELF4b induced premature leaf senescence, evidenced by reduced chlorophyll content and increased expression of senescence-associated genes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: BRK1 (BRK1, root hair development regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BRK1-GFP reduces root hair length by ~46-50% compared to wild type and resembles spi-142 mutant phenotypes under normal conditions. Under 50 mM NaCl, pBRK1:BRK1-GFP plants show hyper-sensitive root hair development with ~97.5% reduction in root hair length and 84% reduction in root hair density.
mechanism: BRK1 negatively modulates root hair tip-growth and initiation. Overexpression stabilizes BRK1 protein, leading to impaired F-actin cytoskeleton organization and salt stress response.

genes: BRK1 (BRK1, root hair development regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of BRK1-GFP in protoplasts reduces root hair growth rate compared to wild type. Under 50 mM NaCl, p35S:BRK1-GFP plants show hyper-sensitive root hair development with ~97.5% reduction in root hair length.
mechanism: BRK1 negatively modulates root hair tip-growth through F-actin cytoskeleton regulation. Overexpression stabilizes BRK1 protein, leading to impaired salt stress response.

genes: ECT2 (ECT2, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), mCherry (mCherry, synthetic, source)
phenotype: Overexpression of ECT2-mCherry leads to phenotypic changes similar to ptre1 mutants, including reduced leaf size and altered proteasome activity.
mechanism: ECT2 interacts with PTRE1 and 20S proteasome subunits on ribosomes, enhancing m6A RNA binding and proteasome activity.

genes: ECT2Δ156-413 (ECT2Δ156-413, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), mCherry (mCherry, synthetic, source)
phenotype: Overexpression of ECT2Δ156-413-mCherry does not result in noticeable phenotypic changes or significant effects on PTRE1 expression, 20S proteasome subunits, or proteasome activity.
mechanism: The middle region of ECT2 (156–413) is required for interactions with PTRE1 and 20S subunits, which are crucial for ECT2's regulatory functions.

genes: CsERF110 (CsERF110, ABA-induced transcriptional activator, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsERF110 increases carotenoid content in citrus peel and calli by ~15%.
mechanism: CsERF110 activates carotenoid biosynthetic genes (CsGGPPS, CsPSY, CsPDS, CsCRTISO, CsLCYB2, CsLCYE, CsHYD, CsNCED2) and functions as a nuclear-localized transcriptional activator.

genes: CsERF110 (CsERF110, ABA-induced transcriptional activator, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: RNAi-CsERF110 reduces carotenoid content in citrus calli and fruits by ~15% and suppresses coloration.
mechanism: CsERF110 knockdown inhibits activation of carotenoid biosynthetic genes (CsGGPPS, CsPSY, CsPDS, CsCRTISO, CsLCYB2, CsLCYE, CsHYD, CsNCED2).

genes: CsERF53 (CsERF53, ABA-induced transcriptional activator, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsERF53 in citrus calli and fruits increases carotenoid content by ~15% and enhances coloration (yellow/orange-red).
mechanism: CsERF53 activates carotenoid biosynthetic genes (CsGGPPS, CsPSY, CsHYD, CsZEP, CsNCED2) and functions as a nuclear-localized transcriptional activator.

genes: CsERF53 (CsERF53, ABA-induced transcriptional activator, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: RNAi-CsERF53 reduces carotenoid content in citrus calli and fruits by ~15% and suppresses coloration.
mechanism: CsERF53 knockdown inhibits activation of carotenoid biosynthetic genes (CsGGPPS, CsPSY, CsHYD, CsZEP, CsNCED2).

genes: CsERF110 (CsERF110, ABA-induced transcriptional activator, Citrus sinensis), CsERF53 (CsERF53, ABA-induced transcriptional activator, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Co-overexpression of CsERF110 and CsERF53 in citrus calli and fruits synergistically increases carotenoid content by ~20% and enhances coloration.
mechanism: The CsERF110–CsERF53 transcriptional regulatory module synergistically activates carotenoid biosynthetic genes (CsGGPPS, CsPSY, CsPDS, CsCRTISO, CsLCYB2, CsLCYE, CsHYD, CsZEP, CsNCED2).

genes: IPT (ISOPENTENYLTRANSFERASE, cytokinin biosynthetic gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of IPT in epidermis/cortex (J2601>>IPT) causes root shortening and increased ACC levels (~4.3-fold), while in provascular tissues (J2351>>IPT) causes weaker root shortening and lower ACC increase (~1.6-fold).
mechanism: Cytokinin-induced ethylene production via ACC biosynthesis, with cell-type-specific effects on root elongation and RAM shortening.

genes: EBF2 (EIN3-BINDING F BOX PROTEIN 2, negative regulator of ethylene signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of EBF2 in outer root cell files (pA14::EBF2) reduces sensitivity to cytokinin-induced root shortening compared to wild type.
mechanism: Attenuation of ethylene signaling in epidermis/LRC reduces cytokinin-mediated root growth inhibition.

genes: EBF2 (EIN3-BINDING F BOX PROTEIN 2, negative regulator of ethylene signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of EBF2 in LRC (pLRC1::EBF2) reduces sensitivity to cytokinin-induced root shortening compared to wild type.
mechanism: Attenuation of ethylene signaling in LRC reduces cytokinin-mediated root growth inhibition.

genes: EBF2 (EIN3-BINDING F BOX PROTEIN 2, negative regulator of ethylene signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of EBF2 in multiple cell types (p35S::EBF2) reduces sensitivity to cytokinin-induced root shortening compared to wild type.
mechanism: Attenuation of ethylene signaling in epidermis reduces cytokinin-mediated root growth inhibition.

genes: ACO3 (ACC OXIDASE 3, ethylene biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana), ACO4 (ACC OXIDASE 4, ethylene biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ACO3 and ACO4 are upregulated in response to cytokinins and ethylene, with ACO3 showing cytokinin-specific activation in stele/vasculature and ACO4 showing ethylene-dependent activation in epidermis/cortex.
mechanism: Cytokinin and ethylene regulate ACO3 and ACO4 expression via ARR1 and ARR2/EIN2-C interactions, controlling ethylene biosynthesis in root growth.

genes: MpARF1 (auxin signaling protein, Marchantia polymorpha, endogenous), MpARF2 (auxin signaling protein, Marchantia polymorpha, endogenous), MpARF3 (auxin signaling protein, Marchantia polymorpha, endogenous), MpIAA (auxin signaling protein, Marchantia polymorpha, endogenous), MpTIR1 (auxin signaling protein, Marchantia polymorpha, endogenous), MpncARF (auxin signaling protein, Marchantia polymorpha, endogenous)
phenotype: Knockin lines displayed macroscopically normal morphologies and responded to auxin similarly to wild type. MpARF1-mScarletI showed highest accumulation in most cell types, MpARF2-mScarletI was absent in distal apical notch regions, and MpARF3-mScarletI showed broad but weak accumulation.
mechanism: Fluorescently tagged proteins are functional and maintain normal auxin response. ARF stoichiometry changes during germination regulate auxin response by altering transcriptional output.

genes: MpARF2 (auxin signaling protein, Marchantia polymorpha, endogenous)
phenotype: Overexpression of MpARF2 prevents thallus growth, causes multiple apical notches, defective growth, lack of gemma cups, and auxin insensitivity.
mechanism: Elevated MpARF2 disrupts normal ARF stoichiometry required for auxin response, leading to developmental defects.

genes: LUC (luciferase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic lines express luciferase in response to PAMPs (flg22 and INF1), showing bioluminescence as a reporter for CYP71D20 gene activity.
mechanism: Luciferase gene expression is driven by the CYP71D20 promoter, allowing real-time monitoring of PAMP-induced defense responses.

genes: hppdPf-4Pa (HPPD-4, bacterial enzyme, synthetic), bar (phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, Agrobacterium tumefaciens, synthetic)
phenotype: Transformation efficiency under HPPD inhibitor selection increased linearly with light intensity (up to 5.2% at 190 μmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹), while glufosinate selection showed no significant light intensity effect (2.8-6.9%)
mechanism: HPPD-4 mitigates high light stress by producing plastoquinone and α-tocopherol precursors, while bar confers glufosinate resistance. Light intensity differentially affects promoter activity (PcsvmvXYYZ vs P35S3) and enzyme function under selection pressure

genes: ZmaFT2 (ZmaFT2, FT/TSF clade gene promoting flowering, Zostera marina)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmaFT2 results in early flowering in Arabidopsis under LD conditions.
mechanism: Interaction with the floral pathway.

genes: ZmaFT4 (ZmaFT4, FT/TSF clade gene promoting flowering, Zostera marina)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmaFT4 results in early flowering in Arabidopsis under LD conditions with a stronger effect than ZmaFT2.
mechanism: Interaction with the floral pathway.

genes: ZmaFT9 (ZmaFT9, FT/TSF clade gene repressing flowering, Zostera marina)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmaFT9 results in delayed flowering in Arabidopsis with a stronger phenotype in homozygous lines.
mechanism: Interaction with the floral pathway.

genes: ZmaTFL1a (ZmaTFL1a, TFL/BFT clade gene repressing flowering, Zostera marina)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmaTFL1a results in delayed flowering in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: Interaction with the floral pathway.

genes: BpBZR1-6 (BpBZR1-6, transcription factor, Betula platyphylla)
phenotype: Overexpression of BpBZR1-6 increases salt tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana by enhancing seed germination rate, root length, fresh weight, and chlorophyll content under salt stress (P < 0.05).
mechanism: BpBZR1-6 overexpression enhances reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging capability by increasing antioxidant enzyme activities, reducing O2− and H2O2 accumulation, and lowering malondialdehyde (MDA) content while upregulating six antioxidant enzyme genes under salt stress.

genes: CLF (Polycomb group protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of CLF rescues the clf-50 mutant phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: CLF associates with numerous RNAs in vivo, including mRNAs from highly expressed genes and lncRNAs from the nuclear mitochondrial genome region marked by H3K27me3

genes: VvLRX7 (VvLRX7, salt stress response regulator, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvLRX7 in Arabidopsis markedly enhances salt tolerance
mechanism: VvLRX7 functions as a positive regulator of plant's response to salt stress

genes: CrBKT (β-carotene ketolase, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii)
phenotype: Overexpression of CrBKT increases carotenoids and ketocarotenoids content 1.5- and 10-fold respectively, inducing orange/red cell coloration in N. oceanica
mechanism: CrBKT overexpression enhances ketocarotenoid production pathway activity

genes: LRR1 (leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of LRR1 increases sensitivity to ABA, resulting in severe growth reduction and heightened ABA responsiveness during seed germination and cotyledon greening.
mechanism: LRR1 positively regulates ABA signaling by interacting with PYL6, modulating downstream transcription factors ABI3, ABI4, and ABI5 to influence seed germination and cotyledon greening.

genes: LRR1 (leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: LRR1 promoter drives GUS expression in roots, stems, and petioles, with down-regulated activity under ABA treatment.
mechanism: LRR1 is ubiquitously expressed across developmental stages and tissues, with ABA treatment reducing GUS activity, indicating ABA-mediated down-regulation of LRR1 expression.

genes: CC1 (CC1, full-length, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CC1 with Venus tag rescues the hypocotyl elongation and cell aspect ratio phenotypes of the cc1 cc2 double mutant under oryzalin and salt stress conditions.
mechanism: CC1 overexpression with Venus tag facilitates the movement of CSCs along cortical microtubules, promoting cellulose biosynthesis and hypocotyl elongation.

genes: CC1 (CC1, S47A, T48A, S52A, S74A, S77A, S79A, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CC16A (phosphorylation-defective variant) fails to rescue the hypocotyl elongation and cell aspect ratio phenotypes of the cc1 cc2 double mutant under oryzalin and salt stress conditions.
mechanism: CC16A overexpression does not restore the phosphorylation status required for CC1 trafficking and microtubule reorganization under salt stress.
