mechanism: Coinfection with TEV/αRBD1-F2A-CP and PVX/αRBD2-F2A-CPTEV vectors allows co-assembly of hybrid virions.

genes: IpWRKY16 (WRKY transcription factor, I. pes-caprae transcriptome)
phenotype: Overexpression of IpWRKY16 under salt stress increases superoxide dismutase (SOD), peroxidase (POD), and catalase (CAT) activity while reducing malondialdehyde (MDA) content in sweet potato roots.
mechanism: IpWRKY16 forms a complex regulatory network involving IbSOS3, IbAHA4-1, and IbAHA4-2 to respond to salt stress by modulating ion transporter genes and Na+ efflux in root elongation zones.

genes: γ-ECS (γ-glutamylcysteine synthetase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Overexpression of γ-ECS increases tolerance to arsenate, cadmium, mercury, lead, and chromium by ~65-125% in Crambe abyssinica, with 73-154% higher metal accumulation in roots and shoots compared to wild type.
mechanism: γ-ECS overexpression enhances γ-glutamylcysteine (γ-EC), glutathione (GSH), and phytochelatin (PC) synthesis, enabling metal chelation and vacuolar sequestration of toxic metals.

genes: H3.1K27M (histone H3.1 variant with K27M mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana, native)
phenotype: Expression of H3.1K27M induces genomic instability in Arabidopsis, leading to stunted growth, smaller leaves, increased anthocyanin content, DNA damage (comet assay), and hypersensitivity to MMS. Plants show increased homologous recombination (GUS assay) and upregulation of DNA damage response genes.
mechanism: H3.1K27M inhibits PRC2 and ATXR5/6 histone methyltransferase activity, leading to loss of H3K27me3 and H3K27me1. This disrupts chromatin maturation, increases TSK activity, and causes DNA damage. The effect is TSK-dependent, as tsk mutants suppress these phenotypes.

genes: H3.1 WT (wild-type histone H3.1, Arabidopsis thaliana, native)
phenotype: Control plants expressing wild-type H3.1 show normal growth and development, with no significant DNA damage or genomic instability compared to H3.1K27M-expressing plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: H3.3K27M (histone H3.3 variant with K27M mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana, native H3.1 promoter)
phenotype: Expression of H3.3K27M under the H3.1 promoter reduces H3K27me3 but not H3K27me1, mimicking PRC2 inhibition without affecting ATXR5/6. Plants show reduced H3K27me3 and similar genomic instability phenotypes as H3.1K27M-expressing plants.
mechanism: H3.3K27M inhibits PRC2 activity but not ATXR5/6, leading to loss of H3K27me3. This disrupts chromatin maturation and increases TSK activity, causing DNA damage. The effect is TSK-dependent, as tsk mutants suppress these phenotypes.

genes: CtFT2 (CtFT2, flowering time regulator, Carthamus tinctorius), CtFT1 (CtFT1, flowering time regulator, Carthamus tinctorius), CtFT3 (CtFT3, flowering time regulator, Carthamus tinctorius)
phenotype: Overexpression of CtFT2 causes early flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: CtFT1 (CtFT1, flowering time regulator, Carthamus tinctorius)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of CtFT1 in safflower leaves causes early flowering.
mechanism: NA

genes: CtFT3 (CtFT3, flowering time regulator, Carthamus tinctorius)
phenotype: Overexpression of CtFT3 causes late flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: CtFT1 (CtFT1, flowering time regulator, Carthamus tinctorius), CtFT2 (CtFT2, flowering time regulator, Carthamus tinctorius), CtFT3 (CtFT3, flowering time regulator, Carthamus tinctorius)
phenotype: Overexpression of CtFT1, CtFT2, and CtFT3 in safflower leaves significantly increases flavonoid synthesis.
mechanism: NA

genes: GABA-T1 (GABA transaminase 1, transmembrane localization, tomato), GABA-T2 (GAME12, cytosolic localization, tomato), GABA-T3 (GABA transaminase 3, plastid localization, tomato), GABA-T4 (GABA transaminase 4, cytosolic localization, tomato)
phenotype: Transient expression of GABA-T homologs fused to RFP in N. benthamiana confirmed their subcellular localization (cytosolic for GABA-T2 and GABA-T4, mitochondrial/cytosolic for GABA-T1, plastid for GABA-T3).
mechanism: NA

genes: GAME12 (steroidal glycoalkaloid biosynthesis gene 12, cytosolic transaminase, tomato)
phenotype: De novo production of steroidal glycoalkaloids (SGAs) in S. nigrum leaves, including soladulcidine (17)-type aglycones, confirmed by UHPLC–MS analysis.
mechanism: GAME12 catalyzes transamination of furostanol intermediates to form steroidal alkaloid aglycone scaffolds, enabling nitrogen incorporation into saponin backbones.

genes: GAME12 (steroidal glycoalkaloid biosynthesis gene 12, cytosolic transaminase, tomato), GAME4 (furostanol oxidase, tomato)
phenotype: Significant increase (~4-fold) in SGA levels in S. nigrum leaves, with a simultaneous decrease in uttroside B (furostanol-type saponin) levels.
mechanism: GAME4 oxidizes furostanol to 26-furostanol aldehyde, which is then transaminated by GAME12 to form steroidal alkaloid aglycones, redirecting metabolic flux from saponin to SGA biosynthesis.

genes: PAIR1 (PAIR1, meiosis-related gene, Oryza sativa), REC8 (REC8, meiosis-related gene, Oryza sativa), OSD1 (OSD1, meiosis-related gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of PAIR1, REC8, and OSD1 through CRISPR/Cas9 in rice leads to MiMe (Mitosis instead of Meiosis) plants with tetraploid progeny and distinct phenotypes including larger and awned spikelets, complete sterility or extremely low fertility, lower tillering, and darker green leaves.
mechanism: Simultaneous knockout of PAIR1, REC8, and OSD1 disrupts meiosis, leading to parthenogenesis in MiMe plants. Fertilization in MiMe plants doubles ploidy at each generation.

genes: BBM1 (BBM1, BABY BOOM gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of BBM1 driven by pDD45 in MiMe-DD45 apomicts results in 1.0%–97.1% diploid progeny in T1 generation, with 7 of 14 lines showing diploid rates >70.0% (72.7%–96.2%). Diploid progeny are morphologically similar to wild type.
mechanism: BBM1-induced parthenogenesis combined with MiMe (knockout of PAIR1, REC8, and OSD1) enables apomixis, producing diploid progeny genetically identical to the mother plant.

genes: BBM1 (BBM1, BABY BOOM gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of BBM1 driven by pECA1.1 in MiMe-ECA1 apomicts results in 1.0%–97.1% diploid progeny in T1 generation, with 8 of 17 lines showing diploid rates >70.0% (71.3%–97.1%). Diploid progeny are morphologically similar to wild type.
mechanism: BBM1-induced parthenogenesis combined with MiMe (knockout of PAIR1, REC8, and OSD1) enables apomixis, producing diploid progeny genetically identical to the mother plant.

genes: BBM1 (BBM1, BABY BOOM gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: SunTag-enhanced overexpression of BBM1 in MiMe-ECA1-AZP1 apomicts results in 5 of 11 XS134 lines and 6 of 15 YY4949 lines showing diploid rates >70.0% in T0 generation. No high-fertile apomixis with >90.0% diploid rate was observed.
mechanism: SunTag technology recruits VP64 via AZP1-10xGCN4 and scFv-sfGFP-VP64 to enhance pECA1.1:BBM1 expression, improving apomixis induction efficiency.

genes: BBM1 (BBM1, BABY BOOM gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: SunTag-enhanced overexpression of BBM1 in MiMe-ECA1-AZP2 apomicts results in 12 of 14 XS134 lines, 10 of 13 YY4949 lines, and 15 of 18 YY1538 lines showing diploid rates >90.0% (90.1%–100.0%) in T1 generation. 3 YY4949 lines and 4 YY1538 lines show diploid fertilities >70.0% (72.8%–83.8%), only 1.3%–14.6% less fertile than wild type.
mechanism: SunTag technology recruits VP64 via AZP2-10xGCN4 and scFv-sfGFP-VP64 to enhance pECA1.1:BBM1 expression, improving apomixis induction efficiency while maintaining nearly normal fertility.

genes: GsMYB10 (Glycine max MYB-CC transcription factor, transcription factor, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GsMYB10 increases taproot length and root fresh weight by ~20% in Glycine max under AlCl3 treatment, while reducing Al3+ accumulation in root tips by ~26% and increasing proline content by 39–45% with 37–42% reduced malondialdehyde content.
mechanism: GsMYB10 acts as a positive regulator enhancing adaptability to acidic aluminum stress by inducing wall modification-related genes (PGs, XTHs, NRAMPs, ABCs) and modulating physiological responses (proline/malondialdehyde levels).

genes: EaNF-YB2 (EaNF-YB2, drought tolerance gene)
phenotype: Overexpression of EaNF-YB2 increases relative water content, chlorophyll content, photosynthetic efficiency, and antioxidant enzyme activities in sugarcane under drought stress.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaCOMT-3B (caffeic acid 3-O-methyltransferase, wheat, TraesCS3B02G612000)
phenotype: Transient expression of TaCOMT-3B in wheat leaves increased sinapyl alcohol content by ~35% compared to controls.
mechanism: TaCOMT-3B catalyzes the biosynthesis of sinapyl alcohol, a lignin monomer, which contributes to cell wall lignification and disease resistance.

genes: EscaSTK (EscaSTK, involved in fruit wall proliferation, seed filling, and seed coat development, Eschscholzia californica)
phenotype: Premature rupture of fruits in Eschscholzia californica
mechanism: EscaSTK restricts cell divisions in the inner cell layer of the valve

genes: PbbHLH164 (PbbHLH164, bHLH transcription factor, Pyrus spp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbbHLH164 accelerates fruit ripening and increases ethylene production in pear cultivars.
mechanism: PbbHLH164 enhances ethylene biosynthesis by inducing PbACS1b expression.

genes: PbbHLH164 (PbbHLH164, bHLH transcription factor, Pyrus spp.)
phenotype: Silencing of PbbHLH164 delays fruit ripening and decreases ethylene production in pear cultivars.
mechanism: PbbHLH164 knockdown reduces PbACS1b expression, leading to lower ethylene biosynthesis.

genes: HvGA2ox9 (gibberellin 2-oxidase, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Knockdown of HvGA2ox9 increases root length by ~14% in barley and accelerates flowering time.
mechanism: Reduced HvGA2ox9 expression leads to increased bioactive GA4 levels, promoting root growth and earlier flowering.

genes: SSS (Shoot-Silicon-Signal gene, Oryza sativa), GFP (Green Fluorescent Protein, synthetic)
phenotype: SSS::GFP protein translocated from leaves and nodes to the root stele through the phloem, while SSS::GFPGFP cannot migrate from the originally expressed organs.
mechanism: SSS::GFP localized in phloem parenchyma cells and translocated to root stele cells, whereas SSS::GFPGFP was not detected in these tissues due to lower molecular mass permeability through plasmodesmata.

genes: SSS (Shoot-Silicon-Signal gene, Oryza sativa), GFP (Green Fluorescent Protein, synthetic)
phenotype: SSS::GFPGFP protein cannot migrate from the originally expressed organs, unlike SSS::GFP.
mechanism: SSS::GFPGFP was not detected in root stele cells or shoot apex tissues, indicating restricted mobility due to higher molecular mass.

genes: SSS (Shoot-Silicon-Signal gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Root Si uptake was enhanced up to 2 times of the WT, with positive correlation between SSS::GFP expression and Si uptake.
mechanism: Ectopic expression of SSS::GFP in root exodermis and endodermis increased Lsi1 and Lsi2 expression, enhancing Si uptake.

genes: SSS (Shoot-Silicon-Signal gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Short-term root Si uptake of the mutants was about half of the wild-type under Si-deficient condition.
mechanism: Knockout of SSS disrupted the signaling pathway regulating Si uptake transporters Lsi1 and Lsi2, leading to reduced Si uptake.

genes: AtWRI1 (WRINKLED1 transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transient expression of AtWRI1:GFP in N. benthamiana leaf epidermal cells with strong nuclear and cytoplasmic fluorescence
mechanism: AtWRI1 functions as a transcription factor regulating fatty acid biosynthesis by binding DNA via AP2 domains

genes: ZjZOG (ZjZOG, candidate gene for fruit size regulation, Ziziphus jujuba)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZjZOG in tomato enhances fruit size
mechanism: Regulation of mesocarp cell numbers during early fruit development

genes: EXO70A1 (EXO70A1, a key member of the EXO70 family in Arabidopsis, involved in cellulose synthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic EXO70A1-GFP rescues the exo70a1-1 mutant phenotypes including reduced cellulose content (23% reduction), short hypocotyl length, impaired cell elongation, plant dwarfism, and sterility.
mechanism: EXO70A1 is functionally associated with CESA6 and plays a regulatory role in hypocotyl growth dependent on CESA6. Mutation in EXO70A1 impairs the trafficking of CSC vesicles, specifically during their journey from the cortex to the PM where they are tethered.

genes: FvALKBH10B (m6A demethylase, Fragaria vesca), firefly luciferase (reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of FvALKBH10B in N. benthamiana leaves reduces total m6A levels by ~50% compared to control.
mechanism: FvALKBH10B oxidatively demethylates m6A in mRNA, reducing m6A levels and stabilizing transcripts like FvSEP3.

genes: FvABF3 (transcription factor, Fragaria vesca)
phenotype: Overexpression of FvABF3 in strawberry fruits accelerates ripening and increases anthocyanin content by ~2-fold.
mechanism: FvABF3 binds to ABRE elements in FvALKBH10B promoter, transcriptionally activating its expression to regulate m6A demethylation.

genes: FvALKBH10B (m6A demethylase, Fragaria vesca)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-induced FvALKBH10B mutants in strawberry show delayed fruit ripening and reduced anthocyanin content by ~50%.
mechanism: FvALKBH10B knockout leads to global m6A hypermethylation, destabilizing FvSEP3 mRNA and inhibiting ripening-related gene expression.

genes: FvALKBH10B (m6A demethylase, Fragaria vesca)
phenotype: Overexpression of FvALKBH10B in strawberry fruits increases anthocyanin content by ~2-fold and accelerates ripening.
mechanism: FvALKBH10B-mediated m6A demethylation stabilizes FvSEP3 mRNA, enhancing its expression and promoting ripening.

genes: FvSEP3 (MADS-box transcription factor, Fragaria vesca)
phenotype: Overexpression of FvSEP3 in Fvalkbh10b mutant strawberry fruits rescues delayed ripening and increases anthocyanin content by ~2-fold.
mechanism: FvSEP3 directly targets ripening-related genes (e.g., FvGH3.1, FvGA3ox1) to regulate ABA and anthocyanin biosynthesis pathways.

genes: ZmNRT1.1 A (nitrate transporter 1.1 A, maize, Zea mays), bar (phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, synthetic)
phenotype: Integration of ZmNRT1.1 A and bar genes into non-coding regions of maize chromosomes 5 and 3, respectively, without disrupting gene-coding regions
mechanism: NA

genes: CP4-epsps (CP4-epsps, glyphosate resistance gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of CP4-epsps confers glyphosate resistance in soybean
mechanism: NA

genes: OsINO80 (OsINO80, catalytic subunit of INO80 complex, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsINO80-YFP rescues the lethal phenotype and partially rescues growth defects of homozygous osino80-/- rice plants at the T1 generation, restoring transgenic plants to wild-type phenotypes in subsequent generations
mechanism: OsINO80-YFP functions as the endogenous OsINO80 protein in planta

genes: OsINO80 (OsINO80, catalytic subunit of INO80 complex, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockdown of OsINO80 results in decreased H3K27me3 and H3K9me2 levels, activation of TEs, and decreased fertility
mechanism: OsINO80 promotes the establishment of H3K27me3 and H3K9me2, which are involved in gene repression and TE silencing

genes: YFP (YFP, fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Serves as a control for the OsINO80-YFP transgenic plants
mechanism: NA

genes: AhMAGL3b (Arachis hypogaea, monoacylglycerol lipase with hydrolase and acyltransferase regions)
phenotype: Overexpression of AhMAGL3b increases leaf fatty acid content by 12.1–27.4% and decreases seed oil content by 10.7–17.3% in Arabidopsis thaliana. Seeds show increased dormancy and reduced sensitivity to ABA treatment.
mechanism: AhMAGL3b is involved in TAG hydrolysis and homeostasis among carbohydrates, lipids, and protein. It functions as a hydrolase in seeds and an acyltransferase in vegetative tissues.

genes: CO (CO, Arabidopsis thaliana), NF-YC9 (NF-YC9, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CO and NF-YC9 rescues late flowering in nf-yc3 nf-yc4 nf-yc9 triple mutant (ycT), promoting floral transition.
mechanism: CO/NF-YC9 condensates maintain functional fluidic state for FT transcription activation, essential for floral transition.

genes: NF-YC9 (NF-YC9-37Q, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NF-YC9-37Q overexpression fails to rescue late flowering in ycT mutant and impairs FT transcription.
mechanism: NF-YC9 polyQ repeat extension disrupts functional condensation of CO/NF-YB2/NF-YC9 complex, impairing FT activation.

genes: NF-YC9 (NF-YC9-∆IDR1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NF-YC9-∆IDR1 overexpression fails to rescue late flowering in ycT mutant and impairs FT transcription.
mechanism: NF-YC9 IDR1 deletion disrupts functional condensation of CO/NF-YB2/NF-YC9 complex, impairing FT activation.

genes: CO (CO-∆B-box, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CO-∆B-box overexpression fails to promote FT transcription and floral transition.
mechanism: B-box motif deletion prevents CO oligomerization and functional condensation, impairing FT activation.

genes: SUB4 (subtilisin-like protease, Oryza sativa, genomic)
phenotype: SUB4-GFP fusion protein localized to the cell periphery in tobacco mesophyll cells, overlapping with propidium iodide staining of cell walls
mechanism: NA

genes: OsGLS1 (Oryza sativa GLS1, negative regulator of root system architecture, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of gls1 mutant restores root growth angle and root system architecture to wild-type levels in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsGLS1 is a negative regulator of root system architecture (RSA) that controls root growth angle by modulating auxin distribution through ubiquitination and degradation of OsPIN2.

genes: OsPIN2 (Oryza sativa PIN-FORMED 2, auxin transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PIN2HL-GFP in Oryza sativa results in increased stability and non-polar localization of OsPIN2 in the plasma membrane of root epidermal cells.
mechanism: OsGLS1 directly ubiquitinates and degrades OsPIN2, and its absence in gls1 leads to non-polar localization and increased abundance of OsPIN2, disrupting auxin gradient distribution.

genes: P3 (Pelota, viral gene, TuMV), NIb (Pelota, viral gene, TuMV)
phenotype: Overexpression of P3 and NIb in transgenic Arabidopsis plants for studying Pelota SUMOylation and viral infection mechanisms.
mechanism: NA

genes: Pelota (Pelota, Arabidopsis thaliana), SUMO1 (Pelota, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Pelota-YFP and Myc-SUMO1 co-expression in transgenic Arabidopsis plants to analyze Pelota SUMOylation during TuMV infection.
mechanism: NA

genes: Pelota (Pelota, Arabidopsis thaliana), NIb (Pelota, viral gene, TuMV)
phenotype: Pelota-YFP and Myc-SUMO1 co-expression with NIb in N. benthamiana leaves to study Pelota SUMOylation inhibition.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsCSN5 (OsCSN5, negative regulator of disease resistance, Oryza sativa)
gene_construct: RNAi construct targeting 594-891 bp of OsCSN5
phenotype: Enhanced resistance to M. oryzae and Xoo with no growth penalties in rice.
mechanism: OsCSN5 negatively regulates disease resistance by suppressing chitin-induced ROS and defense gene expression.

genes: OsPUB45 (OsPUB45, E3 ubiquitin ligase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Enhanced resistance to M. oryzae and Xoo in rice.
mechanism: OsPUB45 ubiquitinates and degrades OsCSN5, promoting OsCUL3a-OsNPR1-mediated immunity.

genes: faeA (Aspergillus niger, esterase, Aspergillus niger)
phenotype: Overexpression of FAEA increases saccharification efficiency by reducing ester-linked hydroxycinnamic acids (HCAs) in maize cell walls, leading to improved glucose release during enzymatic digestion.
mechanism: FAEA hydrolyzes ester-linked ferulate monomers and dimers in cell walls, reducing cross-linking between arabinoxylans and lignin, thereby increasing accessibility of hemicellulose and cellulose to hydrolytic enzymes.

genes: DNR1 (DNR1, DNR1 gene, Oryza sativa), OsARF6 (OsARF6, auxin response factor, Oryza sativa), OsARF17 (OsARF17, auxin response factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of DNR1 increases nitrogen uptake and biomass in rice under elevated CO2 conditions.
mechanism: DNR1 enhances auxin homeostasis, leading to increased expression of nitrate uptake and assimilation genes (OsNRT1.1B, OsNRT2.3a, OsNIA2, OsNPF2.4), thereby improving nitrogen use efficiency and grain yield.

genes: OsARF6 (OsARF6, auxin response factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsARF6 enhances nitrogen uptake and biomass in rice under elevated CO2 conditions.
mechanism: OsARF6 activates nitrate uptake and assimilation genes (OsNRT1.1B, OsNRT2.3a, OsNIA2, OsNPF2.4), leading to increased nitrogen use efficiency and grain yield.

genes: OsARF17 (OsARF17, auxin response factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsARF17 enhances nitrogen uptake and biomass in rice under elevated CO2 conditions.
mechanism: OsARF17 activates nitrate uptake and assimilation genes (OsNRT1.1B, OsNRT2.3a, OsNIA2, OsNPF2.4), leading to increased nitrogen use efficiency and grain yield.

genes: StbHLH47 (StbHLH47, transcription factor, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Overexpression of StbHLH47 increases sensitivity to drought stress in potato plants
mechanism: Regulates drought resistance through phenylalanine and abscisic acid (ABA) signal transduction pathways

genes: ATG8F (autophagy-related ubiquitin-like modifier, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of ATG8F ΔC in ATG4-deficient Arabidopsis restores autophagic activity, with comparable accumulation of autophagic bodies in vacuoles to wild-type plants.
mechanism: ATG8F ΔC forms ATG8–PE adducts that bypass the need for ATG4-dependent delipidation, enabling autophagosome formation and vacuolar delivery despite ATG4 deficiency.

genes: MED21 (MED21, transcriptional coactivator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Loss of MED21 function in lateral roots leads to larger root cap zones, abnormally shaped root hairs, and reduced lateral root length in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Integrase-mediated inversion of the MED21 gene disrupts its expression, phenocopying auxin addition and promoting lateral root initiation.

genes: MED21 (MED21, transcriptional coactivator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Loss of MED21 function in lateral roots leads to larger root cap zones, abnormally shaped root hairs, and reduced lateral root length in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Integrase-mediated inversion of the MED21 gene disrupts its expression, phenocopying auxin addition and promoting lateral root initiation.

genes: MED21 (MED21, transcriptional coactivator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Chemically-inducible loss of MED21 function via β-estradiol treatment causes significant growth reduction in primary and lateral roots, increased root hair development, and higher lateral root density in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: β-estradiol-inducible PhiC31 integrase mediates inversion of the MED21 gene, phenocopying auxin addition and promoting lateral root initiation.

genes: MED21 (MED21, transcriptional coactivator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Switching from wildtype MED21 to mutant MED21 (mMED21) in lateral roots increases lateral root density while maintaining normal lateral root length in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Integrase-mediated isoform switching replaces wildtype MED21 with mutant MED21, which disrupts TPL binding and promotes lateral root initiation.

genes: control (mTurquoise, fluorescent protein, synthetic), mScarlet (fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Switching from mTurquoise to mScarlet in the presence of PhiC31 integrase expressed from the CaMV35S promoter in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: PhiC31 integrase mediates inversion of the reporter gene cassette, switching expression from mTurquoise to mScarlet.

genes: pmi (Phosphomannose isomerase, Ophioglossum pendulum), pat (Phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, synthetic), ipd079Ea (Insecticidal protein, Ophioglossum pendulum)
phenotype: Expression of IPD079Ea in maize provides insect resistance against western corn rootworm with LC50 of 6.93 µg/cm²
mechanism: IPD079Ea binds to gut receptors in western corn rootworm, causing mortality through specific insecticidal activity

genes: TaSal1 (3'(2'),5'-bisphosphate nucleotidase, wheat genome), TaSal1 (3'(2'),5'-bisphosphate nucleotidase, wheat genome), TaSal1 (3'(2'),5'-bisphosphate nucleotidase, wheat genome), TaSal1 (3'(2'),5'-bisphosphate nucleotidase, wheat genome), TaSal1 (3'(2'),5'-bisphosphate nucleotidase, wheat genome), TaSal1 (3'(2'),5'-bisphosphate nucleotidase, wheat genome)
phenotype: TaSal1 knockout in wheat leads to stomatal closure, increased drought tolerance under PEG-induced stress, and morphological changes including leaf rolling and stem bending
mechanism: TaSal1 loss-of-function causes PAP accumulation, enhancing chloroplast-to-nucleus retrograde signaling and inducing stomatal closure to reduce water loss

genes: ZmGRAS46 (Zm00001d044065, DELLA subfamily member in GA pathway, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmGRAS46 delays flowering in maize (tasseling and silking time increased by ~4.6 days compared to wild type)
mechanism: ZmGRAS46 inhibits flowering by downregulating CO, FT, SOC1, and LFY genes

genes: ZmGRAS46 (Zm00001d044065, DELLA subfamily member in GA pathway, Zea mays)
phenotype: Knockout of ZmGRAS46 accelerates flowering in maize (tasseling and silking time decreased by ~1 day compared to wild type)
mechanism: ZmGRAS46 knockout upregulates CO, FT, SOC1, and LFY genes to promote flowering

genes: ZmNF-YB10 (ZmNF-YB10, drought/salt stress-responsive transcription factor, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmNF-YB10 in Arabidopsis thaliana enhances drought and salt tolerance, with 80% survival under drought stress and 75% under salt stress compared to 25% in wild-type. Transgenic plants show increased rosette leaf area, plant height, and root length under stress conditions.
mechanism: ZmNF-YB10 enhances drought/salt tolerance by reducing H2O2 and O2- levels, increasing SOD, POD, and CAT activities, and lowering MDA content. It upregulates stress-related genes like AtDREB2A, AtSAG13, AtCOR15, AtFRY1, AtSAD1, and AtSOS2.

genes: RDM16 (RDM16-GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Complementation of rdm16-4 mutant restores wild-type survival rates and reduces electrolyte leakage after heat stress.
mechanism: RDM16 promotes splicing efficiency of heat stress–responsive genes like HSFA3, enhancing thermotolerance.

genes: RDM16 (RDM16mu-GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: RDM16mu-GFP transgenic plants show significantly lower survival rates and higher electrolyte leakage after heat stress compared to wild-type and RDM16:RDM16-GFP lines.
mechanism: Arginine residues in IDR1 of RDM16 are essential for condensation and splicing efficiency of HSFA3, which is critical for thermotolerance.

genes: RDM16 (FUS-RDM16mu-GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: FUS-RDM16mu-GFP restores condensation ability and enhances splicing efficiency of HSFA3, improving heat tolerance compared to RDM16mu-GFP.
mechanism: FUS domain rescues RDM16mu condensation, enabling proper splicing of HSFA3 transcripts and thermotolerance.

genes: RDM16 (RDS-GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: RDS overexpression in Col-0 promotes heat tolerance, while RDS alone in rdm16-4 background does not rescue mutant defects.
mechanism: RDS interacts with RDL to promote its condensation, enhancing splicing efficiency of HSFA3 and thermotolerance.

genes: RDM16 (RDL-GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: RDL overexpression in Col-0 enhances heat tolerance, with increased survival rates and reduced electrolyte leakage after heat stress.
mechanism: RDL condensation and splicing of HSFA3 transcripts are critical for thermotolerance, which is further enhanced by RDS interaction.

genes: RDM16 (RDL+RDS-GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Co-overexpression of RDL and RDS in Col-0 significantly enhances heat tolerance compared to single overexpression lines.
mechanism: RDS promotes RDL condensation and splicing efficiency of HSFA3, synergistically improving thermotolerance.

genes: SAP54 (SAP54 effector, Aster Yellows phytoplasma), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)

genes: VdCHS2 (CHS2, chalcone synthase 2, Vitis davidii)

mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in CHS2 cause premature termination of protein translation, redirecting metabolic flux from flavonoid to stilbenoid pathways. Downregulation of flavonoid biosynthesis genes (CHS2, CHS3, F3H, etc.) and upregulation of STS genes (stilbene synthase) drive this shift.

genes: miR528 (microRNA 528, banana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR528 in banana peel slices enhances cold tolerance, with significantly higher lightness (L*) and lower chilling injury index compared to controls under 6°C stress for 8 days.
mechanism: miR528 inhibits PPO expression and enzymatic activity, reducing ROS metabolism and membrane lipid peroxidation (MDA and H2O2 levels), thereby preventing peel browning and cold injury.

genes: MaSPL4 (SPL family member 4, banana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MaSPL4 in banana peel slices and whole fruit significantly delays chilling injury, with lower PPO activity, MDA, and H2O2 levels, and higher lightness (L*) under 6°C stress for 14 days.
mechanism: MaSPL4 activates miR528 transcription, which suppresses MaPPO expression and ROS accumulation. MaSPL4 also upregulates lipid metabolism (MaKCS11/20) and antioxidant (MaPOD5) genes, enhancing cold tolerance.

genes: miR156c (microRNA 156c, banana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR156c in banana peel slices exacerbates chilling injury, with higher PPO activity, MDA, and H2O2 levels, and lower lightness (L*) under 6°C stress for 8 days.
mechanism: miR156c cleaves MaSPL4 transcripts, reducing MaSPL4 and miR528 expression, leading to increased MaPPO activity and ROS accumulation, worsening cold injury.

genes: miR156c (microRNA 156c, banana, synthetic)
phenotype: Silencing of miR156c in banana peel slices reduces chilling injury, with lower PPO activity, MDA, and H2O2 levels, and higher lightness (L*) under 6°C stress for 8 days.
mechanism: miR156c silencing increases MaSPL4 and miR528 expression, suppressing MaPPO and ROS accumulation, thereby alleviating cold injury.

mechanism: JrMYB44 suppression downregulates downstream genes (e.g., GST, WRKY, DREB) and disrupts interactions with JrMYC2 and JrDof1, impairing ROS balance

phenotype: OE-CPK28 plants exhibited weaker resistance to P. capsici compared with Col-0, while cpk28 mutants showed stronger resistance.
mechanism: CPK28 phosphorylates PIP2;7 at Ser273 and Ser276, promoting its degradation and suppressing plant immunity.

genes: PIF4 (photoperiodism and hypocotyl elongation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PIF4-MYC in cop1-6 mutants failed to induce hypocotyl growth or gene expression at high temperatures despite elevated PIF4-MYC protein levels.
mechanism: COP1 modulates PIF4 activity by influencing its stability and DNA binding, independent of PIF4 levels.

genes: PHYB (photomorphogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9 targeting PHYB in cop1-6;hfr1-201 mutants partially restored high-temperature-induced hypocotyl growth and PIF4 target gene expression.
mechanism: COP1, phyB, and HFR1 redundantly suppress thermomorphogenesis by reducing PIF4 protein levels and activity.

genes: CRY1 (blue-light photoreceptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9 targeting CRY1 in cbh mutants further enhanced thermoresponsive growth and PIF4 target gene expression compared to cbh mutants.
mechanism: CRY1, along with phyB and HFR1, suppresses thermomorphogenesis by reducing PIF4 stability and activity.

genes: phyB (photomorphogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of phyB-GFP suppressed high-temperature-induced hypocotyl growth, mirroring the cop1 mutation effect.
mechanism: phyB destabilizes PIF4 and prevents its binding to target promoters, suppressing thermomorphogenesis.

genes: HFR1 (helix-loop-helix protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HFR1-GFP did not restore thermoresponsive hypocotyl growth in cop1-6 mutants but partially restored it when combined with phyB mutations.
mechanism: HFR1 forms a heterodimer with PIF4 and inhibits its DNA binding activity, suppressing thermomorphogenesis.

genes: SAP18 (SIN3-ASSOCIATED PROTEIN 18 KDA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAP18-GFP leads to nuclear and cytoplasmic localization changes under heat shock, co-localization with stress granules and processing bodies, and thermoprotective function during heat stress.
mechanism: SAP18 forms part of the ASAP complex in the nucleus, regulating splicing of genes associated with leaf development. Under heat shock, SAP18 relocates to cytoplasmic stress granules and processing bodies, potentially mediating thermoprotection.

genes: SAP18 (SIN3-ASSOCIATED PROTEIN 18 KDA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Genomic overexpression of SAP18-GFP under its endogenous promoter and terminator leads to heat shock-induced cytoplasmic aggregation and thermoprotective function, complementing the sap18 mutant phenotype.
mechanism: SAP18 genomic construct maintains endogenous regulation, enabling dynamic localization changes under stress and participation in cytoplasmic stress granules and processing bodies for thermoprotection.

genes: Jas9 (jasmonic acid signaling reporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), Venus (fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Increased JA action upon doxycycline (Dox) or methyl jasmonate (MeJA) exposure in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Dox-induced mitochondrial translational stress activates jasmonic acid (JA) signaling, as evidenced by increased JA action in Jas9-Venus transgenic plants.

genes: AOS (allene oxide synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (β-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Enhanced GUS accumulation in AOSpro:GUS transgenic plants upon Dox treatment, indicating increased JA biosynthesis in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Dox-induced mitochondrial translational stress activates the JA biosynthesis gene AOS, as shown by increased GUS activity in AOSpro:GUS transgenic plants.

genes: BcSRC2 (ascorbate content regulator, Brassica campestris)
phenotype: Overexpression of BcSRC2 increases ascorbic acid content and drought tolerance in pak choi.
mechanism: BcSRC2 inhibits APX enzyme activity, increasing AsA content and enhancing drought tolerance.

genes: BcSRC2 (ascorbate content regulator, Brassica campestris)
phenotype: Overexpression of BcSRC2 increases chlorophyll content, relative water content, and drought tolerance in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: BcSRC2 inhibits APX enzyme activity, increasing AsA content and enhancing drought tolerance.

genes: BcSRC2 (ascorbate content regulator, Brassica campestris)
phenotype: Silencing of BcSRC2 decreases ascorbic acid content and drought tolerance in pak choi.
mechanism: BcSRC2 silencing increases APX activity, reducing AsA content and drought tolerance.

genes: BcAPX4 (ascorbate peroxidase, Brassica campestris)
phenotype: Silencing of BcAPX4 enhances drought tolerance in pak choi by reducing H2O2 and MDA content.
mechanism: BcAPX4 silencing reduces APX activity, increasing AsA content and drought tolerance.

genes: CPK28 (CALCIUM-DEPENDENT PROTEIN KINASE 28, Arabidopsis thaliana), CPK28T76A (CALCIUM-DEPENDENT PROTEIN KINASE 28 T76A mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restores MET-enhanced flg22-induced ROS burst and bacterial disease resistance to wild-type levels in cpk28 mutant Arabidopsis
mechanism: CPK28 is a MET target; MET inhibits BIK1-CPK28 interaction and transphosphorylation at T76, suppressing CPK28's negative regulation of immunity

genes: NtCOMT10 (caffeic acid O-methyltransferase, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtCOMT10 increases methyl ferulate secretion by 221.09% compared to wild-type, reduces tobacco black shank disease index from 20% to <10%, and enriches rhizosphere Bacillus (relative abundance increases from 4.69% to 13.79%)
mechanism: NtCOMT10 overexpression enhances methyl ferulate production which inhibits P. nicotianae by impairing NADH dehydrogenase function (50% activity decrease) and recruits disease-suppressive rhizosphere microbes

genes: CitGATA7 (transcription factor, Citrus sinensis, Citrus)
phenotype: Overexpression of CitGATA7 in citrus callus reduces citric acid content by ~43% compared to control.
mechanism: CitGATA7 activates the GS pathway by upregulating CitACO3, CitIDH1, and CitGS1, enhancing citric acid degradation.

genes: CitGATA7 (transcription factor, Citrus sinensis, Citrus)
phenotype: Silencing CitGATA7 in citrus seedlings increases citric acid content by ~67% compared to control.
mechanism: CitGATA7 downregulation reduces activation of the GS pathway, decreasing citric acid degradation.

genes: CitHAG28 (histone acetyltransferase, Citrus sinensis, Citrus)
phenotype: Overexpression of CitHAG28 in citrus callus reduces citric acid content by ~27% compared to control.
mechanism: CitHAG28 enhances histone acetylation near TSS of GS pathway genes, upregulating CitACO3, CitIDH1, and CitGS1 to accelerate citric acid degradation.

genes: CitHAG28 (histone acetyltransferase, Citrus sinensis, Citrus)
phenotype: Silencing CitHAG28 in citrus seedlings increases citric acid content by ~43% compared to control.
mechanism: CitHAG28 downregulation reduces histone acetylation near TSS of GS pathway genes, decreasing CitACO3, CitIDH1, and CitGS1 expression and slowing citric acid degradation.

genes: AtD14 (AtD14, receptor for strigolactones, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtD14 in M. polymorpha enables MpSMXL degradation upon perception of endogenous KL and applied (‒)-GR24 by MpKAI2A, and perception of applied (+)-GR24 by AtD14.
mechanism: AtD14, introduced via the 35S promoter, allows M. polymorpha to respond to GR24, leading to MpMAX2-dependent degradation of MpSMXL39.

genes: EGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: EGFP fluorescence is localized in meristem regions, gemma initial cells, and initiating gemmae of M. polymorpha, indicating MpLOG promoter activity in these tissues.
mechanism: The MpLOG promoter drives EGFP expression in meristematic regions and gemma development sites, revealing cell-type-specific regulation by KAI2-dependent signaling.

genes: EGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: EGFP fluorescence is localized in gemma initial cells, initiating gemmae, and slime papillae of M. polymorpha, indicating GCAM1 promoter activity in these tissues.
mechanism: The GCAM1 promoter drives EGFP expression in gemma development sites, revealing its role in cytokinin-regulated vegetative reproduction.

genes: SsdAtox (SsdAtox, catalytic domain of SsdA from Pseudomonas syringae pv. aptata, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of SsdAtox-CBE in N. benthamiana leads to C-to-T editing in GUS reporter system.
mechanism: SsdAtox acts as a cytosine deaminase in the CBE system.

genes: SsdAG103S (SsdAG103S, variant of SsdAtox with G103S mutation, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of SsdAG103S-CBE in N. benthamiana results in efficient C-to-T editing in GUS reporter system.
mechanism: G103S mutation reduces toxicity and enhances deaminase activity in the CBE system.

genes: SsdAG103S (SsdAG103S, variant of SsdAtox with G103S mutation, synthetic)

mechanism: Intron insertion reduces bacterial toxicity and enhances plant-specific expression.

genes: SsdAG103S (SsdAG103S, variant of SsdAtox with G103S mutation, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of SsdAG103S-v1-CBE in rice plants induces C-to-T editing at genomic loci with 30-58.8% efficiency.
mechanism: SsdAG103S-v1-CBE targets cytosines in ssDNA via nCas9-UGI fusion, enabling precise base editing.

genes: SsdAG103S-T1 (SsdAG103S-T1, N-terminal truncated variant of SsdAG103S, synthetic)
phenotype: N-terminal truncation of SsdAG103S (T1 variant) in N. benthamiana maintains C-to-T editing efficiency comparable to full-length protein.
mechanism: Truncation at N-terminal α-helical regions does not affect deaminase activity.

genes: SsdAG103S-T3 (SsdAG103S-T3, truncated variant of SsdAG103S with 114 amino acids, synthetic)
phenotype: 114-amino-acid SsdAG103S-T3 variant in N. benthamiana retains full C-to-T editing activity of full-length protein.
mechanism: C-terminal β-strand is essential for activity; N-terminal truncation does not impair function.

genes: KUDN (Solyc01g091350, truncated Ku80 fragment for NHEJ inhibition, tomato)
phenotype: NKUDN-ttLbCas12a fusion increased HR-based gene targeting (GT) efficiency at SlEPSPS1 (3.55-fold) and SlHKT1;2 (1.71-fold) loci in tomato callus and plant stages.
mechanism: KUDN inhibits cNHEJ, redirecting DSB repair to HDR pathways (MMEJ/HR), enhancing GT efficiency.

genes: KUDN (Solyc01g091350, truncated Ku80 fragment for NHEJ inhibition, tomato)
phenotype: Free KUDN overexpression showed comparable GT performance to NKUDN-ttLbCas12a at SlHKT1;2 and SlEPSPS1 loci.
mechanism: KUDN inhibits cNHEJ, redirecting DSB repair to HDR pathways (MMEJ/HR), enhancing GT efficiency.

genes: GmNPF7.5 (Glyma.18G260000, chloride and nitrate transporter, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmNPF7.5 increases chloride (Cl–) accumulation in roots and shoots, reduces salt tolerance, and decreases fresh weight in soybean plants under NaCl or KCl treatment.
mechanism: GmNPF7.5 mediates Cl– uptake and transport, leading to excessive Cl– accumulation and ionic toxicity under salt stress.

genes: GmNPF7.5 (Glyma.18G260000, chloride and nitrate transporter, Glycine max)
phenotype: Knockdown of GmNPF7.5 reduces chloride (Cl–) accumulation in roots and shoots, enhances salt tolerance, and increases fresh weight in soybean plants under NaCl or KCl treatment.
mechanism: GmNPF7.5 knockdown inhibits Cl– uptake and transport, reducing ionic toxicity and improving salt tolerance.

genes: GmNPF7.5 (Glyma.18G260000, chloride and nitrate transporter, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmNPF7.5HapA increases chloride (Cl–) accumulation in roots and shoots, reduces salt tolerance, and decreases fresh weight in soybean plants under NaCl or KCl treatment.
mechanism: GmNPF7.5HapA mediates Cl– uptake and transport, leading to excessive Cl– accumulation and ionic toxicity under salt stress.

genes: GmNPF7.5 (Glyma.18G260000, chloride and nitrate transporter, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmNPF7.5HapB reduces chloride (Cl–) accumulation in roots and shoots, enhances salt tolerance, and increases fresh weight in soybean plants under NaCl or KCl treatment.
mechanism: GmNPF7.5HapB has reduced Cl– transport activity but retains NO3– transport, decreasing Cl– toxicity and improving salt tolerance.

genes: GmPI4Kγ4 (Glyma.16G02400, phosphatidylinositol-4-kinase, Glycine max)

mechanism: GmPI4Kγ4 phosphorylates GmNPF7.5, inhibiting its Cl– transport activity while retaining NO3– transport, thereby reducing Cl– toxicity and improving salt tolerance.

genes: GmNPF7.5 (Glyma.18G260000, chloride and nitrate transporter, Glycine max)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of GmNPF7.5 reduces chloride (Cl–) accumulation in roots and shoots, enhances salt tolerance, and increases fresh weight in soybean plants under NaCl or KCl treatment.
mechanism: Knockout of GmNPF7.5 inhibits Cl– uptake and transport, reducing ionic toxicity and improving salt tolerance.

genes: GmNPF7.5 (Glyma.18G260000, chloride and nitrate transporter, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmNPF7.54A (a phosphorylation-defective mutant) does not affect Cl– or NO3– transport activity, and GmPI4Kγ4 overexpression does not rescue salt-sensitive phenotypes.
mechanism: Phosphorylation of GmNPF7.5 by GmPI4Kγ4 is essential for inhibiting Cl– transport and improving salt tolerance.

genes: PnWRKY35 (PnWRKY35, WRKY transcription factor, Panax notoginseng)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of PnWRKY35 in tobacco enhanced resistance to Cylindrocarpon destructans, accompanied by increased levels of gibberellins (GA24, GA3, GA8), jasmonic acid, salicylic acid, and brassinolide.
mechanism: Activates multiple plant disease resistance pathways and increases phytohormone levels

genes: DgARF7 (DgARF7, auxin response factor, Dactylis glomerata)
phenotype: Overexpression of DgARF7 in Arabidopsis thaliana enhances drought tolerance and accelerates flowering time.
mechanism: DgARF7 regulates flowering time genes (AtFLC, AtLFY, AtAP1, AtSOC1) and improves drought resistance by increasing relative water content and antioxidant enzyme levels (SOD, POD) while decreasing MDA content.

genes: DgARF7 (DgARF7, auxin response factor, Dactylis glomerata)
phenotype: Subcellular localization of DgARF7 in rice protoplasts shows nuclear localization.
mechanism: NA

genes: EuSWAP70 (EuSWAP70)
phenotype: Transgenic plants show stronger gray mold resistance compared to wildtype, with GWSF-EuSWAP70 transgenic plants exhibiting stronger resistance than CaMV35S-EuSWAP70 transgenic plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: EuSWAP70 (EuSWAP70)
phenotype: Transgenic plants show stronger gray mold resistance compared to wildtype, with GWSF-EuSWAP70 transgenic plants exhibiting stronger resistance than CaMV35S-EuSWAP70 transgenic plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS-GFP (green fluorescent protein fused to GUS, reporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), nucYFP (nuclear yellow fluorescent protein, reporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), SCRM (SCRM, stomatal lineage regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana), scrm-D (SCRM-D, stabilized variant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TMMpro::GUS-GFP and MUTEpro::nucYFP increases stomatal lineage marker expression in Arabidopsis thaliana. SCRMpro::GFP-SCRM and SCRMpro::GFP-scrm-D enable visualization of SCRM protein localization in stomatal lineage cells.
mechanism: TMMpro::GUS-GFP and MUTEpro::nucYFP monitor stomatal lineage development. SCRMpro::GFP-SCRM and SCRMpro::GFP-scrm-D visualize SCRM protein dynamics in stomatal differentiation.

genes: ERF101 (ERF101, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of FLAG-ERF101 inhibits Xa1-mediated immunity, increasing Xoo T7174 bacterial populations by ~2-fold compared to wild type.
mechanism: N-terminal FLAG tag on ERF101 disrupts its interaction with the CC-BED domain of Xa1, impairing Xa1-dependent immunity.

genes: AHP1 (HISTIDINE-CONTAINING PHOSPHOTRANSMITTER 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), DOF2.4 (DNA BINDING WITH ONE FINGER 2.4, Arabidopsis thaliana), NHL1 (NHL1, Arabidopsis thaliana), CDF4 (CYCLING DOF FACTOR 4, Arabidopsis thaliana), ATARFB1A (ADP-RIBOSYLATION FACTOR B1A, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AHP1, DOF2.4, NHL1, CDF4, and ATARFB1A significantly reduces root length and lateral root numbers under CdCl2 stress compared to wild type. Lateral root development in overexpression lines is better than wild type under CdCl2 conditions except for DOF2.4.
mechanism: These genes regulate vascular development and stress response pathways, enhancing resistance to CdCl2 stress through improved photosynthetic function and vascular tissue integrity.

genes: PSBO1 (PS II OXYGEN-EVOLVING COMPLEX 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), J3 (DNAJ HOMOLOGUE 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PSBO1 and J3 improves root length and lateral root numbers under CdCl2 stress compared to wild type. These lines show enhanced chlorophyll fluorescence and preserved chloroplast thylakoid membrane structure.
mechanism: PSBO1 and J3 maintain chloroplast function and starch metabolism under CdCl2 stress, supporting vascular tissue development and photosynthetic efficiency.

genes: COE2 (CHLOROPHYLL A/B-BINDING OVEREXPRESSION 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of COE2 (35S::COE2-1 and 35S::COE2-2) shows reduced sensitivity to CdCl2 stress with improved root length and lateral root numbers compared to wild type. These lines maintain higher chlorophyll fluorescence and starch levels under stress.
mechanism: COE2 regulates chloroplast retrograde signaling, enhancing chloroplast quality control and photosynthetic function under CdCl2 stress.

genes: OsNramp5 (OsNramp5, transporter for Cd uptake, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsNramp5 knockout reduces grain Cd content by ~54.2–56.6% in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: Gene editing disrupts Cd uptake transporter.

genes: OsHMA3 (OsHMA3, tonoplast-localized transporter for Cd detoxification, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsHMA3 overexpression reduces grain Cd content to 0.027±0.005 mg/kg in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsHMA3 transports Cd from cytosol into vacuoles for detoxification.

genes: OsWRKY23 (transcription factor, Oryza sativa)

mechanism: OsWRKY23 targets DNR1 for transcriptional activation, repressing root NO3− uptake and plant growth.

genes: OsARF6 (transcription factor, Oryza sativa)

mechanism: OsARF6 enhances N metabolism by upregulating NO3− uptake and assimilation genes.

genes: OsARF17 (transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsARF17 elevates expression of NRT and NIA genes, mitigating NO3− uptake and NR activity deficiencies caused by OsWRKY23 overexpression.
mechanism: OsARF17 enhances N metabolism by upregulating NO3− uptake and assimilation genes.

genes: OsWRKY23 (transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsWRKY23-GFP localizes to the nucleus, confirming its role as a transcription factor.
mechanism: OsWRKY23 binds to DNR1 promoter and activates its transcription, repressing NO3− uptake.

genes: MdMADS8 (MADS8, floral development gene, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MADS8 promotes precocious flowering and changes tree architecture, with increased flesh tissue and faster ripening in Malus domestica and Arabidopsis.
mechanism: MADS8 acts in a dose-dependent manner to control apple flesh development and ripening, promoting flowering and altering floral organ identity in Arabidopsis.

genes: LUC (luciferase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: The pFRK1::LUC activity is highly induced by multiple MAMPs.
mechanism: NA

genes: BAK1 (BAK1 kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The pFRK1::LUC activity induced by flg22 was restored to WT level in two independent complementation lines.
mechanism: BAK1 kinase activity is essential for the flg22-mediated signaling pathway.

genes: MIR397a (microRNA, Populus trichocarpa)

mechanism: miR397a targets SmLACs for cleavage, reducing their expression and enzymatic activity.

mechanism: miR397a targets LAC genes, reducing their expression and PA polymerization activity.

mechanism: SmLAC1 catalyzes the polymerization of flavan-3-ol monomers into procyanidins and converts B-type to A-type procyanidins.

genes: SmLAC1 (laccase, Salvia miltiorrhiza)
gene_construct: CRISPR/Cas9 vector with sgRNA targeting SmLAC1
phenotype: Knockout of SmLAC1 reduces total extractable and non-extractable PAs by 52.2–66.7% and 33.9%, respectively, in S. miltiorrhiza leaves.
mechanism: SmLAC1 knockout disrupts PA polymerization, leading to accumulation of flavan-3-ol monomers.

mechanism: MDAR1 overexpression elevates ascorbic acid (AsA) levels, which scavenges ROS under salt stress, thereby mitigating oxidative damage and improving root growth and overall plant tolerance to salinity.

genes: CsTST2 (tonoplast-localized sugar transporter 2, Citrus sinensis, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsTST2 in tomato increases fructose and glucose content by ~15% and fruit weight by ~20%.
mechanism: CsTST2 enhances vacuolar sugar transport, increasing soluble sugar accumulation and fruit size.

genes: CsTSI (theanine synthetase I, tea plant, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: GA3 treatment increases GFP expression and theanine biosynthesis in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: GA3 upregulates CsTSI expression through the CsTSI promoter (proCsTSI) to enhance theanine biosynthesis

genes: PagPCaP1a (PagPCaP1a, plasma membrane-anchored protein, Populus alba × P. glandulosa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PagPCaP1a increases sensitivity to salinity stress in poplar, with reduced leaf relative water content, chlorophyll content, and increased malondialdehyde content.
mechanism: PagPCaP1a destabilizes microtubules and forms condensates under salinity stress, accelerating microtubule depolymerization.

genes: PagPCaP1a (PagPCaP1a, plasma membrane-anchored protein, Populus alba × P. glandulosa)

genes: PagPCaP1a (PagPCaP1a, plasma membrane-anchored protein, Populus alba × P. glandulosa)

phenotype: PagPCaP1a-GFP forms condensates in poplar protoplasts under salinity stress, exhibiting liquid-like properties.
mechanism: PagPCaP1a-GFP condensates form in response to Ca2+ elevation during salinity stress, facilitating microtubule depolymerization.

genes: VviPUB19 promoter (cold-responsive promoter region, grapevine, Vitis vinifera), GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, pCAMBIA1301 vector)

mechanism: GFP reporter gene expression for visualizing transgenic events.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, pCAMBIA1300 vector)

mechanism: Nanomaterial-mediated gene delivery using GO-PEG-PEI-GFP complex for efficient transformation.

genes: TaTCP6 (Class I TCP transcription factor, involved in nitrate and phosphate utilization, Triticum aestivum)

mechanism: TaPHR2 enhances phosphorus uptake by interacting with TaTCP6 and releasing it from the TaSPXs-TaPHR2 complex.

genes: TaTCP6 (Class I TCP transcription factor, involved in nitrate and phosphate utilization, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Knockout of TaTCP6 results in reduced plant height, thousand-grain weight, and grain yield in wheat.
mechanism: Loss of TaTCP6 function impairs nitrate and phosphate uptake and utilization, leading to reduced agronomic traits.

genes: GSNOR1 (S-nitrosoglutathione reductase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Pe-TElncRNA2 positively regulates homologous genes (AtFZR2, AtNOT3, AtABCG44, AtAGD6) in Arabidopsis, contributing to early cold stress responses.

mechanism: RsWRKY40 knockdown downregulates RsSPS1 and RsCBF1/2, impairing sucrose synthesis and cold resilience.

genes: RsWRKY40 (Rsa9g000650, WRKY transcription factor, Raphanus sativus)
phenotype: RsWRKY40 promoter activity in N. benthamiana is elevated by cold treatment, as shown by increased LUC intensity.

mechanism: RsWRKY40 binds to the RsSPS1 promoter, directly activating its expression to enhance sucrose synthesis.

mechanism: RsWRKY40 binds to the promoters of RsCBF1 and RsCBF2, activating their expression to enhance cold tolerance via the CBF-dependent pathway.

genes: DlERF10 (Diospyros lotus, AP2/ERF transcription factor, Diospyros lotus)
phenotype: Overexpression of DlERF10 enhances cold tolerance in transgenic tobacco plants, with reduced MDA content and increased SOD, POD, CAT, and Pro levels under low-temperature stress.
mechanism: DlERF10 overexpression enhances cold tolerance by regulating antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, POD, CAT) and osmotic balance (Pro accumulation), reducing membrane lipid peroxidation (MDA).

mechanism: ZHD genes regulate meristem maintenance and boundary formation through interconnected networks with KN1 and other TFs, modulating pleiotropy in tassel and leaf architecture.

mechanism: NA

mechanism: SlHAM4 is a GRAS family transcriptional regulator required for phloem function and vascular integrity. Its loss disrupts phloem gene expression and transport, leading to pericarp ruptures and scarring.

genes: SlHAM4 (Solanum lycopersicum HAM4, transcriptional regulator, Solanum lycopersicum)

mechanism: SlHAM4 overexpression compensates for the loss-of-function mutation, restoring phloem gene expression and vascular integrity required for normal fruit development.

genes: SlHAM4 (Solanum lycopersicum HAM4, transcriptional regulator, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Complementation with SlHAM4-GFP under its native promoter restores normal flower senescence and eliminates fruit catfacing in slham4CRΔ4 mutants.
mechanism: The 4 kb SlHAM4 promoter drives sufficient expression to rescue phloem function and vascular integrity, indicating the promoter's sufficiency for SlHAM4 activity.

genes: SlHAM4 (Solanum lycopersicum HAM4, transcriptional regulator, Solanum lycopersicum)

mechanism: SlHAM4 promoter activity is confined to phloem tissues, including companion cells and sieve elements, indicating its role in phloem function.

genes: SlKNU (transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)

mechanism: SlKNU represses SlCLV3 and SlWUS, which regulate floral meristem (FM) activity and carpel development. Loss of SlKNU results in enlarged FM and increased fruit size.

genes: SlKNU (transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlKNU in Arabidopsis leads to loss of apical dominance, reduced stamen numbers, delayed flowering, and reduced seed-setting rate.
mechanism: SlKNU represses CLV3 and WUS in Arabidopsis, similar to its role in tomato. Overexpression disrupts meristem activity and floral organ development.

genes: SlKNU (transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)

mechanism: SlKNU represses SlCLV3 and SlWUS at the transcriptional level, mediated by the EAR domain. DEX-induced expression enhances this repression.

phenotype: Overexpression of ETO1 does not delay fruit ripening in Lycopersicon esculentum.

phenotype: No significant effect on Pto DC3000 virulence compared to Col-0 and IR-CFA6/HRPL lines.

genes: LUC (luciferase, firefly)
phenotype: No significant effect on Pto DC3000 virulence compared to Col-0 and IR-CFA6/HRPL lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: HTR9 (H3.1, histone variant H3.1 with K27M mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: H3.1K27M expression induces developmental defects (stunted growth, smaller/narrower leaves), reduced germination/survival rates, increased anthocyanin content, DNA damage (elevated comet tail DNA), MMS hypersensitivity, and increased homologous recombination frequency in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: H3.1K27M inhibits PRC2 and ATXR5/6 histone methyltransferase activity, leading to loss of H3K27me3 and H3K27me1 marks. This causes ectopic TSK activity on chromatin, resulting in DNA damage and genomic instability.

genes: HTR9 (H3.1, histone variant H3.1, Arabidopsis thaliana), HTR5 (H3.3, histone variant H3.3 with K27M mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: H3.1::H3.3K27M plants exhibit growth defects (small plant size, curled leaves) but lack H3.1K27M-specific phenotypes like low survival rate, MMS hypersensitivity, and DNA repair gene upregulation. They show reduced H3K27me3 but normal H3K27me1 levels.
mechanism: H3.3K27M inhibits PRC2 activity but not ATXR5/6, leading to reduced H3K27me3 without affecting H3K27me1. This results in PRC2-dependent phenotypes but not ATXR5/6-dependent genomic instability.

mechanism: COP1-mediated K63 ubiquitination of GH3.5 inhibits its enzymatic activity, reducing IAA conjugation and promoting hypocotyl elongation in the dark.

genes: COP1 (AtCOP1, ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: COP1 physically interacts with GH3.5 in the nucleus, mediating K63 ubiquitination that inhibits GH3.5's ability to conjugate IAA, thereby promoting hypocotyl elongation.

genes: PsAGL9 (PsAGL9, MADS-box transcription factor, Paeonia suffruticosa)

mechanism: PsAGL9 directly binds to and activates the expression of PsCYCD and PsEBB3 by interacting with their promoters containing CArG motifs.

genes: MdEIL1 (ethylene-insensitive 3-like 1, transcription factor, Malus domestica)

mechanism: TPSb2 catalyzes the conversion of geranyl pyrophosphate to isoprene.

mechanism: PGSL1 loss of function causes pollen germination to be more sensitive to LatB and high temperature.

mechanism: OsRGA1 accelerates aerenchyma formation by increasing H2O2 levels, enhancing root activity and promoting root growth

genes: UGT73C3 (promoter region, upstream regulatory sequence, Arabidopsis thaliana), UGT73C4 (promoter region, upstream regulatory sequence, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: HB34 transcriptionally activates UGT73C3 and UGT73C4 promoters via direct binding to TAATTA motifs.

genes: HB34 (full-length cDNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: HB34 is a nuclear-localized transcription factor that regulates UGT73C3/C4 expression.

genes: HB34 (full-length cDNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: HB34 overexpression increased UGT73C3 and UGT73C4 expression and enhanced resistance to Pst DC3000.
mechanism: HB34 positively regulates UGT73C3/C4 transcription and PDG-mediated plant immunity.

genes: HY5 (HY5, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: HY5 binds to the promoters of HSFs to repress their transcription, thereby inhibiting thermotolerance.

genes: CRY1 (CRY1, photoreceptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: CRY1 (CRY1, photoreceptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: CRY1 mediates blue-light suppression of thermotolerance by interacting with COP1 and regulating HY5 stability.

genes: COP1 (COP1, E3 ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: COP1 mediates the degradation of HY5 under heat stress, enhancing thermotolerance.

genes: HY5 (HY5, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: HY5 binds to the promoters of HSFs to repress their transcription, thereby inhibiting thermotolerance.

genes: CRY1 (CRY1, photoreceptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Phosphomimetic mutants of CRY1 are hypersensitive to heat stress, indicating phosphorylation's role in thermotolerance.

genes: CRY1 (CRY1, photoreceptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRY1-10D mutants exhibit hypersensitivity to heat stress under blue light in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Phosphomimetic mutants of CRY1 are hypersensitive to heat stress, indicating phosphorylation's role in thermotolerance.

genes: GID1 (Gibberellin Insensitive Dwarf1, rice, Oryza sativa)

mechanism: miR396c-mediated tissue-specific gene silencing via complementary base pairing with target sequence in 3' UTR.

mechanism: Loss of CCA1 prevents effective ER stress management, leading to increased ER stress sensitivity.

genes: TPS5 (trehalose-6-phosphate synthase 5, Arabidopsis thaliana), TPS10 (trehalose-6-phosphate synthase 10, Arabidopsis thaliana), TPS11 (trehalose-6-phosphate synthase 11, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: tps5-1, tps10-2, and tps11-2 mutants exhibit increased vegetative growth (rosette area ~2× larger in tps10-2), delayed flowering (100% flowering delayed by ~2 days in tps10-2), and altered carbohydrate metabolism (elevated starch and soluble NSC levels, particularly in tps10-2). tps11-2 shows reduced rosette size but increased photosynthetic parameters like transpiration and stomatal conductance.
mechanism: Disruption of TPSII genes leads to altered trehalose-6-phosphate (Tre6P) signaling, affecting carbon and nitrogen metabolism. This includes enhanced starch accumulation, modified amino acid profiles (elevated glutamine, aspartate, and isoleucine), and increased nitrate reductase activity. The mechanism involves interactions between TPSII proteins and TPS1/Tre6P to regulate flowering time and resource allocation.

genes: TPS5 (trehalose-6-phosphate synthase 5, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: tps5-1 mutants show increased vegetative growth, delayed flowering, and altered carbohydrate metabolism (elevated starch and glucose levels). They also exhibit reduced glycine levels and increased glutamate and glutamine during photoperiods.
mechanism: TPS5 knockout disrupts Tre6P signaling, leading to altered carbon partitioning and nitrogen assimilation. This affects flowering time regulation via FLOWERING LOCUS T (FT) signaling and modifies TCA cycle intermediates and amino acid metabolism.

genes: TPS10 (trehalose-6-phosphate synthase 10, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: tps10-2 mutants display the most pronounced phenotypes, including ~2× larger rosette area, delayed flowering by ~2 days, and significant increases in starch, sucrose, and glucose levels. They also show elevated amino acids (leucine, valine, alanine) and altered photosynthetic parameters (higher intracellular CO2 but reduced water-use efficiency).
mechanism: TPS10 knockout enhances carbon storage as starch and soluble sugars while perturbing amino acid metabolism and photosynthetic efficiency. This is linked to disrupted Tre6P signaling, which affects flowering time and resource allocation via interactions with TPS1 and FT pathways.

genes: TPS11 (trehalose-6-phosphate synthase 11, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: tps11-2 mutants have smaller rosette size but increased transpiration, stomatal conductance, and photosynthetic activity. They show elevated starch and amino acid levels (asparagine, glutamine) and reduced glycine. NR activity is significantly higher, and CO2 assimilation rates are lower compared to wild type.
mechanism: TPS11 knockout disrupts Tre6P signaling, leading to altered carbon-nitrogen balance. This affects starch metabolism, amino acid biosynthesis, and photosynthetic efficiency, potentially via interactions with TPS1 and SnRK1 pathways to modulate metabolic stress responses.

mechanism: NA

genes: SlARF2a (truncated variant, tomato)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlARF2aTr leads to parthenocarpy in tomato under heat stress.
mechanism: SlARF2aTr interacts with TSP4a to prevent repression of TSP4b transcription, enhancing auxin signaling and parthenocarpy.

genes: PbCRY1a (PbCRY1a, blue light receptor, Pyrus pyrifolia)
phenotype: Antisense suppression of PbCRY1a inhibits blue-light induced lignification in pear calli.
mechanism: Downregulation of PbCRY1a prevents activation of PbbHLH195 and PbNSC, reducing lignin biosynthesis.

genes: PbbHLH195 (PbbHLH195, bHLH transcription factor, Pyrus pyrifolia)
phenotype: Antisense suppression of PbbHLH195 inhibits blue-light induced lignification in pear calli.
mechanism: Downregulation of PbbHLH195 prevents activation of PbNSC and lignin biosynthesis genes.

phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of MusaPUB22/23 confers resistance to Xanthomonas vasicola pv. musacearum (Xvm) in 'Sukali Ndiizi' banana cultivar, with 4 events showing complete resistance and 1 event showing 93.3% resistance
mechanism: Disruption of MusaPUB22/23 activates defense signaling genes (PR1, Rboh-A/C, Oxi1, etc.) and induces reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, leading to programmed cell death (PCD) and enhanced pathogen-associated molecular pattern-triggered immunity (PTI)

genes: KnWSD1 (Klebsormidium nitens wax synthase 1, Klebsormidium nitens), Venus (fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of KnWSD1 increases wax ester (WE) synthesis in Arabidopsis thaliana leaves, restoring WE content in wsd quintuple mutants.
mechanism: KnWSD1 synthesizes wax esters from long-chain alcohols and acyl-CoA, as demonstrated by in vitro and in planta assays.

genes: WSD1 (wax synthase/acyl-CoA acyltransferase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under the WSD1 promoter confirms WSD1 expression in floral tissues of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: KnWSD1 (Klebsormidium nitens wax synthase 1, Klebsormidium nitens)
phenotype: Overexpression of KnWSD1 under the FDH promoter restores wax ester (WE) synthesis in the wsd quintuple mutant of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: KnWSD1 utilizes long-chain alcohols as substrates to synthesize wax esters, as demonstrated in yeast and Arabidopsis.

genes: WSD2 (wax synthase/acyl-CoA acyltransferase 2, Arabidopsis thaliana), WSD3 (wax synthase/acyl-CoA acyltransferase 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of WSD2 and WSD3 in Arabidopsis thaliana reduces wax ester (WE) content in floral tissues under high humidity.
mechanism: Disruption of WSD2 and WSD3 genes impairs wax ester synthesis, leading to floral developmental abnormalities and reduced fertility under high humidity.

genes: SlRBP1 (RNA-binding protein involved in fruit size regulation, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Fruit-specific overexpression of SlRBP1 results in slightly larger fruits compared to wild type, but not significantly different.
mechanism: SlRBP1 regulates fruit size by controlling cell division and expansion.

genes: SlRBP1 (RNA-binding protein involved in fruit size regulation, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Fruit-specific silencing of SlRBP1 reduces tomato fruit size by ~10-25 mm in transverse diameter compared to wild type.
mechanism: SlRBP1 regulates fruit size by controlling cell division and expansion.

genes: SlFBA7 (fructose-bisphosphate aldolase 7, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlFBA7 increases fruit size compared to wild type.
mechanism: SlFBA7 positively regulates fruit size by promoting cell expansion.

genes: SlFBA7 (fructose-bisphosphate aldolase 7, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of SlFBA7 reduces fruit size compared to wild type.
mechanism: SlFBA7 positively regulates fruit size by promoting cell expansion.

genes: SlGPIMT (glycosylphosphatidylinositol mannosyltransferase 1, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlGPIMT increases fruit size compared to wild type.
mechanism: SlGPIMT positively regulates fruit size by promoting cell expansion.

genes: SlGPIMT (glycosylphosphatidylinositol mannosyltransferase 1, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of SlGPIMT reduces fruit size compared to wild type.
mechanism: SlGPIMT positively regulates fruit size by promoting cell expansion.

genes: MdTLP7 (TLP7, tubby-like protein 7, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdTLP7 significantly increased the drought and salt tolerance of apple through regulating gene transcription
mechanism: MdTLP7 interacted with MdNAC72L to regulate the expression of MdHsp70-8 and MdAGP, and the overexpression of these two genes significantly enhanced the drought and salt stresses tolerance of apple

genes: HTR5 (H3.3 coding gene, mutated K4R)
phenotype: K4R mutated H3.3 caused similar developmental defects as K4A mutation, indicating charge-neutralization is not the cause
mechanism: Modifications on K4 are essential, not the positive charge

genes: HTR5 (H3.3 coding gene, mutated K4Q)
phenotype: K4Q mutated H3.3 failed to rescue h3.3ko mutant phenotypes
mechanism: Methylation on K4 is likely required for H3.3 function

mechanism: AtMC1C220A forms stable condensate-like puncta and interacts with immune components (NLRs, PRRs, RBOHF), leading to hyperaccumulation of immune regulators and SA-dependent autoimmunity. Wt AtMC1 suppresses this phenotype through proteostasis and autophagy.

genes: AtMC1 (full deletion CRISPR mutant)
gene_construct: CRISPR-Cas9 deletion of AtMC1 (5′ and 3′ UTRs targeted)
phenotype: CRISPR deletion of AtMC1 (atmc1-CR #1) results in mild autoimmunity with age-dependent growth restriction, spontaneous cell death, and PR1a accumulation, similar to T-DNA mutants.
mechanism: AtMC1 deletion disrupts proteostasis of immune components, leading to SA-dependent autoimmunity through the EDS1-PAD4 immune node.

genes: SNIPER1 (HA-SNIPER1)
phenotype: Overexpression of SNIPER1 in atmc1 AtMC1C220A-GFP plants rescues the autoimmune phenotype, restoring growth, suppressing cell death, and reducing PR1a accumulation.
mechanism: SNIPER1, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, restores proteostasis by degrading hyperaccumulated NLRs and immune components stabilized by AtMC1C220A, preventing condensate formation and autophagy overload.

genes: PH8 (promoter, N-terminal region, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: GUS expression in young roots, leaf sheaths, and developing stems
mechanism: PH8 predominantly expresses in vegetative tissues

genes: PH8 (full-length coding sequence, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: PH8-eGFP localization in cytoplasm and nucleus
mechanism: PH8 subcellular localization in rice protoplasts

genes: RAE1 (RAE1, ABA-responsive gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: RAE1 expression is induced by ABA, leading to enhanced GUS activity

genes: RAE1 (RAE1, ABA-responsive gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ABA sensitivity in rae1 mutant lines was restored to the level of the wild type after complementation
mechanism: RAE1 negatively regulates ABA response at the early seedling stage

genes: STOP1 (STOP1, RAE1 substrate, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: STOP1 overexpressing lines displayed significantly increased sensitivity to ABA
mechanism: STOP1 is a substrate of RAE1, and its overexpression leads to increased ABA sensitivity

genes: LIMYB (LIMYB, transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of LIMYB represses the promoter activity and expression of photosynthetic apparatus-related genes, leading to inhibited photosynthesis and reduced electron transport rate (ETR), CO2 assimilation rate, and growth in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: LIMYB binds to CAAAAC DNA motifs in the promoters of photosynthesis-related genes (e.g., PsbP, FD1) and represses their transcription, reducing photosystem II (PSII) and electron transport chain (ETC) components. This transcriptional repression precedes NIK1-mediated translational suppression, directly inhibiting photosynthesis.

genes: NIK1-T474D (NIK1, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Constitutive activation of NIK1-T474D represses photosynthesis-related genes (PsbP, FD1) and inhibits photosynthesis, reducing ETR, CO2 assimilation, and growth in Arabidopsis thaliana. This effect requires LIMYB function, as T474D expression in limyb mutants does not repress photosynthesis.
mechanism: NIK1-T474D phosphorylates RPL10 and LIMYB, activating the NIK1/RPL10/LIMYB signaling module. LIMYB-mediated transcriptional repression of photosynthesis-related genes occurs independently of NIK1's translational suppression role.

genes: RPL10 (RPL10, ribosomal protein L10, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RPL10-GFP does not directly affect photosynthesis but is part of the NIK1/RPL10/LIMYB signaling module that represses photosynthesis-related genes when activated by NIK1 phosphorylation.
mechanism: RPL10 is phosphorylated by NIK1, which activates LIMYB to repress photosynthesis-related genes. RPL10 itself does not directly regulate photosynthesis but serves as a signaling component in the NIK1-mediated pathway.

genes: LIMYB (LIMYB, transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of YFP-LIMYB represses photosynthesis-related genes (PsbP, FD1) and inhibits photosynthesis, reducing ETR, CO2 assimilation, and growth in Arabidopsis thaliana. This effect is mediated by LIMYB's direct binding to promoter regions of photosynthesis genes.
mechanism: LIMYB binds to CAAAAC motifs in the promoters of photosynthesis-related genes (e.g., PsbP, FD1) and represses their transcription. This transcriptional repression occurs independently of NIK1-mediated translational suppression and directly inhibits photosynthesis.

genes: ZmBAK1 (ZmBAK1, BAK1 receptor kinase, Zea mays)
phenotype: ZmBAK1-GFP protein is expressed in the cell membrane of N. benthamiana epidermis
mechanism: ZmBAK1 is localized at the cell membrane, suggesting it functions in membrane-associated signaling pathways

genes: ZmBAK1 (ZmBAK1, BAK1 receptor kinase, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmBAK1 significantly improves GSR resistance in maize
mechanism: ZmBAK1 activates PTI signaling pathway, leading to increased ROS burst, callose deposition, and expression of immune genes

genes: Cry1Ac (insecticidal crystal protein, Bacillus thuringiensis)

mechanism: Cry1A.105 and Cry2Ab2 proteins derived from Bacillus thuringiensis produce insecticidal crystal (Cry) proteins that target lepidopteran insect pests.

genes: FaWAK35 (FaWAK35, resistance gene, Fragaria x ananassa)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of FaWAK35 increased the strawberry resistance to B. cinerea.
mechanism: NA

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)

mechanism: pCDF4::3xnlsGFP reporter tracks CDF4 spatiotemporal expression patterns in embryogenic transition.

genes: MsJAR1 (MsJAR1, chloroplast localization, Medicago sativa)
phenotype: Subcellular localization of MsJAR1 in chloroplasts, co-localizing with chloroplast autofluorescence.
mechanism: NA

genes: MsJAR1 (MsJAR1, overexpression, Medicago sativa)

mechanism: MsJAR1 regulates plant growth and development by affecting the area of the xylem and phloem, enhancing photosynthetic parameters, and altering enzyme activities in glycolysis and the tricarboxylic acid cycle.

genes: AtNRT2.4 (nitrate transporter 2.4, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: AtNRT2.4 modulates root architecture by altering transcription of AtANR1 and AtCIPK23, suppresses AtNLP7 expression, and induces anthocyanin synthesis genes under nitrate deficiency.

genes: FKBP12 (FKBP12, FKBP12 overexpression, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of FKBP12 decreases drought and oxidative tolerance in rice, with reduced survival rates and increased H2O2 accumulation under stress.
mechanism: Overexpression of FKBP12 compromises antioxidative defense systems, leading to heightened drought sensitivity.

genes: FKBP12 (FKBP12, FKBP12 complementation, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of the fkbp12 mutant restores drought tolerance, with increased survival rates and reduced cellular damage under stress.
mechanism: Complementation of FKBP12 in the mutant rescues drought tolerance by restoring normal stress response pathways.

mechanism: VaMIEL1 ubiquitinates and promotes the degradation of VaMYB4a through the ubiquitin–proteasome pathway, leading to downregulation of cold-responsive genes.

genes: VaMIEL1 (VaMIEL1, E3 ubiquitin ligase, Vitis amurensis)

mechanism: VaMIEL1 ubiquitinates and promotes the degradation of VaMYB4a through the ubiquitin–proteasome pathway, leading to downregulation of cold-responsive genes.

genes: VaMIEL1 (VaMIEL1, E3 ubiquitin ligase, Vitis amurensis)

mechanism: Silencing VaMIEL1 prevents the ubiquitination and degradation of VaMYB4a, allowing for increased expression of cold-responsive genes in the CBF-COR pathway.

genes: VaMYB4a (VaMYB4a, transcription factor, Vitis amurensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of VaMYB4a in grapevine calli enhances cold tolerance, as evidenced by increased fresh weight, reduced ROS accumulation, and upregulation of cold-responsive genes.
mechanism: VaMYB4a activates the CBF-COR pathway, leading to increased expression of cold-responsive genes and improved cold tolerance.

genes: VaMIEL1 (VaMIEL1, E3 ubiquitin ligase, Vitis amurensis), VaMYB4a (VaMYB4a, transcription factor, Vitis amurensis)
phenotype: Coexpression of VaMIEL1 and VaMYB4a in grapevine calli results in intermediate cold tolerance compared to single-gene overexpression lines, with reduced ROS accumulation and partial upregulation of cold-responsive genes.
mechanism: The interplay between VaMIEL1 and VaMYB4a modulates cold tolerance through the CBF-COR signaling pathway, with VaMIEL1 promoting VaMYB4a degradation and VaMYB4a counteracting VaMIEL1's negative effects.

genes: VaMIEL1 (VaMIEL1, E3 ubiquitin ligase, Vitis amurensis)
phenotype: The VaMIEL1 promoter drives GUS expression in response to cold stress, with increased GUS activity observed after 9 hours of cold treatment.
mechanism: The VaMIEL1 promoter contains a low-temperature-responsive element (CCGAAA), which activates gene expression under cold stress conditions.
