mechanism: SmbHLH85 upregulates key biosynthetic genes (SmDXS2, SmDXR, SmGGPPS1, SmCPS1, SmKSL1, SmCYP76AH1, SmCYP76AH3, SmCYP76AK1, SmCYP76AK2) by 1.7- to 2.5-fold, promoting tanshinone biosynthesis.

genes: SmbHLH85 (SmbHLH85, transcription factor, Salvia miltiorrhiza)
phenotype: RNAi of SmbHLH85 reduces tanshinone content by ~31-60% for TI, ~42-65% for TIIA, and ~36-51% for total tanshinone in Salvia miltiorrhiza.
mechanism: SmbHLH85 downregulation decreases key biosynthetic genes (SmDXS2, SmDXR, SmGGPPS1, SmCPS1, SmKSL1, SmCYP76AH1, SmCYP76AH3, SmCYP76AK1, SmCYP76AK2, SmCYP76AK3) by 31-65%, inhibiting tanshinone biosynthesis.

genes: CsMAPK3 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 3, Camellia sinensis)

mechanism: CsMAPK3 knockdown leads to reduced immune response and increased susceptibility.

genes: TrMMV-MCS (multiple cloning site, Trichosanthes mottle mosaic virus)

genes: TaHAKAI (Triticum aestivum, resistance gene, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaHAKAIR increases resistance to WYMV in wheat by promoting P2 protein degradation via the 26S proteasome pathway.
mechanism: TaHAKAIR acts as an E3 ubiquitin ligase that ubiquitinates the viral P2 protein at Lys554, leading to its degradation. Phosphorylation at Ser40 enhances TaHAKAIR's ubiquitination activity without affecting m6A methylation.

genes: TaHAKAI (Triticum aestivum, resistance gene, Triticum aestivum)
gene_construct: TaHAKAI-A (C403G mutation causing premature termination) in JING411 background
phenotype: Knockout of TaHAKAI-A in wheat (tahakai) results in increased WYMV infection with more pronounced mosaic symptoms and higher viral RNA replication levels.
mechanism: TaHAKAI-A knockout disrupts the E3 ubiquitin ligase activity required for P2 protein degradation, allowing increased viral replication.

genes: TaHAKAI (Triticum aestivum, resistance gene, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Silencing of TaHAKAI in wheat using BSMV results in increased WYMV infection with more severe mosaic symptoms and higher viral RNA replication.
mechanism: TaHAKAI silencing reduces E3 ubiquitin ligase activity, leading to decreased P2 protein degradation and enhanced viral replication.

genes: TaHAKAI (Triticum aestivum, resistance gene, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaHAKAIS (non-phosphorylated variant) in wheat results in reduced resistance to WYMV compared to TaHAKAIR, with increased viral RNA replication and CP accumulation.
mechanism: TaHAKAIS has weaker E3 ubiquitin ligase activity than phosphorylated TaHAKAIR, leading to less effective P2 protein degradation and increased viral replication.

genes: TaHAKAI (Triticum aestivum, resistance gene, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaHAKAID (phosphomimic mutant) in wheat enhances resistance to WYMV compared to TaHAKAIS, with reduced viral RNA replication and CP accumulation.
mechanism: Phosphomimic TaHAKAID mimics phosphorylated TaHAKAIR, increasing E3 ubiquitin ligase activity and promoting P2 protein degradation.

genes: TaWPS1 (Triticum aestivum, spike development gene, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaWPS1 in wheat increases panicle length and spikelet number, contributing to higher field yield.
mechanism: TaHAKAIR-mediated m6A modification of TaWPS1 reduces its mRNA stability, leading to increased panicle length and spikelet number.

genes: VcCPC (blueberry CPC homolog, R3-type MYB transcription factor, Vaccinium spp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of VcCPC increases root hair number from 12.4 to 16.4 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: VcCPC promotes root hair formation by initiating ectopic root hairs in non-hair cells (N cells) and inhibiting anthocyanin biosynthesis and trichome formation.

genes: VcCPC (blueberry CPC homolog, R3-type MYB transcription factor, Vaccinium spp.)
phenotype: The P1 construct (VcCPCpro(− 1273 − 1)::VcCPC) failed to restore the root hair-deficient phenotype in the cpc mutant.
mechanism: The VcCPC promoter (− 1273 − 1) lacks regulatory elements present in the AtCPC promoter, leading to low expression activity in root hair fate-determining regions.

genes: VcCPC (blueberry CPC homolog, R3-type MYB transcription factor, Vaccinium spp.)
phenotype: The P2 construct (VcCPCpro(− 1273 − 710) AtCPCpro(− 683 − 1)::VcCPC) restored the root hair phenotype in the cpc mutant.
mechanism: Substitution of the VcCPC promoter region (− 709 to − 1) with the AtCPC promoter introduced regulatory elements (e.g., CWB region) critical for root hair development.

genes: VcCPC (blueberry CPC homolog, R3-type MYB transcription factor, Vaccinium spp.)
phenotype: The P3 construct (VcCPCpro-AtCPCpro CWB::VcCPC) failed to restore the root hair phenotype in the cpc mutant.
mechanism: Replacement of the VcCPC promoter's − 511 to − 467 fragment with the AtCPC CWB region was insufficient to enhance promoter activity for root hair development.

genes: GbWOX2 (WUSCHEL-related homeobox 2, Ginkgo biloba), GbWOX3A (WUSCHEL-related homeobox 3A, Ginkgo biloba)
phenotype: Overexpression of GbWOX2 results in larger and denser callus formation, while GbWOX3A enhances shoot regeneration and increases adventitious shoot induction rate.
mechanism: NA

genes: TksMYC2 (TksMYC2, homolog of AtMYC2, Taraxacum kok-saghyz)

mechanism: TksMYC2 binds to promoter regions of rubber synthesis genes (CPT2, SRPPs) and upregulates their expression.

genes: TksMYC2 (TksMYC2, homolog of AtMYC2, Taraxacum kok-saghyz), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: TksMYC2-GFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus in transient and stable expression lines, enabling chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) analysis of TksMYC2-DNA interactions.
mechanism: TksMYC2-GFP binds to promoter regions of rubber synthesis genes (CPT2, SRPPs) and sesquiterpene lactone (SL) biosynthesis gene GAO, confirming TksMYC2's role as a transcription factor.

mechanism: NA

phenotype: No significant change in fruit firmness compared to wild-type M82

mechanism: GA20ox3 overexpression increases GA content, enhancing fruit development and seed germination.

genes: GA20ox3 (At5g07200, key enzyme GA20ox3, crucial for catalyzing GA biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: MpNEK1 (MpNEK1, Nek kinase, Marchantia polymorpha), MpNEK1K37E (kinase-deficient mutant of MpNEK1, Marchantia polymorpha), MpNEK1dKD (N-terminal kinase domain deletion mutant of MpNEK1, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of MpNEK1 severely suppresses thallus growth and causes juvenile lethality in Marchantia polymorpha. Estradiol-induced MpNEK1 suppresses cell proliferation and mitotic cell division, reduces microtubule density and dynamics, and suppresses rhizoid growth.
mechanism: MpNEK1 induction suppresses cell proliferation by reducing EdU-positive nuclei, disrupts mitotic progression by decreasing mitotic cell numbers, and alters microtubule organization by reducing cortical microtubule density and dynamics. Overexpression of kinase-deficient MpNEK1 (K37E and dKD) also suppresses growth, suggesting kinase-independent mechanisms involving protein aggregation or interaction trapping.

genes: MpNEK1 (MpNEK1, Nek kinase, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of MpNEK1–Citrine severely suppresses thallus growth and causes juvenile lethality in Marchantia polymorpha. Estradiol-induced MpNEK1–Citrine suppresses rhizoid growth and alters localization from apical to whole rhizoid regions.
mechanism: MpNEK1–Citrine overexpression disrupts rhizoid tip growth by mislocalizing to entire rhizoid regions, reduces microtubule foci at apical domes, and suppresses rhizoid elongation. Particles move bidirectionally along microtubules at velocities similar to kinesin-dependent transport.

genes: MpNEK1K37E (kinase-deficient mutant of MpNEK1, Marchantia polymorpha), MpNEK1dKD (N-terminal kinase domain deletion mutant of MpNEK1, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of kinase-deficient MpNEK1 (K37E and dKD) suppresses thallus growth and rhizoid growth in Marchantia polymorpha. K37E and dKD mutants show milder growth suppression compared to full-length MpNEK1.
mechanism: Kinase-deficient MpNEK1 suppresses growth through kinase-independent mechanisms, likely involving protein aggregation or interaction trapping. dKD retains partial normal localization in rhizoids (47% tip-localized vs 94% in K37E), suggesting structural domains contribute to localization.

genes: 14-3-3κ (14-3-3κ, 14-3-3 protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: The C-terminal -PTL> motif of G6PD5.1 and G6PD6 mediates peroxisomal import when fused to GFP, as demonstrated by colocalization with peroxisomal matrix and membrane markers.

genes: G6PD5.1 (cytosolic glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase isoform 5.1, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: The medial insertion site (A139-E140) in G6PD5.1 allows for active dimer formation and catalytic activity, as demonstrated by G6PDH activity measurements and immunoblot analysis.

genes: G6PD6 (cytosolic glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase isoform 6, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The medial GFP fusion of G6PD6 (inserted between amino acids T138 and E139) under the CaMV35S promoter exhibits 58% relative catalytic activity compared to G6PD5.1_medial (A139 E140) in g6pd5-1 g6pd6 double-mutant protoplasts.
mechanism: The medial insertion site (T138-E139) in G6PD6 allows for active dimer formation and catalytic activity, as demonstrated by G6PDH activity measurements and immunoblot analysis.

genes: G6PD5.1 (cytosolic glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase isoform 5.1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The C-terminal 50 amino acids of G6PD5.1 with a modified -SKL> PTS1 motif fused to GFP under the CaMV35S promoter show peroxisomal import and colocalization with peroxisomal markers in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts.
mechanism: The engineered -SKL> PTS1 motif in G6PD5_C-short enables efficient peroxisomal import, as demonstrated by colocalization with peroxisomal matrix and membrane markers.

genes: G6PD6 (cytosolic glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase isoform 6, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The C-terminal 50 amino acids of G6PD6 with a modified -SRL> PTS1 motif fused to GFP under the CaMV35S promoter show peroxisomal import and colocalization with peroxisomal markers in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts.
mechanism: The engineered -SRL> PTS1 motif in G6PD6_C-short enables efficient peroxisomal import, as demonstrated by colocalization with peroxisomal matrix and membrane markers.

genes: G6PD6 (cytosolic glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase isoform 6, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: A double cassette construct containing G6PD6 with a canonical -SKL> PTS1 motif and a G6PD6_medial fusion lacking the last leucine (ΔL) under the CaMV35S promoter results in peroxisomal localization of the PTS1-lacking medial fusion in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts.
mechanism: The presence of the -SKL> PTS1 motif in the unlabelled G6PD6 allows for dimeric import into peroxisomes, even when the medial fusion lacks a functional PTS1 motif.

genes: TTC4 (VIT_204s0023g00470, WRKY transcription factor, Vitis vinifera), TTC4TW (VIT_204s0023g00470, WRKY transcription factor, Vitis davidii), TTC4JX (VIT_204s0023g00470, WRKY transcription factor, Vitis vinifera)

genes: miR1850.2 (24-nt mature miRNA)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR1850.2 does not significantly alter cold tolerance in rice under the tested conditions.
mechanism: miR1850.2 does not directly confer cold tolerance, as no significant differences in survival were observed compared to controls.

genes: miR1850.2 (24-nt mature miRNA)
phenotype: Knockdown of miR1850.2 enhances cold tolerance in rice, with higher survival rates, possibly due to reduced miR1850.1 accumulation.
mechanism: Reduced miR1850.2 accumulation indirectly alleviates miR1850.1-mediated repression of NPR3.

genes: NPR3 (non-expressor of pathogenesis-related genes 3, rice-specific)
phenotype: Overexpression of NPR3 enhances cold tolerance in rice, with higher survival rates, increased pollen fertility, and reduced oxidative damage.
mechanism: NPR3 positively regulates cold tolerance by reducing malondialdehyde (MDA) content and increasing antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD and POD).

genes: DcFAD2-6 (DcFAD2-6, Δ12-acetylenase, Daucus carota), DcFAD2-7 (DcFAD2-7, Δ12-acetylenase, Daucus carota), DcFAD2-8 (DcFAD2-8, Δ12-acetylenase, Daucus carota)
phenotype: Increased production of crepenynic acid (CA) compared with the control in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: DcFAD2-6, -7, and -8 encode Δ12-acetylenases that catalyze the formation of CA.

genes: DcFAD2-1 (DcFAD2-1, Δ12-acetylenase, Daucus carota), DcFAD2-9 (DcFAD2-9, Δ12-acetylenase, Daucus carota)
phenotype: Increased production of crepenynic acid (CA) compared with the control in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: DcFAD2-1 and -9 encode Δ12-acetylenases that catalyze the formation of CA.

genes: DcFAD2-1 (DcFAD2-1, Δ12-acetylenase, Daucus carota), DcFAD2-9 (DcFAD2-9, Δ12-acetylenase, Daucus carota)
phenotype: Significant reductions in falcarindiol content (up to 80% decrease) in carrot hairy roots.
mechanism: Knockout of DcFAD2-1 and -9 disrupts falcarindiol biosynthesis.

genes: VAR1 (chloroplast FtsH5 metalloprotease subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana), VAR2 (chloroplast FtsH8 metalloprotease subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of var1-1 and var2-15 mutants restores cold-stress tolerance, normal growth, and chlorophyll content to wild-type levels.
mechanism: Restoration of VAR1 and VAR2 function in the chloroplast FtsH metalloprotease complex, which is critical for photosystem biogenesis and degradation of damaged photosynthetic complexes under cold stress.

genes: CAT1 (chloroplast catalase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), CAT2 (chloroplast catalase 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of chloroplast-targeted CAT1 and CAT2 increases catalase activity in chloroplasts, degrading H2O2 and conferring salt stress tolerance.
mechanism: Enhanced degradation of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) in chloroplasts, reducing oxidative stress and improving stress tolerance.

genes: YUC8 (YUC8, auxin biosynthesis gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of YUC8 increases root hair (RH) length by ~35% in Arabidopsis thaliana under both 22°C and 10°C conditions.
mechanism: YUC8 enhances auxin biosynthesis in root apical meristems, promoting RH elongation under low-temperature conditions. YUC8-GFP reporter shows increased signal intensity at 10°C, indicating elevated auxin production.

genes: OsSPL14 (OsSPL14, SQUAMOSA PROMOTER-BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE 14, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of OsSPL14 in rice results in chalky endosperm with higher percentage of grains with chalkiness (PGWC) and degree of endosperm chalkiness (DEC), reduced head rice yield, and altered starch granule morphology (loose packing, floury-white appearance).
mechanism: OsSPL14 directly binds to promoters of Wx and PDIL1-1 to activate their expression, which regulates starch and protein accumulation in endosperm. Knockout disrupts this regulation, leading to reduced amylose content and increased protein accumulation.

genes: OsSPL14 (OsSPL14, SQUAMOSA PROMOTER-BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE 14, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSPL14 in rice results in translucent endosperm with lower PGWC and DEC, higher head rice yield, and increased starch granule density (polyhedral, tightly packed).
mechanism: OsSPL14 activates Wx and PDIL1-1 expression, enhancing starch synthesis and inhibiting decomposition. Overexpression increases amylose content and reduces protein accumulation in endosperm.

genes: OsSPL14 (OsSPL14, SQUAMOSA PROMOTER-BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE 14, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsSPL14-RNAi transgenic plants exhibit chalky endosperm with increased PGWC and DEC, reduced head rice yield, and altered starch granule morphology (loose packing).
mechanism: RNAi-mediated downregulation of OsSPL14 reduces its ability to activate Wx and PDIL1-1, leading to decreased starch synthesis and increased protein accumulation.

genes: OsSPL14 (OsSPL14, SQUAMOSA PROMOTER-BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE 14, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: miR156e overexpression (OE) in rice leads to OsSPL14 downregulation, resulting in chalky endosperm with increased PGWC and DEC, reduced head rice yield, and altered starch granule morphology.
mechanism: miR156e cleaves OsSPL14 mRNA, reducing its expression. This disrupts OsSPL14's regulation of Wx and PDIL1-1, leading to decreased starch synthesis and increased protein accumulation.

genes: OsSPL14 (OsSPL14, SQUAMOSA PROMOTER-BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE 14, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: miR529a overexpression (OE) in rice leads to OsSPL14 downregulation, resulting in chalky endosperm with increased PGWC and DEC, reduced head rice yield, and altered starch granule morphology.
mechanism: miR529a cleaves OsSPL14 mRNA, reducing its expression. This disrupts OsSPL14's regulation of Wx and PDIL1-1, leading to decreased starch synthesis and increased protein accumulation.

genes: OsSPL14 (OsSPL14 promoter, SQUAMOSA PROMOTER-BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE 14, Oryza sativa), gusA (β-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Transgenic plants with the OsSPL14 promoter driving gusA show GUS activity in rice grains, with expression decreasing during grain development.
mechanism: The OsSPL14 promoter drives gusA expression in developing endosperm, demonstrating its spatiotemporal activity pattern.

genes: OsYSL9 (OsYSL9, iron transport, Oryza sativa), OsIRT1 (OsIRT1, iron transport, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsYSL9 and OsIRT1 increases grain iron content, grain weight, number of primary branches, and net photosynthetic rate in rice under iron-deficient conditions.
mechanism: Enhanced phloem-mediated iron transport improves iron uptake, translocation, and remobilization, promoting chlorophyll synthesis and mitigating the negative effects of iron deficiency on leaf photosynthesis.

genes: OsYSL9 (OsYSL9, iron transport, Oryza sativa), OsIRT1 (OsIRT1, iron transport, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsIRT1 increases grain iron content, grain number per panicle, and grain weight, as well as primary and secondary branches, and enhances photosynthetic efficiency in rice under iron-deficient conditions.
mechanism: Enhanced phloem-mediated iron transport improves iron uptake, translocation, and remobilization, promoting chlorophyll synthesis and mitigating the negative effects of iron deficiency on leaf photosynthesis.

genes: ELD1 (early flowering at long day 1, Oryza sativa, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of the eld1 mutant fully rescued the early flowering phenotype at T1 generation.
mechanism: ELD1 negatively regulates flowering time in rice under long-day conditions.

genes: ELD1 (early flowering at long day 1, Oryza sativa, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of ELD1-GFP fusion driven by the CaMV35S promoter caused delayed flowering of 3–6 days in the eld1 background.
mechanism: ELD1 negatively regulates flowering time in rice under long-day conditions.

genes: ELD1 (early flowering at long day 1, Oryza sativa, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Three ELD1 RNAi lines showed an early flowering phenotype (5–10 days earlier than WT).
mechanism: ELD1 negatively regulates flowering time in rice under long-day conditions.

genes: OsNKAP (Oryza sativa, Oryza sativa, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Three OsNKAP RNAi lines exhibited 3–5 days earlier flowering phenotypes than the WT under long-day conditions.
mechanism: OsNKAP acts as a flowering suppressor in rice, similar to ELD1.

genes: LIG4 (DNA ligase IV, N. tabacum), POLQ (DNA polymerase theta, N. tabacum)
phenotype: DSBR deficiency increases EGT frequency in somatic cells and male germline by ~20-fold in polqΔCDS-3 and polqΔHel-4 mutants
mechanism: DSBR pathways (NHEJ and TMEJ) suppress EGT by limiting DSB availability; impaired DSBR increases DSBs available for orgDNA integration

genes: RPA1C (RPA subunit, N. tabacum)
phenotype: Unsuccessful mutant isolation; only chimeric plants recovered
mechanism: NA

genes: KU70 (Ku70, N. tabacum), KU80 (Ku80, N. tabacum)
phenotype: Homozygous knockout seedlings display strong growth arrest and altered morphology
mechanism: Ku70/Ku80 have functions in telomere homeostasis and NHEJ

genes: OsKEA1 (K+-efflux antiporter, rice, LOC_Os04g58620)
phenotype: OsKEA1 knockout mutants (cas9-3, cas9-8, oskea1) exhibit salt stress sensitivity with severe leaf shrinkage, wilting, and reduced fresh/dry weight and survival rate compared to wild-type rice under 180 mM NaCl treatment.
mechanism: OsKEA1 maintains ion homeostasis (Na+/K+ balance), mitigates ROS accumulation, stabilizes photosynthetic proteins, and prevents DNA damage under salt stress. Loss of OsKEA1 disrupts these processes, exacerbating salt stress effects.

genes: ScWS (ScWS, wax ester synthase)
phenotype: Overexpression of ScWS increases triacylglycerol accumulation in wood and lipid droplet count in ray parenchyma cells, enhances wood water repellency, and increases wood density in poplars.
mechanism: NA

genes: MdGH3 (auxin conjugating enzyme, Malus domestica), MdGH3 paralogues (auxin conjugating enzyme, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Knockdown of MdGH3 genes in apple rootstock M9-T337 improves saline-alkali stress tolerance by reducing Na+/K+ ratio in leaves and roots, enhancing photosynthetic capacity, and increasing antioxidant capacity. Under stress, MdGH3 RNAi plants show 15-17% growth inhibition vs 30% in wild type, 10-12% root length reduction vs 32%, and 25-26% root vitality reduction vs 67%.
mechanism: Reduced Na+/K+ ratio in leaves and roots, enhanced photosynthetic capacity through chlorophyll maintenance, and increased antioxidant enzyme activity (CAT and POD) to scavenge ROS

genes: TkGGR1 (geranylgeranyl reductase 1, Taraxacum koksaghyz, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of TkGGR1 in latex leads to increased geranylgeraniol (GGOH) and phytol levels in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves when co-expressed with TkGGPS6 and TkHMGR1c.
mechanism: TkGGR1 promotes TkGGPS6 activity by metabolite channeling, enhancing GGPP conversion to GGOH and phytol in the cytoplasmic MVA pathway.

genes: TkGGR1 (geranylgeranyl reductase 1, Taraxacum koksaghyz, synthetic)
phenotype: TkGGR1 RNAi in latex results in reduced β-tocopherol, lup(19,21)-en-3-ol, α-amyrin, β-amyrin, and campesterol levels in T. koksaghyz roots.
mechanism: Knockdown of TkGGR1 disrupts geranylgeranyl reduction, affecting tocopherol and triterpenoid biosynthesis in latex.

genes: TbGGR2 (geranylgeranyl reductase 2, Taraxacum brevicorniculatum, synthetic)
phenotype: TbGGR2 RNAi in T. brevicorniculatum results in a pale green leaf phenotype, reduced biomass, and accumulation of chlorophyll geranylgeranyl esters (chlGG).
mechanism: TbGGR2 knockdown impairs GGPP reduction during chlorophyll synthesis, leading to chlGG accumulation and reduced photosynthetic efficiency.

genes: TkGGR1 (geranylgeranyl reductase 1, Taraxacum koksaghyz, synthetic), mVenus (fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: TkGGR1-mVenus fusion protein localizes to plastid-like particles in the latex pellet phase of T. koksaghyz roots.
mechanism: TkGGR1-mVenus is imported into plastid-like structures in latex, suggesting a role in lipid metabolism or isoprenoid biosynthesis.

genes: GLDP1 (glycine decarboxylase P-protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of GLDP1 in bundle sheath strands of Arabidopsis thaliana leaves
mechanism: MYC and MYB binding motifs in the GLDP1 promoter drive bundle sheath strand expression

genes: GLDP1 (glycine decarboxylase P-protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of GLDP1 in bundle sheath strands of Arabidopsis thaliana leaves
mechanism: MYC and MYB binding motifs in the GLDP1 promoter drive bundle sheath strand expression

genes: GLDP1 (glycine decarboxylase P-protein, Moricandia moricandioides)
phenotype: Expression of GLDP1 in bundle sheath strands of Arabidopsis thaliana leaves
mechanism: MYC and MYB binding motifs in the GLDP1 promoter drive bundle sheath strand expression

genes: GLDP1 (glycine decarboxylase P-protein, Moricandia arvensis)
phenotype: Expression of GLDP1 in bundle sheath strands of Arabidopsis thaliana leaves
mechanism: MYC and MYB binding motifs in the GLDP1 promoter drive bundle sheath strand expression

genes: ApMEKK18 (ApMEKK18, MAPKKK involved in abiotic stress response, Arabidopsis pumila)
phenotype: Overexpression of ApMEKK18 in rice increases single-plant yield by ~20% (1,000-grain weight +20%, tiller number +30%), enhances salt stress tolerance (germination rate +15% at 150mM NaCl), and reduces ABA sensitivity (germination rate +25% at 4μM ABA) in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: ApMEKK18 modulates ABA signaling by downregulating OsNCED1/4 (ABA synthesis) and upregulating OsNCED2/OsABA8ox1 (ABA metabolism), while enhancing salt tolerance through nuclear-localized MAPK cascade regulation.

genes: AtcTP-Δ80MpSKL1 (Arabidopsis SKL1 chloroplast transit peptide fused to Marchantia polymorpha SKL1 Δ80, synthetic), AtcTP-Δ113MpSK (Arabidopsis SKL1 chloroplast transit peptide fused to Marchantia polymorpha SK Δ113, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtcTP-Δ80MpSKL1 rescues chloroplast biogenesis in Arabidopsis skl1−8 mutants, restoring chlorophyll a and b to ~55% and 70% of wild-type levels, respectively, with increased thylakoid membrane stacking. Overexpression of AtcTP-Δ113MpSK does not rescue the phenotype.
mechanism: AtcTP-Δ80MpSKL1 complements the loss of AtSKL1 by restoring chloroplast biogenesis, likely through chloroplast-localized activity. The modified substrate binding pocket in MpSKL1 allows functional complementation despite structural divergence from ancestral SK.

genes: HvLOXB (lipoxygenase B, HORVU.MOREX.r3.4HG0335800, barley), HvLOXC1 (lipoxygenase C1, HORVU.MOREX.r3.5HG0509200, barley)
phenotype: Knockout of HvLOXB and HvLOXC1 reduces total LOX activity by 36–42% and 94%, respectively, increases total protein content, and decreases 1000-grain weight by 5–13% in barley.
mechanism: HvLOXB and HvLOXC1 mutations reduce LOX activity, leading to lower lipid peroxidation (MDA content) and improved grain storability (higher germination rates after artificial aging).

genes: HvLOXA (lipoxygenase A, HORVU.MOREX.r3.4HG0335790, barley), HvLOXC1 (lipoxygenase C1, HORVU.MOREX.r3.5HG0509200, barley)
phenotype: Double knockout of HvLOXA and HvLOXC1 reduces total LOX activity by 94%, increases total fatty acid content by 10–20.73%, and improves grain germination rates by 9–23% after artificial aging in barley.
mechanism: HvLOXA and HvLOXC1 mutations synergistically reduce LOX activity, delay lipid peroxidation (MDA content), and enhance seedling growth after artificial aging, suggesting a key role in grain storability and fatty acid regulation.

genes: OsDREB1A (OsDREB1A, transcription activator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsDREB1A increases postgermination growth and grains per panicle in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsDREB1A regulates postgermination growth through the OsNAC3-mediated GA pathway, enhancing GA biosynthesis.

genes: OsNAC3 (OsNAC3, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNAC3 improves agronomic traits including plant height, panicle length, grains per panicle, grain length, grain width, and 1000-grain weight in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsNAC3 regulates postgermination growth through the GA pathway by inducing OsGA20ox1 expression, enhancing GA biosynthesis.

genes: HKT1 (HKT1, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtTIP2;2 (AtTIP2;2, Arabidopsis thaliana), TMAC2 (TMAC2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HKT1, AtTIP2;2, and TMAC2 in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to altered root architecture under salt stress, including reduced lateral root development and changes in ABA accumulation.
mechanism: HKT1-mediated Na+ transport influences root architecture through transcriptional networks involving ABA signaling. AtTIP2;2 and TMAC2 regulate ABA accumulation and lateral root development, with genotype-dependent effects.

genes: AtTIP2;2 (AtTIP2;2, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtTMAC2 (AtTMAC2, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtPIP1;4 (AtPIP1;4, Arabidopsis thaliana), VAMP711a (VAMP711a, Arabidopsis thaliana), Serrate (Serrate, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of AtTIP2;2, AtTMAC2, and other markers in Nicotiana benthamiana epidermal cells for subcellular localization studies.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtTIP2;2 (AtTIP2;2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtTIP2;2 in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to reduced lateral root development under salt stress, with enhanced Na+ compartmentalization in roots and K+ retention in shoots.
mechanism: AtTIP2;2 localizes to tonoplast and plasma membranes, facilitating Na+ transport and vacuolar compartmentalization, which influences root architecture and ion homeostasis under salt stress.

genes: AtTIP2;1 (AtTIP2;1, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtTIP2;2 (AtTIP2;2, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtTIP2;3 (AtTIP2;3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of AtTIP2;1, AtTIP2;2, and AtTIP2;3 in yeast enhances sensitivity to NaCl, boric acid, H2O2, and urea, indicating their role in solute transport.
mechanism: AtTIP2 isoforms facilitate transport of Na+, water, urea, H2O2, and boric acid in yeast, with AtTIP2;2 and AtTIP2;1 showing similar transport profiles.

genes: BcSWEET1-2 (BcSWEET1-2, hexose transporter, Brassica campestris)
phenotype: Overexpression of BcSWEET1-2 promotes stem carbohydrate accumulation, upregulates flowering gene expression, enhances Arabidopsis stem elongation, and advances flowering time
mechanism: BcSWEET1-2 functions as a hexose transporter

genes: ZmHY5L (ZmHY5L, bZIP transcription factor, Zea mays)
phenotype: Complementary lines of mimic-phosphorylatable ZmHY5L-S25D rescued heat-sensitive phenotypes of Arabidopsis hy5 knockdown mutants.
mechanism: ZmHY5L activation by phosphorylation plays a key role in ABA-regulated thermotolerance.

genes: ZmHY5L (ZmHY5L, bZIP transcription factor, Zea mays)
phenotype: Complementary lines of mimic-nonphosphorylatable ZmHY5L-S25A failed to rescue heat-sensitive phenotypes of Arabidopsis hy5 knockdown mutants.
mechanism: ZmHY5L activation by phosphorylation plays a key role in ABA-regulated thermotolerance.

genes: ZmCHS25 (CHS gene family member, involved in secondary metabolism, Zea mays)
phenotype: Loss of ZmCHS25 function leads to dramatic decrease in flavonoid synthesis, disrupted phenylpropanoid metabolic pathway, and impaired osmotic regulation under salt stress
mechanism: ZmCHS25 knockout disrupts phenylpropanoid metabolic pathway and impairs osmotic regulation ability of plant cells

genes: ZmERS4 (ethylene receptor, Zea mays, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmERS4 increases flag leaf length by ~25% (37.98 cm in L5 vs 30.35 cm in wild-type) and enhances resistance to bacterial leaf streak (lesion length 0.45 cm in L5 vs 0.87 cm in wild-type) in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: ZmERS4 induces salicylic acid (SA) accumulation (16.62 µg/g FW in L5 vs 13.24 µg/g FW in wild-type) and activates SA-dependent signaling pathway (OsNAC4 expression 3.69× higher in L5 vs wild-type), while suppressing jasmonic acid (JA) pathway.

genes: RhUBC32 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Rosa sp., synthetic), RhRED (RING E3 ligase, Rosa sp., synthetic)
phenotype: RhUBC32-RNAi lines displayed decreased plant height, premature leaf abscission, and enhanced petal abscission under ethylene treatment.
mechanism: RhUBC32-RhRED module mediates ethylene-induced degradation of ethylene receptors, and silencing either gene leads to ethylene-hypersensitive phenotypes.

genes: RhRED (RING E3 ligase, Rosa sp., synthetic), RhUBC32 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Rosa sp., synthetic)
phenotype: RhRED-RNAi lines exhibited decreased plant height, premature leaf abscission, and enhanced petal abscission under ethylene treatment.
mechanism: RhUBC32-RhRED module mediates ethylene-induced degradation of ethylene receptors, and silencing either gene leads to ethylene-hypersensitive phenotypes.

genes: SlUBC32 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Solanum lycopersicum, synthetic)
phenotype: slubc32 lines displayed smaller size with extra branches and accelerated fruit ripening under ethylene treatment.
mechanism: SlUBC32-SlRED module mediates ethylene-induced degradation of ethylene receptors, and knockout leads to ethylene-hypersensitive phenotypes.

genes: SlRED (RING E3 ligase, Solanum lycopersicum, synthetic)
phenotype: slred lines exhibited smaller size with extra branches and accelerated fruit ripening under ethylene treatment.
mechanism: SlUBC32-SlRED module mediates ethylene-induced degradation of ethylene receptors, and knockout leads to ethylene-hypersensitive phenotypes.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS reporter activity in inflorescence tips indicates SMR1 promoter activity
mechanism: GUS reporter allows visualization of SMR1 promoter activity in plant tissues

genes: VRN1 (AT3G18990, VRN1 chromatin regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: VRN1-FLAG rescues the WT FRI flowering phenotype in vrn1-4 FRI mutants
mechanism: VRN1 associates with FLC 5' region and regulates chromatin dynamics by limiting H2A.Z incorporation

genes: WG1 (Oryza sativa, glutaredoxin, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of WG1 produces wider but shorter grains than ZH11 (Fig. 5C,E,F).
mechanism: WG1 interacts with GS3 and reduces the oligomerization level of GS3, thereby promoting the function of GS3.

genes: GS3 (Oryza sativa, G-protein γ-subunit, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: pro35S:GFP-GS3;pro35S:MYC-WG1 plants, respectively. Total proteins were extracted from young panicles of these plants and incubated with GFP-Trap® Agarose beads for immunoprecipitation of GFP or GFP-GS3 complex, respectively. As shown in Fig. 1E, MYC-WG1 was detected in the immunoprecipitated GFP-GS3 complex in panicles, but was absent in the negative control (GFP) (Fig. 1E), indicating that GS3 physically associates with WG1 in rice plants.
mechanism: GS3 can form intermolecular disulfide bonds through its Cys residues, which are regulated by WG1.

genes: WG1 (Oryza sativa, glutaredoxin, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: proActin:WG1#1 transgenic line produced wider but shorter grains than ZH11 (Fig. 5C,E,F).
mechanism: WG1 interacts with GS3 and reduces the oligomerization level of GS3, thereby promoting the function of GS3.

genes: GS3 (Oryza sativa, G-protein γ-subunit, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: The gs3-c1 grains were significantly longer than those of ZH11 (Fig. 5C,E), consistent with previous studies.
mechanism: Loss-of-function allele of GS3 increases grain length by reducing its interaction with RGB1.

genes: GS3 (Oryza sativa, G-protein γ-subunit, Oryza sativa), WG1 (Oryza sativa, glutaredoxin, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: The grain length of proActin:WG1#1;gs3-c1 was similar to that of gs3-c1 grains (Fig. 5C,E).
mechanism: WG1 and GS3 function in a common pathway to regulate grain length.

genes: JrbZIP40 (JrbZIP40, bZIP gene involved in stress resistance, Juglans regia)
phenotype: Overexpression of JrbZIP40 in transgenic Arabidopsis seedlings significantly enhanced resistance to salt and drought stress
mechanism: JrbZIP40 may bind to the JrHB7 and JrATG8G promoters and activate their expression, contributing to stress resistance

genes: NaLRR-RK4 (receptor-like kinase gene, Nicotiana attenuata, XM_01937432.3)
phenotype: Silencing of NaLRR-RK4 increases susceptibility to Alternaria alternata infection, with 54.48% larger necrotic lesions in RNAi plants compared to wild-type at 3 days post-inoculation.
mechanism: NaLRR-RK4 mediates disease resistance through activation of MAPK signaling pathway, regulation of WRKY33, PR1, ethylene-responsive transcription factors, and ROS homeostasis. Silencing compromises defense-related pathways including glutathione metabolism, phenylalanine metabolism, and plant hormone signal transduction.

genes: AtLPEAT1 (AtLPEAT1, lysophosphatidylethanolamine acyltransferase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtLPEAT2 (AtLPEAT2, lysophosphatidylethanolamine acyltransferase 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtLPEAT1 increases rosette biomass compared to wild-type plants in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtLPEAT1 (AtLPEAT1, lysophosphatidylethanolamine acyltransferase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtLPEAT2 (AtLPEAT2, lysophosphatidylethanolamine acyltransferase 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtLPEAT2 increases rosette biomass compared to wild-type plants in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: CrSPL (transcription factor, Catharanthus roseus)
phenotype: Overexpression of CrSPL directly regulates the vinblastine biosynthesis pathway in Catharanthus roseus
mechanism: CrSPLs directly regulate the vinblastine biosynthesis pathway

genes: BnaPEL1 (BnaPEL1, negatively regulates chlorophyll content, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnaPEL1 results in yellowing leaves and reduced chlorophyll content in Brassica napus.
mechanism: BnaPEL1 negatively regulates chlorophyll content.

genes: BnaPEL1 (BnaPEL1, negatively regulates chlorophyll content, Brassica napus)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of BnaPEL1 increases chlorophyll content, enhances photosynthesis, and improves yield in rapeseed.
mechanism: BnaPEL1 negatively regulates chlorophyll content.

genes: PAP1 (PAP1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PAP1 induces distinct spatiotemporal regulation of phenylpropanoid pathway genes and widespread upregulation of glycosylation processes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PAP1 overexpression leads to significant changes in phytohormone levels, particularly jasmonate and salicylate, indicating complex crosstalk between flavonoid biosynthesis and hormone homeostasis.

genes: SsJMJ11 (SsJMJ11, H3K4me3 demethylase, Saccharum spontaneum)
phenotype: Ectopic overexpression of SsJMJ11 in Arabidopsis thaliana resulted in a hypersensitivity to soil drought stress as well as abscisic acid (ABA) and mannitol.
mechanism: SsJMJ11-mediated dynamic deposition of H3K4me3 is required for proper adaptation to drought stress in sugarcane.

genes: SsJMJ11 (SsJMJ11, H3K4me3 demethylase, Saccharum spontaneum)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of SsJMJ11 in S. spontaneum protoplasts reduced the ABA-induced transcription of SsRD20 and SsDREB2A, paralleling reduced H3K4me3 levels at these loci.
mechanism: SsJMJ11-mediated dynamic deposition of H3K4me3 is required for proper adaptation to drought stress in sugarcane.

genes: FaGH3.17 (FaGH3.17, auxin-responsive gene, Rosaceae species), FaGH3.18 (FaGH3.18, auxin-responsive gene, Rosaceae species)
phenotype: Overexpression of FaGH3.17 and FaGH3.18 decreases malondialdehyde (MDA) content and relative conductivity while increasing superoxide dismutase (SOD), peroxidase (POD), and catalase (CAT) activities under drought stress in transgenic Arabidopsis.
mechanism: NA

genes: EjXND1 (EjXND1, NAC domain transcription factor repressing lignification, loquat)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of EjXND1 in tobacco leaves and loquat fruit reduces lignin content by ~16% compared to controls.
mechanism: EjXND1 represses lignin biosynthesis by interacting with EjHB1 to inhibit EjPRX12 expression, which is involved in lignin polymerization.

genes: EjXND1 (EjXND1, NAC domain transcription factor repressing lignification, loquat)
phenotype: Stable overexpression of EjXND1 in liverwort reduces lignin content compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: EjXND1 represses lignin biosynthesis by interacting with EjHB1 to inhibit EjPRX12 expression, which is involved in lignin polymerization.

genes: EjXND1 (EjXND1, NAC domain transcription factor repressing lignification, loquat)
phenotype: EjXND1-GFP fusion protein localizes to the apoplast and nucleus in tobacco leaves.
mechanism: NA

mechanism: FLAG-eGFP-ATG8e fusion protein labels autophagosomes, allowing confocal microscopy analysis of autophagy dynamics.

mechanism: MACP2-YFP colocalizes with mCherry-ATG8f-labeled autophagosomes, indicating its role in autophagy regulation.

genes: MACP2 (MACPF domain-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: MACP2-FLAG is degraded via autophagy during prolonged nutrient starvation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Autophagy pathway mediates MACP2-FLAG degradation, maintaining cellular ROS balance under starvation.

mechanism: GbCYP90J6 catalyzes intermolecular C–C dimerization of apigenin via a diradical coupling mechanism, with steric constraints and π–π stacking interactions positioning substrates for C3'-C8" linkage formation.

mechanism: Redirection of carbon flux from starch to lipid pathways by knocking out AGP

mechanism: CmOFP6-19b suppresses cell division and expansion-related genes (CDKF, CycB1;1, CycB1;2, EXPA, XTH), reducing cell number and increasing cell area.

genes: CmOFP6-19b (CmOFP6-19b, negative regulator of fruit size, Cucumis melo)
phenotype: Knockdown of CmOFP6-19b increases melon fruit size by ~6.11% in longitudinal diameter and ~14.9% in fruit weight.
mechanism: CmOFP6-19b knockdown upregulates cell cycle and cell expansion genes (CmCycB1;1, CmCycB1;2, CmEXPA7, CmXTH1), increasing cell area and reducing cell number.

genes: CmKNOX16 (CmKNOX16, negative regulator of fruit size, Cucumis melo)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmKNOX16 reduces melon fruit size by ~10% in longitudinal diameter and ~30% in fruit weight.
mechanism: CmKNOX16 suppresses cell division and expansion-related genes (CDKF, CycB1;1, CycB1;2, EXPA, XTH), increasing cell number and decreasing cell area.

genes: OsWNK9 (OsWNK9, salt stress tolerance gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsWNK9 increases salinity stress tolerance in rice by upregulating stress-responsive genes and phytohormonal pathways.
mechanism: OsWNK9 activates transcription factors (NAC, MYB, AP2/ERF, WRKY) and phytohormonal pathways (auxin, cytokinin, ABA, ethylene), enhances ionic transporters (Na+/H+ antiporters, K+ transporters), and induces cell wall modifications and secondary metabolite pathways to maintain ionic homeostasis and stress adaptation.

genes: BnaA10/C09.TFL1DTI (BnaA10/C09.TFL1, Brassica napus), BnaA10/C09.TFL1IDTI (BnaA10/C09.TFL1, Brassica napus)

genes: CrWRKY57 (CrWRKY57, transcription factor, Citrus reticulata cv. Sanhu)

mechanism: CrWRKY57 is a nuclear protein that localizes to the nucleus, as shown by GFP and DAPI co-localization.

mechanism: CrWRKY57 positively regulates ABA signaling and root development, leading to increased drought tolerance by reducing oxidative damage and maintaining cell membrane integrity.

genes: CrWRKY57 (CrWRKY57, transcription factor, Citrus reticulata cv. Sanhu)
phenotype: RNAi lines (RNAi-2 and RNAi-19) exhibit increased susceptibility to dehydration, with more severe wilting, higher RWL, MDA, and EL compared to controls after 80 minutes of dehydration.
mechanism: CrWRKY57 is necessary for drought tolerance, as its knockdown disrupts ABA signaling and root development, leading to increased oxidative damage and cell membrane leakage.

genes: CrWRKY57 (CrWRKY57, transcription factor, Citrus reticulata cv. Sanhu)
phenotype: Overexpression of CrWRKY57 in tobacco lines (OE4, OE10, OE17) enhances drought tolerance, with reduced wilting, lower RWL, MDA, and EL, and reduced ROS accumulation compared to controls after 14 days of drought treatment.
mechanism: CrWRKY57 promotes drought tolerance by reducing ROS accumulation and maintaining cell membrane integrity, likely through ABA signaling and root development regulation.

genes: FmbHLH1 (drought-responsive transcription factor, Fagus mandshurica)
phenotype: Knockout of FmbHLH1 reduces drought tolerance in Fagus mandshurica, with increased electrolyte permeability, MDA content, and reduced SOD/POD activities under drought stress
mechanism: FmbHLH1 positively regulates drought stress tolerance by enhancing ROS scavenging ability through SOD and POD activities, reducing cell death and membrane lipid peroxidation

genes: Rvi6 (Rvi6, resistance gene)

mechanism: Rvi6 enhances ROS scavenging capacity, osmolyte accumulation, and plasma membrane integrity while suppressing apple growth through reduced auxin accumulation and attenuated auxin signaling, contributing to the 'growth-defense trade-off' hypothesis.

mechanism: The proFT2E-box cis-element is a negative regulator of FT2 transcription, and PIF4 binds to this region to suppress FT2 expression

genes: REL1 (REL1, regulates heat tolerance via flavonoid biosynthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: rel1-D mutants survive ~50% under high-temperature stress compared to ZH11
mechanism: REL1 regulates flavonoid biosynthesis genes (OsCHI, OsF3H, etc.) leading to elevated flavonoid levels which enhance heat tolerance

mechanism: NARY acts as a negative growth regulator

phenotype: Incomplete rescue of the NRCX-silenced dwarf phenotype
mechanism: Additional regulators beyond NRC2, NRC3, and NARY influence growth outcomes

genes: β-glucuronidase (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Overexpression of β-glucuronidase under the Small Rubber Particle Protein 1 promoter leads to significant transgene expression in leaf, stem, and root tissues, especially in the stem.
mechanism: The promoter drives transgene expression in multiple tissues, with highest activity in stem tissue.

genes: TaCEP15 (Cysteine Endopeptidase 15, wheat), TaCEPRL (Cysteine Endopeptidase Receptor-Like, wheat), TaSnRK1α (SNF1-Related Protein Kinase 1α, wheat), TabZIP9 (bZIP Transcription Factor 9, wheat)
gene_construct: Ubiquitin-promoter-TaCEP15-NosT, CRISPR-Cas9-mediated knockout of TaCEP15, Ubiquitin-promoter-TaSnRK1α-NosT, Ubiquitin-promoter-TabZIP9-NosT, CRISPR-Cas9-mediated knockout of TabZIP9
phenotype: TaCEP15 overexpression reduces primary root length by ~16.2-20.4% and decreases drought tolerance (23.6-21.5% survival rate). TaCEP15 knockout increases primary root length by ~18.0-12.0% and enhances drought tolerance (77.1-75.7% survival rate). TaSnRK1α overexpression increases primary root length by ~12.7-18.5% and enhances drought tolerance (93.3-94.4% survival rate). TabZIP9 overexpression increases primary root length by ~16.1-19.5% and enhances drought tolerance (88.9-83.3% survival rate). TabZIP9 knockout reduces primary root length by ~16.1-19.5% and decreases drought tolerance (34.0-33.3% survival rate).
mechanism: TaCEP15 interacts with TaCEPRL to phosphorylate and degrade TaSnRK1α, inhibiting root growth and reducing drought tolerance. TabZIP9 represses TaCEP15 transcription, reducing its expression and allowing TaSnRK1α accumulation, which promotes root growth and enhances drought tolerance.

genes: TaCEPRL (Cysteine Endopeptidase Receptor-Like, wheat)
phenotype: TaCEPRL knockout mutants (Taceprl-6 and Taceprl-7) exhibited 23.0 and 19.6% increases in primary root length, respectively, compared to the WT [average of 18.2 and 17.7 cm versus 14.8 cm for WT (Fielder); Fig. 2C]. These mutants also showed increased seedling survival rates under water-deficient conditions (88.9% and 91.1% versus 41.1% for WT) and enhanced drought tolerance with increased fresh and dry weights.
mechanism: TaCEPRL interacts with TaCEP15 to phosphorylate and degrade TaSnRK1α, inhibiting root growth. Knockout of TaCEPRL disrupts this pathway, leading to TaSnRK1α accumulation and enhanced root growth and drought tolerance.

genes: TaSnRK1α (SNF1-Related Protein Kinase 1α, wheat)
phenotype: TaSnRK1α overexpression lines (TaSnRK1αOE-2 and TaSnRK1αOE-4) showed 12.7 and 18.5% increases in primary root length at the seedling stage, respectively, compared to the control [average of 17.7 cm (TaSnRK1αOE-2) and 18.6 cm (TaSnRK1αOE-4) versus 15.7 cm for WT (Fielder); Fig. 5, A and B]. These lines also showed increased seedling survival rates under drought stress (93.3% and 94.4% versus 6.7% for WT) and maintained longer primary roots under drought stress conditions.
mechanism: TaSnRK1α is phosphorylated and degraded by TaCEPRL in response to TaCEP15, inhibiting root growth. Overexpression of TaSnRK1α prevents this degradation, leading to increased root growth and enhanced drought tolerance.

genes: TabZIP9 (bZIP Transcription Factor 9, wheat)
phenotype: TabZIP9 overexpression lines (TabZIP9OE-3 and TabZIP9OE-5) showed ~16.1 and 19.5% increases in primary root length, respectively, compared to the WT [average of 20.2 cm (TabZIP9OE-3) and 20.8 cm (TabZIP9OE-5) versus 17.4 cm for WT (Fielder); Fig. 6C and fig. S12C]. These lines also showed increased seedling survival rates under water-deficient conditions (88.9% and 83.3% versus 51.4% for WT). TabZIP9 knockout mutants (Tabzip9-6 and Tabzip9-8) showed reduced primary root length (~16.1-19.5% decrease) and decreased drought tolerance (34.0% and 33.3% survival rate versus 51.4% for WT).
mechanism: TabZIP9 binds to the promoter of TaCEP15 and represses its transcription. Overexpression of TabZIP9 reduces TaCEP15 expression, leading to decreased TaCEPRL activity and increased TaSnRK1α accumulation, promoting root growth and drought tolerance. Knockout of TabZIP9 increases TaCEP15 expression, enhancing TaCEPRL activity and reducing TaSnRK1α, which inhibits root growth and reduces drought tolerance.

genes: LfVP1 (vacuolar H+-pyrophosphatase, Leptochloa fusca, cDNA)
phenotype: Overexpression of LfVP1 in Nicotiana tabacum enhances drought and salinity tolerance, with 90% relative water content (vs 53% in WT), 83% RWC in transgenic lines, higher net photosynthetic rate (Pn), stomatal conductance (gs), and membrane stability index (MSI) compared to wild-type plants under osmotic stress.
mechanism: LfVP1 encodes a vacuolar H+-pyrophosphatase that generates a proton gradient for cation detoxification and osmotic adjustment. Overexpression enhances Na+ sequestration, improves water use efficiency, and maintains turgor under stress conditions.

genes: OsBBH (benzoylbenzoate hydroxylase, Oryza sativa), mVenus (fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsBBH increases benzylsalicylate and SA levels in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: OsBBH catalyzes the hydroxylation of benzylbenzoate to benzylsalicylate, which is further converted to SA.

genes: SlBEBT (benzoyltransferase, Solanum lycopersicum), SlBBH (benzoylbenzoate hydroxylase, Solanum lycopersicum), SlBSE (benzylsalicylate esterase, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of SlBEBT, SlBBH, and SlBSE reduces SA levels in tomato plants.
mechanism: Knockdown of the BEBT–BBH–BSE module disrupts SA biosynthesis, leading to decreased SA accumulation.

mechanism: NA

genes: AtPDAT1 (AtPDAT1, enzyme involved in lipid metabolism, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: AtPDAT1's role in lipid metabolism affects cellular processes, leading to altered stress responses.

genes: AtPDAT1 (AtPDAT1, enzyme involved in lipid metabolism, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knock-out lines show opposite results to overexpressors, with downregulated proteins in photoprotection, autophagy, and abiotic stress responses, and upregulated biotic stress proteins.
mechanism: AtPDAT1's absence disrupts lipid metabolism, leading to altered stress responses.

genes: OfGATA9 (Osmanthus fragrans, transcription factor, sweet osmanthus)
phenotype: Ectopic over-expression of OfGATA9 in Nicotiana tabacum resulted in an increase in both flower size and epidermis cell dimensions.
mechanism: Promotes cell expansion and differential expression of genes including EXLB1, XTHs, bHLHs, EFRs, Auxin/IAAs, SAURs, MYB-like, and MADS-box genes in flowers.

genes: ATAF2 (At5g08790, transcription factor involved in BR/IAA regulation and senescence, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ATAF2 increases biomass by ~70% and chlorophyll-a accumulation by ~23% in 12-day-old Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings
mechanism: ATAF2 suppresses BR-inactivating genes BAS1/SOB7 and promotes IAA biosynthesis gene NIT2, while repressing NYC1 which reduces chlorophyll-a degradation

genes: OvPHT1;1 (OvPHT1;1, plasma membrane-localized phosphate transporter, O. violaceus)
phenotype: Enhances P uptake under low-P conditions in rice
mechanism: NA

mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in GhCAD1-A and GhCAD1-C genes disrupt gossypol biosynthesis by altering CAD activity.

genes: GhMYC2-D09 (GhMYC2-D09, MYC2 gene, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhMYC2-D09 in hairy roots increased gossypol content by 2.3-fold compared to control (Fig. 6D).
mechanism: GhMYC2-D09 activates GhCAD transcription, promoting gossypol biosynthesis.

genes: TaCR4 (CRINKLY4 receptor-like kinase homolog in wheat, wheat)

mechanism: TaCR4 regulates wheat grain size by controlling grain epidermal cell size.

genes: BnaC6.ARGOS (BnaC6.ARGOS, drought tolerance modulator, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnaC6.ARGOS significantly enhances seed drought tolerance by reducing seed coat porosity and thickening cell walls, resulting in a threefold increase in germination rates under drought stress compared to wild-type (p < 0.05).
mechanism: BnaC6.ARGOS modulates seed coat structural development to enhance drought resistance through reduced seed coat porosity and cell wall thickening.

genes: LrUFGT (Lycium ruthenicum, UDP-glucosyltransferase, Lycium ruthenicum), GFP (synthetic, green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Subcellular localization of LrUFGT-GFP fusion protein in chloroplasts of tobacco mesophyll protoplasts
mechanism: LrUFGT-GFP fusion protein localizes to chloroplasts, as confirmed by confocal microscopy

genes: OsFLN2 (FRUCTOKINASE-LIKE 2, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Osfln2 knockout rice plants exhibit an albino phenotype at early stages and transcriptional repression of plastid genes even under irrigated conditions
mechanism: OsFLN2 regulates chloroplast development by interacting with the PEP complex, contributing to the transcription of PEP-dependent plastid genes

mechanism: ECA1 pumps excess cytosolic Ca2+ into the ER, preventing ABA overaccumulation and hypersensitivity to osmotic stress.

genes: ECA1 (AT1G07810, ER membrane Ca2+-ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: eca1-2 mutant exhibits shorter root growth under osmotic stress compared to wild-type, with elevated cytosolic Ca2+ and ABA levels.
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9-induced mutation in ECA1 disrupts its Ca2+ pump activity, leading to sustained Ca2+ elevation and ABA overaccumulation.

mechanism: mCherry tagging allows visualization of OsPHR2 localization and oxidation status in planta

mechanism: Cys377 to Ser mutation disrupts key oxidation site in OsPHR2's coiled-coil domain

genes: HY5N (HY5N, altered CaM2-binding variant, tomato)
phenotype: Overexpression of HY5N increases RKN resistance and JA accumulation compared to hy5 mutants but less than HY5 overexpression.
mechanism: Impaired CaM2 interaction reduces HY5N's transcriptional activity, leading to lower JA biosynthesis and resistance compared to HY5.

phenotype: Transgenic plants resistant to herbicides

mechanism: HSTL negatively regulates GA homeostasis by downregulating GA biosynthesis genes (OsCPS2, OsKS1, OsGA20ox7) and upregulating GA metabolism genes (OsGA2ox1, OsGA2ox7, OsGA2ox8). HSTL mutations reduce water loss, ROS accumulation, and Na+ uptake while increasing proline content and antioxidant enzyme activities (CAT, POD, SOD)

genes: GmAP2 (Glyma_02G016100, AP2/ERF transcription factor, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmAP2 increases root length, lateral root length, and lateral root number under aluminum and low-phosphorus stress in Arabidopsis thaliana and soybean.
mechanism: GmAP2 enhances aluminum and low-phosphorus tolerance by upregulating stress-responsive genes, promoting lateral root development, and modulating abscisic acid pathways.

genes: GmAP2 (Glyma_02G016100, AP2/ERF transcription factor, Glycine max)
phenotype: GmAP2-GFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus in Nicotiana benthamiana epidermal cells.
mechanism: NA

mechanism: GNP2 and GNP5 regulate grain number per panicle (GNP) by phosphorylating and stabilizing Gnp4/LAX2, which modulates transcription factors involved in panicle development.

mechanism: GNP2 promoter variation S5779181 (G vs A) affects promoter activity and GNP2 expression, which regulates grain number per panicle (GNP) through phosphorylation of Gnp4/LAX2.

mechanism: Phosphorylation of Gnp4/LAX2 by GNP2 enhances its stability and transcriptional activity, modulating downstream genes involved in panicle development.

genes: aph7" (hygromycin resistance gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Overexpression of aph7" confers hygromycin resistance in Ulva prolifera.
mechanism: The aph7" gene encodes a hygromycin phosphotransferase that inactivates hygromycin B, providing resistance.

genes: UpAPT (adenine phosphoribosyltransferase gene, Ulva prolifera)
gene_construct: CRISPR/Cas9 system with HygR cassette (pUpRbcS-aph7"-CrRbcS2) targeting UpAPT
phenotype: CRISPR-mediated knock-in of HygR cassette at UpAPT locus confers resistance to hygromycin B and 2-fluoroadenine.
mechanism: The HygR cassette integrates into the UpAPT locus, disrupting its function while providing hygromycin resistance via aph7" expression.

genes: LjPUB7 (U-box E3 ubiquitin ligase, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: Ljpub7 mutants exhibit increased infection thread formation and nodule number at 7 dpi with rhizobia.
mechanism: LjPUB7 negatively regulates early symbiotic signaling by ubiquitinating and degrading NFR1/NFR5 receptors.

genes: LjPUB7 (U-box E3 ubiquitin ligase, Lotus japonicus), LjNFR1 (NFR1 receptor kinase, Lotus japonicus), LjNFR5 (NFR5 receptor kinase, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: BiFC assay confirms in vivo interaction between LjPUB7 and LjNFR1/LjNFR5 in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: LjPUB7 interacts with LjNFR1 and LjNFR5 in planta, forming a complex that mediates ubiquitination and degradation.

genes: SRAS1.1 (E3 ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic, source)
phenotype: GUS staining and activity analysis showed decreased expression under drought stress, indicating SRAS1.1 is negatively regulated by drought
mechanism: SRAS1.1 negatively regulates drought tolerance by suppressing its own expression under drought stress

mechanism: Constitutive pCSC formation enhances cysteine synthesis flux, leading to increased ABA production and stomatal closure, resulting in drought tolerance.

genes: CmVNI2 (CmVNI2, NAC domain-containing transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: CmVNI2 overexpression increased total flavonone and flavonol contents under controlled growth conditions and after low-temperature treatment.
mechanism: CmVNI2 directly activates CmF3H and CmMYB3, redirecting metabolic flux toward flavonol biosynthesis and modulating CmFLS expression.

genes: CmMYB3 (CmMYB3, R2R3 MYB transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)

mechanism: CmMYB3 directly binds to promoters of CmCHI and CmFLS, enhancing flavonol biosynthesis by upregulating structural genes.

mechanism: PES2 acylates 1,6-hexadecanediol with medium-chain fatty acids, producing wax diesters that accumulate in chloroplast plastoglobules.

genes: OsDUF846.2 (promoter region, upstream of start codon, Oryza sativa), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)

genes: OsDUF846.2 (full coding sequence, Oryza sativa), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Subcellular localization of OsDUF846.2-GFP fusion protein showed co-localization with ER-localized marker in tobacco epidermal cells.

genes: BoMYB60 (transcription factor involved in regulating anthocyanin synthesis, Brassica oleracea)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of BoMYB60 with BoTT8 leads to anthocyanin accumulation in tobacco leaves.

genes: DlGRAS24 (GRAS family transcription factor, longan)

mechanism: DlGRAS24 promotes flowering by interacting with CO and LFY

mechanism: MiPRX27 enhances stress tolerance by improving root development and ROS scavenging capacity.

genes: PtHSF5 (heat-inducible HSF, P. ternata)

mechanism: PtHSF5 overexpression increases enzymatic activities of peroxidase (POD), catalase (CAT), and superoxide dismutase (SOD) while reducing reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation under heat stress. Transcriptome profiling shows PtHSF5-mediated regulation of phenylpropanoid biosynthesis pathway genes, enhancing ROS scavenging capacity.

mechanism: Enhances antioxidant compound biosynthesis, activates plant hormone signaling pathways, and promotes sulfate uptake to rebalance nitrogen-sulfur homeostasis.

genes: SlMOT2 (SlMOT2, nitrate stress tolerance gene, tomato)

mechanism: The most abundant isoform of Rpi-amr1 (i3) directly recognizes pathogen effectors to confer resistance.

mechanism: GhDP1 proteins mediate hydroxylation of hemigossypol to generate hemigossypolone, requiring apoplastic factors and laccase activity for full catalytic activity.

genes: GhDP1_A1 (Gh_A01G2132, dirigent protein, Gossypium hirsutum)

genes: FveTRM5 (FveTRM5, TON1 RECRUITING MOTIF 5, Fragaria vesca)

genes: OsGGP (uORF, upstream open reading frame that inhibits GGP translation, rice)
phenotype: Mutation of OsGGP uORF increases ascorbic acid (AsA) content by 58.77%–108.65% in rice and enhances salt osmotic stress tolerance.
mechanism: OsGGP uORF mutations increase GGP translation efficiency, leading to higher AsA accumulation. AsA scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS), improving stress tolerance.

phenotype: Mutated OsGGP uORF increases luciferase (LUC)/renilla luciferase (REN) ratio by 1.48–1.83× in rice protoplasts, indicating enhanced translation efficiency of the downstream pORF.

genes: OsLEML2 (OsLEML2, LEM1-like protein 2, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: Antisense-expressing lines show marginally higher survival rates (53.57–45.54%) compared to wild-type (39.29%) after 45°C heat stress.
mechanism: OsLEML2 suppression partially derepresses the HSF-HSP pathway, improving thermotolerance.

genes: OsLEML2 (OsLEML2, LEM1-like protein 2, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: GUS staining is enriched in anther tissues and responsive to abiotic stress, confirming anther-specific expression.
mechanism: OsLEML2 promoter drives GUS expression in anther tissues under stress conditions.

genes: OsLEML2 (OsLEML2, LEM1-like protein 2, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: OsLEML2-GFP localizes to vesicular structures in root and leaf cells, with dynamic redistribution under thermal stress.
mechanism: OsLEML2 undergoes liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) in vivo, modulating vesicle trafficking and auxin homeostasis.

genes: OsSub14 (subtilisin, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Increased sensitivity to ABA and elevated ROS accumulation under external stimuli in rice mutant plants
mechanism: Regulates ABA signaling and ROS content

genes: MsLEA_3-6 (drought-responsive LEA protein, Medicago sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of MsLEA_3–6 enhances drought tolerance in Arabidopsis (improved root growth and germination under mannitol) and Medicago sativa (reduced H2O2 and malondialdehyde accumulation, elevated proline/soluble sugars, and attenuated oxidative stress via ROS scavenging).
mechanism: MsLEA_3–6 enhances osmotic adjustment and oxidative stress mitigation through coordinated regulation of ABA signaling and MsWRKY71-mediated transcriptional activation.

genes: Phchi (CHI, chalcone isomerase, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated silencing of CHI gene results in altered pigment distributions and novel floral morphologies including tetramerous corollas and twisted tubular petal margins in Petunia hybrida
mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of CHI gene exerts a broader repressive effect on subsequent flavonoid biosynthesis pathway components

genes: SmCLE25 (CLE25, CLE peptide involved in stress responses and senescence regulation, Salvia miltiorrhiza)
phenotype: Overexpression of SmCLE25 in Arabidopsis thaliana delays leaf senescence, enhances drought and salt stress tolerance, reduces reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and suppresses ABA- and MeJA-induced senescence.
mechanism: SmCLE25 modulates ROS metabolism by suppressing AtrbohC and AtrbohE expression, inhibiting NTL4-mediated activation of Rboh promoters, and upregulating VN12 to maintain redox equilibrium. It also downregulates senescence-associated genes like SAG12.

genes: ZmHSF10 (heat shock factor 10, maize, ZmHSF10)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmHSF10 increases heat tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with 67.13% and 65.24% survival rates compared to 42.05% in wild type after high-temperature treatment.
mechanism: ZmHSF10 enhances heat tolerance by improving membrane stability (lower relative conductivity) and maintaining chlorophyll content under high-temperature stress.

genes: ZmHSF10 (heat shock factor 10, maize, ZmHSF10)
phenotype: Silencing of ZmHSF10 in maize reduces heat tolerance, with L-1 and L-2 lines showing significantly lower chlorophyll content and higher ion permeability compared to wild type after high-temperature treatment.
mechanism: Reduced ZmHSF10 expression leads to decreased chlorophyll content and increased cell membrane permeability under high-temperature stress, indicating impaired heat tolerance.

genes: NPR1 (NPR1, transcriptional coregulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of NPR1-GFP rescues SA-driven hypocotyl phenotype in npr1 mutants, sustaining hypocotyl elongation in darkness.
mechanism: NPR1 antagonizes SA-driven inhibition of hypocotyl elongation by maintaining auxin-related gene expression, particularly SAURs involved in apoplast acidification.

genes: muNPR1 (muNPR1, mutant NPR1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of muNPR1-GFP fails to rescue SA-driven hypocotyl phenotype in npr1 mutants, indicating cytosolic NPR1 is insufficient for hypocotyl elongation.
mechanism: muNPR1, defective in nuclear localization, remains cytosolic and cannot mediate SA-dependent transcriptional regulation required for hypocotyl growth.

genes: SAUR19 (SAUR19, auxin-responsive gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), SAUR63 (SAUR63, auxin-responsive gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAUR19 or SAUR63 rescues SA-induced short hypocotyl phenotype in npr1 mutants, promoting hypocotyl elongation in darkness.
mechanism: SAUR19 and SAUR63 promote cell expansion by inhibiting PP2C.D phosphatases, maintaining AHA2 phosphorylation and apoplast acidification.

genes: EX1ΔSOS (EX1ΔSOS, truncated EX1 lacking SOS domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of EX1ΔSOS-GFP fails to rescue npr1 ex1 mutant phenotype, indicating SOS domain is required for EX1 function in darkness.
mechanism: EX1ΔSOS lacks the SOS domain necessary for 1O2 sensing and retrograde signaling, preventing functional complementation.

genes: EX1 (EX1, 1O2 sensor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of EX1-GFP rescues npr1 ex1 mutant phenotype, restoring hypocotyl elongation in darkness.
mechanism: EX1 mediates 1O2-triggered retrograde signaling, repressing auxin-related gene expression and modulating hypocotyl growth.

genes: BrSDH1-1A (Brassica rapa succinate dehydrogenase 1-1A, Brassica rapa), BrSDH1-1B (Brassica rapa succinate dehydrogenase 1-1B, Brassica rapa), BrSDH1-1C (Brassica rapa succinate dehydrogenase 1-1C, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: OE-BrSDH1-1A and OE-BrSDH1-1C exhibit enhanced drought tolerance with ~50% survival rate after 7-day drought stress, while OE-BrSDH1-1B shows ~30% survival. H2S treatment increases survival rates in OE-BrSDH1-1A and OE-BrSDH1-1C but not in OE-BrSDH1-1B.
mechanism: H2S persulfidates BrSDH1-1A and BrSDH1-1C to enhance SDH activity and ATP production, scavenging ROS. BrSDH1-1B lacks persulfidation, leading to reduced function.

genes: MdWRKY50 (WRKY transcription factor, Malus domestica Borkh.), GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdWRKY50 increases internode length by ~40% in Malus domestica Borkh. cv. 'GL-3' apple plants.
mechanism: MdWRKY50 activates GA3ox transcription, increasing bioactive GA3/4 levels which promote cell elongation and internode growth.

genes: MdWRKY50 (WRKY transcription factor, Malus domestica Borkh.)
phenotype: RNAi suppression of MdWRKY50 reduces internode length by ~40% in Malus domestica Borkh. cv. 'GL-3' apple plants.
mechanism: MdWRKY50 knockdown decreases GA3ox transcription, lowering bioactive GA3/4 levels which restricts cell elongation and internode growth.

genes: MdWRKY50 (WRKY transcription factor, Malus domestica Borkh.)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdWRKY50 increases internode length by ~40% in Malus domestica Borkh. cv. 'GL-3' apple calli.
mechanism: MdWRKY50 activates GA3ox transcription, increasing bioactive GA3/4 levels which promote cell elongation and internode growth.

genes: MdWRKY50 (WRKY transcription factor, Malus domestica Borkh.)
phenotype: RNAi suppression of MdWRKY50 reduces internode length by ~40% in Malus domestica Borkh. cv. 'GL-3' apple calli.
mechanism: MdWRKY50 knockdown decreases GA3ox transcription, lowering bioactive GA3/4 levels which restricts cell elongation and internode growth.

phenotype: ProMdGA3ox::GUS reporter activity is 2.76-fold higher in apple calli co-expressing 35S::MdWRKY50-GFP compared to controls.
mechanism: MdWRKY50 directly binds to the W-box of MdGA3ox promoter and activates its transcription.

mechanism: V-box insertion upstream of promoter maintains low basal transcriptional activity

phenotype: SlEBF3-KO lines showed no significant differences in resistance to B. cinerea compared to wild-type (WT) plants.
mechanism: SlEBF3 knockout did not impact tomato resistance to B. cinerea, suggesting functional redundancy among SlEBF3 family members.

genes: SlEBF3 (SlEBF3, EIN3-binding F-box protein 3, Solanum lycopersicum)

genes: S-HsfA2 (heat stress transcription factor A2 splice variant, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)

mechanism: S-HsfA2 acts as a transcriptional repressor via its LxLxLx motif in the leucine-rich domain (LRD), inhibiting heat stress response genes.

genes: S-HsfA2 (heat stress transcription factor A2 splice variant, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)

mechanism: RNAi targeting retained intron sequences reduces S-HsfA2 expression, alleviating its repressive effect on heat stress response genes.

genes: S-HsfA2 (heat stress transcription factor A2 splice variant, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of S-HsfA2-GFP reduces root length by ~50% and causes dwarfism in Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings.
mechanism: S-HsfA2-GFP accumulates in the nucleus under heat stress, repressing growth-related gene expression.

genes: HSP17.6B (heat shock protein 17.6B, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)

mechanism: Loss of HSP17.6B function impairs heat shock protein-mediated thermoprotection.

mechanism: HSP17.6B overexpression compensates for the loss of endogenous HSP17.6B function.

genes: HSP17.6B (heat shock protein 17.6B, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)

mechanism: HSP17.6B overexpression represses growth-related gene expression.

genes: HSP17.6B (heat shock protein 17.6B, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)

mechanism: HSP17.6B overexpression enhances biomass accumulation through unknown mechanisms.

mechanism: Overexpression of LsCAS2 enhances chicoric acid synthesis by catalyzing the condensation of caftaric acid and chlorogenic acid.

mechanism: ODR1 represses ABA biosynthesis genes, thereby limiting ABA accumulation and alleviating germination arrest under stress

mechanism: AlbHLH3 interacts with promoters of terpenoid biosynthesis genes (AlHMGR3) and regulates their expression

genes: EPFL2 (EPFL2, AT4G37810, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Increased auxin-repressed EPFL2 production rate (αE) in gEPFL2 lines leads to longer auxin maxima intervals, consistent with computational simulations.

genes: EPFL2 (EPFL2, AT4G37810, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: EPFL2 expression is upregulated upon auxin signaling inhibition, indicating reciprocal inhibition with auxin response.

genes: EPFL1 (EPFL1, AT5G10310, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: EPFL1 promoter-GUS reporter shows broad spatial expression in leaf primordia, with subtle downregulation by auxin application.
mechanism: EPFL1 expression is not strongly auxin-repressed, consistent with its role in maintaining auxin maxima sharpness.

genes: TPST (tyrosine sulfotransferase, Physcomitrella patens)

mechanism: GbNAC2 upregulates structural genes in the flavonoid biosynthesis pathway and interacts with the GbAREB3 promoter to enhance ABA signaling.

genes: ZmSH1gRNA2 (guide RNA for CRISPR-Cas12a, ZmSH1 locus, maize), PMI (phosphomannose isomerase, selectable marker, synthetic)

mechanism: NHEJ (non-homologous end joining) facilitated by LbCas12a cleavage at ZmSH1gRNA2 site with no homology arms.

phenotype: HDR-mediated targeted insertion with eMb2Cas12a-Opt1 achieved djTIN rate of 2.0% in maize immature embryos.
