genes: eMb2Cas12a-Opt2 (engineered Cas12a ortholog from Moraxella bovoculi AAX08, maize codon-optimized, with E797A, F357W mutations), ZmSH1gRNA2 (guide RNA for CRISPR-Cas12a, ZmSH1 locus, maize), PMI (phosphomannose isomerase, selectable marker, synthetic)
phenotype: HDR-mediated targeted insertion with eMb2Cas12a-Opt2 achieved djTIN rate of 2.4% in maize immature embryos.
mechanism: Enhanced Cas12a activity via engineered mutations (E797A, F357W) and optimized T-DNA design improved HDR efficiency.

genes: HB34 (homeobox transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic DNA)
phenotype: Overexpression of HB34 in hb34-1 background increases susceptibility to Botrytis cinerea (lesions 15-30% larger diameter) and promotes plant growth (50-70% increased hypocotyl length, 50-70% larger leaf blade area, 50% increased fresh weight) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HB34 suppresses inappropriate activation of defense-related genes (PDF1.2C, PDF1.3, PR3, AOC1, LOX2) and promotes growth-related genes (EXO70A2, EXL5, SAUR50, SAUR29, IAA6) under normal conditions.

genes: HB34 (homeobox transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic DNA)
phenotype: HB34-ER overexpression in Col-0 background reduces expression of JA biosynthetic genes (AOC1, LOX2, OPR3) by 50-70% and JA content by 50-70% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HB34 directly binds to promoters of JA biosynthetic genes (AOC1, LOX2, OPR3) and negatively regulates their transcription, reducing JA accumulation.

genes: AhMTP9 (AhMTP9, key gene in plant hormone signal transduction pathway, peanut)
phenotype: Increased plant height, rosette leaf diameter, soluble sugar and reduced MDA content under high Mn stress in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NA

genes: QUA2 (Quasimodo2, pectin methyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of QUA2-GFP under the QUA2 promoter rescues the qua2-1 mutant phenotype, restoring normal root meristem size and root growth rate.
mechanism: QUA2-dependent cell wall softening at the transition zone (TZ) restricts cell division in the meristem by generating mechanical constraints on dividing cells.

genes: QUA2 (Quasimodo2, pectin methyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the qua2-1 mutant with QUA2-mCITRINE under the RCH2 promoter rescues root growth and reduces meristem size upon dexamethasone (Dex) induction.
mechanism: QUA2-dependent cell wall softening at the TZ restricts cell division by generating mechanical constraints on dividing cells, as evidenced by reduced meristem size and increased root growth in complemented plants.

genes: QUA2 (Quasimodo2, pectin methyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of QUA2-mCITRINE under the RCH2 promoter in wild-type plants reduces meristem size and increases root length upon Dex treatment.
mechanism: QUA2-dependent cell wall softening at the TZ generates mechanical constraints that restrict cell division, leading to shorter meristems and increased root growth.

genes: QUA2 (Quasimodo2, pectin methyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Tissue-specific knockout of QUA2 at the TZ using the RCH2 promoter recapitulates the qua2-1 mutant phenotype, with enlarged meristems and reduced root growth.
mechanism: Loss of QUA2 activity at the TZ leads to stiffer cell walls, reducing mechanical constraints on dividing cells and promoting meristem expansion.

genes: QUA2 (Quasimodo2, pectin methyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Time-course complementation of the qua2-1 mutant with QUA2-mCITRINE under the QUA2 promoter shows full complementation at 16 hours, with detectable changes in meristem size occurring at 24 hours.
mechanism: QUA2-dependent cell wall softening at the TZ generates mechanical constraints that regulate meristem size by modulating cell division rates.

genes: RIM22 (RIM22B3mut, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Fails to complement the rim22-3 mutant defects, indicating the DNA-binding domain is critical for function.
mechanism: Mutations in the B3 DNA-binding domain of RIM22 disrupt its ability to bind DNA motifs and recruit CLSY3–Pol-IV complexes.

genes: Cry1Ab (Cry1Ab, insecticidal protein, Bacillus thuringiensis), Cry2Aa (Cry2Aa, insecticidal protein, Bacillus thuringiensis), Cry1Bb (Cry1Bb, insecticidal protein, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Transgenic eucalyptus expressing Cry1Ab, Cry2Aa, and Cry1Bb proteins achieves 100% mortality of Thyrinteina arnobia larvae in bioassays with lyophilized leaf tissue.
mechanism: Insecticidal Cry proteins bind to midgut receptors, causing larval mortality.

genes: Cry1Ab (Cry1Ab, insecticidal protein, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Transgenic eucalyptus expressing Cry1Ab achieves 100% mortality of Thyrinteina arnobia larvae even at 100-fold dilution of leaf tissue.
mechanism: Insecticidal Cry1Ab protein binds to midgut receptors, causing larval mortality.

genes: HcEXPA4 (HcEXPA4, cell elongation regulation, Hedychium)
phenotype: Overexpression of HcEXPA4 significantly promoted plant height in tobacco.
mechanism: HcEXPA4 is involved in regulating cell elongation.

genes: HcNAC140 (HcNAC140, transcription factor, Hedychium)
phenotype: Overexpression of HcNAC140 in tobacco led to a significant increase in plant height.
mechanism: HcNAC140 specifically binds to the CACG core motif within the HcEXPA4 promoter, directly activating its transcription.

genes: Bx1 (Bx1, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx2 (Bx2, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx3 (Bx3, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx4 (Bx4, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx5 (Bx5, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx8 (Bx8, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays)
phenotype: Expression of Bx1, Bx2, Bx3, Bx4, Bx5, and Bx8 in Nicotiana benthamiana results in substantial BXD accumulation.
mechanism: The BXD biosynthetic pathway is reconstituted in N. benthamiana using maize Bx genes.

genes: AsTSB-like (AsTSB-like, TSB-like gene, Achnatherum squarrosa), Bx2 (Bx2, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx3 (Bx3, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx4 (Bx4, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx5 (Bx5, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx8 (Bx8, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays)
phenotype: Transient expression of AsTSB-like with maize Bx2, Bx3, Bx4, Bx5, and Bx8 in N. benthamiana results in BXD levels comparable to those produced by plants expressing the entire maize BXD pathway.
mechanism: AsTSB-like allosterically activates TSA to produce indole, which is then used by Bx genes to form BXD.

genes: AsTSB-like-A190E;E386D (AsTSB-like with A190E and E386D mutations, Achnatherum squarrosa), Bx2 (Bx2, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx3 (Bx3, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx4 (Bx4, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx5 (Bx5, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays), Bx8 (Bx8, BXD biosynthetic gene, Zea mays)
phenotype: The double mutant AsTSB-like-A190E;E386D in N. benthamiana shows highly reduced indole production, as evidenced by low BXD levels.
mechanism: The A190E and E386D mutations in AsTSB-like reduce its ability to activate TSA for indole production, leading to decreased BXD formation.

genes: BPC6 (BPC6, BPC6 transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The pBPC6:GFP-BPC6 line was used for ChIP assays to study BPC6 binding to target promoters during gynoecium development.
mechanism: BPC6 directly regulates target genes such as NTT and PILS3 through promoter binding, influencing septum and transmitting tract development.

genes: PILS3 (PILS3, auxin transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), PILS4 (PILS4, auxin transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The pils3 pils4 double mutant lines showed reduced extracellular matrix in the transmitting tract and partial septum fusion defects.
mechanism: PILS3 and PILS4 regulate auxin compartmentalization in the endoplasmic reticulum, affecting septum and transmitting tract development.

genes: SmEa (SmE, core splicing protein, Populus tremula x tremuloides), SmEb (SmE, core splicing protein, Populus tremula x tremuloides)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9 mutagenesis in hybrid aspen identified a role for SmEs in development in plants grown in an environment simulating seasonal photoperiod and temperature changes
mechanism: NA

genes: SgPAL1 (SgPAL1, phenylalanine ammonia-lyase, Solanum guianensis), SgPAL2 (SgPAL2, phenylalanine ammonia-lyase, Solanum guianensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of SgPAL1/2 in Arabidopsis thaliana enhanced resistance to C. gloeosporioides, while integrated transcriptomic, metabolomic, and biochemical analyses demonstrated that SgPAL1/2-mediated resistance operates through upregulation of lignin biosynthesis pathways, resulting in increased total lignin content and altered guaiacyl (G)/syringyl (S) monomer ratios.
mechanism: SgPAL1/2-mediated resistance operates through upregulation of lignin biosynthesis pathways, resulting in increased total lignin content and altered guaiacyl (G)/syringyl (S) monomer ratios

genes: CO (CONSTANS, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S:CO transgenic plants consistently flowered early under both space and ground conditions.
mechanism: Overexpression of CO enhances flowering time by upregulating FT expression.

genes: FT (FLOWERING LOCUS T, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, expression of foreign gene, synthetic)
phenotype: FG transgenic plants expressing FT with the GFP gene controlled by a heat shock-protein (HSP) promoter flowered slightly earlier under spaceflight conditions.
mechanism: Overexpression of FT under HSP17.4 promoter induces flowering, while GFP expression under the same promoter serves as a reporter.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, expression of foreign gene, synthetic)
phenotype: pFT:GFP transgenic plants expressing the green fluorescent protein (GFP) coding region under control of the FT promoter showed altered flowering gene expression profiles.
mechanism: GFP expression under FT promoter serves as a reporter for FT activity.

genes: PvPHR-L7 (Phvul.006G134700, transcription factor regulating nodule formation, Phaseolus vulgaris)
phenotype: Overexpression of PvPHR-L7 reduces nodule formation by ~60% in Phaseolus vulgaris under both optimal and low Pi conditions.
mechanism: PvPHR-L7 acts as a negative regulator of nodule formation by downregulating key symbiosis genes (PvNIN, PvTML, PvRIC1/2) and upregulating nodule-inhibitory genes (NRSYM1, CPK3, LSK1).

genes: PvPHR-L7 (Phvul.006G134700, transcription factor regulating nodule formation, Phaseolus vulgaris)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of PvPHR-L7 increases nodule formation by ~60% in Phaseolus vulgaris under both optimal and low Pi conditions.
mechanism: PvPHR-L7 acts as a negative regulator of nodule formation by downregulating key symbiosis genes (PvNIN, PvTML, PvRIC1/2) and upregulating nodule-inhibitory genes (NRSYM1, CPK3, LSK1).

genes: EYFP (enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: pMC::EYFP reporter shows localized, concentric EYFP fluorescence induction in response to methyl jasmonate (MeJA) and herbivore feeding (CPB larvae) in potato leaves, with a no-response zone adjacent to wounds.
mechanism: The MC promoter is JA-responsive and contains cis-elements for MYC recognition, SA, Ca2+, and ethylene signaling. SA accumulation at wound edges suppresses JA-dependent transcription in proximal cells.

genes: Jas9-Venus-N7 (JA-Ile biosensor, synthetic)
phenotype: Jas9-Venus-N7 sensor degrades in a confluent front from wound edges, indicating JA-Ile accumulation, with no attenuation near wounds. This contrasts with pMC::EYFP's no-response zone.
mechanism: Jas9-Venus-N7 tracks proteasomal degradation of JAZ repressors of MYC transcription factors, revealing JA-Ile dynamics. SA accumulation does not affect this sensor's response.

genes: SlERF.F5 (negative regulator in stress response, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Enhanced drought, salt, and low temperature stress resistance with higher relative water content, lower relative conductivity and MDA content, and higher chlorophyll content compared to wild-type plants
mechanism: Silencing of SlERF.F5 activates stress response genes (P5CS, Cat1, Apx2, SlCOR) and preserves cell membrane integrity by upregulating osmotic regulation and antioxidant defense mechanisms

genes: OLE4 (OLE4, oleosin protein involved in light signaling and ABA regulation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of OLE4 in Arabidopsis thaliana results in shorter hypocotyls under red light compared to wild-type plants, with no significant difference in darkness.
mechanism: OLE4 acts as a negative regulator of hypocotyl elongation under red light by repressing growth, potentially through interactions with PIF3 and HDA5/6 to modulate gene expression and ABA signaling.

genes: AHA2 (AHA2, H+-ATPase involved in RALF1 signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of aha2 mutant root growth phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: AHA2 is involved in RALF1-mediated inhibition of root growth by regulating H+ fluxes and membrane dynamics

genes: ABCG16 (ABCG16, ABA efflux transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ABCG16 increases root growth under ABA treatment.
mechanism: ABCG16 enhances ABA efflux, reducing cytosolic ABA levels and promoting root growth.

genes: ABCG16 (ABCG16, ABA efflux transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), ABCG16T45A (ABCG16T45A, non-phosphorylatable variant, Arabidopsis thaliana), ABCG16T45E (ABCG16T45E, phospho-mimic variant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of g16 mutant with wild-type ABCG16 restores root growth under ABA; non-phosphorylatable variant shows robust growth, while phospho-mimic variant does not.
mechanism: Phosphorylation at Thr45 modulates ABCG16's ABA transport activity and root growth response.

genes: SlMNSI1 (alpha-1,2-mannosidase I, tomato, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: KO of SlMNSI1 results in pleiotropic developmental defects including smaller seeds with reduced germination rates, plant dwarfism, reduced fruit set, and smaller, earlier-ripening fruits. Seeds from KO fruits are not viable. Accumulation of Man8GlcNAc2 in fruits.
mechanism: SlMNSI1 functions as a Golgi α-1,2-mannosidase that trims Man8GlcNAc2 to Man5GlcNAc2. Loss of SlMNSI1 triggers global reprogramming of the fruit proteome and transcriptome, with upregulation of stress response pathways and proteolytic activity.

genes: SlMNSI1 (alpha-1,2-mannosidase I, tomato, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of wild-type SlMNSI1 rescues fruit development defects in slmnsI1 mutants. Overexpression of non-glycosylatable SlMNSI1N288A/N334A partially complements these phenotypes. No significant changes in N-glycan profiles in complemented lines.
mechanism: SlMNSI1 overexpression restores normal fruit development by maintaining proper N-glycan processing. N-glycosylation at N288 and N334 is essential for SlMNSI1's Golgi localization, protein stability, and enzymatic function in trimming Man8GlcNAc2 to Man5GlcNAc2.

genes: PLS (Polaris peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PLS:GFP rescues the short primary root phenotype of the pls mutant in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PLS:GFP localizes to the endoplasmic reticulum and interacts with the ethylene receptor ETR1, modulating ethylene signaling.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of proPLS::GFP in Arabidopsis thaliana does not co-localize with the ER, unlike PLS:GFP.
mechanism: GFP expressed under the PLS promoter lacks subcellular localization to the ER, indicating PLS-specific targeting.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: p35S::GFP seedlings in Arabidopsis thaliana were used as a control for ER localization studies.
mechanism: GFP under the CaMV35S promoter lacks specific subcellular targeting to the ER, unlike PLS:GFP.

genes: PLS (Polaris peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), roGFP2 (redox-sensitive GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PLS:roGFP2 in Nicotiana benthamiana localizes to the cytosolic side of the ER and interacts with ETR1.
mechanism: PLS:roGFP2 fusions under the CaMV35S promoter enable ratiometric analysis of redox-sensitive GFP to determine subcellular localization.

genes: PLS (Polaris peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PLS:GFP in Nicotiana benthamiana co-localizes with the ER and interacts with ETR1.
mechanism: PLS:GFP under the CaMV35S promoter enables visualization of PLS localization and interaction with the ethylene receptor.

genes: ETR1 (ethylene receptor 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), HA (hemagglutinin tag, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of ETR1:HA in Nicotiana benthamiana enables co-immunoprecipitation with PLS:GFP to confirm physical interaction.
mechanism: ETR1:HA under the CaMV35S promoter facilitates detection of PLS-ETR1 interaction via CoIP assays.

genes: FER (FERONIA, receptor kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of fer-4 mutant with kinase-dead FERK565R restores FER expression but fails to recover stigmatic ROS levels or slow pollen hydration rates compared to wild type.
mechanism: FER kinase activity is essential for ROS accumulation in stigma papillae and regulation of pollen hydration. Kinase-dead FERK565R cannot phosphorylate S695/T696, leading to loss of kinase activity.

genes: FER (FERONIA, receptor kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Phosphomimic FERS695D/T696D transgenic lines fully restore stigmatic ROS levels and pollen hydration rates to wild-type levels in fer-4 mutant background.
mechanism: Phosphomimic mutations at S695/T696 mimic phosphorylation, restoring FER kinase activity to promote ROS production and regulate pollen hydration.

genes: SDE5 (SDE5, CLas effector, CLas)
phenotype: Overexpression of SDE5 increases citrus attractiveness to D. citri by reducing terpene synthesis and suppressing defense-related genes.
mechanism: SDE5 acts as a lysozyme inhibitor, suppresses MYC2 transcriptional activity by interfering with its dimerization, and reduces TPS21-7 expression, leading to decreased β-caryophyllene and (E)-β-farnesene emission.

genes: MYC2 (MYC2, Citrus sinensis, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: MYC2 silencing increases citrus attractiveness to D. citri by reducing TPS21-7 expression and β-caryophyllene emission.
mechanism: MYC2 positively regulates TPS21-7 expression and terpene biosynthesis. Silencing MYC2 reduces TPS21-7 transcript levels and β-caryophyllene emission, enhancing psyllid attraction.

genes: MYC2 (MYC2, Citrus sinensis, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: MYC2 overexpression reduces citrus attractiveness to D. citri by increasing TPS21-7 expression and β-caryophyllene emission.
mechanism: MYC2 activates TPS21-7 transcription, leading to increased β-caryophyllene and (E)-β-farnesene emission, which repel D. citri.

genes: TPS21-7 (TPS21-7, Citrus sinensis, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of TPS21-7 increases β-caryophyllene and (E)-β-farnesene emission, repelling D. citri.
mechanism: TPS21-7 catalyzes β-caryophyllene and (E)-β-farnesene biosynthesis, which function as psyllid repellents.

genes: APP3-14 (APP3-14, synthetic peptide, synthetic)
phenotype: APP3-14 treatment reduces psyllid attraction to HLB-positive citrus by enhancing MYC2-regulated terpene defense.
mechanism: APP3-14 inhibits SDE5 lysozyme inhibitor function, restores MYC2 stability, and promotes TPS21-7 expression, increasing β-caryophyllene and β-myrcene emission.

genes: OsSPL10 (squamosa promoter binding protein-like transcription factor, Oryza sativa, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Loss-of-function mutants (spl10) exhibit significantly enhanced salt tolerance with reduced leaf withering (SES=3 vs 7 in WT), higher plant height, and greater fresh weight under 120 mM NaCl stress.
mechanism: OsSPL10 negatively regulates salt tolerance by modulating ROS homeostasis (increased SOD activity and OsCatA expression, reduced APX2/8 expression) and influencing plant hormone signal transduction (e.g., OsGH3-2) and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis (e.g., OsCCR10) pathways.

genes: BjuFIP (BjuFIP, F-box protein interacting with BjuPYL3, tuber mustard)
phenotype: Overexpression of BjuFIP increases germination and greening rates under ABA treatment in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: BjuFIP negatively regulates ABA signaling by interacting with BjuASK1 and BjuPYL3, leading to reduced expression of ABA-responsive genes.

genes: BjuFIP (BjuFIP, F-box protein interacting with BjuPYL3, tuber mustard)
phenotype: GUS staining shows BjuFIP expression in various tissues and ABA response in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: BjuFIP is expressed ubiquitously and induced by ABA in cotyledons and roots.

genes: AtMCM10 (AtMCM10, DNA damage response gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of Atmcm10-1 mutant rescues hypersensitivity to Zeb and MMC, restoring normal root growth and reducing DNA damage.
mechanism: AtMCM10 is required for DNA damage response, particularly in ATM-mediated repair of Zeb-induced DSBs.

genes: AtMCM10 (AtMCM10, DNA damage response gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtMCM10-GFP in Atmcm10-1 mutant rescues hypersensitivity to Zeb and NaCl, but deletion of IDR2 or IDR1/2 fails to rescue.
mechanism: IDRs in AtMCM10 are critical for phase separation and DNA annealing activity required for SDSA-mediated HR repair.

genes: OsNAC74 (NAC transcription factor, salt stress response regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsNAC74 homozygous mutants exhibit reduced germination rate, decreased salt tolerance with lower survival rates under 100/150 mM NaCl, increased ROS accumulation, reduced chlorophyll content, and shorter root length compared to wild-type Zhonghua 11 rice
mechanism: OsNAC74 regulates salt tolerance through plant hormone signaling pathways (auxin, ABA, jasmonic acid, gibberellin) and auxin-mediated root development. Transcriptome analysis shows differential expression of salt stress-related genes and hormone pathway genes

genes: OsSWEET14 (OsSWEET14, SWEET sugar transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Enhanced resistance against Xoo strain KACC10859, with 1–7 days earlier heading, 8.0% longer panicles, and 3.0% reduction in grain weight and 4.4% reduction in grain fertility
mechanism: Enhanced resistance likely due to pathogen starvation from restricted sugar efflux to apoplast

genes: BpPIN3 (BpPIN3, auxin efflux carrier, Betula pendula)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of BpPIN3 in Betula pendula leads to increased lateral branching during seedling stage (10.67% increase vs wild type, 22.2% vs rescue line), reduced stem node diameter (33-42.73% lower than wild type in OE lines), and shorter internode length (9.88-24.75% reduction vs wild type).
mechanism: BpPIN3 enhances polar auxin transport (PAT) from axillary buds to main stem, creating local auxin minima that alleviate inhibition of axillary bud meristems. This mechanism aligns with the canalization hypothesis of auxin transport.

genes: SmBBX5 (regulator of anthocyanin synthesis, Solanum melongena)
phenotype: SmBBX5 positively regulates anthocyanin synthesis in eggplant peel
mechanism: SmBBX5 positively regulates the synthesis of anthocyanin

genes: MsCBF4 (MsCBF4, transcriptional activator, Medicago sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of MsCBF4 in Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings significantly enhanced root length, lateral root number, and fresh weight under cold stress. Lines overexpressing MsCBF4 demonstrated enhanced frost tolerance at both the seedling and mature stages
mechanism: Improved physiological scavenging of reactive oxygen species (ROSs), thereby limiting membrane damage, and upregulation of key genes involved in abiotic stress resistance

genes: OsU3 (promoter, RNA polymerase III terminator, Oryza sativa), SpCas9 (rice codon optimized, SV40 NLS, nucleoplasmin NLS, synthetic), NosT (NOS terminator, synthetic)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9 library enables higher-order knockout of putative redundant gene sets in rice, with observed grain length increases in edited lines (e.g. 15-30% increases in grain length for specific alleles)
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9 system targets conserved sequences in paralogous gene sets, inducing indels that disrupt gene function. Seed-expressed gene knockouts alter grain development through epistatic interactions between Agenet domain-containing genes LOC_Os09g24290 and LOC_Os10g26430

genes: HaSAPK3.8 (HaSAPK3.8, drought-responsive gene from ABA signaling pathway, Helianthus annuus)
phenotype: Overexpression of HaSAPK3.8 in tobacco increases SOD, POD, and CAT activities by 85.18%, 25.03%, and 23.68%, reduces MDA content by 31.34%, and elevates ABA, Pro, and SS levels by 66.54%, 25.07%, and 21.76% under drought stress.
mechanism: HaSAPK3.8 confers drought tolerance by regulating osmotic homeostasis and reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging capacity.

genes: SDE2470 (effector, Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus)
phenotype: Overexpression of SDE2470 in Arabidopsis thaliana increased susceptibility to Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 (Pst DC3000) with exacerbated disease symptoms and higher bacterial biomass compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: SDE2470 suppresses basal immunity by interacting with CsBTS1E3 to promote CsVOZ2 degradation via the 26S proteasome pathway, thereby inhibiting ROS- and ABA-mediated defense responses.

genes: SDE2470 (effector, Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus)
phenotype: Overexpression of SDE2470 in Citrus sinensis increased susceptibility to Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri (Xcc) with exacerbated disease symptoms and higher bacterial biomass compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: SDE2470 suppresses basal immunity by interacting with CsBTS1E3 to promote CsVOZ2 degradation via the 26S proteasome pathway, thereby inhibiting ROS- and ABA-mediated defense responses.

genes: CsVOZ2 (vascular transcription factor, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsVOZ2 in Citrus sinensis enhanced resistance to Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (CLas) with reduced bacterial colonization and delayed symptom development compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: CsVOZ2 activates ROS- and ABA-mediated defense pathways, upregulates immunity-related genes (e.g., CsRbohD, CsFLS2, CsPAD4), and reinforces cell wall barriers, thereby inhibiting CLas proliferation.

genes: CsVOZ2 (vascular transcription factor, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated silencing of CsVOZ2 in Citrus sinensis increased susceptibility to Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (CLas) with accelerated bacterial colonization and severe symptom development compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: CsVOZ2 silencing suppresses ROS- and ABA-mediated defense pathways, downregulates immunity-related genes (e.g., CsRbohD, CsFLS2, CsPAD4), and weakens cell wall barriers, thereby facilitating CLas proliferation.

genes: CsBTS1E3 (E3 ligase, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsBTS1E3 in Citrus sinensis increased susceptibility to Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (CLas) with enhanced bacterial colonization compared to empty vector (EV) controls.
mechanism: CsBTS1E3 promotes degradation of CsVOZ2 via the 26S proteasome pathway, thereby suppressing ROS- and ABA-mediated defense responses and facilitating CLas proliferation.

genes: TdNF-YA2A-1 (nuclear factor Y transcription factor, durum wheat)
phenotype: Overexpression of TdNF-YA2A-1 in tobacco enhances tolerance to salt, osmotic, and oxidative stresses, with 70-78% germination under stress vs 24-40% in non-transgenic plants, and 25% biomass reduction under salt stress vs 80% in non-transgenic plants
mechanism: TdNF-YA2A-1 upregulates antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT, POD) and stress-responsive genes (NtSOS1, NtERD10C, NtDREB1A), reduces ROS accumulation, and maintains chlorophyll content under stress

genes: GmNAC3 (NAC transcription factor, Glycine max, cDNA)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmNAC3 enhances drought tolerance in soybean hairy roots, with reduced ROS accumulation, increased proline content, and improved root architecture under PEG6000-induced drought stress.

mechanism: SlERF.D2 is a nuclear-localized transcription factor, consistent with its role in regulating gene expression during osmotic stress adaptation.

genes: OsMADS56 (OsMADS56, transcription factor, Oryza sativa ssp. Japonica)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsMADS56 increases drought tolerance (75% survival in OX7 vs 59.6% in WT under PEG6000 stress), shorter plant height (65 cm vs 73 cm in WT), earlier heading date, higher panicle count, and increased grain yield in rice.
mechanism: NA

genes: GmMYB331 (Glyma.20G184500, MYB-type transcription factor, Glycine max)
phenotype: Mild overexpression increases seed oil content by ~11.92-13.08% and seed yield per plant by 15.95-39.66% in Glycine max.
mechanism: GmMYB331 activates oil biosynthesis genes (GmOLEO1/2/4, GmACP4) and oil-regulatory transcription factors (GmNFYA, GmZF351, GmZF392).

genes: GmMYB331 (Glyma.20G184500, MYB-type transcription factor, Glycine max)
phenotype: Knockout mutants show significantly smaller seed size, reduced 100-seed weight, and decreased total fatty acid content in Glycine max.
mechanism: GmMYB331 is essential for maintaining seed size/weight and oil accumulation by regulating downstream genes.

genes: MYB10-1B (Fxa1Bg1886930, transcription factor for anthocyanin biosynthesis, octoploid strawberry)
phenotype: Knockout of MYB10-1B in octoploid strawberry results in white fruit phenotype with downregulated anthocyanin biosynthesis genes (CHS, DFR, ANS) in ripened fruits
mechanism: MYB10-1B knockout disrupts anthocyanin biosynthesis by downregulating key pathway genes (CHS, DFR, ANS), preventing fruit pigmentation

genes: CUL4 (At5g46210, E3-ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Impaired H1.1 depletion in the SMC when amiR[CUL4] is induced, with 52% of ovule primordia showing H1.1-GFP persistence compared to 11% in the control.
mechanism: CULLIN4-mediated ubiquitination of H1.1 targets it for proteasome degradation in SMCs.

genes: AIH (At5g08170, AGMATINASE IMINOHYDROLYASE, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced H1.1 depletion in the SMC when amiR[AIH] is induced, with 37% of ovule primordia showing H1.1 persistence compared to 6% in the control.
mechanism: AIH-mediated citrullination of H1.1 facilitates its ubiquitination and degradation via CUL4.

genes: H1.1 (Histone H1.1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: H1.1-RFP is depleted in 95% of SMCs, with 5% showing residual signal, indicating normal degradation.
mechanism: H1.1 is ubiquitinated at lysine residues (e.g., K89) and degraded via CUL4-mediated proteasome pathway.

genes: H1.1 (Histone H1.1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: H1.16xGC-RFP shows persistence in 76–95% of SMCs, indicating resistance to degradation due to K89R mutation.
mechanism: Mutation of six ubiquitinated lysines (including K89) in H1.1 prevents ubiquitination and proteasome-mediated degradation.

genes: H1.1 (Histone H1.1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: H1.1K89R-RFP shows persistence in 7 of 9 lines, indicating that K89R mutation alone is sufficient to prevent degradation.
mechanism: Mutation of lysine 89 (K89R) in the globular domain of H1.1 prevents ubiquitination and subsequent degradation.

genes: GmF3′H (GmF3′H, flavonoid 3′ hydroxylase, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmF3′H increases salt tolerance in soybean seeds and seedlings by enhancing ascorbic acid (AsA) biosynthesis and scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS).
mechanism: GmF3′H competitively binds to CSN5B, inhibiting its interaction with VTC1 and redirecting metabolic flux toward the L-galactose pathway to increase AsA production, which maintains redox homeostasis under salt stress.

genes: gRNA (GmF3′H, targeting GmF3′H, synthetic)
phenotype: Knockout of GmF3′H reduces salt tolerance in soybean seeds and seedlings, with lower germination rates and increased ROS accumulation under salt stress.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaPP2C-a5.1 (TaPP2C-a5.1, negative regulator of seed dormancy and drought stress, wheat), TaPP2C-a5.2 (TaPP2C-a5.2, negative regulator of seed dormancy, wheat)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaPP2C-a5.1 and TaPP2C-a5.2 reduces seed dormancy and promotes seed germination in wheat. TaPP2C-a5.1 also negatively regulates drought stress response.
mechanism: TaPP2C-a5.1 and TaPP2C-a5.2 act as negative regulators of ABA signaling, interacting with TaSnRK2.8 and modulating ABA-responsive gene expression (e.g., TaABI5, TaNCEDs, TaABA8′OHs). TaPP2C-a5.1 interacts with TaDOG1L1 and TaPYL4/5/6 to regulate ABA signaling.

genes: TaPP2C-a5.2 (TaPP2C-a5.2, negative regulator of seed dormancy, wheat)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaPP2C-a5.2 reduces seed dormancy and promotes seed germination in wheat without affecting drought stress response.
mechanism: TaPP2C-a5.2 acts as a negative regulator of ABA signaling by interacting with TaSnRK2.8 but does not interact with TaDOG1L1 or TaPYLs. It modulates ABA-responsive gene expression (e.g., TaABI5, TaNCEDs, TaABA8′OHs) to promote germination.

genes: HvbZIP87 (HvbZIP87, barley-specific transcription factor involved in SAR, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Transgenic wheat lines expressing HvbZIP87 exhibited significantly enhanced SAR levels and improved plant defense to stripe rust, leaf rust, spot blotch, and Fusarium crown rot.
mechanism: HvbZIP87 physically interacts with TaNPR1 in the nucleus and regulates PR genes (TaPR1, TaPR2, TaPR4, TaPR5) and zinc transporters.

genes: HvbZIP87 (HvbZIP87, barley-specific transcription factor involved in SAR, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Recombinant GFP-HvbZIP87 and HvbZIP87-GFP constructs were transiently expressed in N. benthamiana via Agrobacterium. Fluorescence was detected within the nucleus for both constructs.
mechanism: HvbZIP87 contains a nuclear localization signal (NLS) essential for its nuclear localization.

genes: TaMYC2 (TaMYC2, negative regulator of plant defense, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Silencing TaMYC2 further enhanced wheat's resistance to stripe rust, suggesting its negative regulatory role in plant defense.
mechanism: TaMYC2 interacts with HvbZIP87 and functions as a negative regulator of defense responses.

genes: ZmWRKY36 (ZmWRKY36, transcription factor, Zea mays)
phenotype: ZmWRKY36-silenced maize plants exhibit reduced resistance to B. maydis infection and suppressed chitin-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst.
mechanism: ZmWRKY36 positively regulates maize resistance to B. maydis by upregulating disease-related genes and transcriptional activation activity.

genes: ZmWRKY36 (ZmWRKY36, transcription factor, Zea mays)
phenotype: ZmWRKY36-overexpressed maize plants show increased resistance to B. maydis infection and upregulated expression of disease-related genes.
mechanism: ZmWRKY36 positively regulates maize resistance to B. maydis by upregulating disease-related genes and transcriptional activation activity.

genes: MsGT16 (transcription factor involved in abiotic stress responses, Medicago sativa)
phenotype: MsGT16-overexpressing Arabidopsis plants displayed stronger growth and higher antioxidant enzyme activity under salt stress compared to wild-type controls
mechanism: NA

genes: KTN1 (katanin p60 subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), AAA (phosphonull mutant of KTN1, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: AAA mutant shows reduced microtubule severing activity, impaired pollen viability, and male fertility defects in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AAA mutation reduces microtubule binding and ATPase activity, leading to defective pollen tube growth and meiotic spindle abnormalities.

genes: KTN1 (katanin p60 subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), DDD (phosphomimetic mutant of KTN1, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: DDD mutant exhibits impaired microtubule severing, dwarf growth, and partial rescue of ktn1-2 mutant phenotypes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: DDD mutation reduces microtubule binding and ATPase activity, leading to disordered cortical microtubules and reduced anisotropic cell expansion.

genes: ZjuPrec-5xFPIY (synthetic, core peptide with five FPIY repeats, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of ZjuPrec-5xFPIY in transgenic Nicotiana benthamiana via agroinfiltration for seven days.
mechanism: NA

genes: ZjuBURP (BURP-domain-containing gene, burpitide cyclase, Ziziphus jujuba)
phenotype: Co-expression of pEAQ-HT-ZjuPrec-5xFPIY and ZjuBURP led to detection of monocyclic FPIY peptide in transgenic Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: ZjuBURP catalyzes ether-crosslink on core peptide of precursor peptide, leading to cyFPIY formation.

genes: ZjuPrec-5xFPIY (synthetic, core peptide with five FPIY repeats, synthetic), ZjuBURP (BURP-domain-containing gene, burpitide cyclase, Ziziphus jujuba)
phenotype: Expression of ZjuPrec-5xFPIY-ZjuBURP-fusion in transgenic Nicotiana benthamiana increased cyFPIY yields by 2.9-fold compared to split system.
mechanism: Fusion of precursor and cyclase genes enhances catalytic efficiency and substrate proximity, leading to higher cyFPIY yields.

genes: ZjuDC (non-heme-iron and 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase, Ziziphus jujuba)
phenotype: Co-expression of ZjuDC with ZjuPrec-5xFPIY-ZjuBURP-fusion in Nicotiana benthamiana resulted in oxidative decarboxylation of cyFPIY to cyFPIY-dc.
mechanism: ZjuDC catalyzes oxidative decarboxylation of cyFPIY in the presence of 2-oxoglutarate, O2, and Fe(II), generating succinate as a byproduct.

genes: ZjuNMT (SAM-dependent methyltransferase, Ziziphus jujuba)
phenotype: Co-expression of ZjuNMT with ZjuPrec-5xFPIY-ZjuBURP-fusion and ZjuDC in Nicotiana benthamiana resulted in N,N-dimethylation of cyFPIY-dc to lotusine A.
mechanism: ZjuNMT catalyzes N,N-dimethylation of cyFPIY-dc using SAM as a methyl donor, producing lotusine A with L-configuration at amino acid α-carbons.

genes: SkrBURP-5xLLIYxxF (fused burpitide cyclase with five LLIY core peptides, Selaginella kraussiana)
phenotype: Transient expression of SkrBURP-5xLLIYxxF in Nicotiana benthamiana yielded cyLLIY with expected m/z values.
mechanism: SkrBURP-5xLLIYxxF catalyzes 14-membered macrocyclization of LLIY core peptides, forming cyLLIY as an intermediate for adouetine X biosynthesis.

genes: SkrBURP-5xFLLYxxF (fused burpitide cyclase with five FLLY core peptides, Selaginella kraussiana)
phenotype: Transient expression of SkrBURP-5xFLLYxxF in Nicotiana benthamiana yielded cyFLLY with expected m/z values.
mechanism: SkrBURP-5xFLLYxxF catalyzes 14-membered macrocyclization of FLLY core peptides, forming cyFLLY as an intermediate for sanjoinine A biosynthesis.

genes: TUB6 (TUB6, tubulin beta-6, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of mRuby2-TUB6 under the Lat52 promoter in A. thaliana pollen tubes for visualization of microtubules
mechanism: NA

genes: LifeAct-mEGFP (LifeAct-mEGFP, synthetic actin-binding fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of LifeAct-mEGFP under the Lat52 promoter in A. thaliana pollen tubes for visualization of actin filaments
mechanism: NA

genes: EB1b (EB1b, end-binding protein 1b, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of EB1b-mEGFP under the native proEB1b promoter in A. thaliana pollen tubes for visualization of microtubule plus ends
mechanism: NA

genes: AtXAT2 (arabinofuranosyl transferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtXAT2 increases arabinose (Ara) content in xylan by ~30-40% in Arabidopsis thaliana transgenic lines (AtXAT2/Col.0 and AtXAT2/atdgux).
mechanism: AtXAT2 transfers arabinose to xylan side chains, replacing glucuronic acid (GlcA) in wild-type Col.0 and adding Ara to xylan in atdgux mutants lacking GlcA.

genes: Cast_Gnk2-like (antifungal protein, Castanea sativa, Castanea sativa), NPTII (neomycin phosphotransferase, Escherichia coli, synthetic), EGFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of Cast_Gnk2-like increases tolerance to Phytophthora cinnamomi in Castanea sativa, with reduced root necrosis (up to 50% lower) and disease severity in transgenic lines CI-3-G3 and CI-9-G11 compared to wild-type controls.
mechanism: Cast_Gnk2-like likely enhances defense by binding to mannose/mannan residues in fungal cell walls, disrupting their integrity. May also synergize with pectin barriers and lectin activity in roots to prevent Phytophthora cinnamomi zoospore penetration.

genes: GmOFP1b (GmOFP1b, soybean gene)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmOFP1b in Arabidopsis reduced plant height by ~ 40% and shortened siliques.
mechanism: GmOFP1b interacts with GmKNOX4 proteins and negatively regulates the expression of GmGA20ox to control plant height.

genes: GmOFP1b (GmOFP1b, soybean gene), GmOFP2 (GmOFP2, soybean gene), GmOFP7 (GmOFP7, soybean gene)
gene_construct: NA-GmOFP1b (GmOFP1b, soybean gene, NA)-NA---NA-GmOFP2 (GmOFP2, soybean gene, NA)-NA---NA-GmOFP7 (GmOFP7, soybean gene, NA)-NA
phenotype: Transgenic plants expressing GmOFP1b, GmOFP2, and GmOFP7 exhibited higher survival rates under salt stress at the seedling stage.
mechanism: GmOFP1b appears to play a dual role in salt tolerance in mature plants.

genes: PAP3 (PAP3, gene targeted for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knock-out, synthetic), TT2 (TT2, gene targeted for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knock-out, synthetic)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knock-out of PAP3 and TT2 results in pfg1-3 pap1-4 septuple mutant (lacks anthocyanins) and pfg1-3 tt2 quadruple mutant (reduced proanthocyanidin content in seeds).
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis using pDE–Cas9 and XNG–Cas9 vectors with specific sgRNAs targeting PAP3 and TT2, leading to premature stop-codons and loss of DNA binding functionality in truncated proteins.

genes: GhGCS1 (GhGCS1, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhGCS1 enhances lateral root development in cotton and increases resistance to verticillium wilt by upregulating BR-related and PR genes.
mechanism: GhGCS1 inhibits cytokinin (CK) biosynthesis, thereby promoting lateral root development. It also modulates BR-related and PR gene expression to enhance disease resistance.

genes: GhGCS1 (antisense suppression, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Antisense suppression of GhGCS1 inhibits lateral root outgrowth in cotton and reduces resistance to verticillium wilt.
mechanism: Reduced GhGCS1 activity leads to increased cytokinin (CK) biosynthesis, suppressing lateral root development. It also downregulates BR-related and PR gene expression, decreasing disease resistance.

genes: CmGoSAMT1 (CmGoSAMT1, Golgi SAM transporter, Cucumis melo), CmPMT1 (CmPMT1, Pectin methyltransferase, Cucumis melo), CmPMT15 (CmPMT15, Pectin methyltransferase, Cucumis melo)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmPMT1 and CmPMT15 makes fruit susceptible to softening, but not for CmGoSAMT1. Overexpression of CmPMT1 and CmPMT15 reduces the extent of HG-Ca2+ cross-linking.
mechanism: CmPMT1 and CmPMT15 overexpression increases methyl-esterification of HG, reducing HG-Ca2+ cross-linking and making HG more accessible to degrading enzymes like PMEs, PLs, and PGs.

genes: CmbZIP11 (CmbZIP11, basic/region leucine zipper transcription factor, Cucumis melo)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmbZIP11 up-regulates CmPMT1 and CmPMT15 expression, leading to increased fruit softening and reduced HG-Ca2+ cross-linking.
mechanism: CmbZIP11 transcriptionally activates CmPMT1 and CmPMT15, increasing methyl-esterification of HG and reducing cross-linking, making HG more susceptible to degradation.

genes: CmPMT1 (CmPMT1, Pectin methyltransferase, Cucumis melo)
phenotype: The CmPMT1 promoter drives luciferase expression in reporter assays to study its regulation by CmbZIP11.
mechanism: NA

genes: MaMYB69 (transcription factor involved in fruit ripening, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: Overexpression of MaMYB69 in tomato promotes fruit ripening by activating the transcription of SlPL, SlPE3, SlTBG4, and SlPG2, leading to accelerated ripening with visible phenotypic differences at 32 days post-anthesis (DPA), rapid decline in firmness, and ethylene production peak at 35 DPA.
mechanism: MaMYB69 activates the transcription of cell wall-modifying genes (SlPL, SlPE3, SlTBG4, and SlPG2), enhancing fruit ripening.

genes: MaMYB69 (transcription factor involved in fruit ripening, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of MaMYB69 in banana fruits accelerates ripening and softening, with more pronounced yellowing, higher ethylene production, lower fruit firmness, and induced expression of MaPE, MaPL1, MaGAL, and MaPG3.
mechanism: MaMYB69 promotes banana fruit ripening and softening by stimulating the expression of genes involved in softening (MaPE, MaPL1, MaGAL, and MaPG3).

genes: TaARE1-D (TaARE1-D, negative regulator of nitrogen uptake and yield, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Knockout of TaARE1-D increases grain number per spike (~13.5% increase), spike length (~9% increase), grain length (~18% increase), and thousand-grain weight (~8% increase) in Triticum aestivum
mechanism: TaARE1-D is a negative regulator of nitrogen uptake and yield; its knockout enhances yield-related traits by removing this regulatory constraint

genes: Glyma.10G246300 (αʹ subunit of β-conglycinin, Glycine max), Glyma.20G148300 (α subunit of β-conglycinin, Glycine max), Glyma.20G148400 (α subunit of β-conglycinin, Glycine max), Glyma.20G146200 (β subunit of β-conglycinin, Glycine max), Glyma.20G148200 (β subunit of β-conglycinin, Glycine max)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated elimination of β-conglycinin subunits reduces IgE binding to soybean seed proteins and yields lines with stably inherited seed protein phenotypes
mechanism: Elimination of β-conglycinin subunits reduces IgE recognition by soybean seed proteins

genes: HaDREB1D (HaDREB1D, drought stress tolerance, Helianthus annuus)
phenotype: Transgenic lines showed significantly higher survival rates and improved physiological performance after 14 days of drought treatment followed by 4 days of rewatering compared with wild-type plants
mechanism: NA

genes: OsDof1 (LOC_Os01g64590, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsDof1 reduces plant height by 7.31%–17.62% at seedling stage and 10.22%–13.61% at maturity stage in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsDof1 inhibits IAA biosynthesis through the Trp-dependent pathway, leading to reduced plant height and increased lodging resistance.

genes: OsDof1 (LOC_Os01g64590, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of OsDof1 increases plant height by 5.32%–6.29% at seedling stage and 3.62%–5.37% at maturity stage in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsDof1 normally inhibits IAA biosynthesis; its knockout leads to increased IAA levels and taller plants.

genes: PpZAT12 (PpZAT12, drought-induced transcription factor, source not specified)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpZAT12 in transgenic rice resulted in enhanced drought tolerance, with higher relative water content and lower ion leakage compared with the wild type (WT) after osmotic stress
mechanism: PpZAT12 activates antioxidant defense system and regulates gene expression involving starch, sugars and amino acids biosynthesis and metabolism

genes: NtSULTR1;3 (sulfate transporter, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9 knockout mutants of NtSULTR1;3 conferred enhanced root growth under normal conditions but extreme salt hypersensitivity
mechanism: Loss of NtSULTR1;3 disrupts sulfate allocation, reducing sulfate (SO42−) levels in mutant roots

genes: SlMYB12 (flavonoid biosynthesis regulator, tomato, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlMYB12 increases flavonoid accumulation in tomato roots and fruits, leading to ~7-fold higher vitamin C and vitamin B6 in fruits compared to wild-type plants in natural soil.
mechanism: SlMYB12 upregulates flavonoid biosynthesis, which mediates rhizosphere microbiome restructuring and enhances vitamin accumulation through Lysobacter enrichment and spermidine production.

genes: OsIAAGLU (indole-3-acetic acid-amino acid synthetase, Oryza sativa L), OsOxO2 (oxalate oxidase 2, Oryza sativa L)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsIAAGLU in rice variety Dongjin (DJ) results in significantly exaggerated leaf angles (up to 45°) and decreased plant height (30% reduction) compared to wild-type, resembling the lc4 mutant phenotype.
mechanism: OsIAAGLU encodes an IAA-conjugating enzyme that generates IAA-glucose by conjugating free IAA to glucose, reducing auxin availability and altering cell wall development in lamina joints.

genes: OsOxO2 (oxalate oxidase 2, Oryza sativa L)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsOxO2 in rice variety Dongjin (DJ) results in only slight increases in leaf angle (5°) and minor reductions in plant height (10%) compared to wild-type, despite 20-fold increased OxO activity.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsOxO2 (oxalate oxidase 2, Oryza sativa L), OsIAAGLU (indole-3-acetic acid-amino acid synthetase, Oryza sativa L)
phenotype: CRISPR-mediated mutation of OsOxO2 and OsIAAGLU in lc4 background restores wild-type plant architecture (normal leaf angle and plant height) while maintaining comparable OxO activity and transcript levels of OsOxO1-4 and OsIAAGLU.
mechanism: OsOxO2 regulates OsOxO1, OsOxO3, and OsIAAGLU expression in a chromosome position-dependent manner, while OsIAAGLU directly modulates auxin availability through IAA conjugation.

genes: LOC110688032 (LOC110688032, hub gene involved in waterlogging stress response, quinoa)
phenotype: Overexpression of LOC110688032 in Arabidopsis enhances tolerance to waterlogging stress
mechanism: NA

genes: Badh2 (Os08g0424500, BADH2 gene, Oryza sativa), Se14 (Os03g0151300, Se14 gene, Oryza sativa), Wx (Os06g0133000, Waxy gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Triple knockout of Badh2/Se14/Wx in FH676 rice results in early-heading (109.5 days), glutinous (amylose content 1.64-1.95%), and aromatic (2-AP 64-102 µg/kg) traits with reduced plant height (117.8 cm vs 133.6 cm in wild type) and 8.6% lower total grain yield per plant.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in Badh2 (aromatic compound accumulation), Wx (glutinous phenotype via amylose reduction), and Se14 (early heading via RFT1 upregulation) genes.

genes: Badh2 (Os08g0424500, BADH2 gene, Oryza sativa), Wx (Os06g0133000, Waxy gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Double knockout of Badh2/Wx in FH676 rice results in glutinous (amylose content 1.64-1.95%), aromatic (2-AP 64-102 µg/kg) traits with minimal agronomic changes (plant height 133.6 cm, 1.4% lower 1,000-grain weight).
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in Badh2 (aromatic compound accumulation) and Wx (glutinous phenotype via amylose reduction) genes.

genes: RsPDR12 (Raphanus sativus PDR12, involved in reducing Cd accumulation under Cd stress, Raphanus sativus)
phenotype: RsPDR12 overexpression reduces Cd accumulation in Arabidopsis, with longer root length, higher fresh weight, and lower Cd content compared with WT under Cd treatment.
mechanism: RsPDR12 promotes Cd2+ efflux from plant roots under Cd stress.

genes: RsWRKY15 (Raphanus sativus WRKY15, transcription factor that reduces Cd accumulation, Raphanus sativus)
phenotype: RsWRKY15 overexpression reduces Cd accumulation in N. benthamiana, with longer roots, higher fresh weight, and lower Cd content under Cd treatment.
mechanism: RsWRKY15 reduces Cd2+ influx under Cd stress.

genes: RsPDR12 (Raphanus sativus PDR12, involved in reducing Cd accumulation under Cd stress, Raphanus sativus)
phenotype: RsPDR12 RNAi in radish increases Cd accumulation and ROS under Cd stress.
mechanism: NA

genes: RsWRKY15 (Raphanus sativus WRKY15, transcription factor that reduces Cd accumulation, Raphanus sativus)
phenotype: RsWRKY15 RNAi in radish increases Cd accumulation and ROS under Cd stress.
mechanism: NA

genes: HDA19 (HDA19, histone deacetylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: HDA19:GFP restores anthocyanin contents to wild-type levels in hda19 mutant (Figure 2F)
mechanism: HDA19 represses PAP1 expression to inhibit anthocyanin biosynthesis

genes: PAP1 (PAP1, MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PAP1-GUS and PAP1-RYmut-GUS constructs show GUS expression patterns in transgenic lines (Figure 4H)
mechanism: VAL1 and VAL2 recognize RY motifs at PAP1 to repress its expression

genes: VAL1 (VAL1, B3-domain transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: VAL1B3 specifically binds RY-box DNA probe in EMSA (Figure 4C)
mechanism: VAL1 recognizes RY motifs to recruit SNL–HDA19c to PAP1 chromatin

genes: PRPL11 (Plastid ribosomal protein L11, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (Green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of PRPL11-GFP in var2 plants results in similar leaf-variegation phenotypes and comparable proportions of cell types (type a, b, c) as in var2, with 86.83% of green-sector cells containing chloroplasts and 14.04% of white/yellow-sector cells being plastid-free.
mechanism: PRPL11-GFP labeling reveals plastid-free cells in var2 white/yellow sectors and confirms chloroplast presence in green sectors, indicating impaired chloroplast division in var2.

genes: PDV1 (Plastid division protein 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), FLAG (Protein tag, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PDV1-FLAG in var2 significantly alleviates leaf variegation, increasing green-sector area to ~90% compared to 71.68% in var2, with 22.2% of var2 cells containing >50 chloroplasts versus 10.6% in wild type.
mechanism: PDV1 overexpression rescues chloroplast division defects in var2, increasing chloroplast numbers and reducing plastid-free cells, thereby suppressing variegation.

genes: PDV2 (Plastid division protein 2, Arabidopsis thaliana), FLAG (Protein tag, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PDV2-FLAG in var2 significantly alleviates leaf variegation, increasing green-sector area to ~95% compared to 71.68% in var2, with 22.2% of var2 cells containing >50 chloroplasts versus 10.6% in wild type.
mechanism: PDV2 overexpression rescues chloroplast division defects in var2, increasing chloroplast numbers and reducing plastid-free cells, thereby suppressing variegation.

genes: ATG8a (Autophagy-related gene 8a, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (Green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP-ATG8a in var2 significantly suppresses leaf variegation, increasing green-sector area to ~90% compared to 71.68% in var2, with 22.2% of var2 cells containing >50 chloroplasts versus 10.6% in wild type.
mechanism: GFP-ATG8a overexpression promotes chloroplast division and chlorophagy, rescuing var2 chloroplast biogenesis defects and reducing plastid-free cells, thereby suppressing variegation.

genes: PsbS (photosystem II subunit S, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: 35S:PsbSP132A/npq4 Arabidopsis has a slower NPQ relaxation rate compared to wild type and 35S:PsbS/npq4 controls
mechanism: P132A mutation disrupts PsbS dimer conformation, reducing pH sensitivity and altering NPQ relaxation dynamics through structural changes in transmembrane helix 2

genes: PsbS (photosystem II subunit S, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: 35S:PsbSP132A+E122Q+E226Q/npq4 exhibits higher background NPQ without protonation compared to 35S:PsbSE122Q+E226Q/npq4
mechanism: Combined P132A, E122Q, and E226Q mutations alter PsbS dimer conformation and protonation state, enabling partial NPQ induction independent of lumenal pH changes

genes: ZmMs45 (male fertility gene, ZmMs45, Zea mays), ZmMs45-immune (fertility restoration gene, ZmMs45-immune, synthetic), ZmAA1 (pollen inactivation gene, ZmAA1, Zea mays), RUBY (visual marker gene, RUBY, synthetic)

mechanism: NA

mechanism: NA

genes: StHVA22m (StHVA22m, HVA22-like protein with three zinc finger domains, potato)

mechanism: NA

genes: GhGLDH35A (GhGLDH35A, L-galactono-1,4-lactone dehydrogenase, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Heterologous expression of GhGLDH35A in yeast improved its tolerance to alkaline stress.
mechanism: NA

phenotype: Silencing of GhGLDH35A in cotton resulted in reduced tolerance to alkaline stress, disruption of ROS homeostasis, and impairment of photosynthesis and stomatal function.
mechanism: GhGLDH35A knockdown disrupts AsA biosynthesis and antioxidant enzyme activity, leading to ROS accumulation and photosynthetic dysfunction.

mechanism: PbrDHAR5 catalyzes the reduction of DHA into AsA, improving AsA redox status and chilling tolerance. PbrAPX2 scavenges H2O2, reducing oxidative stress. PbrWRKY83 activates PbrDHAR5 transcription via binding to W-box elements in its promoter.

mechanism: GI and WRKY75 form a complex and synergistically activate SAG12 expression, leading to enhanced senescence.

mechanism: PgEXPA4 promotes cell expansion during root development by mediating cell wall modification.

mechanism: OfMYB21 activates OfTPS2 transcription, increasing linalool production.

genes: MdCWINV1 (cell wall invertase, Malus domestica)
phenotype: GUS activity in apple callus transiently coexpressing different combinations of MdCWINV1pro:GUS (HC-P1/P2, QG-P1/P2) and 35Spro:MdWRKY20 showed significantly lower activity in HC-P1 compared to other haplotypes when cotransformed with MdWRKY20.

genes: MdCWINV1 (cell wall invertase, Malus domestica)

mechanism: MdWRKY20 binds to the HC-P1 promoter (W-box element) to repress MdCWINV1 expression, reducing fructose content.

genes: SlBASS4 (SlBASS4, chloroplast inner envelope-localized symporter of pyruvate and Na+, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of SlBASS4 reduces salt tolerance in tomato, with increased Na+ accumulation, decreased K+ content, and higher ROS levels.
mechanism: SlBASS4 knockdown disrupts chloroplast ion homeostasis, impairs ROS scavenging, and downregulates salt stress-related genes (SlSOS1, SlSOS2, etc.).

genes: GmADH13 (alcohol dehydrogenase, Glycine max)

mechanism: GmADH13 enhances antioxidant activity, reduces ROS accumulation, and maintains ionic homeostasis to mitigate cellular damage.

genes: GmADH13 (alcohol dehydrogenase, Glycine max)
phenotype: Knockdown of GmADH13 reduces salt tolerance in soybean, leading to severe growth inhibition and leaf yellowing under NaCl stress.
mechanism: GmADH13 is essential for maintaining ionic homeostasis and ROS scavenging, which are disrupted in knockdown plants.

genes: GmADH13 (alcohol dehydrogenase, Glycine max)
phenotype: GmADH13-GFP fusion protein is localized in the cytoplasm of Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

mechanism: FvSnRK2.6 activates jasmonates biosynthesis and aroma production by phosphorylating FvJAZ12, promoting its degradation and enabling FvMYC2 to transcriptionally activate jasmonate biosynthesis genes.

mechanism: FvSnRK2.6 knockout inhibits jasmonates biosynthesis and aroma production by preventing phosphorylation of FvJAZ12, leading to its stabilization and suppression of FvMYC2 activity.

mechanism: FvJAZ12 complementation allows phosphorylation at S142 by FvSnRK2.6, promoting its degradation and enabling FvMYC2 to activate jasmonate biosynthesis genes.

genes: FvJAZ12 (FvJAZ12, mediator of flavor formation, Fragaria vesca)
phenotype: Complementation of FvJAZ12 S142A in FvJAZ12-CE background fails to restore ABA-induced ester production and aroma in Fragaria vesca.
mechanism: FvJAZ12 S142A mutation prevents phosphorylation by FvSnRK2.6, stabilizing FvJAZ12 and inhibiting FvMYC2 activity, thereby suppressing jasmonate biosynthesis and aroma production.

mechanism: Overexpression enhances HS-related gene expression

mechanism: Enhances cold tolerance by inhibiting leaf enlargement and improving cold resistance during germination and mature stages.

mechanism: TaNSUN2-RFP mediates m5C modification of CWMV RNAs, enhancing viral RNA stability and translation.

genes: DS2 (LOC_Os03g02460, short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase (SDR) with unknown function, Oryza sativa)

phenotype: Complementation of OsABA45 in salt-sensitive Caidao rice restores salt tolerance, with improved shoot/root fresh/dry weights and survival rates under 120 mM NaCl stress.
mechanism: OsABA45 negatively regulates salt tolerance by repressing ABA biosynthesis genes, reducing endogenous ABA levels, and modulating Na+/K+ homeostasis.

genes: OsABA45 (OsABA45, salt stress response gene, Oryza sativa)

mechanism: NA

mechanism: The PagHB7a promoter drives GUS expression in response to NaCl treatment, validated by histochemical staining and RT-qPCR.

genes: PagAREB1-3 (bZIP transcription factor, ABA-responsive, Populus alba × Populus glandulosa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PagAREB1-3-GFP confirms its nuclear localization and role in activating PagHB7a expression.
mechanism: PagAREB1-3 binds to ABRE motifs in the PagHB7a promoter, activating its expression under salt stress.

genes: PagHB7a (homeodomain-leucine zipper transcription factor, salt stress-induced, Populus alba × Populus glandulosa)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of PagHB7a results in increased salt sensitivity, with reduced biomass and elevated ROS levels under salt stress.
mechanism: Disruption of PagHB7a eliminates its regulatory role in ROS scavenging and salt stress adaptation.

mechanism: Nuclear localization of PagHB7a-GFP indicates its function in regulating gene expression under salt stress.

genes: MtCSP1 (CUL3 substrate-adaptor protein, Medicago truncatula)

mechanism: MtCSP1 overexpression enhances symbiotic organogenesis and modulates infection thread dynamics during rhizobial interaction.

mechanism: RIC4 overexpression stabilizes actin filaments, reducing actin dynamics and leading to increased cell circularity.

phenotype: Overexpression of mCherry::AtRIC4 increases cell circularity and solidity in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: RIC4 overexpression stabilizes actin filaments, reducing actin dynamics and leading to increased cell circularity.

genes: miR528 (miR528, microRNA targeting MaPPO, Musa acuminata)

mechanism: miR528 targets MaPPO (polyphenol oxidase), downregulating its expression to reduce peel browning under cold stress.

genes: miR528 (miR528, microRNA targeting MaPPO, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: Silencing of miR528 in ABB banana peel slices increases chilling injury index and peel browning, reducing cold tolerance.
mechanism: miR528 silencing leads to upregulation of MaPPO (polyphenol oxidase), exacerbating peel browning under cold stress.

Pb translocation and accumulation are restricted through cell wall fixation and vacuolar compartmentalization.

genes: GhGRDP1 (Glycine-rich domain protein, Gossypium hirsutum, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of GhGRDP1 reduces cotton seed size and weight without compromising fiber quality.
