genes: PtoCAF1I (PtoCAF1I, involved in plant development and ECM fungal symbiosis, Populus tomentosa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtoCAF1I increases shoot height by ~57% (12.62 cm vs. 8.02 cm in WT), branch numbers, biomass (fresh weight: 2.00 g vs. 0.89 g in WT; dry weight: 0.28 g vs. 0.13 g in WT), and root development (total root length and root tip number) in Populus tomentosa.
mechanism: PtoCAF1I, a CCR4–NOT complex–associated deadenylase, regulates mRNA deadenylation and post-transcriptional gene regulation, influencing root architecture, symbiotic compatibility, and ECM formation through pathways involving phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, ROS homeostasis, and flavonoid-mediated signaling.

genes: PtoCAF1I (PtoCAF1I, involved in plant development and ECM fungal symbiosis, Populus tomentosa)
phenotype: RNAi knockdown of PtoCAF1I reduces root tip number and total root length in Populus tomentosa (RNAi-PtoCAF1I-3: 53 ± 6 ECM root tips vs. 264 ± 22 in WT; ECM rate: 21% vs. 52% in WT), but does not affect shoot growth or biomass compared to wild type.
mechanism: PtoCAF1I, a CCR4–NOT complex–associated deadenylase, regulates mRNA deadenylation and post-transcriptional gene regulation, influencing root architecture, symbiotic compatibility, and ECM formation through pathways involving phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, ROS homeostasis, and flavonoid-mediated signaling.

genes: OsDi19-1 (Di19 transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: BD-OsDi19-1 exhibits significant transcriptional activation activity in rice protoplasts
mechanism: OsDi19-1 functions as a transcriptional activator in the nucleus

genes: OsDi19-1 (Di19 transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsDi19-1 promoter drives luciferase expression in rice protoplasts
mechanism: OsDi19-1 is induced by ABA and regulates ABA signaling pathway genes

genes: OsABI5 (bZIP transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsABI5-GFP binds to OsDi19-1 promoter in rice protoplasts
mechanism: OsABI5 directly activates OsDi19-1 expression via ABRE motifs

genes: SlFATB-03 (SlFATB-03, acyl-acyl carrier protein thioesterase, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlFATB-03 increases palmitic acid content in tomato roots by ~16-fold in line FATB3-4.
mechanism: CRISPR-Act3.0-mediated activation of SlFATB-03 enhances palmitic acid synthesis in root tissues.

genes: RjWRKY11 (WRKY transcription factor, R. japonica)
phenotype: Overexpression of RjWRKY11 enhances Cd tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana, as evidenced by increased root length and fresh weight under Cd stress compared to wild-type plants
mechanism: NA

genes: SDG102 (ZmSDG102, H3K36 methyltransferase, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of SDG102 enhances maize salt tolerance by activating antioxidant systems (21.3% increased SOD activity, 14.3% increased POD activity, 10.0% increased CAT activity) and reducing membrane damage (44.6% lower MDA content) while maintaining K+/Na+ ion homeostasis under 150 mM NaCl stress.
mechanism: SDG102 overexpression induces epigenetic remodeling (45,817 DMRs including 5,896 promoter-associated CHH hypomethylated regions) and transcriptional reprogramming (614 DEGs enriched in ion homeostasis, stress signaling, and ROS detoxification pathways). This epigenetic priming establishes a genomic environment predisposed to robust activation of antioxidant defense and ion homeostasis pathways during salt stress.

genes: OsTHIC (thiamine biosynthesis enzyme, Oryza sativa, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Editing the TPP riboswitch in OsTHIC increases vitamin B1 content in rice grains from 0.92 mg kg⁻¹ to 5.26–5.51 mg kg⁻¹, enhances photosynthetic capacity, improves nitrogen use efficiency, and confers resistance to rice blast and cold stress.
mechanism: TPP riboswitch editing disrupts feedback inhibition of thiamine biosynthesis, activates central carbon metabolism, and rewires transcriptional-metabolic networks to enhance growth, nutrient accumulation, and stress tolerance.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic), CaMV35S (promoter, synthetic), Nos (terminator, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of GFP results in green fluorescence in tobacco cells and leaves, detectable via confocal microscopy and RT-qPCR.
mechanism: AX+ nanocarriers facilitate electrostatic complexation and delivery of pDNA into plant cells, enabling transgene expression through stomatal uptake and apoplastic infiltration.

genes: BnaC03.SEIPIN1 (BnaC03.SEIPIN1, gene involved in lipid droplet regulation, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnaC03.SEIPIN1 increases seed oil content by 4.3–5.4% and thousand-seed weight by 0.43–0.49 g in Brassica napus.
mechanism: BnaC03.SEIPIN1 significantly increases the number of small and large LDs, but does not affect LDs size.

genes: BnaA09.SEIPIN2 (BnaA09.SEIPIN2, gene involved in lipid droplet regulation, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnaA09.SEIPIN2 does not significantly affect seed oil content in Brassica napus.
mechanism: NA

genes: Ah6Q1KS5 (Ah6Q1KS5, S-adenosylmethionine synthetase, peanut)
phenotype: Overexpression of Ah6Q1KS5 in peanut and tobacco reduces cell death and significantly inhibits bacterial growth, confirming its role in positively regulating bacterial wilt resistance responses.
mechanism: Ah6Q1KS5 positively regulates bacterial wilt resistance responses

genes: RNHL-D1 (RNase H-like protein 1, Triticum aestivum, D-subgenome)
phenotype: Overexpression of RNHL-D1 increases plant height, spike length, and internode length in wheat.
mechanism: RNHL1 acts as a positive regulator of culm and spike elongation in wheat.

genes: TaEIL1 (ETHYLENE-INSENSITIVE3-LIKE 1, Triticum aestivum, D-subgenome)
phenotype: eil1 mutants exhibit reduced plant height, spike length, and shortened internodes compared to wild-type.
mechanism: TaEIL1 is essential for normal internode elongation and plant height establishment in wheat.

genes: TaEIL1 (ETHYLENE-INSENSITIVE3-LIKE 1, Triticum aestivum, D-subgenome)
phenotype: TaEIL1 overexpression produces marginal effects on plant height, with line #1 showing a modest increase.
mechanism: TaEIL1 positively regulates internode elongation in wheat.

genes: TaERF1 (Ethylene-response-factor 1, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: TaERF1 overexpression reduces plant height primarily due to decreased internode length.
mechanism: TaERF1 represses TaGA3ox2 expression, inhibiting bioactive GA production.

genes: TaGA3ox2 (Gibberellin 3-beta dioxygenase 2, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: TaGA3ox2 knockout results in extreme dwarfism with near-complete inhibition of culm elongation.
mechanism: TaGA3ox2 is essential for GA biosynthesis, and its loss leads to reduced bioactive GA levels.

genes: PpWRKY13 (PpWRKY13, WRKY domain transcription factor, Prunus persica)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpWRKY13 activates transcription of PpXTH33 and functions as a putative modulator of peach fruit softening
mechanism: PpWRKY13 activates the transcription of PpXTH33, a fruit softening-related gene

genes: ZmSKIP (Zm00001d052186, transcription factor and spliceosome component, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmSKIP increases drought tolerance in maize by reducing stomatal aperture, transpiration rate, and water loss rate under drought stress conditions.
mechanism: ZmSKIP suppresses ZmBAG8 expression via the 'TAATA' motif in its promoter. Under drought stress, ZmSnRK2.3 phosphorylates ZmSKIP at Ser236 and Ser244, enhancing its stability and inhibitory effect on ZmBAG8, which regulates stomatal aperture to reduce water loss.

genes: OsbHLH148 (OsbHLH148, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsbHLH148 causes dwarf plant phenotype with significant reduction in tiller number and ~72% decrease in grain yield per plant in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsbHLH148 modulates gene networks associated with protein phosphorylation, MAPK signaling, and secondary metabolite biosynthesis, regulating hormone signaling pathways (auxin and gibberellin), calcium signaling, and carbon/nitrogen metabolism to inhibit tillering.

genes: AtVPS29 (Arabidopsis thaliana VPS29, retromer complex subunit, ubiquitination target), COP1 (Constitutive Photomorphogenesis 1, E3 ubiquitin ligase)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtVPS29 increases protein levels in Arabidopsis thaliana, with MG132 treatment further elevating levels by ~2.83-fold in 35S-AtVPS29-HA3/WT plants and ~4.16-fold in 35S-AtVPS29-HA3/cop1-6 plants.
mechanism: AtVPS29 is ubiquitinated by COP1 and degraded via the 26S proteasome. COP1 physically interacts with AtVPS29 through its WD40 domain and coiled-coil dimerization domain, promoting ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation.

genes: COP1 (Constitutive Photomorphogenesis 1, E3 ubiquitin ligase)
phenotype: Overexpression of COP1 reduces AtVPS29 protein levels in Arabidopsis thaliana by ~50% upon β-estradiol induction, with no significant change in AtVPS29 transcript levels.
mechanism: COP1 ubiquitinates AtVPS29, targeting it for proteasomal degradation. COP1 interacts with AtVPS29 via its WD40 domain and requires dimerization for this interaction. β-estradiol-inducible expression of COP1-Myc6 leads to AtVPS29 destabilization.

genes: rolA (root oncogenic locus A, R. rhizogenes T-DNA, R. rhizogenes), rolB (root oncogenic locus B, R. rhizogenes T-DNA, R. rhizogenes), rolC (root oncogenic locus C, R. rhizogenes T-DNA, R. rhizogenes), rolD (root oncogenic locus D, R. rhizogenes T-DNA, R. rhizogenes), aux1 (auxin biosynthesis gene 1, R. rhizogenes T-DNA, R. rhizogenes), aux2 (auxin biosynthesis gene 2, R. rhizogenes T-DNA, R. rhizogenes), mas1 (mannopine synthase, R. rhizogenes T-DNA, R. rhizogenes), ags (agropine synthase, R. rhizogenes T-DNA, R. rhizogenes)
phenotype: Ri genotypes exhibit enhanced in vitro root growth with increased root numbers and lengths, shorter internodes, smaller leaves, and reduced shoot and root dry mass compared to wild-types. Potato Ri genotypes show reduced tuber mass but no consistent root hair traits in roses.
mechanism: Altered auxin and cytokinin homeostasis, with increased cytokinins (DHZR, tZR) in stems and elevated IAA in roots. Aux2 expression negatively correlates with leaf IAA content and leaflet size.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic), DsRed (Discosoma striata red fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Reporter gene expression (GFP and DsRed) used for visualization and tracking of Ri genotypes during transformation and regeneration.
mechanism: NA

genes: SMXL4 (Os04g0298700, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: SMXL4-edited rice (smxl4) exhibits short stature (culm length 70.2 cm, 17.7 cm shorter than Samkwang), reduced panicle length (15.5 cm vs 19.4 cm in Samkwang), increased panicle number (14.3 vs 11.7 in Samkwang), reduced grain number per panicle (112.8 vs 136.7 in Samkwang), reduced 1000-grain weight (21.1 g vs 24.5 g in Samkwang), and 22% lower yield per plot compared to Samkwang.
mechanism: SMXL4 knockout induces cell wall remodeling (upregulated BURP16, GNS11, CSLD3) and alters growth-defense balance (upregulated defense-related genes like PID3, OsTPS4, JA Upregulated Protein 1). Reduced assimilate transport to grain likely contributes to yield reduction.

genes: SLOMO (mCherry-SLOMO, name, synthetic), SLOMO (mCherry-SLOMO-Decoy, name, synthetic)
phenotype: 35S-mediated overexpression of mCherry:SLOMO resulted in a delayed primary root response to gravity compared to Col-0.
mechanism: SLOMO modulates auxin transport by influencing both the abundance and activity of the auxin influx carrier AUX1.

genes: AUX1 (AUX1:YFP, name, synthetic), AUX1 (AUX13K>R:YFP, name, synthetic)
phenotype: AUX13K>R variant displayed reduced ubiquitination and impaired auxin transport activity compared to wild-type AUX1.
mechanism: Ubiquitination of K261, K264, and K266 residues in AUX1 enhances its transport activity, likely via SLOMO-mediated ubiquitination.

genes: SLOMO (GFP:SLOMO, name, synthetic)
phenotype: Tissue-specific expression of SLOMO in the root cap and epidermis rescued the slomo-3 phenotype.
mechanism: SLOMO activity in the root cap and epidermis is sufficient to confer AUX1 regulation during gravitropic response.

genes: OsTZF1 (OsTZF1, CCCH-TZF protein that confers delayed senescence and stress tolerance in rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsTZF1-RNAi plants showed enhanced susceptibility to M. oryzae isolates RB22 and RO1-1, with increased fungal biomass in the lesion area.
mechanism: OsTZF1 enhances the transcript levels of OsSGT1 and OsKS4, which are involved in defense responses.

genes: OsTZF1 (OsTZF1, CCCH-TZF protein that confers delayed senescence and stress tolerance in rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsTZF1 knockout in the ZH11 background enhanced resistance to virulent isolates RB22, CHE86, and GZ8 without growth penalty.
mechanism: OsTZF1 knockout leads to increased Piz-t transcript levels, enhancing resistance.

genes: DS1 (DAHPS2, entry enzyme of the shikimate pathway, Oryza sativa), RR26 (type-B CK response regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of the ds1 mutant fully rescued the mutant phenotypes, restoring normal growth and fertility.
mechanism: DS1 encodes DAHPS2, which catalyzes the condensation of phosphoenolpyruvate and erythrose-4-phosphate to form 3-deoxy-D-arabino-heptulosonate 7-phosphate, a key step in aromatic amino acid biosynthesis. RR26 activates DS1 transcription, maintaining IAA biosynthesis and suppressing JA accumulation.

genes: DS1 (DAHPS2, entry enzyme of the shikimate pathway, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CRISPR–Cas9 knockout lines phenocopied the ds1 mutant, exhibiting disrupted DAHPS2 protein structures and pleiotropic developmental defects.
mechanism: DS1 encodes DAHPS2, which catalyzes the condensation of phosphoenolpyruvate and erythrose-4-phosphate to form 3-deoxy-D-arabino-heptulosonate 7-phosphate, a key step in aromatic amino acid biosynthesis. Mutation of DS1 compromises IAA biosynthesis and elevates JA accumulation.

genes: DS1 (DAHPS2, entry enzyme of the shikimate pathway, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: DS1 overexpression significantly enhanced postgermination growth, with longer coleoptiles, first incomplete leaves, and radicles, and improved submergence tolerance under both laboratory and field conditions.
mechanism: DS1 encodes DAHPS2, which catalyzes the condensation of phosphoenolpyruvate and erythrose-4-phosphate to form 3-deoxy-D-arabino-heptulosonate 7-phosphate, a key step in aromatic amino acid biosynthesis. Overexpression of DS1 elevates IAA levels and suppresses JA accumulation, promoting rapid postgermination growth.

genes: RR26 (type-B CK response regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RR26 overexpression increased DS1 transcript abundance and enhanced submergence tolerance, closely resembling the DS1 overexpression phenotype.
mechanism: RR26 directly binds to the DS1 promoter at the DS1-7 element to activate DS1 expression, functioning as a key upstream positive regulator of postgermination growth. RR26 also participates in hormonal regulation during early seedling development, contributing to auxin and JA homeostasis.

genes: DS1 (DAHPS2, entry enzyme of the shikimate pathway, Oryza sativa)
gene_construct: ePE2-mediated editing of the DS1-7 promoter element
phenotype: Precision editing of the DS1-7 element in the promoter increased DS1 transcript levels and improved submergence tolerance without detectable developmental abnormalities.
mechanism: Targeted integration of three tandem copies of the RR26-binding motif DS1-7 into the native DS1 promoter enhanced DS1 expression, leading to elevated IAA levels and suppressed JA accumulation, promoting robust postgermination growth and submergence tolerance.

genes: OsNF-YC8 (regulates endosperm development, rice, native), OsNF-YC9 (regulates endosperm development, rice, native), OsNF-YC10 (regulates endosperm development, rice, native)
phenotype: Triple mutation of OsNF-YC8/9/10 results in chalky endosperm with ~100% grain chalkiness, round loosely packed starch granules, and altered amylopectin chain length distribution in rice.
mechanism: OsNF-YC8/9/10 transcriptionally activate SBE3 by binding the AAGAGG motif in its promoter. Triple knockout reduces SBE3 expression by ~50%, alters amylopectin chain length distribution (increased B2/B3 chains, decreased A/B1 chains), and disrupts starch granule morphology.

genes: LcOFP3 (Litchi chinensis ovate family protein 3, transcriptional regulator, Litchi chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of LcOFP3 in tomato results in heart-shaped fruits with reduced transverse diameter (1.2-fold decrease), lateral diameter (1.5-fold decrease), and single fruit weight (1.8-fold decrease) compared to wild type, while longitudinal diameter remains unchanged
mechanism: NA

genes: HvSCAMP1 (HvSCAMP1, salt tolerance regulator, Hordeum vulgare L.)
phenotype: Overexpression of HvSCAMP1 in Arabidopsis thaliana enhances salt stress tolerance, associated with increased antioxidant enzyme activity, elevated osmoprotectant accumulation, reduced oxidative damage, and decreased leaf Na+ accumulation.
mechanism: HvSCAMP1 positively regulates salt tolerance through antioxidant enzyme activity, osmoprotectant accumulation, and Na+ homeostasis regulation.

genes: RaDFR2 (Dihydroflavonol 4-reductase 2, structural gene for anthocyanins biosynthesis, Rosa agastum)
phenotype: Enhanced anthocyanins accumulation in transgenic tobacco by up-regulating structural and regulatory genes
mechanism: RaDFR2 catalyzes dihydroquercetin and dihydromyricetin, restoring anthocyanins biosynthesis in Arabidopsis tt3 mutant

genes: OsLAT5 (OsLAT5, polyamine uptake transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Loss-of-function mutations in OsLAT5 confer resistance to methyl viologen (MV) in rice calli, seedlings, and seeds.
mechanism: Disruption of OsLAT5/OsPUT3/OsPAR1 function leads to MV resistance by preventing MV-induced cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) and photodestruction of chlorophyll.

genes: OsLAT1 (OsLAT1, polyamine uptake transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Loss-of-function mutations in OsLAT1 do not confer resistance to methyl viologen (MV) in rice.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsLAT7 (OsLAT7, polyamine uptake transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Loss-of-function mutations in OsLAT7 do not confer resistance to methyl viologen (MV) in rice.
mechanism: NA

genes: CHLI2 (CHLI2, single-copy endogenous gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), MC4 (MC4, 20-bp sequence repeated at 8 loci spanning diverse chromatin environments, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Heat stress significantly increases CRISPR editing rates across chromatin contexts, with 29.9-fold increases in heterochromatic regions and 1.2-3.6-fold increases in 1-bp insertion rates at CHLI2 and MC4 sites under 3× 37°C heat stress
mechanism: Heat stress induces DNA Polλ expression (4.6-fold increase in wild-type plants), which mediates error-prone repair of CRISPR-Cas9-induced double-strand breaks, leading to increased 1-bp insertions and transversion mutations

genes: HaNAC11 (HaNAC11, NAC transcription factor, H. ammodendron)
phenotype: Enhanced plant adaptation to high-temperature and wind stress in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Regulating glycerolipid metabolism; in particular, upregulation of glycerolipid metabolism pathways and triacylglycerol accumulation under normal and high-temperature conditions.

genes: gRNA1 (reference, reference gRNA), gRNA2 (variable, variable gRNA)
phenotype: Inversion frequencies vary with genomic distance, reaching up to 1.24% for ~1MB intervals and declining to 0.18% for 37.5MB intervals despite efficient gRNAs.
mechanism: gRNA cutting efficiency is a major determinant of inversion frequency up to ~1MB, while larger inversions face size-dependent constraints. Dual gRNA activity is required for inversions, with large deletions more frequent than inversions when dual breaks occur.

genes: cgr-miR166 (cgr-miR166, microRNA, Chrysanthemum)
phenotype: Under salt treatment, transgenic Arabidopsis plants showed significantly higher seed germination rate and root length compared to wild type. POD and CAT activities were significantly increased, while MDA showed no significant change.
mechanism: miR166 targets and regulates members of the HD-ZipIII family, which are suppressed in transgenic plants. The gene is related to plant hormones and salt stress response.

genes: miR156a (microRNA, regulatory element, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR156a increases lateral branch length by ~3x in 5-week-old tomato plants compared to wild-type.
mechanism: miR156a downregulates SPL13, which in turn upregulates BRC1b and downregulates DWF to promote lateral branch outgrowth.

genes: SPL13 (SQUAMOSA PROMOTER-BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE 13, transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SPL13 reduces lateral branch length to ~1/3 of wild-type in 5-week-old tomato plants.
mechanism: SPL13 upregulates BRC1b and downregulates DWF to suppress lateral branch outgrowth.

genes: DWF (DWARF, BRASSINOSTEROID BIOSYNTHESIS, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: DWF knockout (CR-dwf) in spl13 mutant background reduces lateral branch length by ~50% compared to spl13 single mutant.
mechanism: DWF knockout suppresses the increased lateral branch length phenotype of spl13 mutant by altering BR biosynthesis.

genes: BRC1b (BRANCHED 1b, transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: BRC1b overexpression (BRC1b-OE/flag) in spl13 mutant background reduces lateral branch length by ~50% compared to spl13 single mutant.
mechanism: BRC1b overexpression suppresses the increased lateral branch length phenotype of spl13 mutant by enhancing BRC1b expression.

genes: PnSUS1 (sucrose synthetase, Panax notoginseng), PnWRKY38 (WRKY transcription factor, Panax notoginseng)
phenotype: Co-overexpression of PnSUS1 and PnWRKY38 increases UDPG content by 2.3-fold and total saponin content by 1.68-fold in P. notoginseng cells compared to wild type.
mechanism: PnWRKY38 activates PnSUS1 transcription via W-box motifs, increasing UDPG supply for saponin glycosylation. PnSUS1 catalyzes UDP to UDPG, which is used by UGTs to synthesize saponins.

genes: PnSUS1 (sucrose synthetase, Panax notoginseng)
phenotype: Overexpression of PnSUS1 increases UDPG content by 1.81-fold and total saponin content by 1.24-fold in P. notoginseng cells compared to wild type.
mechanism: PnSUS1 catalyzes UDP to UDPG, which serves as a sugar donor for saponin glycosylation. Increased UDPG availability enhances UGT activity, leading to higher saponin accumulation.

genes: PnSUS1 (sucrose synthetase, Panax notoginseng)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated silencing of PnSUS1 reduces UDPG content by over 50% and total saponin content by over 50% in P. notoginseng cells compared to wild type.
mechanism: Reduced PnSUS1 expression lowers UDPG availability, decreasing the substrate for saponin glycosylation and downstream UGT activity.

genes: PnWRKY38 (WRKY transcription factor, Panax notoginseng)
phenotype: Overexpression of PnWRKY38 increases PnSUS1 expression by 3.5-fold, UDPG content by 68%, and total saponin content by 2.1- to 2.4-fold in P. notoginseng cells compared to wild type.
mechanism: PnWRKY38 binds to W-box motifs in the PnSUS1 promoter, activating its transcription. Increased PnSUS1 expression enhances UDPG production, which fuels saponin glycosylation.

genes: miR1507c (gma-miR1507c-3p, microRNA, synthetic), CsNADH-GOGAT (glutamate synthase, Camellia sinensis), lncR12304.1 (long non-coding RNA, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Co-expression of miR1507c with CsNADH-GOGAT or lncR12304.1 in tobacco leaves significantly reduced luciferase activity and altered gene expression profiles, with CsNADH-GOGAT expression suppressed by miR1507c and enhanced by lncR12304.1.
mechanism: miR1507c directly targets CsNADH-GOGAT and lncR12304.1, while lncR12304.1 acts as a competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) to sponge miR1507c, alleviating its repression on CsNADH-GOGAT.

genes: CsNADH-GOGAT (glutamate synthase, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsNADH-GOGAT in tobacco significantly increased L-glutamate accumulation, with expression levels mirroring glutamate profiles, particularly at the fourth day post-transformation.
mechanism: CsNADH-GOGAT catalyzes glutamate synthesis, which is a precursor for theanine biosynthesis. Overexpression enhances amino acid metabolism.

genes: miR1507c (gma-miR1507c-3p, microRNA, synthetic), CsNADH-GOGAT (glutamate synthase, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Co-expression of miR1507c and CsNADH-GOGAT in tobacco led to suppressed CsNADH-GOGAT expression at the fourth day post-transformation, consistent with miR1507c-mediated repression.
mechanism: miR1507c directly targets CsNADH-GOGAT mRNA for cleavage, reducing its expression and glutamate synthesis.

genes: miR1507c (gma-miR1507c-3p, microRNA, synthetic), CsNADH-GOGAT (glutamate synthase, Camellia sinensis), lncR12304.1 (long non-coding RNA, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Co-expression of miR1507c, CsNADH-GOGAT, and lncR12304.1 in tobacco resulted in significantly higher CsNADH-GOGAT expression compared to miR1507c + CsNADH-GOGAT co-expression, demonstrating lncR12304.1's ceRNA activity.
mechanism: lncR12304.1 competes with CsNADH-GOGAT for miR1507c binding, reducing miR1507c's repressive effect on CsNADH-GOGAT and enhancing amino acid biosynthesis.

genes: CsNADH-GOGATm3 (mutant glutamate synthase, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: CsNADH-GOGATm3, with a 3-base insertion preventing miR1507c cleavage, showed no significant difference in luciferase activity compared to wild-type CsNADH-GOGAT when co-expressed with miR1507c.
mechanism: The mutation in CsNADH-GOGATm3 disrupts miR1507c binding, confirming the specificity of miR1507c's targeting.

genes: WDR48 (phototropin substrate, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic sequence)
phenotype: Phosphodefective S393A variant failed to restore blue light-dependent starch degradation and stomatal opening in wdr48-1 mutant
mechanism: Phosphorylation of WDR48 at Ser-393 is essential for its function in blue light-dependent starch degradation and stomatal opening

genes: WDR48 (phototropin substrate, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic sequence)
phenotype: Phosphomimetic S393E variant complemented the inhibition of starch degradation and stomatal opening in wdr48-1 mutant
mechanism: Phosphorylation of WDR48 at Ser-393 is essential for its function in blue light-dependent starch degradation and stomatal opening

genes: ZmMYB71 (ZmMYB71, negative regulator of starch biosynthesis, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmMYB71 decreases kernel starch content by 1.70%–4.91% in Zea mays.
mechanism: ZmMYB71 suppresses key starch biosynthesis genes (Sh1, Sh2, GBSSI) and reduces enzyme activities (AGPase, GBSS, SSS) by 3.26%–21.39%.

genes: PrpS1 (self-incompatibility receptor, Papaver rhoeas, synthetic), LifeAct-mRuby2 (actin-binding protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of PrpS1 enables SI response in Arabidopsis pollen tubes; LifeAct-mRuby2 labels F-actin for visualization
mechanism: PrpS1 mediates SI response when bound to PrsS1; LifeAct-mRuby2 allows real-time actin cytoskeleton imaging during SI

genes: roGFP2-Orp1 (H2O2 sensor, synthetic)
phenotype: Enables ratiometric detection of H2O2 dynamics in cytosol, mitochondria, plastids, peroxisomes, and nuclei during SI response
mechanism: Orp1 cysteine residue oxidation by H2O2 triggers roGFP2 oxidation, altering fluorescence excitation spectrum for ratiometric H2O2 measurement

genes: CtCYP41 (CtCYP41, involved in flavonoid synthesis, ROS clearance, and drought response, Carthamus tinctorius)
phenotype: Overexpression of CtCYP41 in Arabidopsis and transient expression in tobacco significantly enhanced flavonoid content and drought tolerance, as well as the reduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS).
mechanism: CtCYP41 may play a positive role in these processes of flavonoid synthesis, ROS clearance and drought response.

genes: 2CPA (2-Cys PRX A, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), 2CPA-CP-S (2-Cys PRX A, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
gene_construct: 2-Cys PRX A promoter-2CPA-myc-NA---2-Cys PRX A promoter-2CPA-CP-S-myc-NA
phenotype: Overexpression of 2CPA-myc fully complements the 2cpab mutant phenotype, while 2CPA-CP-S-myc results in 19% albino and 31% variegated/asymmetric cotyledons in sucrose medium.
mechanism: The redox-active form of 2-Cys PRX is partially required for cotyledon development; the Cys-to-Ser mutation abolishes dimerization and redox activity.

genes: 2CPA (2-Cys PRX A, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), 2CPB (2-Cys PRX B, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
gene_construct: 2-Cys PRX A promoter-2CPA-GFP-NA---2-Cys PRX B promoter-2CPB-GFP-NA
phenotype: Confocal microscopy confirmed the pattern of expression of 2-Cys PRXs A and B in developing cotyledons and true leaves, showing plastid localization.
mechanism: The localization of 2-Cys PRXs A and B in plastids supports their role in chloroplast differentiation.

genes: NTRC (NTRC, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: NTRC-OE #1 and #2 lines show 33-42% albino and 25-40% variegated/asymmetric cotyledons in sucrose medium, mimicking the 2cpab mutant phenotype.
mechanism: Overexpression of NTRC causes plastid redox imbalance, impairing cotyledon development via over-reduction of chloroplast enzymes.

genes: cpHSP70-1 (cpHSP70-1, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: cphsp70-1 mutants show variegated/asymmetric cotyledons, and 2cpab-cphsp70-1 mutants exhibit severe cotyledon developmental defects with 80% purple cotyledons.
mechanism: The combined loss of 2-Cys PRXs and cpHSP70-1 disrupts chloroplast biogenesis, indicating their concerted action in proteostasis during cotyledon development.

genes: AtPOT1a (Arabidopsis thaliana telomere protection 1a, telomere protection, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtPOT1b (Arabidopsis thaliana telomere protection 1b, telomere protection, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation with CaMV35S::FLAG-Myc-POT1a rescued developmental defects in pot1a pot1b double mutants, restoring normal growth and biomass in G3/T1 plants.
mechanism: AtPOT1a promotes telomerase activity and genome stability by synergizing with AtPOT1b to maintain telomere length and prevent chromosome end fusions.

genes: PpPOT1 (Physcomitrium patens telomere protection 1, telomere protection, Physcomitrium patens)
phenotype: Complementation with UBQ10::FLAG-Myc-PpPOT1 rescued telomere length and developmental defects in pot1a pot1b double mutants, demonstrating functional conservation of POT1 across species.
mechanism: PpPOT1 from Physcomitrium patens interacts with telomerase and telomere-associated proteins to maintain telomere length and genome stability in Arabidopsis.

genes: CAT2 (catalase 2, antioxidant enzyme, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CAT2 in pot1b mutants restored ROS levels to wild-type levels in seeds and seedlings, reducing genomic oxidation and rescuing biomass.
mechanism: CAT2 interacts with AtPOT1b to enhance peroxisomal ROS detoxification, protecting telomeres and the genome from oxidative damage.

genes: AtPOT1b (Arabidopsis thaliana telomere protection 1b, telomere protection, Arabidopus thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation with pPOT1b::FLAG-Myc-POT1b rescued the developmental defects of pot1b mutants, restoring normal growth and telomere length.
mechanism: AtPOT1b localizes to telomeres and peroxisomes, interacting with catalase to regulate ROS homeostasis and prevent telomere oxidation.

genes: ShAP2-1 (ShAP2-1, AP2 transcription factor, Saccharum hybrid)
phenotype: Overexpression of ShAP2-1 enhances drought tolerance in transgenic rice by promoting primary root growth (2.4-fold) to improve water uptake and mitigating oxidative stress through elevated superoxide dismutase activity and reduced malondialdehyde accumulation.
mechanism: ShAP2-1 promotes root growth for water acquisition and activates antioxidant defenses for cellular protection.

genes: LET7 (AT2G42810, phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of let7-2 with LET7 restores RNAi-MEKK1-induced growth defects.
mechanism: LET7 plays an important role in regulating RNAi-MEKK1-triggered cell death.

genes: LET7TPR (AT2G42810, TPR domain, Arabidopsis thaliana), LET7PPase (AT2G42810, PPase domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: LET7TPR failed to complement RNAi-MEKK1-triggered growth defects; LET7PPase partially restored growth defects.
mechanism: LET7PPase is sufficient to trigger cell death.

genes: LET7 (AT2G42810, phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: LET7(H290N) failed to restore RNAi-MEKK1-triggered growth defects or PR1 expression in let7-2.
mechanism: Phosphatase activity is much reduced in LET7(H290N).

genes: LET7 (AT2G42810, phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of LET7W372F induces growth defects, cell death, and H2O2 production.
mechanism: Phosphatase activity is positively correlated with autoimmunity.

genes: HOP1 (AT1G12270, co-chaperone, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of HOP1–GFP restores RNAi-MEKK1-induced growth defects and PR1 expression in hop1-2.
mechanism: HOP1 interacts with LET7 and is required for mekk1-triggered cell death.

genes: SUMM2 (SUMM2ac, active form, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SUMM2ac-triggered growth defects are alleviated in let7-2.
mechanism: SUMM2ac triggers cell death.

genes: FRO6 (FRO6, ferric reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Cell-type-specific overexpression of FRO6 weakened the stress-avoidance response in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: NA

genes: FRO6 (FRO6, ferric reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Cell-type-specific overexpression of FRO6 weakened the stress-avoidance response in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: NA

genes: mCherry-HDEL (mCherry-HDEL, synthetic)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (GUS, beta-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: GmNPF6.8 (GmNPF6.8, plasma membrane-localized nitrate transporter, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmNPF6.8 reduces root length and root density in Arabidopsis and soybean hairy roots
mechanism: GmARF11 directly binds to the promoter of GmNPF6.8 and represses its transcription

genes: GmAux/IAA16 (GmAux/IAA16, regulates root morphogenesis and low-phosphorus (LP) responses, Glycine max)
phenotype: Stable overexpression enhanced root development and maintained physiological stability under phosphate deprivation, with 27.75% increased IAAO activity, 123.55% increased CAT activity, elevated ATP levels, and higher endogenous IAA/JA/SA levels in tobacco roots under LP stress.
mechanism: GmAux/IAA16 coordinates hormonal responses (IAA, JA, SA) and transcriptional regulation of phosphate-starvation response genes to facilitate LP adaptation.

genes: NtJMJ19 (NtJMJ19, related to nicotine biosynthesis, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Knockout of NtJMJ19 decreases nicotine and JA content in tobacco
mechanism: NtJMJ19 is involved in nicotine biosynthesis

genes: SlCDF4 (SlCDF4, DOF transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Knockout of SlCDF4 compromises the growth of tomato seedlings under LN stress, reducing root length and fresh weight.
mechanism: SlCDF4 knockout leads to downregulation of genes involved in N assimilation and JA biosynthesis.

genes: CAP1 (Arabidopsis thaliana, coding sequence, synthetic), RCAR12 (Arabidopsis thaliana, coding sequence, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of CAP1 reduces drought resilience and increases stomatal aperture in response to ABA, leading to wilting and lower survival rates under drought stress.
mechanism: CAP1 negatively regulates ABA-induced stomatal closure by destabilizing F-actin in guard cells, preventing actin reorganization necessary for stomatal closure.

genes: RCAR12 (Arabidopsis thaliana, coding sequence, synthetic)
phenotype: RCAR12-GFP expression in guard cells allows visualization of ABA receptor localization and interaction with CAP1.
mechanism: RCAR12 interacts with CAP1 to regulate F-actin stability in guard cells, modulating ABA-induced stomatal closure.

genes: CAP1 (Arabidopsis thaliana, coding sequence, native promoter)
phenotype: Complementation of the cap1–1 mutant with CAP1 under its native promoter rescues the ABA-induced stomatal closure phenotype.
mechanism: CAP1 complements the cap1–1 mutant by restoring normal F-actin dynamics and ABA responsiveness in guard cells.

genes: ACTIN (Arabidopsis thaliana, promoter UBQ10), lifeact (synthetic, coding sequence)
phenotype: Expression of lifeact-GFP in guard cells allows visualization of F-actin dynamics during stomatal movement.
mechanism: Lifeact-GFP labels F-actin to monitor actin reorganization in guard cells under ABA treatment and during stomatal closure.

genes: OST1 (Arabidopsis thaliana, coding sequence, CaMV35S promoter)
phenotype: Overexpression of OST1 rescues the ABA-insensitive stomatal closure phenotype of OE-CAP1 plants.
mechanism: OST1 phosphorylates CAP1, inhibiting its interaction with ADF4 and thus modulating F-actin disassembly during stomatal closure.

genes: ADA2b (Arabidopsis thaliana, DNA repair protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ADA2b increases DNA damage resistance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: COP1 interacts with ADA2b to mediate its ubiquitination and degradation via the 26S proteasome pathway.

genes: SMC5 (Arabidopsis thaliana, structural maintenance of chromosomes protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SMC5 increases DNA repair efficiency in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SMC5 recruitment to DNA double-strand breaks is partially restored in cop1-4 mutant background.

genes: COP1 (Arabidopsis thaliana, E3 ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of COP1 reduces DNA damage resistance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: COP1 interacts with ADA2b to mediate its ubiquitination and degradation via the 26S proteasome pathway.

genes: ADA2b (Arabidopsis thaliana, DNA repair protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), COP1 (Arabidopsis thaliana, E3 ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-overexpression of ADA2b and COP1 in Arabidopsis thaliana reveals their interaction in DNA repair pathways.
mechanism: COP1 interacts with ADA2b to mediate its ubiquitination and degradation via the 26S proteasome pathway.

genes: SRK01 (S-locus receptor kinase, Arabidopsis halleri), SCR01 (S-locus cysteine-rich protein, Arabidopsis halleri)
phenotype: Expression of SRK01 and SCR01 in A. thaliana recreates self-incompatibility: pollen from SCR01-expressing males fails to germinate on SRK01-expressing pistils (incompatible reaction).
mechanism: SRK01-SCR01 cognate recognition triggers self-incompatibility by preventing pollen germination.

genes: Ah20mirS3 (sRNA precursor, Arabidopsis halleri)
phenotype: Overexpression of Ah20mirS3 in SCR01-expressing males transforms incompatible SRK01-SCR01 interactions into compatible ones, with ~10-fold reduction in SCR01 transcript abundance.
mechanism: Ah20mirS3-derived sRNAs target SCR01 intronic region, reducing transcript levels below threshold required for self-incompatibility.

genes: SCR01*mir1887 (SCR01 with five point mutations disrupting Ah04mir1887 homology, Arabidopsis halleri)
phenotype: SCR01*mir1887 transgene shows increased basal transcript levels in polIV and polV mutants, suggesting RdDM-mediated repression of transgenes.
mechanism: Point mutations in SCR01*mir1887 disrupt homology with Ah04mir1887 sRNAs, but transgene remains targeted by RdDM pathway.

genes: AHAS (acetohydroxyacid synthase, mutant proline197 to serine, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter, CaMV35S promoter, OCS terminator), NPTII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, kanamycin resistance, NOS promoter, NOS terminator)
phenotype: Chlorsulfuron resistance and biased segregation of transgenic alleles in Brassica napus and potato, with 3:1 GUS activity segregation in water-treated plants and skewed ratios in herbicide-treated plants.
mechanism: Herbicide-induced gametic and embryonic selection against non-transgenic alleles via AHAS mutation, leading to preferential survival of transgenic progeny.

genes: MpARF2 (DNA-binding domain, DBD, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of MpARF2 DBD fused to mNeonGreen under native promoter leads to protein stability assessment via fluorescence intensity in nuclei of transgenic gemmae.
mechanism: Protein stability is regulated by proteasome-mediated degradation; mutations in E297 and R300 residues affect degradation and stability.

genes: MpARF1 (DNA-binding domain, DBD, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of MpARF1 DBD fused to mNeonGreen under UBIQUITIN-CONJUGATING ENZYME E2 promoter leads to protein stability assessment via fluorescence intensity in nuclei of transgenic gemmae.
mechanism: Protein stability is regulated by proteasome-mediated degradation; mutations in R272 residue affect degradation and stability.

genes: MpARF2 (E297K and R300Q mutations, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Conditional stabilization of MpARF2 with E297K and R300Q mutations leads to auxin resistance and impaired thallus development.
mechanism: Protein hyperaccumulation due to impaired degradation disrupts auxin response and developmental programs.

genes: AspiCSE19 (AspiCSE19, lignin biosynthesis, Alsophila spinulosa), AspiCSE35 (AspiCSE35, lignin biosynthesis, Alsophila spinulosa)
phenotype: Overexpression of AspiCSE19 and AspiCSE35 promotes lignin synthesis in Alsophila spinulosa.
mechanism: NA

genes: ROP10 (ROP10, Rho GTPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ROP10 reduces pavement cell lobe number and increases circularity in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ROP10 membrane association via S-acylation with palmitic and stearic acids stabilizes its function in cell polarity regulation.

genes: rop10CA (rop10CA, constitutively active ROP10 mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of rop10CA significantly increases pavement cell circularity (0.44 vs 0.213 in WT) and reduces lobe number (3 vs 9 in WT) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Constitutive activation disrupts membrane association dynamics, weakening interactions with the plasma membrane and altering cell polarity regulation.

genes: rop10Δ183-197 (rop10Δ183-197, hypervariable domain deletion mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of rop10Δ183-197 shows no significant difference in pavement cell lobe number or circularity compared to wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Hypervariable domain deletion compromises membrane association, disrupting ROP10's role in cell polarity regulation.

genes: rop10Δ200-204 (rop10Δ200-204, GC-CG motif deletion mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of rop10Δ200-204 shows no significant difference in pavement cell lobe number or circularity compared to wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GC-CG motif deletion disrupts membrane anchoring, preventing ROP10 from influencing cell polarity.

genes: rop10C199S C205S (rop10C199S C205S, cysteine double mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of rop10C199S C205S shows no significant difference in pavement cell lobe number or circularity compared to wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Cysteine mutations in the hypervariable domain prevent S-acylation, disrupting membrane association and cell polarity regulation.

genes: rop10C160S (rop10C160S, G-domain cysteine mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of rop10C160S shows no significant difference in pavement cell lobe number or circularity compared to wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: C160 mutation disrupts membrane association stability, preventing ROP10 from influencing cell polarity.

genes: TRB2 (telomere repeat binding factor 2, Arabidopsis thaliana), TRB3 (telomere repeat binding factor 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: TRB1 (telomere repeat binding factor 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), TRB3 (telomere repeat binding factor 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: TaWRKY58 (WRKY transcription factor, wheat, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaWRKY58 restores wild-type plant height in Δtawrky58 mutants and suppresses GA accumulation.
mechanism: TaWRKY58 negatively regulates plant height by suppressing GA accumulation through transcriptional repression of TaLRR and TaBCS1.

genes: TaWRKY58 (WRKY transcription factor, wheat, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Δtawrky58 mutants exhibit increased plant height, earlier flowering, and elevated GA levels under drought stress.
mechanism: TaWRKY58 functions as a negative regulator of drought stress responses by modulating hormone homeostasis, particularly GA accumulation.

genes: TaWRKY58 (WRKY transcription factor, wheat, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: 35S::TaWRKY58 represses the promoters of TaLRR and TaBCS1 in transient expression assays.
mechanism: TaWRKY58 directly binds to W-box-containing promoters of TaLRR and TaBCS1 to suppress their expression, modulating plant height and drought response.

genes: OsENTH3 (epsin N-terminal homology domain-containing protein 3, rice, Oryza sativa), OsENTH6 (epsin N-terminal homology domain-containing protein 6, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Disruption of OsENTH3 and OsENTH6 leads to reduced pollen germination rates (53% in Osenth3/6 double mutant vs 88% in WT) and significantly shorter pollen tube lengths (28 μm in Osenth3/6 vs 74 μm in WT), with 16.48% fertility in double mutants.
mechanism: OsENTH3 and OsENTH6 function in clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) during pollen tube growth, potentially regulating vesicle trafficking and calcium channel dynamics via interaction with CNGC proteins.

genes: IMK2 (IMK2, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of IMK2-GFP under CaMV35S promoter localizes to both lateral and cross-walls in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: IMK2 expression level is critical for its polar localization.

genes: IMK2 (IMK2, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of IMK2-GFP under the endogenous promoter rescues the short meristem length phenotype in imk2-1 Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: IMK2-GFP accumulates at the cell plate and newly formed cell walls in the root apical meristem.

genes: IMK2 (IMK2, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of IMK2SP-GFP under CaMV35S promoter causes cytokinetic failure and formation of cell wall stubs in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: IMK2SP-GFP disrupts cell division by mispositioning cross-walls and forming cell wall stubs.

genes: IMK3 (IMK3, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of IMK3-GFP under CaMV35S promoter localizes to cell plates and newly formed cross-walls in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: IMK3-GFP accumulates at every second cross-wall and cell plate attachment sites.

genes: IMK2 (IMK2, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), IMK3 (IMK3, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated knockout of IMK2 and IMK3 in Arabidopsis thaliana results in shorter primary roots and root apical meristems.
mechanism: IMK2-IMK3 module couples cell elongation with differentiation after cytokinesis.

genes: OsLCYE (promoter, carotenoid biosynthesis gene, Oryza sativa), OsGLK1 (transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Co-expression of OsGLK1 with the OsLCYE promoter induces red betalain pigmentation (∼35 µg/g fresh weight) in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: OsGLK1 binds to the OsLCYE promoter, activating tRUBY expression and betalain biosynthesis.

genes: OsPEL1 (interacting protein, Oryza sativa), OsGLK1 (transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Co-expression of VP16-AD-OsGLK1 and GAL4-BD-OsPEL1 induces intense red betalain pigmentation (>170 µg/g fresh weight) in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: Interaction between VP16-AD-OsGLK1 and GAL4-BD-OsPEL1 recruits the AD to the UAS region, activating tRUBY expression and betalain biosynthesis.

genes: CYS6 (CYS6, xylem cysteine peptidase 1 inhibitor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CYS6 enhances resistance to C. higginsianum by sustaining elevated ROS production following pathogen infection.
mechanism: CYS6 inhibits XCP1 activity, stabilizing RBOHD and promoting ROS production to balance growth and defense.

genes: BFP1 (BFP1, F-box protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BFP1 enhances resistance to C. higginsianum by promoting JA accumulation during pathogen infection.
mechanism: BFP1 promotes ubiquitination and degradation of JAOs (JA-inactivating enzymes), maintaining high intracellular JA concentrations.

genes: LENG (LOC_Os05g39410, receptor-like pseudokinase involved in chilling tolerance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of LENG increases chilling tolerance in rice seedlings, with survival rates of 67-87% compared to 43% in wild-type.
mechanism: LENG inhibits OsCRPK1 kinase activity and blocks its interaction with OsGF14d, a positive regulator of chilling tolerance.

genes: LENG (LOC_Os05g39410, receptor-like pseudokinase involved in chilling tolerance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: LENG knockout mutants exhibit increased sensitivity to chilling stress, with survival rates of 5-21% compared to 53% in wild-type.
mechanism: LENG knockout removes inhibition of OsCRPK1, which negatively regulates chilling tolerance by phosphorylating OsGF14d.

genes: LENG (LOC_Os05g39410, receptor-like pseudokinase involved in chilling tolerance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation with WYG promoter and coding region (PwGw) restores high chilling tolerance (96-90% survival) in cr-leng-1 mutants.
mechanism: WYG promoter drives rapid induction of LENG during chilling stress, enhancing inhibition of OsCRPK1 and OsGF14d phosphorylation.

genes: GH9 (GH9, gene family)
phenotype: Expression of GH9-GFP fusion proteins in various tissues including stomata, roots, pollen, ovules, and seed coats, with distinct tissue-specific patterns observed for multiple GH9 family members.
mechanism: GFP translational fusion proteins were used to visualize in vivo expression patterns of GH9 genes across plant tissues.

genes: Raw1 (Hordeum vulgare, putative cytokinin riboside 5ʹ-monophosphate phosphoribohydrolase, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Knockout of Raw1 results in semi-smooth awns in barley, with reduced barb density and size compared to wild-type rough-awned plants.
mechanism: Raw1 is proposed to act in a cytokinin signaling pathway regulating barb formation through endoreduplication and cell expansion.

genes: Raw7 (Hordeum vulgare, putative two-component response regulator, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Knockout of Raw7 results in smooth awns in barley, with complete loss of barbs in the central and basal awn areas.
mechanism: Raw7 is proposed to act in a two-component signaling pathway regulating barb density by restricting epidermal cell differentiation into barbs and enforcing spacing.

genes: FIT (basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), CITF1 (basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-expression of CITF1-MYC and FIT-GFP increases the abundance of the CITF1-FIT complex under copper deficiency, leading to enhanced Cu uptake gene expression and improved Cu deficiency tolerance.
mechanism: The CITF1-FIT complex formed under Cu deficiency upregulates COPT2, FRO4, and FRO5, which are critical for Cu uptake. CITF1 stabilizes FIT protein by inhibiting proteasome-mediated degradation.

genes: CITF1 (basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CITF1-mCherry in protoplasts co-localizes with FIT-EGFP in the nucleus.
mechanism: CITF1-mCherry and FIT-EGFP co-localize in the nucleus, indicating direct interaction and potential cooperative regulation of gene expression.

genes: FIT (basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FIT-EGFP in protoplasts co-localizes with CITF1-mCherry in the nucleus.
mechanism: FIT-EGFP and CITF1-mCherry co-localize in the nucleus, suggesting direct interaction and cooperative regulation of gene expression.

genes: FaCKX11 (FaCKX11, cytokinin degradation gene, tall fescue), FaDAO (FaDAO, auxin degradation gene, tall fescue)
phenotype: Overexpression of FaCKX11 significantly decreased thidiazuron (TZ) content in leaves compared with wild-type plants. Overexpression of FaDAO markedly enhanced oxIAA accumulation while not significantly reducing free IAA levels.
mechanism: FaCKX11-mediated cytokinin oxidation and FaDAO-mediated auxin oxidation regulate elevated [CO2]-enhanced growth under different nitrogen conditions by modulating cell cycle-related genes (OsCycD2 and OsPCNA) and cell elongation gene (OsEXPA10).

genes: SlNAC2 (Solanum lycopersicum NAC2, involved in saline-alkali tolerance, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlNAC2 reduces saline–alkali tolerance in tomato, as evidenced by increased malondialdehyde (MDA) and ion leakage, decreased Fv/Fm ratio and fresh weight under saline–alkali stress.
mechanism: SlNAC2 negatively regulates ROS detoxification and melatonin accumulation under saline–alkali stress by repressing melatonin biosynthesis genes (SlCOMT2, SlSNAT) and activating ROS-related genes (SlCV).

genes: SlNAC2 (Solanum lycopersicum NAC2, involved in saline-alkali tolerance, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: RNAi-SlNAC2 tomato plants exhibited enhanced tolerance to saline–alkali stress, as evidenced by decreased MDA and ion leakage, increased Fv/Fm ratio and fresh weight under saline–alkali stress.
mechanism: SlNAC2 acts as a negative regulator of saline–alkali stress tolerance by repressing melatonin biosynthesis genes (SlCOMT2, SlSNAT) and activating ROS-related genes (SlCV).

genes: PbePEPR1a (PbePEPR1a, receptor for PbePep4 and PdrPep6, Pyrus betulifolia)
phenotype: Transient expression of PbePEPR1a in N. benthamiana enables recognition of PbePep4 and PdrPep6, triggering ROS burst and Ca2+ spiking in response to these peptides.
mechanism: PbePEPR1a binds to PbePep4 and PdrPep6, activating downstream immune responses including ROS production, callose deposition, and MAPK phosphorylation.

genes: PbePEPR1a (PbePEPR1a, receptor for PbePep4 and PdrPep6, Pyrus betulifolia)
phenotype: Mutated PbePEPR1a variants in N. benthamiana show reduced or abolished ROS burst in response to PbePep4 and PdrPep6, identifying key binding residues (Y150, Y152, D222, V248, E273, F319) critical for peptide perception.
mechanism: Six amino acid residues in PbePEPR1a (Y150, Y152, D222, V248, E273, F319) are essential for binding PbePep4 and PdrPep6. D222 is most critical for PbePep4-induced ROS, while all six residues contribute to PdrPep6 perception.

genes: PtrbZIP12 (promoter, 1.5 kb fragment, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: GUS staining revealed a marked rise in reporter expression within the leaves after drought treatment.
mechanism: NA

genes: PtrbZIP12 (promoter, 1.5 kb fragment, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Luminescence intensity from the LUC reporter was approximately threefold higher than that of the control after drought stress.
mechanism: NA

genes: PtrDHN (promoter, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: PtrbZIP12 significantly activated the expression of PtrDHN in dual-LUC reporter assays.
mechanism: PtrbZIP12 directly binds to ABRE motifs in the PtrDHN promoter.

genes: PtrPOD (promoter, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: PtrbZIP12 significantly activated the expression of PtrPOD in dual-LUC reporter assays.
mechanism: PtrbZIP12 directly binds to ABRE motifs in the PtrPOD promoter.

genes: FaRIF (Fragaria × ananassa, NAC transcription factor, synthetic)
phenotype: FaRIF silencing in F. × ananassa cv. Camarosa receptacles results in delayed ripening, increased fruit firmness, and altered sugar/anthocyanin content.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated downregulation of FaRIF disrupts its role in regulating ABA biosynthesis, cell wall remodeling, and sugar metabolism during ripening.

genes: FaRIF (Fragaria × ananassa, NAC transcription factor, synthetic)
phenotype: FaRIF overexpression in F. × ananassa cv. Camarosa receptacles enhances its regulatory role in ABA signaling, cell wall modification, and sugar metabolism during ripening.
mechanism: Overexpression of FaRIF activates downstream targets including FaNAC042, FaSCL8, and FaβGal5, promoting cell wall softening and ABA-dependent ripening processes.

genes: FaRIF (Fragaria × ananassa, NAC transcription factor, synthetic)
phenotype: FaRIF-GFP fusion protein expression in F. × ananassa cv. Camarosa receptacles enables in vivo ChIP-seq analysis of FaRIF binding sites and validation of direct targets.
mechanism: GFP-tagged FaRIF allows chromatin immunoprecipitation to identify genome-wide binding sites, revealing its role in regulating ripening-related genes.

genes: MaCDSP32 (Morus alba CDSP32, full-length, Morus alba)
phenotype: Overexpression of MaCDSP32 increases drought and salt stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with 100% survival rate after drought recovery and higher chlorophyll content under salt stress.
mechanism: MaCDSP32 enhances antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, POD, APX) during post-drought rewatering and suppresses ROS accumulation under abiotic stress, promoting chloroplast redox homeostasis and photosynthetic recovery.

genes: AtCDSP32 (Arabidopsis thaliana CDSP32, promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Atcdsp32 knock-down mutants exhibit reduced drought and salt stress tolerance, with 5% survival rate after drought recovery and severe leaf yellowing under salt stress.
mechanism: T-DNA insertion in the promoter region of AtCDSP32 disrupts gene expression, leading to impaired antioxidant enzyme regulation and ROS scavenging under abiotic stress.

genes: A0A6P4ASV5 (UDP-glucosyltransferase, Ziziphus jujuba), A0A6G1BHK6 (UDP-glucosyltransferase, Oryza meyeriana)
phenotype: Transgenic wheat lines demonstrate increased resistance to Fusarium infection, evidenced by reduced mycotoxin accumulation and milder disease symptoms.
mechanism: UGTs detoxify deoxynivalenol (DON) by converting it into less toxic DON-3-O-glucoside (D3G) through glycosylation reactions.

genes: BcGUN4.1 (regulates chlorophyll and carotenoid accumulation, Brassica chinensis)
phenotype: BcGUN4.1-complementation lines displayed darker green coloration and higher chloroplast density than gun4 mutants, with pigment accumulation restored to wild-type levels.
mechanism: BcGUN4.1 enhances chloroplast development and photosynthetic pigment accumulation by modulating pigment biosynthesis and chloroplast differentiation.

genes: BcGUN4.1 (regulates chlorophyll and carotenoid accumulation, Brassica chinensis)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of 35S:BcGUN4.1 in NHCC leaves resulted in 18.24–58.89% increases in chlorophyll and carotenoid contents compared to controls.
mechanism: BcGUN4.1 enhances chloroplast development and photosynthetic pigment accumulation by modulating pigment biosynthesis and chloroplast differentiation.

genes: BcSG1 (regulates chlorophyll and carotenoid accumulation, Brassica chinensis)
phenotype: BcSG1-complementation lines displayed normal green coloration and restored pigment levels compared to sg1 mutants.
mechanism: BcSG1 positively contributes to chlorophyll and carotenoid accumulation by modulating pigment biosynthesis and chloroplast differentiation.

genes: BcSG1 (regulates chlorophyll and carotenoid accumulation, Brassica chinensis)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of 35S:BcSG1 in NHCC leaves resulted in 47–53% increased chlorophyll and carotenoid contents compared to controls.
mechanism: BcSG1 positively contributes to chlorophyll and carotenoid accumulation by modulating pigment biosynthesis and chloroplast differentiation.

genes: BcTPR4 (regulates chlorophyll and carotenoid accumulation, Brassica chinensis)
phenotype: BcTPR4-GFP fusion localized to the nucleus and cell membranes, and its overexpression in NHCC resulted in restored pigment levels compared to silenced lines.
mechanism: BcTPR4 functions as a positive regulator of chlorophyll and carotenoid accumulation by modulating pigment biosynthesis and chloroplast development.
