plant_species: Medicago truncatula, Medicago sativa, Phaseolus vulgaris
genes: iaaM (tryptophan monoxygenase, Pseudomonas syringae pv. savastanoi), tms2 (hydrolase, Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Increased nodule formation and root growth in Medicago species (Medicago truncatula and Medicago sativa) with indeterminate nodules; no effect on determinate nodules in Phaseolus vulgaris.
mechanism: Auxin synthesized by rhizobia promotes nodulation and root development through auxin transport regulation and nitric oxide (NO) synthesis.

genes: ScFKBP12 (FKBP12, peptidylprolyl isomerase, Saccharomyces cerevisiae)
phenotype: Transgenic lines display rapamycin-dependent reduction of primary root growth and lowered accumulation of high molecular weight polysomes
mechanism: ScFKBP12 forms a ternary complex with AtTOR and rapamycin, inactivating TOR kinase activity which reduces protein synthesis and growth

genes: eqFP611 (red fluorescent protein, Entacmaea quadricolor, synthetic)
phenotype: eqFP611 accumulates in nucleus and cytosol with detectable red fluorescence, no detrimental effects on cell viability
mechanism: eqFP611 is a red fluorescent protein with far-red fluorescence and large Stokes shift, suitable for epifluorescence microscopy

genes: eqFP611 (red fluorescent protein, Entacmaea quadricolor, synthetic)
phenotype: eqFP611 is targeted to peroxisomes with red fluorescence in 1–2 μm roundish structures
mechanism: N-terminal peroxisomal targeting signal 2 (PTS2) from 3-keto-acyl-CoA thiolase 2 (KAT2) directs eqFP611 to peroxisomes

genes: eqFP611 (red fluorescent protein, Entacmaea quadricolor, synthetic), smGFP4 (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Co-expression of eqFP611 and smGFP4 in mitochondria with distinguishable red and green fluorescence
mechanism: Mitochondrial presequence of IVD targets both eqFP611 and smGFP4 to mitochondria; no cross-interference in fluorescence or targeting

genes: eqFP611 (red fluorescent protein, Entacmaea quadricolor, synthetic)
phenotype: Stable transgenic tobacco plants constitutively expressing mitochondrially targeted eqFP611 with red fluorescence transmitted to T3 generation
mechanism: Constitutive expression of mitochondrially targeted eqFP611 in transgenic plants

genes: eqFP611 (red fluorescent protein, Entacmaea quadricolor, synthetic), smGFP4 (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Both red and green fluorescence visible in mitochondria of epidermal cell layers after agroinfiltration
mechanism: Mitochondrial presequence of IVD targets both eqFP611 and smGFP4 to mitochondria; co-expression from single plasmid

genes: PME1 (pectin methyl-esterase 1, Aspergillus aculeatus)
phenotype: Expression of Aspergillus aculeatus PME1 reduces hypocotyl length by ~20% and decreases degree of esterification (DE%) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PME1 reduces DE%, leading to increased pectin cross-linking and reduced cell wall extensibility, thereby inhibiting hypocotyl elongation.

genes: Asr (alternansucrase, Lactobacillus mesenteroides NRRL B-1355)
phenotype: Alternan detected in 4/29 transgenic potato tubers at 0.3-1.2 mg/g fresh weight
mechanism: Overexpression of Asr leads to alternan synthesis in amyloplasts via ferredoxin signal peptide targeting

genes: MdMYB10 (R2R3 MYB transcription factor, Malus × domestica)
phenotype: Induced red color in tobacco leaves when transiently infiltrated with MdMYB10 cDNA.
mechanism: MdMYB10 regulates anthocyanin biosynthesis, leading to red pigmentation.

genes: MdMYB10 (R2R3 MYB transcription factor, Malus × domestica)
phenotype: Red foliage observed in transgenic 'Royal Gala' apple when MdMYB10 cDNA was over-expressed.
mechanism: MdMYB10 regulates anthocyanin biosynthesis, leading to red pigmentation in foliage.

genes: PPV197 (PPV197, 197 bp sequence homologous to PPV RNA genome from base 134 to 330, Plum pox potyvirus)
phenotype: Transgenic plants are resistant to systemic PPV infection; 80% are virus-free and symptomless, 20% show mild leaf mottling but no systemic disease
mechanism: siRNAs homologous to PPV sequence trigger RNA degradation via RNAi, preventing systemic viral spread

genes: RcTGL3 (class-3 triacylglycerol lipase, Ricinus communis), FAH12 (oleate 12-hydroxylase, Ricinus communis)
phenotype: Co-expression of RcTGL3 and FAH12 in transgenic Arabidopsis seeds showed no significant difference in hydroxy fatty acid accumulation compared to CL37 line.
mechanism: NA

genes: RcTGL3-2 (class-3 triacylglycerol lipase homologue, Ricinus communis), FAH12 (oleate 12-hydroxylase, Ricinus communis)
phenotype: Co-expression of RcTGL3-2 and FAH12 in transgenic Arabidopsis seeds showed no significant difference in hydroxy fatty acid accumulation compared to CL37 line.
mechanism: NA

genes: RcOLE2 (oleosin, Ricinus communis), FAH12 (oleate 12-hydroxylase, Ricinus communis)
phenotype: Co-expression of RcOLE2 and FAH12 in transgenic Arabidopsis seeds resulted in moderately increased hydroxy fatty acid accumulation.
mechanism: NA

genes: castorFAD2 (oleate desaturase, Ricinus communis)
phenotype: Overexpression of castor FAD2 in a FAH12-expressing Arabidopsis line resulted in decreased accumulation of hydroxy fatty acids in transgenic seeds.
mechanism: FAD2 overexpression competes with FAH12 for substrate, reducing hydroxy fatty acid synthesis.

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase [GUS], synthetic), PIV2 (portable intron 2 from potato ST-LS1 gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity primarily in leaves and green fruit, with reduced activity in roots and mature fruit. Light-inducible expression in leaves.
mechanism: The Cab19 promoter contains cis-elements for tissue-specific expression in photosynthetic tissues and light responsiveness.

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase [GUS], synthetic)
phenotype: Constitutive GUS expression in leaves, flowers, roots, and fruit. Higher GUS activity in vascular tissues compared to Cab19::GUS constructs.
mechanism: The mas35S promoter is a constitutive promoter with broad tissue activity.

genes: TMV (Tobacco mosaic virus cDNA, expression vector, Cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoter-driven), P19 (RNA silencing suppressor, Tomato bushy stunt virus, Cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoter-driven)
phenotype: Co-introduction of the 35S promoter-driven TMV vector and P19 gene via agroinfiltration results in complete infection of infiltrated plant tissue by 4 days post infiltration and 600–1200 μg of recombinant protein per gram of infiltrated tissue by 6 DPI.
mechanism: P19 suppresses RNA silencing, enhancing TMV vector agroinfection efficiency by preventing degradation of TMV RNA by RISC complexes.

genes: gfp (green fluorescent protein, synthetic, Cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoter-driven)
phenotype: Expression of gfp via the TMV vector results in detectable GFP in infiltrated and systemically infected tissue, with 600–1200 μg of recombinant GFP per gram of infiltrated tissue by 6 DPI.
mechanism: NA

genes: CBM29-1-2 (tandem CBM29-1-2, Piromyces, synthetic)
phenotype: Reduced stem elongation, prolonged juvenility, collapsed cortical cells, enlarged xylem cells
mechanism: CBM29-1-2 binds to polysaccharides in both primary and secondary cell walls, altering cell wall structure and affecting cell expansion and development

genes: CBM29-2 (single CBM29-2, Piromyces, synthetic)
phenotype: No significant difference in stem elongation compared to controls, some cellular changes in high expressers
mechanism: CBM29-2 affects cell wall structure, leading to altered cell enlargement in some tissues

genes: CBM2b-1-2 (tandem CBM2b-1-2, C. fimi, synthetic)
phenotype: Irregularly shaped cortical cells, altered xylem cell enlargement
mechanism: CBM2b-1-2 binds to xylan and non-crystalline cellulose in secondary cell walls, affecting cell wall structure

genes: SCO1 (elongation factor G, plastid-targeted, fused to GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of SCO1::GFP fusion protein in chloroplasts and non-photosynthetic plastids in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: SCO1::GFP fusion allows visualization of protein localization in plastids

genes: FUL (FRUITFULL, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FUL fused to Strep-tag® II-FLAG-tag under CaMV35S promoter results in 57% wild-type, 43% loss-of-function phenotypes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: AG (AGAMOUS, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AG fused to Strep-tag® II-FLAG-tag under CaMV35S promoter results in 29% wild-type, 71% loss-of-function phenotypes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: AG (AGAMOUS, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AG fused to eGFP at C-terminus under CaMV35S promoter results in 12% overexpression, 88% loss-of-function phenotypes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: SEP3 (SEPALLATA3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SEP3 fused to eGFP at C-terminus under CaMV35S promoter results in 8% overexpression, 92% loss-of-function phenotypes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: AG (AGAMOUS, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of eGFP fused to AG at N-terminus under CaMV35S promoter results in 7% overexpression, 93% loss-of-function phenotypes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: AG (AGAMOUS, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AG fused to triple HA-tag under CaMV35S promoter results in 50% loss-of-function phenotypes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: AG (AGAMOUS, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AG genomic fragment fused to eGFP under native promoter results in 20% wild-type, 80% loss-of-function phenotypes in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtS1P (At5g19660, subtilisin-like serine protease, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtS1P rescues salt sensitivity in s1p-3 mutant Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtS1P functions in salt stress tolerance by processing AtbZIP17, leading to nuclear translocation of the transcription factor and activation of salt stress response genes.

genes: AtbZIP17 (At2g40950, membrane-associated bZIP transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtbZIP17 rescues salt sensitivity in zip17 mutant Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtbZIP17 is processed by AtS1P in response to salt stress, leading to nuclear translocation of its cytosolic domain and activation of salt stress response genes.

genes: AtS1P (At5g19660, subtilisin-like serine protease, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of AtS1P-YFP fusion protein localizes to Golgi in Arabidopsis thaliana leaf epidermal cells.
mechanism: AtS1P-YFP co-localizes with BODIPY TR ceramide, a Golgi marker, indicating Golgi localization of AtS1P.

genes: AtbZIP17 (At2g40950, membrane-associated bZIP transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of mGFP-AtbZIP17 fusion protein shows nuclear relocalization in response to salt stress in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Salt stress induces cleavage of AtbZIP17 by AtS1P, leading to nuclear translocation of the cytosolic domain and activation of stress response genes.

genes: AtS1P (At5g19660, subtilisin-like serine protease, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AtS1P promoter:GUS construct shows expression in vasculature of roots, cotyledons, and leaves of Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtbZIP17 (At2g40950, membrane-associated bZIP transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AtbZIP17 promoter:GUS construct shows expression in vasculature of roots, cotyledons, and leaves of Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings.
mechanism: NA

genes: ycf9 (chloroplast-encoded gene involved in photosynthesis, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: ycf9 knockout plants have reduced photosynthetic capacity, especially under low light conditions.
mechanism: Ycf9 acts as a stability factor for CP26, a light-harvesting complex protein.

genes: Re-F-B-α (reporter protein, derived from proaleurain and α-TIP, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of the Re-F-B-α reporter protein in transgenic tobacco plants directs it to a unique compartment marked by the tonoplast intrinsic protein DIP, colocalizing with DIP-positive organelles in root tip cells and PSVs in seeds.
mechanism: Re-F-B-α traffics directly from the ER to a PSV-like compartment, with its α-TIP cytoplasmic tail mediating targeting. DIP organelles serve as prevacuolar compartments for PSVs, aggregating during seed development.

genes: Re-F-R-R (reporter protein, derived from proaleurain and RMR protein JR702, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of the Re-F-R-R reporter protein in tobacco protoplasts traffics through the Golgi apparatus to a PSV-like compartment, colocalizing with α-TIP and DIP organelles.
mechanism: Re-F-R-R utilizes the RMR protein's transmembrane domain and cytoplasmic tail (containing a RING-H2 motif) to traffic via the Golgi to PSVs. DIP organelles serve as Golgi-to-PSV prevacuolar compartments, aggregating during seed development.

genes: TaMSH7 (MSH7, mismatch repair gene, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Reduced MSH7 expression in transgenic barley leads to reduced seed set (~33% reduction in line 12, ~23% in line 41) and lower fertility compared to null segregants and controls
mechanism: MSH7 plays a role in meiotic recombination and DNA repair; reduced expression likely disrupts these processes, leading to chromosomal instability and reduced viable gametes

genes: HPV-11 L1 NLS- (L1 gene with C-terminal nuclear localization signal removed, human papillomavirus type 11)
phenotype: Overexpression of HPV-11 L1 NLS- in Arabidopsis thaliana and Nicotiana tabacum results in stable integration and inheritance of the gene through multiple generations, production of HPV-11 L1 protein (12 μg/g in Arabidopsis, 2 μg/g in tobacco), and assembly into pleomorphic virus-like particles (VLPs) that retain antigenic properties similar to insect cell-derived VLPs.
mechanism: The HPV-11 L1 NLS- protein assembles into VLPs that display conformation-specific and linear epitopes recognized by monoclonal antibodies, suggesting antigenic similarity to native virions. However, plant-derived VLPs failed to elicit neutralizing antibodies in rabbits, indicating structural differences affecting immunogenicity.

genes: AtIpk2β (inositol polyphosphate kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of AtIpk2β increases salt tolerance of transgenic tobacco plants, with improved germination rates (70% vs 28% at 100mM NaCl), reduced growth inhibition under salt stress, and enhanced root growth at 150mM NaCl. Transgenic plants also showed increased tolerance to osmotic, drought, freezing, and oxidative stress.
mechanism: AtIpk2β enhances stress tolerance by increasing expression of stress-responsive genes (lipid transfer protein, raffinose synthase, LEA proteins), elevating antioxidant enzyme activities (APX, CAT), and reducing MDA levels under oxidative stress. Proline accumulation is slightly higher in transgenic plants under 200mM NaCl.

genes: ORFVII (CaMV open reading frame VII, translation initiation, CaMV), ORFI (CaMV open reading frame I, translation reinitiation, CaMV)
phenotype: Shunt-mediated translation of ORFVII increased by 2.5× with TAV, TAV-activated ORF I expression reached 115% in protoplasts of Orychophragmus violaceus.
mechanism: RTBV shunt elements in CaMV leader enable ribosome shunting and TAV-dependent reinitiation at ORF I, bypassing ORF VII start codon.

genes: ORFVII (CaMV open reading frame VII, translation initiation, CaMV), ORFI (CaMV open reading frame I, translation reinitiation, CaMV)
phenotype: Chimeric CaMV-RTBV virus with RTBV shunt elements caused delayed viral symptoms in turnip plants but restored wild-type latency after 1-3 passages.
mechanism: RTBV leader elements in CaMV context support ribosome shunting and TAV-dependent translation, with compensatory mutations restoring local RNA secondary structure for efficient viral replication.

genes: Mlo (Mlo gene, target for RNAi, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: RNAi of Mlo results in phenocopy of resistance mediated by recessive loss-of-function alleles such as mlo5
mechanism: NA

genes: Rar1 (Rar1, CHORD II domain, potato)
phenotype: RB-mediated resistance was not affected in Rar1-silenced lines
mechanism: RAR1 is not required for RB-mediated resistance

genes: Sgt1 (Sgt1, P23/CS domain, potato)
phenotype: Silencing of Sgt1 gene abolished RB-mediated resistance
mechanism: SGT1 is essential for RB-mediated resistance

genes: OsHPL3 (OsHPL3, rice oxylipin pathway enzyme, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsHPL3-GFP increases C6-aldehyde levels by ~50-fold and reduces jasmonate (JA/MeJA) and 12-OPDA levels by ~60% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: OsHPL3 diverts substrate flux from jasmonate biosynthesis to C6-aldehyde production, reducing available precursors for JA synthesis.

genes: GFP (GFP, green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP overexpression in Arabidopsis thaliana serves as a control for transgenic experiments with no observed changes in C6-aldehyde or jasmonate levels.
mechanism: NA

genes: ATM1 (IQ-tail domain of myosin VIII, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GFP-ATM1(IQ-tail) shows differential localization in root cells: diffuse in root cap, punctate in epidermal cells above root cap, and polarized at transverse cell walls in elongation zone. No significant morphological phenotypes observed.
mechanism: ATM1 is involved in endocytosis, BFA-sensitive and insensitive pathways, ER tethering, and plasmodesmatal activity. Co-localizes with ARA6-labeled endosomes and ER.

genes: uidA (GUS reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS reporter gene is expressed in germinating seeds, cotyledons, apical meristem, and lateral root primordia in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: uidA (GUS reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS reporter gene is expressed in germinating seeds, cotyledons, apical meristem, and lateral root primordia in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: Natpi (trypsin proteinase inhibitor, N. attenuata)
phenotype: Silencing of Natpi gene reduces trypsin inhibitory activity, leading to increased larval mass and gut proteinase activity.
mechanism: Knockdown of Natpi reduces inhibition of trypsin in the gut, allowing higher protein digestion and larval growth.

genes: Natpi (trypsin proteinase inhibitor, N. attenuata)
phenotype: Overexpression of Natpi increases trypsin inhibitory activity, leading to reduced larval mass and gut proteinase activity.
mechanism: Overexpression of Natpi enhances inhibition of trypsin in the gut, reducing protein digestion and larval growth.

genes: DFR (dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of DFR increases anthocyanin content but reduces starch content and tuber yield by up to 90% in Solanum tuberosum.
mechanism: DFR catalyzes the reduction of dihydroflavonols to leucoanthocyanidins, a key step in anthocyanin biosynthesis. High anthocyanin levels suppress carbohydrate synthesis, reducing tuber production.

genes: MIR156b (MIR156b, microRNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MIR156b increases rosette leaf initiation rate by ~1.8-fold compared to wild type, causes delayed flowering, and results in bushier, denser rosette architecture with increased side shoot formation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MIR156b targets and downregulates SPL9 and SPL15, which redundantly promote the juvenile-to-adult phase transition and regulate leaf initiation rate. Reduced SPL activity leads to shortened plastochron and altered apical dominance.

genes: ABI4 (ABI4, transcription factor involved in sugar signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic aba2-1/35S::ABI4 lines show a stunted growth phenotype and are glucose insensitive, displaying a sugar-insensitive (gin) phenotype with enhanced ABI4 expression levels.
mechanism: ABI4 overexpression in an ABA deficient background leads to glucose insensitivity by enhancing ABI4 expression, which affects sugar signaling pathways.

genes: MYB28 (At5g61420, transcription factor regulating aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Single knockout of MYB28 reduces long-chain aliphatic glucosinolates (e.g., glucohirsutin) to undetectable levels while short-chain aliphatic glucosinolates (e.g., glucoraphanin) remain at ~40% of wild-type levels in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MYB28 regulates expression of aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis genes (MAM3, CYP83A1) and is epistatic to MYB29 for MAM3 regulation.

genes: MYB28 (At5g61420, transcription factor regulating aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana), MYB29 (At5g07690, transcription factor regulating aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Double knockout of MYB28 and MYB29 completely eliminates all aliphatic glucosinolates (short- and long-chain) below detection limits in Arabidopsis thaliana, leading to 2.6-fold increased Mamestra brassicae larval mass compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: MYB28 and MYB29 are largely complementary and partially redundant regulators of aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis. Their combined knockout causes >100-fold reduction in biosynthetic gene expression (MAM3, CYP83A1) and complete absence of aliphatic glucosinolates.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), YC3.60 (yellow cameleon, calcium FRET reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Strong and specific GUS and YC3.60 expression in guard cells of Arabidopsis and tobacco, enabling calcium imaging in intact plants.
mechanism: pGC1 promoter drives guard cell-specific expression of reporter genes, allowing monitoring of intracellular Ca2+ dynamics.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Reduction of GFP expression in guard cells of 35S::GFP transgenic plants while maintaining expression in epidermal cells.
mechanism: Antisense repression using pGC1(D1) promoter specifically targets GFP in guard cells, demonstrating cell-type preferential gene silencing.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Stronger GUS expression in guard cells compared to full-length pGC1 promoter, with reduced expression in non-guard cells.
mechanism: Serial deletion of pGC1 promoter (D1) retains guard cell specificity while enhancing expression strength.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Weaker GUS expression in guard cells compared to full-length pGC1, with increased non-specific expression in roots and seed coats.
mechanism: Deletion of enhancer elements in pGC1(D2) reduces guard cell specificity and expression strength.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Weaker GUS expression in guard cells compared to full-length pGC1, with increased non-specific expression in roots and seed coats.
mechanism: Deletion of enhancer elements in pGC1(D3) reduces guard cell specificity and expression strength.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Non-specific GUS expression in roots and seed coats, losing guard cell specificity.
mechanism: Deletion of critical regulatory elements in pGC1(D4) abolishes guard cell specificity.

genes: KNAT1 (KNOTTED1-like homeobox gene, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of KNAT1 in Arabidopsis thaliana ovules causes reduced seed coat cell size (half the wild type size), increased cell number in the abaxial layer of the outer integument, and altered integument closure morphology. Seedlings show impaired root growth and increased vulnerability to sodium hypochlorite treatment.
mechanism: KNAT1 promotes extra cell divisions specifically in the abaxial layer of the outer integument. Compensatory mechanisms reduce cell volume to maintain proper integument size. Altered cell division patterns disrupt normal integument morphogenesis and seed coat protection.

genes: HPT2 (hygromycin phosphotransferase, transgene), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, transgene)
phenotype: Hygromycin resistance and GUS expression in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana plants
mechanism: The 148-bp ASN1 promoter region drives constitutive expression of hygromycin phosphotransferase (HPT2) and beta-glucuronidase (GUS) genes in transgenic plants

genes: HPT2 (hygromycin phosphotransferase, transgene)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of hygromycin phosphotransferase (HPT2) in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana plants
mechanism: The nopaline synthase (NOS) promoter drives constitutive expression of the hygromycin phosphotransferase (HPT2) gene in transgenic plants

genes: pat3-k1 (patatin gene, highly conserved target sequence, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Dependent upon the patatin hpRNAi line, patatins decreased by approximately 99% at both the protein and mRNA levels in Solanum tuberosum tubers.
mechanism: Patatin-specific hpRNAi effectively suppressed the expression of a majority of patatin variants via specific degradation of individual mRNAs of the patatin multi-gene family.

genes: IBR5 (IBR5C129S, catalytically inactive mutant of IBR5, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of IBR5C129S does not fully rescue ibr5-1 defects in auxin and ABA responsiveness.
mechanism: IBR5 phosphatase activity is required for full auxin and ABA responsiveness.

genes: IAA28 (IAA28myc, c-Myc epitope-tagged IAA28, synthetic)
phenotype: IAA28myc protein is less abundant in ibr5 mutants, indicating reduced stability.
mechanism: NA

genes: AXR3NT-GUS (AXR3 N-terminal degron region fused to β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: AXR3NT-GUS activity is reduced in ibr5 mutants, indicating altered Aux/IAA stability.
mechanism: NA

genes: atwhy2 (AtWhy2, mitochondrial DNA-binding protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtWhy2 perturbs mitochondrial function by causing a diminution in transcript levels and mtDNA content which translates into a low activity level of respiratory chain complexes containing mtDNA-encoded subunits. This lowered activity of mitochondria yielded plants that were reduced in size and had distorted leaves that exhibited accelerated senescence.
mechanism: AtWhy2 is associated with mtDNA and its overexpression results in the production of dysfunctional mitochondria. We propose that they could play a role in the regulation of the gene expression machinery of organelles.

genes: δOAT (At5g46180, ornithine-δ-aminotransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: δOAT-GFP fusion protein localizes to mitochondria in Arabidopsis and Nicotiana benthamiana
mechanism: δOAT is localized in mitochondria, confirmed by δOAT-GFP fusion protein colocalizing with MitoTracker

genes: SAPK4 (rice SAPK4, serine-threonine protein kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAPK4 in transgenic rice increases salt tolerance by reducing Na+ and Cl- accumulation and maintaining photosynthesis under salt stress.
mechanism: SAPK4 regulates ion homeostasis and oxidative stress response genes including vacuolar H+-ATPase, NHX1, OsCLC1, and catalase.

genes: DDB1A (DDB1A, DNA damage-binding protein 1A, Arabidopsis thaliana), DDB2 (DDB2, DNA damage-binding protein 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of DDB1A and DDB2 enhances UV-C tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: DDB1A and DDB2 act as effectors of the excision repair pathway, facilitating the repair of UV-induced DNA lesions.

genes: SB1.7 (SINE RNA, Brassica napus, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Induces developmental defects including delayed growth, narrower irregular leaves with downward curvature, partial loss of apical dominance, reduced root growth, and abortive siliques in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: SB1 RNA interacts with HYL1 and other dsRBPs, reducing miRNA and tasiRNA accumulation by competing for HYL1 binding, which disrupts miRNA processing and RNAi pathways

genes: AtCPSF30 (cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor 30 subunit, smaller transcript of OXT6 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of oxt6 mutant restores wild-type stress sensitivity to oxidative stress (MV and AT+BSO) and rescues dwarf phenotype
mechanism: Expression of AtCPSF30 (smaller transcript of OXT6 gene) is sufficient to restore wild-type stress-sensitive phenotype in oxt6 mutant

genes: GL3 (trichome developmental regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Plants expressing proGL2:GL3 have large, highly birefringent trichomes with increased branching
mechanism: Enhances trichome expansion and endoreplication by overexpressing GL3 transcription factor

genes: MYB3R2 (NA, NA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MYB3R2 causes delayed phase of leaf movement rhythms and altered CCA1/CCR2 oscillations in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MYB3R2 represses LHY and TOC1 transcript levels while slightly decreasing CCA1 mRNA, suggesting it regulates core-clock gene expression.

genes: bHLH69 (NA, NA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of bHLH69 causes delayed phase of leaf movement rhythms and altered CCA1/CCR2 oscillations in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: bHLH69 represses LHY and TOC1 transcript levels while increasing CCA1 mRNA and inducing GI expression, suggesting it regulates core-clock gene expression.

genes: bHLH92 (NA, NA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of bHLH92 causes lengthened circadian periodicity and altered CCA1 oscillations in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: bHLH92 represses LHY transcript levels while decreasing CCA1 mRNA, suggesting it regulates core-clock gene expression.

genes: CP (coat protein, PnMV), R2 (RNA-dependent RNA-polymerase, PnMV), R3 (RNA-dependent RNA-polymerase, PnMV)
phenotype: Transgenic poinsettia plants remain virus-free after PnMV inoculation, showing resistance to PnMV infection.
mechanism: RNA silencing via transgene-derived siRNA molecules (21–26 nucleotides) indicates the transgenes are expressed and cleaved, conferring resistance.

genes: R2 (RNA-dependent RNA-polymerase, PnMV)
phenotype: Transgenic poinsettia lines with pR2 construct remain virus-free after PnMV inoculation.
mechanism: RNA silencing via transgene-derived siRNA molecules (21–26 nucleotides) indicates the transgenes are expressed and cleaved, conferring resistance.

genes: R3 (RNA-dependent RNA-polymerase, PnMV)
phenotype: Of the five pR3-containing transgenic lines studied, two lines remained virus-free after PnMV inoculation.
mechanism: RNA silencing via transgene-derived siRNA molecules (21–26 nucleotides) indicates the transgenes are expressed and cleaved, conferring resistance.

genes: AtMYB4 (AtMYB4, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtMYB29 (AtMYB29, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtMYB30 (AtMYB30, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtMYB34 (AtMYB34, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtMYB51 (AtMYB51, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtMYB60 (AtMYB60, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtMYB4 maintains normal anthocyanin accumulation (red leaves), while AtMYB60 overexpression inhibits anthocyanin biosynthesis (green leaves) in Lactuca sativa.
mechanism: AtMYB60 represses DFR gene expression, blocking leucoanthocyanidin formation in the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway.

genes: CoxIV (cytochrome oxidase IV signal peptide, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, synthetic), EYFP (enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, Clontech, synthetic)

phenotype: The accumulation of cells expressing CYCB1;1:GUS in teb was largely suppressed by atr (Figure 1I and 1J).
mechanism: ATR is responsible for a cell cycle checkpoint following arrest of DNA replication [40]. Thus, our results suggest that teb activates the ATR-mediated DNA replication checkpoint, which is then followed by cell cycle arrest at G2/M.

genes: FIL (promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of FILp:GFP occurred ectopically in the adaxial regions of some teb and teb atr leaves (Figure 2M, 2N, 2P, and 2Q).
mechanism: Establishment of a boundary between adaxial (upper) and abaxial (lower) cells is required for the formation of flat leaf blades, and thus a complete loss of adaxial-abaxial polarity leads to formation of radially symmetrical leaves [41].

genes: dfr (dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, potato)
phenotype: Overexpression of dfr in Prince Hairy results in purple flowers and red tuber skin in progeny when crossed with Chieftain.
mechanism: dfr encodes dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, which catalyzes the reduction of dihydroflavonols to leucoanthocyanidins, leading to the production of red pelargonidin-based anthocyanins.

genes: AG (AGAMOUS, floral homeotic gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CLV3::AG plants display floral homeotic defects including carpelloid sepals and reduced petals.
mechanism: Enhanced AG expression in the center of the flower leads to ectopic expression in peripheral cells, causing homeotic transformations.

genes: AG intron (regulatory element, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: AG-I::GUS transgene monitors changes in AG transcriptional regulation in response to AG-repressors and activators.
mechanism: The AG intron contains regulatory elements necessary for AG repression and activation, allowing GUS to report AG expression changes.

genes: AG (AGAMOUS, floral homeotic gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: AG-I::GUS; CLV3::AG double transgenic lines show ectopic AG expression and floral homeotic defects.
mechanism: Combining AG overexpression under CLV3 and GUS reporter under AG intron allows monitoring of AG expression dynamics and its regulation.

genes: ZLL (ZLL, AGO1 homolog, Arabidopsis thaliana), AGO1 (AGO1, Argonaute 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reporter constructs rescued corresponding mutant phenotypes in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Functional fusion proteins indicated by rescue of mutant phenotypes

genes: AGO1 (AGO1, Argonaute 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restored development of ago1-1 and ago1-27 mutants and L1 PTGS in ago1-27
mechanism: AGO1 expression from ZLL promoter rescued mutant phenotypes

genes: AGO1 (AGO1, Argonaute 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescued developmental defects of ago1-1 and ago1-27 mutants
mechanism: PAZ domain exchange between AGO1 and ZLL restored function

genes: AGO1 (AGO1, Argonaute 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Partially rescued developmental defects of ago1-1 mutants
mechanism: MID-PIWI domain exchange between AGO1 and ZLL

genes: Lcy-b (lycopene beta-cyclase, tomato, tomato)
phenotype: Overexpression of Lcy-b in transgenic tomato fruits converts lycopene to β-carotene, resulting in orange-colored fruits with 76.6 μg/g β-carotene and 0.5 μg/g lycopene compared to 6.6 μg/g β-carotene and 102.9 μg/g lycopene in control fruits.
mechanism: Overexpression of lycopene beta-cyclase (Lcy-b) enhances the enzymatic conversion of lycopene to β-carotene in tomato fruits, leading to increased β-carotene accumulation and reduced lycopene levels.

genes: pkv (protein kinase viroid-induced, transcriptionally activated in viroid-infected plants, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of pkv in Nicotiana tabacum cv. Xanthi resulted in stunting, reduced root formation, delayed flowering, and male sterility, phenotypes similar to PSTVd-infected tomato.
mechanism: PKV regulates plant development by functioning in gibberellic acid (GA) signaling pathways that control plant height and fertility.

genes: pkv (antisense, downregulation of pkv, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Antisense expression of pkv in Nicotiana tabacum cv. Xanthi resulted in taller plants, increased flower production, and fertility.
mechanism: PKV regulates plant development by functioning in gibberellic acid (GA) signaling pathways that control plant height and fertility.

genes: GmNPR1-1 (GmNPR1-1, non-expressor of PR1 regulatory gene, Glycine max), GmNPR1-2 (GmNPR1-2, non-expressor of PR1 regulatory gene, Glycine max)
phenotype: Complementation of the Arabidopsis npr1-1 mutant with GmNPR1-1 and GmNPR1-2 restores SAR marker gene expression (PR-1 and BGL2) and induces systemic acquired resistance (SAR) following pathogen infection.
mechanism: GmNPR1-1 and GmNPR1-2 proteins complement the lost NPR1 function in the npr1-1 mutant, enabling SA-mediated activation of PR1 and pathogen-induced BGL2 expression.

genes: MEA (maternally expressed imprinted gene involved in seed development, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased MEA expression normalizes triploid seed development and reduces enlarged seed formation in jas mutant plants
mechanism: MEA is a subunit of the FIS PcG complex that represses FIS target genes during seed development; increased MEA expression compensates for reduced transcript levels in triploid seeds

genes: ABP1 (ABP1, auxin-binding protein 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ethanol-induced ABP1AS plants exhibit 60-80% root growth reduction at 3dpg compared to controls, with reduced meristem size (one-third of controls), decreased meristematic cell count, and 40% reduced root diameter due to impaired radial expansion.
mechanism: ABP1 knockdown impairs auxin binding and response, leading to reduced cell division in the root meristem and altered root architecture.

genes: scFv12 (scFv12, recombinant antibody, synthetic)
phenotype: Ethanol-induced SS12K and SS12S plants exhibit 60-80% root growth reduction at 3dpg compared to controls, with reduced meristem size (one-third of controls), decreased meristematic cell count, and 40% reduced root diameter due to impaired radial expansion.
mechanism: scFv12 antibody binds ABP1's auxin-binding site, inactivating its function and disrupting auxin signaling, leading to reduced cell division and altered root development.

genes: FOS1 (CLE-C2, suppressor of fon2 mutation, Oryza sativa indica)
phenotype: Rescue of the floral defect in fon2-1 mutant rice, suppressing the twin-seed phenotype.
mechanism: FOS1 functions as a suppressor of the fon2 mutation by substituting for FON2 in regulating floral meristem maintenance.

genes: FOS1 (CLE-C2, suppressor of fon2 mutation, Oryza sativa indica)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of indica FOS1 causes abnormal shoot development with malformed leaves and compromised shoot apical meristem.
mechanism: FOS1 overexpression terminates meristem function, indicating its role in maintaining stem cells in the vegetative SAM.

genes: FOS1 (CLE-C2, suppressor of fon2 mutation, Oryza sativa japonica)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of japonica FOS1 produces abnormal shoots with malformed leaves, similar to indica FOS1 overexpression.
mechanism: Japonica FOS1, despite a functional nucleotide polymorphism, retains partial activity but fails to fully restrict stem cell proliferation in the floral meristem.

genes: AtIPS1 (AtIPS1, inositol phosphate synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtIPS1-GFP in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to accumulation in both cytoplasm and nucleus.
mechanism: AtIPS1-GFP fusion allows visualization of sub-cellular localization.

genes: AtIPS1 (AtIPS1, inositol phosphate synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtIPS1 in Arabidopsis thaliana complements the atips1 mutant, preventing lesion formation.
mechanism: Overexpression of AtIPS1 restores normal function, preventing spontaneous cell death.

genes: AtIPS1 (AtIPS1, inositol phosphate synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtIPS1 under its own promoter in Arabidopsis thaliana was used for transient expression assays.
mechanism: Promoter replacement allows for tissue-specific expression of AtIPS1.

genes: uidA (GUS reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Cold-inducible GUS expression in Arabidopsis thaliana and peach fruits
mechanism: Promoter contains cis-elements (DRE/CRT, ABRE, MYCR, MYBR) involved in cold response

genes: uidA (GUS reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Cold-inducible GUS expression in Arabidopsis thaliana and peach fruits
mechanism: Promoter contains cis-elements (DRE/CRT, ABRE, MYCR, MYBR) involved in cold response

genes: uidA (GUS reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression not cold-inducible in Arabidopsis thaliana and peach fruits
mechanism: NA

genes: AB28 (anti-Eimeria scFv antibody fragment, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of anti-Eimeria scFv AB28 in pea seeds provides parasite-neutralizing activity and protects antibodies from gastrointestinal protease degradation.
mechanism: NA

genes: AA28 (anti-Eimeria scFv antibody fragment, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of anti-Eimeria scFv AA28 in pea seeds provides parasite-neutralizing activity and protects antibodies from gastrointestinal protease degradation.
mechanism: NA

genes: PsFut1 (PsFut1, 1,2-fucosyltransferase, Pisum sativum)
phenotype: Overexpression of PsFut1 in pea hairy roots results in normal root development and border cell production.
mechanism: NA

genes: ipt (isopentenyltransferase, Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Overexpression of ipt increases cytokinin levels in tobacco leaves (e.g., zeatin, dihydrozeatin, zeatin riboside, and iPA levels are elevated in Pssu-ipt plants compared to controls).
mechanism: NA

genes: AtCKX1 (cytokinin oxidase/dehydrogenase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtCKX1 decreases cytokinin levels in tobacco leaves (e.g., total cytokinin content is lower in 35S:CKX1 plants compared to controls).
mechanism: NA

genes: NaMJE (methyl jasmonate esterase, Nicotiana attenuata)
phenotype: Silencing NaMJE reduces MeJA-cleaving activity by ~84% and inhibits MeJA-induced resistance to M. sexta in asLOX3 plants but not in WT plants
mechanism: NaMJE hydrolyzes MeJA to free JA, which is required for MeJA-induced defense responses including nicotine production and PAL1/TD gene expression

genes: GUS (reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression in immature kernels, specifically in the endosperm transfer cell layer
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression in the endosperm transfer cell layer (modified aleurone layer) and at the base of spikelets
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression in the micropylar endosperm (endosperm cap) during germination and at vascular branching points in stems
mechanism: NA

genes: yeast_invertase (invertase, yeast)
phenotype: Overexpression of yeast invertase in cytosol leads to altered sugar distribution and smaller tubers.
mechanism: Overexpression of invertase increases cytosolic glucose, leading to changes in sugar metabolism and reduced tuber size.

genes: yeast_invertase (invertase, yeast)
phenotype: Overexpression of yeast invertase in apoplast leads to altered sugar distribution and different tuber size.
mechanism: Apoplastic targeting of invertase changes sugar localization, affecting metabolism and tuber development.

genes: PCNA (plant cell cycle regulatory protein, Lycopersicon esculentum)
phenotype: Silencing of PCNA gene in tomato plants leads to stunted growth and reduced plant height and internodal distance by ~50-65%.
mechanism: VA vector produces siRNAs targeting PCNA, leading to gene silencing and reduced PCNA expression, which affects chromosomal replication and cell division.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of GFP in tobacco plants under VA vector, with no significant phenotypic change.
mechanism: NA

genes: AC2 (silencing suppressor, Tomato leaf curl virus)
phenotype: Mutation in AC2 increases the efficiency of VA vector in silencing PCNA by several folds.
mechanism: AC2 functions as a silencing suppressor; its mutation enhances siRNA production and gene silencing efficiency.

genes: AC2 (silencing suppressor, Tomato leaf curl virus), AC4 (silencing suppressor, Tomato leaf curl virus)
phenotype: Double mutation in AC2 and AC4 drastically reduces VA vector replication efficiency by ~4-fold compared to wild type.
mechanism: Synergistic effect of removing both silencing suppressors leads to increased siRNA biogenesis and reduced replication.

genes: PtCOMT (caffeate/5-hydroxyferulate O-methyltransferase, Populus tremuloides L.)
phenotype: Silver birch lines expressing PtCOMT under the 35S promoter showed a reduction in the relative expression of BpCOMT and a decrease in the lignin syringyl/guaiacyl composition ratio.
mechanism: The down-regulation of BpCOMT caused a reduction in the S/G ratio of lignin.

genes: PtCOMT (caffeate/5-hydroxyferulate O-methyltransferase, Populus tremuloides L.)
phenotype: No significant effect was seen in the composition or quantity of phenolic compounds caused by the expression of PtCOMT under the 35S or UbB1 promoter.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtCYS6 (Arabidopsis thaliana cysteine proteinase inhibitor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtCYS6 retards seed germination and seedling growth in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtCYS6 inhibits stored cysteine protease (CP) activity in seeds and during seedling growth, delaying germination and growth.

genes: AtCYS6 (Arabidopsis thaliana cysteine proteinase inhibitor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Genomic complementation of the cys6-2 mutant restores AtCYS6 expression and rescues the mutant phenotype.
mechanism: The genomic AtCYS6 fragment, including its native promoter and regulatory elements, restores normal gene function in the cys6-2 T-DNA insertional mutant.

genes: CTC1 (Conserved Telomere maintenance Component 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CFP-tagged CTC1 in transgenic Arabidopsis shows that CTC1 co-localizes with telomeres in nucleolar periphery (51% overlap in cycling cells, 44.1% in G1-arrested cells).
mechanism: CTC1 associates with telomeres in vivo through an unknown mechanism, maintaining telomere architecture and preventing chromosome end fusions.

genes: CTC1 (Conserved Telomere maintenance Component 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: T-DNA insertion in sixth exon (ctc1-2) and tenth intron (ctc1-3)
phenotype: ctc1 mutants display severe growth defects including distorted floral phyllotaxy, fasciated stems, reduced fertility (10% seed yield), and anaphase bridges (39% of mitotic cells) due to telomere shortening and chromosome fusions.
mechanism: CTC1 deficiency causes telomere uncapping, leading to increased G-overhang signals, telomere recombination, and end-to-end chromosome fusions. CTC1 interacts with STN1 to maintain telomere integrity.

genes: CTC1 (Conserved Telomere maintenance Component 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), STN1 (Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ctc1 stn1 double mutants show similar telomere shortening, G-overhang increases, and anaphase bridge frequencies as single mutants, indicating CTC1 and STN1 act in the same genetic pathway for telomere protection.
mechanism: CTC1 and STN1 physically interact in vitro (B-CTC1 and C-CTC1 fragments bind STN1) and function in the same pathway to maintain telomere integrity. Their combined loss does not exacerbate telomere defects.

genes: CRL (Crumpled Leaf, gene involved in morphogenesis and plastid division, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRL-silenced plants showed reduced susceptibility to CaLCuV infection, with 30% symptomatic plants at 12 dpi compared to 80-100% in wild-type and over-expressing lines. Silenced plants exhibited crumpled leaves, dwarfism, and pale green phenotype.
mechanism: CRL protein may facilitate viral movement by interacting with host cell membranes or metabolic pathways. Reduced CRL levels hindered CaLCuV movement between cells, as evidenced by undetectable GFP fluorescence in systemic tissues of CRL-RNAi plants.

genes: CRL (Crumpled Leaf, gene involved in morphogenesis and plastid division, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRL-overexpressing plants showed increased susceptibility to CaLCuV infection, with 100% symptomatic plants at 12 dpi compared to 85% in wild-type. Symptoms appeared 2-3 days earlier in over-expressing lines. Over-expressing plants exhibited enhanced viral movement, as evidenced by GFP fluorescence in systemic tissues.
mechanism: CRL protein may facilitate viral movement by interacting with host cell membranes or metabolic pathways. Overexpression of CRL accelerated CaLCuV symptom development and systemic spread, suggesting a role in promoting viral transport.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression in maternal chalazal proliferating tissue, inner integuments, and post-meiotic pollen during ovule and anther development
mechanism: Reporter gene expression driven by ASHH2 promoter to study gene expression patterns in reproductive tissues

genes: At5g06280 (puf, protein of unknown function, Arabidopsis thaliana), At5g06290 (2cpb, 2-Cys peroxiredoxin B, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression driven by the intergenic region in 2cpb orientation is enhanced by heat stress and shows tissue-specific expression in vascular tissues, while the intergenic region in puf orientation drives expression in mesophyll tissues and is down-regulated under cold and oxidative stress.
mechanism: The intergenic region functions as a bidirectional promoter, directing GUS expression in a mutually exclusive manner depending on orientation. The promoter contains cis-elements like CCAAT boxes, Y Patches, and homeodomain-leucine zipper binding sites that regulate tissue-specific and stress-responsive expression.

genes: At5g06280 (puf, protein of unknown function, Arabidopsis thaliana), At5g06290 (2cpb, 2-Cys peroxiredoxin B, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression driven by the intergenic region in puf orientation is down-regulated under cold, oxidative stress, and fungal elicitor treatments, while the intergenic region in 2cpb orientation shows enhanced expression under heat stress and is induced in root tips.
mechanism: The intergenic region functions as a bidirectional promoter with orientation-dependent regulation. The promoter contains stress-responsive elements like CCAAT boxes and heat shock factor binding sites, which mediate increased 2cpb expression under heat stress.

genes: GIK (GIANT KILLER, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GIK causes reproductive defects including excessive stigmatic tissue, short valves, and carpelloid organ proliferation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GIK negatively regulates ETTIN (ETT) expression through binding to matrix attachment regions (MARs) in the ETT promoter, leading to histone H3K9 dimethylation and transcriptional repression.

genes: GIK (GIANT KILLER, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of GIK causes low-frequency reproductive defects including delayed anther dehiscence, petalloid anthers, and branched stamens in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GIK loss-of-function leads to upregulation of ETTIN (ETT) and other reproductive regulators (CRC, JAG, KNU), disrupting normal reproductive development.

genes: ETT (ETTIN, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ETT promoter-GUS reporter activity is repressed by GIK overexpression in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GIK binds to matrix attachment regions (MARs) in the ETT promoter, leading to histone H3K9 dimethylation and transcriptional repression.

genes: AGAMOUS (AG, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Inducible AG overexpression activates GIK expression in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AG binds to a CArG box in the GIK genomic region, directly activating its expression.

genes: OsGLK1 (Oryza sativa GLK transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsGLK1 induces chloroplast development in rice calli, resulting in pale green coloration and functional chloroplasts with photosynthetic activity.
mechanism: OsGLK1 upregulates chloroplast-related genes and sigma factors, leading to increased expression of plastid-encoded photosystem genes and chloroplast development.

genes: OsGAD2ΔC (OsGAD2 truncated cDNA, GABA-producing enzyme, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsGAD2ΔC increases GABA content by ~10-fold in rice seeds (Oryza sativa).
mechanism: OsGAD2ΔC overexpression enhances GABA synthesis via glutamate decarboxylation in seeds.

genes: OsGAD2ΔC (OsGAD2 truncated cDNA, GABA-producing enzyme, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Seed-specific overexpression of OsGAD2ΔC increases GABA content by ~10-fold in rice seeds (Oryza sativa).
mechanism: OsGAD2ΔC overexpression under rice glutelin promoter enhances GABA synthesis in seeds.

genes: FT (FLOWERING LOCUS T, floral integrator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: FT::GUS expression detected in marginal minor veins of wild-type leaves and central minor veins of atjmj4-1 mutant leaves in long days; robust expression in major veins of atjmj4-1 mutant leaves in short days
mechanism: AtJmj4 mutation leads to increased FT promoter activity through enhanced chromatin demethylation of H3K4me3

genes: AtJmj4 (Jumonji4, H3K4-specific demethylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Genomic complementation of atjmj4-1 mutants fully rescued the early-flowering phenotype
mechanism: AtJmj4::FLAG fusion protein represses FT expression by demethylating H3K4me3 at the FT locus

genes: AtJmj4 (Jumonji4, H3K4-specific demethylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AtJmj4::GFP fusion protein localized to the nucleus, co-localizing with LHP1::RFP
mechanism: AtJmj4 is a nuclear protein that directly targets FT chromatin for demethylation

genes: AtJmj4 (Jumonji4, H3K4-specific demethylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS activity detected in shoot apex, root tip, trichomes, leaf vascular tissues, and floral organs
mechanism: AtJmj4 is preferentially expressed in vascular tissues and shoot/root apices, overlapping with FT expression domains

genes: ARP5 (Arabidopsis thaliana ARP5 genomic gene, full-length 726 a.a. protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of arp5-1 mutant phenotypes restores normal plant size, organ size, and leaf morphology to wild-type levels in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ARP5 is essential for normal multicellular development and DNA repair in Arabidopsis.

genes: ARP5 (Arabidopsis thaliana ARP5 promoter and 5′UTR, β-glucuronidase reporter gene, Agrobacterium nopaline synthase 3′UTR and polyadenylation site)
phenotype: ARP5p:GUS reporter activity is observed in all organs and tissues of Arabidopsis thaliana, with strong expression in vascular tissue and connective tissue of anthers.
mechanism: The ARP5 promoter drives GUS expression in a tissue-specific pattern, indicating its role in gene regulation.

genes: ahas (acetolactate synthase-herbicide resistance, synthetic), Δgai (gibberellic acid insensitive, synthetic)
phenotype: TM(H) plants are dwarfed (40-60 cm height) and produce less seed and biomass under competitive conditions compared to non-transgenic B. napus. Transgene persistence in TM(B) hybrids decreased by 50-85-fold under competitive and non-competitive conditions.
mechanism: Δgai gene causes dwarfing by insensitivity to gibberellic acid, reducing competitive ability. ahas gene provides herbicide resistance. Tandem construct with 15-bp linker ensures co-segregation of both genes.

genes: dapA (dihydrodipicolinate synthase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Genetically engineered soybeans expressing a lysine insensitive DHPS gene can be selected with the non-antibiotic selection agent AEC
mechanism: Unlike the plant enzyme, dihydrodipicolinate synthase (DHPS) from E. coli is not feed-back inhibited by physiological concentrations of lysine

genes: GI (GIGANTEA, photoperiodic flowering regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: DEX application rescues the late flowering phenotype of gi-2 mutant Arabidopsis thaliana, with transgenic plants flowering at ~20 leaves vs 55 leaves in non-treated plants
mechanism: GI functions in the nucleus to promote flowering by upregulating CO and FT expression; DEX induces nuclear localization of GI-GR fusion protein

genes: ntRAV (transcription factor, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of ntRAV delays the onset of transgene-induced RNA silencing in tobacco
mechanism: ntRAV interacts with TEV HC-Pro, potentially modulating RNA silencing pathways

genes: RAV2 (transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: FLAG-RAV2 interacts with TuMV HC-Pro in vivo in Arabidopsis
mechanism: RAV2 and TuMV HC-Pro interact in planta, confirming RAV2 as a functional homolog of ntRAV

genes: miR172a (miR172a, microRNA, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: no altered phenotypes
mechanism: NA

genes: miR172b (miR172b, microRNA, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Over-expression of miR172b in rice delayed the transition from spikelet meristem to floral meristem, and resulted in floral and seed developmental defects, including changes to the number and identity of floral organs, lower fertility and reduced seed weight.
mechanism: repression of SNB and at least one of the other miR172 targets

genes: TaVRN-B2 (TaVRN2, flowering repressor, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaVRN-B2 delays flowering time by ~5-7 days in Arabidopsis thaliana under long day conditions
mechanism: TaVRN2 increases AtFLC expression 4-fold, counteracting floral inducer genes AtFVE, AtFT, and AtSOC1 to delay flowering

genes: Os01g42880 (Os01g42880, putative arabinoxylan feruloyl transferase, Oryza sativa), Os04g09590 (Os04g09590, putative arabinoxylan feruloyl transferase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Reduces transcript levels of Os01g42880 and Os04g09590 by ~85-90% in rice leaves and stems.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing targeting multiple genes in the arabinoxylan feruloyl transferase family PF02458.

genes: Os05g08640 (Os05g08640, putative arabinoxylan feruloyl transferase, Oryza sativa), Os01g09010 (Os01g09010, putative arabinoxylan feruloyl transferase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Reduces transcript levels of Os05g08640 and Os01g09010 by ~54-61% in rice leaves and stems.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing targeting multiple genes in the arabinoxylan feruloyl transferase family PF02458.

genes: OsMADS34 (OsMADS34, spikelet meristem identity gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of the pap2-1 mutant rescues the elongated sterile lemma phenotype and restores normal panicle architecture in rice.
mechanism: PAP2/OsMADS34 positively regulates spikelet meristem identity and controls the development of rudimentary glumes and sterile lemmas.

genes: OsMADS34 (OsMADS34, spikelet meristem identity gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi suppression of OsMADS34 phenocopies the pap2-1 mutant, causing elongated sterile lemmas and disorganized panicle architecture in rice.
mechanism: OsMADS34 is required for spikelet meristem identity and proper development of rudimentary glumes and sterile lemmas.

genes: uidA (GUS reporter gene, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GUS under P-miR164a promoter leads to GUS activity in vascular tissues and hydathodes, developmentally regulated, increased by ORMV and gibberellic acid (GA3) treatment.
mechanism: P-miR164a promoter activity is induced by viral infection and gibberellic acid, leading to increased GUS expression.

genes: uidA (GUS reporter gene, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS overexpression as a positive control in transgenic Arabidopsis plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: uidA (GUS reporter gene, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: No GUS staining detected in EV::GUS transgenic Arabidopsis plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsMADS15 (OsMADS15, floral organ development, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated down-regulation of OsMADS15 causes degenerative palea phenotype in rice
mechanism: OsMADS15 is required for specification of palea marginal tissue and empty glumes; its down-regulation leads to floral organ transformation

genes: ADF9 (Actin Depolymerizing Factor 9, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ADF9 complements adf9-1 mutant phenotypes, restoring normal flowering time, apical dominance, and seedling size to wild-type levels in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ADF9 overexpression restores normal chromatin structure at FLC, increasing FLC transcript levels and decreasing downstream flowering activators (FT, SOC1, LFY) to wild-type levels. ADF9 may shuttle actin into the nucleus to regulate chromatin remodeling complexes.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: ADF9 promoter-GUS reporter expression is induced by phytohormones (2,4-D, IAA, kinetin, GA3, ABA) in shoot apical meristem, trichomes, and root tip meristem of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ADF9 promoter activity is regulated by phytohormones, suggesting ADF9 expression is part of hormone signaling pathways that control organ development and epigenetic regulation.

genes: ABD2-GFP (Actin-Binding Domain 2 fused to Green Fluorescent Protein, synthetic)
phenotype: ABD2-GFP reporter visualizes F-actin cytoskeleton in trichomes of wild-type and adf9-1 mutant Arabidopsis thaliana, revealing altered microfilament organization in the mutant.
mechanism: ABD2-GFP binds to F-actin filaments, allowing visualization of cytoskeletal changes associated with ADF9 deficiency, which affects actin dynamics and cell polarity in shoot apical meristem.

genes: TAP38 (At4g27800.1, thylakoid-associated phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TAP38 increases LHCII dephosphorylation and alters state transitions in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: TAP38 directly dephosphorylates phosphorylated LHCII (pLHCII) associated with PSI-LHCI complexes, facilitating energy redistribution between photosystems.

genes: TAP38 (At4g27800.1, thylakoid-associated phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of tap38-1 mutants restores normal state transition capacity and LHCII phosphorylation levels in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: TAP38's native promoter drives expression to restore phosphatase activity required for LHCII dephosphorylation during state transitions.

genes: Ath-MIR859 (microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana), Ath-MIR774 (microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of Ath-MIR859-774 leads to DCL1-dependent accumulation of both miRNAs and down-regulation of their F-box protein mRNA targets in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Polycistronic pri-MIRNA is processed by DCL1-dependent pathway to generate mature miRNAs that target F-box protein transcripts for cleavage and/or translational repression.
