mechanism: Ectopic expression of TAGL1 promotes homeotic conversion of sepals into carpel-like organs by activating ethylene-dependent ripening pathways and upregulating genes like ACS2, ACS4, and PSY.

genes: TAGL1 (Solanum lycopersicum, MADS-box gene involved in reproductive development)
phenotype: TAGL1 silencing in Solanum lycopersicum results in non-ripening fruits with reduced ethylene production, altered cell wall properties, and increased lignin content, leading to pale yellow-orange fruits with stiffness and reduced pericarp thickness.
mechanism: TAGL1 silencing disrupts ethylene-dependent ripening pathways, downregulates genes like ACS2, and alters lignin biosynthesis, leading to structural and biochemical changes in fruit pericarp.

genes: MKS1 (mitogen-activated protein kinase substrate 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: mks1 mutants exhibit increased susceptibility to Pseudomonas syringae and Hyaloperonospora arabidopsidis, with up to 10-fold higher bacterial growth compared to wild-type
mechanism: MKS1 plays a role in maintaining basal resistance by interacting with MPK4 and WRKY33 to regulate defense gene expression

genes: EScaAG1 (AG homolog, floral organ identity, Eschscholzia californica), EScaAG2 (AG homolog, floral organ identity, Eschscholzia californica)
phenotype: Homeotic conversion of stamens into petals, defects in floral meristem termination, and increased expression of B function genes in the central whorl.
mechanism: Reduction of EScaAG1/2 function leads to expansion of B function gene expression into the central whorl, suggesting C function regulation of B function genes.

genes: EScaAG1 (AG homolog, floral organ identity, Eschscholzia californica), EScaAG2 (AG homolog, floral organ identity, Eschscholzia californica)
phenotype: Homeotic conversion of stamens into petals, defects in floral meristem termination, and increased expression of B function genes in the central whorl.
mechanism: Reduction of EScaAG1/2 function leads to expansion of B function gene expression into the central whorl, suggesting C function regulation of B function genes.

genes: EScaAG1 (AG homolog, floral organ identity, Eschscholzia californica), EScaAG2 (AG homolog, floral organ identity, Eschscholzia californica)
phenotype: Homeotic conversion of stamens into petals, defects in floral meristem termination, and increased expression of B function genes in the central whorl.
mechanism: Reduction of EScaAG1/2 function leads to expansion of B function gene expression into the central whorl, suggesting C function regulation of B function genes.

genes: TaSnRK2.8 (serine/threonine protein kinase involved in stress responses, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaSnRK2.8 enhances drought, salt, and cold tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Increased ABA biosynthesis and signaling, upregulation of stress-responsive genes such as ABA1, ABA2, ABI3, ABI4, ABI5, CBF1, CBF2, CBF3, RD20A, and RD29B.

genes: AtGCS1 (AtGCS1, HAP2-GCS1 domain disrupted with GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: AtGCS1 promoter-AtGCS1 (GFP in HAP2-GCS1 domain)-AtGCS1 terminator
phenotype: Complementation of gcs1 mutation is almost completely successful in +/gcs1AtGCS1, but +/gcs1GDD and +/gcs1GAH constructs show no complementation.
mechanism: The HAP2-GCS1 domain is critical for gamete fusion function of GCS1.

genes: AtGCS1 (AtGCS1, N-terminal sequence separated from TM by GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: AtGCS1 promoter-AtGCS1 (GFP separating N-terminal from TM)-AtGCS1 terminator
phenotype: Weak complementation of gcs1 mutation in +/gcs1GAA, with occasional incomplete gamete fusion observed.
mechanism: The N-terminal sequence separation from TM by GFP disrupts normal GCS1 function but retains partial activity.

genes: AtGCS1 (AtGCS1, TM domain lost, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: No complementation of gcs1 mutation in +/gcs1GAH, with all plants from GAH pollen dying.
mechanism: The TM domain is required for membrane localization of GCS1, critical for gamete fusion.

genes: AtGCS1 (AtGCS1, HR domain separated from TM by GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: AtGCS1 promoter-AtGCS1 (GFP separating HR from TM)-AtGCS1 terminator
phenotype: Complementation of gcs1 mutation in +/gcs1GHH, GHP, and GPP is comparable to +/gcs1AtGCS1, with no dominant effect of GFP on fertility.
mechanism: The HR domain separation from TM by GFP does not disrupt GCS1 function, indicating the C-terminus is not critical for gamete fusion.

genes: AtGCS1 (AtGCS1, HR domain followed by GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: AtGCS1 promoter-AtGCS1 (GFP following HR domain)-AtGCS1 terminator
phenotype: Complementation of gcs1 mutation in +/gcs1GPP is comparable to +/gcs1AtGCS1, with no dominant effect of GFP on fertility.
mechanism: The HR domain followed by GFP does not disrupt GCS1 function, indicating the C-terminus is not critical for gamete fusion.

genes: ELS1 (Arabidopsis thaliana SUMO protease, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ELS1–GFP localizes to endo-membranes and cytoplasm in Arabidopsis and Nicotiana benthamiana, absent from nucleus
mechanism: ELS1 is a SUMO protease that cleaves carboxyl-terminal extensions of SUMO1, with cytoplasmic localization distinct from nuclear-localized ESD4

genes: ELS1 (Arabidopsis thaliana SUMO protease promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS activity in vasculature and roots of Arabidopsis seedlings
mechanism: ELS1 promoter drives GUS expression in vascular tissues and roots, consistent with SUMO conjugation system activity in these tissues

genes: F5H (ferulate 5-hydroxylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of F5H increases S-unit content in lignin to >90%, resulting in 90% glucose yield after LHW pretreatment in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: S-rich lignin has a more linear structure with lower polymerization, enhancing enzymatic digestibility during LHW pretreatment.

genes: AtERF13 (AtERF13, AP2/ERF transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtERF13 confers ABA hypersensitivity and glucose hypersensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana, with severe inhibition of shoot and root growth at low ABA concentrations and reduced cotyledon greening at 3-4% glucose.
mechanism: AtERF13 enhances ABA response by upregulating ABA-responsive genes like COR15A and ADH1, and its nuclear localization suggests direct transcriptional regulation of stress response pathways.

genes: RAP2.4L (RAP2.4L, AP2/ERF transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RAP2.4L confers glucose hypersensitivity and salt hypersensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana, with severe inhibition of shoot development at 3-4% glucose and reduced cotyledon greening at 125-150 mM NaCl.
mechanism: RAP2.4L enhances glucose and salt stress responses by upregulating ABA-responsive genes like COR15A and ADH1, suggesting a role in sugar-mediated ABA signaling pathways.

genes: RAP2.4 (RAP2.4, AP2/ERF transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RAP2.4 confers glucose hypersensitivity and salt hypersensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana, with severe inhibition of shoot development at 3-4% glucose and reduced cotyledon greening at 125-150 mM NaCl. Salt sensitivity is more pronounced than in RAP2.4L OX lines.
mechanism: RAP2.4 enhances glucose and salt stress responses by upregulating ABA-responsive genes like COR15A and ADH1, suggesting a role in sugar-mediated ABA signaling and ABA-independent drought tolerance.

genes: DWF4 (promoter, promoter region of DWARF4 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (gene, β-glucuronidase reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: DWF4 promoter-GUS reporter gene is strongly expressed in both wild-type and dwf7-1 calli, indicating BR biosynthesis is necessary for dividing cells
mechanism: DWF4 expression represents tissues with enriched BR levels, suggesting BRs are required to maintain callus status

genes: EgCAD2 (cinnamyl alcohol dehydrogenase 2, Eucalyptus gunnii), uidA (β-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS expression in vascular tissues including xylem, cambium, and phloem in transgenic tobacco plants
mechanism: MYB cis-elements in the promoter are crucial for transcriptional activation in vascular tissues

genes: EgCCR (cinnamoyl CoA reductase, Eucalyptus gunnii), uidA (β-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS activity in vascular tissues of transgenic tobacco plants, retained in internal phloem after promoter deletion to -124
mechanism: MYB cis-element in the promoter is essential for transcriptional activation in vascular tissues

genes: EgCAD2 (cinnamyl alcohol dehydrogenase 2, Eucalyptus gunnii), uidA (β-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Significant reduction in GUS activity in xylem rays and parenchyma cells, with retained expression in internal phloem
mechanism: MYBb element is crucial for activator factor binding and promoter activity in vascular tissues

genes: EgCAD2 (cinnamyl alcohol dehydrogenase 2, Eucalyptus gunnii), uidA (β-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Reduced GUS activity in vascular cambium and derived parenchyma cells, with spotted expression in phloem
mechanism: BSb element modulates the balance between DNA-protein complexes and is critical for cambial zone expression

genes: EgCCR (cinnamoyl CoA reductase, Eucalyptus gunnii), uidA (β-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Marked decrease in GUS activity in all vascular tissues compared to wild-type promoter
mechanism: MYB element is essential for transcriptional activation and DNA-protein complex formation

genes: RPT5b (RPT5 subunit of 26S proteasome, AAA-ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Failure to complement rpt5a mutant phenotype in male gametophyte due to 25% non-viable pollen
mechanism: SNP2Ws in intron 7 creates new branchpoint sequence causing mis-splicing, 10bp deletion in exon 8, premature termination codon (PTC) leading to non-functional 35kDa protein

genes: Naα-dox1 (Nicotiana attenuata α-dioxygenase 1, Nicotiana attenuata, source), Naα-dox2 (Nicotiana attenuata α-dioxygenase 2, Nicotiana attenuata, source)
phenotype: Silencing Naα-dox1 results in two growth phenotypes: 11 of 18 transformed lines show severe dwarf growth (IRα-doxS) with reduced α-DOX activity (<10% of wild-type) and 50% reduction in 2-HOT levels, while other lines (IRα-doxM) show mild phenotype with 40% reduced α-DOX activity and 50% reduced 2-HOT levels.
mechanism: Co-silencing of both Naα-dox1 and Naα-dox2 increases constitutive levels of ABA, JA, and anthocyanins, indicating oxidative stress. Silencing Naα-dox1 alone reduces herbivore-induced JA and 2-HOT.

genes: orfH79 (orfH79, chimeric mitochondrial gene causing CMS, CMS-Honglian rice)
phenotype: Expression of orfH79 induces gametophytic male sterility (50% pollen abortion) and retards root growth (2.6 cm shorter primary roots, delayed lateral root emergence) in transgenic rice. Transgenic plants show excessive ROS accumulation, reduced ATP/ADP ratio (59.5% decrease), 7.1-12.1% lower mitochondrial membrane potential, and 11.2-38.3% reduced respiration rates compared to wild type.
mechanism: ORFH79 accumulation in mitochondria impairs mitochondrial function, leading to excessive ROS production, reduced ATP/ADP ratios, and mitochondrial membrane potential loss. ROS accumulation correlates with root growth inhibition, which is partially rescued by ROS scavenger Vitamin C.

genes: GSQUA2 (Gerbera hybrida, overexpression)
phenotype: Overexpression of GSQUA2 in transgenic Gerbera results in an early flowering dwarf phenotype, which displays abnormal vegetative architecture.
mechanism: GSQUA2 is involved in meristem transition

genes: GSQUA2 (Gerbera hybrida, antisense)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: OsIRO3 (OsIRO3, basic helix-loop-helix family transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsIRO3 results in hypersensitivity to Fe deficiency, with reduced shoot Fe concentration and suppressed induction of Fe deficiency response genes.
mechanism: OsIRO3 acts as a negative regulator of the Fe deficiency response by suppressing the induction of Fe uptake-related genes such as OsNAS1, OsNAS2, OsYSL15, and OsIRT1.

genes: AtGRP7 (AtGRP7, RNA-binding protein involved in post-transcriptional regulation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtGRP7 increases expression of circadian clock-controlled genes with dawn-phase peaks and stress-responsive genes like PR1, PR2, and PR5 while reducing evening-phase genes and stress-responsive genes like PDF1.2a and RD29A.
mechanism: AtGRP7 binds to target transcripts via its RNA recognition motif, influencing RNA splicing and stability through NMD pathway. RNA-binding activity is required for regulation, as shown by the loss of effect in the AtGRP7-RQ mutant.

genes: AtGRP7-RQ (AtGRP7 with RNA recognition motif mutation, RNA-binding protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtGRP7-RQ (RNA-binding motif mutant) does not alter expression of target genes like PR1, PR2, THI2.2, and RD29A, indicating RNA-binding activity is required for regulation.
mechanism: The RNA recognition motif mutation in AtGRP7-RQ impairs RNA binding and in vivo function, preventing regulation of target transcripts. This confirms RNA-binding activity is essential for AtGRP7's regulatory role.

genes: AS5 (antisense RNA to 5S-trnR region, chloroplast-encoded)
phenotype: Overexpression of AS5 in tobacco chloroplasts leads to slower growth, pale green leaves, and decreased 5S rRNA stability.
mechanism: AS5 modulates 5S rRNA levels by destabilizing 5S rRNA, potentially affecting chloroplast translation and ribosome assembly.

genes: PtaHB1 (homeodomain leucine zipper class III transcription factor, Populus tremula × Populus alba, Populus tremula × Populus alba)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtaHB1 in transgenic poplars results in altered petiole development with 15% shorter petioles and 30% wider angles between petioles and stems, reduced fiber length in petioles and stems, and altered vascular tissue organization with a 0.80 fiber-to-vascular element ratio compared to 1.55 in controls.
mechanism: PtaHB1 overexpression likely disrupts fiber development and vascular patterning by altering auxin transport and downregulating genes involved in cell wall synthesis and brassinosteroid signaling.

genes: PtaHB7 (homeodomain leucine zipper class III transcription factor, Populus tremula × Populus alba, Populus tremula × Populus alba)
phenotype: No visible physiological effect observed on PtaHB7 transgenic trees.
mechanism: NA

genes: PtrABF (PtrABF, bZIP transcription factor involved in drought tolerance, Poncirus trifoliata)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtrABF in tobacco enhances tolerance to dehydration and drought, with lower ROS accumulation and higher antioxidant enzyme activity.
mechanism: PtrABF activates ROS scavenging system and upregulates stress-responsive genes, leading to reduced oxidative damage and improved stress tolerance.

genes: orf220 (open reading frame 220, CMS-associated gene, Brassica juncea), atp2-1 (mitochondrial-targeting sequence, β subunit of F1-ATPase, Nicotiana plumbaginifolia)
phenotype: Transgenic stem mustard plants exhibit male sterility (unable to produce pollen or produce non-vigorous pollen), delayed bolting and flowering by 2-3 days, aberrant floral development with petal-like structures and five types of abnormal flowers, and pollen with reduced activity (failed in vitro germination and in-situ germination).
mechanism: Mitochondrially-targeted expression of orf220 disrupts mitochondrial function, triggering retrograde signaling to the nucleus that down-regulates genes related to mitochondrial energy metabolism, pollen development, and transcription factors, leading to male sterility.

genes: HvCEBiP (chitin receptor, barley homolog of rice CEBiP, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: HvCEBiP-silenced barley plants show increased susceptibility to M. oryzae ssd1 mutant, producing brown necrotic flecks and blast lesions at inoculation sites
mechanism: HvCEBiP recognizes chitin oligosaccharides from M. oryzae, triggering basal defense responses including papilla formation and localized cell death

genes: AtbZip11 (5' leader, upstream open reading frames, Arabidopsis thaliana), FLUC (firefly luciferase, reporter gene, synthetic), RLUC (Renilla luciferase, reference gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Under-translation of AtbZip11 mRNA in rpl24b and eif3h mutants reduces firefly luciferase (FLUC) activity by ~80% compared to wild type in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: eIF3h and RPL24B promote reinitiation after uORF translation by maintaining ribosome scanning competence and facilitating 40S-60S subunit separation.

genes: U-Omp19 (unlipidated outer membrane protein 19, Brucella abortus 544, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of U-Omp19 in Nicotiana benthamiana elicits a protective immune response against Brucella abortus challenge in mice, with 1.26 units of protection compared to PBS controls.
mechanism: U-Omp19 induces a Th1-Th17 immune response and activates dendritic cells in vivo, leading to protective immunity against Brucella infection.

genes: SVR3 (chloroplast transit peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient expression of P35S:SVR3 CTP:GFP in Arabidopsis leaf protoplasts shows green fluorescence colocalizing with chlorophyll autofluorescence, confirming chloroplast targeting of the SVR3 transit peptide.
mechanism: The SVR3 chloroplast transit peptide (CTP) directs eGFP localization to chloroplasts, as demonstrated by confocal microscopy showing GFP fluorescence colocalization with chlorophyll autofluorescence.

genes: OsHIR1 (rice HIR1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsHIR1 causes spontaneous hypersensitive response (HR) lesions and increases resistance to Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: OsHIR1 triggers hypersensitive cell death and defense responses, likely by enhancing salicylic acid pathway gene expression (PR1/PR2) and pathogen titer reduction.

genes: WRKY18 (WRKY transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), WRKY40 (WRKY transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), WRKY60 (WRKY transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: Overexpression of WRKY18 enhances seed sensitivity to ABA in germination assays, reducing germination rates by ~80% at 1.5 μM ABA compared to wild type.
mechanism: WRKY18 acts as a weak transcriptional activator in plant cells and forms heterocomplexes with WRKY40 to activate WRKY60 expression via W-box recognition in the WRKY60 promoter.

genes: WRKY60 (WRKY transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: Overexpression of WRKY60 increases ABA sensitivity in germination assays, with significantly higher inhibition of germination compared to wild type at 2 μM ABA.
mechanism: WRKY60 acts as a weak transcriptional activator and is directly regulated by WRKY18 and WRKY40 through W-box recognition in its promoter, forming a feedback loop in ABA signaling.

genes: WRKY40 (WRKY transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: Overexpression of WRKY40 reduces ABA sensitivity in germination assays, with less inhibition of germination compared to wild type at 1.5 μM ABA.
mechanism: WRKY40 acts as a transcriptional repressor and antagonizes WRKY18 and WRKY60 in ABA signaling, forming heterocomplexes that modulate gene expression.

genes: WRKY60 (WRKY transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: ABA induces WRKY60 promoter activity by ~3.5-fold in protoplasts, dependent on W-box sequences in the promoter.
mechanism: The WRKY60 promoter contains three W-box sequences recognized by WRKY18 and WRKY40, which activate its expression in protoplasts.

genes: WRKY18 (WRKY transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), WRKY40 (WRKY transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: Co-expression of WRKY18 and WRKY40 activates the WRKY60 promoter by ~5-fold in protoplasts, dependent on W-box sequences.
mechanism: WRKY18 and WRKY40 form heterocomplexes that recognize W-boxes in the WRKY60 promoter, synergistically activating its expression.

genes: WRKY18 (WRKY transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), WRKY40 (WRKY transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), WRKY60 (WRKY transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: LexA DBD-WRKY fusion proteins show distinct transcription-regulating activities: WRKY18 and WRKY60 are weak activators, WRKY40 is a repressor.
mechanism: LexA DBD-WRKY fusion proteins bind to a synthetic promoter with LexA operators, revealing transcriptional activation or repression activities modulated by SA treatment.

genes: NtCesA-1a (cellulose synthase, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: knockdown of NtCesA-1a expression blocked cell wall regeneration in protoplasts
mechanism: NtCesA-1 is a central factor in cell wall deposition in plants

genes: NtCesA-1b (cellulose synthase, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: knockdown of NtCesA-1b expression blocked cell wall regeneration in protoplasts
mechanism: NtCesA-1 is a central factor in cell wall deposition in plants

genes: ACAG1 (ferredoxin--NADP(+) reductase, Nicotiana tabacum, Nicotiana benthamiana), ACAG8 (chloroplast carbonic anhydrase, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Knockdown of ACAG1 increases BaMV coat protein accumulation by ~2-fold; knockdown of ACAG8 reduces BaMV coat protein to 63% of control levels in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: ACAG1 (ferredoxin--NADP+ reductase) may prevent BaMV accumulation by suppressing viral replication; ACAG8 (chloroplast carbonic anhydrase) may facilitate BaMV accumulation by supporting viral replication.

genes: BRI1 (BRI1, receptor of BR, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BRI1 rescues the phenotype of bri1-120, restoring normal growth patterns and BR sensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: BRI1 overexpression compensates for the defective extracellular domain mutation in bri1-120, enabling proper BR signaling and cellular functioning.

genes: BRI1 (BRI1(S399F), mutated receptor of BR, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BRI1(S399F) in bri1-301 rescues the mutant phenotype, restoring wild-type appearance and partial BR sensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: The mutated BRI1(S399F) protein localizes to the plasma membrane and forms functional heterodimers with the kinase-inactive bri1-301 allele, enabling interallelic complementation.

genes: RBP (ribosome binding protein, receptor for ribose, Escherichia coli), GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: ss-RBP-GFP fusion protein localizes to the plant apoplast in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Plant secretory sequence (ss) targets RBP to the apoplast, allowing unrestricted movement of small proteins.

genes: TNT.R3 (computational re-designed receptor for 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene, synthetic), Fls-Trg-PhoR (chimeric histidine kinase, Escherichia coli), PhoB-VP64 (response regulator fused to VP64, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Transgenic Arabidopsis plants show ligand-dependent nuclear translocation of PhoB-GFP and GUS induction in response to TNT.
mechanism: TNT.R3 binds TNT in the apoplast, activates Fls-Trg-PhoR, which phosphorylates PhoB-VP64 to translocate to the nucleus and activate PlantPho promoter-driven GUS.

genes: diRNA POR (protochlorophyllide oxidoreductase, Nicotiana tabacum), AtChlase (chlorophyllase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtRCCR (red chlorophyll catabolite reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants show visible de-greening and reduced Fv/Fm in response to TNT, with AtChlase and AtRCCR upregulated and NtPOR downregulated.
mechanism: TNT activates the synthetic signal transduction system, inducing AtChlase and AtRCCR to degrade chlorophyll while repressing NtPOR, leading to photosystem II disruption.

genes: ω-?ACTX-Ar1 (spider insecticidal peptide, A. robustus), Cry I A (b) C-terminal (Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Transgenic poplar expressing the fusion gene causes 92% cumulative larval mortality in L. dispar compared to 16.7% on nontransgenic poplar, reduces adult oviposition by 95 eggs vs 2516 in controls, and increases midgut proteinase activity 9.2-9.0 fold in larvae
mechanism: Fusion protein activates Bt protoxins in insect midgut via elevated trypsin/chymotrypsin activity, leading to increased mortality and reduced reproductive output

genes: hpt (hygromycin phosphotransferase, selectable marker, Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: The control construct allows selection of transformed plants via hygromycin resistance.
mechanism: NA

genes: PviCAD2 (cinnamyl alcohol dehydrogenase 2, lignin biosynthesis, Panicum virgatum)
phenotype: Silencing of PviCAD2 reduces CAD activity by ~59% and lowers lignin+cutin content by 23%, increasing cell wall digestibility by 2–11% in switchgrass.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of PviCAD2 disrupts lignin polymerization, reducing lignin content and altering cell wall composition to enhance enzymatic saccharification.

genes: NbSerk3 (Nicotiana benthamiana SERK3 homolog, receptor-like kinase involved in immune responses, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Enhanced susceptibility to Phytophthora infestans infection with faster sporulation and extended hyphal growth
mechanism: NbSERK3 is required for INF1-triggered cell death and resistance to P. infestans; silencing disrupts these defense responses

genes: AtPP2-A1 (phloem protein 2-A1, lectin-type phloem protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtPP2-A1 represses phloem-feeding activity of Myzus persicae by ~75% in Arabidopsis thaliana, with 74.8% aphid escape from leaf colonies compared to 17.7% in controls.
mechanism: AtPP2-A1 enhances plant resistance by repressing aphid phloem-feeding activity through an unknown mechanism related to phloem protein plugging and callose closure of sieve pores.

genes: AGO5 (Argonaute protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ago5-3 mutants have no detectable AGO5 protein and affect expression of non-coding RNAs targeted by endogenous siRNAs.
mechanism: NA

genes: AGO8 (Argonaute protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ago8-2 mutants have no detectable AGO8 protein and affect expression of non-coding RNAs targeted by endogenous siRNAs.
mechanism: NA

genes: PHT1;4 (GUS reporter, synthetic), GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS reporter gene is induced by phosphate starvation and expressed in Arabidopsis roots
mechanism: PHT1;4 promoter is activated under phosphate starvation conditions

genes: FRY1 (inositol polyphosphate 1-phosphatase/3',2',5'-bisphosphate nucleotide phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complements the root phenotype of fry1-7 mutant, restoring wild-type root development
mechanism: FRY1 3',2',5'-bisphosphate nucleotide phosphatase activity is sufficient to rescue root growth defects

genes: AHL (3',2',5'-bisphosphate nucleotide phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complements the root phenotype of fry1 mutant and restores PHT1;4 gene expression
mechanism: AHL 3',2',5'-bisphosphate nucleotide phosphatase activity is sufficient to rescue fry1 phenotypes

genes: FRY1 (inositol polyphosphate 1-phosphatase/3',2',5'-bisphosphate nucleotide phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: FRY1-GFP fusion protein localizes to root stele, pericycle, and meristems, overlapping with PHT1;4:GUS expression pattern
mechanism: FRY1 expression pattern is tissue-specific and overlaps with PHT1;4 induction in root stele

genes: GSA (glutamate-1-semialdehyde aminotransferase, from Nicotiana tabacum, NtGSA)
phenotype: Overexpression of GSA inverted repeat (GS-IR) under CaMV35S promoter induces variegated pale-green leaves in Nicotiana benthamiana due to post-transcriptional gene silencing (PTGS) of GSA expression.
mechanism: GS-IR produces siRNA that targets endogenous NbGSA transcripts, reducing chlorophyll synthesis and causing pale-green leaf phenotypes.

genes: GSA (glutamate-1-semialdehyde aminotransferase, from Nicotiana tabacum, NtGSA)
phenotype: Overexpression of GSA inverted repeat (GS-IR) under CoYMV promoter induces pale-green leaf veins in Nicotiana benthamiana due to post-transcriptional gene silencing (PTGS) of GSA expression.
mechanism: GS-IR produces siRNA that targets endogenous NbGSA transcripts, reducing chlorophyll synthesis and causing pale-green leaf vein phenotypes.

genes: GSA (glutamate-1-semialdehyde aminotransferase, from Nicotiana tabacum, NtGSA)
phenotype: Overexpression of GSA inverted repeat (GS-IR) under AtSUC2 promoter induces slightly pale-green leaf veins in Nicotiana benthamiana due to post-transcriptional gene silencing (PTGS) of GSA expression.
mechanism: GS-IR produces siRNA that targets endogenous NbGSA transcripts, reducing chlorophyll synthesis and causing pale-green leaf vein phenotypes.

genes: TMVΔMP (movement protein, partial, Tobacco mosaic virus), CMVΔRep (replication protein, partial, Cucumber mosaic virus)
phenotype: Transgenic tobacco plants expressing partial TMV movement protein gene in the form of an intermolecular intron-hairpin RNA exhibit complete resistance to TMV infection, with stable inheritance through T4 generations and no effect from low temperature (15°C).
mechanism: RNA silencing induced by hairpin RNA leads to siRNA accumulation, which targets viral RNA for degradation, preventing replication and systemic infection.

genes: prosystemin (prosystemin, precursor to systemin, tomato)
phenotype: Overexpression of prosystemin increases resistance to pea leafminer (Liriomyza huidobrensis) by enhancing direct defense (PI-II accumulation) and constitutive emission of indirect defense volatiles (Z3Hol, TMTT).
mechanism: Prosystemin overexpression activates jasmonic acid (JA) signaling pathway, leading to elevated proteinase inhibitor II (PI-II) levels and constitutive release of herbivore-induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) that attract parasitoid wasps.

genes: AtRabD2b (Rab GTPase involved in pollen development and pollen tube growth, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the AtrabD2b/2c mutant phenotype rescues silique length, restores seed fertilization defect, and seed number.
mechanism: Loss of AtRabD2b and AtRabD2c is responsible for the phenotypes.

genes: AtRabD2c (Rab GTPase involved in pollen development and pollen tube growth, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the AtrabD2b/2c mutant phenotype rescues silique length, restores seed fertilization defect, and seed number.
mechanism: Loss of AtRabD2b and AtRabD2c is responsible for the phenotypes.

genes: miraculin (miraculin, over-expressing, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of miraculin in tomatoes does not cause visible differences compared to the control line.
mechanism: NA

genes: GFP (GFP, auxin signaling reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: DR5rev:GFP reporter shows auxin signaling patterns in CIS-incubated Arabidopsis stems, with enhanced signal intensity after 5 days of incubation.
mechanism: DR5rev promoter drives GFP expression in response to auxin, visualizing auxin distribution during secondary growth initiation.

genes: GUS (GUS, phloem identity marker, synthetic)
phenotype: APL:GUS reporter detects phloem identity in interfascicular regions of NAA-treated Arabidopsis stems, showing cell clusters resembling phloem initiation.
mechanism: APL promoter drives GUS expression in phloem cells, visualizing secondary vascular tissue formation during cambium initiation.

genes: CYP79A2 (CYP79A2, cytochrome P450 monooxygenase, Arabidopsis thaliana), CYP83B1 (CYP83B1, cytochrome P450 monooxygenase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-expression of CYP79A2 and CYP83B1 enables BGLS biosynthesis in N. benthamiana leaves
mechanism: CYP79A2 and CYP83B1 catalyze the first two steps of the BGLS biosynthetic pathway

genes: SUR1 (SUR1, C-S lyase, Arabidopsis thaliana), UGT74B1 (UGT74B1, glucosyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtSOT16 (AtSOT16, sulfotransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-expression of SUR1, UGT74B1, and AtSOT16 enables BGLS biosynthesis in N. benthamiana leaves
mechanism: SUR1, UGT74B1, and AtSOT16 catalyze the middle and final steps of the BGLS biosynthetic pathway

genes: UGT74B1 (UGT74B1, glucosyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana), SUR1 (SUR1, C-S lyase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-expression of UGT74B1 and SUR1 enables BGLS biosynthesis in N. benthamiana leaves
mechanism: UGT74B1 and SUR1 catalyze the middle steps of the BGLS biosynthetic pathway

genes: AtSOT16 (AtSOT16, sulfotransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtSOT16 enables BGLS biosynthesis in N. benthamiana leaves
mechanism: AtSOT16 catalyzes the final step of the BGLS biosynthetic pathway

genes: AtSOT17 (AtSOT17, sulfotransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtSOT17 enables BGLS biosynthesis in N. benthamiana leaves
mechanism: AtSOT17 catalyzes the final step of the BGLS biosynthetic pathway

genes: AtSOT18 (AtSOT18, sulfotransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtSOT18 enables BGLS biosynthesis in N. benthamiana leaves
mechanism: AtSOT18 catalyzes the final step of the BGLS biosynthetic pathway

genes: APK2 (APK2, APS kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-expression of APK2 reduces desulfoBGLS accumulation by >98% and increases BGLS accumulation 16-fold in N. benthamiana leaves
mechanism: APK2 increases PAPS availability, resolving the sulfotransferase bottleneck in the BGLS pathway

genes: ABI4 (ABI4, ABA-responsive transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), ABI5 (ABI5, ABA-responsive transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ABI4 and ABI5 enhances ABA-inducible responses in 11-day-old Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings.
mechanism: ABI4 and ABI5 regulate ABA-inducible gene expression by binding to ABRE motifs in promoters and synergizing with bZIP factors.

genes: ABI4 (ABI4, ABA-responsive transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S:GFP:ABI4 overexpression partially complements ABA-resistance of the abi4 mutant and confers ABA and glucose hypersensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GFP:ABI4 fusion protein retains functional activity in transgene complementation assays despite reduced expression or altered conformation.

genes: ABP9 (ABP9, transcription activator, Zea mays)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of ABP9 in Arabidopsis leads to enhanced tolerance to drought, salt, cold, and oxidative stresses, with 65-88% survival rates after stress recovery compared to <40% in wild type
mechanism: ABP9 enhances ABA sensitivity and reduces ROS levels, thus preventing oxidative damage and cell death by upregulating stress/ABA-responsive genes including ROS-scavenging enzymes and regulatory factors

genes: endoglucanase (thermostable, Acidothermus cellulolyticus, synthetic)
phenotype: Increases hydrolysis efficiency for conversion of plant cellulose to ethanol in Zea mays subsp. mays.
mechanism: Endoglucanase generates cellulose chain ends, following an attack by cellobiohydrolase for subsequent hydrolysis.

genes: LC (light chain of trastuzumab, antibody light chain, synthetic), HC (heavy chain of trastuzumab, antibody heavy chain, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of trastuzumab light and heavy chains in N. benthamiana leaves results in high yield of assembled PMT (100–150 µg/g fresh weight).
mechanism: 35S-based vectors drive co-expression of light and heavy chains, enabling antibody assembly and purification via protein A affinity chromatography.

genes: LC (light chain of trastuzumab, antibody light chain, synthetic), HC (heavy chain of trastuzumab, antibody heavy chain, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of trastuzumab light and heavy chains in N. benthamiana leaves using PVX- and TMV-based vectors results in higher yield of assembled PMT (200–300 µg/g fresh weight).
mechanism: PVX- and TMV-based vectors enable co-expression of light and heavy chains with high efficiency, avoiding competition for replication sites and eliminating the need for silencing suppressors.

genes: hrpZ (hypersensitive response and pathogenicity protein Z from Pseudomonas syringae pv. phaseolicola NPS3121, synthetic, Pseudomonas syringae pv. phaseolicola NPS3121)
phenotype: Overexpression of SP/hrpZPsph increases plant growth rate by ~30% and confers high-level resistance to BNYVV in Nicotiana benthamiana and Beta vulgaris hairy roots.
mechanism: SP/hrpZPsph activates defense-related genes (WIPK, hin1) and induces localized necrosis in inoculated leaf areas, preventing virus spread. The signal peptide directs protein secretion to the apoplast, enhancing extracellular defense signaling.

genes: eIF3h (eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 subunit h, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of LAT52:eYFP transgene allows fluorescence-based tracking of eIF3h wild-type alleles in pollen grains during development and germination.
mechanism: Fluorescent protein expression under the LAT52 pollen-specific promoter enables visualization and segregation analysis of wild-type and mutant alleles.

genes: eIF3e (eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 subunit e, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of LAT52:dsRed2 transgene allows fluorescence-based tracking of eIF3e wild-type alleles in pollen grains during development and germination.
mechanism: Fluorescent protein expression under the LAT52 pollen-specific promoter enables visualization and segregation analysis of wild-type and mutant alleles.

genes: OsCYP2 (cyclophilin 2, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsCYP2 confers salt tolerance in rice seedlings by reducing lipid peroxidation products and increasing antioxidant enzyme activities, maintaining photosynthetic efficiency under salt stress.
mechanism: OsCYP2 up-regulates activities of antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT, and APX) at post-translation level to control H2O2 levels, reducing MDA levels and preventing oxidative damage to photosystems.

genes: PAP1 (PAP1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PAP1 produces plants with easily scorable purple pigments in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PAP1 regulates the phenylpropanoid pathway, enhancing anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: CBF3 (CBF3, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CBF3 functions as a cold-induced self-amplicon, enhancing RD29A promoter activity and anthocyanin biosynthesis.
mechanism: CBF3 binds to and promotes expression of the RD29A promoter, creating a feedforward loop.

genes: ESK1 (promoter region, promoter region of ESK1 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter gene, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression restricted to vascular tissue in transgenic Arabidopsis plants
mechanism: ESK1 promoter drives GUS expression specifically in vascular tissues undergoing secondary cell wall deposition

genes: RBL (RbBP5 LIKE, Arabidopsis thaliana, 3′ transcribed region fragment)
phenotype: RBL RNAi lines flowered earlier than parental Col in long days, with reduced RBL transcript levels and reduced FLC, MAF4, and MAF5 expression.
mechanism: RBL promotes the expression of FLC, MAF4, and MAF5 to repress the floral transition.

genes: ASH2R (At_1g51450, Arabidopsis thaliana, 223-bp fragment)
phenotype: ASH2R RNAi lines flowered earlier than Col in long days, with reduced ASH2R transcript levels and reduced FLC, MAF4, and MAF5 expression.
mechanism: ASH2R is required for the expression of FLC, MAF4, and MAF5 to repress Arabidopsis flowering.

genes: ASH2R (At_1g51450, Arabidopsis thaliana, full-length coding sequence)
phenotype: ASH2R overexpression lines flowered later than Col in long days, with increased ASH2R transcript levels and upregulated FLC, MAF4, and MAF5 expression.
mechanism: ASH2R activates the expression of FLC, MAF4, and MAF5 to inhibit flowering.

genes: ASH2R (At_1g51450, Arabidopsis thaliana, full-length coding sequence fused with FLAG tag)
phenotype: ASH2R:FLAG transgenic lines displayed partial functionality with leaf abnormalities and variable flowering time.
mechanism: ASH2R:FLAG's partial functionality caused leaf phenotypes and altered flowering time.

genes: ASH2R (At_1g51450, Arabidopsis thaliana, full-length coding sequence fused with GFP)
phenotype: ASH2R-GFP fusion protein localized specifically in the nucleus.
mechanism: ASH2R's nuclear localization suggests its role as a transcriptional regulator.

genes: ASH2R (At_1g51450, Arabidopsis thaliana, 1.5-kb promoter region and part of coding region)
phenotype: ASH2R-GUS was strongly expressed in root tips, shoot apices, vascular tissues, and developing embryos.
mechanism: ASH2R's spatial expression overlaps with WDR5a and FLC in vegetative and reproductive development.

genes: RBL (At_3g21060, Arabidopsis thaliana, 1.1-kb promoter region and part of coding region)
phenotype: RBL-GUS was strongly expressed in root tips, shoot apices, vascular tissues, and developing embryos.
mechanism: RBL's spatial expression overlaps with ASH2R and WDR5a in vegetative and reproductive development.

genes: Lyc e 2 (β-fructofuranosidase or invertase, vacuolar isoform, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Reduces Lyc e 2 expression in tomato, with no striking phenotype in the greenhouse despite missing vacuolar β-fructofuranosidase activity.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing

genes: Lyc e 2 (β-fructofuranosidase or invertase, vacuolar isoform, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Reduces Lyc e 2 expression in tomato, with no striking phenotype in the greenhouse despite missing vacuolar β-fructofuranosidase activity.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing

genes: GNTI (glycosyltransferase involved in N-glycan biosynthesis, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Efficient general CCD reduction in tomato, with GTI plants showing increased susceptibility to pathogen attack and necrotic fruit parts during ripening.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing

genes: GNTI (glycosyltransferase involved in N-glycan biosynthesis, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Efficient CCD reduction in potato, with no phenotype under greenhouse conditions and residual detection of glycoproteins like Sola t 1 and Sola t 2.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing

genes: GNTI (glycosyltransferase involved in N-glycan biosynthesis, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Efficient CCD reduction in potato, with no phenotype under greenhouse conditions and residual detection of glycoproteins like Sola t 1 and Sola t 2.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: Constitutive GFP expression in rice as a positive control, with higher GFP accumulation than pLex:GFP transgenic lines under all conditions
mechanism: Constitutive expression driven by CaMV 35S promoter

genes: Aox1a (wild-type AOX, tobacco)
phenotype: Increased susceptibility to PVX and inhibited antimycin A-induced resistance to TMV.
mechanism: AOX-regulated mechanisms affect resistance to viruses by modulating mitochondrial signaling and ROS levels.

genes: Aox-E (inactive AOX, tobacco)
phenotype: Enhanced SA-induced resistance to PVX and TMV.
mechanism: AOX-regulated mechanisms affect resistance to viruses by modulating mitochondrial signaling and ROS levels.

genes: Aox1a (wild-type AOX, tobacco), MtRDR1 (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of MtRDR1 did not affect TMV accumulation in directly inoculated leaves but increased resistance to systemic infection.
mechanism: RDR1 activity protects plants from systemic infection, while AOX-regulated mechanisms affect local resistance.

genes: sulI (sulfonamide resistance gene, Escherichia coli R46 plasmid)
phenotype: Overexpression of sulI confers sulfadiazine resistance (5-50 mg/L) in Arabidopsis thaliana. Transgenic plants show less resistance compared to CaMVd35S-sulI constructs.
mechanism: sulI encodes a dihydropteroate synthase insensitive to sulfonamides, allowing folate synthesis in the presence of sulfadiazine.

genes: YUC1 (YUC1, flavin monooxygenase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Vascular defects in cotyledons and floral defects in yuc1 yuc4 double mutants
mechanism: Disruption of YUC1 function in auxin biosynthesis

genes: YUC4 (YUC4, flavin monooxygenase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Vascular defects in cotyledons and floral defects in yuc1 yuc4 double mutants
mechanism: Disruption of YUC4 function in auxin biosynthesis

genes: HAHB1 (homeodomain-leucine zipper, Arabidopsis thaliana), HAHB4 (homeodomain-leucine zipper, Helianthus annuus)
phenotype: Overexpression of HAHB1 increases leaf serration by ~30% in Arabidopsis thaliana. HAHB4 overexpression reduces ethylene sensitivity by ~70% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HAHB1 CTR contains an AHA motif that interacts with basal transcription machinery. HAHB4 CTR lacks typical AHA motifs but inhibits ethylene receptor expression.

genes: HAHB1 (homeodomain-leucine zipper, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HAHB1 increases leaf serration by ~30% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HAHB1 CTR contains an AHA motif that interacts with basal transcription machinery.

genes: HAHB4 (homeodomain-leucine zipper, Helianthus annuus)
phenotype: Overexpression of HAHB4 reduces ethylene sensitivity by ~70% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HAHB4 CTR lacks typical AHA motifs but inhibits ethylene receptor expression.

genes: HAHB1 (homeodomain-leucine zipper, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: HAHB1 without CTR (H1WCT) shows intermediate ethylene sensitivity (50-60% of WT) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CTR deletion removes AHA motif required for full transactivation activity.

genes: HAHB4 (homeodomain-leucine zipper, Helianthus annuus)
phenotype: HAHB4 without CTR (H4WCT) shows high ethylene insensitivity (80-90% of WT) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CTR deletion removes regulatory domain required for ethylene response.

genes: HAHB4 (homeodomain-leucine zipper, Helianthus annuus), HAHB1 (homeodomain-leucine zipper, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Chimeric H4-H1 construct shows intermediate ethylene sensitivity (60-70% of WT) and increased leaf serration in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HAHB1 CTR provides transactivation activity while HAHB4 HD-Zip provides DNA binding specificity.

genes: At1g25330 (CES, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of At1g25330 recapitulates ces-D mutant phenotypes including elongated petioles and outwardly curving leaf growth in adult Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CES positively regulates BR biosynthesis by enhancing expression of DWF4, CPD, and ROT3, leading to increased late BR intermediates and altered BR homeostasis.

genes: At1g25330 (CES, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of CES–SRDX fusion protein causes BR-deficient phenotypes including dwarf growth, reduced petiole elongation, and delayed flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CES–SRDX represses CES-dependent transcriptional activation of BR biosynthetic genes (DWF4, CPD, ROT3), leading to reduced BR levels and impaired BR signaling.

genes: At1g25330 (CES, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CESpro:GUS reporter shows expression in vascular tissues, young organs, and leaf axillary meristems in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CES promoter activity is developmentally regulated and enriched in vascular tissues, overlapping with BR biosynthesis gene expression patterns.

genes: At1g25330 (CES, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CES–YFP fusion localizes to the nucleus in Arabidopsis protoplasts and relocalizes to subnuclear compartments upon BR treatment.
mechanism: CES nuclear localization is regulated by BR signaling and BIN2-mediated phosphorylation, suggesting a role in BR-responsive gene regulation.

genes: At1g25330 (CES, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CES–CFP fusion relocalizes to subnuclear compartments upon BR treatment, co-localizing with BEE1–YFP in Arabidopsis protoplasts.
mechanism: CES interacts with BEE1 in vivo, forming heterodimers that may regulate BR-responsive gene expression through dimerization-dependent mechanisms.

genes: CO (CO, CONSTANS, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (GUS, β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity is significantly increased in BRM-silenced plants compared to wild-type, with gCO::GUS expression restricted to vascular tissue in both genotypes.
mechanism: BRM repression of CO transcription leads to reduced GUS expression; loss of BRM results in ectopic CO expression and increased GUS activity.

genes: FT (FT, FLOWERING LOCUS T, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (GUS, β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity is significantly increased in BRM-silenced plants compared to wild-type, with pFT::GUS showing ectopic expression in BRM-silenced plants.
mechanism: BRM repression of FT transcription leads to reduced GUS expression; loss of BRM results in ectopic FT expression and increased GUS activity.

genes: PdPR5-1 (pathogenesis-related protein 5, Prunus domestica, Prunus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of PdPR5-1 increases resistance to Alternaria brassicicola infection in Arabidopsis thaliana, with transgenic lines showing delayed symptom development and inhibited hyphal growth compared to wild type.
mechanism: PdPR5-1 enhances disease resistance by activating camalexin biosynthesis pathways (increased CYP79B2 and PAD3 expression) and upregulating phenylpropanoid pathway genes (PAL) during fungal infection.

genes: NLA (NLA, E3 ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of NLA reduces Pi content in shoots to wild-type levels in nla mutant plants.
mechanism: NLA acts as a negative regulator of Pi uptake by targeting PHF1 and PHT1.1 for ubiquitination and degradation.

genes: miR827 (miR827, microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR827 increases Pi content in shoots by ~6.4-fold compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: miR827 suppresses NLA transcript levels, leading to reduced NLA activity and increased Pi uptake.

genes: PHF1 (PHF1, PHF1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHF1 in nla-sup1 mutants restores Pi content to wild-type levels.
mechanism: PHF1 facilitates trafficking of PHT1.1, a high-affinity Pi transporter, thereby reducing Pi uptake.

genes: PHT1.1 (PHT1.1, high-affinity Pi transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHT1.1 in nla-sup2 mutants restores Pi content to wild-type levels.
mechanism: PHT1.1 is a high-affinity Pi transporter; its overexpression increases Pi uptake, but this is counteracted by NLA/PHF1 regulation.

genes: APO1 (ABERRANT PANICLE ORGANIZATION1, from Habataki)
phenotype: APO1 transgenic plants show wider culm diameter at internodes and thicker culm walls compared with parental variety Nipponbare, with increased spikelet number per panicle (~20% increase)
mechanism: APO1 regulates cell proliferation in inflorescence meristem, increasing culm size and spikelet number through enhanced cell division in meristem

genes: PepMV-Sp13 (Pepino mosaic virus, European genotype, full-length cDNA), PepMV-Ps5 (Pepino mosaic virus, Chilean genotype, full-length cDNA)
phenotype: Agroinfectious clones initiated typical PepMV infections with symptoms including mild mosaics, leaf bubbling, and stunting. Infection was transmitted via sap and confirmed by dot-blot hybridization.
mechanism: NA

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP expression was observed in single epidermal and mesophyll cells but did not move to adjacent cells. GFP fluorescence was significantly lower compared to the control construct pBGFP.
mechanism: NA

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP fluorescence was maintained for up to four passages, with systemic infection observed by 7-10 dpi. GFP accounted for 0.2-0.4 g/kg of fresh tissue.
mechanism: NA

genes: pds (phytoene desaturase, tomato)
phenotype: Plants infected with PepPDS2a displayed photobleaching symptoms at 3-4 weeks post-infiltration, with pds mRNA levels reduced by 80-90% compared to mock-inoculated leaves.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtHb1 (non-symbiotic hemoglobin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtHb1 increases seed weight by ~30% and improves oxidative stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana seeds.
mechanism: AtHb1 detoxifies nitric oxide (NO), maintains high energy status under hypoxia, and induces stress-related signaling pathways while repressing energy-consuming processes like cell wall metabolism.

genes: OsCERK (ceramide kinase, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: Complementation of acd5 mutant phenotypes including spontaneous cell death, elevated PR1 transcript levels, and enhanced disease susceptibility to Pseudomonas syringae.
mechanism: OsCERK rescues acd5 mutant phenotypes by restoring ceramide kinase activity, modulating ceramide/C1P balance, and suppressing cell death.

genes: OsCERK (ceramide kinase, Oryza sativa, synthetic), C454A, C458A, C461A (site-directed mutants of OsCERK)
phenotype: Partial rescue of acd5 mutant phenotypes with varying degrees of cell death and PR1 expression depending on the mutation (C461A showed strongest defect in complementation).
mechanism: The conserved CXXXCXXC motif in OsCERK is critical for its enzymatic activity and in planta function; mutations in this motif reduce ceramide kinase activity and ability to suppress cell death.

genes: AG (AG, AG gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues the floral determinacy defects of hua1 hua2 hen7 (ag-10) by restoring normal floral organ development.
mechanism: AG overexpression rescues the floral determinacy defects by restoring AG function, which terminates floral stem cells.

genes: AGO10 (AGO10, AGO10 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues the floral determinacy defects of ag-10 ago10-13 by restoring normal floral organ development.
mechanism: AGO10 overexpression rescues the floral determinacy defects by restoring AGO10 function, which terminates floral stem cells.

genes: miR165/166 (artificial miRNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Induces loss of floral determinacy in ag-10 plants, resulting in bulged gynoecia and internal flowers.
mechanism: Overexpression of miR165/166 down-regulates HD-Zip gene expression, compromising floral determinacy.

genes: CaOvate (Ovate-like gene, involved in fruit shape determination, from pepper cultivars)
phenotype: Down-regulation of CaOvate through VIGS in cv. 'Round' changes fruit shape to a more oblong form.
mechanism: CaOvate negatively affects the expression of its target gene CaGA20ox1, which is involved in gibberellin biosynthesis.

genes: UGT73C6 (UDP-glycosyltransferase 73C6, catalyzes 23-O-glucosylation of brassinosteroids, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of UGT73C6 results in BR-deficient phenotypes including dark-green leaves with short petioles, cabbage-like morphology, delayed flowering, and reduced fertility in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: UGT73C6 catalyzes 23-O-glucosylation of castasterone (CS) and brassinolide (BL), reducing their bioactivity and leading to BR deficiency.

genes: UGT73C6 (UDP-glycosyltransferase 73C6, catalyzes 23-O-glucosylation of brassinosteroids, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: UGT73C6 promoter GUS activity is developmentally regulated and expressed in vascular tissues, cotyledons, true leaves, stipules, sepals, stamen filaments, and abscission zones in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: The UGT73C6 promoter drives GUS expression in tissues where brassinosteroids (BRs) are known to act, indicating its role in BR-related processes.

genes: UGT73C5 (UDP-glycosyltransferase 73C5, catalyzes 23-O-glucosylation of brassinosteroids, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: UGT73C5-YFP fusion protein localizes to the cytoplasm and nucleus in Arabidopsis thaliana, similar to UGT73C6-YFP localization.
mechanism: UGT73C5-YFP shows identical subcellular localization pattern to UGT73C6-YFP, indicating similar cellular distribution of these enzymes.

genes: AtMYB117 (AtMYB117/LOF1, transcriptional factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtMYB117 causes wrinkled valves, stigma with more prominent papillae, atypical style cells, wider replum, irregular septum, stacked seeds, and ectopic carpelloid structures in sepals.
mechanism: AtMYB117 enhances SHP1 and SHP2 expression, leading to carpelloid structures and altered fruit morphology.

genes: AtMYB117 (AtMYB117/LOF1, transcriptional factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtMYB105 (AtMYB105/LOF2, transcriptional factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: amiRNA117/105 plants did not show clear morphological changes but had altered funiculi in some cases.
mechanism: Silencing of AtMYB117/LOF1 and AtMYB105/LOF2 affects boundary formation and ovule development.

genes: MdSPDS1 (spermidine synthase, apple), NPTII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic sweet orange plants overexpressing MdSPDS1 show reduced susceptibility to citrus canker caused by Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri, with significantly lower disease index and lesion size compared to wild type plants.
mechanism: Overexpression of MdSPDS1 increases endogenous spermine (Spm) levels, which triggers hypersensitive response (HR) and upregulation of defense-related genes. Enhanced polyamine catabolism via PAO produces more H2O2, which mediates HR and activates defense pathways.

genes: GhCLA1 (GhCLA1, 1-deoxyxylulose 5-phosphate synthase, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Photobleaching phenotype observed in 100% of infiltrated plants, with pink/purple stems and stunted growth.
mechanism: Gene silencing via TRV-based VIGS vector disrupts chlorophyll biosynthesis.

genes: AtCLA1 (AtCLA1, 1-deoxyxylulose 5-phosphate synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Photobleaching phenotype observed in true leaves, limited to veins compared to whole leaves in GhCLA1-silenced plants.
mechanism: Heterologous gene silencing via TRV-based VIGS vector disrupts cotton CLA1 ortholog.

genes: GhNDR1 (GhNDR1, non-race-specific disease resistance 1, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Enhanced susceptibility to Verticillium dahliae, with >80% of plants showing severe wilting.
mechanism: Silencing of GhNDR1 compromises resistance signaling pathways.

genes: GhVe1 (GhVe1, receptor-like protein, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Partial compromise of resistance to Verticillium dahliae, with increased wilting symptoms.
mechanism: Silencing of GhVe1 disrupts pathogen perception or signaling.

genes: GhMKK2 (GhMKK2, mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase 2, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Enhanced susceptibility to Verticillium dahliae, with >65% of plants showing strong wilting.
mechanism: Silencing of GhMKK2 disrupts MAP kinase signaling in defense responses.

genes: GhNPR1 (GhNPR1, non-expressor of pathogenesis-related genes 1, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: No significant compromise of resistance to Verticillium dahliae observed.
mechanism: Silencing of GhNPR1 does not affect resistance, suggesting redundancy or alternative pathways.

genes: OnTI1 (Oncidium trypsin inhibitor 1, flower-abundant gene, Oncidium Gower Ramsey), OnExpansin (expansin, cell wall loosening, Oncidium Gower Ramsey), OnTI2 (Oncidium trypsin inhibitor 2, flower-abundant gene, Oncidium Gower Ramsey), OnDRRP (disease resistance response protein, Oncidium Gower Ramsey)
phenotype: GUS activity in flowers and leaves of Arabidopsis thaliana, with highest activity in flowers for OnTI1 (920 bp promoter) and OnExpansin (various promoters)
mechanism: Promoter regions regulate tissue-specific expression; conserved regions in OnTI promoters control repression in leaves

genes: OnTI1 (Oncidium trypsin inhibitor 1, flower-abundant gene, Oncidium Gower Ramsey), OnTI2 (Oncidium trypsin inhibitor 2, flower-abundant gene, Oncidium Gower Ramsey), OnTI3 (Oncidium trypsin inhibitor 3, flower-abundant gene, Oncidium Gower Ramsey), OnExpansin (expansin, cell wall loosening, Oncidium Gower Ramsey), OnDRRP (disease resistance response protein, Oncidium Gower Ramsey)
phenotype: OnTI proteins form aggregated particles in cells; OnExpansin localized to cell walls; OnDRRP forms a network system throughout cells
mechanism: Fluorescent protein fusion reveals subcellular localization patterns consistent with predicted functions (e.g., cell wall localization for expansin)

genes: CaMV35S ( cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoter, synthetic)
phenotype: Used as reference control in transient transformation experiments
mechanism: NA

genes: FTa1 (FTa1, flowering time gene, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Overexpression of FTa1 rescues the late flowering phenotype of amiR-FT transgenic plants, with 19/22 T1 plants flowering earlier than wild-type Columbia (Col) plants.
mechanism: FTa1 functions to promote flowering in Arabidopsis by upregulating florigen signaling.

genes: FTa1 (FTa1, flowering time gene, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Ethanol vapour treatments induce synchronous flowering in amiR-FT plants carrying the alc::FTa1 construct, with 18/19 T2 families flowering at 20 leaves or less.
mechanism: Ethanol-inducible FTa1 expression promotes flowering in Arabidopsis by upregulating florigen signaling.

genes: AtPV42a (AtPV42a, putative γ-type subunit of SnRK1 complex, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtPV42b (AtPV42b, putative γ-type subunit of SnRK1 complex, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Artificial microRNA-mediated silencing of both AtPV42a and AtPV42b exhibits defects in late stamen development and pollen tube attraction, resulting in reduced seed sets.
mechanism: AtPV42a and AtPV42b play redundant roles in regulating male gametogenesis and pollen tube guidance via SnRK1 complex-mediated metabolic regulation.

genes: AtPV42a (AtPV42a, putative γ-type subunit of SnRK1 complex, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtPV42a does not result in abnormal phenotypes in reproductive development.
mechanism: NA

genes: BAK1 (BAK1, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: BAK1 kinase activity is required for downstream signaling.

genes: BAK1 (BAK1, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: BAK1 (BAK1, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: CHLI (chlorophyll biosynthetic gene, magnesium chelatase subunit, Nicotiana tabacum)

mechanism: CHLI silencing by Y-Sat-derived siRNAs disrupts chlorophyll biosynthesis, leading to reduced chlorophyll content and yellowing symptoms.

genes: CHLI (chlorophyll biosynthetic gene, magnesium chelatase subunit, Nicotiana tabacum)

genes: CHLI (chlorophyll biosynthetic gene, magnesium chelatase subunit, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of modified CHLI (mtCHLI) with 10 silent mutations prevents Y-Sat-induced yellowing symptoms in 44 independent transgenic lines.
mechanism: Modified CHLI transcript is resistant to Y-Sat siRNA-directed cleavage due to 10 nucleotide changes introducing nine mismatches in the siRNA-targeted region, allowing sufficient CHLI expression for normal chlorophyll biosynthesis.

genes: Y-sat (Y-sat, satellite RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic N. benthamiana lines (16c:YsatIR) had a yellow phenotype.
mechanism: Expression of Y-sat dsRNA leads to downregulation of ChlI mRNA, causing chloroplast pigment biosynthesis impairment.

genes: ChlI (ChlI, magnesium protoporphyrin chelatase subunit I, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: N. benthamiana plants infected with CMV-A1:ChlI150 or CMV-H1:ChlI150 had systemic yellow symptoms.
mechanism: Silencing of ChlI gene by CMV vector leads to downregulation of ChlI mRNA and yellow symptoms.

genes: GUS (GUS, synthetic)
phenotype: No yellow phenotype was observed on the N. benthamiana that expressed dsRNA of GUS (16c:GUSIR).
mechanism: NA

genes: GFP (GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP fluorescence was reduced in Y-sat-infected tissues.
mechanism: Y-sat-derived siRNAs target the YR sequence in the GFP sensor, leading to reduced expression.

genes: cry1Ab (cry1Ab, truncated synthetic version from B. thuringiensis ssp. kurstaki HD-1, synthetic), cry3Bb1 (cry3Bb1, synthetically modified from B. thuringiensis ssp. kumamotoensis EG4691, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of Cry1Ab targets Lepidoptera, expression of Cry3Bb1 targets Coleoptera in transgenic maize
mechanism: Cry1Ab and Cry3Bb1 are insecticidal proteins that bind to midgut receptors in target insects, causing cell lysis and death

genes: CYP6AE14 (CYP6AE14, cytochrome P450 monooxygenase, Helicoverpa armigera)
phenotype: Transgenic cotton plants expressing dsCYP6AE14 show enhanced resistance to cotton bollworm (Helicoverpa armigera), with larvae exhibiting 60% weight increase compared to control plants after 4 days of feeding.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated suppression of CYP6AE14, a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase involved in gossypol detoxification, leads to reduced larval growth and increased gossypol accumulation in bollworm midguts.

genes: enhancer-element (CaMV35S enhancer, enhancer element from cauliflower mosaic virus 35S gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Enables identification of both knockout and dominant activation phenotypes for traits of interest in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Enhancer elements on the T-DNA molecule drive transcription of adjacent genes to generate dominant phenotypes

genes: BnBBM (BABY BOOM gene fused with rat glucocorticoid receptor ligand binding domain, synthetic)
phenotype: Enhanced regeneration and transformation efficiency in sweet pepper, producing transgenic shoots that stably transmit the transgene to the next generation
mechanism: BBM induces direct regeneration without callus phase, forming functional shoot apical meristems and vascular bundles that allow shoot elongation and normal plant development

genes: P450SU1 (CYP105A1, cytochrome P450 monooxygenase, Streptomyces griseolus)
phenotype: Overexpression of P450SU1 causes severe stunting, leaf curling, anthocyanin accumulation, delayed flowering, low pollen/seed yields, and delayed senescence in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CYP105A1 disrupts brassinosteroid signaling by inactivating brassinosteroids, leading to aberrant growth and developmental defects.

genes: Glyma18g02680.1 (LRR-kinase, leucine-rich repeat transmembrane receptor kinase, Peking/PI 437654-source), Glyma18g02680.1 (LRR-kinase, leucine-rich repeat transmembrane receptor kinase, PI 88788-source)
phenotype: Overexpression of the Rhg1 locus LRR-kinase gene in SCN-susceptible soybean lines did not significantly increase SCN resistance. amiRNA-mediated silencing of the Rhg1 locus LRR-kinase gene in resistant soybean lines also did not significantly alter SCN resistance, but caused root development delays.
mechanism: NA

genes: Glyma18g02680.1 (LRR-kinase, leucine-rich repeat transmembrane receptor kinase, PI 88788-source)
phenotype: amiRNA-mediated silencing of the Rhg1 locus LRR-kinase gene in resistant soybean lines did not significantly alter SCN resistance, but caused root development delays and reduced transformation efficiency.
mechanism: NA

genes: CpF3'5'H (flavonoid 3',5'-hydroxylase, Cyclamen persicum)
phenotype: Flower color modification with reduced delphinidin-derived anthocyanins and increased cyanidin-derived pigments; total anthocyanin concentration reduced up to 80% in some transgenic lines; hue shifted from purple to red/pink in one cultivar.
mechanism: Antisense suppression of F3'5'H enzyme activity altered anthocyanin biosynthesis pathway, reducing delphinidin-derived pigments and increasing cyanidin-derived pigments while decreasing total anthocyanin levels.

genes: PPV-NK-GFP (full-length cDNA of Plum pox virus with GFP reporter gene, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Variable GFP expression in transgenic plants; some lines (like 10.6) show delayed, sporadic infection foci that progress systemically before recovery
mechanism: RNA silencing and other defense mechanisms limit amplicon expression; low-level silencing may contribute to repression

genes: SBEIIa (starch branching enzyme IIa, Triticum durum)
phenotype: Silencing of SBEIIa increases amylose content to 75% and causes deformed starch granules in durum wheat.
mechanism: SBEIIa silencing disrupts amylopectin branching, leading to increased amylose and altered granule morphology.

genes: gfp (green fluorescent protein, synthetic), nptII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic plants express green fluorescent protein (GFP) in multiple tissues and exhibit kanamycin resistance, with 58.9% transformation efficiency achieved within 12-16 weeks
mechanism: The gfp gene provides visual selection via fluorescence, while the nptII gene confers kanamycin resistance for selection of transgenic plants

genes: YAO (At4G05410, nucleolar protein with seven WD-repeats, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of yao mutant restores seed set and transmission defect, with KanR/KanS ratio increasing to ~2.5:1 in T2 generation.
mechanism: YAO is likely involved in 18S pre-rRNA processing as a component of the U3 snoRNP complex, essential for nucleolar function during gametogenesis and early embryogenesis.

genes: YAO (At4G05410, nucleolar protein with seven WD-repeats, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: YAO-GFP fusion protein localizes to nucleolus in root tip, embryo sac, and endosperm cells, confirming nucleolar localization.
mechanism: YAO-GFP co-localizes with nucleolar marker SWA2-DsRed, indicating nucleolar function. YAO is expressed in tissues with active cell division, including embryos and endosperms.

genes: YAO (At4G05410, nucleolar protein with seven WD-repeats, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS activity detected in tissues active in cell division (shoot apexes, root tips, embryos, endosperms, pollen grains, embryo sacs), confirming YAO's expression pattern.
mechanism: YAO is expressed in tissues with active cell division, including gametophytes and early embryos, consistent with its role in nucleolar function during reproductive development.

genes: AOP2 (AOP2-2, 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase involved in glucosinolate modification, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AOP2-2 converts methylsulfinylalkyl glucosinolates into alkenyl glucosinolates in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AOP2 catalyzes the conversion of methylsulfinylalkyl glucosinolates to alkenyl glucosinolates.

genes: AtNudt7 (nudix hydrolase 7, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Constitutive over-expression of AtNudt7 did not alter NADH levels or resistance to pathogens.
mechanism: NA

genes: hpa1Xoo (harpinXoo, harpin-like protein from Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of hpa1Xoo in cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) confers improved resistance to Verticillium dahliae, with 7.32%-26.22% lower disease severity compared to untransformed Z35. Transgenic T-34 shows enhanced tolerance to V. dahliae conidia, higher cell viability, and up-regulation of defense-related genes (ghAOX1, hin1, npr1, ghdhg-OMT, hsr203J).
mechanism: Hpa1Xoo accumulates along cell walls of T-34, triggering H2O2 generation as an endogenous elicitor. This primes the plant's defense responses, including up-regulation of defense-related genes and microscopic hypersensitive response (HR) to V. dahliae infection.

genes: ProDH2 (ProDH2, Pro dehydrogenase 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ProDH2-GFP rescues the Pro-hypersensitive phenotype of the pdh1-1 mutant and enables utilization of Pro as a single nitrogen source for growth.
mechanism: ProDH2-GFP localizes to mitochondria and mediates Pro degradation, similar to ProDH1.

genes: ProDH1 (ProDH1, Pro dehydrogenase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ProDH1-GFP rescues the Pro-hypersensitive phenotype of the pdh1-1 mutant and enables utilization of Pro as a single nitrogen source for growth.
mechanism: ProDH1-GFP localizes to mitochondria and mediates Pro degradation.

genes: ProDH2 (ProDH2, Pro dehydrogenase 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Functional expression of ProDH2 in yeast complements the Pro utilisation deficiency of the Δput1 mutant.
mechanism: Replacement of the predicted Arabidopsis mTP with the yeast Sdh1 mTP enables functional expression of ProDH2 in yeast.

genes: Sultr4;1 (sulphate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Sultr4;1 mutant seeds show 1.7-fold higher sulphate content compared to wild-type, with unchanged total sulphur content
mechanism: SULTR4;1 mediates vacuolar sulphate efflux; its disruption leads to increased vacuolar sulphate storage and altered redox homeostasis

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic), AtMHX (vacuolar metal/proton exchanger, promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under AtMHX promoter with LI is 272-fold higher than without LI in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: The LI of AtMHX acts by intron-mediated enhancement (IME), not as a transcriptional enhancer or internal promoter.
