phenotype: Expression of GUS under CaMV 35S promoter is 3-fold higher when AtMHX LI is included in the 5'UTR in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: The LI of AtMHX enhances expression by intron-mediated enhancement (IME), but with lower magnitude (3-fold) compared to its effect on the AtMHX promoter.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic), AtMHX (vacuolar metal/proton exchanger, promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: AtMHX-RE-US-MP-GUS-AtMHX ter (with mutated 5' and 3' splice sites)
phenotype: Unspliced LI of AtMHX mediates 5-fold enhancement of GUS expression compared to -Int construct in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Low-level enhancement by unspliced intron depends on internal intron sequence but not splicing. Splicing is essential for substantial IME.

genes: CPK3 (Arabidopsis thaliana, truncated variant of CPK3 lacking junction and calmodulin-like domains, synthetic), HsfB2a (Arabidopsis thaliana, full-length coding region, genomic), PDF1.2 (Arabidopsis thaliana, 1-kb promoter region, genomic)
phenotype: Co-expression of CPK3/HsfB2a in N. benthamiana leaves increased PDF1.2 promoter-driven GUS activity by 6.6- and 1.9-fold compared to HsfB2a alone
mechanism: CPK3/13-mediated phosphorylation of HsfB2a promotes PDF1.2 transcriptional activation in defense response

genes: PparoA1optimized (Pseudomonas putida 4G-1 AroA, codon-optimized for tobacco, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PparoA1optimized confers glyphosate tolerance in tobacco, with 6 out of 60 transgenic lines surviving glyphosate treatment and 75% T1 progeny showing Mendelian segregation of tolerance.
mechanism: PpAroA1 is a glyphosate-tolerant alternative to plant AroA, allowing continued shikimate pathway activity under glyphosate stress.

genes: PparoA1 (Pseudomonas putida 4G-1 AroA, non-optimized, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PparoA1 confers glyphosate tolerance in tobacco, with transgenic plants showing tolerance levels comparable to PparoA1optimized (Fig. 5).
mechanism: PpAroA1 is a glyphosate-tolerant alternative to plant AroA, allowing continued shikimate pathway activity under glyphosate stress.

genes: hIGF-I (human insulin-like growth factor-I, Homo sapiens)
phenotype: Construct I did not produce detectable rhIGF-I protein in rice seeds (Figure 2A).
mechanism: NA

genes: hIGF-I (human insulin-like growth factor-I, Homo sapiens)
phenotype: Construct SI produced rhIGF-I in rice seeds, inducing membrane ruffling and glucose uptake in L6myc cells equivalent to commercial rhIGF-I. One gram of SI rice grain had activity equivalent to 3.2 μM commercial rhIGF-I.
mechanism: Glutelin signal peptide directs rhIGF-I to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) for stable accumulation. The absence of KDEL allows SI protein to proceed through the Golgi and be secreted for storage, avoiding proteolytic degradation.

genes: hIGF-I (human insulin-like growth factor-I, Homo sapiens)
phenotype: Construct SIK produced rhIGF-I in rice seeds but lacked biological activity in L6myc cells. The KDEL retention signal localized rhIGF-I to the ER, preventing secretion and storage.
mechanism: KDEL sequence retains rhIGF-I in the ER lumen, preventing its secretion and storage. This may alter glycosylation patterns or cause ER stress, reducing biological activity.

genes: PAL (L-phenylalanine ammonia-lyase, Medicago sativa), C4H (cinnamate 4-hydroxylase, Medicago sativa), HCT (hydroxycinnamoyl CoA:quinate/shikimate hydroxycinnamoyl transferase, Medicago sativa), C3H (coumarate 3-hydroxylase, Medicago sativa), CCoAOMT (caffeoyl coenzyme A 3-O-methyltransferase, Medicago sativa), F5H (ferulate 5-hydroxylase, Medicago sativa), COMT (caffeic acid 3-O-methyltransferase, Medicago sativa)
phenotype: Down-regulation of individual enzymes (PAL, C4H, HCT, C3H, CCoAOMT, F5H, COMT) in alfalfa leads to altered lignin composition, including changes in H, G, and S lignin proportions and S/G ratios.
mechanism: Flux partitioning at key branch points (p-coumaroyl-CoA, coniferyl aldehyde, coniferyl alcohol) determines lignin monomer ratios. Down-regulation of specific enzymes modulates fluxes, altering lignin composition.

genes: MLC (synthetic chimeric recombinant gene containing PvMSP-1 (Plasmodium vivax Belem isolate, interspecies conserved block 10), Pro-Gly linker motif, and PvCSP (Plasmodium vivax VK210 subtype tandem repeats), synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of MLC chimeric recombinant protein in B. napus with molecular weight ~25 kDa, clinical sensitivity 84.21% (n=38) and specificity 100% (n=24) for vivax malaria diagnosis. Oral immunization induces antigen-specific IgG1 and Th1-related cytokines (IL-12(p40), TNF, IFN-γ) in BALB/c mice.
mechanism: MLC chimeric protein induces Th1 and Th2 immune responses, with Th1 cytokines (IL-12(p40), TNF, IFN-γ) and IgG1 antibodies detected in immunized mice.

genes: prosystemin (prosystemin, constitutive systemic defense activation, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: 35S::prosystemin transgenic plants exhibit stronger and quicker induced resistance to nematodes compared to wild-type and spr2 mutant tomato plants
mechanism: Constitutive activation of systemic defense via the JA pathway in unwounded plants

genes: SHN1 (SHN1, SHN clade transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), SHN2 (SHN2, SHN clade transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), SHN3 (SHN3, SHN clade transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-silencing of SHN1/2/3 causes severe morphological and surface phenotypes in floral organs, including postgenital fusions, restrained petal/carpel expansion, and early abscission.
mechanism: SHN clade genes function redundantly in cell elongation, separation, and nanoridge formation of reproductive organs via cutin and cell wall remodeling.

genes: CYP86A4 (CYP86A4, cytochrome P450, Arabidopsis thaliana), CYP86A7 (CYP86A7, cytochrome P450, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-silencing of CYP86A4 and CYP86A7 causes floral organ fusion and altered conical cell shape and epidermis cell decoration.
mechanism: CYP86A4 and CYP86A7 are putative downstream targets of SHN transcription factors in cutin biosynthesis and cell wall remodeling.

genes: At5g33370 (GDSL-motif lipase/hydrolase, Arabidopsis thaliana), At3g04290 (LTL1, GDSL-motif lipase/hydrolase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-silencing of At5g33370 and At3g04290 causes fused and folded petals with abnormal adaxial epidermis cells.
mechanism: These GDSL-lipases are putative downstream targets of SHN transcription factors in cutin biosynthesis and cell wall remodeling.

genes: FUL-like (floral meristem identity, Actinidia spp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of FUL-like promotes floral transition in Arabidopsis under both long-day and short-day conditions, resulting in terminal flower phenotype.
mechanism: FUL-like likely promotes cellular expansion and differentiation, as reported for FUL in Arabidopsis.

genes: FUL (floral meristem identity, Actinidia spp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of FUL promotes flowering in Arabidopsis, with flowers indistinguishable from wild type, but less efficiently than FUL-like under short-day conditions.
mechanism: FUL likely promotes floral transition through meristem identity function, with day-length-dependent efficacy.

genes: SEP4 (floral meristem identity, Actinidia spp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of SEP4 promotes early flowering in Arabidopsis under long-day conditions and causes small, curled leaves.
mechanism: SEP4 likely promotes floral transition and affects leaf morphology through meristem identity and organ specification.

genes: AG (floral organ identity, Actinidia spp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of AG results in reduced plant height, curled leaves, and early flowering in Arabidopsis under short-day conditions, with loss of inflorescence indeterminacy and homeotic modifications.
mechanism: AG likely affects floral organ identity and meristem determinacy, similar to Arabidopsis AG overexpression.

genes: AaPMT (Putrescine N-methyltransferase, Anisodus acutangulus), AaTRI (tropinone reductase I, Anisodus acutangulus)
phenotype: Co-overexpression of AaPMT and AaTRI in Anisodus acutangulus hairy roots increased total tropane alkaloid (TA) content to 8.104 mg/g dry weight (dw) in line PT18, 8.66× higher than control (0.935 mg/g dw), with 49× and 19× higher scopolamine and anisodine yields than control.
mechanism: Co-overexpression of AaPMT (upstream rate-limiting enzyme) and AaTRI (branch-controlling enzyme) creates a 'push-pull' effect, increasing metabolic flux toward TA biosynthesis while reducing calystegine production.

genes: AaPMT (Putrescine N-methyltransferase, Anisodus acutangulus)
phenotype: AaPMT overexpression in Anisodus acutangulus hairy roots increased total TA content to 2.004 mg/g dw in line P3, 2.14× higher than control (0.935 mg/g dw), with 10.93× higher AaPMT gene expression than control.
mechanism: AaPMT overexpression increases metabolic flux through the TA biosynthesis pathway by enhancing putrescine N-methylation, the first rate-limiting step.

genes: AaTRI (tropinone reductase I, Anisodus acutangulus)
phenotype: AaTRI overexpression in Anisodus acutangulus hairy roots increased total TA content to 2.604 mg/g dw in line T12, 2.79× higher than control (0.935 mg/g dw), with 17.59× higher AaTRI gene expression than control.
mechanism: AaTRI overexpression enhances conversion of pseudotropine to tropine, increasing TA production while reducing calystegine accumulation.

genes: HC-Pro (Helper component-proteinase (P1/HC-Pro) encoded by the 5' proximal region of the TEV, PVY strain N)
phenotype: Overexpression of HC-Pro RSS induced clear phenotypic changes both in growth rate and in leaf and flower morphology of the tobacco plants
mechanism: HC-Pro RSS interferes with the silencing machinery

genes: CENH3 (CENH3, chimeric protein with maize tail, Zea mays and Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complemented GFP-maizetailswap plants showed the vegetative phenotype previously seen in GFP-tailswap plants but were even more sterile than GFP-tailswap plants (although one partially fertile GFP-maizetailswap plant was recovered).
mechanism: Sterility in GFP-tailswap and GFP-maizetailswap is caused by a severe meiosis-specific defect in centromere function.

genes: CENH3 (CENH3, N-terminal tail swapped, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: cenh3-1 plants expressing a tailswap transgene without GFP were viable and fertile, indicating that the meiosis-specific role of the CENH3 tail domain is evident only when protein function is compromised by the presence of an N-terminal GFP tag.
mechanism: Sterility in GFP-tailswap and GFP-maizetailswap is caused by a severe meiosis-specific defect in centromere function.

genes: CAH1 (HA-tagged carbonic anhydrase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of HA-tagged CAH1 results in glycosylated polypeptides with heterogeneous migration patterns in SDS-PAGE, localized primarily to chloroplasts with some ER/Golgi localization
mechanism: N-glycosylation at five sites and intramolecular disulphide bridges between Cys27 and Cys191 are required for proper folding, ER export, and enzymatic activity of CAH1

genes: GFP (Green Fluorescent Protein, marker, synthetic), aFGF (human acidic fibroblast growth factor, therapeutic protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of Green Fluorescent Protein as marker and human acidic fibroblast growth factor (aFGF) in 80% of infiltrated germinating pea seeds, with maximal recombinant protein production achieved 12-15 days post-infiltration.
mechanism: Use of modified pea early browning virus (PEBV) vectors for transient expression via Agrobacterium-mediated vacuum infiltration of germinated seeds.

genes: aFGF (human acidic fibroblast growth factor, therapeutic protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Synthesis of aFGF in pea plants with mitogenic activity confirmed to be similar to commercial product, stimulating NIH 3T3 cell growth.
mechanism: Use of modified pea early browning virus (PEBV) vectors for transient expression via Agrobacterium-mediated vacuum infiltration of germinated seeds.

genes: MIT (mitochondrial Fe transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of mit-2 plants with MITp-MIT significantly reversed growth defects, including plant height, chlorophyll content, and Fe and Mn accumulation.
mechanism: MIT transports Fe into mitochondria, restoring Fe homeostasis and mitochondrial function.

genes: MIT (mitochondrial Fe transporter, Oryza sativa), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: MIT-GFP localized to mitochondria in tobacco BY-2 cells.
mechanism: GFP tagging allows visualization of MIT localization.

genes: AtHaspin (At1g09450, histone H3 threonine kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AtHaspin-GFP was expressed in root meristems, shoot meristems, floral meristems, and throughout the whole embryo at stages of high cell division
mechanism: AtHaspin may have a role in mitotic cell division during plant growth

genes: AtHaspin-KD (kinase domain mutant, histone H3 threonine kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of a kinase domain mutant of AtHaspin decreased the size of the root meristem, which delayed root growth
mechanism: AtHaspin may have a role in mitotic cell division during plant growth

phenotype: GmPT1/GFP and GmPT2/GFP fusion proteins localized to the plasma membrane in onion epidermal cells, as observed by confocal microscopy.
mechanism: The fusion proteins are targeted to the plasma membrane, consistent with their role as phosphate transporters.

genes: FLC (FLOWERING LOCUS C, floral repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: FLC (FLOWERING LOCUS C, floral repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: HB33 (HB33, homeobox protein 33, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Reducing HB33 expression results in ABA resistance, indicating HB33 is a positive regulator in ABA signaling.

phenotype: Transgenic wheat seeds with antisense trx s gene exhibit slowed germination speed, increased seed hardness, and altered metabolism of storage proteins, starch, and nucleic acids compared to wild type Yumai 18 wheat seeds.

genes: AtTSPO (transporter of tetrapyrroles, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, Aequorea victoria)

genes: AtSIZ1 (E3 SUMO ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana), NIA1 (nitrate reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana), NIA2 (nitrate reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtSUMO1 (SUMO, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Sumoylation of NIA1 by AtSIZ1 at lysine 356 stabilizes the protein and enhances its nitrate reductase activity, leading to increased nitrite production and nitrogen assimilation.

genes: NIA1 (nitrate reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana), NIA2 (nitrate reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtSUMO1 (SUMO, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: FLA1 (FLA1 promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: FLA1p:GUS shows developmentally regulated expression in discrete tissues including leaf petiole, stomata, trichomes, anthers, and root tip/primordia. During callus induction, GUS activity increases in pericycle cells and vascular tissue, suggesting FLA1 involvement in early re-differentiation stages.
mechanism: FLA1 likely functions in cell identity regulation and auxin-dependent pathways during lateral root and shoot development. FLA1p:GUS expression correlates with auxin distribution patterns and callus formation processes.

genes: HPPD (p-hydroxyphenyl pyruvate dioxygenase, Pseudomonas fluorescens, Pseudomonas fluorescens)

mechanism: The upstream enhancer drives expression of the GFP reporter gene in shoot and root apical meristem regions.

mechanism: Wild type AGO6 cDNA complements the ago6-4 mutation by restoring RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) and transcriptional silencing of the GFP gene.

mechanism: Ectopic AtJMT diverts JA pathway flux towards MeJA production, depleting free JA pools required for JA-Ile synthesis and defense gene activation. MeJA lacks direct defense signaling function in Nicotiana attenuata

genes: MuSI (MuSI, metallothionein-like gene, sweet potato)
phenotype: Enhanced Cd tolerance in transgenic tobacco plants with reduced Cd accumulation in shoots and leaves (4.65 ± 0.32 mg Cd per plant in wild-type vs 2.37 ± 0.12 mg in transgenic plants at 200 μM Cd).
mechanism: Reduced Cd translocation from roots to shoots via formation of Cd-thiol complexes in trichomes and/or Cd immobilization around roots.

genes: MdEXP2 (expansin-resembling protein, Micrasterias denticulata)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdEXP2 causes phenotypic changes including lobe elongation, loss of growth polarity, and planarity in Micrasterias denticulata cells.
mechanism: MdEXP2 alters cell wall structure, potentially through mechanisms related to land plant expansins during cell morphogenesis.

genes: PlOS (PlOS, (E)-β-ocimene synthase from lima bean, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PlOS in tobacco increases (E)-β-ocimene emission by ~200x compared to wild type (166-384 ng/gFW/h vs 2 ng/gFW/h).
mechanism: Elevated (E)-β-ocimene emission primes indirect defenses in neighboring plants by enhancing VOC emission and attracting predatory mites.

genes: AtRbcX1 (AtRbcX1, RbcX protein involved in Rubisco assembly, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtRbcX2 (AtRbcX2, RbcX protein involved in Rubisco assembly, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NA

mechanism: CJD1 is a chloroplast membrane protein with three transmembrane domains and a J-like domain; CJD1-GFP is protected from Trypsin digestion, indicating inner envelope membrane localization

genes: HPT (hygromycin phosphotransferase, resistance gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of HPT confers hygromycin resistance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HPT expression is regulated by chromatin modifications (H3K4me3 vs H3K9me2) and small RNA abundance, with active epialleles showing open chromatin and no DNA methylation.

genes: AtPORC (AtPORC, chlorophyllide reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtPORC increases chlorophyll content by ~28% and carotenoid content in Arabidopsis thaliana, resulting in greener leaves and increased LHC II protein (33-58% higher).

Increased gene/protein expression of Chl biosynthetic enzymes (GluTR, GSAT, UROD, CHLP) further supports Chl synthesis.

genes: FUT8 (human core α1,6 fucosyltransferase, human), STGalT (human β1,4 galactosyltransferase, human), STGnTIII (human β1,4-mannosyl-β1,4-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase, human)

mechanism: Transient co-expression of human glycosyltransferases (FUT8, STGalT, STGnTIII) in ΔXTFT plants modifies N-glycans on h-13F6 to human-like structures.

genes: FUT11GnTIII (human β1,4-mannosyl-β1,4-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase fused to Arabidopsis thaliana core α1,3 fucosyltransferase CTS, human)
phenotype: Significant reduction of plant-specific N-glycan residues (core α1,3 fucose and xylose) in h-13F6 produced in WT plants, with efficient generation of galactosylated structures when co-expressed with STGalT.
mechanism: Transient co-expression of FUT11GnTIII in WT plants redirects glycosylation machinery to reduce plant-specific residues and enable galactosylation.

genes: PDS (phytoene desaturase, endogenous gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Chemical induction of pX7-Pdsi transgene triggers photobleaching via silencing of endogenous PDS gene in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Intron-containing inverted-repeat Pds transcript (Pdsi) induces RNA silencing pathways (PTGS and TGS) to suppress PDS mRNA, leading to carotenoid deficiency and photobleaching

genes: cry9Aa2 (insecticidal protein conferring resistance to potato tuber moth (PTM), modified version from this study)
phenotype: Overexpression of modified cry9Aa2 confers resistance to potato tuber moth (PTM) in potato cultivars, with 191 of 212 transgenic lines showing significantly reduced larval growth indices (GI) compared to non-transgenic controls.
mechanism: Expression of the Cry9Aa2 protein in transgenic potato foliage inhibits PTM larval growth, with surviving larvae showing substantially lower weights and extensive leaf damage in control plants.

genes: PHYB-401 (photoreceptor, phyB mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana), PHYB (photoreceptor, wild-type, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHYB-401:YFP and PHYB-401:GFP fusion proteins in phyB-9 background causes extreme hypersensitivity to red light (cR), with hypocotyl growth inhibition saturation at ~0.001 µmol m−2 s−1 compared to ~1 µmol m−2 s−1 in wild-type. Transgenic lines display stable phenotypes and fully complement the phyB-9 mutant.
mechanism: PHYB-401:YFP and GFP fusion proteins exhibit reduced dark reversion kinetics in vivo, leading to increased stability of the Pfr form. This enhanced Pfr stability results in heightened sensitivity to low-intensity red light and altered nuclear body (NB) formation dynamics compared to wild-type PHYB:YFP/GFP.

genes: PHYB-401 (photoreceptor, phyB mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHYB-401:GFP in phyB-9 background results in hypersensitivity to red light (R) and far-red light (FR). Transgenic lines show extreme hypersensitivity to R with hypocotyl growth inhibition saturation at ~0.001 µmol m−2 s−1. FR pulses induce CAB2 mRNA accumulation in phyB-401/phyA-201 seedlings at fluences where phyA-201 remains unresponsive.
mechanism: PHYB-401:GFP exhibits reduced dark reversion kinetics and forms a stable Pfr-like Pr* conformer that persists in darkness. This Pr* form is biologically active and accumulates with increasing FR fluence rates, explaining the hypersensitivity to continuous FR and altered photoreversibility.

genes: TSO1 (TSO1, suppressor of tso1-1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Artificial microRNA knockdown of tso1-1 transcripts suppresses tso1-1 phenotype, with tso1-1; amiRTSO1 plants showing wild-type floral and meristem development but severe fertility defects (short siliques, sterility).
mechanism: amiRTSO1 reduces tso1-1 mutant transcripts to ~15% of untransformed levels, removing the antimorphic (interfering) effect of tso1-1 on redundant factors like SOL1/SOL2.

genes: tso1-1 (tso1-1, antimorphic allele, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of tso1-1 in wild-type or tso1-1 heterozygous plants does not produce mutant phenotypes, despite tso1-1 transcripts being higher than endogenous TSO1.
mechanism: tso1-1 overexpression fails to cause phenotypic defects when wild-type TSO1 is present, indicating tso1-1 is recessive to wild-type TSO1.

genes: TSO1 (TSO1, wild-type, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TSO1-GFP in tso1-1 plants rescues the tso1-1 phenotype, with three out of four independent lines showing complete rescue to wild-type morphology.
mechanism: Wild-type TSO1 overexpression suppresses the antimorphic effects of tso1-1, restoring normal floral and meristem development.

genes: EDS1-80 (EDS1-80, EDS1 isoform 80, Arabidopsis thaliana), EDS1-90 (EDS1-90, EDS1 isoform 90, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Both EDS1-80 and EDS1-90 encode functional proteins that complement the enhanced disease susceptibility phenotype in eds1-1 plants by restoring pathogen defense signaling.

phenotype: Overexpression of AIL1 prevents growth cessation and bud set in hybrid aspen after 6 weeks of short day treatment.
mechanism: AIL1 is a downstream target of the SD signal, and its overexpression maintains cell cycle activity, preventing growth cessation.

genes: AIL3 (AINTEGUMENTALIKE 3, transcription factor, Populus tremula x tremuloides)
phenotype: Overexpression of AIL3 prevents growth cessation and bud set in hybrid aspen after 6 weeks of short day treatment.
mechanism: AIL3 is a downstream target of the SD signal, and its overexpression maintains cell cycle activity, preventing growth cessation.

genes: uidA (b-glucuronidase/GUS, reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS reporter gene expression is confined to the zone of dividing cells in the apex, provascular tissues, and leaf primordia of hybrid aspen.
mechanism: The AIL1 promoter drives GUS expression in actively dividing cells, correlating with cell proliferation markers.

genes: amiRNA (artificial microRNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Downregulation of all four AIL genes leads to earlier bud set in hybrid aspen after short day treatment.
mechanism: amiRNA255 targets AIL1-4 transcripts, accelerating the transition from active growth to bud set.

genes: amiRNA (artificial microRNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Downregulation of all four AIL genes leads to earlier bud set in hybrid aspen after short day treatment.
mechanism: amiRNA256 targets AIL1-4 transcripts, accelerating the transition from active growth to bud set.

genes: GPC (Grain Protein Content 1, transcription factor, Triticum aestivum), GPC-2 (Grain Protein Content 2, paralog, Triticum aestivum)

mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of GPC transcription factor, which is an early positive regulator of monocarpic senescence and nutrient remobilization

genes: gusA (wild-type, β-glucuronidase reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Overexpression of wild-type GUS (gusA) in Arabidopsis thaliana results in detectable β-glucuronidase activity at 45°C, with no noticeable morphological differences compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: Wild-type GUS activity is optimal at 45°C but loses activity after 60°C treatment for 10 minutes.

genes: gusA (mutant TR3337, thermostable β-glucuronidase reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Overexpression of thermostable GUS-TR3337 in Arabidopsis thaliana retains ~70% GUS activity after 80°C treatment for 10 minutes and ~50% after 30 minutes, compared to complete inactivation of wild-type GUS at 60°C.
mechanism: Six amino acid substitutions (Q493R, T509A, M532T, N550S, G559S, N566S) in GUS-TR3337 confer thermostability, allowing detection of transgenic activity at high temperatures while endogenous GUS is inactivated.

genes: CaNDR1a (non-race specific disease resistance protein, Coffea arabica, synthetic)

mechanism: CaNDR1a localizes to the plasma membrane and functions similarly to Arabidopsis NDR1 in disease resistance signaling, likely via GPI-anchor tethering and interaction with RIN4.

genes: hG-CSF (hG-CSF, human granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, human)
phenotype: hG-CSF accumulates at ~0.3 mg/g total soluble protein (TSP) in leaves and ~0.5 mg/g TSP in seeds, with no ubiquitin fusion.
mechanism: hG-CSF is secreted into apoplast in leaves and deposited in protein storage vacuole (PSV) in seeds via phaseolin signal peptide.

phenotype: 35S∶GNC overexpression lines demonstrate altered developmental timing, including delayed germination and flowering, and reduced chlorophyll content compared to wild type.

genes: CGA1 (CGA1, GATA-type transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CGA1 overexpression lines show delayed germination, reduced leaf expansion, and increased chlorophyll content compared to wild type.
mechanism: CGA1 enhances chlorophyll biosynthesis and modulates cytokinin-gibberellin cross-talk.

genes: CGA1 (CGA1, GATA-type transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: CGA1 modulates cytokinin and gibberellin signaling, influencing chloroplast development and nitrogen assimilation.

mechanism: GNC promoter drives GUS expression in chloroplast development-related tissues.

genes: CGA1 (CGA1, GATA-type transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: CGA1 promoter drives GUS expression in cytokinin and gibberellin signaling-related tissues.

phenotype: Expression of bZIP60ΔC activates promoters of ER stress-inducible genes in protoplasts
mechanism: bZIP60ΔC activates ER stress-inducible gene promoters by acting as a transcription factor in the nucleus

mechanism: RNA silencing

mechanism: RNA silencing

mechanism: FT RNA function independent of FT protein

mechanism: FT RNA acts as transporter facilitating endogenous tobacco FT protein trafficking to shoot apex

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)

mechanism: The γ-TMT3 promoter from KAS has higher transcriptional activity than the Ichihime promoter due to polymorphisms in cis-regulatory elements including a MYB binding site and altered CAAT box motif.

genes: pm3b (pm3b, race-specific resistance to powdery mildew, hexaploid wheat landrace Chul)
phenotype: Overexpression of pm3b increases resistance to powdery mildew in Triticum aestivum.
mechanism: pm3b confers race-specific resistance to powdery mildew.

genes: chitinase (chitinase, anti-fungal effect, barley seed)
phenotype: Overexpression of chitinase increases quantitative resistance to mildew in Triticum aestivum.
mechanism: Chitinases are known for their anti-fungal effect.

mechanism: Chitinases and glucanases are known for their anti-fungal effect.

genes: OsWRKY13 (OsWRKY13, RNAi, synthetic)
phenotype: Increased susceptibility to Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) in rice variety Minghui 63
mechanism: OsWRKY13 suppression leads to downregulation of defense-related genes and reduced disease resistance

mechanism: ELP-induced PBs exclude heterologous protein from ER-associated degradation (ERAD), encapsulate recombinant proteins in inert organelles, and utilize actin microfilaments/myosin XI-K for dynamic movement

genes: BiP (endoplasmic reticulum luminal binding protein, Nicotiana tabacum, source), CFP (cyan fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)

mechanism: BiP is passively incorporated into PBs during formation; no specific interaction with ELP tag detected

genes: YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic), ELP (elastin-like polypeptide, 28×VPGVG, synthetic), KDEL (ER retention signal, synthetic)
phenotype: ER-targeted YFP-ELP fusion induces PB formation similar to GFP-ELP constructs
mechanism: Same as GFP-ELP constructs: PBs exclude heterologous protein from ERAD and utilize actin/myosin for movement

genes: OsCYP96B4 (cytochrome P450, rice, genomic region including 2 kb promoter and 1 kb 3' UTR)

mechanism: OsCYP96B4 is essential for normal plant height and fertility; its disruption by Ds insertion causes semi-dwarfism and pollen germination defects.

genes: OsCYP96B4 (cytochrome P450, rice, 525 bp 5' UTR and coding region)

genes: OsCYP96B4 (cytochrome P450, rice)

genes: OsCYP96B4 (cytochrome P450, rice)

mechanism: OsCYP96B4 overexpression in Arabidopsis disrupts cell elongation, similar to its effect in rice.

genes: OsCYP96B4 (cytochrome P450, rice)

mechanism: OsCYP96B4 is expressed in multiple tissues with highest activity in reproductive organs, suggesting a role in development.

mechanism: Elevated AOX expression through the alternative respiratory pathway correlates with increased resistance to TSWV, potentially through modulation of reactive oxygen species or pathogen-induced signaling pathways

genes: FLS (flavonol synthase, Nicotiana tabacum)

mechanism: FLS silencing reduces flavonol synthesis, leading to altered flavonoid pathway flux, decreased auxin transport, and impaired pollen function.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)

mechanism: NA

genes: NVCP (Norwalk virus capsid protein, vaccine candidate, synthetic)

genes: AtASY3 (AtASY3, meiotic chromosome axis protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of Atasy3-1 with AtASY3 cDNA under AtDMC1 promoter restores normal meiosis in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtASY3 is required for normal meiosis, SC formation, and crossover formation during meiosis.

genes: R1 (R1, resistance gene, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Overexpression of R1 induces hypersensitive resistance response in potato.
mechanism: R1 confers resistance to P. infestans carrying Avr1.

genes: r1.1 (r1.1, unknown function, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Expression of r1.1 does not confer resistance to P. infestans carrying Avr1.
mechanism: NA

genes: sak (staphylokinase, coding sequence, pTrxFusSTA)
phenotype: Production of recombinant staphylokinase in transgenic potato plants
mechanism: Expression of staphylokinase under CaMV 35S promoter in transgenic plants

genes: b1 (transcription factor activating anthocyanin biosynthetic genes, maize)
phenotype: Overexpression of B-I leads to red/purple anthocyanin pigmentation in tissues where expressed
mechanism: B-I encodes a transcription factor which activates anthocyanin biosynthetic genes

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter), amiRNA-854 (artificial microRNA targeting UBP1b 3'UTR)
phenotype: Plants expressing the siRNA854 sequence as an artificial microRNA show significantly reduced GUS levels compared to control amiRNA-expressing plants.
mechanism: siRNA854 targets the UBP1b 3'UTR via RNAi, leading to translational repression of the GUS reporter protein.

genes: UBP1b (3'UTR modified/deleted), amiRNA-854 (artificial microRNA targeting UBP1b 3'UTR)
phenotype: In wt Col pollen, the UBP1b 3'UTR transgene with siRNA854 target sites shows significantly reduced GFP fluorescence compared to controls. Abrogation of siRNA854 target sites (MOD or DEL transgenes) alleviates this repression.
mechanism: siRNA854 binds to UBP1b 3'UTR target sites via RNAi, causing translational repression of the GFP reporter. RDR6 is required for this regulation.

genes: MYB21 (MYB21, MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP::MYB21 under the CaMV35S promoter rescues the anther dehiscence defect and restores petal and stamen elongation in myb21-5 mutants.
mechanism: GFP::MYB21 fusion protein restores normal MYB21 function, promoting stamen and petal development through jasmonate-dependent pathways.

genes: MYB108 (MYB108, MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MYB108 under its native promoter leads to expression in sepals and stamen filaments, particularly in the vasculature, and in the style.
mechanism: MYB108 may regulate vascular development and style formation in flowers, contributing to pollen tube growth and fertilization.

genes: LecRK-V.5 (LecRK-V.5, lectin receptor kinase involved in stomatal immunity, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of lecrk-V.5-1 mutant restored wild-type susceptibility to Pst DC3000.
mechanism: LecRK-V.5 negatively regulates Arabidopsis resistance to Pst DC3000 by modulating stomatal immunity and ABA signaling.

genes: LecRK-V.5 (LecRK-V.5, lectin receptor kinase involved in stomatal immunity, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of LecRK-V.5 increased susceptibility to Pst DC3000 with bacterial titers ~250 times higher than wild-type.
mechanism: LecRK-V.5 negatively regulates Arabidopsis resistance to Pst DC3000 by promoting stomatal reopening and impairing ABA-mediated ROS production.

genes: LecRK-V.5 (LecRK-V.5, lectin receptor kinase involved in stomatal immunity, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of lecrk-V.5-1 mutant restored wild-type susceptibility to Pst DC3000.
mechanism: LecRK-V.5 negatively regulates Arabidopsis resistance to Pst DC3000 by modulating stomatal immunity and ABA signaling.

genes: LecRK-V.5 (LecRK-V.5, lectin receptor kinase involved in stomatal immunity, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of LecRK-V.5 increased susceptibility to Pst DC3000 with bacterial titers ~250 times higher than wild-type.
mechanism: LecRK-V.5 negatively regulates Arabidopsis resistance to Pst DC3000 by promoting stomatal reopening and impairing ABA-mediated ROS production.

genes: MHBsAg (medium surface antigen of HBV, HBV subtype ayw4), LHBsAg (large surface antigen of HBV, HBV subtype ayw4)
phenotype: Expression of M- and L-HBsAg in transgenic lettuce and tobacco plants, with antigen levels ranging from 0.4–12.8 μg/g fresh weight in tobacco and 0.4–2.2 μg/g in lettuce. Antigens assembled into VLPs (virus-like particles) displaying preS2 and preS1 domains.
mechanism: HBsAg proteins assemble into VLPs (virus-like particles) via their S domain and preS domains, forming immunogenic structures. M-HBsAg forms more stable VLPs than L-HBsAg due to differences in preS domain size and structure.

genes: FT (flowering time gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FT causes precocious flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: FT acts as a floral integrator, promoting flowering by downstream targets like SOC1.

genes: CRP (flowering regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRP::GUS shows ubiquitous expression in seedlings with higher levels in vascular tissue and shoot apex.
mechanism: CRP is expressed in vascular tissue and shoot apex, suggesting roles in flowering regulation.

genes: CRP (flowering regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S::CRP transgenic plants show delayed flowering in long-day conditions.
mechanism: Overexpression of CRP reduces FT and TSF expression, delaying flowering.

genes: FT (flowering time gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SULTR2;1::FT partially suppresses the late-flowering phenotype of crp loss-of-function mutants.
mechanism: Phloem-specific FT expression partially restores flowering time in crp mutants.

genes: TSF (flowering time gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S::TSF overexpression causes precocious flowering, enhanced by crp-1D mutation.
mechanism: TSF acts redundantly with FT, and crp-1D enhances its flowering promotion.

genes: CRP (flowering regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRP-GFP and crp-1D-GFP fusion proteins localize to the nuclear region in onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: CRP and crp-1D proteins are nuclear-localized, suggesting nuclear function in flowering regulation.

genes: granule-bound starch synthase (granule-bound starch synthase, involved in amylose production, Solanum tuberosum)
gene_construct: NA-granule-bound starch synthase (granule-bound starch synthase, involved in amylose production, Solanum tuberosum)-NA
phenotype: Higher relative amylopectin yields in tubers due to blocked amylose production
mechanism: Antisense knock down of granule-bound starch synthase blocks amylose production

genes: nAChRbp (disulphide constrained 7-mer peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic potato lines expressing the nAChRbp peptide confer up to 77±4% resistance to Globodera pallida in field trials.
mechanism: The nAChRbp peptide inhibits nematode chemoreception by binding to acetylcholine receptors, suppressing pathogenesis before cyst formation.

genes: IRE1b (IRE1b, RNAi silencing, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Severe depletion of both basal and induced IRE1b transcripts in Col-0 and ire1a-2 backgrounds
mechanism: RNAi silencing of IRE1b transcript

genes: AtMYB90 (AtMYB90, R2R3-Myb transcription factor associated with anthocyanin pigment production, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtMYB90 in Nicotiana tabacum produces a darkly pigmented (anthocyanins) phenotype in nearly all plant tissues.
mechanism: AtMYB90 enhances anthocyanin pigment production by ectopic over-expression in transgenic tobacco plants.

genes: PtrDFR1 (dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, Populus trichocarpa, synthetic), PtrDFR2 (dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, Populus trichocarpa, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtrDFR1 increases anthocyanin accumulation by ~3-fold in transgenic tobacco flowers and by ~3-fold in transgenic poplar leaves compared to wild-type controls.
mechanism: PtrDFR1 interacts with endogenous enzymes of anthocyanin biosynthetic pathways in tobacco, enhancing anthocyanin accumulation. In poplar, overexpression increases condensed tannin (CT) content by ~3-fold in leaf tissues.

genes: PtrDFR1 (dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, Populus trichocarpa, synthetic), PtrDFR2 (dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, Populus trichocarpa, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtrDFR2 increases condensed tannin (CT) content by ~2-fold in transgenic poplar leaves compared to wild-type controls. No significant increase in anthocyanin accumulation is observed in transgenic tobacco or poplar.
mechanism: PtrDFR2 correlates poorly with anthocyanin accumulation in Populus but correlates well with CT accumulation. Overexpression enhances CT biosynthesis in poplar.

genes: At2S3::GFP (synthetic, selectable marker, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic seeds exhibit green fluorescence under UV illumination due to At2S3::GFP expression
mechanism: At2S3::GFP serves as a selectable marker for transgenic plants

genes: eIF(iso)4E (eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E isoform, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of eIF(iso)4E increases eIF(iso)4E RNA levels by 2.5-3.5 times in 15-day-old seedlings compared to wild type.
mechanism: The eIF(iso)4E-GFP fusion allows functional analysis of eIF(iso)4E in mRNA cap-binding and translation initiation, with increased translational recruitment of specific mRNAs like PHO1.

genes: eIF4E (eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of eIF4E serves as a control for experiments, with no significant changes in polyribosomal distribution of mRNAs compared to wild type.
mechanism: The eIF4E-GFP fusion is used as a control to distinguish eIF(iso)4E-specific effects from general eIF4E function in translation initiation.

genes: PGL1 (Os03g0171300, atypical bHLH gene, rice)
phenotype: Overexpression of PGL1 increases grain length and weight in rice.
mechanism: PGL1 interacts with APG, an atypical bHLH protein, to regulate cell elongation in lemma/palea.

genes: APG (Os05g0139100, typical bHLH gene, rice)
phenotype: Suppression of APG increases grain length and weight in rice.
mechanism: APG is a negative regulator of grain length, and its suppression leads to cell elongation in lemma/palea.

genes: YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: YFP-positive regenerated calli form lateral haustoria that penetrate host roots and can be visualized under UV illumination
mechanism: YFP serves as a visual marker for transgenic tissue identification and tracking

genes: OsNRAMP5 (promoter, promoter of OsNRAMP5, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: GUS staining in root epidermis, exodermis, and outer cortex layers
mechanism: NA

genes: NbPCNA (Nicotiana benthamiana proliferating cell nuclear antigen, sliding clamp of host DNA replicase, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: VIGS of NbPCNA causes stunted growth, distorted leaves, and upward curling of young leaves in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: NbPCNA is a sliding clamp of host DNA replicase; its silencing disrupts DNA replication machinery, but ACMV Rep alone cannot restore replication in older leaves.

genes: Lycb-1 (Lycb-1, citrus Lycb-1, citrus)
phenotype: Overexpression of Lycb-1 increases β-carotene content by ~1.1 mg/gDW in tomato fruit, with 30% higher total carotenoid content than wild type.
mechanism: Up-regulation of upstream flux (Psy, Dxs) and down-regulation of Zep reduces carotenoid degradation, increasing β-carotene accumulation.

genes: SND2 (AT4G28500, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of SND2 in Eucalyptus leads to increased fibre cell area.
mechanism: SND2 regulates cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin biosynthesis genes.

genes: RD21 (RD21 protease domain, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), ΔPG (RD21 protease domain with granulin and proline-rich domains deleted, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), ΔG (RD21 protease domain with granulin domain deleted, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), 3C3A (RD21 protease domain with three Cys residues replaced by Ala, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), C161A (RD21 protease domain with Cys161 replaced by Ala, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), H297A (RD21 protease domain with His297 replaced by Ala, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), N317A (RD21 protease domain with Asn317 replaced by Ala, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), +PGS (RD21 protease domain with D180N and I182T substitutions to create a PGS, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), -PGS (RD21 protease domain with N414A substitution to remove PGS, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
modification_type: overexpression, gene editing (CRISPR), gene editing (CRISPR), gene editing (CRISPR), gene editing (CRISPR), gene editing (CRISPR), gene editing (CRISPR), gene editing (CRISPR), knockout
phenotype: Overexpression of RD21 and its mutants in N. benthamiana leads to accumulation of active iRD21 and mRD21 isoforms that degrade rubisco in extracts. ΔPG mutant is inactive. ΔG and 3C3A mutants are active. C161A and H297A mutants are inactive. N317A mutant has reduced activity. +PGS mutant shows N-glycosylation and Golgi transit. -PGS mutant lacks glycosylation.
mechanism: RD21 protease activity degrades rubisco. Prodomain removal and granulin domain removal are required for activation. N-glycosylation indicates Golgi transit. Catalytic triad (Cys161, His297, Asn317) is essential for activity. SDS activates latent RD21 by denaturing inhibitors.

genes: PtaGTL1 (Populus trichocarpa GTL1 homolog, transcription factor with DNA-binding domains and CaM-binding site, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Suppresses gtl1-4 trichome phenotype by restoring normal trichome branch length to wild-type levels in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: PtaGTL1 trans-represses SDD1 expression, a negative regulator of stomatal development, through binding to GT3/GT2 boxes in the SDD1 promoter and Ca2+/CaM-dependent modulation of transcriptional activity

plant_species: Populus tremula L. × P. tremuloides Michx.
genes: TRANSPOSASE (Ac element from Zea mays), hpt (hygromycin phosphotransferase from Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Enables heat-inducible transposase activity for ATDs excision and reintegration, leading to phenotypic variants in poplar.
mechanism: Heat shock induces transposase expression, enabling ATDs transposition to activate or disrupt endogenous genes.

genes: FUS3 (FUSCA3, transcription factor regulating seed maturation and dormancy, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FUS3 inhibits seed germination at supraoptimal temperature and increases seedling survival when temperatures become optimal for growth
mechanism: FUS3 delays germination by increasing ABA levels and repressing GA biosynthesis, stabilizing FUS3 protein through ABA feedback regulation

genes: nosF (nitrous oxide reductase subunit F, Pseudomonas stutzeri), nosD (nitrous oxide reductase subunit D, Pseudomonas stutzeri), nosY (nitrous oxide reductase subunit Y, Pseudomonas stutzeri), nosL (nitrous oxide reductase subunit L, Pseudomonas stutzeri)
phenotype: Expression of N2OR in tobacco roots enables N2O reduction to N2, with specific activities up to 2.19 µmol N2O reduced min⁻¹ g⁻¹ root secreted protein in some lines.
mechanism: N2OR catalyzes the conversion of N2O to N2, reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

genes: FUS3 (FUS3-glucocorticoid receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Activation of FUS3-GR leads to changes in leaf identity, including increased paddle-like shape and shorter petiole.
mechanism: FUS3 negatively regulates ethylene action, which affects vegetative phase transitions.

genes: FUS3 (FUS3-glucocorticoid receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Partial or full rescue of leaf heteroblasty towards wild-type profile when activated with DEX.
mechanism: FUS3 functions postembryonically to delay vegetative phase transitions by modulating ethylene-regulated gene expression.

genes: EIN3 (EIN3 fused with GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased protein stability of EIN3 in fus3 mutants, which is reduced by ethylene signaling inhibitors.
mechanism: EIN3 is a key positive regulator of ethylene signaling, and its stability is affected by FUS3.

genes: FaZnF (Festuca arundinacea zinc finger protein, transcription factor involved in salt stress response, Festuca arundinacea)
phenotype: Overexpression of FaZnF increases transcription of stress-related genes including MAPK (3-fold), GST24 (5-fold), and lipoxygenase L-2 (3-fold) in Festuca arundinacea calli.
mechanism: FaZnF, containing A20/AN1 zinc finger domains, likely functions as a transcription factor regulating stress response pathways by modulating gene expression of MAPK, GST24, and lipoxygenase L-2 during salt stress.

genes: E1 (cellulose hydrolytic enzyme β-1,4-endoglucanase, Acidothermus cellulolyticus)
phenotype: Overexpression of E1 in rice leads to E1 protein accumulation up to 6.1% of total leaf soluble protein and 43% increased reducing sugars in transgenic rice straw hydrolysis
mechanism: Thermostable E1 enzyme (optimum 81°C) enables efficient cellulose hydrolysis during saccharification

genes: HA (hemagglutinin, from influenza A virus)
phenotype: Expression of recombinant HA (rHA0) in N. benthamiana leaves reaches 210 mg/kg fresh weight, with 9.7% of total soluble protein. rHA0 retains hemagglutination activity and antigenic specificity to H7 subtype.
mechanism: rHA0 is N-glycosylated, retains native structure, and functions as a hemagglutinin. The ER retention signal (SEKDEL) ensures proper folding and stability.

genes: LUC (firefly luciferase, reporter gene, firefly)
phenotype: The LUC activity was profoundly inhibited by the presence of 6% sucrose in the wild type construct, indicating SIRT mediated by the SC-uORF.
mechanism: SIRT mediated by the SC-uORF in tbz17 controls translation of LUC in response to sucrose.

genes: LUC (firefly luciferase, reporter gene, firefly)
phenotype: The LUC activity with the mutated construct was not repressed by sucrose, indicating loss of SIRT regulation.
mechanism: The mutated SC-uORF lost regulation ability, leading to unresponsive LUC translation to sucrose.

genes: tbz17 (tobacco bZIP transcription factor, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: tbz17-ox plants showed smaller and pale-green leaves, thicker leaves with enlarged cells, and increased fresh weight per leaf area.
mechanism: SIRT-insensitive tbz17 overexpression leads to sucrose accumulation and cell enlargement via upregulation of ASN and sucrose-synthesizing genes.

genes: AtbZIP53 (bZIP transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AtbZIP53-ox plants had 1.5- to 2.5-fold higher sucrose content compared to wild type, with reduced glucose and fructose.
mechanism: Overexpression of AtbZIP53 upregulates sucrose-synthesizing genes (SPS, SPP) and ASN, leading to increased sucrose accumulation.

genes: AtbZIP53 (bZIP transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Histochemical GUS staining confirmed SIRT in AtbZIP53, with repression by sucrose but not by glucose or fructose.
mechanism: SIRT in AtbZIP53 is mediated by its SC-uORF, repressing GUS translation in response to sucrose.

genes: hNIS (human sodium-iodide symporter, human, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of hNIS increases iodine uptake in Arabidopsis thaliana, particularly at 30°C, with higher iodine accumulation in roots and young tissues.
mechanism: hNIS acts as a sodium-iodide symporter, facilitating active transport of iodide into plant cells.

genes: OsMCA1 (OsMCA1, putative Ca2+-permeable mechanosensitive channel, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsMCA1 increases Ca2+ uptake in cultured rice cells.
mechanism: OsMCA1 is involved in regulation of plasma membrane Ca2+ influx and ROS generation induced by hypo-osmotic stress.

genes: OsMCA1 (OsMCA1, putative Ca2+-permeable mechanosensitive channel, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsMCA1-suppressed plants showed retarded growth and shortened rachises.
mechanism: OsMCA1 plays a role in regulation of plasma membrane Ca2+ influx and ROS generation induced by hypo-osmotic stress.

genes: PIF4 (PIF4, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PIF4 increases YUC8 expression and elevates endogenous free IAA levels by ~50%, leading to a long hypocotyl phenotype resembling high temperature-grown wild-type seedlings.
mechanism: PIF4 directly binds to the G-box motif in the YUC8 promoter and activates its expression, thereby increasing auxin biosynthesis.

genes: PIF4 (PIF4, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Chemical-inducible overexpression of PIF4 (pMDC7:PIF4) results in increased YUC8 expression and elevated free IAA levels, with a long hypocotyl phenotype similar to 35S-PIF4 plants.
mechanism: PIF4 activates YUC8 expression via direct promoter binding, leading to auxin biosynthesis and hypocotyl elongation.

genes: LUC (luciferase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient expression of pYUC8:LUC in N. benthamiana leaves shows increased luminescence when co-expressed with PIF4, confirming PIF4's activation of YUC8 promoter.
mechanism: PIF4 binds to G-box motifs in the YUC8 promoter, activating its expression in transient assays.

genes: JcFAD2-1 (delta 12 fatty acid desaturase, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcFAD2-1 RNAi increases oleic acid to >78% and reduces polyunsaturated fatty acids to <3% in Jatropha curcas seeds.
mechanism: JcFAD2-1 mediates conversion of oleic acid to linoleic acid; RNAi suppression blocks this conversion, increasing oleic acid and reducing linoleic acid.

genes: TE (LOC_Os03g03150, homologue of Cdh1 involved in cell-cycle regulation and tillering, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of TE in rice reduces tiller number by ~70% compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: TE mediates degradation of MOC1, a positive regulator of tillering, via the ubiquitin-26S proteasome pathway, downregulating meristem identity genes like OSH1.

genes: HvAACT1 (citrate transporter, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Overexpression of HvAACT1 in root tips increases Al-induced citrate secretion by ~50-fold in root tips and 3-fold in other root regions, enhancing Al tolerance in barley.
mechanism: HvAACT1 enhances citrate secretion to the rhizosphere, protecting root tips from Al toxicity by forming citrate-Al complexes.

genes: HvAACT1 (citrate transporter, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Overexpression of HvAACT1 in root tips increases Al-induced citrate secretion by ~50-fold in root tips and 3-fold in other root regions, enhancing Al tolerance in barley.
mechanism: HvAACT1 enhances citrate secretion to the rhizosphere, protecting root tips from Al toxicity by forming citrate-Al complexes.

genes: HvAACT1 (citrate transporter, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: HvAACT1 complements the osfrdl1 rice mutant, restoring Fe translocation to wild-type levels with increased citrate and Fe in xylem sap and reduced root Fe precipitates.
mechanism: HvAACT1 transports citrate into xylem, forming Fe-citrate complexes to prevent Fe precipitation and enable Fe translocation from roots to shoots.

genes: AmDOD (Amanita muscaria DOPA dioxygenase, Amanita muscaria)
phenotype: Stably transformed Arabidopsis thaliana lines containing 35S: AmDOD produced yellow colouration in flowers and orange-red colouration in seedlings when fed L-DOPA. These tissues also showed green autofluorescence. HPLC analysis of the transgenic seedlings fed L-DOPA confirmed betaxanthin production.
mechanism: The product of DOD action on L-DOPA is betalamic acid. Betaxanthins can be produced by spontaneous reactions of the DOD reaction end-product, betalamic acid, with amino acids or amines.

genes: AmDOD (Amanita muscaria DOPA dioxygenase, Amanita muscaria)
phenotype: In the cells transformed with either 35S: PgDOD or 35S: AmDOD and fed L-DOPA, pigmented multi-celled clusters were apparent within 24 h post-bombardment. Both 35S: AmDOD and 35S: PgDOD resulted in yellow and orange cell clusters. The yellow and red pigmentation suggests that betaxanthin and betacyanin production, respectively, had been conferred to the cells.
mechanism: The product of DOD action on L-DOPA is betalamic acid. Betaxanthins can be produced by spontaneous reactions of the DOD reaction end-product, betalamic acid, with amino acids or amines.

genes: PgDOD (Portulaca grandiflora DOPA dioxygenase, Portulaca grandiflora)
phenotype: In the cells transformed with either 35S: PgDOD or 35S: AmDOD and fed L-DOPA, pigmented multi-celled clusters were apparent within 24 h post-bombardment. Both 35S: AmDOD and 35S: PgDOD resulted in yellow and orange cell clusters. The yellow and red pigmentation suggests that betaxanthin and betacyanin production, respectively, had been conferred to the cells.
mechanism: The product of DOD action on L-DOPA is betalamic acid. Betaxanthins can be produced by spontaneous reactions of the DOD reaction end-product, betalamic acid, with amino acids or amines.

genes: PIN1 (PIN1, PIN-FORMED protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PIN1-GFP localizes to the plasma membrane with stronger accumulation at lobe tips in tobacco pavement cells.
mechanism: PIN1-GFP internalization occurs preferentially in indentation regions, suggesting ROP2 inhibition of endocytosis in lobe regions.

genes: PIN1 (PIN1, PIN-FORMED protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PIN1-GFP localizes to the plasma membrane in Arabidopsis pavement cells, with internalization suppressed by ROP2 activation.
mechanism: ROP2 activation inhibits PIN1 endocytosis in lobe regions, allowing polarization.

genes: ROP2 (ROP2, Rho-like GTPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: DN-ROP2 expression promotes PIN1-GFP internalization in tobacco pavement cells.
mechanism: DN-ROP2 induces endocytosis of PIN1-GFP, accelerating vesicle formation and PM signal decrease.

genes: AP180 (AP180, clathrin-binding protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ANTH(C) overexpression inhibits PIN1-GFP internalization in tobacco pavement cells.
mechanism: ANTH(C) suppresses clathrin-dependent endocytosis of PIN1-GFP.

genes: RIC4 (RIC4, ROP interactive CRIB motif-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RIC4 overexpression inhibits FM1-43 internalization in Arabidopsis pavement cells.
mechanism: RIC4 promotes cortical actin accumulation, which inhibits clathrin-dependent endocytosis.

genes: PME (PME gene, involved in methanol emission, from Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Increased methanol production and resistance to TMV in PME-transgenic tobacco line pro1.
mechanism: PME catalyzes methanol production, which induces antibacterial resistance and enhances viral spread.

genes: MIG-21 (methanol-inducible gene-21, cell-to-cell movement, from Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Enhanced cell-to-cell communication and TMV infection in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: MIG-21 upregulation facilitates plasmodesmata dilation, enhancing viral spread.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter, from Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Used as a reporter to monitor cell-to-cell movement in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: GFP expression allows visualization of cell-to-cell movement via plasmodesmata.

genes: crTMV:GFP (tobacco mosaic virus with GFP instead of coat protein, from Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Facilitates local movement of TMV in methanol-treated N. benthamiana.
mechanism: GFP-tagged TMV allows visualization of viral spread enhanced by methanol-induced plasmodesmata dilation.

genes: HBsAg (HBsAg, small form, Genbank S62754.1)
phenotype: Overexpression of HBsAg in maize results in 0.25% total soluble protein (TSP) in some lines.
mechanism: Targeting HBsAg to the cell wall using BAASS signal sequence enhances accumulation in maize grain.

genes: HBsAg (HBsAg, small form, Genbank S62754.1)
phenotype: Overexpression of HBsAg in maize results in low expression levels with plants dying before maturation.
mechanism: Targeting HBsAg to the vacuole using amyloplast signal sequence reduces expression and causes plant mortality.

genes: HBsAg (HBsAg, small form, Genbank S62754.1)
phenotype: Overexpression of HBsAg in maize results in equivalent expression levels to cell wall-targeted constructs.
mechanism: Targeting HBsAg to the ER using KDEL signal sequence does not significantly alter expression levels.

genes: HBsAg (HBsAg, small form, Genbank S62754.1)
phenotype: Overexpression of HBsAg in maize results in 0.46% total soluble protein (TSP) in hybrid grain.
mechanism: Using an embryo-preferred globulin1 promoter with BAASS signal sequence maximizes HBsAg accumulation in maize germ.

genes: At5g59980.1 (GAF1, gametophyte development gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restored seed set from 51.5% to 90.6% in gaf1 plants and increased KanR:KanS ratio to 2.62:1 in T2 seeds.
mechanism: GAF1 is essential for gametophyte development and male fitness.

genes: At5g59980.1 (GAF1, gametophyte development gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Rescued the phenotype with KanR:KanS ratio up to 2.92:1.
mechanism: GAF1 is fully functional and sufficient for gametophyte development.

genes: At5g59980.1 (GAF1, gametophyte development gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), EGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Rescued the phenotype with KanR:KanS ratio up to 2.92:1.
mechanism: GAF1 is fully functional and sufficient for gametophyte development.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP fused to the Art v 1 signal peptide in tobacco leaves results in secretion of GFP and detection of 27 kDa bands.
mechanism: The Art v 1 signal peptide directs GFP to the secretory pathway, confirmed by detection in leaf infiltrates.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
