phenotype: ProCUC2::GUS reporter construct shows GUS activity patterns in gynoecium development, with wild-type expression restricted to adaxial side and spt mutant showing ectopic abaxial expression
mechanism: The construct is used to study transcriptional regulation of CUC2 by SPT in the apical part of the gynoecium

genes: HaEcR (hormone receptor, Helicoverpa armigera)
phenotype: Transgenic tobacco plants expressing HaEcR dsRNA show improved resistance to H. armigera and S. exigua with 40% larval lethality and molting defects
mechanism: HaEcR dsRNA suppresses HaEcR mRNA in H. armigera larvae, disrupting 20E-triggered transcriptional cascade and causing molting defects

genes: bZIP60 (full-length, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of bZIP60 full-length increases ER stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, as evidenced by enhanced root growth and germination under DTT treatment.
mechanism: Overexpression of bZIP60 enhances ER stress tolerance by inducing BiP accumulation, which improves protein folding capacity in the ER.

genes: bZIP60 (spliced variant, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of bZIP60 spliced variant increases ER stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, as evidenced by enhanced root growth and germination under DTT treatment.
mechanism: Overexpression of the spliced bZIP60 variant auto-regulates its own expression and induces BiP accumulation, improving ER stress tolerance.

genes: IRE1b (transmembrane kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated knockdown of IRE1b reduces ER stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, as evidenced by impaired root growth and germination under DTT treatment.
mechanism: IRE1b RNAi impairs bZIP60 splicing, reducing BiP accumulation and ER stress response capacity.

genes: NPR1 (NPR1, receptor for SA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of NPR1-GFP enables monitoring of NPR1 localization and activity in response to pathogen challenge, showing reduced NPR1-GFP signal in developing HR and accumulation in HR margins to restrict PCD spread.
mechanism: NPR1 over-accumulation in npr3 npr4 mutant acts as a negative regulator of PCD; NPR1-GFP degradation by CUL3NPR3 limits PCD spread in HR margins to establish SAR.

genes: DTa (DHAR, dehydroascorbate reductase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of DHAR increases polyembryony (2–3 embryos per seed) and polycotyly (3–4 cotyledons per seedling) in tobacco.
mechanism: Increased DHAR expression raises ascorbate (Asc) pool size, inducing monozygotic twinning during the first zygotic division.

genes: DNt (DHAR, dehydroascorbate reductase, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Suppression of DHAR reduces ascorbate (Asc) pool size in tobacco, leading to lower polyembryony and polycotyly compared to wild-type or overexpressing lines.
mechanism: Reduced DHAR expression lowers Asc pool size, decreasing the frequency of monozygotic twinning and cotyledon abnormalities.

genes: BjRCE1 (BjRCE1, RUB-conjugated enzyme, Brassica juncea)
phenotype: GFP fusion of BjRCE1 in Arabidopsis localizes to the nucleus, as shown by fluorescence microscopy.
mechanism: NA

genes: CP (capsid protein, replaced with GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: TCV-GFPΔCP is restricted to single epidermal cells due to replacement of CP gene with GFP
mechanism: Replacement of the CP gene with GFP eliminates the viral capsid protein, preventing cell-to-cell movement of the virus

genes: RDR6 (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase 6, silenced, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: RDR6 knockdown reduces gfp silencing foci numbers (upper: 25 ± 25 vs 161 ± 6; lower: 4 ± 4 vs 146 ± 12) and decreases average focus size (0.50 ± 0.35 mm vs 0.98 ± 0.39 mm)
mechanism: RDR6 is required for cell-to-cell communication of RNA silencing, likely through small RNA signal trafficking

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, overexpressed, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP overexpression in transgenic lines enables virus-induced RNA silencing assays with TCV-GFPΔCP, resulting in visible gfp-silenced foci under UV light
mechanism: GFP expression provides a target for RNA silencing, allowing visualization of silencing spread through epidermal cells

genes: PhDef1 (Petunia defensin 1, antifungal protein, Petunia hybrida), PhDef2 (Petunia defensin 2, antifungal protein, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of PhDef1 and PhDef2 in banana confers high resistance to Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (Foc) infection, with transgenic plants showing no wilting symptoms and significantly reduced corm tissue discoloration compared to untransformed controls.
mechanism: PhDef1 and PhDef2 act as antifungal defensins, likely inhibiting Foc mycelial growth and colonization in banana vascular tissue.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic), Bt Cry1Ac (insecticidal crystal protein, insect resistance, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Transgenic B. napus (GT) plants show increased biomass (10.9g vs 5.15g in wild mustard), seed number (1608 vs 1802 in wild mustard), and seed weight (3.64g vs 1.71g in wild mustard) in multi-culture experiments
mechanism: Bt Cry1Ac enhances insect resistance, leading to increased biomass and seed production; no transgene-associated fitness costs observed

genes: MSL2 (mechanosensitive channel-like protein 2, Arabidopsis thaliana), MSL2g (genomic context of MSL2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues msl2-3 mutant leaf morphology and plastid morphology phenotypes, producing wild-type-like plants.
mechanism: MSL2g restores normal plastid size and shape by functioning as a mechanosensitive channel in the chloroplast envelope.

genes: CYP81A6 (Bel, cytochrome P450 gene, rice)
phenotype: Overexpression of CYP81A6 (Bel) confers resistance to bentazon herbicide in Gossypium hirsutum
mechanism: Bel gene encodes a cytochrome P450 enzyme that metabolizes bentazon herbicide, providing resistance

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP expression levels in root tissue were measured by qRT-PCR, normalized to copy number and relative to CaMV 35S control.
mechanism: Modified promoters (GR2A and GR11A intergenic regions) drive GFP expression; transversions in 10 bp segments disrupt promoter activity.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP expression levels in root tissue were measured by qRT-PCR, normalized to copy number and relative to CaMV 35S control.
mechanism: Modified promoters (GR2A and GR11A intergenic regions) drive GFP expression; transversions in 10 bp segments disrupt promoter activity.

genes: BoEMF2.1 (BoEMF2, broccoli, Brassica oleracea var. italica)
phenotype: Knockdown of BoEMF2.1 in broccoli causes leaf curling, dwarfism, early flowering (69.0 ± 5.4 days vs 87.7 ± 5.2 days), abnormal flower development with fused pistil-like structures, and reduced seed production.
mechanism: BoEMF2.1 knockdown leads to ectopic expression of flower organ identity genes (AG, SEP3), flowering time genes (FT), and stress response genes, disrupting normal developmental pathways.

genes: BoEMF2.1 (BoEMF2, broccoli, Brassica oleracea var. italica)
phenotype: Overexpression of BoEMF2.1 in Arabidopsis emf2 mutants partially rescues hypocotyl elongation (5.3 ± 0.7 mm vs 3.1 ± 0.3 mm), petiole development, and vegetative growth (5.9 ± 2.5 rosette leaves vs 0 in emf2), but rescued plants still flower early (30.6 ± 2.8 days vs 104.4 ± 5.4 days in wild type) and produce smaller flowers with reduced fertility.
mechanism: BoEMF2.1 restores ~70% of misregulated genes in emf2 mutants, including flower organ identity genes (AP1, AP3, PI), flowering time genes (FT, SVP), and auxin/EXPANSIN genes, but fails to fully repress AG and SEP3, leading to partial rescue.

genes: OYE3 (oxidized flavoprotein, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic Arabidopsis overexpressing OYE3 show enhanced tolerance to TNT with 1.6 cm root length at 10 mg/L TNT vs 20% of wild-type root length
mechanism: OYE3 degrades TNT in planta, reducing phytotoxic effects and enabling 2x higher TNT degradation rates compared to wild-type plants

genes: EcNAC1 (NAC domain-containing transcription factor, finger millet, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of EcNAC1 in tobacco confers tolerance to osmotic, salinity, and oxidative stress, with 1.5–3 fold less growth inhibition under PEG stress, 2–3 fold more root mass under mannitol stress, and 5–7 fold lower ROS levels under water-deficit stress.
mechanism: EcNAC1 activates stress-responsive genes including HB-13, MYB, PP2C, STPK, CytOR, ROP, and ERD1, enhancing ROS scavenging and membrane protection.

genes: EcNAC1 (NAC domain-containing transcription factor, finger millet, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of EcNAC1 in tobacco confers tolerance to osmotic, salinity, and oxidative stress, with 1.5–3 fold less growth inhibition under PEG stress, 2–3 fold more root mass under mannitol stress, and 5–7 fold lower ROS levels under water-deficit stress.
mechanism: EcNAC1 activates stress-responsive genes including HB-13, MYB, PP2C, STPK, CytOR, ROP, and ERD1, enhancing ROS scavenging and membrane protection.

genes: cryIAc (Bacillus thuringiensis, insect resistance, Bacillus thuringiensis), CpTI (cowpea trypsin inhibitor, insect resistance, cowpea)
phenotype: Overexpression of Bt/CpTI increases fecundity traits (panicle number, seed set) by ~25-44% in Oryza sativa under natural insect pressure.
mechanism: Bt/CpTI transgenes control lepidopteran pests by producing insecticidal proteins, reducing herbivore damage and increasing plant fitness.

genes: cry1Ab (synthetically modified cry1Ab gene, resistance to Lepidoptera, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of synthetically modified cry1Ab in KMD rice confers resistance to Lepidoptera.
mechanism: Expression of the cry1Ab protein provides resistance to Lepidoptera by targeting insect pests.

genes: AtAucsia1 (AtAucsia1, auxin transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtAucsia-1 reduces primary root length by ~35% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtAucsia-1 functions as a regulator of auxin transport, affecting root growth.

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: ProAtAucsia-1::GUS expression is detected in seeds, seedlings, roots, and floral organs.
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: ProAtAucsia-2::GUS expression is detected in cotyledons, hypocotyls, and root apices.
mechanism: NA

genes: TbSRPP3 (small rubber particle protein 3, Taraxacum brevicorniculatum, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic plants show 24-37% reduction in latex rubber content and 50-51% reduction in root rubber content compared to wild-type
mechanism: TbSRPPs stabilize rubber particles via steric hindrance; their depletion reduces colloidal stability and impairs rubber biosynthesis

genes: SUVH2 (SUVH2, SET-domain protein family gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of myc-tagged SUVH2 increases SUVH2 transcript levels, resulting in dwarf phenotype, curled leaves, and delayed senescence in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SUVH2 is required for RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) and transcriptional silencing of AtSN1. SUVH2 and SUVH9 act redundantly for RdDM but show developmentally non-redundant roles in seedlings and mature leaves.

genes: OsYSL16 (Oryza sativa, green fluorescent protein fusion, synthetic)
phenotype: OsYSL16-GFP co-localized primarily with the plasma membrane marker FM4-64 in onion epidermal cells
mechanism: OsYSL16-GFP fusion protein localized to the plasma membrane

genes: OsYSL16 (Oryza sativa, promoter-GUS fusion, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: GUS activity detected in leaves, unelongated nodes, and roots of transgenic rice under Fe-sufficient and Fe-deficient conditions
mechanism: OsYSL16 promoter drives GUS expression in vascular bundles and root epidermis

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GUS increases transient protein expression by ~6.6-fold in cell suspensions compared to full-length PVX vector
mechanism: Minimal PVX vector lacking non-essential genes directs more cellular resources to target protein production

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Co-expression with P19 suppressor increases GUS expression by 44% in cell suspensions
mechanism: P19 suppresses post-transcriptional gene silencing, allowing higher transgene accumulation

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Co-expression with HC-Pro suppressor increases GUS expression by 83% in cell suspensions
mechanism: HC-Pro suppresses post-transcriptional gene silencing, allowing higher transgene accumulation

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Non-replicating CPMV-HT vector increases GUS expression by ~70% in cell suspensions
mechanism: Enhanced translation via modified CPMV 5'UTR without viral replication

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: TRV vector increases GUS accumulation by 150-fold in hairy roots compared to PVX vector
mechanism: TRV systemic movement enables higher transgene expression in root tissues

genes: Cr-PTOX1 (plastoquinol oxidase, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii)
phenotype: Transplastomic plants expressing Cr-PTOX1 show increased sensitivity to high-light stress, characterized by chlorotic leaves and significantly retarded growth under 125 µmol photons m−2 s−1 light conditions.
mechanism: Cr-PTOX1 enhances plastoquinol oxidation, leading to faster PQ pool re-oxidation and potentially increased ROS production under high light, which correlates with photoinhibition susceptibility (Fv/Fm drops from 0.75 in WT to 0.43 in transplastomic plants under high light).

genes: bar (phosphinotricin-resistant gene, synthetic), pinII (proteinase inhibitor gene, potato)
phenotype: Overexpression of pinII increases insect resistance in Brassica rapa, with transgenic lines showing up to 90% mortality in diamondback moth larvae and reduced pupation rates.
mechanism: Expression of the PINII protein inhibits protease activity in insect larvae, reducing their ability to digest plant material and leading to developmental arrest and mortality.

genes: Sletr1-1 (Sletr1-1, ethylene receptor gene, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of Sletr1-1 confers delayed fruit ripening and prolonged fruit shelf life in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: Mutated ethylene receptor (Sletr1-1) reduces ethylene sensitivity, leading to delayed ripening and extended shelf life.

genes: Sletr1-2 (Sletr1-2, ethylene receptor gene, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of Sletr1-2 confers delayed fruit ripening and prolonged fruit shelf life in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: Mutated ethylene receptor (Sletr1-2) reduces ethylene sensitivity, leading to delayed ripening and extended shelf life.

genes: PGL2 (POSITIVE REGULATOR OF GRAIN LENGTH 2, atypical bHLH protein of subfamily 16, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PGL2 increases grain length by ~49% and thousand grains weight by ~37% in Oryza sativa
mechanism: PGL2 interacts with APG (typical bHLH protein) in the nucleus to control grain length through heterodimerization

genes: OSD1 (OSD1, APC/C inhibitor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Wild type genomic clone restores normal meiosis (100% tetrads) in osd1-3 mutant, while OSD1ΔMR and OSD1ΔD constructs fail to restore tetrad formation.
mechanism: OSD1 inhibits APC/C activity through its D-box and MR-tail domains, which are essential for meiotic progression.

genes: CYCA1;2/TAM (CYCA1;2/TAM, cyclin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of TAMΔD (non-destructible CYCA1;2/TAM) provokes entry into an aberrant third meiotic division, mimicking the tdm phenotype, leading to male and female sterility.
mechanism: CYCA1;2/TAM regulates meiotic exit via APC/C-mediated cyclin destruction; TAMΔD disrupts this regulation, causing uncontrolled meiotic divisions.

genes: UGD1 (UDP-glucose dehydrogenase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression was observed in UGD1 line at 2 dpi in syncytia, with moderate expression in most syncytia and no expression in ~25% of syncytia.
mechanism: Reporter gene expression driven by UGD1 promoter

genes: UGD2 (UDP-glucose dehydrogenase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression was observed in UGD2 line at 1 dpi in syncytia, with strongest reporter activity at 2 dpi and 7 dpi.
mechanism: Reporter gene expression driven by UGD2 promoter

genes: UGD3 (UDP-glucose dehydrogenase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression was observed in UGD3 line at 1 dpi in syncytia, with strongest reporter activity at 2 dpi and 7 dpi.
mechanism: Reporter gene expression driven by UGD3 promoter

genes: UGD4 (UDP-glucose dehydrogenase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression was observed in UGD4 line at 1 dpi in syncytia, with weak expression in a few syncytia and spread into the vicinity of syncytia.
mechanism: Reporter gene expression driven by UGD4 promoter

genes: TaWRKY45-A (transcription factor, wheat, Triticum aestivum L.)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaWRKY45-A increases resistance to powdery mildew (infection type IT1-3) and leaf rust (infection type IT1-2) in wheat (Triticum aestivum L.)
mechanism: TaWRKY45 functions in wheat defense response through a pathway independent of Pm3 and Lr34, inducing hypersensitive reactions and restricting pathogen growth

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression is significantly higher in Gladiolus and Arabidopsis with the 1.9 kb GUBQ1 promoter compared to the intronless version (G1-3), with GUS activity comparable to CaMV 35S promoter in leaves.
mechanism: The 5′UTR-intron from GUBQ1 enhances translation efficiency in both species, increasing GUS activity despite differing mRNA accumulation patterns.

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression is significantly decreased in Gladiolus and abolished in Arabidopsis when the 5′UTR-intron is absent (G1-3), despite similar mRNA accumulation in both species.
mechanism: The 5′UTR-intron enhances translation efficiency in both species, with intronless G1-3 showing negligible GUS activity in Arabidopsis and reduced activity in Gladiolus.

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression is comparable to GUBQ1 promoter in Gladiolus and higher in Arabidopsis, with widespread expression in leaves and roots.
mechanism: The CaMV 35S promoter drives constitutive expression, but the GUBQ1 intron provides higher translation efficiency in both species.

genes: OsAPx2 (Oryza sativa ascorbate peroxidase 2, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsAPx2 in Medicago sativa increases salt tolerance, with transgenic plants showing longer root lengths under NaCl stress and reduced H2O2 content compared to wild type.
mechanism: OsAPx2 overexpression improves detoxification of reactive oxygen species, reducing membrane lipid peroxidation and H2O2 accumulation under salt stress.

genes: OsAPx2 (Oryza sativa ascorbate peroxidase 2, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsAPx2 in Medicago sativa enhances salt tolerance, with transgenic plants showing longer root lengths under 200 mM NaCl stress and reduced H2O2 content compared to wild type.
mechanism: OsAPx2 overexpression improves detoxification of reactive oxygen species, reducing membrane lipid peroxidation and H2O2 accumulation under salt stress.

genes: PtFT1 (flowering time gene, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Early flowering (within 1-10 months post-planting), altered growth architecture (shrub-like with increased lateral branching), continuous flowering and fruiting regardless of day length or chilling time, and production of multiple fruits per flower (2-5 fruits per flower).
mechanism: FT1 integrates flowering and photoperiod signaling pathways, affecting apical dominance, stem growth, and inflorescence architecture. High temperature represses flowering while lower temperatures promote it.

genes: FLN1 (FLN1, HA-tagged fructokinase-like protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Inducible expression of FLN1-HA rescues the fln1-1 mutant phenotype when applied within 24 hours of germination, allowing seedlings to develop normally and avoid seedling lethality.
mechanism: FLN1 is required early during germination in the light for normal chloroplast development and photosynthetic competency; later induction cannot reverse the mutant phenotype due to irreversible developmental defects.

genes: vIL-10 (viral interleukin 10, Nicotiana tabacum), mIL-10 (murine interleukin 10, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of vIL-10 in BY-2 cells results in 1.4 μg/g fresh weight (FW) protein yield, while mIL-10 yields 9.3 μg/g FW.
mechanism: ER-targeted vIL-10 retention causes plant toxicity and reduced yields compared to mIL-10.

genes: vIL-10 (viral interleukin 10, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Inducible expression of vIL-10 in BY-2 cells using the tetracycline-inducible TripleOp promoter increases yields 3.5-fold compared to constitutive expression.
mechanism: Tetracycline-inducible promoter allows temporal restriction of vIL-10 expression to avoid toxicity and proteolytic degradation.

genes: vIL-10 (viral interleukin 10, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Enhanced tetracycline-inducible promoter with Tobacco etch virus 5'UTR increases vIL-10 yields by 3.5-fold in BY-2 cells.
mechanism: Tobacco etch virus 5'UTR enhances translational efficiency, and scaffold attachment regions (SARs) mitigate silencing effects.

genes: vIL-10 (viral interleukin 10, Nicotiana tabacum), DsRed (Discosoma spp red fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Tandem expression of inducible vIL-10 and constitutive DsRed allows rapid selection of high-yielding clones, achieving 5.3 μg/g FW vIL-10.
mechanism: DsRed fluorescence correlates with vIL-10 expression levels, enabling visual screening of transgenic lines.

genes: eYFP (enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic), DsRed (Discosoma sp. red fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: FTL transgenes enable tetrad analysis of crossovers in Arabidopsis thaliana male meiosis via pollen fluorescence.
mechanism: Fluorescent protein expression in pollen allows visualization of crossover events through segregation patterns in quartet1–2 (qrt1–2) mutant background.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic), RFP (red fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Seed reporter system tracks recombination in the 420 interval of chromosome 3 via fluorescence in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GFP and RFP expression in seeds from the napA promoter enables identification of recombinant progeny through fluorescence patterns.

genes: CDKA;1 (CDKA;1, cell-cycle kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of PROCDKA;1:CDKA;1-YFP completely rescues cdka;1 pollen, resulting in wild-type-like pollen with one vegetative cell and two sperm cells.
mechanism: CDKA;1-YFP accumulation marks gametic cells during male and female gametogenesis.

genes: CDKA;1 (CDKA;1, cell-cycle kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of PROCDKA;1:CDKA;1PSTAIRE-dead does not rescue the cdka;1 pollen phenotype, maintaining typical arrest at anthesis.
mechanism: CDKA;1PSTAIRE-dead cannot bind cyclins, failing to interfere with negative factors.

genes: CDKA;1 (CDKA;1, cell-cycle kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of PROCDKA;1:amiCDKA;1 enhances the cdka;1 mutant phenotype, increasing bicellular pollen from 43% to 57%.
mechanism: amiCDKA;1 reduces CDKA;1 protein levels, enhancing the mutant phenotype.

genes: FBL17 (FBL17, F-box protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of PROUBQ:FBL17 partially rescues the cdka;1 pollen phenotype, increasing tricellular pollen to 78.3%.
mechanism: FBL17 overexpression targets CDK inhibitors for degradation, promoting cell-cycle progression.

genes: FBL17 (FBL17, F-box protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of PROCDKA;1:FBL17 partially rescues the cdka;1 pollen phenotype, increasing tricellular pollen to 72.5%.
mechanism: FBL17 overexpression targets CDK inhibitors for degradation, promoting cell-cycle progression.

genes: TGZ (transglutaminase from maize, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of TGZ in tobacco significantly alters photosynthetic parameters: non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) is 3-fold higher, linear electron transport (LEF) saturates at 600 µmol photons m−2s−1 (vs 800 µmol in WT), and effective quantum yield is half of WT values. TGZ OE shows increased thylakoid stacking (40-60 layers vs 15-20 in WT) and higher sensitivity of antenna downregulation (qE) to light-induced proton motive force.
mechanism: TGZ overexpression increases polyamination of LHCII proteins, leading to larger PSII antenna absorption cross-section (Kα doubled vs WT). This enhances photon harvesting but causes premature photoinhibition due to excessive qE activation at low light intensities. Thylakoid-associated polyamines (Spd/Spm) increase by 80% in TGZ OE.

genes: Bs2 (disease resistance gene, pepper)
phenotype: Overexpression of Bs2 in tomato plants confers resistance to bacterial spot disease and increases marketable and total yields under high disease pressure.
mechanism: Bs2 activates resistance by recognizing AvrBs2, a Xanthomonas effector, leading to a hypersensitive response and disease resistance.

genes: AtACR2 (AtACR2, arsenate reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtACR2 does not enhance arsenate reduction in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtACR2's role in arsenate reduction appears to be redundant.

genes: HD20 (homeodomain-leucine zipper transcription factor involved in ABA accumulation and benzyl acetone emission regulation, Nicotiana attenuata)
phenotype: Reduced HD20 expression leads to 60-70% decrease in benzyl acetone (BA) emission from corollas and 2-fold higher ABA levels in corollas of ir-hd20 plants compared to wild-type.
mechanism: HD20 mediates ABA level regulation and metabolic gene expression changes in corollas, affecting the late phase of BA emission. Salt stress reduces ABA levels in ir-hd20 plants, restoring BA emission to wild-type levels.

genes: NRT2.6 (expression analysis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Blue coloration detectable in lateral roots, collar of young plantlets, and tapetal cells of anthers
mechanism: NRT2.6 promoter drives GUS expression in tapetal cells during pollen development

genes: NRT2.6 (transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased H2O2 accumulation and resistance to E. amylovora infection
mechanism: NRT2.6 overexpression enhances ROS production correlated with pathogen resistance

genes: Icy6 (HvCPI-6 cystatin, barley), Itr1 (BTI-CMe trypsin inhibitor, barley)
phenotype: Overexpression of Icy6 and Itr1 increases resistance to T. urticae, reducing leaf damage by ~70% and increasing mite mortality to ~90% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Icy6 inhibits cathepsin B- and L-like proteases in T. urticae, while Itr1 inhibits trypsin activity, disrupting mite digestion and physiology.

genes: Icy6 (HvCPI-6 cystatin, barley), Itr1 (BTI-CMe trypsin inhibitor, barley)
phenotype: Double transgenic CPI6-CMe plants show highest resistance to T. urticae with 2.1-3.2 mm² leaf damage vs 10.91 mm² in controls and 90% mite mortality, compared to 50-70% in single transgenics.
mechanism: Combined inhibition of cathepsin B/L and trypsin proteases in mites by Icy6 and Itr1 synergistically disrupts digestion and development, preventing adaptive responses.

genes: GUS (GUS, β-glucuronidase reporter gene, pCAMBIA1305.1)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under FRB1 promoter shows activity in germinating seeds and early seedling development, particularly at hypocotyl-root junction and cotyledons.
mechanism: NA

genes: FRB1 (FRB1, Golgi-localized protein involved in cell adhesion, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of GFP-FRB1 fusion protein complements frb1 mutant phenotypes and localizes to the Golgi apparatus.
mechanism: FRB1 is localized to the Golgi apparatus, involved in cell wall metabolism.

genes: 10-kDa δ-zein (10-kDa δ-zein, methionine-rich storage protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of 10-kDa δ-zein increases methionine levels in maize seeds, but reduces cysteine-rich β- and γ-zeins.
mechanism: Methionine-rich δ-zein accumulation is linked to reduced cysteine-rich zein synthesis, likely through translational control.

genes: β-zein (β-zein, cysteine- and methionine-rich storage protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of β-zein reduces methionine and cysteine levels in maize seeds.
mechanism: β-zein is a major sink for both methionine and cysteine in maize seeds.

genes: γ-zein (γ-zein, cysteine-rich storage protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of γ-zein reduces cysteine levels and increases 10-kDa δ-zein accumulation.
mechanism: γ-zeins are a major sink for cysteine in maize seeds.

genes: β-zein (β-zein, cysteine- and methionine-rich storage protein, Zea mays), γ-zein (γ-zein, cysteine-rich storage protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: Simultaneous RNAi silencing of β- and γ-zeins drastically reduces cysteine and methionine levels, while increasing 10-kDa δ-zein.
mechanism: β- and γ-zeins are major sinks for cysteine and methionine, respectively.

genes: 22-kDa α-zein (22-kDa α-zein, lysine-free storage protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of 22-kDa α-zeins increases lysine but not methionine levels in maize seeds.
mechanism: α-zeins are lysine-free and do not contribute to methionine sinks.

genes: GFP (Green Fluorescent Protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic hairy roots express GFP with 85.3% transformation efficiency in maize
mechanism: 35S promoter drives constitutive expression of GFP in root tissues

genes: ZMM4 (ZMM4, floral transition regulator, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZMM4 promotes floral transition and reduces days to tassel initiation in maize
mechanism: ZMM4 regulates floral transition through a positive feedback loop and interacts with DLF1 to activate downstream floral organ identity genes

genes: OsU11/U12-31K (OsU11/U12-31K, involved in U12 intron splicing and plant development, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of AtU11/U12-31K knockdown mutant (amiR1-4) restores wild-type phenotypes including normal inflorescence stem development and prolonged cell division activity
mechanism: OsU11/U12-31K complements the amiR1-4 mutant by restoring normal splicing of U12 intron-containing genes, which is crucial for plant development

genes: IAA8 (IAA8, transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of IAA8 alters root development, including reduced lateral root number in estradiol-treated XVE::IAA8 line #11 and abnormal gravitropism, while iaa8-1 mutant shows increased lateral root number.
mechanism: IAA8 acts as a transcriptional repressor interacting with TIR1 auxin receptor and ARF transcription factors in the nucleus to regulate auxin response.

genes: OsELF3-1 (flowering regulator, rice)
phenotype: OsELF3-1 RNAi plants flower 14-144 days later than wild-type under long-day and short-day conditions
mechanism: OsELF3-1 RNAi represses OsELF3-1 expression, leading to reduced Ehd1 and RFT expression which are required for flowering induction

genes: ORCA3 (ORCA3, transcription factor for MIA pathway, Catharanthus roseus)
phenotype: Overexpression of ORCA3 increases monoterpenoid indole alkaloids (strictosidine, vindoline, catharanthine) and modulates primary metabolism (elevated alanine, threonine, glutamic acid, sucrose, 2,3-DHBA, 4-O-Caffeoyl quinic acid; reduced malic acid, secologanine).
mechanism: ORCA3 up-regulates MIA pathway genes (AS, TDC, STR, D4H) and primary metabolic genes, enhancing alkaloid biosynthesis and altering amino acid/organic acid balances.

genes: G10H (G10H, secoiridoid pathway hydroxylase, Catharanthus roseus), ORCA3 (ORCA3, transcription factor for MIA pathway, Catharanthus roseus)
phenotype: Co-overexpression of G10H and ORCA3 increases monoterpenoid indole alkaloids (strictosidine, vindoline, catharanthine, ajmalicine) and modulates primary metabolism (elevated 2,3-butanediol, glucose, quercetin-3-O-glucoside; reduced secologanine).
mechanism: G10H and ORCA3 co-overexpression enhances MIA pathway gene up-regulation (AS, TDC, STR, D4H), boosts ajmalicine accumulation, and alters primary metabolism (increased glucose, 2,3-butanediol, quercetin-3-O-glucoside).

genes: MyosinXI-1 (class XI myosin, Arabidopsis thaliana), MyosinXI-2 (class XI myosin, Arabidopsis thaliana), MyosinXI-K (class XI myosin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced cell size and altered epidermal cell morphology in trichomes, pavement cells, and stigmatic papillae; dwarf growth, delayed flowering, and reduced fertility in triple mutants.
mechanism: Myosin XI-K, XI-1, and XI-2 regulate actin cytoskeleton dynamics and vesicle transport, which are essential for epidermal cell expansion and organ development.

phenotype: Reduced cell size and altered epidermal cell morphology in trichomes, pavement cells, and stigmatic papillae; dwarf growth, delayed flowering, and reduced fertility in triple mutants.
mechanism: Myosin XI-K, XI-1, and XI-2 regulate actin cytoskeleton dynamics and vesicle transport, which are essential for epidermal cell expansion and organ development.

mechanism: Myosin XI-K, XI-1, and XI-2 regulate actin cytoskeleton dynamics and vesicle transport, which are essential for epidermal cell expansion and organ development.

phenotype: Overexpression of DDB1F reduces organ size (fruits, roots, stems, leaves, flowers, seeds) by ~84-89% in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: DDB1F induces epigenetic demethylation of cell-division regulators (e.g., SlWEE1), upregulating negative regulators of mitotic division and reducing cell number.

genes: DDB1 (DDB1+15, Solanum lycopersicum)

mechanism: DR5 promoter drives GUS expression to monitor auxin signaling in callus initiation

mechanism: SAW1 overexpression fails to alter callus formation despite its role in leaf margin development

phenotype: Overexpression of ATH1 does not affect leaf-to-callus transition in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: ATH1 overexpression fails to alter callus formation despite its role in leaf development

genes: AS2ΔN (AS2 N-terminal deletion, Arabidopsis thaliana), YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: AS2ΔN-YFP forms AS2 bodies in 66.1% of interphase BY-2 cells, suggesting the N-terminal region negatively regulates body formation
mechanism: Deletion of the N-terminal sequence (residues 1-7) increases AS2 body formation in interphase cells, indicating a negative regulatory role for the N-terminal region

genes: AS2ΔN-Cm (AS2 N-terminal and C-motif deletion, Arabidopsis thaliana), YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: AS2ΔN-Cm-YFP shows nucleoplasmic localization in all interphase BY-2 cells, indicating the C-motif is required for AS2 body formation
mechanism: Deletion of the C-motif (perfectly conserved in AS2/LOB family) prevents AS2 body formation, suggesting the C-motif is essential for localization to AS2 bodies

genes: AS2ΔC (AS2 C-terminal deletion, Arabidopsis thaliana), YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: AS2ΔC-YFP forms AS2 bodies in 3.4% of interphase BY-2 cells, indicating the C-terminal domain is not required for body formation
mechanism: Deletion of the C-terminal domain does not prevent AS2 body formation in mitotic cells but reduces it in interphase cells

genes: AS2ΔNΔC (AS2 N-terminal and C-terminal deletion, Arabidopsis thaliana), YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: AS2ΔNΔC-YFP forms AS2 bodies in 85% of interphase BY-2 cells, showing the AS2/LOB domain is sufficient for body formation
mechanism: The AS2/LOB domain (highly conserved in AS2/LOB family) is sufficient for AS2 body formation, indicating the C-terminal half is not required

genes: BnPHR1 (BnPHR1, transcription activator, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnPHR1 increases fresh weight and root length in Arabidopsis thaliana under low Pi conditions, but causes retarded growth in later stages and chlorosis in Brassica napus.
mechanism: BnPHR1 enhances phosphate uptake by up-regulating high-affinity Pi transporters (ATPT2, BnPT2), leading to excessive Pi accumulation and anthocyanin production.

genes: BnPHR1 (BnPHR1, transcription activator, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Complementation of phr1 mutant rescues anthocyanin accumulation and dark-purple leaf phenotypes under Pi starvation.
mechanism: BnPHR1 restores Pi starvation response gene expression in phr1 mutant, including ATPT2 and IPS1.

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS activity is detected in roots of transgenic Arabidopsis, especially at early developmental stages and under low Pi conditions.
mechanism: BnPHR1 promoter activity is modulated by external Pi levels, indicating its role in root development and Pi starvation response.

genes: BnPHR1 (BnPHR1, transcription activator, Brassica napus), GFP (GFP, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: BnPHR1-GFP is localized in the nucleus of transgenic Arabidopsis roots, confirming its nuclear localization.
mechanism: BnPHR1 is a nuclear-localized transcription activator, essential for its function in Pi starvation response.

genes: HmVALT (HmVALT, vacuolar aluminum transporter, Hydrangea macrophylla)
phenotype: Overexpression of HmVALT increases aluminum tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with relative root length significantly increased under aluminum stress.
mechanism: HmVALT transports aluminum into vacuoles, sequestering it and reducing cytosolic toxicity.

genes: HmPALT1 (HmPALT1, plasma membrane aluminum transporter, Hydrangea macrophylla)
phenotype: Overexpression of HmPALT1 decreases aluminum tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with relative root length significantly reduced under aluminum stress.
mechanism: HmPALT1 transports aluminum into the cytosol, increasing intracellular aluminum content and toxicity.

genes: HmVALT (HmVALT, vacuolar aluminum transporter, Hydrangea macrophylla), HmPALT1 (HmPALT1, plasma membrane aluminum transporter, Hydrangea macrophylla)
phenotype: Co-overexpression of HmVALT and HmPALT1 recovers aluminum hypersensitivity caused by HmPALT1 alone, with relative root length comparable to HmVALT-overexpressing plants under aluminum stress.
mechanism: HmPALT1 imports aluminum into the cytosol, while HmVALT exports it into vacuoles, balancing aluminum distribution and toxicity.

genes: TsVP (Thellungiella halophila vacuolar H+-pyrophosphatase, Thellungiella halophila)
phenotype: Overexpression of TsVP increases root biomass by ~23% under sufficient phosphate and enhances root/shoot ratio, root morphology parameters (13-34% increases in axile/lateral roots, root length, etc.), Pi influx rates (18-48% higher Imax), phosphorus accumulation (14-60% higher P content), and grain yield (23-29% higher) in maize under low phosphate conditions.
mechanism: TsVP enhances vacuolar H+-PPase activity (21-24% higher), increases root system development via auxin transport gene expression (ZmPIN1a, ZmPIN1b, AUX1), and improves rhizosphere acidification (lower pH in nutrient solution) to enhance Pi acquisition.

genes: VvZIP3 (VvZIP3, zinc transporter, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Complementation of the ZHY3 yeast mutant's Zn-limited growth defect, enabling growth on media with low and high Zn concentrations.
mechanism: VvZIP3 functions as a Zn transporter, restoring Zn uptake in the yeast mutant.

genes: VvZIP3 (VvZIP3, zinc transporter, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: VvZIP3-mGFP5 fusion protein localized to the plasma membrane in onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: VvZIP3 is a plasma membrane transporter, as demonstrated by the localization of the fusion protein.

genes: PtaSUT4 (tonoplastic SUT, Populus tremula x P. alba)
phenotype: Reduced PtaSUT4 expression increases sucrose levels in leaves and alters water uptake dynamics during drought stress in poplar (Populus tremula x P. alba).
mechanism: RNAi-mediated down-regulation of PtaSUT4 increases vacuolar sequestration of sucrose, which alters hydraulic conductivity and reduces transpirational water loss while promoting leaf expansion under drought conditions.

genes: SMT1 (SMT1, selenocysteine methyltransferase, Astragalus bisulcatus)
phenotype: Overexpression of SMT1 increases accumulation of Se-methylselenocysteine (MeSeCys) and γ-glutamylmethylselenocysteine (γGluMeSeCys) in shoots by up to 3.9 μmol g-1 dry weight, and significantly increases selenite tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SMT1 catalyzes the methylation of selenocysteine to MeSeCys, which detoxifies selenium by converting it into non-protein derivatives, thereby enhancing selenite resistance and Se accumulation.

genes: CAD (Cinnamyl Alcohol Dehydrogenase, Populus tremula × Populus alba, source)
phenotype: Decreased CAD activity in Populus tremula × Populus alba, leading to modified lignin metabolism and improved pulping properties.
mechanism: NA

genes: mCherry-HDEL (mCherry-HDEL, fluorescent marker, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of mCherry-HDEL fluorescent marker for visualization of ER localization in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: mCherry-HDEL is used as a fluorescent marker to track ER localization.

genes: PDIL1-1 (protein disulfide isomerase-like 1-1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: PDIL1-1Δ mutant seeds show shrunken, floury phenotype with lower dry weight compared to wild type; opaque endosperm with round starch granules and altered free sugar content
mechanism: PDIL1-1 regulates protein folding and ER stress; its loss leads to altered starch granule morphology, increased free sugars, and disrupted storage protein processing

genes: hrf1 (harpinXoo-encoding, Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of hrf1 increases resistance to Xoo strains in rice, with disease area reduced from 67.78% (wild-type R109) to 16.72% (transgenic NJH12) at booting stage. Bacterial growth rate in NJH12 is 3.02- to 69.18-fold lower than wild-type (P<0.05).
mechanism: Hrf1 induces broad-spectrum resistance through enhanced phytoalexin production (MA, MB, PA-PE), increased silicon deposition in leaves, and activation of SA/JA defense pathways. Inhibits H2O2 accumulation via enhanced ROS-scavenging ability (SOD, POD, CAT).

genes: DMP1 (DMP1, membrane protein involved in membrane remodeling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of DMP1-eGFP in Nicotiana benthamiana epidermis cells induces membrane remodeling events including formation of spherical structures (bulbs), ER and vacuole vesiculation, and ultimately cell death via ER and vacuole fragmentation.
mechanism: DMP1 is involved in membrane fission during breakdown of the ER and tonoplast during senescence and in membrane fusion during vacuole biogenesis.

genes: DMP1 (DMP1, membrane protein involved in membrane remodeling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: In Arabidopsis thaliana plants expressing DMP1-eGFP by the native DMP1 promoter, formation of ER aggregates (boluses) and vesiculation of the ER network precedes disintegration of the central vacuole during senescence in siliques, rosette and cauline leaves, and in darkened rosette leaves.
mechanism: DMP1 is involved in membrane fission during breakdown of the ER and tonoplast during senescence and in membrane fusion during vacuole biogenesis.

genes: GmRLK18-1 (receptor-like kinase, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmRLK18-1 provides resistance to Fusarium virguliforme (SDS) and partial resistance to Heterodera glycines (SCN), but increases foliar susceptibility to insect herbivory in transgenic soybean plants.
mechanism: GmRLK18-1 confers resistance by inhibiting root infection and leaf scorch caused by F. virguliforme and partially inhibiting SCN cyst formation. The resistance allele reduces root growth and may involve kinase signaling for pathogen recognition.

genes: Scdr1 (Scdr1, drought-responsive gene, sugarcane)
phenotype: Overexpression of Scdr1 in tobacco increases tolerance to drought, salt, and oxidative stress, with 50-75% recovery of photosynthesis after stress and 10% chlorophyll retention under 0.8 M H2O2.
mechanism: Scdr1 reduces ROS accumulation under salt stress and maintains higher chlorophyll content during oxidative stress, suggesting a role in ROS avoidance.

genes: FIT (transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants expressing FIT-GR are fully rescued from the chlorotic phenotype of fit-2 upon dexamethasone treatment, indicating functional nuclear shuttling of the fusion protein.
mechanism: FIT-GR fusion protein is correctly shuttled to the nucleus and fully functional upon DEX treatment.

genes: bHLH100 (transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of a bHLH100 genomic clone in the bhlh100/bhlh101 double mutant rescues the low-iron growth defect.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsLEA3-2 (OsLEA3-2, LEA protein involved in abiotic stress tolerance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsLEA3-2 in Arabidopsis thaliana increases tolerance to salt and osmotic stress, with transgenic seedlings showing significantly stronger growth performance than wild type under 150 mM mannitol or 100 mM NaCl.
mechanism: OsLEA3-2 enhances abiotic stress tolerance by maintaining protein structure or acting as a molecular chaperone to prevent protein aggregation.

genes: OsLEA3-2 (OsLEA3-2, LEA protein involved in abiotic stress tolerance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsLEA3-2 in Oryza sativa enhances drought tolerance, with transgenic plants surviving 20 days of drought stress and recovering growth, producing viable seeds.
mechanism: OsLEA3-2 enhances drought tolerance by maintaining protein structure or acting as a molecular chaperone to prevent protein aggregation.

genes: OsLEA3-2 (OsLEA3-2, LEA protein involved in abiotic stress tolerance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Transient expression of GFP::OsLEA3-2 in onion epidermal cells shows that OsLEA3-2 is localized exclusively in the nucleus.
mechanism: OsLEA3-2 is a nucleus-localized protein, suggesting it functions within the nucleus to confer stress tolerance.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic), gusA (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP under the rice actin 1 promoter leads to constitutive expression in barley, while gusA remains inactive until recombination excises the GFP-Tnos fragment.
mechanism: Site-specific recombination mediated by phiC31 integrase excises the GFP-Tnos fragment flanked by attP and attB sites, activating the promoter-less gusA gene by fusing it to the rice actin 1 promoter.

phenotype: Down-regulation of γ-gliadins increases total glutenins and other prolamins, leading to higher SDS sedimentation volume and improved dough strength in transgenic wheat lines.

genes: NS1 (Influenza A virus NS1, suppressor of RNA silencing, Influenza A virus)
phenotype: Expression of NS1 increases GFP fluorescence and protects GFP mRNA from degradation in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: NS1 suppresses RNA silencing by protecting dsRNA from degradation.

genes: P1b (CVYV P1b, suppressor of RNA silencing, Cucumovirus)
phenotype: Expression of P1b increases GFP fluorescence and protects GFP mRNA from degradation in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: P1b suppresses RNA silencing by sequestering siRNAs.

genes: VP3 (IBDV VP3, suppressor of RNA silencing, Infectious bursal disease virus)
phenotype: Expression of VP3 increases GFP fluorescence and protects GFP mRNA from degradation in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: VP3 suppresses RNA silencing by binding dsRNA and siRNAs.

genes: VP3 (IBDV VP3, suppressor of RNA silencing, Infectious bursal disease virus)
phenotype: Expression of TAP-tagged VP3 increases GFP fluorescence and protects GFP mRNA from degradation in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: VP3 suppresses RNA silencing by binding dsRNA and siRNAs.

genes: VP3 (IBDV VP3, suppressor of RNA silencing, Infectious bursal disease virus)
phenotype: Expression of Patch1 mutant VP3 fails to protect GFP mRNA from degradation in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: Patch1 mutation abolishes dsRNA binding and RNA silencing suppression.

genes: VP3 (IBDV VP3, suppressor of RNA silencing, Infectious bursal disease virus)
phenotype: Expression of Patch2 mutant VP3 partially protects GFP mRNA from degradation in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: Patch2 mutation reduces dsRNA binding but does not abolish RNA silencing suppression.

phenotype: Expression of ΔC mutant VP3 protects GFP mRNA from degradation in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: ΔC mutation does not affect dsRNA binding or RNA silencing suppression.

genes: VP3 (IPNV VP3, suppressor of RNA silencing, Infectious pancreatic necrosis virus)
phenotype: Expression of IPNV VP3 increases GFP fluorescence and protects GFP mRNA from degradation in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: IPNV VP3 suppresses RNA silencing by binding dsRNA and siRNAs.

genes: VP3 (Drosophila X virus VP3, suppressor of RNA silencing, Drosophila X virus)
phenotype: Expression of DXV VP3 increases GFP fluorescence and protects GFP mRNA from degradation in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: DXV VP3 suppresses RNA silencing by binding dsRNA and siRNAs.

genes: TPS1 (trehalose-phosphate synthase 1, drought tolerance, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of TPS1 increases drought tolerance in potato, with higher stomatal conductance and slower leaf wilting under drought stress.
mechanism: TPS1 produces trehalose, an osmolyte that adjusts osmosis and protects macromolecules, enhancing drought tolerance.

genes: PDS (phytoene desaturase, barley)
phenotype: Photobleaching in wheat spikes and grains due to PDS gene silencing, with 92% reduction in PDS transcript abundance in chlorotic grains.
mechanism: RNAi via BSMV-based virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) system, which triggers post-transcriptional gene silencing (PTGS) through siRNA.

genes: 1Bx14 (High-molecular-weight glutenin subunit 1Bx14, wheat)
phenotype: 97% reduction in 1Bx14 transcript abundance and detectable decrease in HMW-GS 1Bx14 protein levels in wheat grains, leading to a 44.73% reduction in glutenin macropolymer protein (GMP) percentage.
mechanism: RNAi via BSMV-based VIGS system, which targets the 1Bx14 gene for silencing, reducing its contribution to glutenin macropolymer formation.

genes: asHMW (artificially assembled sequence homologous to x-type and y-type glutenin subunit genes)
modification_type: gene silencing of entire HMW-GS gene family
phenotype: Detectable down-regulation of multiple HMW-GS genes (1Ax2*, 1Bx17, 1By18, 1Dx5, 1Dy10) in spring wheat cv. Ningchun 16, but no apparent reduction in winter wheat cvs Xiaoyan 6 and Shaanyou 225.

Importantly, increased activity of the antioxidant enzymes POD and APX during infection and enhanced expression of NtAPX1 and NtGPX in transgenic tobacco following methyl viologen treatment were observed. Moreover, GhWRKY15 transcription was greater in the roots and stems compared with the expression in the cotyledon of cotton, and the stems of transgenic plants displayed faster elongation at the earlier shooting stages compared with wide type tobacco.
mechanism: Overexpression of GhWRKY15 may contribute to the alteration of defence resistance to both viral and fungal infections, probably through regulating the ROS system via multiple signalling pathways in tobacco. It is intriguing that GhWRKY15 overexpression in tobacco affects plant growth and development, especially stem elongation. This finding suggests that the role of the WRKY proteins in disease resistance may be closely related to their function in regulating plant growth and development.

mechanism: VND6 promoter-driven xylan biosynthesis in xylem vessels compensates for irx9 mutation by restoring xylem integrity and reducing cell wall recalcitrance.

genes: miraculin (Miraculin, taste-inverting protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of miraculin in Arabidopsis causes sour foods to taste sweet via pH-dependent binding to taste receptors
mechanism: Miraculin binds to taste receptors on the tongue in a pH-dependent manner, causing sour foods to taste sweet by altering receptor activation

genes: SBE I (starch branching enzyme I, Hordeum vulgare), SBE IIa (starch branching enzyme IIa, Hordeum vulgare), SBE IIb (starch branching enzyme IIb, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Simultaneous suppression of all three SBE genes in barley endosperm produces amylose-only starch granules with 99.1% amylose content, 65% resistant starch (RS) in gelatinized form (vs 29% in control), irregular granule morphology, and 25% crystallinity (B/Vh-type polymorphs vs A-type in control).
mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of SBE I, IIa, and IIb prevents amylopectin synthesis, leading to amylose-only starch. Amylose forms Vh-type crystallites instead of A-type amylopectin. Residual SBE activity (18% of control) cannot synthesize amylopectin. Upregulated starch synthases (SSIV, GBSSIb) compensate for yield loss.

genes: BLR (BELLRINGER, homeodomain transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BLR reduces organ size, with shorter hypocotyls, smaller rosette leaves, narrower cauline leaves, and shorter siliques. Epidermal cells in hypocotyls and stems are significantly smaller than wild type.
mechanism: BLR regulates cell wall-associated genes including PME5, MERI-5, EXP17, and lipid transfer proteins (LTPs). Downregulation of LTPs and peroxidases correlates with reduced cell expansion, while upregulation of MERI-5 suggests altered cell wall remodeling.

genes: MTP5 (At3g12100, cation diffusion facilitator/metal transport protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MTP5 restores IAA-conjugate sensitivity to iar1 mutants.
mechanism: MTP5 and IAR1 transport metals in an antagonistic fashion to regulate metal homeostasis, influencing IAA-conjugate hydrolysis.

genes: At5g37830 (OXP1, oxoprolinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced sensitivity to sulfamethoxazole (Smex) with EC50 of 6 μM and LD50 of 10 μM compared to wildtype (EC50 3 μM, LD50 5 μM)
mechanism: NA

genes: At2g23470 (unknown function, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Enhanced sensitivity to sulfamethoxazole (Smex) with EC50 of 0.003 μM and LD50 of 0.03 μM compared to wildtype (EC50 3 μM, LD50 5 μM)
mechanism: NA

genes: HvCKX2 (cytokinin dehydrogenase, barley, synthetic)
phenotype: Agrobacterium-mediated silencing of HvCKX2 increases plant productivity by ~34% in Hordeum vulgare, with higher seed count, grain yield, 1000 grain weight, plant height, and spike number. Biolistic silencing reduces productivity by ~32-51% with lower seed count, grain yield, and germination rates.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of HvCKX2 reduces transcript levels by 34-35% and CKX activity in leaves and spikes, leading to cytokinin accumulation and enhanced reproductive development. Bioblastic method causes imbalanced CKX activity (high in leaves, low in spikes) disrupting anther development and seed setting.

genes: LOS5 (Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of LOS5 increases drought tolerance in maize by enhancing ABA accumulation, reducing stomatal aperture, maintaining higher leaf water potential, and improving root biomass under drought stress.
mechanism: LOS5 overexpression increases aldehyde oxidase (AO) activity, leading to higher ABA accumulation. ABA promotes stomatal closure to reduce water loss, enhances antioxidant enzyme activities, and upregulates stress-responsive genes like ZmAO1, Rab17, and ZmP5CS1.

genes: MED18 (MED18, mediator subunit 18, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MED18 increases carpel and stamen numbers, reduces petal numbers, causes carpel-like sepals, and accelerates flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MED18 regulates floral homeotic gene expression (AG, AP1, PI) and flowering time regulators (FLC, FT), maintaining normal AG expression levels and patterns during floral organ development.

genes: SlTRY (Solanum lycopersicum trichome regulatory gene, tomato), 2xGFP (synthetic green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: CPC::SlTRY transgenic plants exhibit no trichomes on third leaves and increased root-hair density (40-50 root-hairs/mm) compared to wild-type (50 trichomes/leaf, 40 root-hairs/mm).
mechanism: SlTRY represses GL2 expression, which inhibits trichome formation and promotes root-hair development. GL2 expression is strongly repressed in all CPC::SlTRY lines.

genes: SlGL3 (Solanum lycopersicum bHLH transcription factor, tomato), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: GL3::SlGL3 transgenic plants show similar trichome numbers to wild-type (50 trichomes/leaf) but three of five lines exhibit reduced root-hair density (compared to wild-type 40 root-hairs/mm). In gl3-7454 mutant background, three of five lines show increased root-hairs compared to both wild-type and mutant.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtEHD1 (gene, full-length, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtEHD1-GFP increases salt tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, as evidenced by increased germination on NaCl-containing media and reduced ROS production under salt stress.
mechanism: EHD1 is involved in endocytic recycling, and overexpression enhances recycling, leading to increased salt tolerance by reducing ROS production and maintaining cellular integrity under salt stress.

genes: AtEHD1 (gene, 474 bp segment, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knock-down of AtEHD1 in Arabidopsis thaliana increases salt sensitivity, as evidenced by reduced germination on NaCl-containing media and increased ROS production under salt stress.
mechanism: EHD1 knock-down disrupts endocytic recycling, leading to impaired salt tolerance and increased ROS production under stress conditions.

genes: VvWRKY1 (Vitis vinifera WRKY1, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvWRKY1 confers a 40% decrease in susceptibility to Plasmopara viticola in grapevine.
mechanism: VvWRKY1 activates jasmonate (JA) signaling pathways by upregulating LOX and JAZ genes, leading to enhanced resistance to downy mildew.

genes: GhSOD1 (GhSOD1, Cu/Zn SOD1, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhSOD1 increases tolerance to MV-induced oxidative stress and salt stress in Gossypium hirsutum.
mechanism: Overexpression of GhSOD1 enhances antioxidant enzyme activity in chloroplasts, leading to higher SOD activity and improved stress tolerance.

genes: GhAPX1 (GhAPX1, APX1, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhAPX1 increases tolerance to MV-induced oxidative stress and salt stress in Gossypium hirsutum.
mechanism: Overexpression of GhAPX1 enhances antioxidant enzyme activity in chloroplasts, leading to higher APX activity and improved stress tolerance.

genes: GhCAT1 (GhCAT1, CAT1, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhCAT1 increases tolerance to MV-induced oxidative stress and salt stress in Gossypium hirsutum.
mechanism: Overexpression of GhCAT1 enhances antioxidant enzyme activity in chloroplasts, leading to higher CAT activity and improved stress tolerance.

genes: pri-miR171a (miR171a, microRNA, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR171a in barley leads to pleiotropic phenotypes including branching defects, increased short vegetative phytomers, late flowering, dwarfism, and reduced tillering under short day conditions.
mechanism: miR171 regulates shoot branching through a conserved mechanism between monocots and dicots by down-regulating HvSCL genes and activating the miR156 pathway while repressing TRD and HvPLA1 genes.

genes: EuIPI (isopentenyl diphosphate isomerase, Eucommia ulmoides)
phenotype: Transgenic lines overexpressing EuIPI showed 3- to 4-fold increase in total trans-polyisoprenes compared with wild-type control
mechanism: IPI catalyzes conversion of isopentenyl diphosphate to dimethylallyl diphosphate, the first step in biosynthesis of all isoprenoids including polyisoprene

genes: PWR (At3g52250, transcription factor involved in floral determinacy, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues ag-10 pwr-1 floral determinacy defects; flowers rarely produce gynoecia with ectopic floral organs and lack elongated gynophores
mechanism: Enhances CRC and miR172 expression to promote floral stem cell termination

genes: vCBF (Vaccinium myrtillus, coding region), vCBF (Vaccinium uliginosum, coding region), vCBF (Vaccinium vitis-idaea, coding region)
phenotype: Overexpression of vCBF from V. myrtillus increases freezing tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, as evidenced by higher survival rates and preserved Fv/Fm values after freezing compared to wild type and other vCBF-expressing lines.
mechanism: vCBF activates Arabidopsis COR genes (KIN2, GOLS3, LTI78, COR15A, COR414), enhancing freezing tolerance through cold acclimation and DELLA-mediated growth inhibition.

genes: vCBF (Vaccinium myrtillus, coding region), vCBF (Vaccinium uliginosum, coding region), vCBF (Vaccinium vitis-idaea, coding region)
phenotype: GFP-vCBF fusions from V. myrtillus show higher transactivation of CRT::LUC in Nicotiana benthamiana compared to fusions from V. uliginosum and V. vitis-idaea, correlating with stronger freezing tolerance in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: GFP-vCBF localizes to the nucleus and activates DRE/CRT promoters; V. uliginosum CBF exhibits lower protein stability, while V. vitis-idaea CBF shows reduced transactivation despite similar localization.

genes: LUC (Luciferase, reporter gene, Photinus pyralis)
phenotype: Moderate basal luciferase activity in Arabidopsis thaliana, repressed by CHH methylation and de-repressed by cytosine methylation inhibitors.
mechanism: Regulated by RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM)-mediated transcriptional gene silencing (TGS), MOM1, and ROS1-mediated DNA demethylation.

genes: NPTII (NEOMYCIN PHOSPHOTRANSFERASE II, selectable marker, Escherichia coli)

mechanism: NA

genes: SbSOS1 (SbSOS1, Na+/H+ antiporter from Salicornia brachiata, Salicornia brachiata)
phenotype: Overexpression of SbSOS1 in tobacco conferred high salt tolerance, enhanced plant growth, and altered physiological and biochemical parameters in response to salt stress. Transgenic plants showed increased K+/Na+ ratio, membrane stability, and reduced Na+ content in roots and leaves compared to wild type.
mechanism: SbSOS1 facilitates Na+ efflux across the plasma membrane, maintains variable Na+ content in different organs, and indirectly affects other transporters' activity. It reduces cytosolic Na+ content and oxidative damage by decreasing ROS and MDA accumulation.

genes: MADS8 (MADS8, suppression of ethylene biosynthesis, Malus × domestica), MADS9 (MADS9, suppression of ethylene biosynthesis, Malus × domestica)
phenotype: Suppression of MADS8/9 causes delayed ripening in apples, with high auxin concentrations observed in MADS8/9as fruit compared to controls.
mechanism: High auxin concentrations in MADS8/9as apples are maintained through increased auxin synthesis and reduced conjugation via GH3 enzymes, which correlates with delayed ripening.

genes: PpAOS1 (allene oxide synthase 1, Physcomitrella patens, Physcomitrella patens), PpAOS2 (allene oxide synthase 2, Physcomitrella patens, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: PpAOS1-YFP localized in the cytosol, PpAOS2-YFP localized in the plastid
mechanism: YFP fusion for subcellular localization studies

genes: CTB-ESAT6 (cholera toxin B subunit fused to ESAT6, 6 kDa early secretory antigenic target, Mycobacterium tuberculosis)
phenotype: CTB-ESAT6 accumulates up to 0.75% of total leaf protein in mature lettuce leaves. Lyophilization increases antigen content 22-fold per gram of leaf material.
mechanism: Expression driven by psbA promoter and 5′ Utr with multiple ribosome binding sites, and stabilized by psbA 3′ Utr. Lyophilization enhances antigen concentration by removing 95% of water content.

genes: ZmNAC1 (ZmNAC1, NAC domain transcription factor involved in lateral root development, Zea mays)

mechanism: ZmNAC1 enhances lateral root initiation by transmitting auxin signals, which activate downstream genes involved in lateral root primordium formation.

mechanism: ScHK2 knockdown decreases hexose phosphorylation, preserving ATP levels and maintaining glycolytic flux, which promotes root growth.

phenotype: Overexpression of Crr1aG004 in Arabidopsis confers resistance to Ano-01 (mean DI <1.0) but not Wakayama-01 (DI >2.6).
mechanism: Crr1aG004 encodes a TIR-NB-LRR-type disease resistance protein that inhibits plasmodial development during secondary infection by P. brassicae.

genes: Crr1aG004 (Crr1a, resistance to Plasmodiophora brassicae, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Overexpression of Crr1aG004 under its native 2.5-kb promoter in Arabidopsis confers resistance to Ano-01 (mean DI <1.0).
mechanism: Crr1aG004 expression in stele and cortex of roots and hypocotyls inhibits secondary infection by P. brassicae.

genes: Crr1aG004 (Crr1a, resistance to Plasmodiophora brassicae, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Overexpression of Crr1aG004 in susceptible Brassica rapa confers resistance to Ano-01 (DI=0-1) in a dose-dependent manner.
mechanism: Crr1aG004 expression level correlates with resistance strength, suggesting threshold-dependent effector-triggered immunity.

phenotype: Transcriptional gene silencing (TGS) of the transgene occurs in transgenic tobacco, with reactivation upon 5-azacytidine treatment.
mechanism: TGS is mediated by DNA methylation, as indicated by reactivation with DNA methylation inhibitors.

genes: P35S (CaMV 35S enhancer, promoter region), HPT (hygromycin phosphotransferase gene, synthetic)
phenotype: The P35S::HPT construct is used as a selectable marker in transgenic tobacco for supertransformation experiments.

mechanism: ASR candidates prevent transcriptional gene silencing (TGS) by protecting adjacent promoters from DNA methylation.

genes: El (CaMV 35S enhancer region, enhancer), P35S (CaMV 35S promoter region, promoter), GUS (β-glucuronidase gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Supertransformants with ASR602 show higher GUS activity compared to controls, indicating anti-silencing activity.
mechanism: ASR602 prevents DNA methylation of the 35S promoter region, thereby inhibiting transcriptional gene silencing (TGS).

phenotype: Plants transformed with ASR602-fused FWA show significantly later flowering compared to controls, indicating inhibition of FWA transgene silencing.
mechanism: ASR602 prevents DNA methylation of the FWA promoter, maintaining active chromatin state and preventing transcriptional gene silencing (TGS).

genes: SVP (flowering repressor affecting photoperiod response, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: A single amino acid substitution (Ala32 to Val32) in the MADS domain of SVP strongly alters its function, with Val32 generating a SVP loss-of-function allele that displays no effect on flowering initiation, while Ler Ala32 renders SVP functional and delays flowering initiation.

mechanism: WRKY46 promoter activation is mediated by Ca2+ signaling and CPKs phosphorylating WRKY transcription factors.

mechanism: Altered starch metabolism leading to hyperaccumulation of starch, which contributes to increased saccharification

genes: P25 (P25, silencing suppressor, Potato virus X)

mechanism: P25 suppresses RNA silencing, leading to major transcriptome changes in leaves (1350 up-regulated transcripts) and minor changes in flowers. This activates ethylene/jasmonic acid/salicylic acid signaling pathways and defense-related genes, but homeostasis is maintained via proteosomal degradation of proteins.

genes: HAI1 (HAI1, HAI1 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HAI1 increases root length and hypocotyl length in Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings.
mechanism: HAI1 enhances ABA signal transduction, leading to ABA-hypersensitive inhibition of seed germination and reduced water loss under drought stress.

genes: HAI1 (HAI1, HAI1 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: HAI1 promoter is induced by ABA and abiotic stresses, leading to GUS expression in vascular tissues and wound sites.

genes: HAI1 (HAI1, HAI1 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of HAI1-GFP fusion in onion epidermal cells localizes the HAI1 protein to the nucleus.
mechanism: HAI1-GFP fusion protein is targeted to the nucleus, indicating its role in nuclear ABA signaling.

mechanism: MtN5 is an early marker of M. truncatula and S. meliloti interaction

genes: uidA (GUS reporter, synthetic)

mechanism: SRKb promoter activity varies by accession and genetic background, with epigenetic factors influencing expression
