phenotype: Expression of P–INS–RTB fusion protein in potato tubers, with detectable lectin activity and immunological binding to anti-insulin and anti-RTB antibodies.
mechanism: The SEKDEL microsomal retention signal sequesters the P–INS–RTB fusion protein in the endoplasmic reticulum via Golgi cisternae recycling, increasing intracellular concentration.

genes: DWARF5 (At1g50430, Δ5,7-sterol-Δ7-reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restoration of wild-type sterol profile and morphology in dwarf5-2 mutants, including full reversion to wild-type phenotype with normal sitosterol levels and morphology.
mechanism: Catalytic activity of the Δ5,7-sterol-Δ7-reductase enzyme, enabling sitosterol biosynthesis and brassinosteroid production.

genes: DIM (At3g19820, Δ24-sterol-Δ24-reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restoration of wild-type sterol profile and morphology in dim mutants, including full reversion to wild-type phenotype with normal campesterol and sitosterol levels and morphology.
mechanism: Catalytic activity of the Δ24-sterol-Δ24-reductase enzyme, enabling conversion of 24-methylene cholesterol to campesterol and sitosterol.

genes: STE1 (At3g02580, Δ7-sterol-C5-desaturase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restoration of wild-type sterol profile and morphology in ste1-1 mutants, including partial to full reversion of Δ7-sterol accumulation and normalization of brassinosteroid biosynthesis.
mechanism: Catalytic activity of the Δ7-sterol-C5-desaturase enzyme, enabling conversion of Δ7-sterols to Δ5-sterols and maintaining brassinosteroid production.

genes: man5As (Bispora sp. MEY-1, β-mannanase, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic maize seeds express β-mannanase with activities ranging from 2,008 to 26,860 U/kg, significantly higher than non-transgenic Zheng58 (1,265 U/kg).
mechanism: The β-mannanase enzyme breaks down β-mannan polysaccharides in plant cell walls, improving feed digestibility in livestock.

genes: NPR1 (NPR1, steroid hormone binding domain fused, synthetic), HBD (steroid hormone binding domain, synthetic)
phenotype: NPR1-HBD does not complement npr1-1 in RIM, but does in npr1-3 when DEX is applied
mechanism: Cytosolic NPR1 function in RIM

genes: BOP1 (BOP1, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S:BOP1 lines show stronger RIM than Col-0
mechanism: Enhanced MeJA signaling

genes: BOP2 (BOP2, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S:BOP2 lines show strong variation in MeJA-treated plants
mechanism: Enhanced MeJA signaling

genes: BOP1 (BOP1, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), BOP2 (BOP2, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduction of BOP1 and BOP2 expression partially phenocopies the double bop1 bop2, leading to RIM- phenotype
mechanism: Reduced BOP1 and BOP2 expression affecting MeJA signaling

genes: CNGC7 (CNGC7, cyclic nucleotide-gated channel, Arabidopsis thaliana), CNGC8 (CNGC8, cyclic nucleotide-gated channel, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescue of cngc7/8 pollen transmission defect by 23-27% transmission frequency in F1 progeny.
mechanism: Functional complementation of cngc7/8 loss-of-function mutations via pollen-specific expression of GFP-tagged CNGC7.

genes: CNGC7 (CNGC7, cyclic nucleotide-gated channel, Arabidopsis thaliana), CNGC8 (CNGC8, cyclic nucleotide-gated channel, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Partial rescue of cngc7/8 pollen transmission defect with 10-20-fold reduced efficiency compared to wild-type transgenes.
mechanism: Functional impairment of CNGC7 due to F589W substitution in the cyclic nucleotide binding domain.

genes: CNGC7 (CNGC7, cyclic nucleotide-gated channel, Arabidopsis thaliana), CNGC8 (CNGC8, cyclic nucleotide-gated channel, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescue of cngc7/8 pollen transmission defect by 23-27% transmission frequency in F1 progeny.
mechanism: Functional complementation of cngc7/8 loss-of-function mutations via pollen-specific expression of FLAG-tagged CNGC8.

genes: CNGC7 (CNGC7, cyclic nucleotide-gated channel, Arabidopsis thaliana), CNGC8 (CNGC8, cyclic nucleotide-gated channel, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Partial rescue of cngc7/8 pollen transmission defect with 10-20-fold reduced efficiency compared to wild-type transgenes.
mechanism: Functional impairment of CNGC8 due to F624W substitution in the cyclic nucleotide binding domain.

genes: GmGBP1 (Glycine max GAMYB-binding protein gene, soybean), AtSKIP (Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmGBP1 in Arabidopsis thaliana under long-day conditions results in earlier flowering (2 days earlier) and fewer rosette leaves compared to wild type.
mechanism: GmGBP1 up-regulates flowering-related genes CONSTANS (CO) and FLOWERING LOCUS T (FT) in long-day pathways, and interacts with GmGAMYB1 in gibberellin signaling to regulate flowering.

genes: AtSKIP (Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RNAi suppression of AtSKIP in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to growth arrest, delayed flowering, and reduced expression of flowering-related genes (CONSTANS, FLOWERING LOCUS T, LEAFY).
mechanism: AtSKIP functions as a positive regulator in flowering pathways and a component of the spliceosome linking alternative splicing and the circadian clock. Its suppression disrupts these pathways.

genes: GmGBP1 (Glycine max GAMYB-binding protein gene, soybean)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmGBP1 in Arabidopsis thaliana myb33 mutant plants under long-day conditions results in earlier flowering and fewer rosette leaves, similar to wild-type plants.
mechanism: GmGBP1 compensates for the loss of AtMYB33 function by up-regulating flowering-related genes in the photoperiodic pathway.

genes: RPS4 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), RRS1 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RPS4 and RRS1 confers resistance to Colletotrichum higginsianum in Brassica rapa, with only small necrotic flecks at inoculated sites.
mechanism: NA

genes: RPS4 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), RRS1 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RPS4 and RRS1 confers resistance to Colletotrichum higginsianum in Brassica napus, with only small necrotic flecks at inoculated sites.
mechanism: NA

genes: RPS4 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), RRS1 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RPS4 and RRS1 in Nicotiana benthamiana enables recognition of bacterial effectors AvrRps4 and PopP2, inducing cell death upon effector expression.
mechanism: NA

genes: RPS4 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), RRS1 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RPS4 and RRS1 in tomato confers resistance to Ralstonia solanacearum (popP2) and Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato (avrRps4).
mechanism: NA

genes: RPS4 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), RRS1 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RPS4 and RRS1 in cucumber confers resistance to Colletotrichum orbiculare, with only small necrotic flecks at inoculated sites.
mechanism: NA

genes: RPS4 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RPS4 alone in Brassica rapa does not confer resistance to Colletotrichum higginsianum.
mechanism: NA

genes: RRS1 (resistance gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RRS1 alone in Brassica rapa does not confer resistance to Colletotrichum higginsianum.
mechanism: NA

genes: Ehd4 (Ehd4, flowering time regulator, Oryza sativa ssp. japonica)
phenotype: Transgenic plants carrying the full-length cDNA of Ehd4 driven by the maize Ubiquitin-1 promoter fully complemented the ehd4 phenotype under both SDs and LDs, rescuing flowering time.
mechanism: Ehd4 promotes flowering by positively regulating the expression of Hd3a and RFT1 through Ehd1, independent of other known Ehd1 regulators.

genes: Ehd4 (Ehd4, flowering time regulator, Oryza sativa ssp. japonica)
phenotype: Transgenic plants carrying the full-length cDNA of Ehd4 driven by its native promoter (2.7 kb upstream from ATG) partially rescued the ehd4 phenotype under both SDs and LDs.
mechanism: Ehd4 promotes flowering by positively regulating the expression of Hd3a and RFT1 through Ehd1, independent of other known Ehd1 regulators.

genes: Ehd1 (Ehd1, flowering time regulator, Oryza sativa ssp. japonica)
phenotype: Over-expression of Ehd1 driven by the maize Ubiquitin-1 promoter rescued the late flowering phenotype of ehd4 under SDs.
mechanism: Ehd1 acts downstream of Ehd4 to promote flowering by regulating Hd3a and RFT1 expression.

genes: OspA (outer surface protein A, Escherichia coli), YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, Clontech)
phenotype: OA:YFP plants exhibit yellowing compared to wild type and reduced seed production, with OspA-YFP accumulating at ~5% total soluble protein (TSP) in leaves and 1.1% TSP in TIB-grown biomass.
mechanism: OspA-YFP accumulation interferes with photosynthetic electron transport, causing photoinhibition and growth retardation at high expression levels.

genes: GS1a (glutamine synthetase, Pinus sp., synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of pine GS1a in poplar increases growth, nitrogen use efficiency, alters wood chemistry, and enhances drought tolerance
mechanism: GS1a enhances nitrogen assimilation and photosynthesis while modulating antioxidant defense through copper cofactor reallocation to plastocyanins

genes: PICC (Arabidopsis thaliana, full-length, Arabidopsis thaliana), PICL (Arabidopsis thaliana, full-length, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GFP-PICC and GFP-PICL localize to the ER in Arabidopsis thaliana and Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: The C-terminal transmembrane domain fragment (TDF) of PICC and PICL is necessary and sufficient for ER localization.

genes: PICC (Arabidopsis thaliana, promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana), PICL (Arabidopsis thaliana, promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: pPICC::GUS and pPICL::GUS show vascular tissue expression in cotyledons, roots, and leaves of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: The 2.0 kb PICC promoter and 1.0 kb PICL promoter drive GUS expression in vascular tissues and hydathodes.

genes: HDEL-mCherry (synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: HDEL-mCherry marks the ER in Nicotiana benthamiana leaf epidermal cells when co-expressed with other proteins.
mechanism: The HDEL ER retention signal and 35S promoter drive mCherry expression for ER visualization.

genes: E1 (Acidothermus cellulolyticus endo-1,4-β-glucanase, synthetic)
phenotype: Active E1 was produced in plants with yields up to ~11 μg/g fresh weight (FW) for specific variant constructs.
mechanism: E1 was produced using agroinfiltration with CMV-based systems, which allows for rapid production in non-transgenic plants.

genes: E1 (Acidothermus cellulolyticus endo-1,4-β-glucanase, synthetic)
phenotype: Specific variant constructs yielded up to ~21 μg/g FW of E1 in non-transgenic plants.
mechanism: E1 was produced using agroinfiltration with CMV-based systems, which allows for rapid production in non-transgenic plants.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Bright GFP fluorescence was observed in infiltrated regions of N. benthamiana plants at 6 and 10 days post-infiltration.
mechanism: GFP was produced using agroinfiltration with CMV-based systems, which allows for rapid production in non-transgenic plants.

genes: E1 (Acidothermus cellulolyticus endo-1,4-β-glucanase, synthetic)
phenotype: The highest levels of active E1 were obtained for the 33 amino acid truncated CMVarI Ewt variant, yielding up to 21 μg/g of active E1.
mechanism: E1 was produced using agroinfiltration with CMV-based systems, which allows for rapid production in non-transgenic plants.

genes: BvSTI (serine proteinase inhibitor, sugar beet, BvSTI)
phenotype: Overexpression of BvSTI in N. benthamiana reduces larval weights of fall armyworm, beet armyworm, and tobacco hornworm by 19-71% compared to controls, while increasing larval weights of black cutworm and tobacco budworm by 50-100%.
mechanism: BvSTI inhibits trypsin proteases in insect midguts, disrupting protein digestion and altering larval growth dynamics. Reduced trypsin activity correlates with lower larval weights in some species, while others exhibit compensatory feeding responses.

genes: hpPSTVd-ΔTLE (hairpin structure of PSTVd-ΔTLE, non-infectious RNA, PSTVd genome)
phenotype: Overexpression of hpPSTVd-ΔTLE in N. benthamiana suppresses PSTVd accumulation by producing siRNAs in phloem, with suppression evident at 14 dpi and partial attenuation in grafted scions
mechanism: Phloem-specific production of PSTVd-derived siRNAs via pCoYMV promoter mediates RNA silencing, attenuating PSTVd accumulation and potentially transporting silencing signals to scions via grafting

genes: NaJAZd (NaJAZd, JAZ gene, Nicotiana attenuata)
phenotype: NaJAZd-silenced plants showed increased flower abscission and reduced seed capsule production.
mechanism: NaJAZd regulates JA signaling and flower development-related genes like NaMYB305.

genes: OsAPX2 (ascorbate peroxidase 2, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of Osapx2 mutant restores wild-type phenotype including normal seedling height, leaf appearance, anther shape, pollen viability, and seed setting rate.
mechanism: OsAPX2 functions in scavenging H2O2 and maintaining ROS homeostasis, which is critical for growth and abiotic stress tolerance.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: DR5:GUS reporter marks earliest events of lateral root formation and auxin signaling in root cells
mechanism: GUS reporter activity indicates auxin gradient and cell fate specification in root stem cell niche

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein reporter, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: DR5:GFP reporter shows auxin gradient in root cells, with reduced signal intensity and lost gradient maximum in sdg2-3 QC cells
mechanism: GFP reporter activity visualizes auxin distribution and signaling in root stem cell niche

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: QC25:GUS reporter marks quiescent center (QC) cells and root cap cell layers, with reduced expression in sdg2-3 QC cells
mechanism: GUS reporter activity identifies QC cell identity and root cap organization

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: CYCB1;1:GUS reporter marks cell division activity and lateral root primordia formation, showing reduced lateral root formation in sdg2-3
mechanism: GUS reporter activity indicates cell cycle activity and lateral root primordia development

genes: ScAsg1 (ScAsg1, stress-inducible gene, S. commersonii)
phenotype: Overexpression of ScAsg1 increases stomatal resistance under salt stress in potato plants.
mechanism: Asg1 overexpression enhances stomatal closure in response to osmotic stress, likely via ABA-mediated pathways.

genes: AtAsg1 (AtAsg1, stress-inducible gene, Arabidopsis)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtAsg1 slightly reduces leaf water loss in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: Asg1 overexpression improves stomatal closure in Arabidopsis, likely via ABA-mediated pathways.

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene)
phenotype: Asg1 promoter::GUS transgenic Arabidopsis shows high GUS activity in vascular tissues.
mechanism: NA

genes: ScN2.1 (ScN2.1, ASG1 gene, S. commersonii)
phenotype: ScN2.1-GFP fusion protein localizes near the plasma membrane in onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: RD29B-LUC (RD29B promoter-LUC reporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), ABF2 (ABF2 transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), SnRK2.6 (SnRK2.6 kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), ABI1 (ABI1 phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana), RCAR1 (RCAR1 ABA receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-transfection of RD29B-LUC with ABF2, SnRK2.6, ABI1, and RCAR1 in Arabidopsis protoplasts reconstituted ABA signaling pathway for stress-responsive gene expression.
mechanism: RD29B-LUC expression is regulated by ABA signaling through interactions between RCAR1, ABI1, and SnRK2.6. ROP11 antagonizes RCAR1-dependent inhibition of ABI1 activity.

genes: ABI1 (ABI1 phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana), ROP11 (ROP11 GTPase, Arabidopsis thaliana), CA-ROP11 (constitutively active ROP11, Arabidopsis thaliana), DN-ROP11 (dominant-negative ROP11, Arabidopsis thaliana), RCAR1 (RCAR1 ABA receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Luciferase activity in N. benthamiana leaves demonstrated direct interaction between ABI1 and ROP11/CA-ROP11/DN-ROP11/RCAR1.
mechanism: Luciferase complementation imaging (LCI) showed strong activity when ABI1 interacted with ROP11 variants or RCAR1, confirming direct protein-protein interactions.

genes: RCAR1 (RCAR1 ABA receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana), ABI1 (ABI1 phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana), ROP11 (ROP11 GTPase, Arabidopsis thaliana), CA-ROP11 (constitutively active ROP11, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Recombinant proteins expressed in E. coli showed CA-ROP11 protects ABI1 phosphatase activity from RCAR1 inhibition.
mechanism: In vitro assays demonstrated CA-ROP11 (GTP-bound) counteracts RCAR1-mediated inhibition of ABI1 phosphatase activity.

genes: AhSTS1 (stilbene synthase, Arachis hypogaea)
phenotype: Transgenic rice grains accumulate resveratrol (0.1–4.8 µg/g) and piceid (0.1–10.4 µg/g), with resveratrol levels comparable to high-quality red wine (0.8–5.8 µg/mL).
mechanism: AhSTS1 overexpression enables resveratrol biosynthesis from p-coumaric acid and malonyl-CoA. Resveratrol glucosyltransferase activity in leaves converts resveratrol to piceid, with higher resveratrol retention in grains.

genes: IAA15 (IAA15, auxin signaling repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of IAA15 results in reduced auxin sensitivity (impaired root elongation and lateral root formation), agravitropic phenotype, reduced apical dominance, small curled leaves, short crinkled siliques with fewer seeds, and reduced root meristem size.
mechanism: IAA15 overexpression disrupts auxin homeostasis by upregulating auxin biosynthesis genes (YUC1, YUC2, YUC4, YUC6), downregulating auxin transport genes (AUX1, PINs), and reducing auxin conjugation hydrolases (IAR3, ILL2, ILL3). This leads to elevated endogenous IAA levels and impaired auxin response, including reduced gravitropic response and root meristem size.

genes: IAA15 (IAA15, auxin signaling repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: No significant changes in primary root length, lateral root numbers, or gravity responses were observed in amiRNA-IAA15 lines, suggesting IAA15 functions redundantly with other Aux/IAAs.
mechanism: NA

genes: IAA15 (IAA15, auxin signaling repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP-IAA15 fusion protein results in detectable nuclear localization and rapid degradation upon auxin treatment, indicating auxin sensitivity at the protein level.
mechanism: GFP-IAA15 fusion protein localizes to the nucleus and is degraded within 10 minutes of 100 nM IAA treatment, demonstrating auxin-dependent regulation.

genes: IAA15 (IAA15, auxin signaling repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS staining reveals IAA15 expression in root meristematic zone, lateral root primordia, hypocotyls, shoot apical meristem, leaf veins, inflorescence stem, and stigma. Auxin treatment induces GUS activity in roots.
mechanism: IAA15 promoter drives GUS expression in root and aerial tissues, with auxin induction restricted to roots.

genes: ADH1 (alcohol dehydrogenase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: High-frequency ZFN-mediated mutagenesis at the ADH1 locus in Arabidopsis thaliana, with a sixfold increase in smc6b mutants.
mechanism: ZFN-induced DSBs leading to NHEJ and GT

genes: TT4 (At5g13930, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Fourfold increase in ZFN-mediated mutagenesis in smc6b mutants compared to WT.
mechanism: ZFN-induced DSBs leading to NHEJ and GT

genes: MPK8 (At1g18150, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Twofold increase in ZFN-mediated mutagenesis in smc6b mutants compared to WT.
mechanism: ZFN-induced DSBs leading to NHEJ and GT

genes: OsFD2 (OsFD2, overexpression, Oryza sativa), OsFD2 S164A (OsFD2 S164A, phosphorylation site mutation, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsFD2 produces dense panicles with increased spikelet density and abnormal branch shoots with iterated leaf development. S164A mutation suppresses these phenotypes.
mechanism: OsFD2 interacts with 14-3-3 proteins via its SAP motif, which is required for nuclear exclusion and function in leaf development. S164A mutation disrupts 14-3-3 interaction and abolishes the phenotype.

genes: AS2 (AS2, adaxial determinant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of AS2 under AS1 promoter rescues filamentous leaf phenotype in as2-1 mutant by repressing ARF3/ETT and ARF4 expression
mechanism: AS1-AS2 complex represses ARF3/ETT and ARF4 transcription factors, which in turn regulate cell cycle inhibitors (KRP2/KRP5) and cytokinin biosynthesis (IPT3) to stabilize adaxial-abaxial polarity

genes: OsFIE2 (rice FIE homologue, regulates endosperm development and grain filling, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi lines show reduced seed fill (66-81% filled seeds vs 88% in wild-type), smaller fully filled seeds, and partially filled/unfilled seeds with defective endosperm and enlarged embryos
mechanism: OsFIE2 regulates storage protein and starch synthesis in endosperm via H3K27me3 modification; RNAi reduces OsFIE2 expression leading to decreased H3K27me3 and altered gene expression of starch biosynthesis (e.g., AGPS2b) and storage protein genes

genes: OsFIE2 (rice FIE homologue, regulates endosperm development and grain filling, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: No obvious phenotype in overexpression lines; normal endosperm and embryo development
mechanism: NA

genes: MINI3 (At1G55600, full-length, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased seed mass in 35S::MINI3:GFP transgenic lines compared to wild-type Ws plants.
mechanism: MINI3 binds to W-boxes in the promoters of MINI3 and IKU2, facilitating SHB1-mediated transcriptional activation.

genes: SHB1 (At4G25350, N-terminal 520 amino acids, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: N520:GFP interacts with MINI3:MYC:His in Nicotiana leaves.
mechanism: SHB1 N-terminus interacts with MINI3 N-terminus, with the SPX domain playing a key role.

genes: MINI3 (At1G55600, N-terminal 302 amino acids, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: N302:MYC:His interacts with SHB1:GFP in Nicotiana leaves.
mechanism: MINI3 N-terminus mediates interaction with SHB1, independent of its WRKY DNA binding domain.

genes: pBVR3 (pBVR3, phytochrome inactivation, synthetic), pBVR2 (pBVR2, phytochrome inactivation, synthetic)
phenotype: 35S::pBVR3 exhibits constitutive phytochrome inactivation with shorter hypocotyls compared to CAB3::pBVR2 under FRc light. CAB3::pBVR2 shows mesophyll-specific phytochrome inactivation with significantly longer hypocotyls (15-20% increase) under FRc light.
mechanism: pBVR3 and pBVR2 encode phytochrome inactivation domains that disrupt phytochrome signaling, with CAB3::pBVR2's mesophyll-specific expression leading to differential hypocotyl elongation compared to 35S::pBVR3's constitutive expression.

genes: TUD1 (TUD1, functional U-box E3 ligase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of tud1-2 mutant phenotype restores wild-type plant morphology
mechanism: TUD1 functions as a U-box E3 ligase interacting with D1 in the plasma membrane, mediating BR signaling pathway

genes: β-1,3-glucanase (β-1,3-glucanase, pathogenesis-related enzyme, potato)
phenotype: Overexpression of β-1,3-glucanase increases cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin content while decreasing lignin and callose content in flax fibres. Fibres show improved antioxidant potential and altered mechanical properties with no significant change in tensile strength.
mechanism: β-1,3-glucanase hydrolyzes callose (β-1,3-glucan), releasing glucose that redirects to polysaccharide synthesis. Reduced lignin and increased phenolic compound binding to polysaccharides enhance antioxidant properties.

genes: AN (ANGUSTIFOLIA, gene involved in SUB-dependent signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of YFP:AN rescues the an-2 mutant phenotype, restoring normal trichome branching and leaf morphology in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AN is involved in SUB signal transduction pathways, mediating intercellular communication during tissue morphogenesis.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GL2:GUS expression marks atrichoblast cell files in root hair patterning, serving as a marker for cellular patterning in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GUS serves as a reporter for root hair patterning by indicating the expression domain of the GL2 promoter in atrichoblast cells.

genes: GhGalT1 (GhGalT1, galactosyltransferase, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: GhGalT1-GFP fusion protein localizes to the Golgi apparatus in tobacco leaf epidermal cells, as evidenced by co-localization with GONST1-YFP marker.
mechanism: GhGalT1 is a type II membrane protein with a single transmembrane helix and C-terminal galactosyltransferase domain, localized to the Golgi apparatus where it likely participates in AGP glycosylation.

genes: GhGalT1 (GhGalT1, galactosyltransferase, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhGalT1 in Arabidopsis promotes seedling growth with increased root length, biomass, chlorophyll content, and photosynthetic efficiency under normal and stress conditions (sucrose-free or high-sucrose media). Transgenic plants also show enhanced tolerance to exogenous D-arabinose and D-galactose, with longer hypocotyls under dark conditions.
mechanism: GhGalT1 overexpression alters pectin biosynthesis by upregulating GAUT8, GAUT9, and xgd1 genes, leading to increased arabinose, xylose, and galacturonic acid in cell wall fractions. This suggests GhGalT1 may regulate AGP glycosylation in the Golgi apparatus, indirectly affecting pectin synthesis and carbohydrate metabolism.

genes: LOX1 (lipoxygenase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of lox1-2 mutant with 35S:LOX1 restores resistance to Pst DC3000, with complemented line showing ~10-fold lower bacterial growth compared to lox1 mutants
mechanism: LOX1 activity mediates pathogen- and flg22-induced stomatal closure independently of ABA

genes: TdCor410b (promoter region, Triticum durum), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Transient expression of GUS reporter gene in wheat cell suspension cultures showed promoter activity regulation by TaDREB3 and stress responses
mechanism: TdCor410b promoter contains functional DRE/CRT elements that bind TaDREB3 transcription factor, with GCCGAC core element mediating cold/drought response

genes: TdCor410b (promoter region, Triticum durum), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Artificial promoter with GCC-box repeats showed altered activation properties in transient expression assays
mechanism: Substitution of CRT element with GCC-box repeats created a different DNA binding specificity for ERF transcription factors

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, Aequorea victoria), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Used as negative and positive controls for transient expression assays
mechanism: Ubi promoter drives constitutive expression for quantifying biolistic bombardment efficiency

genes: TaERF5a (transcription factor, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Inhibited basal activity of TdCor410b promoter in transient expression assays
mechanism: TaERF5a binds GCC-box but represses promoter activity through unknown mechanism

genes: TaERF6 (transcription factor, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Inhibited basal activity of TdCor410b promoter in transient expression assays
mechanism: TaERF6 binds GCC-box but represses promoter activity through unknown mechanism

genes: TaERF4a (transcription factor, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Restored GCC-box binding and activated artificial promoter in transient expression assays
mechanism: Pro42Arg mutation in AP2 domain altered DNA binding specificity to recognize GCC-box

genes: NIN (Nodule Infection 1, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: Overexpression of NIN induces cortical cell division and formation of bumps similar to root nodule primordia in Lotus japonicus roots.
mechanism: NIN induces cortical cell division and activates transcription of LjNF-YA1 and LjNF-YB1, which are required for root nodule organogenesis.

genes: NIN (Nodule Infection 1, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: Overexpression of NIN-myc induces cortical cell division and suppresses the infection thread-defective nin-2 phenotype in Lotus japonicus roots.
mechanism: NIN-myc binds to the promoters of LjNF-YA1 and LjNF-YB1 in vivo, activating their transcription and promoting root nodule organogenesis.

genes: LjNF-YA1 (Lotus japonicus NF-Y subunit A1), LjNF-YB1 (Lotus japonicus NF-Y subunit B1)
phenotype: Overexpression of LjNF-YA1 and LjNF-YB1 induces cortical cell division and malformed lateral roots in Lotus japonicus roots.
mechanism: LjNF-YA1 and LjNF-YB1 interact in planta to stimulate cell division, with LjNF-YA1 playing a primary role in root nodule primordium development.

genes: LjNF-YA1 (Lotus japonicus NF-Y subunit A1)
phenotype: Knockdown of LjNF-YA1 prevents root nodule formation in Lotus japonicus roots.
mechanism: LjNF-YA1 is required for cortical cell division during root nodule organogenesis downstream of NIN.

genes: LjNF-YA1 (Lotus japonicus NF-Y subunit A1)
phenotype: Overexpression of the 4xyB1a-GFP-GUS reporter gene driven by the CaMV35S minimal promoter with four tandem repeats of NBS-yB1a induces GUS expression in Lotus japonicus root nodule primordia.

genes: PtrANR1 (anthocyanidin reductase, Populus trichocarpa, cloned from poplar cDNA)
phenotype: Antisense suppression of PtrANR1 reduces soluble PA levels by ~40-50% in poplar leaves compared to controls, while increasing anthocyanin accumulation by ~20-30%.
mechanism: PtrANR1 knockdown reduces PA biosynthesis and redirects metabolic flux toward anthocyanin synthesis via UDP-glucose:flavonoid 3-O-glucosyltransferase (UFGT) activity.

genes: SsCBF1 (SsCBF1, cold-responsive transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicoides)
phenotype: Overexpression of SsCBF1 in Arabidopsis enhances salt tolerance (higher seed germination and root length under 150 mM NaCl) and increases freezing tolerance.
mechanism: SsCBF1 up-regulates stress-responsive genes (COR15A, RD29A, KIN2) and activates downstream pathways, improving cold and salt stress resistance.

genes: UidA (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic), GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Strong GUS staining in anthers and male gametophyte (uninucleate microspores, bicellular and tricellular pollen) and GFP labeling in bicellular and tricellular pollen grains
mechanism: The At5g17340 promoter drives expression of UidA and GFP in male gametophyte tissues during development

genes: Cry1Ac (insecticidal protein, Bacillus thuringiensis), npt-II (neomycin phosphotransferase, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of Cry1Ac insecticidal protein in transgenic brinjal for pest resistance
mechanism: Cry1Ac toxin production confers resistance to fruit and shoot borer pests

genes: MtNFP (Medicago truncatula Nodulation Factor Permease, Medicago truncatula), MtLYK3 (Medicago truncatula LysM Receptor-Like Kinase 3, Medicago truncatula), MtDMI2 (Medicago Doesn't Make Infection 2, Medicago truncatula), AtCERK1 (Arabidopsis thaliana Chitin Elicitor Receptor Kinase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-expression of MtNFP and MtLYK3 induces cell death in Nicotiana leaves, with 20/22 infiltrations showing confluent cell death 48 hours after infiltration.
mechanism: Cell death is associated with defense-like responses including phenolic compound accumulation, altered chlorophyll autofluorescence, and induction of defense-related genes (NbHIN1, NbPR1 basic, NbACRE31, NbACRE132). Ca2+ influx is required for cell death progression.

genes: AtCERK1 (Arabidopsis thaliana Chitin Elicitor Receptor Kinase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Heterologous production of AtCERK1-sYFP2 in Nicotiana leaves induces cell death in 20/22 infiltrations 36 hours after infiltration, dependent on kinase activity.
mechanism: AtCERK1 kinase activity is required for cell death induction, suggesting receptor activation and downstream signaling similar to MAMP-triggered immunity.

genes: MtNFP (Medicago truncatula Nodulation Factor Permease, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Co-expression of MtNFP[ΔInR]-sYFP2 with MtLYK3-sYFP2 does not induce cell death in Nicotiana leaves.
mechanism: The InR (intracellular region) of MtNFP is required for cell death induction, suggesting structural requirements for receptor complex formation.

genes: MtLYK3 (Medicago truncatula LysM Receptor-Like Kinase 3, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Co-expression of MtLYK3[G334E]-sYFP2 with MtNFP-sYFP2 does not induce cell death in Nicotiana leaves.
mechanism: The G334E mutation in MtLYK3 disrupts kinase activity, preventing receptor complex formation and downstream signaling.

genes: Rpi-blb1 (Rpi-blb1, disease resistance gene, wild potato species)
phenotype: Overexpression of Rpi-blb1 confers broad-spectrum foliar resistance against late blight and enhanced tuber resistance in Solanum tuberosum.
mechanism: Faster and stronger activation of defense-related genes, gene groups, and ontology bins correlates with successful tuber resistance against Phytophthora infestans.

genes: LUC (Luciferase, synthetic)
phenotype: ProCCA1:LUC expression in constant light (LL) shows shortened circadian periods in cca1-1 and lhy-20 mutants compared to wild type.
mechanism: CCA1 and LHY regulate the circadian clock, which in turn affects LUC expression under the CCA1 promoter.

genes: CCA1 (Circadian Clock Associated 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CCA1ox plants exhibit arrhythmic clock activity in both LL and LD conditions, leading to enhanced susceptibility to P. syringae.
mechanism: CCA1 overexpression disrupts the circadian clock, which negatively regulates its own expression and compromises disease resistance.

genes: LHY (Late Elongated Hypocotyl, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: LHYox plants show arrhythmic clock activity in LL and enhanced susceptibility to P. syringae, similar to CCA1ox plants.
mechanism: LHY overexpression disrupts the circadian clock, leading to compromised disease resistance independently of SA signaling.

genes: PLDδ (phospholipase D delta, AT4G35790, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PLDδ-knockout (PLDδ-KO) plants show delayed ABA-promoted leaf senescence, with less yellowing, higher photosynthesis activity, higher chlorophyll content, and less cell death compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: PLDδ positively regulates ABA-promoted leaf senescence through the regulation of lipid degradation, particularly the hydrolysis of phosphatidylcholine (PC) to produce phosphatidic acid (PA), which accelerates membrane lipid degradation.

genes: PLDδ (phospholipase D delta, AT4G35790, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PLDδ-complemented (PLDδ-RC) plants restore ABA-promoted senescence to wild-type levels, showing similar yellowing, photosynthesis activity, chlorophyll content, and cell death as wild-type plants.
mechanism: Complementation of PLDδ in PLDδ-KO plants restores the ABA-promoted senescence phenotype, confirming that PLDδ is required for this process.

genes: PLDα1 (phospholipase D alpha 1, AT4G35790, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PLDα1-antisense (PLDα1-AS) plants show delayed ABA-promoted leaf senescence, with reduced phosphatidic acid (PA) levels and attenuated lipid degradation compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: PLDα1-mediated PA production contributes to ABA-promoted senescence by regulating membrane lipid degradation, and its suppression reduces PA levels, delaying senescence.

genes: CCI1 (Clavata complex interactor 1, plasma membrane-localized phospholipid-binding protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: CCI1 binds phosphatidylinositols via polybasic regions in its N-terminal domain, localizing to plasma membrane detergent-resistant microdomains (DRMs) where it interacts with CLV signaling components

mechanism: CCI1 binds phosphatidylinositols via polybasic regions in its N-terminal domain, localizing to plasma membrane detergent-resistant microdomains (DRMs) where it interacts with CLV signaling components

genes: GhCAX3 (Ca2+/H+ exchanger, Gossypium hirsutum), sGhCAX3 (N-terminal truncated Ca2+/H+ exchanger, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhCAX3 alleviates ABA sensitivity in tobacco seeds and seedlings, and confers cold tolerance in seedlings. Transgenic plants show impaired ABA sensitivity and enhanced cold stress tolerance.
mechanism: GhCAX3 participates in ABA and cold signal transduction pathways. It modulates Ca2+ homeostasis and antioxidant enzyme activity (CAT, POD) to mitigate cold-induced membrane damage and enhance stress response gene expression (NbERD10C, NbDIN).

genes: GhCAX3 (Ca2+/H+ exchanger, Gossypium hirsutum), sGhCAX3 (N-terminal truncated Ca2+/H+ exchanger, Gossyium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of sGhCAX3 (N-terminal truncated) in tobacco seeds increases cold sensitivity during germination but enhances cold tolerance in seedlings. Transgenic plants show altered ABA sensitivity and enhanced cold stress tolerance.
mechanism: sGhCAX3 modulates Ca2+ transport activity by removing the N-terminal auto-inhibitory domain. This enhances cold tolerance in seedlings through antioxidant enzyme activity (CAT, POD) and stress-responsive gene expression (NbERD10C, NbDIN).

genes: dsRED (DsRed, visible marker, synthetic)
phenotype: AmiR-mediated silencing of dsRED in tobacco leaves reduces DsRED fluorescence by ~90% and significantly lowers dsRED mRNA and protein levels.
mechanism: mtr-miR159b backbone-mediated amiR cleaves dsRED mRNA, triggering RNA interference.

genes: dsRED (DsRed, visible marker, synthetic)
phenotype: AmiR-mediated silencing of dsRED in M. truncatula roots results in non-fluorescent roots, with dsRED mRNA and protein levels reduced by ~80%.
mechanism: mtr-miR159b backbone-mediated amiR cleaves dsRED mRNA, triggering RNA interference.

genes: MtErf1 (AP2-EREBP transcription factor, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: AmiR-mediated silencing of MtErf1 in M. truncatula roots results in deformed, non-fully branched arbuscules and reduced expression of mycorrhizal colonization markers.
mechanism: MtErf1 is required for arbuscule development; its knockdown disrupts fungal structure maturation.

genes: IMT (myo-inositol methyltransferase, Mesembryanthemum crystallinum, synthetic)
phenotype: Reduces phytic acid (PhA) by 19-35% in Brassica napus seeds while increasing inorganic phosphate (Pi) by 10-31% and altering carbohydrate profiles (e.g., increased sucrose, decreased raffinose).
mechanism: IMT converts myo-inositol to ononitol, diverting substrate away from phytic acid biosynthesis and altering carbohydrate metabolism pathways.

mechanism: IMT converts myo-inositol to ononitol, diverting substrate away from phytic acid biosynthesis and altering carbohydrate metabolism pathways.

genes: SmLEC1 (SmLEC1, LEC1-type HAP3 subunit, Selaginella moellendorffii)
phenotype: Transgenic lec1-1 mutant seeds expressing SmLEC1 germinate at 0.73% viability, compared to 0.062% for empty vector controls, indicating genetic suppression of the lec1 mutation
mechanism: SmLEC1 is orthologous and functionally conserved with Arabidopsis LEC1, enabling suppression of the lec1 mutation through LEC1-type HAP3 subunit activity

genes: PTD (PDX-1, protein transduction domain of pancreatic and duodenal homeobox factor-1, synthetic), GFP (synthetic green fluorescent protein, synthetic)

mechanism: ROS (reactive oxygen species) generated by biotic/abiotic stress induce chloroplast membrane leakiness, leading to release of PTD-GFP from intact chloroplasts into cytoplasm.

mechanism: ROS (reactive oxygen species) generated by biotic/abiotic stress induce chloroplast membrane leakiness, leading to release of PTD-GFP from intact chloroplasts into cytoplasm.

genes: PIN1 (PIN1, artificial microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana), PIN3 (PIN3, artificial microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Down-regulation of PIN1 and PIN3 leads to female gametophyte arrest at FG1 or FG3 stages, resulting in high ovule abortion rates (45-70%).
mechanism: PIN1 is involved in auxin flux towards the female gametophyte, which is required for gametophyte progression. PIN3 does not significantly contribute to ovule development.

genes: PIN2 (PIN2, fusion with GFP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PIN2-GFP is localized in the nucellus and inner integument during ovule development.
mechanism: NA

genes: CmMYB1 (R2R3-MYB transcription factor involved in lignin repression, chrysanthemum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmMYB1 reduces lignin content in Arabidopsis thaliana stems by 10-20%.
mechanism: CmMYB1 represses lignin biosynthesis by downregulating key genes such as AtCOMT1, AtCAD6, and others, leading to reduced lignin content.

genes: SlPMR4 (S-lycopersicum PMR4 ortholog, Solyc07g053980, tomato)
phenotype: Silencing of SlPMR4 in tomato reduces O. neolycopersici growth by ~80% at 8 dpi, with no severe growth reduction in 5-week-old plants.
mechanism: SlPMR4 is a susceptibility gene for powdery mildew; its silencing likely disrupts pathogen-induced callose synthase activity or regulatory pathways.

genes: SlDMR1 (S-lycopersicum DMR1 ortholog, Solyc04g008760, tomato)
phenotype: Silencing of SlDMR1 in tomato reduces O. neolycopersici growth by ~80% at 8 dpi, but causes growth retardation and yellowing in transgenic plants.
mechanism: SlDMR1 is a susceptibility gene for powdery mildew; its silencing likely increases homoserine accumulation, which directly inhibits pathogen growth.

genes: CsDFR (dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, Camellia sinensis), CsANR (anthocyanidin reductase, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsDFR in tobacco results in early flowering (86-95 days vs 105 days in control), increased capsule yield, higher seed yield per plant, and elevated flavonoid content (47.63-69.77 mg quercetin equivalent/g DW vs 39.8 mg/g in control). Transgenic lines show 70-185% higher DPPH radical scavenging activity and 15-43% reduced H2O2-induced cell death compared to control.
mechanism: CsDFR overexpression upregulates native NtCHS and NtANR2 genes, increasing flavonoid biosynthesis. Elevated flavonoids enhance antioxidant potential and modulate phytohormones (reduced GA3, increased IAA), contributing to early flowering and stress tolerance. Flavan-3-ols (catechin, epicatechin, epigallocatechin) act as anti-herbivore compounds, reducing S. litura larval growth by 10-70%.

phenotype: Overexpression of CsANR in tobacco results in early flowering (85-88 days vs 105 days in control), increased capsule yield, higher seed yield per plant, and elevated flavonoid content (47.63-69.77 mg quercetin equivalent/g DW vs 39.8 mg/g in control). Transgenic lines show 70-185% higher DPPH radical scavenging activity and 15-43% reduced H2O2-induced cell death compared to control.
mechanism: CsANR overexpression upregulates native NtCHS and NtANR2 genes, increasing flavonoid biosynthesis. Elevated flavonoids enhance antioxidant potential and modulate phytohormones (reduced GA3, increased IAA), contributing to early flowering and stress tolerance. Flavan-3-ols (catechin, epicatechin, epigallocatechin) act as anti-herbivore compounds, reducing S. litura larval growth by 10-70%.

genes: PtUGT72B1 (UDP-glucosyltransferase, xenobiotic detoxification, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Transgenic Arabidopsis plants show increased tolerance to phenol, hydroquinone, and catechol; enhanced glucosylation of these compounds into PGPS, arbutin, and catechol-glucoside; higher removal efficiency of phenolic pollutants from growth medium compared to wild-type plants
mechanism: PtUGT72B1 catalyzes O-glucosylation of phenol, hydroquinone, and catechol, converting them into less toxic glucosides (PGPS, arbutin) which are exported to the surrounding medium. This detoxification process enables plants to tolerate higher concentrations of these phytotoxic compounds.

genes: McMIPB (McMIPB aquaporin, Mesembryanthemum crystallinum L.)
phenotype: Overexpression of McMIPB increases photosynthesis rate by 48%, mesophyll conductance by 52%, and plant biomass (stem diameter +16%, shoot dry weight +62%) in Nicotiana tabacum under well-watered conditions.
mechanism: McMIPB enhances CO2 diffusion through mesophyll cells and chloroplasts, increasing photosynthetic efficiency. Aquaporin localization in mesophyll cells and stomatal chloroplasts facilitates CO2 permeability.

genes: PrpS1 (PrpS1, Papaver male S-determinant, Papaver rhoeas), PrpS3 (PrpS3, Papaver male S-determinant, Papaver rhoeas)
phenotype: Expression of PrpS1-GFP in Arabidopsis thaliana pollen enables S-allele-specific inhibition of pollen germination and tube growth when exposed to cognate PrsS proteins (PrsS1).
mechanism: PrpS1-GFP interacts with PrsS1 to trigger S-specific actin foci formation, programmed cell death (PCD) via caspase-3-like activity, and pollen tube inhibition, mimicking Papaver self-incompatibility (SI) responses.

genes: PrpS1 (PrpS1, Papaver male S-determinant, Papaver rhoeas), PrpS3 (PrpS3, Papaver male S-determinant, Papaver rhoeas)

mechanism: PrpS3-GFP interacts with PrsS3 to trigger S-specific actin foci formation, programmed cell death (PCD) via caspase-3-like activity, and pollen tube inhibition, mimicking Papaver self-incompatibility (SI) responses.

genes: αAI-1 (α-amylase inhibitor 1, from Phaseolus vulgaris)
phenotype: Overexpression of αAI-1 increases resistance to Zabrotes subfasciatus in cowpea seeds, with resistance varying between 89.3-94.4% depending on the line.
mechanism: αAI-1 inhibits α-amylase activity in insect midgut, but this study found no significant host-mediated effects on parasitoid Dinarmus basalis despite αAI-1 expression in seeds.

mechanism: TCU1 encodes a nucleoporin involved in nucleocytoplasmic trafficking and is required for normal leaf morphology, hypocotyl elongation, and flowering time.

genes: RcMADS1 (RcMADS1, MADS-box gene from Rafflesia cantleyi, Rafflesia cantleyi)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of RcMADS1 in Arabidopsis thaliana causes conversion of carpels into inflorescence-like structures and early flowering, with three distinct phenotypic severities (strong, weak, and wild-type-like).
mechanism: RcMADS1 functions similarly to Arabidopsis AGL24 by promoting SOC1 expression, which regulates floral transition. The dosage-dependent effect of RcMADS1 expression correlates with phenotypic severity.

mechanism: RcMADS1 functions as a functional ortholog of AGL24 by complementing the agl24-1 mutant and rescuing the FRI late flowering phenotype, similar to AGL24's role in floral transition.

genes: TaLEA (TaLEA, stress tolerance gene, Triticum aestivum)

mechanism: TaLEA gene product protects cell membranes from damage during salt and drought stress by maintaining membrane stability and reducing lipid peroxidation.

genes: SHN1 (SHN1, gain-of-function mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: shn1-1D plants are more susceptible to B. cinerea, S. sclerotiorum, and A. brassicicola than wild-type plants, with larger lesions, increased chlorotic areas, and faster senescence following infection.
mechanism: Altered cuticle structure and composition in shn1-1D leads to increased ROS accumulation and programmed cell death, which enhances susceptibility to necrotrophic pathogens.

genes: SHN1 (SHN1, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SHN1 under the CaMV35S promoter leads to a 3.5-fold increase in cutin levels compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: Increased cutin content modifies the cuticle structure, affecting plant defense responses and pathogen susceptibility.

genes: PIN6 (AT1G77110, auxin transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PIN6 results in stunted growth, reduced apical dominance, pronounced root waving, reduced root elongation, absence of root hair outgrowths, and altered lateral root development in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PIN6 overexpression perturbs auxin homeostasis and transport, leading to altered auxin gradients and ethylene signaling, which disrupts root elongation, lateral root development, and root hair formation.

genes: FiLUC (firefly luciferase, synthetic)
phenotype: The PIN6 promoter (−705 bp) drives tissue-specific expression of firefly luciferase in Arabidopsis thaliana, with activity observed in root apical meristem, root vasculature, and floral tissues.
mechanism: The PIN6 promoter contains auxin response elements (AS1-like, AuxRE, NDE) that mediate auxin-induced gene expression in root stele and shoot apical meristem.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: The PIN6 promoter (−3763 bp) drives low-level expression of β-glucuronidase in Arabidopsis thaliana, with activity detected in root apical meristem, lateral root primordia, and floral organ boundaries.
mechanism: The PIN6 promoter activity is regulated by developmental cues and auxin, with histone H3K27 trimethylation marks associated with low expression levels in most tissues.

genes: TaCIPK29 (Triticum aestivum CIPK29, salt stress responsive, wheat)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaCIPK29 enhances salt tolerance in transgenic tobacco, with improved germination rates (up to 150-200 mM NaCl), reduced root elongation suppression under salt stress, and higher survival rates after NaCl treatment compared to wild-type and vector control plants.
mechanism: TaCIPK29 regulates K+/Na+ ratios and Ca2+ content through upregulation of transporter genes (NtSOS1, NtNHX2, NtNHX4, NtCAX3), enhances antioxidant enzyme activities (CAT, POD), and interacts with NtCAT1 to reduce H2O2 accumulation and membrane damage under salt stress.

genes: AtELP3 (Elongator complex subunit 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of Atelp3-10 npr1 restores partial SA tolerance, reduces SA accumulation after Psm ES4326 infection, and delays defense gene expression, but enhances susceptibility to Psm ES4326.
mechanism: AtELP3's histone acetyltransferase (HAT) and radical SAM domains are essential for its role in plant immunity, likely through chromatin modification to facilitate defense gene induction.

genes: GFP (Green Fluorescent Protein, synthetic), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP and GUS in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves results in visible fluorescence and enzymatic activity, respectively.
mechanism: NA

genes: PAP1 (Production of Anthocyanin Pigment 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PAP1 in Nicotiana benthamiana leads to the production of dark-red anthocyanic foci and delphinidin-3-O-rutinoside.
mechanism: PAP1 activates the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway by promoting the expression of genes involved in flavonoid 3′5′-hydroxylase (F3′5′H), leading to the accumulation of delphinidin-based anthocyanins and myricetin-3-O-rutinoside.

genes: PAP1 (Production of Anthocyanin Pigment 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of PAP1-GFP fusion protein in Nicotiana benthamiana results in nuclear localization of the PAP1 protein and induction of anthocyanin biosynthesis.
mechanism: The PAP1-GFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus, where it activates the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway by promoting the expression of genes involved in flavonoid 3′5′-hydroxylase (F3′5′H), leading to the accumulation of delphinidin-based anthocyanins.

genes: SeBP (Selenium-Binding Protein 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of SeBP-GFP fusion protein in Nicotiana benthamiana results in cytoplasmic localization of the SeBP protein.
mechanism: NA

genes: ALB3 (ALB3, gene involved in chloroplast biogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: VIGS-ALB3 plants exhibit yellow or slightly albino leaves with severely reduced photosynthetic capacity (Fv/Fm) and chlorophyll content compared to VIGS-GFP controls
mechanism: ALB3 silencing disrupts chloroplast biogenesis, leading to nongreen plastids with few thylakoid membranes and reduced grana stacking

genes: LuWD40-1 (LuWD40-1, WD40 repeat protein, Linum usitatissimum)
phenotype: Overexpression of LuWD40-1 in flax causes male sterility with ~12-16% pollen viability, delayed flowering (~80 days vs 57 days in wild type), reduced branching (3 vs 10 branches per plant), and impaired seed development (shrivelled, bleached seeds with poor germination).
mechanism: LuWD40-1, a WD40 repeat protein, localizes to the nucleus and interacts with histone binding proteins. Its overexpression disrupts pollen development, shoot formation, and gametophyte function, likely through imbalanced protein interactions in pollen tissues.

genes: LuWD40-1 (LuWD40-1, WD40 repeat protein, Linum usitatissimum)
phenotype: RNAi-based knockout of LuWD40-1 prevents shoot regeneration from calli. None of the calli transformed with the KO construct produced shoots even after ten rounds of hygromycin selection.
mechanism: NA

genes: CDKA;1 (CDKA;1, dominant negative allele N146, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of dominant negative CDKA;1.N146 causes epidermal defects including cell loss, gaps in leaf epidermis, and ingrowth-like invaginations of anticlinal cell walls in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Defects in cytoskeleton function and vesicular trafficking during cytokinesis, leading to cuticle defects and impaired anticlinal wall adhesion

genes: PpABI1B (Group A PP2C, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: ppabi1b single disruptant exhibits normal protonemal growth; ppabi1a/b double disruptant shows slow growth with spherical brood cells and enhanced desiccation/freeze/salt tolerance without exogenous ABA
mechanism: Group A PP2C represses intrinsic desiccation tolerance by inhibiting ABA-activated kinase pathway and LEA protein/sugar accumulation; knockout constitutively activates stress tolerance mechanisms

genes: PATROL1 (At5g06970, proton ATPase translocation control 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the patrol1 mutant phenotype restores CO2 response in stomatal opening and rescues growth defects.
mechanism: PATROL1 encodes a protein with a MUN domain involved in intracellular membrane fusion and H+-ATPase localization to the plasma membrane.

genes: PATROL1 (At5g06970, proton ATPase translocation control 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP–PATROL1 rescues the patrol1 mutant phenotype and increases sensitivity to low [CO2] due to enhanced stomatal opening.
mechanism: GFP–PATROL1 localizes to endosomal compartments and plasma membrane, facilitating H+-ATPase tethering for stomatal opening.

genes: AHA1 (Arabidopsis H+-ATPase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP–AHA1 in WT and patrol1 backgrounds shows altered localization to plasma membrane, with increased internalization in patrol1 mutants.
mechanism: PATROL1 is required for proper localization of AHA1 to the plasma membrane, affecting stomatal opening and CO2 assimilation.

genes: AHA1 (Arabidopsis H+-ATPase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RFP–AHA1 in patrol1 mutants shows mislocalization to cytosolic punctate structures, confirming PATROL1's role in H+-ATPase recruitment.
mechanism: PATROL1 is essential for recruiting functional H+-ATPases to the plasma membrane, as evidenced by impaired FC-induced stomatal opening in patrol1.

genes: PATROL1 (At5g06970, proton ATPase translocation control 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under the PATROL1 promoter confirms its activity in guard cells and whole-plant tissues.
mechanism: PATROL1 promoter drives GUS expression in guard cells and other tissues, indicating its role in stomatal regulation and plant growth.

genes: ESP (enhanced sinigrin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ESP increases sensitivity to A. brassicicola in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ESP overexpression shifts glucosinolate-breakdown products to epithionitriles, which A. brassicicola is more sensitive to than ITCs.

genes: MYB29 (transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), MYB34 (transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MYB29 and MYB34 does not alter sensitivity to A. brassicicola or B. cinerea in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: ESP (enhanced sinigrin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ESP in tgg1tgg2 triple mutant does not affect resistance to A. brassicicola or B. cinerea in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: amiR-cad1 (artificial microRNA targeting BdCAD1, synthetic)
phenotype: Downregulation of BdCAD1 caused a leaf brown midrib phenotype, altered flowering time, increased stem count and weight, and reduced syringyl (S) lignin units with a decreased S/G ratio. Ethanol yield by microbial fermentation was enhanced in amiR-cad1-8 plants.
mechanism: BdCAD1 downregulation altered lignin composition by reducing S lignin units and increasing G lignin units, improving biomass digestibility.

genes: AtLEC1 (LEAFY COTYLEDON 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of AtLEC1 induces embryonic characteristics (ivory/fleshy appearance, unexpanded cotyledons) and delays germination by 2 days in tobacco seedlings. Transgenic seedlings produce fleshy true leaves but no callus formation after 40 days on 30 µM DEX.
mechanism: AtLEC1 initiates the transition from vegetative growth to embryonic characteristics but is insufficient to complete somatic embryogenesis in tobacco.

genes: AtLEC2 (LEAFY COTYLEDON 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of AtLEC2 induces 100% embryonic callus formation on shoot apical meristems, somatic embryo development, and plant regeneration in tobacco. Callus induced by 30 µM DEX regenerates 90% plantlets when transferred to hormone-free medium.
mechanism: AtLEC2 activates genes involved in seed maturation (storage proteins, fatty acid biosynthesis), auxin signaling (PIN1/2, ARF5/8/10), and represses GA3ox2 while upregulating GA20ox. It also induces SERK1 and MADS9, key regulators of embryogenesis.

genes: SLAC1 (At1g12480, S-type anion channel, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SLAC1 increases cryptogein-induced Cl− efflux and hypersensitive cell death in tobacco BY-2 cells.
mechanism: SLAC1-mediated anion efflux modulates NADPH oxidase activity and defense gene expression.

genes: SLAC1 (At1g12480, S-type anion channel, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (synthetic, green fluorescent protein, [35])
phenotype: SLAC1-GFP fusion protein localizes to the plasma membrane in BY-2 cells.
mechanism: GFP fusion allows visualization of SLAC1 localization.

genes: AtRDUF1 (At3g46620, RING finger protein involved in stress responses, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AtRDUF1:GFP fusion protein localizes to the cytosol and nuclei in Arabidopsis leaf protoplast cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtRDUF1 (At3g46620, RING finger protein involved in stress responses, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AtRDUF1::GUS transgenic plants show GUS activity in seeds, flowers, hypocotyls, leaves, roots, and reproductive tissues, with expression patterns altered under salt stress.
mechanism: NA

genes: At5g65040 (IRM1, increased resistance to Myzus persicae 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of IRM1 increases aphid resistance in Arabidopsis thaliana, reducing aphid population development by ~60% in 14 days.
mechanism: IRM1 overexpression creates mechanical barriers that hinder aphid stylet penetration and delay phloem access, reducing sustained phloem sap ingestion.

genes: ATAF1 (transcription factor involved in ABA biosynthesis regulation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ATAF1 causes stunted growth and delayed flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ATAF1 activates ABA biosynthesis by transcriptional activation of NCED3, leading to increased ABA levels and stomatal regulation.

genes: GUS (reporter gene)
phenotype: GUS activity detected in shoots but not roots of transgenic rice, with strong staining in guard cells of OsKAT2-GUS and OsKAT3-GUS plants
mechanism: OsKAT1, OsKAT2, and OsKAT3 promoters drive GUS expression in specific tissues including guard cells and aerial parts

genes: GUS (reporter gene)
phenotype: GUS activity localized specifically in guard cells of young and mature rice plants, with strong expression in leaf blades and sheaths
mechanism: OsKAT2 promoter drives GUS expression in guard cells and aerial tissues

genes: GUS (reporter gene)
phenotype: GUS activity observed in guard cells, vascular tissues, and mesophylls of rice leaves, with strong expression in leaf blades, sheaths, and culm
mechanism: OsKAT3 promoter drives GUS expression in guard cells and broad aerial tissues including vascular and mesophyll cells

genes: VRE1-35Smin (promoter, VRE1-35Smin, synthetic), GUSintron (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of VRE1-35Smin-GUSintron leads to GUS histochemical staining in tobacco leaves when co-expressed with VIP1.
mechanism: VIP1 binds to the VRE1 element in the promoter, activating transcription of the GUSintron reporter gene.

genes: VRE1-35Smin (promoter, VRE1-35Smin, synthetic), GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of VRE1-35Smin-GFP leads to GFP expression in transgenic tobacco plants when co-expressed with VIP1.
mechanism: VIP1 binds to the VRE1 element in the promoter, activating transcription of the GFP reporter gene.

genes: VRE2-35Smin (promoter, VRE2-35Smin, synthetic), GUSintron (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of VRE2-35Smin-GUSintron results in ~30% lower GUS activity compared to VRE1-35Smin-GUSintron.
mechanism: VRE2 mutations reduce VIP1 binding efficiency, leading to decreased transcriptional activation.

genes: VRE3-35Smin (promoter, VRE3-35Smin, synthetic), GUSintron (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of VRE3-35Smin-GUSintron results in ~20% higher GUS activity compared to VRE1-35Smin-GUSintron.
mechanism: VRE3 mutations enhance VIP1 binding efficiency, leading to increased transcriptional activation.

genes: VRE4-35Smin (promoter, VRE4-35Smin, synthetic), GUSintron (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of VRE4-35Smin-GUSintron results in ~10% of the GUS activity compared to VRE1-35Smin-GUSintron.
mechanism: VRE4 mutations almost completely disrupt VIP1 binding, leading to minimal transcriptional activation.

genes: VIP1 (VIP1, transcriptional activator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of VIP1 activates VRE1-35Smin-GFP and VRE1-35Smin-GUSintron reporters in tobacco.
mechanism: VIP1 binds to VRE elements in the promoter, activating transcription of downstream reporter genes.

genes: VIP1 (VIP1, transcriptional activator, Arabidopsis thaliana), virE2 (VirE2, Agrobacterium protein, Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Coexpression of VIP1 and virE2 slightly reduces (10–15%) the activation efficiency of VIP1 on VRE1-35Smin-GFP.
mechanism: VirE2 binding to VIP1 does not significantly affect VRE binding but may slightly reduce transcriptional activation.

genes: VIP1 (VIP1, transcriptional activator, Arabidopsis thaliana), virF (VirF, Agrobacterium protein, Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Coexpression of VIP1 and virF reduces VIP1 activity by >50% on VRE1-35Smin-GFP.
mechanism: VirF destabilizes VIP1 via proteasomal degradation, reducing available VIP1 for VRE binding.

genes: VIP1 (VIP1, transcriptional activator, Arabidopsis thaliana), VIP2 (VIP2, plant protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Coexpression of VIP1 and VIP2 slightly reduces (10–15%) the activation efficiency of VIP1 on VRE1-35Smin-GFP.
mechanism: VIP2 binding to VIP1 does not significantly affect VRE binding but may slightly reduce transcriptional activation.

genes: PP2A-Bγ (PP2A-Bγ, protein phosphatase 2A Bγ subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of pp2a-b'γ with 35S-driven PP2A-Bγ restores wild-type flowering time and gene expression patterns
mechanism: PP2A-Bγ represses the floral repressor FLC, promoting flowering through the autonomous pathway

genes: HC (heavy chain of mAb SO57, human)
phenotype: Expression of the heavy chain (HC) of mAb SO57 in transgenic tobacco plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: HCK (heavy chain with KDEL of mAb SO57, human)
phenotype: Expression of the heavy chain with KDEL (HCK) of mAb SO57 in transgenic tobacco plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: LC (light chain of mAb SO57, human)
phenotype: Expression of the light chain (LC) of mAb SO57 in transgenic tobacco plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: BC1 (BC1, cellulose biosynthesis, rice)
phenotype: Overexpression of wild-type BC1 rescued bc1 mutant phenotype with wild-type-like cellulose content and wall structure.
mechanism: BC1 modulates cellulose crystallinity and structure.

genes: BC1 (BC1 W72A, cellulose biosynthesis, rice)
phenotype: Plants expressing BC1 W72A showed partial recovery of cellulose content and wall structure.
mechanism: CBM aromatic residues contribute to cellulose binding and wall localization.

genes: BC1 (BC1 Y46A, cellulose biosynthesis, rice)
phenotype: Plants expressing BC1 Y46A retained bc1-like phenotypes with reduced cellulose content.
mechanism: CBM aromatic residues are critical for cellulose binding and wall localization.

genes: BC1 (BC1 Δω GFP, cellulose biosynthesis, rice)
phenotype: BC1ΔωGFP retained inside cells due to lack of GPI anchor, failing to rescue bc1 phenotype.
mechanism: GPI modification is essential for BC1 delivery to the cell wall.

genes: Thi2.4 (Thi2.4, thionin protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of Thi2.4 increases resistance to F. graminearum and F. sporotrichioides in Arabidopsis thaliana leaves and flower buds
mechanism: Thi2.4 has antifungal activity against F. graminearum and F. sporotrichioides by acting as an antifungal peptide that localizes to the cell wall of Arabidopsis and the cell membrane of F. graminearum

genes: LEC2 (LEC2, LEAFY COTYLEDON2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of LEC2 increases endogenous auxin content and alters morphogenic responses in Arabidopsis thaliana, including callus formation and somatic embryo development.
mechanism: LEC2 upregulates YUC1, YUC4, and YUC10 genes involved in auxin biosynthesis, leading to increased indolic compound levels and auxin sensitivity.

genes: SlCaM2 (SlCaM2, calmodulin, Solanum lycopersicum), SlCaM6 (SlCaM6, calmodulin, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of SlCaM2 and SlCaM6 in tomato plants reduced resistance to Tobacco rattle virus (TRV) and the oomycete pathogen Pythium aphanidermatum, with TRV viral symptoms and higher virus accumulation observed.
mechanism: Altered expression of signaling and defense-related genes, including reduced PR gene expression and differential regulation of calcium channel genes (SlCNGC17/18), glutathione transferase (SlGSTF2), and ubiquitin extension protein (SlUEP).

genes: SlCaM2 (SlCaM2, calmodulin, Solanum lycopersicum), SlCaM6 (SlCaM6, calmodulin, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of SlCaM2 and SlCaM6 in tomato plants resulted in significantly larger necrotic lesions (1.7–1.8 cm diameter) compared to control plants (1.5 cm diameter) when inoculated with Pythium aphanidermatum.
mechanism: Altered expression of signaling and defense-related genes, including reduced PR gene expression and differential regulation of calcium channel genes (SlCNGC17/18), glutathione transferase (SlGSTF2), and ubiquitin extension protein (SlUEP).

genes: AtCTF7 (Arabidopsis thaliana sister chromatid cohesion factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated downregulation of AtCTF7 causes severe growth inhibition during vegetative and reproductive stages, male and female sterility, chromosome fragmentation, and loss of sister chromatid cohesion during meiosis in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtCTF7 is required for association of cohesin with chromatin during meiosis, and its depletion leads to loss of sister chromatid cohesion at both chromosome arms and centromeres.

genes: GsWRKY20 (Glycine soja, WRKY transcription factor involved in flowering regulation)
phenotype: Overexpression of GsWRKY20 accelerates flowering time in Arabidopsis thaliana, reducing vegetative growth days from 39.7 to 32.1 and rosette leaves from 12.3 to 8.2 under LD conditions
mechanism: GsWRKY20 suppresses FLC (flowering repressor) and promotes CO, FT, and SOC1 (flowering activators) expression, leading to early flowering via the autonomous pathway

genes: AtCP2 (cysteine protease, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtCP2 increases gossypol accumulation in bollworm midgut when fed on transgenic Arabidopsis leaves.
mechanism: Cysteine protease increases midgut permeability to gossypol.

genes: GhCP1 (cysteine protease, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhCP1 increases gossypol accumulation in bollworm midgut when fed on transgenic cotton leaves, leading to reduced larval growth.
mechanism: Cysteine protease increases midgut permeability to gossypol.

genes: NAL1 (Os04g0615000, plant-specific protein involved in polar auxin transport, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi-NAL1 plants showed increased photosynthesis rate, higher flag leaf N content, and dwarf plant stature compared to wild-type Koshihikari
mechanism: NAL1 pleiotropically controls both plant stature and photosynthesis rate by modulating mesophyll cell divisions and Rubisco content

genes: AFR1 (AFR1, histone deacetylase complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana), AFR2 (AFR2, histone deacetylase complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AFR1-GUS and AFR2-GUS show strong expression in leaf vasculature, root tips, and shoot apices in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AFR1 and AFR2 downregulate FT expression in leaf vasculature by recruiting HDAC complexes to FT chromatin.

genes: AFR1 (AFR1, histone deacetylase complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana), AFR2 (AFR2, histone deacetylase complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AFR1-GUS and AFR2-GUS show strong expression in leaf vasculature, root tips, and shoot apices in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AFR1 and AFR2 downregulate FT expression in leaf vasculature by recruiting HDAC complexes to FT chromatin.

genes: AFR1 (AFR1, histone deacetylase complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AFR1:GFP and AFR2:GFP fusion proteins are localized in the nuclei of Arabidopsis root cells.
mechanism: AFR1 and AFR2 act as part of nuclear AFR1/AFR2-HDAC complexes in leaf vasculature to downregulate FT expression.

genes: AFR2 (AFR2, histone deacetylase complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AFR1:GFP and AFR2:GFP fusion proteins are localized in the nuclei of Arabidopsis root cells.
mechanism: AFR1 and AFR2 act as part of nuclear AFR1/AFR2-HDAC complexes in leaf vasculature to downregulate FT expression.

genes: AFR1 (AFR1, histone deacetylase complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of afr1-1 with AFR1:HA rescues the early-flowering phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AFR1 and AFR2 act additively to repress the floral transition by downregulating FT expression.

genes: AFR2 (AFR2, histone deacetylase complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of afr2-1 with AFR2:FLAG rescues the early-flowering phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AFR1 and AFR2 act additively to repress the floral transition by downregulating FT expression.

genes: AGL18 (AGL18, MADS-domain transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AGL18 causes moderate late flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AGL18 recruits AFR1/AFR2-HDAC to the FT locus to downregulate FT expression.

genes: FLN2 (At1g69200, FLN2 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complemented fln2–4 mutants exhibited normal morphology as wild type (WT) plants
mechanism: FLN2 is important for chloroplast development and seedling growth

genes: SrKA13H (ent-kaurenoic acid-13 hydroxylase, Stevia rebaudiana), SrUGT85C2 (UDP glycosyltransferase, Stevia rebaudiana), SrUGT74G1 (UDP glycosyltransferase, Stevia rebaudiana), SrUGT76G1 (UDP glycosyltransferase, Stevia rebaudiana)
phenotype: Transient silencing of SrKA13H, SrUGT85C2, SrUGT74G1, and SrUGT76G1 reduced steviol glycoside content by 36–63% and increased gibberellin (GA3) content by 8–34% in Stevia rebaudiana.
mechanism: Downregulation of these genes redirected carbon flux from steviol glycoside biosynthesis to gibberellin accumulation, with SrUGT76G1 showing highest substrate affinity for 19-O-β-glucopyranosyl steviol and rubusoside.

genes: ASAL (Allium sativum lectin, garlic lectin, Allium sativum), BAR (phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, herbicide resistance, Agrobacterium sp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of ASAL and BAR in cotton confers Basta herbicide tolerance and resistance to jassid and whitefly pests with 55-77% reduced nymph survival and 36-57% reduced fecundity
mechanism: ASAL disrupts insect midgut epithelial cells through glycan-mediated interactions with cadherin-like proteins, polycalins, and other midgut components, causing gut lumen closure and metabolic disruption

genes: IDD14 (IDD14, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Introduction of p35S::anti-IDD14 into cuf1-D restored the cuf1-D to WT morphology.
mechanism: NA

genes: IDD14 (IDD14, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants overexpressing IDD14 fully recapitulated the phenotype of cuf1-D, including smaller and down-curling leaves.
mechanism: NA

genes: IDD15 (IDD15, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of IDD15 resulted in a similar leaf phenotype as observed in idd14-1D.
mechanism: NA

genes: IDD16 (IDD16, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of IDD16 resulted in a similar leaf phenotype as observed in idd14-1D.

mechanism: PME activity demethylates pectin, producing methanol which disrupts insect feeding and reproduction. Transgenic plants emit ~12.61-fold higher methanol through stomata, deterring insect herbivores.

mechanism: SDG8i encodes a glucosyltransferase that glycosylates the strigolactone analogue GR24 in vitro, suggesting it affects strigolactone signaling pathways. This activity may reduce strigolactone levels, alter auxin homeostasis, and inhibit stress-related senescence programs.

mechanism: VvUGT72B1 catalyzes glucosylation of xenobiotics, converting them into less toxic glucosides which are either sequestered in vacuoles, bound to cell wall components, or exported to surrounding media as part of phase-II detoxification.

mechanism: Root-specific ZmCKX1 overexpression reduces CK levels in roots, promoting root growth while maintaining CK homeostasis in aerial parts. Feedback regulation upregulates HvIPT2 and downregulates HvCKX1/9 to compensate for CK deficiency.
