mechanism: SO overexpression upregulates AGO1, a component of the miRNA pathway, which may affect plant growth and viral infection resistance.

genes: amiRSO (artificial miRNA targeting SO, Hibiscus cannabinus, synthetic)
phenotype: Silencing of SO reduces AGO1 transcript levels in Hibiscus cannabinus.
mechanism: amiRSO-mediated silencing of SO downregulates AGO1, affecting the miRNA pathway and plant growth.

genes: JcLEA (JcLEA, LEA protein from Jatropha curcas, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcLEA enhances drought and salt tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with increased survival rates and improved physiological indices.
mechanism: JcLEA prevents water loss, maintains plasma membrane integrity, and regulates Na+ transport to maintain ionic balance.

genes: JcLEA-GFP (JcLEA, LEA protein from Jatropha curcas, Jatropha curcas; GFP, green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: JcLEA-GFP fusion protein is localized to the cytosol and nucleus in tobacco leaf cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsNRAMP3 (OsNRAMP3, plasma membrane-localized Mn transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNRAMP3-GFP in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts localizes the protein to the plasma membrane.
mechanism: OsNRAMP3 is a plasma membrane-localized protein that functions as a Mn-influx transporter.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under the OsNRAMP3 promoter in rice tissues is specific to vascular bundles, including phloem cells and companion cells.
mechanism: OsNRAMP3 is expressed in vascular bundles, particularly in phloem cells and companion cells, indicating its role in Mn translocation.

genes: hipI-SOD (high-isoelectric-point superoxide dismutase, Populus trichocarpa, source)
phenotype: Transgenic plants have higher levels of O2- than wild-type counterparts and impaired growth rates with compressed/disorganized cell structures in the cambial region of the stem
mechanism: Overproduction of O2- in the cambial region causes oxidative stress, leading to histological and morphological perturbations in plant development

genes: FcFT1 (name, FT-like gene, Ficus carica)
phenotype: Transgenic lines bloom approximately 17 days earlier than wild type, with fewer leaves per plant and shorter plant height.
mechanism: FcFT1 has a flower promoting function similar to that of FT genes in Arabidopsis and other plants.

genes: FcFT1 (name, FT-like gene, Ficus carica)
phenotype: Transgenic lines bloom approximately 23 days earlier than wild type, with fewer leaves per plant and shorter plant height.
mechanism: FcFT1 has a flower promoting function similar to that of FT genes in Arabidopsis and other plants.

genes: NsCBTS2a (cembratrien-ol synthase, Nicotiana sylvestris)
phenotype: Overexpression of NsCBTS2a leads to accumulation of cembratrien-ol (CBT-ol) in N. benthamiana leaves, with maximum yields reaching 2500 ng/cm² when co-expressed with SlDXS2 and NtGGPPS2.
mechanism: CBTS2a catalyzes the cyclization of geranylgeranyl diphosphate (GGPP) to α- and β-CBT-ol. Co-expression of DXS2 and GGPPS2 increases GGPP availability, enhancing CBT-ol production.

genes: RcCS (casbene synthase, Ricinus communis)
phenotype: Overexpression of RcCS leads to accumulation of casbene in N. benthamiana leaves, with yields up to 227 ng/cm².
mechanism: RcCS catalyzes the cyclization of GGPP to casbene, a diterpene phytoalexin with antifungal activity.

genes: GbLS (levopimaradiene synthase, Ginkgo biloba)
phenotype: Overexpression of GbLS leads to accumulation of levopimaradiene in N. benthamiana leaves, with yields rarely exceeding 100 ng/cm².
mechanism: GbLS catalyzes the formation of levopimaradiene, a precursor of pharmaceutically important ginkgolides.

genes: p19 (viral-encoded protein, Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Co-expression of p19 with target genes suppresses post-transcriptional gene silencing, enabling high levels of transient protein expression in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: p19 inhibits RNA interference pathways, preventing degradation of transgene mRNA and allowing sustained protein accumulation.

genes: AtCGS (Arabidopsis thaliana, feedback-sensitive full-length form, F-AtCGS)
phenotype: Overexpression of F-AtCGS reduces soluble methionine levels in tobacco seeds.
mechanism: F-AtCGS is feedback-sensitive to high levels of methionine/SAM, leading to reduced soluble methionine despite increased flux through synthesis.

genes: AtCGS (Arabidopsis thaliana, feedback-insensitive truncated form, T-AtCGS)
phenotype: Overexpression of T-AtCGS increases protein-incorporated methionine by up to 60% in tobacco seeds.
mechanism: T-AtCGS bypasses feedback inhibition, increasing flux through methionine synthesis and incorporation into storage proteins.

genes: TcNPR3 (Theobroma cacao NPR3 gene, negative regulator of defense response, Theobroma cacao)
phenotype: Overexpression of TcNPR3 partially restores the Arabidopsis npr3-3 mutant's pathogen resistance phenotype (immature flowers susceptible to bacterial infection).
mechanism: TcNPR3 acts as a negative regulator of the defense response by enhancing NPR1 degradation, similar to Arabidopsis NPR3.

genes: At4g29140 (ADP1, auxin biosynthesis regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ADP1 increases first-order rosette branch number by ~2-3 fold and accelerates leaf emergence rate in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ADP1 overexpression reduces auxin biosynthesis by downregulating YUCCA genes, leading to decreased auxin levels in meristematic regions and enhanced shoot branching.

genes: iaaM (bacterial indoleacetic acid-tryptophan monooxygenase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: ProADP1:iaaM transgenic plants show reduced first-order rosette branch number and epinastic leaves in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Domain-specific iaaM overexpression increases auxin levels in ADP1 expression domains, restoring apical dominance but not fully rescuing developmental defects from adp1-D.

genes: At5g19700 (ADP1 homolog, auxin biosynthesis regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana), At2g38510 (ADP1 homolog, auxin biosynthesis regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana), At5g52050 (ADP1 homolog, auxin biosynthesis regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ADP1 homologs recapitulates adp1-D phenotypes including increased first-order rosette branch number and accelerated leaf emergence in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of eGFP in Nicotiana tabacum results in visible fluorescence.
mechanism: NA

genes: SG1 (At5g11470, protein with BAH and RRM domains involved in chromatin modification, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: sg1 mutants exhibit stochastic growth defects, abnormally shaped organs (including flowers and leaves), and sterility with increasing severity across generations.
mechanism: SG1 functions in protection of genes from H3K9me2 and CHG DNA methylation, similar to IBM1.

genes: IBM1-L (At?, histone demethylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of sg1-1 and ibm1-1 mutants with IBM1-L restores wild-type phenotype.
mechanism: IBM1-L complements the compromised function of IBM1 in sg1 mutants, indicating SG1 and IBM1 act in the same pathway.

genes: AtEXP2 (AtEXP2, expansin gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtEXP2 accelerates seed germination in Arabidopsis thaliana, with 35S:AtEXP2 seeds germinating earlier than wild type by the second day.
mechanism: AtEXP2 promotes seed germination through GA signaling by weakening cell walls in endosperm and related structures during germination.

genes: GUS (GUS, β-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: The pAtEXP2:GUS transgenic line shows GUS staining in germinating seeds, confirming AtEXP2 promoter activity during seed imbibition and radicle development.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtMYB14 (AtMYB14, R2R3-MYB domain protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knockdown of AtMYB14 increased freezing tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with a survival rate of 87% compared to 71% in wild-type plants.
mechanism: AtMYB14 knockdown upregulates CBF genes and their downstream targets (KIN1, COR15A, COR47, RD29A), enhancing cold tolerance.

genes: AtMYB14 (AtMYB14, R2R3-MYB domain protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ProAtMYB14::GUS transgenic plants showed decreased GUS activity under cold treatment, confirming AtMYB14 down-regulation by low temperature.
mechanism: NA

genes: GAL2 (Glycine max Agamous Like 2, MADS box gene involved in flowering and organ development, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GAL2 promotes flowering in Arabidopsis, leading to earlier flowering and reduced leaf count. Transgenic plants show smaller leaves, curled upward, smaller flowers with exposed filaments, and shorter siliques with persistent petals.
mechanism: GAL2 upregulates flowering genes (FT, CO, SOC1, AP1, LFY) and downregulates FLC. It also affects leaf and flower morphology through photoperiod-dependent mechanisms.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GUS increases enzymatic activity in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves, with activity levels up to 75% of TMV vectors when co-infiltrated with P19.
mechanism: The CaMV35S promoter drives high-level expression of the GUS reporter gene, while the Nos terminator ensures proper transcription termination.

genes: GFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP increases fluorescence in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves, with fluorescence levels significantly enhanced by co-infiltration of P19.
mechanism: The CaMV35S promoter drives high-level expression of the GFP reporter gene, while the CaMV terminator and ribozyme (Rz) ensure proper transcription termination and RNA processing. RNA-silencing suppression by P19 further enhances expression.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GUS increases enzymatic activity in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves, with activity levels significantly enhanced by co-infiltration of P19.
mechanism: The CaMV35S promoter drives high-level expression of the GUS reporter gene, while the CaMV terminator and ribozyme (Rz) ensure proper transcription termination and RNA processing. RNA-silencing suppression by P19 further enhances expression.

genes: TIFY8 (TIFY8, full-length TIFY8, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: TIFY8 overexpression affects primary root growth, with reduced root growth in transgenic lines under control conditions.
mechanism: TIFY8 acts as a transcriptional repressor by recruiting TOPLESS (TPL) via NINJA, forming a repression complex.

genes: TIFY8 (TIFY8, full-length TIFY8, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: TIFY8 overexpression affects primary root growth, with reduced root growth in transgenic lines under control conditions.
mechanism: TIFY8 acts as a transcriptional repressor by recruiting TOPLESS (TPL) via NINJA, forming a repression complex.

genes: GUS-GFP (GUS-GFP, β-glucuronidase fused to GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: TIFY8 promoter drives expression in cotyledons, young true leaves, shoot apical meristem, root tip, and lateral roots, with expression patterns opposite to JAZ1.
mechanism: NA

genes: TIFY8 (TIFY8, full-length TIFY8, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: TIFY8 acts as a transcriptional repressor in transient expression assays, reducing basal expression of a GAL4-driven reporter gene.
mechanism: TIFY8 recruits TOPLESS (TPL) via NINJA to repress gene expression, similar to JAZ proteins.

genes: TaNAC67 (TaNAC67, stress-responsive NAC transcription factor, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaNAC67 in Arabidopsis thaliana enhances drought, salt, and freezing stress tolerance, with transgenic plants showing higher survival rates (40–65% vs. 12–18% for controls) under stress conditions.
mechanism: TaNAC67 upregulates abiotic stress-responsive genes (DREB2A, COR15, ABI1, ABI2) and enhances photosynthetic potential (Fv/Fm ratios), water retention (higher water potential), and ion homeostasis (Na+ efflux).

genes: CmPT1 (Phosphate Transporter 1, high-affinity phosphate transporter, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Under both Pi sufficient and deficient conditions, transgenic plants constitutively expressing CmPT1 grew taller than the non-transformed wild type, produced a greater volume of roots, accumulated more biomass and took up more phosphate.
mechanism: CmPT1 encodes a typical, root-expressed, high affinity phosphate transporter, plays an important role in coping Pi deficiency of chrysanthemum plants.

genes: BnaCBL1 (BnaCBL1, subcellular localization reporter, Brassica napus), BnaCBL9 (BnaCBL9, subcellular localization reporter, Brassica napus), BnaCBL10 (BnaCBL10, subcellular localization reporter, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK3 (BnaCIPK3, subcellular localization reporter, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK10 (BnaCIPK10, subcellular localization reporter, Brassica napus)
phenotype: BnaCBL1 localized to nuclei and plasma membranes; BnaCBL9 in cytoplasm and nuclei; BnaCBL10 in vacuolar membrane; BnaCIPK3 and BnaCIPK10 in cytoplasm and nuclei
mechanism: GFP fusion for subcellular localization analysis

genes: BnaCBL1 (BnaCBL1, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCBL2 (BnaCBL2, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCBL3 (BnaCBL3, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCBL4 (BnaCBL4, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCBL9 (BnaCBL9, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCBL10 (BnaCBL10, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK1 (BnaCIPK1, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK3 (BnaCIPK3, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK5 (BnaCIPK5, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK6 (BnaCIPK6, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK7 (BnaCIPK7, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK9 (BnaCIPK9, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK10 (BnaCIPK10, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK11 (BnaCIPK11, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK12 (BnaCIPK12, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK15 (BnaCIPK15, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK17 (BnaCIPK17, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK24 (BnaCIPK24, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK25 (BnaCIPK25, interaction study, Brassica napus), BnaCIPK26 (BnaCIPK26, interaction study, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Interactions between BnaCBLs and BnaCIPKs confirmed via yeast two-hybrid and BiFC assays
mechanism: Yeast two-hybrid and bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) for interaction validation

genes: BnaCIPK24 (BnaCIPK24, functional complementation, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Complementation of Arabidopsis sos2-1 mutant restored salt tolerance
mechanism: BnaCIPK24 substitutes for AtCIPK24/SOS2 in Na+ extrusion pathway

genes: SoyFERH1 (soybean ferritin, storage protein, Glycine max L. cv PHI29924), SoyFERH2 (soybean ferritin, storage protein, Glycine max L. cv PHI29924), OsFER1C (rice ferritin, storage protein, Oryza sativa cv Nipponbare), OsFER2C (rice ferritin, storage protein, Oryza sativa cv Nipponbare)
phenotype: Overexpression of ferritin genes increases iron concentration in polished seeds by up to 3.4-fold compared to non-transgenic IR64, with maximum Fe concentration of 7.6 mg kg⁻¹ in GLUB4::SoyFERH1 (single transformation) and 5.9 mg kg⁻¹ in GLUB4::SoyFERH1 (co-transformation).
mechanism: Ferritin proteins store iron in the endosperm, increasing iron concentration in seeds. Expression of ferritin genes upregulates iron homeostasis genes (e.g., NAS2, NAS3, YSL15, YSL18) to enhance iron transport to the seed.

genes: GmCOL2 (GmCOL2, CO ortholog, soybean), GmCOL5 (GmCOL5, CO ortholog, soybean)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmCOL2 did not rescue the flowering phenotype of the Arabidopsis co mutant. Over-expression of GmCOL5 rescued the co mutant phenotype.
mechanism: GmCOL5 functions as a CO ortholog to regulate flowering time through the CO-FT regulon.

genes: StGSL1 (Gibberellin Stimulated-Like 1, potato), StGSL2 (Gibberellin Stimulated-Like 2, potato)
phenotype: Antisense knock-down of GSL1 and GSL2 failed to recover viable plants, indicating essential roles for these genes in potato development.
mechanism: NA

genes: StGSL2 (Gibberellin Stimulated-Like 2, potato)
phenotype: Antisense knock-down of GSL1 and GSL2 failed to recover viable plants, indicating essential roles for these genes in potato development.
mechanism: NA

genes: PfPDS (phytoene desaturase, carotenoid biosynthesis, Physalis floridana)
phenotype: Silencing of PfPDS causes systemic bleaching in leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds due to disrupted carotenoid biosynthesis.
mechanism: PfPDS encodes phytoene desaturase, a key enzyme in the carotenoid biosynthetic pathway. Its knockdown prevents carotenoid production, leading to bleaching.

genes: MPF2 (MADS-box transcription factor, floral development, Physalis floridana)
phenotype: MPF2 knockdown causes reduced pollen maturation, altered calyx cell size, and short pedicels in Physalis.
mechanism: MPF2 regulates floral development and pedicel growth. Its silencing disrupts cell elongation and pollen maturation.

genes: MPF3 (MADS-box transcription factor, floral development, Physalis floridana)
phenotype: MPF3 knockdown results in leaf-like calyx, elongated pedicels, and deformed inferior calyx (ICS) in Physalis.
mechanism: MPF3 controls pedicel elongation and floral organ identity. Its silencing disrupts cell elongation and organ morphology.

genes: AmTEM (Antirrhinum majus TEMPRANILLO, Antirrhinum majus, cDNA)
phenotype: Overexpression of AmTEM in Arabidopsis tem1 mutant results in delayed flowering (54.6 ± 1.8 rosette leaves vs. 32.4 ± 0.9 in tem1 mutant) and prolonged juvenility (JVP extended by ~5 days).
mechanism: AmTEM represses AtFT and AtCO mRNA expression during early development, extending the JVP and delaying flowering.

genes: RcCb5-2 (castor cytochrome b5 isoform 2, highly expressed in developing endosperm, Ricinus communis), RcCb5-3 (castor cytochrome b5 isoform 3, highly expressed in developing endosperm, Ricinus communis), RcCb5-4 (castor cytochrome b5 isoform 4, highly expressed in developing endosperm, Ricinus communis)
phenotype: No significant increase in total hydroxy fatty acid (HFA) levels (18:1-OH + 18:2-OH) in T2 seeds compared to untransformed CL37 plants (mean 19.5% HFA, P=0.5979 for RcCb5-2; 18.3% HFA, P=0.2155 for RcCb5-3; 18.6% HFA, P=0.2470 for RcCb5-4).
mechanism: RcCb5 proteins are predicted to localize to the endoplasmic reticulum and provide electrons to RcFAH12 hydroxylase for fatty acid hydroxylation. Overexpression of RcCb5 isoforms was hypothesized to increase electron supply to RcFAH12.

genes: RcCBR1 (castor cytochrome b5 reductase, Ricinus communis), RcCb5-2 (castor cytochrome b5 isoform 2, Ricinus communis), RcCb5-3 (castor cytochrome b5 isoform 3, Ricinus communis), RcCb5-4 (castor cytochrome b5 isoform 4, Ricinus communis)
phenotype: No significant increase in total HFA levels in T2 seeds compared to untransformed CL37 plants (mean 18.4% HFA, P=0.6820 for RcCBR1+RcCb5-2; 18.5% HFA, P=0.6834 for RcCBR1+RcCb5-3; 17.4% HFA, P=0.0898 for RcCBR1+RcCb5-4).
mechanism: Coexpression of RcCBR1 (electron donor) and RcCb5 isoforms (electron carriers) was hypothesized to reconstitute a complete electron transport chain to RcFAH12 hydroxylase for enhanced fatty acid hydroxylation.

genes: AtCBR1 (Arabidopsis cytochrome b5 reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: No significant change in total HFA levels in T2 seeds compared to untransformed CL37 plants (Supplementary Figure 1).
mechanism: Overexpression of AtCBR1 was hypothesized to increase reductant supply to endogenous AtCb5 proteins for enhanced RcFAH12 hydroxylase activity.

genes: OsARF6 (OsARF6, mutated in Domain IV, rice), OsARF12 (OsARF12, mutated in Domain IV, rice), OsARF16 (OsARF16, mutated in Domain IV, rice), OsARF17 (OsARF17, mutated in Domain IV, rice), OsARF25 (OsARF25, mutated in Domain IV, rice)
phenotype: Overexpression of mutated OsARF(WS)s partially rescues shoot length, root length, and crown root number defects in Osiaa23-3 mutant rice. OsARF12(WS) fully rescues root length, while OsARF25(WS) reduces root growth.
mechanism: Mutated OsARFs (WS) in Domain IV are released from Osiaa23 inhibition, maintaining transcriptional activity and rescuing developmental defects.

genes: PtSOS2.1 (salt tolerance, Populus trichocarpa), PtSOS2.2 (salt tolerance, Populus trichocarpa), PtSOS2.3 (salt tolerance, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtSOS2.1 increases salt tolerance in Populus trichocarpa, with 80% survival under moderate salt stress (51 mM NaCl) and 60% under severe stress (120 mM NaCl). Transgenic lines show reduced water loss (5.08-12.16% vs 24.88% in controls) and higher proline accumulation.
mechanism: PtSOS2.1 encodes a serine/threonine protein kinase with a conserved FISL motif that interacts with calcineurin B-like Ca2+ binding proteins in the Ca2+ signaling pathway. Overexpression enhances osmotic adjustment (proline accumulation, reduced water loss) and activates antioxidant enzymes (SOD, POD, CAT) to mitigate oxidative damage under salt stress.

genes: PtSOS2.1 (salt tolerance, Populus trichocarpa), PtSOS2.2 (salt tolerance, Populus trichocarpa), PtSOS2.3 (salt tolerance, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtSOS2.2 increases salt tolerance in Populus trichocarpa, with 80% survival under moderate salt stress (51 mM NaCl) and 60% under severe stress (120 mM NaCl). Transgenic lines show reduced water loss (5.08-12.16% vs 24.88% in controls) and higher proline accumulation.
mechanism: PtSOS2.2 encodes a serine/threonine protein kinase with a conserved FISL motif that interacts with calcineurin B-like Ca2+ binding proteins in the Ca2+ signaling pathway. Overexpression enhances osmotic adjustment (proline accumulation, reduced water loss) and activates antioxidant enzymes (SOD, POD, CAT) to mitigate oxidative damage under salt stress.

genes: PtSOS2.1 (salt tolerance, Populus trichocarpa), PtSOS2.2 (salt tolerance, Populus trichocarpa), PtSOS2.3 (salt tolerance, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtSOS2.3 increases salt tolerance in Populus trichocarpa, with 75% survival under moderate salt stress (51 mM NaCl) and 50% under severe stress (120 mM NaCl). Transgenic lines show reduced water loss (5.08-12.16% vs 24.88% in controls) and higher proline accumulation.
mechanism: PtSOS2.3 encodes a serine/threonine protein kinase with a conserved FISL motif that interacts with calcineurin B-like Ca2+ binding proteins in the Ca2+ signaling pathway. Overexpression enhances osmotic adjustment (proline accumulation, reduced water loss) and activates antioxidant enzymes (SOD, POD, CAT) to mitigate oxidative damage under salt stress.

genes: HSI2 (Arabidopsis thaliana, transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HSI2 increases drought sensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana, with earlier wilting onset and reduced recovery compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: HSI2 acts as a negative regulator of drought tolerance by reducing transpirational water loss through lower stomatal conductance and altered ABA metabolism.

genes: AT1G21600 (plastid-encoded RNA polymerase complex subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana), AK102323 (similar to AT1G21600, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of AT1G21600 in OsFOX line K06951 causes dark green rosette leaves and altered leaf coloration in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AT1G21600 is a subunit of the plastid-encoded RNA polymerase complex (PTAC6/PAP8), suggesting its role in chloroplast RNA processing and leaf pigmentation.

genes: AT5G56980 (unknown protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), AF385692 (similar to AT5G56980, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AT5G56980 in F21325 line causes abnormal rosette leaf morphology in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AT5G56980 is a pathogen-associated molecular pattern-induced gene responsive to jasmonic acid (JA) and wounding, suggesting its role in stress response pathways.

genes: ONI3 (Oryza sativa, putative ω-alcohol dehydrogenase)
phenotype: Complementation of oni3-6 mutant callus with wild-type ONI3 genomic fragment rescues shoot development, resulting in normal shoot regeneration with wild-type morphology.
mechanism: ONI3 encodes a putative ω-alcohol dehydrogenase necessary for shoot development in rice. The gene is specifically expressed in the outermost cell layer of shoot apex and young leaves, and its function is essential for organ separation and normal epidermal development.

genes: UGT74D1 (UDP-glucosyltransferase 74D1, OxIAA glucosyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Induction of UGT74D1 reduces root gravitropism in Arabidopsis seedlings by glucosylating OxIAA to OxIAA-Glc, which lowers auxin levels. Root gravitropism is recovered by exogenous IAA supplementation.
mechanism: UGT74D1 catalyzes OxIAA glucosylation to OxIAA-Glc, reducing free auxin levels. This decreases auxin availability for gravitropic response pathways.

genes: CdICE1-GFP (bHLH transcription factor involved in freezing tolerance, Chrysanthemum dichrum)
phenotype: CdICE1-GFP localizes predominantly to the nucleus in onion epidermal cells
mechanism: CdICE1 binds to MYC elements in the CdDREBa promoter and activates transcription

genes: CdICE1 (bHLH transcription factor involved in freezing tolerance, Chrysanthemum dichrum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CdICE1 enhances freezing tolerance in Arabidopsis after acclimation at 4°C or 16°C
mechanism: CdICE1 activates CBFs and downstream genes (COR15a, COR6.6, RD29a) involved in freezing tolerance, and reduces miR398 levels to upregulate CSD1 and CSD2

genes: PcGA2ox (GA2ox1, gibberellin 2-oxidase, Phaseolus coccineus)
phenotype: Overexpression of PcGA2ox in poplar accelerates growth inhibition under drought and SD photoperiods, increases branching, and delays leaf senescence.
mechanism: GA2ox overexpression reduces bioactive GA levels, leading to increased DELLA protein accumulation, which represses growth and enhances stress resistance via ROS detoxification, carotenoid production, and ABA biosynthesis.

genes: gai (DELLA domain protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of gai in poplar accelerates growth inhibition under drought and SD photoperiods, causes semidwarfism, and delays leaf senescence.
mechanism: gai overexpression (a truncated DELLA protein) constitutively represses GA signaling, leading to growth inhibition and enhanced stress resistance via ROS detoxification, carotenoid production, and ABA biosynthesis.

genes: rgl1 (DELLA domain protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of rgl1 in poplar accelerates growth inhibition under drought and SD photoperiods, causes semidwarfism, and delays leaf senescence.
mechanism: rgl1 overexpression (a truncated DELLA protein) constitutively represses GA signaling, leading to growth inhibition and enhanced stress resistance via ROS detoxification, carotenoid production, and ABA biosynthesis.

genes: DR5 (auxin response element, synthetic)
phenotype: DR5 activity is increased at the illuminated side of roots exposed to unilateral blue light, revealing asymmetric auxin distribution.
mechanism: DR5 activity reflects auxin distribution, which is regulated by PIN1-mediated polar auxin transport during root negative phototropism.

genes: PIN1 (auxin efflux carrier, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PIN1-GFP relocalizes to the basal plasma membrane upon blue light illumination, enabling acropetal auxin transport to the root tip during root negative phototropism.
mechanism: Blue light induces PIN1 redistribution via a BFA-sensitive, GNOM-dependent trafficking pathway regulated by PID/PP2A antagonism, directing auxin flow to the root tip.

genes: GNOM (vesicle trafficking regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GNOMM696L rescues BFA-sensitive PIN1 redistribution and root negative phototropic response in the presence of BFA.
mechanism: GNOMM696L is a BFA-resistant version of GNOM that mediates PIN1 trafficking to the plasma membrane, enabling blue-light-induced PIN1 redistribution.

genes: PID (serine/threonine kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Pro35S:PID seedlings exhibit apical plasma membrane localization of PIN1-GFP and severe defects in root negative phototropism.
mechanism: PID overexpression disrupts the antagonistic PID/PP2A regulation of PIN1 polarity, leading to apical PIN1 localization and impaired auxin redistribution.

genes: BdCBF1 (transcription factor involved in cold, drought, and salt stress tolerance, Brachypodium distachyon)
phenotype: Overexpression of BdCBF1 increases tolerance to cold, drought, and salt stresses in Brachypodium distachyon and Arabidopsis thaliana by elevating proline and soluble sugar accumulation and upregulating stress-responsive genes like COR15A, COR414, and GolS3.
mechanism: BdCBF1 enhances stress tolerance by upregulating cold-responsive genes such as COR15A, COR414, and GolS3, and increasing proline and soluble sugar accumulation.

genes: ALS1 (Acetolactate synthase 1, catalytic subunit of branched-chain amino acid biosynthesis, tomato), ALS2 (Acetolactate synthase 2, catalytic subunit of branched-chain amino acid biosynthesis, tomato)
phenotype: Simultaneous silencing of ALS1 and ALS2 in NIL-Ol-1 increases susceptibility to Oidium neolycopersici by ~3-fold compared to control plants.
mechanism: ALS-induced amino acid homeostasis is important for Ol-1-mediated resistance to powdery mildew.

genes: ALS1 (Acetolactate synthase 1, catalytic subunit of branched-chain amino acid biosynthesis, tomato)
phenotype: Individual silencing of ALS1 in NIL-Ol-1 does not compromise resistance to Oidium neolycopersici.

phenotype: DefH9-iaaM transgenic plants show 180% increased fruit yield in cultivated strawberry, 140% in wild strawberry, and 100% in raspberry. mechanism: CAD down-regulation activates compensatory mechanisms leading to cellulose and pectin accumulation, which improves fiber strength but reduces pathogen resistance. FT-IR analysis shows altered lignin structure and reduced hydrogen bonding in cellulose.

genes: bar (bar gene, herbicide resistance marker, synthetic), BjNPR1 (BjNPR1, non-expressor of pathogenesis-related genes 1, Brassica juncea),
phenotype: Overexpression of BjNPR1 confers resistance to downy mildew (Sclerospora graminicola) in Pennisetum glaucum, with 91-95% resistant plants in transgenic lines compared to 87-100% infected in untransformed controls. Transgenic plants also exhibit herbicide Basta tolerance.
mechanism: BjNPR1 activates salicylic acid (SA)-mediated systemic acquired resistance (SAR) pathway, enhancing expression of pathogenesis-related genes (PR1) and UDP-glucose salicylic acid glucosyl transferase (SAGT). Transgenic plants show 8.16-10.41× higher PR1 transcript levels post-infection compared to untransformed plants.

genes: BjNPR1 (BjNPR1, non-expressor of pathogenesis-related genes 1, Brassica juncea),

mechanism: SA treatment induces nuclear translocation of BjNPR1-GFP, suggesting NPR1 protein activation of defense signaling pathways. This mimics Arabidopsis NPR1's nuclear translocation role in SA-mediated resistance.

mechanism: CaMSRB2 reduces oxidized methionine residues in target proteins like porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD), preserving chlorophyll synthesis and photosystem function during drought stress.

mechanism: hGAD65's enzymatic activity suppresses its own synthesis, whereas the inactive hGAD65mut escapes this feedback.

genes: SlFYFL (full-length cDNA of SlFYFL, cloned from tomato, Solanum lycopersicon)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlFYFL delays leaf and sepal senescence, fruit ripening, and abscission zone development in tomato. Transgenic fruits show 30-40% lower carotenoid accumulation, 30-60% reduced ethylene production, and delayed AZ cell separation by ~7 days compared to wild type.
mechanism: SlFYFL inhibits ethylene biosynthesis by downregulating ACO1, ACO3, ACS1A, ACS2, and ACS6 (30-80% lower expression). It also downregulates ripening-related genes like E4, E8, PSY1, PDS, ZDS, and SlMADS-RIN (30-80% lower expression). SlFYFL interacts with SlMADS-RIN, SlMADS1, and SlJOINTLESS in yeast two-hybrid assays, suggesting protein complex formation to regulate abscission and ripening.

genes: MIR159a (miR159a variant, miRNA, synthetic), MYB33 (GAMYB-like transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), MYB65 (GAMYB-like transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of mir159ab mutant phenotypes (leaf curliness and dwarfed stature) when transformed with MIR159a0, MIR159a1, or MIR159a2 variants. MIR159a3 and MIR159a4 variants failed to complement.
mechanism: miR159a variants with up to two central mismatches mediate cleavage of MYB33/MYB65 transcripts, maintaining silencing efficacy despite mismatches. Non-cleavage mechanisms also contribute to silencing when cleavage is attenuated.

genes: MYB33 (GAMYB-like transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Central mismatches in MYB33 variants attenuate miR159-guided cleavage. Non-cleavage mechanisms partially repress MYB33-1 cm transcripts, but silencing is less effective than in wild-type MYB33.

genes: MYB33 (GAMYB-like transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: MYB33-2 cm transgenic plants showed severe developmental defects (curled leaves, smaller rosette) compared to wild-type MYB33, indicating poor miR159 silencing with two central mismatches.
mechanism: Two central mismatches in MYB33-2 cm further reduce miR159 cleavage efficiency. Non-cleavage mechanisms partially compensate but fail to fully repress MYB33-2 cm transcripts.

genes: MYB33 (GAMYB-like transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Flanking nucleotide mutations in MYB33-FM disrupt miR159 recognition and cleavage efficiency. Non-cleavage mechanisms are insufficient to fully repress MYB33-FM transcripts.

genes: MYB33 (GAMYB-like transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)

mechanism: Two central mismatches in MYB33-2 cm severely attenuate cleavage. Non-cleavage mechanisms partially repress MYB33-2 cm but fail to fully suppress GUS activity.

mechanism: NA

genes: APUM5 (APUM5, Pumilio RNA binding protein 5, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: APUM5 promoter contains ABA response elements and MYB recognition elements, indicating its role in abiotic stress response.

mechanism: AtCHR23-mediated chromatin remodeling increases variability of gene expression in stress-associated genes, reducing growth robustness.

genes: AtCHR23 (SWI/SNF2-type ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: AtCHR23 (SWI/SNF2-type ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: AtCHR23-mediated chromatin remodeling increases variability of gene expression in stress-associated genes, reducing growth robustness.

genes: ATHB17 (transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana), CAT (chloramphenicol acetyltransferase, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of ATHB17 represses GUS reporter gene expression in Arabidopsis protoplasts; CAT serves as a negative control for DNA binding activity.
mechanism: ATHB17 contains an EAR-like motif (L84A L86A) required for transcriptional repression. ATHB17 binds DNA via homeodomain and leucine zipper motifs, and forms homodimers.

genes: ATHB17 (transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of ATHB17 in maize results in a truncated protein (ATHB17Δ113) lacking the repression domain. This leads to increased ear weight at silking (R1 stage) without altering vegetative biomass.
mechanism: ATHB17Δ113 forms homodimers and heterodimers with maize HD-Zip II proteins, acting as a dominant-negative regulator by sequestering endogenous repressors and competing for DNA binding sites.

genes: ATHB17 (transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Deletion of the first 73 amino acids of ATHB17 eliminates cytoplasmic localization, resulting in exclusive nuclear localization in Arabidopsis protoplasts.
mechanism: The N-terminal extension of ATHB17 contains putative transmembrane domains that tether the protein to the cytoplasm. Deletion of this region removes the cytoplasmic retention signal.

genes: ATHB17 (transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Full-length ATHB17 localizes to both nucleus and cytosol in Arabidopsis protoplasts, while ATHB17Δ73 variant localizes exclusively to the nucleus.
mechanism: ATHB17 contains a nuclear localization signal (NLS) at amino acids 136-142. Mutation of arginine residues R138A and R142A disrupts nuclear retention.

genes: ATHB17Δ113 (truncated ATHB17, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ATHB17Δ113 increases ear weight at silking (R1 stage) in maize without altering vegetative biomass or developmental timing.
mechanism: ATHB17Δ113 lacks the repression domain but retains DNA binding and dimerization domains. It acts as a dominant-negative regulator by forming non-functional heterodimers with maize HD-Zip II proteins.

genes: CLV1 (CLAVATA1, receptor kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Translation efficiency of CLV1 5' leader is eIF3h-dependent; crTMV element has minimal IRES activity but promoter activity
mechanism: crTMV intergenic sequence acts as internal ribosome entry site; eIF3h-dependent translation of CLV1 leader confirmed via luciferase assays

genes: HDA6 (HDA6, histone deacetylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restoration of silencing at Group DL loci such as SDC and soloLTR in hda6-6 null mutants
mechanism: HDA6-F protein is functional and requires histone deacetylase activity for rescue

genes: NRPD1 (NRPD1, RNA polymerase IV subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restoration of silencing at Group DL and Group E loci in pol IV (nrpd1) null mutants
mechanism: Transgene expression of NRPD1 restores silencing by resetting histone acetylation and cytosine methylation

genes: NRPE1 (NRPE1, RNA polymerase V subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restoration of silencing at Group DL and Group E loci in pol V (nrpe1) null mutants
mechanism: Transgene expression of NRPE1 restores silencing by resetting histone acetylation and cytosine methylation

genes: PECT1 (phosphorylethanolamine N-methyltransferase 1, target of amiPECT1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: pFD::amiPECT1 transgenic lines showed a significantly early-flowering phenotype observed both by leaf number and days to flower.
mechanism: Elevated PC levels in the shoot apex promote flowering mainly through FT.

genes: PECT1 (phosphorylethanolamine N-methyltransferase 1, overexpressed, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Plants overexpressing PECT1 in the shoot apical meristems were late flowering compared with the wild type.
mechanism: PC levels at the shoot apical meristems are correlated with flowering time in a dose-dependent manner.

genes: FT (flowering locus T, overexpressed, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: pGAS1::FT ft-10 tsf-1 plants showed early flowering, and introduction of pFD::amiPECT1 further accelerated flowering time.
mechanism: Elevated PC levels in the shoot apex promote flowering mainly through FT.

genes: PRP8 (core splicing factor PRP8, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescue of prp8-6 mutant phenotype, restoring normal FLC repression and flowering time regulation.
mechanism: Complementation of the hypomorphic prp8-6 mutation by restoring PRP8 function.

genes: FLC (floral repressor gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased FLC transcription and delayed flowering due to disruption of COOLAIR splicing and polyadenylation.
mechanism: Disruption of COOLAIR splicing and polyadenylation by replacing the 3′ UTR of FLC with that of rbcs3B.

genes: FLC (floral repressor gene with mutated splice site, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased FLC expression and delayed flowering due to reduced splicing efficiency of the class Ii intron.
mechanism: Reduced splicing efficiency of the class Ii intron in COOLAIR, leading to altered poly(A) site usage and FLC derepression.

genes: HST (HST gene, chloroplast development, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HST rescues the pds2-1 mutant phenotype, restoring normal green coloration and chloroplast development in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HST is essential for pro-plastid growth, thylakoid membrane formation, and pigment accumulation. Overexpression restores chloroplast development and photosynthetic capacity.

genes: HST (HST gene, chloroplast development, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Anti-HST transgenic plants exhibit lighter green leaves, reduced chlorophyll levels, and partial rescue of mutant phenotype with exogenous GA3/ABA.
mechanism: Antisense suppression of HST reduces its expression, leading to impaired chloroplast development and pigment accumulation. GA3 and ABA partially restore growth and chloroplast function.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: HST pro::GUS transgenic plants show GUS activity in green tissues (leaves, stems) and reduced activity in senescent tissues, confirming HST promoter activity.
mechanism: The HST promoter drives GUS expression in green tissues, indicating HST is highly expressed in photosynthetic organs and during active growth phases.

genes: GhMPK17 (GhMPK17, stress response gene, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhMPK17 increases ABA-tolerance, salt stress tolerance, and osmotic stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with higher seed germination rates (83.5–87.5% vs 71.5% under 1 µM ABA), longer root elongation (20.2–21.6 mm vs 18.1 mm under 50 µM ABA), and improved cotyledon greening/expansion (61.2% vs 14.5% under 0.5 µM ABA).
mechanism: GhMPK17 enhances ABA signaling and stress response by altering H2O2 levels and upregulating stress-related genes (ABI1, ABF4, SOS2, RAB18).

genes: GhMPK17::eGFP (eGFP, fluorescent protein, synthetic; GhMPK17, stress response gene, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: GhMPK17-eGFP fusion protein localizes to the cytoplasm of Nicotiana tabacum epidermal cells, as observed by GFP fluorescence under confocal microscopy.
mechanism: Subcellular localization of GhMPK17 in the cytoplasm suggests its role in cytoplasmic signaling pathways related to stress response.

phenotype: Overexpression of GS1;1 and GS1;2 in rice leads to significant decreases in root length, plant height, root and shoot dry weight at tillering and heading stages, reduced yield at mature stage, and altered carbon/nitrogen metabolism with imbalanced soluble protein and carbohydrate concentrations.
mechanism: Overexpression of GS1;1 and GS1;2 disrupts carbon and nitrogen metabolic balance, leading to reduced biomass and yield due to imbalanced carbon/nitrogen ratios, altered soluble protein and carbohydrate distribution, and changes in gene expression profiles of nitrogen and carbon metabolic pathways.

mechanism: GhWRKY40 has nuclear localization signals

mechanism: GhWRKY40 interacts with GhMPK20, affecting defense gene expression

genes: LUC (luciferase, synthetic)

genes: BRI1 (Brassinosteroid receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BRI1 in nonhair cells reduces final cell length and root length in Arabidopsis thaliana, with enhanced sensitivity to brassinosteroids (BL) and BR biosynthesis inhibitors.
mechanism: BRI1 activity in nonhair cells elevates ethylene biosynthesis via ACS9 upregulation and activates ethylene signaling, leading to increased crystalline cellulose deposition and inhibition of unidirectional cell expansion.

genes: BRI1 (Brassinosteroid receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ubiquitous overexpression of BRI1 in pUBQ10-BRI1 lines does not exhibit the same root length reduction as pGL2-BRI1 lines, and is less sensitive to brassinosteroids (BL).
mechanism: NA

genes: BRI1 (Brassinosteroid receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: BRI1 activity in hair cells counteracts the inhibitory effects of nonhair cell BRI1 expression, promoting unidirectional cell expansion.

genes: BRI1 (Brassinosteroid receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Elevated ACC production in nonhair cells activates ethylene signaling, leading to increased crystalline cellulose deposition and inhibition of cell elongation.

genes: BES1-D (Dominant active form of BES1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BES1-D in nonhair cells (pGL2-BES1-D) results in high basal expression of ACS genes and short cortical cells, similar to pGL2-BRI1 lines.
mechanism: BES1-D mediates BRI1's effect on ACS gene upregulation and ethylene signaling, contributing to cell elongation inhibition.

genes: BRI1 (Brassinosteroid receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: BRI1 (Brassinosteroid receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Asparagine at position 23 enables cleavage by asparaginyl endoproteases, removing MEN- N-terminal sequence to generate LMW-s type subunit.

genes: 42K-N23T (low-molecular-weight glutenin subunit, wheat, mutated asparagine→threonine)
phenotype: Expression of 42K-N23T in durum wheat endosperm produces LMW-s type subunits with METSHIP N-terminal sequence
mechanism: Asparagine at position 23 enables cleavage by asparaginyl endoproteases, removing MEN- N-terminal sequence to generate LMW-s type subunit.

genes: FBP21 (FBP21, flowering time regulator, Petunia)

genes: FBP28 (FBP28, flowering time regulator, Petunia)

genes: CHS (CHALCONE SYNTHASE, petal pigment gene, Petunia)

mechanism: Xa21 encodes a receptor-like kinase that recognizes bacterial pathogens and activates defense signaling pathways
