genes: OsChl P (Oryza sativa, chlorophyll phytyl transferase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of the 502ys mutant rescues the yellow-green leaf phenotype and restores normal growth rates in rice.
mechanism: OsChl P catalyzes the reduction of ChlGG to ChlPhy, which is essential for chlorophyll biosynthesis and chloroplast development.

genes: AtDREB1A (dehydration-responsive element-binding protein 1A, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtDREB1A increases drought tolerance in Oryza sativa, with transgenic plants showing 60-69% spikelet fertility under drought stress compared to 29.5% in controls, and maintaining higher relative water content (RWC) and chlorophyll levels during stress.
mechanism: AtDREB1A enhances drought tolerance by regulating downstream genes in an abscisic acid (ABA)-independent pathway, including increased proline accumulation, reduced ion leakage, and maintenance of chlorophyll content and membrane integrity.

genes: Cry1Ab (Cry1Ab protein, Bacillus thuringiensis, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of Cry1Ab in MON810 corn reduces Diatraea saccharalis and Helicoverpa zea infestation by over 80% in stems and ears, respectively.
mechanism: Cry1Ab protein targets insect pests, causing mortality and reducing gallery formation in stems and ear damage.

genes: Cry1Ab/1Ac (hybrid Bt δ-endotoxin, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of Cry1Ab/1Ac in J. curcas leaves results in 80-100% mortality of A. micaceanus larvae at 4 days post-infestation.
mechanism: Cry1Ab/1Ac forms ion channels in insect gut cells, causing cellular lysis and larval death.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: CTU2:GUS fusion construct shows GUS activity in all tissues of Arabidopsis thaliana, including roots, hypocotyl, rosette leaves, cotyledons, siliques, flowers, and cauline leaves.
mechanism: NA

genes: CTU2 (cytoplasmic thiouridylase 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of ctu2-2 mutant restores tRNA thiolation and rescues wild-type-like lateral root formation and root hair development.
mechanism: CTU2 is essential for tRNA thiolation, which is required for proper root development and suppression of lrx1 root hair defects.

genes: WLm (conserved region of Watermelon silver mottle virus L gene, RdRp motifs, Watermelon silver mottle virus)
phenotype: Confers resistance to homologous WSMoV and broad-spectrum resistance to heterologous tospoviruses (TSWV, GRSV, INSV, GCFSV, WBNV, MYSV, TYRV, IYSV, CaCV) in transgenic N. benthamiana and tomato plants.
mechanism: RNA silencing (PTGS) mediated by siRNA accumulation targeting conserved RdRp motifs of tospovirus L genes.

genes: WLmt (non-translatable sense fragment of WSMoV L gene conserved region with in-frame termination codons, Watermelon silver mottle virus)
phenotype: Confers higher resistance (63.3%) to WSMoV and broad-spectrum resistance to heterologous tospoviruses compared to translatable constructs.
mechanism: RNA silencing (PTGS) mediated by siRNA accumulation targeting conserved RdRp motifs of tospovirus L genes.

genes: WLmts (non-translatable sense fragment of WSMoV L gene conserved region with frame-shifted termination codons, Watermelon silver mottle virus)
phenotype: Confers higher resistance (63.3%) to WSMoV and broad-spectrum resistance to heterologous tospoviruses compared to translatable constructs.
mechanism: RNA silencing (PTGS) mediated by siRNA accumulation targeting conserved RdRp motifs of tospovirus L genes.

genes: WLmA (antisense fragment of WSMoV L gene conserved region, Watermelon silver mottle virus)
phenotype: Confers higher resistance (66.7%) to WSMoV and broad-spectrum resistance to heterologous tospoviruses.
mechanism: RNA silencing (PTGS) mediated by siRNA accumulation targeting conserved RdRp motifs of tospovirus L genes.

genes: LUH (Leunig homolog, Arabidopsis thaliana), SLK1 (SEU-like 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), SLK2 (SEU-like 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: native promoter-LUH, native promoter-SLK1, native promoter-SLK2
phenotype: Complementation of salt tolerance phenotype in luh-4, slk1-1, and slk2-1 mutants, restoring wild-type root length and fresh weight under salt and osmotic stress.
mechanism: LUH recruits histone deacetylases (HDACs) to repress target genes via chromatin remodeling, while SLK1 and SLK2 act as adaptors to recruit LUH to DNA-bound transcription factors.

genes: Atgai (Arabidopsis gai gene, gain-of-function DELLA allele of AtGAI, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants exhibit a semi-dwarf phenotype and lower sensitivity to GA3, with shoot stature about one fourth that of wild-type plants.
mechanism: Atgai mRNA is transported through phloem to sieve tubes, where it is translated into protein that attenuates GA responses by reducing expression of many GA response genes.

genes: Atgai (Arabidopsis gai gene, gain-of-function DELLA allele of AtGAI, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic rootstock reduces the stature of the apple cultivar scion, with grafts showing a clearly reduced shoot stature.
mechanism: Atgai mRNA transported through phloem attenuates GA responses in the scion, leading to semi-dwarfism.

genes: MaPIP1;1 (MaPIP1;1, plasma membrane aquaporin, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: Overexpression of MaPIP1;1 increases primary root elongation, root hair numbers, and survival rates under salt or drought conditions in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MaPIP1;1 reduces membrane injury, improves ion distribution (higher K+/Na+ ratio), and maintains osmotic balance under stress.

genes: JcSDP1 (sugar-dependent 1 gene involved in triacylglycerol degradation, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: JcSDP1-RNAi transgenic Jatropha plants accumulated 13 to 30% higher total seed storage lipid and 7% compensatory decrease in protein content compared with control (CK; 35S:GFP) plants. Free fatty acid (FFA) content in seeds was reduced from 27% in control plants to 8.5% in JcSDP1-RNAi plants.
mechanism: Suppression of JcSDP1 expression using RNAi technology promotes increased oil accumulation in Jatropha seeds by blocking triacylglycerol (TAG) degradation.

genes: JcSDP1 (sugar-dependent 1 gene involved in triacylglycerol degradation, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: 35S:JcSDP1 transgenic Arabidopsis sdp1-5 mutant plants displayed normal growth on MS medium without sucrose, rescuing the retarded growth phenotype of sdp1-5.
mechanism: JcSDP1 rescues the sugar-dependent growth defect of the Arabidopsis sdp1-5 mutant, indicating functional equivalence to AtSDP1 in TAG metabolism.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Control (CK; 35S:GFP) plants served as a baseline for comparison with JcSDP1-RNAi transgenic lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: rolB (rolB, root development gene, Agrobacterium rhizogenes)
phenotype: Overexpression of rolB increases lycopene content by 18-62%, ascorbic acid by 24-225%, total phenolics by 11-58%, and antioxidant activity by 11-26% in tomato fruits. RolB transgenic plants show enhanced resistance to Alternaria solani and Fusarium oxysporum with disease incidence reduced to 4.17-25% compared to 91.67-95.83% in wild-type.
mechanism: RolB enhances secondary metabolism and defense responses by synergistically altering pathways for lycopene, ascorbic acid, and phenolic biosynthesis. RolB expression activates calcium balance, PR-2 protein synthesis, and phytoalexin production through kinase/phosphatase cascades.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS transgenic plants serve as control with no significant morphological differences compared to wild-type. Used to confirm transformation efficiency (37%) and as baseline for disease resistance assays.
mechanism: NA

genes: NtMEK2DD (NtMEK2 dominant-negative mutant, synthetic), MPK6 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 6, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: DEX-inducible activation of NtMEK2DD/MPK6 triggers HR-like cell death associated with chloroplast ROS generation but not NADPH oxidase ROS burst
mechanism: NtMEK2DD/MPK6 activation causes metabolic imbalance in chloroplasts leading to ROS accumulation

genes: MPK6YG (mitogen-activated protein kinase 6 gate-keeping mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NA-PP1 inhibitor treatment of MPK6YG-rescued mpk3 mpk6 double mutants recapitulates mpk3 mpk6 stomatal clustering phenotype
mechanism: NA-PP1 specifically inhibits MPK6YG activity without affecting wild-type MAPKs

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, synthetic), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression is strongly localized to guard cells in Arabidopsis thaliana with detectable fluorescence in stomatal precursor cells
mechanism: APK1b promoter directs expression to guard cells and stomatal precursor cells

genes: luc* (firefly luciferase, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: The synthetic luc* transgene generated significantly higher levels of expression than the native firefly luciferase transgene. The fold difference in expression was highest in the youngest tissues.
mechanism: increased mRNA stability and translational efficiency

genes: Renluc* (Renilla luciferase, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: The synthesized Renluc* gene yielded on average 15-fold higher luciferase activity than the native Renilla luciferase gene.
mechanism: increased mRNA stability and translational efficiency

genes: PnLOXA (Vv06s0004g01510, plastidial lipoxygenase, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of PnLOXA in tobacco leaves increases galactolipid peroxidation by ~3.6% (mono-oxidized) and ~5.6% (di-oxidized) compared to control.
mechanism: PnLOXA catalyzes 13-peroxidation of membrane galactolipids (MGDG/DGDG) in vitro and in vivo, producing 13HOTrE and oxylipins.

genes: CFM4 (chloroplast RNA splicing and ribosome maturation family member subfamily 4, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CFM4 causes retarded growth, delayed senescence, and impaired abiotic stress response in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CFM4 possesses RNA chaperone activity that affects chloroplast 16S and 4.5S rRNA processing, which is linked to ABA biosynthesis impairment and disrupted chloroplast function.

genes: CFM4::GFP (chloroplast RNA splicing and ribosome maturation family member subfamily 4 fused to green fluorescent protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CFM4-GFP fusion protein is localized to chloroplasts in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CFM4 contains a chloroplast-targeting transit peptide that directs the fusion protein to chloroplasts, confirmed by GFP fluorescence and MitoTracker staining.

genes: TcLEC2 (leafy cotyledon 2, Theobroma cacao ortholog of Arabidopsis LEC2, cacao)
phenotype: Overexpression of TcLEC2 in cacao explants greatly increased the frequency of regeneration of stably transformed somatic embryos and altered fatty acid composition (increased C18:1n-7 and decreased C18:2n-6). TcLEC2 overexpressing cotyledon explants exhibited high embryogenic competency and iterative embryogenic chain-reaction on hormone-free medium.
mechanism: TcLEC2 regulates embryogenic competency through interactions with transcriptional regulators and auxin. It modulates fatty acid biosynthesis by altering gene expression of enzymes like TcKASII, TcFatA/B, and TcDGAT2, leading to changes in fatty acid composition during seed maturation.

genes: GmMADS28 (Glycine max MADS-box transcription factor, flower-enriched gene, Glycine max)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of GmMADS28 in tobacco promoted early flowering and converted stamens and sepals to petals. Transgenic plants increased the numbers of sepal, petal and stamen from five to six and exhibited male sterility due to the shortened and curly filaments and the failure of pollen release from the anthers.
mechanism: Ectopic expression of GmMADS28 activates expression of tobacco homologs of SOC1, LEAFY, AGL8/FUL, and DEF. GmMADS28 interacts with soybean homologs of SOC1, AP1, and AGL8/FUL proteins.

genes: GmMADS28 (Glycine max MADS-box transcription factor, flower-enriched gene, Glycine max)
phenotype: Antisense expression of GmMADS28 in transgenic tobacco reduces the numbers of petals from five to four but the numbers of other three whorl organs are still five.
mechanism: NA

genes: GmMADS28 (Glycine max MADS-box transcription factor, flower-enriched gene, Glycine max)
phenotype: The GmMADS28-GFP fusion protein was localized to the nucleus.
mechanism: NA

genes: WRKY34 (WRKY34, pollen-specific transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 4myc-WRKY34 protein is expressed specifically in pollen during male gametogenesis, with peak expression in tricellular pollen stages (-2 and -1 buds).
mechanism: NA

genes: WRKY34 (WRKY34, pollen-specific transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PWRKY34:WRKY34-YFP fusion protein is localized in vegetative cell nuclei during pollen development, with expression overlapping WRKY2 in bicellular and tricellular pollen stages.
mechanism: NA

genes: ZIF2 (β-glucuronidase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ZIF2 promoter activity is ubiquitously active in Arabidopsis tissues including floral buds, leaves, roots, and lateral root primordia.
mechanism: NA

genes: ZIF2.1 (yellow fluorescent protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), ZIF2.2 (yellow fluorescent protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ZIF2.2 overexpression confers higher Zn tolerance than ZIF2.1 overexpression in Arabidopsis, with ZIF2.2-overexpressing lines showing significantly greater Zn tolerance levels.
mechanism: ZIF2.2 splice variant produces more ZIF2 protein in planta than ZIF2.1 due to enhanced translation efficiency driven by a Zn-responsive RNA secondary structure in its 5′UTR.

genes: ZIF2 (full-length, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Genomic complementation of the zif2-1 mutant with a full-length ZIF2 gene restores wild-type sensitivity to excess Zn.
mechanism: ZIF2 function participates in basal Zn tolerance in Arabidopsis by driving root Zn immobilization and shoot Zn exclusion.

genes: ZIF2.1 (yellow fluorescent protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), ZIF2.2 (yellow fluorescent protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ZIF2.2-YFP overexpression lines show higher Zn tolerance than ZIF2.1-YFP overexpression lines, with ZIF2.2-YFP transgenic lines being significantly more tolerant to Zn toxicity.
mechanism: ZIF2.2 splice variant produces 2–3 fold higher ZIF2-YFP protein abundance at the tonoplast of root tip cells compared to ZIF2.1, due to enhanced translation efficiency.

genes: At2g42940 (TEK, essential for nexine formation during pollen development, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the tek mutant restores fertility in 19 out of 20 transgenic plants with tek/tek genotype.
mechanism: TEK is essential for nexine formation during pollen development, which is required for intine deposition and microspore viability.

genes: NbSEC14 (3′-terminal cDNA fragment, N. benthamiana, N. benthamiana)
phenotype: Silencing of NbSEC14 reduces PR-4 expression and JA/JA-Ile accumulation, increases SA accumulation, and enhances susceptibility to Ralstonia solanacearum.
mechanism: NbSEC14 regulates JA-dependent signaling pathways and phospholipid metabolism (DAG/PA) during immune responses.

genes: NbSEC14 (full-length ORF with FLAG tag, N. benthamiana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of NbSEC14 increases PR-4 expression and JA/JA-Ile accumulation, reduces PR-1a expression, and enhances resistance to Ralstonia solanacearum.
mechanism: NbSEC14 activates JA-dependent signaling pathways and phospholipid metabolism (DAG/PA) to regulate defense gene expression.

genes: INF1 (N. benthamiana, synthetic)
phenotype: Used as a control for HR induction experiments; INF1 expression induces cell death in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (N. benthamiana, synthetic)
phenotype: Used as a control for transient expression experiments; GUS expression does not alter defense gene expression or hormone levels.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtMYB111 (AtMYB111, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtMYB111 reduces petal pigmentation and increases total phenolic and flavonoid content in tobacco leaves and petals.
mechanism: AtMYB111 modulates flavonoid biosynthesis by upregulating genes in the flavonol pathway, leading to increased flavonol and chlorogenic acid accumulation.

genes: J1-1 (jasmonic acid biosynthesis and pathogenesis-related gene, defensin, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Overexpression of J1-1 in unripe pepper fruits increases resistance to C. gloeosporioides by inhibiting fungal growth and spore production, reducing lesion formation by ~80% compared to wild-type controls.
mechanism: J1-1 protein exhibits antifungal activity by inhibiting appressorium formation in C. gloeosporioides. Overexpression induces JA biosynthetic genes (LOX, AOC, HPL) and pathogenesis-related genes (CaPR10, PepThi), enhancing disease resistance through both JA and SA signaling pathways.

genes: PHYB (mutant C364A, chromophore-less, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of chromophore-less phyB restores phyC levels and function in phyB mutants, enabling phyC-mediated responses to red and far-red light in rice seedlings.
mechanism: phyB stabilizes phyC and enables phyC-mediated signaling through heterodimer formation, independent of phyB's photo-sensing activity.

genes: PHYC-GFP (fusion protein, rice, synthetic)
phenotype: PHYC-GFP is biologically active in phyA phyC mutants (enabling FR and R responses) but inactive in phyB mutants (no FR/R responses).
mechanism: phyC requires phyB for functional activity through heterodimer formation; phyC exists as a monomer in phyB-deficient backgrounds and is biologically inactive.

genes: PsCRN70 (PsCRN70, Phytophthora sojae effector, Phytophthora sojae)
phenotype: Overexpression of PsCRN70 enhances susceptibility to Phytophthora parasitica by suppressing cell death and H2O2 accumulation, and down-regulating defense-related genes.
mechanism: PsCRN70 suppresses cell death triggered by multiple elicitors, reduces H2O2 accumulation, and down-regulates defense-associated genes (PR1b, PR2b, ERF1, LOX) in N. benthamiana.

genes: PsCRN70 (PsCRN70, Phytophthora sojae effector, Phytophthora sojae)
phenotype: Transient expression of PsCRN70 in N. benthamiana enhances susceptibility to P. parasitica by suppressing cell death and H2O2 accumulation.
mechanism: PsCRN70 suppresses cell death induced by multiple elicitors (BAX, PsojNIP, PsAvh241, PsCRN63, R3a/Avr3a) and reduces H2O2 accumulation in N. benthamiana.

genes: cecropinA (antimicrobial peptide, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic rice seeds expressing cecropin A exhibit resistance to fungal and bacterial pathogens (Fusarium verticillioides and Dickeya dadantii).
mechanism: Cecropin A accumulates in protein storage bodies in the rice endosperm, supporting that the glutelin N-terminal signal peptides play a crucial role in directing the cecropin A to this organelle.

genes: cecropinA (antimicrobial peptide, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic rice seeds expressing cecropin A exhibit resistance to fungal and bacterial pathogens (Fusarium verticillioides and Dickeya dadantii).
mechanism: Cecropin A accumulates in protein storage bodies in the rice endosperm, supporting that the glutelin N-terminal signal peptides play a crucial role in directing the cecropin A to this organelle.

genes: cecropinA (antimicrobial peptide, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic rice seeds expressing cecropin A exhibit resistance to fungal and bacterial pathogens (Fusarium verticillioides and Dickeya dadantii).
mechanism: Cecropin A accumulates in protein storage bodies in the rice endosperm, supporting that the glutelin N-terminal signal peptides play a crucial role in directing the cecropin A to this organelle.

genes: cecropinA (antimicrobial peptide, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic rice seeds expressing cecropin A exhibit resistance to fungal and bacterial pathogens (Fusarium verticillioides and Dickeya dadantii).
mechanism: Cecropin A accumulates in protein storage bodies in the rice endosperm, supporting that the glutelin N-terminal signal peptides play a crucial role in directing the cecropin A to this organelle.

genes: OsRACK1A (OsRACK1A, gene for RACK1A protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsRACK1A-GFP fusion protein localizes to cytosol, plasma membrane, and nuclei in rice protoplasts
mechanism: OsRACK1A is a soluble protein that may anchor in the plasma membrane by interacting with other molecules

genes: Ph-3 (ORF3, resistance gene (CC-NBS-LRR type), Solanum pimpinellifolium L3708)
phenotype: Overexpression of Ph-3 in susceptible Solanum lycopersicum cv. Moneymaker confers resistance to P. infestans isolate T1,2,4.
mechanism: Ph-3 (ORF3) encodes a CC-NBS-LRR class resistance protein that provides late blight resistance by recognizing pathogen effectors.

genes: JcFT (FLOWERING LOCUS T homolog, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcFT in Arabidopsis and Jatropha using the CaMV 35S promoter resulted in an extremely early flowering phenotype.
mechanism: JcFT acts as a florigen, promoting flowering by up-regulating downstream genes like AP1 and LFY.

genes: JcFT (FLOWERING LOCUS T homolog, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcFT in Arabidopsis and Jatropha using the SUC2 promoter resulted in an extremely early flowering phenotype.
mechanism: JcFT acts as a florigen, promoting flowering by up-regulating downstream genes like AP1 and LFY.

genes: PpIPT1 (isopentenyltransferase 1, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: IPT1::GFP fusion protein localizes to chloroplasts in Physcomitrella protoplasts, with uneven distribution within chloroplasts
mechanism: IPT1 is localized in chloroplasts and catalyzes tRNA prenylation, which is essential for cytokinin biosynthesis

genes: PpIPT1 (isopentenyltransferase 1, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: d|ipt1 mutants show reduced protonema colony diameter, smaller chloronema and caulonema cells with increased branching, and altered cytokinin profiles (reduced cZ-type cytokinins, increased iP/tZ-type cytokinins)
mechanism: IPT1 knockout disrupts tRNA prenylation, leading to reduced tRNA-bound cytokinins and a tRNA-independent pathway for iP/tZ-type cytokinin biosynthesis

genes: GRF1 (miR396-resistant version, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of rGRF1 causes short-root phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GRF1 regulates cytokinin-responsive genes and signaling, leading to altered root growth.

genes: GRF3 (miR396-resistant version, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of rGRF3 causes short-root phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GRF3 regulates cytokinin-responsive genes and signaling, leading to altered root growth.

genes: p68 (pea p68, DEAD-box RNA helicase, Pisum sativum)
phenotype: Overexpression of p68 in tobacco transgenic plants confers enhanced salinity stress tolerance by improving growth, photosynthesis, and antioxidant machinery, with higher K+ accumulation and lower Na+ levels compared to wild-type plants under stress.
mechanism: Pea p68 overexpression regulates reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation through modulating antioxidative defense machinery, protecting photosynthesis and yield under salinity stress.

genes: AtCb5-D (cytochrome b5 isoform D, hemoprotein involved in electron transfer, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtCb5-D reduces ethylene sensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana, similar to RTE1 overexpression.
mechanism: AtCb5-D acts upstream of RTE1 to negatively regulate ethylene signaling through the ETR1 ethylene receptor.

genes: AtCb5-D (cytochrome b5 isoform D, hemoprotein involved in electron transfer, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtCb5-D with N-terminal 3xFlag and 6xHis tags reduces ethylene sensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtCb5-D acts upstream of RTE1 to negatively regulate ethylene signaling through the ETR1 ethylene receptor.

genes: AtCb5-D (cytochrome b5 isoform D, hemoprotein involved in electron transfer, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Genomic overexpression of AtCb5-D (with 1.9 kb native promoter) restores ethylene-insensitive phenotype in etr1-2 atcb5-d double mutants.
mechanism: AtCb5-D acts upstream of RTE1 to negatively regulate ethylene signaling through the ETR1 ethylene receptor.

genes: SlMYC1 (SlMYC1, transcription factor involved in regulating terpene synthase promoters, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: SlMYC1 transactivates all terpene synthase promoters tested except SlTPS8, with strongest transactivation of SlTPS5 and SlTPS3 promoters in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: SlMYC1 binds to G-box-like elements in terpene synthase promoters, synergistically enhancing transactivation with SlEOT1.

genes: SlWRKY73 (SlWRKY73, transcription factor involved in regulating terpene synthase promoters, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: SlWRKY73 transactivates SlTPS5, SlTPS3, and SlTPS7 promoters in N. benthamiana leaves, but not SlTPS8 or SlTPS9 promoters.
mechanism: SlWRKY73 binds to W-boxes in terpene synthase promoters, transactivating monoterpene synthases but not sesquiterpene synthases.

genes: SlEOT1 (SlEOT1, zinc finger-like transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: SlEOT1 transactivates the SlTPS5 promoter in N. benthamiana leaves, leading to GUS expression.
mechanism: SlEOT1 binds to the SlTPS5 promoter, synergistically enhancing transactivation with SlMYC1.

genes: SlWRKY78 (SlWRKY78, transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: SlWRKY78 does not transactivate any of the tested terpene synthase promoters in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: NA

genes: SlWRKY28 (SlWRKY28, transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: SlWRKY28 does not transactivate any of the tested terpene synthase promoters in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsWRKY53 (OsWRKY53, transcription factor, Oryza sativa L.)
gene_construct: Zea mays polyubiquitin promoter-OsWRKY53-Agrobacterium tumefaciens nopaline synthase terminator
phenotype: Overexpression of OsWRKY53 enhances resistance to rice blast fungus (Magnaporthe oryzae) by upregulating defense-related genes including chitinases, β-1,3-glucanases, and PR-5, and constitutive accumulation of momilactone phytoalexins.
mechanism: OsWRKY53 activates defense-related genes through W-box binding and transactivation, and its phosphorylation by OsMPK3/OsMPK6 enhances transactivation activity, leading to increased expression of pathogenesis-related (PR) proteins and phytoalexins.

genes: OsWRKY53SD (OsWRKY53 phospho-mimic mutant, Oryza sativa L.)
gene_construct: Zea mays polyubiquitin promoter-OsWRKY53SD-Agrobacterium tumefaciens nopaline synthase terminator
phenotype: Overexpression of OsWRKY53SD further enhances resistance to rice blast fungus compared to OsWRKY53-overexpressing plants, with increased necrotic spot lesions and reduced fungal biomass.
mechanism: Phospho-mimic mutation (Ser→Asp) in OsWRKY53's SP cluster enhances transactivation activity, leading to stronger upregulation of defense-related genes and phytoalexin biosynthesis.

genes: OsWRKY53SA (OsWRKY53 phosphorylation-loss mutant, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: Transient expression of GAL4DB-OsWRKY53SA in rice cells reduces transactivation activity by 67% compared to GAL4DB-OsWRKY53.
mechanism: Loss of phosphorylation sites in OsWRKY53SA impairs transactivation activity, indicating phosphorylation-dependent regulation of gene expression.

genes: OsWRKY53SD (OsWRKY53 phospho-mimic mutant, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: Transient expression of GAL4DB-OsWRKY53SD in rice cells increases transactivation activity by >2-fold compared to GAL4DB-OsWRKY53.
mechanism: Phospho-mimic mutation (Ser→Asp) in OsWRKY53SD enhances transactivation activity, suggesting phosphorylation-dependent activation of gene expression.

genes: AtRAV1 (AtRAV1, B3-DBD transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtRAV2 (AtRAV2, B3-DBD transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtRAV2L (AtRAV2L, B3-DBD transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtABI5 (AtABI5, bZIP transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased drought tolerance, higher photosynthesis, improved water use efficiency (WUE), increased root and leaf biomass under drought stress
mechanism: Enhanced ABA signaling through functional interactions with ABI5, ABF3, and VP1; reduced stress marker gene expression (GhAdhA); elevated antioxidant gene expression (GhGST, CuZnSOD); increased root mass and leaf area

genes: WYMV-Nib8 (WYMV-Nib8, antiviral resistance, wheat yellow mosaic virus)
phenotype: Transgenic wheat line N12-1 containing WYMV-Nib8 gene can effectively control WYMV disease transmitted by Polymyxa graminis at turngreen stage
mechanism: WYMV-Nib8 gene provides antiviral resistance against wheat yellow mosaic virus

genes: CHS-A (CHS-A, chalcone synthase A, Petunia hybrida), CHS-J (CHS-J, chalcone synthase J, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: amiRchs1 transgenic flowers exhibit white or pale sectors in petals due to CHS-A and CHS-J gene silencing
mechanism: amiRchs1 guides RISC to cleave CHS-A and CHS-J mRNAs at positions complementary to the 10th and 11th nucleotides of the amiRNA, reducing their transcript accumulation

genes: AtUCP1 (AtUCP1, mitochondrial uncoupling protein 1 ortholog of mammalian UCP1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtUCP1 increases mitochondrial biogenesis, decreases cellular ATP concentration, and induces retrograde signaling to upregulate mitochondrial and stress-responsive genes, resulting in improved performance under abiotic stresses (low pH, high salt, high osmolarity, low temperature, oxidative stress).
mechanism: UCP1 overexpression triggers retrograde signaling, increasing mitochondrial biogenesis and upregulating mitochondrial/nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins and stress-responsive genes (including SOD, GPX, GST), reducing ROS accumulation through uncoupling respiration and altered mitochondrial dynamics.

genes: PHYB (photoperiodism, phytochrome B, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues the phyB-9 mutant stomatal development phenotype, increasing stomatal index (SI) and stomatal density (SD) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: phyB acts locally in the stomatal lineage to regulate epidermal cell fate during stomatal development.

genes: PHYB (photoperiodism, phytochrome B, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues the phyB-9 mutant stomatal development phenotype, increasing stomatal index (SI) and stomatal density (SD) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: phyB acts locally in the stomatal lineage to regulate epidermal cell fate during stomatal development.

genes: PHYB (photoperiodism, phytochrome B, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues the phyB-9 mutant stomatal development phenotype, increasing stomatal index (SI) and stomatal density (SD) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: phyB acts non-cell autonomously in mesophyll cells to regulate stomatal development.

genes: PHYB (photoperiodism, phytochrome B, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues the phyB-9 mutant stomatal development phenotype, increasing stomatal index (SI) and stomatal density (SD) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: phyB acts non-cell autonomously in phloem companion cells to regulate stomatal development.

genes: NtTTG2 (NtTTG2, NtTTG2 gene, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: NtTTG2 silencing causes repressive effects on vegetative growth, floral anthocyanin synthesis, flower colorization, and seed production in tobacco.
mechanism: NtTTG2 silencing reduces expression of EXP1 and EXP2 genes involved in plant growth, and DFR and ANS genes in anthocyanin biosynthesis, leading to reduced anthocyanin production and seed abortion.

genes: NtTTG2 (NtTTG2, NtTTG2 gene, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: NtTTG2 overexpression promotes plant growth, floral anthocyanin synthesis, flower colorization, and seed production in tobacco.
mechanism: NtTTG2 overexpression increases EXP1 and EXP2 expression for growth, and DFR/ANS for anthocyanin biosynthesis, while affecting putative ARF genes in auxin response pathways.

genes: SQN (SQN, gene involved in stem cell regulation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced SQN expression in Ler zll-1 sqn-4 double mutants alleviates stem cell termination, increasing wild-type-like meristems up to 31.2%.
mechanism: SQN acts as a cofactor for AGO1, enhancing its activity to repress Class III HD-ZIP genes, leading to stem cell termination when ZLL is absent.

genes: SQN (SQN, gene involved in stem cell regulation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic SQN expression in Col zllago10-1 mutants induces stem cell termination in up to 22.2% of plants.
mechanism: Increased SQN enhances AGO1 activity, leading to repression of Class III HD-ZIP genes and stem cell termination in the absence of ZLL.

genes: OsHUS1 (OsHUS1, RNAi, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Severe reduction in fertility (93%, n=30) in Yandao 8 rice
mechanism: NA

genes: OsNRAMP5 (OsNRAMP5, cadmium transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockdown of OsNRAMP5 increases cadmium accumulation in shoots by 2.0-fold in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsNRAMP5 is a major transporter for cadmium uptake; its knockdown reduces root cadmium concentration and enhances translocation to shoots.

genes: CaMBF1 (CaMBF1, transcriptional co-activator involved in stress responses, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CaMBF1 in Arabidopsis displayed reduced tolerance to cold and high salt stress during seed germination and post-germination stages, with visible leaf damage, increased electrolyte leakage, and hypersensitivity to salt stress
mechanism: CaMBF1 may reduce stress tolerance by downregulating stress-responsive genes (RD29A, ERD15, KIN1, RD22) to aggravate leaf damage caused by cold stress

genes: H5 (hemagglutinin subtype 5, A/Hatay/2004 strain, GenBank Q5QQ29), H5-ELP (H5 fused with elastin-like polypeptide), H5-HFBI (H5 fused with hydrophobin I)
phenotype: H5-ELP accumulates to ~0.5% of total soluble protein in leaves and seeds, 10-fold higher than H5 and H5-HFBI. H5-HFBI shows no significant increase in accumulation compared to untagged H5.
mechanism: ELPylation enhances protein accumulation by forming phase-separated bodies in the ER and cytoplasm. Hydrophobin fusion does not significantly increase accumulation.

genes: H5 (hemagglutinin subtype 5, A/Hatay/2004 strain, GenBank Q5QQ29)
phenotype: H5 accumulates to ~0.04% of total soluble protein in leaves and seeds.
mechanism: NA

genes: H5-ELP (H5 fused with elastin-like polypeptide)
phenotype: H5-ELP accumulates to ~0.5% of total soluble protein in leaves and seeds, 10-fold higher than untagged H5.
mechanism: ELPylation enhances accumulation by forming phase-separated bodies in the ER and cytoplasm.

genes: H5-HFBI (H5 fused with hydrophobin I)
phenotype: H5-HFBI accumulates to ~0.05% of total soluble protein in leaves and ~0.03% in seeds, showing no significant increase compared to untagged H5.
mechanism: Hydrophobin fusion does not significantly enhance accumulation.

genes: EPSPSn-In (fusion of first 295 amino acids of EPSPS and 123 amino acids of Ssp DnaE intein-N, synthetic), Ic-EPSPSc (fusion of 36 amino acids of Ssp DnaE intein-C and remaining 150 EPSPS amino acids, synthetic)
phenotype: Hybrid plants containing both EPSPSn-In and Ic-EPSPSc exhibit 100% glyphosate resistance, similar to plants with full-length G2-aroA gene
mechanism: Intein-mediated protein trans-splicing reassembles functional EPSPS protein from split fragments, conferring glyphosate resistance

genes: G2-aroA (glyphosate-resistant EPSPS, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of G2-aroA confers glyphosate resistance in transgenic tobacco plants
mechanism: Full-length glyphosate-resistant EPSPS protein provides resistance to glyphosate herbicide

genes: sgRNA (single guide RNA, targeting mutant GFP gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Restoration of functional GFP gene via Cas9/sgRNA-mediated mutagenesis, leading to green fluorescence in transgenic plant cells.
mechanism: Cas9/sgRNA complex induces double strand cleavage at the target site in the nonfunctional GFP gene, repaired by NHEJ, which in ~1/3 of cases restores the reading frame, allowing GFP expression.

genes: SlWAK1 (SlWAK1, cell wall-associated kinase, Solyc09g014720)
phenotype: Silencing of SlWAK1 compromises pattern-triggered immunity (PTI), resulting in increased growth of Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato (Pst) and enhanced disease symptoms in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: SlWAK1 is a cell wall-associated kinase involved in PTI. Its silencing disrupts the plant's ability to suppress Pst growth, suggesting a role in recognizing damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) like oligogalacturonides (OGs) and triggering immune signaling.

genes: FLS2.1 (FLS2.1, pattern recognition receptor, Solyc02g070890)
phenotype: Silencing of FLS2.1 results in intermediate bacterial growth of Pst compared to EC1 and SlWAK1-silenced plants, indicating partial compromise of PTI.
mechanism: FLS2.1 is a pattern recognition receptor (PRR) involved in flagellin perception. Its silencing partially disrupts PTI, highlighting its role in the initial recognition of microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs).

genes: SAD1 (supersensitive to abscisic acid and drought 1 gene, encodes Sm-like protein 5 (LSm5), Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAD1 in Arabidopsis improves salt tolerance in transgenic plants, which correlates with an increase in splicing accuracy and efficiency for stress-responsive genes.
mechanism: SAD1 modulates the splicing of stress-responsive genes, particularly under salt-stress conditions, by strengthening the precision of splice-site recognition and globally inhibiting alternative splicing.

genes: PIF4 (Phytochrome Interacting Factor 4, negative regulator of photopigment synthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PIF4 suppresses carotenoid and chlorophyll biosynthesis by binding to G-box elements in promoters of photosynthetic genes.
mechanism: PIF4 binds to G-box motifs in promoters of PSY, LHCA4, PORC, and GUN5, repressing their transcription. This repression is temperature-dependent, with enhanced binding at 27°C.

genes: HY5 (Long Hypocotyl 5, positive regulator of photopigment synthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HY5 enhances carotenoid and chlorophyll biosynthesis by binding to G-box elements in promoters of photosynthetic genes, particularly at cooler temperatures (17°C).
mechanism: HY5 binds to G-box motifs in promoters of PSY, LHCA4, PORC, and GUN5, activating their transcription. This activation is temperature-dependent, with higher HY5 abundance at 17°C.

genes: PIF1 (Phytochrome Interacting Factor 1, negative regulator of photopigment synthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PIF1 suppresses carotenoid and chlorophyll biosynthesis by binding to G-box elements in promoters of photosynthetic genes, with enhanced effects at 27°C.
mechanism: PIF1 binds to G-box motifs in promoters of PSY, LHCA4, PORC, and GUN5, repressing their transcription. This repression is temperature-dependent, with enhanced binding at 27°C.

genes: YGL7 (Os03g59640, magnesium-chelatase subunit D, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of ygl7-NIL restores green leaf color and chlorophyll/carotenoid levels to wild-type levels.
mechanism: Complementation restores normal magnesium-chelatase function, enabling chlorophyll biosynthesis.

genes: YGL7 (Os03g59640, magnesium-chelatase subunit D, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi suppression of YGL7 causes progressive yellowing and death of transgenic plants due to chlorophyll synthesis disruption.
mechanism: RNAi silencing of YGL7 disrupts magnesium-chelatase function, leading to lethal chlorophyll deficiency.

genes: MtOLEOSIN4 (MtOLEOSIN4, oleosin protein, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Increased somatic embryogenesis in Medicago truncatula when combined with GA+ABA treatment
mechanism: NA

genes: NA
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: psy (Narcissus pseudonarcissus, phytoene synthase, daffodil), crtI (Erwinia uredovora, desaturase, bacterial), pmi (bacterial, phosphomannose isomerase, bacterial)
phenotype: Overexpression of psy, crtI, and pmi increases β-carotene levels in rice endosperm, with carotenoid content varying from 0.257 µg g−1 to 3.188 µg g−1 in transgenic lines.
mechanism: Expression of crtI in the endosperm enhances carotenoid biosynthesis, leading to β-carotene accumulation. The pmi gene serves as a selectable marker for transgenic selection.

genes: prosystemin (prosystemin, defense-related gene, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of prosystemin in 35S tomato genotype increases resistance to whiteflies and enhances volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, including monoterpenes, GLVs, and aldehydes, compared to wild-type plants under elevated O3 and herbivory treatments.
mechanism: Prosystemin constitutively activates the defense system in unwounded plants, leading to stronger and more rapidly induced resistance against herbivores like Bemisia tabaci. Elevated VOC emissions, particularly monoterpenes, repel whiteflies and attract parasitoids like Encarsia formosa.

genes: AGB1 (At4G34460, Gβ subunit of heterotrimeric G protein complex, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of mutated AGB1 (W109A/S129A) confers salt tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with increased green seedling survival under 100 mM NaCl compared to wild type and agb1-2 mutants.
mechanism: Mutations in AGB1 (W109A/S129A) disrupt Gα-Gβγ heterotrimer formation, increasing active Gα and Gβγ subunits at the plasma membrane. This sustained G signaling promotes salt tolerance by balancing growth and senescence under NaCl stress.

genes: OsMYB103L (Oryza sativa, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsMYB103L in rice results in a rolled leaf phenotype with increased cellulose content (~13% higher than wild type) and elevated expression of several cellulose synthase (CESA) genes.
mechanism: OsMYB103L regulates CESA gene expression, which influences cellulose synthesis and leaf morphology. The rolled leaf phenotype is associated with smaller bulliform cells and altered cellulose content.

genes: OsMYB103L (Oryza sativa, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi knockdown of OsMYB103L leads to decreased cellulose content in leaves, reduced mechanical strength (50% less force required to break leaves), and down-regulated expression of several CESA genes.
mechanism: OsMYB103L knockdown reduces CESA gene expression, leading to decreased cellulose synthesis and weakened mechanical strength in rice leaves.

genes: ARP6 (ACTIN RELATED PROTEIN 6, Brachypodium distachyon)
phenotype: Reduced seed weight (60%, P < 0.001) and overall yield per plant (30 to 50%, P < 0.01), increased rate of floret sterility and grain abortion
mechanism: Perturbing H2A.Z occupancy through ARP6 RNAi silencing phenocopies the effects of warmer temperature on grain development, reducing yield

genes: UVI4 (UVI4, cell cycle regulation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of UVI4 and GFP fusion confers a dwarf phenotype with multiple shoots in both wild-type Col-0 and uvi4-1 mutant.
mechanism: NA

genes: OSD1 (OSD1, cell cycle regulation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of OSD1 triggers reduction of endoreduplication, leading to lower ploidy index in leaf cells.
mechanism: OSD1 inhibits APC/C activity, regulating endoreduplication.

genes: PutAMT1;1 (ammonium transporter, Puccinellia tenuiflora)
phenotype: ER-GFP fusion protein localizes to plasma membrane and ER in P. tenuiflora suspension-cultured cells
mechanism: ER signal directs PutAMT1;1-GFP to endoplasmic reticulum and plasma membrane

genes: AtHB12 (homeodomain-leucine zipper transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtHB7 (homeodomain-leucine zipper transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtHB12 increases root elongation and leaf development in young plants under standard growth conditions, while AtHB7 promotes leaf development, chlorophyll levels, and photosynthesis in mature plants.
mechanism: AtHB12 and AtHB7 regulate each other's expression during development, with AtHB12 repressing AtHB7 and AtHB7 inducing AtHB12 at early stages, and a double negative feedback loop in mature plants.

genes: AtHB12 (homeodomain-leucine zipper transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtHB7 (homeodomain-leucine zipper transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Double knock-down mutant at12/7 exhibited reduced rosette leaf area, shorter roots, and altered water stress responses compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: Artificial microRNA targeting both AtHB12 and AtHB7 reduced their expression, leading to developmental and stress-related phenotypes.

genes: SiREM6 (salt stress-responsive remorin, Setaria italica)
phenotype: Overexpression of SiREM6 improves salt stress tolerance in Arabidopsis during germination and seedling stages, with higher germination rates (up to 175 mM NaCl), increased survival rates (60-100% vs <50% in WT under 400 mM NaCl), reduced electrolyte leakage, and elevated proline accumulation under salt stress.
mechanism: SiREM6 enhances salt tolerance by reducing cellular damage through proline accumulation and maintaining membrane integrity, likely via ABA-dependent pathways involving DREB transcription factor SiARDP binding to SiREM6 promoter elements.

genes: cry1A(b) (insecticidal crystal protein, synthetic), zm-upl (HECT type E3 ubiquitin ligase, Zea mays)
phenotype: Production of chimeric poly-A+ transcripts in MON810, encompassing cry1A(b) linked to antisense zm-upl sequences
mechanism: Truncation of zm-upl exon 8 by transgene insertion creates chimeric transcripts with cry1A(b) and antisense zm-upl sequences

genes: replicase (126 kDa replicase component, 183 kDa replicase component), MP (movement protein), CP (capsid protein), ORF6 (open reading frame 6) (replicase, movement, encapsidation, symptomology) (Tobacco mosaic virus)
phenotype: Synthetic virions of Goelet TMV sequence did not produce symptoms in Nicotiana tabacum or Nicotiana sylvestris. After correcting two nucleotide mutations to match consensus TMV sequences, synthetic virions produced classic TMV symptoms.
mechanism: The corrected nucleotide mutations in the replicase component (positions 186-187) likely restored functional methyltransferase domain interactions with host proteins or TMV RNA 3' end.

genes: ToMV_CP (capsid protein) (Tobacco mosaic virus/ToMV chimera)
phenotype: Virus expressing ToMV capsid protein exhibited altered, ToMV-like symptoms in Nicotiana sylvestris.
mechanism: ToMV capsid protein gene created a hybrid ORF6 protein overlapping TMV MP and CP genes, which influenced symptomology in N. benthamiana.

genes: hybrid_ORF6 (overlapping TMV MP and ToMV CP genes) (synthetic hybrid)
phenotype: A hybrid ORF6 protein unknown to nature, created by substituting the capsid protein genes in the virus, was found to be a major symptom determinant in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: The carboxyl end of hybrid ORF6 overlapping the ToMV CP gene influenced symptoms the most, with milder symptoms observed when ORF6 translational starts were mutated.

genes: BSMV_CP (capsid protein) (Tobacco mosaic virus/BSMV chimera)
phenotype: Virus expressing BSMV capsid protein did not have an extended host range to barley, but did produce novel symptoms in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: BSMV capsid protein created a truncated TMV/BSMV hybrid ORF6 protein, which contributed to unique mosaic symptoms without systemic necrosis.

genes: GmAKT2 (K+ transporter gene involved in SMV resistance, Glycine max (L.) Merr.)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmAKT2 increases SMV resistance in soybean by retarding viral development and reducing SMV RNA accumulation by ~200-260-fold in wildtype plants
mechanism: GmAKT2 enhances K+ transport and redistribution, altering phloem environment to be unfavorable for virus movement

genes: Rpi-vnt1.1 (Rpi-vnt1.1, late blight resistance gene, Solanum venturii), Rpi-sto1 (Rpi-sto1, late blight resistance gene, Solanum stoloniferum)
phenotype: Overexpression of Rpi-vnt1.1 confers resistance to specific P. infestans isolates in potato varieties.
mechanism: Functional expression of Rpi-vnt1.1 triggers resistance via recognition of corresponding Avr genes.

genes: Rpi-sto1 (Rpi-sto1, late blight resistance gene, Solanum stoloniferum), Rpi-vnt1.1 (Rpi-vnt1.1, late blight resistance gene, Solanum venturii)
phenotype: Overexpression of Rpi-sto1 confers resistance to specific P. infestans isolates in potato varieties.
mechanism: Functional expression of Rpi-sto1 triggers resistance via recognition of corresponding Avr genes.

genes: Rpi-vnt1.1 (Rpi-vnt1.1, late blight resistance gene, Solanum venturii), Rpi-sto1 (Rpi-sto1, late blight resistance gene, Solanum stoloniferum)
phenotype: Stacking of Rpi-vnt1.1 and Rpi-sto1 provides broad-spectrum late blight resistance in potato varieties.
mechanism: Complementary action of both R genes expands resistance spectra against multiple P. infestans isolates.

genes: PLDε (phospholipase D epsilon, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PLDε increases plant growth, biomass, leaf size, leaf number, and seed yield in Arabidopsis thaliana. PLDε-OE plants exhibit 192% fresh weight and 212% dry weight of wild type after five weeks of growth under well-fertilized conditions.
mechanism: PLDε-derived phosphatidic acid (PA) is involved in growth promotion by enhancing root growth, biomass accumulation, and nitrogen acquisition. PA production is linked to increased nitrate transporter expression (NRT1.1 and NRT2.1), enhanced nitrate uptake, and improved nitrogen assimilation via increased nitrite reductase (NiR) and glutamine synthetase (GS) activity.

genes: PLDε (phospholipase D epsilon, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PLDε-YFP fusion protein localizes to the plasma membrane in transiently expressed tobacco leaves. YFP alone is detected in the nucleus and cytoplasm, whereas PLDε-YFP fluorescence is observed along the plasma membrane.
mechanism: NA

genes: PapsPI-1 (PISTILLATA 1, Papaver somniferum, Papaver somniferum)
phenotype: Overexpression of PapsPI-1 in tobacco leads to partially petaloid sepals in one of twenty transgenic plants, with six-fold increased expression in the transformed sepal.
mechanism: PapsPI-1 overexpression causes sepal-to-petal conversion by upregulating petal identity genes, forming heterodimers with PapsAP3-1 to specify petal identity.

genes: gusA (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Homogeneous GUS staining in cotyledons of 100% infected Arabidopsis seedlings with 4-fold higher GUS activity in efr-1 mutants compared to wild-type Col-0.
mechanism: NA

phenotype: Bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) confirmed interaction between ASK1 and TIR1 in the nucleus of Arabidopsis seedlings.
mechanism: Bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) of nYFP and cYFP fragments upon protein interaction.

genes: GFP (GFP, fusion protein with Protein A, TEV protease cleavage site, and 6xHis, synthetic)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: 14-3-3 omega (At1g78300, fused to YFP and the same affinity tag as 35s::GFP-TAP2, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: HaHSFA4a (Helianthus annuus Heat Shock Factor A4a, sunflower, Helianthus annuus), HaHSFA9 (Helianthus annuus Heat Shock Factor A9, sunflower, Helianthus annuus)
phenotype: Combined overexpression of HaHSFA4a and HaHSFA9 enhanced seed longevity beyond HaHSFA9 alone in tobacco, with 32.95-fold increase in resistance to accelerated aging (P < 0.0001).
mechanism: Synergistic co-activation of a genetic program of longevity and desiccation tolerance via HaHSFA9 and HaHSFA4a interaction, leading to enhanced sHSP accumulation and stress protection.

genes: HaHSFA4a (Helianthus annuus Heat Shock Factor A4a, sunflower, Helianthus annuus), HaHSFA9 (Helianthus annuus Heat Shock Factor A9, sunflower, Helianthus annuus)
phenotype: Combined 35S-driven overexpression of HaHSFA4a and HaHSFA9 in tobacco seedlings enhanced tolerance to severe dehydration (98% water loss) and 300 mM H2O2 oxidative stress, with survival rates doubling compared to HaHSFA9 alone (P ≤ 0.01).
mechanism: Synergistic functional interaction between HaHSFA9 and HaHSFA4a in vegetative organs, leading to enhanced PSII protection (Fv/Fm) and reduced electrolyte leakage under oxidative stress.

genes: HaHSFA4a (Helianthus annuus Heat Shock Factor A4a, sunflower, Helianthus annuus)
phenotype: Single overexpression of HaHSFA4a under DS10 promoter enhanced seed longevity in tobacco, with similar resistance to 52°C accelerated aging as DS10:A9/A4a lines.
mechanism: Enhanced accumulation of HSP101 and sHSP-CII in seeds, though functional effects required HaHSFA9 for stress tolerance in vegetative organs.

genes: HaHSFA4a (Helianthus annuus Heat Shock Factor A4a, sunflower, Helianthus annuus)
phenotype: Single 35S-driven overexpression of HaHSFA4a in tobacco seedlings failed to induce thermotolerance, dehydration tolerance, or sHSP accumulation under unstressed conditions.
mechanism: HaHSFA4a requires HaHSFA9 for functional interaction; no stress tolerance observed in 35S:A4a seedlings despite normal HSP accumulation after heat acclimation.

genes: GUS (uidA, reporter gene, plasmid)
phenotype: GUS expression in cotyledons and hypocotyls in 2-day-old germinating seeds
mechanism: reporter gene expression for AtDFB promoter activity

genes: AtDFB (At5g05980, plastidial isoform of FPGS, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restored wild-type levels of C and N partitioning in mature seeds
mechanism: Complementation of AtDFB loss of function

genes: PpEXP1 (PpEXP1, expansin gene from Poa pratensis, alpha-expansin family)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpEXP1 in tobacco enhances heat tolerance by maintaining higher leaf chlorophyll content, relative water content, net photosynthetic rate, antioxidant enzyme activity, and lower electrolyte leakage, H2O2, and MDA content under heat stress.
mechanism: PpEXP1 promotes leaf photosynthesis and hydration status, strengthens antioxidant activities to suppress reactive oxygen species accumulation, and maintains cell wall extensibility to prevent cellular damage during heat stress.

genes: FPS1L (farnesyl diphosphate synthase 1 long isoform, Arabidopsis thaliana), HMGR1S (hydroxymethylglutaryl CoA reductase 1 short isoform, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FPS1L and HMGR1S increases precursor availability for sesquiterpene synthase, leading to emission of (E)-nerolidol and attraction of parasitoid wasps.
mechanism: Enhances substrate availability for sesquiterpene synthase by overexpressing rate-limiting enzymes in the mevalonate pathway.

genes: FPS1L (farnesyl diphosphate synthase 1 long isoform, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FPS1L increases precursor availability for sesquiterpene synthase, leading to emission of (E)-nerolidol and attraction of parasitoid wasps.
mechanism: Enhances substrate availability for sesquiterpene synthase by overexpressing a rate-limiting enzyme in the mevalonate pathway.

genes: topp4-1 (mutated protein with dominant-negative effect, Arabidopsis thaliana, mutated)
phenotype: Overexpression of topp4-1 recapitulates the dwarfed phenotypes of topp4-1 mutant, including lack of apical dominance, abnormal leaf phyllotaxy, curled rosette leaves, and reduced sterility.
mechanism: The mutated topp4-1 protein has a dominant-negative effect on plant growth, causing dwarfism by disrupting GA signaling and DELLA protein degradation.

genes: topp4-1 (mutated protein with dominant-negative effect, Arabidopsis thaliana, mutated)
phenotype: Transgenic plants with pTOPP4-topp4-1 show topp4-1 mutant-like phenotypes, including dwarfism and reduced sterility.
mechanism: The mutated topp4-1 protein under its own promoter causes dwarfism by disrupting GA signaling and DELLA protein degradation.

genes: TOPP4 (wild-type, Arabidopsis thaliana, wild-type)
phenotype: Overexpression of TOPP4 in wild-type plants results in enlarged organs, including elongated hypocotyls, increased plant height, thickened stems, and enlarged rosette leaves, inflorescences, flowers, and siliques.
mechanism: TOPP4 promotes GA-induced degradation of DELLA proteins (RGA and GAI), enhancing stem elongation and organ growth.

genes: TOPP4 (wild-type, Arabidopsis thaliana, wild-type)
phenotype: Transgenic lines overexpressing TOPP4 under its own promoter show increased rosette width in topp4-1 mutant but do not fully rescue height or leaf phenotypes.
mechanism: TOPP4 under its own promoter partially rescues topp4-1 phenotypes by promoting DELLA protein degradation.

genes: TOPP4 (wild-type, Arabidopsis thaliana, wild-type)
phenotype: amiR-TOPP4-1 transgenic lines exhibit dwarfed phenotypes with reduced inflorescence height, curled leaves, and decreased fertility.
mechanism: Knockdown of TOPP4 by amiRNA-1 reduces its protein levels, leading to impaired GA signaling and DELLA protein degradation.

genes: TOPP4 (wild-type, Arabidopsis thaliana, wild-type)
phenotype: amiR-TOPP4-2 transgenic lines exhibit dwarfed phenotypes with reduced inflorescence height, curled leaves, and decreased fertility.
mechanism: Knockdown of TOPP4 by amiRNA-2 reduces its protein levels, leading to impaired GA signaling and DELLA protein degradation.

genes: TOPP4 (wild-type, Arabidopsis thaliana, wild-type)
phenotype: GUS staining reveals ubiquitous expression of TOPP4 in various organs, including roots, cotyledons, vascular bundles, and reproductive tissues.
mechanism: TOPP4 is ubiquitously expressed in multiple tissues, suggesting its role in diverse developmental processes.

genes: TOPP4 (wild-type, Arabidopsis thaliana, wild-type)
phenotype: TOPP4-YFP is localized in the nucleus and plasma membrane of mesophyll protoplasts and Nicotiana benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: TOPP4 localizes to the nucleus and plasma membrane, indicating its potential role in nuclear signaling and membrane-associated processes.

genes: nahG (salicylate hydroxylase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Depletion of SA suppresses hybrid phenotypes
mechanism: SA depletion suppresses the hybrid phenotypes

genes: β-GFP (mitochondria-targeted green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of β-GFP targeted to mitochondria allows visualization of mitochondrial morphology and dynamics in grapevine leaves.
mechanism: β-GFP is used as a fluorescent marker to track mitochondria in vivo.

genes: SlSRN1 (SlSRN1, stress-related NAC transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of SlSRN1 increases susceptibility to Botrytis cinerea and Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000, with lesion sizes 38% and 16-fold larger, respectively.
mechanism: SlSRN1 regulates defense gene expression (SlPR1a, SlPR1b upregulated; SlPR5, SlTPK1b downregulated) and reactive oxygen species accumulation during pathogen infection.

genes: SlSRN1 (SlSRN1, stress-related NAC transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of SlSRN1 reduces lesion size by 40% in Botrytis cinerea infection.
mechanism: SlSRN1 enhances resistance through upregulation of defense genes and reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation.

genes: LIP5 (At4g26750, positive regulator of SKD1 in MVB biogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of lip5 mutant restores disease resistance to P. syringae.
mechanism: LIP5 interacts with SKD1 to regulate MVB biogenesis, which is critical for plant immunity.

genes: MPK6 (At2g43790, pathogen-responsive MAPK, Arabidopsis thaliana), LIP5 (At4g26750, positive regulator of SKD1 in MVB biogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Enables visualization of MPK6-LIP5 interaction in plant cells.
mechanism: Bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) allows detection of protein-protein interactions in vivo.

genes: LIP5 (At4g26750, positive regulator of SKD1 in MVB biogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased stability of LIP5 protein upon phosphorylation, enhancing disease resistance.
mechanism: Phosphorylation by MPK3/6 increases LIP5 stability, which is critical for MVB biogenesis and plant immunity.

genes: MsHsp23 (small heat shock protein 23, from Medicago sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic tall fescue plants show significantly lower H2O2 and TBARS accumulation under salt and arsenic stress compared to non-transgenic controls, indicating enhanced stress tolerance.
mechanism: MsHsp23 stabilizes membrane proteins and enhances ROS scavenging under stress conditions, reducing lipid peroxidation and reactive oxygen species accumulation.

genes: cry1C (Cry1C toxin, insecticidal protein against lepidopterans, synthetic modified gene)
phenotype: Cry1C protein content in rice pollen was 2.40±0.08 µg/g dry weight (T1C-19 line)

mechanism: SaMT2 binds cadmium and zinc ions, reduces reactive oxygen species (H2O2) accumulation, and activates antioxidant enzymes (SOD, POD) to mitigate metal-induced oxidative stress.

genes: Dlf1 (OsWRKY11, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)

mechanism: Dlf1 suppresses flowering-related genes (Ehd2, Ehd1, Hd1, Hd3a) and regulates plant height by altering cell size in internodes.

genes: Dlf1 (OsWRKY11, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)

mechanism: The C-terminus of Dlf1 regulates its expression level and function in flowering suppression.

genes: Dlf1 (OsWRKY11, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of truncated OsWRKY11.2 causes dwarfism and delayed flowering under both LD and SD conditions.
mechanism: The C-terminal region of Dlf1 influences its expression and function in flowering suppression.

genes: SlERF36 (SlERF36, EAR motif-containing AP2 domain gene, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlERF36 causes early photoperiod-independent flowering (7 days earlier than control), early senescence, reduced chlorophyll content (25-50% lower), smaller rosette diameter (2-3 cm reduction), shorter plant height (35-40% reduction), smaller flowers and siliques, and 38-39% reduction in stomatal density.
mechanism: The EAR motif in SlERF36 is essential for repression activity. Full-length SlERF36 increases FT transcript levels, accelerating flowering. SlERF36 also reduces stomatal density by repressing stomatal development regulators, leading to reduced photosynthesis and growth.

genes: SlERF36ΔEAR (SlERF36ΔEAR, truncated AP2 domain gene lacking EAR motif, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlERF36ΔEAR (lacking EAR motif) results in normal flowering time (27-28 days vs 28.33 days in control), normal senescence, 25-26% reduction in stomatal density, and 27-30% reduction in photosynthesis. Rosette diameter and plant height are similar to wild type.
mechanism: The absence of the EAR motif in SlERF36ΔEAR abolishes repression activity. This construct does not increase FT transcript levels, maintaining normal flowering. Reduced stomatal density is less severe compared to full-length SlERF36, suggesting the EAR motif is critical for repression of stomatal development regulators.

mechanism: ACA2 is localized to endomembranes (ER) rather than the plasma membrane, making it ineffective for rescuing ACA9's pollen-specific function.

genes: GmPIP1;6 (GmPIP1;6, plasma membrane water transporter, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmPIP1;6 increases salt tolerance in soybean by maintaining root hydraulic conductance (Lo) under saline conditions, enhancing net assimilation by ~2-fold under salt stress, and increasing seed weight and size in field conditions.
mechanism: GmPIP1;6 maintains root water transport under salinity, enhances photosynthesis via increased stomatal conductance and transpiration, and facilitates Na+ exclusion from leaves through improved water permeability and root hydraulic conductivity.

genes: CdPCS1 (CdPCS1, phytochelatin synthase, synthetic)

mechanism: CdPCS1 overexpression increased PCS activity (8-fold in roots, 2-fold in shoots), leading to enhanced PC synthesis which chelated arsenic for detoxification and sequestration in vacuoles.

genes: miR839 (microRNA 839, non-coding RNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Ced-9 prevents ROS generation, maintains potassium and calcium levels, and enhances ATP content under stress conditions, thereby inhibiting cell death in root hairs

mechanism: miR171h binds to the NSP2 binding site in the sensor construct, leading to mRFP cleavage and reduced fluorescence. The scrambled sequence prevents this interaction.

mechanism: miR171h and NSP2 promoters are regulated by phosphate and nitrogen levels, with miR171h activity in central cylinder and NSP2 in cortex under mycorrhizal conditions.

genes: Vgb (Vgb, encoding VHb, Vitreoscilla)

mechanism: BtCry3A confers resistance to Coleoptera by producing insecticidal crystal protein; OC-I inhibits the growth of Coleoptera pests by acting as a cysteine protease inhibitor.

genes: JERF36 (JERF36, encoding AP2/EREBP plant transcription factors, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of JERF36 increases tolerance to multiple stresses including drought, salt, waterlogging and insect feeding in Populus × euramericana.
mechanism: JERF36 activates stress-related genes and regulates ethylene (ET), jasmonate (JA), and salicylic acid (SA) signaling pathways to enhance stress resistance.

mechanism: Overexpression of MusaBI1 modulates programmed cell death (PCD) pathways to enhance resistance against Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (Foc) infection.

genes: AtbZIP29 (group I bZIP protein, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: AtbZIP29 binds to CYP707A1/3 promoters via its bZIP domain, enabling transcriptional activation under hypo-osmotic stress.

genes: MIR171c (MIR171c, microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: PORC (PORC, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: SCL27 binds to the PORC promoter and inhibits its activity.

genes: MIR171a (MIR171a, microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: SCL27 activates MIR171 gene expression in a feedback manner.

genes: RcKSII (KSII from Ricinus communis, fatty acid synthase, plant)

mechanism: RcKSII, a plant KSII, interacts with Cr-cACP in the chloroplast, leading to increased C18 fatty acid production.

genes: gus (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic auxin-responsive promoter, synthetic)

mechanism: Auxin-responsive DR5 promoter drives GUS expression.

mechanism: Bar gene confers herbicide resistance by acetylating ammonium glufosinate; GUS gene provides β-glucuronidase activity for visualization

genes: VoGES (geraniol synthase, V. officinalis)

mechanism: NA

genes: AXR1 (At1g05180, E1 enzyme of the neddylation complex, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: AXR1 encodes the E1 enzyme of the neddylation complex, which regulates the activity of CRL4 complexes. AXR1 acts during meiotic recombination through the activation of a CRL4 complex to regulate the localisation of class I COs. The meiotic defects in axr1 are epistatic to those of a Cullin 4 mutant, indicating AXR1 acts upstream of CUL4.

genes: WRKY45 (WRKY45, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of WRKY45 under the maize ubiquitin promoter increases resistance to rice blast and bacterial leaf-blight diseases.
mechanism: WRKY45 upregulates diterpenoid phytoalexin biosynthetic genes, enhancing disease resistance.

genes: WRKY45 (WRKY45, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: DEX-induced expression of WRKY45 leads to upregulation of DP biosynthetic genes.
mechanism: WRKY45 activation by DEX induces DP biosynthetic genes, contributing to disease resistance.

genes: fgf-1 (human acidic fibroblast growth factor 1, Homo sapiens)

mechanism: rFGF-1 promotes fibroblast proliferation and angiogenesis, enhancing wound healing

genes: CHS (chalcone synthase, Petunia hybrida, EMBL/GenBank X04080), CHI (chalcone isomerase, Petunia hybrida, EMBL/GenBank X14589), DFR (dihydroflavonol reductase, Petunia hybrida, EMBL/GenBank X15537)
phenotype: Transgenic flax plants overproducing phenylpropanoid compounds (coumaric acid, ferulic acid, caffeic acid, lignan) in seedcake extract exhibit broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, and Staphylococcus aureus.
mechanism: Phenolic acids in extract inhibit bacterial topoisomerase II (gyrase) activity and cause genomic DNA disintegration, leading to cell death. Synergistic effects between p-coumaric acid and ferulic acid enhance antimicrobial activity.
