plant_species: Oryza sativa L. subsp. indica, Oryza sativa L. subsp. japonica
genes: OsAAP6 (amino acid transporter, Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica)
phenotype: Complementation of OsAAP6 increases grain protein content (GPC) and total amino acids.
mechanism: OsAAP6 enhances amino acid transport, leading to increased storage proteins.

plant_species: Oryza sativa L. subsp. indica, Oryza sativa L. subsp. japonica
genes: OsAAP6 (amino acid transporter, Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica)
phenotype: RNAi of OsAAP6 decreases grain protein content (GPC) and total amino acids.
mechanism: OsAAP6 knockdown reduces amino acid transport, leading to decreased storage proteins.

genes: cry1Ab (insecticide protein (Bt toxin) Cry1Ab, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Expression of insecticide protein Cry1Ab in maize provides resistance against insect pests
mechanism: Cry1Ab toxin binds to midgut epithelial cells of target insects, forming pores that disrupt cell function and cause insect death

genes: MsSN1 (snakin-1, antimicrobial peptide, Medicago sativa)
phenotype: Transgenic alfalfa overexpressing MsSN1 showed increased antimicrobial activity against virulent fungal strains (Phoma medicaginis CT1 and Colletotrichum trifolii CT2) without affecting nitrogen-fixing bacterial strains of alfalfa origin.
mechanism: MsSN1 is a component of the constitutive defense barrier in plant cell walls, acting as an antimicrobial peptide that inhibits fungal spore germination and bacterial growth while sparing symbiotic rhizobia from alfalfa.

genes: gusAINT (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Reduction of GUS enzyme activity by 9-fold and gusA mRNA expression by 4.5-fold in transgenic banana in vitro plantlets.
mechanism: RNAi-induced gene silencing via siRNA production targeting gusAINT mRNA.

genes: gusAINT (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: No significant reduction in GUS activity or mRNA expression in transgenic banana in vitro plantlets.
mechanism: RNAi-induced gene silencing via siRNA production targeting gusAINT mRNA.

genes: OsPsbS1 (promoter region, Oryza sativa japonica), OsPsbS1 (promoter region, Oryza sativa indica)
phenotype: Japonica-type promoter showed higher GUS activity than indica-type promoter in rice calli under high light conditions.
mechanism: The japonica promoter contains a MULE-like element which enhances promoter activity, leading to increased GUS expression.

genes: CCA1 (Circadian Clock Associated 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CCA1 leads to altered lipid metabolism and oil body retention in 5-day-old seedlings, with increased triacylglycerol (TAG) content compared to wild-type Col-0.
mechanism: CCA1 overexpression disrupts diurnal regulation of lipid metabolism genes (e.g., SDP1, ACX2, KAT2), leading to reduced lipid catabolism and TAG accumulation.

genes: BrGRF8 (Brassica rapa, overexpression)
phenotype: Overexpression of BrGRF8 increases leaf and other organ sizes in Arabidopsis thaliana by enhancing cell proliferation.
mechanism: BrGRF8 regulates cell proliferation rather than cell enlargement, leading to increased organ size.

plant_species: Allium porrum, Nicotiana benthamiana, Arabidopsis thaliana
genes: RabA1d (Rab GTPase involved in vesicle trafficking, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GFP-RabA1d localizes to vesicular structures at trans-Golgi network compartment, accumulates in BFA compartments, and participates in cell plate formation and root hair tip growth
mechanism: RabA1d is involved in vesicle trafficking, membrane recycling, and spatio-temporal regulation of vesicle trafficking during cytokinesis and root hair elongation

genes: Rpi-blb2 (resistance gene, Solanum lycopersicum, native)
phenotype: Overexpression of Rpi-blb2 confers resistance to P. infestans in N. benthamiana, with 3.3–3.5% infection area compared to 10–32.5% in control plants.
mechanism: Rpi-blb2-mediated hypersensitive cell death (HCD) suppresses P. infestans colonization by recognizing the effector AVRblb2.

genes: Rpi-blb2 (resistance gene, Solanum lycopersicum, synthetic), Rpi-blb2 N-terminal deletion (synthetic), Rpi-blb2 C-terminal deletion (synthetic)
phenotype: Full-length Rpi-blb2 induces HCD in N. benthamiana when co-expressed with AVRblb2, while N- and C-terminal deletions do not trigger HCD.
mechanism: Both CC and LRR domains of Rpi-blb2 are required for AVRblb2 recognition and HCD induction.

genes: NbSGT1 (signaling component, Nicotiana benthamiana, synthetic), NbEDS1 (signaling component, Nicotiana benthamiana, synthetic), NbNDR1 (signaling component, Nicotiana benthamiana, synthetic)
phenotype: Silencing NbSGT1 suppresses Rpi-blb2-mediated HCD in response to AVRblb2, while silencing NbEDS1 or NbNDR1 does not.
mechanism: SGT1 is required for Rpi-blb2-mediated HCD signaling, whereas EDS1 and NDR1 are not.

genes: At1g68810 (ABS5/T5L1, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of At1g68810 causes upward leaf curling, increased vascular bundle cell numbers, and increased secondary inflorescence numbers in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ABS5/T5L1 overexpression disrupts auxin homeostasis and vascular development, leading to altered leaf morphology and increased secondary inflorescences.

genes: At1g68810 (ABS5/T5L1, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Epidermal-specific overexpression of At1g68810 under the AtML1 promoter causes upward leaf curling and altered auxin distribution in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ABS5/T5L1 overexpression in the epidermis disrupts auxin homeostasis, leading to leaf curvature and vascular development changes.

genes: At2g32460 (ABS7/MYB101, MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of At2g32460 causes upward leaf curling and altered cotyledon vein patterns in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ABS7/MYB101 overexpression disrupts leaf polarity and vascular development, leading to leaf curling and increased vascular complexity.

genes: At2g32460 (ABS7/MYB101, MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Epidermal-specific overexpression of At2g32460 under the AtML1 promoter causes upward leaf curling in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ABS7/MYB101 overexpression in the epidermis alters leaf polarity and vascular development, leading to leaf curvature.

genes: PAP1 (PAP1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PAP1 increases anthocyanin/phenylpropanoid accumulation and herbivore resistance in tobacco
mechanism: PAP1 activates phenylpropanoid/flavonoid pathway, increasing cyanidin-3-rutinoside, kaempferol 3-O-rutinoside, rutin, and chlorogenic acid levels which deter Spodoptera litura larvae

genes: CPC (CPC, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CPC significantly reduces anthocyanin accumulation in cotyledons, leaves, and stems of tomato.
mechanism: CPC regulates gene expression of the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway (PAL, CHS, DFR, ANS), leading to reduced expression and anthocyanin accumulation.

genes: GL3 (GL3, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GL3 significantly increases anthocyanin accumulation in cotyledons, leaves, and stems of tomato.
mechanism: GL3 regulates gene expression of the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway (PAL, CHS, DFR, ANS), leading to increased expression and anthocyanin accumulation.

genes: atzA-22-4 (name, atrazine chlorohydrolase, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of atzA-22-4 increases atrazine tolerance in Oryza sativa, with transgenic lines showing significantly higher germination rates (95.2–100% vs 0–42.2% in controls) and improved seedling growth under 150 µM atrazine.
mechanism: AtzA-22-4 degrades atrazine into hydroxyatrazine, reducing herbicide toxicity and maintaining chlorophyll content (chlorophyll a: 12.25×A663.6–2.55×A646.6; chlorophyll b: 20.31×A646.6–4.91×A663.6) under atrazine stress.

genes: GmFLD (FLOWERING LOCUS D homolog, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmFLD in Arabidopsis thaliana results in early flowering (24.8 vs 28.7 days to visible buds in wild type) and reduced FLC transcript levels while up-regulating floral integrators FT and SOC1.
mechanism: GmFLD represses FLC transcription, leading to increased expression of floral integrators FT and SOC1. Chromatin analysis shows decreased H3K4me3 and H4 acetylation at the FLC locus.

genes: GmLDL2 (LSD1-LIKE2 homolog, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmLDL2 in Arabidopsis thaliana does not significantly alter flowering time (28.1 vs 28.7 days to visible buds in wild type).
mechanism: NA

genes: pds (photodamage gene, Nicotiana attenuata)
phenotype: Photobleaching due to RNAi-mediated silencing of pds gene
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing of pds reduces photosynthetic pigment synthesis

genes: ipt (cytokinin synthase, Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Increased cytokinin (CK) levels leading to growth effects
mechanism: Ectopic expression of ipt from A. tumefaciens increases cytokinin biosynthesis

genes: GLA1 (NaGLA1, lipid hydrolase, Nicotiana attenuata)
phenotype: Reduced accumulation of 9-OH-18:2 and other oxylipins by ~20-fold in P. parasitica-infected leaves compared to wild-type plants
mechanism: GLA1 supplies 18:3 to 9-LOX for the biogenesis of 9-OH-18:2, which modulates defense responses against pathogens

genes: CrChlI (protoporphyrin IX magnesium chelatase, Ceratopteris richardii, Ceratopteris richardii)
phenotype: Systemic silencing of CrChlI results in a 7-fold decrease in endogenous transcript abundance and a colorless cell phenotype in most gametophyte cells, including meristem and gametangia.
mechanism: The hairpin-forming dsRNA triggers RNA interference, leading to sequence-specific degradation of CrChlI transcripts.

genes: CrChlI (protoporphyrin IX magnesium chelatase, Ceratopteris richardii, Ceratopteris richardii)
phenotype: A plasmid containing the CrChlI cDNA insert alone (without a promoter) induced silencing, resulting in a colorless phenotype in ~14% of GUS-positive gametophytes.
mechanism: The cDNA insert alone is sufficient to trigger RNA interference, likely through transcription of dsRNA in the absence of a plant promoter.

genes: CrFtsZ (filamentous temperature sensitive Z, Ceratopteris richardii, Ceratopteris richardii)
phenotype: Silencing of CrFtsZ results in gametophytes with cells containing larger and fewer chloroplasts (as few as three per cell) compared to non-bombarded gametophytes with >50 chloroplasts per cell.
mechanism: The hairpin-forming dsRNA triggers RNA interference, leading to reduced CrFtsZ expression and altered chloroplast division.

genes: CrUrod (uroporphyrin dehydrogenase, Ceratopteris richardii, Ceratopteris richardii)
phenotype: Silencing of CrUrod results in ~60% of gametophytes developing one or two discrete necrotic lesions within one week of bombardment, consisting of several adjacent colorless cells that eventually died.
mechanism: The intron-antisense construct triggers RNA interference, leading to reduced CrUrod expression and accumulation of toxic uroporphyrin upon light exposure.

genes: PIP2a (At3g53420, plasma membrane water channel protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Visualization of Arabidopsis egg and central cell plasma membranes with GFP-PIP2a
mechanism: PIP2a labels plasma membrane surfaces of female gametes

genes: PIP2a (At3g53420, plasma membrane water channel protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Visualization of Arabidopsis central cell plasma membrane with GFP-PIP2a
mechanism: PIP2a labels plasma membrane surfaces of female gametes

genes: GCS1 (GCS1, sperm cell membrane protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Visualization of sperm cell membrane with GCS1-GFP (GPP line)
mechanism: GCS1 localizes to sperm cell membrane components

genes: HTR10 (At1g19890, sperm nucleus marker, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Visualization of sperm nuclei with HTR10-mRFP in Arabidopsis
mechanism: HTR10 promoter drives mRFP expression in sperm nuclei

genes: Dendra2 (Dendra2, photoconvertible fluorescent protein, pDendra2-C vector)
phenotype: Dendra2 is expressed in whole protonemata and localized in the cytoplasm and the nuclei of Physcomitrella patens
mechanism: NA

genes: ASR1 (ASR1, abscisic acid-responsive gene, Solanum esculentum)
phenotype: Overexpression of ASR1 increases water-stress tolerance in tomato plants, with significantly higher survival rates after 22 days of dehydration and 17 days of rewatering compared to wild-type and antisense lines.
mechanism: ASR1 likely enhances water-stress tolerance through increased transcription of ASR1-regulated genes and chaperone activity, stabilizing proteins under stress conditions.

genes: ASR1 (ASR1, abscisic acid-responsive gene, Solanum esculentum)
phenotype: Antisense ASR1 plants show hypersensitivity to water stress, with variable responses across lines; some lines exhibit significantly reduced survival compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: ASR1 knockdown likely reduces the expression of ASR1-regulated genes and diminishes chaperone activity, impairing stress response mechanisms.

genes: BraLTP1 (BraLTP1, non-specific lipid-transfer protein, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Overexpression of BraLTP1 in Brassica napus results in distinct green leaf phenotype with reduced epicuticular wax, humpy and wrinkled leaf surfaces, abaxial edge-curling, and smaller plant size. Leaf water loss increases significantly, and cell proliferation in mesophyll tissue increases with elevated cytokinin levels. Flower development shows elongated carpels, outward-bending stamens, and altered sepal morphology.
mechanism: BraLTP1 overexpression disrupts cuticular wax deposition, increases cell proliferation via cytokinin pathway activation (elevated IPT3 expression), and alters flower development through regulation of ABC model genes (reduced AP1/AP2/AP3/PI expression, increased AG/SPT/LEUNIG expression).

genes: PdUGPase2 (PdUGPase2, UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase 2, Populus deltoides)
phenotype: Overexpression of PdUGPase2 increases leaf area and leaf-to-shoot biomass ratio but decreases shoot and root growth in Populus deltoides.
mechanism: PdUGPase2 is involved in tightly coupled primary and secondary metabolic pathways, affecting growth and metabolism beyond cell wall biosynthesis.

genes: OsABCG15 (full-length, sporopollenin transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Restoration of fertility in osabcg15 mutant through complementation with OsABCG15
mechanism: OsABCG15 is essential for anther cuticle and pollen exine development, exporting sporopollenin precursors from tapetal cells

genes: AtUSPL1 (At1g49320, BURP-domain containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of AtUSPL1 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: uidA (GUS, β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of GUS reporter gene under AtUSPL1 promoter in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtPSS1 (AtPSS1, kinesin-1 like protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transformation of the Atpss1-1 mutant with a 5 kb genomic region containing the AtPSS1 coding and regulatory sequences restored pollen viability (7 independent transformants)
mechanism: NA

genes: EIN3 (ethylene-insensitive 3, transcription factor, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of EIN3-FLAG in ein3 eil1 ebf1 ebf2 quadruple mutant (iE/qm) seedlings confers salt tolerance, with survival rates over 90% under 200 mM NaCl treatment.
mechanism: EIN3-FLAG accumulation is induced by estradiol, leading to enhanced salt tolerance through EIN3/EIL1-dependent pathways.

genes: EBF1 (ethylene response factor), EBF2 (ethylene response factor)
phenotype: Overexpression of EBF1-MYC and EBF2-MYC in Col-0 allows monitoring of EBF1/EBF2 protein degradation under salt stress.
mechanism: Salt treatment promotes EBF1/EBF2 protein degradation in an EIN2-independent manner, leading to EIN3 stabilization.

genes: EIN3 (ethylene-insensitive 3)
phenotype: 5xEBS:GUS activity increases under salt stress in Col-0 and ein2-5 backgrounds, indicating EIN3 transcriptional activity.
mechanism: Salt treatment enhances EIN3 protein accumulation and transcriptional activity, leading to increased GUS expression.

genes: SIED1 (salt-induced and EIN3/EIL1-dependent gene 1)
phenotype: pSIED1:GUS activity is higher in EIN3ox and lower in ein3eil1, confirming EIN3-dependent regulation of SIED1.
mechanism: EIN3 directly binds to the SIED1 promoter, regulating its expression under salt stress.

genes: EIL1 (ethylene-insensitive-like 1)
phenotype: Overexpression of EIL1-GFP in Col-0 and ein2-5 backgrounds increases salt tolerance, with enhanced EIL1 protein accumulation.
mechanism: EIL1 protein stabilization under salt stress contributes to EIN3/EIL1-dependent salt tolerance.

genes: MHZ4 (LOC_Os01g03750, chloroplast-localized membrane protein homologous to Arabidopsis ABA4, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Rescued the enhanced coleoptile elongation and reduced root inhibition phenotypes of mhz4 in the presence of ethylene.
mechanism: MHZ4 is required for ethylene-induced ABA accumulation, which mediates root growth inhibition.

genes: MHZ4 (LOC_Os01g03750, chloroplast-localized membrane protein homologous to Arabidopsis ABA4, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: GUS staining revealed MHZ4 promoter activity in roots, coleoptiles, and vascular tissues of rice seedlings.
mechanism: MHZ4 is expressed in multiple tissues, including roots, coleoptiles, and vascular systems.

genes: At4g19420 (complementation, Arabidopsis thaliana, native promoter and genomic sequence)
phenotype: Complementation of At4g19420 rescues the mutant phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: At4g19420 modulates wall acetate levels in leaves.

genes: PAE9 (At5g23870.1, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana, coding sequence)
phenotype: Overexpression of PAE9 in the pae9-1 background restores wall acetate levels to wild-type in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PAE9 modulates leaf wall acetate levels by acting as a pectin acetylesterase.

genes: PAE9 (At5g23870.1, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana, coding sequence with 6X His tag)
phenotype: Overexpression of PAE9 with a 6X His tag in Arabidopsis thaliana restores wall acetate levels to wild-type.
mechanism: PAE9 modulates leaf wall acetate levels by acting as a pectin acetylesterase.

genes: PAE8 (overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana, coding sequence with 6X His tag)
phenotype: Overexpression of PAE8 with a 6X His tag in Arabidopsis thaliana restores wall acetate levels to wild-type.
mechanism: PAE8 modulates leaf wall acetate levels by acting as a pectin acetylesterase.

genes: P19 (overexpression, Nicotiana benthamiana, gene silencing suppressor)
phenotype: Overexpression of P19 in Nicotiana benthamiana enhances gene silencing suppression during transient expression experiments.
mechanism: P19 suppresses gene silencing to facilitate transient expression of target genes.

genes: PpPPR_63 (PpPPR_63, nuclear-localized PRORP2/3 homolog, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: Complementation of PpPPR_63 KO mutant with full-length PpPPR_63 restores wild-type phenotype, including normal protonemal colony size and leaf regeneration.
mechanism: PpPPR_63 functions in nuclear pre-tRNA processing and is required for normal plant growth and branch formation of protonemata.

genes: PpPPR_63 (PpPPR_63, nuclear-localized PRORP2/3 homolog, Physcomitrella patens)
gene_construct: nptII cassette inserted into 4th intron of PpPPR_63
phenotype: PpPPR_63 KO mutants (Δ63) display smaller protonemal colonies and abnormal regeneration from leaves with defective sub-apical cell growth.
mechanism: PpPPR_63 is required for normal plant growth and branch formation of protonemata, likely through roles in nuclear RNA processing.

genes: PpPPR_63 (PpPPR_63, nuclear-localized PRORP2/3 homolog, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: PpPPR_63-GFP fusion protein localizes to nuclei in protonemal cells, buds, and young leaves but not mature leaves.
mechanism: PpPPR_63 is a nuclear-localized PRORP homolog, confirmed by GFP fluorescence in nuclei of transgenic moss.

genes: PpPPR_67 (PpPPR_67, organelle-localized PRORP1 homolog, Physcomitrella patens)
gene_construct: nptII cassette inserted into 5th exon of PpPPR_67
phenotype: PpPPR_67 KO mutant (Δ67) shows no significant difference in protonemal colony size compared to wild type.
mechanism: PpPPR_67 has redundant functions with PpPPR_104 in organelle tRNA processing, but single knockout is viable.

genes: PpPPR_104 (PpPPR_104, organelle-localized PRORP1 homolog, Physcomitrella patens)
gene_construct: nptII cassette inserted into 4th exon of PpPPR_104
phenotype: PpPPR_104 KO mutant (Δ104) displays smaller protonemal colonies due to reduced caulonemal filament induction and significant reduction in chloroplast tRNAArg (ACG) levels.
mechanism: PpPPR_104 is essential for processing chloroplast pre-tRNAArg (ACG), and its knockout leads to reduced mature tRNAArg (ACG) accumulation.

genes: PpPPR_67 (PpPPR_67, organelle-localized PRORP1 homolog, Physcomitrella patens)
gene_construct: N-terminal PpPPR_67-GFP fusion under NA promoter
phenotype: N-terminal PpPPR_67-GFP fusion protein localizes to mitochondria and chloroplasts in protonemata.
mechanism: PpPPR_67 contains a transit peptide targeting it to organelles, confirmed by GFP fluorescence co-localizing with mitochondria and chloroplasts.

genes: PpPPR_104 (PpPPR_104, organelle-localized PRORP1 homolog, Physcomitrella patens)
gene_construct: N-terminal PpPPR_104-GFP fusion under NA promoter
phenotype: N-terminal PpPPR_104-GFP fusion protein localizes to mitochondria and chloroplasts in protonemata.
mechanism: PpPPR_104 contains a transit peptide targeting it to organelles, confirmed by GFP fluorescence co-localizing with mitochondria and chloroplasts.

genes: Cre (Cre recombinase, full-length, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of Cre leads to GUS activity in transgenic tobacco hairy roots.
mechanism: Cre recombinase mediates site-specific recombination between loxP sites, resulting in excision of the transgene fragment and GUS expression.

genes: NCre (Cre recombinase N-terminal fragment, amino acids 1-59, synthetic) with nuclear localization signal (NLS)
phenotype: Overexpression of NLS-NCre alone does not result in GUS activity in transgenic tobacco hairy roots.
mechanism: NLS-NCre requires complementation with NLS-CCre to reconstitute functional Cre recombinase for site-specific recombination.

genes: CCre (Cre recombinase C-terminal fragment, amino acids 60-343, synthetic) with nuclear localization signal (NLS)
phenotype: Overexpression of NLS-CCre alone does not result in GUS activity in transgenic tobacco hairy roots.
mechanism: NLS-CCre requires complementation with NLS-NCre to reconstitute functional Cre recombinase for site-specific recombination.

genes: PaSOD (Copper-Zinc Superoxide Dismutase, Potentilla atrosanguinea, Potentilla atrosanguinea), RaAPX (Ascorbate Peroxidase, Rheum australe, Rheum australe)
phenotype: Transgenic Arabidopsis over-expressing PaSOD and RaAPX show enhanced cold tolerance with increased root growth, biomass, and reduced electrolyte leakage under cold stress.
mechanism: Overexpression of PaSOD and RaAPX increases antioxidant enzyme activity, reducing ROS accumulation and membrane damage, while inducing lignin biosynthesis in vascular bundles.

genes: At3g50990 (PRX36, class III peroxidase, Arabidopsis thaliana), At5g66390 (PRX72, class III peroxidase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PRX36-GFP localized to the cell wall, PRX72-GFP localized to the cytosol in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: GFP fusion protein used for subcellular localization analysis

genes: At3g50990 (PRX36, class III peroxidase, Arabidopsis thaliana), At5g66390 (PRX72, class III peroxidase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PRX36-GFP localized to the cell wall, PRX72-GFP localized to the cytosol in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: GFP fusion protein used for subcellular localization analysis

genes: ShTRAIL (soluble human TRAIL, recombinant gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of ShTRAIL in N. tabacum cells inhibits A549 cell proliferation by ~40-50% in MTT assays, with ER-targeted ShTRAIL showing higher stability and production levels (up to 24.5 μg/g fresh weight at 12 weeks).
mechanism: ER-targeted ShTRAIL forms trimers (facilitated by ER chaperones and ascorbate buffer's antioxidant properties), which are required for antiproliferative activity. ER localization protects ShTRAIL from proteolytic degradation compared to cytoplasmic expression.

genes: GhMYB80 (Gossypium hirsutum, GhMYB80MD), 32R (Arabidopsis thaliana, 32R)
phenotype: Induces male sterility in Arabidopsis, with 50% of transgenic lines showing more than 75% infertility
mechanism: The 32R EAR motif fused to the truncated GhMYB80MD represses its activity, leading to male sterility by disrupting tapetum and pollen development

genes: BnMYB80 (Brassica napus, C gene), 32R (Arabidopsis thaliana, 32R)
phenotype: Induces male sterility in Arabidopsis, with 57% of transgenic lines showing 0% fertility when driven by a single 700bp BnMYB80 promoter
mechanism: The 32R EAR motif fused to BnMYB80 represses its activity, leading to male sterility by disrupting tapetum and pollen development

genes: BnMYB80 (Brassica napus, C gene), 32R (Arabidopsis thaliana, 32R)
phenotype: Induces male sterility in Arabidopsis, with 30% of transgenic lines showing 0% fertility when driven by a single 700bp BnMYB80 promoter
mechanism: The 32R EAR motif fused to BnMYB80 represses its activity, leading to male sterility by disrupting tapetum and pollen development

genes: BnMYB80 (Brassica napus, C gene), 32R (Arabidopsis thaliana, 32R)
phenotype: Induces male sterility in Arabidopsis, with 59% of transgenic lines showing 0% fertility when driven by two copies of the 700bp BnMYB80 promoter
mechanism: The 32R EAR motif fused to BnMYB80 represses its activity, leading to male sterility by disrupting tapetum and pollen development

genes: R3a (resistance gene, R3a, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of R3a under CaMV35S promoter allows specific mutation and shuffling of the R3a LRR domain for enhanced AVR3aEM recognition.
mechanism: The CaMV35S promoter drives expression of R3a, enabling targeted mutagenesis and shuffling of the LRR domain to improve recognition of AVR3aEM.

genes: R3a (resistance gene, R3a, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of R3a under its native promoter enables protraction of cell death responses for discrimination of R3a* variants.
mechanism: The R3a native promoter regulates R3a expression, delaying cell death responses to facilitate discrimination of R3a* variants.

genes: R3a (resistance gene, R3a, Arabidopsis thaliana), Rd2-1 (mutant variant of R3a), Rd3-1 (mutant variant of R3a), Rd4-1 (mutant variant of R3a)
phenotype: Transgenic potato plants expressing R3a* variants under R3a native regulatory elements show resistance to P. infestans isolates expressing AVR3aKI but not AVR3aEM.
mechanism: R3a* variants under native regulatory elements confer resistance to AVR3aKI-expressing isolates by recapitulating the mechanistic processes of wild-type R3a recognition of AVR3aKI.

genes: SbMT-2 (metallothionein 2 gene involved in ROS scavenging and metal ion sequestration, Sorghum bicolor)
phenotype: Overexpression of SbMT-2 increases stress tolerance in tobacco, with enhanced growth parameters (shoot/root length, fresh/dry weight), higher chlorophyll content, and reduced ROS accumulation under salt, osmotic, and metal stress conditions.
mechanism: SbMT-2 enhances ROS scavenging, reduces lipid peroxidation, and sequesters metal ions (Zn, Cu, Cd), maintaining ionic homeostasis and membrane stability under stress.

genes: CmbHLH1 (CmbHLH1, bHLH transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: GFP expression in the nucleus of onion epidermal cells
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (GUS, β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity significantly enhanced under Fe deficiency or ABA treatment
mechanism: NA

genes: CmbHLH1 (CmbHLH1, bHLH transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Reduced Fe accumulation and root rhizosphere acidification under Fe deficiency
mechanism: CmbHLH1 down-regulation decreases CmHA expression, reducing root acidification and Fe uptake

genes: NtCAS1 (cycloartenol synthase, Nicotiana tabacum), NbLAS1 (lanosterol synthase, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: PVX::CAS1 plants exhibit reduced stature, leaf bleaching, wilting, and necrosis; PVX::LAS1 plants show no significant phenotype.
mechanism: VIGS-mediated gene silencing disrupts CAS1 and LAS1 function, leading to accumulation of 2,3-oxidosqualene and altered sterol biosynthesis.

genes: β-1,3-glucanase (β-1,3-glucanase, endogenous gene, Linum usitatissimum)
phenotype: Overexpression of β-1,3-glucanase increases resistance to Fusarium oxysporum and Fusarium culmorum infection in flax by ~3-fold.
mechanism: Demethylation of CCGG sequences in the β-1,3-glucanase gene and total DNA methylation reduction activate gene expression, leading to increased β-1,3-glucanase and chitinase activity.

genes: Gm06g01650.1 (PPC domain, Glycine max AHL PPC domain, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of Glycine max AHL PPC domain in Arabidopsis thaliana results in longer hypocotyls in white light compared to wild-type controls.
mechanism: The overexpression of the PPC domain may disturb the growth suppression roles of Arabidopsis thaliana AHL genes, leading to the long-hypocotyl phenotype.

genes: AC1 (Rep, replication associated protein, Indian cassava mosaic virus), AC2 (TrAP, transcriptional activator protein, Indian cassava mosaic virus), AC3 (Ren, replication enhancer protein, Indian cassava mosaic virus), AV1 (Coat protein, Indian cassava mosaic virus), AC4 (Indian cassava mosaic virus)
phenotype: Transgenic plants show resistance to ICMV-Dha and ICMV-SG geminiviruses with no detectable virus in resistant lines
mechanism: RNA interference (RNAi) silencing of five key viral genes (AC1, AC2, AC3, AV1, AC4) via hairpin dsRNA

genes: Spoli-DHR (diuretic hormone receptor, Spodoptera littoralis, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic tobacco plants expressing Spoli-DHR dsRNA cause 100% mortality in Spodoptera littoralis larvae within 7 days of feeding, compared to 25% in wild type plants.
mechanism: Hairpin dsRNA formation in plants triggers RNAi-mediated silencing of Spoli-DHR gene in larvae, disrupting diuretic hormone signaling and causing lethargy, reduced feeding, and mortality.

genes: FLS2 (flagellin-sensitive 2, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), FLS2-NoKinase (truncated FLS2 lacking intracellular domain, Arabidopsis thaliana), EFR (elongation factor receptor, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: FLS2-NoKinase interacts with BAK1 in the presence of flg22 in Nicotiana benthamiana
mechanism: FLS2 ectodomain mediates interaction with BAK1 independent of kinase domains

genes: EFR (elongation factor receptor, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: EFR glycosylation defects observed in Nicotiana benthamiana and Arabidopsis efr− plants
mechanism: Mutations in EFR LRR domain disrupt glycosylation and interaction with BAK1

genes: ARF3 (ARF3, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ARF3∷ARF3-GFP transgene rescues floral determinacy and gynoecium developmental defects of ag-10 arf3-29
mechanism: ARF3 represses WUS expression to confer floral meristem determinacy

genes: WUS (WUSCHEL, floral meristem regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: WUS∷DsRed-N7 reporter line shows coexpression with ARF3 in early flower development
mechanism: ARF3 and WUS coexpression in the organizing center of floral meristems

genes: ARF3 (ARF3, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: WUS∷ARF3m-GFP∷WUS3' transgene fails to rescue FM determinacy defects of ag-10 arf3-29
mechanism: ARF3 spatial distribution patterns are critical for FM determinacy function

genes: ARF3 (ARF3, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ARF3∷ARF3m-GFP transgene partially rescues FM determinacy defects of ag-10 arf3-29
mechanism: ARF3 spatial distribution patterns are critical for FM determinacy function

genes: AG (AGAMOUS, floral organ identity gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S∷AG-GR transgene induces AG-GR fusion protein activity on target genes after dexamethasone treatment
mechanism: AG modulates ARF3 expression indirectly

genes: AP2m3 (APETALA2 mutant, floral meristem regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S∷AP2m3-GR transgene induces AP2m3-GR fusion protein activity on target genes after dexamethasone treatment
mechanism: AP2 represses ARF3 expression to mediate FM determinacy

genes: AtVTL1 (AtVTL1, vacuolar Fe transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtVTL2 (AtVTL2, vacuolar Fe transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Localization of AtVTL1 and AtVTL2 to the vacuolar membrane in onion epidermis cells, with AtVTL2 also showing cytoplasmic and plasma membrane localization.
mechanism: GFP fluorescence co-localized with the vacuolar marker, indicating vacuolar membrane localization for AtVTL1 and partial localization for AtVTL2.

genes: AtVTL1 (AtVTL1, vacuolar Fe transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the nramp3/nramp4 double mutant, leading to increased root growth and 40-60% higher Fe content in seeds compared to wild type.
mechanism: Over-expression of AtVTL1 increased vacuolar Fe storage, compensating for impaired Fe efflux in the nramp3/nramp4 mutant.

genes: AtVTL2 (AtVTL2, vacuolar Fe transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the nramp3/nramp4 double mutant, leading to increased root growth and 40-60% higher Fe content in seeds compared to wild type.
mechanism: Over-expression of AtVTL2 increased vacuolar Fe storage, compensating for impaired Fe efflux in the nramp3/nramp4 mutant.

genes: AtVTL5 (AtVTL5, vacuolar Fe transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the nramp3/nramp4 double mutant, leading to increased root growth and 40-60% higher Fe content in seeds compared to wild type.
mechanism: Over-expression of AtVTL5 increased vacuolar Fe storage, compensating for impaired Fe efflux in the nramp3/nramp4 mutant.

genes: AtVTL1 (AtVTL1, vacuolar Fe transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the vit1-1 mutant, restoring root growth to greater than wild-type length under Fe-deficient conditions.
mechanism: Over-expression of AtVTL1 increased vacuolar Fe storage, compensating for mis-localization of Fe in the vit1-1 mutant.

genes: PsnAP1-1 (PsnAP1-1, AP1 homolog from Populus simonii × P. nigra, Populus simonii × P. nigra), PsnAP1-2 (PsnAP1-2, AP1 homolog from Populus simonii × P. nigra, Populus simonii × P. nigra)
phenotype: Overexpression of PsnAP1-1 and PsnAP1-2 in transgenic tobacco and Arabidopsis causes early flowering (10-40 days post-sowing vs. 65+ days in wild-type), dwarfism (aerial height <15 cm vs. >60 cm in wild-type), reduced leaf count (<8 leaves vs. >15 in wild-type), and altered floral morphology (terminal flowers, fused flowers, curled leaves). Transgenic tobacco also shows accelerated lignification and increased chlorophyll content.
mechanism: PsnAP1-1 and PsnAP1-2 promote transition from vegetative to reproductive development by inducing flowering-related genes (NsMADS3, NtMADS4, NtMADS5, NtMADS11, NtSOC1, NtFUL) and accelerating inflorescence meristem formation. Overexpression enhances photosynthesis and chloroplast development but does not complement ap1-10 mutant floral organ defects.

genes: CjAG (C-function gene, ortholog of AGAMOUS, Camellia japonica)
phenotype: Overexpression of CjAG in Arabidopsis results in reduced petals, increased stamens, and abnormal sepal development with pistil-like features
mechanism: CjAG possesses conserved C-class function of determining stamen and carpel identity by antagonizing A-function genes

genes: MYBR1 (AtMYBR1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MYBR1 delays leaf senescence in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MYBR1 represses ABA-responsive genes and stress-related genes, leading to delayed senescence.

genes: GUS (β-GLUCURONIDASE, synthetic)
phenotype: MYBR1 promoter drives GUS expression in tissues after wounding and during senescence in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MYBR1 promoter activity is induced by wounding and senescence, indicating its role in stress and developmental responses.

genes: HYR (Os03g02650, transcription factor involved in photosynthesis and drought tolerance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of HYR increases photosynthesis and drought tolerance in rice.
mechanism: HYR regulates photosynthesis and carbon metabolism, enhancing drought tolerance.

genes: HYR (Os03g02650, TAP-tagged transcription factor for gene regulation studies, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Enables chromatin immunoprecipitation to study HYR's gene regulation.
mechanism: TAP tag allows for affinity purification of HYR-bound chromatin.

genes: Pina (Sina, secaloindoline a, Triticosecale Wittmack), Pinb (Sinb, secaloindoline b, Triticosecale Wittmack)
phenotype: Silencing of Sin genes resulted in a substantial decrease of secaloindoline a and secaloindoline b content, with total seed protein content about 6% lower in silenced lines compared to controls. Grain hardness index ranged from 22 to 56 in silent lines vs. 37 to 49 in controls, showing increased softness.
mechanism: RNAi-based silencing of Sin genes reduced their transcripts and secaloindoline protein levels, but did not affect grain hardness. The lack of correlation between transcript levels and hardness suggests other factors control this trait in triticale.

genes: DAG1 (promoter, reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: DAG1:GUS expression during embryo development in globular, heart, torpedo, and bent cotyledon stages
mechanism: DAG1 promoter activity in vascular tissue during embryogenesis

genes: DAG1 (chimaeric protein, complementation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of dag1gai-t6 embryo defects and restoration of normal germination rates
mechanism: Expression of DAG1-HA chimaeric protein rescues embryo development in dag1gai-t6 double mutant

genes: PIN1 (PIN-FORMED 1, auxin efflux carrier, Arabidopsis thaliana), PIN2 (PIN-FORMED 2, auxin efflux carrier, Arabidopsis thaliana), PIN7 (PIN-FORMED 7, auxin efflux carrier, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Root hair-specific overexpression of wild-type PIN1, PIN2, or PIN7 inhibits root hair growth by depleting auxin levels in root hair cells.
mechanism: Wild-type PINs localize to plasma membrane (PM) and mediate auxin efflux, reducing auxin levels in root hair cells. Phosphorylation-defective mutants fail to localize to PM, leading to less auxin efflux and restored root hair growth.

genes: PIN2 (PIN-FORMED 2, auxin efflux carrier, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 3m1 mutation in PIN2 leads to undetectable protein levels in root hair cells, with partial restoration by wortmannin treatment.
mechanism: 3m1 phosphorylation-defective mutation causes rapid degradation of PIN2 via vacuolar lytic pathway. Wortmannin inhibits this degradation, restoring protein levels.

genes: PIN2 (PIN-FORMED 2, auxin efflux carrier, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: M3 mutation in PIN2 leads to undetectable protein levels in root hair cells, with partial restoration by wortmannin treatment.
mechanism: M3 phosphorylation-defective mutation causes rapid degradation of PIN2 via vacuolar lytic pathway. Wortmannin inhibits this degradation, restoring protein levels.

genes: At3g03150 (promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic), At3g03160 (promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic)
phenotype: GUS expression patterns in vegetative and reproductive tissues, including vascular tissue in leaves, hydathodes, abscission zones, and pollen
mechanism: Regulation by bidirectional promoter containing ABRE and CE3 elements for ABA and stress responses

genes: cry2Aa (cry2Aa, synthesized cry2Aa gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of cry2Aa in transgenic rice line T2A-1 confers high resistance against lepidopteran pests of rice.
mechanism: Cry2Aa protein expression enhances resistance against lepidopteran pests by targeting their gut epithelia.

genes: Pto (Pto kinase, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of Pto in N. benthamiana leads to programmed cell death when infiltrated with P. s. tabaci expressing AvrPto.
mechanism: Pto recognizes AvrPto, triggering effector-triggered immunity and programmed cell death.

genes: avrPto (AvrPto, Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato)
phenotype: Overexpression of AvrPto in N. benthamiana leads to programmed cell death when infiltrated with P. s. tabaci expressing Pto.
mechanism: AvrPto is recognized by Pto, triggering effector-triggered immunity and programmed cell death.

genes: Epk1 (SlEpk1, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of SlEpk1 compromises resistance to Pseudomonas syringae pv. tabaci (AvrPto), leading to increased disease symptoms and bacterial populations.
mechanism: SlEpk1 acts upstream of effector-triggered immunity-associated MAP kinase signaling.

genes: HAE (promoter, regulatory region, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (gene, β-glucuronidase reporter, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Altered expression pattern of abscission zone marker in as1 mutant flowers, with GUS expression in inverted V-shaped proximal regions of medial sepals and remaining petal/lateral sepal stubs
mechanism: HAE regulates abscission zone formation; loss of BP activity rescues abscission zone displacement in as1 flowers

genes: pHsp18 (Os.hsp18, heat shock protein 18, Oryza sativa), pHsp82 (Os.hsp82, heat shock protein 82, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of BP100.2 under pHsp18 promoter is incompatible with plant survival; overexpression under pHsp82 promoter results in phytotoxicity with reduced growth and leaf wilting after heat shock.
mechanism: BP100.2 is a cationic α-helical antimicrobial peptide with phytotoxic properties that disrupts cellular processes, leading to growth inhibition.

genes: pHsp18 (Os.hsp18, heat shock protein 18, Oryza sativa), pHsp82 (Os.hsp82, heat shock protein 82, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of DsRed-tag54 under pHsp18 and pHsp82 promoters results in heat-inducible expression of the reporter protein, with no phytotoxic effects observed.
mechanism: DsRed-tag54 is a fluorescent reporter protein used to monitor transgene expression; its expression under heat-shock promoters confirms inducible activity without toxicity.

genes: pHsp18 (Os.hsp18, heat shock protein 18, Oryza sativa), pHsp82 (Os.hsp82, heat shock protein 82, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of BP100-DsRed-tag54 under pHsp82 promoter results in accumulation of phytotoxic recombinant protein in ER-derived vesicles, with no significant reduction in plant viability.
mechanism: BP100-DsRed-tag54 accumulates in ER-derived vesicles, sequestering the phytotoxic peptide and allowing controlled expression without severe toxicity.

genes: pUbi (Zm.ubi, ubiquitin, Zea mays)
phenotype: Constitutive overexpression of DsRed-tag54 under pUbi promoter results in high-level expression of the reporter protein without phytotoxic effects.
mechanism: The constitutive pUbi promoter drives continuous expression of DsRed-tag54, serving as a control for heat-inducible promoters.

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene for OsARF16 expression, synthetic)
phenotype: OsARF16 promoter-GUS expression increased in root hairs and stele under cytokinin treatment, with 7.5-fold induction in roots
mechanism: OsARF16 promoter activity is upregulated by cytokinin, driving GUS expression in root hairs and shoots

genes: OsARF16 (OsARF16, auxin response factor, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: Complementation of osarf16 mutant restored cytokinin sensitivity in root and shoot growth, matching wild-type NIP under 6-BA treatment
mechanism: OsARF16 is required for cytokinin-mediated inhibition of root and shoot growth

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene for cell division activity, synthetic)
phenotype: Cytokinin treatment increased GUS activity in NIP root tips and primordia by 69.0% compared to osarf16 mutant
mechanism: pCYCB1;1:Dbox-GUS reporter indicates cytokinin-induced cell division activity in roots

genes: PpHsp16.4a (small heat shock protein 16.4, cytosolic class II, Physcomitrella patens), PpHsp16.4b (small heat shock protein 16.4, cytosolic class II, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: Targeted disruption of both PpHsp16.4a and PpHsp16.4b genes resulted in impaired or delayed recovery from heat, salt, and osmotic stress in Physcomitrella patens.
mechanism: PpHsp16.4 is involved in preventing protein aggregation and facilitating refolding during stress recovery, likely through chaperone activity.

genes: GSNOR1 (GSNO reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GSNOR1 increases nitrate reductase (NR) activity and alters nitrate assimilation, leading to elevated leaf nitrate levels and improved growth vigor compared to wild type and gsnor1 mutants.
mechanism: GSNOR1 overexpression enhances NR activity, which increases nitrate assimilation. This is coupled with reduced GSNOR1 activity under high nitrate conditions, allowing NO accumulation that inhibits GSNOR1 via S-nitrosylation, creating a feedback loop to regulate nitrogen homeostasis.

genes: GhSnRK2 (GhSnRK2, stress-related gene, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhSnRK2 in transgenic Arabidopsis plants increases drought and cold stress tolerance, with survival rates of 100% (L2), 94.4% (L4), and 88.9% (L1) under drought stress compared to 4.4% in wild-type plants, and significantly higher survival rates under freezing and cold stress conditions.
mechanism: GhSnRK2 enhances stress tolerance by regulating stress-responsive genes (AtABI5, AtABI3, AtP5CS1, AtRD29A, AtCBF1, AtRD29B), increasing proline accumulation, reducing stomatal aperture, and improving water use efficiency.

genes: GhSnRK2 (GhSnRK2, stress-related gene, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: The GhSnRK2-GFP fusion protein is localized to the nuclei and cytoplasm in onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: GhSnRK2 (GhSnRK2, stress-related gene, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Silencing of GhSnRK2 in cotton reduces drought stress tolerance, with survival rates of 34.66% (CRI99668) and 38.67% (CRI409) compared to 80% (WT) and 77.3% (vector control).
mechanism: GhSnRK2 silencing decreases proline accumulation, increases water loss, and reduces chlorophyll content under salt stress.

genes: PLAT1 (PLAT1, PLAT domain protein involved in abiotic stress tolerance, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PLAT1 increases abiotic stress tolerance (cold, drought, salt) and promotes plant growth in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PLAT1 functions as a direct target of ABF transcription factors in the ABA signaling pathway, enhancing stress tolerance and growth.

genes: ABF1 (ABF1, bZIP transcription factor involved in ABA signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ABF1 activates the PLAT1 promoter, increasing GUS activity in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: ABF1 binds to ABRE elements in the PLAT1 promoter, directly activating its expression.

genes: ABF2 (ABF2, bZIP transcription factor involved in ABA signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ABF2 activates the PLAT1 promoter, increasing GUS activity in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: ABF2 binds to ABRE elements in the PLAT1 promoter, directly activating its expression.

genes: ABF3 (ABF3, bZIP transcription factor involved in ABA signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ABF3 activates the PLAT1 promoter, increasing GUS activity in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: ABF3 binds to ABRE elements in the PLAT1 promoter, directly activating its expression.

genes: ABF4 (ABF4, bZIP transcription factor involved in ABA signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ABF4 activates the PLAT1 promoter, increasing GUS activity in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: ABF4 binds to ABRE elements in the PLAT1 promoter, directly activating its expression.

genes: GSTF8 (promoter, glutathione S-transferase F8, Arabidopsis thaliana), LUC (luciferase, firefly, synthetic), NPTII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, bacterial, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GSTF8::LUC transgene confers luminescence and kanamycin resistance in Arabidopsis thaliana. LUC expression is regulated by HSI2 PHD-like domain via H3K27me3 histone modifications.
mechanism: HSI2 PHD-like domain promotes H3K27me3 histone methylation marks on GSTF8::LUC transgene loci to repress transgene expression. Disruption of HSI2 PHD-like domain leads to increased LUC and NPTII expression with reduced H3K27me3 and increased H3K4me3/H3K36me3 marks.

genes: MsTPS1 (MsTPS1, terpene synthase, Mentha spicata), AtHMGR1 (AtHMGR1, 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MsTPS1 and AtHMGR1 in Nicotiana benthamiana leads to the production of sesquiterpenes such as β-caryophyllene.
mechanism: MsTPS1 catalyzes the formation of β-caryophyllene from farnesyl diphosphate, while AtHMGR1 enhances the mevalonate pathway to increase sesquiterpene precursor availability.

genes: AtHMGR1 (AtHMGR1, 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtHMGR1 in Nicotiana benthamiana enhances the mevalonate pathway, increasing sesquiterpene precursor availability when co-expressed with MsTPS1.
mechanism: AtHMGR1 is a rate-limiting enzyme in the mevalonate pathway, and its overexpression increases the production of farnesyl diphosphate, a precursor for sesquiterpene synthesis.

genes: TcANR (anthocyanidin reductase, Theobroma cacao), AtUbi (ubiquitin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complemented PA-deficient phenotype in Arabidopsis ban mutant seeds, reduced anthocyanidin levels in hypocotyls
mechanism: TcANR converts anthocyanidin to epicatechin, restoring PA synthesis in seeds and diverting metabolic flux from anthocyanin production

genes: TcANS (anthocyanidin synthase, Theobroma cacao), AtUbi (ubiquitin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restored anthocyanin synthesis in hypocotyls and PA accumulation in seeds of Arabidopsis ans (ldox) mutant
mechanism: TcANS complements the ans (ldox) mutant by restoring anthocyanin and PA biosynthesis through its dual role in both pathways

genes: TcLAR (leucoanthocyanidin reductase, Theobroma cacao), NtrRNA (ribosomal RNA, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Reduced anthocyanin levels (50% of wild type) and increased PA levels (5-fold higher than wild type) in tobacco flower petals
mechanism: TcLAR diverts metabolic flux from anthocyanin synthesis to PA synthesis by converting leucoanthocyanidin to catechin

genes: TcLAR (leucoanthocyanidin reductase, Theobroma cacao), AtUbi (ubiquitin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Elevated catechin (2-fold) and epicatechin levels in Arabidopsis ldox mutant siliques, increased total PA levels in seeds
mechanism: TcLAR converts leucoanthocyanidin to catechin in the ldox mutant background, with indirect epicatechin synthesis via unknown mechanism

genes: GtF3H (gentian F3H cDNA, functional, gentian)
phenotype: Overexpression of GtF3H in Crown White torenia recovers pink flower pigmentation, with 30 lines showing intense pink and 5 showing faint pink flowers
mechanism: GtF3H compensates for F3H deficiency caused by TORE1 insertion in Crown White, restoring anthocyanin biosynthesis

genes: At1g74120 (mTERF15, mitochondrial RNA-binding protein involved in nad2 intron 3 splicing, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of mterf15 mutant rescues growth and developmental defects including normal seed germination, leaf morphology, flowering, and seed production in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: mTERF15 functions as an RNA-binding protein required for nad2 intron 3 splicing and mitochondrial complex I activity. Disruption of mTERF15 causes defective mitochondrial membrane potential, impaired complex I activity, and widespread developmental defects.

genes: TAM (TAM, meiosis regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TAM leads to production of polyploid plants and abnormal meiotic products (dyads, triads) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: MeCu/ZnSOD (Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase, cassava, GenBank AY642137), MeAPX2 (ascorbate peroxidase, cassava, GenBank AY973622)
phenotype: Enhanced tolerance to oxidative stress (H2O2, methyl viologen) and chilling stress (4°C) with reduced lipid peroxidation, chlorophyll degradation, and H2O2 synthesis compared to wild type
mechanism: Simultaneous expression of cytosolic SOD and APX activated antioxidative defense mechanisms via cyclic ROS scavenging

genes: At-CHS (CHALCONE SYNTHASE, Arabidopsis thaliana), uidA (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Silencing of At-CHS reduces anthocyanin production and GUS activity in Arabidopsis thaliana, with silencing efficiency dependent on ihpRNA configuration
mechanism: ihpRNA-derived sRNAs mediate cleavage of At-CHS mRNA, triggering RNAi-mediated decay and transitive sRNA production

genes: GUS (GUS, beta-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Silent 35S::GUS transgene (L5-GUS) shows heat-induced release of transcriptional silencing, with GUS mRNA levels increasing during recovery proportional to the number of heat stress cycles.
mechanism: Heat stress destabilizes transcriptional gene silencing (TGS) at the CaMV35S promoter, allowing GUS transcription.

genes: LUC+ (LUC+, luciferase, synthetic)
phenotype: The -1200PromSDC::LUC+ transgene shows heat-induced luciferase activity in young leaves and apical meristem, with re-silencing kinetics dependent on prior heat stress cycles.
mechanism: Heat stress activates the SDC promoter, driving luciferase expression in a tissue-specific and developmentally regulated manner.

genes: SDC (SDC, F-Box protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The UBQ10::SDC-GFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus, confirming SDC's nuclear localization.
mechanism: SDC-GFP fusion protein is targeted to the nucleus, suggesting a role in ubiquitin-mediated degradation of nuclear proteins.

genes: VInv (vacuolar acid invertase, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: RNAi suppression of VInv expression significantly reduces cold-induced sweetening in stored potato tubers, lowering reducing sugar (glucose and fructose) content by ~90% and improving chip color (lighter L-values) compared to wild-type tubers stored at 3-9°C for up to eight months.
mechanism: RNAi silencing of VInv reduces vacuolar invertase activity, preventing sucrose hydrolysis to glucose and fructose during cold storage. This maintains higher sucrose levels and minimizes Maillard reaction products like acrylamide in fried potato products.

genes: SSN1 (conserved region, Gossypium hirsutum), SSN2 (conserved region, Gossypium hirsutum), SSN3 (conserved region, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Downregulation of GhCYP82D leads to lesion mimic phenotype with necrosis on stems and cotyledons, increased resistance to Verticillium dahliae
mechanism: SSN regulates HR-like cell death by modulating oxylipin metabolism and JA anabolism

genes: SSN1 (full-length, Gossypium hirsutum), SSN2 (full-length, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SSN1 and SSN2 in transgenic cotton plants showed no obvious phenotypic differences from wild-type seedlings, but reduced resistance to Verticillium dahliae
mechanism: SSN confers disease resistance by regulating JA anabolism and oxylipin metabolism

genes: SSN1 (promoter region, Gossypium hirsutum), SSN2 (promoter region, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: GUS activity detection showed specific expression in roots and cotyledons of seedlings (Fig. 1c and Supplementary Fig. 2a,b)
mechanism: NA

genes: GhLOX1 (full-length, Gossypium hirsutum), GhLOX2 (full-length, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Silencing GhLOX1 and GhLOX2 induced SSN expression and altered oxylipin metabolism
mechanism: SSN expression is induced when GhLOX1 and LOX2 are silenced, suggesting functional redundancy in the LOX pathway

genes: KEA3.1 (KEA3.1, cation/H+ antiporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Localization of KEA3.1 to the thylakoid membrane
mechanism: NA

genes: KEA3.2 (KEA3.2, cation/H+ antiporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Localization of KEA3.2 to the thylakoid membrane
mechanism: NA

genes: KEA3.2 (KEA3.2-GFP fusion, cation/H+ antiporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of kea3 mutant, restoring NPQ kinetics to wild-type levels
mechanism: KEA3.2-GFP accelerates qE relaxation by providing an additional route for proton efflux

genes: KEA3CPA2 (KEA3CPA2-GFP, cation/H+ antiporter domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Accelerated qE relaxation kinetics compared to wild-type plants
mechanism: KEA3CPA2 accelerates qE relaxation by providing an additional route for proton efflux, retaining Δψ component of p.m.f.

genes: SKS13 (SKU5 SIMILAR 13, pollen-specific gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SKS13 reduces Myzus persicae population development by ~50% and delays phloem feeding by ~2x in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: SKS13 overexpression causes ROS accumulation in leaves, which is regulated through the jasmonic acid pathway and disrupts aphid phloem feeding

genes: SiLEA14 (SiLEA14, LEA gene from foxtail millet, Setaria italica)
phenotype: Overexpression of SiLEA14 in transgenic Arabidopsis increases salt and osmotic stress tolerance, with significantly larger cotyledons and longer roots under stress conditions.
mechanism: SiLEA14 enhances osmotic stress resistance by increasing proline and soluble sugar accumulation under stress.

genes: SiLEA14 (SiLEA14, LEA gene from foxtail millet, Setaria italica)
phenotype: Overexpression of SiLEA14 in transgenic foxtail millet increases salt and drought tolerance, with improved shoot and root growth under stress conditions and higher survival rates after rewatering.
mechanism: SiLEA14 enhances abiotic stress resistance by reducing electrolyte leakage and increasing proline and soluble sugar accumulation under stress.

genes: SiLEA14 (SiLEA14 promoter, from foxtail millet, Setaria italica)
phenotype: The SiLEA14 promoter drives GUS expression in transgenic Arabidopsis under ABA, PEG, and NaCl stress, with GUS activity induced after 6 h ABA, 6 h NaCl, and 18 h PEG treatment.
mechanism: The SiLEA14 promoter contains ABRE, DRE, MYC, and MYB cis-elements that mediate stress-responsive gene expression.

genes: CVY1 (CURVY1, receptor-like kinase involved in cell morphogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CVY1 rescues the cvy1 mutant phenotype, restoring normal trichome and pavement cell morphology, flowering time, and seed production to wild-type levels in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CVY1 regulates cell morphogenesis through actin cytoskeleton functional networks, including WAVE/SCAR2-ARP2/3 pathways, and controls flowering time and seed production via signal transduction cascades.

genes: Ccs (Capsanthin-capsorubin synthase, capsanthin synthesis, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Silencing of Ccs gene in Capsicum annuum cv. R15 results in yellow fruit color instead of red, with capsanthin content reduced significantly.
mechanism: Ccs gene silencing disrupts capsanthin synthesis, leading to reduced capsanthin levels and yellow fruit coloration.

genes: Psy (Phytoene synthase, phytoene synthesis, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Silencing of Psy gene in Capsicum annuum cv. R15 results in orange fruit color, with reduced capsanthin and intermediate carotenoid levels.
mechanism: Psy gene silencing disrupts phytoene synthesis, reducing capsanthin and intermediate carotenoids, leading to orange fruit coloration.

mechanism: Crtz gene silencing disrupts β-carotene hydroxylation, reducing capsanthin and β-cryptoxanthin, leading to yellow fruit coloration.

mechanism: Psy and Lcyb gene silencing disrupts phytoene synthesis and lycopene cyclization, reducing capsanthin and intermediate carotenoids, leading to slightly orange fruit coloration.
