phenotype: Overexpression of IaTCP1 produces flowers with smaller petals in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Enhanced activity of IaTCP1 leads to an earlier stop of cell division and earlier onset of cell expansion in adaxial petals.

genes: TCP1 (TCP1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TCP1 produces flowers with smaller petals in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Enhanced activity of TCP1 leads to an earlier stop of cell division and earlier onset of cell expansion in adaxial petals.

genes: CYC (CYC, transcription factor, Antirrhinum)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of CYC results in the formation of larger petals in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Enhanced activity of CYC leads to an increase in cell size in adaxial petals.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity detected only in young pollen of transgenic rice plants
mechanism: Tissue-preferred URS from LOC_Os03g11350 drives GUS expression specifically in young pollen

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity detected only in mature pollen of transgenic rice plants
mechanism: Tissue-preferred URS from LOC_Os10g22450 drives GUS expression specifically in mature pollen

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity restricted to vascular bundles of leaves, roots and florets in transgenic rice plants
mechanism: Tissue-preferred URS from LOC_Os10g34360 drives GUS expression specifically in vascular bundles

genes: TnBVank1 (ankyrin repeat-containing protein, from T. nigriceps bracovirus, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic tobacco plants expressing TnBVANK1 show reduced survival (9.4-18.8% vs 57.3% control) and delayed development of S. littoralis larvae after 36 days of feeding.
mechanism: TnBVANK1 binds to midgut epithelial cells, forming a clotting layer that inhibits amino acid transport (48% inhibition at 71 µg/mg BBMV protein) and reduces nutrient absorption.

genes: Cry1Ac (Cry1Ac toxin, toxic for Asian corn borer, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Bt corn producing Cry1Ac toxins can control Asian corn borer (ACB) effectively, with leaf feeding rating of 1.09 (low infection) compared to 6.81 (high infection) in non-Bt corn
mechanism: Cry1Ac toxin is toxic to Asian corn borer, reducing leaf feeding damage

genes: PINA (PINA, auxin efflux carrier, Physcomitrella patens), PINB (PINB, auxin efflux carrier, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: pinA and pinB single mutant shoots were not obviously different from wild-type (WT) (Figures 4A and 4B), but quantitative analysis showed that pinB gametophores were longer than WT (Figure S5). Double disruptants had class II shoot defects and defects in oriented leaf growth and cell division (Figures 4A and S5). pinA pinB double mutants therefore resemble plants treated with auxin (Figure S1), suggesting that they accumulate auxin as a result of a deficiency in auxin transport.
mechanism: PIN-mediated auxin transport regulates apical cell function, leaf initiation, leaf shape, and shoot tropisms in moss gametophytes.

genes: OsSerk1 (OsSerk1, receptor-like kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSerk1 results in a semi-dwarf phenotype with reduced internode length and increased lamina joint angle in rice.
mechanism: OsSerk1 controls rice plant stature and lamina joint angle by modulating BR signaling, likely through interaction with OsBRI1.

genes: uidA (GUS reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS staining in various tissues including roots, hypocotyls, vascular tissues, stem apical meristem, developing lateral roots, open flowers, ovules, valves, stigma, and vascular bundles of siliques.
mechanism: NA

genes: pPLAIIIδ (patatin-related phospholipase A III delta, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of pPLAIIIδ inhibited longitudinal growth but promoted transverse growth in most organs of Arabidopsis and Brassica napus. OE plants exhibited shorter hypocotyls, reduced leaf pavement cell polarity, and altered floral organ morphology.
mechanism: Involvement in auxin distribution and regulation of auxin response through phosphatidic acid (PA) production.

genes: AtDREB2A (AtDREB2A, dehydration-responsive element-binding protein 2A, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtHB7 (AtHB7, homeobox protein HB7, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtABF3 (AtABF3, ABA-responsive element-binding factor 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic peanut plants show enhanced salinity and drought tolerance with increased root biomass (3 g DW/plant vs 1.6 g in wild type), higher cell membrane stability (70-80% vs 20%), reduced lipid peroxidation (35% lower MDA), and increased SOD activity under stress. Under drought, transgenic plants maintain 50% relative water content vs 40% in wild type and show 35% higher proline content.
mechanism: Co-expression of AtDREB2A, AtHB7, and AtABF3 activates multiple stress-responsive pathways including ROS scavenging (increased SOD activity), osmotic adjustment (proline accumulation), and protein stabilization (upregulated HSP70, LEA4). Transgenic plants show enhanced expression of downstream genes like AhHSP70, AhAR, and AhDIP.

genes: Os01g0779400 (ALT1, core subunit of Snf2 family chromatin remodeling ATPase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Transgenic plants showed root length comparable to control and displayed alkaline stress (pH 9.5) response similar to wild type (WT).
mechanism: The mutation in Os01g0779400 is responsible for the phenotype of short root and alkaline tolerance exhibited in the alt1 mutant.

genes: ALT1 (hairpin sequence targeting 3516-3882 bp region, synthetic)
phenotype: RNAi transgenic plants displayed reduced root length (98%, 85%, and 70% of WT roots) and enhanced alkaline tolerance compared to WT under pH 9.5 treatment.
mechanism: ALT1 plays a role in regulating tolerance to alkaline stress.

genes: CHS (CHS, flavonoid synthesis, Petunia hybrida), CHI (CHI, flavonoid synthesis, Petunia hybrida), DFR (DFR, flavonoid synthesis, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of CHS, CHI, and DFR increases flavonoid content in flax.
mechanism: The genes are involved in flavonoid synthesis, leading to increased flavonoid levels.

genes: GT (GT, glucosyltransferase, Solanum sogarandinum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GT increases glucosylation of phenylpropanoid compounds, enhancing their stability.
mechanism: GT is responsible for glucosylation, which stabilizes phenylpropanoid compounds.

genes: SUVR2 (AT5G43990, histone methyltransferase-related protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the silencing defect of RD29A-LUC in ros1#87 mutant Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: SUVR2 is necessary for transcriptional gene silencing at RD29A-LUC and endogenous RD29A loci

genes: SUVR2-L32A (AT5G43990, histone methyltransferase-related protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restoration of RD29A-LUC silencing in ros1suvr2 mutant Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Mutations in WIYLD domain (L32A) do not affect SUVR2's function in transcriptional gene silencing

genes: SUVR2-D52A (AT5G43990, histone methyltransferase-related protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restoration of RD29A-LUC silencing in ros1suvr2 mutant Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Mutations in WIYLD domain (D52A) do not affect SUVR2's function in transcriptional gene silencing

genes: SUVR2-H636A (AT5G43990, histone methyltransferase-related protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restoration of RD29A-LUC silencing in ros1suvr2 mutant Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Mutations in SET domain (H636A) do not affect SUVR2's function in transcriptional gene silencing

genes: SUVR2-C638A (AT5G43990, histone methyltransferase-related protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restoration of RD29A-LUC silencing in ros1suvr2 mutant Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Mutations in SET domain (C638A) do not affect SUVR2's function in transcriptional gene silencing

genes: TENGU (TENGU, phytoplasma effector, phytoplasma)
phenotype: Overexpression of TENGU causes sterility in Arabidopsis thaliana, with 37% severe sterility (closed flower buds, no seed production) and 57% mild sterility (low seed production).
mechanism: TENGU represses ARF6 and ARF8 gene expression, reduces JA and auxin levels, leading to flower developmental arrest and sterility.

genes: GFP-cDNA (GFP-cDNA, fusion protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP-cDNA fusions results in GFP fluorescence in the nucleus and cytosol in most transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana lines, with some lines showing unique Q-ball structures.
mechanism: GFP-cDNA fusions target to peroxisomes, as confirmed by colocalization with peroxisome-targeted mCherry.

genes: IKRR (IKRR, peroxisomal targeting sequence, human MAGI3 gene)
phenotype: The GFP-Ala10-EF-IKRR fusion protein accumulates in peroxisomes in Arabidopsis thaliana line CS84743.
mechanism: The IKRR tripeptide functions as a peroxisomal targeting signal (PTS1), directing the fusion protein to peroxisomes.

genes: KPSL (KPSL, peroxisomal targeting sequence, Arabidopsis thaliana UTRs)
phenotype: The GFP-Ala10-EF-KPSL fusion protein accumulates in peroxisomes in Arabidopsis thaliana line CS84812.
mechanism: The KPSL tripeptide functions as a peroxisomal targeting signal (PTS1), directing the fusion protein to peroxisomes.

genes: mCherry-PTS1 (mCherry-PTS1, peroxisome-targeted fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient expression of mCherry-PTS1 in Arabidopsis thaliana lines CS84743 and CS84812 colocalizes with GFP-cDNA fusions in peroxisomes.
mechanism: The PTS1 tripeptide (SKL>) directs mCherry to peroxisomes, confirming that the GFP-cDNA fusions also target to peroxisomes.

genes: ZmHKT1 (Zea mays high-affinity potassium transporter 1, Zea mays)
phenotype: Targeted mutations in ZmHKT1 gene detected in maize protoplasts with ~100% mutation efficiency in transgenic lines
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9 system induces double-strand breaks at target sites via maize-codon optimized Cas9 and gRNA, leading to mutations via non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ)

genes: TRY (TRICHOME INITIATION 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), CPC (CAPRICE, Arabidopsis thaliana), ETC2 (ETC2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Generation of try cpc etc2 triple mutants with highly clustered trichomes and altered plant morphology, with 46.2-100% germline transmission of mutations to T2 plants
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9 system induces targeted mutations in multiple genes via gRNA-guided Cas9 nuclease activity, with sequence specificity dependent on PAM sites and gRNA-target complementarity

genes: CHLI1 (magnesium chelatase subunit I isoform 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), CHLI2 (magnesium chelatase subunit I isoform 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Albino phenotype in 67% of T1 transgenic seedlings due to simultaneous disruption of CHLI1 and CHLI2
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9 system induces double-strand breaks at target sites in CHLI1 and CHLI2 genes, leading to loss of chlorophyll synthesis and albinism

genes: GhHOX3 (GhHOX3, homeobox transcription factor, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhHOX3 decreases fibre length by ~80% in Gossypium hirsutum.
mechanism: GhHOX3 represses cell wall protein genes GhRDL1 and GhEXPA1, which are required for fibre elongation. GhHOX3 interacts with DELLA protein GhSLR1 to suppress GA signaling.

genes: GhHOX3 (GhHOX3, homeobox transcription factor, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhHOX3g increases fibre length by ~20% in Gossypium hirsutum.
mechanism: GhHOX3g activates cell wall protein genes GhRDL1 and GhEXPA1, which promote fibre elongation. GhHOX3g interacts with GhHD1 to synergistically activate these genes.

genes: GhHOX3 (GhHOX3, homeobox transcription factor, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Knockdown of GhHOX3 decreases fibre length by ~80% in Gossypium hirsutum.
mechanism: GhHOX3 knockdown represses cell wall protein genes GhRDL1 and GhEXPA1, which are required for fibre elongation. GhHOX3 interacts with DELLA protein GhSLR1 to suppress GA signaling.

genes: arf3a (GRMZM2G030710_T01, ARF3 transcription factor, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of tasiR-ARF insensitive ARF3a mimics ta-siRNA biogenesis mutant phenotypes in maize
mechanism: ARF3 acts as a repressor of auxin response, modulating it in a spatiotemporal manner

genes: arf3a (GRMZM2G030710_T01, ARF3 transcription factor, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of tasiR-ARF insensitive ARF3a mimics ta-siRNA biogenesis mutant phenotypes in maize
mechanism: ARF3 acts as a repressor of auxin response, modulating it in a spatiotemporal manner

genes: PeMADS6 (Phalaenopsis equestris MADS-box gene 6, promoter-driven expression, Phalaenopsis equestris)
phenotype: The 208-bp promoter sequence of PeMADS6 drives GUS expression in all four floral organs (sepal, petal, lip, column) of Phalaenopsis aphrodite subsp. formosana.
mechanism: The 208-bp promoter region contains no CArG boxes but is sufficient for ubiquitous expression, suggesting tissue-specific transcription factors or other regulatory elements are involved.

genes: PeMADS4 (Phalaenopsis equestris MADS-box gene 4, promoter-driven expression, Phalaenopsis equestris)
phenotype: The 375-bp promoter sequence of PeMADS4 drives higher luciferase activity in lip and column compared to sepal and petal (1.6–3-fold increase), indicating organ-specific expression.
mechanism: The 375-bp promoter region contains conserved CArG boxes and is regulated by increased H3K9K14ac histone acetylation at the translation start site in lip, enhancing transcription factor access.

genes: PeMADS2 (Phalaenopsis equestris MADS-box gene 2, promoter-driven expression, Phalaenopsis equestris)
phenotype: The 291-bp promoter sequence of PeMADS2 drives GUS expression in all four floral organs, similar to its endogenous expression pattern.
mechanism: NA

genes: PeMADS3 (Phalaenopsis equestris MADS-box gene 3, promoter-driven expression, Phalaenopsis equestris)
phenotype: The 407-bp promoter sequence of PeMADS3 drives GUS expression in all four floral organs, consistent with its endogenous expression pattern.
mechanism: NA

genes: PeMADS5 (Phalaenopsis equestris MADS-box gene 5, promoter-driven expression, Phalaenopsis equestris)
phenotype: The 122-bp promoter sequence of PeMADS5 drives GUS expression in all four floral organs, similar to its endogenous expression pattern.
mechanism: NA

genes: PeMADS6 (Phalaenopsis equestris MADS-box gene 6, promoter-driven expression, Phalaenopsis equestris)
phenotype: The full-length 1,514-bp promoter of PeMADS6 drives GUS expression in all four floral organs, similar to its endogenous expression pattern.
mechanism: NA

genes: PeMADS4 (Phalaenopsis equestris MADS-box gene 4, promoter-driven expression, Phalaenopsis equestris)
phenotype: The full-length 3,303-bp promoter of PeMADS4 drives GUS expression in all four floral organs, with higher activity in lip and column.
mechanism: NA

genes: nptII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, antibiotic resistance marker, synthetic), Pt4CL1 (4-coumarate:CoA ligase, lignin biosynthesis, Populus tremuloides)
phenotype: Delayed autumn leaf senescence in transgenic lines A1, A2, A5; altered stem height and diameter; reduced lignin content in line A1; altered growth patterns in nptII-only line E5396/4
mechanism: Antisense Pt4CL1 reduces 4-coumarate:CoA ligase activity, altering lignin biosynthesis and composition; nptII provides kanamycin resistance for selection

genes: HopF2 (HopF2, Pseudomonas syringae), HopF2D175A (HopF2D175A, Pseudomonas syringae)
phenotype: Transgenic expression of HopF2 inhibits stomatal immunity, preventing PAMP-induced stomatal closure and increasing virulence of coronatine-deficient P. syringae.
mechanism: HopF2 blocks PTI responses by inhibiting MAP kinase activation and ROS production, independent of its ADP-ribosyltransferase activity.

genes: HopF2D175A (HopF2D175A, Pseudomonas syringae)
phenotype: Transgenic expression of HopF2D175A inhibits stomatal immunity and increases virulence of coronatine-deficient P. syringae independently of the D175 catalytic residue.
mechanism: HopF2D175A blocks PTI responses by inhibiting ROS production, independent of its ADP-ribosyltransferase activity.

genes: Gr-VAP1 (venom allergen-like protein, Globodera rostochiensis, synthetic)
phenotype: Ectopic Gr-VAP1 increases susceptibility of potato plants to G. rostochiensis by significantly increasing the number of adult females per plant.
mechanism: Gr-VAP1 perturbs the active site of the extracellular defense-related papain-like cysteine protease C14tub of potato, suppressing immunity.

genes: Gr-VAP1 (venom allergen-like protein, Globodera rostochiensis, synthetic)
phenotype: Ectopic Gr-VAP1 increases susceptibility of Arabidopsis to H. schachtii by significantly increasing the number of females per plant.
mechanism: Gr-VAP1 suppresses basal immunity by perturbing extracellular papain-like cysteine proteases and modulating non-photochemical quenching (NPQ4).

genes: Hs-VAP1 (venom allergen-like protein, Heterodera schachtii, synthetic)
phenotype: Ectopic Hs-VAP1 increases susceptibility of Arabidopsis to H. schachtii and multiple unrelated pathogens (e.g., B. cinerea, P. syringae pv. tomato).
mechanism: Hs-VAP1 suppresses basal immunity by inhibiting extracellular papain-like cysteine proteases and modulating non-photochemical quenching (NPQ4).

genes: Hs-VAP2 (venom allergen-like protein, Heterodera schachtii, synthetic)
phenotype: Ectopic Hs-VAP2 increases susceptibility of Arabidopsis to H. schachtii and multiple unrelated pathogens (e.g., B. cinerea, P. syringae pv. tomato).
mechanism: Hs-VAP2 suppresses basal immunity by inhibiting extracellular papain-like cysteine proteases and modulating non-photochemical quenching (NPQ4).

genes: At4g32460 (BDX, pectin methyl esterase regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BDX increases PME activity in meristem and seedlings, accelerates testa and endosperm rupture during germination, and improves germination performance.
mechanism: BDX positively regulates PME activity, which modulates pectin methylesterification to facilitate cell wall remodeling during germination.

genes: At5g11420 (BDX homolog, pectin methyl esterase regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of At5g11420 increases PME activity in meristem and seedlings, accelerates testa and endosperm rupture during germination, and improves germination performance.
mechanism: At5g11420 positively regulates PME activity, which modulates pectin methylesterification to facilitate cell wall remodeling during germination.

genes: At4g32460 (BDX, pectin methyl esterase regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Antisense BDX plants exhibit reduced PME activity in leaves, short siliques with no seeds, and abnormal carpel morphology.
mechanism: BDX knockdown reduces PME activity, impairing pectin methylesterification and cell wall remodeling during reproductive development.

genes: At4g32460 (BDX promoter, vascular tissue-specific expression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GFP expression driven by BDX promoter is localized to vascular tissue in roots, leaves, and floral organs during development.
mechanism: BDX promoter activity is associated with vascular tissue development and hormone-responsive regulation.

genes: IbMas (IbMas, salt-tolerant gene, Ipomoea batatas)
phenotype: Overexpression of IbMas increases salt tolerance in sweetpotato, with 113–220% higher fresh weight and 12–108% higher dry weight under 200 mM NaCl stress compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: IbMas enhances salt tolerance by upregulating proline biosynthesis (P5CS, P5CR), increasing SOD activity, reducing H2O2 accumulation, and maintaining photosynthetic capacity (higher photosynthetic rate, stomatal conductance, and chlorophyll content) under salt stress.

genes: GT-4 (GT-4, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GT-4 increases salt tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with transgenic plants showing enhanced survival rates under 125-150 mM NaCl compared to wild-type Col-0.
mechanism: GT-4 binds to the GT-3b box in the Cor15A promoter and activates its expression, which confers salt stress tolerance by protecting chloroplast membrane and enzymes from salt damage.

genes: AtUGE2 (AtUGE2, UDP-glucose 4-epimerase, Arabidopsis thaliana), GalS1 (GalS1, β-1,4-galactan synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-overexpression of AtUGE2 and GalS1 led to over 80% increase in cell wall galactose levels in Arabidopsis stems.
mechanism: These proteins work synergistically.

genes: NST1 (NST1, NAC secondary wall thickening promoting factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtUGE2 (AtUGE2, UDP-glucose 4-epimerase, Arabidopsis thaliana), GalS1 (GalS1, β-1,4-galactan synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-overexpression of AtUGE2 and GalS1 in combination with overexpression of the NST1 master regulator resulted in increased thickness of fiber cell walls in addition to the high cell wall galactose levels.
mechanism: Overexpression of NST1 enhances secondary cell wall biosynthesis.

genes: SnOLP (osmotin-like protein, drought tolerance, Solanum nigrum), hptII (hygromycin phosphotransferase, marker gene, vector)
phenotype: Transgenic soybean plants expressing SnOLP showed higher leaf water potential at predawn, higher net CO2 assimilation rate, higher stomatal conductance, higher transpiration rate, and higher 100-grain weight under water deficit compared to non-transgenic plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: DM3 (At3g61540, prolyl aminopeptidase, Hh-0)
phenotype: Knockdown of DM3 interacts with DM2h from Bla-1 to induce hybrid necrosis in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: RPP7 (NLR cluster), RPP4/5 (NLR cluster)
phenotype: Knockdown of RPP7 and RPP4/5 NLR clusters confirms their role in DM6 and DM8 hybrid necrosis in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: RPW8.1KZ10 (RESISTANCE TO POWDERY MILDEW8, KZ10)
phenotype: Overexpression of RPW8.1KZ10 induces necrosis in Mrk-0 background at 16°C.
mechanism: NA

genes: DM2dUk-1 (RPP1 paralog, Uk-1), DM2hBla-1 (RPP1 paralog, Bla-1)
phenotype: Overexpression of DM2dUk-1 and DM2hBla-1 in incompatible parents induces hybrid necrosis in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: MPK9 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 9, Gossypium hirsutum, Gossypium hirsutum), MPK13 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 13, Gossypium hirsutum, Gossypium hirsutum), MPK25 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 25, Gossypium hirsutum, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Silencing of MPK9, MPK13, and MPK25 significantly enhances cotton susceptibility to Verticillium dahliae infection, with 69.3% of MPK9-silenced plants, 63.75% of MPK13-silenced plants, and 54% of MPK25-silenced plants exhibiting wilting symptoms compared to 30% in control plants.
mechanism: MPK9, MPK13, and MPK25 confer resistance to Verticillium dahliae by participating in pathogen defense responses; their silencing compromises this resistance, leading to increased susceptibility.

genes: STK (seed coat development regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: STK-GFP fusion protein complements the stk mutant phenotype, allowing seeds to abscise from the fruit upon maturity
mechanism: STK-GFP is biologically active and able to fully complement the absence of the endogenous STK protein

genes: ABO8 (pentatricopeptide repeat protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of ABA-hypersensitive seed germination and root growth phenotype of abo8-1
mechanism: ABO8 is required for splicing of NAD4 intron 3 in mitochondrial complex I

genes: ABO8 (pentatricopeptide repeat protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: High expression in root tips and lateral root primordia
mechanism: ABO8 is localized in mitochondria and its expression is suppressed by ABA treatment

genes: PLT2 (PLETHORA2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Partial rescue of ABA-hypersensitive root growth phenotype in abo8-1
mechanism: PLT2 overexpression partially restores root meristem activity impaired by abo8 mutation

genes: CRA2 (LRR-RLK receptor, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Expression of CRA2 promoter-GFP::GUS fusion reveals CRA2 expression in root stele, vascular bundles, and lateral root initiation sites under non-symbiotic and symbiotic conditions
mechanism: CRA2 acts as a Leucine-Rich Repeat Receptor-Like Kinase (LRR-RLK) that negatively regulates lateral root formation and positively regulates symbiotic nodule development through systemic and local pathways

genes: OSR2 (organ size regulation, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of OSR2 increases organ size by ~46.8% in Arabidopsis thaliana through enhanced cell expansion.
mechanism: OSR2 enhances cell expansion rate during organ growth without altering endoreduplication.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression in OSR2 promoter:GUS transgenic plants shows activity in expanding organs like leaves and lateral roots.
mechanism: NA

genes: ARL RNAi (RNA interference, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: ARL RNAi reduces leaf size by ~9% in Arabidopsis thaliana through impaired cell expansion.
mechanism: ARL RNAi disrupts cell expansion regulation during organ growth.

genes: OSR2 RNAi (RNA interference, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: OSR2 RNAi combined with ARL RNAi reduces leaf size by ~24.4% in Arabidopsis thaliana through impaired cell expansion.
mechanism: OSR2 RNAi disrupts cell expansion regulation during organ growth.

genes: SlNAC1 (SlNAC1, NAC domain transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlNAC1 reduces carotenoids by altering carotenoid pathway flux and decreases ethylene synthesis, leading to yellow/orange mature fruits with reduced firmness and pericarp thickness, and increased abscisic acid content
mechanism: SlNAC1 inhibits fruit ripening by affecting ethylene synthesis and carotenoid accumulation through interaction with regulatory regions of SlPSY1, SlACS2, and SlACO1 genes in ethylene-dependent and ABA-dependent pathways

genes: AtRAD21.1 (cohesin involved in DNA dsb repair, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The AtRAD21.1 complementation construct rescues the atrad21.1 mutant phenotype, promoting resistance to ionising radiation-induced damage in imbibed seeds. Complementation lines exhibit wild-type-like resistance to 150 Gy ionising radiation.
mechanism: The AtRAD21.1 gene and its upstream sequence are required and sufficient to rescue the atrad21.1 mutant phenotype (hypersensitivity to ionising radiation). The epitope-tag (GFP-6xHis) fused to the C-terminal end of AtRAD21.1 does not affect its function in γ-ray irradiated imbibed seeds.

genes: mKate_S158A (far-red fluorescent protein, synthetic), proinsulin (human, synthetic), G6 (5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase, Pseudomonas putida), R450i (inverted repeat of CYP81A6 gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Transgenic rice seeds exhibit bright red coloration due to mKate_S158A::proinsulin fusion protein expression, glyphosate tolerance via G6 (EPSPS) overexpression, and bentazon sensitivity due to CYP81A6 RNAi suppression in Oryza sativa japonica.
mechanism: The mKate_S158A::proinsulin fusion protein provides visual detection; G6 (EPSPS) confers glyphosate tolerance by catalyzing glyphosate resistance; RNAi suppression of CYP81A6 reduces bentazon detoxification, causing bentazon sensitivity.

genes: HvCKX9 (cytokinin dehydrogenase, Hordeum vulgare), HvCKX1 (cytokinin dehydrogenase, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Silencing of HvCKX9 increases plant height by ~11% and grain yield by ~11.9% in Hordeum vulgare. Silencing of HvCKX1 increases grain yield by ~8.33 g in T4 generation compared to control.
mechanism: Reduced CKX activity in leaves and developing kernels leads to increased cytokinin levels, enhancing grain yield and plant height through increased grain number and spike number.

genes: JAZ_1405 (promoter region, promoter region of JAZ_1405 gene, Hevea brasiliensis)
phenotype: GFP expression measured by flow cytometry in tobacco BY-2 cells
mechanism: Regulation of JAZ_1405 transcription by MYC factors

genes: JAZ_1405 (promoter region, promoter region of JAZ_1405 gene, Hevea brasiliensis)
phenotype: GFP expression measured by flow cytometry in tobacco BY-2 cells
mechanism: Regulation of JAZ_1405 transcription by MYC factors

phenotype: GFP expression measured by flow cytometry in tobacco BY-2 cells
mechanism: Regulation of JAZ_1405 transcription by MYC factors

genes: MYC_94937 (MYC transcription factor, MYC transcription factor, Hevea brasiliensis)
phenotype: GFP expression measured by flow cytometry in tobacco BY-2 cells
mechanism: Regulation of JAZ_1405 transcription by MYC factors

genes: 224 (synthetic AGP-elastin motif fusion, synthetic), 242 (synthetic AGP-elastin motif fusion, synthetic), 442 (synthetic AGP-elastin motif fusion, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of synthetic AGP-elastin motif fusion proteins (224, 242, 442) in tobacco BY2 cells leads to secretion of fusion glycoproteins into culture media, incorporation into cell walls, and altered cell wall properties including increased hydration capacity (442-EGFP) and reduced cellulose crystallinity (224-EGFP).
mechanism: Fusion proteins incorporate into cell walls, altering AGP content, cross-linking via di-IDT, and modifying cellulose crystallinity. 442-EGFP saturation disrupts endogenous extensin networks, while 224-EGFP reduces cellulose crystallinity.

genes: CsF3′5′H (Camellia sinensis flavonoid 3′,5′-hydroxylase, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Over-expression of CsF3′5′H resulted in production of new delphinidin derivatives in the corollas of transgenic tobacco plants, increased the content of cyanidin derivatives and produced deeper and redder flowers in transgenic plants.
mechanism: CsF3′5′H performs both 3′,5′- and 3′ -hydroxylation in vivo

genes: TRAIL (soluble human TRAIL, human)
phenotype: Expression of soluble human TRAIL in N. tabacum callus cells yields ~13.5 μg TRAIL per gram fresh weight (Table 3).
mechanism: NA

genes: HaAK (AK gene, arginine kinase, Helicoverpa armigera, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic Arabidopsis plants expressing HaAK dsRNA show enhanced resistance to Helicoverpa armigera with 55% larval mortality after 3 days of feeding and reduced larval growth rates
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing of HaAK (arginine kinase) disrupts energy metabolism in Helicoverpa armigera

genes: AtDREB1A (dehydration-responsive element-binding protein 1A, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtDREB1A improves drought and salinity tolerance in peanut (Arachis hypogaea) by increasing proline content (4598–5463 µg/g FW vs 4011 µg/g FW in wild type), osmotic potential (31.04–41.07% higher than wild type), and relative water content (62.60–62.09% vs 20.84% in wild type at 20% PEG). Transgenic lines show 14.37–32.06% lower electrolytic leakage than wild type under stress.
mechanism: AtDREB1A acts as a transcription factor in abiotic stress response pathways, enhancing osmotic adjustment through proline accumulation and membrane stability. The gene is expressed under the stress-inducible rd29A promoter, leading to rapid induction (2-10-fold) during drought/salinity stress.

genes: AtCPSF30 (Arabidopsis thaliana, wild-type, genomic), AtCPSF30 (Arabidopsis thaliana, calmodulin-binding mutant, genomic)
phenotype: Complementation of the oxt6 mutant restores wild-type sensitivity to methyl viologen (MV) and gibberellic acid (GA3), wild-type lateral root development, and wild-type poly(A) site choice in roots.
mechanism: AtCPSF30 functions in mRNA 3′ end formation and interacts with calmodulin to regulate lateral root development and responses to auxin, cytokinin, and gibberellic acid. The calmodulin-binding domain is required for these functions but not for oxidative stress or ethylene responses.

genes: AtCPSF30 (Arabidopsis thaliana, calmodulin-binding mutant, genomic)
phenotype: Complementation of the oxt6 mutant with the calmodulin-binding mutant AtCPSF30 (C30GM) restores wild-type fertility and poly(A) site choice but retains lateral root deficiency and altered responses to auxin, cytokinin, and gibberellic acid.
mechanism: The calmodulin-binding domain of AtCPSF30 is required for lateral root development and hormone responses but not for floral organ development or oxidative stress/ethylene responses. AtCPSF30 functions in mRNA 3′ end formation, with calmodulin-regulated polyadenylation affecting gene expression.

genes: PBL1 (PBL1, receptor-like cytoplasmic kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), BIK1 (BIK1, Botrytis-induced kinase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of pbl1 T-DNA mutant restores normal calcium elevation and root growth inhibition after flg22 elicitation.
mechanism: PBL1 myristoylation and plasma membrane localization are essential for kinase activity and signaling.

genes: PBL1 (PBL1, receptor-like cytoplasmic kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PBL1 in protoplasts enables in vivo phosphorylation after flg22 treatment.
mechanism: PBL1 kinase activity is required for MAMP/DAMP-induced calcium elevation and downstream signaling.

genes: BIK1 (BIK1, Botrytis-induced kinase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BIK1 in protoplasts enables in vivo phosphorylation after flg22 treatment.
mechanism: BIK1 kinase activity is required for MAMP/DAMP-induced calcium elevation and downstream signaling.

genes: OsGL1-3 (OsGL1-3, a GL-related protein associated with cuticular wax biosynthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsGL1-3 causes stunted growth, reduced uppermost internode length, increased tiller numbers, and decreased yield in rice.
mechanism: OsGL1-3 overexpression increases cuticular wax accumulation, reduces cuticular permeability, and enhances water deficit tolerance by upregulating wax synthesis-related genes like OsLACS1, OsCER7, and OsCER4.

genes: OsGL1-3 (OsGL1-3, a GL-related protein associated with cuticular wax biosynthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi knockdown of OsGL1-3 results in no significant change in plant height but reduced tiller numbers and yield, with decreased cuticular wax accumulation and increased water loss.
mechanism: OsGL1-3 RNAi downregulates wax synthesis-related genes like OsLACS1, OsCER7, and OsCER4, leading to reduced cuticular wax and membrane integrity under water deficit.

genes: OsGL1-3 (OsGL1-3, a GL-related protein associated with cuticular wax biosynthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsGL1-3-GFP fusion protein localizes to the plasma membrane in onion epidermal cells, confirming its membrane-bound localization.
mechanism: NA

mechanism: NA

phenotype: Overexpression of FT-RGEN-A does not cause delayed flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

phenotype: Overexpression of FT-RGEN-B causes delayed flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: FT-RGEN-B induces frameshift mutations in the FT gene, leading to loss of function and delayed flowering.

phenotype: Resistance to Rice Stripe Virus (RSV) in transgenic rice plants
mechanism: siRNAs derived from the ihpRNA construct target RSVCP gene transcripts, inhibiting viral replication

genes: OsBURP16 (LOC_Os10g26940, BURP domain-containing protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsBURP16 increases sensitivity to abiotic stresses (cold, salt, drought) in rice, with reduced survival rates (e.g., 4% survival under cold stress vs 42% in wild type) and increased water loss rates.
mechanism: OsBURP16 encodes a PG1β subunit that enhances polygalacturonase (PG) activity, degrading pectin in cell walls. This reduces cell adhesion and cuticular integrity, increasing transpiration and stress sensitivity.

genes: Se13 (OsHY2, phytochromobilin synthase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Se13-silenced plants exhibit reduced chlorophyll content, white/blighted leaves, and growth arrest at the three-leaf stage.
mechanism: RNAi silencing of Se13 disrupts phytochrome-mediated light signaling, leading to reduced chlorophyll biosynthesis and lethal phenotype due to impaired red light perception.

genes: SlELP2L (Elongator complex protein 2-like, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of SlELP2L inhibits leaf growth, accelerates leaf and sepal senescence, produces dark-green fruits, and causes hypersensitivity to ABA in seedling growth
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing reduces SlELP2L expression, leading to altered hormone levels (GA, IAA, ABA), down-regulation of ethylene- and ripening-related genes, and increased DNA methylation via elevated DNA methyltransferase gene expression

genes: Glyma13g30560 (Mg-chelatase subunit ChlI1a, Glycine max, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic MinnGold plants expressing wild-type Glyma13g30560 recover wild-type green foliage and chlorophyll levels (P < 0.0001 vs. untransformed MinnGold).
mechanism: Wild-type Glyma13g30560 complements the R273Q mutation in MinnGold, restoring Mg-chelatase activity in chlorophyll biosynthesis.

genes: At5g17960 (At5g17960, C1-clan protein with C1_2, C1_3 and ZZ/PHD domains, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of At5g17960 increases transcript levels in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings.
mechanism: Overexpression of At5g17960 modulates stress-responsive marker genes (DREB2A, RD29A, COR15A, ELIP2) under abiotic stress conditions.

genes: At5g17960 (At5g17960, C1-clan protein with C1_2, C1_3 and ZZ/PHD domains, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Suppression of At5g17960 decreases transcript levels in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings.
mechanism: amiRNA-mediated suppression of At5g17960 modulates stress-responsive marker genes (DREB2A, RD29A, COR15A, ELIP2) under abiotic stress conditions.

genes: SlymiR157 (microRNA, miRNA targeting LeSPL-CNR, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Insertion of SlymiR157 target site into PVX/GFP vector blocks GFP translation in Nicotiana benthamiana, demonstrating miRNA-mediated translation repression.
mechanism: SlymiR157 mediates translation repression of target genes through endogenous miR157 in tobacco leaf cells.

genes: SlymiR157 (microRNA, miRNA targeting LeSPL-CNR, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Viral delivery of SlymiR157::GFP into tomato fruits causes Cnr mutant phenotype sectors, while mutated constructs do not.
mechanism: SlymiR157 mediates post-transcriptional regulation of LeSPL-CNR through miRNA-induced mRNA cleavage or translation repression, possibly in a dose-dependent manner.

genes: MIR168a (promoter, promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Promoter activity of MIR168a is transcriptionally activated by fungal elicitors, leading to GFP expression in transgenic Arabidopsis plants.
mechanism: The MIR168a promoter contains pathogen-responsive cis-elements (ERE, W-boxes, etc.) that mediate transcriptional activation in response to fungal elicitors.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic), miR168* (miRNA*, miRNA sensor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Elicitor-induced miR168 activity in transgenic Arabidopsis plants results in loss of GFP fluorescence in roots, confirming miR168 functionality.
mechanism: The miR168* sensor is degraded in cells where miR168 is present, leading to reduced GFP fluorescence as a readout of miR168 activity.

mechanism: Accumulation of lysine-rich histone proteins in protein storage vacuoles (PSVs) enhances lysine content while avoiding endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and chalkiness through pmGT1 promoter regulation.

genes: RLRH1 (rice histone H2 family, lysine-rich, non-allergenic)
phenotype: Overexpression of RLRH1-NLS increases lysine content in rice seeds by ~10% in transgenic lines.
mechanism: Cytoplasmic localization of modified RLRH1-NLS avoids nuclear interference and reduces allergenic potential while maintaining lysine enrichment.

genes: PpMYB10.4 (PpMYB10.4, anthocyanin-activating MYB gene, Prunus persica)
phenotype: Transient expression of PpMYB10.4 induces anthocyanin accumulation in tobacco leaves, resulting in intense pigmentation 7 days post-transformation.
mechanism: PpMYB10.4 activates anthocyanin biosynthesis genes, leading to increased anthocyanin accumulation.

genes: PpMYB10.4 (PpMYB10.4, anthocyanin-activating MYB gene, Prunus persica)
phenotype: Transient expression of PpMYB10.4 in green-colored young leaves of cv. MTH results in red coloration 2 days post-transformation, with anthocyanin accumulation detected.
mechanism: PpMYB10.4 activates anthocyanin biosynthesis genes, leading to increased anthocyanin accumulation.

genes: AAD1 (aryloxyalkanoate dioxigenase herbicide resistance, synthetic), ZmUBI1 (maize ubiquitin 1 promoter, Zea mays)
phenotype: Transgenic maize plants expressing AAD1 show herbicide resistance and increased AAD1 transcript accumulation in young leaves and roots compared to ZmUBI1::AAD1 plants.
mechanism: The SCBV-IM promoter drives AAD1 expression more effectively than the ZmUBI1 promoter in young leaf and root tissues.

genes: LUC (luciferase, synthetic)
phenotype: SCBV839::LUC showed 60% activity of SCBV839, SCBV576::LUC had 60% activity, and SCBV333::LUC had 10% activity in transient assays.
mechanism: The SCBV-IM promoter fragments drive luciferase expression in maize Hi-II cells, with activity decreasing as the promoter fragment shortens.

genes: LUC (luciferase, synthetic)
phenotype: 4x SCBV282::ZmADH1::LUC showed 10-fold higher activity than the control in transient assays.
mechanism: Multiple tandem copies of the SCBV282 enhancer increase transcriptional activity in a dose-dependent manner.

genes: EXO70B1 (exocyst subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic clone)
phenotype: Complementation of exo70B1-3 mutant phenotypes, including spontaneous cell death and powdery mildew resistance.
mechanism: EXO70B1 is a subunit of the exocyst complex involved in vesicle tethering and secretion, which is essential for normal plant immunity and cell death regulation.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic, EXO70B1 promoter)
phenotype: GUS activity observed in seedlings, leaves, calyx, stigma, and siliques, indicating ubiquitous expression of EXO70B1.
mechanism: EXO70B1 is ubiquitously expressed in Arabidopsis tissues, as demonstrated by GUS reporter activity under its native promoter.

genes: EXO70B1 (exocyst subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana), TN2 (TIR-NBS protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: YFP fluorescence observed in N. benthamiana leaves co-transformed with EXO70B1-YFPN and TN2-YFPC, indicating interaction between the proteins.
mechanism: EXO70B1 interacts with TN2 in N. benthamiana, as demonstrated by bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) assays.

genes: EXO70B1 (exocyst subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana), SNAP33 (SNARE complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assays confirmed the interaction between EXO70B1 and SNAP33 in Arabidopsis transgenic plants.
mechanism: EXO70B1-GFP associates with SNAP33-HA in Arabidopsis, as demonstrated by Co-IP assays using transgenic plants expressing both proteins under their native promoters.

genes: omega-5 gliadin (omega-5 gliadin, wheat storage protein, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Silencing of omega-5 gliadins reduces their abundance in flour by ~34-67% depending on fertilizer regimen, improves flour mixing time by ~1.1-1.2 min with fertilizer, and increases mixing tolerance to 4.0 on 0-6 scale when grown with post-anthesis fertilizer.
mechanism: Omega-5 gliadins negatively affect flour functionality by reducing dough mixing properties; their suppression increases polymer size and improves dough elasticity.

genes: SAC56 (RPL4A, ribosomal protein L4, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAC56/RPL4A in acl5–1 plants partially restores plant height to ~60% of wild-type levels and reverses excess xylem differentiation.
mechanism: SAC56/RPL4A mutation alters ribosomal protein L4, affecting translation of SAC51 main ORF and stabilizing SAC51 mRNA, thereby suppressing thermospermine deficiency in acl5–1.

genes: SAC51 (At5g64340, 5' leader region, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CaMV35S-SAC51 5'-GUS expression in acl5–1 plants increases GUS activity by ~2-fold compared to wild-type and shows thermospermine-responsive GUS staining in above-ground tissues.
mechanism: SAC51 5' leader region mediates thermospermine-dependent regulation of GUS expression, with ribosomal mutations (sac52-d, sac53-d, sac56-d) enhancing GUS activity by stabilizing SAC51 mRNA and promoting translation reinitiation.

genes: TOD1 (TurgOr regulation Defect 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the tod1 mutant restores fertility, with 87 independent transgenic lines showing restored silique length and seed set.
mechanism: TOD1 rescues pollen tube growth defects by restoring turgor pressure regulation in pollen tubes and stomatal closure in guard cells.

genes: TOD1 (TurgOr regulation Defect 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: TOD1Δ1-19, containing the transmembrane and phytoceramidase domains, complements the tod1 mutant phenotype, restoring seed set.
mechanism: The transmembrane and phytoceramidase domains of TOD1 are critical for its function in turgor pressure regulation and pollen tube growth.

genes: TOD1 (TurgOr regulation Defect 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: TOD1 is preferentially expressed in pollen grains, pollen tubes, and silique guard cells, as shown by GUS staining.
mechanism: TOD1 expression is driven by its native promoter and is localized to pollen and guard cells, where it regulates turgor pressure.

genes: TOD1 (TurgOr regulation Defect 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: TOD1-eGFP fusion protein localizes to the Golgi apparatus in pollen tubes, as shown by co-localization with Golgi markers.
mechanism: TOD1 is a Golgi-localized protein in pollen tubes, where it functions in turgor pressure regulation.

genes: GhCKX (cytokinin oxidase, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Down-regulation of GhCKX increases endogenous cytokinins by ~20-134% in cotton, delays leaf senescence, enhances photosynthesis by 10-12%, and increases seed and lint yield by 15-20% in Gossypium hirsutum.
mechanism: Down-regulation of GhCKX elevates endogenous cytokinins, which enhances seed development, delays leaf senescence, and increases photosynthetic capacity, leading to improved yield components.

genes: OtΔ6 (Δ6-desaturase, Ostreococcus tauri), PSE1 (Δ6 fatty acid elongase, Physcomitrella patens), TcΔ5 (Δ5-desaturase, Thraustochytrium sp.), PsΔ12 (Δ12-desaturase, Phytophthora sojae), Pi-ω3 (ω3-desaturase, Phytophthora infestans), NPTII (kanamycin resistance, selection marker, synthetic)
gene_construct: seed-specific promoter-OtΔ6-NA---seed-specific promoter-PSE1-NA---seed-specific promoter-TcΔ5-NA---seed-specific promoter-PsΔ12-NA---seed-specific promoter-Pi-ω3-NA---nos promoter-NPTII-NA
phenotype: Seeds from transgenic Camelina sativa accumulated over 20% EPA in oil
mechanism: The five-gene cassette enables EPA synthesis through sequential desaturation and elongation of fatty acids

genes: RfBP (riboflavin-binding protein, Trionyx sinensis japonicus)
phenotype: RfBP-expressing (RfBP+) Arabidopsis plants exhibit early flowering (6 days earlier than wild type) with reduced rosette leaf number (11 fewer leaves) and increased cytosolic H2O2 concentrations (~1.6-fold higher than wild type).
mechanism: RfBP represses 13 of 19 METC genes, leading to flavin content downregulation and electron leakage from METC complexes I/II. This generates cytosolic H2O2 which activates photoperiod pathway genes (FD, AP1) to promote flowering. RfBP-induced H2O2 functions similarly to peroxisomal catalase mutation (cat2) in enhancing FD/AP1 expression.

genes: MdPME2 (pectin methylesterase, Malus x domestica), mRFP (monomeric red fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient expression of MdPME2-mRFP fusion protein localizes to the cell periphery and apoplasm in Nicotiana tabacum leaves, confirming cell wall exportation of the recombinant protein
mechanism: The MdPME2-mRFP fusion protein is secreted into the apoplast, supporting its role in cell wall modification through pectin remodeling

genes: AtVIP1 (AtVIP1, ABA response gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtVIP1 increases drought tolerance and ABA sensitivity in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana, with 51.7-68.3% survival rates after re-watering compared to 18.3% in wild-type
mechanism: AtVIP1 enhances drought tolerance by upregulating stress-responsive genes (RD29A, RAB18, ERD10) and ABA biosynthesis genes (ABA1, ABA2), and increasing proline accumulation

genes: GCN2 (protein kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana, Genetrap GT8359)
phenotype: gcn2 mutant plants show reduced glyphosate effects, less shikimate accumulation, and less photosynthesis inhibition compared to wild-type plants
mechanism: GCN2 is involved in the response to glyphosate by an unknown mechanism

genes: LoCENH3 (Lepidium oleraceum CENH3, centromere-specific histone H3, Lepidium oleraceum), BrCENH3 (Brassica rapa CENH3, centromere-specific histone H3, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Complementation of cenh3–1 null mutation in Arabidopsis thaliana, resulting in plants phenotypically indistinguishable from wild type with normal fertility and meiosis.
mechanism: CENH3 variants from L. oleraceum and B. rapa can fully complement A. thaliana CENH3 mitotic and meiotic functions required for vegetative growth and reproduction.

genes: AtNTT-LoHFD (Arabidopsis thaliana N-terminal tail fused to Lepidium oleraceum histone fold domain, centromere-specific histone H3 chimera, synthetic), LoNTT-AtHFD (Lepidium oleraceum N-terminal tail fused to Arabidopsis thaliana histone fold domain, centromere-specific histone H3 chimera, synthetic)
phenotype: Chimeric CENH3s complement cenh3–1 null mutation but induce genome elimination and aneuploidy in crosses to wild type, with AtNTT-LoHFD showing wild-type fertility and LoNTT-AtHFD causing severe segregation errors.
mechanism: N-terminal tail divergence in CENH3 causes missegregation and genome elimination through centromere dysfunction in hybrid embryos.

genes: VvCENH3 (Vitis vinifera CENH3, centromere-specific histone H3, Vitis vinifera), ZmCENH3 (Zea mays CENH3, centromere-specific histone H3, Zea mays)
phenotype: Complementation of cenh3–1 null mutation in Arabidopsis thaliana with V. vinifera and Z. mays CENH3, resulting in plants phenotypically indistinguishable from wild type with normal fertility and meiosis.
mechanism: CENH3 variants from V. vinifera and Z. mays can fully complement A. thaliana CENH3 mitotic and meiotic functions required for vegetative growth and reproduction.

genes: OsABA8ox3 (OsABA8ox3, ABA 8-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsABA8ox3 increases sensitivity to drought stress in rice, with survival rates of 20–30% after re-watering compared to 70% in wild-type.
mechanism: OsABA8ox3 is an ABA catabolic gene; overexpression reduces ABA levels, leading to decreased drought tolerance.

genes: OsABA8ox3 (OsABA8ox3, ABA 8-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsABA8ox3-RNAi plants improve rice drought tolerance, showing enhanced ABA content and antioxidant enzyme activities under drought stress, with 100% survival after rehydration compared to 70% in wild-type.

genes: C3'H (p-coumarate 3'-hydroxylase, Populus deltoides x Populus nigra var. caudina)
phenotype: Increased enzyme accessibility without pretreatment leading to ~41% reduction in bioethanol production costs in four of five EU countries modeled
mechanism: Reduced lignin content (56% less than wild-type) enhances enzyme accessibility during saccharification, improving sugar yields and reducing pretreatment costs

genes: PpJAZ1 (jasmonate ZIM-Domain protein, Prunus persica, synthetic)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of PpJAZ1 in tobacco converts showy, chasmogamous flowers into non-showy, cleistogamous flowers with reduced corolla pigmentation and petal elongation.
mechanism: PpJAZ1 inhibits JA-dependent processes by stabilizing JAZ proteins that repress JA signaling, leading to JA-insensitivity in transgenic plants. This stability prevents degradation of PpJAZ1 via COI1-mediated ubiquitination, altering spatial localization of JA signaling in different plant organs.

genes: CPT2 (CPT2, cis-prenyltransferase, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of CPT2 results in detectable levels of lycosantalene and lycosantalonol in petiolules of transgenic tomato plants.
mechanism: CPT2 catalyzes the condensation of DMAPP and IPP to produce NNPP, which is further processed into lycosantalene and lycosantalonol by TPS21 and CYP71BN1.

genes: CPT2 (CPT2, cis-prenyltransferase, synthetic)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated knockdown of CPT2 reduces its transcript levels by up to 80% in transgenic tomato petiolules.
mechanism: RNAi construct produces a hairpin RNA targeting CPT2 mRNA, leading to its degradation and reduced expression.

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS histochemical staining showed CYP71Z2 mainly expressed in the leaves, node, lemma, palea and primary roots, indicating tissue-specific expression patterns of CYP71Z2 in rice.
mechanism: The CYP71Z2 promoter contains cis-acting elements involved in salicylic acid, auxin, photo-responsive and flavonoid biosynthesis processes.

genes: CYP71Z2 (CYP71Z2, cytochrome P450 gene involved in diterpenoid phytoalexin biosynthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of CYP71Z2 increases resistance to Xoo strain PXO99A, with average lesion area ranging from 1.86–4.75% compared to 47.37% in wild-type Nipponbare.
mechanism: CYP71Z2 negatively regulates IAA metabolism by suppressing auxin biosynthesis and signaling pathways, including reduced expression of AAO1, NIT1, IAA1, IAA4, IAA14, IAA20, and expansin genes.

genes: CYP71Z2 (CYP71Z2, cytochrome P450 gene involved in diterpenoid phytoalexin biosynthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CYP71Z2-RNAi lines showed no significant difference in Xoo resistance compared to wild-type, suggesting functional redundancy among CYP71Z family proteins.
mechanism: Functional redundancy among CYP71Z family proteins compensates for reduced CYP71Z2 expression, masking the effect of knockdown on Xoo resistance.

genes: rolB (root locus B, Agrobacterium rhizogenes), rolC (root locus C, Agrobacterium rhizogenes), aux1 (auxin-related gene, Agrobacterium rhizogenes)
phenotype: Formation of hairy roots with vigorous growth, lack of geotropism, and extensive lateral branching in I. tinctoria
mechanism: Integration of T-DNA from Agrobacterium rhizogenes LBA9402 into the plant genome, leading to expression of rolB, rolC, and aux1 genes which alter root morphology

genes: GFP (Green Fluorescent Protein, transgene, synthetic)
phenotype: Knock-out of GFP transgene as evidenced by loss of fluorescence in 15/17 5′-target events and 4/22 3′-target events
mechanism: NA

genes: Glyma07g14530 (putative glucosyl-transferase, Glycine max, synthetic)
phenotype: Modifications in 10 independent events including deletions, SNPs, insertions, and replacements
mechanism: NA

genes: Glyma01g38150 (ortholog of A. thaliana DDM1, Glycine max, synthetic), Glyma11g07220 (ortholog of A. thaliana DDM1, Glycine max, synthetic)
phenotype: Average indel frequencies >70% for 01gDDM1 and >95% for 11gDDM1 in hairy-root events
mechanism: NA

genes: miR1514 (microRNA, Glycine max, synthetic), miR1509 (microRNA, Glycine max, synthetic)
phenotype: Indel frequencies >95% in 4/4 miR1509-targeted and 3/4 miR1514-targeted events
mechanism: NA

genes: ISA1 (ISA1, starch-debranching enzyme, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated suppression of ISA1 causes significantly increased grain chalkiness (42.0% PGC in RNAi line NR4 vs 6.8% in control) with altered starch physicochemical properties
mechanism: ISA1 encodes a starch-debranching enzyme; its suppression disrupts amylopectin structure, leading to chalky endosperm and altered RVA parameters (50% reduced breakdown viscosity, 150% increased setback viscosity)

genes: prosys (constitutive JA signaling)
phenotype: Constitutive JA signaling in 35s::prosys tomato reduces P. solenopsis survival by ~80% compared to wild-type plants after 28 days of infestation.
mechanism: Constitutive JA signaling enhances plant defense responses against P. solenopsis by reducing mealybug feeding time in phloem tissue and suppressing larval development.

genes: shCP (purple chromoprotein, Stichodactyla haddoni)
phenotype: Overexpression of shCP results in dark brown coloration in Nannochloropsis oculata colonies due to cytosolic accumulation of the purple chromoprotein.
mechanism: The shCP protein accumulates in the cytosol, overlapping with endogenous chlorophyll to produce a dark brown coloration.

genes: PRORP1 (At2g32230, organellar RNase P, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Down-regulation of PRORP1 causes reduced photosynthetic pigment content (chlorophylls and carotenoids), altered leaf morphology (reduced spongy mesophyll cell layers, increased palisade cell size), and impaired chloroplast function (elevated F0 fluorescence, reduced Fv/Fm quantum efficiency, altered 77K fluorescence spectra).
mechanism: RNAi-mediated suppression of PRORP1 impairs organellar tRNA processing, leading to reduced accumulation of plastid-encoded proteins and disrupted chloroplast gene expression.

genes: PpLrgB1 (PpLrgB1, plastid-targeting transit peptide, Physcomitrella patens), PpLrgB2 (PpLrgB2, plastid-targeting transit peptide, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: GFP fusion proteins localized to chloroplasts in P. patens protonemata, confirming predicted plastid targeting sequences.
mechanism: PpLrgB1 and PpLrgB2 transit peptides direct GFP to chloroplasts via predicted plastid-targeting sequences.

genes: PpLrgB1 (PpLrgB1, gene knockout, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: PpLrgB1 knockout line (ΔB1) exhibited reduced protonemal colony size and growth rate compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: PpLrgB1 gene disruption impaired photorespiratory glycolate/glycerate transport, leading to reduced growth and photosynthetic efficiency.

genes: PpLrgB2 (PpLrgB2, gene knockout, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: PpLrgB2 knockout (ΔB2) showed no significant growth or morphological differences compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: PpLrgB2 knockout did not affect photorespiratory metabolism or growth, suggesting it may transport nonessential metabolites.

genes: AtLrgB (AtLrgB, gene complementation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Stable transformation of AtLrgB into PpLrgB1 knockout line complemented the growth reduction and photosynthetic defects.
mechanism: AtLrgB functionally replaced PpLrgB1 as a plastidic glycolate/glycerate transporter, restoring normal growth and photosynthesis.

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Molecular complementation of gfc1-1 mutant phenotypes when transformed into gfc1-1 plants
mechanism: Complementation of GFC1 mutation through promoter:GUS reporter gene expression

genes: GFC1 (GFC1, full-length cDNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Full rescue of gfc1-1 mutant phenotypes when transformed into gfc1-1 plants
mechanism: Complementation of GFC1 mutation through promoter:GFC1 transgene expression

genes: MBF1c (Arabidopsis thaliana, transcriptional regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of MBF1c in soybean improves yield in plants grown under controlled growth conditions in a greenhouse without adverse effects on growth.
mechanism: NA

genes: MBF1c (Arabidopsis thaliana, DNA-binding domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of the C-terminal DNA-binding domain of MBF1c fused to GFP suppresses thermotolerance to levels similar to the null mbf1c mutant.
mechanism: Dominant-negative effect via competition with endogenous MBF1c for DNA binding without transcriptional activation.

genes: MBF1c (Arabidopsis thaliana, N-terminal domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of the N-terminal domain of MBF1c fused to GFP does not significantly suppress thermotolerance.
mechanism: Lack of DNA-binding activity prevents dominant-negative effect.

genes: PtHsfA2 (heat shock factor A2, transcriptional activator of Hsps, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of PtHsfA2 induces the expression of 11 of 12 tested Hsps in Populus trichocarpa leaves.
mechanism: PtHsfA2 transcriptionally regulates downstream Hsp genes by binding to heat shock elements (HSEs) in their promoters.

genes: PtHsfA6a (heat shock factor A6a, transcriptional activator of Hsps, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of PtHsfA6a induces the expression of 18.1I-sHsp, Hsp60-1, Cpn60-a1, Hsp70-5, mtHsc70-2, cpHsc70-2, Hsp100-ClpB2, and Hsp100-ClpB4 in Populus trichocarpa leaves.
mechanism: PtHsfA6a transcriptionally regulates downstream Hsp genes by binding to heat shock elements (HSEs) in their promoters.

genes: PtHsfB1 (heat shock factor B1, transcriptional regulator of Hsps, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of PtHsfB1 induces the expression of only a few selected Hsps in Populus trichocarpa leaves.
mechanism: PtHsfB1 may indirectly participate in heat stress response but does not directly activate downstream Hsp genes.

genes: PtHsfB2a (heat shock factor B2a, transcriptional activator of Hsps, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of PtHsfB2a induces the expression of 18.1I-sHsp, Hsp60-1, Cpn60-a1, Hsp70-5, mtHsc70-2, cpHsc70-2, Hsp100-ClpB2, and Hsp100-ClpB4 in Populus trichocarpa leaves.
mechanism: PtHsfB2a transcriptionally regulates downstream Hsp genes by binding to heat shock elements (HSEs) in their promoters.

genes: PtHsfB2b (heat shock factor B2b, transcriptional activator of Hsps, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of PtHsfB2b induces the expression of 18.1I-sHsp, Hsp60-1, Cpn60-a1, Hsp70-5, mtHsc70-2, cpHsc70-2, Hsp100-ClpB2, and Hsp100-ClpB4 in Populus trichocarpa leaves.
mechanism: PtHsfB2b transcriptionally regulates downstream Hsp genes by binding to heat shock elements (HSEs) in their promoters.

genes: HRS1 (Hypersensitive to low Pi-elicited primary Root Shortening 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), HHO1 (HRS1 Homolog 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HRS1 and HHO1 leads to hypersensitivity to low Pi conditions and repression of primary root growth in the presence of NO3−.
mechanism: HRS1 and HHO1 act as repressors of primary root development under Pi-depleted conditions, mediated by NO3− signaling and cis-regulatory elements.

genes: HRS1 (Hypersensitive to low Pi-elicited primary Root Shortening 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of HRS1-GFP under its native promoter localizes to the nucleus of root epidermal and cortex cells in elongating roots.
mechanism: HRS1 is a nuclear-localized transcription factor involved in root elongation control.

genes: HHO1 (HRS1 Homolog 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of HHO1-GFP under its native promoter localizes to the nucleus of root epidermal and cortex cells in elongating roots.
mechanism: HHO1 is a nuclear-localized transcription factor involved in root elongation control.

genes: HRS1 (Hypersensitive to low Pi-elicited primary Root Shortening 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of GR-HRS1-RFP fusion protein allows identification of HRS1 direct targets via the TARGET system.
mechanism: HRS1 binds to cis-regulatory elements in promoters of target genes, identified through transient expression assays.

genes: PsnSuSy2 (sucrose synthase, Populus simonii × Populus nigra)
phenotype: Transgenic tobacco plants showed increased height (12/13 lines taller than wildtype), thicker stems (7 lines with significantly higher puncture resistance), increased chlorophyll content (12/13 lines), and altered carbohydrate metabolism (increased cellulose content in 6 lines, reduced lignin in all lines).
mechanism: PsnSuSy2 cleaves sucrose into UDP-glucose and fructose, channeling carbon toward cellulose biosynthesis. Overexpression increases cellulose content while reducing lignin, leading to thicker cell walls and altered growth patterns.

genes: AGO10 (AGO10, catalytically active AGO10DDH, Arabidopsis thaliana), AGO10 (AGO10, catalytically inactive AGO10DAH, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants expressing HA-tagged AGO10DDH or AGO10DAH show altered antiviral defense against TuMV, with AGO10DDH enhancing resistance and AGO10DAH lacking antiviral activity.
mechanism: AGO10DDH associates with TuMV-derived siRNAs to mediate antiviral silencing, while AGO10DAH, a catalytic mutant, fails to bind siRNAs effectively.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of mito-GFP allows visualization of mitochondria in Arabidopsis protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: AOX1a (alternative oxidase 1a, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AOX1a enhances disease resistance against Pst DC3000 by upregulating AOX pathway capacity and reducing mitochondrial ROS.
mechanism: AOX1a dissipates redox potential as heat and protects against oxidative damage by modulating mitochondrial respiration.

genes: AOX1a (alternative oxidase 1a, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AOX1a knockdown increases susceptibility to Pst DC3000 and impairs SA-induced AOX1a expression.
mechanism: Reduced AOX1a activity leads to increased mitochondrial ROS and impaired respiratory homeostasis.

genes: NahG (salicylate hydroxylase, Pseudomonas syringae)
phenotype: NahG overexpression depletes endogenous SA, reducing H2O2 accumulation and impairing SA-mediated defense responses.
mechanism: NahG degrades SA, reducing its signaling and downstream oxidative stress regulation.

genes: SVP (SHORT VEGETATIVE PHASE, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: AtTTP (Arabidopsis thaliana CCCH zinc finger gene, callose synthesis regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtTTP reduces male fertility in Arabidopsis thaliana, causing pollen wall defects, callose synthesis reduction, and pollen grain adhesion
mechanism: AtTTP overexpression downregulates CalS5 expression, disrupts callose wall synthesis, and reduces miR160 levels leading to increased ARF17 expression, affecting pollen wall pattern formation

genes: ScoSAD (stearoyl-acyl carrier protein desaturase, S. commersonii)
phenotype: Overexpression of ScoSAD increases cold acclimation capacity by 1-2°C in transgenic potato plants (Zhongshu8) after 12 days of cold treatment.
mechanism: ScoSAD overexpression increases membrane C18:2 fatty acid content, enhancing cold acclimation capacity through improved membrane stability and unsaturated fatty acid composition.

genes: ROS1 5' inverted repeat (inverted repeat of 228 bp ROS1 5' region, synthetic)
modification_type: overexpression of inverted repeat to induce DNA methylation
phenotype: Restored ROS1 expression in rdr2 mutants when methylation of the 5' region was restored
mechanism: RNA-directed DNA methylation via inverted repeat transgene produces small RNAs that direct DNA methylation

genes: LTB (LTB, cholera toxin B subunit, Escherichia coli), CTB (CTB, cholera toxin B subunit, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Expression of LTB and CTB proteins in rice seeds induces systemic (IgG) and mucosal (IgA) immune responses in mice, with LTB at 3.4 ng μg−1 and CTB at 21.3 ng μg−1 of total soluble protein
mechanism: LTB and CTB proteins function as oral vaccines against cholera and traveler's diarrhea by inducing antigen-specific IgG and IgA immune responses in mucosal tissues

genes: HvAlaAT (Hordeum vulgare alanine aminotransferase, Hordeum vulgare), OsAnt1 (rice aldehyde dehydrogenase 1 promoter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of HvAlaAT under OsAnt1 promoter increases tap root length and lateral root number in Arabidopsis thaliana under non-limiting and limiting NO3- conditions.
mechanism: OsAnt1 promoter drives HvAlaAT expression in roots and vasculature, enhancing nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) by altering root architecture and amino acid metabolism.

genes: HvAlaAT (Hordeum vulgare alanine aminotransferase, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Overexpression of HvAlaAT under 2X CaMV35S promoter increases tap root length and lateral root number in Arabidopsis thaliana under non-limiting and limiting NO3- conditions.
mechanism: Constitutive expression of HvAlaAT enhances nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) by altering root architecture and amino acid metabolism.

genes: MmAlaAT1 (Mus musculus alanine aminotransferase 1, Mus musculus)
phenotype: Overexpression of MmAlaAT1 under 2X CaMV35S promoter increases tap root length and lateral root number in Arabidopsis thaliana under non-limiting and limiting NO3- conditions.
mechanism: Constitutive expression of MmAlaAT1 enhances nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) by altering root architecture and amino acid metabolism.

genes: MmAlaAT2 (Mus musculus alanine aminotransferase 2, Mus musculus)
phenotype: Overexpression of MmAlaAT2 under 2X CaMV35S promoter increases tap root length and lateral root number in Arabidopsis thaliana under non-limiting and limiting NO3- conditions.
mechanism: Constitutive expression of MmAlaAT2 enhances nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) by altering root architecture and amino acid metabolism.

genes: PfAlaAT (Pyrococcus furiosus alanine aminotransferase, Pyrococcus furiosus)
phenotype: Overexpression of PfAlaAT under 2X CaMV35S promoter with His/Myc tag increases tap root length and lateral root number in Arabidopsis thaliana under non-limiting and limiting NO3- conditions.
mechanism: Constitutive expression of PfAlaAT with His/Myc tag enhances nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) by altering root architecture and amino acid metabolism.

genes: CGL160 (At2g31040, chloroplast ATP synthase assembly factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of cgl160-1 mutant restores chloroplast ATP synthase accumulation and activity to wild-type levels in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CGL160 supports assembly/stability of chloroplast ATP synthase by interacting with CF1 subcomplexes and stabilizing assembly intermediates.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Tissue-specific expression of GUS in seed-pedicel junction, stems, coleoptiles of germinated seeds, and scutella of mature seeds in transgenic rice
mechanism: pSH4 promoter drives expression in multiple tissues through cis-acting elements related to ABA and gibberellin signaling

genes: FLC (flowering locus C, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Col-G259T mutation increases FLC expression by ~5.2-fold in FRI background and causes later flowering compared to Col-0
mechanism: SNP259T modulates COOLAIR class II splicing to increase FLC expression through altered capping of nascent transcripts

genes: FLC (flowering locus C, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Col-TEX-G259T transgene shows no change in FLC expression compared to wild-type Col-TEX transgene in COOLAIR terminator exchange construct
mechanism: G259T up-regulation of FLC expression requires aspects of COOLAIR disrupted in Col-TEX

plant_species: Arabidopsis thaliana, Gossypium hirsutum, Nicotiana tabacum
genes: AtHSP101 (heat shock protein 101, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtHSP101 increases heat tolerance in pollen and reproductive tissues, leading to 35% higher boll production under 43°C/28°C day/night conditions in cotton
mechanism: AtHSP101 enhances thermotolerance by improving pollen germination and pollen tube growth under heat stress

genes: Cry1Ac (insecticidal toxin, Bacillus thuringiensis), Cry2A (insecticidal toxin, Bacillus thuringiensis), Tp2 (chloroplast transit peptide, Petunia)
phenotype: 100% mortality in target insect (Heliothis larvae) after 72 hours of feeding on transgenic cotton leaves
mechanism: Chloroplast localization of Cry1Ac and Cry2A proteins increases insect mortality by concentrating toxins at the site of insect attack

genes: cry1Ab (Bt toxin, insecticidal protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Yellow Bt maize leaves contain 40% more Bt protein than white Bt maize leaves under optimal conditions
mechanism: mRNA levels of cry1Ab do not predict protein levels due to post-transcriptional, translational, and protein degradation regulation

genes: ASL3 (rice PPR protein with 10 tandem PPR motifs, chloroplast-targeted, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi of ASL3 causes albino lethal phenotype at seedling stage in rice, with defective chloroplast development and impaired photosynthesis
mechanism: ASL3 is essential for early chloroplast development and photosynthesis; its disruption affects transcriptional levels of genes associated with plastid translation machinery and photosynthesis

genes: AtALS (Arabidopsis acetolactate synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana), NPTII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, pBR322), SpecR/DHFR (spectinomycin resistance/dihydrofolate reductase, Escherichia coli), NOS (nopaline synthase gene, Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Expression of AtALS confers sulphonylurea herbicide resistance, NPTII provides neomycin resistance, and SpecR/DHFR provides spectinomycin resistance in transgenic flax
mechanism: AtALS confers resistance to sulphonylurea herbicides by catalyzing acetolactate synthesis; NPTII phosphorylates neomycin to inactivate it; SpecR/DHFR provides spectinomycin resistance through dihydrofolate reductase activity

genes: FHY1 (FHY1, far-red light signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Constitutive overexpression of FHY1 rescues the far-red light sensing defect but not the chloroplast division defect of cpd45. Hypocotyl length of 35S-FHY1;cpd45 transgenic plants (2.625 mm) is significantly shorter than cpd45 mutant (13.336 mm) and close to wild type (2.772 mm).
mechanism: FHY1 functions in the far-red light signaling pathway but not in chloroplast division.

genes: ARC5 (ARC5, chloroplast division, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Constitutive overexpression of GFP-ARC5 rescues the chloroplast division defect but not the far-red light signaling defect of cpd45. Chloroplasts of 40-day-old GFP-ARC5;cpd45 plants grown under white light are similar to wild type in size and number. Hypocotyl length of GFP-ARC5;cpd45 transgenic plants (12.190 mm) is close to cpd45 mutant (13.336 mm) and four times longer than wild type (2.772 mm).
mechanism: ARC5 functions in chloroplast division but not in far-red light signaling.

genes: GmGATA44 (Glycine max, GATA transcription factor, soybean)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmGATA44 in Arabidopsis thaliana increases chlorophyll content by ~15-20% compared to wild-type plants and restores the pale green phenotype of the gnc mutant to green or even greener leaves.
mechanism: GmGATA44 upregulates chlorophyll biosynthesis genes AtPORA, AtPORB, and AtPORC, particularly AtPORA, which was previously shown to be downregulated in the gnc mutant. This suggests GmGATA44 functions similarly to its ortholog AtGATA21 in chlorophyll biosynthesis regulation.

genes: GmCnx1 (Cnx1, molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis protein, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmCnx1 increases nitrate reductase (NR) activity by 2.6-fold and aldehyde oxidase (AO) activity by 3.9-fold in soybean leaves, and confers resistance to Soybean Mosaic Virus (SMV) with infection rates reduced to 33-47% compared to 87-93% in non-transgenic plants.
mechanism: GmCnx1 enhances molybdenum cofactor (Moco) biosynthesis by catalyzing molybdenum insertion into molybdenopterin (MPT), which activates Moco-dependent enzymes NR and AO. Increased Moco levels likely strengthen cell wall defenses against SMV.

genes: OsPP108 (OsPP108, rice group A PP2C, Oryza sativa ssp. Indica)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsPP108 in Arabidopsis leads to ABA insensitivity, with increased seed germination (80% germination at 10 μM ABA vs. 25–30% in WT) and enhanced tolerance to salt (175mM NaCl) and osmotic (400mM mannitol) stresses.
mechanism: OsPP108 negatively regulates ABA signaling, resulting in ABA insensitivity and abiotic stress tolerance by altering stress marker gene expression and stomatal movement.

genes: OsPP108 (OsPP108, rice group A PP2C, Oryza sativa ssp. Indica)
phenotype: OsPP108 protein localizes predominantly in the nucleus with partial cytosolic distribution in Nicotiana benthamiana epidermal cells.
mechanism: NA
