phenotype: GUS expression detected in radicle, micropylar region, and expanding cotyledons/hypocotyls during germination
mechanism: Study of PCK1 expression patterns during seed germination and early seedling growth

genes: PPDK (phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase, involved in gluconeogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression detected in radicle and micropylar region during germination, but not persistently in aleurone
mechanism: Study of PPDK expression patterns during seed germination and early seedling growth

genes: PCK (phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase, involved in gluconeogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knockdown of PCK leads to reduced seedling growth under suboptimal conditions
mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of PCK to study its role in gluconeogenesis

genes: PPDK (phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase, involved in gluconeogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knockdown of PPDK leads to reduced seedling growth under suboptimal conditions
mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of PPDK to study its role in gluconeogenesis

genes: PPDK (phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase, involved in gluconeogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Partial rescue of ppdk-pck1 mutant phenotype using genomic PPDK
mechanism: Complementation of PPDK function in ppdk-pck1 double mutant

genes: SlIPT3 (isopentenyltransferase, tomato, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: 35S::SlIPT3 tomato plants display improved salinity tolerance through retention of photosynthetic pigments and K+/Na+ ratio, with high accumulation of cytokinin metabolites
mechanism: SlIPT3 overexpression modifies cytokinin biosynthesis, signaling, and degradation gene expression, leading to enhanced cytokinin accumulation and stress response

genes: AV2 (AV2, part of SLCMV AV2 gene, Sri Lanka cassava mosaic virus), AV1 (AV1, half of SLCMV AV1 gene, Sri Lanka cassava mosaic virus)
gene_construct: CaMV35S-SLCMV AV2::AV1 (278 bp cat1 intron spacer)-NosT
phenotype: Transgenic cassava plants expressing hairpin RNA of SLCMV AV2::AV1 display high levels of resistance to Sri Lankan cassava mosaic virus (SLCMV) infection, with 100% resistance in 5 out of 7 transgenic lines and no detectable viral DNA accumulation in resistant lines.
mechanism: RNA silencing via production of transgene-specific siRNA that targets SLCMV viral RNA for degradation, preventing viral replication and symptom development.

genes: TaFBA1 (Triticum aestivum, wheat)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaFBA1 enhances oxidative stress tolerance in transgenic tobacco plants, as evidenced by higher germination rates under MV stress, reduced chlorophyll loss, lower MDA content, and increased antioxidant enzyme activities.
mechanism: TaFBA1 may regulate antioxidant gene expression and enzyme activity in different organelles, reducing oxidative damage and maintaining membrane stability under stress.

genes: OsRTFL3 (OsRTFL3, overexpression, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsRTFL3 reduces organ size, including leaf blade area, petiole length, blade length, and width, with more severe reduction compared to wild type and ROT4 o/x. OsRTFL3 o/x also inhibits root growth, with shorter primary roots and reduced root elongation rates.
mechanism: OsRTFL3 controls polar cell proliferation and cell expansion in lateral organs, similar to ROT4. It also uniquely regulates cell number along the leaf-width axis and inhibits root growth.

genes: AnnAt4 (At2G38750, annexin 4, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AnnAt4-mCherry fusion protein leads to formation of dart-shaped cytosolic protein aggregates in Arabidopsis and Nicotiana tabacum
mechanism: AnnAt4 overexpression causes protein aggregation into dart-shaped structures, likely due to protein-protein interactions maintaining complex shapes without membrane boundaries

genes: Cry1Ab/Cry1Ac (fusion gene conferring insect resistance, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Increased insect resistance to Chilo suppressalis in transgenic rice
mechanism: Expression of Bt toxin proteins Cry1Ab and Cry1Ac confers resistance to Chilo suppressalis

phenotype: Transgenic wheat lines with silenced PM19-A2 show decreased grain dormancy compared to controls
mechanism: PM19 genes are positive regulators of grain dormancy; RNAi silencing reduces their expression, leading to lower dormancy

genes: TaLHY (MYB transcription factor, wheat, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Down-regulating TaLHY affects wheat growth and resistance to stripe rust pathogen, with silenced plants failing to progress to heading stage and losing resistance to CYR32
mechanism: TaLHY acts as a positive regulator in wheat disease resistance and growth regulation

genes: PhyA (phytochrome A, oat, oat)
phenotype: Overexpression of oat PhyA in zoysiagrass increases cold stress tolerance, evidenced by reduced hydrogen peroxide accumulation (54.6% lower than non-transgenic controls), increased proline levels (42% higher than non-transgenic controls), and enhanced ROS-scavenging enzyme activities (1.6- to 2.7-fold higher than non-transgenic controls).
mechanism: PhyA overexpression enhances ROS scavenging and photosynthetic efficiency under cold stress, as indicated by reduced H2O2, increased proline, and higher APx, CAT, GR, and SOD activities. Chlorophyll-a fluorescence analysis shows improved PSII performance with increased PIABS and PItotal indices.

genes: S599A (hyperactive mutant of phytochrome A, oat, oat)
phenotype: Overexpression of hyperactive S599A mutant in zoysiagrass increases cold stress tolerance, evidenced by reduced hydrogen peroxide accumulation (33.3% lower than non-transgenic controls), increased proline levels (88% higher than non-transgenic controls), and enhanced ROS-scavenging enzyme activities (2.1- to 2.7-fold higher than non-transgenic controls).
mechanism: S599A overexpression enhances ROS scavenging and photosynthetic efficiency under cold stress, as indicated by reduced H2O2, increased proline, and higher APx, CAT, GR, and SOD activities. Chlorophyll-a fluorescence analysis shows improved PSII performance with increased PIABS and PItotal indices. The hyperactive mutant blocks a phosphorylation site involved in light-signal attenuation, leading to sustained cold tolerance.

genes: AGO10 (AGO10, involved in stem cell homeostatic control, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of ago10-15 pol-6 with the AGO10 genomic DNA rescued the meristem termination phenotype.
mechanism: AGO10 genomic DNA restores stem cell homeostatic control by complementing the ago10-15 mutation.

genes: HBsAg (hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis B virus)
phenotype: Expression of HBsAg in maize grain at 110-149 μg/g whole seed and 567 μg/g wafer, inducing mucosal (fecal IgA) and systemic (serum IgA, IgG, mIU/mL) immune responses in mice over 1 year
mechanism: Oral delivery of HBsAg-expressing maize wafers induces mucosal and systemic IgA responses, with sustained antibody titers and anamnestic responses after re-boosting

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein)

mechanism: NA

phenotype: Expression of Flg-4M reaches up to 30% of total soluble protein (~1 mg/g fresh leaf tissue) in Nicotiana benthamiana using PVX-based vector.
mechanism: Flagellin acts as a mucosal adjuvant and carrier for M2e peptides, enhancing immunogenicity and protective immunity against influenza.

phenotype: Expression of Flg-4M in Nicotiana benthamiana using CPMV-based vector achieved ~30% of total soluble protein level.
mechanism: Flagellin acts as a mucosal adjuvant and carrier for M2e peptides, enhancing immunogenicity and protective immunity against influenza.

mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9 system induces double-strand breaks (DSBs) repaired via NHEJ or HR pathways, leading to insertions, deletions, or substitutions in target genes.

mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9 system induces double-strand breaks (DSBs) repaired via NHEJ or HR pathways, leading to insertions, deletions, or substitutions in target genes.

genes: TcBBM (Theobroma cacao BABY BOOM, Theobroma cacao)
phenotype: Overexpression of TcBBM in cacao leads to hormone-independent direct somatic embryogenesis, increasing SE proliferation by ~5.5-fold.
mechanism: TcBBM induces somatic embryogenesis by activating SE pathways, leading to spontaneous direct somatic embryogenesis.

genes: PEP (PEP, post-transcriptional regulatory protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PEP overexpression impairs flower morphogenesis, leading to sterile flowers with stamen-to-petal and carpel-to-sepal transformations, and severe indeterminacy defects.
mechanism: PEP overexpression disrupts AG pre-mRNA processing, leading to reduced AG, KNU, and SPL mRNA levels, and aberrant transcripts with premature cleavage and polyadenylation.

genes: βAS (β-amyrin synthase, Panax japonicus)
phenotype: Transgenic rice produces oleanane-type sapogenin oleanolic acid at 8.3–11.5 mg/100 g dw
mechanism: βAS enables rice to synthesize oleanane-type triterpenoid saponins via the isoprenoid pathway

genes: ZmTPS10 (ZmTPS10, multi-product terpene synthase, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmTPS10 increases emission of (E)-β-farnesene and (E)-α-bergamotene in Nicotiana attenuata.
mechanism: Sesquiterpenes produced by ZmTPS10 react with ozone, potentially quenching reactive oxygen species and mitigating oxidative stress.

genes: ZmTPS10M (ZmTPS10M, point mutant terpene synthase, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmTPS10M increases emission of (E)-β-farnesene in Nicotiana attenuata.
mechanism: Sesquiterpenes produced by ZmTPS10M react with ozone, potentially quenching reactive oxygen species and mitigating oxidative stress.

genes: ZmCYP97C19 (ZmCYP97C19, carotenoid ε-hydroxylase, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmCYP97C19 in A. thaliana lut1 mutant increases lutein content to 26.5-49.6% of total carotenoids, compared to trace levels in the lut1 mutant and 54.9% in wild-type plants.
mechanism: ZmCYP97C19 encodes a carotenoid ε-hydroxylase that catalyzes the conversion of zeinoxanthin to lutein by adding a hydroxyl group at the 3′ position of the ε-ring.

genes: OsEREBP1 (LOC_Os02g54160, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of OsEREBP1 in rice does not affect normal plant growth.
mechanism: OsEREBP1 activates genes involved in jasmonates and abscisic acid biosynthetic pathways and defense responses.

genes: Xb22a (LOC_Os07g07540, interacting partner of Xa21K668, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Transient expression in rice protoplasts for subcellular localization studies.
mechanism: Xb22a is localized to chloroplasts.

genes: OsEREBP1 (LOC_Os02g54160, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Transient expression in rice protoplasts for subcellular localization studies.
mechanism: OsEREBP1 is localized to chloroplast nucleoids.

genes: PsCRN115 (CRN effector, Phytophthora sojae, Phytophthora sojae)
phenotype: Expression of PsCRN115 improves plant resistance to Phytophthora pathogens (P. capsici and P. parasitica) and enhances tolerance to salt and drought stress. Transgenic plants show reduced disease severity, increased survival rates, and improved germination/root growth under stress conditions.
mechanism: PsCRN115 upregulates defense-related genes (PR1b, PR2b), promotes H2O2 accumulation via ROS-producing genes (RbohA, RbohB), and increases expression of heat shock proteins (HSPs) and cytochrome P450 genes. It also suppresses programmed cell death (PCD) triggered by biotic and abiotic stresses.

genes: Glyma02g43680 (endo-1,4-β-glucanase, Glycine max, TA-HS allele)
phenotype: Transformation of the qHS1 genomic region into permeable soybean cultivar Kariyutaka (KA) reduced seed coat permeability by 25-57% and decreased crack formation compared to control plants. Seed coats accumulated β-1,4-glucan in palisade cell outer layers.
mechanism: The endo-1,4-β-glucanase encoded by qHS1 (Glyma02g43680) accumulates β-1,4-glucan in palisade cell outer layers, increasing seed coat rigidity and reducing permeability by preventing crack formation during desiccation.

genes: HvPap-1 (entire HvPap-1 gene including signal peptide, pro-peptide, and mature protein, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Transgenic lines showed reduced leaf damage and increased mite mortality when infested with T. urticae compared to non-transformed controls.
mechanism: HvPap-1 pro-peptide inhibits CysProt activities, reducing mite access to essential amino acids and impairing physiological processes.

genes: HvPap-1 (HvPap-1 gene without signal peptide, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Transgenic lines showed reduced leaf damage and increased mite mortality when infested with T. urticae compared to non-transformed controls.
mechanism: HvPap-1 pro-peptide inhibits CysProt activities, reducing mite access to essential amino acids and impairing physiological processes.

genes: HvPap-1 (HvPap-1 pro-peptide sequence, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Transgenic lines showed reduced leaf damage and increased mite mortality when infested with T. urticae compared to non-transformed controls.
mechanism: HvPap-1 pro-peptide inhibits CysProt activities, reducing mite access to essential amino acids and impairing physiological processes.

genes: CNGC19 (CNGC19, full-length CNGC19, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CNGC19FL-GFP co-localizes with vacuole membrane markers αTIP- and γTIP-mCherry in Arabidopsis leaf protoplasts.
mechanism: CNGC19 is localized to vacuolar membranes and may facilitate cation transport or Ca2+ signaling between vacuole and cytosol.

mechanism: CNGC20 is localized to vacuolar membranes and may facilitate cation transport or Ca2+ signaling between vacuole and cytosol.

mechanism: N-terminal region of CNGC20 lacks sufficient information to direct chloroplast targeting.

phenotype: CNGC19FL-mCherry co-localizes with CNGC20FL-GFP in vacuolar membranes when co-expressed in Arabidopsis leaf protoplasts.
mechanism: CNGC19 and CNGC20 may form heteromultimeric channels that traffic to vacuolar membranes.

genes: Erns (Erns glycoprotein, structural protein of BVDV, Bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV))
phenotype: Erns glycoprotein is expressed and retained antigenicity in transgenic ginseng hairy roots, inducing specific humoral and cell-mediated immune responses in sika deer
mechanism: Plant-derived Erns glycoprotein maintains correct folding and glycosylation, enabling it to retain antigenicity and stimulate immune responses against BVDV

genes: lacO (bacterial operator, synthetic), LacI-EGFP (bacterial repressor fused with enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)

mechanism: NA

mechanism: NA

mechanism: amiRNA-mediated silencing of CH42 disrupts chlorophyll biosynthesis

genes: MMS19 (MMS19, MMS19, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: MMS19 associates with Fe-S assembly complex components (CIA1, CIA2, NAR1) and DNA polymerases (ICU2, AT5G63960, ABO4), potentially facilitating Fe-S cluster assembly on DNA polymerases.

mechanism: MMS19 interacts with CIA1 in vivo, as confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation in transgenic plants harboring both MMS19-Myc and CIA1-Flag.

genes: CIA2 (CIA2, CIA2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CIA2-Flag transgenic plants show interaction with MMS19, confirming their association in the cytoplasm.
mechanism: MMS19 interacts with CIA2 in vivo, as confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation in transgenic plants harboring both MMS19-Myc and CIA2-Flag.

genes: ICU2 (ICU2, ICU2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ICU2-Myc transgenic plants show cytoplasmic localization and interaction with MMS19, suggesting a role in Fe-S cluster assembly on DNA polymerases.
mechanism: MMS19 interacts with ICU2 in vivo, as confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation in transgenic plants harboring both MMS19-Flag and ICU2-Myc.

genes: Rpi-blb1 (resistance gene, Solanum bulbocastanum)
phenotype: Confers resistance against P. infestans strain SE-03058 in potato cv. Desiree
mechanism: Rpi-blb1 mediates effector-triggered immunity (ETI) against P. infestans

mechanism: Codon-optimized aga-F75m under endosperm-specific ZM-leg1A promoter enables tissue-specific expression and high enzyme activity.

gene_construct: maize histone H2B promoter-bar-potato protease II terminator
phenotype: Selectable marker enables bialaphos resistance for transgenic plant selection.
mechanism: Bar gene expression confers resistance to bialaphos, allowing selection of transformed maize cells.

genes: TaPP2C1 (Triticum aestivum PP2C family gene, from wheat)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaPP2C1 in tobacco decreases plant sensitivity to ABA and improves salt stress resistance, with transgenic lines showing higher germination rates, reduced membrane injury (lower IL, MDA, H2O2), and increased SOD and CAT activities under salt stress.
mechanism: TaPP2C1 acts as a negative regulator of ABA signaling and enhances antioxidant systems by increasing SOD and CAT activities, reducing ROS accumulation, and upregulating stress-responsive genes like NtERD10C, NtLEA5, and NtDREB3.

genes: StGCS-GS (Streptococcus thermophilus ATCC 19258, γ-glutamylcysteine synthetase-glutathione synthetase, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of StGCS-GS increases Cd, Zn, and Cu tolerance in sugar beet by ~2-9-fold root length and ~2-3-fold fresh weight under 100-200 μM heavy metal stress.
mechanism: StGCS-GS enhances glutathione (GSH) and phytochelatin (PC) production, which chelate heavy metals and improve detoxification capacity.

genes: SDG8 (histone methyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of cli186 mutant restores carbon and light repression of ASN1 gene expression and rescues early flowering phenotype
mechanism: SDG8-mediated H3K36me3 histone modification regulates gene expression of carbon/light responsive genes

genes: OsGRAS23 (OsGRAS23, drought-responsive GRAS transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsGRAS23 improves drought resistance and oxidative stress tolerance in rice.
mechanism: OsGRAS23 enhances ROS scavenging ability and upregulates stress-related genes.

genes: OsGRAS23 (OsGRAS23, drought-responsive GRAS transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsGRAS23-GFP localized in the nucleus of tobacco epidermal cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsGRAS23 (OsGRAS23, drought-responsive GRAS transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: GUS signals detected in root tips and spikes of transgenic rice plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: Sl3-MMP (Solanum lycopersicum Matrix Metalloproteinase 3, Solanum lycopersicum),
phenotype: Silencing of Sl3-MMP in tomato resulted in reduced resistance to Botrytis cinerea and Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000, with increased lesion size (~60% larger) and fungal/bacterial population (3x higher at 24h/48h and 10-25x higher at 2-4 dpi, respectively).
mechanism: Sl3-MMP silencing attenuated defense response through increased ROS accumulation (85% higher at 12h, 24% higher at 24h), excessive cell death (38% higher electrolyte leakage), and downregulated JA/ET-mediated defense genes (SlLapA, SlPI-I, SlPI-II).

genes: Sl3-MMP (Solanum lycopersicum Matrix Metalloproteinase 3, Solanum lycopersicum),
phenotype: Transient expression of Sl3-MMP in N. benthamiana led to enhanced resistance to Botrytis cinerea (40% smaller lesions) and upregulated defense-related genes (PR1, PR2, PR3, PR4 with 5-24x higher expression at 24h).
mechanism: Sl3-MMP overexpression activated defense response through upregulated expression of pathogenesis-related genes (PR1, PR2, PR3, PR4) and increased ROS scavenging activity.

genes: GmFAD3A (fatty acid desaturase 3A, soybean), GmFAD3B (fatty acid desaturase 3B, soybean), GmFAD3C (fatty acid desaturase 3C, soybean)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated silencing of GmFAD3 genes reduces linolenic acid content in soybean seeds by ~50% in T5 homozygous lines
mechanism: RNAi-generated siRNAs target GmFAD3 mRNAs for cleavage, with silencing efficacy correlating to sequence homology between 318-bp inverted repeats and target transcripts

genes: JcPIP2;7 (plasma membrane aquaporin, Jatropha curcas), JcTIP1;3 (tonoplast aquaporin, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcPIP2;7 and JcTIP1;3 in Arabidopsis thaliana enhances salt and drought tolerance, with improved germination and root growth under stress conditions.
mechanism: Aquaporins facilitate water transport, improving cellular water homeostasis under stress conditions.

genes: gusA (beta-glucuronidase, Arabidopsis thaliana), HFR1NT131-TBPm3 (fusion protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of gusA in postmeiotic tapetum cells of Nicotiana tabacum, with GUS activity ranging from 11.45 to 47.57 nmoles mg−1min−1 in stage 2 anthers and 10.45 to 45.65 nmoles mg−1min−1 in stage 3 anthers.
mechanism: High-level and stringent expression in postmeiotic tapetum cells achieved through TGTA-TBPm3 complementation system with HFR1NT131 fusion for controlled degradation.

genes: COP1 (COP1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of COP1 in tapetum cells of Nicotiana tabacum, with highest expression in stage 1 anthers (Supplementary Fig. S3-e).
mechanism: COP1-mediated degradation of HFR1NT131-TBPm3 fusion protein to partially abolish TGTA-TBPm3 complementation system expression.

genes: COP1L105A (COP1 mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of COP1L105A in tapetum cells of Nicotiana tabacum, with highest expression in stage 1 anthers (Fig. 2k).
mechanism: COP1L105A-mediated degradation of HFR1NT131-TBPm3 fusion protein to completely abolish TGTA-TBPm3 complementation system expression.

genes: BECLIN1 (ATG6, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BECLIN1 in postmeiotic tapetum cells of Nicotiana tabacum leads to complete male sterility, with pollen viability ~0.76% and germination ~0.76% compared to 77.71% and 70% in controls.
mechanism: High-level BECLIN1 expression in tapetum causes abnormal tapetal growth, delayed degeneration, and pollen abortion.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression in gametophytes, with nearly 90% of gametophytes showing GUS signal under optimal conditions.
mechanism: NA

phenotype: Stable transformation with GFP6 expression in gametophytes and sporophytes, and hygromycin resistance for selection. GFP6 was detected in gametophyte antheridia, sporophyte tissues (leaf, root), and T1 gametophyte sperm cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtMPT3 (mitochondrial phosphate translocator 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtMPT3 hampers the growth and development in Arabidopsis, causing dwarfism, leaf curling, and reduced fertility.
mechanism: AtMPT3 overexpression impairs mitochondrial function, leading to increased ATP content, respiration rate, ROS accumulation, and programmed cell death.

genes: PHYL1 (PHYL1, phytoplasma effector, PnWB), SAP54 (SAP54, phytoplasma effector, AYWB)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHYL1 and SAP54 in Arabidopsis and N. benthamiana triggers leafy flower phenotypes, with 18.6-33.3% formation rates in recombinant TuGK-infected plants compared to 5.9% in transgenic PHYL1 plants.
mechanism: PHYL1 and SAP54 down-regulate flowering promoters AtAP3 and AtFT while up-regulating flowering repressor AtSVP, leading to leafy flowers.

genes: HvCCA1 (HvCCA1, circadian clock gene, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Overexpression of HvCCA1 causes circadian arrhythmia, elongated hypocotyls (3.5–5 mm vs 1.5–2 mm in controls), and delayed flowering (≥20 days later than wildtype) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HvCCA1 functions similarly to AtCCA1 in Arabidopsis, disrupting circadian rhythms of leaf movement, delayed fluorescence, and stomatal conductance while promoting hypocotyl elongation and delaying flowering.

genes: HvPpd-H1 (HvPpd-H1, circadian clock gene, Hordeum vulgare), Hvppd-H1 (Hvppd-H1, photoperiod-insensitive variant, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Complementation of the prr7-11 Arabidopsis mutant with HvPpd-H1 or Hvppd-H1 under the AtPRR7 promoter restores wildtype circadian leaf movement rhythms (period ~25 h vs 26.6 h in prr7-11), indicating functional orthology to AtPRR7.
mechanism: HvPpd-H1 and Hvppd-H1 function similarly to AtPRR7 in Arabidopsis, restoring circadian period in the prr7-11 mutant despite differing photoperiodic sensitivity in barley.

genes: codA (cytosine deaminase, Pseudomonas sp., bacterial), nptII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, Escherichia coli, bacterial), DSRed (discosoma sp., animal)
phenotype: Overexpression of codA::nptII and expression of DSRed in Carrizo citrange allows for kanamycin resistance and visible red fluorescence, enabling selection and visualization of transgenic plants.
mechanism: The codA gene converts 5-FC to 5-FU, which is toxic to transgenic plants, allowing negative selection. The nptII provides kanamycin resistance for positive selection. DSRed serves as a visual marker.

genes: GsMIOX1a (Glycine soja, GsMIOX1a)
phenotype: Overexpression of GsMIOX1a increases alkaline stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with 70% germination rate under 11 mM NaHCO3 compared to 44.1% in wild type and 27.4% in atmiox1 mutant. Survived better under 100 mM NaHCO3 stress with higher proline content (p<0.01) and POD activity (p<0.01) compared to wild type.
mechanism: GsMIOX1a enhances alkaline tolerance by increasing proline accumulation and POD activity to scavenge ROS, and upregulating stress-responsive genes like H+-Ppase, NADP-ME, KIN1, and RD29B under alkaline stress.

genes: VPg (viral protein genome-linked, Lettuce mosaic virus, synthetic)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of mcherry-VPg fusion protein in Lettuce mosaic virus (LMV) leads to vein clearing and mosaic symptoms in lettuce and Nicotiana benthamiana plants, with mcherry fluorescence localized to nucleus and nucleolus
mechanism: The mcherry-VPg fusion protein localizes to the nucleus and nucleolus, consistent with VPg's role in viral replication and eIF4E interaction during infection

genes: OsCAS (Oryza sativa Ca2+-dependent anion channel, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsCAS increases drought tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana by promoting stomatal closure and reducing membrane damage under drought stress.
mechanism: OsCAS enhances drought tolerance by promoting stomatal closure in the absence of external Ca2+ and reducing membrane lipid peroxidation (MDA) and relative membrane permeability (RMP) while increasing proline accumulation.

genes: LRX3 (leucine-rich repeat extensin protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: The chimeric complementation constructs encode functional proteins that restore normal plant height in the lrx3 lrx4 double mutant.

genes: LRX4 (leucine-rich repeat extensin protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the lrx3 lrx4 double mutant with LRX4:LRR4-EXT1 alleviates the reduced plant height phenotype compared to the wild type.
mechanism: The chimeric complementation constructs encode functional proteins that restore normal plant height in the lrx3 lrx4 double mutant.

genes: ARGOS (ARGOS, involved in ethylene signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana), ARL (ARL, involved in ethylene signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ARGOS and ARL reduces ethylene sensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana, leading to increased leaf area due to enhanced cell expansion and proliferation.
mechanism: ARGOS and ARL function as negative feedback regulators of ethylene signaling, desensitizing the plant to ethylene by modulating the ethylene response pathway.

genes: ARGOS (ARGOS, involved in ethylene signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana), ARL (ARL, involved in ethylene signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ARGOS and ARL under the CaMV 35S promoter reduces ethylene sensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana, resulting in increased leaf area and accelerated desensitization to ethylene.
mechanism: ARGOS and ARL act as negative regulators of ethylene signaling, suppressing ethylene-dependent gene expression and altering the plant's response to ethylene concentrations.

genes: AT1G56190 (chloroplast phosphoglycerate kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Virus-induced gene silencing of cPGK2 in Nicotiana benthamiana reduces Plum pox virus (PPV) accumulation by over 90% in systemic leaves
mechanism: cPGK2 is required for efficient PPV accumulation in Nicotiana benthamiana

phenotype: Overexpression of AtUCP1 in Nicotiana tabacum results in faster vegetative growth and high tolerance to salt and drought stresses
mechanism: NA

mechanism: NA

mechanism: Plastidial targeting of EβfS increases access to FPP, enabling Eβf synthesis.

genes: FPPS (FPPS, farnesyl diphosphate synthase, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of FPPS does not produce detectable Eβf in Triticum aestivum.
mechanism: NA

genes: FPPS (FPPS, farnesyl diphosphate synthase, synthetic)
phenotype: Plastidially-targeted overexpression of FPPS does not produce detectable Eβf in Triticum aestivum.
mechanism: NA

phenotype: Overexpression of Tc-MYBPA in Arabidopsis tt2 mutant complements PA-deficient seed coat phenotype and increases anthocyanin accumulation in hypocotyls
mechanism: Tc-MYBPA activates PA biosynthesis genes DFR, LDOX, and BAN; induces anthocyanin synthesis via LDOX activation

genes: AtGA20ox (GA20 oxidase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtGA20ox increases internode length by ~2.3x in kenaf, alters flowering patterns (short early flowering, short non-flowering, normal flowering, tall non-flowering phenotypes), and modifies fiber dimensions (longer bast fibers, thicker cell walls) and biochemical composition (higher holocellulose, lower lignin).
mechanism: AtGA20ox overexpression elevates endogenous bioactive gibberellins (GA1 and GA4), which promote cell elongation and alter fiber development. Increased GA levels correlate with enhanced vegetative growth but disrupt reproductive development in transgenic lines.

genes: CHS (chalcone synthase, Petunia hybrida), CHI (chalcone isomerase, Petunia hybrida), DFR (dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of CHS, CHI, and DFR in flax increases phenylpropanoid compounds, enhancing oil stability by ~15%.
mechanism: Increased flavonoid content enhances antioxidant activity, which protects against lipid oxidation.

genes: CHS (chalcone synthase, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Down-regulation of CHS in flax increases hydrolysable tannins, enhancing oil stability.
mechanism: Increased tannin content provides antioxidant activity, protecting against lipid oxidation.

genes: SsGT1 (7-O-glycosyltransferase, Solanum sogarandinum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SsGT1 in flax increases glycosylated phenolic acids, enhancing oil stability.
mechanism: Glycosylated phenolics have higher water solubility and stability, providing antioxidant activity.

genes: nNOS (nitric oxide synthase, rat nNOS, rat)
phenotype: Overexpression of rat nNOS increases NOS activity by 2.28-2.63× and NO content in rice, leading to enhanced drought and salt stress tolerance with 69-72% survival rate vs 29% in wild type after 2 weeks drought
mechanism: Enhanced ROS-scavenging capacity via upregulated CAT and POX activities, increased proline accumulation, reduced electrolyte leakage and MDA content, and elevated expression of stress-responsive genes (OsDREB2A, OsSNAC1, etc.)

genes: AtABI1 (ABI1, protein phosphatase 2C, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtABI1 in B. napus reduces water retention capacity, increases chlorophyll content under drought stress, and alters expression of ABA-responsive genes
mechanism: ABI1 acts as a negative regulator of ABA signaling, reducing drought tolerance when overexpressed

genes: SOAR1 (At5g11310, SOAR1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SOAR1 enhances ABA sensitivity in stomatal closure and inhibition of stomatal opening, leading to increased drought tolerance.
mechanism: NA

genes: ABI2 (At5g57050, ABI2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ABI2 results in ABA-insensitive phenotypes in stomatal closure and inhibition of stomatal opening, leading to reduced drought tolerance.
mechanism: NA

genes: LuPDCT1 (LuPDCT1, phosphatidylcholine diacylglycerol cholinephosphotransferase, Linum usitatissimum), LuPDCT2 (LuPDCT2, phosphatidylcholine diacylglycerol cholinephosphotransferase, Linum usitatissimum)
phenotype: Seed-specific expression of LuPDCT1 and LuPDCT2 in Arabidopsis thaliana resulted in 16.4% and 19.7% increases in C18-PUFAs, respectively, with a concomitant decrease in the proportion of oleic acid (18:1cisΔ9; OA).
mechanism: LuPDCTs efficiently channel monounsaturated fatty acids into phosphatidylcholine for desaturation and move the resulting polyunsaturated fatty acids out of phosphatidylcholine for subsequent use in triacylglycerol synthesis.

genes: GhACNAT (acyl-CoA N-acyltransferase, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Silencing of GhACNAT causes anther indehiscence, forked/warped stigmas, and failure to release pollen in Gossypium hirsutum
mechanism: GhACNAT regulates lipid metabolism and jasmonic acid (JA) biosynthesis; reduced JA levels lead to anther indehiscence and reproductive organ abnormalities

genes: KNAT2 (KNOTTED1-LIKE ARABIDOPSIS THALIANA2, SAM-related transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SAM-less rpk1-7 seedlings display variable KNAT2p:GUS expression patterns in cotyledon and hypocotyl-cotyledon structures, with some developing ectopic shoot meristems (eSMs) on cotyledons.
mechanism: Aberrant SAM gene expression pattern due to non-coordinated activity of SAM-specific genes, leading to rare eSM formation when required genes are concurrently active.

genes: PIN1 (PINFORMED1, auxin efflux carrier, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: rpk1-7 seedlings with PIN1p:PIN1::GFP reporter show disturbed PIN1 polarity and auxin homeostasis, leading to vascular defects and monocotyledonous morphology.
mechanism: RPK1 defect disrupts PIN1 polarity and cell division during embryogenesis, altering auxin maxima formation and organ patterning.

genes: HLP1 (HnRNP A1-like protein 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, full-length CDS)
phenotype: Overexpression of HLP1 rescues the delayed-flowering phenotype of hlp1-1 mutant and reduces FLC transcripts, promoting floral transition in an FLC-dependent manner.
mechanism: HLP1 promotes floral transition by regulating FLC antisense processing and polyadenylation site choice in FCA transcripts, thereby suppressing the floral repressor FLC.

genes: HLP1ΔRRM (HnRNP A1-like protein 1 lacking two RRMs, Arabidopsis thaliana, deletion form)
phenotype: Overexpression of HLP1ΔRRM in hlp1-1 mutants does not rescue the delayed-flowering phenotype or repress FLC transcription, indicating that the RRMs are required but insufficient for flowering.
mechanism: The RNA-binding motifs (RRMs) of HLP1 are required for its function in floral transition, as deletion of RRMs abolishes its ability to regulate FLC and polyadenylation site choice.

genes: EGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, photoconvertible to red, synthetic)
phenotype: EGFP photoconverts from green to red fluorescence in vivo, enabling protein tracking in Nicotiana benthamiana cells.
mechanism: Photoconversion of EGFP from green to red state occurs via 405 nm light irradiation, allowing visualization of protein dynamics.

genes: Cry1Ab (Bt gene, insecticidal crystal protein, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Transgenic rice contains Cry1Ab protein, which provides insect resistance
mechanism: Cry1Ab protein is toxic to insects

genes: BcMF26a (Brassica campestris Male Fertility 26a, ortholog of At4g33440, Brassica campestris), BcMF26b (Brassica campestris Male Fertility 26b, ortholog of At4g33440, Brassica campestris)
phenotype: GUS activity driven by BcMF26a promoter was observed in shoot apical meristem, developing leaf, and root tip but not hypocotyl; BcMF26b promoter drove GUS expression in all seedling parts and in anthers, tapetum, and pollen grains during reproductive stages
mechanism: Promoter activity analysis showed spatially distinct expression patterns in Arabidopsis, with BcMF26a restricted to pistils and BcMF26b active in anthers and pollen

plant_species: Brassica campestris subsp. chinensis var. parachinensis
genes: BcMF26a (Brassica campestris Male Fertility 26a, ortholog of At4g33440, Brassica campestris), BcMF26b (Brassica campestris Male Fertility 26b, ortholog of At4g33440, Brassica campestris)
phenotype: Co-inhibition of BcMF26a and BcMF26b led to 37.5–47.8% nonviable pollen, 27.7–35.1% normal pollen tube germination, and abnormal pollen wall development with irregular shapes and defective intine formation
mechanism: amiRNA-mediated gene silencing disrupted pollen wall development and intine formation, causing pollen deformities and impaired pollen tube growth

genes: C4H (C4H, part of the lignin pathway, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of C4H in Arabidopsis thaliana reduces lignin content to 12.9-14% compared to 19.1% in wild type.
mechanism: C4H is part of the lignin biosynthesis pathway; overexpression under the vessel-specific VND6 promoter reduces lignin content.

genes: NST1 (NST1, controls secondary cell wall deposition in fibers, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of NST1 in Arabidopsis thaliana increases secondary cell wall polysaccharide deposition, leading to higher glucose and xylose content in engineered lines.
mechanism: NST1 is a key transcription factor for secondary cell wall deposition in fibers; overexpression under the IRX8 promoter enhances polysaccharide accumulation.

genes: COP1 (COP1, E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in photoperiod and temperature signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of COP1 increases protein stability at low temperatures, leading to enhanced GI degradation and reduced FT expression in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: COP1 stabilizes at low temperatures, triggering ubiquitination and degradation of GI, which down-regulates FT expression to regulate flowering time.

genes: GI (GI, photoperiod and temperature signaling regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GI leads to reduced protein stability at low temperatures, which is counteracted by COP1-mediated degradation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: COP1 regulates GI turnover at low temperatures through ubiquitination, affecting its binding to the FT promoter and subsequent FT expression.

genes: STANN1 (Solanum tuberosum annexin 1, drought-responsive, S. tuberosum)
phenotype: Overexpression of STANN1 in potato enhances drought tolerance, maintains leaf turgor during water deficit, and improves tuber yield under drought conditions.
mechanism: STANN1 overexpression mitigates drought-induced oxidative stress by enhancing redox homeostasis, increasing NPQ capacity, and modulating phytohormone signaling (e.g., cytokinins and salicylic acid).

genes: STANN1 (Solanum tuberosum annexin 1, drought-responsive, S. tuberosum)
phenotype: Transient expression of STANN1-GFP in N. benthamiana confers increased tolerance to methyl viologen (MeV)-induced photooxidative stress, with reduced ROS accumulation and chloroplast damage.
mechanism: STANN1-GFP expression attenuates MeV-induced oxidative stress by maintaining chloroplast structure and reducing superoxide anion and hydrogen peroxide accumulation.

genes: hpt (hygromycin phosphotransferase, Escherichia coli), FLP (recombinase, Saccharomyces cerevisiae)
phenotype: Overexpression of hpt and FLP enables hygromycin resistance and site-specific recombination for marker excision in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: FLP recombinase mediates excision of the hpt marker gene under oxidative stress, leaving marker-free transgenic rice plants.

genes: hpt (hygromycin phosphotransferase, Escherichia coli), mFLP (modified recombinase, Saccharomyces cerevisiae)
phenotype: Overexpression of hpt and mFLP enables hygromycin resistance and site-specific recombination for marker excision in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: mFLP recombinase, optimized for rice codon usage, mediates excision of the hpt marker gene under oxidative stress, leaving marker-free transgenic rice plants.

genes: hpt (hygromycin phosphotransferase, Escherichia coli), mFLP (modified recombinase, Saccharomyces cerevisiae), NtTC (tocopherol cyclase, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtTC increases total tocopherol content by ~61% and γ-tocopherol by ~194% in Oryza sativa seeds.
mechanism: NtTC catalyzes the conversion of DMPBQ to γ-tocopherol, enhancing tocopherol biosynthesis in rice seeds.

genes: GBM5 (AGAMOUS, Ginkgo biloba, Ginkgo biloba)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of Ginkgo AGAMOUS gene causes homeotic transformation of tomato sepals into carpel-like structures with yellowish-orange coloration and fleshy texture
mechanism: The Ginkgo AG gene has a genuine C function that induces fruit-like development in sepals through activation of ripening-related genes

genes: FIN219 (glucocorticoid-inducible transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FIN219 in Arabidopsis thaliana results in a constitutively shorter hypocotyl phenotype compared to wild type and fin219-2 under all concentrations of MeJA.
mechanism: FIN219 mediates negative feedback regulation of JA signaling, reducing sensitivity to MeJA under high FR light.

genes: PdMYB221 (PdMYB221, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Populus deltoides cv nanlin895)
phenotype: Overexpression of PdMYB221 decreases cell wall thickness of fibers and vessels in Arabidopsis inflorescence stems by ~15-32% and reduces cellulose, xylose, and lignin contents by 10-28%.
mechanism: PdMYB221 represses secondary wall biosynthesis by suppressing secondary wall biosynthetic genes and transcription factors like SND1, NST1, VND6, and MYB85.

genes: GhmMDH1 (mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase 1, Gossypium hirsutum, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhmMDH1 increases root length and biomass in cotton under insoluble P conditions.
mechanism: GhmMDH1 enhances malate production, which chelates metals and promotes P absorption.

genes: GhmMDH1 (mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase 1, Gossypium hirsutum, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Knockdown of GhmMDH1 reduces root length and biomass in cotton under insoluble P conditions.
mechanism: GhmMDH1 knockdown decreases malate production, reducing P absorption.

genes: GhmMDH1-GFP (fusion protein, Gossypium hirsutum, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: GhmMDH1-GFP localizes to mitochondria in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: Mitochondrial target signal in GhmMDH1 directs the fusion protein to mitochondria.

genes: GsAG1 (AGAMOUS homolog, C-class MADS-box gene, Gentiana scabra)
phenotype: Overexpression of GsAG1 in transgenic Arabidopsis causes conversion of sepals into carpeloid organs and partial disappearance of petals.
mechanism: GsAG1 functions as a C-class MADS-box gene responsible for stamen organ identity, similar to Arabidopsis AGAMOUS.

genes: GsAG2 (AGAMOUS homolog, C-class MADS-box gene, Gentiana scabra)
phenotype: Overexpression of GsAG2 in transgenic Arabidopsis showed no significant morphological changes compared to the empty vector control.
mechanism: NA

genes: CP (coat protein, modified with lysine at C-terminus, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Production of TMVLys particles with surface lysine residues for peptide conjugation
mechanism: Overexpression of modified CP gene with lysine residues enables chemical conjugation of peptides to the viral surface

genes: SCL15 (SCL15, SCL15 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The SCL15-sGFP fusion protein was able to complement the scl15-1 mutant phenotypes, resulting in no difference between the phenotypes of complemented lines and wild-type plants in terms of seedling establishment, flowering and plant growth.
mechanism: SCL15 interacts with HDA19 to repress seed maturation genes via histone deacetylation.

genes: SCL15 (SCL15 promoter, GUS reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Strong GUS staining was observed in the vascular tissues of cotyledons, leaves, stamen filaments and primary and lateral roots in T1 transgenic Arabidopsis plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: ETC2 (ETC2, ETC2 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), TRY (TRY, TRY gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), CPC (CPC, CPC gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of Cas9 driven by EC1.2 promoter with rbcS E9 terminator results in 8.3% T1 homozygous triple mutants (etc2 try cpc) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Cas9 driven by egg-cell specific promoter EC1.2p allows targeted mutations in one-cell stage embryos, enabling T1 homozygous mutants.

genes: CHLI1 (CHLI1, CHLI1 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), CHLI2 (CHLI2, CHLI2 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Simultaneous disruption of CHLI1 and CHLI2 leads to an albino phenotype in 13% of T1 plants.
mechanism: Cas9 driven by egg-cell specific promoter EC1.2p allows targeted mutations in one-cell stage embryos, enabling T1 homozygous double mutants.

genes: ETC2 (ETC2, ETC2 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), TRY (TRY, TRY gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), CPC (CPC, CPC gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: EC1.1 promoter with rbcS E9 terminator results in 1.8% T1 triple mutants (etc2 try cpc) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: EC1.1 promoter is less egg cell-specific than EC1.2 promoter, leading to lower mutation efficiency.

genes: ETC2 (ETC2, ETC2 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), TRY (TRY, TRY gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), CPC (CPC, CPC gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: EC1.2 promoter with nos terminator results in 0% T1 triple mutants (etc2 try cpc) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Nos terminator performs worse than rbcS E9 terminator in stabilizing Cas9 mRNA.

genes: PtoPDS (phytoene desaturase, required for chlorophyll biosynthesis, Populus tomentosa)
phenotype: Albino phenotype due to loss of PtoPDS function in Populus tomentosa
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced indels cause frameshift or premature termination in PtoPDS, disrupting chlorophyll biosynthesis

genes: McDFR (dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, Malus crabapple), McFLS (flavonol synthase, Malus crabapple)
phenotype: Silencing McDFR in 'Royalty' leaves results in green coloration and increased flavonol content; silencing McFLS in 'Strawberry Jelly' leads to red leaf margins and elevated anthocyanins.
mechanism: McDFR and McFLS compete for dihydroflavonol substrates, directing biosynthesis toward anthocyanins or flavonols. Silencing McDFR reduces anthocyanin production while increasing flavonols, and vice versa.

genes: McDFR (dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, Malus crabapple), McFLS (flavonol synthase, Malus crabapple)
phenotype: Overexpression of McDFR in 'Strawberry Jelly' promotes anthocyanin accumulation and red coloration; overexpression of McFLS in 'Royalty' suppresses anthocyanins and increases flavonol content.
mechanism: McDFR overexpression enhances anthocyanin biosynthesis by upregulating downstream genes (ANS, UFGT) and downregulating McFLS. McFLS overexpression inhibits McDFR expression, redirecting resources to flavonol production.

genes: CPR1 (CPR1, F-box protein involved in cytoskeleton arrangement and plant defense responses, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of CPR1 rescues the morphogenetic defects in cpr1-j594 and cpr1-j2928 mutants, restoring normal pavement cell shape and size in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CPR1, an F-box protein, is essential for normal cytoskeleton arrangement and plant defense responses, with its FBA domain being indispensable for function.

genes: CPR1I247V (CPR1I247V, F-box protein with point mutation in FBA domain, Arabidopsis thaliana), CPR1ΔFBA (CPR1ΔFBA, F-box protein lacking FBA domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CPR1I247V or CPR1ΔFBA in Arabidopsis thaliana results in pavement cell morphogenetic defects similar to cpr1 loss-of-function mutants, including smaller cells with reduced lobes and increased circularity.
mechanism: The FBA domain of CPR1 is essential for its function; mutations or deletion of this domain disrupt CPR1's ability to form functional SCF complexes, leading to impaired cytoskeleton arrangement and defense responses.

genes: CRK2 (CRK2, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), CRK45 (CRK45, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of crk2 mutation rescues dwarf phenotype and restores normal morphology; complementation of crk45 mutation rescues water loss phenotype and increases water loss compared to mutant and wild type
mechanism: CRK2 and CRK45 function in growth regulation and stomatal water loss control through their receptor-like kinase activity

genes: SPCH (SPCH, Arabidopsis thaliana), nucGFP (nucGFP, synthetic)
phenotype: SPCH promoter activity is uniformly active in early protoderm of wild-type leaf primordia, regardless of SPCH or SCRMs presence.
mechanism: SPCH promoter activity is independent of SPCH and SCRMs, indicating self-activation.

genes: SCRM (SCRM, Arabidopsis thaliana), nucGFP (nucGFP, synthetic)
phenotype: SCRM promoter activity is dependent on SPCH and SCRMs; no activity in spch or scrm scrm2 protoderm.
mechanism: SCRM expression relies on self-activation and SPCH, forming a positive feedback loop.

genes: SCRM2 (SCRM2, Arabidopsis thaliana), nucGFP (nucGFP, synthetic)
phenotype: SCRM2 promoter activity is dependent on SPCH and SCRMs; no activity in spch or scrm scrm2 protoderm.
mechanism: SCRM2 expression relies on self-activation and SPCH, forming a positive feedback loop.

genes: SPCH (SPCH, Arabidopsis thaliana), SPCH-GFP (SPCH-GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: SPCH-GFP accumulates in nuclei of protodermal cells and early stomatal precursors, emphasizing post-transcriptional regulation.
mechanism: SPCH requires heterodimeric partners (SCRMs) to initiate stomatal cell-lineages.

genes: SCRM (SCRM, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP-SCRM (GFP-SCRM, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP-SCRM accumulates in nuclei of protodermal cells and early stomatal precursors, dependent on SPCH.
mechanism: SPCH and SCRM are required to activate SCRM reporter expression.

genes: SCRM2 (SCRM2, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP-SCRM2 (GFP-SCRM2, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP-SCRM2 accumulates in nuclei of protodermal cells and early stomatal precursors, dependent on SPCH.
mechanism: SPCH and SCRM are required to activate SCRM2 reporter expression.

genes: ERECTA (ERECTA, Arabidopsis thaliana), ERECTA-YFP (ERECTA-YFP, synthetic)
phenotype: ERECTA-YFP uniformly accumulates in plasma membrane of protodermal cells, independent of SPCH or SCRMs.
mechanism: ERECTA expression is not dependent on the SPCH•SCRMs module.

genes: TMM (TMM, Arabidopsis thaliana), TMM-YFP (TMM-YFP, synthetic)
phenotype: TMM-YFP accumulates in stomatal-lineage cells, dependent on SPCH and SCRMs.
mechanism: SPCH and SCRM activate TMM expression via direct binding to its promoter.

genes: EPF2 (EPF2, Arabidopsis thaliana), erGFP (erGFP, synthetic)
phenotype: EPF2 promoter activity is detected in wild-type but not in spch or scrm scrm2, indicating SPCH and SCRMs are required for EPF2 expression.
mechanism: SPCH and SCRM together induce EPF2 gene expression.

genes: AtMYB12 (transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of AtMYB12 increases flavonoid content in leaves and fruits of tomato by 6- to 30-fold, with enhanced antioxidant capacity and altered fruit coloration.
mechanism: AtMYB12 up-regulates genes in the phenylpropanoid pathway (PAL, 4CL, CHS, CHI, FLS, glycosyltransferase), leading to increased flavonol and CGA biosynthesis.

mechanism: EIN3 directly activates the expression of ORE1 by binding to its promoter.

genes: ORE1 (ORE1, ORE1/NAC2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ORE1 in a WT background causes early leaf yellowing.
mechanism: ORE1 directly activates the expression of CCGs (NYE1, NYC1, NOL, PAO) by binding to their promoters.

genes: NYE1 (NYE1, NYE1/SGR, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Inducible overexpression of NYE1 reverses the stay-green phenotype of ein3 mutant under ethylene treatment.
mechanism: NYE1 directly activates the expression of CCGs by binding to their promoters.

genes: Raf43 (At3g46930, stress-responsive Raf-like MAPKKK, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of Raf43 increases osmotic, drought, salt, and oxidative stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Raf43 enhances stress tolerance by modulating ABA response and stress-responsive gene expression (e.g., RD17, DREB2A).

genes: Raf43 (At3g46930, stress-responsive Raf-like MAPKKK, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Native promoter-driven expression of Raf43 restores drought and salt stress tolerance in raf43-1 mutant Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Raf43 complements the stress tolerance phenotype by restoring stress-responsive gene expression and ABA signaling.

mechanism: JcGA20ox1 encodes gibberellin 20-oxidase, which increases gibberellin levels promoting lateral bud outgrowth.

phenotype: Overexpression of AtWRI1 induces oil accumulation in leaves (up to 2.2% of dry weight) and down-regulates photosynthesis-related genes.

mechanism: WRI1 homolog shifts carbon flow from photosynthesis and starch synthesis to oil biosynthesis by up-regulating glycolysis and fatty acid synthesis genes.

phenotype: Overexpression of PtWRI1ca induces oil accumulation in leaves and down-regulates photosynthesis-related genes.
mechanism: WRI1 homolog shifts carbon flow from photosynthesis and starch synthesis to oil biosynthesis by up-regulating glycolysis and fatty acid synthesis genes.

genes: cv-n (cv-n, anti-HIV protein, GenBank L48551.1)
phenotype: Overexpression of cv-n in soybean seeds produces 350 µg/g of biologically active rCV-N with anti-HIV activity (EC50 0.82–2.7nM).
mechanism: Seed-specific β-conglycinin promoter directs CV-N accumulation to protein storage vacuoles (PSVs) in soybean cotyledons, with 35S terminator ensuring proper transcription termination.

genes: AtNAA10 (N-terminal acetyltransferase catalytic subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Genetic complementation of homozygous naa10-1 plants with AtNAA10 under control of the CaMV35S promoter rescued the embryo lethal naa10-1 phenotype and results in wild-type-like growth of complemented naa10-1 plants.
mechanism: Complementation confirms the lack of NAA10 as the single cause of the observed phenotype.

genes: NAA10 (N-terminal acetyltransferase catalytic subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Artificial microRNAi sequences directed against NAA10 were expressed under the control of the CaMV35S promoter in stably transformed wild-type Arabidopsis, resulting in significant reduction of growth.
mechanism: Downregulation of NAA10 transcript and protein levels caused growth retardation and decreased abundance of the second NatA complex subunit.

genes: NAA15 (N-terminal acetyltransferase auxiliary subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Artificial microRNAi sequences directed against NAA15 were expressed under the control of the CaMV35S promoter in stably transformed wild-type Arabidopsis, resulting in significant reduction of growth.
mechanism: Downregulation of NAA15 transcript and protein levels caused growth retardation and decreased abundance of the second NatA complex subunit.

genes: OsMADS25 (regulates root development through NO3- regulation, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsMADS25 increases root and shoot growth in rice, with significant effects in the presence of nitrate.
mechanism: OsMADS25 regulates root development through NO3- signaling pathway.

mechanism: OsMADS25 regulates root development through NO3- signaling pathway.

mechanism: Cry1Ac toxin binds to midgut receptors in susceptible larvae, causing cell lysis and death; resistant larvae have altered receptors that prevent toxin binding

mechanism: NA
