phenotype: Unigene20441-YFP fusion protein localizes in the nucleus of N. benthamiana leaf epidermal cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: PANS1 (PANS1, meiosis-related protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PANS1-FLAG fusion protein localizes to the nucleus during prophase I of meiosis, showing broad nuclear distribution and declining expression during late prophase I.
mechanism: PANS1 regulates centromere cohesion and cell cycle progression through control of APC/C activity, interacting with APC/C components CDC20.1 and CDC27b.

genes: PANS1 (PANS1, meiosis-related protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PANS1-GFP-GUS fusion protein shows increased expression in growing parts of the plant, including inflorescence, young buds, and roots, with reduced expression in older tissues.
mechanism: PANS1 regulates centromere cohesion and cell cycle progression through control of APC/C activity, interacting with APC/C components CDC20.1 and CDC27b.

genes: PANS1 (PANS1, meiosis-related protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of pans1 mutant with PANS1 genomic DNA restores normal centromere cohesion and meiotic progression, rescuing fertility defects.
mechanism: PANS1 regulates centromere cohesion and cell cycle progression through control of APC/C activity, interacting with APC/C components CDC20.1 and CDC27b.

plant_species: Nicotiana benthamiana, Nicotiana tabacum, Solanum lycopersicum
genes: miR165/166 target mimic (synthetic)
phenotype: Induces stunting, deformation of tissues, altered leaf shape, enations, and flower deformation in Nicotiana benthamiana; small leaves, distorted shape, enations in tobacco; stunting, deformed leaves, enations in tomato.
mechanism: Interference with miR165/166 activity disrupts adaxial/abaxial and medial/lateral features of leaf development.

plant_species: Nicotiana benthamiana, Nicotiana tabacum, Solanum lycopersicum
genes: dummy TM (synthetic)
phenotype: No discernable differences in phenotype compared to mock-inoculated plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: NPR1 (NPR1, non-expressor of PR-genes 1, Capsella rubella), NPR1 (NPR1, non-expressor of PR-genes 1, Capsella grandiflora)
phenotype: Overexpression of 35S::CrNPR1 abolishes stunted growth in NIL(2gg; 7rr) plants and reduces expression of EDS1, EDS5, and PDF1.2. Overexpression of 35S::CgNPR1 has little effect on morphology despite high expression.
mechanism: NPR1 is a central regulator of systemic acquired resistance, which upregulates EDS1 and EDS5 expression. Overexpression of CrNPR1 suppresses constitutive immune response and growth retardation in incompatible hybrids.

genes: RPP5 (RPP5, TIR-NB-LRR pathogen-response regulator, Capsella rubella)
phenotype: Knockdown of CrRPP5 in incompatible NIL(2gg; 7rr) plants suppresses growth defect and constitutive defence-gene expression.
mechanism: RPP5 homologues in A. thaliana are involved in hybrid necrosis. Knockdown of CrRPP5 in Capsella hybrids suppresses the constitutive immune response and growth retardation, indicating an incompatibility between grandiflora NPR1 and rubella RPP5 alleles.

genes: Cas9 (CRISPR-associated protein 9, codon-optimized for dicotyledons, synthetic), sgRNA (single-guide RNA, customized, synthetic), GFP (green fluorescent protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in the bar transgene and soybean endogenous genes (GmFEI2, GmSHR) with indel frequencies ranging from 0.6% to 95.0% in transgenic hairy roots.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9 system introduces double-strand breaks (DSBs) at target sites, leading to small insertions or deletions (indels) through non-homologous end joining (NHEJ).

genes: DhMYB1 (R2R3-MYB gene involved in cell shape development, Dendrobium hybrida)
phenotype: Direct application of 430 bp dsRNA from the 3' region of DhMYB1 to emerging orchid flower buds reduced expression of DhMYB1 RNA and altered epidermal cell shape in the labellum from conical to flattened.
mechanism: DhMYB1 is involved in the development of the conical cell shape of the epidermal cells of the Dendrobium hybrida flower labellum.

genes: cry1Ab/1Ac (insecticidal toxin, Bt gene, Huahui 1)
phenotype: High resistance to stem borers and leaffolders with Cry1Ab/1Ac protein content of 13.6 μg g−1 in leaves at tillering stage
mechanism: Cry1Ab/1Ac protein toxicity to lepidopteran insects

genes: AtWSCP (AtWSCP, water-soluble chlorophyll-binding protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), Venus (Venus, yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of AtWSCP::Venus in Arabidopsis thaliana results in fluorescence detection in spindle-shaped ER bodies in cotyledons and vacuoles in true leaves.
mechanism: AtWSCP and RshWSCP target ER bodies and vacuoles, similar to BoWSCP and LvWSCP, but do not target chloroplasts.

genes: RshWSCP (RshWSCP, water-soluble chlorophyll-binding protein, Raphanus sativus var. raphanistroides Makino), Venus (Venus, yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of RshWSCP::Venus in Arabidopsis thaliana results in fluorescence detection in spindle-shaped ER bodies in cotyledons and vacuoles in true leaves.
mechanism: AtWSCP and RshWSCP target ER bodies and vacuoles, similar to BoWSCP and LvWSCP, but do not target chloroplasts.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS reporter expression observed in many tissues of transgenic Arabidopsis, especially root vascular system, flowers, and local damaged tissues
mechanism: NA

genes: CiNAC3 (stress-responsive NAC transcription factor, Caragana intermedia, native), CiNAC4 (stress-responsive NAC transcription factor, Caragana intermedia, native)
phenotype: Overexpression of CiNAC3 reduces ABA sensitivity during seed germination and enhances salt tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis
mechanism: CiNAC3 counteracts ABA inhibition of seed germination and enhances salt tolerance by modulating ABA signaling and stress-responsive gene expression

genes: CiNAC3 (stress-responsive NAC transcription factor, Caragana intermedia, native), CiNAC4 (stress-responsive NAC transcription factor, Caragana intermedia, native)
phenotype: Overexpression of CiNAC4 reduces ABA sensitivity during seed germination, enhances salt tolerance, and increases lateral root numbers in transgenic Arabidopsis
mechanism: CiNAC4 promotes lateral root development and counteracts ABA inhibition of seed germination by modulating ABA signaling and stress-responsive gene expression

genes: CiNAC3 (stress-responsive NAC transcription factor, Caragana intermedia, native), CiNAC4 (stress-responsive NAC transcription factor, Caragana intermedia, native)
phenotype: GFP fluorescence predominantly observed in nuclei of transgenic Arabidopsis root tips, confirming nuclear localization of CiNAC3 and CiNAC4
mechanism: NA

genes: AhLPAT2 (AhLPAT2, full-length ORF, peanut)
phenotype: Overexpression of AhLPAT2 increases seed oil content by ~12.2% and seed weight by up to 24.4% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AhLPAT2 promotes lipid accumulation by upregulating genes in the Kennedy pathway and sucrose metabolism, enhancing FA and TAG synthesis.

genes: PNRS1 (resveratrol synthase, peanut, Arachis hypogaea), bar (bialaphos resistance, Streptomyces hygroscopicus)
phenotype: Overexpression of PNRS1 increases trans-resveratrol accumulation in Oryza sativa, with levels up to 3.028 μg/g DW in seeds and 0.697 μg/g FW in seedlings under normal conditions. Transgenic plants show reduced UV-C and dark-induced leaf damage compared to wild-type rice.
mechanism: PNRS1 enhances antioxidant activity by producing trans-resveratrol, which mitigates ROS-induced damage and protects against abiotic stress. Resveratrol accumulation correlates with reduced H2O2 accumulation and delayed leaf senescence under stress conditions.

genes: TaNAC2L (heat stress tolerance, Triticum aestivum L.)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaNAC2L improves heat stress tolerance via acquired thermotolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with transgenic plants showing longer hypocotyls after heat stress recovery compared to wild type.
mechanism: TaNAC2L promotes heat stress response by upregulating downstream stress-responsive genes (DREB2A, DREB2B, AtCYP18-1, RD17, HSP26.5, LEA) and is degraded via the 26S proteasome pathway.

genes: EgrC3′H3 (EgrC3′H3, lignin biosynthetic pathway gene, Eucalyptus grandis)
phenotype: Eucalyptus trees with down-regulated C3′H expression displayed lowered overall lignin content (average 21.7% lignin) and reduced recalcitrance with increased sugar release.
mechanism: RNAi knockdown of C3′H reduces lignin content and alters S/G/H ratios, leading to lower recalcitrance.

genes: EgrC4H1 (EgrC4H1, lignin biosynthetic pathway gene, Eucalyptus grandis)
phenotype: Eucalyptus trees with down-regulated C4H expression had an average of 18.9% lignin and reduced recalcitrance with increased sugar release.
mechanism: RNAi knockdown of C4H reduces lignin content and alters S/G/H ratios, leading to lower recalcitrance.

genes: HC-Pro (HC-Pro, viral protein from PVY, PVY)
phenotype: Chloroplasts in HC-Pro transgenic plants were enlarged (horizontal and vertical axes significantly longer than wild-type, P < 0.01)
mechanism: HC-Pro reduces ATPase activity of NtMinD and competes with NtMinE for binding to NtMinD, disrupting Z-ring assembly and causing chloroplast division arrest

genes: prosystemin (prosystemin, precursor of systemin, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of prosystemin increases resistance against Spodoptera littoralis larvae, Botrytis cinerea, Alternaria solani, and Macrosiphum euphorbiae aphids in tomato plants.
mechanism: Prosystemin overexpression induces constitutive expression of proteinase inhibitors and other defense-related genes, activates jasmonic acid (JA) signaling pathways, and upregulates genes involved in phenylpropanoid metabolism, lignin biosynthesis, and stress response pathways.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic), PVY P1-6x-HCPro (hypervariable region of HC-Protein, Potato virus Y), CMV 2b (viral suppressor of RNA silencing, Cucumber mosaic virus)
phenotype: Transient expression of GFP, PVY P1-6x-HCPro, and CMV 2b in agroinfiltrated leaf patches for silencing suppression assays
mechanism: Viral suppressors (HCPro and 2b) counteract RNA silencing to increase GFP reporter expression

genes: PVY P1-6x-HCPro (hypervariable region of HC-Protein, Potato virus Y), CMV 2b (viral suppressor of RNA silencing, Cucumber mosaic virus)
phenotype: Expression of PVY P1-6x-HCPro and CMV 2b in PVX vectors for agroinfiltration and viral infection studies
mechanism: Viral suppressors (HCPro and 2b) counteract RNA silencing to facilitate viral replication and systemic infection

genes: ZmIRT1 (ZmIRT1, iron and zinc transporter, Zea mays), ZmZIP3 (ZmZIP3, zinc transporter, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmIRT1 increases iron (34.87–115.95%) and zinc (61.97–179.5%) in roots and seeds of Arabidopsis thaliana. Overexpression of ZmZIP3 increases zinc (45.13–92.14%) in roots.
mechanism: ZmIRT1 facilitates Zn and Fe uptake in roots and translocation to seeds. ZmZIP3 is associated with Zn uptake from soil to root and disrupts local metal transporter distribution.

genes: GFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, Clontech pIRES2-EGFP plasmid)
phenotype: Complementation of gfp mutants restores GFP fluorescence and protein expression
mechanism: Wild-type GFP gene compensates for loss-of-function mutations in the gfp mutants

genes: LeGSTU2 (glutathione S-transferase, tomato, Lycopersicon esculentum)
phenotype: Overexpression of LeGSTU2 increases salt and osmotic stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with transgenic plants showing 93.5% germination rate under 150mM NaCl vs 68.9% in wild type, and 1.3-2.2-fold longer root growth under stress conditions.
mechanism: LeGSTU2 maintains cellular ROS homeostasis by scavenging reactive oxygen species and preventing cell membrane damage, as evidenced by higher SOD (33-34% increase) and POD (62-73% increase) activity in transgenic plants under stress.

genes: OsPYL/RCAR10 (OsPYL/RCAR10, ABA receptor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsPYL/RCAR10 causes ABA hypersensitivity in rice.
mechanism: OsPYL/RCAR10 functions as an authentic ABA receptor in rice, similar to its Arabidopsis counterpart.

genes: SAPK10 (SAPK10, SnRK2 kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAPK10 causes delayed germination and reduced seedling growth in rice.
mechanism: SAPK10 stabilizes OsPYL/RCAR receptors via phosphorylation of TE and upregulates ABA biosynthesis.

genes: SAPK8 (SAPK8, SnRK2 kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAPK8 causes delayed germination and reduced seedling growth in rice.
mechanism: SAPK8 stabilizes OsPYL/RCAR receptors via phosphorylation of TE and upregulates ABA biosynthesis.

genes: SAPK9 (SAPK9, SnRK2 kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAPK9 causes delayed germination and reduced seedling growth in rice.
mechanism: SAPK9 stabilizes OsPYL/RCAR receptors via phosphorylation of TE and upregulates ABA biosynthesis.

genes: OsPYL/RCAR10 (OsPYL/RCAR10, ABA receptor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Reducing OsPYL/RCAR10 expression via RNAi causes decreased sensitivity to ABA in rice.
mechanism: OsPYL/RCAR10 acts downstream of te and is specifically involved in TE-mediated ABA responses.

genes: YUC6 (YUCCA6, auxin biosynthesis gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: YUC6 overexpression increases drought tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with survival rates of 45% (yuc6-1D) and 50% (yuc6-1DX35S:iaaL) compared to 25% in wild-type plants.
mechanism: YUC6 overexpression reduces ROS accumulation under drought stress, independent of auxin overproduction. YUC6 functions as a thiol reductase (TR) with holdase chaperone activity, improving ROS scavenging and drought tolerance.

genes: iaaL (IAA-lysine synthase, Pseudomonas savastanoi)
phenotype: 35S:iaaL plants show reduced free IAA levels and lower drought tolerance (22.5% survival) compared to YUC6 overexpression lines.
mechanism: Overexpression of iaaL reduces free IAA levels, but does not confer drought tolerance. YUC6 overexpression counteracts this by increasing auxin levels.

genes: YUC6 (YUCCA6, auxin biosynthesis gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), iaaL (IAA-lysine synthase, Pseudomonas savastanoi)
phenotype: yuc6-1DX35S:iaaL plants retain high-auxin morphological features (elongated petioles) but have drought tolerance (50% survival) similar to yuc6-1D.
mechanism: Coexpression of YUC6 and iaaL restores auxin levels to wild-type but maintains drought tolerance through YUC6's TR activity.

genes: NTRA (NADPH-dependent thioredoxin reductase A, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NTRA overexpression lines (NTRA-OX) show drought tolerance (77.5% survival) and reduced ROS accumulation, similar to YUC6 overexpression.
mechanism: NTRA is a positive control for TR activity. Overexpression enhances ROS scavenging and drought tolerance independently of auxin biosynthesis.

genes: OsABA8ox1 (gene, ABA 8'-hydroxylase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsABA8ox1 increases seedling vigor under cold conditions in rice (Oryza sativa).
mechanism: Reduced endogenous ABA levels lead to increased seedling vigor by antagonizing ABA suppression of peroxidase genes and promoting cell wall loosening.

genes: RCG3 (rice chitinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of rice chitinase (RCG3) confers resistance to fusarium wilt (F. oxysporum) and early blight (A. solani) in tomato plants, with transgenic lines showing significantly reduced lesion size and PEBI (6.6-20 vs 100 in controls).
mechanism: Rice chitinase gene (RCG3) expresses antifungal activity against fungal pathogens by degrading chitin in fungal cell walls.

genes: CENH3 (wild-type histone fold domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: native CENH3 promoter-native CENH3 histone fold domain-native 3' UTR
phenotype: Transgenic plants expressing wild-type CENH3 fully complement the cenh3-1 null mutation, producing 100% normal seeds and fully fertile plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: CENH3 (histone fold domain, A86V mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants expressing A86V-CENH3 produce 32–33% dead seeds and 2.7–3.87% paternal haploids upon crossing with Ler gl1-1 CENH3/CENH3 plants.
mechanism: Altered CENH3 A86V disrupts centromere function, leading to maternal genome elimination and paternal haploid induction via missegregation in hybrid embryos.

genes: ARF2 (AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Downregulation of ARF2 partially restores stem cell maintenance in zll-1 mutants.
mechanism: AGO10 represses ARF2 transcription through REV activity.

genes: ARF2 (AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased ARF2 levels enhance stem cell termination in zll-1 mutants.
mechanism: AGO10 represses ARF2 transcription through REV activity.

genes: ARF2 (AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Upregulation of ARF2 expression in zll-1 embryos.
mechanism: AGO10 represses ARF2 transcription through REV activity.

genes: BnaA.TTG2.a.1 (BnaA.TTG2.a.1, trichome development, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnaA.TTG2.a.1 increases trichome numbers in Arabidopsis and B. napus.
mechanism: BnaA.TTG2.a.1 enhances trichome initiation and spatial distribution by affecting auxin biosynthesis genes under salt stress.

genes: AtTTG2 (AtTTG2, trichome development, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtTTG2 rescues trichome defects in the Arabidopsis ttg2-1 mutant.
mechanism: AtTTG2 functions in trichome development by regulating auxin biosynthesis genes.

genes: BnaA.TTG2.a.1 (BnaA.TTG2.a.1, salt stress response, Brassica napus)
phenotype: BnaA.TTG2.a.1-SRDX fusion protein represses auxin biosynthesis gene expression in Arabidopsis under salt stress.
mechanism: BnaA.TTG2.a.1-SRDX binds to the promoters of TRP5 and YUC2, repressing their transcription and reducing IAA levels.

genes: HbCBF1 (Hevea brasiliensis C-repeat binding factor 1, Hevea brasiliensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of HbCBF1 in Arabidopsis increases cold resistance, with 37-36% lower electrolyte leakage and 8-31% survival after -6°C freezing compared to wild type
mechanism: HbCBF1 activates COR genes (COR15a, RD29a) which confer cold tolerance through cellular protection mechanisms

genes: OsPYL3 (OsPYL3, ABA receptor, Oryza sativa), OsPYL9 (OsPYL9, ABA receptor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsPYL3 and OsPYL9 substantially improves drought and cold stress tolerance in rice.
mechanism: OsPYLs positively regulate the ABA response during seed germination and enhance stress tolerance by upregulating ABA-regulated genes.

genes: EcbHLH57 (EcbHLH57, stress-responsive bHLH transcription factor, finger millet)
phenotype: Overexpression of EcbHLH57 in tobacco enhances drought, salinity, and oxidative stress tolerance with increased chlorophyll content, reduced electrolyte leakage, and improved photosynthetic efficiency under stress conditions.
mechanism: EcbHLH57 upregulates stress-responsive genes (LEA14, rd29A, HSP70, SOD, APX) to enhance ROS scavenging, stabilize proteins, and maintain photosynthetic capacity under abiotic stress.

genes: NtMLO1 (NtMLO1, MLO gene required for powdery mildew susceptibility, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtMLO1 restores powdery mildew (PM) susceptibility in tomato Slmlo1 mutant line, with average disease scores of 1.8 and 1.7 in T2 families.
mechanism: NtMLO1 functions as a PM susceptibility gene, required for fungal infection; its overexpression complements the loss-of-function Slmlo1 mutation.

genes: NtMLO1 (NtMLO1-Q198R, MLO gene with Q198R mutation, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtMLO1-Q198R fails to restore PM susceptibility in tomato Slmlo1 mutant line; transgenic plants remain resistant with disease scores similar to the mutant line.
mechanism: The Q198R mutation in NtMLO1 causes complete loss of function, rendering the gene unable to confer PM susceptibility.

genes: AtABCG30 (AtABCG30, promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana), uidA (uidA, β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: The AtABCG30 promoter::uidA construct is used to study gene expression in the endosperm and embryo of Arabidopsis seeds.
mechanism: The uidA reporter gene is expressed under the AtABCG30 promoter to visualize expression patterns in seed tissues.

genes: AtABCG31 (AtABCG31, promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana), uidA (uidA, β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: The AtABCG31 promoter::uidA construct is used to study gene expression in the endosperm and embryo of Arabidopsis seeds.
mechanism: The uidA reporter gene is expressed under the AtABCG31 promoter to visualize expression patterns in seed tissues.

genes: AtABCG31 (AtABCG31, full-length protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), sGFP (sGFP, small green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: The 35Spro::sGFP::AtABCG31 construct is used to study the plasma membrane localization of AtABCG31 in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts and tobacco epidermis cells.
mechanism: The sGFP fusion protein is expressed under the CaMV35S promoter to visualize AtABCG31 localization in protoplasts.

genes: PEX5 (PEX5, peroxin involved in PTS1 import, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PEX5 exacerbates the peroxisomal defects of pex4-1, leading to increased IBA resistance and heightened thiolase PTS2 processing defect.
mechanism: PEX5 lingering on the peroxisomal membrane impedes peroxisome function.

genes: PEX7 (PEX7, PTS2 matrix protein receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PEX7 in wild type does not worsen pex4-1 defects but rescues the mild thiolase PTS2-processing defect at 22°C.
mechanism: NA

genes: PEX7 (PEX7, PTS2 matrix protein receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PEX7 in pex4-1 does not worsen defects but rescues the mild thiolase PTS2-processing defect at 22°C.
mechanism: NA

genes: IbGGPS (geranylgeranyl diphosphate synthase (GGPS), Ipomoea batatas)
phenotype: Overexpression of IbGGPS increases total carotenoid content by ~10% and enhances osmotic stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, as evidenced by significantly longer root growth under PEG-infused conditions.
mechanism: IbGGPS enhances carotenoid biosynthesis in plastids, leading to increased antioxidant activity and osmotic stress tolerance through elevated superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity and reduced malondialdehyde (MDA) content.

genes: DnSIZ1 (DnSIZ1, SUMO E3 ligase, Dendrobium nobile)
phenotype: Overexpression of DnSIZ1 in Arabidopsis siz1-2 mutant partially complements dwarfism, leaf curl, and short leaf phenotypes, increases SUMO conjugate levels under heat shock, and suppresses ABA hypersensitivity in seed germination.
mechanism: DnSIZ1 acts as a SUMO E3 ligase, enhancing SUMO conjugation and modulating stress responses and flowering through vernalization-induced pathways.

genes: DnSIZ1 (DnSIZ1, SUMO E3 ligase, Dendrobium nobile), EGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: DnSIZ1 fused to EGFP localizes to the nucleus in Arabidopsis root cells.
mechanism: Nuclear localization of DnSIZ1 suggests its role in SUMOylation of nuclear substrates.

genes: crtB (phytoene synthase, Pantoea ananatis, synthetic), bkt1 (ketolase, Haematococcus pluvialis, synthetic) (Pisum sativum ribulose 1,5-biphosphate carboxylase small subunit transit peptide)
phenotype: Overexpression of crtB and bkt1 leads to accumulation of canthaxanthin and astaxanthin in soybean seeds, with canthaxanthin levels reaching 18-52 μg/g dry seed and astaxanthin detected in some events.
mechanism: Overexpression of phytoene synthase (crtB) increases β-carotene production, while ketolase (bkt1) converts β-carotene to canthaxanthin and astaxanthin via endogenous hydroxylation.

genes: crtB (phytoene synthase, Pantoea ananatis, synthetic), crtW (ketolase, Brevundimonas sp. SD212, synthetic) (Pisum sativum ribulose 1,5-biphosphate carboxylase small subunit transit peptide)
phenotype: Overexpression of crtB and crtW leads to accumulation of canthaxanthin in soybean seeds, with canthaxanthin levels reaching 4-52 μg/g dry seed and astaxanthin detected in some events.
mechanism: Overexpression of phytoene synthase (crtB) increases β-carotene production, while ketolase (crtW) converts β-carotene to canthaxanthin. Endogenous soybean β-carotene hydroxylase (Glyma10g37560) further converts canthaxanthin to astaxanthin.

genes: cp4EPSPS (glyphosate-resistant gene, codon-optimized for cotton, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic cotton plants expressing cp4EPSPS show glyphosate resistance at 1900 ml/acre application and 100% insect mortality from Bt proteins
mechanism: Cp4EPSPS confers glyphosate resistance by inhibiting the 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase enzyme pathway, while Cry1Ac and Cry2A proteins provide insect resistance

genes: TCF1 (promoter, GUS reporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of TCF1pro::GUS validates induction of TCF1 expression in response to cold.
mechanism: NA

genes: TCF1 (promoter, GFP::TCF1 fusion, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of TCF1pro::GFP-TCF1 in tcf1-1 plants shows nuclear localization of TCF1 protein.
mechanism: NA

genes: TCF1 (RNAi, TCF1 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: TCF1-RNAi lines show increased freezing tolerance under cold acclimation.
mechanism: NA

genes: BCB (amiRNA, BCB gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: amiRNA-BCB plants show increased freezing tolerance and reduced lignin accumulation.
mechanism: BCB regulates lignin accumulation and freezing tolerance.

genes: OsDof25 (OsDof25, Dof transcription factor, Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsDof25 increases GUS activity by ~2-fold in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: OsDof25 activates the OsC4PPDK promoter by binding to the CTTT motif at position −291 bp.

genes: OsDof25 (OsDof25, Dof transcription factor, Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated down-regulation of OsDof25 reduces OsC4PPDK mRNA levels in transgenic rice.
mechanism: OsDof25 regulates OsC4PPDK expression through the CTTT motif in its promoter.

genes: OsDof25 (OsDof25, Dof transcription factor, Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsDof25 increases OsC4PPDK mRNA levels in transgenic rice.
mechanism: OsDof25 activates the OsC4PPDK promoter by binding to the CTTT motif at position −291 bp.

genes: OsDof25 (OsDof25, Dof transcription factor, Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica)
phenotype: OsDof25-GFP fusion protein is localized in the nucleus of rice protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsDof25 (OsDof25, Dof transcription factor, Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica)
phenotype: OsDof25-GFP fusion protein is localized in the nucleus of rice protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: PhAOC (ALLENE OXIDE CYCLASE, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Reduced PhAOC transcript and protein levels, diminished jasmonate accumulation, and delayed adventitious root formation in cuttings
mechanism: RNAi-mediated knock-down of PhAOC reduces jasmonate biosynthesis, leading to delayed adventitious root formation

genes: CHR729 (chromodomain helicase DNA-binding protein 3, rice, synthetic)
phenotype: RNAi transgenic plants exhibit reduced plant height, seed germination rate, chlorophyll content, panicle number, and flag leaf dimensions compared to wild-type Nipponbare, mimicking the t483 mutant phenotype.
mechanism: CHR729 regulates plant development through the gibberellin (GA) pathway, with altered GA biosynthesis and signaling contributing to the observed phenotypes.

genes: CHR729 (chromodomain helicase DNA-binding protein 3, rice, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of the CHR729-GFP fusion protein in rice protoplasts localizes to the nucleus, confirming that CHR729 is a nuclear protein.
mechanism: CHR729 is localized in the nucleus, suggesting it functions as a transcriptional regulator.

genes: Os08g01480 (Os08g01480, metal stress-responsive cytochrome P450, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of Os08g01480 in Arabidopsis confers tolerance to heavy metals (As(III), As(V), Cd, Cr(VI)), salt (NaCl), osmotic (mannitol), and temperature (cold/heat) stresses. Transgenic lines show ~40% increased root length under As(V) stress, ~30% faster germination, and enhanced lateral root formation compared to wild type.
mechanism: Os08g01480 upregulates defense-related genes (HY5, EDS1, COI1) and auxin/ABA pathways, promoting stress tolerance through enhanced root growth and energy dissipation via xanthophyll cycle.

genes: uidA (uidA, β-glucuronidase reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Promoter activity of Os08g01480 drives GUS expression in Arabidopsis flowers (androecium), roots, and shoots under heavy metal (As(III), As(V), Cd, Cr(VI)), salt, osmotic, and temperature stresses. GUS staining shows significant activity during As(III), As(V), and Cd stress but not Cr(VI) at lower concentrations.
mechanism: Os08g01480 promoter contains cis-regulatory elements for stress response and development. GUS activity confirms promoter activation under abiotic stresses, indicating its role in stress-responsive gene regulation.

genes: AtPLC2 (phosphoinositide-specific phospholipase C, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS staining localized to trichomes, leaf vasculature, inflorescence buds, stigma, and root vasculature in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: AtPLC2-GUS fusion protein localizes to plasma membrane and vascular tissues, indicating AtPLC2's role in phosphoinositide metabolism and tissue development

genes: AtPLC2 (phosphoinositide-specific phospholipase C, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Fluorescent PLC2-Venus localized to plasma membrane in root tips, lateral roots, and various cell types, confirming plasma membrane localization of AtPLC2
mechanism: AtPLC2-Venus fusion protein co-localizes with plasma membrane marker FM4-64, demonstrating plasma membrane localization critical for phosphoinositide signaling

genes: AtPLC2 (phosphoinositide-specific phospholipase C, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of plc2-1 mutant restored root length, fresh weight, and dry weight to wild-type levels in both Wassilewskija and Columbia-0 ecotypes
mechanism: Genomic AtPLC2 expression under native promoter rescues growth defects and ER stress hypersensitivity, confirming AtPLC2's essential role in phosphoinositide metabolism and ER homeostasis

genes: mALS (mutated acetolactate synthase gene, resistance to sulfonylurea herbicides, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of mALS confers resistance to chlorsulfuron in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: mALS mutations alter the herbicide binding site in ALS, preventing sulfonylurea herbicide inhibition.

genes: LTI6b (cold-regulated gene, plasma membrane localization, Marchantia polymorpha), TagRFP (tag red fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of TagRFP-LTI6b localizes to plasma membrane in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: TagRFP fusion with LTI6b enables visualization of plasma membrane localization via fluorescence.

genes: SP-GFP-HDEL (signal peptide-GFP-HDEL fusion, endoplasmic reticulum localization, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of SP-GFP-HDEL localizes to endoplasmic reticulum in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: SP-GFP-HDEL fusion contains ER retention signal (HDEL) for endoplasmic reticulum localization.

genes: tdTomato-NLS (tandem dimer Tomato fluorescent protein with nuclear localization signal, synthetic), GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of tdTomato-NLS localizes to nucleus and GUS expression in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: Nuclear localization signal directs tdTomato to nucleus; GUS serves as reporter for gene expression.

genes: IDUA (human α-L-iduronidase, Homo sapiens), RTB (ricin B lectin, plant lectin)
phenotype: Expression of RTB:IDUA fusion protein in N. benthamiana leaves with enzymatic activity detected at ~110 kDa (Fig. 1b).
mechanism: RTB:IDUA fusion retained both lectin binding and IDUA enzymatic activity, with codon-optimized versions showing improved yield.

genes: IDUA (human α-L-iduronidase, Homo sapiens), RTB (ricin B lectin, plant lectin)
phenotype: Codon-optimized IDUA (optIDUA) showed significantly higher yield in N. benthamiana leaves compared to wild-type IDUA (Fig. 1b).
mechanism: Codon optimization based on tobacco preferences improved IDUA expression in plants.

genes: IDUA (human α-L-iduronidase, Homo sapiens), RTB (ricin B lectin, plant lectin)
phenotype: RTB:optIDUA fusion protein showed improved yield and enzymatic activity in N. benthamiana leaves compared to RTB:wtIDUA (Fig. 1b).
mechanism: Codon-optimized IDUA in the RTB fusion retained lectin binding and enzymatic activity with enhanced expression.

genes: OsSar1abc (seed-specific ER stress suppression, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Transgenic seeds show opaque, floury and shrunken endosperm with lethal embryos due to ER stress caused by blocked secretory proteins in the ER
mechanism: RNAi suppression of OsSar1abc blocks secretory protein exit from ER, causing ER stress and abnormal seed development

genes: VQ12 (VQ motif-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic), VQ29 (VQ motif-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic)
phenotype: GUS staining shows VQ12 expression in root, leaf, hypocotyl, and silique base; VQ29 expression similar to VQ12
mechanism: NA

genes: VQ12 (VQ motif-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic), VQ29 (VQ motif-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic)
phenotype: VQ12-GFP and VQ29-GFP fusion proteins show nuclear localization in Nicotiana benthamiana
mechanism: VQ12 and VQ29 are nuclear proteins

genes: VQ12 (VQ motif-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic)
phenotype: amiR-vq12 transgenic plants show reduced VQ12 expression and increased resistance to Botrytis cinerea
mechanism: VQ12 negatively regulates plant resistance against Botrytis cinerea

genes: VQ12 (VQ motif-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic), VQ29 (VQ motif-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic)
phenotype: Overexpression of VQ12 or VQ29 increases susceptibility to Botrytis cinerea
mechanism: VQ12 and VQ29 negatively regulate plant resistance against Botrytis cinerea

genes: AtCASPL4C1 (At3G55390, CASP family member, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AtCASPL4C1 promoter-GUS reporter in Arabidopsis shows expression in roots, leaves, vascular tissues, and floral organs.
mechanism: AtCASPL4C1 is expressed in a wide range of tissues, including roots, leaves, and floral organs, indicating its role in growth and development.

genes: BDT1 (miR156d, microRNA gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Transgenic plants transformed with pWT-BDT1 were moderately short.
mechanism: The nDart1–3 sequence increased the amount of mature miR156d in Bdt1 without disruption of the miR156d gene. The miR156 function is quantitative.

genes: BDT1 (miR156d, microRNA gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: pBdt1-BDT1 lines had aberrant panicles and significantly reduced fertility.
mechanism: The nDart1–3 sequence increased the amount of mature miR156d in Bdt1 without disruption of the miR156d gene. The miR156 function is quantitative.

genes: BDT1 (miR156d, microRNA gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: p35S-BDT1 plants generated no T1 generation due to the lack of inflorescences and a sterile spikelet on a branch.
mechanism: The nDart1–3 sequence increased the amount of mature miR156d in Bdt1 without disruption of the miR156d gene. The miR156 function is quantitative.

genes: Hrap (Hypersensitive Response Assisting Protein, Capsicum annuum), Pflp (Plant Ferredoxin Like Protein, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Resistance to Xanthomonas wilt disease (Xanthomonas campestris pv. musacearum)
mechanism: Hrap and Pflp proteins confer resistance to Xanthomonas wilt disease by triggering plant defense mechanisms

genes: Hrap (Hypersensitive Response Assisting Protein, Capsicum annuum), Pflp (Plant Ferredoxin Like Protein, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Resistance to Xanthomonas wilt disease (Xanthomonas campestris pv. musacearum)
mechanism: Hrap and Pflp proteins confer resistance to Xanthomonas wilt disease by triggering plant defense mechanisms

genes: LjABCG1 (LjABCG1, ABCG transporter, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: Overexpression of LjABCG1 partially complements the pdr8 mutant's resistance to P. infestans in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: LjABCG1 transports Arabidopsis endogenous metabolites such as camalexin and glucosinolates or toxic compounds of pathogens in Arabidopsis upon infection.

genes: LjABCG1 (LjABCG1, ABCG transporter, Lotus japonicus), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity is strongly expressed in steles of lateral roots and young parts of primary roots, especially within a few centimeters of the tips in Lotus japonicus.
mechanism: LjABCG1 promoter drives GUS expression in root tissues, particularly in steles and lateral roots.

genes: Glyma11g13220 (Glycine max vernalization pathway gene, soybean, synthetic)
phenotype: Over-expression of Glyma11g13220 in Arabidopsis Columbia-0 (Col-0) caused early flowering, with transgenic lines flowering 3-4 days earlier than wild type and reduced rosette leaf numbers
mechanism: Glyma11g13220 represses floral repressor FLC and upregulates FT, leading to early flowering through vernalization pathway activation

genes: myosin XI-K (globular tail domain, N. benthamiana, N. benthamiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of myosin XI-K globular tail domain reduces organelle trafficking velocity by ~70% in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: The globular tail domain of myosin XI-K inhibits myosin-dependent transport by competing with endogenous myosin cargo binding.

genes: MyoB1 (DUF593 domain, N. benthamiana, N. benthamiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MyoB1 DUF593 domain reduces MyoB1-GFP compartment trafficking velocity by ~50% in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: The DUF593 domain of MyoB1 inhibits myosin binding to MyoB receptors, disrupting myosin-dependent transport.

genes: MyoB2 (DUF593 domain, N. benthamiana, N. benthamiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MyoB2 DUF593 domain reduces MyoB1-GFP compartment trafficking velocity by ~65% in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: The DUF593 domain of MyoB2 inhibits myosin binding to MyoB receptors, disrupting myosin-dependent transport.

genes: μNS (mammalian reovirus, mammalian reovirus, mammalian reovirus)
phenotype: Overexpression of mCherry-μNS forms motile cytosolic inclusion bodies in N. benthamiana, used as inert tracers for cytoplasmic streaming.
mechanism: mCherry-μNS inclusion bodies passively follow cytoplasmic streaming without direct myosin binding.

genes: MyoB1 (full-length, N. benthamiana, N. benthamiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MyoB1-GFP targets to motile compartments similar to Arabidopsis MyoB1-GFP, validating the construct for dominant negative inhibition experiments.
mechanism: MyoB1-GFP is targeted to myosin-MyoB compartments, serving as a marker for myosin-dependent trafficking.

genes: MyoB2 (full-length, N. benthamiana, N. benthamiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MyoB2-GFP targets to motile compartments similar to Arabidopsis MyoB2-GFP, validating the construct for dominant negative inhibition experiments.
mechanism: MyoB2-GFP is targeted to myosin-MyoB compartments, serving as a marker for myosin-dependent trafficking.

genes: MyoB1 (YFP, N. benthamiana, N. benthamiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MyoB1-YFP rescues defective stem growth and morphology in the xi-k myob1 myob2 myob3 s4KO line.
mechanism: MyoB1-YFP restores myosin-MyoB compartment function, rescuing growth defects in synthetic quintuple mutants.

genes: MyoB2 (YFP, N. benthamiana, N. benthamiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MyoB2-YFP rescues defective stem growth and morphology in the xi-k myob1 myob2 myob3 s4KO line.
mechanism: MyoB2-YFP restores myosin-MyoB compartment function, rescuing growth defects in synthetic quintuple mutants.

genes: hMBP-Sigma (human myelin basic protein fused to Reovirus Sigma 1 protein, synthetic, Homo sapiens/Reovirus)
phenotype: Overexpression of hMBP-Sigma results in 307 differentially expressed genes in soybean seeds, with downregulation of photosynthesis and thylakoid function genes.
mechanism: NA

genes: AS2 (Arabidopsis thaliana, fusion with 35S promoter, synthetic)
phenotype: 35S:AS2 overexpression increases geminivirus susceptibility in Arabidopsis and N. benthamiana.
mechanism: AS2 overexpression enhances DCP2 decapping activity, accelerating mRNA decay and inhibiting PTGS. This promotes viral replication.

genes: BV1 (Cabbage leaf curl virus, fusion with ECFP, synthetic)
phenotype: BV1 overexpression activates AS2 expression and translocates AS2 to cytosolic P bodies.
mechanism: BV1 binds AS2 in the nucleus and shuttles it to cytosol, enhancing DCP2 decapping activity. This suppresses PTGS and promotes viral replication.

genes: RhAG (Rosa hybrida AGAMOUS homolog, Rosa hybrida)
phenotype: Silencing of RhAG increases petal number through increased production of petaloid stamens in Rosa hybrida.
mechanism: RhAG suppression leads to homeotic conversion of stamens into petals, increasing petal number.

genes: LeNCED1 (9-cis-epoxycarotenoid dioxygenase, Solanum lycopersicum, tomato)
phenotype: Overexpression of LeNCED1 under the rd29A promoter increases drought resistance in petunia, with 94.4% recovery after 14 days of drought stress compared to 11% in controls. Transgenic plants show increased ABA and proline accumulation under drought stress.
mechanism: LeNCED1 overexpression enhances ABA biosynthesis, leading to increased stomatal closure and osmoregulation via proline accumulation. Stress-inducible rd29A promoter avoids constitutive ABA overproduction and associated pleiotropic effects like photobleaching.

genes: LeNCED1 (9-cis-epoxycarotenoid dioxygenase, Solanum lycopersicum, tomato)
phenotype: Constitutive overexpression of LeNCED1 under CaMV-35S promoter causes low germination rate, stunted growth, and photobleaching in petunia. Used as a control for pleiotropic effects.
mechanism: Constitutive ABA overproduction leads to stomatal closure and reduced photosynthesis under non-stress conditions, causing growth defects and photobleaching.

genes: PhGID1A (GID1-like gene, Petunia x hybrida), PhGID1B (GID1-like gene, Petunia x hybrida), PhGID1C (GID1-like gene, Petunia x hybrida)
phenotype: Silencing of PhGID1 had a strong impact on plant architecture, resulting in plants with short branches and internodes, small, dark leaves and late flowering.
mechanism: Downregulation of GID1-like genes interferes with GA signal transduction, leading to dwarfism.

genes: gai (GA-insensitive mutant gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of gai caused a dramatic retardation of plant growth in the treated seedlings, resulting in smaller leaf size.
mechanism: Overexpression of the GA-insensitive mutant gene inhibits GA signaling, leading to growth retardation.

genes: BcRISP1 (BcRISP1, ubiquinol cytochrome reductase iron-sulfur subunit, Brassica campestris ssp. chinensis Makino)
phenotype: Overexpression of BcRISP1 in Arabidopsis thaliana reduces pollen formation, impairs pollen tube growth, and causes shorter siliques and lower seed set compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: BcRISP1 overexpression disrupts mitochondrial electron transport chain, increases ROS generation, and affects mitochondrial energy metabolism, leading to reduced fertility.

genes: SlCaM2 (SlCaM2, calmodulin, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlCaM2 delays fruit ripening in tomato, with fruits remaining green until day 8-9 compared to antisense fruits which turn orange/red by day 11.
mechanism: SlCaM2 overexpression suppresses ethylene-dependent ripening by maintaining calmodulin levels during the transition period from mature green to ripe.

genes: SlCaM2 (SlCaM2, calmodulin, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Antisense SlCaM2 accelerates fruit ripening, with fruits turning orange/red by day 11 compared to control fruits at breaker/turning stage.
mechanism: SlCaM2 knockdown reduces total calmodulin levels during the transition period, facilitating ethylene-dependent ripening by allowing ethylene burst and downstream gene activation.

genes: rolB (rolB, root locus gene B, synthetic), rolC (rolC, root locus gene C, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of rolB and rolC increases artemisinin content by 3-7-fold and artesunate by 3-10-fold in Artemisia carvifolia.
mechanism: RolB and RolC overexpression enhances secondary metabolite production by upregulating artemisinin biosynthetic genes (ADS, CYP71AV1, ALDH1) and increasing trichome density (20-30 trichomes/cm² vs. 5-7 in wild type).

genes: rolB (rolB, root locus gene B, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of rolB increases artemisinin content by 3-7-fold and artesunate by 3-10-fold in Artemisia carvifolia.
mechanism: RolB overexpression enhances secondary metabolite production by upregulating artemisinin biosynthetic genes (ADS, CYP71AV1, ALDH1) and increasing trichome density (20-30 trichomes/cm² vs. 5-7 in wild type).

genes: rolC (rolC, root locus gene C, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of rolC increases artemisinin content by 3.8-6-fold and artesunate by 4.4-8.9-fold in Artemisia carvifolia.
mechanism: RolC overexpression enhances secondary metabolite production by upregulating artemisinin biosynthetic genes (ADS, CYP71AV1, ALDH1) and increasing trichome density (20-30 trichomes/cm² vs. 5-7 in wild type).

genes: SsMYB3 (SsMYB3, R2R3 MYB-type PA regulator, Coleus blumei)
phenotype: Complementation of Arabidopsis tt2 mutant seed coat phenotype, restoring brown pigmentation and CT accumulation in T1 transgenic seeds.
mechanism: SsMYB3 interacts with AtTT8 and AtTTG1 to reform the MBW complex, activating PA-specific genes ANR, DFR, and ANS while repressing anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: SsMYB3 (SsMYB3, R2R3 MYB-type PA regulator, Coleus blumei)
phenotype: Overexpression of SsMYB3 in tobacco reduces anthocyanin content by ~80% and increases CT content by ~3-fold, resulting in white flowers with pale-pink veins (e.g., OX-2) or nearly white flowers (e.g., OX-15).
mechanism: SsMYB3 forms a SsMYB3-complex with NtAn1a/NtJAF13-1 and NtAn11-1, upregulating PA biosynthetic genes NtLAR and NtANR while downregulating NtUFGT, the key anthocyanin gene, leading to reduced anthocyanin accumulation.

genes: SP1 (SUPPRESSOR OF PPI1 LOCUS1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SP1 overexpression increases abiotic stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with overexpressors showing enhanced survival under salinity, osmotic, and oxidative stress conditions compared to wild-type and sp1 mutants.
mechanism: SP1 regulates ROS levels by modulating chloroplast protein import machinery, particularly TOC components, to limit photosynthetic activity and reduce ROS overproduction during stress.

genes: oCas9 (codon-optimized Cas9 from Streptococcus pyogenes, with NLS sequences, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of codon-optimized Cas9 (oCas9) with NLS sequences in Nicotiana benthamiana does not cause developmental defects in any developmental stages.
mechanism: NA

genes: fsGUS (frame-shift GUS gene, synthetic), gRNA (20 bp sequence targeting fsGUS, synthetic)
phenotype: Co-infiltration of 35S-fsGUS and U6-gRNA in Nicotiana benthamiana results in GUS expression detected by colored deposition in leaves, indicating Cas9 activity and DNA cleavage at the target site.
mechanism: Cas9 nuclease cleaves DNA 3 bp upstream of the PAM motif guided by gRNA, repaired by NHEJ causing indels that restore GUS functionality.

genes: gRNA (20 bp sequence targeting NbPDS, synthetic)
phenotype: 30% of Nicotiana benthamiana plants co-infiltrated with U6-gRNA::NbPDS and CaLCuV vectors show photobleaching in leaves by three weeks post infiltration, with 85% mutation rate in NbPDS gene.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated cleavage of NbPDS gene by gRNA, repaired by NHEJ causing indels that disrupt PDS function, leading to photobleaching.

genes: gRNA (20 bp sequence targeting NbIspH, synthetic)
phenotype: 50% of Nicotiana benthamiana plants co-infiltrated with U6-gRNA::NbIspH and CaLCuV vectors show photobleaching in leaves by three weeks post infiltration, with 75% mutation rate in NbIspH gene.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated cleavage of NbIspH gene by gRNA, repaired by NHEJ causing indels that disrupt IspH function, leading to photobleaching.

genes: C1 (Curcin 1, ribosome-inactivating protein, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: C1 protein content in endosperm of transgenic seeds is greatly reduced or undetectable; C1 transcripts are undetectable in endosperm of T3 seeds
mechanism: RNA interference generated from the RNAi cassette down-regulates C1 gene expression in endosperm

genes: Bar (Bar gene, selectable marker, synthetic), GFP (GFP, reporter gene, synthetic), NPT II (neomycin phosphotransferase II, selectable marker, synthetic)
phenotype: Enables site-specific integration of multiple genes into pre-determined chromosomal sites in rice, allowing iterative gene stacking with marker excision efficiency of ~20%.
mechanism: Cre-lox and FLP-FRT site-specific recombination systems facilitate gene integration, while I-SceI and ZFN nucleases mediate marker gene excision through double-strand break repair, enabling seamless gene stacking.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Enables FLP-FRT-mediated site-specific integration of GUS gene into marker-free SSI loci in rice, demonstrating reactivity of FRT sites for iterative gene stacking.
mechanism: FLP-FRT site-specific recombination system facilitates gene integration into pre-determined chromosomal sites, allowing promoter activation of selectable marker genes.

genes: ArcLight (SEpHluorinA227D, voltage-sensing domain of Ci-VSD, synthetic), CBL1 (CALCINEURIN B-LIKE PROTEIN 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), WPP (Trp-Pro-Pro motif, Arabidopsis RANGAP1), SUN2 (SAD1/UNC-84 DOMAIN PROTEIN 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of ArcLight and derivatives in plasma membrane and nuclear membranes of Arabidopsis root cells for pH monitoring
mechanism: SEpHluorinA227D detects pH changes via fluorescence intensity; Ci-VSD provides membrane targeting but does not contribute voltage sensing in plants

genes: Case12 (Calcium sensor 12, synthetic), mCitrine (monomeric citrine, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of Case12 and mCitrine derivatives in plasma membrane of Arabidopsis root cells for calcium and voltage monitoring
mechanism: Case12 detects calcium via fluorescence; mCitrine fused to Ci-VSD or CBL1 for membrane targeting

genes: SEpHluorinA227D (pH-sensitive fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of SEpHluorinA227D in root division zone for pH monitoring
mechanism: SEpHluorinA227D detects pH changes via fluorescence intensity

genes: TaSK1 (Triticum aestivum, wheat), TaSK2 (Triticum aestivum, wheat)
phenotype: Overexpression of mutated TaSK1-A.2-1 in Arabidopsis thaliana results in severe dwarf phenotypes resembling Arabidopsis bin2-1 and BR-signaling mutants, including reduced apical dominance, elongated thinner blade leaves, delayed flowering, and compact dark green leaves with downward rolling.
mechanism: The mutated TaSK1-A.2-1 overexpression disrupts brassinosteroid (BR) signaling by deregulating BR downstream genes (SAUR-AC1, CPD, BAS1) and mimicking BR insensitivity, similar to the bin2-1 mutation in Arabidopsis.

genes: TaSK1 (Triticum aestivum, wheat), TaSK2 (Triticum aestivum, wheat)
phenotype: Overexpression of mutated TaSK2-A.2-1 in Arabidopsis thaliana results in severe dwarf phenotypes resembling Arabidopsis bin2-1 and BR-signaling mutants, including reduced apical dominance, elongated thinner blade leaves, delayed flowering, and compact dark green leaves with downward rolling.
mechanism: The mutated TaSK2-A.2-1 overexpression disrupts brassinosteroid (BR) signaling by deregulating BR downstream genes (SAUR-AC1, CPD, BAS1) and mimicking BR insensitivity, similar to the bin2-1 mutation in Arabidopsis.

genes: AsGLO1 (oat GLOBULIN1 promoter, oat, genomic), LeB4SP (LeB4 signal peptide, Vicia faba, genomic), gfp (green fluorescent protein, synthetic), KDEL (endoplasmic reticulum retention signal, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP accumulates in the endosperm of barley grains at up to 1.2 mg per g dry weight, with no detectable signal in the embryo.
mechanism: The oat GLO1 promoter drives endosperm-specific expression of the LeB4 signal peptide-fused GFP with an ER retention signal, leading to accumulation in the endosperm.

genes: 2G12HC (heavy chain of anti-HIV monoclonal antibody 2G12, synthetic), 2G12LC (light chain of anti-HIV monoclonal antibody 2G12, synthetic)
phenotype: 2G12 antibody accumulates in the barley endosperm at 0.1–0.4% of total soluble protein (TSP), with localization at the periphery of protein bodies alongside hordeins.
mechanism: The oat GLO1 promoter drives expression of 2G12 heavy and light chains with KDEL ER retention signals, leading to co-localization with hordeins in the endosperm protein bodies.

genes: BnMAM1 (BnMAM1, aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis gene, Brassica napus), BnCYP83A1 (BnCYP83A1, aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis gene, Brassica napus), BnUGT74B1 (BnUGT74B1, indolic glucosinolate biosynthesis gene, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnMAM1 increases two aliphatic glucosinolates (2OH3B and 3-Butenyl GSL) by ~1.5-1.7 fold in Brassica napus leaves.
mechanism: BnMAM1 enhances aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis by catalyzing side-chain elongation from 3C to 4C glucosinolates.

genes: BnMAM1 (BnMAM1, aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis gene, Brassica napus), BnCYP83A1 (BnCYP83A1, aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis gene, Brassica napus), BnUGT74B1 (BnUGT74B1, indolic glucosinolate biosynthesis gene, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnCYP83A1 increases two aliphatic glucosinolates (2OH3B and 3-Butenyl GSL) by ~1.8-2.2 fold in Brassica napus leaves.
mechanism: BnCYP83A1 enhances aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis by catalyzing side-chain elongation in the GSL pathway.

genes: BnMAM1 (BnMAM1, aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis gene, Brassica napus), BnCYP83A1 (BnCYP83A1, aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis gene, Brassica napus), BnUGT74B1 (BnUGT74B1, indolic glucosinolate biosynthesis gene, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnUGT74B1 increases indolic glucosinolate (I3M) by 1.5 fold and reduces lesion size by ~70% in Brassica napus infected with Sclerotinia sclerotiorum and Botrytis cinerea.
mechanism: BnUGT74B1 enhances indolic glucosinolate biosynthesis, which produces defense compounds against necrotrophic pathogens.

genes: MEF35 (mitochondrial RNA editing factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restores RNA editing at rpl16-209, cob-286, and nad4-1373 sites to wild-type levels in mef35-2 mutant plants
mechanism: MEF35 is required for RNA editing at these mitochondrial sites

genes: TaCRT1 (calcium-binding protein involved in salt tolerance, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaCRT1 increases salt tolerance in Nicotiana tabacum by enhancing seed germination, shoot growth, root length, and chlorophyll content under NaCl stress.

phenotype: Overexpression of HvGA20ox2 causes GA-overdose phenotype in Arabidopsis with elongated hypocotyls, increased internode length, earlier flowering, and higher growth rate compared to wild type and ga5-3 mutant
mechanism: HvGA20ox2 acts as GA 20-oxidase in gibberellin biosynthesis pathway, increasing GA1+3 content and altering expression of GA biosynthesis/catabolic genes

genes: PhpCAT (Ph21511, plastidial cationic amino-acid transporter, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Downregulation of PhpCAT reduces total emission of phenylalanine-derived volatiles by 20–42% and decreases phenylalanine/tyrosine levels by up to 42% in Petunia hybrida flowers.
mechanism: PhpCAT functions as a plastidial aromatic amino-acid exporter; its downregulation leads to feedback inhibition of the arogenate pathway and increased reliance on the cytosolic phenylpyruvate pathway for phenylalanine biosynthesis.

genes: PhpCAT (Ph21511, plastidial cationic amino-acid transporter, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of PhpCAT increases total emission of phenylalanine-derived volatiles by up to 18% and elevates phenylalanine/tyrosine levels by 23–53% in Petunia hybrida flowers.
mechanism: PhpCAT functions as a plastidial aromatic amino-acid exporter; its overexpression enhances phenylalanine export, reduces feedback inhibition of the arogenate pathway, and increases flux through the phenylalanine biosynthetic network.

genes: Ph21511 (plastid-targeting signal, Petunia hybrida), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Ph215111-52-GFP fusion protein localizes to plastids in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves, confirming the plastidial targeting of PhpCAT.
mechanism: The N-terminal 52 amino acids of PhpCAT contain a plastid-targeting signal, as demonstrated by co-localization of the fusion protein with chlorophyll autofluorescence in plastids.

plant_species: Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa, Pyrus communis
genes: JrVTE1 (tocopherol cyclase, Juglans regia)
phenotype: Overexpression of JrVTE1 increases total tocopherol content by 29.8-47.3 μg/g in jujube and pear, with γ-tocopherol content increasing 2.3-16.2-fold in leaves and roots
mechanism: JrVTE1 catalyzes the cyclization of DMPQ to γ-tocopherol, which is a rate-limiting step in tocopherol biosynthesis

genes: SPL (SPLΔEAR-TPLC, fusion of SPLΔEAR and TPLC, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complements male and female sterility in spl-2
mechanism: SPLΔEAR-TPLC can functionally substitute SPL

genes: SPL (SPLΔEAR, truncated SPL without EAR motif, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Fails to complement male and female sterility in spl-2
mechanism: SPLΔEAR lacks functional EAR motif required for interaction with TPL

genes: SPL (SPLmEAR, mutated EAR motif, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SPLmEAR leads to male and female sterility resembling spl-2
mechanism: SPLmEAR disrupts normal SPL function via dominant-negative effect

genes: TCP17 (TCP17-SPLC, fusion of TCP17 and C-terminal half of SPL, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants display up-curled cotyledons and unfurled flower buds
mechanism: TCP17-SPLC confirms functional association between SPL and TCPs

genes: TCP3 (TCP3, Arabidopsis thaliana), TCP5 (TCP5, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TCP3 and TCP5 leads to aborted ovules in 6/10 and 9/10 lines respectively
mechanism: Excessive TCP activity disrupts normal ovule development

genes: AtMAP18 (AtMAP18, microtubule-associated protein with high-lysine content, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtMAP18 increases total protein and lysine contents in maize kernels by up to 33.60% and 32.30%, respectively.
mechanism: AtMAP18 promotes microtubule activity and microfilament organization, leading to increased zein and non-zein protein synthesis and protein body (PB) formation in endosperm, which enhances lysine content.

genes: OscpSRP43 (OscpSRP43, chloroplast signal recognition particle 43, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of the w67 mutant restores normal green leaf phenotype and chlorophyll levels in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OscpSRP43 is responsible for the yellow-green leaf phenotype in the w67 mutant.

genes: OscpSRP43 (OscpSRP43, chloroplast signal recognition particle 43, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OscpSRP43:GFP fusion protein localizes to chloroplasts in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: OscpSRP43 is targeted to the rice chloroplasts.

genes: OsHDY1 (Oryza sativa, ferredoxin-like protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of hdy1 mutant reverts to green leaf phenotype and rescues heading date, pigment content, and expression of OsHDY1.
mechanism: The mutation in OsHDY1 is responsible for heading date delay and yellow leaf of hdy1.

genes: OsHDY1 (Oryza sativa, ferredoxin-like protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Over-expression of OsHDY1 in hdy1 and NIP rescues leaf color, pigment contents, and plant height, with no visible phenotype in wild type.
mechanism: Increased transcription level of OsHDY1 does not affect visible phenotype of wild type.

genes: CmWRKY15 (WRKY transcription factor, chrysanthemum, Chrysanthemum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmWRKY15 increases susceptibility to A. tenuissima infection in chrysanthemum, with disease severity indexes (DSIs) of 57.01 and 56.73 in transgenic lines compared to 14.63 in wildtype.
mechanism: CmWRKY15 downregulates ABA-responsive genes (ABF4, ABI4, ABI5, RAB18, DREB1A, DREB2A, etc.) and ABA signaling genes, reducing ABA content and impairing resistance to A. tenuissima.

genes: CmWRKY15 (WRKY transcription factor, chrysanthemum, Chrysanthemum)
phenotype: CmWRKY15-GFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus in onion epidermal cells, indicating nuclear localization of CmWRKY15.
mechanism: NA

genes: CmWRKY15 (WRKY transcription factor, chrysanthemum, Chrysanthemum)
phenotype: CmWRKY15 functions as a transcriptional repressor in Arabidopsis protoplasts, reducing luciferase activity compared to controls.
mechanism: CmWRKY15 represses transcriptional activation of GAL4DB reporter constructs, indicating it acts as a transcriptional repressor.

genes: PgGPx (glutathione peroxidase, Pennisetum glaucum, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PgGPx in rice increases salinity and drought stress tolerance, maintaining chlorophyll content, reducing ROS accumulation, and preserving photosynthetic efficiency with minimal yield penalty.
mechanism: PgGPx functions as a thioredoxin-dependent peroxidase that detoxifies reactive oxygen species (ROS), enhances antioxidant enzyme activity (SOD, APX, CAT, GR), and maintains membrane stability and photosynthetic machinery under stress.

genes: NbAGO1-1 (Agotone 1-1, gene involved in gene silencing, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: AGO1-1-silenced plants developed downward leaf curling and stunted leaves
mechanism: AGO1-1 is involved in RNA silencing pathway

genes: NbCMT3-1 (CHROMOMETHYLASE 3-1, DNA methyltransferase, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: CMT3-1-silenced plants presented leaf curling symptom
mechanism: CMT3-1 is involved in DNA methylation maintenance

genes: NbRAV2 (RELATED TO ABIOTIC STRESS 2, transcription repressor, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: RAV2-silenced plants showed increased KYP expression and reduced geminivirus titer
mechanism: RAV2 negatively regulates KYP expression

genes: NbKYP (KRYPTONITE, histone H3K9 methyltransferase, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: KYP-silenced plants showed reduced DNA methylation and TGS dysfunction
mechanism: KYP is essential for H3K9 methylation and DNA methylation maintenance

genes: GFP (Green Fluorescent Protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP in 16c line
mechanism: GFP is used as a reporter for TGS

genes: CaMV 35S promoter (promoter region, Cauliflower mosaic virus)
phenotype: TGS of GFP is induced, leading to silencing
mechanism: VIGS targets the promoter to induce methylation and silencing

genes: AtPIP1;4 (AtPIP1;4, aquaporin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Genetic complementation of atpip1;4-3 mutant restores AtPIP1;4 expression, mesophyll CO2 conductance (gm), and photosynthetic assimilation rate (AN) to wild-type levels.
mechanism: AtPIP1;4-GFP fusion protein localizes to plasma membranes and facilitates CO2 transport, enhancing photosynthesis and growth.

genes: AtPIP1;4 (AtPIP1;4, aquaporin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtPIP1;4-GFP increases mesophyll CO2 conductance (gm), photosynthetic assimilation rate (AN), and plant growth compared to wild-type.
mechanism: AtPIP1;4-GFP enhances CO2 and H2O transport across plasma membranes, boosting photosynthesis and growth.

genes: HvPM19-1 (HvPM19-1, ABA-inducible plasma membrane protein, Hordeum vulgare), HvPM19-3 (HvPM19-3, ABA-inducible plasma membrane protein, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Cas9-induced mutations in HvPM19-1 observed in 23% of T0 lines
mechanism: RNA-guided Cas9 system induces mutations in HvPM19-1 and HvPM19-3

genes: HvPM19-3 (HvPM19-3, ABA-inducible plasma membrane protein, Hordeum vulgare), HvPM19-1 (HvPM19-1, ABA-inducible plasma membrane protein, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Cas9-induced mutations in HvPM19-3 observed in 10% of T0 lines
mechanism: RNA-guided Cas9 system induces mutations in HvPM19-1 and HvPM19-3

genes: BolC.GA4.a (BolC.GA4.a, gibberellin biosynthesis enzyme, Brassica oleracea)
phenotype: Dwarf phenotype observed in T0 plants with mutations in BolC.GA4.a
mechanism: RNA-guided Cas9 system induces mutations in BolC.GA4.a, leading to reduced gibberellin biosynthesis

genes: CmbHLH2 (CmbHLH2, basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium), CmMYB6 (CmMYB6, MYB transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Co-expression of CmbHLH2 and CmMYB6 in tobacco leaves triggers anthocyanin accumulation up to 5.0 mg/gFW 8 days post-infiltration.
mechanism: CmbHLH2 forms a transcriptional complex with CmMYB6 to activate CmDFR promoter, enhancing anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: CmbHLH1 (CmbHLH1, basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium), CmMYB6 (CmMYB6, MYB transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Co-expression of CmbHLH1 and CmMYB6 in tobacco leaves does not trigger anthocyanin accumulation.
mechanism: CmbHLH1 cannot form an active transcriptional complex with CmMYB6 to activate CmDFR promoter.

genes: CmbHLH2 (CmbHLH2, basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Single expression of CmbHLH2 in tobacco leaves does not trigger anthocyanin accumulation.
mechanism: CmbHLH2 requires co-expression with CmMYB6 to activate CmDFR promoter and induce anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: CmbHLH1 (CmbHLH1, basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Single expression of CmbHLH1 in tobacco leaves does not trigger anthocyanin accumulation.
mechanism: CmbHLH1 cannot activate CmDFR promoter or form an active transcriptional complex with CmMYB6.

genes: CmMYB6 (CmMYB6, MYB transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Single expression of CmMYB6 in tobacco leaves does not trigger anthocyanin accumulation.
mechanism: CmMYB6 requires co-expression with CmbHLH2 to activate CmDFR promoter and induce anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Strong GUS expression was detected in xylem and phloem of alfalfa stems, indicating PEPC7-P4 promoter activity in vascular tissue.
mechanism: The PEPC7-P4 promoter drives GUS expression in vascular tissues.

genes: MsSUS1 (sucrose synthase 1, cellulose synthesis, Medicago sativa)
phenotype: MsSUS1 transcript accumulation was reduced 75–90% in transgenic alfalfa plants, with SUS activity in stems reduced by >95% compared to controls. SUS protein was undetectable in post-elongation stem internodes.
mechanism: Transgene silencing (co-suppression) caused by overexpression of MsSUS1 under the PEPC7-P4 promoter.

genes: NsbHLH2 (NsbHLH2, transcription factor, Nannochloropsis salina)
phenotype: Overexpression of NsbHLH2 led to increased growth rate in the early growth period, and concomitantly higher nutrient uptake, than wild type (WT). These enhanced growth and nutrient uptake resulted in increased productivities of biomass and FAME. For example, one of the transformants, NsbHLH2 3–6, showed increased biomass productivity by 36% under the normal condition, and FAME productivity by 33% under nitrogen limitation condition.
mechanism: The improved growth in the transformants can be associated with the enhanced nutrient uptake.

genes: FB_MR5 (fire blight resistance gene, native to Malus ×robusta 5, cloned with 1995 bp native 5'-UTR and 1547 bp native 3'-UTR)
phenotype: Increased fire blight resistance compared to non-transformed 'Gala Galaxy' control plants, with significantly lower lesion length (PLL) in three independent inoculation experiments (p < 0.0001-0.02).
mechanism: FB_MR5 confers resistance to fire blight by providing pathogen resistance traits, as demonstrated by its presence in classically bred resistant accessions and its functional expression in transgenic lines.

genes: bHLH129 (bHLH129, basic helix-loop-helix transcription repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of bHLH129-GFP increases primary root length in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: bHLH129-GFP is localized in the nucleus and functions as a transcription repressor, promoting root elongation.

genes: bHLH129 (bHLH129, basic helix-loop-helix transcription repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of bHLH129p:GUS is highly expressed in roots, cotyledons, hypocotyls, and some flower organs in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: The native promoter of bHLH129 drives GUS expression in specific tissues, indicating developmentally regulated expression.

genes: PuICE1 (Pyrus ussuriensis ICE1, homologue of AtICE1, involved in cold tolerance)
phenotype: Overexpression of PuICE1 increases cold tolerance in transgenic tomato plants, as evidenced by lower electrolyte leakage (46-50% vs 78% in WT), higher survival rate (75-87.5% vs 25% in WT), and higher chlorophyll content.
mechanism: PuICE1 enhances cold tolerance by upregulating stress-responsive genes (SlAPX, SlSOD, SlCAT, SlCBF, SlDREB3) and increasing antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, CAT, POD).

genes: NtMYC2a (transcription factor involved in nicotine biosynthesis, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtMYC2a increases leaf nicotine levels by ~150% in Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: NtMYC2a overexpression suppresses the expression of nicotine synthetic genes, potentially triggering negative feedback regulation due to high nicotine levels.

genes: NtMYC2b (transcription factor involved in nicotine biosynthesis, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtMYC2b increases leaf nicotine levels by ~40% in Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: NtMYC2b overexpression moderately reduces the expression of nicotine synthetic genes (NtPMT, NtA622, NtBBL), but does not significantly alter other genes.

genes: VP6 (VP6, capsid protein, human rotavirus G9P[6]), VP8* (VP8*, immunogenic epitope of VP4, human rotavirus G9P[6])
phenotype: Expression of VP6/8*N and VP6/8*C fusion proteins in N. benthamiana results in 43 kDa bands detected by anti-VP6 antibody, with VP6/8*C showing faster accumulation than VP6/8*N.
mechanism: Fusion of VP8* epitope to VP6's N- or C-terminus creates chimeric proteins that retain VP6's structural properties. Positioning of the epitope affects protein accumulation rates, suggesting structural or stability differences.

genes: Luc (luciferase, reporter gene, firefly)
phenotype: Luciferase activity measured in transgenic Arabidopsis seedlings, with reduced expression in NPQ1::Luc seedlings grown in the presence of ACC relative to absence of ACC.
mechanism: NPQ1 promoter activity is repressed by elevated ethylene, leading to reduced luciferase expression.

genes: Luc (luciferase, reporter gene, firefly)
phenotype: Luciferase expression from the 35S::Luc control construct was unaffected by ethylene signaling in eto1-1, ctr1-3, and ein2-5.
mechanism: Constitutive expression of luciferase via the CaMV35S promoter is not regulated by ethylene signaling.

genes: MOR1 (promoter, upstream sequence of MOR1 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP accumulates in root tips, lateral root primordium, pericycle, and adventitious root (AR) primordium during IBA-induced AR formation
mechanism: MOR1 promoter activity is upregulated during AR induction, suggesting it is a target of auxin-responsive transcription factors

genes: HbFd1 (ferredoxin, Hordeum brevisubulatum)
phenotype: HbFd1::GFP fusion protein localizes to chloroplasts in Arabidopsis protoplasts
mechanism: Chloroplast transit peptide (cTP) in HbFd1 directs subcellular localization

genes: HbCIPK2 (CBL-interacting protein kinase, Hordeum brevisubulatum), HbFd1 (ferredoxin, Hordeum brevisubulatum)
phenotype: BiFC assay confirms HbCIPK2 and HbFd1 interact in the nucleus of Arabidopsis protoplasts
mechanism: Split YFP reconstitution via protein-protein interaction between HbCIPK2 and HbFd1

genes: EPSPS (5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase, Escherichia coli, bacterial)
phenotype: Overexpression of EPSPS confers glyphosate resistance in Glycine max
mechanism: EPSPS enzyme allows survival on glyphosate by inhibiting the target enzyme in the shikimate pathway

genes: GTR1 (glucosinolate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), GTR2 (glucosinolate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced glucosinolate content in phloem sap (~2.5-fold) and increased glucosinolate concentration in leaf tissue (~3.5-fold) in gtr1gtr2 dKO compared to wildtype Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: GTR1 and GTR2 are involved in glucosinolate transport and phloem loading, affecting aphid performance through altered glucosinolate distribution

genes: LOX3 (lipoxygenase 3, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: LOX3 knockout mutants show improved seed storability with higher germination rates after 9-11 days of artificial aging compared to wild-type
mechanism: LOX3 knockout reduces lipid peroxidation, leading to enhanced seed longevity without affecting agronomic traits

genes: TaGolS1 (galactinol synthase, Triticum aestivum), TaGolS2 (galactinol synthase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaGolS1 and TaGolS2 in rice increases chilling tolerance, with survival rates of 85.4% and 80.3% respectively after cold treatment, compared to 33.3% in wild-type plants.
mechanism: Overexpression of TaGolS1 and TaGolS2 leads to increased accumulation of galactinol and raffinose, which enhance chilling tolerance by stabilizing cellular structures and protecting against cold-induced damage.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein for auxin distribution visualization, synthetic)
phenotype: Visualization of auxin distribution via GFP fluorescence in rice plants.
mechanism: The pDR5 promoter drives GFP expression in response to auxin levels, allowing monitoring of auxin distribution.

genes: JMJ704 (histone demethylase involved in bacterial blight resistance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knock-down of JMJ704 increases susceptibility to Xoo infection, with lesion areas ranging from 43 to 53% compared to 34% and 26% in wild-type
mechanism: JMJ704 epigenetically suppresses negative defense regulators by reducing H3K4me2/3 activation marks on them

genes: AtNHX5 (AtNHX5, K+/Na+ antiporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtNHX6 (AtNHX6, K+/Na+ antiporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of nhx5 nhx6 double mutant growth and development
mechanism: AtNHX5 and AtNHX6 facilitate K+ and Na+ homeostasis and function in endosomal trafficking

genes: AtNHX5 (AtNHX5, K+/Na+ antiporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtNHX6 (AtNHX6, K+/Na+ antiporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Failure to complement nhx5 nhx6 growth except for E320Q mutants
mechanism: Conserved acidic residues are essential for ion transport activity and cellular functions

genes: AtNHX5 (AtNHX5, K+/Na+ antiporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtNHX6 (AtNHX6, K+/Na+ antiporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Localization to Golgi and TGN
mechanism: AtNHX5 and AtNHX6 are localized to Golgi and TGN

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression in flowers, leaves, root meristem, guard cells, and trichomes after ABA treatment
mechanism: MKKK18 promoter activity regulated by ABA

genes: MKKK18 (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 18, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ABA-insensitive germination, ABA-hypersensitive stomatal closure, and reduced root elongation in ABA-treated seedlings
mechanism: MKKK18 overexpression enhances ABA signaling in germination and root growth

genes: MKKK18-K32M (kinase-inactive mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: MKKK18-K32M-GFP localized outside the nucleus in Arabidopsis protoplasts
mechanism: Kinase-inactive MKKK18 lacks nuclear localization

genes: MKKK18-T161E (permanently active mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: MKKK18-T161E-GFP localized in the nucleus of Arabidopsis protoplasts
mechanism: Permanently active MKKK18 accumulates in the nucleus

genes: MKKK18 (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 18, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ABA-induced MKKK18 activation within 60 minutes of treatment
mechanism: MKKK18 activity is regulated by ABA in tobacco

genes: α-AI1 (alpha-amylase inhibitor, from Phaseolus vulgaris, synthetic)
phenotype: α-AI1 protein expression in seeds reduces coffee berry borer (CBB) offspring development by ~50% at 26 days post-infestation
mechanism: α-AI1 inhibits CBB α-amylase activity (80% inhibition), disrupting insect nutrition and delaying developmental stages (L1 to L2 molting)

genes: HDA6 (histone deacetylase 6, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants showed kanamycin sensitivity and reduced LUC expression, similar to the original ros1–1 mutant
mechanism: The hda6 mutations were responsible for derepression of transgenes silenced by the ros1–1 mutation

genes: PhFBH4 (PhFBH4, bHLH transcription factor, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Silencing PhFBH4 extended flower longevity by two more days in comparison to the controls (WT flowers and white flowers from CHS/TRV).
mechanism: PhFBH4 regulates flower senescence by modulating ethylene biosynthesis, specifically by binding to the G-box in the promoter of ACS1.

genes: PhFBH4 (PhFBH4, bHLH transcription factor, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of PhFBH4 accelerated flower senescence and shortened flower longevity to 5.5 days, while silencing of PhFBH4 extended flower longevity to about 9 days.
mechanism: PhFBH4 regulates flower senescence by modulating ethylene biosynthesis, specifically by upregulating ACO1 and ACS1 gene expression and increasing ethylene production.

genes: PhFBH4 (PhFBH4, bHLH transcription factor, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: PhFBH4 antisense transgenic plants exhibited larger leaves and flowers, longer internode length, and delayed flower senescence compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: PhFBH4 regulates flower senescence by modulating ethylene biosynthesis and gibberellin metabolism, specifically by downregulating ACO1 and ACS1 gene expression and reducing ethylene production, while also affecting GA2ox3 expression.

genes: OTS1 (At1g60220, SUMO protease, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of OTS1 does not significantly alter susceptibility to Pst DC3000 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: OTS1 negatively regulates SA signaling, which is involved in defense responses.

genes: OTS1 (At1g60220, SUMO protease with HA tag, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HA-OTS1 allows monitoring of OTS1 protein stability in response to SA treatment.
mechanism: HA tag facilitates detection; SA promotes degradation of OTS1 via proteasome.

genes: OTS2 (At1g10570, SUMO protease, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transient expression of OTS2 in N. benthamiana allows study of SA and MG132 effects on OTS2 protein stability and SUMO conjugation.
mechanism: SA promotes degradation of OTS2 via proteasome, affecting SUMO conjugate levels.

genes: AtD-CGS (Arabidopsis cystathionine γ-synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtD-CGS increases methionine content in seeds by ~15% in Glycine max
mechanism: NA

genes: StALS1 (StALS1, herbicide resistance, Solanum tuberosum), StALS2 (StALS2, herbicide resistance, Solanum tuberosum)
