phenotype: Targeted mutations in StALS1 and StALS2 genes in potato callus tissues using CRISPR/Cas reagents.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations at the StALS1 and StALS2 loci.

genes: StALS1 (StALS1, herbicide resistance, Solanum tuberosum), StALS2 (StALS2, herbicide resistance, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Targeted mutations in StALS1 and StALS2 genes in potato callus tissues using CRISPR/Cas reagents.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations at the StALS1 and StALS2 loci.

genes: FREE1 (FREE1, hairpin RNAi cassette, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: FREE1 silencing results in seedling lethality in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of FREE1 disrupts membrane trafficking pathways

genes: RLS2 (Os04g58880, encodes EXO70A1, rice)
phenotype: No positive transgenic plants were generated, possibly due to low transformation efficiency in the indica genetic background of rls2-1
mechanism: RLS2 is involved in vesicle trafficking and vascular bundle development, affecting secondary cell wall deposition and nutrient assimilation

genes: OCI (oryzacystatin I, cystatin, GenBank Accession No. J03469)
phenotype: OCI expression delays tuber sprouting at 4 °C, associated with an apparent loss of apical dominance and an increased number of small buds at the skin surface. Soluble protein content remains high for up to 48 weeks in cystatin-expressing tubers compared to control tubers.
mechanism: OCI inhibits cysteine protease activity, stabilizing storage proteins like patatin and multicystatin, and reducing proteolytic degradation.

genes: CCII (corn cystatin II, cystatin, GenBank Accession No. D38130)
phenotype: CCII expression delays storage protein breakdown in potato tubers, with patatin and PMC residual levels remaining significantly higher after 30 weeks of storage compared to control tubers.
mechanism: CCII inhibits cysteine protease activity, preventing degradation of storage proteins like patatin and multicystatin.

genes: FPGS1 (promoter, promoter region of FPGS1, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (gene, β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under the FPGS1 promoter in vascular tissues of cotyledons, hypocotyls, roots, and inflorescence stems.
mechanism: Promoter activity of FPGS1 drives GUS expression in vascular tissues, indicating its role in lignin biosynthesis.

genes: FPGS1 (promoter, promoter region of FPGS1, Arabidopsis thaliana), FPGS1 (gene, folylpolyglutamate synthetase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (gene, green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Complementation of fpgs1-1 mutant root architectural defects and restoration of lignin content to wild-type levels.
mechanism: Functional complementation of FPGS1-GFP in the fpgs1-1 mutant restores normal lignin biosynthesis and vascular tissue development.

genes: RTL1 (RNAse III-like, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RTL1 causes developmental defects including smaller stature, yellowing and curled rosette leaves, late flowering, and sterility in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: RTL1 cleaves dsRNA intermediates of virus replication and inhibits siRNA accumulation by acting upstream of DCL enzymes, preventing processing of dsRNA precursors into siRNAs.

genes: RTL1 (RNAse III-like, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RTL1-Myc in Arabidopsis thaliana results in milder or no developmental defects compared to untagged RTL1 overexpression.
mechanism: RTL1-Myc fusion protein shows reduced stability or activity, leading to less severe phenotypes.

genes: RTL1 (RNAse III-like, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RTL1-GFP fusion protein localizes to both cytoplasmic and nuclear compartments in onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: RTL1 is excluded from the nucleolus but present in nucleoplasm and cytoplasm, suggesting dual localization for dsRNA processing.

genes: RTL1 (RNAse III-like, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RTL1mR3 mutant (E89A/D96A) lacks developmental defects and fails to inhibit siRNA accumulation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Mutations in the RNaseIII domain abolish RTL1's ability to cleave dsRNA, preventing inhibition of siRNA production.

genes: GU-UG (inverted repeat hairpin RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: 35S:GU-UG transgene induces PTGS of GUS reporter in N. benthamiana, which is inhibited by co-expression of RTL1.
mechanism: RTL1 prevents accumulation of transgene-derived siRNAs by cleaving dsRNA precursors, blocking PTGS.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter gene, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MnDREB4A pro::GUS increases GUS activity in Arabidopsis thaliana under abiotic stress (heat, cold, drought, salt) with peak activity at 12 h treatment.
mechanism: MnDREB4A promoter activity is transcriptionally responsive to abiotic stresses, driving GUS expression in leaves and roots, particularly in vascular tissues.

genes: MnDREB4A (dehydration-responsive element-binding protein 4A, transcription factor, Morus notabilis)
phenotype: Overexpression of MnDREB4A in tobacco increases abiotic stress tolerance (heat, cold, drought, salt) with 300-fold higher gene expression in transgenic lines compared to wild type. Transgenic plants show reduced leaf wilting, lower water loss rates, and delayed senescence under stress.
mechanism: MnDREB4A enhances stress tolerance by increasing relative water content (RWC), proline accumulation, and reducing malondialdehyde (MDA) content under abiotic stress.

genes: MnDREB4A::EGFP (green fluorescent protein fusion, transcription factor, Morus notabilis)
phenotype: Overexpression of MnDREB4A::EGFP fusion proteins in onion epidermal cells shows nuclear localization of MnDREB4A, with green fluorescence signals observed only in the nucleus.
mechanism: MnDREB4A is a nuclear-localized transcription factor, as demonstrated by EGFP fusion protein localization in onion epidermal cells.

genes: diTPS-ISO (isopimara-7,15-diene synthase, Picea abies), DXS (1-deoxyxylulose-5-phosphate synthase, Plectranthus barbatus), GGPPs (geranylgeranyl diphosphate synthase, Plectranthus barbatus)
phenotype: Co-expression of diTPS-ISO, DXS, and GGPPs increased isopimaradiene and isopimaric acid accumulation by 3-fold in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves
mechanism: DXS and GGPPs boost GGPP biosynthesis, providing more precursor for diterpenoid production

genes: CYP720B4 (cytochrome P450, Picea sitchensis), Barnes-CYP720B4 (modified CYP720B4, Picea sitchensis), ΔTm-CYP720B4 (truncated CYP720B4, Picea sitchensis), Tp-CYP720B4 (chloroplast-targeted CYP720B4, Picea sitchensis), Tp-Barnes-CYP720B4 (chloroplast-targeted Barnes-CYP720B4, Picea sitchensis), Tp-ΔTm-CYP720B4 (chloroplast-targeted ΔTm-CYP720B4, Picea sitchensis)
phenotype: Expression of modified CYP720B4 variants in N. benthamiana leaves resulted in isopimaric acid accumulation of 45–55 μg/g plant dry weight four days post-infiltration
mechanism: N-terminal modifications enable chloroplast targeting of CYP720B4, facilitating oxygenation of isopimaradiene to isopimaric acid

genes: AlySEP3 (SEPALLATA3, floral organ development, Arabidopsis lyrata)
phenotype: Heterologous expression of AlySEP3 promoter::gene fragment fused to GFP shows similar expression pattern to AthSEP3 GFP reporter gene fusion in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Conservation of SEP3 gene functions in the two species

genes: CSU2 (CSU2, coiled-coil domain-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CSU2-GFP complements the csu2-2 cop1-6 mutant phenotype, restoring constitutive photomorphogenic phenotype in darkness.
mechanism: CSU2 represses COP1 E3 ubiquitin ligase activity, preventing HY5 degradation and maintaining HY5 protein levels.

genes: CSU2 (CSU2, coiled-coil domain-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: YFP-CSU2 complements the csu2-2 cop1-6 mutant phenotype, restoring constitutive photomorphogenic phenotype in darkness.
mechanism: CSU2 represses COP1 E3 ubiquitin ligase activity, preventing HY5 degradation and maintaining HY5 protein levels.

genes: CSU2 (CSU2, coiled-coil domain-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Myc-CSU2 complements the csu2-2 cop1-6 mutant phenotype, restoring constitutive photomorphogenic phenotype in darkness.
mechanism: CSU2 represses COP1 E3 ubiquitin ligase activity, preventing HY5 degradation and maintaining HY5 protein levels.

genes: CSU2 (CSU2, coiled-coil domain-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CSU2 coil-GFP complements the csu2-2 cop1-6 mutant phenotype, restoring constitutive photomorphogenic phenotype in darkness.
mechanism: CSU2 represses COP1 E3 ubiquitin ligase activity, preventing HY5 degradation and maintaining HY5 protein levels.

genes: CSU2 (CSU2, coiled-coil domain-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CSU2Δcoil-GFP does not complement the csu2-2 cop1-6 mutant phenotype, indicating the coiled-coil domain is required for function.
mechanism: CSU2 represses COP1 E3 ubiquitin ligase activity, preventing HY5 degradation and maintaining HY5 protein levels.

genes: Lc (Lc, transcription factor, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of Lc increases anthocyanin content in leaves (3.6-fold), stems (13.63-fold), and storage roots (1.5-fold) in sweet potato, with dark purple pigmentation in all tissues and increased lignin content in storage roots.
mechanism: Lc up-regulates flavonoid biosynthesis (anthocyanins, flavonols) and lignin biosynthesis pathways, leading to increased lignification and reduced starch accumulation in storage roots.

genes: MYB96 (MYB96, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MYB96 enhances drought tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MYB96 mediates ABA signaling and stress responses, enhancing drought tolerance.

genes: MYB96 (MYB96, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: CENH3-GFP (CENH3-GFP, centromere-specific histone H3 variant fused with GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of CENH3-GFP labels centromeric regions in somatic tissues (roots, leaves, petals) and allows ploidy determination in somatic cells.
mechanism: CENH3-GFP binds to centromeric chromocenters, enabling in vivo chromosome quantification via fluorescence.

genes: CENH3-GFP (CENH3-GFP, centromere-specific histone H3 variant fused with GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: CENH3-GFP expression in uninuclear microspores labels centromeres but not in meiotic prophase I cells.
mechanism: ASY2 promoter drives CENH3-GFP expression in uninuclear microspores, enabling centromere labeling in gametophytic cells.

genes: CENH3-GFP (CENH3-GFP, centromere-specific histone H3 variant fused with GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: CENH3-GFP expression in roots, leaves, and petals but not in meiotic prophase I cells.
mechanism: MSH4 promoter drives CENH3-GFP expression in somatic tissues, enabling centromere labeling in non-reproductive cells.

genes: CENH3-GFP (CENH3-GFP, centromere-specific histone H3 variant fused with GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: CENH3-GFP expression in pre-meiotic PMCs but not during meiotic cell division.
mechanism: JAS promoter drives CENH3-GFP expression in pre-meiotic cells, enabling centromere labeling in male sporogenesis.

genes: CENH3-GFP (CENH3-GFP, centromere-specific histone H3 variant fused with GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: CENH3-GFP expression in premeiotic PMCs and somatic tissues (roots, petals, microspores).
mechanism: AtPS1 promoter drives CENH3-GFP expression in premeiotic cells and somatic tissues, enabling centromere labeling in male sporogenesis.

genes: CENH3-GFP (CENH3-GFP, centromere-specific histone H3 variant fused with GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: CENH3-GFP labels centromeres in male and female gametophytic cells (microspores, pollen, embryo sacs) and allows gametophytic ploidy determination.
mechanism: WOX2 promoter drives CENH3-GFP expression in gametophytic cells, enabling centromere labeling in both male and female reproductive lineages.

genes: CENH3-GFP (CENH3-GFP, centromere-specific histone H3 variant fused with GFP, synthetic)
phenotype: CENH3-GFP expression in mature pollen with cytoplasmic and vegetative nucleus fluorescence, but not suitable for centromere labeling.
mechanism: LAT52 promoter drives CENH3-GFP expression in mature pollen, but excessive fluorescence interferes with centromere labeling.

genes: ToGAS1 (germacrene A synthase, Thlaspi officinale)
phenotype: Silencing of ToGAS1 reduces TA-G concentration by over 90%, leading to increased M. melolontha feeding and root mass loss compared to control lines
mechanism: ToGAS1 is involved in the first committed step of TA-G biosynthesis in T. officinale latex

genes: cry2AX1 (synthetic chimeric gene from Cry2Aa and Cry2Ac, codon-optimized, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of Cry2AX1 in rice confers resistance to rice leaffolder (Cnaphalocrocis medinalis) with 53.33–80.00% larval mortality and 20.29–36.32% leaf area damage reduction compared to 92.73% in controls
mechanism: Cry2AX1 toxin expression in chloroplasts targets rice leaffolder larvae, causing mortality and reduced feeding

genes: CHS (CHS-A, x14591, Petunia hybrida), CHS (CHS-J, x14597, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Transgenic plants show loss of flower pigmentation with variegated or nearly white petals in both V26 and 'Carpet Purple' lines.
mechanism: miR173-mediated cleavage of CHS-A and CHS-J transcripts triggers phased siRNA production, leading to gene silencing.

genes: PDS (AY593974, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Transgenic callus lines showed bleaching (35.6% of Basta-resistant lines) and regeneration of albino shoots in MD plants.
mechanism: miR173-mediated cleavage of PDS transcripts triggers gene silencing, disrupting carotenoid biosynthesis.

genes: CYP716A53v2 (CYP716A53v2, cytochrome P450 enzyme involved in ginsenoside biosynthesis, Panax ginseng)
phenotype: Overexpression of CYP716A53v2 increases PPT-group ginsenosides (Rg1, Re, Rf) by ~1.5-fold and decreases PPD-group ginsenosides (Rb1, Rc, Rb2, Rd) in transgenic P. ginseng.
mechanism: CYP716A53v2 catalyzes hydroxylation of dammarenediol-II at C-6 position to produce PPT aglycones, shifting biosynthetic flux toward PPT-group ginsenosides.

genes: CYP716A53v2 (CYP716A53v2, cytochrome P450 enzyme involved in ginsenoside biosynthesis, Panax ginseng)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of CYP716A53v2 reduces PPT-group ginsenosides (Rg1, Re, Rf) and increases PPD-group ginsenosides (Rb1, Rc, Rb2, Rd) in transgenic P. ginseng.
mechanism: CYP716A53v2 knockdown reduces PPT aglycone production, shifting biosynthetic flux toward PPD-group ginsenosides via dammarenediol-II intermediates.

genes: luciferase (firefly luciferase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Activation of luciferase expression when co-expressed with SARD1 in Arabidopsis protoplasts
mechanism: SARD1 activates gene expression through the GAAATTT motif

genes: SARD1 (SARD1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SARD1 enhances the activation of the luciferase reporter gene in Arabidopsis protoplasts
mechanism: SARD1 activates gene expression through the GAAATTT motif

genes: GAA (human acid alpha-glucosidase, Homo sapiens)
phenotype: Recombinant human GAA accumulates in tobacco seeds at ~40 μg/g, maintains enzymatic activity after multiple freeze-thaw cycles, and is taken up by GSDII fibroblasts restoring ~40% of normal GAA activity
mechanism: Soybean β-conglycinin promoter directs seed-specific expression; signal peptide ensures proper ER targeting and processing

genes: BnTTG1 (Brassica napus TRANSPARENT TESTA GLABRA1, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnTTG1 in the hairy AtGL3+ B. napus background resulted in glabrous plants with low fertility, poor stability, and reduced trichome coverage. Only one glabrous plant (O-3-7) survived to the T3 generation.
mechanism: Strong BnTTG1 transcription together with strong GL3 expression inhibits trichome outgrowth and development in B. napus.

genes: BnTTG1 (Brassica napus TRANSPARENT TESTA GLABRA1, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Knockdown of BnTTG1 in the hairy AtGL3+ B. napus background resulted in ultra-hairy lines (K-5-8 and K-6-3) with stable enhancement of trichome coverage, density, and length, and restored wild type growth similar to Westar plants.
mechanism: BnTTG1 controls lateral inhibition of trichome formation in neighboring cells of B. napus. Weak BnTRY expression suggests additional functions for TRY beyond trichome initiation inhibition in Brassicas.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity increased 2.04-fold in aerial parts and 1.77-fold in roots after 12h CdCl2 treatment, and 1.87-fold in aerial parts and 1.22-fold in roots after 24h treatment in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ThVHAc1 promoter confers tissue-specific Cd stress response and regulates gene expression under Cd stress.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity was detected in prokII-ThWRKY7 transgenic leaves with the reporter plasmid containing the ThVHAc1 promoter fragment with its intact WRKY motif, but not in mutated reporters.
mechanism: ThWRKY7 binds specifically to the WRKY motif in the ThVHAc1 promoter to regulate gene expression.

genes: ThVHAc1 (V-ATPase c subunit, Tamarix hispida, Tamarix hispida)
phenotype: Overexpression of ThVHAc1 increased germination by 3.3-fold, fresh weight by 1.5-fold, and root length by 1.7-fold under Cd stress in Arabidopsis thaliana. Cd content in transgenic lines was 1.4-fold lower than in controls.
mechanism: ThVHAc1 enhances V-ATPase activity, antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, POD, GST), and ROS scavenging to reduce cell damage and improve Cd tolerance.

genes: ThVHAc1 (V-ATPase c subunit, Tamarix hispida, Tamarix hispida)
phenotype: RNAi::ThVHAc1 showed higher ROS accumulation, 73.6% of EL compared to T-ck, and 78.2% of MDA content compared to T-ck under Cd stress in Tamarix hispida.
mechanism: Knockdown of ThVHAc1 reduces protective enzyme activities and V-ATPase function, increasing ROS and cell damage.

genes: ThWRKY7 (WRKY transcription factor, Tamarix hispida, Tamarix hispida)
phenotype: 35S::ThWRKY7 overexpression in T. hispida reduced DAB and Evans blue staining, with 58.9% of EL and 69.0% of MDA content compared to T-ck under Cd stress.
mechanism: ThWRKY7 binds to WRKY motifs in ThVHAc1 promoter and regulates Cd stress tolerance by modulating ROS homeostasis and protective enzyme activities.

genes: Ncl (Glyma03g32900, Na+/H+ antiporter gene, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of Ncl increases salt tolerance in transgenic soybean by synchronously regulating Na+, K+, and Cl− accumulation, with grain yield increased 3.6–5.5-fold in saline field conditions.
mechanism: Ncl functions as a cation-chloride cotransporter, regulating Na+, K+, and Cl− transport and accumulation in soybean roots and shoots, reducing ion toxicity under salt stress.

genes: FZP (FZP, floral organ identity, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of FZP in rice reduces panicle branching, causes defects in floral organs (e.g., double terminal spikelets, sterile stamens), and results in shorter panicles, fewer tillers, and sterile spikelets.
mechanism: FZP represses RFL/APO2 expression, which antagonizes panicle branching. Excessive FZP expression in floral meristems promotes class B and E floral identity genes while suppressing class C genes, leading to floral organ abnormalities.

genes: Solyc01g087240 (NF-YA subunit, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: accumulated in the nucleus
mechanism: regulates transcription by binding to promoters in the nucleus

genes: Solyc08g062210 (NF-YA subunit, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: accumulated in the nucleus
mechanism: regulates transcription by binding to promoters in the nucleus

genes: Solyc11g065700 (NF-YA subunit, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: accumulated in the nucleus
mechanism: regulates transcription by binding to promoters in the nucleus

genes: Solyc07g065500 (NF-YB subunit, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: observed in both the nucleus and cytoplasm
mechanism: regulates transcription by binding to promoters in the nucleus

genes: Solyc06g069310 (NF-YB subunit, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: observed in both the nucleus and cytoplasm
mechanism: regulates transcription by binding to promoters in the nucleus

genes: CFLAP1 (CFLAP1, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CFLAP1 causes cuticle defective phenotypes including organ fusion, reduced epicuticular wax crystals in stems, and wax accumulation in rosette leaves in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CFLAP1 negatively regulates cuticle development by interacting with AtCFL1 and modulating lipid-related gene expression.

genes: CFLAP1 (CFLAP1, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S:CFLAP1SRDX plants exhibit opposite phenotypes to 35S:CFLAP1 plants, including delayed flowering and altered epicuticular wax composition in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CFLAP1SRDX represses CFLAP1 function, leading to increased cuticle development and altered lipid metabolism.

genes: CFLAP2 (CFLAP2/FBH1, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CFLAP2 in Arabidopsis thaliana produces cuticle defective phenotypes similar to 35S:CFLAP1 plants, including organ fusion and altered epicuticular wax composition.
mechanism: CFLAP2 interacts with AtCFL1 and negatively regulates cuticle development through lipid-related gene modulation.

genes: AtCFL1 (AtCFL1, WW domain and C4 zinc finger domain-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtCFL1 in Arabidopsis thaliana causes cuticle defective phenotypes including organ fusion and TB staining, which are dependent on the C-terminal C4 zinc finger domain.
mechanism: AtCFL1 interacts with CFLAP1/2 and HDG1 via the C-terminal C4 zinc finger domain to regulate cuticle development.

genes: RPS4 (resistance protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), RRS1 (resistance protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-expression of FLAG-RPS4 and Myc-RRS1 showed strong immunoblot signals and localized in microsomal fractions.
mechanism: RPS4 and RRS1 interact in microsomal fractions, forming a stable complex required for resistance signaling.

genes: RRS1 (resistance protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RRS1Δlz mutants showed autoimmune response with 300,000- to 150,000-fold PR1 overexpression.
mechanism: LZ motif mutation in RRS1 disrupts protein interaction and triggers constitutive defense signaling.

genes: RPS4 (resistance protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of RPS4 TIR domain did not interact with RRS1 in microsomal fractions.
mechanism: TIR domain alone is insufficient for RPS4/RRS1 interaction; other domains are required.

genes: RPS4 (resistance protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), RRS1Δlz (mutant resistance protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-expression induced HR-like cell death dependent on EDS1.
mechanism: RRS1Δlz/RPS4 interaction triggers cell death requiring EDS1 signaling.

genes: PpASCL (hydroxyalkyl α-pyrone synthase, Physcomitrella patens), nptII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, synthetic)
phenotype: Knockout of PpASCL results in spores with defective exine and perine layers, reduced spore size (18 μm vs 28 μm in controls), non-viable spores with irregular cytoplasm distribution, and abnormal spore wall morphology with granulose protrusions instead of perine spines.
mechanism: PpASCL is required for sporopollenin biosynthesis, which is essential for exine and perine layer formation in spore walls. Loss of PpASCL leads to compromised spore wall integrity, cytoplasmic leakage, and developmental arrest during spore maturation.

genes: DRD1 (DRD1 gene, knockdown, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The drd1-p mutant displayed a decrease in DRD1 expression levels compared to WT
mechanism: NA

genes: MtRDR1 (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase 1, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: MtRDR1 expression inhibits TMV spread into apical meristem and adjacent stem tissue, enhances recovery from TMV-induced disease when combined with SA treatment
mechanism: MtRDR1 limits virus spread to meristem region; SA enhances RDR1 activity post-transcriptionally

genes: Ole18-CecA (fusion protein, Ole18::CecA, Oryza sativa ssp. indica cv. IR36)
phenotype: Accumulation of 16-38 μg CecA per gram of rice seed weight in transgenic lines
mechanism: Ole18-CecA fusion targets oil bodies (OBs) for storage; TEV protease cleavage releases active CecA with antimicrobial activity against Dickeya dadantii

genes: OsWAK91 (OsWAK91, wall-associated kinase, rice), OsWAK112d (OsWAK112d, wall-associated kinase, rice)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsWAK91 reduces susceptibility to rice blast by 60%, while overexpression of OsWAK112d increases susceptibility by 264% in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsWAK91 enhances resistance by increasing H2O2 production and defense gene expression during infection. OsWAK112d acts as a negative regulator of blast resistance.

genes: OsERF2 (OsERF2, involved in the regulation of root growth, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Down regulation of OsERF2 by artificial microRNA (Ami-OsERF2) results in longer primary roots (about 10.20 cm) compared with Nip (about 7.04 cm).
mechanism: OsERF2 negatively regulates primary root growth by affecting ABA accumulation and ethylene response.

genes: AtIRT1 (AtIRT1, iron transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtIRT1 increases iron content in rice grains by up to 2.2-fold in polished grains and 1.5-fold in unpolished grains.
mechanism: AtIRT1 enhances iron uptake and translocation in rice, acting synergistically with NAS and FERRITIN to increase iron in polished rice grains.

genes: MYB37 (MYB37, MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MYB37 increases ABA sensitivity in seed germination, cotyledon greening, and stomatal closure; enhances drought tolerance with reduced water loss and higher survival rates; delays flowering but improves biomass and seed productivity
mechanism: MYB37 upregulates ABA-responsive genes (ABF2, ABF3, DREB2A, MYC2) and enhances stomatal closure sensitivity to ABA, promoting dehydration tolerance

genes: RGA (repressor of ga1-3, TAP-tagged, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RGA-TAP rescues the null rga phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NA

genes: SEC (O-GlcNAc transferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SEC overexpression increases plant height by ~35% in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: SEC promotes GA signaling by O-GlcNAcylating DELLA proteins, inhibiting their growth-repressive function

genes: RGA-CT1 (C-terminal truncated RGA with Myc tag, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: rga-CT1 in the sec-3 background displays faster gel mobility than in the wild-type SEC background
mechanism: O-GlcNAcylation of RGA-CT1 in the PolyS/T region affects its gel mobility

genes: RGA-CT2 (C-terminal truncated RGA with Myc tag, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: rga-CT2 mobility is not altered by sec-3 mutation
mechanism: RGA-CT2 lacks the PolyS/T region containing O-GlcNAc sites

genes: SEC (wild-type and mutant variants, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S:SEC rescues the dwarf phenotype of sec-3, while 35S:secm1 and secm12 fail to rescue
mechanism: OGT activity of SEC is required for promoting stem elongation via DELLA O-GlcNAcylation

genes: OsHKT1;4 (OsHKT1;4, high-affinity K+ transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockdown of OsHKT1;4 in rice plants leads to significant Na+ overaccumulation in aerial organs, particularly leaf blades and sheaths, during reproductive growth stage under salinity stress.
mechanism: OsHKT1;4 mediates xylem Na+ unloading in stems and leaf sheaths, preventing Na+ overaccumulation in leaf blades during reproductive growth stage.

genes: PaWOX2 (PaWOX2, WOX2 gene involved in embryo development, Picea abies)
phenotype: Down-regulation of PaWOX2 in early embryos results in aberrant embryos lacking a distinct protoderm, reduced suspensor cell length, and disturbed border between embryonal mass and suspensor. Embryos show vacuolated cells and reduced mature embryo yield.
mechanism: PaWOX2 is required for protoderm formation and suspensor cell expansion during early embryo development. It regulates apical-basal patterning and radial organization of the embryonal mass.

genes: PaWOX2 (PaWOX2, WOX2 gene involved in embryo development, Picea abies)
phenotype: Down-regulation of PaWOX2 in early embryos results in aberrant embryos lacking a distinct protoderm, reduced suspensor cell length, and disturbed border between embryonal mass and suspensor. Embryos show vacuolated cells and reduced mature embryo yield.
mechanism: PaWOX2 is required for protoderm formation and suspensor cell expansion during early embryo development. It regulates apical-basal patterning and radial organization of the embryonal mass.

genes: OsWAK25 (OsWAK25, full-length cDNA, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsWAK25 confers resistance to Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae and Magnaporthe oryzae, with lesion mimic phenotype and upregulation of defense genes like NH1, PBZ1, OsPAL2, and PR10.
mechanism: OsWAK25 acts as a positive regulator of NH1-dependent salicylic acid (SA)-mediated resistance, enhancing resistance to hemibiotrophic pathogens while increasing susceptibility to necrotrophic pathogens via SA-mediated suppression of other defense pathways.

genes: OsWAK25 (OsWAK25, RNAi construct, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: No statistically significant difference in resistance to Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae compared to wild type Kitaake.
mechanism: NA

genes: XB15 (XB15, N-terminal TAP-tagged cDNA, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of XB15 compromises resistance to Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae conferred by OsWAK25 overexpression, resulting in intermediate lesion lengths and bacterial growth.
mechanism: XB15, a protein phosphatase 2C, interacts with OsWAK25 and attenuates its kinase activity, thereby suppressing OsWAK25-mediated resistance.

genes: PhSBP1 (SQUAMOSA PROMOTER BINDING PROTEIN-like, clade-VI SPL gene, Petunia × hybrida), PhSBP2 (SQUAMOSA PROMOTER BINDING PROTEIN-like, clade-VI SPL gene, Petunia × hybrida)
phenotype: Silencing of PhSBP1 delays flowering and inflorescence transition, increases leaf and branch numbers at flowering. Silencing of PhSBP2 alone delays flowering but not leaf initiation, while silencing with PhSBP2code-TRV2 increases leaf number without affecting flowering.
mechanism: PhSBP1 and PhSBP2 regulate flowering time and leaf initiation by modulating downstream targets like FT, ALF, and SOC1-like genes. PhCNR upregulation in PhSBP2code-TRV2 suggests functional overlap with PhSBP1.

genes: PhCHS (CHALCONE SYNTHASE, petal pigment gene, Petunia × hybrida)
phenotype: Silencing of PhCHS results in loss of petal anthocyanin production, used as a control for VIGS efficiency.
mechanism: NA

genes: Vat (Vat, resistance gene, Cucumis melo)
phenotype: Overexpression of Vat in melon confers resistance to Aphis gossypii and resistance to viruses (Cucumber mosaic virus, Zucchini yellow mosaic virus, Watermelon mosaic virus) when inoculated by specific aphid clones (NM1, C9, GWD2).
mechanism: Vat encodes a coiled-coil (CC)-nucleotide-binding site (NBS)-leucine-rich repeat (LRR) protein that recognizes aphid effector proteins, triggering plant defense responses including callose deposition, lignin synthesis, and oxidative burst, which confer resistance to aphid colonization and virus transmission.

genes: OsTCL1 (Oryza sativa TRICHOMELESS1, R3 MYB transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsTCL1 in Arabidopsis results in glabrous phenotypes in aerial parts and increased root hairs in roots.
mechanism: OsTCL1 interacts with GL3 to block the formation of the MBW transcriptional activator complex, repressing GL2 and R3 MYB genes.

genes: OsTCL1 (Oryza sativa TRICHOMELESS1, R3 MYB transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Expression of OsTCL1 under the TRY native promoter in the try mutant background resulted in glabrous phenotypes.
mechanism: OsTCL1 interacts with GL3 to block the formation of the MBW transcriptional activator complex, repressing GL2 and R3 MYB genes.

genes: OsTCL1 (Oryza sativa TRICHOMELESS1, R3 MYB transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Expression of OsTCL1 under the CPC native promoter in the cpc mutant background had little effect on the cpc mutant phenotypes.
mechanism: OsTCL1 interacts with GL3 to block the formation of the MBW transcriptional activator complex, repressing GL2 and R3 MYB genes.

genes: OsTCL1 (Oryza sativa TRICHOMELESS1, R3 MYB transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: GFP-OsTCL1 fusion protein localized in the nucleus and plasma membrane, inhibiting trichome formation and promoting root hair formation.
mechanism: OsTCL1 interacts with GL3 to block the formation of the MBW transcriptional activator complex, repressing GL2 and R3 MYB genes.

genes: OsTCL1 (Oryza sativa TRICHOMELESS1, R3 MYB transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsTCL1 in rice did not affect trichome and root hair formation.
mechanism: Rice may use different mechanisms to regulate trichome and root hair formation compared to Arabidopsis.

genes: OsNAS2 (OsNAS2, nicotianamine synthase, Oryza sativa), SferH-1 (SferH-1, ferritin, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNAS2 and SferH-1 increases iron concentration by ~7.5-fold in polished grains of Oryza sativa, reaching 15 μg g−1 from the 2 μg g−1 baseline in non-transformed IR64 control.
mechanism: Enhanced expression of OsNAS2, OsNAAT1, and OsDMAS1 genes involved in deoxymugineic acid (DMA) biosynthesis leads to significant increase of NA and DMA concentrations in polished grains, facilitating Fe and Zn accumulation.

genes: OsNAS2 (OsNAS2, nicotianamine synthase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNAS2 increases iron concentration to 8.8 μg g−1 in polished grains of Oryza sativa.
mechanism: NA

genes: SferH-1 (SferH-1, ferritin, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of SferH-1 increases iron concentration to 8.8 μg g−1 in polished grains of Oryza sativa.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsNAS2 (OsNAS2, nicotianamine synthase, Oryza sativa), SferH-1 (SferH-1, ferritin, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNAS2 and SferH-1 increases iron concentration to 8.8 μg g−1 in polished grains of Oryza sativa.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaRLK1 (Triticum aestivum LRR-RLK gene, Triticum aestivum), TaRLK2 (Triticum aestivum LRR-RLK gene, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaRLK1 in wheat variety Yangmai 158 significantly enhances powdery mildew resistance, with transgenic plants showing infection type grade 1 at seedling stage and grade 1 at adult stage compared to grade 3 and 8 in the control.
mechanism: TaRLK1 enhances resistance by inducing hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) accumulation at Bgt penetration sites and upregulating salicylic acid (SA) signaling pathway genes like TaPR1 and TaPR2.

genes: TaRLK1 (Triticum aestivum LRR-RLK gene, Triticum aestivum), TaRLK2 (Triticum aestivum LRR-RLK gene, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaRLK2 in wheat variety Yangmai 158 significantly enhances powdery mildew resistance, with transgenic plants showing infection type grade 0 at seedling stage and grade 1 at adult stage compared to grade 3 and 8 in the control.
mechanism: TaRLK2 enhances resistance by inducing hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) accumulation at Bgt penetration sites and upregulating salicylic acid (SA) signaling pathway genes like TaPR1 and TaPR2.

genes: MEA (subunit of FIS-PRC2 complex, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of mea-1 seed abortion phenotype in Ler plants when induced with 10 μM dexamethasone
mechanism: MEA-GR fusion protein rescues mea mutation by restoring MEA function in seed development

genes: mGhCHR (Gossypium hirsutum, zinc finger protein family gene with silent mutations in miRNVL5 binding site, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of cleavage-resistant mGhCHR increases salt stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with higher seed germination rates, biomass, and root elongation under 100–150 mM NaCl stress.
mechanism: mGhCHR promotes Na+ exclusion and activates SOS1, leading to higher K+/Na+ ratio in shoots and enhanced salt tolerance.

genes: miRNVL5 (Gossypium hirsutum, microRNA, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of miRNVL5 increases salt stress hypersensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana, with lower seed germination rates, biomass, and root elongation under 100–150 mM NaCl stress.
mechanism: miRNVL5 represses CBF1, CBF2, CBF3, and ERF4, leading to reduced expression of stress-responsive genes and increased Na+ accumulation.

genes: OsSWN1 (OsSWN1, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSWN1 increases secondary cell wall formation in Arabidopsis inflorescence stem, with 45% increase in secondary cell wall thickness in fiber cells.
mechanism: OsSWN1 upregulates genes associated with secondary cell wall formation, including MYB46, MYB83, and SND2.

genes: VAMP722 (VAMP722, endosomal protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Negative control plants expressing VAMP722 under the control of the NST3 promoter show baseline secondary cell wall formation.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsSWN1-VP16 (OsSWN1, transcription factor, Oryza sativa; VP16, synthetic fusion)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSWN1-VP16 increases secondary cell wall deposition in poplar, with 31% higher AIR content and 57% higher physical strength in stems.
mechanism: OsSWN1-VP16 enhances secondary cell wall formation through upregulation of secondary cell wall biosynthesis genes.

genes: PtrWRKY19 (WRKY transcription factor, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtrWRKY19 in Arabidopsis atwrky12 mutant complements the mutant phenotype, restoring normal lignin deposition in pith cells and reducing ectopic secondary wall thickening.
mechanism: PtrWRKY19 functions as a transcriptional repressor, inhibiting secondary cell wall (SCW) formation in pith cells by repressing SCW biosynthetic genes and transcription factors like PtoSND1-A1.

genes: PtrWRKY19 (WRKY transcription factor, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: 35S-PtrWRKY19::GFP fusion protein localizes exclusively to the nucleus of onion epidermal cells, confirming nuclear localization of PtrWRKY19.
mechanism: The nuclear localization signal (NLS) in PtrWRKY19 directs the fusion protein to the nucleus, indicating its role as a transcription factor.

genes: CmLBD1 (CmLBD1, LBD transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmLBD1 increases lateral root growth and promotes callus formation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CmLBD1 up-regulates genes involved in lateral root formation (AtPLTs, AtPINs, AtCYCDs) and responds to auxin signaling.

genes: CmLBD1 (CmLBD1, LBD transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: GFP localized in the nucleus of onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: CmLBD1 (CmLBD1, LBD transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: CmLBD1 activates the luciferase reporter gene in Arabidopsis protoplasts.
mechanism: CmLBD1 acts as a transcription activator.

genes: Dwarf (CYP85A1, BR biosynthetic gene, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of Dwarf increases net photosynthetic rate (PN) by ~28-17-fold, enhances CO2 assimilation, and improves Calvin cycle enzyme activity in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: BR promotes photosynthesis through redox regulation of Calvin cycle enzymes, increasing GSH/GSSG and AsA/DHA ratios, and activating RuBisCO and FBPase.

genes: ALG3 (Asparagine-linked glycosylation 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of yeast alg3-1 mutant strain (YG170) with the Arabidopsis ALG3 variants restores growth under restrictive conditions (30°C) when expressed under galactose-inducible promoter
mechanism: ALG3 encodes α-1,3-mannosyltransferase responsible for the first step of core oligosaccharide glycan assembly in the ER, enabling proper N-glycosylation of membrane proteins including pattern recognition receptors

genes: PEX19A (PEX19A, peroxin involved in peroxisome biogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana), PEX19B (PEX19B, peroxin involved in peroxisome biogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of YFP-PEX19A rescues embryo lethality of pex19a-1 pex19b-1 double mutant in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: YFP-PEX19A provides functional PEX19 to maintain peroxisome biogenesis during embryogenesis.

genes: PEX19A (PEX19A, peroxin involved in peroxisome biogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana), PEX19B (PEX19B, peroxin involved in peroxisome biogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of YFP-PEX19B rescues embryo lethality of pex19a-1 pex19b-1 double mutant in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: YFP-PEX19B provides functional PEX19 to maintain peroxisome biogenesis during embryogenesis.

genes: ALADIN (At3g56900, nucleoporin component of nuclear pore complex, Arabidopsis thaliana), PSRP5 (At3g56910, plastid-specific ribosomal protein 5, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of aladin-1 mutant with ALADIN + PSRP5 rescues RuBisCO accumulation and growth defects in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PSRP5, not ALADIN, is responsible for the aladin-1 mutant phenotype; PSRP5 knockdown phenocopies the mutant defects in chloroplast protein accumulation and growth.

genes: ALADIN (At3g56900, nucleoporin component of nuclear pore complex, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of aladin-1 mutant with ALADIN alone fails to rescue RuBisCO accumulation or growth defects in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ALADIN defects are not responsible for the aladin-1 mutant phenotype; PSRP5 knockdown phenocopies the mutant defects in chloroplast protein accumulation and growth.

genes: ALADIN (At3g56900, nucleoporin component of nuclear pore complex, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ALADIN knockdown (ALADIN KD) in Arabidopsis thaliana produces no visible growth defects and normal RuBisCO accumulation.
mechanism: ALADIN knockdown does not phenocopy the aladin-1 mutant; PSRP5 knockdown, not ALADIN, is responsible for the mutant phenotype.

genes: PSRP5 (At3g56910, plastid-specific ribosomal protein 5, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PSRP5 knockdown (PSRP5 KD) in Arabidopsis thaliana phenocopies the aladin-1 mutant defects in chloroplast protein accumulation and growth.
mechanism: PSRP5 is responsible for the aladin-1 mutant phenotype; PSRP5 knockdown disrupts chloroplast protein translation and causes growth defects.

genes: OsPGR5 (PGR5, photosystem I cyclic electron transport, rice)
phenotype: PGR5 knockdown plants show reduced photosynthetic response to high light under fluctuating light conditions, with suppressed non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) and increased photoinhibition of photosystem I (PSI), leading to reduced growth.
mechanism: PGR5-dependent cyclic electron transport around photosystem I (CEF-PSI) is required for rapid ΔpH build-up and NPQ formation to prevent photoinhibition and sustain photosynthesis under fluctuating light.

genes: OsCRR6 (CRR6, photosystem I cyclic electron transport, rice)
phenotype: crr6 mutant plants (defective in NDH-dependent CEF-PSI) exhibit reduced photosynthetic capacity under fluctuating light, with progressive accumulation of reducing power in the electron transport chain, leading to photoinhibition of PSI and reduced growth.
mechanism: NDH-dependent CEF-PSI contributes to balancing the redox state of the plastoquinone pool and preventing over-reduction of the electron transport chain during fluctuating light, thereby mitigating photoinhibition.

genes: GbPGF_A12 (Gossypium barbadense pigment gland formation gene, GbPGF_A12, Gossypium barbadense)
phenotype: Glandless or low gland number phenotype in newly emerging tissues 14 days post-agro-infiltration
mechanism: Silencing of GbPGF blocks gland cell differentiation and reduces gossypol content by over 93%

genes: CYP706B1 (P450 monooxygenase in gossypol biosynthesis pathway, CYP706B1, GenBank: AF332974.1)
phenotype: Significantly reduced gossypol levels in transgenic seeds, but lysigenous glands still formed as in non-transgenic plants
mechanism: Silencing of CYP706B1 does not affect gland formation, indicating gossypol biosynthesis and gland morphogenesis are uncoupled

genes: GoPGF (bHLH transcription factor, GoPGF, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: GoPGF protein localized to the nucleus in tobacco epidermal cells
mechanism: NA

genes: XT1 (xylosyltransferase 1, endogenous gene, Nicotiana benthamiana), XT2 (xylosyltransferase 2, endogenous gene, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Targeted mutagenesis of XT1 and XT2 genes resulted in 12.1% and 9.9% mutation rates respectively in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: Cas9 nuclease activity induced double-strand breaks at target sites, leading to insertions/deletions (indels) that disrupt gene function.

genes: fucosyltransferase (multiple genes, Nicotiana benthamiana), xylosyltransferase (multiple genes, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Simultaneous targeting of seven fucosyl/xylosyltransferase genes using five gRNAs in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: Polycistronic tRNA-gRNA constructs enabled multiplexed gRNA expression, directing Cas9 to multiple homologous gene targets.

genes: Pin1At (protein phosphatase-like isomerase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of Pin1At causes agravitropic root phenotype and reduced root growth in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Pin1At affects PIN1 polarity and auxin transport, leading to altered root gravitropism.

genes: Pin1At (protein phosphatase-like isomerase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knockdown of Pin1At results in defective gravitropic responses and increased root growth in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Pin1At modulates PIN1 polarity and auxin transport, which are critical for root gravitropism.

genes: Pin1At (promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Pin1At-GUS-P1 reporter shows GUS staining in root meristematic and elongation zones of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: Pin1At (promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Pin1At-GUS-P2 reporter exhibits stronger GUS staining in root meristematic and elongation zones compared to Pin1At-GUS-P1 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: Pin1At (promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Pin1At-GUS-P3 reporter shows the strongest GUS staining in root meristematic and elongation zones of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: Pin1At (promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Pin1At-GFP reporter shows GFP expression in root meristematic and elongation zones of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: mPin1At (mutated Pin1At, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of mutated Pin1At (35S:mPin1At) does not alter root gravitropic responses in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: The four additional amino acids in the PPIase domain are critical for Pin1At's role in root gravitropism.

genes: VHb (Vitreoscilla hemoglobin, Vitreoscilla stercoraria)
phenotype: Increased waterlogging tolerance with improved growth traits including seedling height, primary root length, lateral root number, and shoot dry weight in Arabidopsis and maize.
mechanism: Enhanced expression of alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH1) and higher peroxidase (POD) enzyme activity under waterlogging conditions.

genes: VHb (Vitreoscilla hemoglobin, Vitreoscilla stercoraria)
phenotype: Increased waterlogging tolerance with improved growth traits including seedling height, primary root length, lateral root number, and shoot dry weight in Arabidopsis and maize.
mechanism: Enhanced expression of alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH1) and higher peroxidase (POD) enzyme activity under waterlogging conditions.

genes: TaAREB3 (TaAREB3, ABA-responsive element binding protein 3, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaAREB3 in Arabidopsis increases ABA sensitivity, freezing tolerance, and drought tolerance.
mechanism: TaAREB3 binds to ABRE cis-elements in promoters of stress-responsive genes (RD29A, RD29B, COR15A, COR47), activating their expression under stress conditions.

genes: TaAREB3 (TaAREB3, ABA-responsive element binding protein 3, Triticum aestivum), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: TaAREB3-GFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus in transient assays of tobacco leaf cells and transgenic Arabidopsis root cells.
mechanism: The TaAREB3-GFP fusion protein is targeted to the nucleus, indicating its role as a transcription factor.

genes: PhPDS (phytoene desaturase, key enzyme in carotenoid biosynthesis, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Disruption of PhPDS causes an albino phenotype in 87.5% of transgenic lines (pGGE1c) and 58.1% (pGGE2c) in Petunia hybrida.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in PhPDS disrupt carotenoid biosynthesis, leading to chlorophyll deficiency and albinism.

genes: PhPDS (phytoene desaturase, key enzyme in carotenoid biosynthesis, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Induction of 867 bp chromosomal fragment deletion between sgR1 and sgR2 cut sites in 5 of 26 albino transgenic lines (3 homozygous, 2 monoallelic).
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced double-strand breaks at sgR1 and sgR2 sites facilitate homology-independent repair mechanisms resulting in large deletions.

genes: PhPDS (phytoene desaturase, key enzyme in carotenoid biosynthesis, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Sequential transformation with hCas9 and sgR2 resulted in 55.6% albino transgenic lines (36/65), comparable to single transformation (58.1%).
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in PhPDS disrupt carotenoid biosynthesis, leading to chlorophyll deficiency and albinism.

genes: PhPDS (phytoene desaturase, key enzyme in carotenoid biosynthesis, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Sequential transformation with hCas9 and paired sgRNAs induced 867 bp homozygous deletions in 2 of 10 transgenic lines.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced double-strand breaks at sgR1 and sgR2 sites facilitate homology-independent repair mechanisms resulting in large deletions.

genes: STTM165/166 (STTM165/166, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: PVX-based expression of STTM165/166 caused strong silencing phenotype with ectopic leaf outgrowths from veins on the leaf abaxial surface, bilateral symmetric leaves with double layered lamina, cup-shaped leaves, and ectopic leaf generation along the mid vein. At the nodes, leaves grew from ectopically generated axillary meristems.
mechanism: Inhibition of miR165/166 function leads to elevated mRNA levels of its target HD-Zip gene TC21810, causing developmental defects.

genes: STTM159 (STTM159, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: PVX-STTM159 inoculated plants were stunted and compact with downward-curled leaves, darker green pigmentation, smaller leaf area, shorter petioles, and clustered leaves at the shoot apex. Internodes were shorter, and leaves exhibited morphogenesis defects.
mechanism: Inhibition of miR159 function leads to elevated mRNA levels of its target MYB-like transcription factor NbMYBL1, causing leaf morphogenesis defects.

genes: PAT14 (protein S-acyl transferase 14, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Functional loss of PAT14 results in precocious leaf senescence, with accelerated leaf chlorosis and increased ion leakage compared to wild type.
mechanism: PAT14 suppresses salicylic acid (SA) biosynthesis and signaling, which are over-represented in pat14-2 mutants. SA-dependent pathways mediate the precocious senescence.

genes: PAT14 (protein S-acyl transferase 14, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: A green fluorescence protein (GFP) translational fusion of the PAT14 genomic fragment driven by its own promoter (PAT14g-GFP) fully restored the mutant phenotype.
mechanism: The PAT14g-GFP construct restores normal leaf senescence by repressing SA biosynthesis and signaling, as evidenced by suppressed expression of SA-responsive genes and delayed chlorosis.

genes: PAT14 (protein S-acyl transferase 14, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpressing PAT14 significantly suppressed the expression of SA biosynthetic and signaling genes (e.g., PR1, PAD4, SID2) but did not extend leaf longevity under regular growth conditions.
mechanism: PAT14 overexpression represses SA biosynthesis and signaling pathways, but this alone is insufficient to extend leaf longevity during age-dependent senescence.

genes: ZmPAT14 (protein S-acyl transferase 14 homolog, Zea mays), TaPAT14 (protein S-acyl transferase 14 homolog, Triticum aestivum), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of ZmPAT14-GFP and TaPAT14-GFP in pat14-2 fully restored leaf longevity, indicating functional conservation of PAT14 homologs across species.
mechanism: The conserved DHHC motif and regulatory domains of PAT14 homologs enable them to suppress SA signaling and rescue the precocious senescence phenotype.

genes: CMT3 (CMT3, CHG methyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CMT3 leads to its destabilization in vivo when JMJ24 is transiently overexpressed, reducing CMT3 protein levels.
mechanism: JMJ24, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, ubiquitinates and destabilizes CMT3, leading to its degradation via the 26S proteasome.

genes: JMJ24 (JMJ24, RING finger E3 ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of JMJ24 destabilizes CMT3 in vivo, reducing CMT3 protein levels and increasing CHG methylation and H3K9me2.
mechanism: JMJ24 ubiquitinates CMT3, targeting it for proteasomal degradation, which disrupts CMT3-mediated CHG methylation and H3K9me2 regulation.

genes: JMJ24 (JMJ24, RING finger E3 ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of the dominant-negative JMJ24 mutant (H244A, C263S) stabilizes CMT3, increasing its protein levels and reducing CHG methylation and H3K9me2.
mechanism: The RING motif mutant JMJ24(H244A, C263S) inhibits wild-type JMJ24 activity, preventing CMT3 ubiquitination and degradation.

genes: JMJ24 (JMJ24, RING finger E3 ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the jmj24 mutant with JMJ24m (H244A, C263S) fails to restore CHG methylation and H3K9me2 levels, confirming the RING motif's essential role.
mechanism: The RING motif is necessary for JMJ24's E3 ligase activity to ubiquitinate and degrade CMT3, which regulates CHG methylation and H3K9me2.

genes: TOGR1 (TOGR1, DEAD-box RNA helicase required for normal cell division at high temperatures, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of togr1-1 with TOGR1 restores normal growth under hot summer conditions in rice.
mechanism: TOGR1 encodes a temperature-dependent DEAD-box RNA helicase required for normal pre-rRNA processing and cell division at high temperatures.

genes: TOGR1 (TOGR1, DEAD-box RNA helicase required for normal cell division at high temperatures, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of TOGR1 in rice enhances thermotolerance, increasing plant height, 1000-grain weight, and number of grains per panicle under hot conditions.
mechanism: TOGR1 promotes effective pre-rRNA processing at high temperatures, coordinating primary metabolic processes required for plant growth.

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression driven by the putative promoter of TOGR1 reveals widespread expression in roots, shoots, leaves, culms, spikelets, and anthers during different developmental stages in rice.
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, pCAMBIA1381Z vector)
phenotype: GUS expression in seedlings and various tissues of transgenic Arabidopsis plants, including germinating stages and different developmental stages.
mechanism: NA

genes: NHL6 (NHL6, full-length genomic sequence, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restored ABA-sensitive phenotype in nhl6 mutant, rescuing the ABA-insensitive germination defect.
mechanism: Complementation of the nhl6 mutation by expressing the native NHL6 gene under its endogenous promoter and 3'UTR.

genes: NHL6 (NHL6, open reading frame, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Hypersensitivity to ABA, NaCl, and osmotic stress in transgenic plants, with increased endogenous ABA accumulation under stress conditions.
mechanism: Overexpression of NHL6 enhances ABA biosynthesis and signaling, leading to increased ABA levels and hypersensitivity to abiotic stress.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: ProMIR475b:GUS plants showed tissue-specific GUS expression in stems and leaves but not roots; Pro35S:GUS plants exhibited constitutive GUS expression in all tissues.
mechanism: Psu-miR475b promoter directs tissue-specific GUS expression, while CaMV 35S promoter drives constitutive expression.

genes: MIR475b (microRNA precursor, Populus suaveolens, genomic)
phenotype: ProMIR475b:MIR475b plants showed 6.1-fold higher Psu-miR475b transcript compared to wild-type, while Pro35S:MIR475b lines showed 0.3-fold increase.
mechanism: Psu-miR475b promoter-driven overexpression significantly enhances miRNA transcription compared to CaMV 35S promoter.

genes: Hcm1 (antimicrobial protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Increased resistance to Fusarium and Verticillium wilts in cotton
mechanism: ROS burst and activation of PR genes

genes: Hcm1 (antimicrobial protein, synthetic), GFP (reporter protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Subcellular localization of Hcm1 in the cell membrane of cotton plants
mechanism: NA

genes: trx-s (anti-sense, antisense thioredoxin s gene, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Increased resistance to pre-harvest sprouting (PHS) in wheat seeds
mechanism: Suppression of overall metabolic activities in seeds to prevent germination

genes: LsMT (Lactuca sativa MPBQ-MT, Lactuca sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of LsMT increases α- and γ-tocopherol levels by ~60-93% and ~41-93% respectively, while decreasing phylloquinone (VK1) levels by ~30-40% in Lactuca sativa. Transgenic plants show enhanced resistance to high light stress with increased photosynthesis products and higher plastoquinone levels.
mechanism: LsMT overexpression enhances tocopherol biosynthesis and plastoquinone levels, leading to improved ROS scavenging, higher thermal dissipation (NPQ), and increased ATP formation. This protects photosystems from photodamage and promotes photosynthetic production under high light stress.

genes: AtMago (HAP1, EJC component, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtMagoΔC (truncated HAP1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtMago and AtMagoΔC complements the hap1-2 mutation, restoring pollen viability and seed yield in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Restoration of HAP1 gene expression in the EJC complex, enabling proper splicing and NMD during pollen development

genes: DCP1 (decapping enzyme, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of CFP-DCP1 allows visualization of P-bodies in Arabidopsis thaliana cells
mechanism: CFP-DCP1 localizes to P-bodies, indicating its role in RNA processing or degradation

genes: SmJAZ3 (SmJAZ3, JASMONATE ZIM-DOMAIN repressor, Salvia miltiorrhiza), SmJAZ9 (SmJAZ9, JASMONATE ZIM-DOMAIN repressor, Salvia miltiorrhiza)
phenotype: Overexpression of SmJAZ3 and SmJAZ9 reduces tanshinone accumulation by ~94% (SmJAZ3-3 line) and ~77% (SmJAZ9-22 line) in Salvia miltiorrhiza hairy roots.
mechanism: SmJAZ3 and SmJAZ9 act as repressors in the JA signaling pathway, inhibiting tanshinone biosynthesis by downregulating key biosynthetic genes like SmKSL and SmDXS2.

genes: SmJAZ3 (SmJAZ3, JASMONATE ZIM-DOMAIN repressor, Salvia miltiorrhiza), SmJAZ9 (SmJAZ9, JASMONATE ZIM-DOMAIN repressor, Salvia miltiorrhiza)
phenotype: Knockdown of SmJAZ3 and SmJAZ9 increases tanshinone accumulation by 2.48-fold (anti-SmJAZ3-3 line) and 1.35-fold (anti-SmJAZ9-23 line) in Salvia miltiorrhiza hairy roots.
mechanism: SmJAZ3 and SmJAZ9 act as repressors in the JA signaling pathway, inhibiting tanshinone biosynthesis by downregulating key biosynthetic genes like SmKSL and SmDXS2.

genes: GAME9 (transcription factor, involved in SGA biosynthesis, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of GAME9 in tomato leads to reduced levels of α-tomatine (21–32 fold) and dehydrotomatine (13–21 fold) compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: GAME9 regulates SGA biosynthesis by controlling the mevalonate pathway and sterol metabolism, including cholesterol and phytosterol biosynthesis.

genes: GAME9 (transcription factor, involved in SGA biosynthesis, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GAME9 in tomato and potato increases levels of α-tomatine (2.4–3 fold) and dehydrotomatine (2.1–2.7 fold) in tomato leaves, and α-solanine (3.5–4.6 fold) and α-chaconine (2.8–4.2 fold) in potato leaves.
mechanism: GAME9 enhances SGA biosynthesis by upregulating genes in the mevalonate pathway and sterol metabolism, including CAS, SSR2, and C5-SD, leading to increased cholesterol and triterpenoid intermediates.

genes: AtPCS1 (phytochelatin synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtPCS1 increases arsenic (As) and cadmium (Cd) detoxification in tobacco, with significantly higher As and Cd accumulation in roots (up to 2.5-fold compared to wild type) and enhanced phytochelatin (PC) production (3-5-fold higher total PCs in roots and shoots).
mechanism: AtPCS1 overexpression enhances PC synthesis, which chelates As and Cd for vacuolar sequestration. PC3 is the dominant PC fraction in Cd treatments, while PC2 dominates in As treatments. Vacuolar Cd compartmentalization is increased in rolB-AtPCS1 roots and leaves, but As+Cd reduces vacuolar Cd sequestration.

genes: CYP76AD5 (CYP76AD5, tyrosine hydroxylase, Beta vulgaris), CYP76AD6 (CYP76AD6, tyrosine hydroxylase, Beta vulgaris)
phenotype: Overexpression of CYP76AD5 and CYP76AD6 increases L-DOPA content in beet roots by ~198 m/z mass spec peak intensity compared to 35S::GUS controls.
mechanism: CYP76AD5 and CYP76AD6 perform tyrosine hydroxylation to produce L-DOPA in beet and Arabidopsis.

genes: PgDODA (PgDODA, DOPA 4,5-dioxygenase, Portulaca grandiflora)
phenotype: Overexpression of PgDODA in Arabidopsis produces yellow betaxanthin pigmentation when co-expressed with CYP76AD5/6.
mechanism: PgDODA catalyzes the conversion of L-DOPA to betalamic acid (step 2) in the betalain pathway.

genes: CYP76AD5 (CYP76AD5, tyrosine hydroxylase, Beta vulgaris), PgDODA (PgDODA, DOPA 4,5-dioxygenase, Portulaca grandiflora)
phenotype: Co-expression of CYP76AD5 and PgDODA in Arabidopsis produces intense yellow betaxanthin pigmentation in non-photosynthetic tissues.
mechanism: CYP76AD5 performs tyrosine hydroxylation (step 1) and PgDODA catalyzes the conversion of L-DOPA to betalamic acid (step 2) in the betalain pathway.

genes: CYP76AD1 (CYP76AD1, tyrosine hydroxylase and cyclo-DOPA synthase, Beta vulgaris), PgDODA (PgDODA, DOPA 4,5-dioxygenase, Portulaca grandiflora)
phenotype: Co-expression of CYP76AD1 and PgDODA in Arabidopsis produces red betacyanin pigmentation in cotyledons when fed tyrosine.
mechanism: CYP76AD1 performs both tyrosine hydroxylation (step 1) and cyclo-DOPA formation (step 3), while PgDODA catalyzes step 2 in the betalain pathway.

genes: SERK2 (SERK2Km, kinase-inactive mutant, synthetic)
phenotype: pHAE::SERK2Km/serk1-1/bak1-5/serk4-1 transgenic lines showed more severe floral organ abscission defects than serk1-1/bak1-5/serk4-1, comparable to hae/hsl2 mutants
mechanism: SERK2Km disrupts SERK2 function in IDA-induced HAE/HSL2-SERKs complex formation and transphosphorylation required for floral organ abscission signaling

genes: sGFPs65T (modified green fluorescent protein, GenBank accession ABB59985, Zea mays)
