genes: ARU (At1g61790, OST3/6 subunit of OST complex, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of ARU in aru-1 mutants restores wild-type-like interspecific pollen tube (PT) reception in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ARU, a subunit of the oligosaccharyltransferase complex, mediates N-glycosylation of proteins involved in interspecific pollen tube recognition, such as FER, enabling proper PT reception.

genes: ipt (isopentenyltransferase, Agrobacterium tumefaciens), miaA (tRNA delta(2)-isopentenylpyrophosphate transferase, Pseudomonas fluorescens G20-18)
phenotype: Restored biocontrol activity in CNT transposon mutants, comparable to wild-type G20-18 biocontrol activity
mechanism: Microbial cytokinin (CK) production via heterologous and homologous expression of CK biosynthetic genes

genes: GFP-CT24 (artificial protein, seed storage protein marker, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP-CT24 is missorted out of the cells in nhx5 nhx6 mutants, indicating impaired protein transport to PSVs.
mechanism: AtNHX5 and AtNHX6 are required for the transport of seed storage proteins into the PSVs in Arabidopsis.

genes: AtNHX5-D164N (mutant, ion transport activity, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Accumulation of precursor proteins of 12S globulin and 2S albumin in nhx5 nhx6 seeds, indicating impaired protein transport.
mechanism: The transport activity of AtNHX5 is required for the transport of seed storage proteins into the PSVs.

genes: AtNHX5 (wild-type, ion transport activity, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: No precursor proteins detected in seeds, indicating functional transport of seed storage proteins.
mechanism: Wild-type AtNHX5 functions efficiently in the transport of seed storage proteins into the PSVs.

genes: AtNHX5 (wild-type, ion transport activity, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-localization of RFP-AtNHX5 with SYP22 in PVC, indicating subcellular localization regulation.
mechanism: AtNHX5 co-localizes with SYP22 and VAMP727 in the PVC, suggesting a role in SNARE complex localization.

genes: VAMP727 (wild-type, SNARE complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: VAMP727-mCherry localizes to PVC in wild-type but is trapped in TGN in nhx5 nhx6, indicating impaired trafficking.
mechanism: AtNHX5 and AtNHX6 regulate the subcellular localization of the SNARE complex in the PVC.

genes: CBD1 (cellulose-binding domain 1, from Phytophthora infestans, Phytophthora infestans)
phenotype: Transgenic Bintje potato plants exhibit increased plant height and female fertility, enabling seed berry production in a previously sterile cultivar. Crosses with CBD1 transgenics introgressed late blight resistance and color/tuber shape traits into Bintje germplasm.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtLecRK-I.9 (AtLecRK-I.9, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtLecRK-I.9 and eGFP in Nicotiana benthamiana enhances resistance to Phytophthora pathogens.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtLecRK-IX.1 (AtLecRK-IX.1, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtLecRK-IX.1 and eGFP in Nicotiana benthamiana enhances resistance to Phytophthora pathogens and induces spontaneous cell death in some lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of eGFP in Nicotiana benthamiana serves as a control for transgene expression and protein accumulation analysis.
mechanism: NA

genes: TCM5 (LOC_Os05g34460, chloroplast-targeted Deg protease protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of the tcm5 mutant with pCAMBIA1301:CaMV35S:TCM5 rescues the albino phenotype and allows survival at high temperatures (32 °C) in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: TCM5 is essential for chloroplast development and maintenance of PSII function under high temperatures.

genes: MaWRKY26 (WRKY transcription factor, banana, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: MaWRKY26-GFP is localized exclusively in the nucleus, indicating it is a nuclear protein and potential transcription factor
mechanism: MaWRKY26 functions as a transcriptional activator, as evidenced by 3.3-fold higher LUC/REN ratio compared to negative control in dual luciferase assays

genes: JcMYB2 (JcMYB2, stress response, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcMYB2 in Arabidopsis confers tolerance to both high salt and low temperature stresses
mechanism: JcMYB2 enhances stress response by interacting with ABA and MeJA signaling pathways and functions in root development

genes: Agl97 (maltase, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Transgenic lines show greatly reduced α-glucosidase activity but normal starch degradation and seedling growth
mechanism: RNA interference silencing cassette targeting Agl97 reduces maltase activity in endosperm

genes: miP1a (miP1a, microProtein, Arabidopsis thaliana), miP1b (miP1b, microProtein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of miP1a or miP1b delays flowering under inductive long day conditions by severely decreasing FT mRNA levels, resulting in extremely late flowering phenotypes.
mechanism: miP1a/b sequester CO into non-functional complexes, inhibiting FT expression and rendering CO non-functional in long day conditions.

genes: COBB (CO B-Box domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of COBB results in a similar late flowering phenotype as miP1a/b overexpression.
mechanism: COBB sequesters CO into non-functional complexes, inhibiting FT expression and rendering CO non-functional in long day conditions.

genes: miP1b (miP1b, microProtein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants overexpressing MIGS-miP1b exhibit slightly earlier flowering under long day conditions with reduced miP1b mRNA levels and slightly increased FT mRNA.
mechanism: MIGS-miP1b reduces miP1b mRNA levels, leading to increased FT expression and earlier flowering.

genes: miP1a (miP1a, microProtein, Arabidopsis thaliana), miP1b (miP1b, microProtein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants overexpressing MIGS-miP1ab exhibit early flowering under long day conditions with strongly reduced miP1a and miP1b mRNA levels and slightly increased FT mRNA.
mechanism: MIGS-miP1ab reduces miP1a and miP1b mRNA levels, leading to increased FT expression and earlier flowering.

genes: ZAR1 (ZAR1, plasma membrane receptor kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Introduction of a 3.5 kb ZAR1 genomic fragment into zar1-1+/- and zar1-2 mutants rescued the seed abortion phenotype, reducing the abortion rate from 26.3% to 8.4% in T1 transgenic lines.
mechanism: The transgene rescues the zar1-1+/- and zar1-2 mutant phenotypes by restoring ZAR1 function, indicating that ZAR1 is required for zygote asymmetric division and cell fate specification.

genes: ZAR1 (ZAR1, plasma membrane receptor kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZAR1ΔK-GFP (kinase domain deleted) in wild-type plants reduced seed set from 95.81% to 76.03–93.04%, with the lowest seed set (76.03%) resembling the zar1-1+/- phenotype. Symmetric zygote division and elongated zygotes were observed.
mechanism: The kinase domain deletion in ZAR1ΔK-GFP disrupts its catalytic activity, leading to impaired zygote asymmetric division and cell fate specification. The transgene mimics the zar1-1 mutant phenotype, confirming the role of the kinase domain in ZAR1 function.

genes: PtrWRKY89 (promoter, from Populus trichocarpa, source), GUS (reporter gene, from Escherichia coli, source)
phenotype: GUS activity detected in calyx, siliques, root, and old leaves of transgenic Arabidopsis.
mechanism: PtrWRKY89 promoter drives GUS expression in response to SA and JA signaling.

genes: PtrWRKY89 (from Populus trichocarpa, source), GFP (from synthetic, source)
phenotype: GFP signal localized exclusively in the nucleus of onion epidermal cells transformed with 35S-GFP:PtrWRKY89 construct.
mechanism: Nuclear localization signal (NLS) in PtrWRKY89 directs the fusion protein to the nucleus.

genes: PtrWRKY89 (from Populus trichocarpa, source)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtrWRKY89 in Arabidopsis resulted in reduced resistance to PstDC3000 and Botrytis cinerea, with increased pathogen growth and chlorophyll loss.
mechanism: PtrWRKY89 suppresses SA and JA signaling pathways, weakening plant defense responses.

genes: TOC75 (translocon at outer membrane 75 kDa, Arabidopsis thaliana, TOC75-III genomic fragment)
phenotype: Complementation of the lethal phenotype of the toc75-III-1 null mutant, with segregation ratios indicating successful complementation (3:1 hygromycin resistant:sensitive plants).
mechanism: Toc75 functions in chloroplast protein import; POTRA domains are required for its function.

genes: TOC75 (translocon at outer membrane 75 kDa, Arabidopsis thaliana, TOC75-III genomic fragment with POTRA-1 deletion)
phenotype: Failure to complement the lethal phenotype of toc75-III-1, with segregation ratios (2:1 or lower) indicating non-complementation. Plants showed pale phenotypes and reduced growth rates.
mechanism: POTRA-1 deletion disrupts Toc75 function in chloroplast protein import, leading to reduced preprotein import and chloroplast biogenesis defects.

genes: TOC75 (translocon at outer membrane 75 kDa, Arabidopsis thaliana, TOC75-III genomic fragment with POTRA-1 and -2 deletions)
phenotype: Failure to complement the lethal phenotype of toc75-III-1, with severe pale phenotypes and reduced chlorophyll content (62% reduction).
mechanism: POTRA-1 and -2 deletions disrupt Toc75's role in preprotein translocation across the outer membrane, leading to impaired chloroplast biogenesis.

genes: TOC75 (translocon at outer membrane 75 kDa, Arabidopsis thaliana, TOC75-III genomic fragment with myc epitope tag)
phenotype: Successful complementation of the toc75-III-1 lethal phenotype, with normal segregation ratios (2.95:1 hygromycin resistant:sensitive plants).
mechanism: Myc-tagged Toc75 retains full function in chloroplast protein import and complements the null mutant.

genes: TOC75 (translocon at outer membrane 75 kDa, Arabidopsis thaliana, TOC75-III genomic fragment with POTRA-1 deletion and myc epitope tag)
phenotype: Failure to complement the toc75-III-1 lethal phenotype, with pale phenotypes and reduced germination rates.
mechanism: POTRA-1 deletion in myc-tagged Toc75 disrupts its function in chloroplast protein import, leading to growth defects.

genes: SlUPA-like (bHLH transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlUPA-like induces cell enlargement, aberrant development, and low stress tolerance in tomato.
mechanism: Overexpression of SlUPA-like promotes GA response, represses JA response, and stimulates stomatal opening under dehydration stress.

genes: gusA (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of gusA gene in roots but not in leaves of transgenic plantains.
mechanism: ZmRCP-1 promoter directs root tip-specific expression.

genes: gusA (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Uniform expression of gusA in leaves and roots of transgenic plantains.
mechanism: Constitutive expression via CaMV35S promoter.

genes: PtrA/NINV (alkaline/neutral invertase involved in abiotic stress tolerance, Poncirus trifoliata)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtrA/NINV enhances cold, salt, and drought tolerance in transgenic tobacco plants by reducing ROS accumulation, improving photosynthesis efficiency, and increasing reducing sugar content.
mechanism: PtrA/NINV promotes sucrose degradation to produce reducing sugars (glucose and fructose), which act as osmoprotectants and ROS scavengers. Enhanced photosynthesis efficiency and reduced oxidative damage contribute to stress tolerance.

genes: MpPHOT (phototropin, blue-light photoreceptor, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Mpphot-Citrine localizes on the plasma membrane and chloroplast periphery in Marchantia polymorpha, enabling visualization of phototropin localization with time-gated fluorescence imaging
mechanism: Citrine fusion allows fluorescence imaging with time-gated rejection of chloroplast autofluorescence, revealing Mpphot localization on chloroplast outer envelope membrane

genes: sgRNA1 (AtMIR169a target, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), sgRNA2 (AtMIR169a target, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), SpCas9 (Cas9 nuclease, Streptococcus pyogenes, synthetic)
phenotype: Targeted deletion of 934-bp AtMIR169a locus in Arabidopsis thaliana, resulting in 57-54% survival under drought stress compared to 0% in wild-type
mechanism: Dual-sgRNA CRISPR/Cas9 induces double-strand breaks at both ends of the target locus, leading to precise deletion via homology-directed repair

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic), AtTFL1 (homologous arms, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic)
phenotype: Successful replacement of AtTFL1 locus with eGFP-SV40NLS cassette in Arabidopsis thaliana, with eGFP expression detected in nuclei of leaves and roots
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced double-strand breaks at AtTFL1 locus enable homology-directed repair with eGFP donor template

genes: VaERF057 (Vitis amurensis ETHYLENE RESPONSE FACTOR 057, Vitis amurensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of VaERF057 increases cold tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis, with 85% survival rate at -11°C compared to 21.4% in wild-type plants
mechanism: VaERF057 reduces malondialdehyde (MDA) content and increases superoxide dismutase (SOD), peroxidase (POD), and catalase (CAT) activities under cold stress

genes: bar (bar, phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, S. hygroscopicus)
phenotype: High resistance to glufosinate
mechanism: The bar gene encodes phosphinothricin acetyltransferase (PAT), which detoxifies glufosinate by acetylating it into non-toxic N-acetyl-phosphinothricin.

genes: pat (pat, phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, S. viridochromogenes)
phenotype: Some level of glufosinate tolerance
mechanism: The pat gene encodes phosphinothricin acetyltransferase (PAT), which detoxifies glufosinate by acetylating it into non-toxic N-acetyl-phosphinothricin.

genes: pat (pat, phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, S. viridochromogenes)
phenotype: Some level of glufosinate tolerance
mechanism: The pat gene encodes phosphinothricin acetyltransferase (PAT), which detoxifies glufosinate by acetylating it into non-toxic N-acetyl-phosphinothricin.

genes: MUTE (promoter region, 1954 bp upstream of translation start site, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression in stomatal-lineage cells and hydathode
mechanism: Stomatal-lineage specific expression driven by full-length MUTE promoter

genes: MUTE (promoter region, 500-325 bp upstream of translation start site, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression in stomatal-lineage cells with low-level vascular expression
mechanism: Stomatal-lineage specific expression driven by 175-bp MUTE promoter fragment fused to CaMV minimal promoter

genes: MUTE (promoter region, 411-325 bp upstream of translation start site, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: No detectable stomatal-lineage GUS expression
mechanism: Insufficient regulatory elements in 86-bp MUTE promoter fragment

genes: MUTE (promoter region, 500-411 bp upstream of translation start site, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Maintained MUTE promoter activity with intensity and spatiotemporal pattern
mechanism: Site-directed mutagenesis of known cis-elements did not disrupt expression

genes: SGT1b (SGT1b, SGT1b gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), SGT1b (SGT1b1-250, truncated SGT1b protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of 35S:SGT1b-FLAG transgene complemented the hsm1 mutant, whereas 35S:SGT1b1–250-FLAG did not.
mechanism: SGT1b stabilizes COI1 protein, which is required for JA signaling.

genes: SGT1a (SGT1a, SGT1a gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), SGT1b (SGT1b, SGT1b gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transient knockdown of SGT1a and SGT1b in mesophyll protoplasts reduced COI1-HA levels.
mechanism: SGT1a and SGT1b stabilize COI1 protein, which is required for JA signaling.

genes: HSP90 (HSP90, cytosolic HSP90 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RNAi knockdown lines (RNAi-A1 and RNAi-C1) showed reduced HSP90 transcript levels and altered JA–COR responses.
mechanism: HSP90 stabilizes COI1 protein, which is required for JA signaling.

genes: COI1 (COI1, COI1 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), TIR1 (TIR1, TIR1 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of HA-tagged COI1 and TIR1 in mesophyll protoplasts for co-IP experiments.
mechanism: COI1 and TIR1 associate with SGT1b–HSP70–HSP90 complexes.

genes: PHT5;1 (PHT5;1, vacuolar phosphate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), PHT5;2 (PHT5;2, vacuolar phosphate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana), PHT5;3 (PHT5;3, vacuolar phosphate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHT5;1-GFP, PHT5;2-HA, and PHT5;3-GFP leads to Pi overaccumulation and ~50% reduction in fresh weight compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: PHT5 proteins mediate vacuolar phosphate (Pi) sequestration, reducing cytosolic Pi levels and disrupting homeostasis, which impairs growth.

genes: PHT5;1 (PHT5;1, vacuolar phosphate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of pht5;1-3 mutants with PHT5;1 genomic sequence restores Pi levels to wild-type levels.
mechanism: PHT5;1 facilitates vacuolar Pi import, restoring Pi homeostasis in mutants.

genes: PHT5;3 (PHT5;3, vacuolar phosphate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHT5;3-GFP increases vacuolar Pi accumulation and reduces cytosolic Pi levels, leading to growth retardation.
mechanism: PHT5;3 mediates Pi influx into vacuoles, reducing cytosolic Pi and disrupting homeostasis.

genes: PHT5;1 (PHT5;1, vacuolar phosphate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: pht5;1 mutants exhibit 40% reduced Pi levels and severe leaf necrosis during Pi recovery.
mechanism: Loss of PHT5;1 impairs vacuolar Pi sequestration, leading to toxic cytosolic Pi accumulation and necrosis.

genes: PHT5;1 (PHT5;1, vacuolar phosphate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: pht5;1 mutants exhibit 40% reduced Pi levels and severe leaf necrosis during Pi recovery.
mechanism: Loss of PHT5;1 impairs vacuolar Pi sequestration, leading to toxic cytosolic Pi accumulation and necrosis.

genes: PHT5;1 (PHT5;1, vacuolar phosphate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHT5;1-GFP triggers Pi starvation-like transcriptional reprogramming, upregulating 65.1% of PSi genes in shoots and 17% in roots under Pi-sufficient conditions.
mechanism: Increased vacuolar Pi sequestration lowers cytosolic Pi, mimicking Pi starvation and activating PSR gene expression.

genes: OsSPX-MFS1 (OsSPX-MFS1, vacuolar phosphate transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSPX-MFS1 in Arabidopsis restores Pi levels in pht5;1 mutants to wild-type levels.
mechanism: OsSPX-MFS1 functions similarly to Arabidopsis PHT5 proteins in mediating vacuolar Pi transport.

genes: OsLSR (Os10g0183000, disease resistance-like protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsLSR results in autoactivation of immune response, accumulation of thiamine, and severe weakness in rice plants with low seed setting rate.
mechanism: OsLSR upregulation activates immune response genes (OsPR1a, OsPR4a, OsPAD4) and thiamine biosynthesis genes (OsDR8, OsTHIC), leading to metabolic imbalance and fitness cost.

genes: OsLSR (Os10g0183000, disease resistance-like protein, Oryza sativa), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of OsLSR::eGFP in tobacco leaf triggers hypersensitive response-like cell death, H2O2 production, and NtPR1 expression.
mechanism: OsLSR::eGFP activates plant immune response pathways, leading to programmed cell death in infiltrated cells.

genes: OsLSR1-437 (N-terminal 437aa of Os10g0183000, disease resistance-like protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsLSR1-437 in rice activates PR genes expression but fails to trigger HR-like cell death in tobacco.
mechanism: The N-terminal portion of OsLSR (CC plus NB domain) triggers transcriptional reprogramming but loses cell death-inducing and thiamine biosynthesis signaling properties.

genes: OsLSR1-437 (N-terminal 437aa of Os10g0183000, disease resistance-like protein, Oryza sativa), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient expression of OsLSR1-437::eGFP in tobacco leaf fails to trigger HR-like cell death compared to 35S::OsLSR.
mechanism: The N-terminal portion of OsLSR loses cell death-inducing signaling properties when overexpressed in tobacco.

genes: OsLSR (Os10g0183000, disease resistance-like protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi of OsLSR results in autoactivation of immune response, thiamine accumulation, and severe growth retardation in rice.
mechanism: OsLSR knockdown increases OsTHIC and OsDR8 expression, leading to elevated thiamine levels and immune response activation.

genes: OsLSR1-178 (N-terminal 178aa of Os10g0183000, disease resistance-like protein, Oryza sativa), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient expression of OsLSR1–178::eGFP in tobacco leaf localizes to chloroplasts and nucleus, indicating chloroplast targeting.
mechanism: OsLSR1–178 fragment contains a chloroplast targeting signal and a nuclear localization signal.

genes: OsLSR464-546 (C-terminal 546aa of Os10g0183000, disease resistance-like protein, Oryza sativa), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient expression of OsLSR464–546::eGFP in tobacco leaf localizes to chloroplasts and cytoplasm, indicating chloroplast targeting.
mechanism: OsLSR464–546 fragment interacts with OsLSR1–178 to target chloroplasts for thiamine biosynthesis.

genes: SAP (At5g35770, causative gene for organ growth, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the sod3-1 mutant restores normal leaf, petal, and silique size in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SAP functions within an SCF complex to target PPD proteins for degradation, promoting meristemoid cell proliferation.

genes: SAP (At5g35770, ubiquitin receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAP increases leaf and flower size in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SAP promotes the proliferation of meristemoid cells, leading to increased cell number and organ size.

genes: SAP (At5g35770, ubiquitin receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SAP promoter activity is detected in young leaves, floral organs, and during early stages of floral organ formation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SAP expression is associated with cell proliferation during organ development.

genes: cry1Ac1 (cry1Ac1, insecticidal toxin, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of cry1Ac1 in cabbage confers insecticidal activity against Plutella xylostella larvae, with survival rates declining rapidly during the first 3-4 days of exposure.
mechanism: NA

genes: ClTCP14a (ClTCP14a, watermelon TCP transcription factor, Citrullus lanatus), ClTCP15 (ClTCP15, watermelon TCP transcription factor, Citrullus lanatus)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of ClTCP14a restores inflorescence height and stem internode length in Arabidopsis tcp14 tcp15 double mutant to wild-type levels.
mechanism: ClTCP14a functions redundantly with ClTCP15 to control plant height via a gibberellic acid (GA)-related pathway, promoting stem internode elongation.

genes: ClTCP14a (ClTCP14a, watermelon TCP transcription factor, Citrullus lanatus), ClTCP15 (ClTCP15, watermelon TCP transcription factor, Citrullus lanatus)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of ClTCP15 restores inflorescence height and stem internode length in Arabidopsis tcp14 tcp15 double mutant to wild-type levels.
mechanism: ClTCP15 functions redundantly with ClTCP14a to control plant height via a gibberellic acid (GA)-related pathway, promoting stem internode elongation.

genes: OsRH2 (Os01g0639100, DEAD box RNA helicase, Oryza sativa), OsRH34 (Os03g0566800, DEAD box RNA helicase, Oryza satativa)
phenotype: OsRH2 and OsRH34 proteins localized in both nucleus and cytoplasm in onion epidermal cells
mechanism: OsRH2 and OsRH34 proteins are localized in both nucleus and cytoplasm, suggesting they shuttle between these compartments

genes: bZIP11 (bZIP11, group S bZIP, Arabidopsis thaliana), bZIP2 (bZIP2, group S bZIP, Arabidopsis thaliana), bZIP44 (bZIP44, group S bZIP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Down-regulation of bZIP11-related group S bZIP factors increases root growth by ~20% in Arabidopsis thaliana under 9-HOT treatment.
mechanism: bZIP11-related bZIPs control root apical growth during energy limiting conditions.

genes: TGA5 (TGA5, bZIP transcription factor group D, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of tga2,5,6 with genomic TGA5 partially reverts the mutant phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana under 9-HOT treatment.
mechanism: TGA5 controls detoxification pathways to metabolize 9- and 13-LOX-derived oxylipins.

genes: TGA2 (TGA2, bZIP transcription factor group D, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TGA2 partially reverts the mutant phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana under 9-HOT treatment.
mechanism: TGA2 controls detoxification pathways to metabolize 9- and 13-LOX-derived oxylipins.

genes: bZIP11 (bZIP11, group S bZIP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of bZIP11 leads to strongly impaired root growth in Arabidopsis thaliana even in the absence of 9-HOT.
mechanism: bZIP11-related bZIPs control root apical growth during energy limiting conditions.

genes: EDS1 (EDS1, disease resistance signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of nuclear-targeted EDS1-YFPNLS causes autoimmunity with stunting, chlorosis, and growth defects in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: EDS1-PAD4 signaling and SA-dependent and SA-independent pathways mediate autoimmunity. High nuclear EDS1 levels trigger defense gene activation and developmental defects.

genes: EDS1 (EDS1, disease resistance signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
modification_type: overexpression with mutated nuclear localization signal
phenotype: EDS1-YFPnls with mutated NLS shows normal growth and no autoimmunity in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: GbSBT1 (Gossypium barbadense subtilase 1, defense response gene, Gossypium barbadense)
phenotype: Overexpression of GbSBT1 in Arabidopsis confers increased resistance to Fusarium oxysporum and Verticillium dahliae infections, with transgenic plants showing smaller necrotic lesions (0.36 ± 0.31 mm vs 2.52 ± 0.66 mm in wild-type) and reduced pathogen colonization.
mechanism: GbSBT1 activates defense-related genes (PR-2, PDF1.2) and mitogen-activated protein kinases (MPK6, MPK3), enhances jasmonic acid (JA) signaling pathway activity, and interacts with prohibitin (PHB) secreted by Verticillium dahliae to trigger resistance responses.

genes: PAGR (Pectic ArabinoGalactan synthesis-Related, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PAGR in Arabidopsis thaliana causes pleiotropic developmental phenotypes including loss of apical dominance and increased RG-I type-II arabinogalactan content
mechanism: PAGR enhances the biosynthesis of RG-I type-II arabinogalactans

genes: OsCESA7 (promoter fragment, Oryza sativa, genomic)
phenotype: GUS activity detected in vascular bundles and sclerenchyma cells of transgenic rice plants
mechanism: OsCESA7 promoter drives GUS expression in mechanical tissues

genes: ARR1 (Arabidopsis Response Regulator 1, transcriptional regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ARR1:GUS expression visualizes ARR1 transcriptional activity in root meristems
mechanism: ARR1 is a transcriptional regulator involved in gibberellin-mediated root meristem size control

genes: RGA (REPRESSOR OF ga1-3, DELLA protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: rga-Delta17 (GA-insensitive RGA mutant) causes dose-dependent root growth inhibition and meristem size reduction
mechanism: RGA-Delta17 stabilizes RGA DELLA protein, blocking GA signaling to suppress ARR1 expression

genes: SCR (SCARECROW, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Endodermis-specific SCR:GR induction rescues GA-dependent root meristem size control in scr-3 mutants
mechanism: SCR activates SNEEZY (SNE) F-box protein to mediate RGA degradation, restoring GA signaling

genes: RGA (REPRESSOR OF ga1-3, DELLA protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RGA:GFP fusion reveals ectopic RGA protein accumulation in scr-1 mutants
mechanism: SCR regulates RGA protein stability, not transcript levels, in root meristems

genes: ARR1 (Arabidopsis Response Regulator 1, transcriptional regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: pARR1:ARR1:GUS reveals ARR1 expression patterns in root meristems
mechanism: ARR1 is transcriptionally regulated by SCR via gibberellin signaling and RGA

genes: CsCH3H (chalcone 3-hydroxylase, Cosmos sulphureus)
phenotype: Increased 3-hydroxyphloridzin content in leaves (up to 11.5% of total dihydrochalcones) correlates with reduced susceptibility to fire blight and apple scab
mechanism: 3-hydroxyphloridzin exhibits higher antioxidant activity than phloridzin and may contribute to disease resistance through its radical scavenging properties

genes: TsApx6 (thylakoid ascorbate peroxidase 6, T. salsuginea), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of TsApx6 increases salt and drought tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with improved germination rates (50% under 150 mM NaCl), root growth, and survival rates (75.4–83.3% after 20 d drought) compared to wild-type.
mechanism: TsApx6 enhances antioxidant enzyme activities (APX, GPX, CAT, SOD), reduces H2O2 and MDA levels, and upregulates stress-responsive genes like Hsp70 and DREB2C under salt stress.

genes: AtApx6 (thylakoid ascorbate peroxidase 6, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtApx6 in Arabidopsis thaliana partially rescues salt and drought tolerance, with survival rates of 76.9–82.5% after 20 d drought and reduced water loss in detached leaves.
mechanism: AtApx6 modulates antioxidant enzyme activities and stress-responsive gene expression, but its effect is less pronounced than TsApx6 under salt stress.

genes: TsApx6 (thylakoid ascorbate peroxidase 6, T. salsuginea), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Ts6P-GUS transgenic Arabidopsis shows weak GUS activity in siliques and under stress conditions, with induction by NaCl and mannitol treatments.
mechanism: TsApx6 promoter contains cis-elements like MBS (MYB binding site) and LTR (low-temperature response), which regulate stress-inducible expression.

genes: TsApx6 (thylakoid ascorbate peroxidase 6, T. salsuginea), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Ts6P-M0-GUS transgenic Arabidopsis shows strong GUS activity throughout the plant and under stress conditions, indicating the MBS motif acts as a negative regulator.
mechanism: Mutation of the MBS element in TsApx6 promoter enhances GUS expression, suggesting MBS is a transcriptional silencer involved in stress response regulation.

genes: AtApx6 (thylakoid ascorbate peroxidase 6, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: At6P-GUS transgenic Arabidopsis shows low GUS activity under stress conditions, with weaker induction compared to Ts6P-GUS.
mechanism: AtApx6 promoter lacks the MBS motif present in TsApx6, leading to lower stress-inducible expression and reduced GUS activity.

genes: AjSOS1 (Artemisia japonica SOS1, Na+/H+ antiporter, Artemisia japonica), CrcSOS1 (Crossostephium chinense SOS1, Na+/H+ antiporter, Crossostephium chinense), CcSOS1 (Chrysanthemum crassum SOS1, Na+/H+ antiporter, Chrysanthemum crassum), CmSOS1 (Chrysanthemum morifolium SOS1, Na+/H+ antiporter, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Overexpression of AjSOS1, CrcSOS1, CcSOS1, and CmSOS1 improves salinity tolerance in transgenic plants, with SOS1s from salt-tolerant species conferring higher tolerance than those from salt-sensitive species.
mechanism: SOS1 proteins function as Na+/H+ antiporters, mediating Na+ efflux to maintain ion homeostasis and enhance salinity tolerance.

genes: PA83 (PA83, full-length protective antigen, synthetic), PNGase F (PNGase F, endoglycosidase F, synthetic)
phenotype: Co-expression of PA83 and PNGase F in N. benthamiana results in deglycosylated pp-dPA83 with enhanced stability and immunogenicity compared to glycosylated pp-PA83.
mechanism: PNGase F enzymatically removes N-linked glycans from PA83 in planta, mimicking the native non-glycosylated form of B. anthracis PA. This preserves native conformation and biological activity, leading to higher toxin neutralization antibody (TNA) titers in mice.

genes: PA83 (PA83, full-length protective antigen, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of glycosylated pp-PA83 in N. benthamiana results in a protein with reduced stability and immunogenicity compared to deglycosylated variants.
mechanism: Glycosylation of pp-PA83 by N. benthamiana's endogenous machinery masks critical epitopes or disrupts protein folding, leading to lower toxin neutralization activity and antibody titers in mice.

genes: PA83 (PA83, full-length protective antigen, synthetic)
phenotype: The N275D/N357D/N417D/N505D/N599D/N693D mutant (pp-PA83M-D) shows improved binding affinity to anti-PA mAb pp-mAbPANG (KD = 3.95×10⁻⁹ M) but reduced immunogenicity compared to pp-dPA83.
mechanism: Asparagine-to-aspartic acid substitutions prevent N-linked glycosylation at six sites, preserving native conformation but altering epitope presentation. The mutant exhibits the lowest off-rate (koff) and highest affinity (KD) for pp-mAbPANG, yet fails to form functional LeTx complexes.

genes: PA83 (PA83, full-length protective antigen, synthetic)
phenotype: The N275Q/N357Q/N417Q/N505Q/N599Q/N693Q mutant (pp-PA83M-Q) shows moderate binding affinity to anti-PA mAb pp-mAbPANG (KD = 1.04×10⁻⁸ M) but poor immunogenicity and LeTx formation capability.
mechanism: Asparagine-to-glutamine substitutions prevent N-linked glycosylation at six sites, but the resulting protein fails to properly fold, leading to reduced toxin neutralization activity and antibody titers in mice.

genes: In-YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), sGFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana and green fluorescent protein (GFP-PTS) in peroxisomes of transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: The cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoter drives constitutive expression of the foreign genes in plant cells.

genes: AtSWEET4 (AtSWEET4, 415-bp fragment, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RNAi4-8 lines showed reduced AtSWEET4 mRNA, leaf chlorosis, smaller plant size, and lower biomass compared to wild-type.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated downregulation of AtSWEET4 reduces glucose/fructose transport, lowers chlorophyll content, and disrupts GSA-AT gene expression.

genes: AtSWEET4 (AtSWEET4, full-length CDS, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: OE4-4 lines showed increased AtSWEET4 mRNA, larger plant size, higher biomass, and enhanced glucose/fructose accumulation compared to wild-type.
mechanism: Overexpression of AtSWEET4 enhances glucose/fructose transport, increases chlorophyll content, and upregulates GSA-AT gene expression.

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: ProAtSWEET4-GUS transgenic plants showed GUS activity in cotyledons, roots (stele), young rosette leaves (veins), and anther filaments.
mechanism: AtSWEET4 promoter drives GUS expression in specific tissues during development.

genes: AtSWEET4 (AtSWEET4, full-length CDS, Arabidopsis thaliana)::YFP (YFP, fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: 35S-AtSWEET4-YFP fusion protein localized to the plasma membrane in Arabidopsis protoplasts.
mechanism: AtSWEET4-YFP fusion protein localizes to the plasma membrane, confirming its cellular localization.

genes: AtOPR3 (coding sequence, functional complementation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced primary root growth in Atopr3 mutant plants under low P conditions when complemented with AtOPR3
mechanism: AtOPR3 inhibits primary root growth via transcriptional regulation under low P conditions

genes: ptxD (phosphite dehydrogenase, Pseudomonas stutzeri, codon-optimized for rice)
phenotype: Transgenic rice exhibits improved root development, chlorophyll retention, and biomass accumulation in phosphite (Phi)-containing media. Transgenic plants can metabolize Phi to Pi and grow vigorously in Phi-rich environments, while wild-type plants show growth inhibition.
mechanism: PtxD oxidizes Phi to Pi using NAD as a cofactor, enabling transgenic rice to utilize Phi as a phosphorus source. This metabolic capability prevents Phi toxicity and allows Phi to function as both fertilizer and herbicide.

genes: AtLFYTERE (AtLFYTERE, mutant of LEAFY (LFY) with TERE mutations in the SAM domain affecting oligomerization and DNA binding, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced complementation efficiency of the lfy-12 mutant compared to wild-type AtLFY, with most transformants producing only a few fertile flowers at the base of the inflorescence.
mechanism: The TERE mutations in the SAM domain of AtLFYTERE impair its ability to oligomerize, reducing its capacity to bind DNA cooperatively and regulate floral development.

genes: AtLFYTERE (AtLFYTERE, mutant of LEAFY (LFY) with TERE mutations in the SAM domain affecting oligomerization and DNA binding, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Absence of ectopic flower formation in T1 transformants despite similar protein expression levels compared to wild-type AtLFY under the CaMV35S promoter.
mechanism: The TERE mutations in the SAM domain of AtLFYTERE prevent oligomerization, which is required for the protein to function as a master switch in flower initiation, leading to failure in triggering precocious termination of shoots and ectopic flower formation.

genes: AGAMOUS (AG, AT4G18840, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Deletion of 450 bp intron fragment in AGAMOUS reduces gene expression by ~40% without affecting splicing, causing partial homeotic transformations of stamens to petals in early arising flowers
mechanism: The 450 bp intron fragment functions as an activator of AGAMOUS gene expression, particularly in early arising flowers, without affecting splicing of the gene transcript

genes: ELF6 (AT5G46910, Arabidopsis thaliana), REF6 (AT5G46910, Arabidopsis thaliana), At5g46910 (AT5G46910, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Multiplex editing of ELF6, REF6, and At5g46910 genes with 50-50% mutation efficiency in T1 transformants when using UBQ10::pcoCas9 system
mechanism: High Cas9 expression in meristematic and embryonic cells via UBQ10 promoter and Arabidopsis codon-optimized Cas9 (pcoCas9) significantly increases mutagenesis efficiency

genes: HvSUT1 (sucrose transporter, Hordeum vulgare, synthetic)
phenotype: Increased grain yield in transgenic wheat lines compared to non-transformed plants
mechanism: NA

genes: OsERF922 (rice ERF transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-induced OsERF922 gene modification in rice enhances resistance to M. oryzae (blast disease) at both seedling and tillering stages, with lesion areas reduced compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: OsERF922 negatively regulates blast resistance in rice; its knockout via CRISPR/Cas9 disrupts this negative regulation, enhancing resistance.

genes: XLG2 (XLG2, complementation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of xlg2 mutant restores flg22-induced ROS burst to wild-type levels.
mechanism: XLG2 stabilizes the FLS2-BIK1 complex and regulates ROS production through phosphorylation.

genes: BIK1 (BIK1, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of BIK1 in agb1 partially restores flg22-induced ROS and Pst resistance.
mechanism: BIK1 accumulation enhances FLS2-mediated immunity by stabilizing the receptor complex and promoting RbohD phosphorylation.

genes: BIK1 (BIK1, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S::BIK1-HA transgenic lines show enhanced flg22-induced ROS and reduced Pst bacterial growth compared to wild-type.
mechanism: Increased BIK1 levels enhance FLS2-mediated immunity by stabilizing the receptor complex and promoting RbohD phosphorylation.

genes: XLG2 (XLG2, complementation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: XLG2 complementation in xlg2 xlg3 mutants restores flg22-induced ROS and Pst resistance to wild-type levels.
mechanism: XLG2 phosphorylation by BIK1 regulates RbohD activity, enhancing ROS production and disease resistance.

genes: SbCLL-7 (cinnamate-CoA ligase, Scutellaria baicalensis, synthetic), SbCHS-2 (chalcone synthase, Scutellaria baicalensis, synthetic), SbFNSII-2 (flavonoid synthase II, Scutellaria baicalensis, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of SbCLL-7, SbCHS-2, and SbFNSII-2 in N. benthamiana produced chrysin without cinnamic acid supplementation, demonstrating the pathway's independence from endogenous enzymes.
mechanism: SbCLL-7 competes with endogenous C4H for cinnamic acid, SbCHS-2 synthesizes pinocembrin, and SbFNSII-2 oxidizes it to chrysin, bypassing the need for SbCHI.

genes: SbCLL-7 (cinnamate-CoA ligase, Scutellaria baicalensis, synthetic), SbCHS-2 (chalcone synthase, Scutellaria baicalensis, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of SbCLL-7 and SbCHS-2 in N. benthamiana produced detectable levels of pinocembrin, confirming SbCHS-2's specificity for cinnamoyl-CoA.
mechanism: SbCLL-7 activates cinnamic acid to cinnamoyl-CoA, which SbCHS-2 uses to synthesize pinocembrin, bypassing the standard 4-coumaroyl-CoA pathway.

genes: PIN1 (PIN FORMED 1, auxin efflux carrier, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PIN1-GFP localization in xylem parenchyma and cambial cells of stem vascular bundles remains stable for up to 6 days after decapitation when auxin is absent, but is maintained when auxin is supplied
mechanism: Auxin promotes ongoing PIN1 localization at the basal plasma membrane of xylem parenchyma cells by preventing endocytosis and maintaining polar localization

genes: PIN7 (PIN FORMED 7, auxin efflux carrier, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PIN7-GFP expression in sup-epidermal cells and xylem parenchyma cells, with dynamic changes during stem development
mechanism: PIN7 contributes to low-conductance polar auxin transport and lateral exchange between PATS and surrounding tissues

genes: DR5rev (auxin response element, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP expression in majority of cell types in stem segments in response to auxin treatment
mechanism: Auxin induces GFP expression through the DR5rev promoter, indicating auxin signaling activity

genes: ABCB19 (ATP-BINDING CASSETTE B19, auxin efflux carrier, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ABCB19-GFP expression in all tissues except xylem and phloem, with apolar localization
mechanism: ABCB19 contributes to non-polar auxin transport and generalized auxin efflux

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase, Agrobacterium tumefaciens, Agrobacterium tumefaciens), NPTII (kanamycin-resistant, Agrobacterium tumefaciens, Agrobacterium tumefaciens), IPT (isopentenyltransferase, Agrobacterium tumefaciens, Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Overexpression of IPT increases endogenous cytokinin levels (trans-Z and trans-ZR) by 4.14- to 11.96-fold, delays leaf senescence by 43.7-82.6% chlorophyll retention in darkness, and alters leaf essential oil composition with higher oxygenated sesquiterpenoids in Asakura-sanshoo.
mechanism: IPT overexpression elevates cytokinin/IAA ratio, leading to cytokinin overproduction, delayed senescence, and altered secondary metabolite pathways in transgenic Asakura-sanshoo.

genes: MIR863 (miR863 precursor, miRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MIR863 does not alter disease resistance to Pst (EV) or Pst (avrRpt2) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: miR863-3p sequentially silences negative and positive regulators of plant immunity through two different modes of action.

genes: ARLPK1 (atypical receptor-like pseudokinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of mutated ARLPK1 increases susceptibility to Pst (EV) and Pst (avrRpt2) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: ARLPKs are negative regulators of plant immune responses.

genes: OsMYB55 (OsMYB55, MYB transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsMYB55 in maize improves tolerance to heat stress and drought, evidenced by higher plant biomass, reduced leaf damage, and lower malondialdehyde (MDA) accumulation under stress conditions compared to wild type.
mechanism: Enhanced expression of stress-associated genes, including those involved in ROS scavenging, antioxidant defense, and regulation of transcription factors (e.g., HSFs, WRKY, MYB), contributes to improved stress tolerance.

genes: SIZ1 (SIZ1, SUMO E3 ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of siz1-2 with ProSIZ1:SIZ1-GFP rescues the short-hypocotyl phenotype under red, blue, and far-red light conditions.
mechanism: SIZ1 negatively regulates photomorphogenesis by mediating SUMO modification of COP1, enhancing its E3 ubiquitin ligase activity.

genes: SUMO2 (SUMO2, SUMO protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: sum1-1 amiR-SUM2 seedlings exhibit a short-hypocotyl phenotype under dark and light conditions, similar to siz1-2.
mechanism: SUMO1/2 modification regulates hypocotyl elongation, but elevated SA levels in siz1-2 do not contribute to the short-hypocotyl phenotype.

genes: COP1 (COP1, E3 ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S-Myc-COP1 seedlings exhibit longer hypocotyls than wild type under white light conditions, indicating enhanced COP1 activity.
mechanism: SIZ1-mediated SUMO modification enhances COP1 E3 ubiquitin ligase activity, promoting HY5 ubiquitination and degradation.

genes: COP1 (COP1K193R, SUMO conjugation-deficient mutant, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S-Myc-COP1K193R seedlings have shorter hypocotyls than 35S-Myc-COP1 under white light, indicating reduced COP1 activity due to lack of SUMO modification.
mechanism: K193 is a critical sumoylation site in COP1; SUMO modification enhances COP1 activity by increasing transubiquitination activity.

genes: WSL12 (LOC_Os12g36194, OsNDPK2, nuclear gene encoding chloroplast-localized protein)
phenotype: Complementation of wsl12 mutant restores wild-type phenotype including normal leaf color, chloroplast development, and pigment content.
mechanism: WSL12 (OsNDPK2) is required for chloroplast development and chlorophyll synthesis. Complementation rescues the mutant phenotype by restoring normal gene expression of chlorophyll biosynthesis and chloroplast development genes.

genes: WSL12 (LOC_Os12g36194, OsNDPK2, nuclear gene encoding chloroplast-localized protein)
phenotype: WSL12-GFP fusion protein localizes to chloroplasts in rice protoplasts, confirming chloroplast targeting of WSL12.
mechanism: Fluorescent signals of WSL12-GFP colocalized with chloroplast auto-fluorescence, demonstrating chloroplast localization of WSL12.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, marker gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of GFP under UV light in transformed plants
mechanism: CaMV35S promoter drives constitutive expression of GFP in plant cells

genes: RBD1 (AT1G70200, RNA-binding domain protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Suppression of chilling sensitive phenotype in rbd1 mutants
mechanism: RBD1 is required for 23S rRNA processing, which affects chloroplast translation

genes: RBD1 (AT1G70200, promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS expression in green tissues throughout development
mechanism: NA

genes: RBD1 (AT1G70200, RNA-binding domain protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Localization of RBD1:GFP fusion protein to chloroplast nucleoids
mechanism: RBD1 localizes to chloroplast nucleoids where 23S rRNA processing occurs

genes: rolA (rolA, Agrobacterium tumefaciens), rolB (rolB, Agrobacterium tumefaciens), rolC (rolC, Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: Artemisinin content was significantly increased in transformed material of both Artemisia species when compared to un-transformed plants. The artemisinin content within leaves of transformed lines was increased by a factor of nine.
mechanism: Expression of all artemisinin biosynthesis genes was significantly increased, and trichome density was also significantly increased in the leaves of transformed plants. This suggests that synthesis is occurring in tissues other than the trichomes.

genes: AFB4 (auxin receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana, AFB5 promoter), AFB5 (auxin receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana, AFB5 promoter)
phenotype: Overexpression of AFB4 and AFB5 under AFB5 promoter rescues auxin response defects in afb5-5 mutant background
mechanism: AFB4 and AFB5 function as auxin receptors that bind IAA and interact with ASK1 to mediate auxin signaling

genes: AFB5 (auxin receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic region)
phenotype: Overexpression of AFB5-mCitrine rescues auxin response defects in afb5-5 mutant background
mechanism: AFB5 functions as an auxin receptor that binds IAA and interacts with ASK1 to mediate auxin signaling

genes: AFB4 (auxin receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic region)
phenotype: Overexpression of AFB4-2×Venus-3×HA rescues auxin response defects in afb4-2 and afb4-8 mutant backgrounds
mechanism: AFB4 functions as an auxin receptor that binds IAA and interacts with ASK1 to mediate auxin signaling

genes: AmA1 (seed storage protein, Amaranth)
phenotype: Overexpression of AmA1 increases total protein content by ~10–83% and amino acid content in sweetpotato tubers.
mechanism: AmA1 acts as a sink protein, redirecting photoassimilates to increase protein and amino acid accumulation while modulating starch/cellulose degradation.

genes: AmA1 (seed storage protein, Amaranth)
phenotype: Tuber-specific overexpression of AmA1 increases protein content by ~18–70% and amino acid content in sweetpotato tubers.
mechanism: AmA1 acts as a sink protein, redirecting photoassimilates to increase protein and amino acid accumulation while modulating starch/cellulose degradation.

genes: PDS (phytoene desaturase, carotenoid biosynthesis enzyme, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Syringe infiltration of amipds-VIGS construct into W. somnifera plants developed bleaching (photobleaching) in systemic leaves 15-20 days post inoculation due to PDS gene silencing. PDS mRNA expression was 75-90% less in systemic tissue of amipds-VIGS lines than in control plants.
mechanism: PDS gene silencing suppresses carotenoid biosynthesis, causing photobleaching and reduced PDS mRNA expression.

genes: WsSGTL1 (sterol glycosyltransferase 1, phytosterol glycosylation enzyme, Withania somnifera), WsSGTL2 (sterol glycosyltransferase 2, phytosterol glycosylation enzyme, Withania somnifera), WsSGTL4 (sterol glycosyltransferase 4, phytosterol glycosylation enzyme, Withania somnifera)
phenotype: 2misgt-VIGS and 4misgt-VIGS lines showed 90% reduced SGT activity compared to control plants. Withanolide A (3.7-fold) and withaferin A (1.7-fold) content increased in silenced lines. Sitosterol (9.9-fold) and stigmasterol (2.8-fold) also increased. Withanoside V content decreased by 45-77%. Silenced lines exhibited delayed growth (shorter height and leaf area) and increased disease susceptibility to A. alternata (higher lesion area, chlorosis, and cfu counts).
mechanism: Down-regulation of WsSGTLs reduces SGT activity, leading to increased free phytosterols and withanolides. This disrupts sterol glycosylation, alters hormone signaling, and compromises basal immunity via reduced callose deposition and increased H2O2/SOD levels.

genes: WsSGTL1 (sterol glycosyltransferase 1, phytosterol glycosylation enzyme, Withania somnifera), WsSGTL2 (sterol glycosyltransferase 2, phytosterol glycosylation enzyme, Withania somnifera), WsSGTL4 (sterol glycosyltransferase 4, phytosterol glycosylation enzyme, Withania somnifera)
phenotype: 4misgt-VIGS lines showed 90% reduced SGT activity compared to control plants. Withanolide A (3.7-fold) and withaferin A (1.7-fold) content increased in silenced lines. Sitosterol (9.9-fold) and stigmasterol (2.8-fold) also increased. Withanoside V content decreased by 45-77%. Silenced lines exhibited delayed growth (shorter height and leaf area) and increased disease susceptibility to A. alternata (higher lesion area, chlorosis, and cfu counts).
mechanism: Down-regulation of WsSGTLs reduces SGT activity, leading to increased free phytosterols and withanolides. This disrupts sterol glycosylation, alters hormone signaling, and compromises basal immunity via reduced callose deposition and increased H2O2/SOD levels.

genes: NPF3 (NPF3, GA transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Accumulation of GA3-Fl was markedly enhanced in these lines (Fig. 1c). This result strongly supports the hypothesis that NPF3 facilitates GA transport in planta.
mechanism: NPF3 facilitates GA transport in planta.

genes: NPF3 (NPF3, GA transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of the NPF3 gene in reverse orientation (p35S:NPF3-antisense) resulted in two and threefold reduction (depending on the line) in NPF3 transcript levels compared with WT (Supplementary Fig. 1d) and in reduced GA3-Fl accumulation in elongating endodermis (Fig. 1c).
mechanism: NPF3 facilitates GA transport in planta.

genes: PvSPL2 (chimeric repressor, switchgrass), SRDX (synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of PvSPL2SRDX increases tiller numbers by 1.6-3.4-fold and reduces lignin accumulation by 12.2-16.0% in switchgrass.
mechanism: PvSPL2SRDX repressor binds to monolignol gene promoters containing GTAC motifs, reducing their expression and lignin biosynthesis.

genes: ASβ (ASβ subunit, feedback-insensitive alpha subunit of anthranilate synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana), ASα (ASα subunit, feedback-resistant alpha subunit of anthranilate synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ASαβ increases tryptophan (3000%), tryptamine, and ajmalicine while decreasing tabersonine, lochnericine, and hörhammericine in Catharanthus roseus hairy roots after 72h induction.
mechanism: AS overexpression triggers global transcriptional changes including stress response and jasmonic acid (JA) biosynthesis pathways, which regulate TIA biosynthesis through altered metabolic flux and transcription factor activity.

genes: NTRC (NADPH-dependent thioredoxin reductase C, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of ntrc mutant restores wild-type resistance to nonhost Pseudomonas syringae pathogens and normal ROS accumulation
mechanism: NTRC detoxifies chloroplast-derived ROS, maintaining redox homeostasis and regulating JA-mediated signaling pathways during nonhost resistance

genes: JcAP1 (JcAP1, APETALA1 homolog, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcAP1 in Arabidopsis causes early flowering (6–10 days earlier under long-day conditions, 1–2 months earlier under short-day conditions) and abnormal flowers with terminal/solitary flowers; overexpression in Jatropha does not cause early flowering.
mechanism: JcAP1 functions as a floral meristem identity gene, repressing TFL1 expression to promote early flowering and floral organ development in Arabidopsis.

genes: CsMYBF1 (CsMYBF1, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsMYBF1 in tomato fruits increases hydroxycinnamic acid derivatives by ~4-8 fold and reduces major sugars (fructose, glucose, etc.) by significant amounts.
mechanism: CsMYBF1 activates promoters of phenylpropanoid pathway genes (SlPAL, SlC4H, Sl4CL) via MYBPLANT cis-elements, increasing carbon flux to secondary metabolism while repressing primary metabolism genes.

genes: AtDPG1 (AtDPG1, putatively chloroplast-localized protein involved in early chloroplast biogenesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the dpg1 mutant results in green cotyledons and true leaves after germination, with no significant phenotypic changes from overexpression
mechanism: AtDPG1 is required for early chloroplast biogenesis

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS expression in green tissues during early Arabidopsis seedling development, with no expression in roots
mechanism: AtDPG1 is expressed in green tissues during early development

genes: TaBASS2 (TaBASS2, pyruvate transporter, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of TaBASS2 in Arabidopsis bass2-1 mutant complemented the mevastatin-sensitive phenotype and enhanced salinity tolerance and reactive oxygen species scavenging.
mechanism: TaBASS2 repressed the expression of ABA INSENSITIVE 4 (ABI4), a node linking ABA signaling and plastid retrograde signaling pathways.

genes: TaBASS2 (TaBASS2, pyruvate transporter, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of TaBASS2 in wheat enhanced salinity tolerance, with relative shoot and root growth rates of 98% and 95% (shoot) and 90% and 91% (root) compared to the vector control under NaCl treatment.
mechanism: TaBASS2 increased ROS content and scavenging activity, and repressed ABI4 expression, leading to enhanced salinity tolerance.

genes: ABI4 (ABI4, ABA INSENSITIVE 4, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Constitutive overexpression of ABI4 in 35S::TaBASS2 transgenic plants restored ABI4 expression to wild-type levels, abolishing the enhanced salinity tolerance conferred by TaBASS2 overexpression.
mechanism: ABI4 negatively regulates salinity tolerance by counteracting the effects of TaBASS2 repression of ABI4.

genes: XPS1 (At3G47110, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Loss of sensitivity to xup25 peptide, no growth inhibition by xup25, no PR1 induction by xup25, no callose deposition by xup25, no pathogen resistance to Pto DC3000 after xup25 treatment
mechanism: XPS1 directly binds xup25 peptide to activate immune responses

genes: FmFLS2-1 (FmFLS2-1, flagellin receptor, Fortunella margarita)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of FmFLS2-1 enhances Xflg22 responsiveness and canker resistance in susceptible 'Duncan' grapefruit.
mechanism: FmFLS2-1 encodes a functional bacterial flagellin/flg22 receptor involved in the perception of the PAMP and induction of the PTI response.

genes: CrFLS2-2 (CrFLS2-2, flagellin receptor, Citrus reticulata)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of CrFLS2-2 enhances Xflg22 responsiveness and canker resistance in susceptible 'Duncan' grapefruit.
mechanism: CrFLS2-2 encodes a functional bacterial flagellin/flg22 receptor involved in the perception of the PAMP and induction of the PTI response.

genes: CpFLS2-2 (CpFLS2-2, flagellin receptor, Citrus paradisi)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of CpFLS2-2 does not significantly enhance Xflg22 responsiveness or canker resistance in susceptible 'Duncan' grapefruit.
mechanism: CpFLS2-2 may contain mutations that compromise the activation of downstream defenses against Xcc.

genes: DcUSAGT1 (UDP-glucose: sinapic acid glucosyltransferase, carrot, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of DcUSAGT1 in E. coli produces recombinant protein capable of glucosylating sinapic acid to 1-O-sinapoylglucose, with optimal activity at pH 7.0 and 30°C
mechanism: DcUSAGT1 catalyzes the transfer of sinapic acid from UDP-glucose to form 1-O-sinapoylglucose, which serves as an acyl donor in anthocyanin acylation, stabilizing cyanidin-based anthocyanins in purple carrots

genes: AtMORC4 (AtMORC4, MORC family ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtMORC7 (AtMORC7, MORC family ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of MYC-tagged AtMORC4 in Arabidopsis thaliana for co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence studies
mechanism: NA

genes: AtMORC4 (AtMORC4, MORC family ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtMORC7 (AtMORC7, MORC family ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of FLAG-tagged AtMORC4 in Arabidopsis thaliana for co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence studies
mechanism: NA

genes: AtMORC4 (AtMORC4, MORC family ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtMORC7 (AtMORC7, MORC family ATPase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: gRNA-A1t (guide RNA, synthetic), gRNA-AB3b (guide RNA, synthetic)

mechanism: Paired gRNAs (A1t + AB3b) direct Cas9 nuclease to create DSBs at two sites in OsDMC1A, but deletions between the sites are not detected, suggesting insufficient proximity for homology-directed repair.

mechanism: Paired gRNAs (AB4t + AB3b) direct Cas9 nickase to create 3′-overhangs, which are less efficient for DSB formation compared to 5′-overhangs. Off-target mutations in OsDMC1B are suppressed due to mismatches in gRNA binding.

mechanism: NtARF19 contributes to NtTTG2-regulated plant growth by modulating auxin signaling.

phenotype: Overexpression of mutated ERS1 (mERS1) in wild-type plants resulted in reduced primary root growth, increased root hair production, and enhanced root-associated APase activity, mimicking hps5 phenotypes.
mechanism: The mutated ERS1 protein interferes with the functions of other ethylene receptors, leading to constitutive ethylene responses and phenotypic changes.

genes: RHS15 (root hair-specific gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), RHS19 (root hair-specific gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: RHS15 and RHS19 are directly targeted by EIN3 and RSL4, promoting root hair development through cell wall modifications and other cellular processes.

genes: Lys11 (Lys11, LysM receptor kinase, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of Lys11 from the 35S promoter led to full complementation of nfr5-2 symbiotic phenotype, forming functional root nodules after Mesorhizobium loti inoculation.
mechanism: LYS11 perceives lipochitooligosaccharides (LCOs) and initiates intracellular signaling for root nodule formation.

genes: Lys11 (Lys11, LysM receptor kinase, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: No complementation of the nfr5-2 symbiotic phenotype when Lys11 was expressed under the Nfr5 promoter.
mechanism: LYS11 protein has reduced affinity for Nod factors or lower intracellular signaling activity compared to NFR5.

genes: Lys11 (Lys11, LysM receptor kinase, Lotus japonicus), NFR5 (NFR5, LysM receptor kinase, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: Both chimeric constructs driven by Nfr5 promoter rescued the nfr5-2 mutant with comparable efficiencies.
mechanism: The extracellular or intracellular domains of LYS11 enable efficient signaling when combined with corresponding domains of NFR5.

genes: Lys15 (Lys15, LysM receptor kinase, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: nfr5-2 plants expressing p35S:Lys15 retained the nitrogen-starved phenotype, with no nodules observed after 5 weeks in the presence of M. loti.
mechanism: Lys15 does not complement the nfr5-2 mutant when overexpressed.

genes: Lys11 (Lys11, LysM receptor kinase, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: Lys11 promoter activity was below visual detection in uninoculated roots and not activated by M. loti Nod factors or inoculation.
mechanism: Lys11 is not expressed during root nodule symbiosis, explaining the lack of redundancy with NFR5.

genes: Lys11 (Lys11, LysM receptor kinase, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: YFP tagged LYS11 localizes to the plasma membrane in N. benthamiana leaf cells.
mechanism: LYS11 is a plasma membrane-localized receptor.

genes: CaDTR1 (CaDTR1, RING type E3 ligase, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CaDTR1 in Arabidopsis leads to enhanced ABA sensitivity and drought tolerance, with 55–85% survival after re-watering compared to 0% in wild-type plants.
mechanism: CaDTR1 increases ABA sensitivity, leading to stomatal closure and reduced transpirational water loss, and upregulates stress-responsive genes like DREB2A, NCED3, RD29A, and KIN1.

genes: CaDTR1 (CaDTR1, RING type E3 ligase, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Transient expression of 35S:CaDTR1-GFP in N. benthamiana shows nuclear localization of CaDTR1 protein.
mechanism: The C-terminal region of CaDTR1 is essential for nuclear localization, as deletion constructs (35S:CaDTR1ΔC-term-GFP) showed cytoplasmic and nuclear localization.

genes: CaDTR1 (CaDTR1, RING type E3 ligase, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: CaDTR1-silenced pepper plants exhibit drought sensitivity, with 55% survival after re-watering compared to 80% in control plants.
mechanism: Silencing CaDTR1 reduces ABA sensitivity, leading to increased transpirational water loss and larger stomatal apertures under ABA treatment.

genes: RB (resistance gene, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Overexpression of RB confers resistance to late blight in both foliage and tubers of Solanum tuberosum.
mechanism: NA

genes: Fld (flavodoxin, plastid-targeted, Anabaena PCC7119)
phenotype: Fld expression protects leaf discs from salt toxicity but not whole plants; increases tolerance to salt toxicity in leaf discs with reduced ROS accumulation and lipid hydroperoxide levels
mechanism: Fld decreases ROS build-up in chloroplasts during salt stress, reducing oxidative damage in leaf tissue

genes: OsARF18 (OsARF18, auxin response factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: mOsARF18 transgenic rice plants exhibit dwarfism, reduced tillering, rolled leaves, abnormal flower and seed development, reduced seed setting, and smaller/abnormal seeds with reduced starch accumulation during seed development
mechanism: Deregulation of OsARF18 disrupts auxin signaling by downregulating auxin-responsive genes (OsARF2, OsGH3-1, OsLAX2, OsPIN1b, OsYUCCA2), leading to abnormal cell division, bulliform cell differentiation, and starch accumulation

genes: TaGLDH-A1 (TaGLDH-A1, L-galactono-1,4-lactone dehydrogenase homoeolog A1, Triticum aestivum), TaGLDH-B1 (TaGLDH-B1, L-galactono-1,4-lactone dehydrogenase homoeolog B1, Triticum aestivum), TaGLDH-D1 (TaGLDH-D1, L-galactono-1,4-lactone dehydrogenase homoeolog D1, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaGLDH-A1, -B1, and -D1 in N. benthamiana significantly increases total GLDH enzyme activity compared to control (PEBV:GUS).
mechanism: Overexpression of TaGLDH homoeologs enhances GLDH activity, which catalyzes the final step of ascorbic acid (AsA) biosynthesis.

genes: TaGLDH-A1 (TaGLDH-A1, L-galactono-1,4-lactone dehydrogenase homoeolog A1, Triticum aestivum), TaGLDH-B1 (TaGLDH-B1, L-galactono-1,4-lactone dehydrogenase homoeolog B1, Triticum aestivum), TaGLDH-D1 (TaGLDH-D1, L-galactono-1,4-lactone dehydrogenase homoeolog D1, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Silencing of TaGLDH homoeologs in wheat via BSMV:GLDHas reduces total GLDH activity by >70% and total AsA content by ~20% in infected seedlings.
mechanism: RNA interference (VIGS) mediated by BSMV:GLDHas specifically targets TaGLDH homoeologs, reducing their expression and subsequent GLDH activity, which impairs AsA biosynthesis.

genes: YL1 (At3g57180, chloroplast rRNA maturation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of yl1-1 mutant restores normal leaf phenotype under salt stress.
mechanism: YL1 participates in chloroplast rRNA maturation, and its loss causes shoot Na+ accumulation under salt stress.

genes: YL1-GSG-GFP (fusion protein, chloroplast localization, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: YL1-GSG-GFP localizes to chloroplast stroma in transgenic plants.
mechanism: YL1 protein is localized in the chloroplast stroma, confirmed by GFP fluorescence and immunoblot analysis.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS activity is detected in most green tissues but low in roots and mature seeds.
mechanism: YL1 gene expression is regulated by salt stress, with reduced transcript levels under high salinity.

genes: AtERF014 (ethylene response factor 014, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)

mechanism: AtERF014 acts as a dual regulator of immunity by modulating pathogen-induced defense responses including ROS accumulation and expression of defense genes (AtPR1, AtPR5, AtPDF1.2). It also affects pectin biosynthesis pathway, altering pectin content in cell walls.

genes: AtERF014 (ethylene response factor 014, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated suppression of AtERF014 decreases resistance to Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 with 7-21-fold increase in bacterial population at 2-4 days post-inoculation, but increases resistance to Botrytis cinerea with 60% reduction in fungal growth at 48 hours post-inoculation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtERF014 suppression weakens SA-induced defense response and alters pathogen-induced ROS accumulation and defense gene expression (AtPR1, AtPR5, AtPDF1.2). It also reduces pectin content by downregulating pectin biosynthetic genes (AtASX2, AtGAE1, AtMUM4, AtQUA1, AtUGP1).

genes: SPA1/SPA2 (chimeric protein, domain swap, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of DS_122-HA (SPA1 N-terminal domain) in spa1 spa2 spa3 mutants complements the mutant phenotype in light, showing moderate hypocotyl length reduction under FRc, Rc, and Bc.
mechanism: The SPA1 N-terminal domain is sufficient to confer SPA1-like activity to the chimeric protein, indicating it is primarily responsible for light responsiveness.

genes: SPA1/SPA2 (chimeric protein, domain swap, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of DS_221-HA (SPA1 WD-repeat domain) in spa1 spa2 spa3 mutants results in strong deetiolation under weak FRc, Rc, and Bc, similar to SPA2-HA.
mechanism: The WD-repeat domain of SPA1 is not sufficient to confer SPA1-like activity to the chimeric protein.

genes: AN8149.2 (AnF, A. nidulans α-fucosidase, A. nidulans)
phenotype: Overexpression of AnF in Arabidopsis apoplast increases α-1,2-fucosidase activity by ~17-fold and reduces fucose content in AGPs by ~50% in roots and leaves
mechanism: AnF cleaves α-1,2-fucose residues from AGP glycans in the apoplast, inducing compensatory upregulation of FUT3, FUT4, FUT6, and downregulation of FUT9

genes: COG3 (COG3, complementation of pollen defects, Arabidopsis thaliana), COG8 (COG8, complementation of pollen defects, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of COG3 and COG8 via pollen-specific promoters rescues male sterility in cog3-/+ and cog8-/+ mutants, increasing male transmission efficiency from ~1:1 to ~1.5:1 (Table 2).
mechanism: COG3 and COG8 overexpression complements pollen tube growth defects in mutants, restoring normal pollen tube morphology and function.

genes: xyn (KJ466334, endo-β-1,4-xylanase from Alicyclobacillus acidocaldarius, synthetic)
phenotype: Endo-β-1,4-xylanase accumulated at 35.66% TSP without detrimental effects on plant development. Heat treatment enriched enzyme activity (105.4 U/mg).
mechanism: NA

genes: OsAHL1 (LOC_Os11g05160, AT-hook content nuclear localized protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsAHL1 increases drought, salt, and cold stress tolerance in rice seedlings, with 70% recovery after osmotic stress, 82% survival under salt stress, and 10% higher survival under cold stress compared to wild type.
mechanism: OsAHL1 regulates root development under drought conditions and activates stress-related genes like HSP101, OsCDPK7, and Rab16b, enhancing drought avoidance and tolerance.

genes: OsAHL1 (LOC_Os11g05160, AT-hook content nuclear localized protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsAHL1 increases drought, salt, and cold stress tolerance in rice seedlings, with 70% recovery after osmotic stress, 82% survival under salt stress, and 10% higher survival under cold stress compared to wild type. Agronomic traits like spikelet fertility, yield per plant, and biomass are 17–50% higher under drought stress.
mechanism: OsAHL1 enhances drought avoidance by regulating root development and activates stress-related genes (HSP101, OsCDPK7, Rab16b) to improve stress tolerance.

genes: OsAHL1 (LOC_Os11g05160, AT-hook content nuclear localized protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi lines of OsAHL1 show reduced root volume under drought stress compared to wild type, indicating that down-regulation of OsAHL1 diminishes root system growth and development.
mechanism: OsAHL1 knockdown reduces root development under drought stress, impairing drought avoidance.

genes: OsAHL1 (LOC_Os11g05160, AT-hook content nuclear localized protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Mutant 1 (AT-hook GRP to AAA) localizes to the nucleus, while mutant 3 (AT-hook and PPC domain mutations) is cytoplasmic, indicating the AT-hook and PPC domain are critical for nuclear localization.
mechanism: The AT-hook and PPC domain guide nuclear localization of OsAHL1; mutations disrupt this localization.

genes: OsAHL1 (LOC_Os11g05160, AT-hook content nuclear localized protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Mutant 2 (DUF296 domain deleted) localizes to the nucleus, indicating the PPC domain is not essential for nuclear localization but contributes to homologous binding.
mechanism: The PPC domain facilitates homologous binding of OsAHL1 proteins but is not required for nuclear localization.

genes: OsAHL1 (LOC_Os11g05160, AT-hook content nuclear localized protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Mutant 3 (AT-hook and PPC domain mutations) is cytoplasmic, confirming the necessity of both domains for nuclear localization.
mechanism: Both AT-hook and PPC domains are required for nuclear localization of OsAHL1.

genes: OtΔ6 (Δ6-desaturase, Ostococcus tauri), PSE1 (Δ6 fatty acid elongase, Physcomitrella patens), TcΔ5 (Δ5-desaturase, Thraustochytrium sp.), PsΔ12 (Δ12-desaturase, Phytophthora sojae), Pi-ω3 (ω3-desaturase, Phytophthora infestans), OtΔ5 (Δ5-elongase, Ostococcus tauri), EhΔ4 (Δ4-desaturase, Emiliania huxleyi)
phenotype: Overexpression of seven genes (OtΔ6, PSE1, TcΔ5, PsΔ12, Pi-ω3, OtΔ5, EhΔ4) in Camelina sativa seeds increases EPA and DHA synthesis.
mechanism: The genes encode desaturases and elongases that catalyze the synthesis of EPA and DHA from precursor fatty acids.

genes: AtRH9 (RNA helicase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Silencing of AtRH9 results in partial resistance to TuMV infection, with reduced viral accumulation and attenuated symptoms.
mechanism: AtRH9 interacts with TuMV RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (NIb) and is recruited to viral replication complexes (VRCs), promoting viral replication.

genes: AtRH9 (RNA helicase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: AtRH9-YFP is transiently expressed in N. benthamiana leaf cells, showing cytoplasmic distribution and chloroplast association during TuMV infection.
mechanism: AtRH9 co-localizes with TuMV 6K2-induced vesicles, suggesting a role in viral replication complex formation.

genes: AtRH9 (RNA helicase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: AtRH9-CFP co-localizes with TuMV 6K2-mCherry vesicles in N. benthamiana leaf cells, indicating recruitment to viral replication complexes.
mechanism: AtRH9 interacts with TuMV NIb and is recruited to VRCs via this interaction, facilitating viral replication.

genes: AtRH9 (RNA helicase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic), NIb (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, Turnip mosaic virus, synthetic)
phenotype: BiFC assay shows interaction between AtRH9 and TuMV NIb in N. benthamiana leaf cells, confirmed by YFP reconstitution.
mechanism: AtRH9 interacts with TuMV NIb in vivo, suggesting a direct role in viral replication.

genes: CYP94B1 (CYP94B1, promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana), CYP94B2 (CYP94B2, promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana), CYP94B3 (CYP94B3, promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana), CYP94C1 (CYP94C1, promoter region, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Histochemical β-glucuronidase (GUS) activity in Arabidopsis tissues to analyze CYP94 gene expression patterns
mechanism: Promoter-driven GUS expression for gene expression analysis

genes: MAP30 (ribosome-inactivating protein with antimicrobial activity, Momordica charantia)
phenotype: The total proteins extracted from the transgenic hairy root clones showed strong antimicrobial activity against various bacteria and fungi, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative species, and exhibited DNase activity.
mechanism: rMAP30-KDEL exerts antimicrobial activity by forming ion channels in microbial membranes or inhibiting microbial adhesion to host polysaccharide receptors.

genes: TTG1 (TRANSPARENT TESTA GLABRA1, Arabidopsis thaliana), K1 (dihydrofolate reductase P67L, mouse), K2 (dihydrofolate reductase T39A/E173D, mouse), K3 (dihydrofolate reductase T39A/P67L/E173D, mouse)
phenotype: Conditional overexpression of TTG1 fused to N-degron cassettes K1, K2, and K3 allows temperature-dependent trichome formation in Arabidopsis thaliana. K2:TTG1 enables tunable protein levels and trichome development at semi-restrictive temperatures.
mechanism: N-terminal degron functionality via the N-end rule pathway, where destabilizing N-terminal residues (Phe) are recognized by PRT1 E3 Ub ligase, leading to temperature-dependent protein degradation.

genes: CO (CONSTANS, Arabidopsis thaliana), K2 (dihydrofolate reductase T39A/E173D, mouse)
phenotype: Conditional overexpression of CO fused to K2 degron enables temperature-dependent floral induction, causing early flowering ~14 days earlier than wild-type at permissive temperatures.
mechanism: N-terminal degron functionality via the N-end rule pathway, where Phe-initiated K2:CO is degraded at restrictive temperatures, preventing floral induction.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic), K2 (dihydrofolate reductase T39A/E173D, mouse)
phenotype: Conditional overexpression of K2:GFP allows temperature-dependent protein accumulation/depletion, with activity levels tunable across permissive to restrictive temperatures.
mechanism: N-terminal degron functionality via the N-end rule pathway, where Phe-initiated K2:GFP is degraded at restrictive temperatures, reducing fluorescence.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic), K2 (dihydrofolate reductase T39A/E173D, mouse)
phenotype: Conditional overexpression of K2:GUS enables temperature-dependent enzyme activity, with activity levels decreasing at restrictive temperatures despite stable transcript levels.
mechanism: N-terminal degron functionality via the N-end rule pathway, where Phe-initiated K2:GUS is degraded at restrictive temperatures, reducing enzymatic activity.

genes: PPME (At3g18020, P-type PPR protein involved in mitochondrial RNA editing, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of ppme−/− rescued defective growth, restored normal vegetative and reproductive development, and rescued mitochondrial complex I activity in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PPME binds to sequences surrounding nad1-898 editing site, modulates RNA editing at nad1-898 and nad1-937, and is essential for mitochondrial complex I function.

genes: PPME (At3g18020, P-type PPR protein involved in mitochondrial RNA editing, Arabidopsis thaliana)
