mechanism: PPME binds to sequences surrounding nad1-898 editing site, modulates RNA editing at nad1-898 and nad1-937, and is essential for mitochondrial complex I function.

genes: CpFTSY (CpFTSY, gene involved in chlorophyll antenna size regulation, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii)
phenotype: CpFTSY knockout results in pale green coloration, three times lower total chlorophyll content, and two to three times higher Chl a to Chl b ratio compared to wild type in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
mechanism: CpFTSY knockout reduces chlorophyll antenna size of photosystems, leading to lower chlorophyll content and altered Chl a/b ratio.

genes: ZEP (ZEP, zeaxanthin epoxidase, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii)
phenotype: ZEP knockout leads to tenfold higher zeaxanthin (Zea) accumulation compared to wild type under low light conditions in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
mechanism: ZEP knockout blocks zeaxanthin epoxidation to violaxanthin, resulting in constitutive Zea accumulation.

genes: ZEP (ZEP, zeaxanthin epoxidase, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii), CpFTSY (CpFTSY, gene involved in chlorophyll antenna size regulation, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii)
phenotype: ΔZEP/ΔCpFTSY double mutant shows tenfold higher Zea accumulation, three times lower total chlorophyll content, and golden coloration compared to wild type in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. The double mutant exhibits 54% higher photosynthetic rate per Chl under high light conditions.
mechanism: Combined ZEP and CpFTSY knockout reduces chlorophyll antenna size and blocks Zea epoxidation, leading to higher Zea accumulation and improved light use efficiency under high light.

genes: FhGL3L (bHLH transcription factor, involved in flavonoid biosynthesis and trichome formation, Freesia hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of FhGL3L increases anthocyanin accumulation by ~15% in Arabidopsis thaliana and inhibits trichome formation on leaf lamina and stems.
mechanism: FhGL3L upregulates AtPAP1 and AtTT8 (anthocyanin biosynthesis regulators) and downregulates AtGL2 (trichome formation repressor).

genes: FhTT8L (bHLH transcription factor, involved in flavonoid biosynthesis, Freesia hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of FhTT8L increases anthocyanin and proanthocyanidin accumulation in Arabidopsis thaliana without affecting trichome formation.
mechanism: FhTT8L upregulates late biosynthetic genes (LBGs) and BAN (proanthocyanidin-specific gene) while interacting with AtPAP1 and AtTT2 (anthocyanin/proanthocyanidin regulators).

genes: Zct1 (ZCT1 transcriptional repressor, Catharanthus roseus, cloned from C. roseus cDNA)

mechanism: RNAi via estrogen-inducible XVE system (LexA promoter driving hairpin RNA expression)

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic, cloned from pUC57(kan))
phenotype: Silencing of GFP used as control; no effect on Zct1 expression or TIA production
mechanism: RNAi via estrogen-inducible XVE system (LexA promoter driving hairpin RNA expression)

genes: KINβγ (KINβγ, fusion with YFP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the kinβγ mutation restores normal pollen morphology and reduces defective pollen grains.
mechanism: The transgene restores normal function of KINβγ, which is involved in pollen development and mitochondrion biogenesis.

genes: KIN10 (KIN10, target of amiRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana), KIN11 (KIN11, target of amiRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: KINβγ works in coordination with KIN10 and KIN11 in the SnRK1 complex for the regulation of Arabidopsis pollen development and mitochondrion biogenesis.

genes: CAT3 (CAT3, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: ROS levels in pollen are essential for hydration and germination on stigmas, as reduced ROS levels impair these processes.

genes: REL2 (REL2, loss-of-function mutation in rel2 mutant, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementary expression of REL2 in rel2 mutant rescues the rolling and erect leaf phenotype, restoring leaf morphology to wild-type levels
mechanism: Normal REL2 protein expression restored the mutant phenotype through complementation

mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9 induces frame-shift mutations in 4′OMT2 via non-homologous end joining (NHEJ), disrupting its function in benzylisoquinoline alkaloid (BIA) biosynthesis.

genes: pevd1 (protein elicitor, V. dahliae, V. dahliae)

mechanism: PevD1 activates JA biosynthesis (LOX4, AOC1, OPR3 up-regulated), Ca2+-responsive pathways (CML38, WRKY22, WRKY33 up-regulated), and suppresses ABA-responsive pathway (WRKY40, PP2CA, HAI2 up-regulated).

genes: MaASR (MaASR, banana ASR gene, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: Overexpression of MaASR causes delayed flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana, with transgenic lines L14 and L38 showing significantly delayed flowering time compared to wild-type plants under long day conditions.
mechanism: MaASR overexpression reduces the expression of photoperiod pathway genes (CO, Col1, Col2, ELF3, ELF4, TCH2), vernalization pathway genes (VRN1, MAF5), GA pathway genes (GAI, RGL1), and floral integrator genes (SOC1), while altering the expression pattern of flower development-related genes (NGA1, SEP3, NAP).

genes: MaASR (MaASR, banana ASR gene, Musa acuminata)
phenotype: Overexpression of MaASR causes delayed flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana, with transgenic lines L14 and L38 showing significantly delayed flowering time compared to wild-type plants under long day conditions.
mechanism: MaASR overexpression reduces the expression of photoperiod pathway genes (CO, Col1, Col2, ELF3, ELF4, TCH2), vernalization pathway genes (VRN1, MAF5), GA pathway genes (GAI, RGL1), and floral integrator genes (SOC1), while altering the expression pattern of flower development-related genes (NGA1, SEP3, NAP).

genes: GUS (reporter gene for GUS activity, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity is strongly enhanced in leaves infiltrated with Pst DC3000 compared to mock-treated leaves at 24 hpi.
mechanism: Activation of the JUB1 promoter by Pst DC3000 treatment.

genes: JUB1 (transcription factor involved in stress response and defense regulation, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Negative regulation of defense responses via accumulation of DELLA proteins and activation of JA signaling.

phenotype: Triple-OX plants exhibit reduced disease symptoms and bacterial proliferation compared to JUB1-OX plants, with bacterial titers similar to wild-type plants.
mechanism: Restoration of defense responses by overexpressing GA3ox1 and DWF4, counteracting JUB1's negative regulation of GA and BR pathways.

genes: GmBZL2 (Glycine max BZR1-like 2, Glycine max)

mechanism: The P216L mutation in GmBZL2 enhances BR signaling through increased nuclear localization and dephosphorylation, mimicking the bzr1-1D mutant phenotype.

genes: MdMADS15 (AG-like gene, Malus domestica), MdMADS22 (AG-like gene, Malus domestica)

mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of MdMADS15 and MdMADS22 reduced their expression, leading to floral organ identity changes and fertility reduction

genes: RPL18aB (ribosomal protein L18aB, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic)

mechanism: Complementation of the rpl18aB-1 mutation with the genomic RPL18aB gene restores normal embryogenesis and seed development.

genes: RPL18aB (ribosomal protein L18aB, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic)
phenotype: pLAT52::RPL18aB complementation increases pollen tube competitiveness in rpl18aB-1 mutants, restoring ~30% male transmission efficiency.
mechanism: Specific expression of RPL18aB in pollen via the LAT52 promoter rescues pollen tube growth defects and improves male gametophyte transmission.

genes: RPL18aB (ribosomal protein L18aB, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic)

mechanism: RVE1 directly binds to EE-expand motifs in the GA3ox2 promoter, repressing its transcription.

It also improves gas exchange attributes and water retention through stomatal regulation.

phenotype: 35S:ROXY19SSMS line #18 was only used later for transcript analysis by qRT-PCR.
mechanism: NA

mechanism: NA

phenotype: Next, we mutated the conserved CCMC motif of ROXY19 into a CPYC motif that is found in class I GRXs.

mechanism: ROXY18 and ROXY19 might function redundantly as negative regulators of TGA-dependent detoxification genes.

genes: CB5C (cytochrome b5, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: RGL2 (RGL2, DELLA protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: EF4 (element tetramer), GmScreamM8 core promoter, gfp (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Synthetic promoter with EF4 tetramer, GmScreamM8 core, and native intron shows 33-fold higher transient GFP expression compared to intron-less counterpart in lima bean cotyledons. In soybean hairy roots, it shows highest expression among element-intron variants.
mechanism: EF4 tetramer and GmScreamM8 intron synergistically enhance promoter activity through IME. Intron enhances core promoter activity by 7-fold even without additional elements.

genes: GmScreamM8 (promoter), gfp (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Synthetic intron with trimeric repeat of intron part 3 (4xEF4-M8CIN23334) shows 2-fold higher transient GFP expression and highest stable expression compared to other intron variants. Stuffed intron enhances IME through repeated regulatory elements.
mechanism: Repeated intron part 3 sequences enhance IME by increasing transcription factor binding sites or altering chromatin structure. Trimeric repeats show additive enhancement effects.

genes: miR165/166 (microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: STTM165/166 plants exhibit drought and cold resistance, with reduced water loss and increased ABA content (~3-fold compared to wild type).
mechanism: miR165/166 knockdown leads to upregulation of targets like PHB, which directly regulate ABI4 and BG1, altering ABA homeostasis and response pathways.

genes: PHB (HD-ZIPIII, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PHB:PHB G202G-YFP lines show increased ABI4 and BG1 expression, contributing to ABA hypersensitivity and altered stress responses.
mechanism: PHB directly binds to ABI4 and BG1 promoters, upregulating their expression and modulating ABA signaling and homeostasis.

genes: BisaboleneSynthase (BisaboleneSynthase, terpenoid biosynthesis, synthetic), FPPSynthase (FPPSynthase, farnesyl diphosphate synthesis, synthetic), DXS (1-Deoxy-D-xylulose 5-phosphate synthase, non-mevalonate pathway, synthetic)
phenotype: Production of bisabolene in tobacco leaves with marginal improvements in yield after stacking FPP synthase and DXS
mechanism: Bisabolene synthase uses farnesyl diphosphate (FPP) as substrate; FPP synthase and DXS enhance precursor availability in the non-mevalonate pathway

genes: ReporterGene1 (NA), ReporterGene2 (NA), ReporterGene3 (NA)
phenotype: Stable expression of three stacked reporter genes in soybean hairy roots confirmed by microscopy and RT-PCR
mechanism: NA

genes: R2Cluster (Rps4-Rrs1 gene cluster, resistance to pathogens, Arabidopsis thaliana), R7Cluster (Rps4-Rrs1 gene cluster, resistance to pathogens, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Synthetic gene cluster fusing R2 and R7 clusters expressed in soybean hairy roots; three of four resistance genes detected by RT-PCR
mechanism: Synthetic gene cluster confers resistance traits by expressing Rps4-Rrs1 gene cluster components

genes: AtSWEET13 (At5g50800, promoter-driven GUS expression, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtSWEET14 (AT4G25010, promoter-driven GUS expression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS activity detected in stamens, vascular tissues, and embryonic cotyledons during flower development
mechanism: Promoter activity of AtSWEET13 and AtSWEET14 drives GUS expression in anthers, vascular tissues, and seeds

genes: AtSWEET13 (AT5G50800, plasma membrane-localized GFP fusion, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtSWEET14 (AT4G25010, plasma membrane-localized GFP fusion, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GFP fluorescence associated with the plasma membrane in transgenic plants
mechanism: 35S promoter drives expression of AtSWEET13/14-GFP fusions localized to plasma membrane

genes: AtSWEET13 (AT5G50800, genomic complementation, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtSWEET14 (AT4G25010, genomic complementation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complemented the reduced fertility and seed size phenotype of sweet13 sweet14 double mutant
mechanism: Genomic DNA of AtSWEET13/14 restores normal anther dehiscence and seed development in double mutant

genes: miR319a (microRNA, endogenous, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduction in CIN-TCP gene expression leads to indeterminate leaf margins with continuous de novo tissue formation in cotyledons, leaves, and floral organs. Plants grow more slowly and flower later.
mechanism: miR319a targets five CIN-TCP transcription factors, reducing their activity and disrupting proximo-distal differentiation gradients. This maintains meristematic properties at leaf margins.

genes: amiR-NGA (artificial microRNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Reduction in NGA gene activity results in increased leaf serrations, larger leaves with smaller cells, and prolonged cell division in distal leaf regions. Plants exhibit delayed flowering.
mechanism: amiR-NGA targets four NGA transcription factors, reducing their activity and disrupting leaf margin differentiation. This maintains meristematic properties at leaf margins.

genes: miR319a (microRNA, endogenous, Arabidopsis thaliana), amiR-NGA (artificial microRNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Simultaneous reduction in nine genes (five CIN-TCPs and four NGAs) results in continuous de novo tissue formation at all lateral organ margins. Plants grow more slowly, flower later, and have leaf margins with proliferative cell populations.
mechanism: Combined knockdown of CIN-TCP and NGA genes disrupts both proximo-distal differentiation gradients and margin differentiation, maintaining meristematic properties at all organ margins.

genes: SMXL6 (At1g07200, SMXL6, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: StrigoQuant allows monitoring SMXL6 degradation in response to SLs, leading to a decrease in FF/REN ratio.
mechanism: SLs trigger SMXL6 degradation via the 26S proteasome, dependent on MAX2 and AtD14.

genes: (GA)7 (synthetic, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: CtrlQuant does not show degradation upon SL treatment, serving as a control.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsD14 (Q10QA5, D14, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsD14 in Atd14 (col) protoplasts rescues SMXL6 degradation upon rac-GR24 induction.
mechanism: OsD14 can substitute for AtD14 in SL signaling, enabling SMXL6 degradation.

genes: neoR (neomycin phosphotransferase for G418 resistance, E. coli)
phenotype: G418 resistance in Physcomitrella patens
mechanism: NA

genes: OsCOL9 (OsCOL9, pathogen-responsive transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Oscol9-ko plants show reduced resistance to M. oryzae infection and downregulated PR genes (PR1a, PR1b, PR10) compared to wild-type.
mechanism: OsCOL9 knockout disrupts SA/ET signaling pathways, reduces NPR1 and WRKY45 expression, and alters ACC synthase/oxidase gene expression.

genes: OsCOL9 (OsCOL9, pathogen-responsive transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsCOL9-GFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsCOL9 (OsCOL9, pathogen-responsive transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsCOL9 and its MR domain show transcriptional activation activity in yeast.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsCOL9 (OsCOL9, pathogen-responsive transcription factor, Oryza sativa), OsRACK1 (OsRACK1, WD40 repeat domain protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsCOL9 CCT domain and OsRACK1 physically interact in vitro.
mechanism: NA

genes: BASL (BASL, polarity protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The fusion protein driven by the endogenous promoter fully complements basl loss-of-function mutants.
mechanism: NA

genes: BASL (BASL, polarity protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Myr-GFP-BASL maintained polar distribution at the PM (Figure 1D) and rescued basl-3 mutants effectively.
mechanism: NA

genes: BASL (BASL, polarity protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: One represents a high phosphorylation form (GFP-BASL_123456D) with all six SP sites mutated to phospho-mimicking DPs (AspPro), which fully rescued basl and showed polarity comparable to that of GFP-BASL.
mechanism: NA

genes: BASL (BASL, polarity protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The other one represents a low phosphorylation form (GFP-BASL_12356A) with five SPs mutated to phospho-deficient APs (AlaPro) that displayed disrupted polarity and function.
mechanism: NA

genes: BASL (BASL, polarity protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GFP-BASL_14D showed severely retarded recovery at the cell cortex (Figure 1E, I600 = 17.02% vs. GFP-BASL 38.11%). The protein abundance and stability of GFP-BASL_14D at the polarity site are comparable to those in WT.
mechanism: NA

genes: MPK6 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 6, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: MPK6-mRFP (driven by the BASL promoter) was expressed in Arabidopsis stomatal lineage cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: MPK6 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 6, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: A kinase-dead version of MPK6 (MPK6_AEF-YFP; the conserved catalytic loop TEY amino acids mutated to AEF)[23] was used as a negative control.
mechanism: NA

genes: SPCH (SCREAM, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Introducing an extra copy of SPCH (SPCHpro::SPCH-CFP) in WT plants induced an elevated stomatal index.
mechanism: NA

genes: SPCH (SCREAM, bHLH transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: expression of a degradation-resistant version SPCH_1-5A-CFP resulted in over-proliferation of stomatal cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: V2 (V2, symptom determinant and suppressor of gene silencing, Cotton leaf curl Kokhran virus-Burewala)
phenotype: Transgenic cotton plants show resistance to Cotton Leaf Curl Disease (CLCuD) with reduced disease symptoms and viral titer compared to non-transgenic controls.
mechanism: RNAi targeting the V2 gene of begomovirus suppresses viral replication and symptom development.

genes: CpFAH (CpFAH, fatty acid hydroxylase, C. purpurea)
phenotype: Overexpression of CpFAH increases ricinoleic acid (RA) production to 2.2 pg/cell in Chaetoceros gracilis.
mechanism: CpFAH catalyzes hydroxylation of fatty acids to produce RA, which is esterified into monoestolide triacylglycerols (ME TAG) to reduce toxicity.

genes: MALCE1 (MALCE1, fatty acid elongase, fungal)
phenotype: Co-expression of MALCE1 with CpFAH increases RA content to 3.3 pg/cell in Chaetoceros gracilis.
mechanism: MALCE1 enhances conversion of 16:0 to 18:0, providing more substrates for CpFAH to produce RA.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS expression driven by the PME6 promoter localizes predominantly to mature guard cells in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: The PME6 promoter directs GUS expression in guard cells, indicating guard-cell-specific activity of PME6.

genes: PME6 (pectin methylesterase inhibitor/proPME, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the pme6-1 mutant with proPME6::PME6 restores PME6 mRNA levels and normal guard cell wall pectin methyl-esterification patterns.
mechanism: Restoration of PME6 expression in pme6-1 mutants re-establishes guard cell-specific pectin de-esterification, enabling normal stomatal function.

genes: ADH1 (Alcohol dehydrogenase 1, hypoxia-responsive gene involved in ethanol fermentation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS staining reveals ADH1 induction localized in infected cortical cells of root galls at 21 dpi
mechanism: ADH1 induction suggests localized oxygen deficiency in infected root tissues during clubroot development

genes: LcIDL1 (LcIDL1, IDA-like gene involved in abscission, Litchi chinensis)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of LcIDL1 driven by the 35S promoter strongly activated floral organ abscission in Arabidopsis, with flowers dropping at position 5 compared to position 9 in wild-type.
mechanism: LcIDL1 activates abscission-related gene expression (TCH4, EXO, EXL1, GAD4) and induces pH changes in abscission zone (AZ) cells, leading to earlier floral organ abscission.

genes: AtIDA (AtIDA, IDA gene involved in abscission, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtIDA in Arabidopsis caused precocious floral organ abscission, with flowers dropping at position 5 compared to position 9 in wild-type.
mechanism: AtIDA activates abscission-related gene expression and induces pH changes in AZ cells, leading to earlier floral organ abscission.

genes: NRAMP1 (NRAMP1, iron and manganese transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues nramp1-1 and nramp1-1 irt1-1 mutant phenotypes by restoring iron uptake and growth under iron-replete conditions.
mechanism: NRAMP1 expressed under IRT1 promoter can transport iron, compensating for IRT1 loss of function.

genes: IRT1 (IRT1, iron and manganese transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues irt1-1 mutant hyper-sensitivity to iron deficiency and partially rescues nramp1-1 irt1-1 double mutant under iron-deficient conditions.
mechanism: IRT1 expressed under NRAMP1 promoter can transport iron in root outer cell layers, compensating for IRT1 loss of function.

genes: VoGES (geraniol synthase, Valeriana officinalis, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of geraniol synthase leads to production of geraniol and its glycosides in tobacco cell cultures, which are not naturally present in tobacco.
mechanism: Geraniol synthase catalyzes the formation of geraniol, which is then glycosylated to produce various glycosides in the transgenic tobacco cells.

genes: ipt (isopentenyl transferase, Agrobacterium tumefaciens)
phenotype: SAG12-ipt plants exhibit improved drought tolerance compared to null-transformed controls, maintaining higher relative water content and photosynthetic activity under drought stress.
mechanism: Overexpression of ipt increases endogenous cytokinin levels, which enhances drought tolerance through metabolic regulation (carbon metabolism, energy production), stress defense (catalase activity, glyoxalase), and maintenance of photosynthetic machinery.

genes: OsSAP (OsSAP, senescence-associated protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSAP increases drought tolerance in rice, with transgenic lines showing 10-15% higher survival rates compared to wild type under drought stress.
mechanism: OsSAP overexpression elevates abscisic acid (ABA), jasmonic acid (JA), and gibberellic acid (GA3) levels, modulating hormonal signaling pathways to enhance drought acclimation and cell membrane stability.

genes: AtBI-1 (AtBI-1, Bax inhibitor-1 homolog, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtBI-1 increases drought tolerance in rice, with transgenic lines showing 15-20% higher survival rates compared to wild type under drought stress.
mechanism: AtBI-1 overexpression elevates ABA, JA, and GA3 levels, modulating hormonal signaling pathways to enhance drought acclimation and cell membrane stability.

genes: AtNACK1 (kinesin-like protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, cDNA)
phenotype: GFP-AtNACK1 localizes to the site of cell plate formation in BY-2 cells and disappears after maturation
mechanism: AtNACK1 is degraded via ubiquitin-proteasome pathway after cytokinesis, with motor domain and BC stalk region critical for localization

genes: AtNACK1 (kinesin-like protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, cDNA)
phenotype: No GFP signals observed in phragmoplast region or cell plate formation site
mechanism: Motor domain alone is insufficient for proper localization; requires BC stalk region

genes: AtNACK1 (kinesin-like protein, Arabidopsis thaliana, cDNA)
phenotype: GFP signals detected in wide regions around cell plate formation site (phragmoplast area)
mechanism: C-terminal GFP fusion disrupts localization to cell plate formation site

genes: TaVIP2 (viral infection protein 2, cloned from Triticum aestivum, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaVIP2 increases Agrobacterium-mediated transformation efficiency by 2.1-2.5-fold and confers near-complete resistance to powdery mildew in Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: TaVIP2 up-regulates NtPR-1 gene expression, a pathogenesis resistance-related gene in tobacco, which correlates with enhanced disease resistance.

genes: JcLFY (JcLFY, floral identity gene, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcLFY in Arabidopsis induced early flowering, solitary flowers, and terminal flowers.
mechanism: JcLFY overexpression promotes flowering by upregulating FM identity genes AP1, SOC1, and CAL, and floral organ identity genes AG, AP3, SEP1, SEP2, and SEP3, while downregulating TFL1.

genes: JcLFY (JcLFY, floral identity gene, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: JcLFY overexpression in lfy-15 mutant Arabidopsis induced early flowering and complemented mutant phenotypes.
mechanism: JcLFY overexpression complements the lfy-15 mutant by upregulating FM identity genes AP1, SOC1, and CAL, and floral organ identity genes AG, AP3, SEP1, SEP2, and SEP3, while downregulating TFL1.

genes: JcLFY (JcLFY, floral identity gene, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: JcLFY overexpression in Jatropha induced early flowering.
mechanism: JcLFY overexpression in Jatropha promotes flowering by upregulating floral identity genes JcAP1, JcAP3, JcAG, JcSEP1, and JcSEP3, while downregulating JcAP2 and JcTFL1c.

genes: OsACOS12 (acyl-CoA synthetase for sporopollenin precursor synthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Partial restoration of male fertility in the Arabidopsis acos5 mutant.
mechanism: OsACOS12 can fulfill the function of ACOS5 in Arabidopsis.

genes: OsACOS12 (acyl-CoA synthetase for sporopollenin precursor synthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complete male sterility in the Arabidopsis acos5 mutant.
mechanism: OsACOS12 promoter is not strong enough to drive expression in Arabidopsis.

genes: JIOsPR10 (pathogenesis-related protein 10 (PR10) family protein involved in biotic and abiotic stress tolerance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of JIOsPR10 increases drought and salt stress tolerance, enhances resistance to M. oryzae infection, and promotes early root and shoot development in rice by upregulating defense-related proteins (TLP, DUF26-like protein, beta-1,3-glucanase, Cu/Zn-SOD) and downregulating metabolic enzymes (enolase, NDK, etc.).
mechanism: JIOsPR10 overexpression induces oxidative stress tolerance through increased peroxidase and Cu/Zn-SOD activity, upregulates pathogenesis-related proteins (TLP, DUF26-like protein, beta-1,3-glucanase) for biotic/abiotic stress defense, and downregulates metabolic pathways to balance development and stress adaptation.

genes: AtNUDX19 (Nudix hydrolase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: nudx19 mutants show increased photooxidative stress tolerance, higher NADPH levels, and enhanced carbon assimilation rates under high light conditions
mechanism: AtNUDX19 regulates cellular levels and redox states of pyridine nucleotides, modulating photooxidative stress responses and hormonal signaling pathways

genes: TMS5a (thermo-sensitive genic male sterility gene, target site in TMS5 coding region, Oryza sativa), TMS5b (thermo-sensitive genic male sterility gene, target site in TMS5 coding region, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Development of thermo-sensitive genic male sterile (TGMS) rice lines with pollen sterility under high temperature (HT) and restored fertility under low temperature (LT).
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of TMS5 gene disrupts male fertility, creating temperature-sensitive sterility. Homozygous mutations in TMS5a and TMS5b sites result in stable TGMS phenotypes with low critical sterility-inducing temperature (CSIT).

genes: HDA9 (histone deacetylase 9, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: HDA9-FLAG rescued the dwarf phenotype of hda9 mutant
mechanism: HDA9-FLAG is functional in vivo and interacts with PWR and WRKY53 to regulate histone acetylation and leaf senescence

genes: PWR (POWERDRESS, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PWR-FLAG interacts with HDA9 and promotes leaf senescence
mechanism: PWR-FLAG binds to HDA9 and regulates histone acetylation at similar genomic regions as HDA9

genes: cry1A.105 (cry1A.105, chimeric delta-endotoxin, Bacillus thuringiensis), cry2Ab2 (cry2Ab2, delta-endotoxin, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Expression of cry1A.105 and cry2Ab2 transgenes confers insect resistance in maize
mechanism: Production of Bt delta-endotoxins that target lepidopteran insect species

genes: CmFTL1 (FLOWERING LOCUS T-like, Chrysanthemum morifolium, cloned from 'Jimba')
phenotype: Complementation of A. thaliana ft-10 mutant results in partial rescue of flowering time delay, with 5/19 transformants showing strong recovery (13-18 rosette leaves) and 14 showing moderate recovery (19-24 leaves).
mechanism: CmFTL1 shares 72% sequence identity with AtFT and contains conserved residues Tyr85 and Gln140 critical for FT function. The archetypal CmFTL1 transcript promotes flowering by interacting with CmFDL1.

genes: CmFTL1astIn1-1 (alternative splicing variant of CmFTL1, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Transgenic chrysanthemum OX-CmFTL1astIn1-1 lines show advanced flowering time by 5-8 days compared to wild type. In Arabidopsis, 8/25 transformants showed strong recovery (13-18 rosette leaves), 11 moderate (19-24), and 6 weak (>25).
mechanism: Post-transcriptional processing of CmFTL1astIn1-1 generates archetypal CmFTL1 transcript, which interacts with CmFDL1 to promote flowering. The AS transcript contains a frame shift but undergoes processing to restore functionality.

genes: CmFTL1astIn1-2 (alternative splicing variant of CmFTL1, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Transgenic chrysanthemum OX-CmFTL1astIn1-2 lines show advanced flowering time by 5-8 days. In Arabidopsis, 4/15 transformants showed strong recovery (13-18 rosette leaves), 9 moderate (19-24), and 2 weak (>25).
mechanism: Post-transcriptional processing of CmFTL1astIn1-2 generates archetypal CmFTL1 transcript. The AS transcript contains an alternative donor site but undergoes processing to restore functionality.

genes: CmFTL1astIn1-3 (alternative splicing variant of CmFTL1, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Transgenic chrysanthemum OX-CmFTL1astIn1-3 lines show advanced flowering time by 2-4 days. In Arabidopsis, 1/15 transformants showed strong recovery (13-18 rosette leaves), 12 moderate (19-24), and 8 weak (>25).
mechanism: Post-transcriptional processing of CmFTL1astIn1-3 generates archetypal CmFTL1 transcript. The AS transcript contains an exon skip but undergoes processing to restore functionality.

genes: RNaseA (RNase A, ribonuclease, Bos taurus)
phenotype: Increased resistance to Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) with suppressed disease symptoms and reduced viral proliferation in transgenic plants
mechanism: Elevated extracellular RNase activity in the apoplast increases non-specific resistance against RNA viruses by potentially hydrolyzing viral genomic RNA or inducing cell death

genes: OsWRKY80 (OsWRKY80, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsWRKY80 in rice plants significantly enhanced disease resistance to R. solani, concomitant with elevated expression of OsWRKY4, another positive regulator in rice defense against R. solani.
mechanism: OsWRKY80 functions upstream of OsWRKY4 as an important positive regulatory circuit that is implicated in rice defense response to sheath blight pathogen R. solani.

genes: OsWRKY80 (OsWRKY80, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Suppression of OsWRKY80 by RNA interference (RNAi), on the other hand, compromised disease resistance to R. solani.
mechanism: OsWRKY80 functions upstream of OsWRKY4 as an important positive regulatory circuit that is implicated in rice defense response to sheath blight pathogen R. solani.

genes: NahG (salicylate hydroxylase, bacterial)
phenotype: NahG tomato plants are hypersusceptible to CEVd and TSWV pathogens
mechanism: NA

genes: H10 heavy chain (H10 heavy chain, antibody heavy chain, H10 antibody), H10 light chain (H10 light chain, antibody light chain, H10 antibody)
phenotype: Overexpression of H10 heavy and light chains increases antibody accumulation in N. benthamiana leaves, with leaf age-dependent yield variation (upper leaves show highest accumulation).
mechanism: Stabilization of H10 antibody against proteolysis by inhibiting endogenous proteases.

genes: SlCYS8 (SlCYS8, cysteine protease inhibitor, tomato), α1-ACT (α1-ACT, cysteine protease inhibitor, human)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlCYS8 increases heavy chain accumulation by ~1.5-fold in upper/middle leaves; α1-ACT reduces heavy chain accumulation by ~50%.
mechanism: Inhibition of endogenous Cys proteases stabilizes H10 heavy chain against degradation.

genes: SlCYS8 Q47P (SlCYS8 Q47P, inactive cysteine protease inhibitor, tomato)
phenotype: Inactive SlCYS8 Q47P variant shows no stabilizing effect on H10 heavy chain accumulation.
mechanism: NA

genes: TOR (target of rapamycin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: TOR inactivation by estradiol-inducible RNAi suppression in tor-es seedlings diminishes sugar-dependent hypocotyl elongation by 61% compared to untreated tor-es plants.
mechanism: TOR plays an essential role in sugar-induced hypocotyl elongation in the dark.

genes: TOR (target of rapamycin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Two independent transgenic RNAi lines (tor 5.2 and tor 6.3) silence TOR expression upon ethanol induction, resulting in short hypocotyls in the dark.
mechanism: TOR silencing suppresses BR-regulated genes and BR-biosynthetic genes, indicating TOR promotes the BR pathway.

genes: BZR1 (Brassinazole-resistant 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)::CFP (Cyan Fluorescent Protein)
phenotype: BZR1-CFP/tor-es plants show estradiol-induced BZR1 protein degradation in the dark.
mechanism: TOR is required for sugar stabilization of BZR1; inactivation of TOR leads to BZR1 degradation via autophagy.

genes: TOR (target of rapamycin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TOR (oxTOR lines 7817 and G548) increases BZR1 accumulation under sugar starvation conditions.
mechanism: TOR overexpression reduces BZR1 degradation, demonstrating TOR sufficiency for sugar stabilization of BZR1.

genes: FZL (FZL, protein in the dynamin superfamily regulating chloroplast morphology and cell death, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of fzl-Ler phenotypes including cell death, high SA accumulation, and elevated PR1 expression in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: FZL functions as a negative regulator of disease resistance to biotrophic pathogens by modulating chloroplast morphology, autophagy, and ROS pathways.

genes: SMG11 (D2, LOC_Os01g10040, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SMG11 increases grain size, grain weight, and grain yield in rice by promoting cell expansion in spikelet hulls.
mechanism: SMG11 promotes cell expansion in spikelet hulls by influencing expression of grain size genes involved in cell expansion regulation.

genes: OsVPE3 (vacuolar processing enzyme 3, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsVPE3 promotes vacuole rupture during salt-induced PCD, leading to increased genomic DNA fragmentation and reduced salt stress tolerance in rice.
mechanism: OsVPE3 localizes to vacuoles and triggers vacuolar membrane collapse, which initiates programmed cell death (PCD) under salt stress.

genes: OsVPE3 (vacuolar processing enzyme 3, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Suppression of OsVPE3 attenuates vacuole rupture during salt-induced PCD, reduces genomic DNA fragmentation, and enhances salt stress tolerance in rice. Suppression also causes decreased leaf width and guard cell length.
mechanism: OsVPE3 regulates vacuole-mediated PCD by maintaining vacuolar membrane integrity under salt stress. Suppression downregulates stomatal development genes (OsTMM, OsSPCH1, OsMUTE), reducing guard cell size.

genes: Rpi-vnt1.1 (resistance to Phytophthora infestans, Solanum venturii)
phenotype: Cisgenic potato line confers resistance to Phytophthora infestans (late blight) without significant impact on nematode community diversity or structure
mechanism: Rpi-vnt1.1 gene from Solanum venturii provides resistance to Phytophthora infestans by conferring pathogen resistance

genes: ZmCHB101 (ZmCHB101, chromatin remodeling subunit, Zea mays)
phenotype: ZmCHB101 knockdown causes leaf rolling toward abaxial surface, erected upper leaves, reduced bulliform cell count (14-17 vs 8-12), sparse tassels with fewer spikelets, smaller/less massive ears, and hyposensitive ABA response in seedling growth and stomatal closure.
mechanism: ZmCHB101 regulates nucleosome density and chromatin structure at target gene loci (e.g., GRMZM2G047065, AC208201.3_FG002) and 45S rDNA clusters. Reduced ZmCHB101 leads to decreased nucleosome occupancy at promoter regions, upregulation of target genes, and chromatin relaxation at 45S rDNA.

genes: PhlD (PhlD, PhlD enzyme from Pseudomonas fluorescens, Pseudomonas fluorescens)
phenotype: Overexpression of PhlD leads to production of phloroglucinol (PG) and its glycosylated form phlorin in Arabidopsis thaliana, with highest accumulation in chloroplastic lines.
mechanism: PhlD catalyzes the biosynthesis of PG from malonyl-CoA, and PG is glycosylated to phlorin by Arabidopsis glycosyltransferases.

genes: PhlDsyn (PhlDsyn, codon-optimized PhlD, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of codon-optimized PhlDsyn leads to production of PG and phlorin in Arabidopsis thaliana, with highest accumulation in chloroplastic lines.
mechanism: PhlDsyn catalyzes the biosynthesis of PG from malonyl-CoA, and PG is glycosylated to phlorin by Arabidopsis glycosyltransferases.

genes: PhlD (PhlD, PhlD enzyme from Pseudomonas fluorescens with AtCpNifS transit peptide, Pseudomonas fluorescens)
phenotype: Overexpression of PhlD with chloroplast targeting sequence leads to production of PG and phlorin in Arabidopsis thaliana, with highest accumulation in chloroplastic lines.
mechanism: PhlD targeted to chloroplasts catalyzes the biosynthesis of PG from malonyl-CoA, and PG is glycosylated to phlorin by Arabidopsis glycosyltransferases.

genes: PhlDsyn (PhlDsyn, codon-optimized PhlD with AtCpNifS transit peptide, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of codon-optimized PhlDsyn with chloroplast targeting sequence leads to production of PG and phlorin in Arabidopsis thaliana, with highest accumulation in chloroplastic lines.
mechanism: PhlDsyn targeted to chloroplasts catalyzes the biosynthesis of PG from malonyl-CoA, and PG is glycosylated to phlorin by Arabidopsis glycosyltransferases.

genes: SlSLD2 (SlSLD2, sphingolipid delta-8 desaturase, Solanum lycopersicum), SlSLD1 (SlSLD1, sphingolipid delta-8 desaturase, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Silencing of SlSLD2 reduces chilling resistance in tomato, as evidenced by increased relative electrolytic leakage (REL), malondialdehyde (MDA) content, and reduced chlorophyll content after chilling treatment.

mechanism: PaNAC03 represses flavonoid biosynthesis pathway genes (CHS, F3'H, PaLAR3) through transcriptional regulation, though transactivation studies showed PaNAC03 activates PaLAR3A promoter in Nicotiana benthamiana, suggesting indirect repression via altered regulatory networks.

genes: ZmPsy (phytoene synthase, Zea mays), CrtI (phytoene desaturase, Erwinia uredevora)
phenotype: Homozygous plants exhibit reduced plant height (47.2 ± 5.5 cm vs. 87.2–91 cm), delayed heading by nine days, incomplete panicle exertion (46.2% enclosed), smaller panicle size (13.9 ± 3.2 cm vs. 25.3–26.2 cm), increased tiller number (2× more), atypical nodal branching, reduced spikelet fertility, and pale green leaves with lower chlorophyll content.
mechanism: Transgene insertion disrupts OsAux1 gene (auxin influx carrier protein), leading to hormonal imbalances (elevated ABA, reduced GA3, altered cytokinin levels) and auxin homeostasis disruption. Leaky expression of endosperm-specific Gt1 promoter in vegetative tissues causes substrate competition among GGPP-dependent pathways (β-carotene, GA, ABA, chlorophyll), further reducing GA levels and altering auxin signaling.

mechanism: The mobile element in the Hd1 promoter of Erythroceros Hokkaido suppresses transcription of Hd1, leading to reduced sensitivity to day length and early flowering.

genes: ENDO2 (endo-1, endonuclease, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ENDO2 with N-terminal His tag and GFP increases nuclease activity in protoplasts, with His tag cleavage observed at 24h post-transformation.
mechanism: ENDO2 undergoes N-terminal cleavage in protoplasts, removing the signal peptide, and is localized to the cytoplasm/ER in healthy cells but associates with fragmented nuclei in senescing cells.

genes: ENDO2 (endo-1, endonuclease, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ENDO2 with C-terminal His tag increases nuclease activity in protoplasts, with no cleavage observed at the C terminus.
mechanism: ENDO2 with C-terminal His tag remains intact in protoplasts, suggesting no cleavage at the C terminus. The protein is localized to the cytoplasm/ER in healthy cells but associates with fragmented nuclei in senescing cells.

genes: ENDO2 (endo-1, endonuclease, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ENDO2 in endo2 mutant protoplasts recovers nuclease activity (N1 and N2 variants) at ~35 kDa, confirming ENDO2 as the source of these activities.
mechanism: ENDO2 is cleaved at its N terminus in protoplasts, generating N1 and N2 variants. N1 is glycosylated and localized to the cytoplasm/ER, while N2 is non-glycosylated and associated with fragmented nuclei in senescing cells.

genes: ENDO2 (endo-1, endonuclease, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ENDO2-GFP is cytoplasmic in healthy protoplasts, co-localized with ER markers, but associates with fragmented nuclei in senescing cells.
mechanism: ENDO2-GFP localizes to the cytoplasm/ER in healthy cells via N-terminal signal peptide cleavage. In senescing cells, it translocates to fragmented nuclei, likely via de-glycosylation and phosphorylation.

genes: Cry51Aa2.834_16 (Cry51Aa2.834_16, insecticidal protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of Cry51Aa2.834_16 in cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) provides high efficacy against Lygus lineolaris, Pseudatomoscelis seriatus, and Frankliniella spp. pests, with 19-fold reduction in large nymphs of L. lineolaris and 3-fold reduction in adults of P. seriatus on transgenic MON 88702 plants compared to non-transgenic DP393 controls.
mechanism: Cry51Aa2.834_16 protein exhibits insecticidal activity against hemipteran pests by disrupting their development and survival, as demonstrated by reduced nymphal populations and delayed development in caged trials.

genes: AtPUB46 (promoter::GUS, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression in vascular systems of leaves, roots, stem-root transition zone, trichomes, and reproductive organs; no staining in root tips or petals/anthers.
mechanism: Promoter activity directs GUS expression in specific tissues.

genes: AtPUB47 (promoter::GUS, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression in vascular systems of leaves, roots, stem-root transition zone, trichomes, and reproductive organs; no staining in root tips or petals/anthers.

phenotype: Expression of AtPUB47::eGFP fusion protein in plants under CaMV 35S promoter.
mechanism: CaMV 35S promoter drives constitutive expression of AtPUB47::eGFP fusion protein.

genes: AtPUB48 (AtPUB48::eGFP, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of AtPUB48::eGFP fusion protein in plants under CaMV 35S promoter.
mechanism: CaMV 35S promoter drives constitutive expression of AtPUB48::eGFP fusion protein.

genes: PIF4 (Arabidopsis thaliana, transcriptional regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PIF4 increases hypocotyl elongation at 20°C and 28°C, which is suppressed by UV-B treatment.
mechanism: PIF4 promotes auxin biosynthesis and signaling, leading to hypocotyl elongation. UV-B suppresses PIF4 activity, reducing auxin-related gene expression.

genes: PIF4 (Arabidopsis thaliana, transcriptional regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Constitutively expressed HA-tagged PIF4 is degraded by UV-B at 20°C but not at 28°C.
mechanism: UV-B induces PIF4 degradation at 20°C, but high temperature protects PIF4 from degradation.

genes: UVR8 (Arabidopsis thaliana, photoreceptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Plants expressing a constitutively dimeric form of UVR8 (GFP-UVR8W285F) show no UV-B-mediated inhibition of thermomorphogenesis.
mechanism: UVR8W285F cannot bind COP1, preventing photomorphogenic signaling required for UV-B inhibition of thermomorphogenesis.

genes: OsPORA (OsPOR, NADPH: protochlorophyllide oxidoreductase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsPORA rescues necrotic lesions and restores chlorophyll synthesis in fgl mutant rice under natural long days and short days, but shows reduced chlorophyll and carotenoid levels under constant light conditions and mild defects in mature leaves during reproductive growth.
mechanism: OsPORA overexpression compensates for OsPORB deficiency by restoring protochlorophyllide conversion, reducing reactive oxygen species accumulation, and recovering chloroplast and etioplast structure during leaf development.

genes: GhPGIP1 (GhPGIP1, polygalacturonase-inhibiting protein 1, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Transgenic Arabidopsis plants overexpressing GhPGIP1 exhibit enhanced resistance to Verticillium dahliae and Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum, with reduced leaf etiolation symptoms and restricted fungal growth at inoculation sites.
mechanism: GhPGIP1 inhibits fungal polygalacturonases (VdPG1 and FovPG1), reducing cell wall degradation and enhancing disease resistance.

genes: GhPGIP1 (GhPGIP1, polygalacturonase-inhibiting protein 1, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: GhPGIP1-silenced cotton plants show increased susceptibility to Verticillium dahliae and Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum, with larger necrotic lesions and thinner cell walls compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: GhPGIP1 silencing reduces inhibition of fungal polygalacturonases, leading to increased cell wall degradation and pathogen susceptibility.

genes: NtabMPO1 (N-methyl putrescine oxidase, Nicotiana tabacum, source)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtabMPO1 increases intracellular nicotine accumulation by ~15-fold in Nicotiana tabacum BY-2 cells after jasmonic acid elicitation.
mechanism: NtabMPO1 catalyzes oxidative deamination of N-methylputrescine to produce nicotine, enhancing nicotine biosynthesis.

genes: BnLATE (Brassica napus LATE, transcription factor, Brassica napus)
phenotype: BnLATE promoter drives GUS expression specifically in silique walls and replum of yellowing siliques in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: NA

genes: SPL9 (SPL9, transcriptional activator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SPL9:GFP-SPL9 plants show increased SPL9 protein levels with age, leading to reduced JA response and insect resistance.
mechanism: SPL9 stabilizes JAZ3 by preventing COI1-mediated degradation, thereby repressing JA signaling.

genes: MIR156 (MIR156, microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S:MIR156 plants exhibit prolonged juvenile stage and enhanced JA response, leading to increased insect resistance.
mechanism: Overexpression of miR156 downregulates SPL genes, which in turn reduces JAZ3 accumulation and enhances JA signaling.

genes: SPL9 (SPL9, miR156-resistant form, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SPL9:rSPL9 plants show accelerated adult traits and reduced JA response, leading to decreased insect resistance.
mechanism: SPL9 interacts with JAZ3 to stabilize it, repressing JA signaling and reducing insect resistance.

genes: JAZ3 (JAZ3, JAZ family protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: JAZ3:JAZ3-FLAG plants exhibit elevated JAZ3 protein levels, leading to reduced JA response and insect resistance.
mechanism: JAZ3 accumulation stabilizes JAZ proteins, repressing JA signaling and reducing insect resistance.

genes: JAZ3 (JAZ3, JAZ family protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S:JAZ3-HA plants show increased JAZ3 protein levels, leading to reduced JA response and insect resistance.
mechanism: Elevated JAZ3 accumulation stabilizes JAZ proteins, repressing JA signaling and reducing insect resistance.

genes: JAZ3 (JAZ3, JAZ family protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S:JAZ3δC-HA plants exhibit JAZ3δC protein levels resistant to MeJA, leading to reduced JA response and insect resistance.
mechanism: JAZ3δC lacks the Jas motif, making it resistant to COI1-mediated degradation, thus repressing JA signaling.

genes: JAZ3 (JAZ3, JAZ family protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S:JAZ3δN-HA plants show JAZ3δN protein levels insensitive to plant age, leading to reduced JA response and insect resistance.
mechanism: JAZ3δN lacks the N-terminal domain, making it insensitive to age-related regulation, thus repressing JA signaling.

genes: SPL9 (SPL9, miR156-resistant form, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SPL9:rSPL9-GR plants show inducible SPL9 expression, leading to reduced JA response and insect resistance upon DEX treatment.
mechanism: SPL9-GR fusion protein translocates to the nucleus upon DEX, interacting with JAZ3 to repress JA signaling.

genes: MsHPPD (MsHPPD, HPPD gene from Medicago sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: Native promoter-driven MsHPPD expression in transgenic Arabidopsis shows tissue-specific activity in cotyledons, roots, and floral organs, with no activity in root tips or hypocotyls.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaFER-5B (ferritin, iron storage protein, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaFER-5B in wheat enhances thermotolerance, reduces electrolyte leakage, and increases Fv/Fm ratio under heat stress.
mechanism: TaFER-5B enhances thermotolerance by scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) and protecting photosynthetic activity.

genes: TaFER-5B (ferritin, iron storage protein, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaFER-5B in Arabidopsis functionally complements the heat stress-sensitive phenotype of ferritin-lacking mutants (fer1-2-3-4 and fer1-3-4).
mechanism: TaFER-5B enhances thermotolerance by scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) and protecting photosynthetic activity.

genes: MtDef4.2 (defensin, Medicago truncatula, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MtDef4.2 in wheat confers resistance to leaf rust (Puccinia triticina) with infection type scores of 0-1 compared to 2-3 in non-transgenic controls
mechanism: Apoplast-targeted MtDEF4.2 permeabilizes fungal plasma membrane, disrupts calcium homeostasis, and interacts with intracellular targets to induce programmed cell death in the pathogen

genes: JcARF19 (JcARF19, auxin response factor, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcARF19 increased seed size and dry seed weight in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: JcARF19 enhances auxin signaling by upregulating downstream genes like LBD18 and LBD29, leading to increased cell number and size.

genes: JcARF19 (JcARF19, auxin response factor, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcARF19 increased seed size, seed dry weight, and oil yield in Jatropha curcas.
mechanism: JcARF19 promotes cell differentiation and increases cell number and length during seed development via auxin signaling pathways involving LBD18, LBD29, and ARGOS.

genes: JcARF19 (JcARF19, auxin response factor, Jatropha curcas)

mechanism: JcARF19 is essential for proper auxin-mediated signaling transduction process in leaf cells of Jatropha.

genes: JcCH42 (JcCH42, subunit of Magnesium (Mg) chelatase, Jatropha curcas)

mechanism: TuVipp1 restores normal chloroplast structure and function, including thylakoid membranes and vesicular transport

genes: TuVipp1 (TuVipp1, chloroplast-targeted protein, Triticum urartu)

genes: T-6b (Agrobacterium tumefaciens T-DNA oncogene, A. tumefaciens, GenBank X56185)

mechanism: T-6b up-regulates endosperm development genes (IKU1, IKU2, MINI3), down-regulates starch synthesis genes (SBE2.1, APS1), and increases sucrose degradation (Sus2, A/N-InvA), while enhancing lipid synthesis genes (WRI1, DGAT1) and reducing mucilage biosynthesis (GLABRA2 repression).

genes: TPI (triose-phosphate isomerase, CBB-cycle, Bienertia sinuspersici)

genes: TPI (triose-phosphate isomerase, CBB-cycle, Bienertia sinuspersici)

genes: PPDK (phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase, C4 cycle, Bienertia sinuspersici)

genes: PtoMYB156 (PtoMYB156, R2R3 MYB transcription factor, Populus tomentosa Carr.)

phenotype: PtoMYB156 knockout in Populus tomentosa Carr. results in ectopic lignin deposition in phloem cells and increased secondary wall thickening in xylem cells.
mechanism: PtoMYB156 knockout abolishes its repression of secondary wall biosynthetic genes, leading to upregulation of lignin, cellulose, and xylan biosynthesis genes.

genes: OsAP2 (Os02g0669100, drought tolerance gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsAP2 increases drought tolerance by 20–35% in Oryza sativa at the vegetative growth stage.
mechanism: NA

genes: PMI (PHOSPHOMANNOSE ISOMERASE, foreign gene, synthetic), ZmUBIQUITIN (ZmUBIQUITIN, constitutive promoter, Zea mays)

genes: PIF4Δb (PIF4Δb, dominant negative variant of PIF4, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: PIF4Δb acts as a dominant negative, downregulating growth-related genes and upregulating defense genes.

genes: PIF4 (PIF4, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: PIF4 upregulates growth-related genes and downregulates defense genes.

genes: GaMYB62L (GaMYB62L, R2R3 MYB transcription factor, Gossypium arboreum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GaMYB62L increases drought tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with 40–60% survival rate after rewatering compared to 20% in wild-type plants, reduced water loss rate (32–28% vs 52% in wild-type), and higher relative water content (80–85% vs 69% in wild-type).
mechanism: GaMYB62L enhances drought tolerance by improving water retention, up-regulating stress-responsive genes (RD22, ADH, RD29A, COR15A), increasing proline content, and reducing stomatal density and aperture size under ABA treatment.

genes: GoGID1 (GoGID1, gibberellin receptor, G. orientalis)
phenotype: Overexpression of GoGID1 increases plant height by 59%–107%, rosette diameter by 43%–82%, and dry weight by 0.96- to 1.68-fold in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GoGID1 enhances GA signaling by interacting with RGA and GAI proteins, leading to increased sensitivity to GA.

genes: GoGID1 (GoGID1, gibberellin receptor, G. orientalis)
phenotype: Overexpression of GoGID1 increases plant height by 0.20- to 0.35-fold and dry weight by 14.9–46.3% in Medicago sativa.
mechanism: GoGID1 enhances GA signaling by interacting with RGA and GAI proteins, leading to increased sensitivity to GA.

genes: OsBT1-3 (plastidic adenine nucleotide uniporter, Oryza sativa, full-length coding sequence)
phenotype: Transient expression of OsBT1-3-YFP fusion protein in rice protoplasts confirmed chloroplast localization of OsBT1-3.
mechanism: OsBT1-3 is localized to chloroplasts and specifically to the chloroplast envelope membrane, where it functions as a membrane-spanning protein involved in adenine nucleotide transport.

genes: Fd-GOGAT (ferredoxin-dependent glutamine synthetase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of the spl32 mutant with pFd-GOGAT rescues the lesion mimic phenotype, restoring normal leaf development and increasing GOGAT activity.
mechanism: Fd-GOGAT is involved in ammonia reassimilation and photorespiration, which affects glutathione synthesis and antioxidant pathways, leading to reduced oxidative stress and enhanced disease resistance.

phenotype: Transgenic tobacco expressing hpaXm showed increased resistance to TMV, with 60.12% reduction in lesion number compared to controls.
mechanism: hpaXm induces defensive responses including micro-HR and enhances resistance to TMV by activating cell death and pathogen-associated molecular pattern (PAMP) signaling.

genes: hpaXmΔLP (N-terminal leader peptide-deleted mutant of hpaXm, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic tobacco expressing hpaXmΔLP showed increased resistance to TMV, with 56.67% reduction in lesion number compared to controls.
mechanism: hpaXmΔLP induces defensive responses including micro-HR and enhances resistance to TMV by activating cell death and PAMP signaling, though it lacks cell wall localization due to signal peptide deletion.

mechanism: PhCESA3 encodes a cellulose synthase catalytic subunit involved in primary cell wall biosynthesis. mechanism: AtFD interacts with Hd3a and RFT1 in rice, potentially affecting cell elongation and developmental processes.

genes: AtFDP (Arabidopsis FD PARALOGUE, Arabidopsis thaliana)

phenotype: Inducible overexpression of CPK31 in cpk31-1 mutant plants reduces As(III) tolerance, with shorter root lengths compared to wild-type when exposed to dexamethasone.
mechanism: CPK31 regulates As(III) uptake through interaction with NIP1;1, potentially activating its transport activity.

mechanism: CPK31 promoter drives GUS expression in root vascular tissues and guard cells, overlapping with NIP1;1 expression patterns.

genes: AKT2 (Arabidopsis thaliana potassium channel, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of AKT2-eGFP under UBI10 promoter results in localization in plasma membrane and ER in Arabidopsis protoplasts and leaves.
mechanism: Physical interaction with MRH1 indicated by FRET and BiFC experiments.

genes: MRH1 (Arabidopsis thaliana receptor-like pseudokinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of MRH1-mRFP under UBI10 promoter results in localization in plasma membrane and ER in Arabidopsis protoplasts and leaves.
mechanism: Physical interaction with AKT2 indicated by FRET and BiFC experiments.

genes: EIN3 (AtEIN3, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of EIN3 improves salt tolerance in root growth and shoot fresh weight in ein3-1 background.
mechanism: EIN3 activates downstream salt-responsive genes like ESE1, which enhances salt tolerance by upregulating stress-responsive gene expression.

genes: SOS2 (AtSOS2, protein kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SOS2 increases plant salt tolerance by enhancing kinase activity.
mechanism: SOS2 activates SOS1, a plasma membrane Na+/H+ antiporter, under salt stress, thereby improving salt tolerance.

genes: EIN3 (AtEIN3, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of EIN3S325A partially rescues ein3-1 salt hypersensitivity.
mechanism: S325 phosphorylation is critical for EIN3's transcriptional activating activity on ESE1, and its mutation reduces this activity.

genes: PLA1 (ZmPLA1, maize CYP78A family member, involved in leaf growth and cell division, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmPLA1 under the UBIL promoter increases leaf blade area by ~15% in Zea mays, resulting in long and broad leaves. Constitutive expression reduces mature cell length (P<0.001) and prevents flowering in transgenic maize.
mechanism: PLA1 stimulates cell division, producing more but smaller cells, extending the duration of cell division.

genes: PLA1 (ZmPLA1, maize CYP78A family member, involved in leaf growth and cell division, Zea mays)
phenotype: Localized overexpression of ZmPLA1 under the GA2ox promoter increases stover biomass, seed yield, and leaf area by 19–20.5% in Zea mays. Transgenic plants are taller, have increased kernel number (7–14%), kernel volume (6–16%), ear length (17–26%), and cob dry weight (18–27%) compared to non-transgenic controls.
mechanism: PLA1 extends the leaf elongation duration (LED) by prolonging the active cell division period. Auxin levels and auxin response markers (DR5rev:mRFPer) are elevated in the basal growth zone of transgenic plants.

genes: MdJAZ2 (Jasmonate ZIM-domain protein 2, repressor of anthocyanin accumulation, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdJAZ2 reduces anthocyanin content by ~50% in apple peel, causing loss of red coloration in 'Red Delicious' fruit.
mechanism: MdJAZ2 represses expression of anthocyanin regulatory genes (MdMYB1, MdMYB9, MdMYB11) and structural genes (MdCHS, MdCHI, etc.), inhibiting anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: MdHIR4 (Hypersensitive Induced Reaction protein 4, repressor of anthocyanin accumulation, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdHIR4 in apple peel reduces anthocyanin content by ~40% and inhibits red coloration in fruit.
mechanism: MdHIR4 stabilizes MdJAZ2 protein, maintaining repression of anthocyanin biosynthesis genes.

mechanism: STF represses cytokinin oxidase/dehydrogenase (CKX) genes, increasing cytokinin levels, which promotes cell proliferation and leaf blade expansion

mechanism: NA

mechanism: NA

genes: MIR396B (miR396b precursor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased susceptibility to P. cucumerina infection in 35Sprom::MIR396B plants
mechanism: miR396 negatively regulates immunity against fungal pathogens by targeting GRF transcription factors

genes: AG (AGAMOUS, transcription factor for stamen and carpel specification, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Homozygous ag plants develop Wild-Type (WT)-like flowers.
mechanism: T-DNA insertion in the second intron disrupts AG function, but suppression in presence of additional T-DNA allows WT phenotype.

genes: LFY (LEAFY, involved in floral meristem development, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Homozygous lfy plants show transformation of flowers into inflorescence shoots, but suppression in presence of additional T-DNA results in WT-like flowers.
mechanism: T-DNA insertion in the second intron disrupts LFY function, but suppression in presence of additional T-DNA allows WT phenotype.

genes: GL2 (GLABRA2, homeodomain protein regulating epidermal cell identity, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: T-DNA insertion in the third intron does not induce suppression, and plants retain the mutant phenotype.
mechanism: T-DNA insertion in the third intron disrupts GL2 function, but suppression is not observed due to exceptionally long intron length.

genes: PdDUF266A (PdDUF266A, cellulose biosynthesis-related, Populus deltoides)
phenotype: Overexpression of PdDUF266A increases glucose and cellulose contents by ~7.6-37.1% and reduces lignin content in Populus deltoides, while also enhancing biomass production.
mechanism: PdDUF266A upregulates cellulose biosynthesis-related genes (CESA, SUSY) in mature leaf and xylem, leading to increased cellulose content and reduced recalcitrance.

genes: Del (Delila, bHLH transcription factor, Antirrhinum majus)
phenotype: Overexpression of Del enhances anthocyanin production in tobacco leaves and flowers, increases antioxidant activity (ABTS/DPPH scavenging), and improves salt/drought stress tolerance with reduced MDA content and stomatal density
mechanism: Del upregulates anthocyanin biosynthetic genes (NtCHS, NtCHI, NtF3H, NtDFR, NtANS) and antioxidant-related genes (NtSOD, NtCAT, NtPOX, NtOsmotin), leading to increased ROS scavenging and stress tolerance

genes: ZDS (zeta-carotene desaturase, Zea mays, Zea mays)
phenotype: ZDS-YFP fusion protein localizes to chloroplasts in maize protoplasts and tobacco leaves
mechanism: ZDS protein is targeted to chloroplasts via a 36-amino acid chloroplast transit peptide

genes: DcMYB6 (carrot MYB6, Daucus carota)
phenotype: Overexpression of DcMYB6 in Arabidopsis induces anthocyanin accumulation, with total anthocyanin content 66-228-fold higher than control plants, and upregulates anthocyanin biosynthetic genes (AtCHS, AtCHI, AtF3H, AtF3′H, AtDFR, AtLDOX, AtUGT78D2).
mechanism: DcMYB6 enhances anthocyanin biosynthesis by upregulating structural genes in the anthocyanin pathway, likely through interaction with bHLH and WD40 proteins to form regulatory complexes.

genes: HsCYP1B1 (HsCYP1B1, human CYP1B1 gene, human)
phenotype: Overexpression of HsCYP1B1 enables bioconversion of trans-resveratrol (t-R) into trans-piceatannol (t-Pn) in tobacco hairy root cultures, with maximum t-Pn production of 7 ± 0.46 mg L−1 in MBCD-treated cultures.
mechanism: HsCYP1B1 catalyzes the hydroxylation of t-R to t-Pn, with MBCD enhancing solubilization and permeabilization of t-R, improving bioconversion efficiency.

genes: VvROMT (VvROMT, Vitis vinifera ROMT gene, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvROMT enables bioconversion of t-R into trans-pterostilbene (t-Pt) in tobacco hairy root cultures, with maximum t-Pt production of 2.6 ± 0.019 μg L−1 in MBCD-treated cultures.
mechanism: VvROMT catalyzes the methylation of t-R to t-Pt, with MBCD enhancing solubilization and permeabilization of t-R, improving bioconversion efficiency.

genes: DXS1 (1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate synthase, Solanum lycopersicum), DXS2 (1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate synthase, Solanum lycopersicum), DXS3 (1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate synthase, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of DXS1 partially rescues the albino phenotype in wls-2297 mutant tomato seedlings, but leaves eventually turn yellow and die.

genes: DXS1 (1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate synthase, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of DXS1 in tomato results in an albino phenotype and arrested development, similar to the wls-2297 mutant.
mechanism: DXS1 gene silencing disrupts isoprenoid biosynthesis, leading to reduced chlorophyll and carotenoid levels.

genes: POX24-Solyc01g067860 (peroxidase, Solanum lycopersicum), POX24-Solyc01g067870 (peroxidase, Solanum lycopersicum), POX27-Solyc01g067880 (peroxidase, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of three POX genes does not produce an albino phenotype, indicating these genes are not responsible for the wls-2297 mutant phenotype.
mechanism: POX gene silencing does not affect isoprenoid biosynthesis or chloroplast development.

mechanism: TALEN-induced indels leading to loss of function of MpNOP1, which is a U-box E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in air chamber formation

genes: BPH26 (Brown planthopper resistance 26, resistance gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Transgenic rice plants expressing BPH26 show resistance to brown planthopper (BPH) with significantly decreased BPH survival rates (~1h phloem ingestion vs 7h in susceptible cultivar) and reduced honeydew excretion compared to vector controls.
mechanism: BPH26 inhibits phloem ingestion by brown planthoppers and increases probing behavior, suggesting it mediates defense in the phloem sieve element against BPH feeding.

genes: CTB4a (LOC_Os04g04330, LRR-RLK, KMXBG)
phenotype: Rescued cold sensitivity of Towada with significantly higher relative seed setting under cold stress (Fig. 2b).
mechanism: CTB4a confers cold tolerance by mediating ATP supply to reinforce pollen fertility at low temperature.

genes: CTB4a (LOC_Os04g04330, LRR-RLK, KMXBG)
phenotype: Stable and enhanced cold tolerance in K-OE1 and K-OE12 lines under CS-DW, CS-PT, and CS-HAA conditions with significantly increased seed setting (Fig. 2c,d).
mechanism: CTB4a overexpression increases ATP synthase activity and ATP content, enhancing pollen fertility and seed setting under cold stress.

genes: CTB4a (LOC_Os04g04330, LRR-RLK, Towada)
phenotype: Enhanced cold tolerance in T-OE3 and T-OE14 lines with significantly increased seed setting, showing little difference from K-OE lines (Fig. 2c).
mechanism: CTB4a overexpression increases ATP synthase activity and ATP content, enhancing pollen fertility and seed setting under cold stress.

genes: CTB4a (LOC_Os04g04330, LRR-RLK)

mechanism: Downregulation of CTB4a reduces ATP synthase activity and ATP content, impairing pollen fertility and seed setting under cold stress.

genes: CTB4a (LOC_Os04g04330, LRR-RLK)

mechanism: CTB4a promoter from Towada drives lower GUS expression under cold stress, indicating promoter activity differences.

mechanism: CTB4a-GFP fusion protein localizes to cell surface and chloroplasts, suggesting roles in membrane and chloroplast-associated processes.

genes: TaHSP70 (heat shock protein 70, Triticum aestivum), NbHSP70 (heat shock protein 70, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaHSP70 increases CWMV genomic RNA accumulation in N. benthamiana by ~30-fold compared to control plants.
mechanism: TaHSP70 interacts with the N-terminal region (aa 1–670) of CWMV replicase, recruiting it to intracellular membranes for viral RNA replication.

genes: NbHSP70 (heat shock protein 70, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of NbHSP70 increases CWMV genomic RNA accumulation in N. benthamiana compared to control plants.
mechanism: NbHSP70 interacts with the N-terminal region (aa 1–670) of CWMV replicase, recruiting it to intracellular membranes for viral RNA replication.

genes: TaHSP70 (heat shock protein 70, Triticum aestivum), NbHSP70 (heat shock protein 70, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Silencing of NbHSP70 reduces CWMV RNA accumulation in N. benthamiana by ~70% compared to control plants.
mechanism: NbHSP70 is required for CWMV replicase interaction and membrane recruitment during viral RNA replication.

genes: TaHSP70 (heat shock protein 70, Triticum aestivum), NbHSP70 (heat shock protein 70, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: GFP-fused TaHSP70 and NbHSP70 localize to cytoplasmic granules in CWMV-infected N. benthamiana cells, unlike their uniform cytoplasmic/nuclear distribution in healthy cells.
mechanism: CWMV replicase modifies subcellular distribution of HSP70 by recruiting it to cytoplasmic granules via interaction with the N-terminal region (aa 1–670) of the replicase.

genes: H (heavy chain of hybrid-IgG/IgA, mouse), L (light chain of hybrid-IgG/IgA, mouse), J (joining chain, mouse), SC (secretory component, mouse)
phenotype: Transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana produces secretory hybrid-IgG/IgA (S-hyIgA) specific for Stx1, with 8.0 μg/g leaf tissue of assembled hybrid-IgG/IgA and 57.7 μg/g leaf tissue of total SC. S-hyIgA neutralizes Stx1 cytotoxicity in human colon epithelial cells and Vero cells.
mechanism: S-hyIgA binds to Stx1B and neutralizes its cytotoxicity by preventing DNA fragmentation and cell death in target cells.

genes: SlMAPKKKα (SlMAPKKKα, kinase domain of SlMAPKKKα, Solanum lycopersicum, cloned into pER8 with N-terminal HA tag)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlMAPKKKα induces programmed cell death (PCD) in tomato and N. benthamiana leaves within 36–48 h of β-estradiol application.
mechanism: Phosphorylation at Ser360 and Ser364 of SlMAPKKKα is required for PCD induction. Mutation of these residues to alanine abolishes PCD, suggesting these sites are critical for kinase activity and downstream signaling.

genes: SlMAPKKKα (K231M, kinase-inactive mutant, Solanum lycopersicum, cloned into pER8 with N-terminal HA tag)
phenotype: Overexpression of the kinase-inactive SlMAPKKKα (K231M) variant does not induce PCD in tomato or N. benthamiana leaves, serving as a negative control.
mechanism: The K231M mutation in the ATP-binding site of SlMAPKKKα renders it kinase-inactive, preventing phosphorylation of downstream targets and PCD induction.

genes: SlMAPKKKα (T353A, threonine-to-alanine mutant, Solanum lycopersicum, cloned into pER8 with N-terminal HA tag)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlMAPKKKα (T353A) induces PCD in tomato and N. benthamiana leaves, similar to wild-type SlMAPKKKα.
mechanism: Thr353 is not essential for PCD induction, as the T353A mutation does not abolish kinase activity or downstream signaling.

genes: SlMAPKKKα (S360A, serine-to-alanine mutant, Solanum lycopersicum, cloned into pER8 with N-terminal HA tag)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlMAPKKKα (S360A) does not induce PCD in tomato or N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: Mutation of Ser360 to alanine prevents phosphorylation at this site, which is critical for PCD induction and kinase activity.

genes: SlMAPKKKα (S364A, serine-to-alanine mutant, Solanum lycopersicum, cloned into pER8 with N-terminal HA tag)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlMAPKKKα (S364A) does not induce PCD in tomato or N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: Mutation of Ser364 to alanine prevents phosphorylation at this site, which is critical for PCD induction and kinase activity.

genes: CaWRKYa (WRKY transcription factor, pathogen resistance, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Silencing of CaWRKYa reduces HR cell death by ~40% and ion conductivity by ~30% in TMV-P0-infected hot pepper plants, leading to systemic TMV-P0 infection.
mechanism: CaWRKYa positively regulates PR genes (CaPR1, 2, 4, 5, 10) and plant hormone-related genes (CaICS1, NDR1, CaLOX2) to mediate L-mediated resistance against TMV-P0.

genes: CaWRKYa (WRKY transcription factor, pathogen resistance, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CaWRKYa increases CaPR10 promoter activity by ~37% in tobacco leaves.
mechanism: CaWRKYa binds to W-box motifs in CaPR10 promoter and activates its transcription.

genes: CaMK1 (mitogen-activated protein kinase, Capsicum annuum), CaMK2 (mitogen-activated protein kinase, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Co-expression of CaMK1 and CaWRKYa in hot pepper protoplasts results in nuclear-localized YFP fluorescence, confirming physical interaction.
mechanism: CaMK1 and CaMK2 phosphorylate SP clusters of CaWRKYa, enhancing its DNA binding affinity to W-box motifs.

genes: CaPR10 (pathogenesis-related gene, Capsicum annuum)

mechanism: Synergistic overexpression of AACT and HMGR enhances flux through the MVA pathway, increasing precursor availability for squalene and sterol biosynthesis.

mechanism: RICE1 and RICE2 positively regulate miRNA accumulation in vivo by maintaining functional RISC complexes.

genes: PDH45 (PDH45, DNA helicase involved in abiotic stress tolerance, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Overexpression of PDH45 increases plant height, biomass, and yield by 15-58% in Capsicum annuum under non-stress conditions. Transgenic plants show improved root length (1.3-2.0 cm/seedling vs 0.2 cm/seedling in WT), shoot length, root volume, and leaf area. Under stress conditions (PEG6000, NaCl, methyl viologen), transgenic plants maintain higher root length (0.8-1.2 cm/seedling vs 0.2 cm/seedling in WT), fresh weight (0.25-0.31 g/seedling vs 0.14 g/seedling in WT), and chlorophyll stability. Yield per plant ranges from 192-289 g/plant vs 154 g/plant in WT.
mechanism: PDH45 enhances abiotic stress tolerance by modulating stress-responsive genes (SOD, RD29A, LEA), improving photosynthetic efficiency (26.7-31.4 µmol CO2 m−2 s−1 vs 28.0 µmol CO2 m−2 s−1 in WT), and maintaining membrane integrity (31-91% lower membrane leakage vs 83-95% in WT). Increased SOD activity (67-75% inhibition of NBT reduction vs 56% in WT) and lower carbon isotope discrimination (Δ13C) indicate improved water use efficiency.

mechanism: CsERF004 up-regulates CsPR1 and CsPR4 genes, increases salicylic acid (SA) and ethylene (ET) levels, which enhance resistance to P. cubensis and C. cassiicola through SA- and ET-dependent pathways

genes: BAF60 (BAF60, SWI/SNF chromatin remodeler subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: BAF60 overexpression represses hypocotyl elongation by modulating DNA accessibility of hypocotyl cell size regulatory genes, antagonizing the promoting effect of PIF4.

genes: BAF60 (BAF60, SWI/SNF chromatin remodeler subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The BAF60 promoter drives higher GFP expression under light conditions compared to dark conditions, indicating light-regulated transcriptional activity.
mechanism: BAF60 promoter activity is regulated by light and the circadian clock, with increased transcriptional activity in light conditions.

mechanism: McTPS1 catalyzes the production of (R)-linalool from geranyl diphosphate, identified as the major monoterpene in champak flowers.

genes: LUC (luciferase, reporter gene, synthetic)

mechanism: The pPtaLHY2 promoter drives luciferase expression in a circadian rhythm, enabling real-time monitoring of gene transcription.

genes: SMU1 (SMU1, WD40 repeat-containing protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Complementation of the mutant phenotype by reintroducing the wild-type SMFa gene under its endogenous regulatory sequences.

phenotype: Transient expression of ClMKK2-2 in Nicotiana benthamiana led to increased susceptibility to Botrytis cinerea.
mechanism: ClMKK2-2 negatively regulates resistance to B. cinerea by downregulating defense-related gene expression.

mechanism: ClMPK7 functions as a regulator of HR-like cell death through modulating the generation of H2O2.

mechanism: Promoter-driven expression of GUS reporter gene in specific tissues (root for Os1-CysPrxB, endosperm for Os1-CysPrxA).

mechanism: CHIQ1 interacts with CHIQL6 and EMF2 subunit of PRC2 to regulate organ size through transcriptional mechanisms involving histone modification.

mechanism: CHIQ1 is expressed in dividing and expanding tissues, suggesting a role in organ growth regulation.

mechanism: GAL4BD-fused regulators bind to UAS promoter driving GUS expression, with P19 suppressing RNA silencing to enhance transactivation.

mechanism: β-1,3-glucanase cleaves β-1,3-glycosidic bonds in C. falcatum hyphal cell walls, causing hyphal lysis. Active site residues Glutamate 628 (proton donor) and Aspartate 569 (nucleophile) mediate this antifungal activity.

genes: PgCPT1 (gene, cis-prenyltransferase, Panax ginseng)
phenotype: Overexpression of PgCPT1 did not show any plant growth defect in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: PgCPT1 requires an accessory component for proper function

mechanism: HyPer2 is a ratiometric H2O2 sensor that undergoes oxidation-dependent conformational changes, altering its fluorescence emission ratio when excited at 488 nm vs. 405 nm.

mechanism: sAPX catalyzes the reduction of H2O2 using ascorbate as a reductant, decreasing H2O2 levels and thus reducing HyPer2 oxidation.

mechanism: HyPer2 reports H2O2 via oxidation-dependent fluorescence changes (F488/405), while pHRed reports pH via ratiometric fluorescence changes (F543/458).

genes: HD1 (human dopamine receptor, Homo sapiens)

mechanism: HD1 activates catecholamine cAMP signaling pathway, altering carbon metabolism by inhibiting starch synthesis (AGPase, SuSy, PGM activities reduced) and enhancing sucrose synthesis (SPS activity increased). Catecholamine levels (dopamine, norepinephrine, normetanephrine) are increased 2-4 fold.

mechanism: ScPDR5 transporter extrudes herbicides and xenobiotics from plant cells, reducing their toxicity.

mechanism: AUX1-mediated IAA influx is required for IBA-induced AR formation

phenotype: LAX3 expression is induced by IBA during adventitious rooting in Arabidopsis TCLs
mechanism: LAX3-mediated IAA influx is required for IBA-induced AR formation

genes: DEK1 (DEK1, calpain domain, Physcomitrella patens)
