mechanism: Retention of the hybrid intron 17/23 in the DEK1 transcript introduces a premature stop codon, causing a frame-shift mutation and a null mutant phenotype.

genes: DEK1 (DEK1, calpain domain, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: Overexpression of DEK1 knockout leads to filamentous growth and lack of gametophores in Physcomitrella patens.
mechanism: Splicing of the mutagenized, loxP-harboring DEK1 intron 17 of the dek1ΔlinkerG2/cre mutant occurred properly, resulting in an in-frame deletion of the Linker segment.

genes: DEK1 (DEK1, LG3 domain, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: Knock-in of DEK1-LG3 sequences into the dek1Δlg3 mutant results in filamentous growth without gametophores due to splicing defects.
mechanism: Retention of the loxP-harboring intron 23 in the DEK1 transcript caused a frame-shift mutation leading to a premature termination codon and a putative truncated DEK1 protein lacking the catalytic calpain domain.

genes: DEK1 (DEK1, LG3 domain, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: Knock-in of DEK1-LG3 sequences into the dek1Δlg3 mutant results in well-developed gametophores, demonstrating successful complementation.
mechanism: In-frame fusion of exon 23 and exon 24 in the DEK1 transcript, with proper splicing at the locus, leading to functional DEK1 calpain activity.

genes: hTPC2 (human TPC2 channel, fused to EGFP, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of hTPC2-EGFP in Arabidopsis thaliana protoplasts allows functional characterization of the human TPC2 channel via patch-clamp recordings.
mechanism: NA

genes: hTPC1 (human TPC1 channel, fused to EGFP, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of hTPC1-EGFP in Arabidopsis thaliana protoplasts enables functional analysis of the human TPC1 channel using patch-clamp techniques.
mechanism: NA

genes: SmMYB36 (R2R3-MYB transcription factor, from Salvia miltiorrhiza, NCBI KF059390.1)
phenotype: Overexpression of SmMYB36 increases tanshinone biosynthesis (dihydrotanshinone I, cryptotanshinone, tanshinone I, tanshinone II A) by ~2-4-fold while decreasing phenolic acids (rosmarinic acid, salvianolic acid B) and flavonoids by ~40-60% in Salvia miltiorrhiza hairy roots
mechanism: SmMYB36 binds MYB-binding elements in promoters of metabolic pathway genes, represses phenylpropanoid pathway genes (PAL1, 4CL2, TAT1) and activates MEP pathway genes (DXS1, DXR, MCT), shifting metabolic flux from phenolic acid to tanshinone biosynthesis

genes: KTN1 (KTN1, kinesin-like protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of ktn1-6 mutant restores wild-type conical cell shape.
mechanism: KTN1 promotes tip sharpening of conical cells during late development stages by regulating microtubule organization.

genes: CTB (CTB, cholera toxin B subunit, Vibrio cholerae)
phenotype: CTB is expressed in the endosperm and endogenous storage proteins are down-regulated in MR-CTB51A.
mechanism: CTB expression in the endosperm affects metabolic pathways, leading to altered amino acid, lipid, and γ-oryzanol levels.

genes: DOG1 (DOG1, dormancy regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the dog1-1 non-dormant phenotype, with dormancy levels correlating with YFP-DOG1 protein accumulation. Seeds from the dormant NIL DOG1 and complemented lines fully germinate on ABA biosynthesis inhibitor fluridone.
mechanism: DOG1 forms complexes with protein phosphatases (RDO5, AHG1, AHG3, PDF1) in seeds, influencing dormancy through interactions with ABA signaling pathway components. DOG1 suppresses the action of AHG1 and AHG3 in dormancy release.

genes: OsMPH1 (MYB-like gene of plant height 1, Oryza sativa japonica)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsMPH1 increases plant height by ~41.3-44.8% in Oryza sativa japonica.
mechanism: OsMPH1 regulates plant height by altering internode cell length.

genes: OsMPH1 (MYB-like gene of plant height 1, Oryza sativa japonica)
phenotype: Knockdown of OsMPH1 decreases plant height in Oryza sativa japonica.
mechanism: OsMPH1 regulates plant height by altering internode cell length.

genes: ISA1 (ISA1, isoamylase, Solanum tuberosum), ISA2 (ISA2, isoamylase, Solanum tuberosum), ISA3 (ISA3, isoamylase, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Silencing of ISA1, ISA2, and ISA3 significantly reduces tuber starch content by 50% in line 39, increases sucrose content, and induces early sprouting (3 weeks earlier than wild type) with 3-10× higher soluble glucan levels in transgenic potato tubers
mechanism: Reduced ISA1/ISA2 activity impairs starch granule formation, leading to smaller granules with increased surface area for degradation. This results in elevated sucrose levels that promote early sprouting. Altered starch structure (increased soluble glucans with lower degree of polymerization) may enhance accessibility to degrading enzymes

genes: PYR1 (PYR/PYL family member, ABA receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana), PYL1 (PYR/PYL family member, ABA receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana), PYL2 (PYR/PYL family member, ABA receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana), PYL4 (PYR/PYL family member, ABA receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana), PYL5 (PYR/PYL family member, ABA receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana), PYL8 (PYR/PYL family member, ABA receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Generation of homozygous sextuple pyl1pyl2pyl4pyl5pyl8pyr1 mutants with ABA-insensitive root elongation and reduced fresh weight compared to wild type
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in six PYR/PYL ABA receptor genes disrupt ABA signaling pathway

genes: FBS1 (F-BOX STRESS INDUCED 1, transcriptional regulator of stress responses, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Loss of FBS1 function leads to altered expression of stress response genes, including reduced expression of jasmonic acid (JA) biosynthesis genes and increased expression of ABA-related lipid transfer protein (LTP) genes under chilling stress
mechanism: FBS1 regulates stress hormone pathways by modulating JA and ABA gene networks, including repression of type I LTP genes which influence ABA biosynthesis and stress responses

genes: At5g23960 (β-caryophyllene synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of At5g23960 increases β-caryophyllene emission by three orders of magnitude in Arabidopsis thaliana, making the plant repellent to D. citri.
mechanism: β-caryophyllene acts as a repellent to D. citri by interfering with the insect's ability to locate citrus hosts.

genes: At5g23960 (β-caryophyllene synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knockout of At5g23960 in Arabidopsis thaliana results in no β-caryophyllene production, with no repellent effect on D. citri.
mechanism: NA

genes: ATeam1.03-nD/nA (ATP sensor, synthetic), TkTp (transketolase target peptide, Nicotiana tabacum), β-ATPase (Nicotiana plumbaginifolia)
phenotype: Cytosolic and plastidic lines showed wild-type-like whole-plant phenotypes (root length, rosette size, inflorescence height, siliques). Mitochondrial lines showed weaker fluorescence and strong developmental phenotype with abnormal mitochondrial organization.
mechanism: ATeam1.03-nD/nA is an ATP-binding Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) sensor that reports MgATP2- concentrations via ratiometric Venus/CFP fluorescence. Cytosolic and plastidic sensors localized to their target compartments without disrupting normal plant development.

genes: MdMYB10 (MdMYB10, transcription factor, Malus sieversii), GFP43 (GFP43, codon-optimized green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdMYB10/GFP43 fusion gene results in strong red coloration of all plant organs (leaves, stems, petals, sepals, stamens, carpels) in transgenic Fragaria vesca L. plants.
mechanism: MdMYB10 enhances anthocyanin biosynthesis by activating flavonoid pathway genes, leading to visible red pigmentation.

genes: MdMYB10 (MdMYB10, transcription factor, Malus sieversii), GFP43 (GFP43, codon-optimized green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdMYB10/GFP43 fusion gene under F3′H promoter results in faint red coloration in specific tissues (petal base, stigmas, young flower buds) but no significant coloration in leaves or stems in transgenic Fragaria vesca L. plants.
mechanism: F3′H promoter drives tissue-specific expression of MdMYB10/GFP43, leading to localized anthocyanin accumulation in floral organs.

genes: BIL4 (BIL4, BRI1 receptor interacting protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: BIL4 overexpression increases hypocotyl elongation in dark-grown seedlings and promotes cell elongation in hypocotyls and leaf epidermal cells.
mechanism: BIL4 positively regulates BR signaling by enhancing BRI1 trafficking and stabilizing BRI1 protein levels.

genes: BIL4 (BIL4, BRI1 receptor interacting protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: BIL4-RNAi plants exhibit shorter hypocotyls, reduced inflorescence length, and smaller leaf epidermal cells compared to wild-type.
mechanism: BIL4 knockdown inhibits BR signaling by reducing BRI1 endosomal localization and increasing vacuolar trafficking of BRI1.

genes: BIL4 (BIL4 promoter activity reporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: BIL4 promoter::GUS expression is detected in root apical meristems, hypocotyls during dark-grown germination, and young rosette leaves.
mechanism: NA

genes: BIL4 (BIL4, BRI1 receptor interacting protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: BIL4-GFP localizes to TGN/EE, LE/MVB, and vacuolar membranes in root cells and interacts with BRI1 in endosomes.
mechanism: BIL4 localizes to endomembrane compartments and interacts with BRI1 to regulate its trafficking and stability.

genes: BIL4 (BIL4, BRI1 receptor interacting protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S::BIL4-GFP transgenic plants exhibit longer hypocotyls in dark-grown seedlings and functional BIL4-GFP localization to vacuolar membranes.
mechanism: BIL4-GFP under 35S promoter enhances cell elongation and interacts with BRI1 in endosomes.

genes: 3α-HSD (3α-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase/carbonyl reductase, Comamonas testosteroni)
phenotype: Exogenous 3α-HSD expression causes outward rolled leaf trait in transgenic rice mutants
mechanism: The 3α-HSD enzyme degrades steroid compounds in environmental contaminants, and T-DNA insertion at chromosome 9 long arm (non-gene region) inhibits nearby gene expression, leading to increased bulliform cells in upper epidermis and leaf rolling

genes: SlPRE2 (SlPRE2, atypical bHLH transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlPRE2 causes leaf rolling, increased internode length, reduced chlorophyll content in leaves and fruits, and decreased carotenoid accumulation in fruits in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: SlPRE2 represses chlorophyll and carotenoid accumulation by down-regulating GLK2, RbcS, Cab7, HY5, PSY1, PDS, and ZDS genes involved in chlorophyll metabolism and carotenoid biosynthesis.

genes: GNS4 (LOC_Os04g39430, cytochrome P450 protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of gns4 mutant phenotypes, including increased grain number per panicle (86.4% of WT) and 1000-grain weight (9.4% lower in gns4) in transgenic plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: GNS4 (LOC_Os04g39430, cytochrome P450 protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi lines (RNAi1 and RNAi2) displayed semi-dwarf stature, 10.3-11.1% fewer grains per panicle, and 7.8-11.1% lower 1000-grain weight compared to Nipponbare (NIP).
mechanism: Down-regulation of GNS4 reduces BR synthesis and signaling, leading to smaller grains and reduced panicle size.

genes: GNS4 (LOC_Os04g39430, cytochrome P450 protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression lines (OE1 and OE2) showed 16.8-15.7% increased grain yield per plant, 5.9-7.9% higher 1000-grain weight, and 10.4-6.8% more grains per panicle compared to Nipponbare (NIP) and Wuyunjing7 (WYJ7) backgrounds.
mechanism: Elevated GNS4 expression enhances BR synthesis and signaling, promoting cell elongation and increasing grain size and number.

genes: OsBEIIa (Starch branching enzyme IIa, Oryza sativa), OsISA1 (Isoamylase1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated knockdown of OsBEIIa and OsISA1 in transgenic rice plants showed co-segregation of phenotype, genotype, and RNA expression in the OsBEIIa-RNAi-4/sug-h F2 population, indicating their association with the sug-h phenotype.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsBEIIa (Starch branching enzyme IIa, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsBEIIa in sug-h mutant rice resulted in grains that were less wrinkled compared to the sug-h mutant, with increased OsBEIIa transcript levels in transgenic T1 plants.
mechanism: OsBEIIa overexpression likely restores normal starch biosynthesis by modulating amylopectin structure, reducing the severity of the sugary phenotype caused by OsISA1 mutation.

genes: dep (LOC_Os05g2730, WUSCHEL-related homeobox 3B protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Restoration of bristle type trichomes on leaf blade and glumes in glabrous rice.
mechanism: dep encodes a WUSCHEL-related homeobox 3B protein involved in trichome formation.

genes: dep (LOC_Os05g2730, WUSCHEL-related homeobox 3B protein, Oryza sativa), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Localization of dep in the nucleus in onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: dep localizes in the nucleus, indicating its function as a transcription factor.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Spatial expression of dep in shoot base, lateral roots, leaf sheath, nodes, and mid-vein of rice.
mechanism: dep promoter activity detected in developing tissues, indicating its role in trichome formation.

genes: OsWOX3B (trichome development gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Trichome deficiency in RNAi lines was associated with increased efficiency of grain packaging but did not affect main agronomic traits.
mechanism: OsWOX3B is responsible for trichome development; RNAi suppression leads to glabrous phenotype.

genes: OsWOX3B (trichome development gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation transgenic lines showed pubescent trichomes on leaves, indicating OsWOX3B's role in trichome development.
mechanism: OsWOX3B expression restores trichome development in glabrous HMK rice.

genes: NbUBC9 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbUBC10 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbUBC11 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbUBC12 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbUBC30 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbUBC39 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Knockdown of twelve group III E2 genes results in slower plant growth, crinkled leaves, reduced ROS production, downregulated NbRbohB gene expression, and diminished suppression of immunity-associated PCD by AvrPtoB.
mechanism: RNA interference (RNAi) via virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) using TRV-based vector with chimeric DNA fragments.

genes: NbUBC12 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbUBC10 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbUBC28 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbUBC31 (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Specific and efficient knockdown of four group III E2 genes (NbUBC12, 10, 28, 31) without significant effects on flg22-induced ROS production or plant development.
mechanism: RNA interference (RNAi) via virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) using TRV-based vector with optimized gene fragments containing at least 3 nt mismatches in any 21-bp stretch to avoid off-target silencing.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under the ORB1 promoter reveals tissue-specific expression patterns in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NA

genes: PtFLA6 (promoter region, ~1.5 kb, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: PtFLA6 promoter activity is mainly activated in tension wood (TW) tissues during mechanical stress-induced TW formation.
mechanism: NA

genes: PtFLA6 (antisense construct, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Antisense expression of PtFLA6 inhibits tension wood (TW) formation, reduces TW-to-xylem area ratio by ~40-80%, and increases abnormal G-fibers with thin G-layers.
mechanism: PtFLAs play important roles in TW formation and differentiation by regulating G-layer biosynthesis in differentiating G-fibers.

genes: A1 (A1, anthocyanin biosynthesis, Zea mays), nptII (nptII, neomycin phosphotransferase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Expression of maize A1 and nptII genes results in orange petunia flowers containing pelargonidin as the main anthocyanidin.
mechanism: The maize A1 gene encodes an anthocyanin biosynthesis enzyme that directs pelargonidin production, while nptII serves as a selectable marker for transgenic plants.

genes: ACS2 (ACC-synthase 2, silenced, Ohio8245)
phenotype: Ethylene-deficient tomato line (ACS2-AS) shows suppressed SlHSP gene transcripts compared to wild type
mechanism: Antisense silencing of ACS2 reduces ethylene production, which in turn suppresses class-I SlHSP gene transcripts during fruit ripening

genes: ESC (ESC, S/MAR-binding protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: ESC binds to the YUC9 promoter and recruits the SWR1 complex to exchange H2A.Z, repressing YUC9 expression and suppressing hypocotyl elongation in light.

genes: SOB3 (SOB3, S/MAR-binding protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: SOB3 binds to the YUC9 promoter and recruits the SWR1 complex to exchange H2A.Z, repressing YUC9 expression and suppressing hypocotyl elongation in light.

genes: SEF (SEF, SWR1 complex component, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: SEF binds to the YUC9 promoter and recruits the SWR1 complex to exchange H2A.Z, repressing YUC9 expression and suppressing hypocotyl elongation in light.

genes: DR5 (synthetic auxin-responsive promoter, synthetic)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: The DR5 promoter drives GUS expression in response to auxin signaling, used to visualize auxin activity in wild-type and sob3-6 mutants.

genes: OsFH15 (OsFH15, formin gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of OsFH15 decreases grain length (3.28%), grain width (6.64%), grain thickness (7.91%), and 1,000-grain weight (20.95%) in rice.
mechanism: OsFH15 regulates grain size by controlling cell size through actin filament (AF) and microtubule (MT) organization.

genes: OsFH15 (OsFH15, formin gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsFH15 increases grain length (2.87%), grain width (4.21%), grain thickness (2.93%), and 1,000-grain weight (8.09%) in rice.
mechanism: OsFH15 regulates grain size by controlling cell size through actin filament (AF) and microtubule (MT) organization.

genes: OsFH15 (OsFH15, formin gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi of OsFH15 decreases grain length (2.48%), grain width (4.80%), grain thickness (6.16%), and 1,000-grain weight (9.78%) in rice.
mechanism: OsFH15 regulates grain size by controlling cell size through actin filament (AF) and microtubule (MT) organization.

genes: CsTIR1 (Cucumis sativus TIR1-like auxin receptor, cucumber, Cucumis sativus), CsAFB2 (Cucumis sativus AFB2-like auxin receptor, cucumber, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsTIR1 and CsAFB2 in tomato plants causes pleiotropic phenotypes including compact stature, leaf abnormalities (inward curling, convex leaf surface, reduced stomata), reduced seed size and germination rate, parthenocarpic fruit set, and altered fruit shape (elongated in CsAFB2-OE lines).
mechanism: CsTIR1 and CsAFB2 overexpression disrupts auxin signaling by altering expression of auxin response genes (e.g., upregulation of SlARF10, downregulation of SlSPCH/SlMUTE in CsTIR1-OE lines; upregulation of SlSPCH/SlMUTE in CsAFB2-OE lines), affecting leaf morphogenesis, stomata differentiation, and fruit development.

genes: atFT (FLOWERING LOCUS T, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of Arabidopsis FT in cassava reduces time to flowering by ~45% (from 120 to 75 days after transplanting), increases lateral branching by 7-11 branches per plant, and enhances flower prolificacy with 33-77 flowers per plant compared to aborted flowers in controls
mechanism: FT enhances floral initiation and branching by altering meristem activity and apical dominance

genes: ORF1 (OsCNGC13, gene encoding cyclic nucleotide-gated channel 13, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Reduced seed-setting rate (37.8–51.9%) and decreased ovule pollen tube percentage (38.7–50.0%)
mechanism: OsCNGC13 is required for normal pollen tube growth and seed-setting rate

genes: ORF3 (uncharacterized expressed protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: No effect on seed-setting rate
mechanism: ORF3 is not required for pollen tube growth or seed-setting rate

genes: ORF1 (OsCNGC13-D, chimeric gene with premature termination, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Reduced seed-setting rate and decreased ovule pollen tube percentage
mechanism: OsCNGC13-D suppresses OsCNGC13 expression, leading to haploinsufficiency

genes: ORF1 (OsCNGC13, gene encoding cyclic nucleotide-gated channel 13, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Reduced seed-setting rate and decreased ovule pollen tube percentage
mechanism: OsCNGC13 is required for normal pollen tube growth and seed-setting rate

genes: epsps (glyphosate-resistant 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of epsps increases tiller number by 19-49%, advances flowering by 3-15 days, and raises seed set ratios by 29-30% in transgenic rice-wild rice hybrids compared to non-transgenic controls
mechanism: Overexpressed EPSPS enhances shikimate pathway activity, increasing aromatic amino acids and secondary metabolites which promote tillering, flowering, and seed production. Higher EPSPS levels also improve glyphosate resistance and cold tolerance

genes: PaCRTI (phytoene carotene isomerase, from Pisum sativum), ZmPSY (phytoene synthase, from Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of PaCRTI and ZmPSY increases β-carotene content in rice endosperm by 1.57–2.69 μg/g DW, while iron content ranges from 6.1–9.1 μg/g DW in CP lines compared to 5.9 μg/g DW in control NFP.
mechanism: PaCRTI and ZmPSY enhance β-carotene synthesis in endosperm by converting phytoene to β-carotene. AtNAS1 increases nicotianamine and deoxymugineic acid production, facilitating iron and zinc uptake and translocation.

genes: PvFERRITIN (ferritin, from Phaseolus vulgaris), AtNAS1 (nicotianamine synthase, from Arabidopsis thaliana), ZmPSY (phytoene synthase, from Zea mays), PaCRTI (phytoene carotene isomerase, from Pisum sativum)
phenotype: Overexpression of PvFERRITIN, AtNAS1, ZmPSY, and PaCRTI increases iron content up to 6.02 μg/g DW (3.3-fold over control), zinc up to 29.7 μg/g DW (1.28-fold), and β-carotene up to 3.4 μg/g DW in NFCP lines compared to Nipponbare control.
mechanism: PvFERRITIN stores iron in endosperm. AtNAS1 enhances nicotianamine and deoxymugineic acid production for iron/zinc uptake. ZmPSY and PaCRTI synthesize β-carotene from phytoene. Combined activity results in multi-nutrient enrichment.

genes: C3′H (p-coumaroyl shikimate 3′-hydroxylase, lignin synthesis, Populus alba × Populus tremula)
phenotype: Reduced lignin (S and G content) in Populus alba × Populus tremula
mechanism: C3′H catalyzes the synthesis of monolignols, and its knockdown reduces lignin content.

genes: COMT (caffeic acid o-methyltransferase, lignin composition, Populus alba × Populus tremula)
phenotype: Altered S:G ratio (low S) in Populus alba × Populus tremula
mechanism: COMT catalyzes the synthesis of monolignols, and its knockdown reduces syringyl (S) lignin subunit content.

genes: RNA1 (genomic RNA1 of Cucumber Mosaic Virus Fny strain, viral RNA, Cucumovirus), RNA2 (genomic RNA2 of Cucumber Mosaic Virus Fny strain, viral RNA, Cucumovirus), RNA3 (genomic RNA3 of Cucumber Mosaic Virus Fny strain, viral RNA, Cucumovirus)
phenotype: Overexpression of CMV genomic RNAs induces mosaic symptoms in N. benthamiana leaves, with CMVRA causing severe leaf distortion, stunting, and loss of apical dominance compared to CMVWT.
mechanism: CMV CP RNA binding activity inhibits translation of viral RNA and host factors, leading to RNA silencing amplification via RDR6/SGS3 complexes, which restricts viral accumulation and promotes symptom recovery.

genes: RNA1 (genomic RNA1 of Cucumber Mosaic Virus Fny strain, viral RNA, Cucumovirus), RNA2 (genomic RNA2 of Cucumber Mosaic Virus Fny strain, viral RNA, Cucumovirus), RNA3 (genomic RNA3 of Cucumber Mosaic Virus Fny strain, viral RNA, Cucumovirus)
phenotype: Overexpression of CMV genomic RNAs in A. thaliana results in visible disease symptoms in fully expanded leaves, with CMVRA causing severe leaf distortion, late bolting, and reduced apical dominance compared to CMVWT.
mechanism: CMV CP RNA binding activity inhibits translation of viral RNA and host factors, leading to RNA silencing amplification via RDR6/SGS3 complexes, which restricts viral accumulation and promotes symptom recovery.

genes: GhSKIP35 (ubiquitin-protein ligase family, Gossypium hirsutum, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Over-expression of GhSKIP35 confers Arabidopsis thaliana increased tolerance to Verticillium wilt, with transgenic plants showing reduced disease symptoms and lower disease index compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: GhSKIP35, as an SKP1-interacting partner in SCF-type E3 ubiquitin ligases, mediates ubiquitylation of proteins involved in resistance (R) protein-mediated immunity, enhancing defense against Verticillium wilt.

genes: KIN10 (KIN10, catalytic subunit of SnRK1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of KIN10 leads to increased basal autophagy activity in Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings, with significantly more autophagosomes compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: KIN10 acts upstream of TOR in the regulation of autophagy, likely by phosphorylating the TOR complex to positively regulate autophagy.

genes: ZmDHN13 (ZmDHN13, dehydrin involved in stress tolerance, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmDHN13 enhances transgenic tobacco tolerance to oxidative stress, reducing ROS accumulation and electrolyte leakage by ~50%.
mechanism: ZmDHN13 protects LDH activity during oxidative stress and reduces ROS generation, with the K-segment being essential for this protective effect.

genes: ZmDHN13ΔK (ZmDHN13ΔK, dehydrin with deleted K-segment, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmDHN13ΔK in transgenic tobacco shows reduced oxidative stress tolerance compared to full-length ZmDHN13.
mechanism: The K-segment is essential for protecting LDH activity during oxidative stress, and its deletion weakens the protective effect.

genes: ZmDHN13ΔS (ZmDHN13ΔS, dehydrin with deleted S-segment, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmDHN13ΔS in transgenic tobacco shows reduced oxidative stress tolerance compared to full-length ZmDHN13.
mechanism: The S-segment is essential for nuclear localization and phosphorylation of ZmDHN13, which contributes to its protective role.

genes: ZmDHN13ΔNLS (ZmDHN13ΔNLS, dehydrin with deleted NLS-segment, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmDHN13ΔNLS in transgenic tobacco shows reduced oxidative stress tolerance compared to full-length ZmDHN13.
mechanism: The NLS-segment is essential for nuclear localization of ZmDHN13, which contributes to its protective role against oxidative stress.

genes: ZmDHN13-GFP (ZmDHN13-GFP, dehydrin-GFP fusion, Zea mays)
phenotype: ZmDHN13-GFP fusion protein localizes to nuclei and cytosol in transgenic tobacco, with nuclear accumulation being predominant.
mechanism: The S-segment and NLS-segment are essential for nuclear targeting of ZmDHN13.

genes: ZmDHN13ΔK-GFP (ZmDHN13ΔK-GFP, dehydrinΔK-GFP fusion, Zea mays)
phenotype: ZmDHN13ΔK-GFP fusion protein localizes to nuclei and cytosol in transgenic tobacco, with nuclear accumulation being predominant.
mechanism: The K-segment deletion does not affect nuclear localization but reduces phosphorylation capability.

genes: ZmDHN13ΔNLS-GFP (ZmDHN13ΔNLS-GFP, dehydrinΔNLS-GFP fusion, Zea mays)

mechanism: PIF4 is necessary for BOP2-mediated suppression of hypocotyl elongation and promotion of cotyledon separation.

genes: PIF4 (PIF4, PIF transcription factor involved in phytochrome signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: CsSTS enhances phloem loading of carbohydrates by synthesizing stachyose, preventing starch accumulation and improving cold tolerance.

mechanism: CsSTS knockdown inhibits stachyose synthesis and phloem loading, leading to starch accumulation and reduced cold tolerance.

mechanism: OsHsp18.0 functions as a molecular chaperone, prevents protein aggregation, and increases salicylic acid (SA) accumulation, which correlates with enhanced resistance to Xoo and abiotic stress tolerance.

genes: BpGH3.5 (BpGH3.5, early auxin-response gene regulating root elongation, Betula platyphylla × B. pendula)

mechanism: T-DNA insertion disrupts BpGH3.5, leading to H2O2 accumulation, SA increase, and induction of defense-related genes.

genes: AmRosea1 (AmRosea1, transcription factor, Antirrhinum majus), AmDelila (AmDelila, transcription factor, Antirrhinum majus), MtANR (MtANR, anthocyanidin reductase, Medicago truncatula), MtLAR (MtLAR, leucoanthocyanidin reductase, Medicago truncatula)

genes: OsPPR676 (OsPPR676, plastid-localized PPR-SMR protein, Oryza sativa)

mechanism: OsPPR676 is essential for the translation of atpB, affecting ATP synthase activity and lipid biosynthesis

genes: EG (EG, hyperthermophilic endoglucanase, hyperthermophilic)

mechanism: EG remains inactive at normal plant temperatures but becomes active during high-temperature processing, enhancing cellulose hydrolysis.

genes: Xyn (Xyn, hyperthermophilic xylanase, hyperthermophilic)
phenotype: Overexpression of Xyn increases saccharification efficiency by ~1.5-fold in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Xyn remains inactive at normal plant temperatures but becomes active during high-temperature processing, enhancing xylan hydrolysis.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: GUS activity in lignifying vascular tissues of Arabidopsis, including midrib and vascular veins in leaves, xylem and cambial regions in stems
mechanism: SbCAD2 promoter directs GUS expression in lignifying tissues, suggesting conserved regulatory mechanisms for monolignol biosynthesis between grasses and dicots

genes: OsSUS3 (sucrose synthase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSUS3 increases biomass yields by 6–8%, enhances biomass saccharification by 23–33% (NaOH pretreatment) and 29–49% (H2SO4 pretreatment), and improves lodging resistance with 17–50% reduced lodging index and 8–44% increased extension/pushing forces in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsSUS3 provides UDPG for cellulose/hemicellulose biosynthesis, reducing cellulose crystallinity (7–10% lower CrI) and increasing cell wall thickness (75–90% thicker secondary walls), which enhances saccharification and lodging resistance.

genes: PEX6 (PEX6, ATPase, peroxisomal import, Arabidopsis thaliana), PEX26 (PEX26, ATPase, peroxisomal import, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of HA-PEX6 or HA-PEX26 restored sucrose independence and IBA sensitivity to pex6-3, pex6-4, and pex26-1 seedlings
mechanism: NA

mechanism: PgGUX glucuronosylates xylan, reintroducing [Me]GlcA branches that protect cellulose from enzymatic degradation by sheathing hemicellulose and embedding in lignin.

genes: FAEA (ferulic acid esterase A, Aspergillus niger)

genes: MYB3R3 (MYB3R3, repressor MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MYB3R3-GFP leads to accumulation of the protein in root meristems under DNA damage conditions, resulting in cell cycle arrest and inhibition of root growth.
mechanism: MYB3R3-GFP binds to promoters of G2/M-specific genes (e.g., KNOLLE, CYCB1;2) and represses their expression, blocking cell cycle progression. Protein accumulation is regulated by CDK-mediated phosphorylation and proteasomal degradation.

genes: MYB3R4 (MYB3R4, repressor MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MYB3R4-GFP results in low protein accumulation under normal conditions but rapid degradation upon DNA damage. No significant effect on root growth arrest in response to DNA damage.
mechanism: MYB3R4-GFP is rapidly downregulated by DNA damage at the transcriptional level, unlike Rep-MYBs which are regulated post-translationally via proteasomal degradation.

genes: MYB3R5 (MYB3R5, repressor MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MYB3R5-GFP leads to accumulation in root meristems under DNA damage conditions, contributing to cell cycle arrest and inhibition of root growth.
mechanism: MYB3R5-GFP binds to promoters of G2/M-specific genes and represses their expression. Protein accumulation is regulated by CDK-mediated phosphorylation and proteasomal degradation, similar to MYB3R3.

genes: MYB3R3 (MYB3R3, repressor MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MYB3R3AAA-GFP (non-phosphorylatable mutant) leads to constitutive high protein accumulation, resulting in delayed cell cycle progression and reduced root and shoot growth.
mechanism: Phosphorylation at S394, T407, and S461 residues is required for MYB3R3 degradation. The AAA mutant lacks these phosphorylation sites, leading to persistent protein accumulation and enhanced repression of G2/M-specific genes.

genes: MYB3R3 (MYB3R3, repressor MYB transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of MYB3R3DDD-GFP (phosphomimic mutant) results in low protein accumulation under DNA damage conditions, leading to failure to rescue the myb3r3 mutant phenotype and increased tolerance to DNA damage.
mechanism: Phosphomimic substitutions at S394, T407, and S461 residues prevent MYB3R3 accumulation, impairing its ability to repress G2/M-specific genes and block cell cycle progression.

genes: Cas9 (Cas9, nuclease, from parsley), gRNA1 (gRNA1, guide RNA, synthetic), gRNA2 (gRNA2, guide RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: CRISPR-induced deletions in BcFLA1 reduce root hair length by trend in Brassica carinata.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced indels in BcFLA1 disrupt its function, leading to reduced root hair elongation.

genes: BcFLA1amut (BcFLA1amut, mutated BcFLA1, Brassica carinata)
phenotype: Complementation with BcFLA1amut increases root hair length compared to CRISPR roots in Brassica carinata.
mechanism: Overexpression of BcFLA1amut compensates for BcFLA1 loss-of-function, restoring and enhancing root hair elongation.

genes: oAANAT (oAANAT, melatonin biosynthesis enzyme, Ovis aries), oHIOMT (oHIOMT, melatonin biosynthesis enzyme, Ovis aries)
phenotype: Overexpression of oAANAT and oHIOMT increases plant height by 1.10–1.64-fold and 1.12–1.31-fold, respectively, and promotes flowering in Panicum virgatum under greenhouse conditions.

genes: oAANAT (oAANAT, melatonin biosynthesis enzyme, Ovis aries), oHIOMT (oHIOMT, melatonin biosynthesis enzyme, Ovis aries)
phenotype: Overexpression of oAANAT and oHIOMT increases melatonin content by 32–76% in Panicum virgatum, with tissue-specific accumulation in roots and stems, and circadian rhythm peaks at 05:00 and 14:00.
mechanism: Melatonin accumulation correlates with upregulated expression of oAANAT and oHIOMT (r²=0.88 and 0.90), and melatonin acts as a free-radical scavenger, enhancing salt tolerance via Na+ exclusion and vacuolar compartmentation (PvNHX1 upregulation).

genes: A/N-InvH (mitochondrial invertase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of A/N-InvH::gfp fusion protein in hairy roots of black bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) allows visualization of mitochondrial localization via confocal microscopy.
mechanism: A/N-InvH::gfp fusion protein co-localizes with mitochondrial red-dye probe (MitoTracker) in hairy root cells.

genes: A/N-InvH (mitochondrial invertase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: A/N-InvH promoter drives gfp expression in reproductive tissues and root meristematic regions, indicating tissue-specific regulation.

genes: OsSIZ2 (OsSIZ2, SUMO E3 ligase, rice)
phenotype: Mutation in OsSIZ2 reduces biomass, root length, plant height, panicle length, and 1000-grain weight in rice.

genes: OsSIZ2 (OsSIZ2, SUMO E3 ligase, rice)

mechanism: OsSIZ2 negatively regulates Pi uptake and mobilization by modulating Pi transporter genes (OsPT1, OsPT8, OsPHO1;2) and xylem sap Pi transport.

genes: CHI (CHI, flavonoid biosynthesis, Allium cepa)
phenotype: Highest rutin content in CHI lines (12.7 mg/g) compared to wild type (1.09 mg/g); inverse relationship with naringenin chalcone content.
mechanism: CHI converts naringenin chalcone to naringenin, increasing flavonoid flux. Depletion of naringenin chalcone removes negative feedback in the pathway.

genes: FLS (FLS, flavonoid biosynthesis, Allium cepa)
phenotype: 3.5× increase in rutin content compared to wild type; no significant increase in quercetin-glucoside or kaempferol rutinoside.
mechanism: FLS converts dihydrokampferol to quercetin. When stacked with CHI, FLS increases rutin content by utilizing CHI's increased naringenin pool.

genes: PAP1 (PAP1, transcription factor, synthetic)
phenotype: 6-fold increase in anthocyanin content in CHI x PAP1 lines; pale pinkish coloration in shoots and green fruit.
mechanism: PAP1 upregulates PAL, CHS, and DFR in Arabidopsis. In tomato, PAP1 increases anthocyanin content without stress, but requires CHI to relieve early pathway bottlenecks.

genes: MUR1 (MUR1, GDP-fucose biosynthesis gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: MUR1 mutation reduces fucose residues in cell walls, alters lignin structure (17% reduced thioacidolysis yield), causes stem developmental defects including collapsed tracheary elements, ectopic lignification, and regenerative xylem formation in inflorescence stems
mechanism: Defective RG-II dimerization due to MUR1 knockout disrupts cell wall cross-linking, triggering jasmonic acid signaling pathway and overexpression of secondary cell wall-related genes like VND6, leading to abnormal lignification and tissue repair responses

genes: AP1 (APETALA1, floral meristem identity gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), FLuc (firefly luciferase, reporter gene, Photinus pyralis)
phenotype: Luciferase activity serves as an early marker for flowering transition in Arabidopsis thaliana, detectable 2-3 weeks before visible flowering
mechanism: AP1 is a floral meristem identity gene specifically activated during the vegetative-to-reproductive phase transition; luciferase reporter allows non-destructive detection of AP1 expression in developing floral meristems

genes: EGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Chloroplast-targeted expression of EGFP in C. vulgaris
mechanism: the cTP sequence functioned efficiently to target heterologous gene into chloroplast in C. vulgaris

genes: sFBA (fructose 1,6-bisphosphate aldolase, Synechocystis sp. PCC6803)
phenotype: transgenic C. vulgaris cells showed significantly enhanced photosynthetic capacity and cell growth
mechanism: aldolase overexpression in chloroplast enhanced the photosynthetic capacity of C. vulgaris cells

genes: NRPE1 (C-terminal domain, RNA-directed DNA methylation subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)

mechanism: The overexpressed CTD interferes with Pol V activity via RNAi, impairing RdDM and leading to transposon derepression and SDC overexpression.

genes: SMC4 (condensin subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic clone)

mechanism: SMC4, as a condensin subunit, partners with cytosine methylation and histone modifications to silence transposons and repress chromatin decondensation.

phenotype: Very low infectivity requiring >20 µg RNA for infection. Rapid deletions of duplicated CP observed in 6/8 lineages. Virus discontinued due to extreme instability.

genes: Pns11 (non-structural protein of Rice dwarf virus, RDV, synthetic)

genes: OsSAMS1 (S-adenosylmethionine synthetase 1, Oryza sativa, native)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSAMS1 increases SAM, ACC, and ethylene levels, enhancing RDV infection and reducing rice tolerance to viral infection.
mechanism: OsSAMS1 activity is enhanced by Pns11 interaction, leading to increased ethylene production which promotes viral susceptibility.

genes: OsSAMS1 (S-adenosylmethionine synthetase 1, Oryza sativa, native)
phenotype: RNAi knockdown of OsSAMS1 reduces SAM, ACC, and ethylene levels, increasing rice tolerance to RDV infection.
mechanism: Reduced OsSAMS1 activity lowers ethylene production, enhancing antiviral defense and reducing viral accumulation.

genes: CmNF-YB8 (CmNF-YB8, silencing, Chrysanthemum morifolium)

mechanism: CmNF-YB8 regulates the aging pathway by modulating cmo-miR156 expression, which in turn affects SPL gene expression to control flowering time.

genes: CmNF-YB8 (CmNF-YB8, overexpression, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: CmNF-YB8 overexpression delays flowering time in chrysanthemum.
mechanism: CmNF-YB8 overexpression prolongs the juvenile phase by repressing cmo-miR156 and SPL gene expression, thereby modulating the aging pathway.

genes: CmNF-YB8 (CmNF-YB8, overexpression, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: CmNF-YB8 overexpression in Arabidopsis thaliana delays flowering time and prolongs the juvenile phase.
mechanism: CmNF-YB8 overexpression in Arabidopsis thaliana represses miR156 and SPL gene expression, modulating the aging pathway to delay flowering.

genes: OsCu/Zn-SOD (LOC_Os08g44770, Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsCu/Zn-SOD increases tolerance to saline-sodic stress in rice, with higher SOD activity and lower MDA content under NaCl and NaHCO3 stress.
mechanism: OsCu/Zn-SOD enhances ROS scavenging, reducing oxidative stress damage and membrane lipid peroxidation (MDA production).

phenotype: Restoration of fertility in siliques of CPNA2pro:gCPNA2 transgenic plants
mechanism: Complementation of CPNA2 function in Arabidopsis embryos

genes: CPNA2 (chaperonin subunit AtCpn60α2, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)

mechanism: Visualization of CPNA2 expression pattern in Arabidopsis

genes: CPNA2 (chaperonin subunit AtCpn60α2, Arabidopsis thaliana), H2B-GFP (histone 2B fused to green fluorescent protein, synthetic)

mechanism: Visualization of CPNA2 expression in embryonic cotyledons

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic), CPNA2-GFP (chaperonin subunit AtCpn60α2 fused to green fluorescent protein, synthetic)

mechanism: Subcellular localization of CPNA2 in chloroplasts

genes: phyA (photoreceptor phytochrome A, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: SoPIN1 (SoPIN1, auxin efflux carrier, Brachypodium distachyon), PIN1b (PIN1b, auxin efflux carrier, Brachypodium distachyon)

mechanism: SoPIN1 restores wild-type levels of bulk auxin transport to pin1-613 basal internodes but fails to fully complement the organ initiation defects.

phenotype: SoPIN1 and PIN1b show different behaviors when expressed in the meristem epidermis under the proAtML1 promoter.
mechanism: SoPIN1 forms convergent polarization patterns around sites of organ initiation, while PIN1b accumulates in intracellular bodies and fails to form convergent patterns.

genes: PvDREB1C (PvDREB1C, cold-inducible transcription factor, Panicum virgatum)

phenotype: PvDREB1C activates GUS expression in N. benthamiana when co-transformed with the rd29A promoter containing ACCGAC DRE cis-elements.

mechanism: BAK1 functions as a co-receptor for AtRALF1 signaling, mediating root growth inhibition through cell expansion regulation.

mechanism: BAK1 promoter activity is induced by AtRALF1, leading to increased BAK1-GFP expression in root meristematic zones.

mechanism: McWRI1 binds to GCC-box elements in promoters of McKCS, McLACS, and McWAX, activating their expression to regulate long-chain fatty acid biosynthesis and cuticular wax composition.

phenotype: Overexpression of RSV-encoded proteins (NS2, NS3, SP, NSvc4) leads to elevated miR168 and miR395 levels in rice plants, with NS3 specifically recapitulating RSV-induced miRNA perturbations.
mechanism: NS3 binds dsRNA and interacts with OsDRB1 to promote miRNA processing, enhancing miRNA accumulation and reducing target gene expression.

phenotype: Overexpression of mNS3 (mutant NS3) in rice plants results in reduced miRNA accumulation compared to wild-type NS3, indicating dsRNA binding activity is critical for miRNA regulation.
mechanism: NS3's dsRNA binding domain is essential for its interaction with OsDRB1 and miRNA processing; disruption of this domain (mNS3) abolishes the effect.

phenotype: Overexpression of OsDRB1a and mOsDRB1a in rice plants affects miRNA processing and NS3 interaction, with mOsDRB1a failing to form homodimers or interact with NS3.
mechanism: OsDRB1a interacts with NS3 to facilitate miRNA processing; mutations in OsDRB1a disrupt this interaction and homodimerization.

mechanism: NS3 binds pri-miRNAs and facilitates their processing by the miRNA machinery, while mNS3 lacks this activity.

phenotype: Overexpression of NS3-ΔD1D2-HYL1 in Arabidopsis hyl1-2 mutants rescues miRNA levels and ameliorates the mutant phenotype, similar to wild-type AtHYL1.
mechanism: NS3 compensates for the dsRNA binding domain of AtHYL1, enabling miRNA processing and restoring normal miRNA accumulation.

mechanism: TCSn is a synthetic promoter containing concatemerized type-B RR-binding motifs that respond to cytokinin signaling. Cytokinin induces TCSn-driven GUS expression, while auxin antagonizes this response.

mechanism: CjWRKY1 transcriptionally activates biosynthetic enzymes (EcCYP719A3, EcG3OMT, EcG11OMT) involved in benzophenanthridine alkaloid biosynthesis, correlating with increased alkaloid accumulation.

phenotype: Overexpression of MdMIR156a6 increases leaf number (double that of the wild type [WT]), shortens internode length, and inhibits flowering in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: Overexpression of MdMIR156a6 increases miR156 levels, which affects phase change by altering redox homeostasis and developmental signals.

mechanism: MIM156 inhibits miR156 activity, which affects phase change by altering redox homeostasis and developmental signals.

genes: AtBAT1 (AtBAT1, BR-related acyltransferase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtBAT1 in creeping bentgrass results in semi-dwarf phenotypes with reduced plant height (~34 cm vs 57.8 cm in controls), shorter internode lengths (49.5 mm vs 74.2 mm), reduced leaf growth rates, and increased chlorophyll content (especially chlorophyll b). Transgenic plants also display erect leaves with smaller lamina joint bending angles (~37° vs ~75° in controls), delayed leaf senescence (21% chlorophyll loss vs 77% in controls), and enhanced drought tolerance (80% survival vs 20% in controls).
mechanism: AtBAT1 reduces endogenous brassinosteroid (BR) intermediates (typhasterol, 6-deoxocastasterone, castasterone) by ~45-60% of wild-type levels, leading to BR-deficient phenotypes. This BR reduction increases abscisic acid (ABA) responsiveness, enhancing stomatal closure (52% closed stomata vs 22% in controls) and drought tolerance. The semi-dwarfism and erect leaf phenotypes are attributed to reduced cell elongation and altered vascular bundle development.

genes: AtFC1 (Ferrochelatase-1, terminal enzyme of heme biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtFC1 increases Cd tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with improved primary root elongation (1.2–1.4× wild-type), 13.5–22.8× higher AtFC1 transcript levels, increased biomass (15–30% over wild-type), elevated chlorophyll content, and reduced ROS (H2O2, O·2−, TBARS) under 50–150 μM Cd stress.
mechanism: AtFC1-generated heme activates GSH-dependent phytochelatin (PC) synthesis pathway, increasing non-protein thiol (NPT) compounds (2–3× wild-type) and Cd accumulation (1.5–2× wild-type). Heme also upregulates GSH1, GSH2, PCS1, PCS2, and GR1 gene expression under Cd stress.

genes: OsNramp5 (cation transporter involved in Cd and Mn uptake, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of OsNramp5 reduces Cd and Mn accumulation in grains by ~98% and ~41%, respectively, in indica rice without affecting yield or agronomic traits.
mechanism: OsNramp5 functions as a transporter for Cd and Mn uptake; its knockout disrupts metal transport, reducing grain accumulation while maintaining Mn sufficiency in shoots.

genes: CBC1 (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), CBC2 (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CBC1-GFP or CBC2-GFP in cbc1 cbc2 double mutant restores temperature decrease in response to blue light, indicating stomatal opening restoration.
mechanism: CBC1 and CBC2 redundantly function to open stomata in response to blue light by inhibiting S-type anion channels.

genes: Sc-j (Sc-j, pollen development gene, Oryza sativa), Sc-ib1 (Sc-ib1, pollen development gene, Oryza sativa), Sc-ib2 (Sc-ib2, pollen development gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Reduction of Sc-i dosage rescues hybrid male sterility (HMS) by restoring Sc-j-pollen fertility in rice hybrids.
mechanism: Targeted deletion of the ~28-kb segment containing Sc-ib1 and Sc-ib2 reduces Sc-i gene dosage, alleviating allelic suppression of Sc-j and restoring pollen fertility.

genes: Sc-j (Sc-j, pollen development gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Antisense transgenic plants show partial male sterility, mimicking Sc-mediated hybrid male sterility (HMS).
mechanism: Reduced Sc-j expression in anthers leads to impaired pollen development, resulting in semi-sterility.

genes: AtFC1 (AtFC1, salt stress-responsive gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtFC1 enhances salt resistance in Arabidopsis, increasing seed germination rates by ~43% under 100 mM NaCl and increasing fresh weight by 27-34% under 150 mM NaCl compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: AtFC1 overexpression maintains Na+ and K+ homeostasis by reducing Na+ accumulation in roots and shoots (1.4-1.5-fold lower in 35 S::AtFC1 plants vs. wild-type under 150 mM NaCl) and increasing K+ concentration, while upregulating SOS1 and SOS3 expression under salt stress.

mechanism: Cry1Ab/Cry1Ac fusion gene encodes insecticidal toxin that targets lepidopteran pests; elevated CO2 and N-fertilization modulate transgene expression and methylation status

genes: ZmG2 (ZmG2, transcription factor for chloroplast development, Zea mays), ZmGLK1 (ZmGLK1, transcription factor for chloroplast development, Zea mays)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of ZmG2 or ZmGLK1 in rice induces greening of callus, embryos, and roots, and enhances greening in shoots. mechanism: ZmG2 and ZmGLK1 increase chloroplast size in bundle sheath and mestome sheath cells without reducing chloroplast number, leading to larger chloroplast volume per cell. Photosynthetic enzymes (RuBisCo, RuBisCo activase, FBPase) accumulate in vascular sheath chloroplasts. Mitochondrial volume and plasmodesmatal frequency increase, mimicking proto-Kranz anatomy seen in C4 grasses.

mechanism: ZmG2 expression in bundle sheath cells increases chloroplast size and photosynthetic enzyme accumulation. Mitochondrial volume and plasmodesmatal frequency increase, leading to proto-Kranz anatomy. Chloroplast development in mestome sheath cells is induced, with photosynthetic enzymes accumulating to levels significantly higher than wild-type.

genes: miR159 (microRNA, Oryza sativa, synthetic)
phenotype: STTM159 transgenic plants exhibit reduced plant height (23.70-25.08% reduction), shorter main panicle (15.10-17.37% reduction), shorter flag leaf (24.37-25.14% reduction), reduced stem diameter (9.16-38.00% reduction), smaller grain size (12.68-16.90% reduction in length, 6.06-9.09% in width, 15.51-16.35% in thickness), and 32.11-33.58% reduction in 1000-grain weight in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: Suppression of miR159 leads to increased expression of its target genes OsGAMYB and OsGAMYBL1. This results in downregulation of cell cycle genes (OsCycB1;1, OsCDKF, OsCKL2, OsDEL1, OsCDKB) and hormone biosynthesis/signaling genes (auxin, cytokinin, brassinosteroids). Reduced cell division and altered hormone homeostasis contribute to smaller organ size.

phenotype: Overexpression of AtMPC1 reduces ABA sensitivity and increases drought stress sensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtMPC1 negatively regulates ABA-induced stomatal closure by transporting pyruvate into mitochondria, reducing cytosolic pyruvate accumulation and ROS-dependent anion channel activation.

genes: AtMPC1 (mitochondrial pyruvate carrier 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the mpc1 mutant restores wild-type ABA sensitivity and drought response in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Complementation with AtMPC1 under its native promoter rescues the negative regulation of ABA-induced stomatal closure by restoring mitochondrial pyruvate transport and reducing ROS-dependent anion channel activation.

mechanism: EgMYB4 suppresses the expression of COMT (caffeic acid O-methyltransferase) and F5H (ferulate-5-hydroxylase) genes, redirecting carbon flux from lignin biosynthesis to phenylpropene production

Specifically, KAI2 overexpression leads to thicker cuticles, reduced electrolyte leakage, increased anthocyanin content, and improved ABA-mediated stomatal closure.

mechanism: miR156 targets SQUAMOSA PROMOTER BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE (SPL) transcription factors involved in vegetative-to-reproductive phase transition. Overexpression of miR156 leads to downregulation of five SPL genes, causing delayed flowering and increased biomass production.
