mechanism: NRT2.1 promoter activity is modulated by CLF-PRC2-mediated H3K27me3 enrichment; reduction in H3K27me3 in clf-29 leads to increased GUS expression.

genes: LUC (luciferase reporter, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of ProNRT2.1:LUC increases LUC transcripts in clf-29 mutants under low nitrate (0.3 mM NO3−) compared to wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NRT2.1 promoter activity is modulated by CLF-PRC2-mediated H3K27me3 enrichment; reduction in H3K27me3 in clf-29 leads to increased LUC expression.

genes: hpt (hygromycin phosphotransferase gene, selectable marker, Agrobacterium tumefaciens), Cry1B (synthetic Cry1B gene, insect resistance, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of Cry1B confers insect resistance in Oryza sativa L. Japonica cv Ariete.
mechanism: Cry1B protein provides insect resistance by forming insecticidal toxins.

genes: Ptr (blast resistance gene, Oryza sativa, LOC_Os12g18729)
phenotype: CRISPR-edited ptr mutants exhibited larger lesion areas and higher disease ratings to M. oryzae isolates compared to wild-type Katy
mechanism: Ptr is required for rice blast resistance; disruption of Ptr leads to susceptibility to avirulent isolates

genes: pds (phytoene desaturase, Zea mays, endogenous)
phenotype: Silencing pds reduces downstream carotenoid expression and increases phytoene accumulation in maize leaves, resulting in a variegated white phenotype with mosaic spatial distribution at the cellular level.
mechanism: pds gene silencing disrupts carotenoid biosynthesis, leading to reduced downstream carotenoids and accumulation of the colorless phytoene precursor.

genes: TaCIPK23 (TaCIPK23, drought-responsive CBL-interacting protein kinase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaCIPK23 in wheat increases drought tolerance, with higher survival rates under drought conditions, enhanced root growth, increased osmolyte accumulation, and reduced water loss rates.
mechanism: TaCIPK23 enhances ABA sensitivity, induces stomatal closure, and upregulates drought- and ABA-responsive genes under stress. It interacts with TaCBL1 on the plasma membrane to mediate stress responses.

genes: Venus-Luciferase (reporter, constitutive, synthetic)
phenotype: Auxin treatment increased overall fluorescence in transgenic plants.
mechanism: Auxin triggers relief of repression on HACR target genes by degrading the HACR.

genes: Venus-Luciferase (reporter, constitutive, synthetic)
phenotype: A HACR with a stabilized degron showed significantly lower reporter signal upon auxin treatment.
mechanism: Stabilized degron reduces auxin-induced degradation of HACR, maintaining repression.

genes: Venus-Luciferase (reporter, constitutive, synthetic)
phenotype: Treatment of transgenic plants with jasmonate significantly increased reporter signal.
mechanism: Jasmonate triggers degradation of HACR, relieving repression on the reporter.

genes: Venus-Luciferase (reporter, constitutive, synthetic)
phenotype: Treatment of transgenic plants with gibberellin significantly increased reporter signal.
mechanism: Gibberellin triggers degradation of HACR, relieving repression on the reporter.

genes: PIN1 (auxin transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants with HACR targeting PIN1 showed reduced branching and fewer co-initiations of lateral organs.
mechanism: HACR represses PIN1 transcriptional feedback, reducing auxin canalization and branching.

genes: TRY (trichome formation, Arabidopsis thaliana), CPC (trichome formation, Arabidopsis thaliana), ETC2 (unknown, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: High-frequency off-target mutations in CPC (87% in T1 lines) and TRY (medium frequency) genes due to CRISPR/Cas9 activity
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced DNA cleavage at off-target sites with three mismatches to sgRNA, enhanced by adjacent on-target mutations

genes: mCherry (fluorescent marker, synthetic), TRY (trichome formation, Arabidopsis thaliana), CPC (trichome formation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Introduction of mCherry cassette lowered editing efficiency to 2.4% compared to >10% in previous studies
mechanism: mCherry cassette negatively affects CRISPR/Cas9 system efficiency

genes: TRY (trichome formation, Arabidopsis thaliana), CPC (trichome formation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Fusion of tRNA-Met with mutant sgRNA scaffold increased editing efficiency to 3.7% (pE-T&C) compared to 2.1% (pT&C-E) with original scaffold
mechanism: tRNA-sgRNA fusion ensures precise sgRNA processing and full complementarity to targets

genes: SpCas9 (CRISPR endonuclease, synthetic), eSpCas9(1.0) (high-specificity variant, synthetic), eSpCas9(1.1) (high-specificity variant, synthetic), eSpCas9(1.2) (high-specificity variant, synthetic), SpCas9-HF1 (high-specificity variant, synthetic), HF1-e(1.1) (high-specificity variant, synthetic), HF1a-e(1.1) (high-specificity variant, synthetic), HF1b-e(1.2) (high-specificity variant, synthetic), HF1a-e(1.2) (high-specificity variant, synthetic)
phenotype: Eight high-specificity SpCas9 variants showed significantly reduced editing efficiency (0.64-13.4%) compared to wild-type SpCas9 (>10%)
mechanism: High-specificity variants require higher expression levels for on-target activity due to increased stringency of guide RNA-DNA complementation

genes: SaCas9 (CRISPR endonuclease, synthetic), ADH1 (alcohol dehydrogenase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 15% of T1 plants harbored homozygous or biallelic mutations in ADH1 gene
mechanism: SaCas9 requires longer PAM for target recognition, reducing off-target effects

genes: TcWRKY8 (TcWRKY8, WRKY transcription factor, Taxus chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of TcWRKY8 increases DBAT (3.1 times), T5H (4.6 times), and TcERF15 (3.2 times) expression while decreasing TcERF12 (0.8 times) in Taxus chinensis.
mechanism: TcWRKY8 regulates taxol biosynthesis-related genes via W-box elements in their promoters.

genes: TcWRKY20 (TcWRKY20, WRKY transcription factor, Taxus chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of TcWRKY20 increases DBAT (2.7 times), T5H (2.8 times), TcERF12 (2.8 times), and TcERF15 (4.7 times) expression in Taxus chinensis.
mechanism: TcWRKY20 regulates taxol biosynthesis-related genes via W-box elements in their promoters.

genes: TcWRKY26 (TcWRKY26, WRKY transcription factor, Taxus chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of TcWRKY26 increases DBAT (2.2 times), T5H (1.5 times), and TcERF15 (1.4 times) expression in Taxus chinensis.
mechanism: TcWRKY26 regulates taxol biosynthesis-related genes via W-box elements in their promoters.

genes: TcWRKY41 (TcWRKY41, WRKY transcription factor, Taxus chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of TcWRKY41 increases DBAT (11.2 times) and T5H (4.1 times) expression but decreases TcERF12 (0.4 times) in Taxus chinensis.
mechanism: TcWRKY41 regulates taxol biosynthesis-related genes via W-box elements in their promoters.

genes: TcWRKY44 (TcWRKY44, WRKY transcription factor, Taxus chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of TcWRKY44 decreases DBAT (0.7 times), T5H (0.4 times), and TcERF12 (0.5 times) expression while increasing TcERF15 (0.3 times) in Taxus chinensis.
mechanism: TcWRKY44 regulates taxol biosynthesis-related genes via W-box elements in their promoters.

genes: TcWRKY47 (TcWRKY47, WRKY transcription factor, Taxus chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of TcWRKY47 increases DBAT (5.4 times), T5H (4.1 times), and TcERF15 (5.5 times) expression while decreasing TcERF12 (0.4 times) in Taxus chinensis.
mechanism: TcWRKY47 regulates taxol biosynthesis-related genes via W-box elements in their promoters.

genes: TcWRKY52 (TcWRKY52, WRKY transcription factor, Taxus chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of TcWRKY52 decreases DBAT (0.2 times), T5H (0.3 times), and TcERF12 (0.4 times) expression while increasing TcERF15 (2.0 times) in Taxus chinensis.
mechanism: TcWRKY52 regulates taxol biosynthesis-related genes via W-box elements in their promoters.

genes: OsSND2 (transcription factor involved in secondary cell wall biosynthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: The knockout of OsSND2 using CRISPR/Cas9 system decreased cellulose content and down-regulated the expression of SCWs related genes.
mechanism: OsSND2 is a master regulator that directly binds to the promoters of SCWs-related genes, and its absence leads to reduced gene expression and cellulose content.

genes: SlAN11 (SlAN11, WD40 repeat protein involved in anthocyanin/PA biosynthesis, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlAN11 increases anthocyanin accumulation in leaves and stems by 50–130% and 100–160%, respectively.
mechanism: SlAN11 enhances anthocyanin biosynthesis by upregulating SlDFR and downregulating SlFLS1, altering dihydroflavonol flow.

genes: SlAN11 (SlAN11, WD40 repeat protein involved in anthocyanin/PA biosynthesis, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: RNAi of SlAN11 reduces anthocyanin content in leaves and stems by 5- to 8-fold and 23- to 35-fold, respectively.
mechanism: SlAN11 knockdown downregulates SlDFR and fails to suppress SlFLS1, reducing anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: SlAN11 (SlAN11, WD40 repeat protein involved in anthocyanin/PA biosynthesis, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: SlAN11-GFP fusion protein localizes exclusively to the nucleus in tomato mesophyll protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: SlAN11 (SlAN11, WD40 repeat protein involved in anthocyanin/PA biosynthesis, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: GUS activity detected in all tomato organs (roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, seeds) but not in trichomes.
mechanism: NA

genes: THyPRP (THyPRP, hypersensitive response-related protein, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Stable silencing of the THyPRP gene under the control of an AZ-specific promoter (TAPG4::antisense THyPRP) significantly inhibited pedicel abscission during 20 h after flower removal.
mechanism: THyPRP silencing inhibits ethylene biosynthesis and response, and affects regulatory genes related to cell wall modification and programmed cell death.

genes: cry1Ac::asal (fusion of Cry1Ac domains I/II and ASAL carbohydrate binding domain, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of Cry1Ac::ASAL fusion protein in rice confers 100% mortality against yellow stem borer and 80-100% mortality against leaf folder, with 87-93% reduction in brown planthopper feeding and 3-12-fold reduction in BPH survival compared to untransformed controls.
mechanism: Cry1Ac::ASAL binds to multiple receptor proteins (~70kDa, ~55kDa, ~40kDa) in BPH gut cells, enhancing toxin binding affinity and causing insecticidal effects against both lepidopteran and hemipteran pests.

genes: ZmPIP1;1 (aquaporin protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmPIP1;1 improves drought and salt tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with enhanced survival rates and reduced water loss under stress conditions.
mechanism: ZmPIP1;1 up-regulates stress responsive genes (RD29A, RD29B, LEA18, TRX5) and increases activities of ROS scavenging enzymes (CAT, SOD), reducing oxidative damage and enhancing osmoprotection.

genes: orf20fukkoku (orf20fukkoku, responsible for fertility restoration, Beta vulgaris)
phenotype: Expression of orf20fukkoku::flag in sugar beet suspension cells results in the formation of a 200-kDa protein complex with preSATP6, indicating functional interaction with mitochondrial preSATP6.
mechanism: The ORF20fukkoku protein interacts with preSATP6 to form a 200-kDa complex, suggesting a role in disrupting the 250-kDa preSATP6 oligomer associated with male sterility.

genes: orf20NK-198 (orf20NK-198, fertility-restoring gene, Beta vulgaris)
phenotype: Expression of orf20NK-198::flag in sugar beet suspension cells results in the formation of a 200-kDa protein complex with preSATP6, similar to the effect of orf20fukkoku::flag.
mechanism: NA

genes: orf20L (orf20L, gene from a maintainer sugar beet line, Beta vulgaris)
phenotype: Expression of orf20L::flag in sugar beet suspension cells does not result in the formation of a 200-kDa protein complex with preSATP6, indicating no functional interaction.
mechanism: NA

genes: VcFT (FLOWERING LOCUS T orthologue, Vaccinium corymbosum L.)
phenotype: Overexpression of VcFT causes continuous and precocious flowering in in vitro shoots and one-year old 'Aurora' plants.
mechanism: VcFT promotes flowering by up-regulating downstream genes such as VcSOC1, VcFUL, VcAP1, and VcLFY.

genes: SlIPT4 (isopentenyltransferase, tomato)
phenotype: Accelerated leaf senescence and orange fruits with ~75% reduced lycopene content in tomato
mechanism: SlIPT4 regulates lycopene biosynthesis via directly affecting ZISO expression, with feedback regulation between ABA and lycopene biosynthesis

genes: NbHAOX8 (Nbv5tr6245008, GOX family gene involved in disease resistance, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbGOX1 (NbS00060838g0004.1, GOX family gene involved in disease resistance, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbGOX4 (NbS00005125g0015.1, GOX family gene involved in disease resistance, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Silencing of NbHAOX8, NbGOX1, and NbGOX4 reduces resistance to TRV, alters nonhost resistance to Xoo, and modifies host resistance to Sclerotinia sclerotiorum. NbHAOX8 and NbGOX1 play a negative role in nonhost resistance to Xoo, while NbGOX4 plays a positive role. NbGOX1 negatively regulates SA pathway, NbGOX4 negatively modulates JA and WRKY45/WRKY62 pathways.
mechanism: Modulation of H2O2 accumulation and ROS regulation. Silencing of NbHAOX8 and NbGOX1 increases Xoo-elicited H2O2, while silencing of NbGOX4 reduces it. NbGOX4 suppresses NbHAOX8 and NbGOX1 expression.

genes: AHG1 (AHG1, group A PP2C, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of YFP-AHG1 causes ABA-insensitive phenotypes in seed germination and root growth response, but normal plant sizes and similar ABA sensitivities in stomatal responses.
mechanism: AHG1 interacts with DOG1 to regulate ABA signaling in seed germination and dormancy.

genes: DOG1 (DOG1, seed dormancy regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of YFP-DOG1 reduces germination and post-germination growth efficiencies in the presence of ABA, indicating ABA-dependent inhibition of germination.
mechanism: DOG1 interacts with AHG1 to regulate ABA signaling in seed dormancy and germination.

genes: AHG1 (AHG1, group A PP2C, Arabidopsis thaliana), DOG1 (DOG1, seed dormancy regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Double overexpression of HA-AHG1 and YFP-DOG1 shows a strong ABA-insensitive phenotype similar to HA-AHG1ox line, suggesting DOG1 functions upstream of AHG1.
mechanism: DOG1 inhibits AHG1 PP2C activity in an ABA-dependent manner, regulating SnRK2s activation.

genes: DOG1 (H245A mutant, seed dormancy regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: YFP-DOG1H245Aox lines exhibit lower germination and post-germination growth efficiencies similar to YFP-DOG1ox line in the presence of ABA.
mechanism: Heme binding via His245 is essential for DOG1 function in ABA signaling.

genes: DOG1 (H245AH249A mutant, seed dormancy regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: YFP-DOG1H245AH249Aox lines show similar germination and post-germination growth efficiencies to YFPox control line in the presence of ABA.
mechanism: Heme binding via His245 and His249 is essential for DOG1 function in ABA signaling.

genes: ScPDAT (phospholipid: diacylglycerol acyltransferase, Saccharomyces cerevisiae)
phenotype: Overexpression of ScPDAT in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii increases total fatty acid content by 22% and triacylglycerol (TAG) content by 32% compared to wild type.
mechanism: ScPDAT converts polar lipids (e.g., monogalactosyldiacylglycerol) to TAG, enhancing TAG accumulation pathway. Increased C16:3n6 and C16:4n3 fatty acids in TAG suggest chloroplast lipid metabolism redirection.

genes: TaPSTOL (putative kinase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaPSTOL increases root biomass, flowering time independent of P treatment, tiller number, and seed yield in wheat.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaPSTOL (putative kinase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of TaPSTOL decreases root biomass, flowering time independent of P treatment, tiller number, and seed yield in wheat.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaPSTOL (putative kinase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: TaPSTOL promoter drives GUS expression in root tips and hairs under P limiting conditions in wheat.
mechanism: NA

genes: HDS (hydroxyl methyl butenyl diphosphate synthase, enzyme catalyzing conversion of MEcPP to hydroxymethylbutenyl diphosphate, cloned from Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Accumulation of MEcPP correlates with reduction of auxin and PIN1 abundance in HDS RNAi lines
mechanism: MEcPP-mediated reduction of auxin and PIN1 abundance through RNAi suppression of HDS

genes: cry2Aa (synthetic, insecticidal crystal protein, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of cry2Aa increases resistance to Helicoverpa armigera, with 80–100% larval mortality and <5–10% leaf/pod damage in Cajanus cajan.
mechanism: Cry2Aa protein expression confers insecticidal activity against H. armigera larvae, causing high mortality and reduced plant damage.

genes: GFP-MBD (GFP fused to MBD, methyl-CpG-binding domain protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Used for visualizing CLASPs and microtubules in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: RFP-CLASP (RFP fused to CLASP, cytoskeleton-associated protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Used for visualizing CLASPs and microtubules in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: GFP-ɣTIP (GFP fused to ɣTIP, tonoplast intrinsic protein, reference [37])
phenotype: Used for visualizing vacuoles in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: YL2 (LOC_Os01g73450, UMP kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of yl2 mutant rescues yellow leaf phenotype and restores chlorophyll content to wild-type levels in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: YL2 is required for chloroplast development and accumulation of cpATPase subunits (AtpA/AtpB), which are essential for photosynthesis and chloroplast biogenesis.

genes: YL2 (LOC_Os01g73450, UMP kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi suppression of YL2 in Oryza sativa recapitulates the yl2 mutant phenotype, including yellow leaves, chlorophyll deficiency, and reduced plant height.
mechanism: YL2 knockdown disrupts chloroplast development and cpATPase activity, leading to impaired photosynthesis and chlorophyll biosynthesis.

genes: YL2 (LOC_Os01g73450, UMP kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: YL2-GFP fusion protein localizes to chloroplasts in rice protoplasts, confirming its chloroplast targeting and thylakoid membrane localization.
mechanism: YL2 is a thylakoid membrane-associated protein with intrinsic membrane properties, essential for chloroplast development and cpATPase function.

genes: HopF2 (HA epitope tagged HopF2-BirA*, membrane localization), BirA* (HA epitope tagged BirA*, soluble localization) (synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of HopF2-BirA* localizes predominantly to insoluble (membrane) fraction, while BirA* localizes mainly to soluble fraction in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: BirA* biotinylates proximal proteins in vivo, enabling identification of membrane-associated interactors via BioID.

genes: BirA* (HA epitope tagged BirA*, soluble localization) (synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of BirA* localizes mainly to soluble fraction with limited membrane association in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: BirA* biotinylates proximal proteins in vivo, enabling identification of membrane-associated interactors via BioID.

genes: PtRabE1b (constitutively active mutant Q74L, Rab GTPase involved in vesicular transport, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtRabE1b(Q74L) enhances salt tolerance in poplar by maintaining root growth under 50-100 mM NaCl stress conditions
mechanism: PtRabE1b(Q74L) activates vesicular transport pathways involving trafficking-related genes (Got1-like, KEU, p24, etc.), stress-related TFs (bZIP60), and calcium signaling components (SOS2, CAM7) to improve salt stress response

genes: WD40-2 (WD40-2, putative M. truncatula transducin/WD40 repeat gene, Medicago sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of WD40-2 causes stunted growth, reduced shoot and root biomass, lower water potential, and increased water loss under drought stress in alfalfa.
mechanism: WD40-2 acts as a negative regulator of drought responses in alfalfa by reducing root growth, water conservation, and biomass accumulation.

genes: WD40-2 (WD40-2, putative M. truncatula transducin/WD40 repeat gene, Medicago sativa)
phenotype: RNAi of WD40-2 increases shoot and root biomass, root length, water potential, and reduces water loss under drought stress in alfalfa.
mechanism: WD40-2 RNAi alleviates its negative regulatory role in drought responses by enhancing root growth, water conservation, and biomass accumulation.

genes: eIF4E1.S (eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E isoform, N. tabacum, synthetic)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of eIF4E1.S restores potyvirus susceptibility in tobacco plants possessing either the va or VAM mutant loci.
mechanism: eIF4E1.S facilitates PVY susceptibility by enabling viral VPg protein binding during replication

genes: HTT2 (HTT2, heat-induced TAS1 target 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HTT2 increases thermotolerance in Brassica rapa by decreasing leaf electrical conductivity and increasing hypocotyl length under high-temperature and heat-shock treatments.
mechanism: HTT2 upregulates the expression of heat-shock factor genes (BrpHsfs) under high-temperature and heat-shock conditions, enhancing thermotolerance.

genes: GhGPX1 (GhGPX1, glutathione peroxidase 1, Gossypium hirsutum), GhGPX8 (GhGPX8, glutathione peroxidase 8, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhGPX1 and GhGPX8 increases transcript levels by 3–10 times in Gossypium hirsutum.
mechanism: NA

genes: DGTT5 (DGTT5, type II acyl-CoA:diacylglycerol acyltransferase 5, Nannochloropsis oceanica)
phenotype: Overexpression of DGTT5 increases triacylglycerol (TAG) content in N. oceanica by ~10% of dry weight (DW) compared to wild type (~6% of DW).
mechanism: DGTT5 encodes type II acyl-CoA:diacylglycerol acyltransferase 5, which is involved in TAG synthesis.

genes: NS3 (nonstructural protein, viral suppressor of RNA silencing, Rice stripe virus)
phenotype: Reduces RSV symptoms and viral accumulation in Nicotiana benthamiana compared to wild type
mechanism: NS3 induces host resistance by affecting gene expression in ribosome, photosynthesis, and carbon metabolism pathways

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase A, transient expression reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Used for transient expression analysis in Triticum monococcum suspension cells
mechanism: NA

genes: hpt (hygromycin resistance, selectable marker, synthetic)
phenotype: Used as a selectable marker in stable transformation of wheat cv. Gladius
mechanism: NA

genes: CSN5a (COP9 signalosome subunit 5a, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restored the entire WT trichome phenotype to the mutant transgenic lines
mechanism: Disrupted CSN5a was responsible for the morphological alterations observed in sk372

genes: GL3 (GLABRA3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Increased the number of single pointed trichomes only in sk372
mechanism: Overexpression of GL3 driven by cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promotor increased the number of single pointed trichomes only, no other phenotypic recovery in sk372

genes: OsMDHAR4 (monodehydroascorbate reductase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsMDHAR4 increases stomatal opening and decreases hydrogen peroxide content in rice leaves, leading to enhanced sensitivity to heat stress.
mechanism: OsMDHAR4 negatively regulates H2O2-induced stomatal closure by reducing H2O2 accumulation, thereby decreasing heat tolerance in rice.

genes: OsMDHAR4 (monodehydroascorbate reductase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsMDHAR4 is localized to the chloroplasts in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsGSK2 (OsGSK2typeA, OsGSK2typeB) (GSK3 kinase, BR signaling component, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsGSK2typeA transgenic rice has shorter mesocotyls than OsGSK2typeB transgenic rice (P < 0.05).
mechanism: OsGSK2typeA has higher kinase activity than OsGSK2typeB, inhibiting mesocotyl elongation via BR signaling.

genes: CYC U2 (CYC U2T21AS24AS30A) (U-type cyclin, cell cycle regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CYC U2m transgenic rice has longer mesocotyls than wild-type Ni (P < 0.05).
mechanism: CYC U2 promotes mesocotyl elongation via cell division; phosphorylation by OsGSK2 regulates its stability.

genes: CmCPL1 (CmCPL1, RNA polymerase II CTD phosphatase, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmCPL1 enhances heat tolerance in chrysanthemum, as evidenced by delayed wilting and higher Fv/Fm under heat stress.
mechanism: CmCPL1 upregulates heat-responsive genes (HSP, sHSP, HSFA2, DREB2A) and downregulates WRKY41, contributing to enhanced heat tolerance.

genes: CmCPL1 (CmCPL1, RNA polymerase II CTD phosphatase, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Knockdown of CmCPL1 increases sensitivity to heat stress in chrysanthemum, as evidenced by earlier wilting and lower Fv/Fm under heat stress.
mechanism: CmCPL1 downregulation leads to reduced expression of heat-responsive genes (HSP, sHSP, HSFA2, DREB2A) and upregulation of WRKY41, contributing to increased heat sensitivity.

genes: CymMV RdRp (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, viral replication target, CymMV), ORSV RdRp (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, viral replication target, ORSV)
phenotype: High resistance to CymMV (100% resistant in F3/F4 generations) and weak resistance to ORSV (16-0% resistance in F3/F4 generations) in transgenic N. benthamiana plants
mechanism: amiRNA targeting viral RdRp genes inhibits viral replication by blocking translation initiation at the 5' end of CymMV RdRp and potentially failing to suppress ORSV RdRp due to suboptimal targeting of 3' end and lower amiR-ORSV production

genes: NA (NA)
phenotype: Off-target mutations are minimal in rice plants edited with Cas9 and Cpf1 constructs.
mechanism: Cas9 and Cpf1 nucleases are highly specific, with off-target mutations largely due to tissue culture and Agrobacterium transformation rather than the nucleases themselves.

genes: NA (NA)
phenotype: Off-target mutations are minimal in rice plants edited with Cas9 and Cpf1 constructs.
mechanism: Cas9 and Cpf1 nucleases are highly specific, with off-target mutations largely due to tissue culture and Agrobacterium transformation rather than the nucleases themselves.

genes: PID (PID kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: PID phosphorylates PIN3, affecting its polarity and auxin transport directionality during gravitropic responses.

genes: PID (PID kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: PID phosphorylates PIN3, affecting its polarity and auxin transport directionality during gravitropic responses.

genes: PIN3 (PIN3, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Phosphorylation at P2 site regulates PIN3 polarization and auxin transport during gravitropic responses.

genes: PIN3 (PIN3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Phosphomimic mutation at P2 site (S316D, S317D, S321D) in PIN3 shows defective gravitropic bending and reduced PIN3 polarization.
mechanism: Phosphorylation at P2 site regulates PIN3 polarization and auxin transport during gravitropic responses.

genes: PIN3 (PIN3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PIN3-YFP rescues pin3-4 mutant phenotype and shows normal PIN3 polarization during gravitropic responses.
mechanism: PIN3-YFP tagging allows visualization of PIN3 localization and relocalization during gravitropic responses.

genes: Cry1Ac (Bacillus thuringiensis cry1Ac, toxin, Bacillus thuringiensis)

genes: TnCelB (hyperthermophilic endoglucanase from Thermotoga neapolitana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of TnCelB in transgenic poplar lines resulted in altered growth (increased stem diameter, height in some lines, wrinkled leaves in CaMV-4), reduced lignin content, and lower cellulose crystallinity, leading to a more digestible cell wall.
mechanism: TnCelB activity reduces lignin and cellulose crystallinity, making the cell wall more digestible.

genes: CLE16 (CLE gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Loss-of-function mutations in CLE16 lead to delayed bolting and increased leaf number prior to flowering in some alleles.
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9-induced frame shifts and premature stop codons in CLE16 coding sequence.

genes: CLE17 (CLE gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Loss-of-function mutations in CLE17 show no significant effect on axillary meristem formation or floral transition.
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9-induced frame shifts and premature stop codons in CLE17 coding sequence.

genes: CLE27 (CLE gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Loss-of-function mutations in CLE27 cause plants to flower one day earlier than wild-type under constant light conditions.
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9-induced frame shifts and premature stop codons in CLE27 coding sequence.

genes: AtD-CGS (cystathionine γ-synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtD-CGS increases methionine content in soybean seeds
mechanism: Seed-specific expression of AtD-CGS enhances methionine biosynthesis in soybean seeds

genes: TUBG1 (TUBG1, γ-tubulin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knockout of TUBG1 reduces nematode infection sites by ~75% and female nematode development by ~22% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: TUBG1 deficiency disrupts microtubule organization in syncytia, reducing cytoplasmic streaming efficiency and nutrient delivery to nematodes.

genes: TUBG2 (TUBG2, γ-tubulin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Knockout of TUBG2 reduces nematode infection sites by ~57% and female nematode development by ~51% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: TUBG2 deficiency disrupts microtubule organization in syncytia, reducing cytoplasmic streaming efficiency and nutrient delivery to nematodes.

genes: OsABIL2 (OsABIL2WT, wild-type protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsABIL2WT in Arabidopsis reduces ABA sensitivity during germination and seedling establishment, with germination rates higher than wild-type but lower than abi1-1 mutant.
mechanism: OsABIL2 interacts with ABA receptors in an ABA-dependent manner; the G183D mutation disrupts this interaction, leading to ABA insensitivity.

genes: OsABIL2 (OsABIL2G183D, mutated protein with G183D substitution, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsABIL2G183D in Arabidopsis causes strong ABA insensitivity, with germination rates over 90% on ABA-containing media.
mechanism: OsABIL2 interacts with ABA receptors in an ABA-dependent manner; the G183D mutation disrupts this interaction, leading to ABA insensitivity.

genes: OsABIL2 (OsABIL2WT, wild-type protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsABIL2WT in rice reduces ABA sensitivity during germination and seedling growth, with seminal root emergence suppressed by ABA in WT but not in transgenic lines.
mechanism: OsABIL2 interacts with ABA receptors in an ABA-dependent manner; the G183D mutation disrupts this interaction, leading to ABA insensitivity.

genes: OsABIL2 (OsABIL2G183D, mutated protein with G183D substitution, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsABIL2G183D in rice causes strong ABA insensitivity, with seminal root emergence over 70% on ABA-containing media and precocious germination rates of 20–40%.
mechanism: OsABIL2 interacts with ABA receptors in an ABA-dependent manner; the G183D mutation disrupts this interaction, leading to ABA insensitivity.

genes: OsbZIP73 (bZIP73Jap, cold tolerance candidate gene, Oryza sativa), OsbZIP73 (bZIP73Ind, cold tolerance candidate gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of bZIP73Jap in japonica rice (ZH11) showed no significant difference in cold tolerance compared to wild type (22% survival rate), while overexpression of bZIP73Ind and RNAi of bZIP73Jap resulted in <2% survival rates under cold stress.
mechanism: bZIP73Jap interacts with bZIP71 to enhance cold tolerance by trans-activating peroxidase (POX) gene precursors and reducing reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, while also repressing ABA biosynthesis genes OsNCED3 and OsNCED5 to fine-tune ABA levels.

genes: OsbZIP71 (cold tolerance QTL-associated gene, Oryza sativa), OsbZIP73 (bZIP73Jap, cold tolerance candidate gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Co-overexpression of bZIP71 and bZIP73Jap in japonica rice (ZH11) significantly improved cold tolerance with >70% survival rate after cold stress, compared to 22% in wild type.
mechanism: bZIP71 enhances bZIP73Jap activity by promoting trans-activation of POX gene precursors, reducing ROS levels, and repressing ABA biosynthesis genes to fine-tune ABA homeostasis.

genes: FZP (FRIZZY PANICLE, AP2/ERF-type transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: FZP antisense transgenic plants have ~40% more secondary rachis branches (SBs) per panicle and 30-50% increased total grain number compared to vector control plants in Oryza sativa
mechanism: Reduced FZP expression prevents transition from branch to spikelet meristem, increasing higher-order branching in upper panicle regions

genes: CP4 EPSPS (Agrobacterium sp. strain CP4 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase, Agrobacterium sp. strain CP4)
phenotype: Inducible male sterility is achieved in Zea mays L. when glyphosate is applied, leading to complete male sterility and viable female fertility for hybrid seed production.
mechanism: The mts-siRNAs trigger sequence-specific cleavage of the CP4 EPSPS mRNA in tassels, reducing CP4 EPSPS protein in male reproductive cells, making them glyphosate-sensitive.

genes: bZIP63 (AT5G28770.2, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RNAi knockdown of bZIP63 reduces PRR7 transcript abundance under high light and attenuates PRR7 upregulation in low-energy conditions, disrupting circadian period and phase entrainment to sugars.
mechanism: bZIP63 RNAi suppresses PRR7 transcription, which is required for circadian oscillator responses to low-energy conditions and sugar signals.

genes: oleosin-rhFGF9 (fusion protein, recombinant human fibroblast growth factor 9 fused to safflower oleosin, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of oleosin-rhFGF9 in safflower seeds results in 0.14% oil body protein expression level, with mitogenic activity towards NIH3T3 cells and promotes hair growth and wound healing in C57BL/6 mice
mechanism: Oil body-bound oleosin-rhFGF9 promotes hair growth by up-regulating β-catenin expression and enhances wound healing through FGF9 signaling pathways

genes: LAIR (long non-coding RNA, antisense transcript of LRK gene cluster, Oryza sativa ssp. indica MH63)
phenotype: Overexpression of LAIR increases primary panicle size and number of panicles per plant, leading to a considerable increase in total grain yield in Oryza sativa ssp. indica.
mechanism: LAIR activates LRK gene transcription through epigenetic modifications (H3K4me3 and H4K16ac enrichment) and interacts with chromatin-modifying proteins OsMOF and OsWDR5.

genes: LAIR (long non-coding RNA, antisense transcript of LRK gene cluster, Oryza sativa ssp. indica MH63)
phenotype: Antisense LAIR (anti-LAIR) transgenic plants exhibited inhibited growth and decreased grain yield in Oryza sativa ssp. indica.
mechanism: Anti-LAIR suppresses LRK gene expression and disrupts histone modification marks (H3K4me3 and H4K16ac), leading to reduced transcription of LRK genes.

genes: hEGF (human epidermal growth factor, synthetic, Homo sapiens), bar (phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, synthetic, Streptomyces hygroscopicus)
phenotype: Expression of oleosin-hEGF-hEGF in T3 transgenic safflower seeds reaches 69.32 mg/g of seeds. The oil body expressing this fusion protein shows significant proliferative activity on NIH/3T3 cells and accelerates wound healing in rats with >98% wound coverage after 14 days of treatment.
mechanism: Oleosin-hEGF-hEGF fusion protein promotes cell proliferation, enhances granulation tissue formation, increases collagen deposition, and stimulates neovascularization. It activates EGFR signaling, upregulates TGF-β1, bFGF, and VEGF expression during wound healing.

genes: OsCCD7 (carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 7, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: ccd7 mutants exhibit increased tillering and reduced plant height in rice (Oryza sativa). Application of synthetic SL analog GR24 rescues the phenotype to wild-type levels.
mechanism: Disruption of OsCCD7 impairs strigolactone (SL) biosynthesis, leading to increased tillering and reduced height. SL deficiency in root exudates also reduces Striga germination.

genes: OsCCD7 (carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 7, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: ccd7 mutants exhibit increased tillering and reduced plant height in rice (Oryza sativa). Application of synthetic SL analog GR24 rescues the phenotype to wild-type levels.
mechanism: Disruption of OsCCD7 impairs strigolactone (SL) biosynthesis, leading to increased tillering and reduced height. SL deficiency in root exudates also reduces Striga germination.

genes: DCL2b (DCL2b, gene for dicer-like 2b, tomato)
phenotype: dcl2b mutants displayed abnormal leaf morphology (long, narrow, twisted leaves), elongated fruits with reduced seed development, and increased susceptibility to ToMV infection in greenhouse II
mechanism: DCL2b knockout disrupted 22-nt siRNA biogenesis and secondary siRNA production, leading to compromised antiviral defense and developmental defects during ToMV infection

genes: CsAG1 (Cymbidium sinense AGAMOUS-like gene 1, floral organ identity determinant, Cymbidium sinense)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of CsAG1 in Arabidopsis disrupts normal petal identity, causing homeotic conversion of petals to stamenoid structures with fused pollen sacs at the petal margin.
mechanism: CsAG1 confers a C function in Cymbidium flower development, similar to eudicots, by regulating floral organ identity through MADS-box protein interactions and CArG-box binding.

genes: VlbZIP30 (VIT_13s0175g00120, group A bZIP TF involved in ABA and drought stress signaling, grapevine)
phenotype: Overexpression of VlbZIP30 increases germination and cotyledon greening rates under mannitol and ABA stress in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: VlbZIP30 regulates downstream drought-related genes via G-box cis-element in ABA signaling pathway.

genes: GUS (β-glucosidase, reporter gene, vector)
phenotype: ProVlbZIP30 promoter drives GUS expression in Arabidopsis thaliana under ABA and dehydration stress.
mechanism: Promoter-driven GUS expression for studying gene activity.

genes: slDCL2a (slDCL2a, Dicer-like 2 isoform a, Solanum lycopersicum), slDCL2b (slDCL2b, Dicer-like 2 isoform b, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: CRISPR-induced mutations in slDCL2a and slDCL2b result in nonfunctional proteins, with deletions and substitutions in the RNase III domain. Mutant plants show altered sRNA accumulation patterns and increased susceptibility to viral infections like TMV and PVX.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing disrupts the RNase III domain of slDCL2a and slDCL2b, impairing their ability to process sRNAs. This leads to reduced miR6026 levels and altered secondary sRNA pathways, weakening antiviral defense.

genes: target mimic RNA (synthetic, miR6026 target mimic, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic expression of miR6026 target mimic RNA reduces miR6026 levels, up-regulates slDCL2a and slDCL2b, and enhances resistance to TMV and PVX infections without developmental defects.
mechanism: The miR6026 target mimic RNA sequesters miR6026, preventing its interaction with slDCL2a/b/d mRNAs. This leads to increased slDCL2 expression, which boosts sRNA production and antiviral defense.

genes: CbbL (Cyanobium Rubisco large subunit, Cyanobium), CbbS (Cyanobium Rubisco small subunit, Cyanobium)
phenotype: Expression of Cyanobium Rubisco in tobacco chloroplasts leads to autotrophic growth at 2% CO2 and formation of carboxysomes with CsoS1A and CsoS2 in CyLS-S1S2 plants.
mechanism: Cyanobium Rubisco and carboxysome proteins self-assemble into structurally intact carboxysomes in tobacco chloroplasts, enabling CO2 fixation.

genes: CbbL (Cyanobium Rubisco large subunit, Cyanobium), CbbS (Cyanobium Rubisco small subunit, Cyanobium), CsoS1A (carboxysome shell protein, Cyanobium), CsoS2 (carboxysome linker protein, Cyanobium)
phenotype: CyLS-S1S2 plants form carboxysomes with CsoS1A and CsoS2, enabling CO2 assimilation at 2% CO2, though with lower efficiency compared to wild-type tobacco.
mechanism: Carboxysomes encapsulate Cyanobium Rubisco and are structurally similar to native cyanobacterial carboxysomes, but lack vertex proteins and carbonic anhydrase, leading to kinetic impairments.

genes: OsWRKY42 (OsWRKY42, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsWRKY42 leads to enhanced callose deposition in rice and Arabidopsis but this does not enhance tolerance to bacterial infection.
mechanism: OsWRKY42 suppresses jasmonic acid (JA) mediated responses, acting as a negative regulator of JA responses induced by cell wall damage or salinity stress.

genes: OsWRKY42 (OsWRKY42, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of OsWRKY42 in Arabidopsis leads to enhanced callose deposition but does not provide enhanced tolerance to bacterial infection.
mechanism: OsWRKY42 suppresses jasmonic acid (JA) mediated responses, acting as a negative regulator of JA responses induced by cell wall damage or salinity stress.

genes: OsWRKY42 (OsWRKY42, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of OsWRKY42 in Arabidopsis transgenic plants enhances tolerance to salt stress and suppresses cellulase and salt stress induced expression of jasmonic acid biosynthesis and response genes.
mechanism: OsWRKY42 suppresses jasmonic acid (JA) mediated responses, acting as a negative regulator of JA responses induced by cell wall damage or salinity stress.

genes: PeMADS5 (PeMADS5, MADS-box transcription factor, Phyllostachys edulis)
phenotype: Overexpression of PeMADS5 in Arabidopsis triggered an earlier flowering time and the development of an aberrant flower phenotype
mechanism: PeMADS5 acts as a floral activator and is involved in bamboo flowering

genes: CmDREB6 (DREB6 dehydration-responsive element-binding transcription factor, Chrysanthemum morifolium)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmDREB6 increases heat tolerance in chrysanthemum, with survival rates of 85% and 50% in transgenic lines compared to 3.8% in wild-type plants under heat stress.
mechanism: CmDREB6 upregulates heat shock response genes (CmHsfA4, CmHSP90) and reactive oxygen species scavenging genes (CmSOD, CmCAT) to enhance thermotolerance.

genes: HvACT1 (acyltransferase 1, GenBank AB334132, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Overexpression of HvACT1 in Phyllostachys nigra cells increases p-coumaroyl agmatine (pCA) production by ~359 mg/L in suspension culture under LG2 conditions.
mechanism: HvACT1 intercepts p-coumaroyl-CoA and agmatine from lignin biosynthesis pathway, redirecting metabolic flow to produce pCA instead of feruloyl agmatine (FP).

genes: psbS (photoprotective regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of psbS increases non-photochemical quenching (NPQ), biomass by ~22% radiation use efficiency (RUE), and 26% grain yield in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: Enhanced NPQ dynamics improve photoprotection by accelerating recovery from photoinhibition and maintaining higher effective quantum yield under fluctuating light conditions.

genes: OsAT10 (Oryza sativa acyltransferase, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsAT10 increases saccharification efficiency by ~40% in green tissues and ~30% in senesced tissues of switchgrass
mechanism: OsAT10 reduces cell wall-bound ferulic acid (FA) and increases p-coumaric acid (p-CA), decreasing lignin-carbohydrate crosslinks and improving enzyme accessibility

genes: Cas9 (CRISPR-Cas9 endonuclease, Streptococcus pyogenes), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic), AtFT (flowering time gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), GBSSsgRNA4 (synthetic guide RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Targeted mutagenesis of GBSS in cassava plants results in amylose-free or reduced amylose starch, altering physicochemical properties such as lower pasting temperatures and higher viscosities.
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated disruption of GBSS and PTST1 genes reduces amylose synthesis in cassava storage roots, affecting starch granule properties and gelatinization behavior.

genes: Cas9 (CRISPR-Cas9 endonuclease, Streptococcus pyogenes), eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic), AtFT (flowering time gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), PTSTsgRNA2 (synthetic guide RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Targeted mutagenesis of PTST1 in cassava plants reduces amylose content and alters starch properties, with intermediate effects compared to wild-type, including modified viscosity profiles.
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated disruption of PTST1 affects GBSS localization and amylose synthesis in cassava storage roots, leading to reduced amylose content and altered starch granule properties.

genes: AtFH2 (At2g43800, plasmodesmata-localized formin involved in cell-to-cell trafficking, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtFH2-eGFP localizes to plasmodesmata in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtFH2 localizes to plasmodesmata in a TM domain-dependent manner.

genes: AtFH2 (At2g43800, plasmodesmata-localized formin involved in cell-to-cell trafficking, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of atfh2 mutant with AtFH2-eGFP rescues the increased SEL of PD.
mechanism: AtFH2 stabilizes actin filaments at PD, reducing SEL.

genes: BoNAC019 (Brassica oleracea NAC transcription factor, Brassica oleracea)
phenotype: Overexpression of BoNAC019 reduces drought tolerance in Arabidopsis, with 38% survival rate after three weeks of drought compared to wild type, increased leaf wilting, and reduced relative water content (50-53% vs 65% in wild type).
mechanism: BoNAC019 downregulates stress-responsive genes (AtP5CS1, AtDREB2A, AtRD29A, AtRAB18), reduces antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, POD, CAT), and decreases anthocyanin accumulation by suppressing anthocyanin biosynthesis genes (PAL, CHS, UFGT).

genes: ARF6 (Auxin Response Factor 6, Arabidopsis thaliana), ARF8 (Auxin Response Factor 8, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under the control of ARF6 promoter in transgenic Arabidopsis seedlings and TCLs, with GUS activity detected in AR primordia and adventitious root tips under darkness.
mechanism: The reporter gene GUS is expressed under the control of the ARF6 promoter, allowing visualization of ARF6 activity in root formation processes.

genes: ARF8 (Auxin Response Factor 8, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under the control of ARF8 promoter in transgenic Arabidopsis seedlings and TCLs, with GUS activity detected in AR primordia and adventitious root tips under darkness.
mechanism: The reporter gene GUS is expressed under the control of the ARF8 promoter, allowing visualization of ARF8 activity in root formation processes.

genes: ARF17 (Auxin Response Factor 17, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under the control of ARF17 promoter in transgenic Arabidopsis seedlings and TCLs, with GUS activity detected in vascular tissues and xylogenic cells under darkness.
mechanism: The reporter gene GUS is expressed under the control of the ARF17 promoter, allowing visualization of ARF17 activity in vascular and xylogenesis processes.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP overexpression serves as a control for transformation efficiency in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: UBP22 (histone H2B deubiquitinase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: UBP22 overexpression decreases histone H2Bub global level
mechanism: UBP22 is a Ubp8 homolog acting with SGF11 and ENY2 in H2Bub deubiquitination, possibly promoting transcription under optimal growth conditions

genes: UBP22 (histone H2B deubiquitinase, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: UBP22 overexpression decreases histone H2Bub global level
mechanism: UBP22 is a Ubp8 homolog acting with SGF11 and ENY2 in H2Bub deubiquitination, possibly promoting transcription under optimal growth conditions

genes: SGF11 (SAGA DUB module component, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: SGF11 overexpression increases H2Bub levels in darkness
mechanism: SGF11 is a central component of the DUBm that associates with UBP22 and ENY2 to mediate H2Bub deubiquitination

genes: SGF11 (SAGA DUB module component, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: SGF11 overexpression increases H2Bub levels in darkness
mechanism: SGF11 is a central component of the DUBm that associates with UBP22 and ENY2 to mediate H2Bub deubiquitination

genes: MIM396 (miR396 target mimic, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of 9X-MIM396 increases leaf area by up to 70% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MIM396 acts as a sponge for miR396, reducing its activity and leading to increased GRF2 and GRF3 transcript levels.

genes: At-GRF2 (growth-regulating factor 2, Arabidopsis thaliana), At-GRF3 (growth-regulating factor 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of rGRF3 increases leaf area by up to 70% in Arabidopsis thaliana, while rGRF2 requires a 25-fold increase in transcript levels for a similar effect.
mechanism: GRF3 enhances cell proliferation without altering cell size, whereas GRF2 causes morphological defects at high expression levels.

genes: At-GRF2 (growth-regulating factor 2, Arabidopsis thaliana), At-GRF3 (growth-regulating factor 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: pGRF3:rGRF3 increases leaf area more effectively than pGRF3:rGRF2 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GRF3 promoter-driven expression of GRF3 enhances organ size more efficiently than GRF2 under the same promoter.

genes: Gm-rGRF (growth-regulating factor, Glycine max), Os-rGRF4 (growth-regulating factor 4, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Expression of soybean and rice GRF3-like genes in Arabidopsis increases leaf area.
mechanism: GRF3-like sequences from soybean and rice, when decoupled from miR396 regulation, enhance organ size similarly to At-GRF3.

genes: At-GRF3 (growth-regulating factor 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of At-rGRF3 in Brassica oleracea increases leaf area by 20-32%, root growth by 10%, and seed size by 10%.
mechanism: At-GRF3 enhances cell proliferation without altering cell size, leading to increased organ size under both normal and drought conditions.

genes: CPL1 (At4g21670, RNA Polymerase II carboxyl terminal domain (CTD) phosphatase-like 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Introduction of the CPL1p:CPL1 construct reduced esr3-1 constitutive GSTF8:LUC expression and restored wild-type phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Mutations in CPL1 are responsible for the esr3 mutant phenotypes; CPL1 functions in transcriptional and post-transcriptional metabolism of mRNA, including RNA capping efficiency and decay of abnormally spliced transcripts, as well as dephosphorylation of the CTD of RNA Pol II.

genes: ZmGa1P (pollen PME, SDGa25)
phenotype: Expressing ZmGa1P endows ga1 pollen with the ability to penetrate the female barrier of Ga1-S.
mechanism: ZmGa1P encodes a pollen PME that modulates pollen tube growth.

genes: ZmGa1P (pollen PME, SDGa25)
phenotype: Expressing ZmGa1P endows ga1 pollen with the ability to penetrate the female barrier of Ga1-S.
mechanism: ZmGa1P encodes a pollen PME that modulates pollen tube growth.

genes: GmGRPL (promoter, Glyma.17G139700, Glycine max)
phenotype: GUS staining in root tips and stele of soybean hairy roots and root tips of Arabidopsis
mechanism: NA

genes: GmGRPL (Glyma.17G139700, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmGRPL promotes root growth and Al resistance in Arabidopsis
mechanism: GmGRPL reduces IAA and ethylene levels by regulating TAA1 and ACO, and enhances antioxidant activity

genes: GmGRPL (Glyma.17G139700, Glycine max)
phenotype: RNAi-GmGRPL hairy roots show increased Al sensitivity and higher ethylene content
mechanism: RNAi-GmGRPL disrupts GmGRPL function, leading to elevated IAA and ethylene levels and reduced antioxidant activity

genes: GmGRPL (Glyma.17G139700, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmGRPL in Arabidopsis promotes root growth and Al resistance
mechanism: GmGRPL reduces IAA and ethylene levels by regulating TAA1 and ACO, and enhances antioxidant activity

genes: OsbHLH035 (basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, salt-induced gene, regulates ABA-dependent and ABA-independent pathways, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Genetic complementation restores delayed seed germination and impaired recovery from salt stress in Osbhlh035 mutants to normal growth in rice.
mechanism: OsbHLH035 mediates seed germination through ABA-dependent repression of ABA biosynthesis genes (OsABA2, OsAAO3) and catabolic gene (OsABA8ox1). For salt-stress recovery, OsbHLH035 activates OsHKT1;3 and OsHKT1;5 sodium transporters in an ABA-independent pathway to prevent Na+ overaccumulation in aerial tissues.

genes: CitCHS2 (chalcone synthase, citrus, cloned)
phenotype: Overexpression of CitCHS2 increases total flavonoid production by ~41% in transgenic citrus plants compared to controls
mechanism: CitCHS2 encodes chalcone synthase, the first enzyme in the flavonoid biosynthesis pathway, which catalyzes the formation of naringenin chalcone from malonyl CoA and 4-coumaroyl CoA

genes: Cry1F (Cry1F, insecticidal toxin, Bacillus thuringiensis), PAT (phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, herbicide resistance, Streptomyces viridochromogenes)
phenotype: Overexpression of Cry1F and PAT in Bt maize provides insect resistance and herbicide tolerance
mechanism: Cry1F targets insect pests by forming pores in their gut, while PAT confers resistance to phosphinothricin herbicides by acetylating the herbicide

genes: CLPC1 (full-length, complementation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Restores normal levels of most proteins and wild-type morphology in clpc1 mutant.
mechanism: CLPC1 maintains proteome and transcriptome homeostasis.

genes: CLPC1 (ΔN, complementation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Partially restores some proteins but not the full complementation.
mechanism: CLPC1 maintains proteome and transcriptome homeostasis.

genes: CLPC2 (overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Causes chlorosis phenotypes under normal light conditions.
mechanism: CLPC2 accelerates photooxidative stress.

genes: Cas9 (Cas9 nuclease, CRISPR-associated protein 9, synthetic), gRNA1 (guide RNA 1, guide RNA, synthetic), gRNA3 (guide RNA 3, guide RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Significantly increased targeted mutagenesis efficiency in potato GBSSI gene alleles, with 79% of transformants containing dMac3 showing mutations compared to 30% with ADH enhancer and 29% with no enhancer.
mechanism: The dMac3 translational enhancer increases Cas9 protein expression, enhancing CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis efficiency in potato GBSSI gene alleles.

genes: Cas9 (Cas9 nuclease, CRISPR-associated protein 9, synthetic), gRNA1 (guide RNA 1, guide RNA, synthetic), gRNA2 (guide RNA 2, guide RNA, synthetic), gRNA3 (guide RNA 3, guide RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: 28% of transformants containing four mutant alleles in the GBSSI gene, with significantly lower amylose content in tuber starch compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: The combination of dMac3 translational enhancer and three gRNA genes increases CRISPR/Cas9 mutagenesis efficiency, leading to multiple GBSSI gene allele mutations and reduced amylose synthesis.

genes: Cas9 (Cas9 nuclease, CRISPR-associated protein 9, synthetic), gRNA1 (guide RNA 1, guide RNA, synthetic), gRNA3 (guide RNA 3, guide RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: 30% of transformants with ADH enhancer and 29% with no enhancer showed mutations in GBSSI gene alleles, with reduced amylose content in tuber starch.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9 vectors without translational enhancers (ADH or dMac3) result in lower mutagenesis efficiency compared to vectors with enhancers, leading to partial GBSSI gene mutations and reduced amylose.

genes: BnaC4.BOR1;1c (boron transporter, Brassica napus, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnaC4.BOR1;1c alleviates shoot B-deficiency symptoms in W10 by distributing more B from roots to shoots, resulting in significantly higher shoot dry weights and B concentrations compared to wild-type W10 under low B conditions.
mechanism: BnaC4.BOR1;1c functions as a boron transporter involved in xylem loading and B distribution from roots to shoots, similar to AtBOR1 in Arabidopsis. Enhanced expression increases B concentration in shoots while reducing root B content, lowering the root/shoot B ratio.

genes: MpFRH1 (FEW RHIZOIDS1, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of MpFRH1 results in few rhizoids, defective rhizoid precursor cell differentiation, and reduced gemma and mucilage papilla formation in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: MpFRH1 functions as a microRNA (miRNA) that targets and cleaves the MpRSL1 mRNA, repressing its expression and inhibiting rhizoid development.

genes: MpFRH1 (FEW RHIZOIDS1, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of the 150 bp miRNA hairpin-containing fragment of MpFRH1 results in few rhizoids and defective rhizoid precursor cell differentiation in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: The 150 bp fragment contains the predicted miRNA hairpin structure, which functions as a microRNA (miRNA) targeting MpRSL1 mRNA for cleavage, repressing its expression and inhibiting rhizoid development.

genes: MpFRH1 (FEW RHIZOIDS1, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of the MpFRH1 transcript with mutated start codons in putative small open reading frames (PSORFs) results in few rhizoids and defective rhizoid precursor cell differentiation in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: The mutated PSORFs confirm that MpFRH1 functions as a microRNA (miRNA) rather than encoding peptides, as the phenotype persists despite the mutations.

genes: MpRSL1 (RSL class I gene, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of the MpFRH1 miRNA-resistant version of MpRSL1 restores rhizoid and gemma development in the MpFRH1GOF2 mutant background in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: The miRNA-resistant MpRSL1 (MpRSL1res) is not targeted by MpFRH1 miRNA, allowing it to function and promote rhizoid and gemma development despite elevated MpFRH1 levels.

genes: MpFRH1 (FEW RHIZOIDS1, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Expression of the 3xYFP:NLS reporter under the MpFRH1 promoter reveals activity in rhizoid precursor cells, rhizoids, and epidermal papillae in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: The MpFRH1 promoter drives expression in cells undergoing rhizoid, mucilage papilla, and gemma development, indicating its role in these processes.

genes: QPT (Quinolinate phosphoribosyl transferase, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Increased scopolamine production (up to 19.34 mg/gm) and reduced nicotine content in hairy root lines
mechanism: RNAi silencing of QPT diverts methylpyrrolinium cation towards enhanced scopolamine synthesis

genes: QsMYB1 (Quercus suber MYB1, transcription factor, Quercus suber)
phenotype: Overexpression of QsMYB1::3xFLAG increases expression of target genes involved in lignin and suberin biosynthesis, transport, and assembly in Quercus suber.
mechanism: QsMYB1 regulates lignin and suberin biosynthesis by targeting genes encoding enzymes in the phenylpropanoid pathway, lipid metabolism, and transporters like ABCG and LTPs.

genes: DEP1 (DENSE AND ERECT PANICLE 1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing of DEP1 reduces panicle length in rice
mechanism: DEP1 is a pleiotropic major QTL responsible for grain number and panicle architecture

genes: SAPK1 (SAPK1, osmotic stress/ABA-activated protein kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAPK1 increases germination rates and reduces salt sensitivity in rice.
mechanism: SAPK1 promotes osmotic adjustment by increasing proline accumulation, enhances ROS detoxification by increasing ascorbic acid and SOD/CAT expression, and improves Na+/K+ homeostasis by regulating OsSOS1, OsNHX1, OsHKT1;1, and OsHKT1;5.

genes: SAPK2 (SAPK2, osmotic stress/ABA-activated protein kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAPK2 increases germination rates and reduces salt sensitivity in rice.
mechanism: SAPK2 promotes osmotic adjustment by increasing proline accumulation, enhances ROS detoxification by increasing ascorbic acid and SOD/CAT expression, and improves Na+/K+ homeostasis by regulating OsSOS1, OsNHX1, OsHKT1;1, and OsHKT1;5.

genes: TfALOG1 (TfALOG1, transcription factor, Torenia fournieri), TfALOG2 (TfALOG2, transcription factor, Torenia fournieri)
phenotype: 35S:TfALOG1 transgenic lines show disrupted petal epidermal cell development with flattened conical cells and increased cell size; 35S:TfALOG2 transgenic lines exhibit abnormal leaf mesophyll cell development and altered leaf shape.
mechanism: TfALOG1 regulates petal epidermal cell differentiation by inhibiting MIXTA-like gene expression; TfALOG2 affects leaf development through unknown mechanisms.

genes: ffgLUC (firefly luciferase, reporter gene, synthetic), TCP (TEOSINTE BRANCHED1/CYCLOIDEA/PROLIFERATING CELL FACTOR1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Impaired LUC mRNA splicing but efficient silencing of TCP target genes (~90% reduction in TCP2/3/4 expression) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Spatial interference between intron splicing and miRNA processing complexes likely causes impaired LUC mRNA splicing. miR319a is efficiently processed from the intron, leading to TCP gene silencing.

genes: ffgLUC (firefly luciferase, reporter gene, synthetic), TCP (TEOSINTE BRANCHED1/CYCLOIDEA/PROLIFERATING CELL FACTOR1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Correct LUC mRNA splicing and efficient silencing of TCP target genes (~90% reduction in TCP2/3/4 expression) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: miR319a is efficiently processed from the intron without interfering with LUC mRNA splicing. Dual functionality achieved by proper intron positioning (55 bp from 5′-splice site).

genes: ffgLUC (firefly luciferase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: 65% reduction in LUC activity in stable transformants of Arabidopsis thaliana compared to control plants.
mechanism: amiR-LUC targets LUC mRNA in-cis. Silencing efficiency in-cis is comparable to silencing in-trans (69-53% reduction in LUC activity).

genes: PHYB (PHYTOCHROME B, photoreceptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: No significant downregulation of PHYB mRNA in Arabidopsis thaliana transformants despite correct LUC mRNA splicing.
mechanism: Lack of silencing likely due to insensitive target site in PHYB mRNA forming a double-stranded stem structure.

genes: mAb CO HC (heavy chain, monoclonal antibody, synthetic), mAb CO LC (light chain, monoclonal antibody, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of mAb CO heavy and light chains in Arabidopsis thaliana results in reduced primary root length in COK plants (12.2 mm vs 23.2 mm in CO plants) under kanamycin-containing media, with no significant difference in germination rates compared to non-transgenic plants.
mechanism: ER retention motif KDEL on mAb COK heavy chain increases ER stress-related gene expression (e.g., BiP3 upregulated 3×), leading to reduced root growth via unfolded protein response (UPR) activation.

genes: mAb COK HC (heavy chain with KDEL ER retention motif, monoclonal antibody, synthetic), mAb COK LC (light chain, monoclonal antibody, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of mAb COK heavy and light chains in Arabidopsis thaliana results in significantly reduced primary root length (12.2 mm) compared to CO plants (23.2 mm) under kanamycin-containing media, with 5× higher mAb accumulation in COK plants (1,950 μg vs 410 μg).
mechanism: ER retention motif KDEL on mAb COK heavy chain enhances recombinant antibody accumulation in ER, increasing ER stress-related gene expression (BiP3 upregulated 3×) and inducing unfolded protein response (UPR) pathways (bZIP17, bZIP60, NAC103 upregulated).

genes: Pha13 (Phalaenopsis aphrodite, stress-associated protein), PhaNPR1 (Phalaenopsis aphrodite, NPR1 homolog), PhaPR1 (Phalaenopsis aphrodite, pathogenesis-related protein 1)
phenotype: Overexpression of Pha13 increases RNA levels of PhaNPR1 and PhaPR1 in Phalaenopsis aphrodite.
mechanism: Pha13 enhances expression of SA-related genes PhaNPR1 and PhaPR1, contributing to virus resistance.

genes: Pha13 (Phalaenopsis aphrodite, stress-associated protein)
phenotype: Knockdown of Pha13 decreases RNA levels of PhaNPR1 and PhaPR1 in Phalaenopsis aphrodite.
mechanism: Pha13 knockdown reduces expression of SA-related genes PhaNPR1 and PhaPR1, impairing virus resistance.

genes: PhaNPR1 (Phalaenopsis aphrodite, NPR1 homolog)
phenotype: Knockdown of PhaNPR1 does not affect Pha13 RNA accumulation in Phalaenopsis aphrodite.
mechanism: PhaNPR1 knockdown does not alter Pha13 expression, indicating unidirectional regulation.

genes: Pha13 (Phalaenopsis aphrodite, stress-associated protein)
phenotype: Overexpression of Pha13 in transgenic Arabidopsis enhances resistance to Tobacco rattle virus (TRV), Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV), and Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000.
mechanism: Pha13 overexpression activates SA-dependent and -independent immune pathways, enhancing broad-spectrum pathogen resistance.

genes: AtSAP5 (Arabidopsis thaliana, stress-associated protein)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtSAP5 in transgenic Arabidopsis enhances resistance to Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV).
mechanism: AtSAP5 overexpression activates SA-dependent and -independent immune pathways, enhancing virus resistance.

genes: AtSAP5 (Arabidopsis thaliana, stress-associated protein)
phenotype: Knockdown of AtSAP5 in transgenic Arabidopsis increases Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) accumulation.
mechanism: AtSAP5 knockdown impairs SA-dependent and -independent immune pathways, reducing virus resistance.

genes: Pha13A20m (Phalaenopsis aphrodite, A20 domain mutant of Pha13)
phenotype: Overexpression of Pha13A20m increases PhaNPR1 expression but reduces PhaRdR1 and PhaGRX expression in Phalaenopsis aphrodite.
mechanism: A20 domain mutation in Pha13 disrupts E3 ligase activity, altering regulation of SA-dependent and -independent genes.

genes: Pha13AN1m (Phalaenopsis aphrodite, AN1 domain mutant of Pha13)
phenotype: Overexpression of Pha13AN1m reduces PhaRdR1 expression but has no effect on PhaNPR1 or PhaGRX in Phalaenopsis aphrodite.
mechanism: AN1 domain mutation in Pha13 disrupts regulation of SA-independent genes like PhaRdR1.

genes: Pha13A20mAN1m (Phalaenopsis aphrodite, A20 and AN1 domain double mutant of Pha13)
phenotype: Overexpression of Pha13A20mAN1m reduces PhaRdR1 and PhaGRX expression in Phalaenopsis aphrodite.
mechanism: Double mutation in A20 and AN1 domains of Pha13 disrupts E3 ligase activity and regulation of SA-dependent and -independent genes.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Cytosolic GFP accumulates exclusively in the stele of Arabidopsis roots.
mechanism: SHR promoter activity is restricted to the stele, driving GFP expression in this tissue.

genes: SHR-GFP (short-root fused to green fluorescent protein, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SHR-GFP localizes in the nuclei of the stele and endodermis, moving from the stele to the endodermis.
mechanism: SHR is a nucleus-localized transcription factor that translocates from the stele to the endodermis.

genes: sbZIP60-GFP (spliced bZIP60 fused to green fluorescent protein, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: sbZIP60-GFP accumulates in the nuclei and cytoplasm of cells in the stele, endodermis, cortex, and epidermis, indicating transcellular movement.
mechanism: sbZIP60 translocates transcellularly from the stele to the epidermis through the endodermis and cortex.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: pBiP3-GUS expression in Col-0 shows GUS activity in the endodermis, stele, and under ER stress in cortex and epidermis. In bzip28/60; pSHR-sbZIP60-GFP/pBiP3-GUS, GUS activity mirrors sbZIP60-GFP distribution.
mechanism: BiP3 promoter drives GUS expression in response to UPR activation by sbZIP60.

genes: sbZIP60 (spliced bZIP60, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Root-expressed sbZIP60 transcripts are translocated to the shoot, inducing UPR gene expression systemically.
mechanism: pRoot promoter drives root-specific sbZIP60 expression, which translocates to the shoot to activate UPR signaling.

genes: sbZIP60-YFP (spliced bZIP60 fused to yellow fluorescent protein, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: YFP-sbZIP60 localizes to nuclei and plasmodesmata, confirming its transcellular movement and PD association.
mechanism: YFP-sbZIP60 co-localizes with PDLP1-CFP and Aniline Blue, indicating plasmodesmata targeting.

genes: PDLP1-CFP (plasmodesmata-localized protein 1 fused to cyan fluorescent protein, receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PDLP1-CFP localizes to plasmodesmata, used as a marker for co-localization with sbZIP60-YFP.
mechanism: PDLP1 is a known plasmodesmata-localized receptor-like transmembrane protein.

genes: AtIRT1 (iron transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtIRT1 increases Cd sensitivity and Cd accumulation by ~40.1% in yeast cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsZIP1 (zinc transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsZIP1 increases Cd sensitivity and Cd accumulation in yeast cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsZIP3 (zinc transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsZIP3 increases Cd sensitivity and Cd accumulation in yeast cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: Cas9 (CRISPR-associated protein 9, synthetic), sgRNA (synthetic guide RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Mutation efficiency of Cas9-mediated gene disruption in the Myb gene (Pt_Myb1R_SHAQKYF5) with 33–50% of primary colonies showing targeted mutations when delivered via bacterial conjugation or biolistic transformation.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene disruption using two sgRNAs (Myb PAM1 and PAM2) targeting the Myb transcription factor gene.

genes: OsCas9 (Cas9, nuclease, Staphylococcus pyogenes)
phenotype: Knockout of TaGASR7 leads to reduced grain length and weight in wheat.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeted mutagenesis of TaGASR7 genes.

genes: gRNA (guide RNA, targeting TaGASR7, synthetic)
phenotype: Knockout of TaGASR7 leads to reduced grain length and weight in wheat.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeted mutagenesis of TaGASR7 genes.

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient GFP expression in shoot apical meristems (SAMs) of wheat embryos.
mechanism: GFP reporter gene expression for monitoring CRISPR/Cas9 delivery and activity.

genes: AtTOP3α (TOP3α, DNA topoisomerase 3α, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of TOP3α-ΔTOPRIM in top3α mutants leads to embryo lethality, with ¼ seeds showing deformed or missing embryos.
mechanism: The TOPRIM domain is essential for catalytic activity; its deletion results in a non-functional protein that induces lethality in the absence of functional TOP3α.

genes: AtTOP3α (TOP3α, DNA topoisomerase 3α, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of TOP3α-Y342F in top3α mutants leads to embryo lethality, with ¼ seeds showing deformed or missing embryos.
mechanism: The catalytic tyrosine substitution with phenylalanine inhibits enzymatic activity, resulting in a non-functional protein that induces lethality in the absence of functional TOP3α.

genes: AtTOP3α (TOP3α, DNA topoisomerase 3α, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of TOP3α-ΔZnFT1 in top3α mutants leads to a reduced root length compared to mus81-1 mutants in the absence of MUS81.
mechanism: The zinc-finger domain T1 is required for TOP3α function in the repair of replication-associated DNA damage in a pathway parallel to MUS81.

genes: AtTOP3α (TOP3α, DNA topoisomerase 3α, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of TOP3α-ΔZnFCCHC1 in top3α mutants does not significantly affect root length in the absence of MUS81.
mechanism: The zinc-finger domains CCHC1 are not required for TOP3α function in the repair of replication-associated DNA damage in the absence of MUS81.

genes: AtTOP3α (TOP3α, DNA topoisomerase 3α, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of TOP3α-ΔZnFGRF in top3α mutants does not significantly affect root length in the absence of MUS81.
mechanism: The zinc-finger domain GRF is not required for TOP3α function in the repair of replication-associated DNA damage in the absence of MUS81.

genes: AtTOP3α (TOP3α, DNA topoisomerase 3α, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of TOP3α-ΔZnFCCHC2 in top3α mutants does not significantly affect root length in the absence of MUS81.
mechanism: The zinc-finger domain CCHC2 is not required for TOP3α function in the repair of replication-associated DNA damage in the absence of MUS81.

genes: AtTOP3α (TOP3α, DNA topoisomerase 3α, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of TOP3α-N-Term in top3α mutants rescues all mutant phenotypes, including root length, recombination rate, genotoxin sensitivity, and fertility.
mechanism: The C-terminal zinc-finger domains are expendable for most functions of the protein, and the N-terminal part is sufficient for full complementation.

genes: AtTOP3α (TOP3α, DNA topoisomerase 3α, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of TOP3α-Central in top3α mutants leads to an enhanced growth defect compared to the top3α mutant lines, with deformed cotyledons and no root formation.
mechanism: The central domain alone is insufficient for full function, leading to a rescue of the embryo lethal phenotype but with residual growth defects.

genes: AtTOP3α (TOP3α, DNA topoisomerase 3α, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of full-length TOP3α in top3α mutants rescues all mutant phenotypes, including root length, recombination rate, genotoxin sensitivity, and fertility.
mechanism: The full-length TOP3α gene restores all functions of the protein, complementing the null mutant phenotype.

genes: E. coli RusA (RusA, Holliday junction resolvase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Expression of RusA in recq4A-4 mus81-1 double mutants rescues the synthetic lethal phenotype, allowing plants to reach seed ripening.
mechanism: RusA resolves persisting Holliday junction-like recombination intermediates in the absence of both MUS81 and TOP3α zinc-finger domain T1.

genes: ERF8 (ERF8, transcriptional repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ERF8 induces programmed cell death (PCD) in Arabidopsis thaliana and Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: ERF8 induces cell death through its transcriptional repression activity.

genes: ERF8L176A/L178A (ERF8 with EAR motif mutation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Mutation of the EAR motif abolishes ERF8-induced cell death in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: ERF8 induces cell death through its transcriptional repression activity.

genes: ERF8S103A (ERF8 with Ser103 to Ala, Arabidopsis thaliana), ERF8S103D (ERF8 with Ser103 to Asp, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Neither mutation affected the localization of ERF8 to the nucleus, but mutation of all four phosphorylation sites weakened ERF8-induced cell death.
mechanism: Phosphorylation by MPK4 and MPK11 positively regulates ERF8 to induce cell death.

genes: ERF8quad A (ERF8 with all four phosphorylation sites to Ala, Arabidopsis thaliana), ERF8quad D (ERF8 with all four phosphorylation sites to Asp, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Mutation of all four phosphorylation sites weakens ERF8-induced cell death.
mechanism: Phosphorylation by MPK4 and MPK11 positively regulates ERF8 to induce cell death.

genes: TT4 (TRANSPARENT TESTA 4, target gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), SpCas9 (Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9, nuclease, Streptococcus pyogenes)
phenotype: Overexpression of CRISPR/Cas9 components increases mutagenesis frequency in TT4 gene, resulting in pale yellow seeds in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced double-strand breaks in TT4 gene lead to mutations via NHEJ or HDR repair pathways.

genes: AGO1 (ARGONAUTE1, RNAi target, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated silencing of AGO1 increases CRISPR/Cas9 mutagenesis frequency in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AGO1 silencing reduces RNA silencing, allowing higher Cas9 and sgRNA transcript levels, enhancing gene editing efficiency.

genes: p19 (tomato bushy stunt virus silencing suppressor, foreign gene, Tomato bushy stunt virus)
phenotype: Overexpression of p19 in Arabidopsis thaliana causes serrated and curled leaf phenotypes, correlating with increased CRISPR/Cas9 mutagenesis frequency.
mechanism: p19 suppresses RNA silencing, increasing sgRNA and Cas9 transcript levels, enhancing gene editing efficiency.

genes: GsMATE (GsMATE, Al-induced citrate transporter of MATE family, Glycine soja)
phenotype: Overexpression of GsMATE increases Al tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis plants by reducing Al accumulation in roots.
mechanism: GsMATE enhances Al tolerance by mediating root citrate efflux, which detoxifies Al.

genes: GsMATE (GsMATE, Al-induced citrate transporter of MATE family, Glycine soja)
phenotype: GsMATE protein localizes to the plasma membrane in Arabidopsis protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: CmANR1 (CmANR1, overexpression, Chrysanthemum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmANR1 increases adventitious root (AR) and lateral root (LR) development in chrysanthemum under tissue and hydroponic culture conditions.
mechanism: CmANR1 activates the transcription of CmPIN2 by direct binding to the CArG-box motif in its promoter, facilitating auxin polar transport.

genes: CmPIN2 (CmPIN2, promoter, Chrysanthemum)
phenotype: Used in luciferase imaging assay to study CmANR1's effect on CmPIN2 expression.
mechanism: NA

genes: CmANR1 (CmANR1, overexpression, Chrysanthemum)
phenotype: Used in co-expression with CmPIN2pro::LUC to demonstrate CmANR1's activation of CmPIN2.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaCKX2.4 (cytokinin oxidase/dehydrogenase, wheat, JN381555.1)

mechanism: Reduced TaCKX2.4 expression leads to cytokinin accumulation in inflorescence meristems, increasing reproductive organ numbers

genes: sgRNA-PDS (sgRNA-PDS, CRISPR guide RNA targeting Phytoene desaturase, synthetic)

mechanism: Higher sgRNA expression levels driven by GhU6.3 promoter enhance CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis efficiency

genes: RUP2 (RUP2, repressor of flowering under SD conditions containing UV-B, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescued early flowering phenotype of rup2 under SD + UV
mechanism: RUP2 represses UVR8-induced flowering in SD + UV by inhibiting CO activity

mechanism: LjPUB13 promoter drives GUS expression in symbiotically active root and nodule tissues

genes: Citrine-PTS1 (Citrine, peroxisome targeting signal 1, synthetic), mRFP1-PTS1 (monomeric red fluorescent protein, peroxisome targeting signal 1, synthetic)

genes: PTS2-Citrine (peroxisome targeting signal 2, Citrine, synthetic)

mechanism: Lifeact-Venus binds to F-actin, enabling visualization of actin filaments in sperm cells under the control of the PROTAMINE promoter.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
