mechanism: NA

genes: SHH1 (H3K9me2 reader, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Myc-tagged SHH1 is used to study interactions with Pol-IV in vivo.
mechanism: NA

genes: RSM1 (promoter of RSM1 gene, reporter gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter gene, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: RSM1 promoter activity was detected in all tested organs including cotyledons, hypocotyls, radicles, true leaves, roots, rosette leaves, floral organs, and developing siliques, with vascular tissue localization
mechanism: RSM1 promoter activity is regulated by ABA and salinity stress during seed germination and seedling development

genes: RSM1 (full-length gene, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP-RSM1 protein localized in the nucleus and plasma membrane vicinity of epidermal cells, guard cells, and vascular tissues
mechanism: RSM1 interacts with HY5/HYH to regulate ABI5 expression and ABA signaling

genes: RSM1 (full-length gene, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of RSM1 increased sensitivity to ABA, NaCl, and mannitol during seed germination and enhanced salt tolerance during seedling development
mechanism: RSM1 binds to ABI5 promoter to regulate ABA signaling and interacts with HY5/HYH to modulate stress responses

genes: PhCM2 (chorismate mutase 2, Petunia hybrida, synthetic)
phenotype: RNAi downregulation of PhCM2 reduces cytosolic chorismate mutase activity by 66–81%, decreases phenylalanine levels by 33–64%, and reduces phenylalanine-derived volatile emissions by 30–37% in petunia flowers.
mechanism: PhCM2 catalyzes chorismate to prephenate in the cytosol, enabling phenylalanine biosynthesis via the phenylpyruvate pathway. RNAi suppression disrupts this pathway, reducing flux through both phenylalanine biosynthetic routes.

genes: PhADT3S (arogenate dehydratase 3 short isoform, Petunia hybrida, synthetic)
phenotype: PhADT3S-GFP fusion protein localizes to the cytosol in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves, confirming the cytosolic localization of the PhADT3S isoform.
mechanism: PhADT3S catalyzes prephenate to phenylpyruvate in the cytosol, enabling phenylalanine biosynthesis via the phenylpyruvate pathway. Cytosolic localization is critical for this pathway's function.

genes: PhADT3 (arogenate dehydratase 3, Petunia hybrida, synthetic)
phenotype: RNAi downregulation of PhADT3 reduces phenylalanine levels and phenylalanine-derived volatile emissions by 19–35% in wild-type petunia flowers but has no effect in PhCM2 RNAi background.
mechanism: PhADT3 catalyzes prephenate to phenylpyruvate in the cytosol, enabling phenylalanine biosynthesis via the phenylpyruvate pathway. RNAi suppression disrupts this pathway, reducing phenylalanine production.

genes: PhpCAT (plastidial cationic amino acid transporter, Petunia hybrida, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of PhpCAT increases phenylalanine levels and phenylalanine-derived volatile emissions in both wild-type and PhCM2 RNAi petunia flowers.
mechanism: PhpCAT facilitates the export of phenylalanine from plastids, alleviating feedback inhibition and enhancing phenylalanine biosynthesis via the phenylpyruvate pathway.

genes: GmPLDα1 (phospholipase Dα1, soybean)
phenotype: PLDα1KD seeds have higher oil content, improved germination rates, and increased unsaturation in triacylglycerol (TAG) and phospholipids under high temperature and humidity conditions.
mechanism: Knockdown of GmPLDα1 reduces phosphatidic acid (PA) and lysophospholipid levels, enhances acyl editing via increased FAD2/3 expression, and upregulates ROS-scavenging genes, leading to improved lipid unsaturation and stress tolerance.

genes: RTPFPS (RbcS secretion signal fused to FPS, Arabidopsis thaliana), SaSSy (santalene synthase, Santalum album)
phenotype: Overexpression of RTPFPS and SaSSy increases production of α-santalene, α-bergamotene, epi-β-santalene, and β-santalene by ~50-fold in Nicotiana benthamiana and Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: RTPFPS and SaSSy enhance carbon flux in the MVA pathway, increasing santalene and bergamotene biosynthesis.

genes: RTPSaSSy (RbcS secretion signal fused to SaSSy, Santalum album)
phenotype: Overexpression of RTPSaSSy increases production of α-santalene, α-bergamotene, epi-β-santalene, and β-santalene by ~50-fold in Nicotiana benthamiana and Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: RTPSaSSy enhances carbon flux in the MVA pathway, increasing santalene and bergamotene biosynthesis.

genes: LTPFPS (linalool synthase transit peptide fused to FPS, Arabidopsis thaliana), SaSSy (santalene synthase, Santalum album)
phenotype: Overexpression of LTPFPS and SaSSy increases production of α-santalene, α-bergamotene, epi-β-santalene, and β-santalene by ~50-fold in Nicotiana benthamiana and Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: LTPFPS and SaSSy enhance carbon flux in the MVA pathway, increasing santalene and bergamotene biosynthesis.

genes: LTPSaSSy (linalool synthase transit peptide fused to SaSSy, Santalum album)
phenotype: Overexpression of LTPSaSSy increases production of α-santalene, α-bergamotene, epi-β-santalene, and β-santalene by ~50-fold in Nicotiana benthamiana and Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: LTPSaSSy enhances carbon flux in the MVA pathway, increasing santalene and bergamotene biosynthesis.

genes: tHMGR (truncated 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana), SaSSy (santalene synthase, Santalum album)
phenotype: Co-expression of tHMGR and SaSSy increases production of α-santalene, α-bergamotene, epi-β-santalene, and β-santalene by ~500-1000-fold in Nicotiana benthamiana and Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: tHMGR enhances carbon flux in the MVA pathway, increasing santalene and bergamotene biosynthesis.

genes: HMGR (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase, Arabidopsis thaliana), SaSSy (santalene synthase, Santalum album)
phenotype: Co-expression of HMGR and SaSSy increases production of α-santalene, α-bergamotene, epi-β-santalene, and β-santalene by ~500-1000-fold in Nicotiana benthamiana and Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: HMGR enhances carbon flux in the MVA pathway, increasing santalene and bergamotene biosynthesis.

genes: PGLP (phosphoglycerate 2-phosphatase, Flaveria bidentis, synthetic)
phenotype: Knockdown of PGLP expression in Flaveria bidentis leads to reduced PGLP protein levels (up to ~0% in line L11), impaired growth in low CO2 (atmospheric air), and severe photorespiratory phenotypes including leaf bleaching, necrosis, and complete photosynthesis inhibition at high O2 concentrations.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of PGLP disrupts 2-phosphoglycerate (2PG) degradation, leading to 2PG accumulation which inhibits key enzymes in carbon metabolism (phosphofructokinase, triosephosphate isomerase, sedoheptulose-1,7-bisphosphatase) and disrupts C4 photosynthesis. 2PG accumulation also causes amino acid and TCA cycle metabolic reprogramming.

genes: Lxx18460 (anti-sigma K factor, Leifsonia xyli subsp. xyli)
phenotype: Overexpression of Lxx18460 reduces plant height, leaf area, net photosynthetic rate, and endogenous hormones (IAA, ABA, GA3) in Nicotiana tabacum. Transgenic plants show lower antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, POD, CAT) and reduced total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC) compared to wild type.
mechanism: Lxx18460 inhibits photosynthesis by suppressing photosynthetic enzyme gene expression (e.g., Rubisco, PEPC), disrupts antioxidant defense mechanisms by reducing SOD/POD/CAT activity, and suppresses endogenous hormone biosynthesis pathways (GA3, IAA, ABA). Transcriptome analysis shows differential regulation of genes in signal transduction, carbohydrate metabolism, and secondary metabolism.

genes: GPT1 (glucose-6-phosphate/phosphate translocator 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GPT1-eYFP rescues pollen viability, germination, and lipid accumulation in gpt1 mutant plants.
mechanism: GPT1-eYFP promotes lipid body biosynthesis by transporting Glc6P into plastids for fatty acid synthesis.

genes: ADH1 (alcohol dehydrogenase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CRISPR-induced mutations in ADH1 result in allyl-alcohol resistance and homozygous knockout alleles in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9 system with sgRNA targeting ADH1 induces double-strand breaks, leading to homology-independent repair and loss-of-function mutations.

genes: ADH1 (alcohol dehydrogenase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: UBI10 promoter-driven Cas9_2 increases mutation rates in ADH1 compared to 35S promoter in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: UBI10 promoter enhances germline-specific Cas9 expression, improving CRISPR efficiency in ADH1 targeting.

genes: ADH1 (alcohol dehydrogenase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: YAO promoter-driven Cas9_3 with E9 terminator and sgRNAEF increases CRISPR efficiency in ADH1 knockout in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: YAO promoter enhances germline Cas9_3 expression, while sgRNAEF modification improves sgRNA stability for ADH1 targeting.

genes: ADH1 (alcohol dehydrogenase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Plant codon-optimized Cas9_3 with intron and sgRNAEF achieves high mutation rates in ADH1 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Cas9_3's plant codon optimization, intron, and dual NLSs enhance expression and nuclear localization for efficient ADH1 targeting.

genes: ADH1 (alcohol dehydrogenase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Human codon-optimized Cas9_4 with dual NLSs increases mutation rates in ADH1 compared to Arabidopsis-optimized Cas9_2 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Cas9_4's human codon optimization and dual NLSs enhance nuclear localization and activity for ADH1 targeting.

genes: ADH1 (alcohol dehydrogenase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Modified sgRNAEF with extended hairpin and A-T transversion increases mutation efficiency in ADH1 compared to classic sgRNA in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: sgRNAEF's structural modifications enhance stability and Cas9 binding for improved ADH1 targeting.

genes: ADH1 (alcohol dehydrogenase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: UBI10 promoter and Ocs terminator combination with Cas9_2 and sgRNAEF achieves high mutation rates in ADH1 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: UBI10 promoter enhances germline Cas9_2 expression, while Ocs terminator and sgRNAEF improve sgRNA stability for ADH1 targeting.

genes: ADH1 (alcohol dehydrogenase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: YAO promoter and plant codon-optimized Cas9_3 with E9 terminator and sgRNAEF achieve high mutation rates in ADH1 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: YAO promoter enhances germline Cas9_3 expression, while E9 terminator and sgRNAEF improve sgRNA stability for ADH1 targeting.

genes: ZmGPDH1 (NAD+-dependent glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmGPDH1 enhances salinity/osmotic stress tolerance in Arabidopsis by increasing glycerol production, antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, CAT, APX), and maintaining cellular redox homeostasis (NADH/NAD+, ASA/DHA, GSH/GSSG).
mechanism: ZmGPDH1 modulates glycerol synthesis, stomatal closure, cellular redox, and ROS homeostasis to confer stress tolerance.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: The proZmGPDH1::GUS construct reveals tissue-specific and stress-responsive expression of the ZmGPDH1 promoter in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: GUS activity under the ZmGPDH1 promoter indicates promoter activity in response to salinity and osmotic stress.

genes: OsRH58 (Oryza sativa, DEAD-box RNA helicase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsRH58 increases plant height, seed yield, and stress tolerance under salt/drought conditions in Arabidopsis thaliana. Transgenic plants show faster germination, better seedling growth, and higher survival rates under stress.
mechanism: OsRH58 confers stress tolerance by increasing translation of chloroplast mRNAs through RNA chaperone activity, leading to elevated levels of chloroplast proteins like ClpB3, PsbA, PetA, POR, and RbcL under stress.

genes: CrFAX1 (CrFAX1, fatty acid exporter, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii)
phenotype: Overexpression of CrFAX1 increases the intracellular lipid content, especially triacylglycerol (TAG) content in C. reinhardtii by ~38%.
mechanism: CrFAX1 mediates fatty acid export from chloroplast into the cytosol for Acyl-CoA synthesis, which is then used for TAG biosynthesis.

genes: CrFAX2 (CrFAX2, fatty acid exporter, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii)
phenotype: Overexpression of CrFAX2 increases the intracellular lipid content, especially triacylglycerol (TAG) content in C. reinhardtii by ~38%.
mechanism: CrFAX2 mediates fatty acid export from chloroplast into the cytosol for Acyl-CoA synthesis, which is then used for TAG biosynthesis.

genes: Vp23 (coat protein subunit, Tomato torrado virus), Vp26 (coat protein subunit, Tomato torrado virus), Vp35 (coat protein subunit, Tomato torrado virus)
phenotype: Induction of necrosis in Solanum lycopersicum (cv. Beta Lux) when expressed from PVX-based vector, with Vp26 causing severe systemic necrosis
mechanism: Increased PR10 mRNA accumulation and ribonuclease activity associated with Vp26 expression

genes: TaPR-1-1 (pathogenesis-related protein 1, wheat, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaPR-1-1 enhances freezing tolerance (70% survival vs 40% control), salinity tolerance (longer root growth and higher chlorophyll content), and osmotic tolerance (100% green cotyledons vs 50% control) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: CgSVP2 (CgSVP2, CgSVP gene, Cymbidium goeringii)
phenotype: Transient over-expression of CgSVP2 inhibits flower bud development, showing 16–21% decrease in length and 10–14% decrease in width of flower buds compared to control.
mechanism: CgSVP genes act as repressors of flower bud development, and their decreased expression during cold treatment negates the repressive effects, allowing floral growth.

genes: eGFP (eGFP, enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Used as a control for transient expression experiments; no specific phenotype reported.
mechanism: NA

genes: BSK3 (Brassinosteroid Signaling Kinase 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of brr1 mutant phenotypes including root growth defect and BL resistance
mechanism: BSK3 genomic DNA complements the brr1 mutant phenotypes by restoring normal BR signaling

genes: BSK3 (Brassinosteroid Signaling Kinase 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Full rescue of bsk3-1 mutant phenotypes but less efficient than wild-type BSK3
mechanism: TPR deletion impairs BSK3 function, suggesting TPR motifs are required for full function in BR signaling

genes: BSK3 (Brassinosteroid Signaling Kinase 3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Plasma membrane localization of BSK3-mCitrine protein
mechanism: N-myristoylation is required for BSK3 plasma membrane localization

genes: GAUT4 (GAUT4, pectin biosynthesis gene, switchgrass)
phenotype: GAUT4 knockdown in switchgrass reduces hemicellulose molecular weight by 12-20% (Mn) and 7-14% (Mw), decreases ferulic acid (FA) content in lignin, and reduces lignin-carbohydrate cross-linkages (LCC), leading to lower biomass recalcitrance and enhanced lignin migration during pretreatment.
mechanism: GAUT4 down-regulation reduces pectin biosynthesis, decreasing homogalacturonan (HG) and rhamnogalacturonan II (RGII) cross-linking with hemicellulose and lignin. This reduces hemicellulose molecular weight, FA content, and LCC linkages, increasing cell wall porosity and lignin mobility during pretreatment.

genes: nptII (nopaline synthase, nptII gene, pROK2), multiple cloning site (multiple cloning site, synthetic, pROK2)
phenotype: Overexpression of nptII in SALK lines leads to antibiotic resistance gene silencing, resulting in loss of kanamycin resistance after several generations.
mechanism: Epigenetic silencing via RdDM pathways involving 21/22nt and 24nt siRNAs targeting nptII and vector elements, leading to DNA methylation and gene inactivation.

genes: bar (phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, bar gene, pCSA110)
phenotype: Overexpression of bar in SAIL_232 confers herbicide resistance, with functional transgene expression confirmed by herbicide application.
mechanism: Transgene expression driven by mannopine synthase promoter, targeted by 21nt siRNAs but not 24nt siRNAs, avoiding full RdDM-mediated silencing.

genes: PlHSP70 (heat shock protein 70, Paeonia lactiflora)
phenotype: Overexpression of PlHSP70 increases high temperature tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana by reducing hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anion free radical (O2·-), and relative electric conductivity (REC) while increasing chlorophyll fluorescence parameters (Fv/Fm, Y(II), qN, ETR) by ~6.77-163.09% under stress.
mechanism: PlHSP70 acts as a molecular chaperone to reduce reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and maintain cell membrane integrity, thereby alleviating photoinhibition and chloroplast damage during high temperature stress.

genes: SlNPR1 (Nonexpressor of pathogenesis-related gene 1, drought response regulator, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: slnpr1 mutants exhibit reduced drought tolerance with increased stomatal aperture, higher electrolytic leakage, MDA and H2O2 levels, and lower antioxidant enzyme activity compared to wild type plants
mechanism: SlNPR1 regulates drought tolerance by modulating stomatal closure, antioxidant enzyme activity, and expression of drought-related genes (SlGST, SlDHN, SlDREB) through SA and ABA signaling pathways

genes: MKKK62 (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 62, Oryza sativa L., cloned from ZH11)
phenotype: Overexpression of MKKK62 in rice leads to loss of seed dormancy and decreased abscisic acid (ABA) sensitivity, with seeds germinating at 3 days after imbibition (DAI) compared to wild type.
mechanism: MKKK62 negatively controls seed dormancy by regulating the transcription of OsMFT, a homolog of a gene that controls seed dormancy in wheat.

genes: MKK3 (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase 3, Oryza sativa L.), MAPK7 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 7, Oryza sativa L.), MAPK14 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 14, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: Knockout of MKK3 or MAPK7/14 in MKKK62-overexpressing rice lines restored seed dormancy, with seeds from homozygous OE/mkk3 and OE/mapk7/mapk14 lines not germinating at 23 days after heading (DAH).
mechanism: The MKKK62-MKK3-MAPK7/14 module controls seed dormancy by regulating the transcription of OsMFT, a gene homologous to wheat TaMFT, which is involved in seed dormancy regulation.

genes: IDD4 (promoter, 2.5 kb upstream of translational start, Arabidopsis thaliana), GUS (reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS reporter expression in cotyledons, root tips, rosette leaves, and flower organs of Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NA

genes: IDD4 (promoter, 2.5 kb upstream of translational start, Arabidopsis thaliana), NLS:3xGFP (reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: NLS:3xGFP reporter expression in trichomes, stomata, epidermal cells, and mesophyll cells of Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NA

genes: IDD4 (full-length, Arabidopsis thaliana), YFP (tag, synthetic)
phenotype: Restored wild-type growth phenotype in idd4 mutant background
mechanism: Complementation of IDD4 knockout phenotype by re-introducing functional IDD4:YFP under native promoter

genes: IDD4 (phospho-mutant S73A/T130A, Arabidopsis thaliana), RFP (tag, synthetic)
phenotype: Reduced bacterial titers in Pst DC3000 hrcC- infection compared to wild-type and IDD4-DD lines
mechanism: Phospho-dead IDD4-AA shows weak DNA-binding and low transcriptional activation after flg22-treatment

genes: BSR2 (AK072163, cytochrome P450 protein, Oryza sativa)
gene_construct: Zea mays ubiquitin promoter-BSR2-nopaline synthase terminator
phenotype: Resistance to Pst DC3000, C. higginsianum, and R. solani in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NA

genes: eGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, reporter gene, synthetic), nptII (kanamycin resistance gene, Agrobacterium tumefaciens, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of eGFP enables visual detection of transgenic cells via green fluorescence; nptII confers kanamycin resistance for selection of transformed grapevine genotypes
mechanism: Agrobacterium-mediated transformation using binary vector pK7WG2 with eGFP and nptII cassettes

genes: GhWRKY33 (GhWRKY33, transcription factor, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhWRKY33 increases transgenic plant sensitivity to drought stress, with reduced chlorophyll content (~15% lower) and proline accumulation (~40% lower) under drought conditions.
mechanism: GhWRKY33 overexpression impairs stomatal closure during drought, leading to higher water loss rates and reduced ABA responsiveness. It negatively regulates drought-related genes (RD29A, DREB2A, SOS2) and ABA-responsive genes (ABI1, RAB18) by binding to W-box elements in their promoters.

genes: GhWRKY33 (GhWRKY33, transcription factor, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhWRKY33 reduces transgenic plant sensitivity to ABA, with increased seed germination rates and root growth under ABA treatment. Stomatal closure is impaired in ABA-treated transgenic plants.
mechanism: GhWRKY33 overexpression disrupts ABA signaling by reducing ABA-induced stomatal closure and altering expression of ABA-responsive genes (ABI1, RAB18). It acts as a negative regulator in ABA-mediated drought response pathways.

genes: GUSmgfp5 (GUS::GFP fusion, synthetic)
phenotype: OMG1 promoter activity observed in roots, pollen tubes, and heightened upon wounding in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: OMG1 promoter activity is induced by wounding, leading to increased GUS activity in roots and leaves.

genes: OMG1cds-sGFPS65T (OMG1::GFP fusion, synthetic)
phenotype: OMG1 localizes to the nucleus in Nicotiana benthamiana leaf cells.
mechanism: The conserved CCT domain in OMG1 mediates nuclear localization.

genes: TaCNR2 (Triticum aestivum, heavy metal transporter, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaCNR2 in Arabidopsis increases tolerance to Cd, Zn, and Mn, with root length and fresh weight distinctly better than wild-type under heavy metal treatments (p < 0.05).
mechanism: TaCNR2 enhances translocation of Cd and Zn from roots to shoots, but prevents Mn translocation in Arabidopsis. It may bind and transport heavy metals, reducing their toxicity.

genes: NobZIP1 (Nannochloropsis oceanica, transcription factor, Nannochloropsis oceanica)
phenotype: Overexpression of NobZIP1 increases extracellular lipid content by 16.2-fold and intracellular lipid content by 1-fold in Nannochloropsis oceanica without impairing growth or photosynthetic efficiency.
mechanism: NobZIP1 upregulates lipid biosynthetic genes (ACBP, KAS, LC-FACS, LPAAT) and downregulates cell wall carbohydrate genes (CPS, UGDH), leading to lipid overproduction and secretion via weakened cell walls.

genes: NobZIP1 (Nannochloropsis oceanica, transcription factor, Nannochloropsis oceanica)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of NobZIP1 does not alter growth or photosynthetic efficiency but reduces lipid content compared to overexpressing cells.
mechanism: NobZIP1 silencing increases carbohydrate and protein content while decreasing lipid content, indicating its role in redirecting carbon flux toward lipid biosynthesis.

genes: UGDH (Nannochloropsis oceanica, UDP-glucose dehydrogenase, Nannochloropsis oceanica)
phenotype: Overexpression of UGDH reduces extracellular and intracellular lipid content while increasing carbohydrate and protein content in Nannochloropsis oceanica.
mechanism: UGDH overexpression enhances carbohydrate metabolism and strengthens cell walls, redirecting carbon flux away from lipid biosynthesis.

genes: phaC1 (PHA synthase, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of phaC1 increases PHA levels up to 1.6 mg/g DW in flax, with line 11 showing 3-hydroxyoctanoic acid as dominant PHA monomer and improved mechanical properties including 2.4-fold higher tensile strength compared to wild-type.
mechanism: PHA synthesis enhances mechanical properties through increased cellulose crystallinity (2x higher crystallinity index) and altered cell wall composition (elevated cellulose-to-lignin ratio in line 11).

genes: G6PD5 (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase 5, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of G6PD5 increases ABA tolerance in Arabidopsis, with significantly higher seed germination rates and reduced ABA sensitivity in root growth compared to wild type.
mechanism: G6PD5 enhances ROS scavenging by increasing NADPH production for the ascorbate-glutathione cycle, suppresses ABA signaling via downregulation of ABI5, and modulates ABA biosynthesis/catabolism genes (NCED6/9, CYP707A3/4).

genes: AtSIZ1 (AtSIZ1, RNAi suppression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced AtSIZ1 expression in inflorescence stem cells leads to thinner secondary cell walls in interfascicular fiber cells and xylary fiber cells.
mechanism: RNAi suppression of AtSIZ1 disrupts its role in regulating the transcriptional network controlling secondary cell wall (SCW) formation.

genes: AtSIZ1 (AtSIZ1, RNAi suppression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced AtSIZ1 expression in inflorescence stem cells leads to thinner secondary cell walls in interfascicular fiber cells and xylary fiber cells.
mechanism: RNAi suppression of AtSIZ1 disrupts its role in regulating the transcriptional network controlling secondary cell wall (SCW) formation.

genes: gRNA1 (ORF1, CRISPR guide RNA targeting BSOLV, synthetic), gRNA2 (ORF2, CRISPR guide RNA targeting BSOLV, synthetic), gRNA3 (ORF3, CRISPR guide RNA targeting BSOLV, synthetic)
phenotype: Knockout of integrated eBSOLV sequences in Gonja Manjaya plantain prevents activation of episomal BSV under stress conditions, resulting in asymptomatic plants with no viral symptoms
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in all three ORFs of eBSOLV disrupt viral gene expression and prevent production of infectious episomal BSV

genes: SlMYB75 (SlMYB75, transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlMYB75 induces anthocyanin accumulation in vegetative and reproductive organs, including purple pigmentation in stamens and fruits, smaller seeds, delayed fruit ripening (3-5 days), and increased ethylene production during ripening.
mechanism: SlMYB75 regulates the phenylpropanoid pathway, upregulating genes involved in anthocyanin biosynthesis (e.g., phenylalanine ammonia-lyase, chalcone synthase) and aroma volatile metabolism (e.g., LOXC, AADC2, TPS). It binds to conserved cis-elements MYBPLANT (AAACCAACCC) and MYBPZM (ACCTACCC) in target gene promoters.

genes: lncRNA23468 (lncRNA23468, long non-coding RNA, tomato), mlncRNA23468 (mlncRNA23468, mutated lncRNA23468, tomato)
phenotype: Overexpression of lncRNA23468 increases resistance to P. infestans by suppressing miR482b and upregulating NBS-LRR genes in tomato.
mechanism: lncRNA23468 acts as a miRNA decoy, sequestering miR482b and preventing its repression of NBS-LRR genes, which are involved in pathogen resistance.

genes: lncRNA23468 (lncRNA23468, long non-coding RNA, tomato)
phenotype: Silencing of lncRNA23468 decreases resistance to P. infestans by increasing miR482b accumulation and downregulating NBS-LRR genes in tomato.
mechanism: lncRNA23468 silencing reduces its decoy activity for miR482b, allowing miR482b to repress NBS-LRR genes, which are critical for pathogen resistance.

genes: Solyc02g036270.2 (NBS-LRR, nucleotide-binding site-leucine-rich repeat, tomato)
phenotype: Silencing of NBS-LRR gene Solyc02g036270.2 increases susceptibility to P. infestans in tomato.
mechanism: NBS-LRR genes are direct targets of miR482b; their silencing reduces pathogen resistance by impairing the plant's defense response.

genes: miR482b (miR482b, microRNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR482b in tobacco reduces its accumulation when co-expressed with lncRNA23468, validating the decoy mechanism.
mechanism: lncRNA23468 sequesters miR482b in tobacco, demonstrating the ceRNA effect across species.

genes: AtRPL18 (Arabidopsis ribosomal protein L18, phloem-specific ribosome tagging, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of His6-FLAG-tagged AtRPL18 in phloem tissues enables isolation of phloem-specific ribosome-associated mRNAs via anti-FLAG affinity purification
mechanism: Phloem-specific expression of tagged ribosomal protein allows immunopurification of translating ribosomes to capture tissue-specific mRNAs

genes: AtRPL18 (Arabidopsis ribosomal protein L18, phloem-specific ribosome tagging, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of His6-FLAG-tagged AtRPL18 in phloem companion cells enables isolation of phloem-specific ribosome-associated mRNAs via anti-FLAG affinity purification
mechanism: Phloem-specific expression of tagged ribosomal protein allows immunopurification of translating ribosomes to capture tissue-specific mRNAs

genes: AtRPL18 (Arabidopsis ribosomal protein L18, phloem-specific ribosome tagging, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of His6-FLAG-tagged AtRPL18 in phloem companion cells and bundle sheath cells enables isolation of phloem-specific ribosome-associated mRNAs via anti-FLAG affinity purification
mechanism: Phloem-specific expression of tagged ribosomal protein allows immunopurification of translating ribosomes to capture tissue-specific mRNAs

genes: SlPG (pectin methylesterase, Solanum lycopersicum), SlEXP1 (expansin, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Suppression of SlPG and SlEXP1 in ripe fruit increases fruit firmness by ~30% and reduces cracking incidence by ~13% in Solanum lycopersicum
mechanism: Reduced cell wall disassembly due to suppressed PG and EXP1 activity maintains pectin integrity, thicker cell walls, and higher total soluble solids (TSS) in pg/exp transgenic tomatoes

genes: qPE9-1 (qPE9-1, G protein gamma subunit, Oryza sativa), qpe9-1 (qPE9-1, G protein gamma subunit, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of qPE9–1 leads to 4.37–5.08% reduction in grain length and 6.17–9.52% reduction in 1000-grain weight in Nipponbare.
mechanism: qPE9–1 acts as a positive regulator of grain length and weight; its knockout results in short, small grains due to loss of the C-terminal VWFC domains' inhibitory effect on the N-terminal GGL domain.

genes: qPE9-1 (qPE9-1, G protein gamma subunit, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of full-length qPE9–1 increases grain length by 11.36% and 1000-grain weight by 14.44% in Nipponbare.
mechanism: qPE9–1 acts as a positive regulator of grain length and weight; its full-length form promotes grain development by suppressing the negative effects of the N-terminal GGL domain via C-terminal VWFC domains.

genes: qPE9-1 (qPE9-1, G protein gamma subunit, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of D3 (GGL with one VWFC domain) increases grain length by 6.13% and 1000-grain weight by 7.88% in Nipponbare.
mechanism: The C-terminal VWFC domains in D3 partially suppress the N-terminal GGL domain's negative effects, leading to mild grain size increase.

genes: qPE9-1 (qPE9-1, G protein gamma subunit, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of D4 (GGL with two or three VWFC domains) increases grain length by 11.96% and 1000-grain weight by 12.71% in Nipponbare.
mechanism: The C-terminal VWFC domains in D4 effectively suppress the N-terminal GGL domain's negative effects, leading to grain size similar to full-length qPE9–1.

genes: qPE9-1 (qPE9-1, G protein gamma subunit, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of qPE9–1 in Wuxianggeng 9 increases grain yield per plant by 9.90–16.35% but causes lodging in some years.
mechanism: qPE9–1 promotes plant growth and grain yield by increasing grain size and 1000-grain weight, but its overexpression leads to taller plants with reduced lodging resistance.

genes: LBD16 (LATERAL ORGAN BOUNDARIES DOMAIN 16, Arabidopsis thaliana), LBD18 (LATERAL ORGAN BOUNDARIES DOMAIN 18, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of LBD16 or LBD18 under their own promoters in lbd16 or lbd18 mutants rescued the reduced number of ARs to wild-type levels.
mechanism: LBD16 and LBD18 play significant roles in AR development by regulating cell cycle gene expression.

genes: LBD16 (LATERAL ORGAN BOUNDARIES DOMAIN 16, Arabidopsis thaliana), LBD18 (LATERAL ORGAN BOUNDARIES DOMAIN 18, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of LBD16 or LBD18 in arf7 arf19 mutants rescued LR formation but did not induce AR formation.
mechanism: LBD16 and LBD18 require additional factors produced by ARF7 and ARF19 to induce AR initiation.

genes: LBD16 (LATERAL ORGAN BOUNDARIES DOMAIN 16, Arabidopsis thaliana), LBD18 (LATERAL ORGAN BOUNDARIES DOMAIN 18, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: LBD16:SRDX and LBD18:SRDX suppressed cell cycle gene promoter activities during AR formation.
mechanism: LBD16 and LBD18 regulate expression of cell cycle genes during AR development at distinctive stages.

genes: Zmm22 (Zm00001d042315, MADS box transcription factor 69, Zea mays), Zm00001d021188 (Flowering time control protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of Zmm22 significantly reduces plant height (19-50% reduction), stalk diameter (11-35% reduction), tassel branch number (35-50% reduction), and stover yield (37-50% reduction) in transgenic maize lines compared to wild-type siblings.
mechanism: Zmm22 overexpression induces pleiotropic effects on plant architecture by regulating vegetative to floral transition pathways, reducing overall plant size through altered cell proliferation and organogenesis.

genes: CUC2 (RFP-tagged, synthetic), AlcR (synthetic)
phenotype: Ethanol-inducible CUC2 expression restores tooth formation in cuc2-1 mutant leaves, with tooth aspect ratio and sinus angle dynamics resembling wild-type development.
mechanism: CUC2 acts as a quantitative trigger for tooth outgrowth by activating downstream relays (CUC3, KLUH, and auxin response).

genes: ZmCCT10 (ZmCCT10, flowering repressor, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmCCT10 in maize results in delayed flowering, increased plant height (up to 300 cm), increased leaf number (up to 38 leaves), and severe architectural modifications including vegetative apical structures (phyllody) and extensive brace roots.
mechanism: ZmCCT10 represses flowering by downregulating florigen genes (ZCN8, ZCN7, ZCN12, ZCN15) and floral activators (ZmEhd1). High expression of ZmCCT10 delays floral transition, leading to prolonged vegetative growth and altered meristem identity.

genes: ZmCCT10 (ZmCCT10, flowering repressor, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmCCT10 in maize results in extreme delayed flowering, plant heights up to 300 cm, 38 leaves, vegetative apical structures (phyllody), and extensive brace roots. BSVpro-driven expression causes more severe phenotypes than UBIpro-driven expression.
mechanism: ZmCCT10 represses flowering by downregulating florigen genes (ZCN8, ZCN7, ZCN12, ZCN15) and floral activators (ZmEhd1). High expression of ZmCCT10 delays floral transition, leading to prolonged vegetative growth and altered meristem identity.

genes: MdTLP7 (full-length, stress tolerance gene, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of full-length MdTLP7 increases abiotic stress tolerance (osmotic, salt, cold, heat) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: MdTLP7 localizes to the plasma membrane and participates in stress signal transduction via PIP2 binding site K190/R192.

genes: MdTLP7 (tubby domain, stress tolerance gene, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of truncated MdTLP7 (tubby domain) increases abiotic stress tolerance (osmotic, salt) in Arabidopsis thaliana, but with reduced efficacy for cold/heat stress.
mechanism: Tubby domain localization to plasma membrane via PIP2 binding site K190/R192 contributes to stress tolerance, though F-box domain may provide synergistic effects.

genes: MdTLP7 (stress tolerance gene, Malus domestica)
phenotype: MdTLP7-GFP fusion protein localizes to the plasma membrane in tobacco leaf cells.
mechanism: Plasma membrane localization of MdTLP7 via PIP2 binding site K190/R192 confirmed by GFP fusion protein visualization.

genes: LcMYB5 (Litchi chinensis MYB transcription factor, anthocyanin biosynthesis regulator, Litchi chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of LcMYB5 in tobacco results in enhanced anthocyanin biosynthesis (4.0–5.5 mg g⁻¹ FW in petals vs 1.4 mg g⁻¹ FW in wild type), increased flower size (29 mm corolla diameter vs 24 mm), and significantly lower pH values in petals and leaves compared to wild type.
mechanism: LcMYB5 upregulates endogenous bHLH regulators (NtAn1a, NtAn1b) and key structural genes (NtCHI, NtF3H, NtDFR) in anthocyanin biosynthesis. It also induces vacuolar acidification by downregulating vacuolar pH.

genes: LcMYB5 (Litchi chinensis MYB transcription factor, anthocyanin biosynthesis regulator, Litchi chinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of LcMYB5 in petunia W115 (an2−an4−) results in lavender pink corolla coloration (vs white in untransformed line), increased anthocyanin accumulation in corollas, and significantly lower pH values in flowers and leaves compared to wild type.
mechanism: LcMYB5 upregulates endogenous bHLH regulator PhAN1 and key structural gene PhDFR in anthocyanin biosynthesis. It also induces vacuolar acidification by downregulating vacuolar pH and upregulating cell acidification genes (PhPH5).

genes: AtCSN4 (At5g42970, COP9 Signalosome subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RNAi-AtCSN4 exhibited significant delay in rosette development compared to Col-0, with shorter inflorescence stems and a dwarf phenotype. RNAi-AtCSN4 plants had very short internodes between siliques resulting in a 'bushy' plant phenotype.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtCSN4 (At5g42970, COP9 Signalosome subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Plants overexpressing AtCSN4 (line 35S::AtCSN4) had normal development and adult plants had similar size as WT Col-0 plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtTCTP (At3g16640, translationally controlled tumor protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtCSN4 (At5g42970, COP9 Signalosome subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The AtTCTPg-GFP/35S::AtCSN4-Flag line was used to study the interaction between AtTCTP and AtCSN4. This construct was part of experiments confirming their physical interaction.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtTCTP (At3g16640, translationally controlled tumor protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtCSN4 (At5g42970, COP9 Signalosome subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Crosses between RNAi-AtTCTP and AtCSN4 overexpressor lines (line RNAi-AtTCTP/35S::AtCSN4) yielded plants with delayed growth compared to the WT, similar to the single RNAi-AtTCTP and RNAi-AtCSN4 knockdown plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtTCTP (At3g16640, translationally controlled tumor protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtCSN4 (At5g42970, COP9 Signalosome subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Crosses between RNAi-AtCSN4 and AtTCTP overexpressor lines (line 35S::AtTCTP/RNAi-AtCSN4) yielded plants with delayed growth compared to the WT, similar to the single RNAi-AtTCTP and RNAi-AtCSN4 knockdown plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtTCTP (At3g16640, translationally controlled tumor protein, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtCSN4 (At5g42970, COP9 Signalosome subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The double overexpressor line (35S::AtCSN4/35S::AtTCTP) exhibited no additive effect and behaved as the single overexpressor line 35S::AtTCTP (Fig 2).
mechanism: NA

genes: AtDDM1 (DDM1, DNA damage repair gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of DDM1 mutation rescues DNA damage-sensitive phenotypes in ddm1 mutants, restoring WT-like growth after gamma irradiation.
mechanism: DDM1 facilitates γ-H2AX and RAD51 induction for HR repair, and chromatin remodeling to enable DSB repair.

genes: CfJMT (jasmonic acid carboxyl methyltransferase, Cymbidium faberi)
phenotype: Constitutive ectopic expression of CfJMT in tomato could not increase volatile emission of MeJA, but increased transcription levels of MeJA biosynthesis genes (SlLOX, SlAOS, SlAOC, SlOPR3, SlJMT) by 11.49- to 28.66-fold following wounding compared to wild-type controls
mechanism: CfJMT may participate in resistance to abiotic stress by modulating MeJA biosynthesis gene expression in response to wounding

genes: PbLAC1 (PbLAC1, laccase gene involved in lignin synthesis, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbLAC1 in Arabidopsis thaliana increased lignin content in inflorescence stems by ~17% compared to wild-type and significantly increased cell wall thickness in xylem and interfascicular fibre cells.
mechanism: PbLAC1 is involved in lignin polymerization and cell wall development, as evidenced by increased lignin accumulation and cell wall thickening in transgenic plants.

genes: PbLAC14 (PbLAC14, laccase gene involved in lignin synthesis, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbLAC14 in Arabidopsis thaliana did not significantly increase lignin content or cell wall thickness compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: SlGLK2 (SlGLK2, transcription factor for chloroplast differentiation, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlGLK2 in aurea Slglk2 mutant background increases chlorophyll content in green fruits by ~3-fold, restores wild-type tocopherol levels in ripe fruits, and enhances total soluble solids by ~20% in ripe fruits.
mechanism: SlGLK2 promotes chloroplast biogenesis with increased grana stacking and reduced starch grains, enhances phytol recycling via upregulation of SlVTE5/SlVTE6, and increases chlorophyll biosynthesis genes (SlDXS, SlGGDR).

genes: TIpRFD1 (promoter), GUS (beta-glucuronidase), eYFP (enhanced Yellow Fluorescent Protein)
phenotype: Expression of GUS and eYFP reporter genes in transient assays in N. benthamiana and A. thaliana leaves
mechanism: TIpRFD1 promoter drives reporter gene expression in transient expression assays

genes: TIpRFD1 (promoter), RFD1 (riboflavin biosynthesis enzyme)
phenotype: Complementation of rfd1-1 photo-bleaching phenotype in Arabidopsis
mechanism: TIpRFD1 promoter drives RFD1-FLAG expression to restore wild-type phenotype

genes: TIpQUA1 (promoter), QUA1 (glycosyltransferase for pectin biosynthesis)
phenotype: Complementation of qua1-1 dwarf hypocotyl and cell adhesion defects in Arabidopsis
mechanism: TIpQUA1 promoter drives QUA1-FLAG expression to restore wild-type phenotype

genes: FWA (flowering time regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic activation of FWA in T1 and T2 transgenic Arabidopsis plants, with strong activation observed in T2 plants (Supplementary Fig. 2a-c). RNA-seq confirmed robust FWA upregulation (Fig. 1a).
mechanism: SunTag VP64-mediated transcriptional activation via dCas9-10×GCN4 and scFv-sfGFP-VP64 recruitment to the FWA promoter.

genes: FWA (flowering time regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: FWA expression levels in T1 and T2 plants reached levels similar to fwa epiallele plants, resulting in a late flowering phenotype (Supplementary Fig. 5a; Fig. 1c). RNA-seq confirmed FWA transcript levels matched fwa plants (Fig. 1c).
mechanism: Dual gRNA (gRNA4+gRNA17) targeting the FWA promoter with 22aa linkers enhanced VP64 mobility and transcriptional activation.

genes: FWA (flowering time regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Targeted methylation establishment at the FWA promoter in fwa epiallele plants, leading to FWA silencing and early flowering (Fig. 3a-d). Methylation was meiotically heritable in T2- plants (Fig. 3b,c).
mechanism: NtDRMcd methyltransferase recruitment to the FWA promoter via SunTag system induced CG/CHG/CHH methylation, silencing FWA expression.

genes: FWA (flowering time regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Heritable methylation and silencing of FWA in T2- plants (Fig. 3b,c). T3- plants maintained methylation and early flowering phenotype (Supplementary Fig. 13d,f).
mechanism: Triple gRNA (g4+g10+g18) targeting with 22aa linkers enabled robust methylation establishment across the FWA promoter, silencing FWA expression.

genes: FWA (flowering time regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Targeted methylation at FWA promoter with reduced off-target effects (Fig. 4b; Supplementary Fig. 17c). Global methylation levels matched fwa controls.
mechanism: Removal of SV40-type NLS from scFv-sfGFP-NtDRMcd reduced nuclear off-target methylation while maintaining FWA promoter methylation.

genes: OsPSL (OsPSL, premature senescence leaf gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of the psl mutation rescues the mutant phenotype in rice
mechanism: OsPSL is responsible for the mutant phenotype, as shown by complementation

genes: OsFTL10 (flowering time regulator, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi lines show no significant difference in heading time compared to wild-type rice.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsFTL10 (flowering time regulator, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: GUS staining confirms OsFTL10 promoter activity in immature leaves, mature leaves, flowers, and shoot tips.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsFTL10 (flowering time regulator, rice, Oryza sativa), GF14c (14-3-3 protein, rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsFTL10-EGFP localizes to nucleus and cytoplasm; GF14c-EGFP localizes mainly to cytoplasm in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: SiMYB3 (involved in K+ deficiency tolerance, Setaria italica)
phenotype: Overexpression of SiMYB3 promotes main root elongation and improves K+ deficiency tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis plants, with higher fresh weight, longer primary root length, and larger root surface-area compared to control plants after K+ deficiency treatments.
mechanism: SiMYB3 promotes root elongation and enhances K+ deficiency tolerance by improving root development and K+ absorption.

genes: FTL9 (flowering time regulator, Brachypodium distachyon)
phenotype: Overexpression of FTL9 significantly shortens flowering time under SDs in Brachypodium distachyon.
mechanism: FTL9 forms a functional flowering activator complex (FAC) with FD1 and 14-3-3 proteins, promoting VRN1 and FUL2 expression to induce flowering under SDs.

genes: FTL9 (flowering time regulator, Brachypodium distachyon)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated FTL9 knockout delays flowering by ~190 days under SDs in Brachypodium distachyon.
mechanism: FTL9 knockout reduces VRN1 and FUL2 expression, indicating its role in flowering promotion under SDs.

genes: CO1 (photoperiodic flowering regulator, Brachypodium distachyon)
phenotype: CO1 overexpression promotes flowering under LDs and suppresses FTL9 expression under SDs in Brachypodium distachyon.
mechanism: CO1 activates FT1 and represses FTL9, creating a dual regulatory role in photoperiodic flowering.

genes: CO1 (photoperiodic flowering regulator, Brachypodium distachyon)
phenotype: CO1 RNAi increases FTL9 expression under LDs and delays flowering in Brachypodium distachyon.
mechanism: CO1 repression leads to FTL9 upregulation, demonstrating its role as a repressor of FTL9.

genes: FTL9 (flowering time regulator, Brachypodium distachyon), FT1 (flowering time regulator, Brachypodium distachyon)
phenotype: Chimeric FTL9-FT1 PEBP fusion enhances flowering inductive activity under SDs in Brachypodium distachyon.
mechanism: PEBP domain swapping increases VRN1p-LUC activity, indicating enhanced FAC function.

genes: Vvgai1 (VvGAI, modified DELLA domain, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of Vvgai1 causes dwarf stature with shorter internode lengths (~3.36-3.67 cm vs 3.67 cm in NT), reduced leaf size (0.31-1.20 g vs 1.06 g in NT), and disrupted tendril distribution patterns in Vitis vinifera 'Thompson Seedless'.
mechanism: Vvgai1 encodes a non-degradable DELLA protein that disrupts GA signaling by preventing formation of the GA:GID1:DELLA complex, leading to reduced GA activity and altered meristem regulation.

genes: GmNAC42-1 (GmNAC42-1, NAC-domain transcription factor, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmNAC42–1 in elicited soybean hairy roots increased glyceollin metabolite amounts and biosynthesis gene mRNAs by >10-fold upon elicitation.
mechanism: GmNAC42–1 directly binds promoters of glyceollin biosynthesis genes IFS2 and G4DT, acting as a positive regulator in the glyceollin gene regulatory network.

genes: GmNAC42-1 (GmNAC42-1, NAC-domain transcription factor, Glycine max)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of GmNAC42–1 in elicited soybean hairy roots suppressed glyceollin metabolite amounts and biosynthesis gene mRNAs by 4.0- to 3.2-fold.
mechanism: GmNAC42–1 is necessary for full elicitation of glyceollin biosynthesis, as its silencing reduced gene expression and metabolite accumulation.

genes: CKX2 (CKX2, cytokinin oxidase/dehydrogenase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CKX2 increases root biomass by ~15% in Brassica napus L.
mechanism: Cytokinin deficiency enhances root growth by increasing lateral and adventitious roots, leading to a higher root-to-shoot ratio.

genes: Cry j 1 (major allergen, Japanese cedar pollen, Cryptomeria japonica), Cry j 2 (major allergen, Japanese cedar pollen, Cryptomeria japonica)
phenotype: Oral administration of Tg-rice seeds induces immune tolerance against JC pollinosis, suppressing allergen-specific CD4+ T-cell proliferation, IgE and IgG levels, and reducing sneezing frequency and inflammatory cell infiltration in nasal tissue.
mechanism: Tg-rice seeds express structurally disrupted Cry j 1 and Cry j 2 allergens in rice endosperm, which are protected from digestive enzymes by protein bodies and cell walls. Antigenic proteins retain stability and induce mucosal immune tolerance through oral delivery.

genes: AtWRI11-397 (WRINKLED1, Arabidopsis thaliana), NoLDSP (lipid droplet surface protein, Nannochloropsis oceanica)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtWRI11–397 increases triacylglycerol levels ~3-fold, and co-expression with NoLDSP increases it 12-fold in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: NoLDSP enhances lipid droplet accumulation by anchoring on lipid droplets, increasing triacylglycerol storage.

genes: PcPAS (patchoulol synthase, Pogostemon cablin), ElHMGR159-582 (HMGR, Euphorbia lathyris), AtFDPS (farnesyl diphosphate synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Co-expression of ElHMGR159–582 and AtFDPS with PcPAS increases patchoulol content ~5-fold in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: Enhanced precursor availability via ElHMGR159–582 and AtFDPS boosts patchoulol synthesis by PcPAS.

genes: PcPAS (patchoulol synthase, Pogostemon cablin), PbDXS (1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate synthase, Plectranthus barbatus), AtFDPS (farnesyl diphosphate synthase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtWRI11-397 (WRINKLED1, Arabidopsis thaliana), NoLDSP (lipid droplet surface protein, Nannochloropsis oceanica)
phenotype: Co-expression of PbDXS, AtFDPS, AtWRI11–397, and NoLDSP with PcPAS yields ~45 μg patchoulol g−1 fresh weight, 90-fold higher than plastid:PcPAS alone.
mechanism: Synthetic lipid droplet accumulation and enhanced precursor flux via PbDXS and AtFDPS increase patchoulol retention in leaves.

genes: AgABS85-868 (abietadiene synthase, Abies grandis), ElHMGR159-582 (HMGR, Euphorbia lathyris), MtGGDPS (geranylgeranyl diphosphate synthase, Methanothermobacter thermautotrophicus), AtWRI11-397 (WRINKLED1, Arabidopsis thaliana), NoLDSP (lipid droplet surface protein, Nannochloropsis oceanica)
phenotype: Co-expression of ElHMGR159–582, MtGGDPS, AtWRI11–397, and NoLDSP with AgABS85–868 increases diterpenoid yield 400-fold in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: Enhanced precursor flux via ElHMGR159–582 and MtGGDPS, combined with lipid droplet sequestration via AtWRI11–397 and NoLDSP, boosts diterpenoid production.

genes: PbMYB12b (PbMYB12b, PFG-type MYB transcription factor, Pyrus bretschneideri Rehd.), PbCHSb (chalcone synthase, Pyrus bretschneideri Rehd.), PbFLS (flavonol synthase, Pyrus bretschneideri Rehd.)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbMYB12b enhances the biosynthesis of quercetin glycosides and isorhamnetin glycosides in pear fruit and young leaves.
mechanism: PbMYB12b positively regulates the expression of PbCHSb and PbFLS, which are involved in flavonol biosynthesis.

genes: PbMYB12b (PbMYB12b, PFG-type MYB transcription factor, Pyrus bretschneideri Rehd.)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of PbMYB12b reduces the biosynthesis of quercetin glycosides and isorhamnetin glycosides in pear fruit and young leaves.
mechanism: PbMYB12b silencing leads to down-regulation of PbCHSb and PbFLS, which are involved in flavonol biosynthesis.

genes: MnEIL3 (Morus notabilis, ethylene response factor, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of MnEIL3 enhances salt and drought tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with reduced MDA and H2O2 content and increased proline content under stress.
mechanism: MnEIL3 positively regulates abiotic stress tolerance by upregulating ethylene biosynthetic genes (AtACS4/6/8/10/12 and AtACO1/2/4) and activating downstream stress-responsive genes.

genes: MnACS1 (Morus notabilis, ethylene biosynthesis gene, synthetic)
phenotype: MnACS1 promoter activity is induced in leaves under salt and drought stress, with GUS expression detected in stems and leaves after 6 h of NaCl and 3 h of mannitol treatment.
mechanism: MnACS1 promoter activity is regulated by abiotic stresses, with PERE and ECBS motifs in the promoter suggesting EIN3/EIL-mediated regulation.

genes: MnACS3 (Morus notabilis, ethylene biosynthesis gene, synthetic)
phenotype: MnACS3 promoter activity is primarily in roots under salt stress, with GUS expression in stems after 6 h of NaCl and in stems and leaves after 3 h of mannitol treatment.
mechanism: MnACS3 promoter activity is regulated by abiotic stresses, with PERE and ECBS motifs in the promoter suggesting EIN3/EIL-mediated regulation.

genes: NERD1 (NERD1, NEW ENHANCER OF ROOT DWARFISM 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of nerd1-2 and nerd1-4 mutants fully rescues the reduced ovule phenotype, resulting in plants with ovule numbers indistinguishable from Col-0.
mechanism: NERD1 is a positive regulator of ovule number, with its native promoter driving expression in developing flowers and reproductive tissues.

genes: NERD1 (NERD1, NEW ENHANCER OF ROOT DWARFISM 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)

However, some plants exhibit male sterility correlated with NERD1 expression levels.

mechanism: NA

mechanism: Strong UBQ10 promoter-driven expression of lt-BAR bypassed the N-end rule degradation system, leading to constitutive toxicity.

genes: MdGSTF6 (glutathione S-transferase, anthocyanin transporter, Malus × domestica)

mechanism: MdGSTF6 is located on the vacuolar membrane and functions as an anthocyanin transporter.

genes: MdGSTF6 (glutathione S-transferase, anthocyanin transporter, Malus × domestica)

mechanism: MdGSTF6 complements the anthocyanin transport defect in the tt19 mutant.

genes: MdGSTF6 (glutathione S-transferase, anthocyanin transporter, Malus × domestica)
phenotype: Knockdown of MdGSTF6 reduces anthocyanin accumulation in apple fruit peel.
mechanism: MdGSTF6 is essential for anthocyanin transport in apple fruit.

genes: MdGSTF6 (glutathione S-transferase, anthocyanin transporter, Malus × domestica)

mechanism: MdGSTF6 is required for anthocyanin transport in apple.

mechanism: AtPiezo promoter activity is induced by viral infection and expressed in vascular tissues

mechanism: GFP fused with rice GBSSI transit peptide targets to amyloplast stroma, revealing starch grain morphology

mechanism: GFP fused with rice GBSSI transit peptide targets to amyloplast stroma, revealing starch grain morphology

mechanism: SSG6-GFP localizes to outer amyloplast membrane, controlling starch grain size during seed development

mechanism: SlAR enhances carotenoid and chlorophyll biosynthesis by upregulating the MEP pathway, which shares geranylgeranyl diphosphate as a precursor for both carotenoids and chlorophyll phytol groups

mechanism: α-AIC3 inhibits AGA by preventing the processing of complex sugars, thereby inhibiting insect larval growth.

mechanism: dep1 overexpression enhances nitrogen uptake and assimilation, upregulates GS and GOGAT genes, downregulates RUBISCO and PEPC genes, leading to unbalanced carbon-nitrogen metabolism but increased grain yield through higher panicle density and grain numbers

genes: SOS2 (SOS2, SOS2 kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Mutation of SOS2Ser294 to Ala abolishes PKS5-mediated phosphorylation, which enhances 14-3-3/SOS2 interaction and represses SOS2 kinase activity.

genes: PKS5 (PKS5, sucrose non-fermenting-1-related protein kinase-3, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PKS5 negatively regulates salt tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PKS5 phosphorylates SOS2Ser294, enhancing 14-3-3/SOS2 interaction and repressing SOS2 kinase activity, which reduces Na+ efflux under salt stress.

genes: 14-3-3λ (14-3-3λ, 14-3-3 protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: 14-3-3λ represses PKS5 kinase activity, which relieves the repression of SOS2 kinase activity and enhances PM H+-ATPase activity under alkaline stress.

genes: PtoUBC34 (PtoUBC34, ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Populus tomentosa), PtoMYB221 (PtoMYB221, transcriptional repressor, Populus tomentosa), PtoMYB156 (PtoMYB156, transcriptional repressor, Populus tomentosa)

mechanism: PtoUBC34s interacts with PtoMYB221 and PtoMYB156 in the ER, leading to their translocation from the nucleus to the ER and reducing their repression activity. This interaction is confirmed by BiFC and coimmunoprecipitation assays.

genes: PtoUBC34 (PtoUBC34, ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, Populus tomentosa), PtoMYB221 (PtoMYB221, transcriptional repressor, Populus tomentosa), PtoMYB156 (PtoMYB156, transcriptional repressor, Populus tomentosa)

mechanism: PtoUBC34 interacts with PtoMYB221 and PtoMYB156 in the ER, likely via ER-associated degradation (ERAD), reducing their transcriptional repression activity by sequestering them in the ER and/or promoting their degradation.

genes: miR171 (microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana), miR390 (microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Deactivation of miR390 leads to increased lateral root formation, potentially through auxin homeostasis regulation.

phenotype: Overexpression of TpSnRK2.11 significantly increased Cd accumulation in roots and shoots, enhanced Cd translocation from roots to shoots, decreased Fe accumulation in roots but increased in shoots
mechanism: Regulates expression of AtNRAMP1 and AtHMA4, alters subcellular distribution of Cd and Fe in cell wall and organelle fractions

genes: MpFGMYB (female gametophyte MYB, Marchantia polymorpha)

genes: JMJ13 (JMJ13, histone demethylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Both DEP1 and OsAP2–39 are involved in the ABA response mechanism.

mechanism: ZmCYP94B1 catabolizes JA-Ile to control flower and fruit development in planta.

genes: CYP71AU87 (CYP71AU87, hydroxylase, Marrubium vulgare), MvCPS1 (MvCPS1, diterpene synthase, Marrubium vulgare), MvELS (MvELS, diterpene synthase, Marrubium vulgare)

genes: CYP71AU87 (CYP71AU87, hydroxylase, Marrubium vulgare), MvCPS1 (MvCPS1, diterpene synthase, Marrubium vulgare), MvELS (MvELS, diterpene synthase, Marrubium vulgare)

mechanism: CYP71AU87 catalyzes the hydroxylation of 9,13-epoxy-labd-14-ene at C-18 or C-19, while MvCPS1 and MvELS sequentially produce the epoxy intermediate. These products are proposed as intermediates in marrubiin biosynthesis.

genes: BoCCD4 (carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 4, Brassica oleracea, BoCCD4)

genes: PpHKT1 (Prupe.1G067100, HKT1 transporter, Prunus persica)

mechanism: PpHKT1 functions as a Na+ transporter localized to the plasma membrane, restricting Na+ movement from roots to shoots during salt stress. This reduces Na+ accumulation in leaves and maintains membrane integrity under salinity.

phenotype: Fails to complement reduced PELPIII activity in RNAiPIII transgenic line, resulting in increased N. obtusifolia pollen tube growth

genes: Cry2A* (Bt protein, synthetic)

mechanism: Bt protein synthesis imposes a 'bio-burden' that disrupts carbon and nitrogen metabolism, affecting nutrient allocation and plant growth.

genes: SlF3HL (SlF3HL, 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase, Solanum lycopersicum)

genes: SlF3HL (SlF3HL, 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Knockdown of SlF3HL increases sensitivity to chilling stress in tomato, as evidenced by severe leaf wilting, higher membrane damage (MDA and ion leakage), and lower proline content compared to wild-type and overexpression lines.
mechanism: SlF3HL knockdown impairs chilling stress tolerance by increasing ROS accumulation (higher H2O2 and O2− levels), reducing antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD and POD), and dysregulating JA biosynthesis and cold-responsive gene expression.

genes: HAT1 (HAT1, histone acetyltransferase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: HAT1 represses anthocyanin biosynthesis by sequestering the MBW protein complex and recruiting TPL corepressor to inhibit gene expression.

genes: HAT1mEAR1 (HAT1 with mutated EAR motif 1, histone acetyltransferase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: The fusion protein converts MYB75 into a repressor by recruiting TPL corepressor, inhibiting MBW complex activity.

genes: OsPT8 (OsPT8, phosphate transporter, Oryza sativa)

genes: OsPT8 (OsPT8, phosphate transporter, Oryza sativa)

genes: PcD6DES (Δ6 desaturase from Phytophthora citrophthora, Phytophthora citrophthora)

GLA and SDA accumulated in both polar lipids and neutral lipids in mature perilla seeds expressing PcD6DES, especially in neutral lipids. Although the seed weight in PcD6DES perilla was 87–96% that of wild type, the total oil content per seed weight was similar between lines. The PcD6DES perilla plants contained very high content (over 45%) of both GLA and SDA in seed oil.

genes: YUC6 (YUCCA6, auxin biosynthesis gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: Increased auxin activity in the seed coat disrupts normal seed development, leading to seed abortion.

genes: SlEXA1 (EXA1 homolog, Solanum lycopersicum)

mechanism: MYB96 recruits HDA15 to ROP promoters, leading to histone deacetylation and gene repression.

genes: GAS2 (GA 20-oxidase-like, Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)

genes: SaGLIP8 (SaGLIP8, GDSL esterase/lipase, Sedum alfredii)

mechanism: NA

genes: GhMFT1 (GhMFT1, cotton MFT homolog, Gossypium hirsutum), GhMFT2 (GhMFT2, cotton MFT homolog, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhMFT2 inhibits seed germination in Arabidopsis thaliana, with significantly lower germination rates at early stages compared to wild type.
mechanism: GhMFT2 upregulates ABA signaling pathway genes (AtABI3, AtABI5) and DELLA proteins (AtRGA, AtRGL2), repressing GA signaling and promoting seed dormancy.
