phenotype: Overexpression of S2Lb under its endogenous promoter rescues the growth defects of s2lb-2 mutant plants, restoring normal leaf size, root length, and fertility.
mechanism: S2Lb associates with AtCOMPASS-like complexes and SDG2 to mediate H3K4me3 enrichment over highly transcribed genes, facilitating optimal gene induction during cellular transitions.

genes: AVP1 (Arabidopsis vacuolar H+-pyrophosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana), OsSIZ1 (rice SUMO E3 ligase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Co-overexpression of AVP1 and OsSIZ1 significantly enhances tolerance to salt, heat, and water deficit stresses, with 150% higher seed yield under salt stress, 110% higher under heat stress, and 4-fold higher under drought stress compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: AVP1 increases vacuolar H+ gradient and Na+ sequestration; OsSIZ1 enhances sumoylation pathways. Co-overexpression leads to synergistic upregulation of HSPs (HSP70, HSP101, HSP17.4), increased root acidification (35% more protons released), and enhanced ABA-dependent stress response (NCED3 upregulation).

genes: GhPDAT1d (phospholipid:diacylglycerol acyltransferase, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of GhPDAT1d increased Arabidopsis seed oil content by 6.55 to 17.61% compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: GhPDAT1d enhances triacylglycerol (TAG) biosynthesis through phospholipid:diacylglycerol acyltransferase activity, increasing seed oil accumulation without altering fatty acid composition.

genes: SmMDS (2-c-methyl-d-erythritol 2,4-cyclodiphosphate synthase, tanshinone biosynthesis gene, Salvia miltiorrhiza)
phenotype: Overexpression of SmMDS in transgenic Salvia miltiorrhiza hairy roots significantly increased the tanshinone yield compared to the control, with total tanshinone content increasing to 2.5, 2.3, and 3.2 mg/g DW after Ag+, YE, and MJ treatments, respectively.
mechanism: Overexpression of SmMDS enhances the MEP pathway, leading to increased accumulation of tanshinones.

genes: HCT (hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA shikimate/quinate hydroxycinnamoyltransferase, lignin biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Chimeric plants with ~90% reduction in HCT activity and ~20-30% reduction in total lignin, with normal growth and 50% increased reducing sugar release after saccharification.
mechanism: Fiber-specific knockout of HCT via CRISPR/Cas9 using NST3/SND1 promoter reduces lignin in fiber cells while maintaining vessel function.

genes: HCT (hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA shikimate/quinate hydroxycinnamoyltransferase, lignin biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: No significant lignin composition changes compared to wild type, despite transgenic expression of the low-efficiency sgRNA.
mechanism: Low-efficiency sgRNA (HCT_gRNA12) failed to achieve sufficient editing in fiber cells to alter lignin composition.

genes: GONST2 (Golgi-localized nucleotide sugar transporter 2, GDP-mannose transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Triallelic mutants in T1 generation with no wild-type allele detected at the target site, enabling heritable germline editing.
mechanism: Constitutive UBQ10 promoter-driven Cas9 with high-efficiency GONST2_gRNA1 enables early embryonic editing, producing triallelic mutants in T1.

genes: GONST2 (Golgi-localized nucleotide sugar transporter 2, GDP-mannose transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Lower editing efficiency compared to GONST2_gRNA1, with one-third of transgenic plants remaining wild type at the target site.
mechanism: Low-efficiency GONST2_gRNA2 failed to achieve sufficient germline editing despite constitutive UBQ10 promoter.

genes: AtIPCS1 (AtIPCS1, AtIPCS1 gene from Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtIPCS1 increases early flowering by ~4 days and alters stress response gene expression in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtIPCS1 acts as a negative regulator of biotic and abiotic stress responses while positively regulating photosynthesis and lipid storage genes.

genes: AtIPCS2 (AtIPCS2, AtIPCS2 gene from Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtIPCS2 increases early flowering by ~4 days and alters stress response gene expression in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtIPCS2 acts as a negative regulator of biotic and abiotic stress responses while positively regulating photosynthesis and lipid storage genes.

genes: AtIPCS3 (AtIPCS3, AtIPCS3 gene from Arabidopsis thaliana, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtIPCS3 increases early flowering by ~4 days and alters stress response gene expression in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtIPCS3 acts as a negative regulator of biotic and abiotic stress responses while positively regulating photosynthesis and lipid storage genes.

genes: MIPS1 (MIPS1 isoform, phytate biosynthesis, Glycine max)
phenotype: Reduces seed phytic acid content by ~38.75% in Glycine max
mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of MIPS1, the rate-limiting enzyme in phytate biosynthesis, decreases phytate accumulation in seeds

genes: MIPS1 (MIPS1 isoform, phytate biosynthesis, Glycine max)
phenotype: Reduces seed phytic acid content by ~41.34% in Glycine max
mechanism: Antisense suppression of MIPS1, the rate-limiting enzyme in phytate biosynthesis, decreases phytate accumulation in seeds

genes: sha-miR319d (microRNA involved in temperature stress regulation, Solanum habrochaites)
phenotype: Overexpression of sha-miR319d increases tomato chilling and heat stress tolerance, with lower REL and MDA levels, higher chlorophyll content, and reduced ROS accumulation compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: sha-miR319d regulates temperature stress tolerance by modulating expression of CBF1, HsfA1a, HsfA1b, and ROS signaling genes (ZAT12, ZAT10), and potentially inhibiting GAMYB-like1 expression.

genes: LC (light chain of anti-rabies virus mAbPSO57, rabies virus), HC (heavy chain of anti-rabies virus mAbPSO57, rabies virus)
phenotype: Expression of anti-rabies virus mAbPSO57 in Arabidopsis thaliana, with mAbPSO57 purified at concentrations up to 550 µg/mL using optimized resins.
mechanism: ER retention via KDEL motif ensures proper folding and accumulation of mAbPSO57 in the endoplasmic reticulum.

genes: TBSV P19 (TBSV, suppressor of gene silencing, TBSV)
phenotype: Overexpression of TBSV P19 promotes SMV infection in soybean hairy roots, with significantly higher SMV concentration compared to control at 10, 15, and 20 dpi.
mechanism: TBSV P19 prevents the onset of post-transcriptional gene silencing, a natural plant antiviral mechanism, thereby promoting pathogen infection.

genes: SMV CP (SMV SC15, capsid protein, SMV SC15)
phenotype: Overexpression of SMV CP suppresses SMV infection in soybean hairy roots, with significantly lower SMV concentration compared to control at 10, 15, and 20 dpi.
mechanism: SMV CP enhances resistance via pathogen-derived resistance (PDR) mechanisms involving post-transcriptional RNA silencing or the CP itself.

genes: GFP (synthetic, green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP overexpression serves as a control vector for transformation efficiency monitoring in soybean hairy roots.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsSLAC1 (OsSLAC1, slow-type anion channel, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSLAC1 in rice significantly reduces water loss in detached leaves by ~15% compared to control plants.
mechanism: OsSLAC1 functions as a slow-type anion channel in rice guard cells, enhancing stomatal closure and reducing transpiration.

genes: SAPK10 (SAPK10, Osmotic Stress/ABA-Activated Protein Kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAPK10 in rice significantly reduces water loss in detached leaves by ~15% compared to control plants.
mechanism: SAPK10 phosphorylates OsSLAC1 in rice guard cells, enhancing stomatal closure and reducing transpiration.

genes: MfEF2 (MfEF2, eukaryotic elongation factor 2, Medicago falcata)
phenotype: Overexpression of MfEF2 in transgenic tobacco plants resulted in enhanced cold tolerance. Compared to the wild type, transgenic plants showed higher survival rate after freezing treatment (7% vs 54-90%), higher levels of net photosynthetic rate (A), maximum photochemical efficiency of photosystem (PS) II (Fv/Fm) and nonphotochemical quenching (NPQ), and lower levels of ion leakage and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production after chilling treatment.
mechanism: MfEF2 confers cold tolerance through regulating hundreds of proteins synthesis under low temperature conditions. The elevated cold tolerance in MfEF2 transgenic plants was associated with downregulation of the subunits of PSI and PSII as well as LHC, which leads to reduced capacity for capturing sunlight and ROS production for protection of plants, and upregulation of proteins involving in splicesome, which promotes alternative splicing of pre-mRNA under low temperature.

genes: PTB1 (female fertility gene, essential for pollen tube growth and female fertility in rice, Oryza sativa), ZM-AA1 (pollen-lethal gene, maize α-amylase gene with amyloplast-targeting signal peptide, Zea mays), DsRed (red fluorescence protein gene, synthetic)
gene_construct: native promoter-PTB1-NA---PG47-ZM-AA1-NA---35S enhancer and LTP2 promoter-DsRed-NA
phenotype: Transgenic rice plants exhibit female fertility restoration, pollen lethality in transgenic pollen grains, and red fluorescence in seeds for fluorescence-assisted sorting. Self-pollination produces 1:1 ratio of fluorescent (transgenic) and non-fluorescent (female sterile) seeds.
mechanism: PTB1 restores female fertility by promoting pollen tube growth; ZM-AA1 disrupts starch accumulation in transgenic pollen causing lethality; DsRed enables fluorescence-based sorting of transgenic seeds. Hemizygous transgenic plants produce viable non-transgenic pollen for hybrid seed production.

genes: OgCytAPX1 (Oncidium CytAPX1, cytosolic ascorbate peroxidase 1, Oncidium), AtCytAPX1 (Arabidopsis CytAPX1, cytosolic ascorbate peroxidase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of OgCytAPX1 increases GPX activity and reduces H2O2 content by ~66% in Arabidopsis thaliana under 30°C stress. Overexpression of AtCytAPX1 shows no GPX activity. OgCytAPX1-OE plants flower earlier with ~20 rosette leaves compared to ~25 in AtCytAPX1-OE and ~37 in wild-type.
mechanism: OgCytAPX1 exhibits dual antioxidant-binding activities for ascorbate (AsA) and glutathione (GSH), enabling GSH-dependent H2O2 scavenging and redox homeostasis under stress. AtCytAPX1 only binds AsA.

genes: AtHAC1 (Histone AcetylTransferase 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of dCas9HAT increases mOFP fluorescence and dCas9 expression in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: dCas9HAT enhances transcription via histone acetylation, promoting chromatin relaxation and transcriptional machinery interaction.

genes: GUS (β-Glucuronidase reporter gene)
phenotype: dCas9HAT-sgRNA1 and sgRNA2 increase GUS enzymatic activity by ~2.4-fold and ~2-fold, respectively, in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: AREB1 (ABA-responsive element binding factor 1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: dCas9HAT-sgA lines exhibit a 1.7- to 2-fold increase in AREB1 expression and a dwarf phenotype with ~3-fold smaller rosette diameter under normal growth conditions.
mechanism: dCas9HAT-mediated histone acetylation at AREB1 loci enhances gene expression and chromatin rearrangement, improving drought stress tolerance.

genes: BSK3 (BSK3, BSK3 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Compared with bsk3, the elongation of both primary and lateral roots in response to LN could be significantly increased by introducing a genomic fragment containing the promoter and coding regions of BSK3 into the bsk3 mutant.
mechanism: BSK3-mediated BR signaling plays a critical role in modulating cell elongation and, consequently, root elongation in response to LN.

genes: BSK3 (BSK3, BSK3 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic lines overexpressing BSK3-L showed significantly shorter and slower growing primary roots than those expressing BSK3-P.
mechanism: The BSK3-L allele relays a stronger BR signaling output than the BSK3-P allele.

genes: BSK3 (BSK3, BSK3 gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Confocal microscopy of plants expressing proBSK3::BSK3-GFP further revealed that the protein was present from the meristematic zone all the way through the elongation zone of epidermal, cortical, and endodermal cells.
mechanism: BSK3 localization coincides spatially with developmental stages associated with cell elongation in roots.

genes: miR156f (microRNA, mimicry, synthetic)
phenotype: MIM156OE plants showed decreased number of SBs (Fig. 1c), which were partially due to the down regulation of axillary meristem regulating genes LAX1 and LAX2 (Fig. 1f).
mechanism: mediated through the direct binding of OsSPL7 and OsSPL13, the miR156 target genes, to the promoter regions of LAX1 gene, and interaction between OsSPL7 and LAX2 protein

genes: RCN2 (RCN2, gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: this phenotype was restored in the MIM156fOE/A989 hybrid by over expression of RCN2 (Fig. 5b, c), indicating that miR156 regulated the number of branches in the panicle through RCN2.
mechanism: NA

genes: PoPDS (phytoene desaturase, Paeonia ostii, Paeonia ostii)
phenotype: Photobleaching in systemically-infected leaves of P. ostii at 4 weeks post inoculation, with white spots/sectors persisting for 2 months.
mechanism: Silencing of PoPDS reduces photoprotective carotenoid levels, leading to chlorophyll photooxidation and tissue bleaching.

genes: EGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, Aequorea victoria, synthetic)
phenotype: GFP fluorescence observed in newly emerging leaves and roots of P. ostii at 5 days post inoculation, with higher accumulation in roots than leaves.
mechanism: Overexpression of EGFP fused to TRV2 coat protein (CP) allows visualization of viral spread and systemic infection.

genes: Fm4CL-like 1 (Fm4CL-like 1, a 4-coumarate:CoA ligase gene from Fraxinus mandshurica, Fraxinus mandshurica)
phenotype: Overexpression of Fm4CL-like 1 increases lignin content by 39.5%, S/G ratio by 19.7%, xylem cell layer by 40%, and xylem cell wall thickness by 21.6% in transgenic tobacco. Under mannitol stress, root length is 64% longer, seed germination rate 47% higher, H2O2 content 22% lower, and stomatal apertures 30% smaller than wild type.
mechanism: Fm4CL-like 1 promotes lignin biosynthesis and secondary cell wall development. It enhances drought tolerance by reducing ROS accumulation, maintaining cell membrane integrity, and modulating stomatal aperture and photosynthesis.

genes: TCP17 (TCP17, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: TCP17-GFP accumulation increases in response to elevated temperature, promoting thermoresponsive hypocotyl elongation.
mechanism: TCP17 stabilizes at higher temperatures, binds to PIF4 promoter, and enhances PIF4 expression and activity to drive thermomorphogenesis.

genes: TCP17 (TCP17, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Constitutive overexpression of TCP17-FLAG causes elongated hypocotyls at 22°C and enhanced thermoresponsive elongation at 28°C.
mechanism: TCP17-FLAG stability increases at higher temperatures, interacts with PIF4 to enhance auxin biosynthesis gene expression (YUC8, IAA19, IAA29), driving hypocotyl elongation.

genes: PIF4 (PIF4, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PIF4-FLAG causes extreme hypocotyl elongation at 22°C and enhances thermoresponsive elongation at 28°C.
mechanism: PIF4-FLAG upregulates auxin biosynthesis genes (YUC8, IAA19, IAA29) and interacts with TCP17 to amplify thermomorphogenesis.

genes: SlILL1 (IAA-amino acid hydrolase, tomato), SlILL3 (IAA-amino acid hydrolase, tomato), SlILL5 (IAA-amino acid hydrolase, tomato), SlILL6 (IAA-amino acid hydrolase, tomato), SlILL7 (IAA-amino acid hydrolase, tomato)
phenotype: Silencing SlILL1, 3, 5, 6, and 7 using VIGS significantly accelerated pedicel abscission in tomato plants, with triple-silenced SlILL1+5+6 showing the most pronounced effect.
mechanism: Downregulation of SlILL1, 5, and 6 reduced auxin conjugate hydrolysis activity, leading to decreased free auxin levels in the abscission zone and altered PIN gene expression, which disrupted auxin transport and accelerated abscission.

genes: ib-pri-MIR156 (ib-pri-MIR156, miRNA precursor, Ipomoea batatas)
phenotype: Overexpression of ib-pri-MIR156 in Arabidopsis results in a purplish phenotype with increased anthocyanin accumulation, as evidenced by upregulated expression of CHS, CHI, DFR, and ANS genes and suppressed SPL abundance.
mechanism: ib-pri-MIR156 represses SPL expression, which destabilizes the MBW complex, leading to upregulation of anthocyanin biosynthesis genes (CHS, CHI, DFR, ANS).

genes: GmFILa (Glyma.17G138200, YABBY transcription factor, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmFILa in Arabidopsis thaliana alters the partial abaxialization of the adaxial epidermises of leaves, increases leaf length and number, reduces leaf width, and inhibits shoot apical meristem development.
mechanism: GmFILa functions as a nuclear-localized transcription factor, leading to altered leaf polarity and SAM development.

genes: GmFILa (Glyma.17G138200, YABBY transcription factor, Glycine max)
phenotype: GmFILa-GFP fusion protein is localized exclusively to the nucleus in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: GmFILa is a nuclear-localized protein, implying it functions as a transcription factor.

genes: OsFIP (OsFIP, RNA N6-methyladenosine methyltransferase subunit, Oryza sativa), OsMTA2 (OsMTA2, RNA N6-methyladenosine methyltransferase subunit, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsFIP increases anther length, panicle length, seed number, and seed-setting rate in rice. Overexpression of OsMTA2 increases panicle length and seed number but reduces fertility compared to wild-type.
mechanism: OsFIP and OsMTA2 mediate m6A RNA methylation, which regulates sporogenesis and embryo development by modulating threonine protease and NTPase gene expression.

genes: MGD1 (MGD1, membrane-associated galactolipid biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: MGD1 suppression impairs greening after dark growth, with cotyledon greening remaining strongly impaired even after 72-h illumination and reduced fresh weight in +DEX seedlings.
mechanism: MGD1 suppression impairs thylakoid membrane biogenesis during etioplast-to-chloroplast differentiation, disrupts galactolipid biosynthesis, and reduces chlorophyll accumulation due to impaired membrane-associated processes of the tetrapyrrole biosynthesis pathway.

genes: GUSPlus (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS reporter gene expression was observed in GV3101 strain at the 2nd day after infiltration, and lasted to the 9th day, with the highest expression level at the 8th and 9th day.
mechanism: NA

genes: CiDREB1C (dehydration responsive element binding protein 1C, transcription factor, Caragana intermedia)
phenotype: Transiently expressed CiDREB1C in C. intermedia leaves enhanced drought, salt and ABA stress tolerance, indicated by higher survival rate (48.9% under drought, 25.83% under salt), increased chlorophyll content (0.94 mg/g FW under drought, 1.45 mg/g FW under salt), and reduced lodging rate and leaf shedding compared to control seedlings.
mechanism: CiDREB1C enhances stress tolerance by upregulating stress-related genes, as evidenced by its role in cold stress response and abiotic stress tolerance in other species.

genes: TaAMT2;3a (ammonium transporter, wheat), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: TaAMT2;3a-GFP fusion protein localized to cell and nuclear membranes in wheat protoplasts
mechanism: TaAMT2;3a is an ammonium transporter localized to membranes, enabling ammonium transport in plants

genes: S1TPR (S1TPR, gamete-killer/protector, Oryza glaberrima)
phenotype: T0 plants hemizygous for S1TPRt had fully fertile pollen and spikelets (~95% fertility).
mechanism: S1TPR alone is insufficient to induce hybrid sterility (HS); requires S1A4 and S1A6 for gamete-killer function.

genes: S1A4 (S1A4, gamete-killer, Oryza glaberrima), S1A6 (S1A6, gamete-killer, Oryza glaberrima)
phenotype: Plants transformed with S1A4t or S1A6t alone did not show semi-sterile phenotypes. Pyramiding S1A4–S1A6t with S1TPRt induced semi-sterility (45–55% sterility).
mechanism: S1A4 and S1A6 are required for S1 HS; their combination with S1TPR forms a killer-protector system.

genes: S1TPR (S1TPR, gamete-protector, Oryza glaberrima)
phenotype: S1TPRt transgene rescued gametes containing S1-s allele, increasing fertility from ~50% to ~75–100% in F1/F2 hybrids.
mechanism: S1TPR protects gametes from sterility induced by S1A4–S1A6; provides transmission advantage in F2 progeny.

genes: S1A4 (S1A4, gamete-killer, Oryza glaberrima), S1A6 (S1A6, gamete-killer, Oryza glaberrima), S1TPR (S1TPR, gamete-protector, Oryza glaberrima)
phenotype: Pyramided S1A4–S1A6t and S1TPRt transgenes induced semi-sterility (45–55% sterility) in F1 plants.
mechanism: Tripartite complex S1A4-S1TPR-S1A6 acts as gamete-killer system; S1TPR protects gametes from sterility.

genes: PPR287 (At3g59040, chloroplast-targeted PPR protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PPR287-GFP fusion protein localizes to chloroplasts in transgenic Arabidopsis
mechanism: Nucleus-encoded PPR287 is transported into chloroplasts via chloroplast transit peptide

genes: PPR287 (At3g59040, chloroplast-targeted PPR protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: amiRNA knockdown mutants display yellowish and pale-green leaves, reduced root growth, and decreased seed yield
mechanism: Artificial microRNA targets first exon of PPR287, reducing transcript levels to 30-60% of wild-type levels

genes: PPR287 (At3g59040, chloroplast-targeted PPR protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation line rescues ppr287 mutant phenotypes to wild-type levels
mechanism: Full-length PPR287 expressed under CaMV35S promoter restores chloroplast rRNA stability and normal growth

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Strong GUS expression in young seedlings, leaves, and flowers
mechanism: 1.5-kb PPR287 promoter drives GUS expression in transgenic Arabidopsis

genes: PLIM2a (PLIM2a, actin-bundling factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), PLIM2b (PLIM2b, actin-bundling factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: PLIM2a-EGFP and PLIM2b-EGFP fusion constructs rescue the plim2a plim2b mutant phenotype by decorating actin filaments throughout pollen tubes.
mechanism: PLIM2a/PLIM2b decorate actin filaments and regulate actin bundle organization in pollen tubes.

genes: mGFP5 (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of green fluorescent protein (GFP) allows identification of transformants in Brassica rapa
mechanism: NA

genes: LUX (LUX, wild-type gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expressing LUX-GFP in lux-4 rescues the increased susceptibility to PmaDG3 observed in lux mutants, restoring normal bacterial growth and disease symptoms in both LL25 and LL37 infection conditions.
mechanism: LUX-GFP likely restores normal circadian regulation of stomatal aperture and defense signaling pathways disrupted by the lux mutation, thereby re-establishing temporal defense mechanisms against P. syringae.

genes: NPTII (kanamycin resistance gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Variable kanamycin resistance in transgenic seedlings correlates with transgene silencing via KNOT-linked interactions; silenced transgenes show reduced viability on kanamycin
mechanism: KNOT-linked silencing (KLS) involving 3D nuclear organization perturbations, independent of DNA methylation and RNAi

genes: PtNF-YB1 (PtNF-YB1, transcription factor involved in flowering regulation, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PtNF-YB1 in transgenic Arabidopsis and tomato results in significantly earlier flowering (e.g., 7.1 vs 12.5 rosette leaves in Arabidopsis, 50 vs 65 days in tomato).
mechanism: PtNF-YB1 upregulates flowering genes CO and FT in Arabidopsis, and interacts with PtCO1/PtCO2 proteins in poplar to promote flowering through photoperiod pathway.

genes: SlBRI1 (Brassinosteroid Insensitive 1, tomato, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Complementation of the cu3-abs1 mutant restores normal growth and BR signaling.
mechanism: SlBRI1 functions as a receptor kinase in BR signaling, restoring normal autophosphorylation and growth.

genes: SlBRI1 (Brassinosteroid Insensitive 1, tomato, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Dephosphorylation of Thr-1050 increases BR signal strength, leading to enhanced vegetative growth, higher yields, and altered fruit quality.
mechanism: Thr-1050 acts as a negative regulator of SlBRI1 kinase activity, enhancing autophosphorylation and BR signaling.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter gene, reporter gene, pBI121 vector)
phenotype: Spatiotemporal expression of GUS in roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and silique pods but not in seeds. GUS activity increased under ABA, NaCl, PEG, and cold stresses, with highest activity in roots (47.3% increase under PEG6000).
mechanism: PsDREB2 promoter contains cis-acting elements responsive to abiotic stresses (ABRE, MYB, MYC, etc.) that regulate GUS expression in a tissue-specific and stress-inducible manner.

genes: MPK3 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 3, Arabidopsis thaliana), MPK6 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 6, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Conditional knockout of MPK3 and MPK6 using estradiol-inducible system bypasses embryonic lethality in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: NA

genes: VP1 (poliovirus capsid protein, viral antigen, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of codon-optimized VP1 in lettuce chloroplasts forms 22.3 nm monomer and 138.2–165.9 nm multimer VLPs, with 9.29–15.36 fold higher expression than native VP1
mechanism: Codon optimization enhances chloroplast expression; VLP assembly enables GM1 receptor binding for oral antigen delivery

genes: OsbZIP62 (drought stress-related bZIP transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsbZIP62-VP64 enhances drought tolerance and oxidative stress tolerance in transgenic rice, with 45–46% survival rate under PEG-simulated drought stress compared to 24% in wild-type plants.
mechanism: OsbZIP62 upregulates stress-related genes (e.g., OsGL1, OsNAC10, DSM2) and interacts with SAPKs to activate downstream targets.

genes: OsbZIP62 (drought stress-related bZIP transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: osbzip62 mutants exhibited reduced drought and oxidative stress tolerance, with 20–36% survival rate under PEG-simulated drought stress compared to 45% in wild-type plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsbZIP62 (drought stress-related bZIP transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsbZIP62-GFP localized to the nucleus in rice protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: NbRRAall1 (REDUCED RESIDUAL ARABINOSE arabinosyl transferase, N. benthamiana, N. benthamiana), NbPDS2 (PHYTOENE DESATURASE, N. benthamiana, N. benthamiana)
phenotype: FACS of GFP-expressing protoplasts resulted in 3–5 fold mutation enrichment in selected populations (20–30% in unsorted to >80% in sorted) for NbRRAall1 and NbPDS2 loci
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated double stranded breaks at target loci followed by NHEJ repair

genes: OsSNB (grain width regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSNB decreases grain width and 1,000-grain weight in transgenic rice plants compared to wild type.
mechanism: OsSNB regulates grain width by affecting cell size during organ development and modulating the expression of grain size-related genes like GS5 and TGW6.

genes: FtMYB8 (FtMYB8, transcription factor, Fagopyrum tataricum)
phenotype: Overexpression of FtMYB8 reduces the accumulation of anthocyanin/proanthocyanidin by specifically inhibiting TT12 expression in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: FtMYB8 may depend on the interaction between FtMYB8 and TT8 to inhibit TT12 expression, which may also negatively regulate marginal trichome initiation.

genes: GUS (GUS, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity was observed in bud trichomes, roots, and root primordia in transgenic Arabidopsis.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsLHT1 (amino acid transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of OsLHT1 results in growth inhibition and reduced grain yields in rice, with plant height, stem length, and tiller number reduced by 67.8-42.5% depending on the mutant line.
mechanism: Disruption of OsLHT1 function inhibits amino acid transport, leading to impaired root and shoot growth and reduced fecundity.

genes: OsIAA23 (OsIAA23, auxin/IAA protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Kasalath mutants show dwarfism, reduced tillers, and semi-sterility; Wuyunjing24 mutants exhibit slight dwarfing with normal tiller number and seed setting rate
mechanism: OsIAA23 disruption affects root architecture (crown root, lateral root formation) and fertility via auxin signaling pathway

genes: GmSDP1-1 (GmSDP1-1, RNAi target, Glycine max), GmSDP1-4 (GmSDP1-4, RNAi target, Glycine max)
phenotype: Knockdown of GmSDP1 genes increases seed oil content by 2.2-3.1% and alters fatty acid composition (increased oleic acid, decreased linoleic acid) in soybean.
mechanism: GmSDP1 genes regulate fatty acid composition by preferentially cleaving oleic acid in triacylglycerol (TAG) degradation, leading to higher oleic acid retention in seeds when knocked down.

genes: PhC3H (PhC3H, coumarate 3-hydroxylase, Petunia x hybrida), PhHCT (PhHCT, hydroxycinnamoyl transferase, Petunia x hybrida)
phenotype: Downregulation of PhC3H and PhHCT reduces emission of phenylpropene volatiles (eugenol, isoeugenol, benzyl benzoate) and benzenoid volatiles (benzaldehyde, phenylacetaldehyde) in petunia flowers. Novel volatile p-cresol is detected in ir-PhC3H lines.
mechanism: PhC3H and PhHCT are key enzymes in the phenylpropanoid pathway. Their downregulation disrupts monolignol biosynthesis and volatile phenylpropene production. Reduced PhC3H causes widespread downregulation of 16/18 FVBP-related genes including PhPALs, PhC4Hs, and PhHCT.

genes: SLR1 (SLR1, rice tiller number regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SLR1 fused with GFP increases tiller number and plant height in rice.
mechanism: SLR1 inhibits tiller bud outgrowth by interacting with MOC1 and preventing its degradation.

genes: SLR1 (SLR1, rice tiller number regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi knockdown of SLR1 results in fewer tillers and taller plants.
mechanism: SLR1 promotes tiller bud outgrowth by stabilizing MOC1 protein levels.

genes: GID1 (GID1, GA signaling component, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of GID1 reduces tiller number and increases plant height.
mechanism: GID1 promotes GA signaling, leading to degradation of SLR1 and MOC1.

genes: gRNA (guide RNA targeting SLR1, synthetic)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated disruption of SLR1 increases tiller number and reduces plant height.
mechanism: Disruption of SLR1 leads to accumulation of MOC1, promoting tiller bud outgrowth.

genes: GA20ox-1 (GA20ox-1, GA biosynthesis gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of GA20ox-1 reduces tiller number and increases plant height.
mechanism: GA20ox-1 enhances GA biosynthesis, promoting stem elongation and inhibiting tiller bud outgrowth.

genes: CpCYC-B (promoter, Carica papaya)
phenotype: GUS expression levels vary with promoter length
mechanism: regulation via promoter elements

genes: CpLCY-B (promoter, Carica papaya)
phenotype: GUS expression levels vary with promoter length
mechanism: regulation via promoter elements

genes: GhBOP1 (NPR1-like gene, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: GhBOP1pro:GUS transgenic plants show GUS staining focused at lateral-organ boundaries (LOBs) and expanded staining after V. dahliae inoculation
mechanism: GhBOP1 expression is spatially induced by V. dahliae infection, with GUS activity increasing 7.5-fold in infected zones

genes: GhBOP1 (NPR1-like gene, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: GhBOP1 overexpression plants show increased resistance to V. dahliae with reduced disease symptoms and fungal biomass
mechanism: GhBOP1 enhances lignin synthesis gene expression (PAL1, C4H1, 4CL1, C3H1, CCoMT1, CAD5) and promotes GhTGA3 transcriptional activity for GhPR1

genes: GhCYP3 (GhCYP-3, cyclophilin, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhCYP-3 in Arabidopsis significantly improves Verticillium wilt resistance, with transgenic plants showing less wilting, smaller leaf etiolation, and reduced fungal colonization compared to wild type.
mechanism: GhCYP-3 exhibits antifungal activity, inhibiting conidia germination and hyphal growth of Verticillium dahliae. Recombinant GhCYP-3 and transgenic plant extracts show significant antifungal effects in vitro.

genes: RcWRI3 (RcWRI3, transcription factor involved in TAG synthesis, castor), RcDGAT1 (RcDGAT1, diacylglycerol acyltransferase, castor)
phenotype: Co-expression of RcWRI3 and RcDGAT1 resulted in 11.0 µg TAGs per mg of dry leaves, compared to 2.0 µg TAGs from the control.
mechanism: RcWRI3 and RcDGAT1 cooperate to enhance TAG synthesis in leaves.

genes: RcWRI3 (RcWRI3, transcription factor involved in TAG synthesis, castor), RcDGAT1 (RcDGAT1, diacylglycerol acyltransferase, castor), RcFATB (RcFATB, acyl-ACP thioesterase B, castor)
phenotype: Addition of RcFATB increased TAG content up to 17.4 µg per mg of dry leaves.
mechanism: RcFATB enhances C16:0 accumulation in TAGs, contributing to increased TAG synthesis when combined with RcWRI3 and RcDGAT1.

genes: RcWRI3 (RcWRI3, transcription factor involved in TAG synthesis, castor), RcDGAT1 (RcDGAT1, diacylglycerol acyltransferase, castor), RcFATB (RcFATB, acyl-ACP thioesterase B, castor), RcACS2 (RcACS2, acyl-CoA synthetase 2, castor)
phenotype: Combination of RcWRI3, RcDGAT1, RcFATB, and RcACS2 resulted in 20.1 µg TAGs per mg of dry leaves, a tenfold increase compared to the p19 control.
mechanism: Synergistic action of RcWRI3, RcDGAT1, RcFATB, and RcACS2 enhances TAG accumulation by optimizing fatty acid metabolism and TAG assembly.

genes: RcFATB (RcFATB, acyl-ACP thioesterase B, castor)
phenotype: Overexpression of RcFATB alone in leaves resulted in a 13-fold increase in TAG content compared to the P19 control.
mechanism: RcFATB increases C16:0 accumulation in TAGs by releasing C16:0 from acyl-ACP, enhancing TAG synthesis.

genes: RcACS2 (RcACS2, acyl-CoA synthetase 2, castor)
phenotype: Overexpression of RcACS2 increased TAG content from 0.35 µg/mg in the control to 1.55 µg per mg of dry leaves.
mechanism: RcACS2 enhances TAG accumulation by converting free fatty acids into acyl-CoA, which are then used in TAG synthesis.

genes: RcDGAT1 (RcDGAT1, diacylglycerol acyltransferase, castor)
phenotype: Overexpression of RcDGAT1 led to a significant increase in TAG accumulation in leaves.
mechanism: RcDGAT1 catalyzes the final step of the Kennedy pathway, enhancing TAG synthesis in non-seed tissues.

genes: RcWRI3 (RcWRI3, transcription factor involved in TAG synthesis, castor)
phenotype: Expression of RcWRI3 led to an increase in TAG content in leaves compared to the p19 control.
mechanism: RcWRI3 activates genes involved in fatty acid biosynthesis and TAG assembly, enhancing oil accumulation.

genes: miR319g (microRNA 319g, non-coding regulatory RNA, Stevia rebaudiana), miRStv_11 (microRNA Stv_11, non-coding regulatory RNA, Stevia rebaudiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR319g represses its target genes KO, KS, and UGT85C2, reducing steviol glycosides content by 69.9% for stevioside and 72.5% for rebaudioside-A.
mechanism: miR319g binds to the 3′-UTR of its target mRNAs (KO, KS, UGT85C2), causing post-transcriptional repression.

genes: miRStv_11 (microRNA Stv_11, non-coding regulatory RNA, Stevia rebaudiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of miRStv_11 enhances its target gene KAH, increasing steviol glycosides content by 12.9% for stevioside and 22.8% for rebaudioside-A.
mechanism: miRStv_11 binds to the promoter region of KAH gene, inducing its expression through transcriptional activation.

genes: anti-miR319g (antisense precursor of miR319g, non-coding regulatory RNA, synthetic), anti-miRStv_11 (antisense precursor of miRStv_11, non-coding regulatory RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Knockdown of miR319g derepresses its target genes KO, KS, and UGT85C2, increasing steviol glycosides content by 16.96% for stevioside and 19.43% for rebaudioside-A.
mechanism: Anti-miR319g binds to miR319g, blocking its interaction with target mRNAs and derepressing gene expression.

genes: anti-miRStv_11 (antisense precursor of miRStv_11, non-coding regulatory RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: Knockdown of miRStv_11 represses its target gene KAH, reducing steviol glycosides content by 35.67% for stevioside and 19.22% for rebaudioside-A.
mechanism: Anti-miRStv_11 binds to miRStv_11, blocking its interaction with the KAH promoter and repressing gene expression.

genes: anti-miR319g (antisense precursor of miR319g, non-coding regulatory RNA, synthetic), miRStv_11 (microRNA Stv_11, non-coding regulatory RNA, Stevia rebaudiana)
phenotype: Co-expression of anti-miR319g and miRStv_11 increases stevioside by 24.5% and rebaudioside-A by 51%, enhancing the rebaudioside-A to stevioside ratio from 0.39 to 0.47.
mechanism: Anti-miR319g derepresses KO, KS, and UGT85C2, while miRStv_11 upregulates KAH, collectively enhancing steviol glycosides biosynthesis.

genes: WRKY72 (WRKY72, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-generated wrky72-4 and wrky72-7 mutant lines show no significant difference in Xoo susceptibility compared to wild-type.
mechanism: Functional redundancy of other WRKY genes compensates for WRKY72 knockout, maintaining susceptibility to Xoo.

genes: WRKY72 (WRKY72, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OxWRKY72T129A lines show higher susceptibility to Xoo than OxWRKY72 lines, with 45% lesion area and increased bacterial growth rates.
mechanism: Phosphorylation at Thr129 normally inhibits WRKY72's DNA-binding activity; mutation to Ala removes this inhibition, enhancing suppression of JA biosynthesis.

genes: ONAC066 (Oryza sativa NAC domain-containing protein 066, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of ONAC066 in transgenic rice improved drought and oxidative stress tolerance and increased ABA sensitivity, accompanied with decreased rate of water loss, increased contents of proline and soluble sugars, decreased accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and upregulated expression of stress-related genes under drought stress condition.
mechanism: ONAC066 binds directly to a JBS-like cis-element in OsDREB2A promoter and activates the transcription of OsDREB2A.

genes: ONAC066 (Oryza sativa NAC domain-containing protein 066, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated suppression of ONAC066 attenuated drought and oxidative stress tolerance and decreased ABA sensitivity, accompanied with increased rate of water loss, decreased contents of proline and soluble sugars, elevated accumulation of ROS and downregulated expression of stress-related genes under drought stress condition.
mechanism: ONAC066 suppression reduces activation of OsDREB2A through JBSL cis-element binding.

genes: BnPDFL (BnaC02g23620D, defensin-like protein with Cd-chelating activity, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Heterologous overexpression of BnPDFL in Arabidopsis significantly enhanced Cd tolerance, as evidenced by longer root growth on 50 μM CdCl2 compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: BnPDFL chelates Cd, reducing its toxicity and enhancing plant tolerance.

genes: AtPDF2.2 (At2g02100, plant defensin, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtPDF2.3 (At2g02130, plant defensin, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Functional disruption of AtPDF2.2 and AtPDF2.3 in Arabidopsis significantly decreased Cd tolerance, with roots of mutants showing increased sensitivity to Cd compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: Plant defensins AtPDF2.2 and AtPDF2.3 mediate Cd chelation and detoxification, and their disruption reduces Cd tolerance.

genes: HTA9 (histone variant H2A.Z, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FLAG-HTA9_N partially rescues the early-flowering phenotype in hta9hta11 mutants, with increased FLC expression and reduced FT expression compared to hta9hta11.
mechanism: H2A.Z monoubiquitination (H2A.Zub) mediated by AtBMI1 proteins is required for transcriptional repression of genes like FT and FLC, which regulates flowering time.

genes: HTA9 (histone variant H2A.Z, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FLAG-HTA9_RK (K129R mutation) partially rescues the early-flowering phenotype in hta9hta11 mutants, with increased FLC expression but less reduction in FT expression compared to FLAG-HTA9_N.
mechanism: H2A.Z monoubiquitination at lysine 129 is required for full repression of FT and activation of FLC, indicating that both incorporation of H2A.Z and its modification are necessary for flowering time regulation.

genes: HTA9 (histone variant H2A.Z, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FLAG-HTA9_RR (K129R and K132R mutations) partially rescues the early-flowering phenotype in hta9hta11 mutants, with increased FLC expression but minimal reduction in FT expression compared to hta9hta11.
mechanism: H2A.Z monoubiquitination at lysine 129 is the primary target for repression of FT and activation of FLC, while lysine 132 may contribute to a lesser extent.

genes: OsZIP1 (transporter for Zn, Cu, Cd, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsZIP1 increases rice growth under excess Zn, Cu, and Cd stress and reduces metal accumulation in plants.
mechanism: OsZIP1 functions as a metal exporter, reducing metal accumulation in roots and shoots.

genes: OsZIP1 (transporter for Zn, Cu, Cd, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi lines show reduced growth under excess metal stress and increased metal accumulation.
mechanism: Knockdown of OsZIP1 leads to higher metal accumulation.

genes: OsZIP1 (promoter region, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: GUS expression under Cd stress.
mechanism: OsZIP1 promoter activity is induced by Cd.

genes: SAP1 (secreted aspartic protease 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), SAP2 (secreted aspartic protease 2, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAP1ΔSP and SAP2ΔSP (cytosolic variants) in Arabidopsis thaliana does not reduce P. syringae bacterial growth compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: Apoplastic localization of SAP1 and SAP2 is essential for bacterial growth suppression; cytosolic variants lack this effect.

genes: SAP1 (secreted aspartic protease 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: SAP1 RNAi plants show increased susceptibility to P. syringae compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: SAP1 and SAP2 redundantly contribute to resistance against P. syringae; SAP1 RNAi disrupts this defense mechanism.

genes: SAP1 (secreted aspartic protease 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), SAP2 (secreted aspartic protease 2, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: sap1 sap2 CRISPR-Cas9 knockout plants show increased susceptibility to P. syringae compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: SAP1 and SAP2 redundantly contribute to resistance against P. syringae; their knockout disrupts this defense mechanism.

genes: SAP1 (secreted aspartic protease 1, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)
phenotype: Overexpression of SAP1D63/136A (protease-dead variant) in Arabidopsis thaliana does not reduce P. syringae bacterial growth compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: SAP1 protease activity is essential for its function in P. syringae growth suppression; the D63/136A mutation inactivates this activity.

genes: AtKASI (target gene, CRISPR/Cas9 disruption, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Disruption of KASI leads to defective growth (smaller and shorter seedlings, semi-dwarf phenotype) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: KS-B (ketoacyl-ACP synthase domain from PUFA synthase, Thraustochytrium)
phenotype: Seed-specific expression of the KS domain in wild-type Arabidopsis significantly increased seed weight and seed oil, and altered the unsaturation level of fatty acids in seeds, as well as promoted seed germination and early seedling growth.
mechanism: The condensation process of fatty acid biosynthesis in plants is a limiting step, and overexpression of the KS domain from a PUFA synthase of microbial origin offers a new strategy to increase oil production in oilseed plants.

genes: SDG701 (H3K4-specific methyltransferase important for rice plant development, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockdown of SDG701 results in global decrease in H3K4me2/H3K4me3 levels and misregulation of genes involved in diverse developmental processes in rice
mechanism: RNAi-mediated knockdown of SDG701, an H3K4-specific methyltransferase, disrupts histone methylation patterns and gene regulation

genes: CsMYB5-1 (CsMYB5-1, transcription factor, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsMYB5-1 increases anthocyanin, total flavonoid, and proanthocyanidin accumulation in stems/leaves by ~6-10 fold compared to wild type.
mechanism: CsMYB5-1 up-regulates flavonoid pathway genes including DFR2 and ANS, enhancing anthocyanin and proanthocyanidin biosynthesis.

genes: CsMYB5-2 (CsMYB5-2, transcription factor, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsMYB5-2 increases anthocyanin, total flavonoid, and proanthocyanidin accumulation in stems/leaves by ~4-10 fold compared to wild type.
mechanism: CsMYB5-2 up-regulates flavonoid pathway genes including DFR2 and ANS, enhancing anthocyanin and proanthocyanidin biosynthesis.

genes: PHYB (wild-type coding region, Arabidopsis thaliana, native promoter)
phenotype: Complementation studies using the wild type PHYB coding region under the control of the native promoter reestablished the ceh1 mutant phenotypes in the revertants
mechanism: NA

genes: AtOLE1 (oleosin, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtOLE2 (oleosin, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtOLE3 (oleosin, Arabidopsis thaliana), BnaOLE1 (oleosin, Brassica napus), BnaOLE2 (oleosin, Brassica napus), BnaOLE3 (oleosin, Brassica napus), BnaOLE4 (oleosin, Brassica napus)
gene_construct: glycinin promoter-AtOLE1-terminator, glycinin promoter-AtOLE2-terminator, glycinin promoter-AtOLE3-terminator, glycinin promoter-BnaOLE1-terminator, glycinin promoter-BnaOLE2-terminator, glycinin promoter-BnaOLE3-terminator, glycinin promoter-BnaOLE4-terminator
phenotype: Overexpression of these oleosin genes in Arabidopsis increased the seed oil content slightly, except for BnaOLE3. The average oil body size of the transgenic seeds was slightly larger than that of the wild type (WT), except for BnaOLE1. The seed size and thousand-seed weight (TSW) also increased in the transgenic lines, which could lead to increased total lipid production.
mechanism: Oleosin enhances oil body stabilization and lipid metabolism, leading to increased oil content and altered fatty acid profiles.

genes: OsSUF4 (OsSUF4, transcription factor, rice), RFT1 (RFT1, florigen gene, rice), Hd3a (Hd3a, florigen gene, rice)
phenotype: Knockdown of OsSUF4 results in late-flowering phenotype in rice under both long day and short day conditions.
mechanism: OsSUF4 promotes flowering by activating the expression of florigen genes RFT1 and Hd3a. Knockdown reduces RFT1 and Hd3a expression, delaying flowering.

genes: OsSUF4 (OsSUF4, transcription factor, rice)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSUF4 increases the transcription levels of OsSUF4 in rice plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsSUF4 (OsSUF4, transcription factor, rice), SDG725C (SDG725C, H3K36 methyltransferase, rice)
phenotype: Co-expression of OsSUF4-YN and SDG725C-YC in tobacco leaves results in YFP signals in nuclei, indicating in planta interaction.
mechanism: OsSUF4 interacts with SDG725C in Nicotiana benthamiana leaf epidermal cells, as shown by BiFC experiments.

genes: DAD1 (carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 8, SL biosynthesis enzyme, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of DAD1 increases HPC density by ~2-fold and promotes arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) symbiosis in Petunia hybrida.
mechanism: DAD1 catalyzes SL biosynthesis, which stimulates HPC formation and AM colonization through SL signaling.

genes: OsNHX5 (OsNHX5, Na+/H+ antiporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of gpa6 mutant phenotypes including floury endosperm appearance, proglutelin accumulation, and abnormal glutelin deposition
mechanism: OsNHX5 regulates luminal pH of Golgi, TGN, and PVC, essential for proglutelin trafficking

genes: OsNHX5 (Os09g0286400, Na+/H+ antiporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Rescue of gpa6 mutant phenotypes including floury endosperm appearance, proglutelin accumulation, and abnormal glutelin deposition
mechanism: OsNHX5 regulates luminal pH of Golgi, TGN, and PVC, essential for proglutelin trafficking

genes: MtmiR156B (microRNA, miR156 regulatory element, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Overexpression of MtmiR156B results in small seeds and pods with loss of spines on pod surface in Medicago truncatula.
mechanism: MtmiR156/MtSPL regulation module controls pod and seed development by repressing targeted MtSPL genes involved in spiky pod formation and seed size regulation.

genes: BOA (BROTHER OF LUX ARRHYTHMO, rhythmic transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: BOA-NL3F10H fusion shows rhythmic bioluminescence with low amplitude in constant light, correlates with increased period of CCA1p:LUC reporter in transgenic lines
mechanism: NanoLUC stability allows tracking of BOA protein dynamics; estimated half-life of BOA-NL3F10H fusion is ~57 hours, with BOA protein degradation dominating reporter dynamics (half-life 8.66 hours)

genes: NL3F10H (NanoLUC with 3× FLAG-10× His tag, engineered luciferase, Oplophorus gracilirostris)
phenotype: 35S:NL3F10H expression in protoplasts decays from 9 hours, with bioluminescence detected in agroinfiltrated seedlings
mechanism: NanoLUC stability (half-life ~37 days at 4°C) enables long-term quantification in plant extracts; 35S promoter drives constitutive expression

genes: JcHDZ16 (homeodomain-leucine zipper transcription factor, Jatropha curcas, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Transgenic rice plants overexpressing JcHDZ16 show increased sensitivity to salinity stress (leaf rolling, yellowing, 100% mortality after 12-day recovery) and ABA (shorter shoots and roots under ABA treatment) compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: JcHDZ16 negatively regulates salinity responses through ABA-mediated signaling pathways, downregulating salt stress-responsive genes and reducing antioxidant enzyme activities.

genes: TT16 (TT16, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of tt16 mutant phenotypes in the nucellus and ii1' cell layer
mechanism: TT16 regulates IAB deposition non-cell autonomously along the proximal-distal axis

genes: TT16 (TT16, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Heterogeneous complementation of tt16 IAB defects ranging from faint auramine O staining to wild type-looking phenotype
mechanism: TT16 regulates IAB deposition non-cell autonomously along the proximal-distal axis

genes: TT1 (TT1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Strong fluorescence in the endothelium from the first stages of ovule development until globular embryo stage
mechanism: TT1 is specifically expressed in sporophytic maternal tissues

genes: MYB30 (MYB30, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS staining in the endothelium and funiculus of seeds at early globular embryo stage
mechanism: MYB30 might play a role in de novo cutin deposition after fertilization

genes: WRKY56 (Potri.002G193000, WRKY transcription factor, Populus simonii × P. nigra)
phenotype: Overexpression of WRKY56 increases salt tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with transgenic lines showing 40.9-80% higher fresh weight under 100-150 mmol/L NaCl, 18.97-51.62% higher seed germination rates, and elevated SOD/POD activities and proline content compared to wild type
mechanism: WRKY56 enhances salt tolerance by increasing ROS scavenging capacity through elevated SOD and POD activities, proline accumulation, and reduced MDA content in transgenic Arabidopsis

genes: POLLUX (POLLUX, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), SEC13 (SEC13, nucleoporin, Arabidopsis thaliana), ShRK1 (ShRK1, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), ShRK2 (ShRK2, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana), SYMRK (SYMRK, receptor-like kinase, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: Complementation of SNUPO mutants restores wild-type levels of Hpa reproductive success and haustoria morphology in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: Rp1-D21 (hypersensitive response-inducing NLR, maize), HA (hemagglutinin tag, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient overexpression induces hypersensitive response (HR) in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: Rp1-D21 is an autoactive NLR that triggers HR through effector-triggered immunity.

genes: HCT1806 (hydroxycinnamoyltransferase, maize), EGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Co-expression with Rp1-D21-HA almost completely suppresses Rp1-D21-induced HR in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: HCT1806 suppresses HR by interacting with Rp1-D21 and modulating cell wall-related processes.

genes: ZmPGH1 (polygalacturonase homolog, maize), EYFP (enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Co-expression with Rp1-D21-HA partially suppresses Rp1-D21-induced HR in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: ZmPGH1 suppresses HR by modulating programmed cell death through cell wall-related mechanisms.

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic), EYFP (enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Used as a negative control; does not affect Rp1-D21-induced HR in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: NA

genes: RPM1(D505V) (autoactive NLR, Arabidopsis)
phenotype: Induces strong and rapid HR in N. benthamiana leaves; co-expression with ZmPGH1-EYFP partially suppresses HR.
mechanism: ZmPGH1 suppresses HR by modulating programmed cell death through cell wall-related mechanisms.

genes: SHB1 (suppressor of hybrid breakdown 1, transcriptional coactivator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of SHB1:GFP driven by CaMV35S promoter increases PIF4 expression and promotes hypocotyl elongation under red light in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SHB1 interacts with CCA1 and LHY to enhance PIF4 expression, which mediates red light-induced hypocotyl elongation and thermomorphogenesis.

genes: CCA1 (circadian clock-associated 1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), LHY (late elongated hypocotyl, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CCA1:FLAG and LHY:MYC driven by CaMV35S promoters enhances PIF4 expression and rescues hypocotyl elongation in cca1 lhy double mutants under red light in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CCA1 and LHY bind to the PIF4 promoter via MYB elements, recruit SHB1 to activate PIF4 expression, and mediate red light and thermomorphogenesis.

genes: CCA1 (circadian clock-associated 1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), LHY (late elongated hypocotyl, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), SHB1 (suppressor of hybrid breakdown 1, transcriptional coactivator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: BiFC assays in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves show physical interaction between CCA1/LHY and SHB1, confirming their co-action in regulating PIF4 expression in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CCA1 and LHY interact with SHB1 via their C-terminal domains, forming a complex that binds to the PIF4 promoter to activate expression under red light.

genes: CCA1 (circadian clock-associated 1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), LHY (late elongated hypocotyl, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), SHB1 (suppressor of hybrid breakdown 1, transcriptional coactivator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Trans-activation assays in cca1 lhy protoplasts show that CCA1 and LHY recruit SHB1 to activate PIF4 promoter-driven luciferase expression under red light in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: CCA1 and LHY bind to the PIF4 promoter via MYB elements, recruit SHB1 to mediate red light-induced PIF4 expression, and require phyB for full activity.

genes: CymMV CP (CymMV coat protein, CymMV), ORSV CP (Odontoglossum ringspot tobamovirus coat protein, ORSV)
phenotype: Transgenic plants show resistance to CymMV and ORSV, with reduced viral accumulation and symptoms in systemic leaves.
mechanism: RNA-mediated interference (RNAi) likely triggers gene silencing for viral resistance.

genes: CymMV CP (CymMV coat protein, CymMV), ORSV CP (Odontoglossum ringspot tobamovirus coat protein, ORSV)
phenotype: Transgenic plants show resistance to CymMV and ORSV, with reduced viral accumulation and symptoms in systemic leaves.
mechanism: RNA-mediated interference (RNAi) likely triggers gene silencing for viral resistance.

plant_species: Lycium ruthenicum, Lycium barbarum var. auranticarpum
genes: LbNCED1 (9-cis-epoxycarotenoid dioxygenase, Lycium)
phenotype: Silencing of LbNCED1 gene significantly reduces ABA content (by 68.43-81.65%) and anthocyanin accumulation (by 10.48-65.48%) in Lycium fruits, delays fruit coloration, and decreases coloration rate (CR) by 60-80% compared to controls
mechanism: LbNCED1-derived ABA transcriptionally activates MYB-bHLH-WD40 transcription factor complex, which upregulates structural genes in flavonoid biosynthetic pathway to promote anthocyanin production

genes: GmFAD2-1A (delta-12 Fatty Acid Desaturase 2, soybean), GmFAD2-1B (delta-12 Fatty Acid Desaturase 2, soybean)
phenotype: Overexpression of CRISPR-induced mutations in GmFAD2–1A and GmFAD2–1B increases oleic acid content to over 80% and decreases linoleic acid to 1.3–1.7% in soybean seeds.
mechanism: Loss of GmFAD2 function reduces linoleic acid conversion from oleic acid, leading to increased oleic acid accumulation.

genes: AtIPT3 (adenosine phosphate isopentenyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtIPT7 (adenosine phosphate isopentenyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtIPT9 (tRNA isopentenyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtIPT3 in AtLEC2-GR transgenic tobacco did not form embryogenic callus under DEX induction, but increased lateral branching and floral number at reproductive stage.
mechanism: AtIPT3 down-regulated embryo development regulators (BBM, PLT2, LAFL, AGL15), auxin biosynthesis (GH3.6, YUC4), and auxin transport (PIN1, PIN2) genes, while up-regulating GA biosynthesis enzymes (GA20ox1, GA20ox2, GA3ox1), which may inhibit embryogenic callus formation.

genes: AtIPT3 (adenosine phosphate isopentenyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtIPT7 (adenosine phosphate isopentenyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana), AtIPT9 (tRNA isopentenyltransferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtIPT7 in AtLEC2-GR transgenic tobacco formed embryogenic callus under DEX induction and increased shoot regeneration efficiency by 2-3.5 folds on hormone-free medium compared to AtLEC2-GR alone.

genes: OsLIS-L1 (lissencephaly type-1-like 1, Oryza sativa)

mechanism: OsLIS-L1 regulates cell proliferation in the first internodes under the panicle, and its knockout leads to shortened internodes.

genes: PvC3H72 (transcriptional activation factor, Panicum virgatum)

mechanism: PvC3H72 up-regulates ICE1–CBF–COR regulon and ABA-responsive genes during cold treatment, enhancing cold tolerance through increased expression of cold-responsive genes like PvCOR47 and PvWCOR413.

mechanism: NcHCT functions as a hydroxycinnamoyl transferase in lignin biosynthesis, partially restoring expression of upstream genes (C3H, C4H, HCT) but not fully normalizing lignin monomer composition (S/G ratio 0.78 vs 0.84 in cse mutant).

phenotype: Knockdown of lncRNA973 in Gossypium hirsutum reduces salt tolerance, as evidenced by severe wilting, leaf yellowing, and stem browning under 250 mM NaCl stress, along with increased malondialdehyde (MDA) and proline (Pro) content, reduced relative water content, and impaired ROS-scavenging enzyme activities.
mechanism: LncRNA973 knockdown decreases salt tolerance by downregulating ROS-scavenging genes (e.g., SOD, CAT, POD), transcription factors (e.g., MYB5, WRKY46), and Na+/K+ transporters (e.g., NHX7), while upregulating proline-synthesizing genes (e.g., P5CS). It also disrupts miR399/PHO2 regulation in cotton.

genes: Gt5GT (glucosyltransferase, Gentiana triflora × Gentiana scabra), Gt3′GT (glucosyltransferase, Gentiana triflora × Gentiana scabra), Gt5/3′AT (acyltransferase, Gentiana triflora × Gentiana scabra)
phenotype: Knockout of Gt5GT, Gt3′GT, and Gt5/3′AT leads to altered anthocyanin profiles and flower coloration (pale red violet, dull pink, pale mauve) in Gentiana triflora × Gentiana scabra.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout disrupts anthocyanin modification pathways, altering glucosylation and acylation of delphinidin derivatives, which affects flower coloration and anthocyanin composition.

genes: NIK1 (AtNIK1, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of nik1-1 knockout phenotype restores enhanced susceptibility to Cabbage leaf curl virus (CaLCuV) and Tobacco rattle virus (TRV), and suppresses constitutive SA accumulation and cell death.
mechanism: NIK1 negatively regulates FLS2/BAK1 complex formation and PTI responses. Complementation restores NIK1's negative regulation of immune signaling.

genes: NIK1 (AtNIK1, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of NIK1-6HA increases susceptibility to Pst DC3000 by ~5-fold compared to wild-type, suppresses flg22-induced MAPK activation and ROS burst, and reduces expression of PTI early response genes.
mechanism: NIK1 overexpression impairs FLS2/BAK1 complex formation and attenuates PTI signaling, leading to compromised innate immunity.

genes: NIK1 (AtNIK1, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of NIK1-T474D (phosphomimetic mutant) suppresses ribosomal gene expression and activates antiviral defense signaling in bak1-4 and fls2 mutants.
mechanism: Phosphomimetic NIK1-T474D enhances interaction with FLS2/BAK1 complex, leading to RPL10 phosphorylation and translational control of antiviral immunity.

genes: GHD8 (Ghd8, transcription factor, Oryza sativa L.), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GHD8-GFP in rice delays heading date by ~3 days under natural long-day conditions compared to wild type.
mechanism: GHD8-GFP binds to the Ghd7 promoter via a heterotrimeric complex with OsHAP5b and HD1, activating Ghd7 transcription to suppress Hd3a and delay flowering.

genes: PvRbohB (respiratory burst oxidase homolog B, NADPH oxidase involved in ROS production, Phaseolus vulgaris)
phenotype: PvRbohB silencing reduces lateral root density by ~15% and alters symbiotic responses: enhances AM colonization while impairing rhizobial infection in Phaseolus vulgaris
mechanism: PvRbohB regulates ROS scavenging, cell wall remodeling, and phytohormone homeostasis during nodulation and mycorrhization by modulating peroxidase activity, cell wall biosynthesis genes, and auxin/ethylene signaling pathways

genes: osa-MIR156f (microRNA, miR156f, Oryza sativa L.), OsGA3ox2 (GA3ox2, gibberellin 3-oxidase, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: Transgenic line D18–11 shows moderate height, more effective tillers, and increased grain yield in both seasonal and ratooning rice. Axillary buds outgrow from basal nodes before seasonal harvest, contributing to improved plant architecture and yield.
mechanism: osa-miR156f down-regulates tillering regulators (TB1, LAX1) and strigolactone (SL) biosynthesis/signaling genes (D10, D27, D53). Stem-specific expression reduces SL content in shoots while increasing it in roots, promoting tiller outgrowth without severe dwarfism.

genes: PDX1.2 (PDX1.2, pyridoxine synthase 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PDX1.2-YFP increases fluorescence intensity in cotyledons and roots under heat stress in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PDX1.2 protein accumulation under heat stress enhances fluorescence in guard cells.

genes: YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: 35S-YFP plants display higher fluorescence intensity compared to non-transformed controls.
mechanism: NA

genes: SWEET11 (SWEET11, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa), SWEET13 (SWEET13, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa), SWEET14 (SWEET14, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: GUS activity detected in uninfected and infected leaves, with vein-specific accumulation for SWEET13 and SWEET14
mechanism: Translational reporter fusion enables visualization of SWEET protein accumulation during Xoo infection

genes: SWEET11 (SWEET11, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa), SWEET13 (SWEET13, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa), SWEET14 (SWEET14, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Vein-specific GUS activity in uninfected leaves, inducible by Xoo strains harboring PthXo2B
mechanism: Translational reporter fusion enables visualization of SWEET13 protein accumulation during Xoo infection

genes: SWEET11 (SWEET11, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa), SWEET13 (SWEET13, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa), SWEET14 (SWEET14, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Vein-specific GUS activity in uninfected leaves, inducible by Xoo strains harboring PthXo3, AvrXa7, or TalF
mechanism: Translational reporter fusion enables visualization of SWEET14 protein accumulation during Xoo infection

genes: SWEET11 (SWEET11, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Reduced SWEET11 mRNA levels and defects in seed filling
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9-induced frameshift mutations disrupt SWEET11 function

genes: SWEET13 (SWEET13, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Reduced SWEET13 mRNA levels and no detectable growth or yield defects
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9-induced frameshift mutations disrupt SWEET13 function

genes: SWEET14 (SWEET14, SWEET gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Reduced SWEET14 mRNA levels and no detectable growth or yield defects
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9-induced frameshift mutations disrupt SWEET14 function

genes: GmNHX1 (Glycine max Na+/H+ exchanger 1, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmNHX1 in Arabidopsis increases stem length by ~30%, rosette leaves by ~25%, fresh weight by ~40%, and dry weight by ~35% under salt stress compared to wild-type.
mechanism: GmNHX1 enhances salt tolerance by maintaining a high K+/Na+ ratio in roots, elevating Na+ efflux rate, and inducing expression of SKOR, SOS1, and AKT1.

genes: GmNHX1 (Glycine max Na+/H+ exchanger 1, Glycine max)
phenotype: GmNHX1-GFP fusion protein localizes to vacuolar membranes in onion bulb endothelium cells.
mechanism: Vacuolar membrane localization of GmNHX1 enables Na+ efflux regulation and K+/Na+ homeostasis maintenance under salt stress.

genes: OsICL (OsICL, isocitrate lyase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: The Aticl mutant expressing OsICL driven by the native AtICL promoter showed improved germination rates and seedling growth under salt stress compared to the Aticl mutant.
mechanism: OsICL expression reverted the salt sensitivity phenotypes of the Aticl knockout mutant by modulating energy metabolism through the glyoxylate cycle.

genes: OsICL (OsICL, isocitrate lyase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: The Aticl mutant overexpressing OsICL driven by the 35SCaMV promoter exhibited higher germination rates and seedling growth under salt stress compared to the Aticl mutant.
mechanism: OsICL expression reverted the salt sensitivity phenotypes of the Aticl knockout mutant by modulating energy metabolism through the glyoxylate cycle.

genes: OsICL (OsICL, isocitrate lyase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: WT overexpressing OsICL driven by the 35SCaMV promoter showed improved germination rates and seedling growth under salt stress compared to the Aticl mutant.
mechanism: OsICL expression reverted the salt sensitivity phenotypes of the Aticl knockout mutant by modulating energy metabolism through the glyoxylate cycle.

genes: SNC1-1 (SNC1-1, active mutant form of SNC1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of SNC1-1 in guard cells causes stomatal closure defect in response to pathogens and ABA, which is temperature-dependent
mechanism: SNC1 activation in guard cells inhibits ABA response, leading to stomatal closure defect

genes: BON1 (BON1, wild-type, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of BON1 in guard cells restores wild-type stomatal response to pathogens and ABA in bon1-1 mutants
mechanism: BON1 has cell autonomous activity in guard cells to restore stomatal defense function

genes: VdMYB1 (VdMYB1, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Vitis davidii)
phenotype: VdMYB1-GFP fusion protein localized to the nucleus in Arabidopsis protoplasts and onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: VdMYB1 functions as a transcriptional activator in yeast and localizes to the nucleus in plant cells.

genes: PgUGT84A23 (Punica granatum UGT84A23, UDP-glucosyltransferase, Punica granatum), PgUGT84A24 (Punica granatum UGT84A24, UDP-glucosyltransferase, Punica granatum)
phenotype: Single-gene CRISPR/Cas9 editing in pomegranate hairy roots did not produce the gallic acid 3-O- and 4-O-glucoside accumulation seen in dual-edited lines; the phenotype required editing both PgUGT84A23 and PgUGT84A24.
mechanism: NA

genes: PgUGT84A23 (Punica granatum UGT84A23, UDP-glucosyltransferase, Punica granatum), PgUGT84A24 (Punica granatum UGT84A24, UDP-glucosyltransferase, Punica granatum)
phenotype: Single-gene CRISPR/Cas9 editing in pomegranate hairy roots did not produce the gallic acid 3-O- and 4-O-glucoside accumulation seen in dual-edited lines; the phenotype required editing both PgUGT84A23 and PgUGT84A24.
mechanism: NA

genes: PgUGT84A23 (Punica granatum UGT84A23, UDP-glucosyltransferase, Punica granatum), PgUGT84A24 (Punica granatum UGT84A24, UDP-glucosyltransferase, Punica granatum)
phenotype: Single-gene CRISPR/Cas9 editing in pomegranate hairy roots did not produce the gallic acid 3-O- and 4-O-glucoside accumulation seen in dual-edited lines; the phenotype required editing both PgUGT84A23 and PgUGT84A24.
mechanism: NA

genes: PgUGT84A23 (Punica granatum UGT84A23, UDP-glucosyltransferase, Punica granatum), PgUGT84A24 (Punica granatum UGT84A24, UDP-glucosyltransferase, Punica granatum)
phenotype: Dual CRISPR/Cas9 editing of PgUGT84A23 and PgUGT84A24 in pomegranate hairy roots caused a unique accumulation of gallic acid 3-O- and 4-O-glucosides, not seen in empty-vector controls or single-edited lines.
mechanism: NA
