phenotype: Dual CRISPR/Cas9 editing of PgUGT84A23 and PgUGT84A24 in pomegranate hairy roots caused a unique accumulation of gallic acid 3-O- and 4-O-glucosides, not seen in empty-vector controls or single-edited lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: Solyc04g082540 (cwp, cuticular wax protein, S. habrochaites)
phenotype: Transgenic plants expressing VAR1 and VAR2 exhibit microfissures and dehydration in ripe fruits, while other variants show no cwph-related phenotypes
mechanism: The functional VAR1 variant (270-amino acid CWP protein) leads to microfissures in the fruit cuticle, likely through altered cuticle development

genes: LBD16 (LATERAL ORGAN BOUNDARIES 16, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Roots overexpressing LBD16 showed extensive curling with ectopic root primordia initiation.
mechanism: LBD16 controls root organogenesis through the regulation of auxin biosynthesis via STY.

genes: YUC2 (YUCCA 2, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Expression of YUC2 from the constitutive LjUBI promoter resulted in initiation and emergence of ectopic root primordia.
mechanism: YUC2 promotes auxin biosynthesis, leading to root primordia formation.

genes: YUC2 (YUCCA 2, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Dex-inducible YUC2 expression resulted in ectopic root primordia.
mechanism: Inducible expression of YUC2 promotes auxin biosynthesis, leading to root primordia formation.

genes: WUS (WUSCHEL, transcriptional regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Ectopic activation of pUBQ10:WUS-GR leads to enlarged SAMs with more cells after 4 days. After 24 h of DEX treatment, the central auxin signaling minimum and CLV3 domain expand, indicating WUS reduces auxin signaling output in the SAM center.
mechanism: WUS represses auxin signaling output by binding to and reducing transcription of auxin pathway genes. This repression is mediated via histone deacetylation, maintaining low auxin signaling in stem cells.

genes: BDL-D (IAA12, dominant auxin signaling output inhibitor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Stem cell-specific expression of pCLV3:BDL-D causes meristem termination in 45 of 90 plants. DR5v2 signal is reduced in the SAM center, indicating auxin signaling inhibition.
mechanism: BDL-D inhibits ARF transcription factors, reducing auxin signaling output. This leads to stem cell differentiation and meristem termination, showing auxin signaling is required for stem cell maintenance.

genes: BcEPSPS (BcEPSPS, 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase, Baphicacanthus cusia)
phenotype: Overexpression of BcEPSPS increases indigo alkaloid accumulation (indigo, secologanin, indole, isorhamnetin) by ~5.83- to 5.09-fold in Isatis indigotica hairy roots.
mechanism: BcEPSPS catalyzes the production of 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate (EPSP) in the shikimate pathway, which provides chorismic acid for indole alkaloid biosynthesis.

genes: ZmPEPC (ZmPEPC, phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmPEPC increases phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase (PEPC) content by ~65% and activity by ~25-fold in rice leaves compared to wild type.
mechanism: ZmPEPC enhances carboxylation by PEPC, contributing ~6% of total carboxylation compared to 0% in wild type, and lowers 13CO2 carboxylation fractionation (b) by ~2‰.

genes: Cry1A.105 (Cry1A.105, insecticidal protein, Bacillus thuringiensis), Cry2Ab2 (Cry2Ab2, insecticidal protein, Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. kurstaki)
phenotype: The MON 89034 transgene produces two insecticidal proteins (Cry1A.105 and Cry2Ab2) that protect against feeding damage caused by several lepidopteran insect pests.
mechanism: Cry1A.105 is a modified Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) Cry1A protein and Cry2Ab2 is a Bt (subsp. kurstaki) protein.

genes: Cry3Bb1 (Cry3Bb1, insecticidal protein, Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. kumamotoensis), CP4 EPSPS (5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase, glyphosate tolerance, Agrobacterium sp. strain CP4)
phenotype: The MON 88017 transgene produces a modified Bt (subsp. kumamotoensis) Cry3Bb1 protein that protects against corn rootworm larval feeding. In addition, MON 88017 produces a protein (5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase) from Agrobacterium sp. strain CP4 (CP4 EPSPS), which confers tolerance to glyphosate, the active ingredient in the Roundup®1 family of agricultural herbicides.
mechanism: Cry3Bb1 is a modified Bacillus thuringiensis (subsp. kumamotoensis) protein that protects against corn rootworm larval feeding. CP4 EPSPS is a 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase protein from Agrobacterium sp. strain CP4 that confers tolerance to glyphosate.

genes: OsSAPK9 (stress-activated protein kinase 9, Oryza sativa L., Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: OsSAPK9-RNAi lines Ri-21 and Ri-27 were more sensitive to salt stress in comparison with the wild-type (WT), and the survival rates of Ri-21 and Ri-27 were significantly reduced 7 d after treatment with 100 mM NaCl.
mechanism: OsSAPK9 positively regulates rice tolerance to salt stress.

genes: OsSAPK9 (stress-activated protein kinase 9, Oryza sativa L., Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: OsSAPK9-overexpression (OE) lines OE1 and OE2 were more tolerant to salt treatment, and their survival rates significantly increased in comparison with the wild-type (WT).
mechanism: OsSAPK9 positively regulates rice tolerance to salt stress.

genes: OsSGT1 (SGT1, Oryza sativa L., Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: OsSGT1-overexpression (SA) lines SA24 and SA28 exhibited significantly lower survival rates (13.3% and 38.0%) under salt-stress conditions compared to the wild-type (67.5%), and showed significantly increased resistance to bacterial blight.
mechanism: OsSGT1 negatively regulates rice responses to salt stress but positively regulates strain-specific resistance to bacterial blight.

genes: CsAlaAT2 (cucumber alanine aminotransferase 2, Cucumis sativus, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsAlaAT2 increases nitrogen use efficiency, biomass, tiller number, and grain yield in transgenic rice. One event (FAM13) showed 27.9% yield increase and 27.4% biomass increase under low nitrogen conditions.
mechanism: CsAlaAT2 enhances nitrogen metabolism by improving root architecture and nitrogen uptake efficiency. Overexpression triggers hypoxic-like response and ethylene biosynthesis, promoting root growth and tillering.

genes: PdWND3A (WOOD-ASSOCIATED NAC DOMAIN protein 3, Populus deltoides)
phenotype: Overexpression of PdWND3A increases vessel cell density, lignin content, and lignin S/G ratio in Populus deltoides. Transgenic plants show reduced saccharification efficiency and biomass production compared to wild-type.
mechanism: PdWND3A regulates lignin biosynthesis by upregulating FERULATE 5-HYDROXYLASE1 (F5H1) expression, altering lignin monomer composition and interunit linkages (e.g., increased β-β resinol linkages).

genes: NPR1 (NPR1, transcription coactivator, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of NPR1-GFP increases SA-induced immune gene expression and enhances resistance to Psm ES4326 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NPR1-GFP binds to target promoters and activates transcription of SA-responsive genes, while UBE4-mediated polyubiquitination inactivates NPR1 and promotes its degradation.

genes: UBE4 (UBE4, E4 ubiquitin ligase, Arabidopsis thaliana), YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of YFP-UBE4 localizes to the nucleus and promotes NPR1 polyubiquitination and degradation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: UBE4 polyubiquitinates NPR1 coactivator and targets it for proteasomal degradation, suppressing SA-mediated immunity in unchallenged plants.

genes: UBP6 (UBP6, ubiquitin-specific protease, Arabidopsis thaliana), FLAG ( FLAG epitope tag, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of FLAG-UBP6 stabilizes NPR1 and restores SA-induced gene expression in ubp6 ubp7 double mutants of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: UBP6 deubiquitinates NPR1, preventing its proteasomal degradation and maintaining its transcriptional activity.

genes: UBP6 (UBP6, ubiquitin-specific protease, Arabidopsis thaliana), FLAG ( FLAG epitope tag, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of catalytically inactive FLAG-UBP6(C113S) partially restores SA-induced gene expression in ubp6 ubp7 double mutants of Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: UBP6(C113S) retains proteasome inhibitory activity but lacks deubiquitination activity, suggesting non-catalytic roles in NPR1 regulation.

genes: BpCCR1 (BpCCR1, overexpression construct, Betula platyphylla)
phenotype: Overexpression of BpCCR1 increases lignin content in transgenic lines compared to wild type, but br exhibits lower lignin content despite BpCCR1 overexpression due to T-DNA insertion in BpCOI1.
mechanism: BpCCR1 is involved in lignin biosynthesis; however, the reduced lignin in br is attributed to T-DNA insertion affecting BpCOI1, which disrupts jasmonate signaling and leads to abnormal hormone perception.

genes: PabHLH1 (Plagiochasma appendiculatum, transcription factor, Plagiochasma appendiculatum)
phenotype: Overexpression of PabHLH1 increases bibenzyls and flavonoids content in Plagiochasma appendiculatum and activates flavonoids and anthocyanins synthesis in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: Up-regulation of structural genes in phenylpropanoid and flavonoid biosynthesis pathways (PAL, C4H, 4CL, CHS, CHI, F3H, DFR, FLS)

genes: LOW (Vr07g10060/LOC106767037, Dof-like transcription factor, Vigna radiata)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of LOW in Arabidopsis disrupts petal vasculature pattern, with vascular strands failing to form loops compared to wild type
mechanism: LOW functions in floral vasculature pattern development

genes: SlOFP20 (SlOFP20, OVATE family protein, tomato)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlOFP20 in tomato results in altered flower and fruit morphology (shorter, wider floral organs), exserted stigmas causing sterility in strong overexpression lines, reduced male fertility (pollen germination rate 2.36-fold lower than WT), and increased seed germination rate in mild overexpression lines.
mechanism: SlOFP20 negatively regulates BR response by promoting KNOX1 and suppressing GRAS41, altering BR and GA metabolism genes (upregulating BR biosynthesis genes CPD, D2, DWARF and GA inactivation genes GA2ox1/2), and downregulating cell division/elongation genes (CDKA1, SlCycA3;1, SlCycB2, SlCycD2;1, PRE1-5).

genes: miR169d (microRNA 169d, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR169d in Brassica napus resulted in one transgenic plant exhibiting a dwarf phenotype with down-curved leaves, though subsequent analysis showed this was not due to transgenic elements but a somatic mutation during tissue culture.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsNR2 (nitrate reductase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Expression of 9311 OsNR2 allele increases ClO3− sensitivity and enhances grain yield in Nipponbare rice.
mechanism: OsNR2 enhances nitrate assimilation and NO3− uptake, increasing tiller number and nitrogen use efficiency.

genes: OsNR2 (nitrate reductase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Reduction of OsNR2 mRNA abundance increases ClO3− resistance in Nipponbare rice.
mechanism: OsNR2 knockdown reduces nitrate reductase activity and NO3− uptake, decreasing ClO3− sensitivity.

genes: OsNR2 (nitrate reductase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Transgenic expression of the 9311 OsNR2 allele increases grain yield and nitrogen use efficiency in Nipponbare rice.
mechanism: Enhanced nitrate reductase activity and NO3− uptake improve nitrogen assimilation and tiller number.

genes: OsNR2 (nitrate reductase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsNR2 promoter activity is expressed in shoot and root vasculature, young root elongation zones, flowers, and leaves.
mechanism: NA

genes: SlNCED1 (full length, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlNCED1 increases ABA levels in the ovary, leading to premature ovary expansion, parthenocarpic fruit development, and abnormal pistil morphology in tomato.
mechanism: SlNCED1 overexpression enhances ABA biosynthesis, which regulates ovary development through ABA signaling pathways involving PYL, PP2C, and SnRK2 proteins, as well as pistil-specific CCCH-ZFP transcription factors.

genes: Z15 (LOC_Os05g12680, receptor-like protein kinase, rice)
phenotype: Complementation of z15 mutant restores wild-type phenotype, including normal chloroplast structure and agronomic traits (plant height, grain number, etc.)
mechanism: Z15 encodes a receptor-like kinase involved in moderate low temperature signaling, regulating downstream genes OsWRKY71 and OsMYB4

genes: Z15 (LOC_Os05g12680, receptor-like protein kinase, rice)
phenotype: GUS expression in vascular bundles and mesophyll cells of rice tissues (root, stem, leaf, panicle)
mechanism: Z15 promoter drives GUS expression in vascular bundles and epidermal cells, indicating tissue-specific expression patterns

genes: Z15 (LOC_Os05g12680, receptor-like protein kinase, rice), z15 (mutant allele, receptor-like protein kinase, rice)
phenotype: Z15-GFP and z15-GFP fusion proteins localized to the plasma membrane in rice protoplasts, similar to the plasma membrane marker ESL4-GFP
mechanism: Z15 and z15 proteins localize to the plasma membrane, with the mutation (Gly-409 to Asp-409) not altering localization but abolishing kinase activity

genes: CO (CO, photoperiodic flowering transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CO under the CaMV35S promoter causes strong early-flowering phenotype with drastically increased FT mRNA levels and growth termination associated with necrosis and chlorophyll bleaching, especially under constant blue light.
mechanism: CO enhances photoperiodic flowering by inducing FT expression, leading to early flowering and growth termination under high CO activity.

genes: UCH3 (UCH3, deubiquitylating enzyme, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of UCH3:GFP in Arabidopsis protoplasts results in accumulation of the fusion protein in both cytoplasm and nucleus.
mechanism: UCH3:GFP accumulated in the cytoplasm as well as in the nucleus (Fig. 1c), indicating that it shares the same intracellular location with UCH1 and 2.

genes: uidA (uidA, β-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Overexpression of uidA under pGmRD26 promoter increases GUS activity in A. thaliana under ABA, PEG, and drought treatments.
mechanism: The pGmRD26 promoter contains cis-regulatory elements responsive to ABA, PEG, and drought, leading to enhanced GUS expression under these conditions.

genes: uidA (uidA, β-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Overexpression of uidA under pGmRD26A promoter increases GUS activity in A. thaliana under ABA, PEG, and drought treatments.
mechanism: The pGmRD26A promoter module contains cis-regulatory elements responsive to ABA, PEG, and drought, leading to enhanced GUS expression under these conditions.

genes: uidA (uidA, β-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Overexpression of uidA under pGmRD26B promoter increases GUS activity in A. thaliana under ABA, PEG, and drought treatments.
mechanism: The pGmRD26B promoter module contains cis-regulatory elements responsive to ABA, PEG, and drought, leading to enhanced GUS expression under these conditions.

genes: GmERF75 (GmERF75, ABA-responsive ERF gene from soybean, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmERF75 increases chlorophyll content by ~20.11-39.66% under salt and drought stress in Arabidopsis.
mechanism: GmERF75 enhances osmotic tolerance by modulating stress signaling pathways, possibly integrating SA and ET/JA pathways.

genes: GmERF75 (GmERF75, ABA-responsive ERF gene from soybean, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmERF75 improves root growth under exogenous ABA and salt stress in soybean hairy roots.
mechanism: GmERF75 enhances osmotic tolerance by modulating stress signaling pathways, possibly integrating SA and ET/JA pathways.

genes: VvSNAT2 (serotonin N-acetyltransferase, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvSNAT2 increases melatonin and chlorophyll content and enhances resistance to powdery mildew in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: VvSNAT2 overexpression activates the SA and JA signaling pathways; the SA pathway plays a central role in VvSNAT2-mediated plant defense.

genes: OsNPF6.1 (OsNPF6.1HapB, nitrogen transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of OsNPF6.1HapB in Nipponbare significantly increased effective panicle number (EPN) and yield per plant (YPP) compared to wild-type Nipponbare under both high and low nitrogen conditions.
mechanism: OsNPF6.1HapB enhances nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) by increasing nitrate uptake and transport activity, leading to improved agronomic traits.

genes: OsNPF6.1 (OsNPF6.1HapA, nitrogen transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of OsNPF6.1HapA in Nipponbare significantly reduced plant height (PH) and yield per plant (YPP) under both high and low nitrogen conditions.
mechanism: OsNPF6.1HapA knockout disrupts nitrate uptake and transport, leading to reduced NUE and agronomic performance.

genes: rAPOBEC1 (cytidine deaminase, from Rattus norvegicus), UGI (uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor, synthetic)
phenotype: SpCas9-rBE achieves 0-20% C-to-T editing efficiency in rice, significantly lower than SpCas9-pBE
mechanism: rAPOBEC1-mediated cytosine deamination coupled with SpCas9 nickase creates C-to-T conversions with tRNA-sgRNA multiplex architecture

genes: eSpCas9(1.1) (high-fidelity SpCas9 variant, engineered), PmCDA1 (cytidine deaminase, from Petromyzon marinus), UGI (uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor, synthetic)
phenotype: eSpCas9(1.1)-pBE achieves 19.6-25.5-fold increased C-to-T editing efficiency compared to baseline when using tRNA-modified sgRNA
mechanism: tRNA-modified sgRNA architecture enhances eSpCas9(1.1) nickase activity while maintaining PmCDA1-mediated cytosine deamination

genes: SpCas9-HF2 (high-fidelity SpCas9 variant, engineered), PmCDA1 (cytidine deaminase, from Petromyzon marinus), UGI (uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor, synthetic)
phenotype: SpCas9-HF2-pBE shows 3.5-1.3-fold increased C-to-T editing efficiency at ALS and NRT1.1B sites with tRNA-modified sgRNA
mechanism: tRNA-modified sgRNA architecture enhances SpCas9-HF2 nickase activity while maintaining PmCDA1-mediated cytosine deamination

genes: HypaCas9 (high-fidelity SpCas9 variant, engineered), PmCDA1 (cytidine deaminase, from Petromyzon marinus), UGI (uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor, synthetic)
phenotype: HypaCas9-pBE shows 5-30% C-to-T editing efficiency at CDC48 site with tRNA-modified sgRNA, up from 5%
mechanism: tRNA-modified sgRNA architecture enhances HypaCas9 nickase activity while maintaining PmCDA1-mediated cytosine deamination

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, Agrobacterium rhizogenes, synthetic), TDT (tomato deaminase threonine, Agrobacterium rhizogenes, synthetic)
phenotype: Induction of hairy roots with green and red epifluorescence, confirmed by epifluorescence microscopy in Hyptis suaveolens hairy root lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: LHCSR1 (LHCSR1, light-harvesting complex stress-related 1, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: Expression of P. patens LHCSR1 in A. thaliana npq4 mutants enables NPQ activity, with NPQ levels correlating with LHCSR1 accumulation levels (R²=0.75 for maximum NPQ, R²=0.82 for qE).
mechanism: LHCSR1 binds zeaxanthin and mediates NPQ through energy dissipation in thylakoid membranes, with activity dependent on zeaxanthin availability and thylakoid localization in stroma-exposed membranes.

genes: TaGGP1-A (GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase, Triticum aestivum), TaGGP1-B (GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase, Triticum aestivum), TaGGP1-D (GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase, Triticum aestivum), TaGGP2-A (GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase, Triticum aestivum), TaGGP2-B (GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Transient transformation of the TaGGP coding sequences in N. benthamiana leaf increased ascorbate concentrations by up to 5.3-fold (TaGGP1-D) relative to the control.
mechanism: GGP catalyzes the conversion of GDP-L-galactose to L-galactose-1-P, representing the first committed step toward ascorbate biosynthesis.

genes: FSD3 (FSD3, plastid-encoded RNA polymerase-associated protein 4, Arabidopsis thaliana), FSD3S (FSD3S, splicing variant of FSD3 with transmembrane domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FSD3-GFP and FSD3S-GFP in Arabidopsis thaliana shows distinct subcellular localization patterns: FSD3 localizes to chloroplast nucleoids while FSD3S localizes to chloroplast membranes, with FSD3S overexpression reducing photosynthetic activity by ~6% and chlorophyll content by ~15%.
mechanism: FSD3S contains a transmembrane domain in its C-terminal region that promotes membrane localization, disrupting PEP complex formation and downregulating PEP-dependent photosynthesis genes like rbcL, psbA, and psaB.

genes: FSD3S (FSD3S, splicing variant of FSD3 with transmembrane domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of FSD3SΔTM-GFP (FSD3S lacking transmembrane domain) in Arabidopsis thaliana results in diffuse chloroplast localization and reduced photosynthetic activity, similar to full-length FSD3S overexpression.
mechanism: The transmembrane domain of FSD3S is required for membrane localization; its absence leads to stromal accumulation, which still negatively regulates PEP-dependent gene expression and chloroplast development.

genes: VvHB58 (homeodomain-leucine zipper (HD-Zip I) transcription factor, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvHB58 in tomato leads to loss of apical dominance, reduced fruit pericarp expansion, reduced fruit size and seed number, and larger endosperm cells.
mechanism: VvHB58 expression results in significant changes in auxin, gibberellin and ethylene signaling pathways, affecting fruit and seed development.

genes: OsPUB41 (Oryza sativa ubiquitin ligase, defense response regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsPUB41 in rice increases callose deposition and enhances tolerance to Xoo infection by ~50% (14cm vs 29cm lesions). In Arabidopsis, ectopic expression induces callose deposition and provides enhanced tolerance to Rhizoctonia solani infection.
mechanism: OsPUB41 enhances defense responses through E3 ubiquitin ligase activity, inducing callose deposition and upregulating JA/SA biosynthetic genes. The E3 ligase activity is essential for immune response activation.

genes: CasRx (CasRx, Ruminococcus flavefaciens), LwaCas13a (LwaCas13a, Leptotrichia wadei), PspCas13b (PspCas13b, Bergeyella zoohelcum)
phenotype: CasRx mediated robust RNA virus interference compared to other variants in transient assays targeting a highly replicating RNA virus. Transgenic plants overexpressing CasRx exhibited efficient interference against TuMV RNA.
mechanism: CasRx-mediated RNA virus interference is dependent on the catalytic activity of CasRx, leading to targeted viral genomic degradation. CasRx lacks collateral activity in planta.

genes: CasRx (CasRx, Ruminococcus flavefaciens)
phenotype: Catalytically deactivated (dCasRx) version could not mediate any virus targeting, indicating that the HEPN-dependent catalytic activity of CasRx is required for virus RNA degradation.
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of the GUS gene under the TCP8 promoter shows ubiquitous expression in vascular bundles, leaf primordia, and stomatal guard cells in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: TCP8 (Teosinte Branched 1/Cycloidea/Proliferating Cell Factors family member, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TCP8 significantly delays flowering under both long-day and short-day conditions in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: TCP8 upregulates FLC mRNA level, a central floral repressor.

genes: TCP8 (Teosinte Branched 1/Cycloidea/Proliferating Cell Factors family member, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of TCP8 under its native promoter delays flowering, though less severely than 35S::TCP8, in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: TCP8 upregulates FLC mRNA level, a central floral repressor.

genes: TCP8-EAR (Teosinte Branched 1/Cycloidea/Proliferating Cell Factors family member fused with EAR motif, synthetic)
phenotype: Dominant repression by TCP8-EAR under native promoter leads to growth defects, including dark green leaves, hyponastic cotyledons, and floral abnormalities in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsMYB102 (OsMYB102, R2R3-type MYB TF, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsMYB102 inhibits shoot growth (shorter petioles, lower fresh weight), delays leaf senescence (retains greenness, higher chlorophyll/carotenoids), and decreases abiotic stress tolerance (hypersensitivity to salt/drought) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: OsMYB102 modulates ABA metabolism and signaling by upregulating AtCYP707A3 (ABA catabolic enzyme) and downregulating ABA signaling genes, reducing ABA accumulation.

genes: TH1 (Triangular Hull1, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: Homozygous TH1 KO lines show defects in lemma/palea development and grain filling, leading to infertility.
mechanism: Hormone-related genes and starch/sucrose metabolism genes may act as downstream targets of TH1, affecting lemma/palea development and grain filling.

genes: TH1 (Triangular Hull1, Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: No phenotypic change observed in TH1 overexpression line compared to wild type.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsHBP1b (histone gene binding protein/transcription factor-1b, Oryza sativa L., synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsHBP1b in rice improves salinity tolerance with better survival, osmotic parameters, antioxidant enzyme activity (ascorbate peroxidase and superoxide dismutase), chlorophyll maintenance, and photosynthesis under stress.
mechanism: OsHBP1b restricts ROS accumulation, maintains chlorophyll and organellar structure, enhances antioxidant enzyme activity, and regulates photosynthesis and stress-related genes.

genes: AHSV1VP2 (AHSV1 VP2, outer capsid protein, AHSV serotype 1), AHSV1VP5 (AHSV1 VP5, outer capsid protein, AHSV serotype 1), AHSV1VP7 (AHSV1 VP7, core protein, AHSV serotype 1), AHSV1VP3 (AHSV1 VP3, core protein, AHSV serotype 1)
phenotype: Assembly of homogenous AHSV-1 virus-like particles (VLPs) in Nicotiana benthamiana dXT/FT plants.
mechanism: Co-expression of AHSV-1 capsid proteins (VP2, VP5, VP3, VP7) in plant cells allows self-assembly into VLPs.

genes: AHSV7VP2 (AHSV7 VP2, outer capsid protein, AHSV serotype 7), AHSV1VP5 (AHSV1 VP5, outer capsid protein, AHSV serotype 1), AHSV1VP7 (AHSV1 VP7, core protein, AHSV serotype 1), AHSV1VP3 (AHSV1 VP3, core protein, AHSV serotype 1)
phenotype: Assembly of single chimeric AHSV-1/AHSV-7 VLPs in Nicotiana benthamiana dXT/FT plants.
mechanism: Exchange of AHSV-1 VP2 with AHSV-7 VP2 while retaining AHSV-1 VP5, VP7, and VP3 core proteins allows chimeric VLP assembly.

genes: AHSV7VP2 (AHSV7 VP2, outer capsid protein, AHSV serotype 7), AHSV7VP5 (AHSV7 VP5, outer capsid protein, AHSV serotype 7), AHSV1VP7 (AHSV1 VP7, core protein, AHSV serotype 1), AHSV1VP3 (AHSV1 VP3, core protein, AHSV serotype 1)
phenotype: Assembly of double chimeric AHSV-1/AHSV-7 VLPs in Nicotiana benthamiana dXT/FT plants.
mechanism: Exchange of AHSV-1 VP2 and VP5 with AHSV-7 VP2 and VP5 while retaining AHSV-1 VP7 and VP3 core proteins allows chimeric VLP assembly.

genes: AHSV6VP2 (AHSV6 VP2, outer capsid protein, AHSV serotype 6), AHSV3VP5 (AHSV3 VP5, outer capsid protein, AHSV serotype 3), AHSV1VP7 (AHSV1 VP7, core protein, AHSV serotype 1), AHSV1VP3 (AHSV1 VP3, core protein, AHSV serotype 1)
phenotype: Assembly of triple chimeric AHSV-1/AHSV-3/AHSV-6 VLPs in Nicotiana benthamiana dXT/FT plants.
mechanism: Exchange of AHSV-1 VP2 and VP5 with AHSV-6 VP2 and AHSV-3 VP5 while retaining AHSV-1 VP7 and VP3 core proteins allows chimeric VLP assembly.

genes: CCA1 (CIRCADIAN CLOCK ASSOCIATED 1, circadian clock regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CCA1 increases SDG2 expression and decreases JMJ14 expression in Arabidopsis thaliana under diurnal conditions.
mechanism: CCA1 regulates diurnal expression of SDG2 (histone methyltransferase) and JMJ14 (histone demethylase) to modulate H3K4me3 levels, establishing rhythmic histone modifications for circadian clock gene regulation.

genes: EgWRI1 (promoter of EgWRI1, Elaeis guineensis)
phenotype: ProEgWRI1::GUS construct shows strong GUS activity in whole seedlings, especially in stems and leaves, and in silique coats but weak in seeds in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: EgWRI1 promoter activity is induced under darkness and low temperature, and suppressed by ethylene, indicating its role in stress response and carbon flux regulation.

genes: RcLEC1-B (LEAFY COTYLEDON1-B, R. sceleratus, R. sceleratus)
phenotype: Overexpression of RcLEC1-B results in dwarfing and abnormal flower organs in R. sceleratus, including folded leaves with defective cuticle, variable floral organ numbers (0–5 sepals, 2–14 petals, 0–16 stamens), and transition state petals with notches.
mechanism: RcLEC1-B affects floral organ development and cuticle formation, leading to morphological abnormalities and altered organ counts.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene)
phenotype: The GUS reporter gene is used to analyze transgenic efficiency via histochemical staining of somatic embryos.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsSPL10 (SST, salt tolerance regulator, Oryza sativa ssp. japonica)
phenotype: Knockout of OsSPL10 increases salt tolerance (100% survival vs 0% in wild type) and reduces trichome density to ~2-0 trichomes/field vs ~43-88 in wild type in Oryza sativa ssp. japonica
mechanism: OsSPL10 functions as a negative regulator of salt tolerance and positive regulator of trichome formation

genes: OsSPL10 (SST, salt tolerance regulator, Oryza sativa ssp. japonica)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSPL10 reduces salt tolerance (0-9% survival vs 44% in wild type) and increases trichome density to ~43-88 trichomes/field in Oryza sativa ssp. japonica
mechanism: OsSPL10 functions as a negative regulator of salt tolerance and positive regulator of trichome formation

genes: OsSPL10 (SST, salt tolerance regulator, Oryza sativa ssp. japonica)
phenotype: OsSPL10-GFP fusion protein localizes exclusively to nucleus in Nicotiana benthamiana
mechanism: OsSPL10 is localized in nucleus, suggesting it functions as a transcription factor

genes: PbPAL1 (phenylalanine ammonia-lyase 1, lignin biosynthesis, Pyrus bretschneideri), PbPAL2 (phenylalanine ammonia-lyase 2, lignin biosynthesis, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbPAL1 and PbPAL2 increases lignin content by ~20% in Arabidopsis thaliana stems and leaves
mechanism: PbPAL1 and PbPAL2 enhance lignin biosynthesis by increasing cell wall thickness and xylem lignification

genes: StSERK3A (StSERK3A, receptor kinase SERK3A, potato), StSERK3B (StSERK3B, receptor kinase SERK3B, potato)
phenotype: StSERK3A/B-RNAi plants display dwarfism in tissue culture, darker green crinkled leaves with leaf curling, reduced leaf expansion, delayed senescence, and decreased tuber yield compared to control plants. Metabolite analysis shows elevated hydroxycinnamic acid amides and reduced coumarin/flavonoid compounds.
mechanism: StSERK3A/B are required for Pep-13-induced ROS formation and MAP kinase activation. The RNAi phenotype resembles brassinosteroid deficiency, with altered phenylpropanoid pathway metabolism channeling 4-coumaroyl-CoA into HCAA production instead of flavonoids.

genes: OsDim1 (Os.12368, AK063786, gene encoding thioredoxin-like protein)
phenotype: OsDim1 expression observed in endosperm, seminal root zones (EZ/HZ), nodal septal, auricles, leaf sheath, leaf blade, immature panicle, style, stigma, pollen grains, embryonic callus, and pollen tube elongation during rice development.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsDim1 (Os.12368, AK063786, gene encoding thioredoxin-like protein)
phenotype: OsDim1-EGFP fluorescence signals localized exclusively in the nucleus of onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: Zm00001d018816 (tin1, controls tiller number in maize, Zea mays (B37))
phenotype: Overexpression of tin1 increased tiller number in maize
mechanism: TIN1 functions as a transcription factor that represses the expression of gt1 and other tiller-related genes, leading to increased tiller outgrowth

genes: Zm00001d018816 (tin1, controls tiller number in maize, Zea mays (P51))
phenotype: Overexpression of tin1 increased tiller number in maize
mechanism: TIN1 functions as a transcription factor that represses the expression of gt1 and other tiller-related genes, leading to increased tiller outgrowth

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, Aequorea victoria)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP in N. benthamiana leaves reaches ~60% of total soluble proteins (TSP) within 4-8 days post-inoculation
mechanism: Viral RNA-based overexpression vector (pJL TRBO-G) with duplicated CaMV 35S promoter and TMV replicase enables high-level transient expression

genes: OsPUB73 (ubiquitin ligase activity-related protein, Oryza sativa, OsPUB73)
phenotype: Mutation of OsPUB73 causes pollen semi-sterility with 19.45% pollen fertility in Oryza sativa, compared to 85.37% in wild type. Cytological analysis shows tapetum vacuolation during meiosis and abnormal pollen exine at bi-cellular pollen stage.
mechanism: OsPUB73 may regulate tapetum degradation and pollen exine development through ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis. Down-regulation of 7 key genes (CYP703A3, CYP704B2, DPW, PTC1, UDT1, OsAP37, OsABCG15) associated with tapetal cell death and pollen wall formation in ospub73 mutants.

genes: rolB (root morphogenesis gene, Agrobacterium rhizogenes Ri plasmid, Agrobacterium rhizogenes)
phenotype: Induction of hairy roots in Centella asiatica via Agrobacterium rhizogenes-mediated transformation
mechanism: Expression of the rolB gene from Agrobacterium rhizogenes Ri plasmid triggers hairy root formation through auxin and cytokinin imbalance

genes: Solyc03g007780 (ovary-specific promoter, Solanum lycopersicum), Solyc02g067760 (ovary-specific promoter, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Tissue-specific GUS activity in ovary, stamen, and fruit tissues of transgenic tomato plants, with no GUS activity in vegetative tissues.
mechanism: Psol80 and Psol60 promoters drive GUS expression in ovary and reproductive tissues, demonstrating tissue-specific regulation.

genes: SlIAA9 (Aux/IAA transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Parthenocarpic fruit formation in transgenic tomato plants without abnormal vegetative phenotypes, with 62–68% parthenocarpic fruit set efficiency in Psol80-SlIAA9i lines and 40–44% in Psol60-SlIAA9i lines.
mechanism: Ovary-specific downregulation of SlIAA9 by Psol80/60 promoters suppresses auxin response inhibition, enabling parthenocarpy without affecting vegetative tissues.

genes: GUS (uidA, β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity detected in stigmas across developmental stages in the inflorescence for BKN1p:GUS transgenic plants
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (uidA, β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity detected primarily in the floral abscission zones and stems for BKN2p:GUS transgenic plants
mechanism: NA

genes: BKN1 (At5g11400, receptor-like cytoplasmic pseudokinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: CRISPR-Cas9 system with sgRNAs targeting BKN1
phenotype: No discernible developmental defects in bkn1 mutants; mild hydration defects observed for wild-type Col-0 pollen on bkn2 mutant stigmas
mechanism: NA

genes: BKN2 (At5g11410, receptor-like cytoplasmic pseudokinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: CRISPR-Cas9 system with sgRNAs targeting BKN2
phenotype: Stigmas carrying a mutation in the BKN2 gene showed reduced Col-0 pollen hydration compared to Col-0 stigmas
mechanism: NA

genes: CsGH3.1 (CsGH3.1, auxin amido synthetase, Citrus sinensis Osbeck)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsGH3.1 causes abnormal phenotypes including leaf drooping, upward curling, bushy dwarfism, and reduced susceptibility to citrus canker (Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri).
mechanism: CsGH3.1 represses auxin signaling by conjugating free IAA to amino acids, downregulates auxin transport and signaling genes (AUX/IAA, PIN1/3), and activates biotic stress response pathways (PR proteins, WRKY transcription factors).

genes: CsGH3.1L (CsGH3.1L, auxin amido synthetase, Citrus sinensis Osbeck)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsGH3.1L causes abnormal phenotypes including leaf drooping, upward curling, bushy dwarfism, and reduced susceptibility to citrus canker (Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri).
mechanism: CsGH3.1L represses auxin signaling by conjugating free IAA to amino acids, downregulates auxin transport and signaling genes (AUX/IAA, PIN1/3), and activates biotic stress response pathways (PR proteins, WRKY transcription factors).

genes: AhSRK03 (S-locus receptor kinase, Arabidopsis halleri), AhSRK28 (S-locus receptor kinase, Arabidopsis halleri)
phenotype: Expression of S03 and S28 recognition specificities in A. thaliana, with distinct self-incompatibility (SI) responses to cognate pollen
mechanism: SRK-mediated SI response involves recognition of cognate SCR ligands, leading to pollen tube inhibition

genes: AhSRK03p:GFP (promoter-GFP fusion, Arabidopsis halleri), AhSRK28p:GFP (promoter-GFP fusion, Arabidopsis halleri)
phenotype: GFP expression specifically in stigmatic papillae cells of A. thaliana, confirming SRK promoter activity
mechanism: Promoter-driven GFP expression localizes to stigmatic papillae cells, indicating SRK expression pattern

genes: SRKa (ancestral S-locus receptor kinase, reconstructed from AhSRK03 and AhSRK28)
phenotype: Ancestral SRKa receptors retain S03 recognition specificity but not S28, showing functional diversification of S-haplotypes
mechanism: Ancestral SRKa interacts with SCR03 ligand via conserved amino acid contacts, while S28-specific interactions diverged

genes: OsPGIP1 (OsPGIP1, polygalacturonase-inhibiting protein 1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsPGIP1 enhances resistance to Xoc in rice, reducing lesion length by ~15% in ZH11.
mechanism: OsPGIP1-mediated resistance is induced by XocPG and other pathogenicity factors, involving PR genes and cell wall defense.

genes: OsPGIP1 (OsPGIP1, polygalacturonase-inhibiting protein 1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Silencing OsPGIP1 increases susceptibility to Xoc, with lesion lengths ~40% longer in ZH11.
mechanism: OsPGIP1 is a defense-related gene contributing to BLS resistance by interacting with Xoc pathogenicity factors.

genes: PrMADS10 (Prunus radiata MADS-box transcription factor, lignin and flavonoid regulation, Prunus radiata)
phenotype: Overexpression of PrMADS10 increases lignin content by ~30% in Arabidopsis thaliana and reduces anthocyanin content in two transgenic lines
mechanism: PrMADS10 modulates genes in the phenylpropanoid pathway, including upregulation of PAL, 4CL, CCoAOMT, and MYB transcription factors that regulate lignin biosynthesis

genes: MsLAC1 (MsLAC1, laccase isoform involved in lignification, Miscanthus sinensis)
phenotype: Complements the Arabidopsis lac4–2 lac17 mutant, restoring lignin content and composition to wild-type levels, with increased G-lignin and reduced S/G ratio.
mechanism: MsLAC1 oxidizes monolignols to radicals, promoting lignin polymerization and interfascicular fiber development.

genes: MsLAC1 (MsLAC1, laccase isoform involved in lignification, Miscanthus sinensis)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of MsLAC1 in Arabidopsis promotes interfascicular fiber development, increases lignin content by ~13.4–16.8%, and lowers S/G ratio due to higher G-lignin deposition.
mechanism: MsLAC1 enhances lignin polymerization by oxidizing monolignols, leading to increased interfascicular fiber lignification and altered lignin composition.

genes: SD1 (semi-dwarf 1, gibberellin 20-oxidase, Oryza sativa), SE5 (photoperiod-sensitivity 5, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Simultaneous knockout of SD1 and SE5 in TTP background results in early flowering (2 weeks earlier than TTP in Hangzhou, China) and increased resistance to rice blast compared to TTP.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in SD1 and SE5 disrupt gibberellin biosynthesis and photoperiod sensitivity, leading to dwarfism and altered flowering time.

genes: SD1 (semi-dwarf 1, gibberellin 20-oxidase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of SD1 in Kasalath background reduces plant height by 15-20% (82.5-91.5 cm vs 152 cm in wild type), increases lodging resistance, and improves nitrogen use efficiency under high nitrogen conditions.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced premature termination of SD1 (gibberellin 20-oxidase) disrupts gibberellin biosynthesis, leading to dwarfism and altered agronomic traits.

plant_species: Citrus reticulata Blanco, Citrus sinensis (L.) Osbeck
genes: PsCBL (Calcineurin B-like protein of Pisum sativum, abiotic stress tolerance, Pisum sativum), PsCIPK (CBL-interacting protein kinases of Pisum sativum, abiotic stress tolerance, Pisum sativum)
phenotype: Transgenic plantlets showed improved abiotic stress tolerance, surviving up to 4 weeks on 50 mM NaCl and 1 week on 200 mM NaCl compared to control plants that died within 10 days.
mechanism: PsCBL and PsCIPK form a CBL-CIPK signaling network that maintains ion balance during abiotic stress, enhancing resistance to drought and salt.

genes: pporRFP (Porites porites red fluorescent protein, Porites porites), HYG (hygromycin B phosphotransferase II, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of pporRFP orange fluorescent protein and hygromycin B resistance in transgenic switchgrass plants
mechanism: Switchgrass polyubiquitin 1 promoter (PvUbi1) drives pporRFP expression; switchgrass polyubiquitin 2 promoter (PvUbi2) drives hygromycin B phosphotransferase (HYG) expression for antibiotic resistance

genes: NBR1 (NBR1, autophagy receptor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of mCherry-NBR1 allows visualization of NBR1 localization and aggregation dynamics in Arabidopsis root cells during heat stress.
mechanism: NBR1 binds to ATG8 via its AIM domain to mediate aggrephagy of cytosolic protein aggregates.

genes: FL2 (FLOURY2, aggregation-prone storage protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of FL2-GFP in Arabidopsis mesophyll cells leads to ER-localized protein aggregates that are targeted for autophagic degradation via reticulophagy.
mechanism: FL2-GFP aggregates are sequestered by NBR1 and delivered to the vacuole via ATG8-mediated autophagy.

genes: FL2ΔSP (FL2 lacking signal peptide, aggregation-prone storage protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of FL2ΔSP-GFP in Arabidopsis mesophyll cells leads to cytosolic protein aggregates that are selectively degraded via NBR1-mediated aggrephagy.
mechanism: FL2ΔSP-GFP aggregates are recognized by NBR1, which binds to ATG8 via its AIM domain to facilitate autophagic clearance.

genes: HvCslF6 (cellulose synthase-like F6, Hordeum vulgare, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of HvCslF6 increases (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan (MLG) content in barley endosperm by ~2-3x compared to wild type, reduces starch content by ~30-40%, and alters endosperm cell morphology with smaller starch granules and thicker cell walls in transgenic lines.
mechanism: HvCslF6 enhances MLG synthesis in endosperm cell walls, leading to altered carbohydrate partitioning and disrupted endosperm transfer cell (ETC) development. This causes increased sucrose and fructan accumulation in the grain cavity, reduced starch synthesis, and morphological changes including elongated aleurone cells and cavity expansion.

genes: cry1Ab (cry1Ab, codes for expression of Cry1Ab protein, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of cry1Ab in Bt maize results in Cry1Ab protein concentrations ranging from 8.9 to 24.0 μg/g dry weight in leaf tissue, which reduces Busseola fusca larval survival to 5.3-24.0% after 14 days of feeding.
mechanism: Cry1Ab protein is toxic to Busseola fusca larvae, causing high mortality rates in bioassays.

genes: DEP1/qPE9-1 (DEP1/qPE9-1, a G protein γ subunit involved in grain size and starch biosynthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of DEP1/qPE9–1 increases grain length by ~12% and 1000-grain weight in Oryza sativa, with enhanced endosperm cell proliferation and starch accumulation.
mechanism: DEP1/qPE9–1 enhances endosperm cell proliferation during early grain development and prolongs the grain-filling period, increasing starch biosynthesis through upregulated OsSUS3, OsSSSIIa, OsGBSSI, and OsBEIIb gene expression and enzyme activities. It also modulates auxin and cytokinin homeostasis to sustain starch accumulation.

genes: AtPDF2.1 (AtPDF2.1, small cysteine-rich peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtPDF2.1-mRFP in Arabidopsis thaliana localizes to the cell wall, as shown by confocal microscopy.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtPDF2.1 (AtPDF2.1, small cysteine-rich peptide, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtPDF2.1-mRFP under the native promoter in Arabidopsis thaliana localizes to the cell wall, as shown by confocal microscopy.
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of GUS under the AtPDF2.1 promoter in Arabidopsis thaliana shows strong activity in root vascular bundles, cotyledons, and leaves.
mechanism: NA

genes: MtPHD6 (MtPHD6, drought stress-responsive transcription factor, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Overexpression of MtPHD6 increases drought tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with transgenic plants showing 80% survival after rehydration compared to <30% in wild type, reduced water loss rate, lower MDA and ROS contents, and higher antioxidant enzyme activities under drought stress.
mechanism: MtPHD6 activates ZINC FINGER, AP2/EREBP, and WRKY transcription factors through ABA-dependent and independent pathways, which regulate stress-induced proteins, antioxidant enzymes, and osmotic adjustment.

genes: OsIAGT1 (UDP-glucosyltransferase, rice auxin glucosyltransferase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsIAGT1 leads to reduced plant stature and root length in rice, with decreased endogenous IAA content and altered auxin-responsive gene expression.
mechanism: OsIAGT1 catalyzes auxin glucosylation, reducing active auxin levels and altering auxin signaling pathways, leading to reduced growth.

genes: OsJAC1 (OsJAC1, jacalin-related lectin from rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsJAC1 overexpression confers hyper-resistance to gamma radiation in Arabidopsis thaliana, with transgenic lines showing 3-fold higher plant height and fresh weight after 300 Gy irradiation compared to wild-type controls
mechanism: OsJAC1 overexpression activates DNA damage perception and DNA damage checkpoints via upregulation of ATM, MRE11, MCMs, RPA, and DNA polymerase genes

genes: AtHMA3 (AtHMA3, vacuolar transporter for Cd and Zn, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtHMA3 reduces leaf Cd concentration by ~45% and slightly reduces Zn concentration in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AtHMA3 transports Cd and Zn into vacuoles; transcriptional buffering of Zn homeostasis network maintains leaf Zn concentration despite increased vacuolar sequestration.

genes: PlyCP41p (PlyCP41 endolysin, synthetic), PlyCP41pc (PlyCP41 endolysin, synthetic)
phenotype: PlyCP41p accumulates to ~1% total soluble protein (100μg/gm fresh weight leaf tissue) in Nicotiana benthamiana without toxic effects, and plant sap containing PlyCP41p lysed C. perfringens strain Cp39 in plate lysis assays.
mechanism: PlyCP41p is a glycosyl hydrolase endolysin that hydrolyzes peptidoglycans in C. perfringens cell walls, causing lysis.

genes: EAS4 (EAS4 promoter, Nicotiana tabacum), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: 1126p-GUS is activated by wounding, showing ~200-fold induction of GUS transcript levels.
mechanism: The EAS4 promoter contains wound-responsive elements that mediate activation by wounding and WIPK/SIPK signaling.

genes: EAS4 (EAS4 promoter, Nicotiana tabacum), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: 160p-GUS is activated by wounding, showing ~20-fold induction of GUS transcript levels.
mechanism: The 160p region of the EAS4 promoter contains essential wound-responsive elements required for activation by wounding.

genes: EAS4 (EAS4 promoter, Nicotiana tabacum), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Four tandem repeats of the −160 to −116 region confer strong wound-responsive activity on a 35S minimal promoter.
mechanism: The −160 to −116 region of the EAS4 promoter contains cis-elements required for wound-induced activation.

genes: EAS4 (EAS4 promoter, Nicotiana tabacum), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: Four tandem repeats of the −115 to −64 region confer strong wound-responsive activity on a 35S minimal promoter.
mechanism: The −115 to −64 region of the EAS4 promoter contains cis-elements required for wound-induced activation.

genes: MEK2DD (constitutively active MEK2, synthetic), GUS (β-glucuronidase, synthetic)
phenotype: MEK2DD activates the EAS4 promoter, inducing GUS expression, though less strongly than wounding.
mechanism: MEK2DD activates WIPK and SIPK, which in turn activate the EAS4 promoter.

genes: GUS (uidA, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: ProSlLYK10:GUS is expressed in arbuscule-containing cells of tomato roots and in nodule primordia and mature nodules of Medicago truncatula.
mechanism: The SlLYK10 promoter drives expression in arbuscule-containing cells and nodules, indicating its role in both arbuscular mycorrhiza and root nodule symbiosis.

genes: GUS (uidA, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: ProPhLYK10:GUS is expressed in arbuscule-containing cells of tomato roots and in nodule primordia and mature nodules of Medicago truncatula.
mechanism: The PhLYK10 promoter drives expression in arbuscule-containing cells and nodules, indicating its role in both arbuscular mycorrhiza and root nodule symbiosis.

genes: PhLYK10 (PhLYK10, LysM receptor-like kinase, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Pro35S:PhLYK10 partially complements the lack of nodules in Mtnfp and Ljnfr5 mutants, restoring nodule formation and rhizobial colonization.
mechanism: PhLYK10 functions as a receptor for Myc-LCOs in both arbuscular mycorrhiza and root nodule symbiosis, enabling signal transduction for symbiotic interactions.

genes: SlLYK10 (SlLYK10, LysM receptor-like kinase, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Pro35S:SlLYK10 partially complements the lack of nodules in Mtnfp mutants, restoring nodule formation and rhizobial colonization.
mechanism: SlLYK10 functions as a receptor for Myc-LCOs in both arbuscular mycorrhiza and root nodule symbiosis, enabling signal transduction for symbiotic interactions.

genes: PhLYK10 (PhLYK10, LysM receptor-like kinase, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: ProLjUBI:PhLYK10-mOrange triggers spontaneous nodule formation in L. japonicus in the absence of rhizobia.
mechanism: PhLYK10 overexpression activates nodule formation independently of rhizobial signals, suggesting a role in autoregulation of nodule development.

genes: JcWRKY (JcWRKY, WRKY transcription factor)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcWRKY improves photosynthetic response during salinity stress, with increased photosynthesis rate (13% improvement with NaCl treatment), enhanced water use efficiency (WUE), and increased epicuticular wax accumulation (alkanes, fatty alcohols, carboxylic acids) in tobacco transgenics.
mechanism: JcWRKY enhances photosynthetic efficiency through improved stomatal regulation, increased non-photochemical quenching (NPQ), and altered wax composition. The WRKY transcription factor likely regulates downstream genes involved in photosynthesis (NtCab40, NtLhcb5, NtRca1) and wax biosynthesis (NtWIN1), while modulating stomatal aperture and salt crystal deposition.

genes: CsDFRa (CsDFRa, dihydroflavonol 4-reductase, Camellia sinensis), CsDFRaΔ87 (CsDFRaΔ87, truncated N-terminal variant of CsDFRa, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Both CsDFRa and CsDFRaΔ87 are localized in the cytoplasm of Arabidopsis thaliana protoplasts.
mechanism: Fusion of CsDFRa and its N-terminal-truncated variant with yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) for subcellular localization tracking.

genes: FaPRE1 (FaPRE1, atypical HLH transcription factor, Fragaria x ananassa)
phenotype: Transitory silencing of FaPRE1 transcription by agroinfiltration in receptacle produced the down-regulation of a group of genes related to the ripening process while inducing the transcription of genes involved in receptacle growth and development.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated silencing of FaPRE1 antagonistically coordinates the transcription of genes related to both receptacle growth and ripening.

genes: GRMZM2G308463 (NAD(P)-binding Rossmann-fold superfamily protein of unknown function, Zea mays)
phenotype: GUS expression in a root-preferential manner
mechanism: the promoters are root-specific or root-preferential

genes: GRMZM2G125023 (tonoplast intrinsic protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: GUS expression in a root-preferential manner
mechanism: the promoters are root-specific or root-preferential

genes: GRMZM2G091534 (extensin-like protein, Zea mays)
phenotype: GUS expression in a root-preferential manner
mechanism: the promoters are root-specific or root-preferential

genes: GRMZM2G088531 (polygalacturonase inhibitor, Zea mays)
phenotype: GUS expression in a root-preferential manner
mechanism: the promoters are root-specific or root-preferential

genes: GRMZM2G036629 (metallothionein-like protein 1, Zea mays)
phenotype: GUS expression in a root-preferential manner
mechanism: the promoters are root-specific or root-preferential

genes: LpP5CS (LpP5CS, proline biosynthesis gene, Panicum virgatum)
phenotype: Overexpression of LpP5CS increases proline synthesis and decreases proline degradation in switchgrass, leading to higher proline content, increased tiller number, and thicker stems compared to wild type.
mechanism: Proline metabolism is coordinated with lignin biosynthesis pathways, affecting plant growth and development through altered NADP(H) ratios and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis.

genes: CHS (chalcone synthase, from Anoectochilus roxburghii and Anoectochilus formosanus)
phenotype: Overexpression of CHS in onion cells localizes the protein to the nucleus.
mechanism: CHS protein contains a nuclear localization signal (Arg66-Lys67-Arg68-His69) at the N-terminal.

genes: CHS (chalcone synthase, from Anoectochilus roxburghii and Anoectochilus formosanus)
phenotype: Transgenic rice lines show increased total flavonoids content (1.40–1.68 times higher than untransformed lines).
mechanism: CHS is a rate-limiting enzyme in flavonoid biosynthesis of the phenylpropanoid pathway.

genes: PDS (Phytoene DeSaturase, reporter gene, synthetic), ABC-C6 (ABC transporter gene, root-expressed, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Knockdown of ABC-C6 reduces transcript abundance by 63.29%±11.64% (syringe) and 64.92%±9.44% (topical), alters root exudate composition, and inhibits nematode hatching/attraction.
mechanism: ABC-C6 modulates root exudate composition by altering lipid profiles (e.g., reduced 2-methyloctacosane, increased nonadecane/tetradecanoic acid), which affects nematode chemosensory behavior.

genes: PDS (Phytoene DeSaturase, reporter gene, synthetic), ABC-G33 (ABC transporter gene, root-expressed, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Knockdown of ABC-G33 reduces transcript abundance by 66.30%±8.68% (syringe) and 46.40%±5.90% (topical), alters root exudate composition (elevated eicosane/octadecanoic acid), and inhibits nematode hatching/attraction.
mechanism: ABC-G33 modulates root exudate composition by altering lipid profiles (e.g., elevated eicosane, heptadecane, octadecanoic acid), which affects nematode chemosensory behavior and microbial attraction.

genes: PbrPG6 (polygalacturonase 6, key gene in fruit softening, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Higher firmness observed in PbrPG6-silenced fruit compared to control (empty vector) during storage
mechanism: Silencing PbrPG6 reduces PG activity, maintaining fruit firmness by preventing pectin degradation

genes: AtOXS2 (AtOXS2, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: No significant differential phenotype observed in overexpressing lines compared to wild-type under salt stress.
mechanism: AtOXS2 translocates to the nucleus under salt stress, suggesting it regulates downstream genes involved in salt tolerance.

genes: AtOXS2 (AtOXS2, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: FLAG-tagged AtOXS2 was used to recover the salt-sensitive phenotype of oxs2-1 mutants, confirming its role in salt tolerance.
mechanism: AtOXS2 binds to promoters of downstream genes (e.g., CA1 and Araport11) containing BOXS2 motifs, regulating salt stress responses.

genes: AtOXS2 (AtOXS2, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: AtOXS2 translocates from the cytoplasm to the nucleus under salt stress in onion epidermal cells, indicating its role in stress response.
mechanism: Salt stress induces nuclear localization of AtOXS2, enabling it to regulate downstream genes involved in salt tolerance.

genes: OsNPPR3 (nucleolus-localized P-subfamily PPR protein, rice, Os03g0728200)
phenotype: Complementation of the flo14 mutant restored normal seed appearance and starch granule structure, with transparent endosperm and viable seeds.
mechanism: OsNPPR3 regulates nuclear and mitochondrial gene expression and splicing, affecting starch biosynthesis and seed development.

genes: OsNPPR3 (nucleolus-localized P-subfamily PPR protein, rice, Os03g0728200)
phenotype: Knockout of OsNPPR3 by CRISPR/Cas9 system produced seeds with chalky endosperm and seed-lethal phenotypes, similar to the flo14 mutant.
mechanism: OsNPPR3 is essential for mitochondrial gene expression and splicing, and its disruption leads to impaired starch biosynthesis and seed development.

genes: OsNPPR3 (nucleolus-localized P-subfamily PPR protein, rice, Os03g0728200)
phenotype: OsNPPR3-GFP fusion protein localized to the nucleolus in rice protoplasts and tobacco leaves, confirming nucleolar targeting.
mechanism: OsNPPR3 contains a nucleolar localization signal, as evidenced by co-localization with nucleolus markers RPL23aB.

genes: OsNPPR3 (nucleolus-localized P-subfamily PPR protein, rice, Os03g0728200)
phenotype: Histochemical analysis of GUS activity in transgenic plants showed constitutive expression in roots, stems, leaves, panicles, and leaf shoots.
mechanism: OsNPPR3 promoter drives ubiquitous expression of the GUS reporter gene, indicating its constitutive activity in rice tissues.

genes: GmWRKY40 (WRKY transcription factor, group IIc, involved in resistance to Phytophthora sojae, Glycine max)
phenotype: Suppression of GmWRKY40 increased soybean susceptibility to Phytophthora sojae, with enhanced pathogen biomass accumulation and larger lesions compared to control roots.
mechanism: GmWRKY40 functions as a positive regulator in soybean resistance to Phytophthora sojae through modulating hydrogen peroxide accumulation and jasmonic acid (JA) signaling pathways.

genes: GmWRKY40 (WRKY transcription factor, group IIc, involved in resistance to Phytophthora sojae, Glycine max)
phenotype: GmWRKY40 protein is localized in the nucleus of Nicotiana benthamiana leaf cells, as demonstrated by GFP fluorescence and DAPI staining.
mechanism: Nuclear localization of GmWRKY40 suggests it functions as a transcription factor in plant defense responses.

genes: PhLSH7a (PhLSH7a, transcription factor, Petunia hybrida), PhLSH7b (PhLSH7b, transcription factor, Petunia hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of PhLSH7a and PhLSH7b in Arabidopsis results in small round leaves, late flowering, deformed flowers with abnormal petals and exposed pistil, and sterile fruits. Strongly overexpressing lines (35S:PhLSH7a-1 and 35S:PhLSH7b-2) are infertile, with no progeny from self-pollination and only few seeds from crosses with wild-type pollen.
mechanism: NA

genes: Cs-UGT78D3 (UDP-GLUCOSYL TRANSFERASE, Citrus sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of Cs-UGT78D3 results in high proanthocyanidins accumulation in seed coats (dark brown color), increased flavonoid and anthocyanin content in leaves, and enhanced antioxidant activity under high light stress.
mechanism: Cs-UGT78D3 upregulates flavonoid and anthocyanin biosynthesis genes (TT3, TT8, TTG2, BAN) by 4–15 folds, leading to increased antioxidant capacity via photoprotective anthocyanin accumulation.

genes: BcpLH (Brassica rapa, antisense), BcpLH2 (Brassica rapa, antisense)
phenotype: Knockdown of BcpLH and BcpLH2 in Chinese cabbage causes earlier leaf curvature (10 days earlier), earlier heading time (63.7 days vs 74.6 days in wild type), and transition from round to oval head shape. Leaves show crinkles, bulges, and wavy margins. Head height increases from 18.5 cm to 21.0 cm, and head weight increases from 0.65 kg to 0.75 kg.
mechanism: BcpLH and BcpLH2 regulate miRNA processing. Knockdown disrupts miR156, miR165/6, and miR319 accumulation, altering their target genes (BrpSPL9-2, BrpREV-1, BrpTCP4) to affect leaf curvature timing and head formation.

genes: BcpLH (Brassica rapa, C-terminus-GFP), BcpLH2 (Brassica rapa, C-terminus-GFP)
phenotype: Rescues hyl1 mutant phenotype in Arabidopsis with 91.7% and 89.5% rescue efficiency, respectively. Restores miRNA accumulation (miR156, miR166) and corrects leaf curvature and phase transition defects.
mechanism: BcpLH and BcpLH2 function in miRNA biogenesis by binding pri-miRNAs and facilitating cleavage. They colocalize with DCL1 and SE in the nucleus and bind pri-miR168a in vitro.

genes: BcpLH (Brassica rapa, C-terminus-GFP)
phenotype: Rescues hyl1 mutant phenotype in Arabidopsis with 95.2% rescue efficiency. Restores miRNA accumulation and corrects leaf curvature and phase transition defects.
mechanism: BcpLH functions in miRNA biogenesis by binding pri-miRNAs and facilitating cleavage. It colocalizes with DCL1 and SE in the nucleus and binds pri-miR168a in vitro.

genes: miR156a (synthetic), miR166g (synthetic), 5mTCP4 (synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR156a delays heading time by 40 days; overexpression of miR166g increases downward leaf curvature; overexpression of 5mTCP4 reduces leaf wrinkles. Crosses with LHas-1 partially rescue the antisense BcpLH phenotype.
mechanism: miR156a regulates phase transition via BrpSPL9-2; miR166g regulates leaf curvature via BrpREV; 5mTCP4 regulates leaf flatness via BrpTCP4. These miRNAs interact with BcpLH-regulated pathways.

genes: amiR-ax1117 (artificial microRNA targeting M3Kδ5, M3Kδ7, M3Kδ1, M3Kδ6, M3Kδ-CTR1, source Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of amiR-ax1117 reduces ABA sensitivity in seed germination, leading to reduced stomatal conductance and impaired ABA response.
mechanism: The amiR-ax1117 targets M3K genes, which are required for ABA activation of SnRK2 kinases.

genes: m3k amiRNA (artificial microRNA targeting seven overlapping Arabidopsis Raf-like kinase members from subgroup B1 and B3, source Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of m3k amiRNA reduces ABA sensitivity in seed germination and impairs ABA-dependent stomatal closure.
mechanism: The m3k amiRNA targets M3K genes, which are required for ABA activation of SnRK2 kinases and SLAC1 anion channel activation.

genes: amiRNA-HsMYO (artificial microRNA targeting human myosin 2 gene (HsMYO2), source synthetic)
phenotype: Control line for amiRNA experiments; no specific phenotype described.
mechanism: NA

genes: OST1-HF(S171A) (mutant isoform of OST1/SnRK2.6 with Ser171 replaced by alanine, source Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of OST1-HF(S171A) in the ost1-3 background fails to rescue ABA-induced stomatal closure and warm leaf temperatures.
mechanism: OST1-HF(S171A) lacks the ability to be reactivated by M3K-mediated phosphorylation at Ser171, which is essential for ABA signaling.

genes: nnH3H (luciferase, codon-optimized for A. thaliana, FASMAC), nnLuz (luciferase, codon-optimized for A. thaliana, FASMAC)
phenotype: Overexpression of nnH3H and nnLuz increases luminescence intensity in Arabidopsis thaliana T87 cells.
mechanism: Codon-optimized luciferase genes enhance expression and activity in plant cells.

genes: FLuc (firefly luciferase, Photinus pyralis), NLuc (Nano-lantern luciferase, Renilla reniformis), GeNL (green enhanced Nano-lantern, fusion of mNeonGreen and NLuc)
phenotype: Overexpression of FLuc produces detectable luminescence in Arabidopsis thaliana T87 cells.
mechanism: Firefly luciferase catalyzes d-luciferin oxidation to emit light.

genes: NLuc (Nano-lantern luciferase, Renilla reniformis), GeNL (green enhanced Nano-lantern, fusion of mNeonGreen and NLuc)
phenotype: Overexpression of NLuc increases luminescence intensity in Arabidopsis thaliana T87 cells.
mechanism: NLuc catalyzes furimazine oxidation to emit light at 450 nm.

genes: GeNL (green enhanced Nano-lantern, fusion of mNeonGreen and NLuc)
phenotype: Overexpression of GeNL increases luminescence transmittance through plant cells by ~25% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GeNL's emission wavelength (520 nm) avoids chlorophyll absorption bands, enhancing light transmission.

genes: secFLuc (firefly luciferase with secretory signal, Photinus pyralis), secNLuc (Nano-lantern luciferase with secretory signal, Renilla reniformis), secGeNL (green enhanced Nano-lantern with secretory signal)
phenotype: Secretory signal addition to FLuc reduces luminescence intensity in Arabidopsis thaliana T87 cells.
mechanism: Secretory signal directs luciferase to extracellular space, where pH-dependent activity is reduced.

genes: secNLuc (Nano-lantern luciferase with secretory signal, Renilla reniformis)
phenotype: Secretory signal addition to NLuc reduces luminescence intensity in Arabidopsis thaliana T87 cells.
mechanism: Secretory signal directs luciferase to extracellular space, where pH-dependent activity is reduced.

genes: secGeNL (green enhanced Nano-lantern with secretory signal)
phenotype: Secretory signal addition to GeNL increases luminescence intensity at pH 8.2 in Arabidopsis thaliana T87 cells.
mechanism: Secreted GeNL activity is pH-dependent, with optimal activity at pH 8.2.

genes: RLD1 (RLD1, RLD gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues the GSA phenotype of rld1 rld4 lateral roots by expressing RLD1-GFP in root statocytes
mechanism: Functional RLD1-GFP in root statocytes is responsible for GSA control of lateral roots

genes: RLD1 (RLD1, RLD gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescues embryo development and root formation in rld1 rld2 rld3 rld4 quadruple mutants but fails to rescue gravitropic growth of primary roots
mechanism: Vascular-specific expression of RLD1-mCherry rescues embryo and root development but not gravitropic growth

genes: RLD1 (RLD1, RLD gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expressed in protoplast cells to study RLD1 localization and interaction with LZY proteins
mechanism: Used to confirm LZY-dependent recruitment of RLD1 to the plasma membrane

genes: LZY2 (LZY2, LZY gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Used to study LZY2 recruitment of RLD1 to the plasma membrane in root cap cells
mechanism: LZY2-mCherry expression in root cap cells co-localizes with RLD1-GFP at the plasma membrane

genes: LZY3 (LZY3, LZY gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Inducible expression of LZY3-mCherry in root cap cells to study its role in GSA control
mechanism: Overexpression of LZY3-mCherry disrupts RLD1 polarization and causes random LR growth angles

genes: RLD1 (RLD1, RLD gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Used to study the role of the RCC1 domain in RLD1 function
mechanism: Truncated RLD1 lacking the RCC1 domain is expressed to analyze its interaction with LZY proteins

genes: RLD1 (RLD1, RLD gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Used to study the role of the FYVE domain in RLD1 function
mechanism: Truncated RLD1 lacking the FYVE domain is expressed to analyze its interaction with LZY proteins

genes: RLD2 (RLD2, RLD gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of the BRX domain of RLD2 causes wider LR growth angles in wild type and rld1 rld4 mutants
mechanism: BRX domain expression disrupts LZY-RLD interaction, leading to altered GSA control

genes: LZY3 (LZY3, LZY gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Mutant LZY3 fails to complement the triple mutant phenotype, demonstrating the importance of CCL-BRX interaction
mechanism: Disruption of CCL-BRX interaction prevents LZY3 function in GSA control

genes: eIF4E (potato4E:pvr12, name, modified eIF4E allele for virus resistance, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of potato4E:pvr12 protects tetraploid Russet Burbank, Russet Norkotah, and Atlantic potato cultivars from PVYO, PVYN:O and PVYNTN infection with 4.6-fold increased eIF4E expression and 13-15% remaining native eIF4E transcript levels.
mechanism: Modified eIF4E:pvr12 disrupts virus ability to recruit ribosomes to VPg protein linked to viral genome, suppresses native eIF4E transcript abundance, and induces cell stress response gene deregulation.

genes: GhSOS3 (Gh_A01G1607, calcium-binding EF-hand protein involved in salt-alkali stress response, Gossypium hirsutum), GhCBL10 (Gh_D05G0440, calcineurin B-like protein 10 involved in salt-alkali stress response, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Salt-alkali sensitivity was increased in GhSOS3 and GhCBL10 Virus-induced Gene Silencing (VIGS) plants.
mechanism: GhSOS3/GhCBL10-SOS2 network plays a core role in specific regulation of salt-alkali stress in upland cotton. SOS3 and CBL act preferentially in roots and shoot under salt stress in Arabidopsis thaliana, respectively. GhSOS3/GhCBL10-GhSOS2 network in upland cotton may be similar to SOS signal pathway in Arabidopsis thaliana.

genes: IRE1A (At2g17520, IRE1A genomic sequence, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of bli ire1a double mutant phenotype in Arabidopsis thaliana
mechanism: IRE1A's protein kinase domain regulates non-canonical UPR gene expression and shoot growth phenotype in bli mutant plants

genes: BLI (At3g23980, BLI coding region, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Subcellular localization analysis of BLI in Arabidopsis thaliana root cells
mechanism: BLI localizes to the Golgi and nucleus, and negatively regulates the expression of ER stress responsive genes

genes: AdoIspS (AdoIspS, isoprene synthase, Arundo donax L.), AplIspS (AplIspS, isoprene synthase, Arundo plinii)
phenotype: Overexpression of AdoIspS and AplIspS increases isoprene emission by ~70-80 ppbv mg FW−1 in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: IspS catalyzes isoprene synthesis, confirmed by strong linear correlation between transgene expression and isoprene emission (R²=0.999 for AdoIspS vs. AplIspS).

genes: OsFPFL4 (OsFPFL4, FPF1-like 4 of rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsFPFL4 increases lateral root density and adventitious root number, reduces primary root length, promotes shoot growth, and causes helix primary root in rice. It also leads to shrunken anthers and abnormal pollen grains.
mechanism: OsFPFL4 modulates auxin homeostasis by affecting auxin biosynthesis (OsYUC1, OsYUC4, OsYUC6) and transport (OsPIN1a, OsPIN1b, OsPIN5a, OsPIN8, OsAUX1, OsAUX2), and alters ROS homeostasis by balancing ROS-producing (OsRbohs) and scavenging enzymes (peroxidases, glutathione S-transferases).

genes: OsFPFL4 (OsFPFL4, FPF1-like 4 of rice, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi of OsFPFL4 inhibits root system growth, delays flowering time, and causes shrunken anthers and abnormal pollen grains in rice. It also reduces auxin accumulation and increases ROS levels in roots and inflorescence.
mechanism: OsFPFL4 modulates auxin homeostasis by affecting auxin biosynthesis (OsYUC1, OsYUC4, OsYUC6) and transport (OsPIN1a, OsPIN1b, OsPIN5a, OsPIN8, OsAUX1, OsAUX2), and alters ROS homeostasis by balancing ROS-producing (OsRbohs) and scavenging enzymes (peroxidases, glutathione S-transferases).

genes: OsNADK1 (OsNADK1, NAD kinase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNADK1 enhances drought tolerance in rice plants, with increased proline content under drought conditions.
mechanism: OsNADK1 maintains intracellular redox balance, affecting NADP(H)/NAD(H), GSH/GSSG, and ASA/DHA ratios, leading to enhanced drought tolerance.

genes: OsNADK1 (OsNADK1, RNAi, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi of OsNADK1 reduces drought tolerance, with decreased proline content under drought conditions.
mechanism: OsNADK1 deficiency disrupts redox balance, leading to increased oxidation states and sensitivity to drought.

genes: NAC15 (NAC15, nucleus-targeted gene, Populus simonii×P. nigra)
phenotype: Overexpression of NAC15 increases hemicellulose, cellulose, and lignin content by 1.09–1.58× in transgenic tobacco compared to control lines. Phloroglucinol staining shows darker vascular bundle lignification in transgenic lines.
mechanism: NAC15 upregulates lignin- and cellulose-related genes (CesA, CAD, PAL, 4CL, C4H) in transgenic tobacco, enhancing secondary cell wall biosynthesis.

genes: FvPME38 (pectin methylesterase, Fragaria vesca), FvPME39 (pectin methylesterase, Fragaria vesca)
phenotype: Overexpression of FvPME38 and FvPME39 accelerates strawberry fruit ripening and reduces fruit firmness by decreasing pectin content and altering cell wall structure.
mechanism: FvPME38 and FvPME39 catalyze pectin demethylesterification, leading to cell wall loosening and reduced intercellular adhesion, which correlates with decreased fruit firmness.

genes: FvPME38 (pectin methylesterase, Fragaria vesca), FvPME39 (pectin methylesterase, Fragaria vesca)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of FvPME38 and FvPME39 delays strawberry fruit ripening and increases fruit firmness by elevating pectin content and strengthening cell wall structure.
mechanism: RNAi suppression of FvPME38 and FvPME39 reduces pectin demethylesterification, maintaining cell wall rigidity and intercellular adhesion, which correlates with increased fruit firmness.

genes: psaA (Photosystem I P700 chlorophyl a apoprotein A1, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii), Cas9c (codon-optimized Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9, synthetic), GFPc (codon-optimized green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: No detectable donor DNA insertion in Chlamydomonas chloroplasts with YP14 construct
mechanism: Cas9/gRNA-mediated double-strand cleavage without effective homology-directed repair

genes: psbD (photosystem II protein D, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii), Cas9c (codon-optimized Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9, synthetic), GFPc (codon-optimized green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: No detectable donor DNA insertion in Chlamydomonas chloroplasts with YP21 construct
mechanism: Cas9/gRNA-mediated double-strand cleavage without effective homology-directed repair due to weak promoter

genes: psbD (photosystem II protein D, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii), Cas9c (codon-optimized Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9, synthetic), GFPc (codon-optimized green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: No detectable donor DNA insertion in Chlamydomonas chloroplasts with YP22 construct
mechanism: Cas9/gRNA-mediated double-strand cleavage without effective homology-directed repair due to weak promoter and less effective gRNAs

genes: psaA (Photosystem I P700 chlorophyl a apoprotein A1, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii), sgRNA1c (guide RNA targeting psaA gene, synthetic), sgRNA2c (guide RNA targeting psaA gene, synthetic), GFPc (codon-optimized green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: No detectable donor DNA insertion in Chlamydomonas chloroplasts with YP23 construct (negative control without Cas9)
mechanism: Homologous recombination without Cas9 activity is insufficient for DNA insertion

genes: psaA (Photosystem I P700 chlorophyl a apoprotein A1, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii), sgRNA3c (guide RNA targeting psaA gene, synthetic), sgRNA4c (guide RNA targeting psaA gene, synthetic), GFPc (codon-optimized green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: No detectable donor DNA insertion in Chlamydomonas chloroplasts with YP24 construct (negative control without Cas9)
mechanism: Homologous recombination without Cas9 activity is insufficient for DNA insertion

genes: FER (Feronia, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: FER is up-regulated by CCA1 and binds to clock genes, modulating their expression patterns. FER also regulates flowering by repressing FLC and MAFs through pre-mRNA splicing and transcript accumulation, linking the circadian clock to floral transition.

genes: FER (Feronia, receptor-like kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: FT (FLOWERING LOCUS T, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

genes: CCA1 (circadian clock-associated 1, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)

mechanism: CCA1 binds to the FER chromatin and promotes its expression. FER in turn regulates clock genes and flowering-related genes like FLC and MAFs through mRNA splicing and transcript accumulation, forming an interlocking feedback loop with the circadian clock.
