mechanism: NtAGIP1 promoter drives tissue-specific expression in reproductive organs.

genes: NtAGIP1 (NtAGIP1 promoter with 35S enhancer, Nicotiana tabacum, source), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli, source)
phenotype: 35SNtAGIP1::GUS expression is observed in stamens, carpels, sepals, and pedicels but not in vegetative tissues.
mechanism: 35S enhancer broadens tissue-specificity to whole inflorescence while maintaining reproductive organ specificity.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli, source)
phenotype: Promoterless::GUS shows no detectable GUS activity in transgenic tobacco.
mechanism: Lack of promoter prevents gene expression.

genes: NtAGIP1 (NtAGIP1 promoter deletion variant, Nicotiana tabacum, source), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli, source)
phenotype: NtAGIP1(-2835)::GUS shows no GUS expression in leaves of transgenic tobacco.
mechanism: Deletion of -2835 to -2735 region suppresses vegetative expression.

genes: NtAGIP1 (NtAGIP1 promoter deletion variant, Nicotiana tabacum, source), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli, source)
phenotype: NtAGIP1(-2365)::GUS shows 36.3% GUS expression frequency in leaves of transgenic tobacco.
mechanism: Deletion removes repressive elements, allowing partial vegetative expression.

genes: NtAGIP1 (NtAGIP1 promoter with repressive fragment, Nicotiana tabacum, source), GUS (beta-glucuronidase, Escherichia coli, source)
phenotype: 35SRF::GUS shows 50.0% GUS expression in leaves with reduced activity compared to controls.
mechanism: Repressive fragment suppresses 35S enhancer activity in vegetative tissues.

genes: IDD3 (IDD3, transcription factor, Oryza sativa), IDD13 (IDD13, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: IDD3 overexpression increases susceptibility to sheath blight disease (ShB) in rice.
mechanism: IDD3 negatively regulates PIN1a expression, reducing resistance to ShB.

genes: IDD13 (IDD13, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: IDD13 RNAi increases susceptibility to sheath blight disease (ShB) in rice.
mechanism: IDD13 positively regulates PIN1a expression, enhancing resistance to ShB.

genes: IDD13 (IDD13, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: IDD13 overexpression decreases susceptibility to sheath blight disease (ShB) in rice.
mechanism: IDD13 positively regulates PIN1a expression, enhancing resistance to ShB.

genes: SlKYP (KYP, tomato ortholog of AtKYP, Solyc02g094520), SlCMT3a (CMT3a, tomato ortholog of AtCMT3, Solyc01g006100), SlCMT3b (CMT3b, tomato ortholog of AtCMT3, Solyc12g100330)
phenotype: Mutants exhibit stunted growth, wrinkled asymmetric leaves with yellow spots, few abnormal flowers, reduced fruit production, and no seeds in Solanum lycopersicum.
mechanism: Disruption of CHG/CHH methylation maintenance by KYP/CMT3a leads to gene overexpression in promoter regions, causing developmental defects.

genes: CbuSPL9 (SQUAMOSA promoter-binding protein-LIKE, Catalpa bungei, cloned from 'Bairihua')
phenotype: Overexpression of CbuSPL9 in Arabidopsis leads to accelerated flowering time (bolting with <9 rosette leaves vs. 14 in wild type) and aberrant floral organ morphology (shrunken petals, increased stamens, overlapping petals).
mechanism: CbuSPL9 functions similarly to Arabidopsis SPL homologues in regulating flowering development, likely through conserved SBP-box domain interactions with DNA and protein partners like CbuHMGA.

genes: CbuHMGA (AT-HOOK MOTIF NUCLEAR LOCALIZED PROTEIN, Catalpa bungei, cloned from 'Bairihua')
phenotype: Overexpression of CbuHMGA in Arabidopsis results in aberrant floral organ morphology (shrunken petals, dislocated petals, increased petals) but does not affect flowering time.
mechanism: CbuHMGA interacts with CbuSPL9 in the nucleus to form a heterodimer, suggesting a role in floral organ development but not flowering time regulation.

genes: PcDWF1 (PcDWF1, plasma membrane-localized BR biosynthetic enzyme, Pyrus ussuriensis)
phenotype: PcDWF1-GFP fluorescence overlaps with plasma membrane marker FM4–64 in Nicotiana benthamiana cells
mechanism: PcDWF1 is located in the plasma membrane

genes: NbMLP28 (NbMLP28, defense-related protein, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of NbMLP28 enhances resistance to PVY infection in N. benthamiana, reducing viral accumulation by ~37-42% at 3-4 dpi and decreasing infected leaf area.
mechanism: NbMLP28 is responsive to jasmonic acid (JA) signaling, which modulates its expression and contributes to PVY resistance.

genes: NbMLP28 (NbMLP28, defense-related protein, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Constitutive overexpression of NbMLP28::RFP in N. benthamiana promotes seed germination (45% at 3 days vs. 23% in wild type) and root growth (2.8 cm vs. 2.0 cm in wild type), while enhancing PVY resistance.
mechanism: NbMLP28 overexpression activates JA signaling, which is critical for PVY resistance. Silencing COI1 (a key JA pathway gene) reduces NbMLP28 expression and increases PVY accumulation.

genes: PTR2 (AtPTR2, peptide transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of ptr2 mutant germination delay phenotype, rescuing testa rupture (TR) and endosperm rupture (ER) timing
mechanism: PTR2 facilitates water uptake during phases II and III of germination by transporting di/tripeptides to the cytosol, increasing osmotic potential

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of GUS reporter gene under PTR2 promoter in germinating embryos during phase II
mechanism: PTR2 promoter activity is regulated by ABI4, with reduced expression in ABI4 overexpression lines

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of GUS reporter gene under CaMV35S promoter in germinating embryos
mechanism: CaMV35S promoter drives constitutive expression for baseline comparison with PTR2 promoter activity

genes: OsXDH (LOC4333171, xanthine dehydrogenase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsXDH increases plant height, chlorophyll content, and chlorophyll fluorescence parameters in rice, leading to higher seed-setting rate and 1000-grain weight compared to wild-type.
mechanism: OsXDH enhances antioxidant capacity by reducing reactive oxygen species (ROS) and lipid peroxidation, maintaining photosynthetic efficiency and delaying leaf senescence.

genes: OsXDH (LOC4333171, xanthine dehydrogenase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi of OsXDH reduces plant height, chlorophyll content, and chlorophyll fluorescence parameters in rice, leading to lower seed-setting rate and 1000-grain weight compared to wild-type.
mechanism: OsXDH knockdown increases reactive oxygen species (ROS) and lipid peroxidation, impairing photosynthetic efficiency and accelerating leaf senescence.

genes: miR173 (microRNA, microRNA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants accumulate miR173 much higher than the wild type
mechanism: NA

genes: OTU1 (OTU1, histone deubiquitinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CFP-OTU1 accumulates in cytoplasm and nucleus of Arabidopsis leaf epidermis cells
mechanism: NA

genes: mRFP (mRFP, fluorescent reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: mRFP partitions between cytoplasm and nucleus of Arabidopsis leaf epidermis cells
mechanism: NA

genes: mRFP-VirD2 NLS (mRFP-VirD2 NLS, nuclear localization signal reporter, Agrobacterium VirD2)
phenotype: mRFP-VirD2 NLS accumulates in nucleus of Arabidopsis leaf epidermis cells
mechanism: NA

genes: OTU1 (OTU1, histone deubiquitinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: otu1-1 and otu1-2 mutants exhibit reduced seed size, leaf rosette diameter, and stem length in Arabidopsis
mechanism: OTU1 loss of function leads to transcriptional activation of DA1 and DA2 genes, which negatively regulate seed and organ size

genes: scFvFc 2G8 (single-chain fragment variable fused to human IgG1 Fc, anti-β1-3 glucan antibody, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of scFvFc 2G8 in hairy roots of Nicotiana benthamiana and Solanum lycopersicum achieves up to 68 μg/g root fresh weight antibody yield with antifungal activity against Candida albicans
mechanism: scFvFc 2G8 binds to β1,3-glucan in fungal cell walls, inhibiting Candida albicans growth through antigen recognition

genes: NaEAH1-g12 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic), NaEAH1-g14 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of two gRNAs increases editing efficiency from 3.0% to 15% and induces large deletions between cleavage sites in NaEAH1.
mechanism: SpCas9-gRNA cleavage at proximal sites induces large deletions via non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) repair.

genes: NaNEC1c-g1 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic), NaNEC1c-g2 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic), NaNEC1c-g3 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of three gRNAs increases total mutation frequency to 25.7% in protoplasts and induces heritable mutations in T0 and T1 plants.
mechanism: SpCas9-gRNA cleavage at three proximal sites induces large deletions and small indels via NHEJ repair.

genes: NaEAH1-g12 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic), NaEAH1-g14 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic), NaNEC1c-g1 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic), NaNEC1c-g2 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of four gRNAs edits two genes (NaEAH1 and NaNEC1c) with >50% mutation frequency in calli.
mechanism: SpCas9-gRNA cleavage at four sites induces large deletions and small indels via NHEJ repair.

genes: NaMYC2-g2 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic), NaEAH1-g14 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic), NaNEC1c-g1 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic), NaNEC3a-g4 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic), NaNEC5b-g21 (guide RNA, target sequence, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of five gRNAs induces targeted mutations in five genes with variable indel frequencies (2.3–65.2%) in calli.
mechanism: SpCas9-gRNA cleavage at five sites induces indels via NHEJ repair.

genes: ATR1 (ATR1, putative ABC transporter, Cercospora nicotianae), CFP (CFP, putative MFS transporter, Cercospora nicotianae), 71cR (71cR, hypothetical protein, Cercospora nicotianae)
phenotype: Overexpression of ATR1 and 71cR reduces disease symptoms (lesion size and number) in Nicotiana tabacum inoculated with C. nicotianae by ~40-60% compared to cv 'Hicks'.
mechanism: ATR1 encodes an ABC transporter involved in cercosporin resistance; 71cR encodes a hypothetical protein with unknown function but induced in cercosporin-resistant mutants.

genes: CTB1 (CTB1, polyketide synthase, Cercospora nicotianae), CTB8 (CTB8, pathway transcriptional activator, Cercospora nicotianae)
phenotype: RNAi silencing of CTB1 and CTB8 reduces disease severity in Nicotiana tabacum inoculated with C. nicotianae by ~40-60% compared to cv 'Hicks'.
mechanism: CTB1 is the first enzyme in cercosporin biosynthesis; CTB8 regulates the pathway. Silencing these genes inhibits cercosporin production.

genes: OsGAD3 (glutamate decarboxylase, rice), gRNA-F1 (guide RNA for OsGAD3), gRNA-R1 (guide RNA for OsGAD3)
phenotype: Seven-fold higher GABA content in seeds, increased seed weight (12%) and protein content (20%) in line #8_8 compared to wild-type
mechanism: Truncation of OsGAD3's Ca2+/CaMBD domain removes autoinhibitory regulation, leading to constitutive GAD activity and increased GABA synthesis

genes: WsAP2 (AP2/ethylene response factor, Withania somnifera)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of WsAP2 increases expression of secondary metabolic pathway genes (CAS, HMGR, DXS, DXR, GGPPS) in Withania somnifera, with GGPPS showing >80-fold induction.
mechanism: WsAP2 acts as a master regulator of terpenoid biosynthesis by inducing MVA and MEP pathway genes (HMGR, CAS, DXS, DXR) and strongly upregulating GGPPS.

genes: EdVP1 (EdVP1, V-type H+-PPase, Elymus dahuricus)
phenotype: Overexpression of EdVP1 increases grain yield and K utilization efficiency in the field.
mechanism: EdVP1 might promote K+ uptake by affecting the distribution of auxin in roots and the activity of K+ transporter in the plasma membrane.

genes: EdVP1 (EdVP1, V-type H+-PPase, Elymus dahuricus)
phenotype: Overexpression of EdVP1 increases potassium influx in transgenic plant root.
mechanism: EdVP1 might promote K+ uptake by affecting the distribution of auxin in roots and the activity of K+ transporter in the plasma membrane.

genes: MED9 (MED9, Mediator subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced total chlorophyll accumulation in med9 mutants compared to Col-0.
mechanism: MED9 is involved in stress response regulation, possibly through interaction with WRKY and CAMTA TFs.

genes: MED16 (MED16, Mediator subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced rosette diameter, biomass, and total chlorophyll accumulation in med16 mutants compared to Col-0.
mechanism: MED16 is required for WRKY, HSF, and CAMTA TF-dependent repression of stress-response genes prior to stress.

genes: MED18 (MED18, Mediator subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced rosette diameter and biomass in med18 mutants compared to Col-0.
mechanism: MED18 is involved in salt stress response through interaction with bZIP, bHLH, and Myb TFs.

genes: CDK8 (CDK8, Mediator subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced rosette diameter and biomass in cdk8 mutants compared to Col-0.
mechanism: CDK8 is required for function of circadian clock TFs in early salt stress response.

genes: miR319 (microRNA 319, non-coding RNA, switchgrass)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR319 in switchgrass increased plant height by ~40 cm, stem diameter, and biomass yield by ~15% compared to wild type. Lignin content was reduced, and enzymatic hydrolysis efficiency improved significantly.
mechanism: miR319–PvPCF5 module negatively regulates lignin content by downregulating PvMYB58/63B and PvHCT, altering lignin composition (higher S/G ratio and β-O-4 linkages).

genes: PvPCF5-SRDX (PvPCF5 transcription factor fused to SRDX repression domain, switchgrass)
phenotype: Overexpression of PvPCF5-SRDX reduced lignin content by ~20%, increased S/G ratio by ~30%, and β-O-4 linkages. Sugar yield per plant improved by ~25% after alkali pretreatment.
mechanism: PvPCF5-SRDX suppresses lignin biosynthesis genes (PvMYB58/63B, PvHCT) and alters lignin polymer structure, enhancing saccharification efficiency.

genes: GmNFYA5 (Glycine max, drought-induced transcription factor, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmNFYA5 in transgenic Arabidopsis plants caused enhanced drought tolerance in seedlings by decreasing stomatal aperture and water loss from leaves.
mechanism: GmNFYA5 probably regulated the transcript abundance of GmDREB2 and GmbZIP1 by binding to the promoters in vivo.

genes: GmNFYA5 (Glycine max, drought-induced transcription factor, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression and suppression of GmNFYA5 in soybean resulted in increased and decreased drought tolerance, respectively, relative to plants with an empty vector (EV).
mechanism: GmNFYA5 probably regulated the transcript abundance of GmDREB2 and GmbZIP1 by binding to the promoters in vivo.

genes: GmNFYA5 (RNAi hairpin, synthetic, Glycine max)
phenotype: Suppression of GmNFYA5 transcript produced opposite results relative to overexpression, with decreased drought tolerance in soybean.
mechanism: GmNFYA5 probably regulated the transcript abundance of GmDREB2 and GmbZIP1 by binding to the promoters in vivo.

genes: SmWRKY26 (SmWRKY26, cold tolerance gene, Solanum melongena)
phenotype: Silencing SmWRKY26 increases sensitivity to cold stress in eggplant.
mechanism: SmWRKY26 positively regulates cold tolerance.

genes: SmWRKY32 (SmWRKY32, cold tolerance gene, Solanum melongena)
phenotype: Silencing SmWRKY32 increases sensitivity to cold stress in eggplant.
mechanism: SmWRKY32 positively regulates cold tolerance.

genes: BCM1 (Arabidopsis thaliana, overexpression)
phenotype: Overexpression of BCM1 increases chlorophyll biosynthesis and reduces chlorophyll breakdown during senescence.
mechanism: BCM1 stimulates MgCh activity via interaction with GUN4 and destabilizes SGR1 to inhibit chlorophyll breakdown.

genes: BCM2 (Arabidopsis thaliana, overexpression)
phenotype: Overexpression of BCM2 rescues the pale-green leaf phenotype of bcm1 mutants and reduces chlorophyll breakdown during senescence.
mechanism: BCM2 functions similarly to BCM1 by interacting with GUN4 and destabilizing SGR1.

genes: ipaD (Shigella dysentery, N-terminal region, synthetic), PA20 (Bacillus anthracis, a-1 domain, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient expression of ipaD and PA20 in tomato leaves and fruits, with 4x higher expression in green fruits compared to leaves and red fruits
mechanism: CTxB acts as an adjuvant delivering antigens to mucosal-associated lymphoid tissues (MALTs) and enhancing immune response

genes: aadA (aminoglycoside 3'-adenylyltransferase, Escherichia coli), BACE (beta-secretase, Homo sapiens)
phenotype: Accumulation of BACE protein at 2.0% of total soluble protein (TSP)
mechanism: Dicistronic expression under the Prrn promoter with a ribosome binding site allows co-expression of aadA and BACE

genes: Pi54 (blast resistance gene, Tetep, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic rice lines show complete resistance to M. oryzae blast disease and moderate resistance to X. oryzae and R. solani
mechanism: Pi54 activates general defense response pathways including WRKY6, WRKY45, NAC6 transcription factors and defense-related genes

genes: CYP88D6 (CYP88D6, beta-amyrin 11-oxidase, Glycyrrhiza glabra)
phenotype: Overexpression of CYP88D6 increases glycyrrhizin content in some transgenic lines (e.g., D1) but not in others (D2, D3) in Glycyrrhiza glabra.
mechanism: NA

genes: Bt-cry1Aabc (domain shuffled, synthetic), nptII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of Bt-cry1Aabc in chickpea confers resistance to gram pod borer without significant agronomic differences compared to parent cv DCP 92-3.
mechanism: Expression of Bt-cry1Aabc toxin targets insect pests, providing resistance against gram pod borer.

genes: Bt-cry1Ac (plant codon optimized chimeric, synthetic), nptII (neomycin phosphotransferase II, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of Bt-cry1Ac in chickpea confers resistance to gram pod borer without significant agronomic differences compared to parent cv DCP 92-3.
mechanism: Expression of Bt-cry1Ac toxin targets insect pests, providing resistance against gram pod borer.

genes: SnRK1α1 (SnRK1 catalytic subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana), SnRK3.22 (SnRK3.22, Arabidopsis thaliana), AFP2 (AFP2, Arabidopsis thaliana), DUF828 (DUF828, Arabidopsis thaliana), MYB77 (MYB77, Arabidopsis thaliana), SnRK1α2 (SnRK1 catalytic subunit, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Validated in planta interactions between SnRK1α1 and SnRK3.22, AFP2, DUF828, MYB77, and between SnRK1α2 and SnRK3.22, AFP2 using Bimolecular Fluorescence Complementation (BiFC) assays
mechanism: NA

genes: PcGSTF12 (glutathione S-transferase, pear), AtGSTF12 (glutathione S-transferase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PcGSTF12 in Arabidopsis tt19–7 mutant rescues red hypocotyl phenotype and promotes anthocyanin/PA accumulation (7 anthocyanins and 7 PAs upregulated)
mechanism: PcGSTF12 functions as an anthocyanin and PA transporter, showing opposite affinity to AtGSTs for procyanidin A3 and petunidin 3,5-diglucoside

genes: PpSnRK1α (PpSnRK1α, α subunit of Prunus persica SnRK1, Prunus persica)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpSnRK1α increases salt tolerance in tomato by reducing leaf damage, increasing proline content, decreasing MDA, and enhancing ROS metabolism with higher antioxidant enzyme activities.
mechanism: PpSnRK1α enhances ROS metabolism by upregulating antioxidant enzyme genes and interacts with ABA signaling pathway components (SlPYL4, SlPYL8, SlPP2C37) to improve salt tolerance.

genes: HY5 (3×HA-tagged HY5, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HY5 reduces BZR1 accumulation and inhibits hypocotyl elongation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HY5 enhances BIN2 kinase activity, leading to phosphorylation and degradation of BZR1.

genes: HY5 (3×HA-tagged HY5L137D, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of HY5L137D mutant fails to suppress BZR1 accumulation and results in longer hypocotyls in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: HY5L137D mutation disrupts interaction with BIN2, reducing BIN2 kinase activity and BZR1 phosphorylation.

genes: TMV2 (TMV resistance gene, potato), TMV3 (TMV resistance gene, potato), DisRes (disease resistance gene, potato), Phloem1 (phloem protein-coding gene, potato), Phloem2 (phloem protein-coding gene, potato), Phloem3 (phloem protein-coding gene, potato), Phloem4 (phloem protein-coding gene, potato)
phenotype: Transgenic lines expressing TMV2, TMV3, DisRes, or phloem gene pairs showed no significant resistance to PVYNTN in repeated experiments.
mechanism: NA

genes: CsOPR3 (C. sinensis OPR3, involved in JA biosynthesis, Camellia sinensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsOPR3 in Arabidopsis opr3 mutant recovers wound-induced JA production.
mechanism: CsOPR3 functions as an OPR in JA biosynthesis.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase reporter gene, from the vector, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS activity in transgenic Arabidopsis represents CsOPR3 expression changes in tea plants.
mechanism: GUS reporter is used to monitor CsOPR3 promoter activity.

genes: MdDEP1 (dehydratase/enolase/phosphatase, Malus domestica, PCR amplified)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdDEP1 increases ethylene production and accelerates leaf senescence in apple (Malus domestica).
mechanism: MdDEP1 enhances ethylene biosynthesis via the Yang cycle, promoting leaf senescence by accelerating chlorophyll degradation.

genes: MdbHLH3 (basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Malus domestica, PCR amplified)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdbHLH3 causes severe leaf senescence symptoms, faster chlorophyll degradation, and increased ethylene production in apple (Malus domestica).
mechanism: MdbHLH3 directly activates MdDEP1 expression and ethylene biosynthetic genes (MdACO1, MdACS1, MdACS5A), accelerating leaf senescence.

genes: MdbHLH3 (basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Malus domestica, PCR amplified)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdbHLH3 enhances GUS activity in transgenic calli and increases MdDEP1 transcript levels in apple (Malus domestica).
mechanism: MdbHLH3 binds to the MdDEP1 promoter via E-box motifs, transcriptionally activating MdDEP1 expression.

genes: MdDEP1 (dehydratase/enolase/phosphatase, Malus domestica, PCR amplified)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdDEP1 causes severe leaf senescence symptoms, faster chlorophyll degradation, and increased ethylene production in apple (Malus domestica).
mechanism: MdDEP1 enhances ethylene biosynthesis via the Yang cycle, promoting leaf senescence by accelerating chlorophyll degradation.

genes: uidA (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, Escherichia coli, PCR amplified)
phenotype: PMdDEP1::uidA transgenic calli exhibit higher GUS activity when co-expressed with 35S::MdbHLH3 in apple (Malus domestica).
mechanism: MdbHLH3 binds to the MdDEP1 promoter, transcriptionally activating the uidA reporter gene.

genes: SlGlyI (Solyc09g082120.3.1, glyoxalase I, tomato)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlGlyI increases root biomass by ~7.8% under Al-treated conditions in tomato plants compared to 24% in empty vector controls and 25% in wild type
mechanism: SlGlyI enhances methylglyoxal (MG) detoxification by increasing glyoxalase I and II activity, reducing MG accumulation in root tips under Al stress

genes: PlWRKY65 (PlWRKY65, transcription factor, Paeonia lactiflora)
phenotype: Overexpression of PlWRKY65 localizes the protein to the nucleus in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: PlWRKY65 is a transcriptional regulator present in the nucleus.

genes: PlWRKY65 (PlWRKY65, transcription factor, Paeonia lactiflora)
phenotype: Silencing of PlWRKY65 reduces transcript abundance in Paeonia lactiflora.
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing.

genes: ZmGLK1 (ZmGLK1, transcription factor, Zea mays), ZmG2 (ZmG2, transcription factor, Zea mays)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of ZmGLK1 or ZmG2 in rice increases photosynthetic capacity, with ZmG2 showing greater effects than ZmGLK1, including 48% higher net photosynthetic rate at 1500 μmol m⁻² s⁻¹ light intensity and increased biomass and grain yield by 30–40% in field conditions.
mechanism: Overexpression of ZmGLK1 and ZmG2 enhances photosynthetic capacity by increasing PSII supercomplexes, PSI/PSII dimers, LHCII trimers, and xanthophyll pigments (zeaxanthin and lutein), leading to improved NPQ, ΦPSII, and resistance to photoinhibition under high or fluctuating light conditions.

genes: Rpi-amr1e (resistance gene, Solanum americanum)
phenotype: Overexpression of Rpi-amr1e reduces P. infestans growth in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves at 6 dpi.
mechanism: Rpi-amr1e recognizes Avramr1 effectors from P. infestans, triggering resistance.

genes: Rpi-amr1 (resistance gene, Solanum americanum)
phenotype: Transgenic potato plants with Rpi-amr1 resist P. infestans isolate 88069.
mechanism: Rpi-amr1 recognizes Avramr1 effectors from P. infestans, triggering resistance.

genes: CsIVP (Cucumis sativus Irregular Vasculature Patterning, transcription factor, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: Knockdown of CsIVP leads to dwarfism, fasciated stems, downwardly curled leaves, reduced fruit length, and decreased seed viability in Cucumis sativus.
mechanism: CsIVP regulates vascular development and auxin signaling by directly promoting the expression of vascular-related genes such as CsYAB5, CsBP, and CsAUX4. Knockdown increases auxin accumulation in leaf veins and disrupts vascular patterning.

genes: CsYAB5 (Cucumis sativus YABBY5, developmental regulator, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: Knockdown of CsYAB5 results in reduced plant height, abnormal leaf morphology, shorter fruit, and disrupted vascular configuration in Cucumis sativus.
mechanism: CsYAB5 functions downstream of CsIVP to regulate vascular patterning and organ morphogenesis. Knockdown phenocopies CsIVP-RNAi plants, indicating a direct regulatory relationship.

genes: ZAT1 (ZINC-FINGER OF ARABIDOPSIS THALIANA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic expression of Q2610>>ZAT1 induces severe growth inhibition in the root of transgenic seedlings.
mechanism: ZAT1 inhibits growth by suppressing cell division in the root apical meristem (RAM) and reducing meristematic zone size.

genes: ZAT4 (ZINC-FINGER OF ARABIDOPSIS THALIANA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic expression of Q2610>>ZAT4 induces severe growth inhibition in the primary root comparable to Q2610>>ZAT1.
mechanism: ZAT4 functions redundantly with ZAT1 to suppress growth in specific tissues.

genes: ZAT9 (ZINC-FINGER OF ARABIDOPSIS THALIANA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic expression of Q2610>>ZAT9 induces severe growth inhibition in the primary root comparable to Q2610>>ZAT1.
mechanism: ZAT9 functions redundantly with ZAT1 to suppress growth in specific tissues.

genes: ZAT1 (ZINC-FINGER OF ARABIDOPSIS THALIANA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic expression of J1721>>ZAT1 during embryogenesis induces rudimentary roots reminiscent of the mp phenotype.
mechanism: ZAT1 overexpression during embryogenesis disrupts root development by mimicking MONOPTEROS (MP) expression.

genes: ZAT1 (ZINC-FINGER OF ARABIDOPSIS THALIANA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic expression of J0571>>ZAT1 causes growth inhibition in roots and siliques, correlating with ZAT1 transcription levels.
mechanism: ZAT1 overexpression suppresses root and silique growth through tissue-specific regulation.

genes: ZAT1 (ZINC-FINGER OF ARABIDOPSIS THALIANA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of UASp:ZAT1-L251A induces growth inhibition comparable to wild-type ZAT1.
mechanism: EAR motif 2 is not essential for growth inhibition by ZAT1.

genes: ZAT1 (ZINC-FINGER OF ARABIDOPSIS THALIANA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of UASp:ZAT1-L253A induces growth inhibition comparable to wild-type ZAT1.
mechanism: EAR motif 2 is not essential for growth inhibition by ZAT1.

genes: ZAT1 (ZINC-FINGER OF ARABIDOPSIS THALIANA, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of UASp:ZAT1-mEAR2 fails to inhibit growth in 30 independent transgenic lines.
mechanism: The conserved EAR motif 2 is required for ZAT1-mediated growth inhibition.

genes: PheNAC3 (PheNAC3, NAC transcription factor, Phyllostachys edulis)

genes: BdbZIP26 (basic leucine zipper transcription factor, Brachypodium distachyon)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of BdbZIP26:GFP results in reduced stature and stunted growth in Brachypodium distachyon under control conditions, with similar stress responses to wild type plants under salt stress.
mechanism: Overexpression of BdbZIP26 places the plant in a constant state of stress, activating multiple stress-related pathways including hormone signaling (ABA, ethylene, auxin, JA) and defense responses.

genes: Ht1-FFT (fructan: fructan 1-fructosyl-transferase, Helianthus tuberosus)
phenotype: Overexpression of Ht1-FFT increases fructan concentration by ~179.81 mg·g−1 dry weight in transgenic tobacco, enhances PEG-simulated drought stress tolerance with higher soluble sugar and proline concentrations and reduced MDA levels.
mechanism: Ht1-FFT catalyzes fructan formation and extension, which participates in osmotic regulation and membrane stability during drought stress.

genes: BCHL (LHRS, rhodoxanthin synthase, Lonicera sp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of BCHL (LHRS) in N. benthamiana leads to accumulation of rhodoxanthin in leaves.
mechanism: BCHL facilitates rhodoxanthin biosynthesis.

genes: SpCas9 (CRISPR/Cas nuclease, Streptococcus pyogenes)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas-induced deletions in three wheat genes (TraesCS1A02G338200, TraesCS3A02G289300, TraesCS5A02G116500) observed in wheat protoplasts.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeted mutagenesis via guide RNA-directed DNA cleavage.

genes: sgRNA1 (guide RNA, synthetic), sgRNA2 (guide RNA, synthetic), sgRNA3 (guide RNA, synthetic), sgRNA4 (guide RNA, synthetic), sgRNA5 (guide RNA, synthetic), sgRNA6 (guide RNA, synthetic)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas-induced deletions in three wheat genes (TraesCS1A02G338200, TraesCS3A02G289300, TraesCS5A02G116500) observed in wheat protoplasts.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeted mutagenesis via tRNA-sgRNA polycistronic array processing into individual guide RNAs.

genes: TEX1 (transcription termination factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic sequence)
phenotype: Transformation of the genomic TEX1 construct into pho1-7 suppressor led to a pho1-like phenotype, confirming that the mutation in TEX1 was the causal mutation for restoration of pho1-7 shoot growth.
mechanism: The TEX1 mutation suppresses the shoot growth phenotype of pho1-7 by restoring PHO1 expression through impaired mRNA termination at the NOS terminator.

genes: TEX1 (transcription termination factor, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic sequence), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: pTEX1:gTEX1:GFP fusion confirmed nuclear localization of TEX1 protein in Arabidopsis roots.
mechanism: The TEX1-GFP fusion protein localizes to the nucleus, consistent with its role in mRNA termination.

genes: GUS (beta-glucuronidase, synthetic), TEX1 promoter (transcription termination factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: TEX1 promoter-GUS fusion showed expression in roots, cotyledons, and rosettes of Arabidopsis.
mechanism: The TEX1 promoter drives GUS expression in root, cotyledon, and rosette tissues.

genes: PHO1Δ83-114 (truncated phosphate transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic sequence), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of PHO1Δ83–114::GFP in pho1-4 null mutant partially restored shoot growth while maintaining low Pi content.
mechanism: The truncated PHO1Δ83–114 variant retains partial Pi export activity, sufficient to improve shoot growth in pho1 mutants.

genes: nLUC (nano-luciferase, synthetic), 3'UTR of AT1G76560/AT1G03160 (Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transient expression of nLUC fused to 3'UTR of AT1G76560/AT1G03160 in protoplasts showed increased long-to-short transcript ratios in hpr1-6 and tex1-4 mutants.
mechanism: 3'UTR extensions in hpr1-6 and tex1-4 mutants correlate with impaired mRNA termination and altered polyadenylation site choice.

genes: FHY3 (FHY3, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: FHY3 overexpression increases rosette branching by 27.3% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: FHY3 inhibits the DNA-binding activity of SPL9 and SPL15 to the BRC1 promoter, reducing BRC1 expression and promoting branching.

genes: FHY3 (FHY3, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S::FLAG-FHY3-HA transgenic plants show reduced FHY3 protein accumulation under simulated shade conditions.
mechanism: FHY3 protein stability is regulated by the 26S proteasome pathway, as MG132 treatment slows degradation.

genes: BRC1 (BRC1, branching repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana), SPL9 (SPL9, miR156-resistant form, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: BRC1 overexpression reduces rosette branching by ~44.2%, while rSPL9 overexpression reduces branching by ~72.4% in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SPL9 and SPL15 repress branching by upregulating BRC1 expression, which inhibits axillary bud outgrowth.

genes: SPL9 (SPL9, transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: 35S::rSPL9-HA transgenic plants show increased BRC1 promoter enrichment under normal light conditions.
mechanism: SPL9 binds to the BRC1 promoter and enhances its transcriptional activation, repressing branching.

genes: SMXL6 (SMXL6, strigolactone signaling component, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SMXL6D overexpression increases rosette branching by ~15.7% compared to rSPL9-OE in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: SMXL6/7/8 suppress the transactivation activity of SPL9/15 on BRC1, promoting branching.

genes: BRC1 (BRC1, branching repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: pBRC1wt::gBRC1 restores branching in brc1 brc2 mutants to WT levels, while pBRC1m::gBRC1 does not.
mechanism: BRC1 expression is regulated by SPL9/15 binding to its promoter; mutations in the SBP-binding site disrupt this regulation.

genes: JcMADS40 (JcMADS40, transcriptional activator, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcMADS40 reduces grain size, grain length, grain width, 1000-seed weight, and yield per plant in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: JcMADS40 functions as a transcriptional activator, reducing expression of positive regulators (GS2, SMG11) and increasing expression of negative regulators (OsMKP1, GW2) of grain size.

genes: TaOAT-5BL (ornithine aminotransferase, proline biosynthesis, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaOAT-5BL in transgenic wheat enhances drought and salt tolerance by increasing proline accumulation under stress conditions.
mechanism: TaOAT-5BL enhances drought and salt tolerance by increasing proline accumulation through proline biosynthesis and interacts with proline biosynthesis enzymes (TaP5CS, TaP5CR) and nitrogen metabolism gene (TaARG).

genes: AsHSP26.8a (AsHSP26.8a, chloroplast-localized sHSP gene from creeping bentgrass, Agrostis stolonifera L.)
phenotype: Overexpression of AsHSP26.8a in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to reduced tolerance to heat stress, hypersensitivity to ABA, and increased salinity susceptibility.
mechanism: AsHSP26.8a may negatively regulate plant response to abiotic stresses through modulating ABA and other stress signaling pathways.

genes: EsMYB90 (regulator for anthocyanin synthesis, Eutrema salsugineum)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of EsMYB90 in tobacco and Arabidopsis enhanced pigmentation and anthocyanin accumulation in various organs, with total anthocyanin contents increased up to 95.2-fold in young leaves and 48.8-fold in stems of transgenic tobacco plants compared to wild type.
mechanism: EsMYB90 promotes expression of anthocyanin biosynthesis genes including early biosynthesis genes (PAL, CHS, CHI) and late biosynthesis genes (DFR, ANS, UFGT), particularly functioning in the late biosynthesis genes.

genes: PpPPR_56 (wild-type, RNA editing factor, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: Overexpression of PpPPR_56 rescues RNA editing defects at nad3-C230 and nad4-C272 sites in PpPPR_56 knockout moss.
mechanism: PpPPR_56 functions as an RNA editing factor by positioning the DYW domain near the editing site to catalyze cytidine deamination.

genes: PpPPR_56 (variant with altered L motifs, RNA editing factor, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: The 56nad3L variant of PpPPR_56 fails to rescue RNA editing defects at nad3-C230 and nad4-C272 sites in PpPPR_56 knockout moss.
mechanism: Altered L motifs in PpPPR_56 disrupt correct positioning of the DYW domain for RNA editing, despite retaining RNA binding activity.

genes: PpPPR_78 (variant with altered L motifs, RNA editing factor, Physcomitrella patens)
phenotype: The 78-16L19L variant of PpPPR_78 shows reduced RNA editing efficiency at rps14-C137 and cox1-C755 sites in PpPPR_78 knockout moss.
mechanism: Altered C-terminal L motifs in PpPPR_78 disrupt correct positioning of the DYW domain for RNA editing, despite retaining RNA binding activity.

genes: SMAX1 (rice SMAX1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of smax1-1 mutant restored wild-type phenotype with significantly lower total colonisation relative to smax1-1.
mechanism: SMAX1 negatively regulates AM symbiosis.

genes: PbMC1a/1b (PbMC1a/1b, PCD-associated gene, Pyrus bretschneideri)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbMC1a/1b increases lignin deposition in transgenic Arabidopsis plants.
mechanism: PbMC1a/1b promotes lignin deposition and cell wall lignification by increasing the expression levels of lignin biosynthetic genes.

genes: AaCPS1 (β-caryophyllene synthase, Artemisia annua, Artemisia annua)
phenotype: Overexpression of AaCPS1 in N. benthamiana produces β-caryophyllene, achieving 27.5 mg/kg fresh weight in 6 h with maximum production at 9 days post-infiltration.
mechanism: AaCPS1 catalyzes the conversion of farnesyl diphosphate (FPP) to β-caryophyllene and α-humulene via conserved motifs (DDxxD, NSE/DTE) that bind Mg²⁺ ions for substrate complexing and catalysis.

genes: RhHB1 (RhHB1, transcription factor, Rosa hybrida)
phenotype: Silencing of RhHB1 decreases the dehydration tolerance of rose petals, with reduced recovery rate (47% vs 55%) and fresh weight after rehydration.
mechanism: RhHB1 silencing leads to increased JA biosynthesis gene expression (e.g., LOX, AOS, AOC) and elevated JA-Ile levels, which suppress osmotic stress response genes, reducing dehydration tolerance.

genes: RhLOX4 (RhLOX4, lipoxygenase, Rosa hybrida)
phenotype: Silencing of RhLOX4 increases JA-Ile levels during dehydration, leading to reduced dehydration tolerance in rose petals.
mechanism: RhLOX4 is a key gene in JA biosynthesis; its silencing elevates JA-Ile, which suppresses osmotic stress response genes, impairing dehydration recovery.

genes: HC (heavy chain, part of monoclonal antibody mAbPCO, synthetic), LC (light chain, part of monoclonal antibody mAbPCO, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of mAbPCO in Arabidopsis thaliana resulted in 0.52 relative expression level compared to mAbPCOK (2.42), with 750 μg of purified mAbPCO obtained from 300 g of fresh biomass.
mechanism: NA

genes: HC (heavy chain with ER retention motif, part of monoclonal antibody mAbPCOK, synthetic), LC (light chain, part of monoclonal antibody mAbPCOK, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of mAbPCOK in Arabidopsis thaliana resulted in 2.42 relative expression level (compared to 0.52 for mAbPCO), with 3,400 μg of purified mAbPCOK obtained from 300 g of fresh biomass. The ER retention motif (ERRM) added to the C-terminus of HC in pBI CO17-1AK enhanced accumulation in plant cells.
mechanism: ER retention motif (ERRM) at C-terminus of HC retained mAbPCOK in ER, enhancing accumulation in plant cells.

genes: SGN1 (AtSGN1, receptor-like cytoplasmic kinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of myrpalm SGN1 leads to ectopic lignin accumulation and precocious suberization in endodermal cells.
mechanism: Apolar SGN1 localization allows SGN3 to encounter SGN1 on the stele-facing side, leading to constitutive CIF1/2 signal transduction through SGN3 and ROS-dependent lignification.

genes: CASP1 (AtCASP1, Casparian strip membrane domain protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CASP1-GFP expression under CASP1 promoter visualizes Casparian strip domain connectivity and complements CIF1/2 double mutant phenotypes.
mechanism: CASP1-GFP expression under its native promoter allows visualization of Casparian strip domain formation and connectivity, which is disrupted in cif1/2 mutants but restored by CIF peptide treatment.

genes: MpBHLH12 (MpBHLH12, basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of MpBHLH12 reduces gemma cup size by ~4-fold and number by ~50% in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: MpBHLH12 suppresses gemma cup development through gene repression rather than activation, as shown by transient reporter assays in Arabidopsis protoplasts.

genes: MpBHLH12 (MpBHLH12, basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, Marchantia polymorpha)
phenotype: Overexpression of MpBHLH12 reduces gemma cup size by ~4-fold and number by ~50% in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: MpBHLH12 suppresses gemma cup development through gene repression rather than activation, as shown by transient reporter assays in Arabidopsis protoplasts.

genes: GaCASP27 (Ga08G0117, Casparian strip membrane domain protein, Gossypium arboreum)
phenotype: GUS staining in roots indicates GaCASP27 is primarily expressed in roots of Arabidopsis.
mechanism: GaCASP27 is a membrane protein localized in root tissues, suggesting its role in Casparian strip formation.

genes: GaCASP27 (Ga08G0117, Casparian strip membrane domain protein, Gossypium arboreum)
phenotype: GaCASP27-silenced plants exhibited a 2.3-fold increase in lateral root number compared to controls.
mechanism: GaCASP27 negatively regulates lateral root development by modulating Casparian strip formation.

genes: GaCASP27 (Ga08G0117, Casparian strip membrane domain protein, Gossypium arboreum)
phenotype: GaCASP27::GFP fusion protein co-localized with plasma membrane markers in tobacco leaves.
mechanism: GaCASP27 is a plasma membrane-localized protein, confirming its role in Casparian strip formation.

genes: MSH1 (RNAi, MSH1 suppression, synthetic)
phenotype: MSH1 disruption produces transgenerational memory with reduced growth rate, delayed flowering, and pale leaves in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Epigenomic modifications involving cytosine methylation changes in circadian rhythm, auxin response, and spliceosome pathways.

genes: GUS (uidA, reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Promoter-driven GUS activity is pronounced in vascular tissue of leaves and roots, with stronger expression in roots than shoots.
mechanism: The NCS1 promoter drives GUS expression in vascular tissues and roots, indicating tissue-specific regulation.

genes: gma-miR398c (gma-miR398c, microRNA, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of gma-miR398c in Arabidopsis thaliana L. resulted in decreased percentage germination, increased leaf water loss, and reduced survival under water deficiency, displaying sensitivity to drought during seed germination and seedling growth.
mechanism: gma-miR398c negatively regulates multiple peroxisome-related genes (GmCSD1a/b, GmCSD2a/b/c, and GmCCS), weakening the ability to scavenge O2.−.

genes: gma-miR398c (gma-miR398c, microRNA, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpressing gma-miR398c in soybean decreased GmCSD1a/b, GmCSD2a/b/c and GmCCS expression, which weakened the ability to scavenge O2.−, resulting in increased relative electrolyte leakage and stomatal opening compared with knockout miR398c and wild-type soybean under drought conditions.
mechanism: gma-miR398c negatively regulates multiple peroxisome-related genes (GmCSD1a/b, GmCSD2a/b/c, and GmCCS), weakening the ability to scavenge O2.−.

genes: Cry1IE (Cry1IE, insecticidal toxin, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Expression of Cry1IE in maize leaves for insect resistance
mechanism: Cry1IE protein binds to insect gut receptors causing cell lysis

genes: Cry1Ac (Cry1Ac, insecticidal toxin, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Expression of Cry1Ac in maize leaves for insect resistance
mechanism: Cry1Ac protein binds to insect gut receptors causing cell lysis

genes: VP60 (coat protein subunit, CPMV, source)
phenotype: Production of CPMV.p524opt virus particles with the p524opt peptide displayed on the surface, yielding 10 mg/kg leaf fresh weight.
mechanism: The p524opt peptide is displayed on the surface of CPMV particles without interfering with self-assembly.

genes: coat protein (TBSV, source)
phenotype: Production of TBSV.pLIP1 virus particles with the pLIP1 peptide displayed on the surface, yielding 72 mg/kg leaf fresh weight.
mechanism: The pLIP1 peptide is displayed on the surface of TBSV particles without interfering with self-assembly.

genes: coat protein (TBSV, source)
phenotype: Production of TBSV.pFADK2 virus particles with the pFADK2 peptide displayed on the surface, yielding 114 mg/kg leaf fresh weight.
mechanism: The pFADK2 peptide is displayed on the surface of TBSV particles without interfering with self-assembly.

genes: MdSUT4.1 (sucrose transporter, Malus x domestica)
phenotype: MdSUT4.1-YFP fusion protein localizes to the tonoplast in tobacco leaves
mechanism: MdSUT4.1 is a tonoplast-localized protein that may function in vacuolar sugar transport

genes: MdSUT4.1 (sucrose transporter, Malus x domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdSUT4.1 in strawberry and apple callus significantly reduces sucrose accumulation (35% decrease in strawberry, 1.77 mg/g FW increase in apple callus) and alters hexose content
mechanism: MdSUT4.1 functions to remobilize sugar out of the vacuole, reducing sucrose accumulation while increasing hexose efflux

genes: OsGRF1 (OsGRF1, miR396-resistant version, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR396-resistant OsGRF1 (mOsGRF1) results in expanded leaves due to increased cell proliferation in rice.
mechanism: mOsGRF1 promotes leaf growth by enhancing cell proliferation, likely through upregulation of cell-cycle-related genes cycOs1 and cycOs2.

genes: OsGRF1 (OsGRF1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockdown of OsGRF1 by RNAi displays a phenotype of shrunken leaves in rice.
mechanism: OsGRF1 knockdown inhibits leaf growth by reducing cell proliferation, likely through downregulation of cell-cycle-related genes cycOs1 and cycOs2.

genes: OsGIF1 (OsGIF1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsGIF1 does not exhibit new phenotype in rice.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsGIF1 (OsGIF1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockdown of OsGIF1 exhibits pleiotropic growth defects including shrunken leaves in rice.
mechanism: OsGIF1 knockdown inhibits leaf growth and other developmental processes, likely through downregulation of cell-cycle-related genes cycOs1 and cycOs2.

genes: GmHAK1 (Glycine max HAK1, receptor-like kinase involved in defense response to Spodoptera litura OS, Glycine max), GmHAK2 (Glycine max HAK2, receptor-like kinase involved in defense response to Spodoptera litura OS, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmHAK1 and GmHAK2 in Arabidopsis thaliana increases PDF1.2 transcript levels in response to Spodoptera litura oral secretions (OS) and mechanical damage, enhancing defense responses.
mechanism: GmHAK1 and GmHAK2 recognize Spodoptera litura OS elicitors, triggering jasmonate and ethylene signaling pathways to activate defense genes like PDF1.2.

genes: GmHAK1 (Glycine max HAK1, receptor-like kinase involved in defense response to Spodoptera litura OS, Glycine max), GmHAK2 (Glycine max HAK2, receptor-like kinase involved in defense response to Spodoptera litura OS, Glycine max)
phenotype: Expression of GmHAK1-GFP and GmHAK2-GFP in Arabidopsis thaliana localizes to the plasma membrane, confirming their subcellular localization.
mechanism: GFP fusion proteins retain plasma membrane localization, indicating functional integration of GmHAK1 and GmHAK2 into the membrane for elicitor perception.

genes: AtNBR1 (AtNBR1, NBR1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtNBR1 changes gene expression profiles in shoots and roots, including altered ABA signaling, delayed seed germination, reduced stomatal aperture, and enhanced lateral root initiation in knockout lines.
mechanism: AtNBR1 interacts with ABA signaling components ABI3, ABI4, and ABI5, modulating ABA sensitivity and autophagy pathways.

genes: AtNBR1 (AtNBR1, NBR1, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtNBR1 reduces stomatal aperture and enhances ABA sensitivity, with YFP localization in guard cells indicating involvement in stomatal movement.
mechanism: AtNBR1 is involved in ABA signaling and stomatal movement, potentially through interactions with ABI3, ABI4, and ABI5.

phenotype: Expression of S1 in maize seed at >20 µg/g seed
mechanism: Expression of PEDV S1 in maize to produce a subunit vaccine

genes: TPPI (Arabidopsis thaliana, peroxisomal targeting domain, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of TPPI fused to EYFP targets peroxisomes, nucleus, and nucleolus in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts and onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: TPPI contains a novel PTS1 (PRM>) at its C-terminus, enabling peroxisomal targeting. The N-terminal fusion also targets plastids, suggesting dual localization.

genes: TPPI (Arabidopsis thaliana, peroxisomal targeting domain, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of EYFP-TPPI targets peroxisomes, nucleus, and nucleolus in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts and onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: TPPI contains a novel PTS1 (PRM>) at its C-terminus, enabling peroxisomal targeting. The C-terminal fusion also targets plastids, suggesting dual localization.

genes: TPPI (Arabidopsis thaliana, peroxisomal targeting domain, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of EYFP fused to the C-terminal 10 residues of TPPI (PRM>) targets peroxisomes in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts and onion epidermal cells.
mechanism: The PRM> tripeptide at the C-terminus of TPPI functions as a novel PTS1, directing peroxisomal targeting of the fusion protein.

genes: TPPI (Arabidopsis thaliana, full-length, synthetic)
phenotype: Complementation of the tppi mutant with 35S-TPPI rescues the late-flowering phenotype but not the salt-stress hypersensitivity.
mechanism: TPPI overexpression restores normal flowering time in the tppi mutant, indicating its role in flowering regulation. However, it does not rescue salt-stress hypersensitivity, suggesting other factors are involved.

genes: PDS (PHYTOENE DESATURASE, gene involved in carotenoid biosynthesis, Solanum tuberosum L.)
phenotype: PDS mutants appear in regenerating population with 2–10% frequency; includes albino plants, chimeras with white/green leaf areas, and green plants with small deletions/substitutions (1–117 bp). Vegetative propagation maintains stable phenotype despite Cas9 presence.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9 system cleaves PDS gene at target site, generating deletions and substitutions. Transient expression with 3-day selection yields small mutations; stable integration causes large deletions. DNA repair mechanisms active during vegetative growth.

genes: ZmPMT (monolignol transferase, Zea mays), BdPMT (monolignol transferase, Brachypodium distachyon)
phenotype: RNAi suppression of ZmPMT reduces lignin-bound pCA by ~50% in Zea mays
mechanism: ZmPMT catalyzes p-coumaroyl transfer to lignin monomers; RNAi suppression lowers lignin-bound pCA

genes: ZmPMT (monolignol transferase, Zea mays), BdPMT (monolignol transferase, Brachypodium distachyon)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmPMT increases lignin-bound pCA by ~50% in Zea mays
mechanism: ZmPMT catalyzes p-coumaroyl transfer to lignin monomers; overexpression raises lignin-bound pCA

genes: AtNDT2 (NAD+ mitochondrial transporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Reduced NDT2 expression leads to lower silique number, fewer seeds per silique, and reduced total seed production in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: Upregulation of NAD+ biosynthesis genes (AtNDT1, AtPXN, AO, QS, QPRT, NaMNAT, NADS, NIC1, NaPRT) to compensate for reduced NAD+ import into mitochondria.

genes: DgF3'5'H (DgF3'5'H, flavonoid-3′,5′-hydroxylase, Delphinium grandiflorum), PeMYB2 (PeMYB2, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Phalaenopsis equestris)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of DgF3'5'H and PeMYB2 in a white Phalaenopsis cultivar resulted in 53.6% delphinidin accumulation and a novel blue color formation.
mechanism: DgF3'5'H catalyzes the 3′,5′-hydroxylation of dihydroflavonols to produce delphinidin, while PeMYB2 activates downstream structural genes (PeF3H, PeDFR, PeANS) to enhance anthocyanin biosynthesis. The higher vacuolar pH and increased Al3+, Ca2+, and Fe3+ molar ratios to anthocyanin in violet-blue Phalaenopsis contribute to blue coloration.

genes: PhF3'5'H (PhF3'5'H, flavonoid-3′,5′-hydroxylase, Phalaenopsis hybrid), PeMYB2 (PeMYB2, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Phalaenopsis equestris)
phenotype: Overexpression of PhF3'5'H and PeMYB2 resulted in 1.6% delphinidin accumulation and 98.4% cyanidin accumulation with a red-purple color, indicating PhF3'5'H has no enzyme activity for delphinidin production.
mechanism: PhF3'5'H lacks functional 3′,5′-hydroxylation activity due to amino acid substitutions in the substrate recognition site 6 (SRS6), leading to incorrect substrate binding orientation. PeMYB2 activates downstream genes but cannot compensate for the inactive PhF3'5'H.

genes: LTBentero (synthetic multiepitopic gene, designed from epitopes of ETEC ST, S. typhimurium FliC, V. parahaemolyticus LptD, and E. coli LTB, with signal peptide from Glycine max and ER retention signal), LTB (B subunit of E. coli heat-labile enterotoxin, carrier protein), ST (ST antigen from ETEC), FliC (FliC flagellin from S. typhimurium), LptD (LptD outer membrane protein from V. parahaemolyticus)
phenotype: Expression of LTBentero in tobacco leaves at 0.07-5.29 µg g⁻¹ fresh weight, inducing IgG and IgA antibodies against LTB, ST, and LptD epitopes in mice via oral and subcutaneous immunization
mechanism: LTB serves as an immunogenic carrier enhancing mucosal uptake and adaptive immune responses; epitopes from ST, FliC, and LptD are presented for immune recognition

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, Aequorea victoria), DsRed (red fluorescent protein, Discosoma sp.)
phenotype: Expression of GFP in BY-2 cells results in green fluorescence detectable under UV light
mechanism: 35S promoter drives constitutive expression of GFP in plant cells

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, Aequorea victoria), P19 (RNA silencing suppressor, Tobacco mosaic virus), DsRed (red fluorescent protein, Discosoma sp.)
phenotype: Co-expression of GFP and P19 in BY-2 cells results in enhanced green fluorescence compared to GFP alone
mechanism: P19 suppresses RNA silencing, allowing higher levels of GFP expression

genes: DsRed (red fluorescent protein, Discosoma sp.), P19 (RNA silencing suppressor, Tobacco mosaic virus)
phenotype: Co-expression of DsRed and P19 in BY-2 cells results in red fluorescence without significant enhancement compared to DsRed alone
mechanism: P19 does not significantly affect DsRed expression in this system

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, Aequorea victoria), DsRed (red fluorescent protein, Discosoma sp.)
phenotype: Co-expression of GFP and DsRed in BY-2 cells results in both green and red fluorescence with position-dependent expression levels
mechanism: Position of expression cassettes within the vector affects protein expression levels

genes: DsRed (red fluorescent protein, Discosoma sp.), GFP (green fluorescent protein, Aequorea victoria)
phenotype: Co-expression of DsRed and GFP in BY-2 cells results in both red and green fluorescence with position-dependent expression levels
mechanism: Position of expression cassettes within the vector affects protein expression levels

genes: GhRAF4 (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase, Gossypium hirsutum), GhMEKK12 (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Silencing of GhRAF4 and GhMEKK12 in cotton results in decreased drought tolerance, with higher malondialdehyde (MDA) content, lower proline accumulation, reduced relative leaf water content, and decreased activities of superoxide dismutase (SOD) and peroxidase (POD) under drought stress.
mechanism: Impaired reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging and osmotic adjustment due to reduced SOD/POD activity and proline accumulation, leading to increased membrane lipid peroxidation (evidenced by higher MDA) and wider stomatal aperture under drought stress.

genes: CmWIP1 (Cucumis melo, coding sequence)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmWIP1 in Arabidopsis thaliana results in serrated leaves, smaller rosettes, dwarf plants, defective floral organs, and reduced plant fertility.
mechanism: CmWIP1 shares conserved protein structure and function with Arabidopsis TT1 and NTT, leading to growth inhibition and cell death.

genes: CmWIP1 (Cucumis melo, coding sequence)

genes: TT1 (Arabidopsis thaliana, coding sequence-GFP), NTT (Arabidopsis thaliana, coding sequence-GFP)

genes: AtΔKinase (ERECTA gene truncated in the kinase domain, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic soybean plants exhibit reduced leaf number and area, increased branching, and enhanced drought and salt tolerance compared to wild-type. Seed yield is increased under water deficit stress.
mechanism: Expression of AtΔKinase suppresses ERECTA signaling, leading to morphological changes (reduced leaf area) and altered stress responses (reduced transpiration, increased root biomass under drought).

genes: GhMYB1a (GhMYB1a, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Gerbera hybrida)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhMYB1a in tobacco and Gerbera suppresses anthocyanin accumulation in petals.
mechanism: GhMYB1a activates the promoters of flavonol pathway genes, leading to increased flavonol accumulation and reduced anthocyanin.

genes: GhMYB1a (GFP::GhMYB1a, R2R3-MYB transcription factor fused to GFP, Gerbera hybrida)
phenotype: GFP-GhMYB1a localizes to the nucleus in tobacco leaves.
mechanism: NA

genes: MsTMT (MsTMT, γ-tocopherol methyltransferase, Medicago sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of MsTMT increases α-tocopherol and total tocopherol levels by ~36-31% in transgenic alfalfa, enhances drought tolerance with reduced stomatal density (36.6-22.6% decrease), lower transpiration rate, and higher water use efficiency (WUE) by ~17-28%.
mechanism: MsTMT suppresses MsSPCH gene expression, inhibiting stomatal development. Increased tocopherol content enhances ROS scavenging, and involves ABA-dependent and ABA-independent pathways in drought response.

genes: JcSPL3 (JcSPL3, floral activator, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcSPL3 in Arabidopsis resulted in earlier flowering time, shorter silique length and reduced biomass of roots.
mechanism: NA

genes: CiFT (FLOWERING LOCUS T, citrus, synthetic)
phenotype: Precocious flowering and fertile pollen in transgenic trifoliate orange, enabling one breeding generation per year instead of 5 years
mechanism: CiFT overexpression induces flowering by mimicking the natural flowering pathway, bypassing the long juvenile phase in woody perennials

mechanism: Increased photoactivated phototropin influences the transitional light intensity between accumulation and avoidance responses.

phenotype: Complementation of the MpphotKO line with Mpphot-Citrine restores the cold-avoidance response in Marchantia polymorpha.
mechanism: Increased photoactivated phototropin influences the transitional light intensity between accumulation and avoidance responses.

genes: Citrine (synthetic gene for yellow fluorescent protein, synthetic)

mechanism: NA

genes: HFR1 (HFR1, Arabidopsis thaliana, native)
phenotype: Stabilization of HFR1 under UV-B, leading to suppression of shade marker genes.
mechanism: UVR8-dependent stabilization of HFR1 through COP1 inhibition.

genes: PIF4 (PIF4, Arabidopsis thaliana, native)
phenotype: UV-B-induced degradation of PIF4 under low R:FR, leading to reduced hypocotyl elongation.
mechanism: UVR8-mediated degradation of PIF4 through COP1 inhibition.

genes: PIF5 (PIF5, Arabidopsis thaliana, native)
phenotype: UV-B-induced degradation of PIF5 under low R:FR, leading to reduced hypocotyl elongation.
mechanism: UVR8-mediated degradation of PIF5 through COP1 inhibition.

genes: sgRNA (targeting S653 codon of ALS gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Herbicide resistance in Arabidopsis thaliana due to S653N mutation in ALS gene
mechanism: The S653N mutation in ALS gene confers resistance to imidazolinone herbicides by altering the herbicide binding site

genes: TCD3 (TCD3, chloroplast development gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of TCD3 rescues the yellowish white leaf phenotype of tcd3 mutant at 20°C, restoring green coloration and chloroplast development.
mechanism: TCD3 encodes a pseudouridine synthase required for chloroplast development under cold stress. Overexpression restores normal chloroplast structure and photosynthetic pigment biosynthesis at low temperatures.

genes: TCD3 (TCD3, chloroplast development gene, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of TCD3 in wild-type plants recapitulates the tcd3 mutant phenotype at 20°C, with yellowish white leaves and defective chloroplast development.
mechanism: TCD3 is essential for chloroplast rRNA processing and tRNA metabolism under cold stress. Disruption of TCD3 leads to impaired chloroplast development and photosynthetic gene expression at low temperatures.

genes: egfp (enhanced green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of EGFP leads to fluorescence in Arabidopsis thaliana protoplasts
mechanism: Integrase-mediated flipping of the egfp gene from reverse to forward orientation

genes: ARK1 (secondary growth-related transcription factor, Populus tremula × Populus alba)
phenotype: ARK1 overexpression causes slender stem segments, multi-branched growth, slender leaves, and reduced leaf development in hybrid poplar '717' with significant differences in internode distance (11.86 mm vs 6.19 mm), stem diameter (0.72 mm vs 1.29 mm), and seedling height (76.27 cm vs 48.53 cm) compared to non-transgenic plants
mechanism: ARK1 regulates cambium cell differentiation and meristem activity, with down-regulation of lignin synthesis enzymes in phenylpropanoid pathway and up-regulation of plant hormone signal transduction genes including cyclin-D3-1, PYR1 abscisic acid receptor, and indole-3-acetic amide synthetases

genes: ChPUM2 (ChPUM2, nucleolar Pumilio protein, Chara corallina)
phenotype: Complementation of apum23 mutant phenotypes (normal germination, root growth, inflorescence stem length, leaf color, and streptomycin susceptibility) and rescue of pre-rRNA processing defects.
mechanism: ChPUM2 binds to the same target RNA sequence as APUM23 (5′-GGAAUUGACGG in 18S rRNA) and shares structural similarity with APUM23, enabling functional replacement in pre-rRNA processing.

genes: ChPUM3 (ChPUM3, nucleolar Pumilio protein, Chara corallina)
phenotype: Failure to rescue apum23 and apum24 mutant phenotypes (maintained apum23–2 mutant phenotype and did not restore apum24–1+/− seed development or pre-rRNA processing).
mechanism: ChPUM3 has structural differences from APUM24 (longer random coil in C-R5 domain, distinct amino acids in N-terminal Puf domains) and cannot bind to Arabidopsis pre-rRNA due to shorter ITS2 sequence in Arabidopsis compared to Chara corallina.

genes: NtFAD2-2a (NtFAD2-2a, Δ12 oleate desaturase, Nicotiana tabacum), NtFAD2-2b (NtFAD2-2b, Δ12 oleate desaturase, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Knockout of NtFAD2–2a and NtFAD2–2b increases oleic acid content from 11% to over 79% in tobacco seeds, while linoleic acid decreases from 72% to 7%
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of NtFAD2–2a and NtFAD2–2b prevents linoleic acid production by disrupting Δ12 desaturation of oleic acid

genes: AsWRI1 (Avena sativa endosperm WRI1 homolog, oat endosperm WRI1, Avena sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of AsWRI1 in wheat endosperm results in reduced seed weight (29% reduction in line with 12 inserts), wrinkled seed phenotype, increased triacylglycerol (TAG) content in endosperm (up to 6.4% by dry weight vs 0.7% in controls), reduced starch content (from 62% to 22% by dry weight), increased sucrose content (from 1.5% to 10% by dry weight), and multiple layers of elongated peripheral aleurone cells.
mechanism: AsWRI1 induces oil accumulation by diverting carbon allocation from starch biosynthesis to fatty acid synthesis and TAG assembly, with increased expression of genes involved in glycolysis and fatty acid synthesis while down-regulating starch synthesis genes. Transcriptomic data shows up-regulation of genes in cytosolic glycolysis and de novo fatty acid synthesis, and down-regulation of starch synthesis genes.

genes: OsNIP2;1 (Lsi1, silicon transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of Lsi1 (OsNIP2;1) in Dular rice enhances chilling tolerance, maintains green leaf color under 4°C treatment, and increases silica body size in leaves.
mechanism: OsNIP2;1 interacts with ATP synthase subunit β and functions in reducing reactive oxygen species (ROS), with ATP-synβ acting as an intermediate junction between OsNIP2;1 and OsSHMT.

genes: OsSHMT (LOC_Os03g52840, serine hydroxymethyltransferase, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSHMT in Arabidopsis thaliana reduces H2O2 content under chilling treatment compared to non-transgenic lines.
mechanism: OsSHMT interacts with ATP synthase subunit β, heat shock protein Hsp70, mitochondrial substrate carrier family protein, ascorbate peroxidase 1, and ATP synthase subunit α to scavenge H2O2 and enhance chilling tolerance.

genes: AtGLYI2 (AtGLYI2, glyoxalase I, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtGLYI2 increases salinity stress tolerance, maintaining lower methylglyoxal (MG) levels and producing more siliques under 150 mM and 300 mM NaCl stress.
mechanism: AtGLYI2 detoxifies methylglyoxal (MG) more effectively than AtGLYI3 and AtGLYI6, reducing MG accumulation and enhancing stress tolerance.

genes: AtGLYI3 (AtGLYI3, glyoxalase I, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtGLYI3 improves salinity stress tolerance, maintaining siliques under 150 mM and 300 mM NaCl stress, though less effectively than AtGLYI2.
mechanism: AtGLYI3 contributes to MG detoxification, but with lower enzymatic activity compared to AtGLYI2, resulting in moderate stress tolerance.

genes: AtGLYI6 (AtGLYI6, glyoxalase I, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtGLYI6 enhances salinity stress tolerance, maintaining siliques under 150 mM and 300 mM NaCl stress, though less effectively than AtGLYI2.
mechanism: AtGLYI6 contributes to MG detoxification, but with lower enzymatic activity compared to AtGLYI2, resulting in moderate stress tolerance.

genes: GSA1 (grain size QTL, Oryza sativa japonica)
phenotype: Overexpression of GSA1WYJ increases 1000-grain weight by +12.06%, grain length by +4.41%, and grain width by +5.27% in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: GSA1 is a UDP-glucosyltransferase that modulates flavonoid and monolignol glycosylation, affecting auxin levels and cell proliferation/expansion during spikelet development.

genes: GSA1 (grain size QTL, Oryza sativa japonica)
phenotype: Knockout of GSA1WYJ results in smaller grains compared with WYJ (Supplementary Fig. 7b–j and Supplementary Table 2).
mechanism: GSA1 knockout disrupts flavonoid and monolignol glycosylation, leading to reduced auxin levels and impaired cell proliferation/expansion.

genes: GSA1 (grain size QTL, Oryza glaberrima)
phenotype: Overexpression of GSA1CG14 in the WYJ background results in smaller grains compared with WYJ (Supplementary Fig. 7b–j and Supplementary Table 2).
mechanism: GSA1CG14 is a weakly functioning allele with reduced glucosyltransferase activity, leading to impaired flavonoid and monolignol glycosylation and disrupted auxin signaling.

genes: GSA1 (grain size QTL, Oryza sativa japonica)
phenotype: Complementation of NIL-GSA1CG14 with full-length GSA1 transgene restores 1000-grain weight, grain length, and grain width to NIL-GSA1WYJ levels (Supplementary Fig. 7k–n).
mechanism: Complementation restores normal GSA1 function, including flavonoid and monolignol glycosylation, auxin signaling, and cell proliferation/expansion.

genes: TEK (tapetum-specific transcription factor, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Premature expression of TEK-GFP in tapetal nuclei leads to male sterility, microspore degeneration, and defective pollen wall morphology in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: TEK-GFP represses CalS5 expression via H3K9me2 histone modification, disrupting callose synthesis and exine patterning during pollen development.

mechanism: TEK-GFP localization in tapetal nuclei during pollen development, but no direct link to male sterility or exine defects.

genes: calB (coniferaldehyde dehydrogenase, Pseudomonas sp. HR199), F6H1 (feruloyl-CoA 6′-hydroxylase, Arabidopsis thaliana), couA (hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA hydratase/lyase, Rhodopseudomonas palustris), F5H (ferulate 5-hydroxylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic plants exhibit altered lignin monomeric composition with increased S units and improved sugar release from cell walls after alkaline pretreatment.
mechanism: Enzymatic activity of calB, couA, and F5H alters lignin structure by modifying monolignol biosynthesis pathways, leading to structural changes in lignin that enhance saccharification efficiency.

genes: calB (coniferaldehyde dehydrogenase, Pseudomonas sp. HR199)
phenotype: CalB overexpression leads to altered lignin composition with reduced G units and increased S units, resulting in a 21% improvement in glucose release after alkaline pretreatment.
mechanism: CalB oxidizes coniferaldehyde and sinapaldehyde to their corresponding hydroxycinnamic acids, altering lignin structure and enhancing saccharification efficiency.

genes: F6H1 (feruloyl-CoA 6′-hydroxylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: F6H1 overexpression results in lignin enriched with S units and production of scopoletin, but does not significantly improve lignin recalcitrance.
mechanism: F6H1 converts feruloyl-CoA to 6′-hydroxyferuloyl-CoA, which is non-enzymatically converted to scopoletin, altering lignin structure without reducing recalcitrance.

genes: couA (hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA hydratase/lyase, Rhodopseudomonas palustris)
phenotype: CouA overexpression causes irregular xylem (irx) phenotype with collapsed vessels and a 55% improvement in glucose release after alkaline pretreatment.
mechanism: CouA converts hydroxycinnamoyl-CoAs to hydroxybenzaldehydes, reducing lignin monomer yield and increasing vinylic pyrolysis products, which enhances saccharification efficiency.

genes: F5H (ferulate 5-hydroxylase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: F5H overexpression increases S unit proportion in lignin by 31% and improves glucose release after alkaline pretreatment without affecting plant growth.
mechanism: F5H catalyzes 5-hydroxylation of ferulic acid, leading to S-enriched lignin with reduced molecular weight and enhanced saccharification efficiency.

genes: AchnFAR (AchnFAR, fatty acyl reductase, Actinidia chinensis)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of AchnFAR in tobacco leaves significantly increased C18–C24 primary alcohols (4.1–4.6-fold for C20–C24 and 3.8-fold for C18) compared to controls.
mechanism: AchnFAR encodes a fatty acyl reductase involved in suberin primary alcohol biosynthesis, generating substrates for suberin cross-linking.

genes: AchnMYB41 (AchnMYB41, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Actinidia chinensis)

mechanism: AchnMYB41 binds to MYBREs in the AchnFAR promoter, activating gene expression and suberin biosynthesis pathways.

genes: AchnMYB107 (AchnMYB107, R2R3-MYB transcription factor, Actinidia chinensis)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of AchnMYB107 in tobacco leaves increased AchnFAR promoter activity by 2.6-fold and elevated primary alcohols by 2.7-fold.
mechanism: AchnMYB107 binds to MYBREs in the AchnFAR promoter, activating gene expression and suberin biosynthesis pathways.

mechanism: AchnMYC2 binds to MYCREs (CACATG) in the AchnFAR promoter, activating gene expression and suberin biosynthesis pathways.

mechanism: HtMYB2 acts as a MYB transcription factor that upregulates anthocyanin synthesis-related structural genes in tobacco.

genes: sp-Xeg (xyloglucanase, Penicillium canescens)

mechanism: Xyloglucanase cleaves xyloglucan in cell walls, altering hemicellulose composition (reduced xylose, increased glucose) and promoting cellulose biosynthesis through microfibril separation and increased intracellular pressure.

genes: SDC (promoter), GFP (green fluorescent protein), source: synthetic
phenotype: Expression of SDC:GFP is silenced in wild-type plants but upregulated in morc1 mutants. In ddc mutants, SDC:GFP is strongly activated regardless of MED12/13 status.

genes: MED12 (gene), MED13 (gene)

genes: MED12 (gene)

mechanism: MED12 interacts with histone acetyltransferases and is required for light-induced gene expression. It binds to genes with high H3K4me3 and low H3K27me3, facilitating transcriptional activation.

genes: LOC_Os06g35900 (BZR3, BES1/BZR1 homolog protein, putative, expressed, Oryza sativa), LOC_Os06g35970 (NRFG2, meiosis 5, putative, expressed, Oryza sativa), LOC_Os06g36010 (NRFG3, plastocyanin-like domain containing protein, putative, expressed, Oryza sativa), LOC_Os06g40020 (NRFG4, DEAD-box ATP-dependent RNA helicase 52A, putative, expressed, Oryza sativa), LOC_Os11g16590 (CLPC3, ATP-dependent Clp protease ATP-binding subunit clpA homolog CD4B, chloroplast precursor, putative, expressed, Oryza sativa), LOC_Os11g35090 (KIN7L, kinesin motor domain containing protein, putative, expressed, Oryza sativa), LOC_Os06g36080 (KIN14M, kinesin motor domain containing protein, expressed, Oryza sativa), LOC_Os06g34420 (NRFG5, DEAD/DEAH box helicase domain protein, putative, expressed, Oryza sativa), LOC_Os06g40030 (NRFG6, S-locus-like receptor protein kinase, putative, expressed, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout mutants showed an average 25.63% decrease in seed setting (SS) and 4.88 g decrease in yield per plant (YPP). Specific genes like KIN7L and BZR3 exhibited significant reductions (e.g., 44.65% SS decrease and 8.81 g YPP decrease for KIN7L).
