phenotype: Overexpression of MdWRKY11 in transgenic apple plants confers enhanced Cu tolerance, with reduced Cu accumulation in roots and leaves compared to controls.
mechanism: MdWRKY11 binds to the promoter of MdHMA5 (a Cu-transporting P1B-type ATPase gene) and activates its transcription, increasing Cu transmembrane transport in root cells to reduce cytoplasmic Cu levels.

genes: MdWRKY11 (WRKY transcription factor, involved in Cu resistance, Malus x domestica)
phenotype: MdWRKY11-GFP is localized exclusively to the nucleus of N. benthamiana cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: MdWRKY11 (WRKY transcription factor, involved in Cu resistance, Malus x domestica)
phenotype: Knockdown of MdWRKY11 in transgenic apple calli results in decreased Cu tolerance and increased Cu accumulation compared to controls.
mechanism: Reduced MdWRKY11 expression leads to decreased activation of MdHMA5, impairing Cu transmembrane transport and increasing cytoplasmic Cu levels.

genes: MdHMA5 (Cu-transporting P1B-type ATPase, involved in Cu detoxification, Malus x domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdHMA5 in transgenic apple calli confers increased Cu tolerance and reduced Cu accumulation compared to controls.
mechanism: MdHMA5 promotes transmembrane Cu transport, reducing cytoplasmic Cu levels and enhancing Cu detoxification.

genes: MdHMA5 (Cu-transporting P1B-type ATPase, involved in Cu detoxification, Malus x domestica)
phenotype: Knockdown of MdHMA5 in transgenic apple calli results in decreased Cu tolerance and increased Cu accumulation compared to controls.
mechanism: Reduced MdHMA5 expression impairs Cu transmembrane transport, leading to elevated cytoplasmic Cu levels and reduced detoxification.

genes: MdHMA5 (Cu-transporting P1B-type ATPase, involved in Cu detoxification, Malus x domestica)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of MdWRKY11 in apple calli increases GUS activity driven by the MdHMA5 promoter, indicating activation of MdHMA5 transcription.
mechanism: MdWRKY11 binds to the W-box in the MdHMA5 promoter and activates its transcription.

genes: CmWRKY53 (CmWRKY53, WRKY transcription factor, Chrysanthemum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CmWRKY53 increases aphid susceptibility in chrysanthemum, with aphid multiplication rates (MR) of 34.06 and 33.48 compared to 28.92 in wild-type plants.
mechanism: CmWRKY53 negatively regulates aphid resistance by altering secondary metabolism, including reduced expression of peroxidase and polyphenol oxidase genes involved in plant defense.

genes: CmWRKY53 (CmWRKY53, WRKY transcription factor, Chrysanthemum)
phenotype: CmWRKY53-SRDX transgenic plants show reduced aphid susceptibility, with aphid multiplication rates (MR) of 20.86 and 22.34 compared to 28.92 in wild-type plants.
mechanism: CmWRKY53-SRDX acts as a dominant repressor, increasing secondary metabolite biosynthesis genes (e.g., polyphenol oxidase and peroxidase) to enhance aphid resistance.

genes: MdMYB88 (transcription factor, R2R3-MYB, Malus × domestica), MdMYB124 (transcription factor, R2R3-MYB, Malus × domestica)
phenotype: Knockdown of MdMYB88 and MdMYB124 leads to decreased phenylalanine content and downregulation of secondary metabolites in apple roots under drought and control conditions.
mechanism: MdMYB88 and MdMYB124 regulate phenylpropanoid and flavonoid biosynthesis pathways by targeting MdCM2 and other MdCMs, leading to reduced phenylalanine biosynthesis.

genes: MdMYB88 (transcription factor, R2R3-MYB, Malus × domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdMYB88 increases phenylalanine content and upregulates secondary metabolites in apple roots and leaves, enhancing resistance to oxidative stress and fungal infection.
mechanism: Overexpression of MdMYB88 upregulates MdCM2 and other MdCMs, enhancing phenylalanine biosynthesis, leading to increased downstream metabolites involved in oxidative stress and pathogen resistance.

genes: MdMYB124 (transcription factor, R2R3-MYB, Malus × domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdMYB124 increases phenylalanine content and upregulates secondary metabolites in apple roots and leaves, enhancing resistance to oxidative stress and fungal infection.
mechanism: Overexpression of MdMYB124 upregulates MdCM2 and other MdCMs, enhancing phenylalanine biosynthesis, leading to increased downstream metabolites involved in oxidative stress and pathogen resistance.

genes: CsMYB60 (CsMYB60, key regulator of flavonol and PA biosynthesis, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsMYB60 increases accumulation of flavonols and PAs in different tissues, especially in spines of cucumber
mechanism: CsMYB60 directly activates CsFLS and CsLAR promoters and indirectly regulates Cs4CL and CsCHS through interacting proteins

genes: CrBKT (Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, β-carotene ketolase, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii)
phenotype: Overexpression of CrBKT leads to canthaxanthin production and pale green phenotype in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii under heterotrophic conditions.
mechanism: CrBKT converts β-carotene to canthaxanthin; spatial separation of enzyme and substrate explains absence of astaxanthin.

genes: TaMIPS-B (myo-inositol-1-phosphate synthase, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaMIPS-B in rice increases thermotolerance, as evidenced by higher myo-inositol levels, improved membrane stability index (MSI), lower MDA levels, and faster recovery of photosynthetic efficiency (Fv/Fm) under heat stress.
mechanism: TaMIPS-B overexpression leads to increased myo-inositol accumulation, which enhances membrane stability and reduces lipid peroxidation. It also activates defense pathways including ethylene/jasmonate (ET/JA) signaling, upregulating genes like chitinase3, WRKY6, and ERF1B.

genes: PhCS (PhCS, chorismate synthase, Petunia axillaris)
phenotype: PhCS-GFP is localized in chloroplasts and peroxisomes in petunia protoplasts.
mechanism: GFP fusion allows visualization of PhCS localization.

genes: PhCS (PhCS, chorismate synthase, Petunia axillaris)
phenotype: PhCS silencing leads to dwarf phenotype, leaf curling, reduced chlorophyll and carotenoid levels, and abnormal flower development in petunia.
mechanism: VIGS-mediated suppression of PhCS expression.

genes: uidA (GUS, β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: GUS expression detected in root laticiferous tissues (secondary xylem and phloem) and latex of transgenic T. kok-saghyz plants
mechanism: HbPEP16 promoter drives tissue-specific expression in laticiferous tissues under normal growth conditions

genes: QS (quinolinate synthase, AT5G50210, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the qs-2 mutant with QSpro:QS-3×FLAG fully restores chilling tolerance to wild-type levels.
mechanism: QS encodes quinolinate synthase, a critical enzyme in NAD biosynthesis. Complementation restores NAD levels, which are reduced in the qs-2 mutant, thereby rescuing chilling hypersensitivity.

genes: QS (quinolinate synthase, AT5G50210, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: QS-YFP fusion protein localizes to chloroplasts in transgenic Arabidopsis plants.
mechanism: The QS-YFP fusion protein retains chloroplast targeting signals, confirming that the Q288E substitution in the qs-2 mutant does not affect chloroplast localization.

genes: QS (quinolinate synthase, AT5G50210, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: qs-2-YFP fusion protein localizes to chloroplasts in transgenic Arabidopsis plants.
mechanism: The Q288E substitution in the qs-2 mutant does not disrupt chloroplast targeting signals of QS, as the mutated QS protein retains chloroplast localization.

genes: LcMYB4 (LcMYB4, cold-responsive MYB transcription factor, sheepgrass)
phenotype: Overexpression of LcMYB4 increases chilling and freezing tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, as evidenced by increased germination rate (64.3-69.1% vs 30.1% in WT under 4 °C), survival rate (92-96% vs 60% after -8 °C treatment), and seed setting rate under cold stress. Transgenic plants show increased soluble sugar content, chlorophyll content, and SOD activity but decreased MDA under chilling stress.
mechanism: LcMYB4 overexpression increases soluble sugar content and cold-inducible gene expression (CBF1, KIN1, KIN2, RCI2A), alleviates oxidative damage and membrane damage, and interacts with LcFBA1 protein to regulate cold stress response.

genes: Rfg1 (resistance to nodulation gene, Glycine max (L.) Merr., synthetic)
phenotype: Knockout of Rfg1 allows nodulation in Williams 82 by Sinorhizobium fredii USDA193.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of Rfg1 removes nodulation restriction in soybean.

genes: GUSPlus (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, synthetic), YAO (promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana, genomic DNA)
phenotype: Expression of GUSPlus driven by YAO promoter in soybean roots, with high activity in root tips.
mechanism: YAO promoter activity is conserved in soybean roots, driving GUSPlus expression.

genes: OsSWEET14 (sugar transporter, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Disruption of OsSWEET14 in rice cv. Zhonghua 11 (CR-S14) increases plant height by ~8% without reducing yield.
mechanism: OsSWEET14 disruption likely reduces sugar transportation efficiency in the stem, leading to increased plant height.

genes: GhCenH3 (centromere histone H3, cotton, native)
phenotype: RNAi-mediated suppression of GhCenH3 reduces native transcript by >80%, causes defective microspore production, anther dehiscence defects, and pollen abnormalities in cotton
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing disrupts CenH3 function during meiosis, leading to chromosome missegregation and haploid induction

genes: HEB (Solyc12g036480, NAC transcription factor, tomato)
phenotype: Silencing of HEB in tomato leaves leads to a stay-green phenotype, delaying senescence and preventing chlorophyll degradation. Plants exhibit prolonged leaf greenness and reduced expression of senescence-associated genes (SlSAG12, SlSAG113, SlNYC1, SlSGR1, SlPaO).
mechanism: HEB is a positive regulator of senescence mechanisms in tomato leaves. Its downregulation prevents activation of chlorophyll degradation pathways and senescence-associated genes, maintaining photosynthetic efficiency and chlorophyll content.

genes: HEB (Solyc12g036480, NAC transcription factor, tomato)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of HEB in tomato leaves results in a slight increase in photosynthetic yield compared to control regions. However, HEB transcript accumulation is not observed, suggesting instability of the transcript.
mechanism: HEB transcript is difficult to accumulate and might be quite unstable, preventing transient overexpression analysis. The slight increase in photosynthetic yield may indicate a regulatory role in photosynthesis.

genes: GFP (Green Fluorescent Protein, jellyfish)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP serves as a negative control in VIGS experiments. It does not affect leaf senescence or chlorophyll degradation.
mechanism: GFP is used as a reporter gene to confirm the effectiveness of the VIGS system. Its overexpression does not interfere with senescence pathways.

genes: PDS (PHYTOENE DESATURASE, tomato)
phenotype: Silencing of PDS leads to a photo-bleached phenotype in tomato plants, indicating successful gene silencing. This serves as a positive control for the VIGS protocol.
mechanism: PDS is an enzyme necessary for carotenoid biosynthesis. Its silencing results in photo-bleached leaves and fruits due to impaired lycopene accumulation.

genes: p19 (p19 gene, suppressor of RNA silencing, Tomato bushy stunt virus), ads (amorpha-4,11-diene synthase, key enzyme in artemisinin biosynthesis, Artemisia annua L.)
phenotype: Co-transformation of p19 and ads genes increases artemisinin content by 2.57-fold in Artemisia annua L. leaves compared to untransformed leaves.
mechanism: p19 suppresses RNA silencing, enhancing ads gene expression which is critical for artemisinin biosynthesis.

genes: p19 (p19 gene, suppressor of RNA silencing, Tomato bushy stunt virus)
phenotype: Overexpression of p19 gene increases artemisinin content by 2.25-fold in Artemisia annua L. leaves compared to untransformed leaves.
mechanism: p19 suppresses RNA silencing, indirectly enhancing artemisinin biosynthesis.

genes: CaWRKY70 (Cicer arietinum WRKY70, transcription factor, Cicer arietinum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CaWRKY70 promotes susceptibility in resistant chickpea (WR315) plants to Foc1 infection, with 100% plant mortality at 12 dpi compared to 20% in control transgenics. Overexpressing plants show reduced SA concentrations, suppressed ROS production, and inhibited cell death in Foc1-infected roots, stems, and leaves.
mechanism: CaWRKY70 suppresses SA biosynthesis (CaICS1, CaPAL), SA signaling (CaEDS1, CaPAD4, CaNPR1), and ROS production. It directly represses CaWRKY40 promoter activity and interacts with RPP2-like CC-NB-ARC-LRR protein to inhibit hyper-immune signaling.

genes: CaAMP1 (antimicrobial peptide gene, from Capsicum annuum, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CaAMP1 enhances Phytophthora root and stem rot (PRR) tolerance in soybean by eliciting resistance responses mediated by multiple defense signaling pathways, with survival rates of 66.17–94.68% in transgenic lines compared to 43.67–56.17% in wild-type plants.
mechanism: CaAMP1 induces salicylic acid (SA)- and jasmonic acid (JA)-dependent defense signaling pathways and plant disease resistance genes (R-genes), leading to up-regulation of GmPR1, GmPR2, GmPR3, GmPR5, GmPR12, GmPAL, GmAOS, GmPPO, GmSGT1, and GmRAR1 genes after P. sojae inoculation.

genes: PPC2 (Arabidopsis thaliana, phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase 2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PPC2 rescues the growth arrest and chlorosis in ppc2 mutant under low CO2 conditions.
mechanism: PPC2 is a major PEPC in Arabidopsis leaves, involved in carbon assimilation and photorespiration under low CO2.

genes: ABI5 (Arabidopsis thaliana, ABA insensitive 5, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ABI5 rescues the growth arrest in ppc2 mutant under low CO2 conditions.
mechanism: ABI5 regulates photorespiratory enzyme expression, modulating carbon assimilation under low CO2.

genes: GUS (Arabidopsis thaliana, β-glucuronidase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: GUS activity indicates PPC2 expression in leaves, flowers, and siliques.
mechanism: PPC2 is expressed in guard cells and various tissues, indicating its role in growth regulation.

genes: XTH43 (Glycine max XTH43, xyloglucan endotransglucosylase/hydrolase, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of XTH43 in G. hirsutum reduces M. incognita gall formation by ~20%, egg masses by ~50%, eggs by ~62.6%, and J2s by ~62.6%.
mechanism: XTH43 impairs M. incognita parasitism by modifying cell wall components, likely through xyloglucan chain length alteration.

phenotype: Ectopic expression of AtMyb75 induces purple/red anthocyanin accumulation in transgenic hairy roots of soybean, Lotus japonicus, Lotus corniculatus, and Medicago truncatula.
mechanism: AtMyb75 regulates anthocyanin production by acting as an R2R3 type MYB transcription factor.

genes: VviERF6L1 (VviERF6L1, ERF transcription factor, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VviERF6L1 in a Seyval Blanc background did not result in detectable morphological phenotypes.
mechanism: Genes differentially expressed in response to VviERF6L1 overexpression were associated with abiotic and biotic stress responses.

genes: GAPC1 (Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase C1, Arabidopsis thaliana, source), GAPC2 (Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase C2, Arabidopsis thaliana, source)

mechanism: GAPC nuclear localization and interaction with NF-YC10 are required for heat tolerance; GAPC2mut lacks NF-YC10 binding but retains nuclear translocation.

genes: WSL9 (WSL9, encodes an HNH endonuclease domain-containing protein, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of wsl9 mutant restores wild-type phenotype in rice seedlings
mechanism: WSL9 encodes an HNH endonuclease domain-containing protein that is essential for early chloroplast development

phenotype: Overexpression of A1 DFR increases orange flower coloration in Petunia x hybrida
mechanism: A1 DFR enhances anthocyanin biosynthesis by catalyzing dihydroflavonol 4-reduction

genes: Rad51 (Rad51, DNA recombinase, Homo sapiens)
phenotype: Expression of Rad51 increases ICR frequency in pollen by 18.8- to 91-fold in Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: Stimulation of HR via eukaryotic recombinase promoting DSB repair.

genes: LOC_Os11g37390 (OsFBDUF54, F-box gene family member, Oryza sativa), LOC_Os11g37300 (OsFBDUF53, F-box gene family member, Oryza sativa), LOC_Os11g37320 (LTPL79, protease inhibitor gene, Oryza sativa)

mechanism: OsSBPase contains a chloroplast transit peptide

genes: OsASN1 (OsASN1, asparagine synthetase 1, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsASN1 increases grain yield by 130-147% and nitrogen content by 131-140% in Oryza sativa under N-limiting conditions.
mechanism: OsASN1 enhances nitrogen uptake and assimilation, leading to increased nitrogen and protein content in grains.

genes: OsSTAP1 (salt stress-responsive AP2/ERF transcription factor, Oryza sativa L., synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSTAP1 increases salt tolerance in rice with higher SOD, POD, and CAT activities, and lower Na+/K+ ratios in shoots. Transgenic lines show ~62% survival rate in wild type vs 81-91% in OE lines after salt stress recovery.
mechanism: OsSTAP1 decreases Na+/K+ ratio and maintains cellular redox homeostasis by upregulating antioxidant enzymes and stress-responsive genes like ERF113, ERF1, aquaporin NIP2-1, and peroxidases.

genes: LOC_Os03g52170 (4-hydroxy-3-methylbut-2-enyl diphosphate reductase, rice), OsHMBPP (4-hydroxy-3-methylbut-2-enyl diphosphate reductase, rice)
phenotype: The las1 mutant exhibits an albino phenotype with significantly reduced chlorophyll content and eventually dies due to defective chloroplast development.
mechanism: LAS1/OsHMBPP is essential for early chloroplast development in rice. The mutation disrupts the MEP pathway, leading to impaired chlorophyll biosynthesis and chloroplast ribosome biogenesis.

genes: LAS1 (4-hydroxy-3-methylbut-2-enyl diphosphate reductase, rice)
phenotype: The LAS1-GFP fusion protein is localized in chloroplasts, confirming the chloroplast-targeted function of LAS1/OsHMBPP.
mechanism: LAS1/OsHMBPP is targeted to chloroplasts, as demonstrated by transient expression of the LAS1-GFP fusion protein in rice protoplasts.

genes: SlartRDR6 (artificial gene, based on tomato homologs of RDR6, synthetic)
phenotype: Suppression of endogenous SlRDR6 expression by ~60% in transgenic tomato line 91B
mechanism: RNAi-mediated gene silencing via inverted-repeat transgene

genes: GhGLP2 (germin-like protein 2, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhGLP2 in Arabidopsis increases resistance to Verticillium dahliae and Fusarium oxysporum, reduces lesion areas, and enhances callose deposition and lignification.
mechanism: GhGLP2 has SOD activity, leading to H2O2 accumulation and activation of JA/ET pathways.

genes: GhGLP2 (germin-like protein 2, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Silencing of GhGLP2 in cotton increases susceptibility to Verticillium dahliae and Fusarium oxysporum, with larger lesions and reduced callose deposition.
mechanism: GhGLP2 is involved in callose formation and lignification; its silencing disrupts these defenses.

genes: MdCERK1-2 (LysM-containing protein kinase, Malus × domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdCERK1–2 increases resistance to Alternaria alternata in Nicotiana benthamiana, with significantly milder lesions (p < 0.01) and reduced fungal mass compared to wild type and empty vector controls.
mechanism: MdCERK1–2 overexpression enhances ROS accumulation, callose deposition, and polyphenol content in response to A. alternata infection, contributing to improved resistance.

genes: Sl-AACS1 (acylsugar acyl-CoA synthetase 1, Solanum lycopersicum, synthetic), Sl-AECH1 (acylsugar enoyl-CoA hydratase 1, Solanum lycopersicum, synthetic)
phenotype: Knockout of Sl-AACS1 or Sl-AECH1 eliminates detectable medium chain (C10/C12) acylsugars in tomato trichomes.
mechanism: Sl-AACS1 activates medium chain fatty acids to acyl-CoAs, which are substrates for acylsugar biosynthesis. Sl-AECH1 participates in acyl-CoA metabolism, channeling into lipid biosynthesis.

genes: ThiC (putative TPP riboswitch, Elaeis guineensis)
phenotype: Successful amplification and cloning of 242 bp putative TPP riboswitch fragment from Elaeis guineensis ThiC gene
mechanism: TPP riboswitch binds to thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) ligand, inducing conformational changes that regulate gene expression through RNA architecture

genes: GlMYB4 (Glycyrrhiza uralensis MYB transcription factor 4, transcription factor, Glycyrrhiza uralensis), GlMYB88 (Glycyrrhiza uralensis MYB transcription factor 88, transcription factor, Glycyrrhiza uralensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of GlMYB4 and GlMYB88 increases total flavonoid content by 1.57-1.80× and isoliquiritigenin content by 2.11-5.57× in Glycyrrhiza uralensis cells.
mechanism: GlMYB4 and GlMYB88 upregulate key flavonoid biosynthesis genes CHS and C4H, enhancing phenylpropane metabolic pathway activity for flavonoid production.

genes: GlMYB4 (Glycyrrhiza uralensis MYB transcription factor 4, transcription factor, Glycyrrhiza uralensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of GlMYB4 increases total flavonoid content by 1.57× and isoliquiritigenin content by 2.11× in Glycyrrhiza uralensis cells.
mechanism: GlMYB4 upregulates key flavonoid biosynthesis genes CHS and C4H, enhancing phenylpropane metabolic pathway activity for flavonoid production.

genes: Csa1G085390 (C2H2 zinc finger protein, cucumber, Cucumis sativus L.), Csa7G071440 (C2H2 zinc finger protein, cucumber, Cucumis sativus L.)
phenotype: Csa1G085390 decreases leaf necrosis in response to pathogen attack and enhances salt/drought tolerance through H2O2 induction; Csa7G071440 induces leaf necrosis and enhances salt/drought tolerance through H2O2 induction
mechanism: Csa1G085390 promotes pathogen resistance by reducing necrosis and activating H2O2-mediated stress responses; Csa7G071440 represses pathogen resistance by inducing necrosis but activates H2O2-mediated stress tolerance

genes: Csa4G642460 (C2H2 zinc finger protein, cucumber, Cucumis sativus L.), Csa6G303740 (C2H2 zinc finger protein, cucumber, Cucumis sativus L.)
phenotype: Csa4G642460 and Csa6G303740 induce cell death in tobacco and tomato leaves after 5 days transformation
mechanism: Induce cell death through hypersensitive response pathways, potentially activating PR genes to trigger defense responses

genes: ScADH3 (ScADH3, alcohol dehydrogenase gene, Saccharum spp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of ScADH3 enhances cold tolerance in transgenic tobacco, with reduced ROS accumulation and increased transcript levels of ROS-related genes (NtPOD and NtCAT).
mechanism: ScADH3 regulates ROS-related genes to maintain ROS homeostasis, reducing oxidative stress under cold conditions.

genes: SlNRC4a (SlNRC4a, disease resistance gene, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: slnrc4a gain of function mutant shows 71% decrease in Xcv and 46% decrease in Pst bacterial growth, 35% and 85% decrease in Bc and Ss lesion area, 65% decrease in On infected leaf area, 73% reduction in whitefly numbers, and 87% reduction in T. absoluta infected leaf area in Solanum lycopersicum
mechanism: Increased basal immunity with elevated ethylene production (46%), callose deposition (30%), and defense gene expression (2-9-fold) in steady state conditions; enhanced MAMP-mediated defense responses (200% ROS, 200% ethylene, 60% callose) upon elicitation

genes: gusA (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Tissue-specific GUS expression in roots, leaves, and reproductive organs; inducible by abiotic stresses (NaCl, PEG, cold, GA, ABA, MeJA, heavy metals) and wounding in transgenic rice.
mechanism: PrLmSAP promoter contains cis-elements for stress response, tissue-specific expression, and hormone regulation, driving gusA expression in specific tissues and under stress conditions.

genes: gusA (beta-glucuronidase, reporter gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Constitutive GUS expression in transgenic rice plants (35S:gusA) used as positive control for promoter activity.
mechanism: NA

genes: VvMLO3 (Vitis vinifera MLO3, susceptibility gene for powdery mildew, Vitis vinifera), VvMLO4 (Vitis vinifera MLO4, susceptibility gene for powdery mildew, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Targeted mutagenesis of VvMLO3 and VvMLO4 using CRISPR-Cas9 results in enhanced resistance to powdery mildew in Vitis vinifera cv. Thompson Seedless, with reduced fungal sporulation and increased cell death in infected leaves.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in VvMLO3 and VvMLO4 lead to callose deposition, H2O2 accumulation, and mesophyll cell death in infected epidermal cells, which correlates with enhanced resistance to powdery mildew.

genes: VvMLO3 (Vitis vinifera MLO3, susceptibility gene for powdery mildew, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Homozygous and heterozygous mutations in VvMLO3 result in early senescence-like phenotypes, reduced rooting potential, and enhanced resistance to powdery mildew with ~2-fold reduction in fungal sporulation.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in VvMLO3 lead to premature leaf chlorosis, mesophyll cell death, and increased callose deposition and H2O2 accumulation in infected cells, which correlate with enhanced resistance to powdery mildew.

genes: VvMLO4 (Vitis vinifera MLO4, susceptibility gene for powdery mildew, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Targeted mutagenesis of VvMLO4 using CRISPR-Cas9 results in deformed leaves and plant death, with no detectable edited lines for the CM4G4 construct.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in VvMLO4 lead to lethal phenotypes and failure to produce viable edited lines, suggesting potential functional redundancy or essential roles in grapevine development.

plant_species: Populus alba × P. tremula var. glandulosa
genes: MtmiR156b (microRNA, Medicago truncatula)
phenotype: Overexpression of miR156b in poplar leads to increased branching, reduced leaf size, dwarf phenotype, and anthocyanin accumulation in stems, leaf margins, and petioles. Total anthocyanin content increases 8.3-fold compared to wild type.
mechanism: miR156-SPL module regulates downstream genes including LDOX, UFGT, and GST in flavonoid biosynthesis. Downregulation of miR156-targeted SPLs (SPL15, SPL17, SPL24) and auxin signaling pathway components (ARF18, MYB39) correlates with increased anthocyanin accumulation.

genes: omega-1,2 gliadins (omega-1,2 gliadins, storage protein, Triticum aestivum), alpha gliadins (alpha gliadins, storage protein, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Transgenic line SA-30-118a-5 lacks all omega-1,2 gliadins; transgenic line SA-35a-124j lacks all alpha gliadins.
mechanism: RNA interference suppresses target gliadins.

genes: FaHsfA2a (heat shock factor A2a, Festuca arundinacea), FaNAC029 (NAC domain-containing protein 029, Festuca arundinacea), FaNAM-B1 (NAM-B1, Festuca arundinacea)
phenotype: Overexpression of FaHsfA2a reduces cell membrane damage caused by heat stress in Nicotiana benthamiana, while overexpression of FaNAC029 and FaNAM-B1 increases membrane damage.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaHsfA2-10 (heat shock transcription factor A2-10, wheat, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: TaHsfA2–10 is localized in the nucleus under the normal growth conditions.
mechanism: NA

genes: TrihDEFa-SRDX (TrihDEFa-SRDX, B class gene of Tricyrtis sp. fused with ERF-associated amphiphilic repression (EAR) motif repression domain (SRDX), Tricyrtis sp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of TrihDEFa-SRDX in Lilium cv. Acapulco results in severe morphological alterations including reduced papillae, pale pink tepals, and non-fully-opened flowers.
mechanism: TrihDEFa-SRDX suppresses endogenous B class gene expression, leading to reduced petaloid identity and anthocyanin synthesis.

genes: P1/HC-Pro (P1/HC-Pro, viral suppressor of PTGS, TuMV), HC-Pro (HC-Pro, viral suppressor of PTGS, TuMV)
phenotype: Overexpression of P1/HC-Pro in Arabidopsis thaliana causes severe serrated and curled leaf phenotypes, increased ethylene emission, and abnormal miRNA/miRNA* accumulation.
mechanism: P1/HC-Pro enhances HC-Pro-mediated PTGS suppression by binding to VIP3/SKI8, interfering with 5′-fragment degradation, and triggering AGO1 posttranslational degradation via autophagy.

genes: P1/HC-Pro (P1/HC-Pro, viral suppressor of PTGS, TuMV)
phenotype: Overexpression of P1/HC-Pro in Arabidopsis thaliana causes severe serrated and curled leaf phenotypes, increased ethylene emission, and abnormal miRNA/miRNA* accumulation.
mechanism: P1/HC-Pro enhances HC-Pro-mediated PTGS suppression by binding to VIP3/SKI8, interfering with 5′-fragment degradation, and triggering AGO1 posttranslational degradation via autophagy.

genes: P1/HC-Pro (P1/HC-Pro, viral suppressor of PTGS, ZYMV)
phenotype: Overexpression of P1/HC-Pro in Arabidopsis thaliana causes severe serrated and curled leaf phenotypes, increased ethylene emission, and abnormal miRNA/miRNA* accumulation.
mechanism: P1/HC-Pro enhances HC-Pro-mediated PTGS suppression by binding to VIP3/SKI8, interfering with 5′-fragment degradation, and triggering AGO1 posttranslational degradation via autophagy.

genes: P1/HC-Pro (P1/HC-Pro, viral suppressor of PTGS, TEV)
phenotype: Overexpression of P1/HC-Pro in Arabidopsis thaliana causes severe serrated and curled leaf phenotypes, increased ethylene emission, and abnormal miRNA/miRNA* accumulation.
mechanism: P1/HC-Pro enhances HC-Pro-mediated PTGS suppression by binding to VIP3/SKI8, interfering with 5′-fragment degradation, and triggering AGO1 posttranslational degradation via autophagy.

genes: P1/HC-Pro (P1/HC-Pro, viral suppressor of PTGS, recombinant)
phenotype: Overexpression of recombinant P1/HC-Pro in Arabidopsis thaliana causes severe serrated and curled leaf phenotypes, increased ethylene emission, and abnormal miRNA/miRNA* accumulation.
mechanism: P1/HC-Pro enhances HC-Pro-mediated PTGS suppression by binding to VIP3/SKI8, interfering with 5′-fragment degradation, and triggering AGO1 posttranslational degradation via autophagy.

genes: LTG5 (Low Temperature Growth 5, UDP-glucosyltransferase, Oryza rufipogon)
phenotype: Overexpression of LTG5 increases cold tolerance in indica rice, with germination rates enhanced by 96.97%, 61.11%, and 37.78% in OE-LTG5 lines compared to non-transgenic lines under cold stress.
mechanism: LTG5 encodes a UDP-glucosyltransferase that enhances cold tolerance by maintaining membrane and nuclear localization, possibly through glycosylation processes affecting stress response.

genes: GST1 (anthocyanin transport, Gentiana triflora × Gentiana scabra)
phenotype: GST1 genome-edited lines exhibited two types of mutant flower phenotypes, severe (almost white) and mild (pale blue). The phenotypes were associated with decreased anthocyanin accumulation in flower petals.
mechanism: GST1 is necessary for anthocyanin transport in Japanese gentian.

genes: GST1 (anthocyanin transport, Gentiana triflora × Gentiana scabra)
phenotype: The anthocyanin accumulation of GST1 genome-edited line #12 was restored by the transient expression of GST1.
mechanism: GST1 is necessary for anthocyanin accumulation in gentian plants.

genes: OsRR22 (OsRR22, rice response regulator 22, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutations in OsRR22 significantly enhance salinity tolerance at the seedling stage, with mutant lines showing 10.1-2.1% reduction in shoot fresh weight vs 50.3% in wild type under 0.75% NaCl stress
mechanism: OsRR22 functions as a negative regulator of salt tolerance; its knockout removes this repression, enhancing salt tolerance without altering agronomic traits

genes: CWC15 (CWC15, splicing factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CWC15 rescues the cwc15-1 mutant seedling phenotypes, including stunted growth and cotyledon defects.
mechanism: CWC15 is part of the spliceosome complex, and its overexpression restores normal splicing function, thereby rescuing developmental defects.

genes: CWC15 (CWC15, splicing factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CWC15 under the RPS5A promoter rescues the cwc15-1 mutant seedling phenotypes, including stunted growth and cotyledon defects.
mechanism: CWC15 is part of the spliceosome complex, and its overexpression restores normal splicing function, thereby rescuing developmental defects.

genes: CWC15 (CWC15, splicing factor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CWC15 under the AT3G10100 promoter does not rescue the cwc15-1 mutant seedling phenotypes, indicating that promoter activity during later development is necessary.
mechanism: CWC15 is part of the spliceosome complex, and its overexpression under a promoter active only during early embryogenesis fails to rescue developmental defects, highlighting the need for sustained protein activity.

genes: TomloxB (TomloxB, lipoxygenase, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Decreased LOX activity in transgenic lines compared to wild type
mechanism: Silencing of TomloxB gene reduces LOX activity and ethylene production

genes: NahG (NahG, salicylate hydroxylase, Pseudomonas syringae)
phenotype: SA-deficient potato plants (NahGD2 and NahGA) show larger leaf lesions and higher fungal biomass after Alternaria solani infection than wild type plants
mechanism: Intact SA signaling is necessary to mount an efficient defence response to A. solani in both foliage and tubers

genes: coi1 (COI1, jasmonate-insensitive mutant, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: JA-insensitive potato plants (coi1H1 and coi1X5) show no significant difference in lesion size compared to wild type after Alternaria solani infection
mechanism: Intact SA signaling is more important than JA signaling for resistance to A. solani in potato

genes: LOC_Os03g19590 (phytochromeB, rice phytochromeB, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: osphyb plants show increased drought tolerance compared to wild type, with lower water use efficiency (WUE), plant water loss rate (PWLR), and transpiration rate (TR) under drought stress.
mechanism: Lower stomatal density and size in osphyb plants reduce transpiration and water loss, contributing to drought resistance.

genes: LePDS1 (phytoene desaturase, L. erythrorhizon, LC512725)
phenotype: Knockdown of LePDS1 results in albino leaves in L. erythrorhizon with ~70% escape rate
mechanism: ALSV-mediated VIGS silences PDS gene expression, inhibiting carotenoid biosynthesis

genes: Cry3Bb1 (Cry3Bb1, insecticidal toxin, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Cry3Bb1 corn exhibits resistance to western corn rootworm larvae by producing the Cry3Bb1 toxin.
mechanism: The Cry3Bb1 toxin targets and kills western corn rootworm larvae by binding to specific receptors in their gut, causing cell lysis and death.

genes: Cry34/35Ab1 (Cry34/35Ab1, insecticidal toxin, Bacillus thuringiensis), Cry3Bb1 (Cry3Bb1, insecticidal toxin, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Pyramided Cry34/35Ab1 + Cry3Bb1 corn provides enhanced resistance to western corn rootworm compared to single-trait Bt corn.
mechanism: The combination of Cry34/35Ab1 and Cry3Bb1 toxins targets multiple receptors in the rootworm gut, reducing the likelihood of resistance development.

genes: Cry34/35Ab1 (Cry34/35Ab1, insecticidal toxin, Bacillus thuringiensis), mCry3A (mCry3A, insecticidal toxin, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Pyramided Cry34/35Ab1 + mCry3A corn provides enhanced resistance to western corn rootworm compared to single-trait Bt corn.
mechanism: The combination of Cry34/35Ab1 and mCry3A toxins targets multiple receptors in the rootworm gut, reducing the likelihood of resistance development.

genes: miraculin (miraculin, sweet-tasting protein, synthetic), FLAG (FLAG, epitope tag, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of FLAG-tagged miraculin in carrot callus increases miraculin protein production by 30- to 90-fold in bioreactor cultures compared to initial cultures.
mechanism: The stress-inducible SWPA2 promoter drives miraculin expression in response to abiotic stress (H2O2, NaCl) and specific light conditions, leading to increased recombinant protein production.

genes: BvLzm (bovine lysozyme, synthetic)
phenotype: Bovine lysozyme (BvLzm) yield ranges from 0.08–0.4 mg/kg culm mass (0.01–0.06% of total soluble protein [TSP]) in single promoter pU:BvLzm lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: BvLzm (bovine lysozyme, synthetic)
phenotype: Bovine lysozyme (BvLzm) yield ranges from 0.5–0.7 mg/kg culm mass (0.07–0.1% of TSP) in double promoter pUD:BvLzm lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: BvLzm (bovine lysozyme, synthetic)
phenotype: Bovine lysozyme (BvLzm) yield ranges from 1.0–6.0 mg/kg culm mass (0.1–0.8% of TSP) in triple promoter pUPE:BvLzm and pUDE:BvLzm lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: BvLzm (bovine lysozyme, synthetic)
phenotype: Bovine lysozyme (BvLzm) yield ranges from 2.0–10.0 mg/kg culm mass (0.3–1.4% of TSP) in quadruple promoter pUPBE:BvLzm lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: BvLzm (bovine lysozyme, synthetic)
phenotype: Bovine lysozyme (BvLzm) yield ranges from 11.0–82.5 mg/kg culm mass (1.5–11.5% of TSP) in event-stacked five promoter pUDEPB:BvLzm lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: ACT3 (acetyltransferase, watermelon, synthetic)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of ACT3 in watermelon leaves leads to accumulation of 16-O-acetyl CuE in response to wounding stress.
mechanism: ACT3 catalyzes C16-acetylation of cucurbitacins, contributing to the formation of 16-O-acetyl CuE and other derivatives.

genes: AtPIG-S (Arabidopsis thaliana subunit of GPI transamidase, GPI-T), GFP (synthetic green fluorescent protein)
phenotype: Rescues pollen tube emergence and growth defects in pigs-1 mutant pollen, enabling generation of pigs-1/pigs-1 seedlings. However, sporophyte function is not rescued, as pigs-1/pigs-1, pPIGS:GFP-PIGS seedlings die soon after germination.
mechanism: Complementation of AtPIG-S function in male gametophyte by restoring GPI transamidase activity required for GPI anchor addition to GPI-anchored proteins (GAPs).

genes: OsCAF2 (chloroplast RNA splicing factor, rice), OsCRS2 (chloroplast RNA splicing factor, rice)
phenotype: Disruption of OsCAF2 causes albino seedling phenotype and death at the three-leaf stage in rice due to impaired chloroplast development.
mechanism: OsCAF2 promotes splicing of subgroup IIA and IIB chloroplast introns (rpl2, rps12, atpF, ndhA, ndhB, ycf3) and interacts with OsCRS2 via its C-terminal region to form the OsCAF2-OsCRS2 complex. OsCAF2 also forms homodimers via its N-terminal region.

genes: OsCAF2 (chloroplast RNA splicing factor, rice)
phenotype: OsCAF2-GFP fusion protein localizes to chloroplasts in rice protoplasts, confirming its chloroplast localization.
mechanism: NA

genes: GUSPlus (beta-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: CitSEPp shows fruit/seed-specific expression in ripe tomato fruit with no detectable expression in leaves or other vegetative organs
mechanism: Promoter contains TATA-box, CAAT-boxes, and fruit-specific regulatory elements

genes: GUSPlus (beta-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: CitWAXp shows high fruit-preferential expression with strong activity in fruit and weak activity in floral tissues
mechanism: Promoter contains hormone, light, and stress response cis-elements

genes: GUSPlus (beta-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: CitUNKp shows high expression in unripe fruit, leaf, and seedling tissues with strong fruit-preferential expression
mechanism: Promoter contains cold, drought, heat-responsive elements and light response elements

genes: GUSPlus (beta-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: CitVO1p shows strong fruit expression with detectable activity in abscission zones and wound sites
mechanism: Promoter contains defense-related cis elements and AT-rich sequence for elicitor-mediated activation

genes: GUSPlus (beta-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: CitVO2p (intron-lacking CitVO1p) shows predominant expression in seeds
mechanism: Promoter lacks native intron affecting expression pattern

genes: GUSPlus (beta-glucuronidase reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: PamMybAp shows strong fruit expression with unique leaf staining pattern
mechanism: Promoter contains MBSI, MRE, and as-2 box for flavonoid and light responsive signaling

genes: TaCPK34 (drought response gene, wheat)
phenotype: TaCPK34-silenced wheat plants showed increased drought sensitivity with reduced biomass and relative water content, and increased soluble sugar and MDA content
mechanism: TaCPK34 regulates drought tolerance through ABA-dependent gene expression and interacts with GST1 and prx113

genes: LcINDEHISCENT (LcINDEHISCENT, gene involved in fruit dehiscence, Lepidium campestre)
phenotype: Silencing of LcINDEHISCENT by RNAi results in indehiscent fruits with two seeds enclosed within un-detached fruit valves from replum
mechanism: Post-transcriptional silencing of LcINDEHISCENT by RNAi abolishes the dehiscence zone at the fruit valve margin

genes: LeGPA1 (LeGPA1, G-protein alpha subunit, Lycopersicon esculentum)
phenotype: Overexpression of LeGPA1 increases plant height by 4–11.6%, stem thickness by 13.5–18.3%, and cold stress tolerance in tomato plants. Transgenic plants show reduced ROS accumulation, increased antioxidant enzyme activity (SOD, POD, CAT), and enhanced expression of cold-response genes (LeICE1, LeCBF1, LeCOR413PM2, LeTPS1, LeDRCi7).
mechanism: LeGPA1 enhances cold tolerance by upregulating antioxidant systems (SOD, POD, CAT), reducing ROS and membrane lipid peroxidation, and activating the ICE-CBF-COR signaling pathway for cold acclimation.

genes: LeGPA1 (LeGPA1, G-protein alpha subunit, Lycopersicon esculentum)
phenotype: RNAi transgenic plants show reduced plant height by 28.9–36.9%, increased stem thickness by 34.1–37.4%, and decreased cold stress tolerance. Transgenic plants exhibit higher ROS accumulation, reduced antioxidant enzyme activity, and downregulated cold-response genes.
mechanism: LeGPA1 silencing impairs antioxidant systems, increases ROS and membrane damage, and suppresses ICE-CBF-COR signaling, reducing cold acclimation capacity.

genes: LeGPA1 (LeGPA1, G-protein alpha subunit, Lycopersicon esculentum)
phenotype: LeGPA1-GFP fusion protein localizes to the plasma membrane in Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts.
mechanism: NA

genes: CYP79A2 (CYP79A2, phenylalanine-oxidizing enzyme, Setaria italica), CYP79A1 (CYP79A1, tyrosine-oxidizing enzyme, Sorghum bicolor), CYP79D3 (CYP79D3, isoleucine- and valine-oxidizing enzyme, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: Accumulation of new-to-nature methyldithiocarbamates (benzyl crucifalexin, 4-hydroxybenzyl crucifalexin, 1-methylpropyl crucifalexin) in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: Substrate promiscuity of the brassinin pathway enzymes allows oxidation of non-native amino acids (phenylalanine, tyrosine, isoleucine/valine) to produce novel crucifalexins.

genes: CYP79A1 (CYP79A1, tyrosine-oxidizing enzyme, Sorghum bicolor)
phenotype: Accumulation of 4-hydroxybenzyl crucifalexin and its putative glycosylated version in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: Tyrosine oxidation by CYP79A1 generates 4-hydroxybenzyl isothiocyanate, which is further converted to crucifalexin via the brassinin pathway.

genes: CYP79D3 (CYP79D3, isoleucine- and valine-oxidizing enzyme, Lotus japonicus)
phenotype: Accumulation of propyl isothiocyanate but not propyl crucifalexin in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: CYP79D3 oxidizes valine to propyl isothiocyanate, but downstream pathway limitations prevent crucifalexin formation.

genes: TGG4 (TGG4, promiscuous myrosinase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Higher activity for new-to-nature crucifalexins compared to B. rapa myrosinase BABGLU.A in N. benthamiana.
mechanism: TGG4's promiscuity enables efficient conversion of isothiocyanates to crucifalexins.

genes: BrCYP79B2 (BrCYP79B2, tryptophan-specific enzyme, Brassica rapa), SbCYP79A2 (SbCYP79A2, phenylalanine-oxidizing enzyme, Sorghum bicolor), SiCYP79A1 (SiCYP79A1, tyrosine-oxidizing enzyme, Setaria italica)
phenotype: Simultaneous accumulation of multiple crucifalexins (brassinin, benzyl crucifalexin, 4-hydroxybenzyl crucifalexin) in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: Co-expression of multiple CYP79 enzymes enables parallel oxidation of different amino acids, leading to diverse crucifalexin production.

genes: PyrH (PyrH, halogenase, Streptomyces rugosporus), RebF (RebF, reductase, Lechevalieria aerocolonigenes)
phenotype: Accumulation of 5-chlorobrassinin in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: PyrH/RebF pair produces 5-chlorotryptophan, which is incorporated into the brassinin pathway to form 5-chlorobrassinin.

genes: RebH (RebH, halogenase, Morchella esculenta), RebF (RebF, reductase, Lechevalieria aerocolonigenes)
phenotype: Accumulation of 7-chlorobrassinin and 7-bromobrassinin in N. benthamiana leaves after potassium bromide treatment.
mechanism: RebH/RebF pair produces 7-chloro and 7-bromotryptophan, which are incorporated into the brassinin pathway to form halogenated derivatives.

genes: BrCYP71CR1 (BrCYP71CR1, spirobrassinin synthase, Brassica rapa), BrCYP71CR2 (BrCYP71CR2, cyclobrassinin synthase, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Production of halogenated spirobrassinin and cyclobrassinin derivatives (5- and 7-chloro, 7-bromo) in N. benthamiana leaves.
mechanism: BrCYP71CR1 and BrCYP71CR2 modify halogenated brassinin precursors to form structurally diverse derivatives.

genes: VvPR4b (VvPR4b, pathogenesis-related protein 4b, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Knockout of VvPR4b in 'Thompson Seedless' decreases resistance to P. viticola, with relative genomic abundance of P. viticola 1.2-2.5 times higher in knockout lines compared to wild type
mechanism: VvPR4b plays a role in downy mildew resistance through regulation of ROS production and pathogen colonization; knockout lines show reduced H2O2 accumulation and increased sporangia formation

genes: VlbZIP30 (VlbZIP30, bZIP transcription factor, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VlbZIP30 increases lignin accumulation in grapevine stems by 1.3- to 1.6-fold and enhances drought tolerance, as evidenced by higher relative water content (RWC), lower electrolyte leakage, and increased photosynthetic efficiency under drought stress.
mechanism: VlbZIP30 binds to G-box motifs in promoters of lignin biosynthetic genes (VvPRX4, VvPRX72) and drought-responsive genes (VvNAC17), activating their expression to promote lignin biosynthesis and drought resistance.

genes: CgMYB58 (CgMYB58, transcription factor, Citrus grandis)
phenotype: Overexpression of CgMYB58 increases lignin content in citrus calli.
mechanism: CgMYB58 promotes lignin biosynthesis by upregulating CgPAL1, CgPAL2, Cg4CL1, and CgC3H.

genes: Cas9 (Cas9, CRISPR-associated endonuclease, synthetic), GFP (GFP, green fluorescent protein, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of GFP under CaMV35S promoter results in uniform fluorescence in all tissues of transgenic tomato plants.
mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9 system driven by PPC2 promoter enables fruit-specific gene editing while maintaining low Cas9 expression in seeds.

genes: SlMYB33 (GAMYB-like gene, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Knockdown of SlMYB33 results in delayed flowering (50-56 days to anthesis vs 40.3 days in WT) and poor fertility (3.1-7.3 seeds per fruit vs 22.9 in WT) with aberrant pollen morphology (70-86% abnormal vs 3% in WT)
mechanism: SlMYB33 regulates flowering-related genes (AN, FA, S, SPGB, FPF1, FCA) and pollen development through starch/sucrose metabolism genes (Lin7, SPS, SUS, TPS, AGPase, SlSTP13). SlMYB33 knockdown disrupts pollen maturity and reduces sugar content in anthers.

genes: MdMIPS1 (myo-inositol-1-phosphate synthase, apple), MdMIPS2 (myo-inositol-1-phosphate synthase, apple)
phenotype: RNAi lines (Ri-1 and Ri-2) exhibit leaf and root necrosis, plant death under MI-depleted conditions, increased sorbitol/sucrose, and ROS-mediated PCD
mechanism: Reduced MI biosynthesis causes WS pectin accumulation → SA signaling activation → compromised antioxidant system → ROS overaccumulation → ET bursts → PCD/necrosis

genes: MdMIPS1 (myo-inositol-1-phosphate synthase, apple)
phenotype: Overexpression lines (OE-4 and OE-6) show increased MI accumulation, decreased sorbitol/sucrose, normal growth under MI-depleted conditions, and delayed leaf senescence
mechanism: Enhanced MI biosynthesis suppresses SA/ET signaling, maintains antioxidant capacity, and delays ROS-induced PCD during senescence

genes: GhSAMDC1 (SAMDC, cotton, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhSAMDC1 increases vegetative growth and early flowering in transgenic tobacco plants.
mechanism: GhSAMDC1 enhances polyamine conversion, leading to increased spermine and decreased spermidine, which promotes flowering.

genes: VIT_08s0032g01110 (VIT_08s0032g01110, predicted axial regulator YABBY 5, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VIT_08s0032g01110 in transgenic Arabidopsis plants caused the change of pod shape
mechanism: NA

genes: AhGPAT9A (AhGPAT9A, glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase 9A, Arachis hypogaea)
phenotype: Overexpression of AhGPAT9A increases seed oil content by ~5.35% in T1 transgenic peanuts and ~8.82% in T2 transgenic peanuts compared to wild-type FH2.
mechanism: AhGPAT9A encodes a glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase involved in lipid synthesis, promoting triacylglycerol (TAG) accumulation in seeds.

genes: AhGPAT9A (AhGPAT9A, glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase 9A, Arachis hypogaea)
phenotype: Antisense expression of AhGPAT9A decreases seed oil content by ~6.70% in T1 transgenic peanuts and ~9.13% in T2 transgenic peanuts compared to wild-type FH2.
mechanism: AhGPAT9A encodes a glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase involved in lipid synthesis, suppressing triacylglycerol (TAG) accumulation in seeds.

genes: OsF3H (flavanone 3-hydroxylase, Oryza sativa, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsF3H increases resistance to white-backed planthopper (WBPH) in rice, with 0% infection in transgenic plants after 10 days vs 16.6% in wild-type
mechanism: OsF3H enhances flavonoid biosynthesis (kaempferol and quercetin accumulation) and anthocyanin production, which confer mechanical and biochemical resistance to WBPH through cell wall reinforcement and direct pesticidal effects

genes: SBA (soybean agglutinin, Glycine max, with 6×His-tag)
phenotype: Accumulation of recombinant SBA (rSBA) reaches 4% of total soluble protein (TSP) in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves and up to 0.31% TSP in Solanum tuberosum tubers.
mechanism: SBA binds to N-acetylgalactosamine, enabling purification via N-acetylgalactosamine–agarose columns and maintaining stability in simulated gastric/intestinal fluids.

genes: MAX2a (NaMAX2a, strigolactone receptor, Nicotiana attenuata), MAX2b (NaMAX2b, strigolactone receptor, Nicotiana attenuata)
phenotype: Increased branching, shorter plant height, higher anthocyanin levels in stems, increased susceptibility to T. mucorea larvae
mechanism: RNAi silencing of MAX2a and MAX2b disrupts strigolactone (SL) signaling, leading to increased branching and altered phytohormonal responses (JA and IAA) that affect herbivore resistance

genes: D14 (NaD14, strigolactone receptor, Nicotiana attenuata)
phenotype: Increased branching, shorter plant height, higher anthocyanin levels in stems, increased susceptibility to T. mucorea larvae
mechanism: RNAi silencing of D14 disrupts strigolactone (SL) signaling, leading to increased branching and altered phytohormonal responses (JA and IAA) that affect herbivore resistance

genes: CCD7 (NaCCD7, carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase, Nicotiana attenuata)
phenotype: Increased branching, shorter plant height, higher anthocyanin levels in stems, increased susceptibility to T. mucorea larvae
mechanism: RNAi silencing of CCD7 disrupts strigolactone (SL) biosynthesis, leading to increased branching and altered phytohormonal responses (JA and IAA) that affect herbivore resistance

genes: KAI2a (NaKAI2a, karrikin receptor, Nicotiana attenuata), KAI2b (NaKAI2b, karrikin receptor, Nicotiana attenuata)
phenotype: No significant differences in branching or herbivore resistance compared to control plants
mechanism: RNAi silencing of KAI2a and KAI2b does not affect strigolactone (SL) signaling or herbivore resistance, indicating KAR signaling is not involved in the observed phenotypes

genes: pinA (puroindoline A, storage protein, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Overexpression of PINA decreases grain hardness in Triticum aestivum with a dose-related effect.
mechanism: PINA interacts with gliadins, forming heteromeric complexes that facilitate cooperative aggregation of gliadins, reducing adhesion between starch grains and the protein matrix.

genes: BoaCRTISO (carotenoid isomerase, target of CRISPR editing, Brassica oleracea var. alboglabra)
phenotype: BoaCRTISO mutants exhibit yellowing of leaves and bolting stems, with M6 being the most yellow.
mechanism: Knockdown of BoaCRTISO leads to reduced expression of carotenoid and chlorophyll biosynthesis-related genes, resulting in decreased carotenoid and chlorophyll concentrations.

genes: AU (phytochromobilin synthase, promotes chlorophyll synthesis and represses AR formation, Solyc01 g008930)
phenotype: Overexpression of AU in the rf mutant repressed adventitious root (AR) formation but increased survival rate after 5 days of flooding stress.
mechanism: AU plays dual roles in promoting chlorophyll synthesis in leaves and repressing AR formation in stems. The loss of function of AU possibly led to the massive accumulation of heme in leaves, which was transported to stems, where the high heme level enhanced HO-1 activity, leading to the emission of CO, which induced the initiation of ARs in stems.

genes: ARR5 (cytokinin response regulator, promoter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: ARR5::eGFP transgenic plants show strong GFP signal in root tips, indicating cytokinin accumulation in roots.
mechanism: NA

genes: AREB-1 (ABA-responsive element binding protein 1, transcription factor involved in ABA-dependent drought tolerance, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: CRISPRa (dCas9 fused with histone acetyl-transferase) targeting AREB-1 promoter
phenotype: Overexpression of AREB-1 increases drought tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with a high survival ratio, green and healthy phenotype, and complete recovery after re-watering.
mechanism: AREB-1 accumulation enhances ABA-dependent signaling, leading to transcriptional activation of genes involved in drought tolerance, improving water use efficiency, and reducing oxidative damage.

genes: MhSnf7 (Snf7 gene, double-stranded RNA, M. hieroglyphica)
phenotype: MhSnf7 GM maize exhibits robust insecticidal capacity by demising M. hieroglyphica larvae, with a mortality rate approximately fourfold greater than non-GM maize.
mechanism: NA

genes: GFP (green fluorescent protein, source of fluorescence, synthetic), BAR (phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, confers herbicide resistance, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic plants exhibit GFP fluorescence and herbicide resistance (PPT resistance).
mechanism: NA

genes: GUS (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, reporter gene, Z. japonica)
phenotype: The ZjFes1 promoter drives GUS expression in Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings, leaves, flowers, and siliques under heat stress, with higher activity under heat treatment compared to normal temperature.
mechanism: NA

genes: NtMLP423 (major latex protein, drought tolerance, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtMLP423 increases drought tolerance in Arabidopsis and tobacco, with transgenic plants showing higher survival rates, increased root length, and improved water retention under drought stress.
mechanism: NtMLP423 enhances drought tolerance by increasing ABA sensitivity and accumulation, upregulating ABA biosynthesis genes (ABA2, AAO3, NCED3), and improving osmotic adjustment through increased proline accumulation and reduced MDA levels.

genes: NtMLP423 (major latex protein, drought tolerance, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: NtMLP423 was localized in the cytoplasm and nucleus of Nicotiana benthamiana cells.
mechanism: NA

genes: gusA (β-glucuronidase reporter gene, intron-containing, synthetic)
phenotype: The gusA gene was efficiently integrated into the passion fruit genome, confirmed by GUS histochemical staining and PCR analysis.
mechanism: NA

genes: Sobic.002G279100 (nuclear localization protein, predicted by TargetP 2.0, sorghum)
phenotype: Sobic.002G279100-GFP was localized in the nucleus as predicted.
mechanism: NA

genes: CAO (chlorophyllide a oxygenase, target gene for editing, sorghum)
phenotype: 14 protoplasts showed five types of editing in the target gene region, indicating an editing efficacy of 46.7%.
mechanism: NA

genes: GmSPX-RING1 (SPX-RING domain-containing protein, negative regulator of phosphorus concentration, Glycine max (L.) Merr.)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmSPX-RING1 reduces P concentration in soybean hairy roots by 32.75% under +P condition; RNAi of GmSPX-RING1 increases P concentration by 38.90% and 14.51% under +P and -P conditions, respectively.
mechanism: GmSPX-RING1 negatively regulates soybean phosphorus concentration in soybean hairy roots.

genes: cry1Ac (Bacillus thuringiensis toxin, insect resistance, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic sugarcane plants expressing the cry1Ac gene showed 100% mortality of Sesamia cretica larvae at 1000 ppm concentration of dried transformed sugarcane leaves.
mechanism: The cry1Ac toxin produced by the transgenic sugarcane plants binds to cadherin receptors in the insect gut, leading to membrane insertion, pore formation, and toxin oligomerization, resulting in insect mortality.

genes: Osa-miR396c (microRNA, repressor of GRF family genes, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of Osa-miR396c eliminates vernalization requirement for flowering in Agrostis stolonifera, but does not affect long-day requirements.
mechanism: Osa-miR396c represses GRF family genes, which modulates vernalization pathway genes (VRN1, VRN2, VRN3) to bypass vernalization requirement.

genes: CeWRI4 (WRI4-like gene, promotes cuticular wax biosynthesis and deposition, Cyperus esculentus)
phenotype: Overexpression of CeWRI4 improves drought stress tolerance in Arabidopsis by reducing stomatal conductance, transpiration rate, chlorophyll leaching, water loss and improving water use efficiency (WUE).
mechanism: CeWRI4 promotes cuticular wax biosynthesis and deposition, which lowers chlorophyll leaching, stomatal conductance, transpiration rate, water loss and improves water use efficiency under drought stress.

genes: miR156 (microRNA, regulator of gene expression, Medicago sativa)
phenotype: miR156 overexpression increases proline and antioxidant contents in alfalfa under heat stress.
mechanism: NA

genes: bar (ammonium glufosinate resistance, source: Agrobacterium tumefaciens), CFP (enhanced cyan fluorescent protein, source: synthetic), GFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein, source: synthetic), YFP (enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, source: synthetic), RFP (mCherry variant of red fluorescent protein, source: synthetic)
