phenotype: Fluorescence expression in carrot callus cells with varying intensities depending on the fluorescent protein used (CFP, GFP, YFP, RFP).
mechanism: NA

genes: BrrADC2.2 (arginine decarboxylase, involved in putrescine synthesis, Brassica rapa var. rapa), BrrICE1.1 (Inducer of CBF Expression 1, transcription factor, Brassica rapa var. rapa)
phenotype: Overexpression of BrrADC2.2 and BrrICE1.1 increases putrescine accumulation, enhancing freezing tolerance in Brassica rapa var. rapa.
mechanism: BrrICE1.1 binds to the BrrADC2.2 promoter, activating BrrADC2.2 to promote putrescine synthesis, which enhances freezing tolerance.

genes: Gly m Bd 28K (major allergen, source: Glycine max), Gly m Bd 30K (major allergen, source: Glycine max)
phenotype: No Gly m Bd 28K or Gly m Bd 30K protein accumulated in the seeds of the Cas9-free plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaMYB344 (transcriptional activator, weak, wheat)
phenotype: Overexpression of TaMYB344 enhances drought, heat, and high salt stress tolerance in Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: NA

genes: gRNA1 (guide RNA, targeting CsPDS gene, synthetic), gRNA2 (guide RNA, targeting CsPDS gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Albino phenotype observed in transgenic embryos due to mutations in the CsPDS gene.
mechanism: Disruption of the CsPDS gene impairs chlorophyll and carotenoid production, resulting in an albino phenotype.

genes: gRNA1 (guide RNA, targeting CsPDS gene, synthetic), gRNA2 (guide RNA, targeting CsPDS gene, synthetic)
phenotype: Albino phenotype observed in transgenic embryos due to mutations in the CsPDS gene.
mechanism: Disruption of the CsPDS gene impairs chlorophyll and carotenoid production, resulting in an albino phenotype.

genes: Pm4CL2 (4-coumarate-CoA ligase, involved in lignin biosynthesis, Prunus)
phenotype: Enhanced resistance to crown gall disease, with relative expression of Pm4CL2 being ~14-fold higher than the control group at 12 h post-treatment.
mechanism: Pm4CL2 functions crucially during the plant defense response by enhancing lignin biosynthesis, which contributes to increased resistance against the pathogen A. tumefaciens.

genes: OsERA1 (OsERA1, alternative transcript, Oryza sativa L. ssp japonica cv. Nipponbare)
phenotype: The osera1 mutants display increased primary root growth and sensitivity to ABA.
mechanism: OsERA1 is a negative regulator of ABA signaling, similar to Arabidopsis thaliana ERA1.

genes: AtAHL20 (transcription factor, negative regulator of flowering time, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtAHL20 causes late flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana under both short and long days.
mechanism: AtAHL20 is a negative regulator of FT expression and other downstream flowering time regulating genes.

genes: CsAHL20 (transcription factor, negative regulator of flowering time, Camelina sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of CsAHL20 confers a late-flowering phenotype in Camelina sativa via suppression of CsFT expression.
mechanism: CsAHL20 acts as a photoperiod-independent negative regulator of transition to flowering.

genes: TaABF3 (abscisic acid responsive element binding factor 3, drought stress response, Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Transgenic Arabidopsis plants overexpressing TaABF3 displayed enhanced drought tolerance.
mechanism: NA

genes: PpOle1 (Pp1S84_138V6.1, oleosin, Physcomitrium patens), PpSeipin325 (Pp1S325_14V6.1, seipin, Physcomitrium patens), AtLDAP1 (At1g67360, lipid droplet associated protein 1, Arabidopsis thaliana), PTS (AAS86323, patchoulol synthase, synthetic), LP4/2A (LP4/2A linker, synthetic)
gene_construct: ZmUbi:PpOle1, ZmUbi:PpOle1-Venus, ZmUbi:PpOle1-PTS, ZmUbi:PpOle1-LP4/2A-PTS, ZmUbi:PpSeipin325, ZmUbi:PpSeipin325-Venus, ZmUbi:PpSeipin325-PTS, ZmUbi:AtLDAP1, ZmUbi:AtLDAP1-Venus, ZmUbi:PpLDAP1-PTS, ZmUbi:PTS
phenotype: Expression of PpOle1, PpSeipin325, AtLDAP1, and PTS in Physcomitrium patens leads to altered lipid droplet (LD) localization and increased patchoulol production.
mechanism: Oleosins and seipin localize to LDs, while AtLDAP1 and PTS are targeted to LDs, influencing lipid droplet dynamics and patchoulol biosynthesis.

genes: TaClpS1 (chloroplast-localized protein with ClpS domain and transit peptide, source: Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Knockdown of TaClpS1 via VIGS increases wheat resistance against Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Pst), accompanied by increased hypersensitive response (HR), reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and expression of TaPR1 and TaPR2, and reduced number of haustoria, length of infection hypha, and infection area of Pst.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaClpS1 (chloroplast-localized protein with ClpS domain and transit peptide, source: Triticum aestivum)
phenotype: Heterologous expression of TaClpS1 in Nicotiana benthamiana enhanced the infection by Phytophthora parasitica.
mechanism: NA

genes: GRPL1 (AT4G18280, multi-stress responsive gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GRPL1 increases salt, drought, and heat stress tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, as evidenced by higher survival rates, improved fresh weight, and enhanced chlorophyll content under stress conditions.
mechanism: GRPL1 is strongly induced under abiotic stresses, suggesting a potential role in modulating plant's response to abiotic stresses.

genes: GRPL1 (AT4G18280, multi-stress responsive gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: pGRPL1::GUS transgenic lines showed weak GUS staining under control conditions but strong induction of pGRPL1 promoter activity under abiotic stresses, as indicated by strong GUS staining.
mechanism: The promoter activity of GRPL1 is strongly induced under abiotic stresses, indicating its role in stress response.

genes: OpWRKY2 (transcription factor, regulates camptothecin biosynthesis, Ophiorrhiza pumila)
phenotype: Overexpression of OpWRKY2 increases camptothecin levels in O. pumila hairy roots.
mechanism: OpWRKY2 positively regulates camptothecin biosynthesis by binding to the W-box in the OpTDC promoter and activating the expression of OpTDC.

genes: OpWRKY2 (transcription factor, regulates camptothecin biosynthesis, Ophiorrhiza pumila)
phenotype: Silencing of OpWRKY2 via SRDX repression domain decreases camptothecin levels in O. pumila hairy roots.
mechanism: OpWRKY2-SRDX repressor domain suppresses OpWRKY2 activity, leading to decreased expression of OpTDC and reduced camptothecin biosynthesis.

genes: SpG (SpCas9 variant, engineered nuclease, synthetic), SpRY (SpCas9 variant, engineered nuclease, synthetic), hAID*Δ (cytidine deaminase, foreign gene, Homo sapiens), TadA8e (adenosine deaminase, foreign gene, synthetic)
phenotype: SpRY-fused hAID*Δ and TadA8e induce C-to-T and A-to-G conversions in target genes with non-canonical PAMs, and SpRY causes high-frequency self-editing events in T-DNA fragments.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsAAP4 (neutral amino acid transporter, splicing variant, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsAAP4 splicing variants increases rice tillering and grain yield, with enhanced neutral amino acid concentrations of Val, Pro, Thr, and Leu.
mechanism: OsAAP4 may affect nitrogen transport and metabolism, and auxin, cytokinin signaling in regulating rice tillering.

genes: OsAAP4 (neutral amino acid transporter, splicing variant, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsAAP4 RNA interference (RNAi) and mutant lines displayed opposite trends compared with overexpressing (OE) lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: CaNAC46 (transcription factor, involved in abiotic stress resistance, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CaNAC46 improves the tolerance of transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana plants to drought and salt stresses, resulting in longer roots and more lateral roots under prolonged drought and high salt stress conditions.
mechanism: CaNAC46 is a positive regulator that activates ROS-scavenging enzymes and enhances root formation. It promotes the expression of SOD, POD, RD29B, RD20, LDB18, ABI, IAA4, and P5CS, while the expression levels of stress-responsive genes such as ABA2, P5CS, DREB, RD22, CAT, and POD are down-regulated in TRV2-CaNAC46 plants.

genes: HpDGAT2D (acyl-CoA:diacylglycerol acyltransferase 2, TAG biosynthesis, Hydrilla verticillata)
phenotype: Heterologous expression of HpDGAT2D significantly increased TAG content and promoted MUFAs and PUFAs contents in Arabidopsis thaliana and Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
mechanism: NA

genes: GmbZIP1 (AREB/ABF transcription factor, regulator of nodulation and ABA response, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmbZIP1 results in reduced rhizobial infection and decreased nodule number in soybean. In Arabidopsis, it increases sensitivity to ABA during seed germination and postgerminative growth and confers enhanced drought tolerance.
mechanism: GmbZIP1 directly binds to the promoter of GmENOD40–1, a marker gene for nodule formation, to repress its expression.

genes: MLX56 (anti-herbivory defense protein, source: mulberry)
phenotype: Overexpression of MLX56 increases resistance to S. litura, F. occidentalis, and H. vigintioctopunctata, with line 73 showing significantly higher resistance than line 69 and controls.
mechanism: MLX56 causes abnormal swelling of the plasma membrane (PM) by binding to chitin, creating a barrier to insect digestion. This anti-digestive effect may also target chitin-containing structures in thrips and beetles.

genes: AtDREB1a (transcription factor, stress response, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic chickpea lines exhibited higher relative water content, longer chlorophyll retention capacity, higher osmotic adjustment, enhanced quantum yield of PSII, electron transport rate at saturated irradiance levels, and higher seed yield under severe drought stress.
mechanism: AtDREB1a modifies important physiological traits, including osmotic adjustment, chlorophyll retention, and water use efficiency, to enhance drought tolerance.

genes: CaATHB-12 (transcription factor, regulates cold stress response, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CaATHB-12 in Arabidopsis decreases the level of antioxidant enzymes activities.
mechanism: NA

genes: CaATHB-12 (transcription factor, regulates cold stress response, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: CaATHB-12 silencing increased the antioxidant enzyme activities in the fruits of pepper, exposed to cold stress.
mechanism: NA

genes: AhRS3 (resveratrol synthase, resveratrol biosynthesis, Arachis hypogaea)
phenotype: Overexpression of AhRS3 increases resveratrol and piceid biosynthesis in Oryza sativa subsp. japonica cv. Dongjin.
mechanism: AhRS3 catalyzes the synthesis of resveratrol via the phenylpropanoid pathway, leading to increased resveratrol and piceid production.

genes: miR408b (microRNA, regulates fungal disease resistance, Zea mays)
phenotype: Ectopic accumulation of miR408b contributes to increased susceptibility to F. verticillioides in the susceptible genotype.
mechanism: miR408b likely plays a negative role in FER resistance, possibly through control of target genes involved in lignin biosynthesis, leading to hypersensitivity and epidermis rupture.

genes: Avr-Pita (effector protein, suppresses host innate immunity by perturbing ROS metabolism, Magnaporthe oryzae), OsCOX11 (cytochrome c oxidase assembly protein, key regulator of mitochondrial ROS metabolism, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of Avr-Pita increases susceptibility to M. oryzae and suppresses PAMP-triggered defense responses. Overexpression of OsCOX11 increases susceptibility to M. oryzae, whereas OsCOX11-knockdown plants show resistance to M. oryzae.
mechanism: Avr-Pita enhances COX activity, decreasing ROS accumulation, thereby suppressing host innate immunity by perturbing ROS metabolism in the mitochondria. OsCOX11 regulates mitochondrial ROS metabolism, and its overexpression or knockdown alters susceptibility to M. oryzae.

genes: rty (RNY, auxin and ABA biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic strawberry plants show increased IAA and ABA contents, enhanced adventitious root and trichome production, improved water use efficiency, and reduced water loss rate under drought conditions.
mechanism: rty improves drought tolerance by promoting auxin and ABA accumulation, leading to increased root production, trichome density, and stomatal closure.

genes: HbCAld5H1 (catalyzes the hydroxylation of monolignols, involved in lignin biosynthesis, Hevea brasiliensis)
phenotype: Overexpression of HbCAld5H1 increases secondary xylem thickness and syringyl lignin content, while antisense constructs reduce secondary xylem thickness and syringyl lignin content in Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: HbCAld5H1 regulates lignin biosynthesis, specifically affecting syringyl monolignol composition in secondary cell walls, which influences cell wall thickness and lignin distribution.

genes: QsuB (3-dehydroshikimate dehydratase, from Corynebacterium glutamicum)
phenotype: Engineered switchgrass lines containing a pShOMT::QsuB construct showed reductions of lignin content, improvements of biomass saccharification efficiency, and accumulated higher amount of protocatechuate compared to control plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: IbVP1 (vacuolar pyrophosphatase, enhances starch biosynthesis and sucrose transport, Ipomoea batatas)
phenotype: Overexpression of IbVP1 increases photosynthesis ability, sucrose content in source leaves, phloem loading, and sucrose transport to sink organs, resulting in increased total starch content and yield of storage roots.
mechanism: IbVP1 enhances starch biosynthesis by upregulating AGPase gene expression, which is the rate-limiting enzyme in starch metabolism. It also increases phloem loading and sucrose transport, leading to increased carbon fixation in storage roots.

genes: ERF2 (ERF transcription factor, regulates resistance to S. lycopersici, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: ERF2-silenced plants exhibited a susceptible phenotype after inoculation with S. lycopersici.
mechanism: ERF2 may directly or indirectly regulate Pto, PR1b1 and PR-P2 expression and enhance tomato resistance to S. lycopersici. ERF2 played a key role in multiple SA, JA and ROS signaling pathways to confer resistance to invasion by S. lycopersici.

genes: SiFBA5 (cold-responsive gene, involved in initial stress response, S. involucrata)
phenotype: Transgenic tomato plants overexpressing SiFBA5 displayed increased cold tolerance and photosynthetic efficiency compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: PeWRKY31 (WRKY transcription factor, salt tolerance and insect resistance, Populus × euramericana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PeWRKY31 improves salt tolerance and insect resistance in Nicotiana tabacum L.
mechanism: Elevated expression of genes related to glutathione metabolism, plant hormone signal transduction, and MAPK signaling pathways, which are important in plant salt tolerance and insect resistance.

genes: ictB (bicarbonate transporter, source: Synechococcus PCC 7942), PAT (Phosphinothricin acetyltransferase, source: Streptomyces viridochromogenes)
gene_construct: Zea mays RbcS promoter-ictB-Zea mays RbcS 3′ untranslated region-nos terminator---Zea mays ubiquitin promoter-PAT-CaMV 35S terminator
phenotype: Transgenic maize plants with ictB insertion showed increased starch and sucrose content, and improved grain yield in field trials.
mechanism: ictB interacts with photosynthetic proteins and enzymes involved in glycolysis and starch synthesis, enhancing carbohydrate metabolism downstream of photosynthesis.

genes: Cel6A (endoglucanase from Thermobifida fusca, foreign gene), TetC (5′ DB peptide from TetC bacterial protein, foreign gene)
phenotype: TetC-cel6A tobacco plants produce Cel6A at levels of up to 28% of total soluble protein (TSP) with a slight dwarf phenotype but no loss in biomass.
mechanism: NA

genes: TALEN (transcription activator-like effector nuclease) (gene editing tool, synthetic)
phenotype: Induction of mutations in the HvPAPhy_a promoter region in barley.
mechanism: TALEN-3 induces targeted double-strand breaks at the HvPAPhy_a promoter, leading to short deletions and heterozygous mutations.

genes: TALEN (transcription activator-like effector nuclease) (gene editing tool, synthetic)
phenotype: Increased transformation efficiency and mutation frequency in barley using the N∆152/C∆63 scaffold.
mechanism: Truncation of the TALEN backbone at the N- and C-termini reduces T-DNA size, increasing transformation efficiency and mutation frequency.

genes: hptII (hygromycin phosphotransferase 2, conferring hygromycin resistance, Arabidopsis thaliana), Rluc (Renilla luciferase, conferring Renilla luciferase activity, Renilla reniformis), TBS (Transformation Booster Sequence, enhancer blocking insulator, synthetic), Fluc (Firefly luciferase, conferring firefly luciferase activity, Photinus pyralis), GUSPlus (β-glucuronidase encoding reporter gene, conferring β-glucuronidase activity, Escherichia coli), bar (bialaphos resistance, conferring glufosinate herbicide tolerance, Streptomyces hygroscopicus), eGFP (enhanced Green Fluorescent Protein, conferring green fluorescence, jellyfish), tdTomatoER (red fluorescent protein, nonfunctional in pollen, Drosophila melanogaster), EPSPS (5-enol-pyruvylshikimate-3-phospate synthase, conferring glyphosate herbicide tolerance, Escherichia coli), nptII (neomycin phosphotransferase 2, conferring paromomycin resistance, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Transgenic rice plants exhibited hygromycin resistance, Renilla and firefly luciferase activity, β-glucuronidase activity, glufosinate herbicide tolerance, green fluorescence, nonfunctional red fluorescence in pollen, glyphosate herbicide tolerance, and paromomycin resistance.
mechanism: NA

genes: ATG8a (autophagy-related protein 8a, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ATG8a reduces symptom severity in Arabidopsis thaliana infected with D. dadantii.
mechanism: Enhanced autophagy activity positively contributes to Arabidopsis tolerance to D. dadantii.

genes: PttVAP27-17 (vesicle-associated membrane protein (VAMP)-associated protein, Populus tremula × tremuloides)
phenotype: Overexpression of PttVAP27-17 increases whole-tree saccharification yields due to increases in biomass production in Populus tremula × tremuloides.
mechanism: NA

genes: MAX1 (MAX1, SL-biosynthesis gene, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: MAX1-Cas9 mutated plants show decreased plant height, increased axillary bud growth, and reduced dry root mass compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: The MAX1 mutation leads to a reduction in orobanchol content, a major strigolactone (SL) in tomato root exudates, which acts as a specific germination inducer for P. aegyptiaca. This reduction in SL content results in reduced germination of the parasitic weed.

genes: MaMAPK3 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 3, cold response, Musa spp.)
phenotype: RNAi of MaMAPK3 causes wilting and severe necrotic symptoms in banana leaves after cold exposure.
mechanism: RNAi of MaMAPK3 significantly changes the expressions of cold-responsive genes and oxidoreductase activity in WT plants, but no changes are observed in transgenic plants.

genes: MaICE1 (inducer of CBF expression 1, cold response, Musa spp.)
phenotype: Over-expression of MaICE1 in Cavendish banana results in superior cold resistance compared to WT plants.
mechanism: MaICE1 interacts with MaMAPK3, and its expression level is significantly decreased in MaMAPK3 RNAi transgenic plants.

genes: POD P7 (peroxidase P7, cold response, Musa spp.)
phenotype: POD P7 gene is significantly up-regulated in MaICE1-overexpressing transgenic plants compared with WT plants.
mechanism: POD P7 was proved to interact with MaICE1.

genes: OsMBD707 (class I MBD protein, involved in rice growth and development, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Transgenic rice overexpressing OsMBD707 displayed larger tiller angles and reduced photoperiod sensitivity—delayed flowering under short day (SD) and early flowering under long day (LD).
mechanism: NA

genes: CgWRKY57 (WRKY transcription factor, involved in abiotic stress response, Cymbidium goeringii)
phenotype: Overexpression of CgWRKY57 in Arabidopsis thaliana reduces root length and germination rate under ABA stress compared to wild type plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: NtCIPK11 (salt and drought stress tolerance, Nitraria tangutorum)
phenotype: Overexpression of NtCIPK11 improves seed germination on medium containing different levels of NaCl and increases plant growth under salt stress, with longer roots under salt or drought conditions compared to WT plants.
mechanism: NtCIPK11 promotes plant growth and mitigates damage associated with salt stress by regulating the expression of genes controlling proline accumulation.

genes: GgSQE1 (squalene epoxidase, catalyzes the stereo-specific conversion of squalene to 2,3-oxidosqualene, Glycyrrhiza glabra)
phenotype: Overexpression of GgSQE1 increases α-tocopherol (vitamin E) accumulation in Nicotiana tabacum compared to control and empty vector-transformed plants.
mechanism: GgSQE1 enhances sterol biosynthesis, leading to increased phytosterol content, including α-tocopherol.

genes: PEN1 (pentacyclic triterpene synthase 1, key enzyme in DMNT biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PEN1 increases resistance to P. xylostella infestation, with significantly lower survival rates of larvae compared to non-transgenic controls.
mechanism: PEN1 encodes the key enzyme responsible for DMNT biosynthesis, which repels and kills P. xylostella larvae by inducing strong resistance in transgenic plants.

genes: OsDRAP1 (OsDRAP1, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsDRAP1 increases seedling survival rates by ~40% under 120 mM NaCl stress in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsDRAP1 enhances salt tolerance by maintaining membrane integrity and enhancing the ROS-scavenging system.

genes: CkWRKY33 (WRKY transcription factor, Group-I type, Caragana korshinskii)
phenotype: Overexpression of CkWRKY33 increases survival rates, relative soluble sugar, proline, and peroxidase contents, but decreases malondialdehyde contents in Arabidopsis thaliana under drought stress.
mechanism: NA

genes: Fra a 1.02 (hypothetical RNAi target, allergen protein, Fragaria x ananassa)
phenotype: Silencing of Fra a 1.02 in strawberry fruits has no effect on fruit color development.
mechanism: NA

genes: AITR3 (ABA-induced transcription repressor, negative regulator in ABA signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana), AITR4 (ABA-induced transcription repressor, negative regulator in ABA signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
gene_construct: pHEE401E vector with CRISPR/Cas9 system targeting AITR3 and AITR4
phenotype: Knockout of AITR3 and AITR4 in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to reduced sensitivity to ABA and enhanced tolerance to drought and salt, with no effect on plant growth and development.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsGRP3 (glycine-rich protein 3, drought stress response regulator, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsGRP3 increases drought tolerance, while knockdown decreases drought tolerance in Oryza sativa.
mechanism: OsGRP3 modulates the transcript level and mRNA stability of stress-responsive genes, including ROS-related genes, thereby reducing ROS accumulation and conferring drought tolerance.

genes: GhARF2b (auxin response factor, homolog of AtARF2, Gossypium hirsutum)
phenotype: Overexpression of GhARF2b inhibits fiber cell elongation but promotes initiation; RNAi downregulation results in fewer but longer fibers.
mechanism: GhARF2b directly interacts with GhHOX3 and represses the transcriptional activity of GhHOX3 on target genes.

genes: Bract1 (glutathione S-transferase, anthocyanin-related, poinsettia)
phenotype: Overexpression of Bract1 wild-type allele restores the anthocyanin phenotype in Arabidopsis tt19 mutants.
mechanism: NA

genes: GmCHIT1 (chitinase, upregulated during P. pachyrhizi infection, Glycine max)
phenotype: GFP fluorescence detected around appressoria after P. pachyrhizi inoculation, with no response to ethylene or methyl jasmonate treatments.
mechanism: NA

genes: VvBAM1 (beta-amylase, starch hydrolysis, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvBAM1 increases total amylase and BAM activities by 6.5- and 6.01-fold, respectively, and increases glucose and sucrose contents while decreasing starch contents by 1.5-fold under low temperature (LT) stress in tomato plants.
mechanism: VvBAM1 promotes ROS scavenging and improves cold tolerance by modulating starch hydrolysis to affect soluble sugar levels.

genes: ClBG1 (ClBG1, β-glucosidase, Citrullus lanatus)
gene_construct: CRISPR/Cas9-targeted sites in ClBG1 gene (two gRNAs targeting first exon)
phenotype: Clbg1-mutant lines showed significantly decreased seed size, including decreased seed weight, length, and width.
mechanism: ClBG1 dysfunction led to decreased ABA content in seeds, which affected cell number and size, ultimately reducing seed size.

genes: AhHDA1 (histone deacetylase 1, histone deacetylase, Arachis hypogaea)
phenotype: AhHDA1 overexpression in hairy roots caused growth retardation, increased accumulation of superoxide anions and hydrogen peroxide, and altered metabolic pathways including upregulation of flavonoid, isoflavonoid, and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis genes and downregulation of photosynthesis-related genes.
mechanism: AhHDA1 overexpression altered histone acetylation levels, which correlated with changes in gene expression, affecting metabolic pathways and root development.

genes: MdATG8i (autophagy-related gene, involved in autophagy, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdATG8i increases plant height, trunk diameter, total fresh weight (TFW), total dry weight (TDW), and relative growth rate (RGR) under long-term moderate drought stress. The MdATG8i-OE apple lines also maintain higher relative water content (RWC) and water use efficiency (WUE) compared to WT plants.
mechanism: MdATG8i enhances autophagic activity, which contributes to the accumulation of carbohydrates and amino acids, leading to better osmotic adjustment, improved photosynthetic capacity, and increased ROS scavenging under drought conditions.

genes: SPPV117 (viral protein, antigenic subunit vaccine candidate, synthetic)
phenotype: Recombinant SPPV117 protein accumulated to about 0.3% and 0.9% of total soluble protein in leaves when expressed from psbA and rrn promoters, respectively. The protein yield was 19.67 ± 1.25 µg g−1 (FW).
mechanism: NA

genes: AbhemC (PBG deaminase, catalyzes PBG to Urogen III conversion, Ananas comosus var. bracteatus)
phenotype: Transgenic tobacco leaves with pFGC5941-AbhemC-RNAi vector were substantially less green with significantly reduced hemC expression and Chl content, as well as reduced PBGD enzyme activity and significantly decreased content of Chl biosynthesis precursors from Urogen III onwards.
mechanism: The absence of hemC expression reduces the enzyme activity of PBGD, which blocks the transition of PBG to Urogen III, and in turn suppresses Chl synthesis leading to the pale-green leaf color.

genes: katE (E. coli catalase gene, bacterial catalase, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Overexpression of katE increases resistance to Fusarium wilt by improving the plant's ability to remove H2O2, leading to enhanced activity of defense enzymes such as CAT, SOD, and POD.
mechanism: The expression of the katE gene in tomato plant cells enhances the enzymatic H2O2 scavenging mechanism, which involves SOD and CAT enzymes. This reduces oxidative stress and prevents damage caused by excessive H2O2.

genes: RrNUDX1 (NUDX1 gene related to monoterpenes biosynthesis, Rosa rugosa)
phenotype: Overexpression of RrNUDX1 increases leaf width and length by 10.83 mm and 8.19 mm, respectively, and enhances fragrance with significantly increased methyl benzoate content in Petunia hybrida.
mechanism: NA

genes: MeSWEET10a (sucrose transporter, induced during CBB infection, Manihot esculenta), TAL20 (transcription activator, Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. manihotis), GFP (fluorescent protein, synthetic)
modification_type: expression of foreign gene, gene editing (CRISPR)
phenotype: Scarless integration of GFP at the 3' end of MeSWEET10a allows visualization of MeSWEET10a-GFP expression in response to Xanthomonas infection.
mechanism: The TAL20 promoter drives expression of the TA component, enabling nondestructive screening for HDR products. The HDEL ER-localization signal sequesters the tagged protein away from the plasma membrane.

genes: B'φ (PP2A B'φ subunit, overexpression, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of B'φ decreases mycorrhization frequency in vermiculite-grown tomato plants and reduces the number of seeds per fruit by 60% compared to the original cultivar.
mechanism: B'φ overexpression is related to abscisic acid and gibberellic acid responses involved in plant growth and mycorrhization.

genes: CER3 (wax biosynthesis gene, from Arabidopsis thaliana, source: Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of CER3 increases epicuticular wax content in Gossypium hirsutum, reducing whitefly attraction and CLCuV titer.
mechanism: Increased epicuticular wax content reduces whitefly attraction and virus transmission by altering the interaction between wax compounds and whitefly chitin.

genes: OsGATA16 (GATA-type zinc finger transcription factor, improves cold tolerance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsGATA16 improves cold tolerance of rice at seedling stage.
mechanism: OsGATA16 acts as a positive regulator of cold tolerance by repressing some cold-related genes such as OsWRKY45–1, OsSRFP1, OsCYL4 and OsMYB30.

genes: TcFT (florigen, flowering time regulator, Theobroma cacao)
phenotype: Transgenic expression of TcFT partially rescues the Arabidopsis ft-10 mutant to wild-type flowering time.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtFT (florigen, flowering time regulator, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtFT in cacao resulted in precocious flowering in cacao tissue culture.
mechanism: NA

genes: thaumatin II (thaumatin II gene, a protein involved in plant defense, Cucumis sativus)
phenotype: NA
mechanism: NA

genes: RUS6 (embryo development, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: RUS6 knockout mutants display a strong embryo-lethal phenotype, with homozygous mutants not surviving and embryo lethality occurring at the mid-globular stage.
mechanism: RUS6 is required for early embryo development, and its loss results in embryo lethality at the mid-globular stage.

genes: RUS6 (embryo development, gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The embryo-lethality phenotype was complemented by a RUS6::RUS6-GFP transgene.
mechanism: NA

genes: syn cry1Ab (insecticidal toxin, synthetic, Bacillus thuringiensis), bar (herbicide resistance, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: Transgenic pigeon pea lines expressing syn cry1Ab showed 70–90% mortality rate and 79.1–85.5% bodyweight reduction in H. armigera larvae.
mechanism: NA

genes: cre (recombinase, synthetic, pX6-GFP plant DNA expression vector)
phenotype: Cre recombinase expression enabled the elimination of the selectable marker (bar) gene through Cre/lox-mediated recombination.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtGLK1 (transcription factor, regulates anthocyanin biosynthesis, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtGLK1 enhances the accumulation of anthocyanin in transgenic Arabidopsis seedlings.
mechanism: AtGLK1 acts upstream of MYBL2, which is a key negative regulator of anthocyanin biosynthesis, to genetically regulate sucrose-induced anthocyanin biosynthesis.

genes: NtLs (lateral shoot formation, knockdown, Nicotiana tabacum), NtBl1 (lateral shoot formation, knockdown, Nicotiana tabacum), NtREV (lateral shoot formation, knockdown, Nicotiana tabacum), VE7 (highly expressed in axillary bud primordial stages, knockdown, Nicotiana tabacum), VE12 (highly expressed in axillary bud primordial stages, knockdown, Nicotiana tabacum)

phenotype: Inhibited development of secondary and tertiary lateral shoots in tobacco.
mechanism: NA

genes: CsLAZY1 (regulates shoot gravitropism, tea plant)
phenotype: CsLAZY1 overexpressed plants responded more effectively than wild-type plants to a gravity inversion treatment under light and dark conditions.
mechanism: CsLAZY1 plays an important role in regulating shoot gravitropism in tea plants.

genes: AITRL (ABA response transcription repressor, overexpression, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AITRL increases ABA sensitivity in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AITRL negatively regulates ABA responses by modulating the expression of ABA signaling component genes.

genes: XTH43 (xyloglucan endotransglycosylase/hydrolase, involved in cell wall remodeling, Glycine max)
phenotype: XTH43 overexpression decreases H. glycines parasitism by 70–89% (p < 0.05). XTH43 RNAi increases H. glycines parasitism.
mechanism: XTH43 overexpression increases XyG content and shortens XyG chain length, potentially strengthening the cell wall and impairing nematode parasitism. XTH43 RNAi decreases XyG content and chain length, weakening the cell wall and increasing nematode parasitism.

genes: XTH43 (xyloglucan endotransglycosylase/hydrolase, involved in cell wall remodeling, Glycine max)
phenotype: XTH43 overexpression increases XyG content and shortens XyG chain length, potentially strengthening the cell wall and impairing H. glycines parasitism.
mechanism: XTH43 overexpression increases XyG content and shortens XyG chain length, potentially strengthening the cell wall and impairing nematode parasitism.

genes: XTH43 (xyloglucan endotransglycosylase/hydrolase, involved in cell wall remodeling, Glycine max)
phenotype: XTH43 RNAi decreases XyG content and chain length, weakening the cell wall and increasing H. glycines parasitism.
mechanism: XTH43 RNAi decreases XyG content and chain length, weakening the cell wall and increasing nematode parasitism.

genes: RCD2 (pheophorbide a oxygenase, key enzyme in the PAO pathway, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: The complementation of RCD2 in rcd2 restores normal chlorophyll degradation and reduces lesion formation.
mechanism: RCD2 encodes pheophorbide a oxygenase, a key enzyme in the PAO pathway. The I576F mutation in RCD2 leads to impaired PAO function, resulting in the accumulation of Pheide a, which causes necrotic lesions.

genes: RCD2 (pheophorbide a oxygenase, key enzyme in the PAO pathway, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of RCD2 in Oryza sativa results in rapid cell death and necrotic lesions.
mechanism: The A1726T mutation in the RCD2 gene leads to impaired PAO function, resulting in the accumulation of Pheide a, which causes necrotic lesions.

genes: CytoRP (cytosolic PRORP, truncated PRORP2 with NLS deletion, source: Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: CytoRP lines showed statistically significant reductions of both TYMV and ORMV RNA content as compared to wild type plants in some sets of experiments.
mechanism: NA

genes: CytoRP (cytosolic PRORP, truncated PRORP2 with NLS deletion, source: Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Cisgenic CytoRP plant lines were generated by genome editing through the deletion of 16 amino acids of PRORP2 starting at the 11th amino acid using CRISPR-Cas9 technology.
mechanism: NA

genes: CytoRP (cytosolic PRORP, truncated PRORP2 with NLS deletion, source: Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: The selected plants contain the three PRORP expressed from endogenous genes, as well as the additional CytoRP expressed from the transgene and localized in the cytosol.
mechanism: NA

genes: Osa-miR159a (microRNA, regulates target genes, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of Osa-miR159a increases rice resistance to M. oryzae.
mechanism: Osa-miR159a positively regulates rice immunity against M. oryzae by downregulating its target genes.

genes: Osa-miR159a (microRNA, regulates target genes, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockdown of Osa-miR159a via STTM expression enhances susceptibility to M. oryzae.
mechanism: Osa-miR159a positively regulates rice immunity against M. oryzae by downregulating its target genes.

genes: OsGAMYB (transcription factor, target of Osa-miR159a, Oryza sativa), OsGAMYBL (transcription factor, target of Osa-miR159a, Oryza sativa), OsZF (transcription factor, target of Osa-miR159a, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockout of OsGAMYB, OsGAMYBL, and OsZF leads to resistance to M. oryzae.
mechanism: Osa-miR159a positively regulates rice immunity against M. oryzae by downregulating its target genes.

genes: Cry1C* (insect resistance, synthetic, Bacillus thuringiensis)
phenotype: Transgenic Cry1C* rice T1C-19 shows lower vegetative and reproductive growth abilities than parental rice MH63 in farmland or uncultivated land without weed competition, but no significant differences under farmland or uncultivated land with weed competition.
mechanism: NA

genes: PbCSE1 (Pbr002315.3, CSE family member involved in lignin biosynthesis, Pyrus communis)
phenotype: Overexpression of PbCSE1 in transgenic Arabidopsis plants increased lignin content in stems by 31.74% compared to wild-type (WT), with the OE6 line showing the highest increase.
mechanism: PbCSE1 promotes lignin deposition by upregulating lignin biosynthetic genes, particularly HCT and C3H, in transgenic Arabidopsis stems.

genes: PbCSE1 (Pbr002315.3, CSE family member involved in lignin biosynthesis, Pyrus communis)
phenotype: Transient overexpression of PbCSE1 in pear fruits increased lignin content by 26.9% at the injection sites compared to non-injected sites.
mechanism: PbCSE1 promotes lignin deposition in pear fruits by upregulating lignin biosynthetic genes, particularly HCT and C3H.

genes: PtoPIP1;1 (root-specific aquaporin, poplar)
phenotype: Constitutive overexpression of PtoPIP1;1 accelerates bolting and flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PtoPIP1;1 overexpression increases turgor pressure and changes water status, promoting faster cell growth in leaves and roots. It upregulates flowering-related genes (CRY1, CRY2, FT, SOC1) and downregulates the floral repressor FLC.

genes: OsOXO2 (oxalate oxidase, blast resistance, Oryza sativa), OsOXO3 (oxalate oxidase, blast resistance, Oryza sativa), OsOXO4 (oxalate oxidase, blast resistance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsOXO2, OsOXO3, and OsOXO4 individually enhances panicle blast resistance in rice.
mechanism: OsOXO genes modulate H2O2 accumulation and PR gene expression, and mediate panicle blast resistance through activation of JA and ABA signaling pathways and suppression of SA signaling pathway.

genes: OsOXO2 (oxalate oxidase, blast resistance, Oryza sativa), OsOXO3 (oxalate oxidase, blast resistance, Oryza sativa), OsOXO4 (oxalate oxidase, blast resistance, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Simultaneous silencing of OsOXO2, OsOXO3 and OsOXO4 decreases rice resistance to panicle blast.
mechanism: OsOXO genes modulate H2O2 accumulation and PR gene expression, and mediate panicle blast resistance through activation of JA and ABA signaling pathways and suppression of SA signaling pathway.

genes: NbenIDA1 (NbenIDA1 homeolog, small peptide of the IDA-like family, Nicotiana benthamiana), NbenHAE.1 (receptor, NbenHAE.1, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Inoculation of two VIGS constructs suppressed NbenIDA1 homeologs and NbenHAE.1 expression, arresting corolla abscission and increasing corolla breakstrength.
mechanism: Gene suppression preserved parenchyma tissue at the base of the corolla tube, preventing corolla abscission.

genes: NbenIDA1A (NbenIDA1 homeolog, small peptide of the IDA-like family, Nicotiana benthamiana)
phenotype: Overexpression of NbenIDA1A accelerated corolla senescence and abscission, negatively affecting plant growth.
mechanism: NbenIDA1A overexpression triggered premature corolla senescence and abscission.

genes: OsGSAM (GSAM protein, involved in ALA synthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of the ys53 mutant with the wild-type OsGSAM gene rescues the mutant phenotype, including restored photosynthetic pigment contents and chloroplast development.
mechanism: The point mutation in OsGSAM reduces ALA-synthesis ability, leading to GSA accumulation and affecting the expression of tetrapyrrole biosynthetic and photosynthetic genes.

genes: anaPCS (phytochelatin synthase, from Anabaena sp. PCC 7120)
phenotype: Transformed hairy roots expressing anaPCS accumulated 143.4% and 191% higher arsenic and cadmium, respectively, than control. The bioconcentration factor (BCF) for Cd and As was significantly higher in transformed hairy roots.
mechanism: AnaPCS enhances heavy metal tolerance by increasing phytochelatin (PC) synthesis, which forms metal-complexes sequestered into vacuoles. This is supported by higher PC levels and increased activity of glutathione reductase (GR), which maintains GSH levels for PC synthesis.

genes: ObDMR6 (DMR6 homolog, susceptibility gene for Peronospora belbahrii, Ocimum basilicum)
gene_construct: pKSE401-S1 (AtU6-26 promoter-sgRNA1-AtU6-26 terminator)---pKSE401-S1S2 (AtU6-26 promoter-sgRNA1-AtU6-26 terminator---AtU6-29 promoter-sgRNA2-AtU6-26 terminator)
phenotype: Mutation of ObDMR6 significantly enhanced basil downy mildew resistance, with pathogen biomass reduced by 69–93% and sporangia production reduced by 61–68% compared to wild-type (WT) plants.
mechanism: ObDMR6 plays a significant role in the compatibility of the non-model sweet basil-Peronospora belbahrii pathosystem, and its knockout disrupts the susceptibility factors required for pathogen infection.

genes: Hyd-BMP2 (hydrophobin-BMP2 fusion protein, fusion of hydrophobin and BMP2 for protein expression, synthetic)
phenotype: Hyd-BMP2 fusion protein was expressed in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves and purified using A2P method, with expression levels of 30 ng/g (0.003%) and 180 ng/g (0.018%) in TSP of fresh leaf in the presence and absence of P19 silencing suppressor, respectively.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsFAD2 (fatty acid desaturase 2, involved in fatty acid biosynthesis, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Mutations consisting of deletions of the DNA region between the two target sgRNAs in the FAD2 gene of rice.
mechanism: NA

genes: MdFRK2 (fructokinase 2, involved in fructose metabolism, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdFRK2 in apple and poplar increases cellulose content and thickness of the phloem region.
mechanism: MdFRK2 overexpression shifts fructose 6-phosphate or glucose 6-phosphate towards UDPG formation, increases sucrose synthase (SUSY) activity and transcript levels of PtrSUSY1, and increases sink strength, leading to more carbohydrate availability for increased cambial activity and secondary phloem development.

genes: NtbHLH1 (bHLH transcription factor, regulatory complex component, Chinese Narcissus), NtMYB6 (R2R3-MYB transcription factor, proanthocyanidin biosynthesis regulator, Chinese Narcissus)
phenotype: Ectopic overexpression of NtbHLH1 in tobacco resulted in an increase in anthocyanin accumulation in flowers, and an up-regulation of expression of the endogenous tobacco bHLH AN1 and flavonoid biosynthesis genes. In contrast, the expression level of LAR gene was significantly increased in NtMYB6-transgenic tobacco.
mechanism: NtbHLH1 interacts with NtMYB6 to enhance proanthocyanidin accumulation in Chinese Narcissus. Dual luciferase assays showed that co-infiltration of NtbHLH1 and NtMYB6 significantly activated the promoter of Chinese Narcissus DFR gene.

genes: ZmSOC1 (maize SOC1 gene, MADS-box transcription factor, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmSOC1 promotes flowering and reduces plant height in soybean (Glycine max).
mechanism: ZmSOC1 functions as a flowering pathway integrator, similar to SOC1 in Arabidopsis, and its expression affects the GA signaling pathway (e.g., GID1B) to induce flowering and plant dwarfing.

genes: CEMB-Cry1Ac (Bacillus thuringiensis Cry1Ac toxin, insecticidal, Bacillus thuringiensis), CEMB-Cry2A (Bacillus thuringiensis Cry2A toxin, insecticidal, Bacillus thuringiensis), CEMB-GTGene (modified CP4 EPSPS, herbicide resistance, synthetic)
gene_construct: maize Ubiquitin promoter-CEMB-Cry1Ac-Nos terminator---maize Ubiquitin promoter-CEMB-Cry2A-Nos terminator---maize Ubiquitin promoter-CEMB-GTGene-Nos terminator
phenotype: Transgenic sugarcane lines showed 60–100% insect mortality against Chilo infuscatellus larvae and complete glyphosate tolerance at 3000 mL/ha.
mechanism: CEMB-Cry1Ac and CEMB-Cry2A toxins induce insect mortality through insecticidal activity, while CEMB-GTGene confers glyphosate tolerance by encoding a modified EPSPS enzyme.

genes: LbHLH (leucine zipper helix-loop-helix domain protein, salt tolerance regulator, L. bicolor)
phenotype: Overexpression of LbHLH increases trichome number and reduces root hair number in Arabidopsis thaliana. Transgenic lines show higher germination percentages and longer roots under NaCl treatment, and enhanced osmotic resistance under sorbitol stress.
mechanism: LbHLH might interact with GLABRA1 to influence trichome and root hair development. It enhances salt tolerance by reducing root hair development and enhancing osmotic resistance under NaCl stress.

genes: NtCPS2 (cis-abienol synthase, involved in diterpenoid biosynthesis, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: NtCPS2 knockdown decreases cis-abienol and labdene diol contents, while increasing gibberellin and abscisic acid (ABA) contents in tobacco.
mechanism: NtCPS2 is involved in the biosynthesis of cis-abienol, and its knockdown disrupts this pathway, leading to altered secondary metabolite profiles.

genes: PbCYP78A6 (cytochrome P450, parthenocarpy-related, Pyrus betulaefolia)
phenotype: Ectopic overexpression of PbCYP78A6 contributes to parthenocarpic fruit production in tomato.
mechanism: NA

genes: C4-PEPC (sugarcane phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase, foreign gene, Saccharum spp.)
phenotype: Transgenic rice expressing C4-PEPC displayed shorter primary roots and fewer crown roots at the seedling stage. Total nitrogen content was significantly higher in transgenic rice than in wild type (WT) plants.
mechanism: PEPC affects nitrogen metabolism through regulating GST.

genes: rpk (receptor-like protein kinase, enhances water and oxidative stress tolerance, Zea mays), nced (9-cis-epoxycarotenoid dioxygenase, up-regulates endogenous ABA levels under drought, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of rpk and nced genes increases drought tolerance in maize (Zea mays), with transgenic plants showing significant survival capacity under drought stress compared to control plants.
mechanism: The overexpression of nced increases endogenous ABA levels, leading to lower transpiration rates, while rpk controls reactive oxygen species homeostasis and enhances water and oxidative stress tolerance.

genes: SbMATE (MATE transporter, aluminum tolerance, Sorghum bicolor)
phenotype: Overexpression of SbMATE improves tolerance to aluminum in sugarcane plants, characterized by sustained root growth and exclusion of aluminum from the root apex.
mechanism: NA

genes: MrRPV1 (resistance protein, effector recognition, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of MrRPV1 in Vitis vinifera Shiraz transgenic line S8-1 results in a 92–98% reduction in DM sporulation at 6 days postinoculation compared to wild-type controls.
mechanism: MrRPV1 recognizes the AvrRPV1 effector protein secreted by P. viticola and mediates the activation of the hypersensitive response (HR), leading to leaf resistance to DM.

genes: SVL (SHORT VEGETATIVE PHASE-LIKE, flowering suppression, Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Overexpression of SVL delays floral onset and decreases floral abundance in Populus trichocarpa.
mechanism: NA

genes: GmTCF1a (cold stress response gene, cold tolerance mediator, Glycine max)
phenotype: Ectopic overexpression of GmTCF1a increases plant survival rate and decreases electrolyte leakage under freezing stress in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GmTCF1a enhances cold tolerance and upregulates COR15a levels.

genes: ZmSOC1 (flowering pathway regulator, MADS-box gene, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmSOC1 accelerates flowering, reduces plant height, and increases grain dry weight in Zea mays.
mechanism: ZmSOC1 enhances expression of downstream flowering genes (ZmFT and ZmGI) and modulates metabolic processes, leading to changes in plant growth and flowering.

genes: BoCRP1 (cold resistance protein, source: Brassica oleracea)
phenotype: Overexpression of BoCRP1 increases seed germination rate by ~80% and improves seedling growth under cold stress (4°C) in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum).
mechanism: BoCRP1 enhances cold tolerance by increasing osmoprotectant accumulation (proline and soluble sugars) and modulating antioxidant enzyme activity.

genes: DTA (toxic gene, diphtheria toxin A, Nicotiana tabacum L.)
phenotype: The expression of the optimized DTA gene inhibits the growth of axillary buds in transgenic tobacco plants, with the growth inhibition maintained for 4 weeks compared to normal plants.
mechanism: The DTA toxin acts only at the intended site and does not transfer to other unapplied sites in plants, precisely restricting the toxin to the axillary bud of the 1st leaf without disturbing the size and yield of tobacco leaves.

genes: MiTFL1 (flowering time regulation, mango)
phenotype: Overexpression of MiTFL1 delayed flowering in transgenic Arabidopsis.
mechanism: NA

genes: MiTFL1-1 (flowering time regulation, mango), MiTFL1-3 (flowering time regulation, mango)
phenotype: Overexpression of MiTFL1-1 and MiTFL1-3 affected floral organ development in some transgenic plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsSWEET14 (susceptibility gene for Xoo strains, source: Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica)
phenotype: Editing of the OsSWEET14 promoter in TBR225 rice confers resistance to Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) without yield penalty.
mechanism: Modification of the OsSWEET14 promoter disrupts the binding sites of Xoo TALEs (AvrXa7, PthXo3, TalF, TalC), thereby preventing the induction of OsSWEET14 during infection and reducing susceptibility to bacterial blight.

genes: Gln1-3 (glutamine synthetase, cytosolic, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of Gln1-3 increases total leaf GS activity by approximately three-fold at 15 days after silking (15DAS) and increases kernel yield by an average of 7% compared to control hybrids.
mechanism: NA

genes: VyRCHC114 (E3 ubiquitin ligase, drought tolerance, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VyRCHC114 improves drought tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, increasing transgenic plant survival rate by 30%.
mechanism: VyRCHC114 may regulate the expression of AtCOR15a, AtRD29A, AtERD15, and AtP5CS1, which participate in the response to drought stress.

genes: L.albABCG29 (phosphate transporter, overexpression, Lupinus albus)
phenotype: Overexpression of L.albABCG29 in white lupin hairy root enhanced P accumulation in cluster root under LP and improved plant growth.
mechanism: NA

genes: L.albABCG29 (phosphate transporter, overexpression, Lupinus albus)
phenotype: Overexpression of L.albABCG29 in rice significantly improved P use under combined soil drying and LP by improving root growth associated with increased rhizosheath formation.
mechanism: NA

genes: BnaFAX1-1 (fatty acid exporter, localized to the plastid envelope, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnaFAX1-1 increases biological yield (total plant dry matter), seed yield, and seed oil content per plant in Brassica napus.
mechanism: BnaFAX1-1 overexpression up-regulates gibberellic acid 4 (GA4) biosynthesis, which may contribute to biological yield improvement. Furthermore, oleic acid (C18:1) significantly increases in BnaFAX1-1 overexpression seeds.

genes: GUS (glucuronidase reporter, reporter gene, Escherichia coli)
phenotype: Stable overexpression of GUS genes in grape hyacinth petals confirmed by PCR and GUS quantitative analyses.
mechanism: NA

genes: MaGT (anthocyanidin 3-O-glucosyltransferase, involved in anthocyanin biosynthesis, Muscari armeniacum)
phenotype: Reduced expression of the MaGT gene in transgenic petals caused pigmentation loss by repressing anthocyanin accumulation.
mechanism: MaGT repression leads to reduced anthocyanin accumulation, resulting in pigmentation loss.

genes: GmFULa (transcription factor, regulates plant growth and development, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmFULa increases biomass accumulation, promotes vegetative growth, and increases yield in soybean.
mechanism: GmFULa regulates the expression of sucrose synthase (GmSUS12) and sucrose transporter (GmSUT5) by binding to their promoters, synchronizing sucrose biosynthesis in source organs and transportation to sink organs.

genes: GmFULa (transcription factor, regulates plant growth and development, Glycine max), GmSUS12 (sucrose synthase, involved in sucrose metabolism, Glycine max), GmSUT5 (sucrose transporter, involved in sucrose transport, Glycine max)
phenotype: GmFULa overexpression increases soluble sugar content, sucrose synthase activity, and biomass accumulation in soybean.
mechanism: GmFULa promotes the expression of GmSUS12 and GmSUT5 by binding to their promoters, enhancing sucrose biosynthesis and transportation.

genes: NUD (Nud, Ethylene Response Factor, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: Targeted knockout of the NUD gene leads to the conversion from hulled to naked barley phenotype in 57% of primary transformants.
mechanism: NA

genes: NUD (Nud, Ethylene Response Factor, Hordeum vulgare)
phenotype: T-DNA-free homozygous lines with independently generated mutations in the NUD gene were obtained in the T1 generation, and at homozygous state, all obtained mutations caused the naked grain phenotype.
mechanism: NA

genes: cas9 (Cas9, CRISPR-associated protein 9, synthetic), gRNA (guide RNA, RNA-guided endonuclease, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression cassettes harboring the cas9 and guide RNA genes were used to transform barley cv. Golden Promise via Agrobacterium-mediated DNA transfer.
mechanism: NA

genes: gRNA (guide RNA, RNA-guided endonuclease, synthetic)
phenotype: The Nud45 gRNA showed the highest activity in both preliminary tests.
mechanism: NA

genes: gRNA (guide RNA, RNA-guided endonuclease, synthetic)
phenotype: The Nud50 gRNA was used for stable plant transformation, which enabled us to compare its activity between transient expression assay and stably transformed plants.
mechanism: NA

genes: MdCPK1a (calcium-dependent protein kinase, from Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdCPK1a increases cold tolerance in Nicotiana benthamiana, as evidenced by increased survival rates after cold stress and improved root growth under cold conditions.
mechanism: MdCPK1a enhances cold tolerance by scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, as indicated by reduced MDA content, electrolyte leakage, and increased activities of antioxidant enzymes (CAT, POD, SOD).

genes: ABA3 (ABA synthesis, source: Arabidopsis thaliana), DES1 (L-cysteine desulfhydrase, source: Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of both ABA3 and DES1 in guard cells of aba3 des1 double mutants fully restores the wild-type phenotype, including wilting behavior and dehydration responses.
mechanism: ABA3-mediated guard-cell ABA synthesis and DES1-produced H2S signals synergistically control stomatal closure and dehydration responses.

genes: ABA3 (ABA synthesis, source: Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of ABA3 in guard cells of aba3 mutants rescues the wilting phenotype and dehydration-induced DES1 expression.
mechanism: ABA3-mediated guard-cell ABA synthesis is sufficient to trigger dehydration-induced DES1 expression and related dehydration tolerance.

genes: DES1 (L-cysteine desulfhydrase, source: Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of DES1 in guard cells of aba3 mutants does not rescue the wilting phenotype, but delays wilting and reduces water loss under dehydration stress.
mechanism: DES1-produced H2S signals are required for ABA-triggered dehydration responses in guard cells.

genes: OsCPS2 (cycloartenol synthase 2, involved in ent-CPP derived LRD production, Oryza sativa L. ssp. japonica), OsCPS4 (cycloartenol synthase 4, involved in ent-CPP derived LRD production, Oryza sativa L. ssp. japonica)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsCPS2 and OsCPS4 increases production of both syn- and ent-CPP derived LRDs, leading to increased resistance to Xoo infection and no change in susceptibility to drought stress.
mechanism: Increased production of LRDs, including ent-CPP derived more effective antibiotics against Xoo, likely due to increased GGPP availability from metabolic drain imposed by CPS over-expression.

genes: OsCPS2 (cycloartenol synthase 2, involved in ent-CPP derived LRD production, Oryza sativa L. ssp. japonica), OsCPS4 (cycloartenol synthase 4, involved in ent-CPP derived LRD production, Oryza sativa L. ssp. japonica)
gene_construct: CRISPR gRNA array: rice U6 promoter-gRNA-FT1+gRNA-FT2-terminator
phenotype: Knockout of OsCPS2 and OsCPS4 leads to reduced production of ent-CPP derived LRDs, increased susceptibility to Xoo infection, and increased susceptibility to drought stress.
mechanism: Defect in stomatal closure in response to drought stress, which is independent of ABA signaling, likely due to reduced production of LRDs that promote stomatal closure.

genes: PCM1 (plant calmodulin-like protein 1, stress response, Arabidopsis thaliana), PCM2 (plant calmodulin-like protein 2, stress response, Arabidopsis thaliana), PCM3 (plant calmodulin-like protein 3, stress response, Arabidopsis thaliana), PCM4 (plant calmodulin-like protein 4, stress response, Arabidopsis thaliana), PCM5 (plant calmodulin-like protein 5, stress response, Arabidopsis thaliana), PCM6 (plant calmodulin-like protein 6, stress response, Arabidopsis thaliana), PCM7 (plant calmodulin-like protein 7, stress response, Arabidopsis thaliana), PCM8 (plant calmodulin-like protein 8, stress response, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of PCM1, PCM2, PCM3, PCM5, PCM7, and PCM8 provides protection against Hpa infection and increases hypocotyl growth in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: PCMs may influence membrane structure and activity of proteins that reside in the membrane or that bind to PCMs, like the subunit 5 of the COP9 signalosome, leading to altered membrane environment and enhanced defense responses.

genes: GmNAC065 (senescence-associated gene, soybean), GmNAC085 (senescence-associated gene, soybean)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of GmNAC065 and GmNAC085 caused growth and development retardation, decreased number of leaves and rosette diameter, and reduced inflorescence length.
mechanism: GmNAC065 and GmNAC085 differentially co-relate to stress-responsive genes in soybean. GmNAC065 is co-expressed with genes involved in plant maintenance and redox homeostasis, while GmNAC085 is expressed in drastic conditions with ROS accumulation and depletion of biomolecules.

genes: GmNAC065 (senescence-associated gene, soybean)
phenotype: GmNAC065-OX plants exhibited a longer life cycle, with late flowering and delayed senescence.
mechanism: GmNAC065-OX plants do not exhibit a robust anti-oxidative performance associated with lower transcription and activity of CAT, SOD, and APX, soluble sugars and carotenoids levels, and a remarkable decrease in chlorophyll content.

genes: GmNAC085 (senescence-associated gene, soybean)
phenotype: GmNAC085-OX plants exhibited accelerated senescence and growth dwarfism.
mechanism: The impaired enzymatic and non-enzymatic anti-oxidative systems of GmNAC085-OX lines result in the highest protein decay ratio in response to multiple stresses and the activation of ePCD mechanisms, observed as extensive cell damage in leaves and roots.

genes: psbD (plastid-encoded D2 subunit, gene in the psbD-psbC operon, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of psbD increases transcript accumulation of the psbD–psbC operon by read-through transcription from the aadA gene in transplastomic tobacco lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: psbD (plastid-encoded D2 subunit, gene in the psbD-psbC operon, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Knockdown of psbD reduces transcript accumulation of the psbD–psbC operon in transplastomic tobacco lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: psbD (plastid-encoded D2 subunit, gene in the psbD-psbC operon, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Introduction of point mutations into the translation initiation codon of psbD reduces translation efficiency in transplastomic tobacco lines.
mechanism: NA

genes: Lifeact (actin-binding protein, fluorescent marker, synthetic), eGFP (fluorescent marker, synthetic)
phenotype: Expression of Lifeact-GFP in N. benthamiana cells allows visualization of microfilament depolymerization induced by hyperoside.
mechanism: NA

genes: AeADF1 (actin-depolymerizing factor, microfilament severing, Abelmoschus esculentus), eGFP (fluorescent marker, synthetic)
phenotype: AeADF1-eGFP fusion protein localizes to F-actin in N. benthamiana cells, indicating its interaction with microfilaments.
mechanism: AeADF1 colocalizes with F-actin, suggesting its role in microfilament dynamics.

genes: GUX1 (cell wall gene, single-copy, Pinus radiata)
phenotype: Biallelic INDELs with 15% efficiency using a single gRNA; 12% of transgenic embryogenic tissue was edited with two gRNAs, but regenerated plants had single nucleotide insertions and no large deletions.
mechanism: NA

genes: GUX1 (cell wall gene, single-copy, Pinus radiata)
phenotype: 33% editing efficiency with a two-gRNA strategy using RNPs, generating INDELs including large deletions; deletions in embryogenic tissue were present in plantlets, but all plants were monoallelic.
mechanism: NA

genes: LhGR2 (transcriptional activator, codon-optimized for Arabidopsis, drives expression of reporter genes, source: heterologous plant origin), uidA (encoding β-glucuronidase; GUS, source: Escherichia coli), YFP (yellow fluorescent protein, source: synthetic)
phenotype: Inducible expression of GUS and YFP in rice seedlings upon treatment with Dex, with GUS activity up to 8-fold higher in roots compared to shoots.
mechanism: NA

genes: PdGA20ox1 (GA20-oxidase, from Populus deltoides), PtrMYB3 (MYB transcription factor, from Populus trichocarpa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PdGA20ox1 and PtrMYB3 increases stem fresh weight by threefold in Arabidopsis thaliana and 2.6-fold in Populus spp., with enhanced woody biomass production and improved saccharification efficiency.
mechanism: NA

genes: Gene (synthetic construct, tandem repeats of HN and F epitopes, synthetic)
phenotype: The transgene was transcribed and translated in maize leaves only 48 hours after infiltration.
mechanism: NA

genes: DcBCH1 (beta-carotene hydroxylase, carotenoid synthesis, Daucus carota)
phenotype: Overexpression of DcBCH1 increases antioxidant capacity and enhances drought tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with higher endogenous ABA levels and lower malondialdehyde content after drought treatment.
mechanism: DcBCH1 increases antioxidant capacity and promotes endogenous ABA levels by regulating the synthesis rate of carotenoids, thereby enhancing drought resistance.

genes: OsANN4 (calcium-binding protein, involved in ABA response, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Knockdown of OsANN4 results in lower rooting rate and shorter shoot and root lengths in rice (Oryza sativa).
mechanism: OsANN4 modulates ROS production, mediates Ca2+ influx, or interacts with OsCDPK24.

genes: LsaGRF5 (transcriptional factor, cell nucleus function, Lactuca sativa), LsaMIR396a (microRNA, down-regulates LsaGRF5, Lactuca sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of LsaGRF5 increases leaf size in Lactuca sativa, while overexpression of LsaMIR396a decreases leaf size.
mechanism: LsaGRF5 acts as a transcriptional factor in the cell nucleus, and LsaMIR396a down-regulates LsaGRF5, affecting leaf growth.

genes: TaBG1-A (seed size regulation, wheat)
phenotype: Increased TaBG1-A expression leads to larger seed size but reduces seed number per plant, with no significant overall increase in yield.
mechanism: NA

genes: BoCER2 (cuticular wax biosynthesis, Brassica oleracea)
phenotype: Ectopic expression of BoCER2 rescues the phenotype of cer2 mutant in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsSYT-5 (synaptotagmin 5, negative regulator of ABA signaling, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Silencing of OsSYT-5 gene improves drought tolerance, enhances yield, and increases plant growth in transgenic rice lines.
mechanism: OsSYT-5 may act as a negative regulator of ABA signaling, and its silencing leads to enhanced ABA content and regulation of stress-responsive genes, improving drought tolerance.

genes: ZjSEP3 (transcription factor, floral organ expression, Ziziphus jujuba Mill.), AtLHY (circadian rhythm gene, flowering regulation, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZjSEP3 in Arabidopsis thaliana causes an early-flowering phenotype and suppresses the expression of AtLHY.
mechanism: ZjSEP3 inhibits the transcription of AtLHY by binding to the CArG-boxes in its promoter, leading to early flowering.

genes: AhHLH112 (basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, drought response, Arachis hypogaea)
phenotype: Overexpression of AhHLH112 improves drought tolerance in transgenic peanut plants, reducing reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and increasing antioxidant enzyme activity, while decreasing MDA concentration and water loss rate under drought conditions.
mechanism: AhHLH112 enhances ROS-scavenging ability through regulation of POD-mediated H2O2 homeostasis and may participate in the ABA-dependent stress-responding pathway by improving ABA levels and elevating the expression of ABA biosynthesis and responding genes such as AtNCED3 and AtRD29A.

genes: SlINVINH1 (invertase inhibitor, regulates soluble sugar accumulation, Solanum lycopersicum), SlVPE5 (vacuolar processing enzyme, regulates soluble sugar accumulation, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Knockout of SlINVINH1 and SlVPE5 genes significantly increased glucose and fructose content in fruits by 40.19–69.44% and TSS content by 31.90–62.07% compared to wild-type.
mechanism: SlINVINH1 inhibits cell wall invertase activity, increasing glucose and fructose accumulation. SlVPE5 targets vacuolar hydrolases, negatively regulating soluble sugar accumulation. The synergistic effect of both genes enhances soluble sugar content.

genes: OsAT10 (acyltransferase, acylates arabinosyl residues on xylan with p-coumarate, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsAT10 increases xylan-bound p-coumaroyl-arabinose in Sorghum bicolor without changing total p-coumarate or fatty acid ester content, but reduces lignin content and increases biomass saccharification efficiency.
mechanism: OsAT10 acylates arabinosyl residues on xylan with p-coumarate, which may be linked to lignification in cell walls.

genes: Rvi6 (resistance gene, pathogen recognition, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Transgenic pear clones constitutively expressing Rvi6 show strong defense reactions and very limited sporulation when inoculated with V. pyrina.
mechanism: NA

genes: SexiDES5 (Δ11 and Δ12 desaturase, sex pheromone biosynthesis, Spodoptera exigua)
phenotype: ΔSexi5 mutant females do not produce sex pheromone components, leading to loss of female attractiveness.
mechanism: Deletion of SexiDES5 disrupts sex pheromone biosynthesis, as no sex pheromone components were detected in ΔSexi5 females.

genes: SexiDES5 (Δ11 and Δ12 desaturase, sex pheromone biosynthesis, Spodoptera exigua)
phenotype: ΔSexi5 mutant females exhibit smaller pupal size and lower emergence rate and female fecundity compared to wild-type females.
mechanism: NA

genes: AtPDI1 (disulfide isomerase, wild-type), AtPDI1 (disulfide isomerase, double-cysteine-mutant)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtPDI1 increases germination ratios and root length under abiotic stresses and exogenous ABA treatment, while pdi-AtPDI1m1 and pdi-AtPDI1m2 show significantly lower germination ratios and root lengths.
mechanism: AtPDI1's anti-stress function is directly related to the activity of disulfide isomerase.

genes: GH_A07G0501 (oil-related OLEO, overexpression), GH_D10G0941 (oil-related OLEO, overexpression), GH_D01G1686 (oil-related OLEO, overexpression)
phenotype: Overexpression of GH_A07G0501, GH_D10G0941, and GH_D01G1686 increases seed oil content and decreases seed germination rates in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: NA

genes: TaVIH2-3B (phosphatidylinositol kinase, drought tolerance, Triticum aestivum L.)
phenotype: Ectopic overexpression of TaVIH2-3B confers tolerance to drought stress and rescues the sensitivity of Atvih2 mutants.
mechanism: RNAseq analysis shows genome-wide reprogramming with remarkable effects on genes involved in cell-wall biosynthesis, supported by enhanced accumulation of polysaccharides (arabinogalactan, cellulose, and arabinoxylan) in the transgenic plants.

genes: ScPIP2-1 (aquaporin, osmotic stress response, Saccharum spp.)
phenotype: Overexpression of ScPIP2–1 enhances salt tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana, as evidenced by healthier state, more stable relative water content, longer root length, more stable ion leakage, lower malondialdehyde content, higher proline content, higher superoxide dismutase activity, and higher expression levels of AtKIN2, AtP5CS1, AtP5CS2, AtDREB2, AtRD29A, AtNHX1, AtSOS1, and AtHKT1 genes, along with a lower expression level of AtTRX5.
mechanism: ScPIP2–1-mediated osmotic stress signaling cascade plays a positive role in plant response to salt stress.

genes: FAR (FATTY ACYL-COA/ACP REDUCTASE, WE biosynthesis, Marinobacter aquaeoleoi), WSD2 (WAX SYNTHASE/ACYL-COA:DIACYLGLYCEROL O-ACYLTRANSFERASE, WE biosynthesis, Marinobacter aquaeoleoi), WSD5 (WAX SYNTHASE/ACYL-COA:DIACYLGLYCEROL O-ACYLTRANSFERASE, WE biosynthesis, Marinobacter aquaeoleoi)
phenotype: WE formation with plastid and cytosol-localized FAR and WSD in seeds. A comparative WE analysis revealed the production of shorter and more saturated WE by plastid-localized WE biosynthesis compared to cytosolic WE synthesis.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsMYB103L (R2R3-MYB transcription factor, regulates cellulose biosynthesis and deposition, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Down-regulation of OsMYB103L in rice significantly enhances biomass enzymatic saccharification by 10–28% after pretreatments.
mechanism: OsMYB103L specifically mediates cellulose biosynthesis and deposition by regulating OsCesAs and other genes associated with microfibril assembly.

genes: SlSRM1-like (transcription factor, regulates leaf development, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Knockout of SlSRM1-like results in abnormal tomato leaf morphology, including thinner leaves, wrinkled edges, raised veins, disordered edge veins, and left and right asymmetry.
mechanism: SlSRM1-like regulates tomato leaf development through auxin-related pathways.

genes: NpLyc (lycopene β-cyclase, from Narcissus pseudonarcissus), BsCrtW (β-carotene ketolase, from Brevundimonas sp. strain SD212), BsCrtZ (β-carotene hydroxylase, from Brevundimonas sp. strain SD212), T7RNAP (RNA polymerase, from phage T7)
phenotype: Transplastomic Nt-iAXT plants displayed a conspicuous orange–brown phenotype both upon in vitro culture and when grown in soil under standard greenhouse conditions.
mechanism: NA

genes: OsCSL1 (MAPK kinase kinase22, endoplasmic reticulum-localized, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Functional complementation of OsCSL1 restores the normal phenotype in csl1 plants.
mechanism: OsCSL1 regulates the expression of multiple chloroplast synthesis-related genes, affecting their functions and leading to chlorotic seedlings and disrupted chloroplasts.

genes: OsCSL1 (MAPK kinase kinase22, endoplasmic reticulum-localized, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Disruption of OsCSL1 led to yellow seedlings phenocopying the csl1 mutant.
mechanism: OsCSL1 regulates the expression of multiple chloroplast synthesis-related genes, affecting their functions and leading to chlorotic seedlings and disrupted chloroplasts.

genes: WAPO-A1 (spikelet number per spike gene, loss-of-function mutation, Triticum aestivum), WAPO-B1 (spikelet number per spike gene, loss-of-function mutation, Triticum aestivum)
gene_construct: CRISPR-Cas9 transgene with guide RNA targeting both WAPO-A1 and WAPO-B1
phenotype: Loss-of-function mutations in WAPO-A1 and WAPO-B1 reduce spikelet number per spike (SNS) by 1.7-3 spikelets and cause floral abnormalities.
mechanism: NA

genes: WAPO-A1 (spikelet number per spike gene, overexpression, Triticum monococcum), WAPO-A1 (spikelet number per spike gene, overexpression, Triticum aestivum), WAPO-A1 (spikelet number per spike gene, overexpression, Triticum aestivum)
gene_construct: BAC-derived genomic region of WAPO-A1 from Triticum monococcum (DV92) and tetraploid wheat Langdon (LDN-C47), including intron and regulatory regions; site-directed mutagenesis to change cysteine at position 47 in LDN-C47 to phenylalanine (LDN-F47)
phenotype: Transgenic plants with additional WAPO1 copies show increased spikelet number per spike (SNS) by 13.4-15.5% and delayed heading date by 5.4-7.0%.
mechanism: NA

genes: GmD53a (suppressor of strigolactone MAX2, soybean)
phenotype: GmD53a-knockdown chimerical plants have a higher number of nodules compared to control lines.
mechanism: GmD53a knockdown alters the expression of several nodulation genes essential for initiation and formation of nodules.

genes: MdBBX1 (basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, involved in abiotic stress response, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdBBX1 enhances tolerance to abiotic stresses, including salt and drought, and increases seed germination and seedling growth under exogenous ABA treatment.
mechanism: MdBBX1 may interfere with the expression of ABI5 and HY5 to promote seed germination and seedling growth in transgenic plants. It also enhances the ROS-scavenging system and alleviates oxidative stress, improving salt tolerance.

genes: JcBSP1 (vegetative storage protein, nitrogen storage, Jatropha curcas)
phenotype: Overexpression of JcBSP1 in Arabidopsis results in enlarged rosette leaves, flowers, and seeds, and significantly increases seed weight and yield in transgenic plants.
mechanism: JcBSP1 might be a form of nitrogen storage in plants, serving as a nutrient provider that promotes growth and development.

genes: AgGMP (GDP-D-mannose pyrophosphorylase, involved in AsA biosynthesis, Apium graveolens)
phenotype: Overexpression of AgGMP increases root length in Arabidopsis thaliana under 300 mM mannitol stress, with AgGMP-2 showing significantly increased root length compared to WT.
mechanism: AgGMP enhances AsA accumulation, which neutralizes stress effects by removing ROS and H2O2, thereby improving drought stress resistance.

genes: RBV (AT5G64730, WD40 domain protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of the rbv-1 mutant with pRBV:RBV-eYFP fully rescued the morphological defects of amiR-SUL rbv-1, including leaf bleaching and miRNA accumulation.
mechanism: RBV (AT5G64730) is essential for miRNA biogenesis and the restoration of miRNA levels and morphological defects in the rbv-1 mutant.

genes: TgNAC01 (transcription factor, promotes secondary cell wall deposition and stress response, teak)
phenotype: Overexpression of TgNAC01 increases salt stress tolerance in Nicotiana tabacum.
mechanism: TgNAC01 enhances salt stress tolerance by promoting secondary cell wall deposition and modulating ABA-mediated signaling.

genes: AtCKX2 (cytokinin catabolism gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtCKX2 reduces endogenous cytokinin levels in tomato fruits, leading to decreased fruit weight (32.7% of WT), reduced fruit size (62.6% length, 65.9% diameter), and thinner pericarp (1.00 mm vs. 2.25 mm in WT).
mechanism: Reduced endogenous CK levels lead to downregulation of GA biosynthetic genes, upregulation of GA-inactivating genes, reduced active GA levels, repression of auxin biosynthesis and signaling pathways, and altered expression of cell division- and expansion-related genes, resulting in reduced pericarp cell number and size.

genes: BjCET1 (metal ion transporter, cation diffusion facilitator protein, Brassica juncea)
phenotype: Constitutive expression of BjCET1 rescues the heavy-metal tolerance capability of transgenic tobacco plants.
mechanism: BjCET1 is a membrane-localized efflux transporter that plays essential roles in heavy metal ion homeostasis and hyper-accumulation.

genes: PHR2 (phosphate response 2, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of PHR2 enables root colonization by AM fungi at higher phosphate conditions (40% total root length colonization and 25% arbuscule colonization at 200 µM Pi, MP).
mechanism: PHR2 promotes AM development at Pi starvation and its inactivity may be responsible for the absence of AM at high phosphate.

genes: PHR2 (phosphate response 2, transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: phr2 mutants show severely impaired root colonization by AMF at low phosphate conditions (25 µM Pi, LP), with very few colonization attempts on mutant roots.
mechanism: PHR2 is critical for root colonization at LP, and its inactivity may be responsible for the absence of AM at high phosphate.

genes: HAP (histone lysine methyltransferase, SET-domain SUVH, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: HAP gene silencing via RNAi and overexpression leads to increased trichome density in vegetative and inflorescence stems of Solanum lycopersicum. CRISPR-Cas9 editing of HAP also results in increased trichome density.
mechanism: HAP encodes a SET-domain SUVH putative histone lysine methyltransferase. Mutations in HAP lead to a premature stop codon, resulting in the loss of functional domains characteristic of this gene family, including the SAD-SRA and SET-domain. This loss of function results in altered trichome formation and density.

genes: ahas (acetohydroxyacid synthase, mutated, Arabidopsis thaliana), ricf (460-bp ricin gene fragments, sense and antisense, Ricinus communis), gus (β-glucuronidase, reporter, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transgenic castor bean event TB14S-5D shows tolerance to imazapyr herbicide at 250 g ha−1 and stable silencing of ricin/RCA120 proteins across three generations.
mechanism: The mutated Atahas gene confers herbicide tolerance, while the intron-hairpin cassette silences endogenous ricin genes.

genes: AkFT1 (flowering time regulator, overexpressed, Amorphophallus konjac), AkFT2 (flowering time regulator, overexpressed, Amorphophallus konjac)
phenotype: Overexpression of AkFT1 and AkFT2 reduces the vegetative growth period and accelerates flowering in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: AkFT1 and AkFT2 may function similarly to florigen during flowering transition in A. konjac, promoting flowering by integrating signals from various flowering pathways.

genes: PgMyb308-like (R2R3 Myb transcription factor, regulates shikimate pathway metabolites, P. granatum)
phenotype: Overexpression of PgMyb308-like increases shikimate, amino acids (tyrosine, tryptophan, phenylalanine), and lignins, while reducing hydroxytyrosol (HTs) and flavonoids in pomegranate hairy roots.
mechanism: PgMyb308-like may regulate the shikimate pathway by modulating the balance between shikimate and gallic acid biosynthesis, affecting downstream metabolites such as amino acids and lignins.

genes: aMIR46-48 (artificial microRNA targeting PUB46, PUB47, and PUB48, synthetic)
phenotype: Overexpression of aMIR46-48 in Arabidopsis thaliana increases drought hypersensitivity, resembling the phenotype of pub46 and pub48 single mutants.
mechanism: aMIR46-48 silences PUB46, PUB47, and PUB48 genes, leading to reduced activity of these E3 ubiquitin ligases, which affects drought tolerance and ABA signaling.

genes: AmCBF1 (C-repeat binding factor 1, transcription factor, Gossypium hirsutum)
