phenotype: Overexpression of AmCBF1 increases root to shoot ratio and improves drought and cold stress resistance in Gossypium hirsutum.
mechanism: AmCBF1 enhances drought and cold stress resistance by reducing membrane damage, increasing soluble sugar content, and altering stomatal density and epidermal cell morphology.

genes: OsNF-YA1 (NF-YA transcription factor, involved in viral defense, Oryza sativa), OsNF-YA2 (NF-YA transcription factor, involved in viral defense, Oryza sativa), OsNF-YA10 (NF-YA transcription factor, involved in viral defense, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsNF-YA1, OsNF-YA2, and OsNF-YA10 increases susceptibility to RSV and SRBSDV, with more severe symptoms, higher viral RNA and protein accumulation, and increased wilting.
mechanism: OsNF-YAs negatively modulate rice resistance to RSV and SRBSDV by suppressing jasmonic acid-mediated antiviral defense.

genes: OsNF-YA1 (NF-YA transcription factor, involved in viral defense, Oryza sativa), OsNF-YA2 (NF-YA transcription factor, involved in viral defense, Oryza sativa), OsNF-YA10 (NF-YA transcription factor, involved in viral defense, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: RNAi suppression of OsNF-YA1, OsNF-YA2, and OsNF-YA10 increases resistance to RSV and SRBSDV, with less severe symptoms, lower viral RNA and protein accumulation, and reduced wilting.
mechanism: Repression of OsNF-YA expression increases rice resistance to RSV and SRBSDV by enhancing jasmonic acid-mediated antiviral defense.

genes: MdWOX11 (WUSCHEL-RELATED HOMEOBOX GENE 11, transcription factor, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdWOX11 decreases AS regeneration ability, while RNAi of MdWOX11 increases AS regeneration ability in Malus domestica.
mechanism: MdWOX11 inhibits AS formation by modulating hormone levels and gene expression during AS development.

genes: LtKNOX1 (class I KNOX gene, involved in cell fate specification and maintenance of shoot apical meristem (SAM), Liriodendron tsingtauense)
phenotype: Overexpression of LtKNOX1 in Nicotiana benthamiana leads to curled leaves, reduced leaf size, and altered leaf shape with narrower leaves after flattening, particularly in OE#1 and OE#2 lines.
mechanism: Ectopic overexpression of LtKNOX1 affects leaf shape by altering cell proliferation and differentiation, potentially through inhibition of the gibberellic acid (GA) biosynthetic pathway and interaction with genes such as AS1, PIN1, GA20ox, CUC2, CLV1, and WUS.

genes: SHP (soybean hull peroxidase, degrades lignin, Glycine max), GLOX (glyoxal oxidase, generates H2O2 for lignin degradation, Glycine max)
phenotype: Transgenic rice plants with enhanced lignin degradation in stalks, making them more amenable to degradation for energy use.
mechanism: SHP and GLOX work synergistically to degrade lignin by generating H2O2 and catalyzing lignin monomer polymerization.

genes: CYP81Q1 (cytochrome P450, lignan biosynthesis, Sesamum indicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CYP81Q1 in Forsythia intermedia and Forsythia koreana leads to the accumulation of (+)-piperitol (14.23–51.66 µg/g DW) and (+)-sesamin (5.57–21.50 µg/g DW) in leaves.
mechanism: CYP81Q1 catalyzes the biosynthesis of (+)-piperitol and (+)-sesamin in Forsythia leaves.

genes: MKP1 (MKP1, dual-specificity phosphatase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of MKP1 in ntx1 plants restores vascular resistance to Xoo.
mechanism: MKP1 regulates vascular resistance to Xoo by inactivating MPK3.

genes: VQ1 (VQ domain-containing protein 1, stress-related gene, Populus davidiana×P. bolleana)
phenotype: Overexpression of VQ1 increases salt stress resistance in Arabidopsis thaliana, with transgenic seedlings showing less severe growth inhibition under 150 mM NaCl treatment compared to WT seedlings.
mechanism: VQ1 enhances salt stress tolerance by increasing the expression of ABA-related genes (AtKUP6, AtNCED2, AtABI1) and decreasing the expression of SA-related genes (AtNPR1, AtWRKY70, AtPDF1.2, AtMPK6), suggesting a role in ABA signaling and antagonistic interactions via the SA signaling pathway.

genes: RDD1 (rice gene, target of miR166, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: In-frame mutations in RDD1 increased transcript levels by 1.2- to 1.3-fold at peak, enhanced NH4+ and PO43− uptake, and improved grain appearance quality but decreased panicle weight.
mechanism: In-frame editing of RDD1 disrupted miR166 binding, leading to increased RDD1 transcript levels and altered amino acid residues (Asp to Glu) that may mimic phosphorylation states, affecting NH4+ and PO43− uptake and starch degradation.

genes: S3H (SA catabolism enzyme, S3H gene, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: SA deficient phenotypes with SA levels similar to or slightly lower than NahG transgenic Arabidopsis
mechanism: S3H converts SA to 2,3-DHBA for catabolism, reducing SA levels in a feedback mode controlled by endogenous SA

genes: AtMYB12 (transcription factor, regulatory gene, Arabidopsis thaliana), AmDel (transcription factor, regulatory gene, Antirrhinum majus), AmRos1 (transcription factor, regulatory gene, Antirrhinum majus), VvStSy (structural gene, stilbene synthase, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtMYB12, AmDel, AmRos1, and VvStSy increases total polyphenol content and antioxidant capacity in Bronze tomato compared to wild type.
mechanism: AtMYB12 TF activates the phenylpropanoid pathway, leading to increased polyphenol synthesis and antioxidant activity.

genes: VvASMT1 (melatonin biosynthesis enzyme, homolog of MzASMT1, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvASMT1 increases melatonin content, improves salt and osmotic stress tolerance, increases germination rates, root lengths, and relative water content, and reduces electrolyte leakage and MDA content in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: VvASMT1 enhances melatonin production, which reduces ROS accumulation and improves antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, CAT, POD, APX), thereby enhancing stress tolerance.

genes: VvASMT1 (melatonin biosynthesis enzyme, homolog of MzASMT1, Vitis vinifera)
phenotype: Overexpression of VvASMT1-GFP increases melatonin content and improves salt and osmotic stress tolerance in Nicotiana benthamiana.
mechanism: VvASMT1 enhances melatonin production, which reduces ROS accumulation and improves antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, CAT, POD, APX), thereby enhancing stress tolerance.

genes: AfPAL (phenylalanine ammonia-lyase, from Anoectochilus formosanus), ArPAL (phenylalanine ammonia-lyase, from Anoectochilus roxburghii)
phenotype: Overexpression of AfPAL and ArPAL increases flavonoids and anthocyanin content in transgenic Arabidopsis.
mechanism: AfPAL and ArPAL play a crucial role in flavonoid biosynthesis in Anoectochilus, and their overexpression enhances flavonoid and anthocyanin content in Arabidopsis.

genes: DPH1 (diphthamide synthase, required for diphthamide modification of eEF2, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Complementation of dph1-1 mutants with pDPH1:DPH1-GFP restores hygromycin tolerance and normal biomass and primary root length to wild-type levels.
mechanism: DPH1 is required for diphthamide modification of eEF2, which contributes to translational fidelity and normal growth rates.

genes: CaERF1A (ethylene-responsive factor, transcription factor, Capsicum annuum), CaERF1Anls (ethylene-responsive factor with nucleus localization signal deleted, transcription factor, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CaERF1A enhances resistance to necrotrophic pathogen Alternaria alternata via ET and JA synthesis-related gene regulation.
mechanism: CaERF1A enhances ET/JA synthesis-related gene expression and ET production against fungal pathogen infection.

genes: CaERF1A (ethylene-responsive factor, transcription factor, Capsicum annuum), CaERF1Anls (ethylene-responsive factor with nucleus localization signal deleted, transcription factor, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: CaERF1A silencing reduces TMV-P0-mediated cell death by about 52% as measured by electrolyte leakage.
mechanism: CaERF1A is involved in TMV-P0-mediated cell death.

genes: OAK (OUTGROWTH-ASSOCIATED KINASE, gene encoding a kinase involved in hybrid outgrowth phenotypes, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Silencing OAK in the Sha parent (amiROAK Sha) crossed to Lag2-2 resulted in hybrids without outgrowths and restored typical shoot architecture.
mechanism: OAK is necessary for the hybrid phenotype in Sha × Lag2-2 hybrids, as silencing it rescues the shoot phenotype.

genes: GI (GIGANTEA, a key clock protein, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of GI increases lateral root density in Arabidopsis thaliana under red light conditions.
mechanism: GI functions upstream of TIR1 and might bind to the regulatory elements present in the promoter regions of TIR1 to modulate its expression, thereby modulating auxin signaling and downstream pathways involved in lateral root development.

genes: ZmSAMDC (SAM decarboxylase, involved in polyamine synthesis, Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmSAMDC increases the number of rows and 100-seed weight in maize, while reducing bald tip length, thereby increasing yield under cold stress.
mechanism: ZmSAMDC overexpression enhances polyamine (PA) content, which increases antioxidant enzyme activity (POD, SOD, CAT, APX), reduces reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and positively regulates CBF and downstream COR gene expression, improving cold tolerance.

genes: bZIP60 (bZIP transcription factor, IRE1-targeted intron, splicing regulation, Arabidopsis thaliana), GFP (green fluorescent protein, reporter, synthetic)
phenotype: The 35S::bZIP60 intron:GFP reporter construct shows significant upregulation of GFP fluorescence in response to DTT treatment, indicating enhanced splicing of the bZIP60 intron during ER stress.
mechanism: The bZIP60 intron is spliced by IRE1 during ER stress, placing GFP in frame with the bZIP60 start codon, resulting in GFP expression as a detection method for IRE1-mediated UPR activation.

plant_species: Malus domestica, Malus cv. 'Royalty', Malus cv. 'Flame'
genes: MdROS1 (DNA demethylation gene, involved in LT-induced anthocyanin accumulation, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Silencing of MdROS1 in 'Royalty' and 'Gala' apple leaves reduces anthocyanin accumulation, resulting in green coloration in 'Royalty' leaves after LT treatment.
mechanism: MdROS1 promotes anthocyanin accumulation by enhancing demethylation of anthocyanin-related genes, including MdMYB10, MdCHS, MdCHI, MdF3′H, MdANS, and MdUFGT.

plant_species: Malus domestica, Malus cv. 'Royalty', Malus cv. 'Flame'
genes: MdROS1 (DNA demethylation gene, involved in LT-induced anthocyanin accumulation, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdROS1 in 'Royalty' leaves results in deep red coloration and significantly higher levels of cyanidin-3-O-glucoside compared to control 'Gala' leaves.
mechanism: MdROS1 promotes anthocyanin accumulation by enhancing demethylation of anthocyanin-related genes, including MdMYB10, MdCHS, MdCHI, MdF3′H, MdANS, and MdUFGT.

genes: MS3 (transcription factor with PHD-finger domain, essential for male gametophyte development, Glycine max)
gene_construct: CRISPR/Cas9 plasmid with two knockout targets: 5'-GTTGTGCTTGAGGGTTGGCA-3' and 5'-GAGGGTTGGCAAGGTGACAT-3' in the MS3 coding region
phenotype: MS3-KNOCKOUT transgenic plants produced almost no pollen grains or selfing pods, similar to the ms3 mutant.
mechanism: The PHD-finger domain of MS3 is required for environmental response and male gametophyte development.

genes: OsPG2 (pectin methylesterase, overexpression, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsPG2-FOX rice shows a 37.1% reduction in uronic acid content (main component of pectin) and ~55% lower relative root elongation under 100 µM Al treatment compared to WT rice.
mechanism: Reduced pectin content in root cell walls allows increased Al accumulation, leading to reduced Al tolerance and root elongation inhibition.

genes: OsPG1 (pectin methylesterase, overexpression, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: OsPG1-FOX rice shows a 39.6% reduction in uronic acid content in roots and ~54% lower relative root elongation under Al treatment compared to WT rice.
mechanism: Reduced pectin content in root cell walls allows increased Al accumulation, leading to reduced Al tolerance and root elongation inhibition.

genes: GsERF1 (ethylene response factor, AP2/ERF domain, Glycine soja)
phenotype: Overexpression of GsERF1 increases relative root growth and fresh weight under AlCl3 stress in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GsERF1 enhances tolerance to aluminum stress mainly through an ethylene-mediated pathway, increasing the transcription of ACC biosynthesis-related genes and ABA-responsive and/or stress-responsive genes together with proline accumulation.

genes: GsERF1 (ethylene response factor, AP2/ERF domain, Glycine soja)
phenotype: Knockdown of GsERF1 in soybean hairy roots results in reduced resistance to aluminum stress compared to control lines.
mechanism: GsERF1 enhances tolerance to aluminum stress mainly through an ethylene-mediated pathway, increasing the transcription of ACC biosynthesis-related genes and ABA-responsive and/or stress-responsive genes together with proline accumulation.

genes: RZ1AL (RNA-binding protein, involved in fruit ripening, Solyc01g104840)
phenotype: cr-rz1al mutants display delayed fruit ripening, reduced coloring, and decreased weight.
mechanism: RZ1AL plays a role in fruit ripening and development by influencing gene expression of ribosomal subunits and key enzymes of the carotenoid biosynthesis pathway, leading to reduced lycopene content.

genes: CvGME (GME homolog, geranylgeranyl diphosphate synthase, Chrysanthemum vestitum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CvGME in tobacco increases ascorbate (AsA) content and enhances drought tolerance.
mechanism: CvGME enhances drought tolerance via increased ascorbate accumulation.

genes: PFA-DSP1 (PFA-DSP1, PP-InsP phosphohydrolase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Transient expression of PFA-DSP1 in N. benthamiana leaves specifically decreases 5-InsP7 and InsP8.
mechanism: PFA-DSP1 hydrolyzes 5-InsP7 and InsP8, reducing their levels in planta.

genes: PFA-DSP1 (PFA-DSP1, PP-InsP phosphohydrolase, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Expression of catalytically inactive PFA-DSP1C150S-EYFP does not decrease 5-InsP7 and InsP8 levels.
mechanism: The catalytically inactive PFA-DSP1C150S-EYFP lacks phosphohydrolase activity, so it does not hydrolyze 5-InsP7 and InsP8.

genes: ZmGa1Ps-m (ZmGa1P.1, ZmGa1P.2, ZmGa1P.3, ZmGa1P.4, ZmGa1P.5, overexpression, source: Zea mays), ZmPME3 (pectin methylesterase, source: Zea mays), ZmPRP3 (barwin domain, source: Zea mays)
phenotype: Overexpression of ZmGa1Ps-m, ZmPME3, and ZmPRP3 increases pollen tube growth in Zea mays, allowing successful fertilization and overcoming cross incompatibility.
mechanism: ZmGa1Ps-m and ZmPME3 enhance pectin esterification, facilitating pollen tube elongation through improved cell wall modification. ZmPRP3 may modulate cell wall integrity or signaling pathways involved in pollen tube growth.

genes: MPK17 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 17, negative regulator in Xa21-mediated immunity, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: MPK17 knockdown enhances resistance to Xoo (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae) in rice 4021.
mechanism: MPK17 is a negative regulator in the Xa21-mediated immunity pathway, and its knockdown enhances resistance by modulating WRKY62 and PR1A expression.

genes: MPK17 (mitogen-activated protein kinase 17, negative regulator in Xa21-mediated immunity, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: MPK17 overexpression impairs resistance to Xoo (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae) in rice 4021.
mechanism: MPK17 is a negative regulator in the Xa21-mediated immunity pathway, and its overexpression impairs resistance by modulating WRKY62 and PR1A expression.

genes: P25 (viral movement protein, 25 kDa, potato), HC-Pro (helper component proteinase, major factor in viral pathogenicity, potato), Brp1 (bromodomain-containing RNA-binding protein for Virp1, potato)
phenotype: Transgenic potato plants showed resistance to PVX, PVY, and PSTVd coinfection, with no viral symptoms observed and higher tuber yield compared to nontransgenic plants.
mechanism: amiRNAs targeting P25, HC-Pro, and Brp1 genes induced gene silencing, thereby preventing viral replication and systemic spread.

genes: BrDREB2B (transcription factor, abiotic stress response, Brassica rapa)
phenotype: Transgenic plants overexpressing BrDREB2B showed better growth status and higher survival rates after drought, high-salt, and high-temperature stresses compared to wild-type plants.
mechanism: BrDREB2B improves tolerance to abiotic stress by maintaining the homeostasis of intracellular reactive oxygen species.

genes: SS1G_01703 (ABHYDROLASE-3, gene involved in aflatoxin synthesis, Sclerotinia sclerotiorum)
phenotype: hpRNA expression targeting SS1G_01703 reduces S. sclerotiorum infection in Brassica napus, with reduced lesion sizes and fungal rDNA accumulation in stems.
mechanism: hpRNAi transgene construct results in gene silencing of the S. sclerotiorum ABHYDROLASE-3 transcript, reducing fungal infection.

genes: eIF4E1-S (eukaryotic initiation factor 4E1, from Nicotiana sylvestris), eIF4E1-T (eukaryotic initiation factor 4E1, from Nicotiana tomentosiformis), eIF4E2-S (eukaryotic initiation factor 4E2, from Nicotiana sylvestris), eIF4E2-T (eukaryotic initiation factor 4E2, from Nicotiana tomentosiformis)
phenotype: Knockout of eIF4E1-S, eIF4E1-T, eIF4E2-S, and eIF4E2-T genes results in durable and broad resistance against PVY without jeopardizing plant performance.
mechanism: Deletion of multiple eIF4E genes disrupts the ability of PVY to recruit paralog gene products, thereby inhibiting viral replication and spread.

genes: MIR160a (miRNA, part of potato immune response, regulates cell death and auxin signaling, Solanum tuberosum), MIR160b (miRNA, part of potato immune response, regulates cell death and auxin signaling, Solanum tuberosum), MIR390a (miRNA, part of potato immune response, regulates cell death and auxin signaling, Solanum tuberosum)
phenotype: CRISPR-edited MIR160a transgenic lines (40% in Désirée and 100% in Rywal) exhibit sickle-shaped leaves and lamina growth arrest; one Désirée transgenic line had small circular leaves when grown in soil.
mechanism: Perturbation of miR160-5p targets auxin response factors (ARFs), leading to disrupted auxin signaling and resulting in the observed phenotypes.

genes: BoALG10 (leaf margin development gene, smooth leaf margin, Brassica oleracea var. oleracea)
phenotype: Overexpression of BoALG10 produces an S0835-like smooth leaf margin in F0819.
mechanism: BoALG10 sustains the smooth leaf margin shape by maintaining the N-glycan biosynthesis pathway.

genes: BoALG10 (leaf margin development gene, smooth leaf margin, Brassica oleracea var. oleracea)
gene_construct: Cas9 vector with gRNA targeting first and second exons of BoALG10
phenotype: Knockout of BoALG10 produces a feathered leaf margin in S0835.
mechanism: Mutation of BoALG10 causes a loss of function, blocking the N-glycan biosynthesis pathway, meaning that the smooth leaf margin phenotype cannot be maintained.

genes: SSA1 (pentapeptide repeat (PPR) protein, involved in Photosystem I (PSI) assembly, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Expression of SSA1 under the actin promoter reverses the albino phenotype to the wild type (WT) phenotype in rice (Oryza sativa).
mechanism: SSA1 regulates early chloroplast development and plays a critical role in RNA editing and intron splicing in rice.

genes: peroxidase7 (peroxidase, ROS scavenging, Nicotiana tabacum)
phenotype: Overexpression of peroxidase7 increases shoot dry weight by 25.0%, root length by 12.9%, and secondary root number by 48.2% in Nicotiana tabacum under Cu stress, while decreasing Cu content in plant leaves by 38.24% compared with wild type.
mechanism: Peroxidase7 enhances Cu resistance by increasing ROS scavenging ability and reducing lipid peroxidation, thereby improving the plant's ability to tolerate Cu stress.

genes: METTL4 (methyltransferase-like protein 4, responsible for m6Am modification, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescue of the early flowering phenotype in mettl4-1 mutant plants.
mechanism: The reintroduction of a wild-type copy of METTL4 restores the m6Am modification in U2 snRNA, which is critical for normal flowering time regulation.

genes: METTL4 (methyltransferase-like protein 4, responsible for m6Am modification, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Rescue of the early flowering phenotype in mettl4-1 mutant plants with a catalytically inactive METTL4 variant.
mechanism: The reintroduction of a catalytically inactive METTL4 variant (D233A/W236A) does not restore the m6Am modification in U2 snRNA, indicating that the catalytic activity of METTL4 is essential for the rescue of the early flowering phenotype.

genes: OsWHY1 (WHY1 protein, whirly structural domain, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Loss-of-function oswhy1 mutants exhibit an albino-lethal phenotype at the seedling stage.
mechanism: OsWHY1 interacts with OsTRX z and affects chloroplast RNA editing and splicing, PEP activity, and plastid ribosomes development, leading to impaired chloroplast development.

genes: PlCO (photoperiod pathway gene, transcription factor, Paeonia lactiflora)
phenotype: Overexpression of PlCO significantly advances the flowering time in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana plants.
mechanism: PlCO acts as a transcription factor with nucleus localization and activates downstream genes regulating flowering.

genes: CcPDS (phytoene desaturase, enzyme involved in carotenoid biosynthesis, Coffea canephora)
phenotype: Knockout of CcPDS gene results in albino, variegated, and green phenotypes in Coffea canephora.
mechanism: Mutations in the CcPDS gene lead to early stop codons, resulting in truncated proteins and loss of function, which disrupts carotenoid biosynthesis and causes the albino phenotype.

genes: MdPUB23 (U-box E3 ubiquitin ligase, negative regulator of cold-stress response, Malus domestica), MdICE1 (key positive regulator of cold-stress response, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdPUB23 reduces cold-stress tolerance in apple calli and leaves, while antisense constructs increase cold-stress tolerance. In Arabidopsis, MdPUB23 overexpression also reduces cold-stress tolerance.
mechanism: MdPUB23 interacts with MdICE1 and promotes its ubiquitination and degradation via the 26S-proteasome pathway, thereby negatively regulating MdICE1-induced cold-stress tolerance.

genes: SlIAA9 (Indole Acetic Acid 9, negative regulator of the auxin response pathway, Solanum lycopersicum), SlAGL6 (SlAGAMOUS-LIKE 6, MADS-box protein, Solanum lycopersicum)
gene_construct: dsIAA9 (DNA fragment covering part of the 3′ coding sequence and part of the 3′ untranslated terminal region of SlIAA9)---dsAGL6 (DNA fragment comprising the guide sequence for CRISPR/Cas9 editing of SlAGL6)
phenotype: Downregulation of SlIAA9 and SlAGL6 transcripts resulted in increased ovary size and parthenocarpic fruit development.
mechanism: Silencing of SlIAA9 and SlAGL6 repressor genes allows ovary growth before and/or independently of fertilization.

genes: IgA heavy chain (IgA heavy chain gene, Stx1-neutralizing antibody heavy chain, mouse IgA-derived, mouse IgA), IgA light chain (IgA light chain gene, Stx1-neutralizing antibody light chain, mouse IgA-derived, mouse IgA), immunoglobulin joining chain (J chain gene, Stx1-neutralizing antibody joining chain, mouse IgA-derived, mouse IgA)
phenotype: Production of Stx1-specific IgA plantibody with improved expression levels and antigen recognition compared to hyIgA.
mechanism: Optimized codon usage for Arabidopsis thaliana, addition of ER retention signal (KDEL) to increase expression, and replacement of vulnerable regions with mouse IgA sequences to avoid proteolytic digestion.

genes: Refre1/372 (Fe-related gene, source: Oryza sativa L.), OsHRZ2 (3'UTR, source: Oryza sativa L.)
phenotype: HRZ2i + Refre lines show increased Fe concentrations in brown seeds and straw under calcareous soil conditions, with Fe concentrations increasing by ×3.0–4.0 in Fe-sufficient soil, ×5.4 in non-submerged calcareous soil, and ×4.3 in submerged calcareous soil.
mechanism: Concomitant enhancement of strategy II (increased metal accumulation) and strategy I (Fe uptake) contributes to extended Fe deficiency tolerance in rice.

genes: LsPIN1 (auxin efflux carrier, from L. secalinus)
phenotype: Overexpression of LsPIN1 increases the length of primary roots (PRs) and the number of lateral roots (LRs) in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: LsPIN1 alters auxin transport and promotes auxin accumulation in root tips.

genes: StHRC (histidine rich Ca2+ binding protein, functional gene, Russet Burbank potato), Sthrc (histidine rich Ca2+ binding protein, mutated gene, Russet Burbank potato)
gene_construct: CRISPR-Cas9 construct with guide RNA targeting StHRC
phenotype: Silencing of StHRC in Russet Burbank potato confers multiple disease resistance, including reduced late blight (Phytophthora infestans) lesion diameter by 3.0-fold, reduced pathogen biomass in stem by 24.6-fold and in leaf by 14.4-fold, and reduced early blight (Alternaria solani) lesion diameter by 2.3-fold and pathogen biomass by 12.5-fold.
mechanism: Silencing of HRC in plants confers multiple disease resistance, likely through modulation of defense-related gene expression and induction of programmed cell death (AL-PCD).

genes: MYC2-like (transcription factor, ABA-responsive transcription factor, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: MYC2-like overexpression in wild-type and cyp2-RNAi lines improves salt tolerance, as evidenced by increased antioxidant enzyme activity and reduced lipid peroxidation.
mechanism: MYC2-like increases resistance to salt stress by enhancing the activity of antioxidative enzymes and post-translational regulation in transformed plants.

genes: AGL42 (transcription factor, repressor, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AGL42 increases total chlorophyll, chlorophyll a, and chlorophyll b content in transgenic cotton plants compared to non-transgenic controls.
mechanism: AGL42 acts as a transcriptional repressor, downregulating NAC senescence genes (GhNAC8, GhNAC9, GhNAC12, GhNAC14, GhNAC16, GhNAC17) under drought stress, which delays leaf senescence and improves drought tolerance.

genes: SiER1_X4 (ER family member, involved in thermotolerance and photosynthesis, Setaria italica), SiER4_X1 (ER family member, involved in thermotolerance and photosynthesis, Setaria italica)
phenotype: Overexpression of SiER1_X4 and SiER4_X1 increases plant height and biomass accumulation in Arabidopsis thaliana, and enhances thermotolerance under high-temperature stress.
mechanism: SiER1_X4 and SiER4_X1 may be involved in the regulation of SOD synthesis or activity at high temperature and alleviate the damage to cells inflicted by O2− and H2O2 during adversity.

genes: GmRR11d (cytokinin response regulator, positive regulator of CK signaling, Glycine max)
phenotype: Overexpression of GmRR11d increases sensitivity of soybean roots to cytokinin-induced growth inhibition.
mechanism: GmRR11d acts as a positive regulator of CK signaling and the plant CK response in soybean.

genes: GlPS1 (psoralen synthase, involved in coumarin biosynthesis, G. littoralis)
phenotype: Overexpression of GlPS1 increases salt tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
mechanism: GlPS1 may accumulate secondary metabolites, enhancing salt tolerance.

genes: O3 (O3 gene, encoding a protein involved in storage protein processing and export from the ER, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Complementation of the o3 mutant restores normal grain filling, increases total starch, amylose, and total protein contents, and reduces the accumulation of 57-kDa proglutelins in endosperm.
mechanism: O3 facilitates the maturation and export of proglutelins from the ER, thereby promoting normal storage protein processing and starch grain formation.

genes: O3 (O3 gene, encoding a protein involved in storage protein processing and export from the ER, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of O3 results in defective grain filling, reduced total starch, amylose, and total protein contents, and increased accumulation of 57-kDa proglutelins in endosperm.
mechanism: O3 facilitates the maturation and export of proglutelins from the ER, thereby promoting normal storage protein processing and starch grain formation.

genes: FD (floral regulator, SAM-localized, Arabidopsis thaliana), CLAVATA3 (CLV3, synthetic, synthetic)
phenotype: Phenocopied loss of function of FD and CLV3 targets, altering target gene expression.
mechanism: Phloem-to-SAM silencing communication axis connects distal regions of the plant to SAM stem cells.

genes: MdcyMDH1 (malate dehydrogenase 1, cytoplasmic, Malus domestica)
phenotype: Overexpression of MdcyMDH1 increases malate content in mature fruit at 120 DAB and alters sugar content by increasing sucrose and sorbitol while decreasing glucose and starch.
mechanism: MdcyMDH1 enhances malate metabolism in both cytoplasm and mitochondria, influencing sugar content through altered enzyme activities involved in sugar metabolism.

genes: SlGCR (G2-LIKE CAROTENOID REGULATOR, transcription factor, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Fruit-specific overexpression of SlGCR enhances lutein biosynthesis in tomato fruit, resulting in orange phenotypes at the Br7 stage compared to the red pericarp of MicroTom.
mechanism: RNA-seq and RT-qPCR results showed that the expression levels of most carotenoid biosynthetic genes were significantly higher than those of MicroTom (SlPDS1, SlZDS, SlZISO, SlCRTISO, SlLCYE).

genes: BnaC08.PPT1 (phosphoenolpyruvate/phosphate translocator, involved in PEP transport from cytosol to plastid, Brassica napus)
phenotype: Overexpression of BnaC08.PPT1 significantly promotes seed oil content by 2.1 to 3.3% in Brassica napus.
mechanism: BnaPPT1 facilitates PEP transport from the cytosol to the plastid, which is essential for glycolysis, fatty acid (FA) synthesis, and lipid droplet formation, thereby promoting seed oil accumulation.

genes: OsRNS1 (RNase T2 class 1 gene, involved in root development and ROS regulation, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsRNS1 under the Os1-CysPrxB (Per) promoter increases root length, plant height, and grain yield compared to wild-type (WT).
mechanism: The use of a root-preferred promoter effectively optimizes the function of OsRNS1 and is a useful strategy for improving root-related agronomic traits as well as ROS regulation.

genes: CabHLH035 (basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, salt stress response, Capsicum annuum)
phenotype: Overexpression of CabHLH035 increases salt tolerance in pepper and Arabidopsis, as evidenced by reduced wilting, lower MDA content, and higher Fv/Fm values. Knockdown of CabHLH035 decreases salt tolerance in pepper, leading to increased wilting, higher MDA content, and lower Fv/Fm values.
mechanism: CabHLH035 enhances salt tolerance by modulating ion homeostasis and proline biosynthesis through interactions with CaNAC035 and regulation of CaSOS1 and CaP5CS.

genes: SlbHLH96 (bHLH transcription factor, drought stress response, Solanum lycopersicum)
phenotype: Overexpression of SlbHLH96 in tomato improves drought tolerance, with ~45–53% survival rate after 7 days of recovery compared to <20% in wild-type plants.
mechanism: SlbHLH96 enhances ROS detoxification by increasing antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD and POD), elevating proline accumulation, and reducing membrane damage and MDA content under drought stress.

genes: AtSOAR1 (Arabidopsis SOAR1, negative regulator in ABA signaling, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Overexpression of AtSOAR1 in rice exhibits salt tolerance phenotype at seedling growth stage as indicated by the higher survival rate, higher chlorophyll content and lower relative ion leakage of the transgenic plants compared with that of wild-type under salt stress.
mechanism: AtSOAR1 influences ABA signaling, salt-responsive genes expression and pre-mRNA splicing under salt stress.

genes: OsSOAR1 (Os01g0506100, homologous gene in rice, positive regulator in response to salt stress, Oryza sativa)
phenotype: Overexpression of OsSOAR1 in rice exhibits salt tolerance phenotype at seedling growth stage as indicated by the higher survival rate, higher chlorophyll content and lower relative ion leakage of the transgenic plants compared with that of wild-type under salt stress.
mechanism: OsSOAR1 plays positive roles in response to salt stress.

genes: OsBBM1 (parthenogenesis inducer, rice)
phenotype: Induction of synthetic apomixis with a high frequency of diploid progeny plants (up to 97%) in T0 T315 events.
mechanism: The OsBBM1 gene driven by the rice egg cell-specific promoter (OsECA1) triggers parthenogenesis from the egg cell, leading to the production of diploid progeny plants.

genes: BBM1 (parthenogenesis inducer, Arabidopsis thaliana)
phenotype: Induction of synthetic apomixis with a high frequency of diploid progeny plants (up to 97%) in T0 T314 events.
mechanism: The BBM1 gene driven by the Arabidopsis egg cell-specific promoter (EC1.2) triggers parthenogenesis from the egg cell, leading to the production of diploid progeny plants.

genes: PAIR1 (meiosis-related, rice), REC8 (meiosis-related, rice), OSD1 (meiosis-related, rice)
phenotype: Induction of apomeiosis (meiosis suppression) in T0 T313 events, resulting in tetraploid progeny plants.
mechanism: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated inactivation of PAIR1, REC8, and OSD1 suppresses meiosis, leading to the formation of tetraploid progeny plants.
